records.full_text:
FINANCIAL.

The Commissioners made a thorough and careful examination of the debt of San Domingo, and find the sum total of all debts and outstanding claims against the Republic to be $1,565,831. The receipts of the government for 1870 were $772,684, of which $728,605 was from customs and $35,466 from taxes. The Commissioners lay great stress on their efforts to get the exact state of the debt of the Dominican Republic, and believe their conclusions substantially correct. San Domingo is not believed to be liable for any of the indemnity exacted by France from Hayti, and the Commission is assured that no obligation or negotiations have been entered into with any country except the United States.

The extent of undisputed Dominican territory is 22,512 square miles. The portion which formerly involved a dispute with Hayti being 1000 square miles. The Commissioners present a full statement of all the grants and concessions of public lands and franchise, and declare that after the most searching and complete investigation they were unable to find any grant or concession in any form or manner to any U. S. official, either in connection with the negotiation or preparation of the treaty.

records.headline: The St. Cloud Journal notes that Senator Charles Sumner's speech
records.summary_en: The St. Cloud Journal notes that Senator Charles Sumner's speech against Dominican annexation was, in the view of leading newspapers, injudicious, delivered before the San Domingo Commissioners submitted their report. It quotes the New York Tribune, which argues that Sumner erred by speaking before Commissioners Wade, White, and Howe concluded their municipal inquiries across the Dominican Republic, adding that Sumner holds no superiority in honesty or information over the commissioners. The paper also quotes the New York Times, which asserts that Sumner's facts fail to warrant his conclusions and cannot sustain his charge of usurpation against President Grant.
records.summary_es: El St. Cloud Journal señala que destacados periódicos consideran imprudente el discurso del senador Charles Sumner contra la anexión dominicana, pronunciado antes de que los comisionados de Santo Domingo presentaran su informe. Cita al New York Tribune, que sostiene que Sumner se equivocó al hablar antes de que los comisionados Wade, White y Howe concluyeran sus investigaciones municipales en casi toda la República Dominicana, añadiendo que Sumner no aventaja a los comisionados en honradez ni en información. El diario cita también al New York Times, el cual afirma que los datos expuestos por Sumner apenas justifican sus conclusiones y fracasan por completo en fundamentar su acusación de usurpación contra el presidente Grant.

records.headline: An excerpt from the report of the San Domingo Commission characterizes
records.summary_en: An excerpt from the report of the San Domingo Commission characterizes the insurgent band under Luperón as a small guerrilla force possessing only the strength of a desperado. The Commissioners state that Dominican insurgent leaders would have been suppressed long ago without foreign intrigue and the armed backing of Haiti, which possesses nearly three times the population and revenue of the Dominican Republic. Under the heading "Causes of Disturbance," the report explains that internal strife is further aggravated by intense provincial rivalry between the northern and southern regions. It contrasts the thriving northern commercial centers of Puerto Plata and Santiago with the historic capital of Santo Domingo in the south.
records.summary_es: Un extracto del informe de la Comisión de Santo Domingo califica la partida insurgente de Luperón como una pequeña fuerza guerrillera que solo posee la fuerza de un forajido. Los comisionados afirman que los líderes insurgentes dominicanos habrían sido reprimidos hace mucho tiempo de no ser por las intrigas extranjeras y el respaldo armado de Haití, país que cuenta con casi tres veces la población y los ingresos de la República Dominicana. Bajo el subtítulo «Causas de los disturbios», el informe explica que las contiendas internas se ven agravadas además por una marcada rivalidad provincial entre las regiones del norte y del sur. Contrasta los prósperos centros comerciales norteños de Puerto Plata y Santiago con la histórica capital de Santo Domingo en el sur.

records.headline: An installment of the San Domingo Commission report in the Tribune describes
records.summary_en: An installment of the San Domingo Commission report in the Tribune describes the agricultural and social condition of the Dominican people. The report notes that pineapples flourish widely and that wheat grows in the high valley of Constanza, yet observes that underdeveloped agriculture forces reliance on imported French sugar, Danish butter, and American condensed milk. Turning to education and civic life, the Commissioners note that only one small, poorly equipped printing office operates in the capital, though teachers report good native ability among students. Under the heading "General Political Capacity," the report judges the populace to be by no means hopeless, emphasizing that generations without slavery or caste divisions have fostered self-reliance, industry, and capable patriotic leaders.
records.summary_es: Una entrega del informe de la Comisión de Santo Domingo en el Tribune describe la situación agrícola y social del pueblo dominicano. El informe señala que las piñas prosperan ampliamente y que el trigo crece en el alto valle de Constanza, aunque observa que el subdesarrollo agrícola obliga a depender de azúcar francés, mantequilla danesa y leche condensada estadounidense importadas. En cuanto a la educación y la vida cívica, los comisionados indican que solo funciona una imprenta pequeña y mal equipada en la capital, si bien los maestros informan de una buena capacidad innata en los estudiantes. Bajo el subtítulo «Capacidad política general», el informe considera que el pueblo no es en modo alguno desesperanzador, destacando que generaciones sin esclavitud ni castas han fomentado la dignidad, el trabajo y líderes patriotas capaces.

records.headline: The Commissioners' report describes St. Domingo's forests
records.summary_en: The Commissioners' report describes St. Domingo's forests as its most striking feature, with palms near the coast and mahogany, satinwood, Dominican oak, pitch pine, lignum vitae, logwood and other valuable woods inland. It says wide forests in the interior remain untouched for lack of roads, that large mahogany logs are left to decay by the roadside within thirty miles of the principal northern seaport, and that no sawmill was found in the country.
records.summary_es: El informe de los Comisionados describe los bosques de Santo Domingo como su rasgo más llamativo, con palmas cerca de la costa y caoba, palo satín, roble dominicano, pino resinoso, guayacán, campeche y otras maderas valiosas en el interior. Dice que amplios bosques del interior permanecen intactos por falta de caminos, que grandes troncos de caoba se dejan pudrir junto a los caminos a menos de treinta millas del principal puerto del norte, y que no se encontró ningún aserradero en el país.

The testimony of the head of a thrifty New England family, who had resided in the neighborhood of Samana Bay nearly two years, was to the effect that there was as little difficulty in keeping a house clear from troublesome insects, as in our Northern States. products [illegible] The most striking characteristic of St. Domingo, at first sight, is the wonderful luxuriance of its forests. In many parts, and especially in the neighborhood of the Bay of Samana, although there are abrupt ridges, perpendicular cliffs and bold headlands, no bare rocks can be seen, being hidden by a mass of strong vegetation. But on close observation another and not less striking characteristic is revealed: an astonishing variety in forest products. The cause of this variety is to be found, doubtless, in the great difference in elevation of the surface exposure and character of the soil. Near the coast various species of palm are abundant, and very valuable in constructing such houses as have been generally found best suited to the climate. On the mountain slopes, at different heights, grow in abundance both the choicest cabinet woods, as mahogany, satinwood, &c., and a great variety of timber especially valuable in housebuilding. The roble, or Dominican oak, and a hard pitch pine were found in abundance in various parts of the country. In the more dry districts flourish several valuable woods, the best known of which, perhaps, is the lignum vitae, of which the quantity is very great. records.headline: An excerpt from the report of the San Domingo Commission in the Herald reviews
records.summary_en: An excerpt from the report of the San Domingo Commission in the Herald reviews the political leadership of President Buenaventura Báez. The Commissioners state that a large majority of the Dominican people esteem Báez for his administrative capacity, regarding him as the sole leader capable of maintaining national unity against internal discord and external threats. The report recounts that following the overthrow of Haitian rule, Báez presided over the constituent congress and was elected president in 1849, presiding over the only administration in Dominican history to serve out its complete constitutional term. After Gen. Pedro Santana succeeded him in 1853, recurrent civil turmoil and Spanish annexation followed, during which Báez was repeatedly summoned from exile to re-establish provisional government.
records.summary_es: Un extracto del informe de la Comisión de Santo Domingo publicado en el Herald examina el liderazgo político del presidente Buenaventura Báez. Los comisionados afirman que una gran mayoría del pueblo dominicano aprecia a Báez por su capacidad administrativa, considerándolo el único líder capaz de preservar la unidad nacional frente a las discordias internas y las amenazas externas. El informe relata que, tras la expulsión del dominio haitiano, Báez presidió el congreso constituyente y fue elegido presidente en 1849, encabezando la única administración en la historia dominicana que completó todo su período constitucional. Después de que el general Pedro Santana lo sucediera en 1853, sobrevinieron recurrentes disturbios civiles y la anexión española, durante los cuales Báez fue convocado reiteradamente desde el exilio para restablecer el gobierno provisional.

records.headline: Border rebellions and foreign interference in Dominican affairs
records.summary_en: Border rebellions and foreign interference in Dominican affairs are addressed in an extract of the Commission's report printed by the Herald. The Commissioners confirm government charges that insurgent forces received arms and troops through Haiti, citing depositions and the examination of Haitian prisoners carrying muskets with Haitian government stamps. The report characterizes Luperón's force near Manzanillo Bay as a small guerrilla band lacking broad support, asserting that neither Cabral nor Luperón could have sustained their resistance without foreign intriguers and the active backing of Haiti. Under the heading "Causes of Disturbance," the Commissioners add that regional jealousy between the northern and southern provinces has further weakened national cohesion.
records.summary_es: El Herald publica un extracto del informe de la Comisión sobre las rebeliones fronterizas, que aborda la injerencia extranjera en los asuntos dominicanos. Los comisionados confirman las acusaciones gubernamentales de que las fuerzas insurgentes recibieron armas y tropas a través de Haití, citando declaraciones y el interrogatorio de prisioneros haitianos que portaban fusiles con el sello del gobierno haitiano. El informe califica la fuerza de Luperón cerca de la bahía de Manzanillo como una pequeña partida guerrillera carente de apoyo amplio, afirmando que ni Cabral ni Luperón habrían sostenido su resistencia sin intrigantes extranjeros y el respaldo activo de Haití. Bajo el subtítulo «Causas de los disturbios», los comisionados agregan que el recelo regional entre las provincias del norte y del sur ha debilitado aún más la cohesión nacional.

records.headline: The United States Commissioners report that of the great bays of Samana, Azua and Manzanilla, which admit vessels of the largest
records.summary_en: The United States Commissioners report that of the great bays of Samana, Azua and Manzanilla, which admit vessels of the largest draft, only Samana has importance from a military point of view, and that its acquisition would give the United States a powerful military and naval station and the site of an important commercial city. The report also sets out the Dominican government's debt and obligations in detail, along with its receipts for 1870, while noting that the statement includes much the Dominican government itself believes to be partially or wholly groundless.
records.summary_es: Los comisionados de los Estados Unidos informan que de las grandes bahías de Samaná, Azua y Manzanillo, que admiten buques del mayor calado, solo Samaná tiene importancia desde el punto de vista militar, y que su adquisición daría a los Estados Unidos una poderosa estación militar y naval y el sitio de una importante ciudad comercial. El informe expone también en detalle la deuda y las obligaciones del gobierno dominicano, junto con sus ingresos de 1870, señalando que la relación incluye mucho que el propio gobierno dominicano cree parcial o totalmente infundado.

records.summary_en: According to the newspaper, Dominican authorities informed the Commissioners that their current administration has had no diplomatic representation, treaties, or engagements with any government except the United States. The Commissioners also found that undisputed Dominican territory spans 22,212 square miles, with about 1,000 square miles formerly involved in disputes with Hayti. Additionally, after examining government and municipal grants, including records in Samana, the Commissioners found no truth to rumors that land concessions or grants had been made to officials of the Government or the United States during the negotiation of the 1869 annexation treaty.
records.summary_es: Según el diario, las autoridades dominicanas manifestaron a los comisionados que la administración en funciones carecía de representaciones diplomáticas, alianzas o compromisos con nación alguna fuera de los Estados Unidos. Los comisionados determinaron igualmente que el territorio dominicano incontestado comprendía 22.212 millas cuadradas, con cerca de 1.000 millas cuadradas sujetas antiguamente a diferendos con Haití. Asimismo, tras registrar los archivos oficiales y municipales, incluidos los protocolos de Samaná, la comisión constató la total falsedad de las imputaciones sobre concesiones de tierras otorgadas a dignatarios del gobierno dominicano o de los Estados Unidos durante la negociación del tratado de anexión de 1869.

records.full_text:
The following statement of receipts for 1870 is here presented, in order to give, as far as possible, a complete view of the financial condition of the Dominican Republic: Resume of the income of the Government for 1870: First, Customs receipts, tonnage, $2,730,660; entrance fees, $147,995; light houses, $67,901; anchorage, $196,995; pilotage, $142,827; lighterage, $21,800; interpreter, $640 26; signal men, $59,410; quarantine, $48,016; wharfage, $679,888; recargo municipal, $110,586; recargo for steamer, $588,014; water, $24,100; impost dues, $691,393 64; export dues, $71,419 20; coast fees, $7,511 11.

The Commissioners believe that the statement of the public debt given above includes all the indebtedness or obligations for which the Dominican Republic is in any degree liable, as well as that which it considers valid and binding, as that which it regards as unfounded or overstated by the claimants. Throughout the inquiry it was urged upon the Dominican authorities that every claim known to exist, of whatever character, should be exhibited to the Commission, whose object was not to determine the precise amount that was justly due and binding, but to get at the bottom and find the utmost limit of their obligations, and setting forth everything for which the Government could under any circumstances be made liable. The above account contains much that the Dominican Government believes to be partially or wholly groundless, and some which upon the inspection will appear questionable. Among the pending claims is one of President Baez for the destruction of property. It is alleged by the claimant that the Spanish Government recognized this claim as valid, and ordered an examination to fix the amount, but the Commission cannot understand how this claim could be valid against the Dominican Government.

A question has been raised in our country whether the Government and people of the Dominican Republic, having once been under the rule of Haytiens, might not be liable for a portion of the indemnity exacted for France from Hayti, for the estates of French families which had been confiscated by the Haytiens during the revolution of 1791. The Commission made inquiries on the subject of the Dominican Government, and also in Hayti, and they could not learn that the Haytien Government had ever made this claim upon the Dominican Republic, and they think that if made it would be wholly without foundation.

The Commissioners were informed by the Dominican authorities that the present administration of the Government has not had diplomatic representation or made treaties or engagements with any other government except the United States. An enumeration of the treaties made during the previous history of the Republic of France, Great Britain, and other powers, will be found in Ex. Doc. 17, Forty-first Congress, second session. They are mostly treaties of navigation and commerce, and contain no unusual provision requiring notice here.

The extent of undisputed Dominican territory is 22,212 square miles, the portion of which has been formerly involved in dispute with Hayti being about 1,000 square miles.

records.headline: A special correspondent describes the history and commercial vitality of Santiago de los Caballeros
records.summary_en: A special correspondent describes the history and commercial vitality of Santiago de los Caballeros, noting that after repeated destruction by French forces, Haitian invasions, the 1842 earthquake, and fires during the 1864 restoration war against Spain, the town was substantially rebuilt. The writer highlights the enterprise of its residents, observing that Santiago now boasts the finest shops in the Dominican Republic and bustling streets filled with pack trains transporting coffee and tobacco from Moca and La Vega to Puerto Plata. The letter reports that local merchants maintain commercial ties across the interior but remain financially dependent on trading houses in St. Thomas and Hamburg, where most purchases and exports are concentrated.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal especial describe la historia y la vitalidad comercial de Santiago de los Caballeros, destacando que, tras repetidas destrucciones a manos de tropas francesas, invasiones haitianas, el terremoto de 1842 y los incendios de la guerra restauradora contra España en 1864, la ciudad fue reconstruida sólidamente. El autor resalta la iniciativa de sus pobladores y observa que Santiago cuenta hoy con los mejores comercios de la República Dominicana y calles concurridas por recuas que transportan café y tabaco desde Moca y La Vega hacia Puerto Plata. La carta informa que los comerciantes locales mantienen vínculos mercantiles en todo el interior, pero dependen financieramente de las casas comerciales de Saint Thomas y Hamburgo, donde se concentran la mayoría de sus compras y exportaciones.

records.headline: A correspondent travelling with the Commission reports being repeatedly
records.summary_en: A correspondent travelling with the Commission reports being repeatedly urged that, following annexation, the United States should organize Dominican men into a paid uniform militia capable of maintaining domestic order without foreign troops. Small American garrisons at Puerto Plata, Samaná, and Azua were considered sufficient additions to such a local force. The writer notes that in Santiago and across the country, most landowners and educated residents favor annexation to secure stability. Upon reaching Puerto Plata, described as the republic's primary commercial port and chief center of unrest, the party rendezvoused with Commissioner White and sailed on March 5th aboard the warship Nantasket for Port-au-Prince to rejoin their colleagues.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal que viajaba con la Comisión relata que le sugirieron reiteradamente que, tras la anexión, los Estados Unidos deberían organizar a los dominicanos en una milicia remunerada y uniformada, capaz de mantener el orden interno sin tropas extranjeras. Se consideraba que bastaría añadir pequeñas guarniciones estadounidenses en Puerto Plata, Samaná y Azua a dicha fuerza local. El autor señala que en Santiago y en todo el país, la mayoría de los terratenientes y ciudadanos educados apoyan la anexión para asegurar la estabilidad. Al llegar a Puerto Plata, descrita como el principal puerto comercial y foco de disturbios de la república, la comitiva se reunió con el comisionado White y zarpó el 5 de marzo en el buque de guerra Nantasket rumbo a Puerto Príncipe para unirse a sus colegas.

records.headline: A published joint resolution details the scope of inquiry for the commissioners
records.summary_en: A published joint resolution details the scope of inquiry for the commissioners appointed to examine conditions in the Dominican Republic. It directs them to investigate meteorological phenomena, public debt whether funded or unadjusted, foreign treaties, territorial boundaries, and concession grants, as well as the terms under which the Dominican government may desire annexation as a United States territory. The commissioners are instructed to report to the President for transmittal to Congress, serving without compensation beyond expenses. The resolution specifies that nothing contained within it shall be construed as committing Congress to annexing the territory of the republic of Dominica.
records.summary_es: Una resolución conjunta publicada detalla el alcance de la investigación para los comisionados designados para examinar las condiciones en la República Dominicana. Les ordena investigar los fenómenos meteorológicos, la deuda pública ya sea consolidada o no liquidada, los tratados extranjeros, los límites territoriales y las concesiones otorgadas, así como los términos bajo los cuales el gobierno dominicano pueda desear la anexión como territorio de los Estados Unidos. Se instruye a los comisionados a informar al presidente para su remisión al Congreso, prestando sus servicios sin más compensación que sus gastos. La resolución especifica que nada de lo contenido en ella se interpretará como un compromiso del Congreso con la anexión del territorio de dicha república de Dominica.

records.headline: The Springfield Weekly Republican prints findings from the San Domingo commission
records.summary_en: The Springfield Weekly Republican prints findings from the San Domingo commission report regarding local governance, the Spanish occupation, and annexation sentiment. The commissioners report that difficulties in local self-government would disappear under connection with a strong nation, noting that many town councils remain efficient and capable. Under the heading 'The Spanish Occupation,' the report finds that the 1861 annexation was consummated by fraud and proved oppressive, threatening Freemasonry and risking the return of slavery until popular revolt forced Spanish troops into unhealthy coastal strongholds, where between 6,000 and 8,000 of Spain's 35,000 soldiers died of disease or deserted. The commissioners add that desire for annexation to the United States was found to be widespread and ardently shared by colonies of colored immigrants from the United States.
records.summary_es: El Springfield Weekly Republican publica conclusiones del informe de la comisión de Santo Domingo relativas a la gobernanza local, la ocupación española y el sentimiento hacia la anexión. Los comisionados informan que las dificultades en el autogobierno local desaparecerían bajo la conexión con una nación fuerte, señalando que muchos ayuntamientos siguen siendo eficientes y capaces. Bajo el título «The Spanish Occupation», el informe determina que la anexión de 1861 se consumó mediante fraude y resultó opresiva, amenazando a la masonería y arriesgando el restablecimiento de la esclavitud hasta que la sublevación popular obligó a las tropas españolas a retirarse a fortalezas costeras insalubres, donde entre 6,000 y 8,000 de los 35,000 soldados de España murieron por enfermedades o desertaron. Los comisionados añaden que encontraron un deseo generalizado de anexión a los Estados Unidos, compartido fervientemente por las colonias de inmigrantes de color procedentes de dicho país.

records.headline: The Springfield Weekly Republican publishes extracts from the commission
records.summary_en: The Springfield Weekly Republican publishes extracts from the commission report assessing the character of the Dominican people and the mineral resources of the republic. The commissioners favorably regard the political capacity of the population, citing their proverbial shrewdness, the absence of slavery or caste distinctions, and the courage shown in past struggles, while noting that only one small printing office exists in the country. They estimate the population at 150,000, over nineteen-twentieths of whom are native Dominicans, reporting that white blood largely preponderates. Under the heading 'Minerals of the Country,' expedition geologists report extensive deposits of iron ore, accessible copper beds, gold regions, petroleum, and valuable rock salt near Neyba, while finding that coal reported at Samaná and Puerto Plata is only low-value lignite.
records.summary_es: El Springfield Weekly Republican publica extractos del informe de la comisión que evalúan el carácter del pueblo dominicano y los recursos minerales de la república. Los comisionados valoran favorablemente la capacidad política de la población, citando su proverbial agudeza, la ausencia de esclavitud o distinciones de casta y el valor demostrado en luchas pasadas, al tiempo que señalan que en el país solo existe una pequeña imprenta. Estiman la población en 150,000 habitantes, de los cuales más de diecinueve vigésimos son dominicanos nativos, e informan que la sangre blanca prepondera ampliamente. Bajo el encabezado «Minerals of the Country», los geólogos de la expedición informan sobre extensos yacimientos de mineral de hierro, vetas de cobre accesibles, regiones auríferas, petróleo y valiosa sal gema cerca de Neyba, determinando que el carbón reportado en Samaná y Puerto Plata es únicamente lignito de escaso valor.

records.headline: An editorial in the Register contends that the commission report
records.summary_en: An editorial in the Register contends that the commission report presents nothing new regarding Santo Domingo, remarking that the public already knows its mixed population has alternated between internal conflicts and wars with Haiti. The paper asserts that the so-called President of Dominica desires to sell out to President Grant, who is reported to be anxious to complete the purchase. It concludes that the Senate's course remains to be seen, while claiming evidence shows President Grant regrets introducing the measure and would gladly escape the consequences of his folly.
records.summary_es: Un editorial en el Register sostiene que el informe de la comisión no presenta nada nuevo sobre Santo Domingo, señalando que el público ya sabe que su población mixta se ha debatido entre conflictos internos y guerras con Haití. El periódico afirma que el supuesto presidente de Dominica desea venderse al presidente Grant, de quien se informa que está ansioso por concretar la compra. Concluye que el proceder del Senado aún está por verse, al tiempo que afirma que existen pruebas de que el presidente Grant lamenta haber presentado la medida y escaparía con gusto de las consecuencias de su insensatez.

records.headline: In a Senate speech against annexing San Domingo, Mr. Morrill argues
records.summary_en: In a Senate speech against annexing San Domingo, Mr. Morrill argues that the Bay of Samana would be a source of weakness rather than a defensive point, and that the Dominican people would prove a serious political, moral and financial encumbrance. He says Dominican commerce has steadily declined, the island would yield no revenue, and the United States would have to pay for a civil service, a permanent naval squadron, regiments of soldiers, harbors and railroads, while placing little reliance on claims that Dominicans favor annexation.
records.summary_es: En un discurso en el Senado contra la anexión de Santo Domingo, el señor Morrill sostiene que la bahía de Samana sería una fuente de debilidad y no un punto defensivo, y que el pueblo dominicano resultaría una carga política, moral y financiera seria. Dice que el comercio dominicano ha disminuido constantemente, que la isla no produciría ingresos y que los Estados Unidos tendrían que pagar una administración civil, una escuadra naval permanente, regimientos de soldados, puertos y ferrocarriles, mientras da poco crédito a las afirmaciones de que los dominicanos favorecen la anexión.

records.headline: The Tribune publishes Senator Justin S. Morrill of Vermont's Senate speech
records.summary_en: The Tribune publishes Senator Justin S. Morrill of Vermont's Senate speech opposing President Grant's Santo Domingo annexation policy. Senator Morrill states that although he differs sharply with the administration on the policy, he freely accords President Grant the credit of being actuated by pure motives and disclaims any intent to assault his personal reputation. He criticizes the commissioners' report, arguing they praised the climate merely because a five-week stay caused them no harm, commended the soil simply for producing bananas and pineapples not grown in northern states, and treated mineral resources slightingly.
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica el discurso en el Senado del senador Justin S. Morrill de Vermont, en oposición a la política de anexión de Santo Domingo del presidente Grant. El senador Morrill manifiesta que, aunque difiere profundamente de la administración en cuanto a esta política, le reconoce plenamente al presidente Grant el mérito de haber actuado con intenciones puras y rechaza cualquier propósito de atacar su reputación personal. Critica el informe de los comisionados, sosteniendo que elogiaron el clima meramente porque una estancia de cinco semanas no les causó daño, alabaron el suelo simplemente por producir plátanos y piñas que no se cultivan en los estados del norte, y trataron los recursos minerales con ligereza.

records.headline: Senator Morrill, speaking on President Grant's Santo Domingo policy, treats the commissioners' report with open
records.summary_en: Senator Morrill, speaking on President Grant's Santo Domingo policy, treats the commissioners' report with open skepticism, saying they praised the soil for producing bananas and pine-apples and were despondent about finding coal at Samana, where there is only a poor show of lignite. Their report, he argues, will be found neither more exhaustive nor more trustworthy than the works of impartial travelers who spent far more time on the island, and will be chiefly valuable for vindicating the personal integrity of the President and of the officer charged with negotiating the defeated treaty.
records.summary_es: El senador Morrill, hablando sobre la política del presidente Grant hacia Santo Domingo, trata el informe de los comisionados con abierto escepticismo, diciendo que alabaron el suelo por producir bananas y piñas y que se mostraron desalentados por encontrar carbón en Samaná, donde solo hay una pobre muestra de lignito. Su informe, sostiene, no resultará ni más exhaustivo ni más digno de confianza que las obras de viajeros imparciales que pasaron mucho más tiempo en la isla, y será valioso sobre todo para vindicar la integridad personal del Presidente y la del oficial encargado de negociar el tratado derrotado.

records.headline: A Washington dispatch to the American Press Association reports
records.summary_en: A Washington dispatch to the American Press Association reports that the secretary of the San Domingo commission received a letter dated March 30 from the Dominican Republic's Secretary of War. The Dominican official states that the country is completely tranquil and increasingly anxious for speedy annexation to the United States as its only salvation against the intrigues of Haiti. He further reports that President Báez has returned to Santo Domingo from Azua after routing Cabral, leaving that district peaceful and in the best of order.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Washington para la American Press Association informa que el secretario de la comisión de Santo Domingo recibió una carta con fecha del 30 de marzo del ministro de Guerra de la República Dominicana. El funcionario dominicano manifiesta que el país se encuentra en completa tranquilidad y cada vez más ansioso por una rápida anexión a los Estados Unidos como su única salvación frente a las intrigas de Haití. Informa además que el presidente Báez regresó a Santo Domingo desde Azua tras derrotar a Cabral, dejando esa comarca en paz y en el mejor orden.

records.headline: An article in The Evening Telegraph acknowledges Senator Sumner
records.summary_en: An article in The Evening Telegraph acknowledges Senator Sumner as a sincere and honest friend of the colored race, but criticizes his opposition to the annexation of Santo Domingo. The writer argues that Sumner's stance is unfortunate and injurious to the colored inhabitants of Santo Domingo and potentially disastrous for black Americans. The piece maintains that Sumner's resistance divides the Republican party, encourages the notion that no further members of the colored race should be incorporated into the United States, and plays directly into the hands of the Democratic party.

El texto afirma que la resistencia de Sumner divide al Partido Republicano, fomenta la idea de que no se deben incorporar más personas de la raza de color a los Estados Unidos y favorece directamente los intereses del Partido Demócrata.

records.headline: A commentary in the Grant County Herald disputes the idea that Senator Sumner
records.summary_en: A commentary in the Grant County Herald disputes the idea that Senator Sumner was dropped from the Committee on Foreign Relations because of his opposition to annexing Santo Domingo. The writer argues that it is far from certain that a Senate majority favors acquiring Santo Domingo, insisting that no effort was made to displace Sumner on that account and that his Dominican views were never urged against him. The article notes that Sumner had opposed annexation long before December without losing his post, adding that other senators who opposed annexation with equal determination remained entirely unmolested.

El artículo señala que Sumner se había opuesto a la anexión mucho antes de diciembre sin perder su cargo, y añade que otros senadores que se opusieron a la anexión con igual determinación no fueron molestados en absoluto.

records.headline: The Western Reserve Chronicle publishes President Grant's transmittal
records.summary_en: The Western Reserve Chronicle publishes President Grant's transmittal message and the opening section of the San Domingo commission report. The commissioners state that they traversed the Dominican Republic in several directions, either in person or through agents, spending several weeks at the capital conferring daily with President Báez and reviewing official records while taking testimony. The report describes the Dominican government as theoretically a constitutional republic with executive, legislative, and judicial branches. It outlines the six-year terms of the president and vice president, their ineligibility for immediate re-election, the composition of the Council of State, and the structure of the Senate.
records.summary_es: El Western Reserve Chronicle publica el mensaje de remisión del presidente Grant y la sección inicial del informe de la comisión de Santo Domingo. Los comisionados manifiestan que recorrieron la República Dominicana en varias direcciones, ya sea en persona o mediante comisionados, pasando varias semanas en la capital conferenciando diariamente con el presidente Báez y examinando registros oficiales a la vez que tomaban testimonios. El informe describe el gobierno dominicano como teóricamente una república constitucional con poderes ejecutivo, legislativo y judicial. Detalla los mandatos de seis años del presidente y vicepresidente, su inelegibilidad para la reelección inmediata, la integración del Consejo de Estado y la estructura del Senado.

records.headline: An editorial in the Green-Mountain Freeman discusses President Grant's transmittal of the San Domingo commission
records.summary_en: An editorial in the Green-Mountain Freeman discusses President Grant's transmittal of the San Domingo commission report to Congress, arguing that the commission was devised to aid annexationists and added nothing new to public knowledge. Summarizing the findings, the paper observes that the commissioners describe the government of the republic of Dominica as republican, a fact already well established. The editorial points out that President Báez obtained power through irregular usurpation rather than election, criticizing the commissioners for defending his coup on the claim that he is superior to his predecessor, an assertion the paper dismisses as biased information coming from Báez himself.
records.summary_es: Un editorial en el Green-Mountain Freeman analiza la remisión al Congreso del informe de la comisión de Santo Domingo por parte del presidente Grant, argumentando que la comisión se ideó para favorecer a los anexionistas y no añadió nada nuevo al conocimiento público. Al resumir los hallazgos, el periódico observa que los comisionados describen el gobierno de la república de Dominica como republicano, un hecho que ya era bien conocido. El editorial señala que el presidente Báez llegó al poder mediante una usurpación irregular y no por elección, y critica a los comisionados por defender su golpe bajo el argumento de que es superior a su predecesor, afirmación que el periódico descarta como información parcial procedente del propio Báez.

records.headline: The New National Era prints an excerpt from the San Domingo commission
records.summary_en: The New National Era prints an excerpt from the San Domingo commission report examining the bays and harbors of the Dominican Republic. The report notes that while most harbors admit only light-draft craft, the three great bays of Samaná, Ocoa, and Manzanillo accommodate the largest vessels. The commissioners highlight the Bay of Samaná, describing it as thirty miles long, ten miles wide, sheltered by mountains, and capable of holding large fleets. They emphasize that its narrow entrance is easily fortified and commands the Mona Passage to the Gulf of Mexico, concluding that its strategic value as a naval coaling station cannot be overrated and that a great commercial center would flourish there under a secure government.
records.summary_es: El New National Era publica un extracto del informe de la comisión de Santo Domingo que examina las bahías y puertos de la República Dominicana. El informe señala que, si bien la mayoría de los puertos solo admiten embarcaciones de poco calado, las tres grandes bahías de Samaná, Ocoa y Manzanillo dan cabida a los buques más grandes. Los comisionados destacan la bahía de Samaná, describiéndola como de treinta millas de largo por diez millas de ancho, resguardada por montañas y con capacidad para albergar grandes flotas. Subrayan que su estrecha entrada es fácilmente fortificable y domina el canal de la Mona hacia el golfo de México, concluyendo que su valor estratégico como estación naval de carbonero no puede sobreestimarse y que un gran centro comercial prosperaría allí bajo un gobierno seguro.

records.headline: The New National Era publishes an extract from the commission
records.summary_en: The New National Era publishes an extract from the commission report analyzing Dominican political conditions and popular feeling regarding annexation. The commissioners observe that the influence of petty military chieftains and constant intrigues by exiles on neighboring islands have generated lawlessness and fabricated rumors of insurrection, driving many citizens to seek annexation to a strong power for protection. Under the heading 'Local Liberties,' the report notes that constant struggles have greatly impaired municipal liberties, though local councils could become centers of good governance under a stable system. Under 'Desire for Annexation,' the commissioners state that across all parts of the country, even the most remote districts, the people were found to be well informed about annexation and eager for its accomplishment.
records.summary_es: El New National Era publica un extracto del informe de la comisión que analiza las condiciones políticas dominicanas y el sentimiento popular respecto a la anexión. Los comisionados observan que la influencia de pequeños caudillos militares y las constantes intrigas de exiliados en islas vecinas han generado desorden y rumores ficticios de insurrección, llevando a muchos ciudadanos a buscar la anexión a una potencia fuerte en busca de protección. Bajo el título «Local Liberties», el informe señala que las continuas luchas han menoscabado gravemente las libertades municipales, aunque los ayuntamientos locales podrían convertirse en centros de buena gobernanza bajo un sistema estable. Bajo «Desire for Annexation», los comisionados manifiestan que en todas partes del país, incluso en los distritos más remotos, la población se encontraba bien informada sobre la anexión y deseosa de su consumación.

records.headline: The New National Era publishes a portion of the commission report
records.summary_en: The New National Era publishes a portion of the commission report detailing the mineral resources and soil characteristics of San Domingo. Expedition geologists report that iron ore is abundant and easily accessible for pig-iron production, copper ores show fair richness, an extensive gold region awaits exploration, and high-purity rock-salt deposits near Neyba can be quarried in large transparent blocks. They report that supposed coal deposits at Samaná and Puerto Plata proved upon examination to be low-grade lignite of little value compared to English or Pennsylvania coal. The report then begins a classification of Dominican soils into five agricultural categories, starting with uniformly rich mountain slopes and fertile valleys.
records.summary_es: El New National Era publica una parte del informe de la comisión que detalla los recursos minerales y las características del suelo de Santo Domingo. Los geólogos de la expedición informan que el mineral de hierro es abundante y de fácil acceso para la producción de arrabio, las menas de cobre presentan una riqueza razonable, una extensa región aurífera aguarda exploración y los depósitos de sal gema de gran pureza cerca de Neyba pueden extraerse en grandes bloques transparentes. Señalan que los supuestos yacimientos de carbón en Samaná y Puerto Plata resultaron ser, tras su examen, lignito de baja calidad y escaso valor comparado con el carbón inglés o de Pensilvania. El informe inicia luego una clasificación de los suelos dominicanos en cinco categorías agrícolas, comenzando con laderas montañosas uniformemente ricas y valles fértiles.

records.headline: The New National Era prints findings from the commission report
records.summary_en: The New National Era prints findings from the commission report regarding agriculture, crops, and cattle raising in San Domingo. The commissioners state that northern vegetables grow in perfection, pineapples thrive luxuriantly, and wheat has been successfully raised at an elevation of 4,000 feet in the valley of Constanza. The report emphasizes that tobacco is cultivated everywhere as the nation's principal export, while corn easily yields three crops a year. It describes city markets as richly supplied with tropical fruits and vegetables at all seasons, and observes that abundant natural grasses across the vast eastern savannas give San Domingo pre-eminence over neighboring islands in cattle raising.
records.summary_es: El New National Era publica las conclusiones del informe de la comisión relativas a la agricultura, las cosechas y la ganadería en Santo Domingo. Los comisionados indican que las hortalizas del norte se cultivan a la perfección, las piñas prosperan con exuberancia y el trigo se ha cosechado con éxito a una altitud de 4,000 pies en el valle de Constanza. El informe destaca que el tabaco se cultiva en todas partes como el principal renglón de exportación del país, mientras que el maíz rinde fácilmente tres cosechas al año. Describe los mercados urbanos como abundantemente provistos de frutas y verduras tropicales en todas las estaciones, y señala que los abundantes pastos naturales de las extensas sabanas orientales confieren a Santo Domingo preeminencia sobre las islas vecinas en la cría de ganado.

records.headline: The Tiffin Tribune publishes the concluding section and signatures of the report
records.summary_en: The Tiffin Tribune publishes the concluding section and signatures of the report submitted to President Grant by commissioners B. F. Wade, Andrew D. White, and S. G. Howe. The commissioners report that their request to explore the interior of Haiti met with an effective refusal, restricting their inquiries to what could be gathered without giving offense. Reviewing both divisions of the island, they express firm persuasion that the annexation of Santo Domingo to the United States would benefit both the Haitian and Dominican peoples. They argue that annexation would offer an example of an orderly and prosperous state and establish a guaranteed boundary between the French-speaking and Spanish-speaking nations, putting an end to destructive border wars.
records.summary_es: El Tiffin Tribune publica la sección final y las firmas del informe presentado al presidente Grant por los comisionados B. F. Wade, Andrew D. White y S. G. Howe. Los comisionados informan que su solicitud para explorar el interior de Haití se topó con una negativa efectiva, lo que limitó sus averiguaciones a lo que pudo recopilarse sin causar ofensas. Al examinar ambas divisiones de la isla, expresan la firme convicción de que la anexión de Santo Domingo a los Estados Unidos beneficiaría tanto al pueblo haitiano como al dominicano. Sostienen que la anexión ofrecería el ejemplo de un Estado ordenado y próspero y establecería una frontera garantizada entre las naciones de habla francesa y española, poniendo fin a destructivas guerras fronterizas.

records.headline: An editorial reprinted from the New York Tribune in the New National Era analyzes
records.summary_en: An editorial reprinted from the New York Tribune in the New National Era analyzes the border disputes and political rivalries between Haiti and Santo Domingo. The piece states that Cabral is backed by Haitian men and munitions along the contested border to overthrow President Báez, appealing to Dominican patriotism against Báez's annexation overtures. It defends President Grant's orders directing naval officers to give moral support to Báez, framing it as a warning preventing Haiti and Cabral from subverting the Dominican government by force while annexation remains under consideration. The paper rejects Senator Sumner's criticisms of this policy, questioning whether Haitian President Saget possesses any greater legitimacy than Báez.
records.summary_es: Un editorial reproducido del New York Tribune en el New National Era analiza las disputas fronterizas y las rivalidades políticas entre Haití y Santo Domingo. El texto afirma que Cabral cuenta con el respaldo de tropas y pertrechos haitianos a lo largo de la frontera en disputa para derrocar al presidente Báez, apelando al patriotismo dominicano contra las propuestas anexionistas de este. Defiende las órdenes del presidente Grant que instruyen a los oficiales navales a brindar apoyo moral a Báez, calificándolas de advertencia para evitar que Haití y Cabral derroquen por la fuerza al gobierno dominicano mientras la anexión se encuentre bajo consideración. El periódico rechaza las críticas del senador Sumner a esta política y cuestiona si el presidente haitiano Saget posee mayor legitimidad que Báez.

The paper first notes the commissioners' assessment that Samaná Bay would become an important commercial center and naval asset under United States authority. It then provides an itemized statement of government debt, listing unpaid salaries, treasury notes, Cabral's obligations, and various loans, reporting a sum total of $1,606,831.59 in debts and claims. A second table summarizes Dominican government income for 1870, showing total receipts of $728,805.58 primarily derived from customs and maritime duties.

records.headline: The Herald and Tribune publishes the concluding section of the report of the San Domingo commissioners.
records.summary_en: The Herald and Tribune publishes the concluding section of the report of the San Domingo commissioners. The commissioners recount that when seeking to ascertain Haitian views and claims upon Santo Domingo, their requests to travel into the interior were met with an effective refusal from the Haitian government. Looking to the interests of both divisions of the island, they conclude that the annexation of Santo Domingo to the United States would be scarcely less beneficial to Haiti than to the Dominican Republic. They argue that annexation would set an example of an orderly and prosperous state while establishing a guaranteed boundary between the French-speaking and Spanish-speaking nations to end destructive border conflicts.
records.summary_es: El Herald and Tribune publica la sección final del informe de los comisionados de Santo Domingo. Los comisionados relatan que, al intentar conocer las opiniones y reclamaciones haitianas sobre Santo Domingo, sus solicitudes para viajar al interior recibieron una negativa efectiva por parte del gobierno de Haití. Considerando los intereses de ambas divisiones de la isla, concluyen que la anexión de Santo Domingo a los Estados Unidos sería casi tan provechosa para Haití como para la República Dominicana. Sostienen que la anexión sentaría el ejemplo de un Estado ordenado y próspero, a la vez que fijaría una frontera garantizada entre las naciones de habla francesa y española para poner fin a los destructivos conflictos fronterizos.

records.headline: The Holmes County Republican summarizes the commissioners' findings
records.summary_en: The Holmes County Republican summarizes the commissioners' findings on Dominican resources and examines the arguments for and against annexation. The paper outlines the report's favorable view of the island's iron ores, healthy mountain climate, and diverse agricultural lands spanning mountain valleys, the Llanos savannas, and the fertile plains of La Vega. The article notes that while the people, climate, and terms of purchase are all favorable, the United States already possesses far more territory than its population requires. The paper contends that the decisive argument for annexation is the acquisition of Samaná Bay to prevent the island from falling under European monarchical influence, observing that German commercial interests have already absorbed trade in San Domingo.
records.summary_es: El Holmes County Republican resume las conclusiones de los comisionados sobre los recursos dominicanos y examina los argumentos a favor y en contra de la anexión. El periódico reseña la visión favorable del informe sobre los minerales de hierro de la isla, su clima montañoso saludable y sus diversas tierras agrícolas que abarcan valles de montaña, las sabanas de los Llanos y las fértiles llanuras de La Vega. El artículo señala que, si bien la población, el clima y los términos de compra resultan favorables, los Estados Unidos ya poseen mucho más territorio del que requiere su población. El periódico sostiene que el argumento decisivo para la anexión es la adquisición de la bahía de Samaná para evitar que la isla caiga bajo la influencia monárquica europea, observando que los intereses comerciales alemanes ya han absorbido el comercio en Santo Domingo.

records.headline: The Kenosha Telegraph publishes extracts from the San Domingo commission
records.summary_en: The Kenosha Telegraph publishes extracts from the San Domingo commission report highlighting the advantages of acquisition and the condition of Dominican public finances. Under 'The Advantages of Annexation,' the commissioners state that acquiring the territory would provide a powerful military and naval base and foster an important commercial city at Samaná Bay, where an American citizen has already acquired waterfront property. They emphasize that easy water and rail communications with the interior make Samaná's future of national importance. The paper also reproduces the commissioners' statement of the government's debt and claims, listing unpaid salaries, treasury notes, and loans, followed by a summary of revenue from licenses and registry taxes.
records.summary_es: El Kenosha Telegraph publica extractos del informe de la comisión de Santo Domingo que resaltan las ventajas de la adquisición y el estado de las finanzas públicas dominicanas. Bajo el encabezado «The Advantages of Annexation», los comisionados afirman que adquirir el territorio proporcionaría una poderosa base militar y naval y propiciaría una importante ciudad comercial en la bahía de Samaná, donde un ciudadano estadounidense ya adquirió terrenos en el litoral. Destacan que las fáciles comunicaciones fluviales y ferroviarias con el interior confieren a Samaná una importancia nacional para el futuro. El periódico también reproduce el balance de los comisionados sobre la deuda y reclamaciones del gobierno, enumerando sueldos impagos, billetes de tesorería y préstamos, seguido de un resumen de ingresos por licencias e impuestos de registro.

records.full_text:
UNANIMOUS FOR ANNEXATION.
The Dominicans repeat their wish to be annexed on the terms of the treaty of 1869, asking, in addition payment for rent for Samana bay during the two years the negotiations were pending. They are also willing to appropriate one-fifth of the public funds for schools, providing the United States will appropriate $300,000 for the establishment of an agricultural and scientific college. In relation to Dominican independence, the Commissioners say that there is but one chance for that republic ever to retain its independence; to become, after a period of probation, one of a union of states, the freedom and substantial dependence of each being guaranteed by the strength of all. It is under the resolution of Congress, to recommend that such a course be adopted or abstained from. They simply state as their belief, founded upon the observations they could make, and all the facts they could learn, that this is the only way in which Dominican independence can be secured, that if it should be judged best not to adopt that course, even the present shadow of independence will be taken away. The Dominican territory is one of the purest and richest on the earth. Unless some such means as are above mentioned are resorted to, it will lie exhausted and helpless until some nation shall seize and hold it in colonial subjection.

The Commissioners were not unmindful of various rumors which had been circulated on divers occasions, that concessions or grants of land were made to officials of the Government of the United States when the treaty of annexation was negotiated in 1869. No pains were spared to ascertain the exact truth of this statement. In addition to the examination of all grants from the government of the republic, the Commission further carried their researches to all municipal grants by the town of Samana, where rumor had located the supposed grants. The officers of the municipality and the records were carefully examined. Inquiries were also made of the authorities of the city of San Domingo. After this investigation the Commissioners can declare, without hesitation, that there is no particle of evidence for these charges.

records.headline: The Buchanan County Bulletin publishes the conclusion of the San Domingo commission
records.summary_en: The Buchanan County Bulletin publishes the conclusion of the San Domingo commission report alongside findings from their investigation into municipal administration. The commissioners explain that Haitian reluctance to permit exploration into the interior obliged them to rely on indirect information regarding that republic. In their conclusion, they affirm their conviction that annexing Santo Domingo to the United States would benefit Haitians as well as Dominicans by offering an example of orderly government and establishing a permanent, guaranteed frontier between the two nations to halt border warfare. The report also notes that a careful inquiry into municipal officers and records in the city of Santo Domingo revealed no evidence supporting charges against local authorities.
records.summary_es: El Buchanan County Bulletin publica la conclusión del informe de la comisión de Santo Domingo junto con los resultados de su investigación sobre la administración municipal. Los comisionados explican que la renuencia haitiana a permitir exploraciones en el interior los obligó a recurrir a información indirecta sobre esa república. En su conclusión, afirman su convicción de que la anexión de Santo Domingo a los Estados Unidos beneficiaría tanto a los haitianos como a los dominicanos, al ofrecer el ejemplo de un gobierno ordenado y fijar una frontera permanente y garantizada entre ambas naciones para frenar las guerras fronterizas. El informe señala asimismo que una minuciosa pesquisa sobre los funcionarios y registros municipales de la ciudad de Santo Domingo no arrojó prueba alguna que sustentara las acusaciones contra las autoridades locales.

records.headline: The Buchanan County Bulletin prints sections of the San Domingo commission
records.summary_en: The Buchanan County Bulletin prints sections of the San Domingo commission report evaluating the strategic value of Samaná Bay and the state of the Dominican public debt. The commissioners describe Samaná, Ocoa, and Manzanillo as deep-water harbors, highlighting Samaná as a future military and naval stronghold capable of sustaining a major commercial city linked to the interior by rail and water. Under 'The Debt of the Government,' the paper reproduces the commissioners' itemized balance sheet of public obligations, listing unpaid salaries, treasury notes, Cabral's obligations, and various loans, followed by a summary of revenue from licenses, stamped paper, and postal services.
records.summary_es: El Buchanan County Bulletin publica secciones del informe de la comisión de Santo Domingo que evalúan el valor estratégico de la bahía de Samaná y el estado de la deuda pública dominicana. Los comisionados describen a Samaná, Ocoa y Manzanillo como puertos de aguas profundas, destacando a Samaná como una futura plaza fuerte militar y naval capaz de albergar una gran ciudad comercial conectada con el interior por ferrocarril y vías navegables. Bajo «The Debt of the Government», el periódico reproduce el balance desglosado de las obligaciones públicas elaborado por los comisionados, enumerando sueldos impagos, billetes de tesorería, obligaciones de Cabral y diversos préstamos, seguido de un resumen de ingresos por licencias, papel sellado y servicios postales.

records.summary_en: Advices from Haiti received in Havana state that great excitement continued over the annexation question, while otherwise the republic was quiet. A St. Thomas dispatch reports the defeat of Cabral's army by Baez near Azua and that Luperon's army was making progress in the northern provinces, with the country anxious to see the annexation question settled.

Un despacho de Santo Tomás informa de la derrota del ejército de Cabral a manos de Báez cerca de Azua y de que el ejército de Luperón avanzaba en las provincias del norte, con el país ansioso por ver resuelta la cuestión de la anexión.

records.headline: The Vermont Phœnix reports arguments delivered by Senator Justin Morrill
records.summary_en: The Vermont Phœnix reports arguments delivered by Senator Justin Morrill against the annexation of Santo Domingo. Morrill warns that displaying American naval and financial power excites the jealousy and fear of neighboring republics, whereas the United States should serve as their counselor and guide rather than a beast of prey. He questions whether the American population is sufficiently homogeneous to assimilate new territory, pointing out that recently acquired regions like Alaska, Arizona, Utah, and New Mexico remain largely un-American. Observing that former slaveholders in the South will do little to elevate emancipated laborers, he urges against multiplying national risks, concluding that Samaná Bay would prove a costly burden rather than a necessary commercial harbor.
records.summary_es: El Vermont Phœnix informa sobre los argumentos presentados por el senador Justin Morrill contra la anexión de Santo Domingo. Morrill advierte que el despliegue del poder naval y financiero estadounidense despierta los celos y el temor de las repúblicas vecinas, cuando los Estados Unidos deberían servirles de consejero y guía en lugar de actuar como una bestia de presa. Cuestiona si la población estadounidense es lo bastante homogénea como para asimilar nuevos territorios, señalando que regiones recientemente adquiridas como Alaska, Arizona, Utah y Nuevo México siguen siendo en gran medida no asimiladas. Al observar que los antiguos amos en el Sur harán pocos sacrificios para elevar a los trabajadores emancipados, insta a no multiplicar los riesgos nacionales, concluyendo que la bahía de Samaná resultaría una carga costosa en vez de un puerto comercial necesario.

records.headline: The Springfield Weekly Republican reports Mr. Morrill's remarks
records.summary_en: The Springfield Weekly Republican reports Mr. Morrill's remarks, urging the United States to suspend annexations and cultivate friendship with neighboring nations. If any territory is acquired, Morrill contends it should be Canada, a contiguous land of kindred stock and tongue, rather than San Domingo. He argues that annexing San Domingo would heavily increase American taxes, asserting it is absurd to expect that a country with no public lands and 120,000 to 160,000 poor inhabitants unwilling to labor could contribute anything toward the national debt. Criticizing President Grant's December message, he maintains that treasury funds would only flow outward, and begins addressing the commercial argument regarding Samaná Bay.
records.summary_es: El Springfield Weekly Republican informa sobre las declaraciones del señor Morrill, en las que insta a los Estados Unidos a suspender las anexiones y cultivar la amistad con las naciones vecinas. Si se adquiere algún territorio, Morrill sostiene que debería ser Canadá, una tierra contigua de linaje e idioma afines, en lugar de Santo Domingo. Sostiene que anexar a Santo Domingo aumentaría considerablemente los impuestos estadounidenses, afirmando que es absurdo esperar que un país sin tierras públicas y con entre 120,000 y 160,000 habitantes pobres y poco dispuestos a trabajar pueda aportar algo al pago de la deuda pública. Al criticar el mensaje de diciembre del presidente Grant, sostiene que los fondos del tesoro solo saldrían sin retorno, y comienza a abordar el argumento comercial relativo a la bahía de Samaná.

records.headline: The Burlington Weekly Free Press reports Senator Morrill's speech
records.summary_en: The Burlington Weekly Free Press reports Senator Morrill's speech warning that the proposed annexation of Santo Domingo would burden the United States with a costly elephant. Morrill questions whether the American people are sufficiently homogeneous to assimilate the territory, noting that populations in earlier acquisitions lack attachment to American institutions. He argues that the voyage of the Tennessee, which remained out of communication with the world for thirty-three days, demonstrates the total absence of commercial traffic along the Samaná route and its useless remoteness. Furthermore, he declares that the bay is proverbially unhealthy and too shallow for large vessels to approach within three miles of the shore, offering no protection to American shipping.
records.summary_es: El Burlington Weekly Free Press informa sobre el discurso del senador Morrill en el que advierte que la propuesta anexión de Santo Domingo impondría a los Estados Unidos la carga de un elefante costoso. Morrill cuestiona si el pueblo estadounidense es suficientemente homogéneo para asimilar el territorio, señalando que las poblaciones de adquisiciones anteriores carecen de apego a las instituciones estadounidenses. Sostiene que el viaje del Tennessee, que permaneció incomunicado del mundo durante treinta y tres días, demuestra la total ausencia de tráfico comercial en la ruta de Samaná y su inútil lejanía. Además, afirma que la bahía es proverbialmente malsana y demasiado poco profunda para que buques de gran calado se acerquen a menos de tres millas de la costa, sin ofrecer protección alguna a la marina mercante estadounidense.

records.headline: The commissioners describe the republic's institutions - senate, courts, alcaldes whose practice is better than the theory
records.summary_en: The commissioners describe the republic's institutions - senate, courts, alcaldes whose practice is better than the theory - and find Báez, first elected in 1848 after the expulsion of the Haitian power, without a rival of superior title.
records.summary_es: Los comisionados describen las instituciones de la república - senado, tribunales, alcaldes cuya práctica es mejor que la teoría - y encuentran a Báez, elegido por primera vez en 1848 tras la expulsión del poder haitiano, sin un rival de título superior.
records.passage: CONDITION OF THE COUNTRY. The Commissioners found the government organized and in complete operation in all its departments, exercising every function of legitimate Government, with Gen. Buenaventura Baez as Chief Magistrate, in full and peaceable possession of all parts of the republic except on the Haytien border, which is disturbed by insurrectionary leaders, aided by the Haytiens and political intriguers. These are incited to be extraordinarily active at this time by the fear of annexation to the United States. From all that the Commissioners could ascertain, President Baez has the respect of a great majority of the Dominican people for his administrative abilities, and the strong attachment of many leading men, who regard him as the only statesman among them who can hold them together against domestic factions and foreign foes. In [illegible], after five years of anarchy, consequent on the expulsion of the Haytien power, Gen. Baez was regularly elected President of the republic. It appears that he was chosen as the man who, by his education, fortune and public services, would be most likely to secure general confidence and heal the wounds inflicted by the civil and foreign wars. In one of the delegations of leading citizens who tendered to him the Chief Magistracy, was Gen. Cabral. There is credible testimony to the fact that, under him, despite the difficulties that have beset him, the republic has enjoyed as much liberty as any of his predecessors dared to allow, and more tranquility than they knew how

records.headline: The South-eastern Independent prints extracts from the report of the United States Commissioners
records.summary_en: The South-eastern Independent prints extracts from the report of the United States Commissioners to Santo Domingo concerning border warfare and Dominican internal stability. The Commissioners conclude that Dominican insurgents would long ago have been suppressed had they not received foreign assistance and backing from Haiti, a neighboring state with nearly three times the Dominican Republic's population and revenue. They state that Haitian authorities have maintained an unrelenting aggressive policy under a president brought to power by a bloody insurrection. Additionally, the Commissioners observe that provincial rivalries and regional chieftains aggravate Dominican difficulties, but express their belief that these challenges would disappear if the republic were protected through connection with a stronger power.
records.summary_es: El South-eastern Independent publica extractos del informe de los comisionados de los Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo sobre la guerra fronteriza y la estabilidad interna dominicana. Los comisionados concluyen que los insurgentes dominicanos habrían sido sofocados hace mucho tiempo de no haber contado con auxilio extranjero y con el respaldo de Haití, un Estado vecino que casi triplica la población y los ingresos de la República Dominicana. Señalan que las autoridades haitianas han mantenido una política agresiva implacable bajo el mando de un presidente elevado al poder mediante una insurrección sangrienta. Asimismo, los comisionados observan que las rivalidades provinciales y los caudillos regionales agravan las dificultades dominicanas, pero expresan su convicción de que estos problemas desaparecerían si la república fuera protegida mediante su vinculación con una potencia más fuerte.

records.headline: The commissioners' report describes the island's navigable rivers and its three great bays, Samana, Azua and Manzanillo
records.summary_en: The commissioners' report describes the island's navigable rivers and its three great bays, Samana, Azua and Manzanillo, and calls Samana a powerful military and naval station whose future under United States authority would be of national importance. It then sets out the Dominican government's finances, giving a total of $1,565,831 in debt and claims, together with the government's income for 1869, and states the commissioners' belief that the statement includes every obligation for which the republic could be held liable, while noting that some claims appear questionable.
records.summary_es: El informe de los comisionados describe los ríos navegables de la isla y sus tres grandes bahías, Samaná, Azua y Manzanillo, y califica a Samaná como una poderosa estación militar y naval cuyo futuro bajo la autoridad de los Estados Unidos sería de importancia nacional. A continuación expone las finanzas del gobierno dominicano, con un total de $1,565,831 en deudas y reclamaciones, junto con los ingresos del gobierno en 1869, y declara la convicción de los comisionados de que el estado incluye toda obligación por la que la república pudiera ser responsable, señalando a la vez que algunas reclamaciones parecen cuestionables.

A BULLY AMONG REPUBLICS.
Our reputation among sister republics in America the Senator did not consider wholly unblemished, and it was not likely to grow brighter from Santo Domingo complications. Our experience with Mexico when Texas became a part of this Union; the Greytown affair in 1852; the career of Walker, the fillibuster; our difficulty with Paraguay for ten years or more; our attitude toward Cuba; the trouble with Peru in 1860; a recent unpleasantness with Brazil in regard to the passage of the gunboat Wasp, up the Paraguay to relieve Minister Washburn, were recited to show that there was no special love for this government among those nations. records.headline: An editorial in the Bellows Falls Times argues that the Dominican people
records.summary_en: An editorial in the Bellows Falls Times argues that the Dominican people do not favor American annexation, recalling that they previously drove Spanish forces from their territory through revolution. The paper asserts that the plebiscite favoring annexation was a delusive juggle engineered through the inducements of President Báez and the intimidating presence of United States naval guns. It notes that General Cabral and his followers actively contest the transaction in arms, holding an estimated 10,000 of the republic's 22,212 square miles in conjunction with Haiti. Under the heading "Santo Domingo and Her Debts Go Together," the editorial warns that the United States would be legally and honorably bound to assume all Dominican liabilities, rendering any disclaimer by Báez worthless.
records.summary_es: Un editorial en el Bellows Falls Times sostiene que el pueblo dominicano no favorece la anexión a los Estados Unidos, recordando que anteriormente expulsó a las fuerzas españolas de su territorio mediante una revolución. El periódico afirma que el plebiscito a favor de la anexión fue una maniobra engañosa orquestada mediante las dádivas del presidente Báez y la presencia intimidatoria de los cañones de la Armada estadounidense. Señala que el general Cabral y sus partidarios combaten activamente la transacción con las armas en la mano, controlando unas 10,000 de las 22,212 millas cuadradas de la república conjuntamente con Haití. Bajo el encabezado «Santo Domingo y sus deudas van juntos», el editorial advierte que los Estados Unidos quedarían obligados jurídica y moralmente a asumir todas las deudas dominicanas, careciendo de valor cualquier compromiso en contrario suscrito con Báez.

records.headline: The Bellows Falls Times publishes the concluding portion of Senator Justin Morrill's speech
records.summary_en: The Bellows Falls Times publishes the concluding portion of Senator Justin Morrill's speech against the annexation of Santo Domingo. Morrill observes that the American Constitution provides no direct authority for territorial annexations and denies the existence of any enlightened public sentiment favoring the measure. He contends that President Grant's personal popularity constitutes the entire backbone of the annexation project, asserting that without executive endorsement it would lack even a corporal's guard of supporters. In closing, Morrill appeals to national honor, declaring that he will not jeopardize the country's enduring character or exchange its moral grandeur for mere material greatness.
records.summary_es: El Bellows Falls Times publica la parte final del discurso del senador Justin Morrill contra la anexión de Santo Domingo. Morrill observa que la Constitución estadounidense no otorga autoridad directa para anexiones territoriales y niega la existencia de una opinión pública ilustrada que respalde la medida. Sostiene que la popularidad personal del presidente Grant constituye la única fuerza motriz del proyecto de anexión, afirmando que sin el respaldo del ejecutivo la iniciativa no contaría ni con un piquete de partidarios. Para concluir, Morrill apela al honor nacional, declarando que no pondrá en riesgo el carácter perdurable del país ni cambiará su grandeza moral por mera grandeza material.

records.headline: The Spirit of Democracy publishes findings from the report of the United States Commissioners
records.summary_en: The Spirit of Democracy publishes findings from the report of the United States Commissioners to Santo Domingo detailing the island's population, minerals, and agriculture. The report states that white ancestry largely predominates among native Dominicans and affirms that the country possesses vast resources capable of extensive development through labor. Geologists accompanying the expedition identify deposits of iron, copper, gold, lignite, rock salt, and petroleum, noting that abundant iron ore could support cheap pig iron production, while reported coal at Samaná and Puerto Plata proved to be inferior lignite. The Commissioners report that extensive salt formations near Neiba yield pure blocks for commerce, and they identify rich mountain slopes and valleys as the first of five agricultural land classes.
records.summary_es: The Spirit of Democracy publica las conclusiones del informe de los comisionados de los Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo sobre la población, los minerales y la agricultura de la isla. El informe señala que la ascendencia blanca predomina ampliamente entre los dominicanos nativos y afirma que el país posee vastos recursos susceptibles de un gran desarrollo mediante el trabajo. Los geólogos de la expedición identifican yacimientos de hierro, cobre, oro, lignito, sal gema y petróleo, destacando que el abundante mineral de hierro permitiría una producción económica de arrabio, mientras que el supuesto carbón en Samaná y Puerto Plata resultó ser lignito de escaso valor. Los comisionados informan que extensos depósitos de sal cerca de Neiba producen bloques puros para el comercio, y clasifican las ricas laderas y valles montañosos como la primera de cinco clases de tierras agrícolas.

records.headline: The Spirit of Democracy prints an extract regarding the mission
records.summary_en: The Spirit of Democracy prints an extract regarding the mission to Haiti and conclusions on Santo Domingo of the United States Commissioners. their mission to Haiti and conclusions on Santo Domingo. The Commissioners state that they sought to ascertain Haitian claims regarding Santo Domingo and the views of the Haitian people concerning political changes on the island, but their requests to travel into the interior were met with what amounted to a refusal. Reviewing the interests of both divisions of the island, the Commissioners express their conviction that annexation to the United States would be hardly less beneficial to Haitians than to Dominicans. They argue that annexation would establish a peaceful, orderly state in the region and provide an equitable boundary line between the French-speaking and Spanish-speaking populations.
records.summary_es: The Spirit of Democracy publica un extracto del informe de los comisionados de los Estados Unidos, relativo a su misión en Haití y sus conclusiones sobre Santo Domingo. Los comisionados exponen que procuraron conocer las reclamaciones haitianas sobre Santo Domingo y la opinión del pueblo haitiano respecto a los cambios políticos en la isla, pero sus solicitudes para viajar al interior recibieron una respuesta equivalente a una negativa. Al examinar los intereses de ambas divisiones de la isla, los comisionados manifiestan su convicción de que la anexión a los Estados Unidos resultaría casi tan beneficiosa para los haitianos como para los dominicanos. Sostienen que la anexión implantaría un Estado pacífico y ordenado en la región y establecería una línea fronteriza equitativa entre las poblaciones francófona e hispanohablante.
