records.headline: The Star prints the Associated Press 'Pen Picture' of President Heureaux
records.summary_en: The Star prints the Associated Press 'Pen Picture' of President Heureaux: its correspondent writes from Cape Haytien, Hayti, June 12, that the remarkable audiences President Heureaux granted on his gunboat, the Restauracion, in that harbor on Thursday last deserve a special record, and that the interview may be properly appreciated it is necessary to give it a descriptive setting. The correspondent went out to the Restauracion accompanied by the American consul, Dr. Livingston, and Mr. A. J. Redpar, who is in charge of the most successful foreign enterprise there and who met Heureaux some years ago in his own capital; they did not need to send their cards ahead, and were received on the quarter deck by Ulysses himself, the dreaded tyrant president, clad in a modest naval uniform, of which a short blue jacket with small gold buttons and a white cap with hardly any gold lace were the conspicuous features; he greeted them with a scrutinizing air, and with a gesture of bonhomie invited them to be seated. The president is a mulatto of medium color, with rather regular features, showing the blending of the African and Caucasian blood.

El corresponsal salió hacia la Restauracion acompañado por el cónsul americano, el Dr. Livingston, y el señor A. J. Redpar, quien está a cargo de la empresa extranjera más exitosa de allí y quien conoció a Heureaux hace algunos años en su propia capital; no necesitaron enviar sus tarjetas por adelantado, y fueron recibidos en el alcázar por Ulises mismo, el temido presidente tirano, vestido con un modesto uniforme naval, del cual una chaqueta azul corta con pequeños botones dorados y una gorra blanca casi sin galón dorado eran los rasgos conspicuos; los saludó con un aire escrutador, y con un gesto de bonhomía los invitó a sentarse. El presidente es un mulato de color medio, de facciones más bien regulares, que muestran la mezcla de la sangre africana y caucásica.

records.headline: The Star's pen picture of President Heureaux goes on to his manner
records.summary_en: The Star's pen picture of President Heureaux goes on to his manner: even in his most dangerous moments, it is said, can be bland, caressing and patronizing, and they even have a saying in Santo Domingo that many of the poor devils he sends to the tragic blank wall or freshly opened wayside ditch feel almost flattered when he tells them personally he cannot afford to pardon them; it is no wonder his astuter friends, as well as enemies, have learned to study his smile more closely than his frown. The president is about five feet eight inches in height, of athletic mold, though his right arm is still half disabled from the effects of two old wounds near the elbow; his movements are usually deliberate, as if all that he did in public was nicely calculated, yet he is capable of great animation, volubility and vivacity, spices his talk with satire and irony, and occasionally laughs broadly at his own joke or epigram, and it is impossible not to be impressed by the strong grasp of his mind and by the subtlety of his cunning. All the time the conversation went on, something over an hour, first with the correspondent and at intervals with visitor after visitor who came to pay his respects, there were three or four poor fellows down in the bowels of the ship, revolutionists taken with arms in their hands, who were waiting the word of this imperturbable dictator to determine whether they should live or die.

records.summary_en: The Star's pen picture of President Heureaux closes with the story of his brother-in-law: it would matter very little to Heureaux, the correspondent writes, who of his own family interceded with him in favor of one of his enemies, and his conduct toward his own brother-in-law is still vividly remembered; he took the man to live with him in the presidential palace at Santo Domingo, clothed him, fed him and gave him official dignities, and twice the beneficiary conspired against the benefactor — the first time he was forgiven, but the second time Heureaux called him to him and said: 'I have tried to make a gentleman of you. Now I want you to put on your full-dress costume. In one hour you will be shot. There is no use for you to say anything. It must be. Only I particularly request that you behave like a gentleman' — and the brother-in-law was shot dead at the hour and minute. records.headline: The Herald's account gives Heureaux's views on Hayti and the United States
records.summary_en: The Herald's account gives Heureaux's views on Hayti and the United States: the President spoke without reserve of the errors of the Haytien nation and denounced the unwisdom of their repellent attitude toward foreigners; he recognized the fact that the future progress of his own country lay in the encouragement of foreign enterprises within its borders, and, above all, he would be chary of provoking the ill will of the United States of America. Some day, he declared, all of the greater Antilles would either belong to him or be under the protectorate of the American republic, and there was but one sensible course for Santo Domingo or for Hayti — to cultivate the best political and commercial relations with the United States. On the subject of neutrality General Heureaux was somewhat ambiguous: he was indisposed, he said, to offend either Spain or the United States, the enmity of the former being as disastrous to his government as that of the latter, but he allowed it to be understood that, if it came to choice, he must decide to stand with the Americans. It was when the conversation turned to the late abortive uprising at Monte Cristo that the real opportunity to study the character of the dictator presented itself, and some of the Dominicans and prominent Haytiens who came aboard to pay homage to Heureaux had been hand in glove with the conspirators.
records.summary_es: El relato del Herald recoge las opiniones de Heureaux sobre Haití y los Estados Unidos: el presidente habló sin reserva de los errores de la nación haitiana y denunció la insensatez de su actitud repelente hacia los extranjeros; reconoció el hecho de que el progreso futuro de su propio país residía en el fomento de las empresas extranjeras dentro de sus fronteras, y, sobre todo, sería cauteloso en provocar la mala voluntad de los Estados Unidos de América. Algún día, declaró, todas las Antillas mayores o le pertenecerían a él o estarían bajo el protectorado de la república americana, y no había sino un camino sensato para Santo Domingo o para Haití: cultivar las mejores relaciones políticas y comerciales con los Estados Unidos. Sobre el tema de la neutralidad, el general Heureaux fue algo ambiguo: no estaba dispuesto, dijo, a ofender ni a España ni a los Estados Unidos, pudiendo la enemistad de la primera ser tan desastrosa para su gobierno como la de los segundos, pero dejó entender que, si llegaba a tener que escoger, debía decidirse a estar con los americanos. Fue cuando la conversación giró hacia el reciente alzamiento abortado en Monte Cristi que se presentó la verdadera oportunidad de estudiar el carácter del dictador, y algunos de los dominicanos y prominentes haitianos que subieron a bordo a rendir homenaje a Heureaux habían estado en íntima connivencia con los conspiradores.

records.headline: The Star prints the feature on the Columbus remains at Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The Star prints the feature on the Columbus remains at Santo Domingo: the news of the discovery sent those of San Domingo into spasms of delight and those of Spain into corresponding rage, and when the news reached Madrid the Royal Academy instituted a searching inquiry, which resulted in sustaining the Havana theory, but the learned men of San Domingo are still firm in their belief that they have the only and original bones — the true and authenticated remains of the immortal Columbus. The writer was sent to San Domingo for the express purpose of sifting the existing evidence and making a personal examination, and bore letters of recommendation from the then Secretary of State, Mr. Blaine, to the president of the Dominican republic, and every opportunity was afforded him for a rigid investigation: the minister of public affairs himself accompanied him to the cathedral, and by his command the revered relics were brought from their place of deposit, in an ancient cedar chest within a dark cell near the presbytery, and exposed to the light of day. Photographs were then taken of the vault, the original place of sepulture being pointed out, the two vaults opened and their relative position shown, and also of the casket at present holding the bones, and of the crystal and satinwood case in which this is contained; this last is bound about with ribbons, secured by the great seal of the republic, and to obtain even a glimpse of the remains it is first necessary to get the sanction of the ecclesiastical, the municipal and the national authorities.

Photographs were then taken of the vault, the original place of sepulture being pointed out, the two vaults opened and their relative position shown, and also of the casket at present holding the bones, and of the crystal and satinwood case in which this is contained; this last is bound about with ribbons, secured by the great seal of the republic, and to obtain even a glimpse of the remains it is first necessary to get the sanction of the ecclesiastical, the municipal and the national authorities, the three keys to the cell in which they are guarded.
records.summary_es: El News publica el reportaje sobre los restos de Colón en Santo Domingo: la noticia del descubrimiento envió a los de Santo Domingo a espasmos de deleite y a los de España a una rabia correspondiente, y cuando la noticia llegó a Madrid la Real Academia instituyó una indagación escudriñadora, que resultó en sostener la teoría habanera, pero los sabios de Santo Domingo se mantienen firmes en su creencia de que tienen los únicos y originales huesos: los verdaderos y autenticados restos del inmortal Colón. El escritor fue enviado a Santo Domingo con el propósito expreso de escudriñar la evidencia existente y hacer un examen personal, y llevaba cartas de recomendación del entonces secretario de Estado, el señor Blaine, al presidente de la República Dominicana, y se le brindó toda oportunidad para una investigación rigurosa: el ministro de fomento, o de asuntos públicos, lo acompañó él mismo a la catedral, y por su orden las veneradas reliquias fueron traídas de su lugar de depósito, en un antiguo cofre de cedro dentro de una celda oscura cerca del presbiterio, y expuestas a la luz del día. Se tomaron entonces fotografías de la bóveda, señalándose el lugar original de sepultura, abiertas las dos bóvedas y mostrada su posición relativa, y también del ataúd que actualmente contiene los huesos, y de la caja de cristal y madera de satín en que este está contenido; esta última está ceñida con cintas, aseguradas por el gran sello de la república, y para obtener siquiera una mirada a los restos es primero necesario conseguir la sanción de las autoridades eclesiástica, municipal y nacional, las tres llaves de la celda en que están guardados.

records.headline: The Sun prints the Puerto Rican Correo's English editorial on San Domingo
records.summary_en: The Sun prints the Puerto Rican Correo's English editorial on San Domingo: its editor takes strong ground for a free San Domingo, and 'The time is changed,' the editorial begins; not long ago the Spanish authorities did not allow them there the expression of their thoughts, and they were called to court to answer for their attacks on the murderer who commands in Santo Domingo, and a little after, in a moment of indignation in the Spanish government against the Antillean satrap, they could at least utter their complaints; now liberty commands in Puerto Rico, and the editorial makes one of its first English articles under the new state of affairs in that island a warm calling for help to withdraw the murderer who stains the Dominican Republic's humble but bright history. Cuba will be free and happy after her four centuries of shadows, Puerto Rico, if not independent, will no doubt be soon a prosperous people, and the Dominican Republic, the heroic and beautiful sister of Cuba and Puerto Rico, will only remain, the editorial cries, under the feet of a ferocious and savage tyrant.

Cuba será libre y feliz tras sus cuatro siglos de sombras, Puerto Rico, si no independiente, sin duda será pronto un pueblo próspero, y la República Dominicana, la heroica y hermosa hermana de Cuba y Puerto Rico, solo permanecerá, exclama el editorial, bajo los pies de un tirano feroz y salvaje.

records.headline: The Leader prints a feature on the Columbus remains and Ober's report
records.summary_en: The Leader prints a feature on the Columbus remains and Ober's report: the honor of possessing these relics is claimed alike by Havana and San Domingo, and there seems to be no doubt that at each place there is the tomb of a Columbus, but which is the original and only genuine is a matter subject to argument. Some years ago Frederick A. Ober was sent to San Domingo for the express purpose of sifting the existing evidence and making a personal examination, and bore letters of recommendation from the then secretary of state, Mr. Blaine, to the president of the Dominican republic, and every opportunity was afforded him for a rigid investigation: the minister of public affairs himself accompanied him to the cathedral, and by his command the revered relics were brought from their place of deposit, in an ancient cedar chest within a dark cell near the presbytery, and exposed to the light of day. Photographs were then taken of the vault, the original place of sepulture being pointed out, the two vaults opened and their relative position shown, and also of the casket at present holding the bones, and of the crystal and satinwood case in which this is contained. In his report to this government, Mr. Ober said in substance that the conclusion reached by the Spanish academy is that the remains of Columbus are in the cathedral of Havana, in the shadow of the glorious banner of Castile, and that it is most fitting that over his sepulcher waves the same flag that sailed with him from Palos.

Se tomaron entonces fotografías de la bóveda, señalándose el lugar original de sepultura, abiertas las dos bóvedas y mostrada su posición relativa, y también del ataúd que actualmente contiene los huesos, y de la caja de cristal y madera de satín en que este está contenido. En su informe a este gobierno, el señor Ober dijo en sustancia que la conclusión alcanzada por la academia española es que los restos de Colón están en la catedral de La Habana, a la sombra de la gloriosa bandera de Castilla, y que es muy apropiado que sobre su sepulcro ondee la misma bandera que navegó con él desde Palos.

records.headline: The News, commenting on the finances of San Domingo, reports
records.summary_en: The News, commenting on the finances of San Domingo, reports the denial of the report that they are in so bad a way that bankruptcy is threatened: the authority for the denial is the president of the New York syndicate that collects and disburses the revenue of San Domingo — that is, the customs receipts, for, it is said, San Domingo has no other taxes of any nature, and survives and thrives on customs. Incidentally, interest is aroused in San Domingo's financial machinery by the revenues being collected at its ports and handled in New York; from all accounts, the policy of the San Domingo government of hiring expert New York financiers to run its money affairs works well, and might be imitated with advantage by other nations, though there is probably something in it too for the syndicate, especially as its agent doubtless has the first hand on the revenues.
records.summary_es: El News, comentando las finanzas de Santo Domingo, reporta la negación del reporte de que están en tan mal estado que la bancarrota amenaza: la autoridad para la negación es el presidente del sindicato de Nueva York que cobra y desembolsa las rentas de Santo Domingo — es decir, los ingresos de aduanas, pues, según se dice, Santo Domingo no tiene otros impuestos de ninguna naturaleza, y sobrevive y prospera con las aduanas. Incidentalmente, el interés se despierta en la maquinaria financiera de Santo Domingo por el hecho de que las rentas se cobran en sus puertos y se manejan en Nueva York; según todos los informes, la política del gobierno de Santo Domingo de contratar financieros expertos de Nueva York para manejar sus asuntos de dinero funciona bien, y podría ser imitada con ventaja por otras naciones, aunque probablemente hay también algo en ello para el sindicato, especialmente porque su agente tiene sin duda la primera mano en las rentas.

records.headline: The Journal prints a list of the capitals of the autonomous governments of the world
records.summary_en: The Journal prints a list of the capitals of the autonomous governments of the world, with their populations: Port au Prince, Hayti, is given at 33,000, and Santo Domingo, capital of the Dominican Republic, at 20,000. This list, the paper says, is believed to include every autonomous government in the world, but there are a number in doubt, like Nepal, in India, and Monaco, which are said to be independent principalities; there are no doubt still other obscure governments in the interior of Asia which are independent, but there are no statistics of any reliability concerning such; and a number of capitals, like Calcutta, Budapest, Havana and Manila, are not technically capitals of autonomous governments, but are the seats of the governments which administer affairs for those peoples.

records.headline: The News reports that President Ulysses Heureaux has been assassinated
records.summary_en: The News reports that President Ulysses Heureaux has been assassinated while attending a christening incognito, and gives a sketch of him: Gen. Ulysses Heureaux has been president of the republic of San Domingo for about ten years; he is a Haytian, about 58 years of age, and a fine type physically of the West Indian negro; while in office he has become immensely wealthy, and has several manufacturing monopolies, notably that of soap, the importation of which is practically impossible; several insurrections have taken place with the idea of overthrowing President Heureaux, but he has succeeded in putting them all down, shooting the leaders very often without trial; and in the early part of June last it was also reported that Gen. Heureaux had been assassinated during a revolution in San Domingo.
records.summary_es: El News reporta que el presidente Ulysses Heureaux ha sido asesinado mientras asistía de incógnito a un bautizo, y ofrece un esbozo de él: el general Ulysses Heureaux ha sido presidente de la república de Santo Domingo por unos diez años; es haitiano, de unos 58 años de edad, y un fino tipo físico del negro antillano; en el cargo se ha hecho inmensamente rico, y tiene varios monopolios de manufactura, notablemente el del jabón, cuya importación es prácticamente imposible; han tenido lugar varias insurrecciones con la idea de derrocar al presidente Heureaux, pero él ha logrado sofocarlas todas, fusilando a los líderes muy a menudo sin juicio; y a principios de junio pasado también se reportó que el general Heureaux había sido asesinado durante una revolución en Santo Domingo.

records.headline: The Tribune prints part of an editorial on the report of President Heureaux's assassination
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints part of an editorial on the report of President Heureaux's assassination: it recalls the president of Uruguay, who was murdered at a public ceremony, and, as to the incognito, General Heureaux has been admitted by his most bitter enemies to be a daring man, going everywhere without an escort, even after he had caused the execution of some of his adversaries; still, he must have sown many seeds of vengeance, and if he is ever assassinated it will be as the result of a personal hatred and not of politics. The people of San Domingo seem to be resigned to the dictatorship of President Heureaux, as shown in the latest revolutionary landing last June at Monte Cristi, where the unfortunate General Morales did not meet a single man of all those who had promised to support him on landing; he was killed, with the twelve men who landed with him, but M. Isidro Jimenes, the merchant banker and aspirer to the Presidency in his country, succeeded in saving his own life by pulling out from the shore, where his friends were slaughtered; he is now in exile at Paris, but, naturally, he must follow the course of events in San Domingo, inasmuch as he has one of his mercantile houses at Cape Haytien, whence the false report was received. There were recently some financial difficulties in the Dominican Republic, but they were reported as having been satisfactorily settled at a conference held between General Heureaux and the president of an American company largely interested in the industrial and commercial development of San Domingo.
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica parte de un editorial sobre el reporte del asesinato del presidente Heureaux: recuerda al presidente del Uruguay, que fue asesinado en una ceremonia pública, y, en cuanto al incógnito, el general Heureaux ha sido admitido por sus enemigos más encarnizados como un hombre audaz, que va a todas partes sin escolta, aun después de haber causado la ejecución de algunos de sus adversarios; aun así, debe haber sembrado muchas semillas de venganza, y si alguna vez es asesinado será como resultado de un odio personal y no de la política. El pueblo de Santo Domingo parece estar resignado a la dictadura del presidente Heureaux, como se mostró en el último desembarco revolucionario en junio pasado en Monte Cristi, donde el desafortunado general Morales no encontró ni un solo hombre de todos los que habían prometido apoyarlo al desembarcar; fue muerto, con los doce hombres que desembarcaron con él, pero el señor Isidro Jimenes, el comerciante banquero y aspirante a la Presidencia en su país, logró salvar su propia vida alejándose de la orilla, donde sus amigos fueron masacrados; ahora está exiliado en París, pero, naturalmente, debe seguir el curso de los eventos en Santo Domingo, ya que tiene una de sus casas mercantiles en Cabo Haitiano, de donde se recibió el reporte falso. Recientemente hubo algunas dificultades financieras en la República Dominicana, pero se reportó que habían sido satisfactoriamente arregladas en una conferencia celebrada entre el general Heureaux y el presidente de una compañía americana ampliamente interesada en el desarrollo industrial y comercial de Santo Domingo.

records.headline: The Star reports a bill in equity filed today by Ogden P. Pell
records.summary_en: The Star reports a bill in equity filed today by Ogden P. Pell, who seeks an accounting and to have a lien declared: the Secretary of State of the United States of America and others are named defendants. Mr. Pell sets forth that in 1887 the city of Santo Domingo, in the Dominican Republic, granted Mr. McKay a concession to build a bridge across the Ozama river, agreeing to pay him a certain amount and allow him a certain proportion of the tolls; Mr. Pell claims that he advanced money to Mr. McKay and the bridge company, he to have a lien for his advances in the sum to be paid for compensation for the building of the bridge; he carried out his part of the contract, he says, but has not received in return what is due him. It is further represented that the republic of Santo Domingo has entered into an agreement with the United States under which the sum of $75,000 is to be paid, through the Secretary of State, to discharge all claims of Mr. McKay or his assigns in connection with the bridge; Mr. Pell asks that his claim be adjudicated as a lien in the fund of $75,000, and that all other persons be enjoined from collecting from it until his claim is paid; and Judge Cox, in Equity Court No. 1, issued a rule to show cause, returnable January 18, why Mr. Pell's prayers should not be granted.
records.summary_es: El Star reporta una demanda en equidad presentada hoy por Ogden P. Pell, quien busca una rendición de cuentas y que se declare un gravamen: el secretario de Estado de los Estados Unidos de América y otros son nombrados demandados. El señor Pell expone que en 1887 la ciudad de Santo Domingo, en la República Dominicana, concedió al señor McKay una concesión para construir un puente sobre el río Ozama, acordando pagarle cierta cantidad y permitirle cierta proporción de los peajes; el señor Pell alega que adelantó dinero al señor McKay y a la compañía del puente, habiendo de tener un gravamen por sus adelantos en la suma a pagarse como compensación por la construcción del puente; él cumplió su parte del contrato, dice, pero no ha recibido a cambio lo que se le debe. Se representa además que la república de Santo Domingo ha entrado en un acuerdo con los Estados Unidos bajo el cual la suma de $75,000 ha de pagarse, a través del secretario de Estado, para saldar todas las reclamaciones del señor McKay o sus cesionarios en conexión con el puente; el señor Pell pide que su reclamación sea adjudicada como un gravamen en el fondo de $75,000, y que a todas las demás personas se les prohíba cobrar de él hasta que su reclamación sea pagada; y el juez Cox, en la Corte de Equidad No. 1, emitió una orden de mostrar causa, retornable el 18 de enero, de por qué no deben concederse las peticiones del señor Pell.

records.summary_en: The *Anaconda Standard* published an overview of the Dominican Republic, detailing its geography, population of 610,000, and history from colonial rule through its independence on February 27, 1844. The report described the nation's political structure, public education system, and major agricultural exports, including tobacco, sugar, coffee, and mahogany. It also observed that while rich mineral deposits of gold, copper, and iron existed, the country's mineral resources remained largely undeveloped.
records.summary_es: *The Anaconda Standard* publicó una reseña general de la República Dominicana, detallando su geografía, una población de 610.000 habitantes y su historia desde la época colonial hasta su independencia el 27 de febrero de 1844. El informe describía la estructura política del país, el sistema de educación pública y sus principales exportaciones agrícolas, entre ellas tabaco, azúcar, café y caoba. Observó asimismo que, si bien existían ricos yacimientos minerales de oro, cobre y hierro, los recursos mineros del país permanecían en gran medida inexplotados.
records.passage: expand in the West Indies than in the East Indies. The island of Santo Domingo is the largest of the West Indies next to Cuba. There are two republics on the island, the republic of Dominica being the larger and comprising about two-thirds of the island, while the republic of Hayti occupies the western end of the island. The island was first settled by the Spanish and was called Hispaniola. Then French buccaneers gained a foothold on it. In 1697 the western part was ceded by Spain to France. In 1800 Toussaint Louverture seized the Spanish part of the island and also stirred up an insurrection in the French part. Through treachery he was enticed to France and died in jail. On February 27, 1844, the Spanish or eastern part of the island threw off allegiance to Spain and formed the republic of Dominica. The republic contains 18,045 square miles and has a population of 610,000. The president is elected for four years, chosen by universal suffrage. He is assisted by a congress of twenty-two deputies elected for two years by popular vote with restricted suffrage. The Spanish language is principally spoken. Education is free and obligatory. The schools are good. The products are mainly tobacco, sugar, rice, coffee, maize, cocoa, bananas, pine apples, sweet potatoes and cotton. Gold, silver, copper, coal, iron and tin exist on the island, but no efforts have been made to develop the mineral resources. Logwood and mahogany are among the principal exports. records.headline: Under the head 'Only Nine Heroes in Sight,' the Tribune prints
records.summary_en: Under the head 'Only Nine Heroes in Sight,' the Tribune prints Juan I. Jimenes's explanation of why his last revolution failed: Jimenes, who has desired for years to overthrow President Heureaux of the Dominican Republic, has issued an 'appeal to the Dominican people,' which, for fluency in the use of adjectives and power of vituperation, is hard to beat, and the translation into English, which he is distributing in this country, makes interesting, if not lucid, reading. Of his last attempt at a revolution, which ended in a fizzle, he writes: 'The proof of my determination was made evident on my landing in the harbor of Monte Cristi for the purpose of taking that city, with the nine men who accompanied me; upon seeing that my plan had failed, by which the city was to be surrendered to me by those expected to storm the place, in spite of this disappointment, I took the city and made its Governor my prisoner; but for the fact that the chief of the fortress managed to escape and give the alarm amongst the few soldiers asleep in the fortress, the latter would have fallen more easily, and the revolution would have continued its successful course; the uprisings that were to take place in other sections of the country did not occur, because of the instructions I had given to the effect that such uprisings must be carried out only after the city was in my possession, or not at all should I fail to take it.'

records.headline: The Democrat prints a story accusing General Maximo Gomez of plotting
records.summary_en: The Democrat prints a story accusing General Maximo Gomez of plotting to overthrow the government of Santo Domingo: 'Having abandoned the hope of becoming the head of the Cuban republic and unwilling to emulate the example of those patriots who, in similar conditions, have thrust aside personal interest and retired to private life, Gomez is conferring with discontented Dominicans, among whom is General Bautista, who is now in Havana, with a view of organizing an expedition composed of former American and Cuban soldiers to attack Santo Domingo, kill President Heureaux and proclaim Gomez dictator. We are informed that Gomez, though an old man, is of infinitely more value than all the Dominican generals put together.' It is scarcely necessary to say, the Democrat adds, that this story is generally discredited.

records.headline: The Tribune prints an article on the Caracas government's effort
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints an article on the Caracas government's effort to secure the body of Alonzo de Ojeda: it is probably upon the invitation of Dr. Jesus Munoz Tebar, governor of the Venezuelan state of Zulia, formerly Minister of Public Works, who has resided for nearly two years in New-York, where he wrote a book on the political philosophy of Latin America, that the government at Caracas has tried to secure the body. The Dominican President, General Ulysses Heureaux, is also a worshipper of all memories and relics relative to the history of his country; he caused recently the building of a handsome mausoleum at Santo Domingo, where were deposited last December the alleged remains of Columbus — the real ones, according to the Dominicans, who say that it is only the ashes of Diego, the son of Columbus, which have been transported by the Spaniards to the Seville cathedral; and the newspapers of Santo Domingo and public opinion there approve the intention of the government to decline the request of Venezuela and to keep the ashes of Ojeda in the lands of Cibao and San Juan, his last abode on earth.
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica un artículo sobre el esfuerzo del gobierno de Caracas por asegurar el cuerpo de Alonzo de Ojeda: probablemente por invitación del Dr. Jesus Munoz Tebar, gobernador del estado venezolano de Zulia, antes ministro de Obras Públicas, que ha residido por casi dos años en Nueva York, donde escribió un libro sobre la filosofía política de América Latina, el gobierno de Caracas ha tratado de asegurar el cuerpo. El presidente dominicano, el general Ulysses Heureaux, es también un adorador de todas las memorias y reliquias relativas a la historia de su país; causó recientemente la construcción de un hermoso mausoleo en Santo Domingo, donde fueron depositados en diciembre pasado los supuestos restos de Colón — los verdaderos, según los dominicanos, que dicen que son solo las cenizas de Diego, el hijo de Colón, las que han sido transportadas por los españoles a la catedral de Sevilla; y los periódicos de Santo Domingo y la opinión pública allí aprueban la intención del gobierno de declinar la petición de Venezuela y de guardar las cenizas de Ojeda en las tierras del Cibao y San Juan, su última morada en la tierra.

records.headline: Under the head 'Bullet Pierced Heureaux's Heart,' the News prints
records.summary_en: Under the head 'Bullet Pierced Heureaux's Heart,' the News prints details of the murder of President Heureaux of Santo Domingo, received at Cape Haytien, July 27: the president was assassinated as he was about to leave on horseback for Santiago de los Caballeros; the assassin, who was surrounded by several accomplices, approached the president as he was talking with some friends and fired twice with a revolver — the first bullet struck the president in the left side and penetrated the heart, causing instant death, and the second bullet killed an old man who was standing near. The assassin and his accomplices then fled to avoid the shots fired at them by the president's friends, and it is not known whether any of them were wounded; the body of the president was taken to the palace of the governor of Moca.

El asesino y sus cómplices huyeron entonces para evitar los disparos que les hicieron los amigos del presidente, y no se sabe si alguno de ellos fue herido; el cuerpo del presidente fue llevado al palacio del gobernador de Moca.

records.headline: The Argus closes its assassination dispatch with the remains of President Heureaux
records.summary_en: The Argus closes its assassination dispatch with the remains of President Heureaux to be taken to Santo Domingo for the funeral services, and, under the head 'Comments at Washington on the Event,' prints a Washington item of July 27: pending official notice of the assassination of President Heureaux of the Dominican republic, which has not been received at this writing, no formal action will be taken by this government; officials here recall that attempts have been made heretofore on the life of Heureaux, and Secretary Hay paid a brief tribute to the work of the deceased president, saying he understood that he had given the country a good administration; should the developments of the next few days show a feeling of unrest and uncertainty regarding the future affairs of the republic, a United States man-of-war will be dispatched to that vicinity to look out for the protection of American interests. Under the head 'Consul General Is Amazed,' the Argus prints a New York item of July 27: Señor Don Alejandro Woss y Gil, consul general of the Dominican republic, when seen at his home there last night, could scarcely credit the news of the assassination of his president, Señor Ulysses Heureaux: 'President Heureaux did wonders to make our people happy and give us prosperity. He was serving his second term, and in a year would have finished his labors as president. He was formerly minister of the interior, and also served as secretary of war. Moca is a town three days' ride by horse from Santo Domingo.'
records.summary_es: El Argus cierra su despacho del asesinato con los restos del presidente Heureaux a ser llevados a Santo Domingo para los servicios fúnebres, y, bajo el título «Comments at Washington on the Event», publica una nota de Washington del 27 de julio: pendiente el aviso oficial del asesinato del presidente Heureaux de la República Dominicana, que no se ha recibido al momento de escribir, no se tomará ninguna acción formal por este gobierno; los funcionarios aquí recuerdan que se han hecho antes intentos contra la vida de Heureaux, y el secretario Hay rindió un breve tributo a la obra del presidente fallecido, diciendo que entendía que él había dado al país una buena administración; si los acontecimientos de los próximos días muestran un sentimiento de inquietud e incertidumbre respecto a los asuntos futuros de la república, un buque de guerra de los Estados Unidos será despachado a esa vecindad para velar por la protección de los intereses americanos. Bajo el título «Consul General Is Amazed», el Argus publica una nota de Nueva York del 27 de julio: el señor don Alejandro Woss y Gil, cónsul general de la República Dominicana, al ser visitado en su casa allí anoche, apenas podía creer la noticia del asesinato de su presidente, el señor Ulysses Heureaux: «El presidente Heureaux hizo maravillas para hacer feliz a nuestro pueblo y darnos prosperidad. Estaba sirviendo su segundo período, y en un año habría terminado sus labores como presidente. Fue antes ministro del interior, y también sirvió como secretario de guerra. Moca es un pueblo a tres días de camino a caballo desde Santo Domingo».

records.headline: The Scranton Tribune completes the Fort de France dispatch of July 27
records.summary_en: The Scranton Tribune completes the Fort de France dispatch of July 27 and prints the news at Washington: General Ulysses Heureaux, president of the Dominican republic, was assassinated at Moca, San Domingo, at half past four o'clock this afternoon; the name of the murderer is Ramon Casceros; he succeeded in making his escape, but an energetic pursuit was at once begun and it is probable that he will soon be captured; Vice-President General Wenceslao Figuereo, immediately upon the announcement of the president's death, assumed the direction of affairs; at present calmness prevails in the republic; and the remains of President Heureaux will probably be taken to San Domingo for the funeral services. The Washington item, of July 26, says no information was received up to a late hour tonight from the consular representatives of the United States in Santo Domingo regarding the assassination of President Heureaux, and that, pending official advices of the assassination, no formal action will be taken by this government: Hon. William F. Powell, the minister to Hayti, is also chargé d'affaires to Santo Domingo, while this government is directly represented in the republic in the person of Campbell L. Maxwell, who is consul general, and John A. Read, who is vice consul; officials here recall that attempts have been made heretofore on the life of Mr. Heureaux; and Secretary Hay paid a brief tribute to the work of the deceased president, saying he understood that he had given the country a good administration.
records.summary_es: El Scranton Tribune completa el despacho de Fort de France del 27 de julio y publica las noticias de Washington: el general Ulysses Heureaux, presidente de la República Dominicana, fue asesinado en Moca, Santo Domingo, a las cuatro y media de esta tarde; el nombre del asesino es Ramon Casceros; logró hacer su escape, pero una persecución enérgica se comenzó de inmediato y es probable que pronto sea capturado; el vicepresidente general Wenceslao Figuereo, inmediatamente después del anuncio de la muerte del presidente, asumió la dirección de los asuntos; al presente prevalece la calma en la república; y los restos del presidente Heureaux serán probablemente llevados a Santo Domingo para los servicios fúnebres. La nota de Washington, del 26 de julio, dice que no se recibió hasta tarde esta noche ninguna información de los representantes consulares de los Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo respecto al asesinato del presidente Heureaux, y que, pendientes los avisos oficiales del asesinato, no se tomará ninguna acción formal por este gobierno: el honorable William F. Powell, el ministro en Haití, es también encargado de negocios en Santo Domingo, mientras el gobierno está directamente representado en la república en la persona de Campbell L. Maxwell, que es cónsul general, y John A. Read, que es vicecónsul; los funcionarios aquí recuerdan que se han hecho antes intentos contra la vida del señor Heureaux; y el secretario Hay rindió un breve tributo a la obra del presidente fallecido, diciendo que entendía que él había dado al país una buena administración.

Gen. Ulysses Heureaux was born in 1838, when San Domingo was a Spanish colony, the republic not being established until 1845; he lived to fight for his country's independence, being one of the bravest leaders in the insurrection which ended the brief Spanish occupation during the civil war; he was first elected president in 1882, taking his seat in 1883, and was re-elected in 1884, 1888, 1892 and 1896, his first term being the unexpired term of his predecessor; he was a brave and determined man, and whenever there was a disturbance in his country he always proceeded to the scene in person, as a soldier, not as president of the country; during his lifetime he passed through many battles and escaped several attempts at assassination — no longer ago than May of last year he outwitted a band of revolutionists headed by Gen. Jiminez, and though another attempt was made to overturn the government by the hand of an assassin, he escaped unharmed; he was a man of medium height, a mulatto, and weighed about 170 pounds, and he spoke English fluently.

records.headline: Under the head 'Full Details of the Crime,' the Star prints
records.summary_en: Under the head 'Full Details of the Crime,' the Star prints a Cape Haytien dispatch of July 27 with details of the murder of President Heureaux of Santo Domingo, received there: a financial crisis having arisen in Santo Domingo, and an insurrection being feared owing to the number of malcontents, President Heureaux went to the north and west of the island to prepare for all eventualities; he was assassinated as he was about to leave Moca on horseback for Santiago de las Caballeros — booted and spurred, ready to mount his horse, he sat under the gallery of a house in the Rue Colon, talking with two friends, at 4:30 in the afternoon, when an old man approached to ask for alms, and just as the president gave the old man some money, Caceres, the assassin, rushed forward quickly and fired twice from his revolver: one bullet struck the heart of the president, killing him instantly, and the other killed the old man by his side. The crime was committed so rapidly that the friends of the president were not able to interfere in time to prevent it, but they fired a number of shots at Caceres, who ran away, accompanied by several persons; the assassin's party returned the fire of the president's friends, and Caceres escaped, and it is not known whether he was wounded or not.
records.summary_es: Bajo el título «Full Details of the Crime», el Star publica un despacho de Cabo Haitiano del 27 de julio con detalles del asesinato del presidente Heureaux de Santo Domingo, recibidos allí: habiendo surgido una crisis financiera en Santo Domingo, y temiéndose una insurrección debido al número de descontentos, el presidente Heureaux fue al norte y al oeste de la isla para prepararse para todas las eventualidades; fue asesinado cuando estaba a punto de partir de Moca a caballo para Santiago de los Caballeros — con botas y espuelas, listo para montar su caballo, estaba sentado bajo la galería de una casa en la Rue Colon, hablando con dos amigos, a las 4:30 de la tarde, cuando un anciano se acercó a pedir limosna, y justo cuando el presidente le dio al anciano algún dinero, Caceres, el asesino, se abalanzó rápidamente y disparó dos veces con su revólver: una bala alcanzó el corazón del presidente, matándolo instantáneamente, y la otra mató al anciano a su lado. El crimen se cometió tan rápidamente que los amigos del presidente no pudieron intervenir a tiempo para impedirlo, pero dispararon un número de tiros a Caceres, que huyó, acompañado por varias personas; el partido del asesino devolvió el fuego de los amigos del presidente, y Caceres escapó, y no se sabe si fue herido o no.

records.headline: The Star prints the text of President McKinley's message of condolence
records.summary_en: The Star prints the text of President McKinley's message of condolence: 'In the name of the American people and my own, I offer to your excellency and the Dominican nation most sincere condolences by reason of the death of President Heureaux. (Signed) William McKinley.' With the message the Star prints the Washington item and the opening of a sketch of the dead president's career: Mr. William F. Powell, the minister to Hayti, is also chargé d'affaires to Santo Domingo, while this government is directly represented in the republic in the person of Campbell L. Maxwell, who is consul general, and John A. Read, who is vice consul; officials here recall that attempts have been made heretofore on the life of Mr. Heureaux; Secretary Hay paid a brief tribute to the work of the deceased president, saying he understood that he had given the country a good administration; and Secretary Long said that there were no ships of the United States navy now in Santo Domingo waters, and that, should the developments of the next few days show a feeling of unrest and uncertainty regarding the future affairs of the republic, a United States man-of-war will be dispatched to that vicinity to look out for the protection of American interests. Heureaux has been called the Napoleon of the south: he was born at Puerto Plata, a town on the north coast of Santo Domingo, in 1846; he became a private soldier in 1862, volunteering in the native service in the uprising against the Spaniards; when the Spaniards left the island, Heureaux had risen to the rank of colonel; and he was a leader in the various attempts to drive from power Buenaventura Baez, who in 1867 usurped absolute power.

records.headline: The Courier completes its assassination dispatch: the remains of President Heureaux
records.summary_en: The Courier completes its assassination dispatch: the remains of President Heureaux will probably be taken to San Domingo for the funeral services; upon the announcement of the president's death, the direction of affairs was assumed, and at present calmness prevails everywhere in the republic. Under the head 'Assassination Confirmed,' a Washington item of July 27 says the State Department today received a dispatch from the United States consul at Puerto Plata — 'President Heureaux was assassinated' — and Consul Read at San Domingo also confirms the report, but neither gives any details; and a Port au Prince, Hayti, item says nothing is known at the Dominican legation there or at other quarters regarding the assassination of Ulysses Heureaux, president of the republic of San Domingo. Under the head 'President Sympathizes,' a Washington item of July 27 says the official confirmation of Heureaux's death was forwarded to the president at Lake Champlain today, and he directed the following to be forwarded in his name to President Figuereo, Heureaux's successor: 'In the name of the American people and my own, I offer your excellency and the Dominican nation the most sincere condolences by reason of the death of President Heureaux.' Under the head 'Details of the Assassination,' a Cape Haytien item of July 27 says the details of the murder of President Heureaux, of Santo Domingo, received there are to the effect that he was assassinated as he was about to leave on horseback for Santiago de las Caballeros; the assassin was Ramon Caceros.
records.summary_es: El Courier completa su despacho del asesinato: los restos del presidente Heureaux serán probablemente llevados a Santo Domingo para los servicios fúnebres; tras el anuncio de la muerte del presidente, la dirección de los asuntos fue asumida, y al presente prevalece la calma en todas partes en la república. Bajo el título «Assassination Confirmed», una nota de Washington del 27 de julio dice que el Departamento de Estado recibió hoy un despacho del cónsul de los Estados Unidos en Puerto Plata — «El presidente Heureaux fue asesinado» — y el cónsul Read en Santo Domingo también confirma el reporte, pero ninguno da detalles; y una nota de Puerto Príncipe, Haití, dice que nada se sabe en la legación dominicana allí ni en otros lugares respecto al asesinato de Ulysses Heureaux, presidente de la república de Santo Domingo. Bajo el título «President Sympathizes», una nota de Washington del 27 de julio dice que la confirmación oficial de la muerte de Heureaux fue enviada al presidente en Lake Champlain hoy, y él dirigió que lo siguiente se enviara en su nombre al presidente Figuereo, el sucesor de Heureaux: «En nombre del pueblo americano y en el mío propio, ofrezco a su excelencia y a la nación dominicana las más sinceras condolencias por motivo de la muerte del presidente Heureaux». Bajo el título «Details of the Assassination», una nota de Cabo Haitiano del 27 de julio dice que los detalles del asesinato del presidente Heureaux, de Santo Domingo, recibidos allí son al efecto de que fue asesinado cuando estaba a punto de partir a caballo para Santiago de los Caballeros; el asesino fue Ramon Caceros.

records.headline: The Democrat prints a dispatch from Hayti of July 27 on the assassination of President Heureaux
records.summary_en: The Democrat prints a dispatch from Hayti of July 27 on the assassination of President Heureaux: the authorities have sent troops in pursuit of the assassin, and the news of the president's death spread rapidly and has caused much commotion among the inhabitants of the country; it is believed by many that the murder was the result of a political conspiracy; the vice president has taken precautions to prevent disorder and has taken command of the troops to that end, but up to the present time all is quiet. Details of the murder of President Heureaux are to the effect that he was assassinated while about to leave on horseback for Santiago de las Caballeros: the assassin, Raymond Caceres, surrounded by several accomplices, as he was talking with several friends, fired upon him twice with a revolver — the first bullet struck the left side and penetrated his heart, and the second bullet killed an old man who was standing near the president; the assassin and his friends then fled to escape the shots fired after them by the friends of the president; and the body of the president was taken to the palace of the governor of Moca, and the president's death has caused a panic.
records.summary_es: El Democrat publica un despacho de Haití del 27 de julio sobre el asesinato del presidente Heureaux: las autoridades han enviado tropas en persecución del asesino, y la noticia de la muerte del presidente se extendió rápidamente y ha causado mucha conmoción entre los habitantes del país; se cree por muchos que el asesinato fue el resultado de una conspiración política; el vicepresidente ha tomado precauciones para prevenir el desorden y ha tomado el mando de las tropas con ese fin, pero hasta el presente todo está tranquilo. Los detalles del asesinato del presidente Heureaux son al efecto de que fue asesinado mientras estaba a punto de partir a caballo para Santiago de los Caballeros: el asesino, Raymond Caceres, rodeado por varios cómplices, mientras él hablaba con varios amigos, disparó sobre él dos veces con un revólver — la primera bala alcanzó el costado izquierdo y le penetró el corazón, y la segunda bala mató a un anciano que estaba parado cerca del presidente; el asesino y sus amigos huyeron entonces para escapar de los disparos que les hicieron tras ellos los amigos del presidente; y el cuerpo del presidente fue llevado al palacio del gobernador de Moca, y la muerte del presidente ha causado un pánico.

records.headline: The Democrat completes its assassination dispatch: the remains of President Heureaux
records.summary_en: The Democrat completes its assassination dispatch: the remains of President Heureaux will probably be taken to Santo Domingo for the funeral services; upon the announcement of the president's death, the direction of affairs was assumed, and at present calmness prevails everywhere in the republic; and it prints a sketch of the dead president: Ulysses Heureaux, who for 17 years had been president of the republic of Santo Domingo, was a sort of Napoleon in this negro republic of the West Indies: it was a queer sight for visitors to this bankrupt little republic on the eastern end of the island of Haiti to see a ruler with the airs of a czar, the politeness of a Parisian, at times the morals of a sultan, and a defiant bravado that made him a dictator, and all this under the thin guise of a republican form of government. Heureaux was 53 years old; he was born in Puerto Plata, the nearest city to the little town of Moca, where he was assassinated Tuesday; he became a common soldier, and by bravery, brains and dash soon won high command; all the West Indies at one time or another have fought Spain — Santo Domingo did, and Heureaux became a general in that war; he was a fighter, a fearless, reckless one, whom bullets could not stop, and he received several of them in his body, but did not mind them; finally, when warfare palled, he became a politician, and his success in that exciting game was so great that his military record was overshadowed; and in 1882 Heureaux was elected president of the republic.
records.summary_es: El Democrat completa su despacho del asesinato: los restos del presidente Heureaux serán probablemente llevados a Santo Domingo para los servicios fúnebres; tras el anuncio de la muerte del presidente, la dirección de los asuntos fue asumida, y al presente prevalece la calma en todas partes en la república; y publica un esbozo del presidente muerto: Ulysses Heureaux, que por 17 años había sido presidente de la república de Santo Domingo, era una especie de Napoleón en esta república negra de las Indias Occidentales: era un espectáculo extraño para los visitantes de esta pequeña república en bancarrota en el extremo oriental de la isla de Haití ver a un gobernante con los aires de un zar, la cortesía de un parisino, a veces la moral de un sultán, y una bravata desafiante que lo hacía un dictador, y todo esto bajo la fina apariencia de una forma republicana de gobierno. Heureaux tenía 53 años; nació en Puerto Plata, la ciudad más cercana al pequeño pueblo de Moca, donde fue asesinado el martes; se hizo soldado raso, y por bravura, inteligencia y arrojo pronto ganó alto mando; todas las Indias Occidentales en un momento u otro han luchado contra España — Santo Domingo lo hizo, y Heureaux se hizo general en esa guerra; era un luchador, uno temerario y sin miedo, a quien las balas no podían detener, y recibió varias de ellas en su cuerpo, pero no les hacía caso; finalmente, cuando la guerra cansó, se hizo político, y su éxito en ese juego emocionante fue tan grande que su historial militar fue eclipsado; y en 1882 Heureaux fue elegido presidente de la república.

records.headline: The Journal's sketch of Heureaux continues with anecdotes of his rule
records.summary_en: The Journal's sketch of Heureaux continues with anecdotes of his rule: stumbling upon a group of suspects, he learned their whole plans, and the next day he sent for the men, and there was a seance of terror in the palace. Another time Heureaux went alone to a place where he knew conspirators were meeting; bursting into the room he confronted them, slowly looked around the group, and then dramatically pointed his finger at each, exclaiming, 'You here?'; he was one man in the power of fifty — they were plotting his death, and had him now in their hands, but not one dared move against him; the next day the conspirators were summoned to the palace and lined up before the President, and no ancient despot ever gloated more over victims than Heureaux did over these conspirators, whom he had defied with his bravado, and before sundown they were shot. Enemies accused President Heureaux of the crimes of Oriental monarchs: he rid himself of troublesome opponents, they declared, by poison; secret assassination was another of his favorite methods of heading off plots, and insurrections were nipped in the bud by almost indiscriminate executions; and men were sent on journeys of state and never reached their destinations.
records.summary_es: El esbozo del Journal sobre Heureaux continúa con anécdotas de su gobierno: tropezando con un grupo de sospechosos, aprendió todos sus planes, y al día siguiente hizo venir a los hombres, y hubo una sesión de terror en el palacio. En otra ocasión Heureaux fue solo a un lugar donde sabía que los conspiradores se estaban reuniendo; irrumpiendo en el cuarto los confrontó, miró lentamente alrededor del grupo, y luego apuntó dramáticamente con su dedo a cada uno, exclamando: «¿Usted aquí?»; era un hombre solo en poder de cincuenta — estaban tramando su muerte, y lo tenían ahora en sus manos, pero ni uno se atrevió a moverse contra él; al día siguiente los conspiradores fueron citados al palacio y alineados ante el Presidente, y ningún déspota antiguo se regocijó más sobre sus víctimas que Heureaux sobre estos conspiradores, a quienes había desafiado con su bravata, y antes de la puesta del sol fueron fusilados. Los enemigos acusaron al presidente Heureaux de los crímenes de los monarcas orientales: se deshizo de oponentes molestos, declararon, por veneno; el asesinato secreto era otro de sus métodos favoritos de cortar las conspiraciones, y las insurrecciones eran cortadas de raíz por ejecuciones casi indiscriminadas; y los hombres eran enviados a viajes de estado y nunca llegaban a sus destinos.

records.headline: The Journal's sketch of Heureaux, continuing, gives the Liberals' verdict
records.summary_en: The Journal's sketch of Heureaux, continuing, gives the Liberals' verdict on his rule: that was the way Heureaux maintained his power. Secret assassination was another of his favorite methods of heading off plots, and insurrections were nipped in the bud by almost indiscriminate executions; men were sent on journeys of state and never reached their destinations, and others were arrested and nothing more heard of their fate. Three years ago General Castillo, Minister of War, thought the opportunity favorable for starting a revolution for his own benefit: there was some trouble in the province, and Castillo got 1,000 rifles from the President on the plea of sending them to the province to put down the rebellion — of course, Castillo saw that they fell into the hands of his friends. Heureaux was for a time fooled, but discovered what was going on; he ordered General Estay, governor of the province, to execute Castillo, but the order was not carried out; by a neat stratagem the President enticed Castillo to the capital and arrested him, and the Minister was put aboard a war ship and taken to the province, where he was shot, and General Estay, surprised and protesting, was executed also because he had not obeyed orders. During the past two years Heureaux had lively times with the Jimenes insurrection that would not completely down, although he succeeded in driving Jimenes and General Morales out of the country; despotism was wearing on the people, and Heureaux was waning a bit in popular favor, and besides, Heureaux was piling up the national debt of the country.
records.summary_es: El esbozo del Journal sobre Heureaux, continuando, ofrece el veredicto de los Liberales sobre su gobierno: esa era la manera en que Heureaux mantenía su poder. El asesinato secreto era otro de sus métodos favoritos de cortar las conspiraciones, y las insurrecciones eran cortadas de raíz por ejecuciones casi indiscriminadas; los hombres eran enviados a viajes de estado y nunca llegaban a sus destinos, y otros eran arrestados y nada más se supo de su suerte. Hace tres años el general Castillo, ministro de Guerra, creyó favorable la oportunidad para comenzar una revolución para su propio beneficio: había algún disturbio en la provincia, y Castillo consiguió 1,000 rifles del Presidente con el pretexto de enviarlos a la provincia para sofocar la rebelión — por supuesto, Castillo se aseguró de que cayeran en manos de sus amigos. Heureaux estuvo por un tiempo engañado, pero descubrió lo que estaba pasando; ordenó al general Estay, gobernador de la provincia, ejecutar a Castillo, pero la orden no se llevó a cabo; por una estratagema ingeniosa el Presidente atrajo a Castillo a la capital y lo arrestó, y el Ministro fue puesto a bordo de un buque de guerra y llevado a la provincia, donde fue fusilado, y el general Estay, sorprendido y protestando, fue ejecutado también porque no había obedecido las órdenes. Durante los últimos dos años Heureaux tuvo tiempos animados con la insurrección de Jimenes que no se dejaba sofocar por completo, aunque logró expulsar a Jimenes y al general Morales del país; el despotismo estaba cansando al pueblo, y Heureaux estaba perdiendo un poco de favor popular, y además, Heureaux estaba acumulando la deuda nacional del país.

records.headline: The Times prints a dispatch on the assassination and the State Department's confirmation of it
records.summary_en: The Times prints a dispatch on the assassination and the State Department's confirmation of it: three men at once opened fire upon the president with revolvers, mortally wounding him; the names of the assassins are Juan Pichardo, Horacio Vasquez, and Ramon Caceres, all prominent residents of Moca; the murderers of the president made their escape, and it is not probable that they will be captured; and business is paralyzed, but at present the country is quiet. The State Department received this morning from Campbell L. Maxwell, American consul general at Santo Domingo, an official confirmation of the assassination of President Heureaux; and through the State Department, President McKinley sent a cablegram of condolence to President Figuereo: 'Lake Champlain, via Washington, July 27, 1899. His Excellency Wenceslao Figuereo, President of the Dominican Republic, Santo Domingo: In the name of the American people, and in my own, I offer to your Excellency and the Dominican Nation most sincere condolences, by reason of the death of President Heureaux. William McKinley.' It was said at the State Department this afternoon that the assassination of President Heureaux will probably not disturb the diplomatic relations between that country and the United States, and that, unless it shall appear that American business interests on the island are in danger by a possible revolution or political agitation growing out of the tragedy, no action will be taken by this Government beyond the official expression of sympathy with the inhabitants of the Republic.

records.summary_en: The Gazette completes its assassination dispatch: the remains of President Heureaux will probably be taken to Santo Domingo for the funeral services; General Wenceslao Figuereo, immediately upon the announcement of the President's death, assumed the direction of affairs, and at present calmness prevails everywhere in the republic. President Heureaux was a soldier during his entire lifetime: one of his arms was paralyzed from a wound he received by a rifle ball in battle; he is described by Americans familiar with his career as a man without fear, and when there was any disturbance or revolution in any part of the republic, he mounted his horse and went pellmell himself to the front as leader, and learned all the details of the revolution as well as the causes leading to it; President Heureaux was about fifty-four years of age, he spoke English fluently, and treated everybody who approached him with courtesy. The Gazette also prints a Puerto Plata item of July 27: it is learned that President Heureaux met his death at the hands of three men as he was entering a friend's house: the three fired at Heureaux with revolvers, and one shot entered the heart, causing instant death; friends of the President returned the fire, but the assassins fled and their whereabouts are not known; Heureaux was at Moca on one of his periodical trips to investigate affairs on the island; and the assassination is believed to be due to the personal animosity of Caceres, the chief assassin, whose father was executed by orders of Heureaux in 1884.

records.headline: The Standard prints part of an article on the annexation attempt
records.summary_en: The Standard prints part of an article on the annexation attempt under Grant: a speech quoted in the article declares that "the idea of annexing the Dominican republic to the United States may acquire such a degree of popularity among members of congress as will be necessary for its accomplishment," and asks, "Shall I read the rest of the document? It is in the same tenor. There are questions of money in it, cash down, all of which must have been particularly agreeable to the three confederates." After the delivery of this speech Grant and Sumner had no personal intercourse; public opinion did not justify the course of Senator Sumner; no further attempt was made by the president to urge the acquisition of San Domingo upon congress, it being evident that neither the Senate nor the House could be induced to approve the scheme, and the administration was necessarily compelled to abandon it; but defeat did not change General Grant's view of the question, and in his last annual message to congress, in December, 1876, nearly six years after the controversy closed, he recurred to the subject to record once more his approval of it.
records.summary_es: El Standard publica parte de un artículo sobre el intento de anexión bajo Grant: un discurso citado en el artículo declara que «la idea de anexar la República Dominicana a los Estados Unidos puede adquirir tal grado de popularidad entre los miembros del congreso como será necesario para su realización», y pregunta: «¿Leo el resto del documento? Es del mismo tenor. Hay en él cuestiones de dinero, en efectivo, todo lo cual debe haber sido particularmente agradable a los tres confederados». Después de la pronunciación de este discurso, Grant y Sumner no tuvieron más trato personal; la opinión pública no justificó el curso del senador Sumner; no se hizo ningún intento más por el presidente de instar la adquisición de Santo Domingo ante el congreso, siendo evidente que ni el Senado ni la Cámara podrían ser inducidos a aprobar el plan, y la administración se vio necesariamente obligada a abandonarlo; pero la derrota no cambió la opinión del general Grant sobre la cuestión, y en su último mensaje anual al congreso, en diciembre de 1876, casi seis años después de cerrada la controversia, volvió sobre el tema para registrar una vez más su aprobación.

records.headline: The Times prints a New York item of July 26 on the assassination
records.summary_en: The Times prints a New York item of July 26 on the assassination: private despatches received late this afternoon in this city from Santo Domingo reported that Gen. Ulysses Heureaux, president of the Dominican Republic, had been assassinated at Moca at 4:30 o'clock in the afternoon; the despatches were without details, but the crime was undoubtedly inspired by political motives. Alejandro Wos y Gil, who preceded Heureaux as president of the republic, is its consul general at New York and charge d'affaires; he heard the news this afternoon, but had no particulars, and said tonight that he did not believe the report of the assassination: "In fact," he said, "I feel sure that it is false. There have been a number of similar rumors within the past two years, but they have always been contradicted next day. The meagre details of the alleged murder also argue to me that the report is unfounded. I am positive that I would have been notified either by the officials of my own country or by the United States government at Washington if the president had been killed. I received a cipher cable despatch from him on Monday. Now, the village of Moca is three days' journey by horse from the place from which the cable was sent. There are no railroads between the two places, and I am positive that it would have been impossible for the president to have gone to Moca and for the news of his murder there to have reached a place from which the news could be cabled here in so short a time."

Alejandro Wos y Gil, que precedió a Heureaux como presidente de la república, es su cónsul general en Nueva York y encargado de negocios; oyó la noticia esta tarde, pero no tenía particulares, y dijo esta noche que no creía el reporte del asesinato: «De hecho», dijo, «estoy seguro de que es falso. Ha habido un número de rumores similares dentro de los pasados dos años, pero siempre han sido contradichos al día siguiente. Los escasos detalles del alegado asesinato también me arguyen que el reporte es infundado. Estoy positivo de que habría sido notificado, ya por los funcionarios de mi propio país o por el gobierno de los Estados Unidos en Washington, si el presidente hubiera sido muerto. Recibí de él un despacho cifrado por cable el lunes. Ahora bien, el pueblo de Moca está a tres días de camino a caballo desde el lugar desde el cual se envió el cable. records.headline: The Times' sketch of Heureaux's career continues with the executions
records.summary_en: The Times' sketch of Heureaux's career continues with the executions: men who had conspired against Heureaux were executed; in June, 1895, it was reported that his enemies had succeeded in killing him, but he had escaped, and it was thought he had succeeded in downing all the opposition to him; he was elected to the presidency in 1887, and the constitution of the republic was changed so as to permit him to succeed himself; he was already in his second term in 1893, and the attempts upon his life have all been made since then; in spite of the conspiracies that had begun in his second term he was twice again re-elected and was in his fourth term; while the prosperity under his administration has been unusual for Santo Domingo, it has not been such as to mark a material advance in the republic's general condition; the president's policy has been a progressive one, but the nation has not gone forward with any degree of rapidity in the way of civilization; under Heureaux American and English capital has been welcomed and railroads have been begun and have been extended, and the telegraphic facilities of the country, by which most of the chief towns are now connected, were furthered at his instance. Under the head 'The Castillo Rebellion,' the sketch continues: in the spring of 1896 the president found himself called upon to deal with a conspiracy against his power in the province of San Pedro de Macoris; General Ramon Castillo, his minister of war, had shortly before asked for 1,000 rifles to put down an incipient rebellion in that province, and had gone there in command to restore order, as he said.

Bajo el título «The Castillo Rebellion», el esbozo continúa: en la primavera de 1896 el presidente se vio llamado a lidiar con una conspiración contra su poder en la provincia de San Pedro de Macorís; el general Ramon Castillo, su ministro de guerra, había pedido poco antes 1,000 rifles para sofocar una rebelión incipiente en esa provincia, y había ido allí al mando para restaurar el orden, según dijo.

records.headline: The Times' sketch continues with the order to kill Castillo
records.summary_en: The Times' sketch continues with the order to kill Castillo in San Pedro de Macoris, and, under the head 'Other Plots,' with the later conspiracies: in June, 1898, there was a good deal of discontent in Santo Domingo, owing partly to commercial and industrial depressions, and, when the operations of the Spanish-American war caused more or less excitement in the West Indies, Juan Jiminez, a former New York merchant who before had had political aspirations in Santo Domingo, led an attack upon Heureaux's power; he sailed with an expedition from the Bahamas for Cape Haitien and went thence to Monte Cristo, a town of Santo Domingo which he had founded; Jiminez landed in an American ship, the Fanita; General Garcia, who was in charge of affairs for him at Monte Cristo, was unprepared for action, but the two conspirators, together with Gen. Augustin Morales and eleven men, essayed to carry out their purpose and called upon the governor to surrender; the governor had twenty soldiers, who opened fire on the insurrectionists, killing five of them; Jiminez escaped to his ship; all the others except Garcia were captured, and Jiminez's secretary had turned informer; Jiminez went to Great Inagua, where he was arrested; he was tried at Nassau and acquitted, and since then he has carried on a propaganda against the administration of President Heureaux. In 1891 there was a carefully laid dynamite plot to blow up Heureaux; Heureaux has been described as humane when not thwarted, but ferocious when provoked by attempts on his authority; he was diplomatic and could speak four languages.

records.headline: The Spy prints the close of the assassination dispatch and the Washington item of July 26
records.summary_en: The Spy prints the close of the assassination dispatch and the Washington item of July 26: the remains of President Heureaux will probably be taken to San Domingo for the funeral services. The Washington item, under the head 'No Official News,' says that no information was received up to half past 9 o'clock tonight from the consular representatives of the United States in San Domingo regarding the assassination there today of President Heureaux, and that, pending official advices of the assassination, no formal action will be taken by this government: Hon. William F. Powell, the minister to Hayti, is also charge d'affaires to San Domingo, while this government is directly represented in the republic in the person of Campbell L. Maxwell, who is consul general, and John A. Read, who is vice consul; officials here recall that attempts have been made heretofore on the life of Mr. Heureaux; Secretary Hay paid a brief tribute to the work of the deceased president, saying he understood that he had given the country a good administration; and Secretary Long said he could not recall that there were any ships of the United States navy in San Domingo waters, and that, should the developments of the next few days show a feeling of uncertainty regarding the future affairs of the island, a United States man-of-war will be dispatched to that vicinity to look out for the protection of American interests.
records.summary_es: El Spy publica el cierre del despacho del asesinato y la nota de Washington del 26 de julio: los restos del presidente Heureaux serán probablemente llevados a Santo Domingo para los servicios fúnebres. La nota de Washington, bajo el título «No Official News», dice que no se recibió hasta las nueve y media de esta noche ninguna información de los representantes consulares de los Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo respecto al asesinato allí hoy del presidente Heureaux, y que, pendientes los avisos oficiales del asesinato, no se tomará ninguna acción formal por este gobierno: el honorable William F. Powell, el ministro en Haití, es también encargado de negocios en Santo Domingo, mientras este gobierno está directamente representado en la república en la persona de Campbell L. Maxwell, que es cónsul general, y John A. Read, que es vicecónsul; los funcionarios aquí recuerdan que se han hecho antes intentos contra la vida del señor Heureaux; el secretario Hay rindió un breve tributo a la obra del presidente fallecido, diciendo que entendía que él había dado al país una buena administración; y el secretario Long dijo que no podía recordar que hubiera ninguno de los buques de la marina de los Estados Unidos en aguas de Santo Domingo, y que, si los acontecimientos de los próximos días muestran un sentimiento de incertidumbre respecto a los asuntos futuros de la isla, un buque de guerra de los Estados Unidos será despachado a esa vecindad para velar por la protección de los intereses americanos.

records.headline: The Age-Herald prints details of the murder of President Heureaux
records.summary_en: The Age-Herald prints details of the murder of President Heureaux, received at Cape Haytien in a dispatch of July 27: he was assassinated as he was about to leave on horseback for Santiago de los Caballeros; the assassin, Ramon Caceros, surrounded by several accomplices, approached the president as he was talking with some friends and fired twice with a revolver; the first bullet struck the president in the left side and penetrated the heart, causing instant death; the second bullet killed an old man who was standing near the president; the assassin and his accomplices then fled to avoid the shots fired at them by the president's friends, and it is not known whether any of them were wounded; the body of the president was taken to the palace of the governor of Moca; President Heureaux's death has caused a panic; it is said that one Juan Isidoro Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection of June, 1898, is a candidate for the presidency; and it is reported that General Maximo Gomez, formerly president of the Cuban insurrectionists, who is a native of San Domingo, also aspires to the presidency.
