records.headline: The Age-Herald completes its account of the assassination aftermath
records.summary_en: The Age-Herald completes its account of the assassination aftermath: the successor assumes the presidential functions, acting with the ministers, and has informed the widow of President Heureaux that the body of her husband will be interred at Santiago de los Caballeros, orders for carrying out the plan having been given to the governors of Santiago; it is concurrently reported that this course was decided on in order to avoid the excitement and manifestations which would be the result of the removal of the remains to the city of Santo Domingo; foreseeing the possibility of disturbances, and in order to prepare for any emergency, General Pepin, governor of Santiago, has taken important precautionary measures and has decided to demand that arms and ammunition be forwarded to him from Santo Domingo; and advices from Santiago received here at a late hour report that the situation there is becoming more serious. Under the head 'A Political Crime,' a Fort de France dispatch of July 27 says that the body of President Heureaux has been taken to Santiago de los Caballeros; the president's widow has requested that the remains be transported by railway to Puerto Plata and from there to Santo Domingo by sea, but the government of Santiago fears disorder if the body should be removed from there by train; the government of Santiago confirms the general opinion that the assassination of the president was a political crime; and it is reported that the assassin's party is gathering forces preparatory to an attack on the government troops.
records.summary_es: El Age-Herald completa su relato de las secuelas del asesinato: el sucesor asume las funciones presidenciales, actuando con los ministros, y ha informado a la viuda del presidente Heureaux que el cuerpo de su esposo será enterrado en Santiago de los Caballeros, habiéndose dado a los gobernadores de Santiago las órdenes para llevar a cabo el plan; se reporta concurrentemente que este curso se decidió para evitar la excitación y las manifestaciones que serían el resultado del traslado de los restos a la ciudad de Santo Domingo; previendo la posibilidad de disturbios, y para prepararse para cualquier emergencia, el general Pepin, gobernador de Santiago, ha tomado importantes medidas precautorias y ha decidido demandar que se le envíen armas y municiones desde Santo Domingo; y avisos de Santiago recibidos aquí a hora avanzada reportan que la situación allí se está volviendo más seria. Bajo el título «A Political Crime», un despacho de Fort de France del 27 de julio dice que el cuerpo del presidente Heureaux ha sido llevado a Santiago de los Caballeros; la viuda del presidente ha pedido que los restos sean transportados por ferrocarril a Puerto Plata y de allí a Santo Domingo por mar, pero el gobierno de Santiago teme desorden si el cuerpo fuera removido de allí por tren; el gobierno de Santiago confirma la opinión general de que el asesinato del presidente fue un crimen político; y se reporta que el partido del asesino está reuniendo fuerzas en preparación para un ataque contra las tropas del gobierno.

records.headline: The Argus prints the Santiago dispatch on the assassination
records.summary_en: The Argus prints the Santiago dispatch on the assassination aftermath: the remains will be interred at Santiago de los Caballeros, and orders for the carrying out of this plan have been given to the governor of Santiago; it is currently reported that this course was decided upon in order to avoid the excitement and manifestations which would be the result of the removal of the remains to the City of Santo Domingo; foreseeing the possibility of disturbances, and in order to be prepared for any emergency, General Pepin, governor of Santiago, has taken important precautionary measures and has decided to demand that arms and ammunition be forwarded to him from Santo Domingo; and advices from Santiago report that the situation there is becoming more serious. Under the head 'It Was a Political Assassination,' the paper continues: the governor of Santiago confirms the general opinion that the assassination of President Heureaux was a political crime; it is reported that the assassin's party is gathering forces preparatory to an attack on the government troops; it has been learned that Caceros' companions when President Heureaux was killed were Juan Pichardo and Horacio Vasquez, the latter the brother of a deputy in parliament; a financial crisis having arisen in Santo Domingo, and an insurrection being feared owing to the number of malcontents, President Heureaux went to the north and west of the island to prepare for what might happen, and he was about to leave Moca for Santiago de los Caballeros when he was killed.
records.summary_es: El Argus publica el despacho de Santiago sobre las secuelas del asesinato: los restos serán enterrados en Santiago de los Caballeros, y las órdenes para llevar a cabo este plan han sido dadas al gobernador de Santiago; se reporta corrientemente que este curso se decidió para evitar la excitación y las manifestaciones que serían el resultado del traslado de los restos a la ciudad de Santo Domingo; previendo la posibilidad de disturbios, y para estar preparado para cualquier emergencia, el general Pepin, gobernador de Santiago, ha tomado importantes medidas precautorias y ha decidido demandar que se le envíen armas y municiones desde Santo Domingo; y avisos de Santiago reportan que la situación allí se está volviendo más seria. Bajo el título «It Was a Political Assassination», el periódico continúa: el gobernador de Santiago confirma la opinión general de que el asesinato del presidente Heureaux fue un crimen político; se reporta que el partido del asesino está reuniendo fuerzas en preparación para un ataque contra las tropas del gobierno; se ha sabido que los compañeros de Caceros cuando el presidente Heureaux fue muerto eran Juan Pichardo y Horacio Vasquez, este último hermano de un diputado en el parlamento; habiendo surgido una crisis financiera en Santo Domingo, y temiéndose una insurrección debido al número de descontentos, el presidente Heureaux fue al norte y al oeste de la isla para prepararse para lo que pudiera suceder, y estaba a punto de partir de Moca para Santiago de los Caballeros cuando fue muerto.

records.headline: The Fisherman and Farmer prints the Fort de France dispatch
records.summary_en: The Fisherman and Farmer prints the Fort de France dispatch and the Washington item of July 26: Ulises Heureaux, president of the Dominican Republic, was assassinated at Moca, Santo Domingo, at half past four o'clock this afternoon; the name of the murderer is Ramon Caceros; he succeeded in making his escape, but an energetic pursuit was at once begun and it is probable he will soon be captured; and at present calmness prevails everywhere in the republic. The Washington item says that no information was received up to 9:30 o'clock tonight from the consular representatives of the United States in Santo Domingo regarding the assassination there today of President Heureaux, and that, pending official advices of the assassination, no formal action will be taken by this government: Hon. W. F. Powell, the minister to Hayti, is also charge d'affaires to Santo Domingo, while this government is directly represented in the republic in the person of Campbell L. Maxwell, who is consul-general, and John A. Read, who is vice consul; officials here recall that attempts have been made heretofore on the life of Mr. Heureaux; Secretary Hay paid a brief tribute to the work of the deceased president, saying he understood that he had given the country a good administration; and, should the developments of the next few days show a feeling of unrest and uncertainty regarding the future affairs of the island, a United States man-of-war will be dispatched to that vicinity to look out for the protection of American interests.
records.summary_es: El Fisherman and Farmer publica el despacho de Fort de France y la nota de Washington del 26 de julio: Ulises Heureaux, presidente de la República Dominicana, fue asesinado en Moca, Santo Domingo, a las cuatro y media de esta tarde; el nombre del asesino es Ramon Caceros; logró hacer su escape, pero una persecución enérgica se comenzó de inmediato y es probable que pronto sea capturado; y al presente prevalece la calma en todas partes en la república. La nota de Washington dice que no se recibió hasta las 9:30 de esta noche ninguna información de los representantes consulares de los Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo respecto al asesinato allí hoy del presidente Heureaux, y que, pendientes los avisos oficiales del asesinato, no se tomará ninguna acción formal por este gobierno: el honorable W. records.headline: The News prints a Kingston dispatch of July 28 on the Jimenez plot
records.summary_en: The News prints a Kingston dispatch of July 28 on the Jimenez plot: advices from Santo Domingo to a Dominican at Kingston, Jamaica, describe the existence of a well-planned and widespread plot by adherents of Jimenez to depose President Heureaux, which it was thought was sure to succeed, and the assassination of President Heureaux is regarded there as an indication of the success of the plot. The Washington item, under the head 'The Entering Wedge,' reports that a naval vessel is to be sent immediately to Santo Domingo; this is a measure of precaution rather than one of necessity at the present time, for Minister Powell has not suggested any such action to the government, but it is deemed well, in view of the press reports indicating the disturbed condition of affairs, to have a representative of the United States authority within reach of the minister to protect American interests should the need arise.

La nota de Washington, bajo el título «The Entering Wedge», reporta que un buque de guerra será enviado inmediatamente a Santo Domingo; esta es una medida de precaución más que de necesidad en el momento presente, pues el ministro Powell no ha sugerido al gobierno ninguna acción semejante, pero se estima bien, en vista de los reportes de prensa que indican la condición perturbada de los asuntos, tener un representante de la autoridad de los Estados Unidos al alcance del ministro para proteger los intereses americanos si surge la necesidad.

records.headline: The Register prints a sketch of Heureaux's career: he was born
records.summary_en: The Register prints a sketch of Heureaux's career: he was born in Puerto Plata, San Domingo, in 1846; he became a private soldier in 1862 and was soon after appointed commandant in the district of Puerto Plata; he served continuously in the war against Spain from 1868 to 1874; twice he was exiled for political reasons; for two years he retired to private life, and again in 1878 assumed command to put down a Spanish uprising; he had been wounded many times and narrowly escaped several plots to kill him; during the recent Spanish-American war a filibustering expedition, alleged to have been fitted out in a port in the southern part of the United States, made an attempt to land in San Domingo, but was met and checked by Heureaux's prompt action, and at that time his assassination was rumored and had undoubtedly been planned; Gen. Heureaux was re-elected president of San Domingo at a general election, November 1, 1898, and was serving his fourth term; Gen. Heureaux was first elected president, September 1, 1882, to succeed Fernando A. Merino, when the national party, of which he was an active representative, was powerful; General Maximo Gomez, former president of the Cuban insurrectionists, who is a native of San Domingo, also aspires to the presidency; the father of Caceros, the assassin, was put to death by order of President Heureaux in 1884; and a financial crisis having arisen in Santo Domingo, and an insurrection being feared owing to the number of malcontents, President Heureaux went to the north and west of the island to prepare for all eventualities.

records.headline: The Times continues its New York item with Consul General Gil's reaction
records.summary_en: The Times continues its New York item with Consul General Gil's reaction: Alejandro Wos y Gil, consul general and charge d'affaires of the Dominican Republic in this city, who had received no answer to his message of inquiry, was much shocked when he read the despatches verifying the reports received last night: "It is very sad news," he said. "I had hoped that this rumor, like many others I have heard in the course of the past year, would prove false." Consul General Gil then expressed the opinion that the president's death would not have a serious effect upon the republic. Mr. York, of the Santo Domingo Improvement Company, was very positive that no serious results would follow the president's death: "The affairs of the country are in a sound, healthy condition and things will go on as usual. The fact that the President was assassinated does not mean that there is any general discontent among the citizens of the country. That would be a false assumption. Discontented persons with murderous instincts are to be found in every country, but as a rule they do not represent the great body of the people. You will appreciate the extent of my confidence in the strength of the Government when I tell you my wife and children sail for Santo Domingo today on the Clyde line steamship Carib. I am sorry to hear of General Heureaux's death, very sorry, but it will surely not affect the country seriously." Moca is the principal town of the Espaillat province; it is situated in the mountains on the north coast of the island, and has no railroad communication.

records.headline: The Republican prints the Fort de France dispatch on the assassination
records.summary_en: The Republican prints the Fort de France dispatch on the assassination: Gen. Ulises Heureaux, president of the Dominican republic, was assassinated at Moca at 4:30 o'clock Wednesday afternoon; the name of the murderer is Ramon Caceros; he succeeded in making his escape, but an energetic pursuit was at once begun and it is probable that he will soon be captured; the vice-president, Gen. Wenceslao Figuereo, immediately upon the announcement of the president's death assumed the direction of affairs; at present calmness prevails everywhere in the republic; and the body of President Heureaux will probably be taken to San Domingo for the funeral services.

records.headline: The Telegram prints the details of the assassination at Moca
records.summary_en: The Telegram prints the details of the assassination at Moca: the assassin, surrounded by several accomplices, approached the president as he was talking with some friends and fired twice with a revolver; the first bullet struck the president in the left side and penetrated to the heart, causing instant death; the second bullet killed an old man who was standing near the president; the assassin and his accomplices then fled to avoid the shots fired at them by the president's friends, and it is not known if any of them was wounded; the body of the president was taken to the palace of the governor of Moca; President Heureaux's death has caused a panic; it is said that one Juan Isidoro Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection of June, 1898, is a candidate for the presidency; it is reported that General Maximo Gomez, former president of the Cuban insurrectionists, who is a native of Santo Domingo, also aspires to the presidency; and the father of Caceres, the assassin, was put to death by order of President Heureaux in 1881. The other account, under the head 'Another Version of the Affair,' says that a financial crisis having arisen in Santo Domingo, and an insurrection being feared owing to the number of the malcontents, President Heureaux went to the north and west of the island to prepare for all eventualities; he was about to leave Moca for Santiago de los Caballeros when he was killed; booted and spurred, ready to mount his horse, he sat under the gallery of a house in the Rue Colon talking with two friends at 4:30 in the afternoon, when an old man approached to ask for alms.
records.summary_es: El Telegram publica los detalles del asesinato en Moca: el asesino, rodeado por varios cómplices, se acercó al presidente mientras él hablaba con algunos amigos y disparó dos veces con un revólver; la primera bala alcanzó al presidente en el costado izquierdo y le penetró hasta el corazón, causando la muerte instantánea; la segunda bala mató a un anciano que estaba parado cerca del presidente; el asesino y sus cómplices huyeron entonces para evitar los disparos que les hicieron los amigos del presidente, y no se sabe si alguno de ellos fue herido; el cuerpo del presidente fue llevado al palacio del gobernador de Moca; la muerte del presidente Heureaux ha causado un pánico; se dice que un tal Juan Isidoro Jiminez, que tomó parte en la insurrección intentada de junio de 1898, es candidato para la presidencia; se reporta que el general Maximo Gomez, antiguo presidente de los insurrectos cubanos, que es nativo de Santo Domingo, también aspira a la presidencia; y el padre de Caceres, el asesino, fue condenado a muerte por orden del presidente Heureaux en 1881. La otra versión, bajo el título «Another Version of the Affair», dice que habiendo surgido una crisis financiera en Santo Domingo, y temiéndose una insurrección debido al número de descontentos, el presidente Heureaux fue al norte y al oeste de la isla para prepararse para todas las eventualidades; estaba a punto de partir de Moca para Santiago de los Caballeros cuando fue muerto; con botas y espuelas, listo para montar su caballo, estaba sentado bajo la galería de una casa en la Rue Colon hablando con dos amigos a las 4:30 de la tarde, cuando un anciano se acercó a pedir limosna.

records.headline: The Bee completes its assassination items with a report on the political crime
records.summary_en: The Bee completes its assassination items with a report on the political crime and a Puerto Plata item of July 27: the body of President Heureaux has been taken to Santiago de las Caballeros; the president's widow has requested that the body be transported by railway to Puerto Plata and from there to Santo Domingo by sea, but the governor of Santiago fears disorder if the body should be removed from there by train; the governor of Santiago confirms the general opinion that the assassination of President Heureaux was a political crime; it is reported that the assassin's party is gathering forces preparatory to an attack on the government troops; and it has been learned that Cacero's companions when President Heureaux was killed were Juan Pichardo and Horacio Vasquez, the latter a brother of a deputy in Parliament. The Puerto Plata item says President Heureaux, who was assassinated in Moca yesterday afternoon, had gone there to see Jacobo Lara; the president, at the entrance to the city, was fired at by four individuals; enemies of the government are trying to disturb the peace; General Wenceslao Figuereo, who succeeds to the presidency, will continue the plan of retiring paper money; and President Heureaux went to Moca attended by only six persons.

records.headline: The Journal prints the close of an interview, Erwin York's statement
records.summary_en: The Journal prints the close of an interview, Erwin York's statement, and a Fort de France item of July 28: the speaker prophesies that the United States will eventually be compelled to interfere to establish peace in the island, just as this country did in Cuba, declares that he favors the policy of peace and will be glad to return to his country and support such a policy if it is inaugurated by Gen. Figuereo, the vice president, who succeeds to the head of the government, and warns that if something is not quickly done to establish order and peace more revolutionary expeditions will follow, like that of Gen. Jimines and Gen. Morales, who led a band from Cuba against Heureaux. Erwin York, secretary of the Santo Domingo improvement company which controls the country's finances, said: 'Should the new administration attempt to repudiate our contracts we shall certainly, as American citizens, call upon the Washington administration for protection. I do not believe there will be any revolution.' The contract with the improvement company was signed by President Heureaux in 1883; it gives to the company the railroads and the right to collect the customs, and in return for those concessions the company has assumed the national debt of the country, which is principally held by the United States. Under the head 'Murder Was Political,' the Fort de France dispatch says Vice President Figuereo, who assumes the presidential functions acting with the ministers, has informed the widow of President Heureaux that the body of her husband will be interred at Santiago de las Caballeros.

records.headline: The Sun prints the consul general's account of the assassination
records.summary_en: The Sun prints the consul general's account of the assassination news in a New York item: Alejandro Woss y Gil, the consul general of the Dominican Republic in this city, had received no word from his home government directly yesterday confirming the assassination of President Heureaux, but two cablegrams were taken to him by Secretary Erwin D. York of the Santo Domingo Improvement Company; one came from the manager of the Santo Domingo Railroad, dated at Puerto Plata, and read: 'Gen. Heureaux assassinated at Moca Wednesday afternoon. Country quiet'; the other came from the city of Santo Domingo and contained a similar announcement. The consul general said the country was prosperous, with no serious question for the government to settle except the paper issue of the currency, and this he thought would be taken up and disposed of in a satisfactory manner by Vice-President Figuereo, whom he declared to be a very able man. Mr. York, whose company has charge of the collection of the revenue of the Dominican Republic as the representative of foreign bondholders, also expressed confidence in the vice president, who will now become the executive, and thought the death of President Heureaux was not the precursor of revolution: 'The government in Santo Domingo,' he said, 'has been stable for many years now, and I know of no party or faction that has been threatening it.'

records.headline: The Democrat prints a Puerto Plata dispatch of July 28 and the opening of a sketch of Heureaux's career
records.summary_en: The Democrat prints a Puerto Plata dispatch of July 28 and the opening of a sketch of Heureaux's career: President Heureaux, who was assassinated in Moca Wednesday, had gone there to see Jacobo Lara; he was attended by only six persons; the president, at the entrance to the city, was fired at by four individuals; the situation is critical, and enemies of the government are trying to disturb the peace; General Wenceslao Figuereo, the vice president, succeeds to the presidency, and will continue the plan of retiring paper money. Ulises Heureaux was born in 1846 and became president of the Dominican republic in 1886; he ruled with a firm hand, putting down insurrection after insurrection, and shooting the leaders very often without trial; he was immensely wealthy, and his term of office would have expired in October, 1901; he himself had caused reports to be circulated that he had been seized by revolutionists, imprisoned, and subsequently shot, to throw his enemies off their guard, so that they would betray themselves; he was twice exiled for political reasons; and his military career dated from 1862, when he enlisted as a private soldier to assist in driving the Spaniards from his native land, in a war that lasted three years and was followed by the Baez revolution, in which Colonel Heureaux also took a prominent part, conspicuous for his dash and bravery.

records.headline: This article describes Santo Domingo as long disturbed by dissensions and revolutionary movements, naming Juan
records.summary_en: This article describes Santo Domingo as long disturbed by dissensions and revolutionary movements, naming Juan Jiminez, a former merchant of Monte Christi and permanent candidate for the presidency, as one of the chief troublemakers. It recounts how Jiminez in June 1898 organised a filibustering expedition against the Heureaux government and landed at Monte Christi, but failed, his men being killed or captured while he escaped, and how another invasion was hourly expected there in July; it also describes the country's recent acute financial crisis, when the rate of exchange on New York rose more than 100 per cent and a commercial panic followed.
records.summary_es: Este artículo describe a Santo Domingo como perturbado durante mucho tiempo por disensiones y movimientos revolucionarios, y señala a Juan Jiménez, antiguo comerciante de Monte Cristi y candidato permanente a la presidencia, como uno de los principales agitadores. Cuenta cómo Jiménez organizó en junio de 1898 una expedición filibustera contra el gobierno de Heureaux y desembarcó en Monte Cristi, pero fracasó, pues sus hombres fueron muertos o capturados mientras él escapaba, y cómo en julio se esperaba allí otra invasión de un momento a otro; también describe la reciente crisis financiera aguda del país, cuando el tipo de cambio sobre Nueva York subió más del 100 por ciento y siguió un pánico comercial.

But he escaped, and his opponents feared more than ever his smile which he graciously accorded to each one doomed by him to be shot against the "long, brick wall." Santo Domingo has been disturbed by internal dissensions and revolutionary movements for a long period, one of the chief trouble-makers being Juan Jiminez, formerly a prosperous merchant of Monti Christi, and who considers himself a permanent candidate for the presidency, his father having at one time been president of the republic. Jiminez, in June, 1898, organized a filibustering expedition against the Heureaux government, making a successful landing at Monti Christi. The attempt, however, failed, all Jiminez's men being killed or captured. Jiminez himself escaped, and, on July [illegible] last, it was reported that panic reigned at Monti Christi, where another invasion by Jiminez's followers was hourly expected. The country has also recently passed through an acute financial crisis, owing to the peculiar financial system of the country. records.headline: The Globe prints the burial decision for Santiago de los Caballeros
records.summary_en: The Globe prints the burial decision for Santiago de los Caballeros and the governor's precautions: Vice President Figuereo, who assumes the presidential functions acting with the ministers, has informed the widow of President Heureaux that the body of her husband will be interred at Santiago de los Caballeros, and orders for the carrying out of this plan have been given to the governor of Santiago; this course was decided on in order to avoid the excitement and manifestations which would result from the removal of the remains to the city of Santo Domingo. Foreseeing the possibility of disturbances, Gen. Peppin, governor of Santiago, has taken important precautionary measures, and has ordered that arms and ammunition be forwarded to him from Santo Domingo; advices from Santiago received at a late hour say the situation is becoming more serious. The governor of Santiago confirms the general opinion that the assassination of President Heureaux was a political crime; it was reported that the assassin's party are gathering preparatory to an attack upon the government troops; and it has been learned that Cacero's companions when President Heureaux was killed were Juan Picharde and Horacio Vasquez, the latter a brother of a deputy in parliament. President Heureaux's death has caused a panic: one Juan Isidore Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection of June, 1898, is said to be a candidate for the presidency; and Gen. Maximo Gomez, formerly president of the Cuban insurrectionists, who is a native of Santo Domingo, also aspires to the presidency.
records.summary_es: El Globe publica la decisión del entierro para Santiago de los Caballeros y las precauciones del gobernador: el vicepresidente Figuereo, que asume las funciones presidenciales actuando con los ministros, ha informado a la viuda del presidente Heureaux que el cuerpo de su esposo será enterrado en Santiago de los Caballeros, y órdenes para la ejecución de este plan han sido dadas al gobernador de Santiago; este curso fue decidido para evitar la excitación y las manifestaciones que resultarían del traslado de los restos a la ciudad de Santo Domingo. Previendo la posibilidad de disturbios, el gen. Peppin, gobernador de Santiago, ha tomado importantes medidas precautorias, y ha ordenado que armas y municiones le sean enviadas desde Santo Domingo; avisos de Santiago recibidos a última hora dicen que la situación se está volviendo más seria. El gobernador de Santiago confirma la opinión general de que el asesinato del presidente Heureaux fue un crimen político; se reportó que el partido del asesino se está reuniendo en preparación de un ataque a las tropas del gobierno; y se ha sabido que los compañeros de Cacero cuando el presidente Heureaux fue muerto fueron Juan Picharde y Horacio Vasquez, el último hermano de un diputado en el Parlamento. La muerte del presidente Heureaux ha causado un pánico: se dice que un tal Juan Isidore Jiminez, que tomó parte en el intento de insurrección de junio de 1898, es candidato a la presidencia; y el gen. Máximo Gómez, ex presidente de los insurrectos cubanos, que es nativo de Santo Domingo, aspira también a la presidencia.

records.headline: After the assassination of President Heureaux, Vice President Figueroa, who assumes the presidential functions
records.summary_en: After the assassination of President Heureaux, Vice President Figueroa, who assumes the presidential functions, informed the president's widow that the body would be buried at Santiago de los Caballeros rather than taken to Santo Domingo, for fear of hostile manifestations there. Government officials expect an uprising: arms and ammunition have been ordered sent to Santiago, the assassin's party is reported to be gathering to attack the government troops, and the president was shot down at Moca by Ramon Caceres just as he gave alms to an old man who had asked for help.
records.summary_es: Tras el asesinato del presidente Heureaux, el vicepresidente Figueroa, que asume las funciones presidenciales, informó a la viuda del presidente que el cuerpo sería enterrado en Santiago de los Caballeros en vez de ser llevado a Santo Domingo, por temor a manifestaciones hostiles allí. Las autoridades del gobierno esperan un levantamiento: se ha ordenado enviar armas y municiones a Santiago, se informa que el partido del asesino se está reuniendo para atacar a las tropas del gobierno, y el presidente fue derribado a tiros en Moca por Ramón Cáceres justo cuando daba limosna a un anciano que le había pedido ayuda.

FORT DE FRANCE, July 27.—[illegible] financial crisis having arrived in Santo Domingo and an insurrection being feared owing to the number of malcontents, President Heureaux went to the north and west of the island to prepare for all eventualities. He was about to leave Moca for Santiago de los Caballeros when he was killed. Booted and spurred, ready to mount his horse, he sat under the gallery of a house in the Rue Colon, talking to two friends, at 4:30 in the afternoon, when an old man approached to ask for alms. Just as the president gave the old man some money, Caceros, the assassin, rushed forward quickly and fired twice from his revolver. One bullet struck the heart of the president, killing him instantly, and the other killed the old man by his side. The crime was committed so rapidly that the friends of the president were not able to interfere in time to prevent it, but they fired a number of shots at Caceros, who ran away, accompanied by several persons. The assassin's party returned the fire of the president's friends and Caceros escaped. It is not known whether he was wounded or not. The authorities immediately sent troops to pursue him. The body of President Heureaux was taken to the house of the governor of Moca. The news of the president's death spread rapidly and caused much emotion among the inhabitants of the island. records.headline: The Globe completes its dispatch and prints E. D. York's opinion of the murder
records.summary_en: The Globe completes its dispatch and prints E. D. York's opinion of the murder under the head 'Deed of a Fanatic': Vice President Figuero has taken precautions to prevent disorder, and has taken command of the troops to that end, but up to the present all is quiet. E. D. York, secretary of the Santo Domingo Improvement company, who has large interests in Santo Domingo and supported President Heureaux, said in New York on July 27 that the assassination was the act, no doubt, of some fanatical native, who thought he was making a martyr of himself, and that it only illustrates the temper of the race; that Gen. Heureaux, in his opinion, was in every way what President Diaz is to Mexico, and with a firm hand had put the country in a substantial and prosperous condition; that two months ago he was in the interior of the island, and from personal observation never had it experienced such a period of prosperity, with over 100 miles of road in the interior, the sugar and coffee crops the largest known in years, and, while prices are not as high, the exports the highest known; and that the currency question was causing the administration no little uneasiness, the government trying to move from an old silver basis to the modern gold standard, the transition having occasioned no little bitterness and discontent.

records.headline: The Globe prints the McKinley cable of condolence and a Puerto Plata dispatch
records.summary_en: The Globe prints the McKinley cable of condolence and a Puerto Plata dispatch headed 'Situation Critical': official confirmation of President Heureaux's death was communicated to the president at Lake Champlain by the state department, and the following cable message was sent by his direction: 'Lake Champlain, via Washington, July 27. — Excellency, Wenaslao de Figuereo, President of the Dominican Republic, Santo Domingo: In the name of the American people and in my own, I offer to your excellency and the Dominican nation most sincere condolences by reason of the death of President Heureaux. William McKinley.' Wenaslao is the officer next in line to President Heureaux, and succeeds to the office of president. The Puerto Plata dispatch says President Heureaux, who was assassinated in Moca yesterday afternoon, had gone there to see Jacobo Lara; the president, at the entrance to the city, was fired at by four individuals; the body has been brought to Santiago, attended by a government escort and members of the president's family; the situation is critical, and enemies of the government are trying to break the peace; Gen. Wenceslao Figuereo, the vice president, succeeds to the presidency, and will continue the plan of retiring paper money; and President Heureaux went to Moca attended by only six persons.

records.headline: The Journal prints a brief dispatch on the assassination of the Dominican president
records.summary_en: The Journal prints a brief dispatch on the assassination of the Dominican president: Gen. Ulises Heureaux, president of the Dominican Republic, was assassinated at Moca, Santo Domingo, at 4:30 o'clock Wednesday afternoon; several attempts have before been made on the life of Heureaux; the name of the murderer is Ramon Caceros; he succeeded in making his escape, but an energetic pursuit was at once begun, and it is probable that he will soon be captured. The item appears under the head 'The President of San Domingo Assassinated'.

La nota aparece bajo el título «The President of San Domingo Assassinated».

records.headline: The Herald prints an editorial paragraph on the death of President Heureaux
records.summary_en: The Herald prints an editorial paragraph on the death of President Heureaux and the danger of disorder in the West Indies: the death of President Heureaux of the Dominican republic emphasizes, it says, the danger of preserving order among the hotblooded races of the West Indies; assassination in the Spanish-American republics is no uncommon occurrence, preceding and almost invariably following every political revolution, and almost every campaign assumes the seriousness of civil war before an election is reached; but in this particular republic President Heureaux was especially popular and pleasing in his administration of public affairs, and no reason for the murder can be divined except that such acts are an expression of a race characteristic.
records.summary_es: El Herald publica un párrafo editorial sobre la muerte del presidente Heureaux y el peligro de desorden en las Indias Occidentales: la muerte del presidente Heureaux de la República Dominicana enfatiza, dice, el peligro de preservar el orden entre las razas apasionadas de las Indias Occidentales; el asesinato en las repúblicas hispanoamericanas no es una ocurrencia infrecuente, precediendo y casi invariablemente siguiendo a cada revolución política, y casi cada campaña asume la seriedad de una guerra civil antes de que se alcance una elección; pero en esta república en particular el presidente Heureaux era especialmente popular y agradable en su administración de los asuntos públicos, y ninguna razón para el asesinato puede adivinarse excepto que tales actos son una expresión de una característica de la raza.

records.headline: The Journal prints the McKinley cable of condolence and Erwin York's statement
records.summary_en: The Journal prints the McKinley cable of condolence and Erwin York's statement on protection for American debtors: by direction of President McKinley, who is now at Lake Champlain, the following message was sent in his name to Vice-President Wenaslao de Figuereo, who has assumed the reins of government in Santo Domingo: 'In the name of the American people, and in my own, I offer to your excellency and the Dominican nation most sincere condolences by reason of the death of President Heureaux.' Under the head 'American Debtors Will Insist on Protection,' Erwin York, secretary of the Santo Domingo Improvement Company, which controls the country's finances, said yesterday: 'Should the new administration attempt to repudiate our contracts we shall certainly, as American citizens, call upon the Washington administration for protection. I do not believe there will be any revolution.' The contract with the improvement company was signed by President Heureaux in 1863; it gives to the company the railroads and the right to collect the customs, and in return for these concessions the company has assumed the national debt of the country, which is principally held in the United States; and this fact alone, the Journal adds, has generally been considered sufficient for the interference of a power in the affairs of another country when conditions become disturbed.
records.summary_es: El Journal publica el cable de condolencia de McKinley y la declaración de Erwin York sobre protección para los deudores americanos: por dirección del presidente McKinley, que está ahora en Lake Champlain, el siguiente mensaje fue enviado en su nombre al vicepresidente Wenaslao de Figuereo, que ha asumido las riendas del gobierno en Santo Domingo: «En nombre del pueblo americano, y en el mío propio, ofrezco a su excelencia y a la nación dominicana las más sinceras condolencias por razón de la muerte del presidente Heureaux». Bajo el título «American Debtors Will Insist on Protection», Erwin York, secretario de la Santo Domingo Improvement Company, que controla las finanzas del país, dijo ayer: «Si la nueva administración intentara repudiar nuestros contratos ciertamente, como ciudadanos americanos, llamaremos a la administración de Washington para protección. No creo que habrá ninguna revolución». El contrato con la compañía de mejoras fue firmado por el presidente Heureaux en 1863; da a la compañía los ferrocarriles y el derecho de cobrar las aduanas, y en retorno por esas concesiones la compañía ha asumido la deuda nacional del país, que es principalmente poseída en los Estados Unidos; y este hecho solo, añade el Journal, ha sido generalmente considerado suficiente para la interferencia de una potencia en los asuntos de otro país cuando las condiciones se perturban.

records.summary_en: The Journal prints General Moscoso's account of Heureaux's rule and a Puerto Plata dispatch on the assassin's revenge: speaking of General Heureaux, General Moscoso said the assassination ought not to be unexpected by those who have followed the political history of the island; the president of San Domingo was assassinated by the son of a prominent statesman who was himself assassinated in very much the same manner; the assassin had evidently cherished the memory of his father's death, and there was much of revenge in his act; General Heureaux has ruled San Domingo with an iron hand, has killed more than a thousand persons who were opposed to him politically, and put many others in jail; and he drove out more than four hundred prominent persons who were opposed to him from the country, twenty of them now in this country like himself, seventy-five in Cuba, a hundred in Venezuela, and seventy-five in Puerto Rico. Under the head 'President Heureaux Shot for Revenge,' the Puerto Plata dispatch says President Heureaux was killed by the son of a man whom the president had put to death in 1884: the son, Ramon Caceres, vowed revenge for the execution of his father, who was merely suspected of joining in a rebel plot, and has never lost an opportunity to foment insurrection. During the past few weeks there has been much discontent, owing to the financial crisis, and a revolution was feared.
records.summary_es: El Journal publica el relato del general Moscoso sobre el gobierno de Heureaux y un despacho de Puerto Plata sobre la venganza del asesino: hablando del general Heureaux, el general Moscoso dijo que el asesinato no debía ser inesperado por aquellos que han seguido la historia política de la isla; el presidente de Santo Domingo fue asesinado por el hijo de un prominente estadista que fue él mismo asesinado de una manera muy similar; el asesino había evidentemente atesorado la memoria de la muerte de su padre, y hubo mucho de venganza en su acto; el general Heureaux ha gobernado Santo Domingo con mano de hierro, ha matado a más de mil personas que se le oponían políticamente, y puesto a muchas otras en la cárcel; y expulsó del país a más de cuatrocientas personas prominentes que se le oponían, veinte de ellas ahora en este país como él mismo, setenta y cinco en Cuba, cien en Venezuela, y setenta y cinco en Puerto Rico. Bajo el título «President Heureaux Shot for Revenge», el despacho de Puerto Plata dice que el presidente Heureaux fue muerto por el hijo de un hombre a quien el presidente había ejecutado en 1884: el hijo, Ramon Caceres, juró venganza por la ejecución de su padre, que fue meramente sospechado de unirse a un complot rebelde, y nunca ha perdido una oportunidad de fomentar insurrección. Durante las pasadas pocas semanas ha habido mucho descontento, por la crisis financiera, y se temía una revolución.

records.headline: The Journal completes its assassination account: the pursuit
records.summary_en: The Journal completes its assassination account: the pursuit, the conveyance of the body, and the burial decision at Santiago. Pursuit was hurriedly sent after Caceres, but he had a good start and has so far escaped capture; President Heureaux's body was taken to the house of the governor of Moca, and this morning it was conveyed to Santiago de las Caballeros; the president's widow requested that the remains be brought to Puerto Plata by train, and then conveyed to Santo Domingo, the capital, by sea; as soon as the news of the assassination reached the capital, Vice-President Figuereo assumed the presidential functions and issued strict orders to suppress the rebellion that is rapidly fomenting, and disorder is feared in many sections; the new president declined to accede to the request of the widow and notified her that the body of her husband will be interred at Santiago under direction of the governor of that town, a course decided upon in order to avoid the excitement and manifestations that would result from the removal of the body to the capital. Meantime the situation in the country is critical: enemies of the government are trying to disturb the peace; it is reported that the assassin's party are gathering forces preparatory to an attack upon the government troops; and General Pepin, governor of Santiago, says the murder was the result of a political conspiracy, with Caceres, who had a personal desire for revenge, as the assassin, and has asked the government to send him more arms and ammunition.
records.summary_es: El Journal completa su relato del asesinato: la persecución, el traslado del cuerpo, y la decisión del entierro en Santiago. La persecución fue enviada apresuradamente tras Caceres, pero él tenía una buena ventaja y hasta ahora ha escapado de la captura; el cuerpo del presidente Heureaux fue llevado a la casa del gobernador de Moca, y esta mañana fue trasladado a Santiago de los Caballeros; la viuda del presidente solicitó que los restos fueran traídos a Puerto Plata por tren, y luego trasladados a Santo Domingo, la capital, por mar; tan pronto como la noticia del asesinato llegó a la capital, el vicepresidente Figuereo asumió las funciones presidenciales y emitió órdenes estrictas de suprimir la rebelión que se está fomentando rápidamente, y se teme desorden en muchas secciones; el nuevo presidente declinó acceder a la solicitud de la viuda y le notificó que el cuerpo de su esposo será enterrado en Santiago bajo la dirección del gobernador de esa ciudad, un curso decidido para evitar la excitación y las manifestaciones que resultarían del traslado del cuerpo a la capital. Mientras tanto la situación en el país es crítica: enemigos del gobierno están tratando de perturbar la paz; se reporta que el partido del asesino está reuniendo fuerzas en preparación de un ataque a las tropas del gobierno; y el general Pepin, gobernador de Santiago, dice que el asesinato fue el resultado de una conspiración política, con Caceres, que tenía un deseo personal de venganza, como el asesino, y ha pedido al gobierno que le envíe más armas y municiones.

records.headline: Details of Heureaux's assassination at Moca: Ramón Cáceres, whose father Heureaux had put to death in 1884, shot the president
records.summary_en: Details of Heureaux's assassination at Moca: Ramón Cáceres, whose father Heureaux had put to death in 1884, shot the president as he mounted for Santiago; Figuereo succeeds; President McKinley's condolence cable to the Dominican nation.
records.summary_es: Detalles del asesinato de Heureaux en Moca: Ramón Cáceres, cuyo padre fue ejecutado por orden de Heureaux en 1884, disparó contra el presidente cuando montaba para ir a Santiago; Figuereo lo sucede; el cable de condolencia del presidente McKinley a la nación dominicana.
records.passage: ed by several accomplices, approached the President as he was talking with some friends and fired twice with a revolver. The first bullet struck the President in the left side and penetrated the heart, causing instant death. The second bullet killed an old man who was standing near the President. ASSASSIN FLED. The assassin and his accomplices then fled to avoid the shots fired at them by the President's friends. It is not known whether any of the men were wounded. The body of the President was taken to the Palace of the Governor of Moca. President Heureaux's death has caused a panic. It is said that one Juan Isidoro Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection in June, 1898, is candidate for President. It is reported that General Maximo Gomez, former President of the Cuban insurrectionists, who is a native of Santo Domingo, also aspires to the Presidency. The father of Caceres, the assassin, was put to death by order of President Heureaux in 1884. FIRED AT THEM. The crime was committed so rapidly that the friends of the President were not able to interfere in time to prevent it, but they fired a number of shots at Caceres, who ran away accompanied by several persons. The assassin's party returned the fire of the President's party and Caceres escaped. It is not known whether he was wounded or not. The authorities immediately sent troops to pursue him. The Governor of Santiago confirms the general opinion that the assassination of the President was a political crime.

records.headline: The Dispatch prints an editorial squib on the president's name
records.summary_en: The Dispatch prints an editorial squib on the president's name: Heureux means 'happy' in French, it says, yet the lot of the recently assassinated Heureux was not a happy one, though he accumulated much wealth and wielded some power while he was president of the Dominican republic; the Dominicans twisted his 'Heureux' into 'Heureaux,' and to this distortion of what should mean 'happy' is due, the paper suggests, the unhappiness of his career and his end, an explanation the French at least would accept, in view of the suggested violence done to their beautiful language. The squib is headed 'What's in a Name?'.
records.summary_es: El Dispatch publica una nota editorial sobre el nombre del presidente: Heureux significa «feliz» en francés, dice, sin embargo la suerte del recientemente asesinado Heureux no fue una feliz, aunque acumuló mucha riqueza y ejerció algún poder mientras fue presidente de la República Dominicana; los dominicanos torcieron su «Heureux» en «Heureaux», y a esta distorsión de lo que debería significar «feliz» se debe, sugiere el periódico, la infelicidad de su carrera y su fin, una explicación que los franceses al menos aceptarían, en vista de la violencia sugerida hecha a su hermoso idioma. La nota se titula «What's in a Name?».

records.headline: The Spy prints an editorial comment on the report of Heureaux's death
records.summary_en: The Spy prints an editorial comment on the report of Heureaux's death and the caution it was received with: President Heureaux of the Dominican republic has been captured by rebels and put to death more than once, only to return to life after his hidden enemies had exposed themselves and brought about their ruin, and therefore the report of his death was to be received with caution and even incredulity; a man who has been through several revolutions, helped drive the Spaniards from the island, and carried the scars of many wounds, not to mention two unextracted bullets in his body, can have no great fear of death; and Heureaux has ruled despotically and not without cruelty, but on the whole, the paper says, the black republic has been the gainer thereby, for it was a case of dog eat dog whoever held the reins of government.
records.summary_es: El Spy publica un comentario editorial sobre el reporte de la muerte de Heureaux y la cautela con que fue recibido: el presidente Heureaux de la República Dominicana ha sido capturado por rebeldes y ejecutado más de una vez, solo para volver a la vida después de que sus enemigos ocultos se habían expuesto ellos mismos y acarreado su ruina, y por tanto el reporte de su muerte debía ser recibido con cautela y hasta incredulidad; un hombre que ha pasado por varias revoluciones, ayudó a expulsar a los españoles de la isla, y llevó las cicatrices de muchas heridas, sin mencionar dos balas no extraídas en su cuerpo, no puede tener gran temor a la muerte; y Heureaux ha gobernado despóticamente y no sin crueldad, pero en conjunto, dice el periódico, la república negra ha salido ganando con ello, pues era un caso de perro come perro quienquiera que tuviera las riendas del gobierno.

records.headline: The Tribune prints an editorial on the assassination and the standing of the republic
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints an editorial on the assassination and the standing of the republic among nations: there were not a few who, on hearing the news of General Heureaux's assassination, cynically remarked, 'What, another?' as though such tragedies were common in that land; the fact is, however, that it is unique: two of our own Presidents have been murdered, and one of France's; recent years have witnessed the murder of a Russian Czar and an Austrian Empress; there were attempts upon the life of the first German Emperor, and even the Queen of England has not escaped such outrage; but now, for the first time, Santo Domingo mourns a murdered Chief of State, and it is for other nations not to rail at her, but to sympathize. Nor is the little republic thus brought into prominence in other respects a fitting target for our scorn: it has had numerous revolutions, but we think it has fared no worse in that respect than many others, certainly not if we take into account the disabilities under which it has labored — a republic of mixed races, by the side of a negro State and isolated from all others and treated with scorn and selfishness by all its betters, is not a likely candidate for the title of Utopia; nevertheless, this one has of late years been making steady progress, peace has prevailed, and industrial and commercial prosperity has been maintained and increased.

Ni es la pequeña república así traída a la prominencia en otros respectos un blanco apropiado para nuestro desprecio: ha tenido numerosas revoluciones, pero pensamos que no ha salido peor en ese respecto que muchas otras, ciertamente no si tomamos en cuenta las desventajas bajo las cuales ha trabajado — una república de razas mezcladas, al lado de un Estado negro y aislada de todos los demás y tratada con desprecio y egoísmo por todos sus superiores, no es una candidata probable para el título de Utopía; sin embargo, esta ha estado en años recientes haciendo un progreso constante, la paz ha prevalecido, y la prosperidad industrial y comercial ha sido mantenida y aumentada.

records.headline: The News prints the Fort de France details of the assassination
records.summary_en: The News prints the Fort de France details of the assassination and the vice president's precautions: a financial crisis having arisen in Santo Domingo and an insurrection being feared owing to the number of malcontents, President Heureaux went to the north and west of the island to prepare for all eventualities; he was about to leave Moca for Santiago de las Caballeros when he was killed: booted and spurred, ready to mount his horse, he sat under the gallery of a house in the Rue Colon, talking with two friends in the afternoon, when an old man approached and asked for alms, and just as the president gave the man some money, Caceros, the assassin, rushed forward quickly and fired twice with his revolver; the first bullet struck the heart of the president, killing him instantly, and the other killed the old man by his side. The crime was committed so quickly that the friends of the president were not able to interfere in time to prevent it, but they fired a number of shots at Caceros, who ran away, accompanied by several persons; the assassin's party returned the fire of the president's friends, and Caceros escaped; it is not known whether he was wounded or not; and the authorities immediately sent troops to pursue him. The news of the president's death spread rapidly and caused much emotion among the inhabitants of the island; it is believed by many that the murder was the result of a political conspiracy; and Vice President Figuereo has taken precautions to prevent disorder.
records.summary_es: El News publica los detalles de Fort de France sobre el asesinato y las precauciones del vicepresidente: habiendo surgido una crisis financiera en Santo Domingo y temiéndose una insurrección por el número de descontentos, el presidente Heureaux fue al norte y al oeste de la isla a prepararse para todas las eventualidades; estaba a punto de partir de Moca para Santiago de los Caballeros cuando fue muerto: con botas y espuelas, listo para montar su caballo, estaba sentado bajo la galería de una casa en la Rue Colon, hablando con dos amigos en la tarde, cuando un anciano se acercó y pidió limosna, y justo cuando el presidente le dio al hombre algún dinero, Caceros, el asesino, se abalanzó rápidamente y disparó dos veces con su revólver; la primera bala hirió el corazón del presidente, matándolo instantáneamente, y la otra mató al anciano a su lado. records.headline: The News completes its account with the Santiago burial decision
records.summary_en: The News completes its account with the Santiago burial decision, the panic item, the Puerto Plata report, and the opening of the condolence item: the removal of the remains to the city of Santo Domingo would have brought excitement and manifestations, and foreseeing the possibility of disturbances, Gen. Pepin, governor of Santiago, has taken important precautionary measures and has decided to demand that ammunition be forwarded to him from Santo Domingo; advices from Santiago received at a late hour report the situation there is becoming more serious. President Heureaux's death has caused a panic: one Juan Isidoro Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection of June, 1898, is said to be a candidate for President; Gen. Maximo Gomez, formerly president of the Cuban insurrectionists, who is a native of Santo Domingo, aspires to the presidency; and the father of Caceros, the assassin, was put to death by order of President Heureaux in 1884. Under the head 'Situation Is Critical,' a Puerto Plata item of July 27 says the body of President Heureaux has been brought to Santiago, attended by a government escort and members of the late president's family; the situation is critical; enemies of the government are trying to disturb the peace; Gen. Wenceslao Figuereo, the vice president, succeeds to the presidency and will continue the plan of retiring paper money; and President Heureaux went to Moca attended by only six persons. Under the head 'McKinley's Condolence,' a Washington item of July 27 says the State Department received confirmation of the death of the president of Santo Domingo in a despatch from the United States consul at Puerto Plata, 'President Heureaux assassinated,' and the news was communicated to the president at Lake Champlain by the State Department, and a cable message was sent by his direction.
records.summary_es: El News completa su relato con la decisión del entierro en Santiago, la nota del pánico, el reporte de Puerto Plata, y el comienzo de la nota de condolencia: el traslado de los restos a la ciudad de Santo Domingo habría traído excitación y manifestaciones, y previendo la posibilidad de disturbios, el gen. Pepin, gobernador de Santiago, ha tomado importantes medidas precautorias y ha decidido demandar que municiones le sean enviadas desde Santo Domingo; avisos de Santiago recibidos a última hora reportan que la situación ahí se está volviendo más seria. La muerte del presidente Heureaux ha causado un pánico: se dice que un tal Juan Isidoro Jiminez, que tomó parte en el intento de insurrección de junio de 1898, es candidato a la Presidencia; el gen. Máximo Gómez, ex presidente de los insurrectos cubanos, que es nativo de Santo Domingo, aspira a la presidencia; y el padre de Caceros, el asesino, fue ejecutado por orden del presidente Heureaux en 1884. Bajo el título «Situation Is Critical», una nota de Puerto Plata del 27 de julio dice que el cuerpo del presidente Heureaux ha sido traído a Santiago, atendido por una escolta del gobierno y miembros de la familia del difunto presidente; la situación es crítica; enemigos del gobierno están tratando de perturbar la paz; el gen. Wenceslao Figuereo, el vicepresidente, sucede a la presidencia y continuará el plan de retirar el papel moneda; y el presidente Heureaux fue a Moca atendido por solo seis personas. Bajo el título «McKinley's Condolence», una nota de Washington del 27 de julio dice que el Departamento de Estado recibió confirmación de la muerte del presidente de Santo Domingo en un despacho del cónsul de los Estados Unidos en Puerto Plata, «Presidente Heureaux asesinado», y la noticia fue comunicada al presidente en Lake Champlain por el Departamento de Estado, y un mensaje por cable fue enviado por su dirección.

records.headline: The Journal prints the Cape Haytien details of the murder in a dispatch of July 27
records.summary_en: The Journal prints the Cape Haytien details of the murder in a dispatch of July 27: under the head 'It Was a Conspiracy,' details of the murder of President Heureaux, of Santo Domingo, are that he was assassinated as he was about to leave on horseback for Santiago de las Caballeros to take action against a suspected insurrection following a financial crisis in the island; he was about to leave Moca: booted and spurred, ready to mount his horse, he sat under the gallery of a house in the Rue Colon, talking with two friends at 4:30 o'clock in the afternoon, when an old man approached to ask for alms, and just as the president gave the old man some money, Ramon Caceros, the assassin, rushed forward quickly and fired twice from his revolver; one bullet struck the heart of the president, killing him instantly, and the other killed the old man by his side. The crime was committed so quickly that the friends of the president were not able to interfere in time to prevent it, but they fired a number of shots at Caceros, who ran away, accompanied by several persons; the assassin and party returned the fire of the president's friends, and Caceros escaped; it is not known whether he was wounded or not; the authorities immediately sent troops to pursue him, and the body of the president was taken to the house of the governor of Moca; and the news of the president's death spread rapidly and caused a panic among the inhabitants.

records.headline: The New Mexican completes an item on Caceres and prints a Cape Haytien dispatch
records.summary_en: The New Mexican completes an item on Caceres and prints a Cape Haytien dispatch on the funeral: Caceres started on his mission a few weeks ago, leaving Mrs. Caceres behind, and his friends are confident he took precautions to insure his escape. The Cape Haytien dispatch says the funeral of President Heureaux took place at 5 o'clock last evening in Santiago de las Caballeros; the population was panic-stricken, but there was no disorder; a report has been received here that the adversaries of the government attacked Moca last night; the news of the death of President Heureaux was hardly credited by the people generally until last evening, when undoubted confirmation was received; and there was great rejoicing among Dominican exiles, many of whom live around Cape Haytien — exiles driven out of their country by Heureaux, who are preparing to arm and enter Santo Domingo, where they expect their chief, Don Juan Isidoro Jiminez, to join them; and the Dominican government is making preparations on a large scale to maintain itself. Under the head 'Timely Precaution,' the Washington item of July 28 says a naval vessel is to be sent immediately to Santo Domingo on the request of Secretary Hay: the Machias, now at San Juan, Porto Rico, only a day's run from Santo Domingo, will proceed to that island; this is a measure of precaution, rather than a necessity, at present, for Minister Powell has not suggested any such action.
records.summary_es: El New Mexican completa una nota sobre Caceres y publica un despacho de Cabo Haitiano sobre el funeral: Caceres partió en su misión hace unas semanas, dejando atrás a la señora Caceres, y sus amigos confían en que tomó precauciones para asegurar su escape. El despacho de Cabo Haitiano dice que el funeral del presidente Heureaux tuvo lugar a las 5 en punto de anoche en Santiago de los Caballeros; la población estaba aterrada por el pánico, pero no hubo desorden; se ha recibido aquí un reporte de que los adversarios del gobierno atacaron Moca anoche; la noticia de la muerte del presidente Heureaux apenas fue creída por la gente en general hasta anoche, cuando se recibió confirmación indudable; y hubo gran regocijo entre los exiliados dominicanos, muchos de los cuales viven alrededor de Cabo Haitiano — exiliados expulsados de su país por Heureaux, que se están preparando para armarse y entrar en Santo Domingo, donde esperan que su jefe, don Juan Isidoro Jiminez, se les una; y el gobierno dominicano está haciendo preparativos en gran escala para mantenerse. Bajo el título «Timely Precaution», la nota de Washington del 28 de julio dice que un buque naval será enviado inmediatamente a Santo Domingo a solicitud del secretario Hay: el Machias, ahora en San Juan, Puerto Rico, a solo un día de navegación de Santo Domingo, procederá a esa isla; esta es una medida de precaución, más bien que de necesidad, en el presente, pues el ministro Powell no ha sugerido ninguna acción semejante.

records.headline: The Review completes its assassination dispatch and prints a Washington item of July 27
records.summary_en: The Review completes its assassination dispatch and prints a Washington item of July 27 on the official attitude: at present calmness prevails in the republic, and the remains of President Heureaux will probably be taken to Santo Domingo for the funeral services. The Washington item says no information was received last night from the consular representatives of the United States in San Domingo regarding the assassination of President Heureaux, and that pending official advices of the assassination no formal action will be taken by this government: William F. Powell, the minister to Hayti, is also chargé d'affaires to San Domingo, while this government is directly represented in the republic in the person of Campbell Maxwell, who is consul general, and John A. Read, who is vice consul; officials here recall that attempts have heretofore been made on the life of President Heureaux, and Secretary Hay paid a brief tribute to the work of the deceased president, saying he understood that he had given the country a good administration; and Secretary Long said he could not recall that there were any ships of the United States now in San Domingo waters, but that should the developments of the next few days show a feeling of unrest and uncertainty a United States man-of-war will be dispatched to protect American interests.
records.summary_es: El Review completa su despacho del asesinato y publica una nota de Washington del 27 de julio sobre la actitud oficial: en el presente prevalece la calma en la república, y los restos del presidente Heureaux probablemente serán llevados a Santo Domingo para los servicios fúnebres. La nota de Washington dice que anoche no se recibió información de los representantes consulares de los Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo respecto al asesinato del presidente Heureaux, y que, pendientes los avisos oficiales del asesinato, este gobierno no tomará ninguna acción formal: William F. Powell, el ministro en Haití, es también chargé d'affaires en Santo Domingo, mientras este gobierno está directamente representado en la república en la persona de Campbell Maxwell, que es cónsul general, y John A. Read, que es vicecónsul; los funcionarios aquí recuerdan que antes se han hecho atentados contra la vida del presidente Heureaux, y el secretario Hay rindió un breve tributo a la labor del presidente fallecido, diciendo que entendía que él había dado al país una buena administración; y el secretario Long dijo que no podía recordar que hubiera ahora ninguno de los buques de los Estados Unidos en aguas de Santo Domingo, pero que si los acontecimientos de los próximos días mostraran un sentimiento de inquietud e incertidumbre, un buque de guerra de los Estados Unidos será despachado para proteger los intereses americanos.

records.headline: The Silver State prints an editorial sketch of Heureaux's career
records.summary_en: The Silver State prints an editorial sketch of Heureaux's career and character: the sketch, in the paper's editorial voice, traces the development of his character to his ancestry, and says that in a more civilized community he would have become a more or less successful highwayman, while in the West Indies he developed into a patriot, a revolutionary leader, and a President. He commenced his public and military career at the same time, as a common soldier; he soon distinguished himself, for none dispute his bravery, and eventually became a commander; he served with distinction in Santo Domingo's war with Spain, pushing himself to the fore until the dignity of the title of General was his; after the war he kept on pushing himself forward, and in 1882 he was elected President of the Republic; he had, at the time of his death, held that office for seventeen years, having passed through four elections, more dangerous than war, and numerous plots to assassinate, more dangerous than either. The Dominican Republic, the paper says, is scarcely a republic as Americans understand it, nor Heureaux a President made such by popular suffrage: he was, in fact, a little tyrant of a small field, as proud as the queen of all the English, who took upon himself the airs of the greatest of rulers, yet could, when occasion required, assume the ways of the polished man of the world, and none were more courteous and thoughtful than he; and his morals, it adds, were quite as bad as those of the Prince of Wales.
records.summary_es: El Silver State publica una semblanza editorial de la carrera y el carácter de Heureaux: la semblanza, en la voz editorial del periódico, atribuye el desarrollo de su carácter a su ascendencia, y dice que en una comunidad más civilizada él se habría convertido en un salteador de caminos más o menos exitoso, mientras en las Indias Occidentales se desarrolló en un patriota, un líder revolucionario, y un Presidente. Él comenzó su carrera pública y militar al mismo tiempo, como soldado raso; pronto se distinguió, pues nadie disputa su valentía, y eventualmente llegó a ser un comandante; sirvió con distinción en la guerra de Santo Domingo con España, abriéndose paso hasta que la dignidad del título de General fue suya; después de la guerra siguió abriéndose paso hacia adelante, y en 1882 fue elegido Presidente de la República; él había, al tiempo de su muerte, ocupado ese cargo por diecisiete años, habiendo pasado por cuatro elecciones, más peligrosas que la guerra, y numerosos complots para asesinarlo, más peligrosos que cualquiera de las dos. La República Dominicana, dice el periódico, es escasamente una república como los americanos la entienden, ni Heureaux un Presidente hecho tal por el sufragio popular: él era, de hecho, un pequeño tirano de un campo pequeño, tan orgulloso como la reina de todos los ingleses, que tomó sobre sí los aires del más grande de los gobernantes, pero podía, cuando la ocasión lo requería, asumir las maneras del hombre de mundo refinado, y ninguno era más cortés y considerado que él; y su moral, añade, era tan mala como la del Príncipe de Gales.

records.headline: The Democrat prints a Havana item on General Gomez and the succession
records.summary_en: The Democrat prints a Havana item on General Gomez and the succession in Santo Domingo: Gomez will write himself anything he may hereafter have to say to the press — 'I believe all papers lie,' said Gomez, 'and those of one country are in this respect no better than those of another' — and General Gomez refused to discuss the presidency of the Dominican republic, claiming to know nothing regarding the matter. With regard to the rumor that Gomez will be the next president of the republic of Santo Domingo, it is stated here that the most popular candidate is Senor Juan Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection of June, 1898, and who is now in Havana; it is possible, however, so it is reported, that if a revolution takes place Senor Jiminez's opponents will offer Gomez the leadership.
records.summary_es: El Democrat publica una nota de La Habana sobre el general Gómez y la sucesión en Santo Domingo: Gómez escribirá él mismo cualquier cosa que en adelante tenga que decir a la prensa — «Creo que todos los periódicos mienten», dijo Gómez, «y los de un país no son en este respecto mejores que los de otro» — y el general Gómez se negó a discutir la presidencia de la República Dominicana, alegando no saber nada respecto al asunto. Con respecto al rumor de que Gómez será el próximo presidente de la república de Santo Domingo, se afirma aquí que el candidato más popular es el señor Juan Jiminez, que tomó parte en el intento de insurrección de junio de 1898, y que está ahora en La Habana; es posible, sin embargo, según se reporta, que si tiene lugar una revolución, los oponentes del señor Jiminez ofrezcan a Gómez el liderazgo.

records.headline: The Dispatch prints the close of the Cape Haytien exiles item
records.summary_en: The Dispatch prints the close of the Cape Haytien exiles item and a Washington item of July 28 on the warships: the death of President Heureaux was hardly credited by the people generally until last evening, when undoubted confirmation was received, and then there was great rejoicing among the Dominican exiles, many of whom live in and around Cape Haitien; these exiles, who were driven out of their country by Heureaux, are now preparing to arm themselves and enter Santo Domingo, where they expect their chief, Don Juan Isidoro Jiminez, to join them. Under the head 'To Protect American Interests,' the Washington item says Secretary Long to-day issued orders detaching the cruiser New Orleans from the North Atlantic squadron at Newport, and directing her to proceed at once to Santo Domingo city; orders were issued also to the Machias, now at St. Thomas, to proceed to the same point, via San Juan; these orders were made at the instance of the State Department, and as a precautionary measure, owing to the disturbed condition following the assassination of President Heureaux; neither the State nor the Navy Department has received any advices of an alarming character, but owing to the large American interests on the island it was deemed advisable to take every precaution; and it is understood that American capitalists have an arrangement with the Dominican authorities by which practically the entire machinery of the island administration is under their direction.
records.summary_es: El Dispatch publica el cierre de la nota de los exiliados de Cabo Haitiano y una nota de Washington del 28 de julio sobre los buques de guerra: la muerte del presidente Heureaux apenas fue creída por la gente en general hasta anoche, cuando se recibió confirmación indudable, y entonces hubo gran regocijo entre los exiliados dominicanos, muchos de los cuales viven en Cabo Haitiano y sus alrededores; estos exiliados, que fueron expulsados de su país por Heureaux, se están preparando ahora para armarse y entrar en Santo Domingo, donde esperan que su jefe, don Juan Isidoro Jiminez, se les una. Bajo el título «To Protect American Interests», la nota de Washington dice que el secretario Long hoy emitió órdenes separando al crucero New Orleans de la escuadra del Atlántico Norte en Newport, y dirigiéndolo a proceder de inmediato a la ciudad de Santo Domingo; se emitieron órdenes también al Machias, ahora en St. Thomas, de proceder al mismo punto, vía San Juan; estas órdenes se dieron a instancia del Departamento de Estado, y como medida precautoria, por la condición perturbada que siguió al asesinato del presidente Heureaux; ni el Departamento de Estado ni el de Marina han recibido avisos de carácter alarmante, pero por los grandes intereses americanos en la isla se estimó aconsejable tomar toda precaución; y se entiende que los capitalistas americanos tienen un arreglo con las autoridades dominicanas por el cual prácticamente toda la maquinaria de la administración de la isla está bajo su dirección.

records.headline: The Call prints a Washington item on the crisis in Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The Call prints a Washington item on the crisis in Santo Domingo and the foreign interests at stake: the vessels are being sent solely as a precautionary measure; the press dispatches indicate political intrigues which may result in revolution; and, as American interests in the little republic are paramount to those of any other country, it is the part of prudence to have ample force at hand to see that full protection is given to those interests. As to the possibility of annexation as an immediate outcome of the assassination, Secretary Hay and Secretary Long think that it is going too fast to expect such a result and rather discourage this kind of talk; they do not deny, however, that the United States may be forced to serious responsibilities in connection with the future government of San Domingo. While no detailed information has been received regarding the plot which resulted in the assassination of President Heureaux, it is believed to be probable that it was planned and executed by partisans of Jiminez, the revolutionary leader; it is known that Heureaux had lived in fear of assassination for many months, and had frankly announced that he proposed to continue the Presidency as long as he lived. German interests in this republic are considerable, and President Heureaux was strongly backed by them; the future of the republic may depend largely upon the course taken by the foreign element in this crisis, and the course of the German Government in the present crisis will be watched with considerable interest by the American Government.
records.summary_es: El Call publica una nota de Washington sobre la crisis en Santo Domingo y los intereses extranjeros en juego: los buques están siendo enviados únicamente como medida precautoria; los despachos de prensa indican intrigas políticas que pueden resultar en revolución; y, como los intereses americanos en la pequeña república son primordiales frente a los de cualquier otro país, es propio de la prudencia tener amplia fuerza a mano para ver que se dé plena protección a esos intereses. En cuanto a la posibilidad de la anexión como resultado inmediato del asesinato, el secretario Hay y el secretario Long piensan que es ir demasiado rápido esperar tal resultado y más bien desalientan esta clase de conversación; ellos no niegan, sin embargo, que los Estados Unidos puedan verse forzados a serias responsabilidades en conexión con el gobierno futuro de Santo Domingo. Aunque no se ha recibido información detallada respecto al complot que resultó en el asesinato del presidente Heureaux, se cree probable que fue planeado y ejecutado por partidarios de Jiminez, el líder revolucionario; se sabe que Heureaux había vivido en temor de un asesinato por muchos meses, y había anunciado francamente que se proponía continuar la Presidencia mientras viviera. Los intereses alemanes en esta república son considerables, y el presidente Heureaux estaba fuertemente respaldado por ellos; el futuro de la república puede depender en gran medida del curso que tome el elemento extranjero en esta crisis, y el curso del Gobierno alemán en la crisis presente será vigilado con considerable interés por el Gobierno americano.
