records.headline: The Register prints the New York interview with General Moscoso
records.summary_en: The Register prints the New York interview with General Moscoso under the head 'An Exile's Views': Gen. Abelardo A. Moscoso, an exiled leader of the Liberal party of Santo Domingo, now living in New York, said last night: 'The death of President Heureaux will, I think, surely be followed by a long state of disorder and revolution. I want to emphasize this prophecy — that the United States will eventually be compelled to interfere to establish peace in the island, just as this country did in Cuba. I favor the policy of peace. I shall be glad to return to my country and support such a policy if it is inaugurated by Gen. Figuereo, the vice president, who succeeds to the head of the government. But if something is not quickly done to establish order and peace, more revolutionary expeditions will follow, like that of Gen. Jimenez and Gen. Morales, who led a band from Cuba against Heureaux. There are now in this country Gen. Toribio Garcia and Edward Grullon, who share my views. We think that the United States ought to take an interest in our West Indian republic. It will be a great commercial ally. It lies between Cuba and Porto Rico. It must of necessity, I believe, ultimately become attached to this country.' Gen. Moscoso has been an exile in New York for three years; he opposed the late president politically and had to flee to save his life.

records.summary_en: The Eagle completes its Havana item and opens the Moscoso interview under the head 'More Manifest Destiny': in the clubs and cafes Gomez is seriously accused of conspiring to bring both the islands of Hayti and Cuba under the dominion of the United States; on alluding to the cafe conspirators Gomez made use of a contemptuous term which is used among Cubans to signify cowards, and said he did not believe that many men belonging to the army would have anything to do with such people, who, he declared, do not represent Cuba, yet cause much misrepresentation; he also classed a number of papers in the same category. General Gomez's wife and family left Santo Domingo on board the steamer Maria Herrera and are expected to arrive in Havana on Monday next. With regard to the rumor that Gomez will be the next president of the republic of Santo Domingo, it is stated here that the most popular candidate is Senor Juan Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection of June, 1898, and who is now in Havana; it is possible, however, so it is reported, that if a revolution takes place Senor Jiminez's opponents may offer Gomez the leadership; and El Diario de La Marina and La Lucha express the opinion that, considering the present expansion policy, the United States may intervene in San Domingo. The interview with General Abelardo Moscoso, an exiled leader of the liberal party of Santo Domingo, now living in New York, opens with his prophecy that the death of President Heureaux will be followed by a long state of disorder.

La entrevista con el general Abelardo Moscoso, un líder exiliado del partido liberal de Santo Domingo, que vive ahora en Nueva York, abre con su profecía de que la muerte del presidente Heureaux será seguida de un largo estado de desorden.

Snow, the naval commandant of that port. Under the head 'Gomez Aspires to Presidency,' a Tribune special from Washington, dated Chicago, July 28, says that by the assassination of President Heureaux, of Santo Domingo, Cuba may lose one of its central figures, as it is well known Gen. Maximo Gomez aspires to the presidency of the republic. Under the head 'Gomez Refuses to Talk,' a Havana item of July 28 says that with regard to the rumor that Gomez will be the next president of the republic of Santo Domingo, it is stated here that the most popular candidate is Senor Juan Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection of June, 1898, and who is now in Havana; it is possible, however, so it is reported, that if a revolution takes place Senor Jiminez's opponents may offer Gomez the leadership; and Gen. Gomez refused to discuss the presidency of the Dominican republic, claiming to know nothing regarding the matter.

records.headline: The Tribune continues its editorial on the assassination and the standing of the republic
records.summary_en: The Tribune continues its editorial on the assassination and the standing of the republic: President Heureaux had been an eminently popular Chief Magistrate, commanding the support of all parties and credited by all with having secured for the country a stability of government and a general prosperity never known before; and the argument is strengthened by the fact that neither before the murder were there any symptoms of revolution nor have there been any since; Dominicans may not be versed in the highest culture of political revolutionists, but they probably know that a revolution is not to be effected by killing just one man and doing nothing more. There will doubtless be, as indeed there already is, a flocking to the scene of all manner of discontented and ambitious men eager to profit from whatever disturbance of affairs there may be; some professional revolutionists may try to stir up trouble; it is even rumored that General Gomez, having finished his work in Cuba, will make some effort to secure the Dominican Presidency — a rumor which it is difficult to credit. All such attacks upon the established order in Santo Domingo will be deplorable from every point of view, and will especially meet with the reprobation of Americans; in past years individual citizens of this country have more than once contributed to disorder and to revolt in the lands of tropical America, but they have never done so with the sympathy or countenance of the United States Government, and it is to be hoped none will be so unworthy as to join in such movements now.
records.summary_es: El Tribune continúa su editorial sobre el asesinato y la posición de la república: el presidente Heureaux había sido un Magistrado Jefe eminentemente popular, que comandaba el apoyo de todos los partidos y a quien todos acreditaban haber asegurado para el país una estabilidad de gobierno y una prosperidad general nunca conocidas antes; y el argumento se fortalece por el hecho de que ni antes del asesinato hubo síntomas de revolución ni los ha habido desde entonces; los dominicanos pueden no estar versados en la más alta cultura de los revolucionarios políticos, pero probablemente saben que una revolución no se efectúa matando a un solo hombre y no haciendo nada más. Habrá sin duda, como de hecho ya la hay, una afluencia a la escena de toda clase de hombres descontentos y ambiciosos deseosos de aprovechar cualquier perturbación de los asuntos que pueda haber; algunos revolucionarios profesionales pueden tratar de agitar problemas; se rumora incluso que el general Gómez, habiendo terminado su labor en Cuba, hará algún esfuerzo para asegurarse la Presidencia dominicana — un rumor que es difícil de creer. Todos tales ataques sobre el orden establecido en Santo Domingo serán deplorables desde todo punto de vista, y encontrarán especialmente la reprobación de los americanos; en años pasados ciudadanos individuales de este país han contribuido más de una vez al desorden y a la revuelta en las tierras de la América tropical, pero nunca lo han hecho con la simpatía o el consentimiento del Gobierno de los Estados Unidos, y es de esperar que ninguno sea tan indigno como para unirse ahora a tales movimientos.

records.headline: The Free Lance prints an editorial on Heureaux's policy and a sketch of his career
records.summary_en: The Free Lance prints an editorial on Heureaux's policy and a sketch of his career: he hoped that San Domingo might flourish through the aid of foreign capital, and constructed railroads and telegraph lines to develop the resources of the country, but the atmosphere of insurrection and the fear of maladministration kept investors away, and the republic has remained in obscurity save for the recurrence of such tragedies as that now reported; the assassination of the president will be followed by upheavals, as long-suppressed aspirants for power step forward. Under the head 'Career of the Dead President': Heureaux has been called the Napoleon of the south; he was born at Puerto Plata, a town on the north coast of Santo Domingo, in 1846; he became a private soldier in 1862, volunteering in the native service in the uprising against the Spaniards; when the Spaniards left the island Heureaux had risen to the rank of colonel; he was a leader in the various attempts to drive from power Buenaventura Baez, who, in 1867, usurped absolute power in the island; Baez was successful, and Heureaux went into exile; in 1869 he again led the revolt against Baez: Baez's troops, regulars, 1,500 strong, were encamped about eighteen miles from the border line, and Colonel Heureaux had only seventy men, volunteers; after five hours' desperate fighting, the enemy having been surprised, Baez's troops fled — twenty-eight men were killed and eighty wounded, and on Heureaux's side eleven men were killed; and in 1874 the government of Baez ceased and General Gonzales came in.
records.summary_es: El Free Lance publica un editorial sobre la política de Heureaux y una semblanza de su carrera: él esperaba que Santo Domingo pudiera florecer mediante la ayuda del capital extranjero, y construyó ferrocarriles y líneas telegráficas para desarrollar los recursos del país, pero la atmósfera de insurrección y el temor de la mala administración mantuvieron alejados a los inversionistas, y la república ha permanecido en la oscuridad salvo por la recurrencia de tales tragedias como la ahora reportada; el asesinato del presidente será seguido de trastornos, a medida que aspirantes al poder por largo tiempo reprimidos den un paso adelante. Bajo el título «Career of the Dead President»: Heureaux ha sido llamado el Napoleón del sur; nació en Puerto Plata, una ciudad en la costa norte de Santo Domingo, en 1846; llegó a ser soldado raso en 1862, ofreciéndose como voluntario en el servicio nativo en el levantamiento contra los españoles; cuando los españoles salieron de la isla Heureaux había ascendido al rango de coronel; fue un líder en los varios intentos de expulsar del poder a Buenaventura Báez, que, en 1867, usurpó el poder absoluto en la isla; Báez tuvo éxito, y Heureaux se fue al exilio; en 1869 él de nuevo condujo la revuelta contra Báez: las tropas de Báez, regulares, 1,500 fuertes, estaban acampadas a unas dieciocho millas de la línea fronteriza, y el coronel Heureaux tenía solo setenta hombres, voluntarios; después de cinco horas de lucha desesperada, habiendo sido sorprendido el enemigo, las tropas de Báez huyeron — veintiocho hombres fueron muertos y ochenta heridos, y del lado de Heureaux once hombres fueron muertos; y en 1874 el gobierno de Báez cesó y el general Gonzales entró.

records.headline: The Free Lance completes the career sketch and prints the President's cable of condolence
records.summary_en: The Free Lance completes the career sketch and prints the President's cable of condolence: in his adventurous career he received nine serious wounds and carried two bullets in his body. The Secretary of State forwarded the following cable message from the President, dated Lake Champlain, via Washington, D.C., July 27, 1899: 'His Excellency, Wenceslao Figuereo, President of the Dominican Republic, Santo Domingo: In the name of the American people and my own I offer to your excellency and the Dominican nation most sincere condolences by reason of the death of President Heureaux.'
records.summary_es: El Free Lance completa la semblanza de la carrera y publica el cable de condolencia del Presidente: en su aventurera carrera él recibió nueve heridas serias y llevaba dos balas en su cuerpo. El Secretario de Estado remitió el siguiente mensaje por cable del Presidente, fechado en Lake Champlain, vía Washington, D.C., el 27 de julio de 1899: «Su Excelencia, Wenceslao Figuereo, Presidente de la República Dominicana, Santo Domingo: En nombre del pueblo americano y en el mío propio ofrezco a su excelencia y a la nación dominicana las más sinceras condolencias por razón de la muerte del presidente Heureaux».

records.headline: The Times prints two items on the uprising in Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The Times prints two items on the uprising in Santo Domingo and the sailing of the warships: advices received from the Dominican frontier say that the insurgents have cut the telegraph wires in the neighborhood of Santiago de los Caballeros, and also near Moca, and that the insurgents in the western part of San Domingo await the arrival of Don Juan Isidoro Jiminez, under whose leadership they expect to attack Santiago. Under the head 'Ships for San Domingo,' Captain Taylor, commanding the North Atlantic Squadron, telegraphed the Navy Department today that the cruiser New Orleans would be ready to sail from Newport for Santo Domingo city this afternoon; word came also from Commander Logan, of the gunboat Machias, that this vessel would get away from St. Thomas, Danish West Indies, on Sunday, and will go first to San Juan, Porto Rico — this will be good news, as the Navy Department believed that the Machias would not be ready for sea service for several days, Commander Logan having telegraphed on Thursday that she would be obliged to remain at St. Thomas for nine days while repairs were being made.
records.summary_es: El Times publica dos notas sobre el levantamiento en Santo Domingo y la partida de los buques de guerra: avisos recibidos de la frontera dominicana dicen que los insurgentes han cortado los cables telegráficos en el vecindario de Santiago de los Caballeros, y también cerca de Moca, y que los insurgentes en la parte occidental de Santo Domingo esperan la llegada de don Juan Isidoro Jiminez, bajo cuyo liderazgo esperan atacar Santiago. Bajo el título «Ships for San Domingo», el capitán Taylor, comandante de la Escuadra del Atlántico Norte, telegrafió hoy al Departamento de Marina que el crucero New Orleans estaría listo para partir de Newport para la ciudad de Santo Domingo esta tarde; vino palabra también del comandante Logan, de la cañonera Machias, de que este buque saldría de St. Thomas, Indias Occidentales Danesas, el domingo, e irá primero a San Juan, Puerto Rico — esto será buena noticia, pues el Departamento de Marina creía que el Machias no estaría listo para el servicio marítimo por varios días, habiendo telegrafiado el comandante Logan el jueves que él estaría obligado a permanecer en St. Thomas por nueve días mientras se hacían reparaciones.

records.headline: The Argus completes its Havana item and prints the Moscoso interview
records.summary_en: The Argus completes its Havana item and prints the Moscoso interview under the head 'Annexation to Uncle Sam': with regard to the rumor that Gomez will be the next president of the republic of Santo Domingo, it is stated here that the most popular candidate is Senor Juan Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection of June, 1898, and who is now in Havana; it is possible, however, so it is reported, that if a revolution takes place Senor Jiminez's opponents may offer Gomez the leadership; and El Diario de la Marina and La Lucha express the opinion that, considering the present expansion policy, the United States may intervene in San Domingo. The New York item of July 29 prints General Abelardo A. Moscoso, an exiled leader of the liberal party of Santo Domingo, now living in New York, who said Thursday night: 'The death of President Heureaux will, I think, surely be followed by disorder and revolution. I want to emphasize this prophecy that the United States will eventually be compelled to interfere to establish peace in the island, just as this country did in Cuba. If San Domingo must of necessity, I believe, ultimately become attached to this country.' General Moscoso has been an exile in New York for three years; he opposed the late president politically and had to flee to save his life.

records.headline: The Globe completes its Havana item, prints the warships item
records.summary_en: The Globe completes its Havana item, prints the warships item, and opens the Moscoso interview: the Havana papers express the opinion that, considering the present expansion policy, the United States may intervene in San Domingo. Under the head 'Warships Dispatched,' a Washington item of July 28 says Secretary Long this afternoon sent telegraphic orders to the cruiser New Orleans at Newport directing that she proceed at once to San Domingo, and at the same time an order was sent to the gunboat Machias, at St. Thomas, to leave for San Domingo; it is expected that the New Orleans will be able to leave today, and the Machias will be in San Domingo waters within a day or two; and this action was not due to the receipt of any official advices indicating possible trouble, but entirely to the desire to be beforehand in dealing with any possible disturbance. Under the head 'More Trouble,' the Moscoso interview opens: Gen. Abelardo A. Moscoso, an exiled leader of the Liberal party of Santo Domingo, now living in New York, said last night that the death of President Heureaux will, he thinks, surely be followed by a long state of disorder and revolution, and wants to emphasize his prophecy that the United States will eventually be compelled to interfere to establish peace.
records.summary_es: El Globe completa su nota de La Habana, publica la nota de los buques de guerra, y abre la entrevista de Moscoso: los periódicos habaneros expresan la opinión de que, considerando la presente política de expansión, los Estados Unidos pueden intervenir en Santo Domingo. Bajo el título «More Trouble», la entrevista de Moscoso abre: el gen. Abelardo A. Moscoso, un líder exiliado del partido Liberal de Santo Domingo, que vive ahora en Nueva York, dijo anoche que la muerte del presidente Heureaux será, según él piensa, seguramente seguida de un largo estado de desorden y revolución, y quiere enfatizar su profecía de que los Estados Unidos serán eventualmente obligados a intervenir para establecer la paz.

records.headline: The Globe prints the plot item and completes its exile interview
records.summary_en: The Globe prints the plot item and completes its exile interview: if order and peace are not established, more revolutionary expeditions will follow that of Gen. Jiminez and Gen. Morales, who led a band from Cuba against Heureaux; advices from Santo Domingo to a Dominican here describe the existence of a well-planned and widespread plot by adherents of Jiminez to depose President Heureaux, which, it was thought, was sure to succeed; the assassination of President Heureaux is regarded here as an indication of the success of the plot; the city of Santo Domingo, it is reported, is in a state of great unrest and business is entirely suspended; the people fear an outbreak; last night a band of armed men attacked Moca, where President Heureaux was killed, and fired a number of shots; it is reported that the forces supporting the assassins have been augmented considerably; and the government has taken measures to put down the threatened insurrection.
records.summary_es: El Globe publica la nota del complot y completa su entrevista del exiliado: si el orden y la paz no se establecen, seguirán más expediciones revolucionarias como la del gen. Jiminez y el gen. records.headline: The Times completes the plot item and prints two dispatches
records.summary_en: The Times completes the plot item and prints two dispatches and the opening of the Plattsburg item: the government has taken measures to put down the threatened insurrection. A Cape Haytien dispatch of July 29 says the news of the death of President Heureaux was hardly credited there by the people generally until last evening, when undoubted confirmation was received; then there was great rejoicing among the Dominican exiles, many of whom live in and around Cape Haytien — exiles who were driven out of their country by Heureaux and are now preparing to arm themselves and enter Santo Domingo, where they expect their chief, Don Juan Isidoro Jiminez, to join them. A Port au Prince item of July 28 says William F. Powell, United States minister to Hayti and diplomatic representative to the Republic of Santo Domingo, has sent a telegram to Vice-President Figuereo, who has assumed the presidency, expressing the keen regret of the United States government at the assassination of President Heureaux; and the latest news from Santo Domingo is that all is quiet throughout the territory of the republic. Under the head 'Figuereo's Thanks,' the Plattsburg item opens with the President's receipt of Figuereo's dispatch in reply to his message of condolence sent yesterday.
records.summary_es: El Times completa la nota del complot y publica dos despachos y la apertura de la nota de Plattsburgh: el gobierno ha tomado medidas para sofocar la insurrección amenazada. Un despacho de Cabo Haitiano del 29 de julio dice que la noticia de la muerte del presidente Heureaux apenas fue creída allí por la gente en general hasta anoche, cuando se recibió confirmación indudable; entonces hubo gran regocijo entre los exiliados dominicanos, muchos de los cuales viven en Cabo Haitiano y sus alrededores — exiliados que fueron expulsados de su país por Heureaux y que ahora se están preparando para armarse y entrar en Santo Domingo, donde esperan que su jefe, don Juan Isidoro Jiminez, se les una. Una nota de Port au Prince del 28 de julio dice que William F. Powell, ministro de los Estados Unidos en Haití y representante diplomático ante la República de Santo Domingo, ha enviado un telegrama al vicepresidente Figuereo, que ha asumido la presidencia, expresando la profunda pena del gobierno de los Estados Unidos por el asesinato del presidente Heureaux; y que las últimas noticias de Santo Domingo son que todo está quieto en todo el territorio de la república. Bajo el título «Figuereo's Thanks», la nota de Plattsburgh abre con la recepción por el Presidente del despacho de Figuereo en respuesta a su mensaje de condolencia enviado ayer.

records.summary_en: After the killing of President Heureaux at Moca, the government decreed nine days of national mourning, flags were at half-mast, and Santo Domingo City was in great unrest with business entirely suspended and people fearing an outbreak. records.headline: The State Journal completes its Havana item on General Gomez
records.summary_en: The State Journal completes its Havana item on General Gomez and the succession in Santo Domingo: Gen. Gomez refused to discuss the presidency of the Dominican republic, claiming to know nothing regarding the matter; when questioned concerning the rumors circulating in the cafes as to his aspirations regarding a Dominican republic, Gomez's action proved his contempt for the stories, yet in the clubs and cafes he is seriously accused of conspiring to bring both the island of Hayti and Cuba under the dominion of the United States; in alluding to the cafe conspirators Gomez made use of a contemptuous term which is used among Cubans to signify cowards, and said he did not believe that many men belonging to the army would have anything to do with such people, who, he declared, do not represent Cuba, yet cause much misrepresentation; and he also classed a number of papers in the same category. General Gomez's wife and family left Santo Domingo on board the steamer Maria Herrera and are expected to arrive in Havana on Monday next; and with regard to the rumor that Gomez will be the next president of the republic of Santo Domingo, it is stated here that the most popular candidate is Senor Juan Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection of June, 1898, and who is now in Havana; it is possible, however, so it is reported, that if a revolution takes place Senor Jiminez's opponents may offer Gomez the leadership; and El Diario de La Marina and La Lucha express the opinion that, considering the present expansion policy, the United States may intervene in San Domingo.

La esposa y la familia del general Gómez salieron de Santo Domingo a bordo del vapor Maria Herrera y se espera que lleguen a La Habana el próximo lunes; y con respecto al rumor de que Gómez será el próximo presidente de la república de Santo Domingo, se afirma aquí que el candidato más popular es el señor Juan Jiminez, que tomó parte en el intento de insurrección de junio de 1898, y que está ahora en La Habana; es posible, sin embargo, según se reporta, que si tiene lugar una revolución, los oponentes del señor Jiminez ofrezcan a Gómez el liderazgo; y El Diario de La Marina y La Lucha expresan la opinión de que, considerando la presente política de expansión, los Estados Unidos pueden intervenir en San Domingo.

records.headline: The Leader prints the Washington warships item and a Chicago item
records.summary_en: The Leader prints the Washington warships item and a Chicago item on General Gomez under the head 'Gomez May Go Home': Secretary Long has sent telegraphic orders to the cruiser New Orleans, at Newport, directing that she proceed at once to San Domingo, and at the same time an order was sent to the gunboat Machias, at St. Thomas, to leave for San Domingo; it is expected that the New Orleans will be able to leave during the day, and the Machias will be in San Domingo waters within a day or two; and this action was not due to the receipt of any official advices indicating possible trouble, but entirely to the desire to be beforehand in dealing with any possible disturbance. The Chicago item, a Tribune special from Washington of July 29, says that by the assassination of President Heureaux, of San Domingo, Cuba may lose one of its central figures, as it is well known General Maximo Gomez aspires to the presidency of the republic; this bar will not confront General Gomez in San Domingo, as he was born on that island and his family still reside there; some time ago, General Gomez issued a manifesto to the Cuban army, in which he bade his soldiers good bye and signified his intention to return to San Domingo, his native land; and as Gomez's love for adventure and fighting for what he calls liberty are well known, it is believed he will start for San Domingo at once, organize an army, and endeavor to fight his way to the presidency.
records.summary_es: El Leader publica la nota de Washington de los buques de guerra y una nota de Chicago sobre el general Gómez bajo el título «Gomez May Go Home»: el secretario Long ha enviado órdenes telegráficas al crucero New Orleans, en Newport, dirigiéndolo a proceder de inmediato a San Domingo, y al mismo tiempo se envió una orden a la cañonera Machias, en St. Thomas, de partir para San Domingo; se espera que el New Orleans pueda partir durante el día, y el Machias estará en aguas de San Domingo dentro de un día o dos; y esta acción no se debió a la recepción de ningún aviso oficial que indicara posible problema, sino enteramente al deseo de estar prevenidos al tratar con cualquier posible disturbio. La esposa y la familia del general Gómez salieron de Santo Domingo a bordo del vapor Maria Herrera, y se espera que lleguen a La Habana el próximo lunes; con respecto al rumor de que Gómez será el próximo presidente de la República de Santo Domingo, se afirma aquí que el candidato más popular es Jiminez, que tomó parte en el intento de insurrección de junio de 1898, y que está ahora en La Habana; es posible, sin embargo, según se reporta, que si tiene lugar una revolución, los oponentes del señor Jiminez ofrezcan a Gómez el liderazgo; y «El Diario de la Marina» y «La Lucha» expresan la opinión de que, considerando la presente política de expansión, el Gobierno de los Estados Unidos puede intervenir en Santo Domingo. records.summary_en: The Journal and Courier prints a Plattsburgh item with President Figuereo's reply to the President's message of condolence: 'San Domingo, via Hayti, July 27, 1899. To His Excellency, the President of the United States: In the name of the Dominican republic, and in my own, I hurry to present to your excellency the testimony of our most fervent gratitude for your condolence on account of the death of President Heureaux. W. Figuereo.' Among those who called on the President to-day were Colonel Rice and Lieutenant Colonel Duvall, of the Twenty-sixth Volunteer Regiment at Plattsburgh, Hon. Smith M. Weed and Henry W. Cannon, president of the Fourth National Bank of New York City; the President has been deluged with invitations from the surrounding places, but owing to Mrs. McKinley's health he has been compelled to decline all invitations, and will accept no invitations that will take him away from Mrs. McKinley even for a day; and on Sunday the President and Miss Duncan, accompanied by Dr. and Mrs. Rixey, will attend divine worship at the First Methodist Church of Plattsburgh, if Mrs. McKinley continues to improve.

records.headline: The Press completes a naval item and prints a Cape Haytien dispatch
records.summary_en: The Press completes a naval item and prints a Cape Haytien dispatch on the insurgents in Santo Domingo: the vessel is on the way to Porto Rico, to land Commander Snow, who is to take charge of the naval station there, and the commander of the New Orleans also announced his readiness to start for San Domingo to-day, so that before the middle of next week the American navy will be sufficiently represented in San Domingo to protect American interests of all kinds should there be a revolution. The Cape Haytien dispatch of July 29 says advices just received from the Dominican frontier say that the insurgents have cut the telegraph wires in the neighborhood of Santiago de los Caballeros, and near Moca, and that the insurgents in the western part of San Domingo await the arrival of Don Juan Isidoro Jiminez, under whose leadership they intend to attack Santiago.

records.headline: The Times prints a Havana item on the choice of a successor
records.summary_en: The Times prints a Havana item on the choice of a successor to President Heureaux: there is a good deal of agitation in the Havana press regarding the selection of Gen. Maximo Gomez or Gen. Juan Antonio Jiminez as President of the Republic of Santo Domingo, to succeed General Heureaux, who was assassinated the other day. General Gomez has said that he would not go to Santo Domingo in any event, his only ambition and mission in life being to see an independent Cuban Republic; and General Jiminez, whose father was at one time President of the Dominican Republic, is now living in Havana, and his business here is not of a character to interfere with his candidacy.

records.headline: The Call completes a Washington item on the foreign navies and the errand of the men-of-war
records.summary_en: The Call completes a Washington item on the foreign navies and the errand of the men-of-war: there is no foreign man-of-war in these waters to protect its citizens in the event of a revolution, the absence of such vessels being taken as an indication that other countries are satisfied to depend upon the United States to look after foreign interests in case of an uprising; Germany, the correspondent is told, has not a single man-of-war on this station, her North Atlantic squadron having recently been withdrawn to participate in the autumn maneuvers at Kiel; it was stated that a vessel was to be sent to Guatemala to demand the payment of debts due to certain German subjects, but the Navy Department has not been informed of her departure. The only possible fear of any undue interference in affairs in San Domingo has been from Germany: it is known that she has some interests there, and it has been stated that some of the German residents are in sympathy with Jiminez, who is said to be heading a movement antagonistic to the legitimate successor of Heureaux; while, keeping a careful watch that there is no foreign interference, the immediate work of the two men-of-war to be sent to San Domingo will be to protect American citizens, and if necessary marines will be landed to protect the American consulate and American property; the moral effect of the presence of these ships will, the authorities hope, be sufficient to put a damper on any revolutionary movements; and Secretary Long said to-day that he expected the Machias would reach San Domingo city by Monday, her repairs having been expedited so that she will be able to sail from St. Thomas to-morrow evening.
records.summary_es: El Call completa una nota de Washington sobre las marinas extranjeras y la misión de los buques de guerra: no hay ningún buque de guerra extranjero en estas aguas para proteger a sus ciudadanos en el evento de una revolución, tomándose la ausencia de tales buques como una indicación de que otros países están satisfechos de depender de los Estados Unidos para cuidar los intereses extranjeros en caso de un levantamiento; Alemania, según se dice al corresponsal, no tiene un solo buque de guerra en esta estación, habiendo sido retirada recientemente su escuadra del Atlántico Norte para participar en las maniobras de otoño en Kiel; se afirmó que un buque iba a ser enviado a Guatemala a demandar el pago de deudas debidas a ciertos súbditos alemanes, pero el Departamento de Marina no ha sido informado de su partida. El único posible temor de cualquier interferencia indebida en los asuntos en San Domingo ha sido de Alemania: se sabe que ella tiene algunos intereses allí, y se ha afirmado que algunos de los residentes alemanes simpatizan con Jiminez, de quien se dice que encabeza un movimiento antagónico al sucesor legítimo de Heureaux; mientras, manteniendo una vigilancia cuidadosa de que no haya interferencia extranjera, la labor inmediata de los dos buques de guerra que serán enviados a San Domingo será proteger a los ciudadanos americanos, y si fuera necesario se desembarcarán infantes de marina para proteger el consulado americano y la propiedad americana; el efecto moral de la presencia de estos buques será, esperan las autoridades, suficiente para poner un freno a cualquier movimiento revolucionario; y el secretario Long dijo hoy que esperaba que el Machias llegaría a la ciudad de San Domingo para el lunes, habiéndose acelerado sus reparaciones para que pueda partir de St. Thomas mañana por la noche.

records.headline: The Call prints the Port de France dispatch of July 29 on Monte Cristi
records.summary_en: The Call prints the Port de France dispatch of July 29 on Monte Cristi and Moca: tranquility prevails at Monte Cristi, but all the people are anxiously awaiting the important events which it is expected will occur shortly; General Pichardo, the governor of the city, has taken all possible measures to repel any attack which may be made by the followers of Senor Juan Jiminez, one of the candidates for the presidency of the republic; it is said that General Pichardo has advised the Government to issue a decree proclaiming amnesty for all Dominican exiles, with a view to appeasing the people; at La Vega General Don Pedro Bobea has taken steps to suppress outbreaks should any occur; up to the present time perfect order has been maintained, but notwithstanding that fact all law-abiding citizens have been called upon to bear arms and hold themselves in immediate readiness for service; and at Moca, where the people criticize harshly the laxity of the governor, General Juan Gonzales, many versions are in circulation regarding the killing of the President — one has it that the assassin shot him with the muzzle of the weapon held close to Heureaux's body.
records.summary_es: El Call publica el despacho de Port de France del 29 de julio sobre Monte Cristi y Moca: prevalece la tranquilidad en Monte Cristi, pero todo el pueblo espera ansiosamente los importantes eventos que se espera ocurrirán en breve; el general Pichardo, gobernador de la ciudad, ha tomado todas las medidas posibles para repeler cualquier ataque que pueda ser hecho por los seguidores del señor Juan Jiminez, uno de los candidatos a la presidencia de la república; se dice que el general Pichardo ha aconsejado al Gobierno emitir un decreto proclamando amnistía para todos los exiliados dominicanos, con miras a apaciguar al pueblo; en La Vega el general don Pedro Bobea ha tomado pasos para suprimir estallidos si alguno ocurriera; hasta el presente momento se ha mantenido un orden perfecto, pero no obstante ese hecho todos los ciudadanos respetuosos de la ley han sido llamados a tomar las armas y mantenerse en disposición inmediata para el servicio; y en Moca, donde el pueblo critica duramente la laxitud del gobernador, el general Juan Gonzales, circulan muchas versiones respecto a la muerte del Presidente — una sostiene que el asesino le disparó con la boca del arma pegada al cuerpo de Heureaux.

records.headline: The Republican completes the uprising item and prints two Washington items of July 29
records.summary_en: The Republican completes the uprising item and prints two Washington items of July 29 on the sailing of the warships: the insurgents in the western part of Santo Domingo await the arrival of Don Juan Isidoro Jiminez, under whose leadership they expect to attack Santiago. Under the head 'To Protect Americans,' the first item says a cablegram has been received at the Navy Department from the commander of the Machias, now at St. Thomas, W. I., stating that he would sail to-morrow for San Domingo, and that the commander of the New Orleans also announced his readiness to start for San Domingo to-day, so that before the middle of next week the American navy will be sufficiently represented in San Domingo to protect American interests should there be a revolution. Under the head 'Nothing Officially Heard,' the second item says the Navy Department had not heard up to the close of office hours this morning of the sailing of the New Orleans for Santo Domingo, and that there were no dispatches indicating cause for alarm over the situation in the island.

records.headline: The Tribune prints the views of Charles W. Wells on the situation
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints the views of Charles W. Wells on the situation in the republic: the Santo Domingo Improvement Company, of this city, whose offices are in the Empire Building, own the railroad system in the republic, and are trustees for the Government bonds, as security for which they have charge of the collection of the revenues of the country. Mr. Wells, president of the company, has often visited in Santo Domingo; he returned from there about a month ago, after having spent several weeks with President Heureaux and other State officials, and was to have met the President in August; he is thoroughly familiar with the political, social and industrial condition of the republic, and, having large interests at stake himself, his views on the situation should be of comfort to other foreigners who hold Dominican securities: 'I am not in the least worried about Santo Domingo. To be sure, the republic has lost an able man and a good President by the death of Senor Heureaux, but one man does not make or even hold together a nation. In the United States it seems to be the prevailing opinion that the inhabitants of Santo Domingo are a lot of ignorant, uneducated savages. On the other hand, they are, as a whole, well bred, intelligent and refined. They devote a great deal of attention to education. Fathers whose means will permit of it educate their children.'

records.headline: The Dispatch prints the Havana item on General Gomez and the succession
records.summary_en: The Dispatch prints the Havana item on General Gomez and the succession in Santo Domingo: 'I believe all papers lie,' said Gomez, 'and those of one country are in this respect no better than those of another; in the future I will give over my own signature, or through the Associated Press alone, anything I may have to say to the press.' General Gomez refused to discuss the presidency of the Dominican republic, claiming to know nothing regarding the matter; when questioned concerning the rumors circulating in the cafes as to his aspirations regarding the presidency of the Dominican republic, his action proved his contempt for the stories, yet in the clubs and cafe he is seriously accused of conspiracy to bring both the island of Haiti and Cuba under the dominion of the United States. With regard to the rumor that Gomez will be the next President of the republic of Santo Domingo, it is stated here that the most popular candidate is Senor Juan Jiminez, who took part in the attempted insurrection of June, 1898, and who is now in Habana; it is possible, however, so it is reported, that if a revolution takes place Senor Jiminez's opponents may offer Gomez the leadership.

records.headline: The Leader completes the Havana papers item, then prints the Moscoso interview
records.summary_en: The Leader completes the Havana papers item, then prints the Moscoso interview and the Cape Haytien wires item: considering the present expansion policy, the United States may intervene in San Domingo. Under the head 'More Trouble Feared,' a New York item of July 31 prints General Abelardo A. Moscoso, an exiled leader of the Liberal party of Santo Domingo, now living in New York: 'The death of President Heureaux will, I think, surely be followed by a long state of disorder and revolution. I want to emphasize this prophecy — that the United States will eventually be compelled to interfere to establish peace in the island, just as this country did in Cuba. I favor the policy of peace. I shall be glad to return to my country and support such a policy if it is inaugurated by General Figuereo, the vice president, who succeeds to the head of the government. But if something is not quickly done to establish order and peace, more revolutionary expeditions will follow that of General Jiminez and General Morales, who led a band from Cuba against Heureaux.' Under the head 'Telegraph Wires Cut,' the Cape Haytien dispatch says advices just received from the Dominican frontier say the insurgents have cut the telegraph wires in the neighborhood of Santiago de los Caballeros and also near Moca, and that the insurgents in the western part of Santo Domingo await the arrival of Don Juan Isidoro Jiminez, under whose leadership they expect to attack Santiago.
records.summary_es: El Leader completa la nota de los periódicos habaneros, luego publica la entrevista de Moscoso y la nota de los cables de Cabo Haitiano: considerando la presente política de expansión, los Estados Unidos pueden intervenir en San Domingo. records.headline: The State Journal prints an editorial on the assassination of the president of San Domingo
records.summary_en: The State Journal prints an editorial on the assassination of the president of San Domingo and the republic's future. In the paper's own voice it argues that when the islands become parts of the great republic, revolutions and assassinations will cease, calling such responsibilities a part of the burden that must be shouldered some time whether we wish it or not. The president of San Domingo who was assassinated last week, the paper says, was serving his fourth term in the presidency, having been first chosen to that office in 1886; the Dominican republic occupies the larger part of the eastern end of the island of Hayti; it has a population of about 425,000; was organized in 1844, and its constitution was readopted in 1865 when the Spanish left the island; its government is complicated — besides the president and vice president, the president's cabinet, and a legislative body of twenty-two members, each province and district, parish and town has its distinctive officers; and having a republican form of government already in operation, it could fall into place as a state of the American union much more readily perhaps than could Cuba or Porto Rico.
records.summary_es: El State Journal publica un editorial sobre el asesinato del presidente de San Domingo y el futuro de la república. En su propia voz argumenta que cuando las islas lleguen a ser partes de la gran república, las revoluciones y los asesinatos cesarán, llamando tales responsabilidades una parte de la carga que debe ser asumida algún día lo deseemos o no. El presidente de San Domingo que fue asesinado la semana pasada, dice el periódico, estaba sirviendo su cuarto término en la presidencia, habiendo sido elegido por primera vez a ese cargo en 1886; la República Dominicana ocupa la mayor parte del extremo oriental de la isla de Hayti; tiene una población de cerca de 425,000; fue organizada en 1844, y su constitución fue readoptada en 1865 cuando los españoles salieron de la isla; su gobierno es complicado — además del presidente y el vicepresidente, el gabinete del presidente, y un cuerpo legislativo de veintidós miembros, cada provincia y distrito, parroquia y pueblo tiene sus funcionarios distintivos; y teniendo ya en operación una forma republicana de gobierno, podría caer en su lugar como un estado de la unión americana mucho más fácilmente quizás que Cuba o Puerto Rico.

records.headline: The News prints the Fort de France assassination dispatch of July 27
records.summary_en: The News prints the Fort de France assassination dispatch of July 27: Gen. Ulises Heureaux, president of the Dominican Republic, was assassinated last evening at Moca; the name of the murderer is Ramon Caceros, and he succeeded in making his escape, but an energetic pursuit was at once begun, and it is probable that he will soon be captured; the vice-president, General Wenceslao Figuereo, immediately upon the announcement of the president's death assumed direction of affairs; at present calmness prevails everywhere in the republic; and the remains of Heureaux will probably be taken to Santo Domingo for funeral services. Gen. Ulises Heureaux, the paper adds, had been president of the Dominican republic since Sept. 1, 1886.
records.summary_es: El News publica el despacho del asesinato de Fort de France del 27 de julio: el gen. Ulises Heureaux, presidente de la República Dominicana, fue asesinado anoche en Moca; el nombre del asesino es Ramón Caceros, y logró escapar, pero se inició de inmediato una persecución enérgica y es probable que pronto sea capturado; el vicepresidente, general Wenceslao Figuereo, inmediatamente después del anuncio de la muerte del presidente asumió la dirección de los asuntos; en el presente prevalece la calma en todas partes de la república; y los restos de Heureaux probablemente serán llevados a Santo Domingo para los servicios fúnebres. El gen. Ulises Heureaux, añade el periódico, había sido presidente de la República Dominicana desde el 1 de septiembre de 1886.

records.headline: The Intelligencer prints an editorial on the three serious possibilities
records.summary_en: The Intelligencer prints an editorial on the three serious possibilities which directly concern Americans in San Domingo: the first is the extent of American investments on the island; the second reason is the approximation of the interests of the people of the Dominican republic to our own, both in a material and sentimental way, it being regarded that in no other of the islands of the West Indies, with the exception of Cuba and Porto Rico, is the confidence so strong in the United States, and this country has been looked to rather than any other country for good favor when needed; and the Sun and other papers commenting on the situation, as well as naval and military officers, point out the new political and strategic relations proceeding from our possession of Porto Rico on one side and our occupation of Cuba on the other. These are logical arguments for the exercise of watchfulness on the part of our government; and in view of the fact that the death of Heureaux is followed by disorder and insurrection, naval vessels to protect our interests will be necessary for the waters of San Domingo — in all probability this course will be taken, for the matter is too serious to be ignored.
records.summary_es: El Intelligencer publica un editorial sobre las tres serias posibilidades que conciernen directamente a los americanos en San Domingo: la primera es la extensión de las inversiones americanas en la isla; la segunda razón es la aproximación de los intereses del pueblo de la República Dominicana a los nuestros, tanto en el sentido material como en el sentimental, considerándose que en ninguna otra de las islas de las Indias Occidentales, con la excepción de Cuba y Puerto Rico, es tan fuerte la confianza en los Estados Unidos, y se ha mirado a este país más que a ningún otro en busca de buen favor cuando se ha necesitado; y el Sun y otros periódicos que comentan la situación, así como oficiales navales y militares, señalan las nuevas relaciones políticas y estratégicas que proceden de nuestra posesión de Puerto Rico por un lado y nuestra ocupación de Cuba por el otro. Estos son argumentos lógicos para el ejercicio de la vigilancia por parte de nuestro gobierno; y en vista del hecho de que la muerte de Heureaux es seguida de desorden e insurrección, buques navales para proteger nuestros intereses serán necesarios para las aguas de San Domingo — en toda probabilidad este curso será tomado, pues el asunto es demasiado serio para ser ignorado.

records.headline: The Intelligencer prints an editorial on the killing of Heureaux
records.summary_en: The Intelligencer prints an editorial on the killing of Heureaux, whom the paper calls despotic, and on the succession that follows: the leaders of the uprising will offer the presidency to General Gomez, the hero of the Cuban insurrection; Gomez has been identified with San Domingo, and it is practically his home; coupled with the statement is the assertion that his choice for President would likely prove acceptable to all parties. If this is true, and the United States is not compelled to take possession, Gomez, who is so brave a champion of human liberty, would be a decided improvement over the late ruler; and even should the United States assume simply a protectorate, it could not do better than place the matter in his hands, if his popularity among the Dominicans is so great as reported.
records.summary_es: El Intelligencer publica un editorial sobre la muerte de Heureaux, a quien el periódico llama despótico, y sobre la sucesión que sigue: los líderes del levantamiento ofrecerán la presidencia al general Gómez, el héroe de la insurrección cubana; Gómez ha estado identificado con San Domingo, y es prácticamente su hogar; unida a la afirmación está la aseveración de que su elección como Presidente probablemente resultaría aceptable a todos los partidos. Si esto es cierto, y los Estados Unidos no se ven obligados a tomar posesión, Gómez, que es un campeón tan valiente de la libertad humana, sería una mejora decidida sobre el difunto gobernante; e incluso si los Estados Unidos asumieran simplemente un protectorado, no podrían hacer mejor que poner el asunto en sus manos, si su popularidad entre los dominicanos es tan grande como se reporta.

records.headline: The Monitor prints a dispatch announcing the assassination of President Heureaux
records.summary_en: The Monitor prints a dispatch announcing the assassination of President Heureaux at Moca: Gen. Ulysses Heureaux, president of the Dominican republic, was assassinated last Wednesday at Moca; the name of the murderer is Ramon Caceres; he succeeded in making his escape, but an energetic pursuit was at once begun and it is probable that he will soon be captured; calmness prevails everywhere in the republic; and the remains of President Heureaux were taken to San Domingo for the funeral and burial.

records.headline: The Sun prints a Washington item of July 31 on the movements of the warships
records.summary_en: The Sun prints a Washington item of July 31 on the movements of the warships for San Domingo: the Navy Department received a telegram to-day reporting the departure of the gunboat Machias from San Juan, Porto Rico, for San Domingo City yesterday; the Machias left St. Thomas, Danish West Indies, yesterday morning for San Juan, and after landing Capt. Snow, commandant of the Porto Rico naval station, proceeded without delay to San Domingo waters, and probably got to the Dominican capital to-day; the cruiser New Orleans, which left Newport, R. I., for San Domingo City early yesterday morning, is expected to join the Machias there on Friday or Saturday; and no official news of the situation in the Dominican republic has been received here.

records.headline: The Washington officials are not crossing any bridges until they come
records.summary_en: The *Evening Times-Republican* reported that Washington officials were prepared to intervene and establish a protectorate over the Dominican Republic if violent conflict erupted over the succession to the assassinated President Heureaux. Cuban newspapers debated remarks by General Maximo Gomez's secretary suggesting foreign intervention would be required to maintain order on the island. Meanwhile, Dominican Vice President Wenceslao Figuereo reportedly accepted the presidency to maintain constitutional continuity.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Times-Republican* informó que las autoridades en Washington estaban preparadas para intervenir y establecer un protectorado sobre la República Dominicana si estallaba un conflicto violento por la sucesión del asesinado presidente Heureaux. Periódicos cubanos debatieron declaraciones del secretario del general Máximo Gómez en las que sugería que se requeriría una intervención extranjera para preservar el orden en la isla. Entretanto, según se informó, el vicepresidente dominicano Wenceslao Figuereo asumió la presidencia para asegurar la continuidad constitucional.

records.headline: The Republican prints an item of July 28 headed 'Look to Uncle Sam'
records.summary_en: The Republican prints an item of July 28 headed 'Look to Uncle Sam': an exiled leader of the Liberal party of Santo Domingo, Gen. Abelardo A. Moscoso, now living in New York, said last night: 'The death of President Heureaux will, I think, surely be followed by long state of disorder and revolution. I want to emphasize this prophecy — that the United States will eventually be compelled to interfere to establish peace in the island, just as this country did in Cuba. I favor the policy of peace. I shall be glad to return to my country and support such a policy if it is inaugurated by Gen. Figuereo, the vice-president, who succeeds to the head of the government. But if something is not quickly done to establish order and peace, more revolutionary expeditions will follow, like that of Gen. Jiminez and Gen. Morales, who led a band from Cuba against Heureaux.' The secretary of the Santo Domingo Improvement Company, which controls the country's finances, said yesterday: 'Should the new administration attempt to repudiate our contracts we shall certainly, as American citizens, call upon the Washington administration for protection' — the contract with the Improvement Company being the railroads and the right to collect the customs, and in return for these concessions the company has assumed the national debt.

records.headline: The Journal prints an interview with Señor Lluberes, who had arrived
records.summary_en: The Journal prints an interview with Señor Lluberes, who had arrived from St. John, Porto Rico, to rest here several days before leaving for Europe, and who left Santo Domingo before the assassination of President Heureaux and was shocked on learning the news: the report of a revolution in his country, which the Journal's representative brought him, was news to him; he was in a position to say, however, that nothing serious would result from it, and that General Wenceslao Figuereo, who succeeds General Heureaux as President, is strong enough to protect American interests; the dispatching of war ships by the United States to the scene of disturbance is a natural movement of a country in a case of this kind — there are many Americans in Santo Domingo who have large interests there, and the action of this country in sending war ships will be regarded by his countrymen as a precautionary measure. Señor Lluberes was very evasive when asked his opinion of a possibility of annexation of the Dominican Republic by the United States, and how his people would receive such a proposition; he would only say that he had never heard the subject discussed in his country, and that it would be a question to be settled only by the people. 'I do not believe the report that the real mission of the New Orleans and Machias is to force the annexation of Santo Domingo,' he said.

records.headline: The Times prints part of an editorial on Santo Domingo and annexation
records.summary_en: The Times prints part of an editorial on Santo Domingo and annexation: the country might have been had without bloodshed and heavy expenditure through the forces of 'benevolent assimilation,' which would have been set in motion; what we foolishly refused to accept then as a free offering we may have to fight for in the not distant future; nothing has occurred since 1871 to kill the spirit of genuine Americanism which animated the request of the Dominicans for annexation to this country — it represents one of those impulses of a people which can be chilled but not slain by indifference; but the natural enemies of the project have grown stronger through organization than they were twenty-eight years ago, and it will now require an effort on our part, either through the slow processes of diplomacy or the undue aggressions of war, to compose the differences in the little Republic before we can set up our authority there; our solemn obligation to Porto Rico and Cuba admonishes us of our duty in Santo Domingo; if we permit disorder to reign there we may expect to see the infectious spirit of anarchy communicated to the nearby islands, and if we allow old Maximo Gomez and the other leaders driven from the island by the despotic Heureaux to return and ply their trade, we may expect to see rebellion break out in our own new possessions; and this can be prevented in only one way, and that is a very simple way — run up the Stars and Stripes at San Domingo City and take possession of the country.
records.summary_es: El Times publica parte de un editorial sobre Santo Domingo y la anexión: el país podría haberse obtenido sin derramamiento de sangre y sin gran gasto a través de las fuerzas de la «asimilación benévola», que se habrían puesto en movimiento; lo que tontamente rehusamos aceptar entonces como una oferta gratuita puede que tengamos que pelear por ello en un futuro no distante; nada ha ocurrido desde 1871 que mate el espíritu de genuino americanismo que animó la solicitud de los dominicanos de anexión a este país — representa uno de esos impulsos de un pueblo que pueden ser enfriados pero no muertos por la indiferencia; pero los enemigos naturales del proyecto se han hecho más fuertes a través de la organización que lo que eran hace veintiocho años, y ahora requerirá un esfuerzo de nuestra parte, ya a través de los lentos procesos de la diplomacia o de las indebidas agresiones de la guerra, para componer las diferencias en la pequeña República antes de que podamos establecer nuestra autoridad allí; nuestra solemne obligación hacia Puerto Rico y Cuba nos amonesta de nuestro deber en Santo Domingo; si permitimos que el desorden reine allí podemos esperar ver el espíritu infeccioso de la anarquía comunicado a las islas cercanas, y si permitimos que el viejo Máximo Gómez y los otros líderes expulsados de la isla por el despótico Heureaux regresen y ejerzan su oficio, podemos esperar ver estallar la rebelión en nuestras propias nuevas posesiones; y esto puede prevenirse de una sola manera, y es una manera muy simple — izar las Barras y Estrellas en la ciudad de Santo Domingo y tomar posesión del país.

records.headline: The Journal prints part of an editorial urging the acquisition of Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The Journal prints part of an editorial urging the acquisition of Santo Domingo as a more desirable acquisition than Porto Rico, for, with over five times the area, it has only two-thirds the population, so that the opportunities remaining open for development are much greater; it has 18,045 square miles, almost exactly the area of New Hampshire and Vermont combined, with something over 600,000 inhabitants; unlike Haiti, the black republic on the same island, it does not have a majority of negroes; the bulk of its land is available for cultivation; it is rich in all varieties of tropical woods and plants; it is solvent, and its standard of value is the United States gold dollar; with the acquisition of Santo Domingo we should almost complete our cordon of defence of the Nicaragua Canal; of course nobody would urge the forcible annexation of an unwilling people, but if the former sentiments of the Dominicans toward the United States still exist, or are likely to revive, we should be ready to take advantage of them; and we ought to have a couple of war ships always at hand, with instructions to meet any friendly overtures in the proper spirit before the opportunity goes by.
records.summary_es: El Journal publica parte de un editorial que urge la adquisición de Santo Domingo como una adquisición más deseable que Puerto Rico, pues, con más de cinco veces el área, tiene solo dos tercios de la población, de modo que las oportunidades que permanecen abiertas para el desarrollo son mucho mayores; tiene 18,045 millas cuadradas, casi exactamente el área de New Hampshire y Vermont combinados, con algo más de 600,000 habitantes; a diferencia de Haití, la república negra en la misma isla, no tiene una mayoría de negros; el grueso de su tierra está disponible para el cultivo; es rica en todas las variedades de maderas y plantas tropicales; es solvente, y su estándar de valor es el dólar de oro de los Estados Unidos; con la adquisición de Santo Domingo casi completaríamos nuestro cordón de defensa del Canal de Nicaragua; por supuesto nadie urgiría la anexión forzosa de un pueblo no dispuesto, pero si los sentimientos anteriores de los dominicanos hacia los Estados Unidos todavía existen, o es probable que revivan, debemos estar listos para aprovecharnos de ellos; y debemos tener un par de buques de guerra siempre a mano, con instrucciones de recibir cualquier insinuación amistosa en el espíritu apropiado antes de que la oportunidad pase.

records.headline: The Transcript completes a cable item on the revolution in Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The Transcript completes a cable item on the revolution in Santo Domingo and prints two dispatches: according to a private cablegram, demoralization is growing through the death of the president, and in the event of the revolution succeeding it is probable that Jiminez and the other reputed leaders will agree to retire, offering the presidency to General Maximo Gomez, who would prove acceptable to all parties, and a deputation is reported to be going to Cuba to confer with General Gomez. Under the head 'The Situation Critical,' a Puerto Plata dispatch of July 31 says the situation is critical and an outbreak momentarily expected; the friends of the government are under arms and ready for action to protect property and preserve the peace; the burial of President Heureaux was conducted with fitting honors; Governor Pepin had assembled troops in Moca, and the governor of La Vega Real has 1,000 men; the minister of the treasury has arrived at Moca in hot haste; the government is taking steps for the protection of business and the finance of the country, and expects to carry out the cancellation of the state bank notes; and in Puerto Plata there is an urgent demand that the government send a sufficient force to Moca to hunt down the assassins of the president. Under the head 'Telegraph Wires Cut,' a Cape Haytien dispatch of July 31 says advices just received from the Dominican frontier say the insurgents have cut the telegraph wires in the neighborhood of Santiago de los Caballeros and also near Moca.
records.summary_es: El Transcript completa una nota cablegráfica sobre la revolución en Santo Domingo y publica dos despachos: según un cablegrama privado, la desmoralización está creciendo a través de la muerte del presidente, y en el evento de que la revolución triunfe es probable que Jiminez y los otros líderes reputados acuerden retirarse, ofreciendo la presidencia al general Máximo Gómez, que probaría ser aceptable a todos los partidos, y se reporta que una diputación va a Cuba a conferenciar con el general Gómez. Bajo el título «The Situation Critical», un despacho de Puerto Plata del 31 de julio dice que la situación es crítica y que un estallido es esperado momentáneamente; los amigos del gobierno están bajo las armas y listos para la acción para proteger la propiedad y preservar la paz; el entierro del presidente Heureaux fue conducido con honores apropiados; el gobernador Pepín había reunido tropas en Moca, y el gobernador de La Vega Real tiene 1,000 hombres; el ministro de la tesorería ha llegado a Moca en gran prisa; el gobierno está tomando pasos para la protección de los negocios y las finanzas del país, y espera llevar a cabo la cancelación de los billetes del banco del estado; y en Puerto Plata hay una demanda urgente de que el gobierno envíe una fuerza suficiente a Moca para cazar a los asesinos del presidente. Bajo el título «Telegraph Wires Cut», un despacho de Cabo Haitiano del 31 de julio dice que avisos recién recibidos de la frontera dominicana dicen que los insurgentes han cortado los cables telegráficos en el vecindario de Santiago de los Caballeros y también cerca de Moca.

records.headline: The Eagle prints part of a sketch of the late President Heureaux
records.summary_en: The Eagle prints part of a sketch of the late President Heureaux, a man of unbending will, endowed with much intellectual force, and possessed of great courage, he strove honestly for the people of his fatherland, but with methods which found their only counterpart in the middle ages; in the less than fifty years of his life, he rose from a peasant to the dictatorship of San Domingo, and in the thirteen years of his administration he materially advanced the country in civilization, welding out of a mass of brigands an army of considerable strength, and building up a financial system which brought prosperity to his people; his people looked upon him either with a devotion akin to idolatry, or with horror and fear, for his vigorous personality admitted of no lukewarm sentiment — whether they loved or hated him, they obeyed him without question; thirty years ago, an ill-clad, half-starved boy from the hills of the interior, he joined as a private the so-called army, a lawless, impotent mob controlled by corrupt politicians and incompetent generals; despite a withered arm, which was almost useless, Heureaux developed into a good soldier, and soon rose from the ranks to an under officership; his genius for organization developed, and by rapid promotions the young officer advanced until he became commander in chief; then came the turbulent days of 1885-'86, and in the disorder of the time Heureaux found his opportunity — with his power as head of the army, he forced his election as president.
records.summary_es: El Eagle publica parte de un bosquejo del difunto presidente Heureaux, un hombre de voluntad inflexible, dotado de mucha fuerza intelectual y poseedor de gran valor, que se esforzó honestamente por el pueblo de su patria, pero con métodos que encontraron su único contrapeso en la edad media; en los menos de cincuenta años de su vida, se elevó de campesino a la dictadura de San Domingo, y en los trece años de su administración avanzó materialmente el país en civilización, soldando de una masa de bandidos un ejército de fuerza considerable, y construyendo un sistema financiero que trajo prosperidad a su pueblo; su pueblo lo miraba ya con una devoción parecida a la idolatría, o con horror y miedo, pues su vigorosa personalidad no admitía ningún sentimiento tibio — lo amaran o lo odiaran, le obedecían sin cuestión; hace treinta años, un muchacho mal vestido y medio hambriento de las lomas del interior, se unió como soldado raso al llamado ejército, una muchedumbre sin ley e impotente controlada por políticos corruptos y generales incompetentes; a pesar de un brazo marchito, que era casi inútil, Heureaux se desarrolló en un buen soldado y pronto se elevó de las filas a una suboficialidad; su genio para la organización se desarrolló, y por rápidas promociones el joven oficial avanzó hasta llegar a ser comandante en jefe; entonces vinieron los días turbulentos de 1885-86, y en el desorden de la época Heureaux encontró su oportunidad — con su poder como jefe del ejército, forzó su elección como presidente.

records.headline: The Eagle prints part of a sketch of President Heureaux and his courage
records.summary_en: The Eagle prints part of a sketch of President Heureaux and his courage: it was difficult to secure from Dominicans expressions of opinion on any subject touching the president or his policy, but when it was possible to find a Dominican who was willing to talk of the life of Heureaux, the stories told had the flavor of old-time romance; one of the striking instances of the president's personal courage is to be found in the story of his suppression of the 'Santiago' rebellion a few years ago — Santiago is inland from the famous Samana Bay, and at a distance from the capital which made it possible for the residents to foment trouble with the possibility of escaping immediate punishment; here a band of malcontents from all parts of the island gathered and soon succeeded in enlisting the sympathies of almost the entire population of the town, and, encouraged by the fact that the terrible president was several days' journey distant, the ringleaders finally became bold enough to issue a manifesto declaring Heureaux a monstrous tyrant, and urging an uprising, and great posters were printed bearing the picture of a coffin and calling on all patriots to aid in ridding the fatherland of its oppressor; the government secret service soon apprised the president of the affair, and in his usual picturesque manner he proceeded with preparations for revenge: he ordered made a tough black coffin, and, putting it aboard his little armoured yacht, he took a detail of soldiers and sailed around the coast for Santiago, and, landing with thirty soldiers, he started on the twenty-five-mile horseback journey.

records.headline: A profile of President Heureaux tells how his brother-in-law, the husband of the half sister for whom he had a real
records.summary_en: A profile of President Heureaux tells how his brother-in-law, the husband of the half sister for whom he had a real affection, was advanced rapidly in the government service, warned once after joining a plot to assassinate the president, and found within six months plotting again. Heureaux gave a state breakfast in the young man's honor, seated him at his side, and as the meal ended told him he was going to be shot in five minutes; the official was then shot in the courtyard while the president's sister screamed from the windows above, and the uncoffined body was quickly buried in a flower garden.
records.summary_es: Un perfil del presidente Heureaux cuenta cómo su cuñado, el esposo de la media hermana por quien sentía un verdadero afecto, fue ascendido rápidamente en el servicio del gobierno, advertido una vez tras unirse a un complot para asesinar al presidente, y descubierto en menos de seis meses conspirando de nuevo. Heureaux ofreció un desayuno de Estado en honor del joven, lo sentó a su lado y, al terminar la comida, le dijo que iba a ser fusilado en cinco minutos; el funcionario fue fusilado entonces en el patio mientras la hermana del presidente gritaba desde las ventanas de arriba, y el cuerpo sin ataúd fue enterrado rápidamente en un jardín de flores.
records.passage: "Heureaux's heartlessness in the discharge of what he believed to be his duty was never better shown than in the execution, for conspiracy, of his brother-in-law. With the president lived a half sister, much younger than he, and the one person in the world for whom he seemed to have a real affection. The girl met and married a young Dominican merchant Heureaux soon took the young man into the government service and advanced him rapidly. But the young official was soon deep in the councils of a group of conspirators who had for their object the assassination of the president and the overthrow of his government. The young man's treachery was kept from the public and was allowed to retain his government position on promise of future good behavior. records.headline: This profile of Heureaux recounts how he walked among men who had been swearing to take his life, told them they
records.summary_en: This profile of Heureaux recounts how he walked among men who had been swearing to take his life, told them they were not nearly so anxious for his life as they believed, and let them go free without taking any action. It describes his polished manner and entertaining conversation, his three-story palace in Santo Domingo covering a block, and the keen slight he felt because the aristocratic Dominicans refused to admit him to their social circles on account of his blood.
records.summary_es: Este perfil de Heureaux relata cómo caminó entre hombres que habían estado jurando quitarle la vida, les dijo que no estaban ni de lejos tan ansiosos por su vida como ellos creían, y los dejó ir libres sin tomar ninguna medida. Describe su trato cortés y su conversación entretenida, su palacio de tres pisos en Santo Domingo que ocupa una manzana, y el desaire que sentía agudamente porque los dominicanos aristocráticos se negaban a admitirlo en sus círculos sociales a causa de su sangre.
records.passage: "I wished to show you," Heureaux said, "that you are not nearly so anxious for my life as you believed. I know you all, but I shall take no action. You are free." And he turned and went away. He kept [illegible] left the country. Heureaux had the features of a full-blooded negro. His manner was polished and his conversation entertaining. The aristocratic Dominicans, who are of pure Spanish blood, refused to admit him to their social circles because of his negro blood, and he felt their slight keenly. Little was known of his family history or his parentage, and he was always reticent about the incidents of his life before he became famous. His palace in Santo Domingo is a three-story building covering a block, and built in the typical style of the tropics. records.headline: The Transcript prints the Moscoso interview, the warships item
records.summary_en: The Transcript prints the Moscoso interview, the warships item, and the opening of a Havana item: General Abelardo A. Moscoso, an exiled leader of the Liberal party of Santo Domingo, now living in New York, said: 'The death of President Heureaux will, I think, surely be followed by a long state of disorder and revolution. I want to emphasize this prophecy — that the United States will eventually be compelled to interfere to establish peace in the island, just as this country did in Cuba. I favor the policy of peace. I shall be glad to return to my country and support such a policy if it is inaugurated by General Figuereo, the vice president, who succeeds to the head of the government. But if something is not quickly done to establish order and peace, more revolutionary expeditions will follow that of General Jiminez and General Morales, who led a band from Cuba against Heureaux.' Under the head 'Precautionary Measure,' a Washington item of July 29 says Secretary Long has sent telegraphic orders to the cruiser New Orleans, at Newport, directing that she proceed at once to San Domingo, and at the same time an order was sent to the gunboat Machias, at St. Thomas, to leave for San Domingo; it is expected that the New Orleans will be able to leave during the day, and the Machias will be in San Domingo waters within a day or two; and this action was not due to the receipt of any official advices indicating possible trouble, but entirely to the desire to be forehanded in dealing with any possible disturbance. A Havana item of July 29 opens under the head 'Gomez Says All Papers Lie.'
records.summary_es: El Transcript publica la entrevista de Moscoso, la nota de los buques de guerra, y la apertura de una nota de La Habana: el general Abelardo A. Moscoso, un exiliado líder del partido Liberal de Santo Domingo, que vive ahora en Nueva York, dijo: «La muerte del presidente Heureaux será, pienso, seguramente seguida de un largo estado de desorden y revolución. Quiero enfatizar esta profecía — que los Estados Unidos serán eventualmente obligados a intervenir para establecer la paz en la isla, justo como este país hizo en Cuba. Favorezco la política de paz. Estaré contento de regresar a mi país y apoyar tal política si es inaugurada por el general Figuereo, el vicepresidente, que sucede a la jefatura del gobierno. Pero si no se hace algo rápidamente para establecer el orden y la paz, seguirán más expediciones revolucionarias como la del general Jiminez y el general Morales, que condujeron una banda desde Cuba contra Heureaux». Bajo el título «Precautionary Measure», una nota de Washington del 29 de julio dice que el secretario Long ha enviado órdenes telegráficas al crucero New Orleans, en Newport, dirigiéndolo a proceder de inmediato a San Domingo, y al mismo tiempo se envió una orden a la cañonera Machias, en St. Thomas, de partir para San Domingo; se espera que el New Orleans pueda partir durante el día, y que el Machias estará en aguas de San Domingo dentro de un día o dos; y esta acción no se debió al recibo de ningún aviso oficial que indicara posible problema, sino enteramente al deseo de estar prevenidos al tratar con cualquier posible disturbio. records.headline: The Dispatch prints a Santo Domingo dispatch of August 1 and a Washington item
records.summary_en: The Dispatch prints a Santo Domingo dispatch of August 1 and a Washington item on recognition: Vice President Figuereo, as a result of the assassination of President Heureaux, has taken charge of the government of Santo Domingo as President, and has formed a cabinet as follows: Minister of the Interior, F. D. Morales; Minister of War and Marine, Tilo Palino; Minister of Foreign Affairs, E. Henriquez; Minister of Finance, J. Alvarez; Minister of Justice, S. Valverde; Minister of Agriculture, T. C. Bido; and Minister of Posts and Telegraphs, J. R. Vidal. The country is quiet and no fears of disturbances are entertained, and the United States gunboat Machias arrived here from Porto Rico yesterday. Under the head 'Our Recognition to Be Prompt,' the Washington item of August 1 says the State Department will not delay in recognizing the new government set up by Figuereo, but as soon as United States Minister Powell notifies the department that the Vice-President has assumed the presidential office and is at the head of a de facto government, the Minister will be instructed to extend the formal recognition of the United States Government.
records.summary_es: El Dispatch publica un despacho de Santo Domingo del 1 de agosto y una nota de Washington sobre el reconocimiento: el vicepresidente Figuereo, a resultado del asesinato del presidente Heureaux, ha tomado a su cargo el gobierno de Santo Domingo como Presidente, y ha formado un gabinete como sigue: ministro del Interior, F.
