Bajo el título «Our Recognition to Be Prompt», la nota de Washington del 1 de agosto dice que el Departamento de Estado no tardará en reconocer el nuevo gobierno establecido por Figuereo, sino que tan pronto como el ministro Powell de los Estados Unidos notifique al departamento que el vicepresidente ha asumido el oficio presidencial y está a la cabeza de un gobierno de facto, el ministro será instruido a extender el reconocimiento formal del Gobierno de los Estados Unidos.

records.summary_en: The Journal prints a Santo Domingo dispatch of August 1 with the new cabinet: Vice President Wenceslao Figuereo has taken charge of the government of Santo Domingo as president, and has formed a cabinet as follows: F. D. Morales, Minister of the Interior; Tilo Palino, Minister of War and Marine; E. Henriquez, Minister of Foreign Affairs; Sebastian Valverde, Minister of Justice; T. Cordero Bido, Minister of Agriculture; Jaime R. Vidal, Minister of Posts and Telegraphs; Braulio Alvarez, Sub-Secretary of the Interior; and Pedro T. Perez, Sub-Secretary of Justice. The country is quiet and no fears of disturbances are entertained. The dispatch adds that the place was visited during the afternoon of July 27 by a severe tornado, which blew at the rate of forty miles an hour; three coasting vessels, loaded with produce and anchored in the outer harbor, were wrecked, and about fifteen men perished; and the damage done ashore was not great. records.summary_en: The Spy prints a Santo Domingo dispatch headed 'How It Happened', in which the latest story of the assassination of President Heureaux received here agrees with previously published accounts in nearly all particulars; according to advices just at hand, President Heureaux was with the administrator of finances in Moca, when a beggar came to the house and requested a gratuity; the president went to the door of the house in answer to the appeal of the mendicant, but he had no sooner made his appearance than a shot was fired, wounding him; despite his wounds, Gen. Heureaux started toward the street, firing his revolver as he advanced; and six more shots were fired, all taking effect in the president's body. The United States gunboat Machias arrived here from Porto Rico today, August 1. The assassins of President Heureaux and their seconds are in a mountainous district about 25 miles northward of Moca, and Señor Don Cordero, the late minister of the interior, has taken the field against them with 400 men.

records.headline: The Spy prints an editorial on the island and the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: The Spy prints an editorial on the island and the Dominican Republic: the conflict between Hippolyte and Legitime furnished the most constant and exciting items of news from the West Indies, and all the force and ability of the extraordinary Heureaux were required to restore order in the republic; the condition of the island is of vastly more importance to the United States now than it was a dozen years ago, and the affairs of the islands therefore deserve the more consideration; the island of Hispaniola, Hayti or Santo Domingo, as it has been at various times called, is divided into two republics — the western third of the territory is occupied by the republic of Hayti, which dates back to 1800, and is of French character, even the language being a French patois; the remaining two-thirds, representing an area of some 19,000 square miles, or somewhat more than the combined areas of New Hampshire and Vermont, constitute the Dominican republic; the language is Spanish, and the people are of mixed French, Spanish, English and African blood; the soil is wonderfully fertile, bearing tobacco, cotton, sugar cane, cocoa, coffee, fruits and valuable woods; the scenery is mountainous and picturesque, and under proper government the country would be a pleasant place of residence; and while the island has not been remarkable for prosperity, there is a certain rich class which indulges in educational aspirations, and not a few of its sons have been sent to this country or to Europe to study, and two sons of the late President Heureaux are said to be studying law and medicine in Paris.

records.headline: The Enterprise prints the Fort de France assassination dispatch
records.summary_en: The Enterprise prints the Fort de France assassination dispatch and a sketch of President Heureaux: Gen. Ulises Heureaux, president of the Dominican Republic, was assassinated at Moca, Santo Domingo; the name of the murderer is Ramon Caceros; he succeeded in making his escape, but an energetic pursuit was at once begun, and it is probable that he will soon be captured; Vice President General Wenceslao Figuereo, immediately upon the announcement of the president's death, assumed the direction of affairs; at present calmness prevails everywhere in the republic; and the remains of President Heureaux will probably be taken to Santo Domingo for the funeral services. President Heureaux was a soldier during his entire lifetime: one of his arms was paralyzed from a wound he received by a rifle ball in battle; he is described by Americans familiar with his career as a man without fear, and when there was any disturbance or revolution in any part of the republic, he mounted his horse and went pell-mell himself to the front as leader, and learned all the details of the revolution as well as the causes leading to it; he went as a soldier, not as President or General, and thus was unknown by his people; he generally traveled on horseback and made frequent excursions through the country, and when on such trips he avoided hotels and private houses and slept along the roadside; he had a wonderful career, and was held in high regard by the majority of his people; and he participated in many battles, and always with success.
records.summary_es: El Enterprise publica el despacho del asesinato de Fort de France y un bosquejo del presidente Heureaux: el gen. Ulises Heureaux, presidente de la República Dominicana, fue asesinado en Moca, Santo Domingo; el nombre del asesino es Ramón Caceros; logró escapar, pero se inició de inmediato una persecución enérgica, y es probable que pronto sea capturado; el vicepresidente general Wenceslao Figuereo, inmediatamente después del anuncio de la muerte del presidente, asumió la dirección de los asuntos; en el presente prevalece la calma en todas partes de la república; y los restos del presidente Heureaux probablemente serán llevados a Santo Domingo para los servicios fúnebres. El presidente Heureaux fue un soldado durante toda su vida: uno de sus brazos estaba paralizado por una herida que recibió de una bala de rifle en batalla; es descrito por americanos familiarizados con su carrera como un hombre sin miedo, y cuando había cualquier disturbio o revolución en cualquier parte de la república, montaba su caballo e iba precipitadamente él mismo al frente como líder, y aprendía todos los detalles de la revolución así como las causas que la motivaron; iba como soldado, no como Presidente o General, y así era desconocido por su pueblo; generalmente viajaba a caballo e hacía frecuentes excursiones a través del país, y cuando en tales viajes evitaba hoteles y casas privadas y dormía a la orilla del camino; tuvo una carrera maravillosa y era tenido en alta estima por la mayoría de su pueblo; y participó en muchas batallas, y siempre con éxito.

records.headline: The Review completes a cable item on the revolution in Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The Review completes a cable item on the revolution in Santo Domingo and prints two dispatches: according to a private cablegram, demoralization is growing through the death of the president, and in the event of the revolution succeeding it is probable that Jiminez and the other reputed leaders will agree to retire, offering the presidency to General Maximo Gomez, who would prove acceptable to all parties, and a deputation is reported to be going to Cuba to confer with General Gomez. Under the head 'The Situation Critical,' a Puerto Plata dispatch of August 1 says the situation is critical and an outbreak momentarily expected; the friends of the government are under arms and ready for action to protect property and preserve the peace; the burial of President Heureaux was conducted with fitting honors; Governor Pepin had assembled troops in Moca, and the governor of La Vega Real has 1,000 men; the minister of the treasury has arrived at Moca in hot haste; the government is taking steps for the protection of business and the finance of the country, and expects to carry out the cancellation of the state bank notes; and in Puerto Plata there is an urgent demand that the government send a sufficient force to Moca to hunt down the assassins of the president. Under the head 'Telegraph Wires Cut,' a Cape Haytien dispatch of August 1 says advices just received from the Dominican frontier say the insurgents have cut the telegraph wires in the neighborhood of Santiago de los Caballeros and also near Moca.
records.summary_es: El Review completa una nota cablegráfica sobre la revolución en Santo Domingo y publica dos despachos: según un cablegrama privado, la desmoralización está creciendo a través de la muerte del presidente, y en el evento de que la revolución triunfe es probable que Jiminez y los otros líderes reputados acuerden retirarse, ofreciendo la presidencia al general Máximo Gómez, que probaría ser aceptable a todos los partidos, y se reporta que una diputación va a Cuba a conferenciar con el general Gómez. Bajo el título «The Situation Critical», un despacho de Puerto Plata del 1 de agosto dice que la situación es crítica y que un estallido es esperado momentáneamente; los amigos del gobierno están bajo las armas y listos para la acción para proteger la propiedad y preservar la paz; el entierro del presidente Heureaux fue conducido con honores apropiados; el gobernador Pepín había reunido tropas en Moca, y el gobernador de La Vega Real tiene 1,000 hombres; el ministro de la tesorería ha llegado a Moca en gran prisa; el gobierno está tomando pasos para la protección de los negocios y las finanzas del país, y espera llevar a cabo la cancelación de los billetes del banco del estado; y en Puerto Plata hay una demanda urgente de que el gobierno envíe una fuerza suficiente a Moca para cazar a los asesinos del presidente. Bajo el título «Telegraph Wires Cut», un despacho de Cabo Haitiano del 1 de agosto dice que avisos recién recibidos de la frontera dominicana dicen que los insurgentes han cortado los cables telegráficos en el vecindario de Santiago de los Caballeros y también cerca de Moca.

records.headline: The News prints part of a statement in defense of General Gomez
records.summary_en: The News prints part of a statement in defense of General Gomez, and an interview with the ex-President of Venezuela: the statement says that Gomez strove to obtain independence for the island for thirty years, and his efforts have been little recognized; those make a mistake who think he aspires to anything in Santo Domingo or Cuba — God forbid that he should even be an employe of high rank; he thinks it a veritable misfortune to be president, as on the field of battle a brave man exposes his life, while in the presidential chair he exposes his honor, even if he has no valor; Jiminez is the man he hopes will be president of the Dominican Republic; those in Cuba to whom he is a cause of worry need not be disturbed at seeing his family, which only came here from a pious motive, which being fulfilled, he and his family will abandon the land which has repaid his many efforts with rancor; and those who want posts need not fear that he wants the dictatorship — he goes home leaving the field free. A New York item of August 1 prints Dr. Laurens Villanova, ex-President of Venezuela, who is at present in New York: asked this morning through his interpreter whether it was true that the South American countries were about to form an offensive and defensive alliance against the United States on account of its 'Imperialism policy,' he replied that he had not heard of it, but thought that such an alliance ought to be made; and asked, 'Do the South American nations fear the United States?' the ex-President shrugged his shoulders and said something in Spanish.

records.headline: The Tribune prints part of an editorial on the course of the government
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints part of an editorial on the course of the government after the assassination: the assassination of President Heureaux, it is proposed, shall not be made the pretext for a demonstration of naval force by foreign Powers, such as has usually attended the outbreak of the chronic happenings of a revolutionary character in the independent republics, so called, in the West Indies; this action of the Government, without awaiting the usual formulary of a request by the United States representative at the point of disturbance, is regarded as a public notice of an intention on the part of this Government to command order among these turbulent people; and aside from the 'sphere of influence' of the United States on the American Hemisphere, as set forth by President Monroe and repeatedly backed up by his long line of successors in the Presidential office.
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica parte de un editorial sobre el curso del gobierno después del asesinato: el asesinato del presidente Heureaux, se propone, no será hecho el pretexto para una demostración de fuerza naval por Potencias extranjeras, como ha usualmente asistido el estallido de los sucesos crónicos de un carácter revolucionario en las repúblicas independientes, así llamadas, en las Indias Occidentales; esta acción del Gobierno, sin esperar el formulario usual de una solicitud por el representante de los Estados Unidos en el punto de disturbio, es considerada como un aviso público de una intención de parte de este Gobierno de imponer orden entre esa gente turbulenta; y aparte de la «esfera de influencia» de los Estados Unidos en el Hemisferio Americano, como establecida por el presidente Monroe y repetidamente respaldada por su larga línea de sucesores en el oficio Presidencial.

records.headline: The Herald prints an editorial on the talk of revolution in the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: The Herald prints an editorial on the talk of revolution in the Dominican Republic: the revolts there have been so many in the past quarter of a century that no one would be surprised if a rising should occur at this time; the assassination of its President shows that the conditions which ordinarily lead to revolts are at hand; there is a comparatively large number of Europeans and Americans in the Dominican Republic, and almost all of them, it is understood, favor annexation to the United States; if that annexation project of thirty years ago which President Grant favored, and which the people of the island approved, had been carried out, it would undoubtedly have been a benefit to all parties; the present disturbance may lead to another annexation movement — this time it would succeed; and the country is a little wiser than it was then.

INSTANTLY KILLED.
Joseph H. Thyng Crushed by a Falling
Pulley in Suncook.
SUNCOOK, July 27.—Joseph H. Thyng,
a machinist, while at work last night in
the China mill removing shafting and pul
leys, was instantly Kkilled, about midnight,
by being crushed under a falling pulley.
He was 24 years of age and belongs in
Lakeport and has worked here but a few
months. A wife survives. Mr. Thyng
was a corporal in Company K, First New
Hampshire, in the Spanish-American war.
The remains were taken to Lakeport to
day on the afternoon train.

records.headline: The Censor prints a dispatch from Santo Domingo and a sketch of President Heureaux
records.summary_en: The Censor prints a dispatch from Santo Domingo and a sketch of President Heureaux: the former reports that immediately upon the announcement of the president's death, Vice President Gen. Wenceslao Figuereo assumed control of the government; several attempts have been made before to take the life of President Heureaux, but they were frustrated — on one occasion, while passing through the arched entrance to the palace between lines of guards, his quick eye caught one of the soldiers, who appeared to lower his rifle in his direction, and, quickly pulling a revolver, he shot the man in his tracks, passed on to his private office, and gave orders to remove a dead man lying at the main entrance; Gen. Heureaux was born in Porto Plata in 1846, and served in the war against Spain from 1868 to 1874; later he was put at the head of the advanced Dominicans, who sought to improve their country by inducing foreign capital to locate on the island; as he advanced, the wealthy inhabitants joined his forces, and when he arrived at the gates of the historic city of Santo Domingo he was chosen president of the republic, and served his term of four years; at the expiration of every four years an electoral college assembles in the city to vote for a president for the following term, but owing to Gen. Heureaux's popularity and ability he has always been unanimously re-elected, and was serving his fifth term.
records.summary_es: El Censor publica un despacho de Santo Domingo y un bosquejo del presidente Heureaux: el primero reporta que inmediatamente después del anuncio de la muerte del presidente, el vicepresidente gen. Wenceslao Figuereo asumió el control del gobierno; varios intentos se han hecho antes por tomar la vida del presidente Heureaux, pero fueron frustrados — en una ocasión, mientras pasaba a través de la entrada arqueada al palacio entre líneas de guardias, su ojo rápido captó a uno de los soldados, que parecía bajar su rifle en su dirección, y, rápidamente sacando un revólver, le disparó al hombre en el sitio, pasó a su oficina privada, y dio órdenes de remover un hombre muerto que yacía en la entrada principal; el gen. Heureaux nació en Puerto Plata en 1846, y sirvió en la guerra contra España desde 1868 hasta 1874; más tarde fue puesto a la cabeza de los dominicanos avanzados, que buscaban mejorar su país induciendo capital extranjero a localizarse en la isla; al avanzar él, los habitantes ricos se unieron a sus fuerzas, y cuando llegó a las puertas de la histórica ciudad de Santo Domingo fue elegido presidente de la república y sirvió su término de cuatro años; a la expiración de cada cuatro años una asamblea electoral se reúne en la ciudad para votar por un presidente para el término siguiente, pero debido a la popularidad y habilidad del gen. Heureaux siempre ha sido unánimemente reelegido, y estaba sirviendo su quinto término.

records.headline: The Tribune prints the closing part of a statement on the situation
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints the closing part of a statement on the situation in Santo Domingo: there is no fear that the insurrectionists will interfere in any way with the property of foreigners on the island; notwithstanding the many revolutions which have taken place in Santo Domingo since it attained its independence, in no instance has either life been taken or property molested of any foreigner, with the single exception of the action of Heureaux, who opened the vaults of the French bank because of a personal quarrel with one of its directors; women and children are safe at all times, as the Dominicans never stoop to war with the helpless, nor do they ever sack or pillage, but fight for what they believe to be right in the open, as men and soldiers should do; Mr. Jiminez and General Gomez are warm personal friends — in fact, both reside in the same house in Havana; as Heureaux was a usurper, the Vice-President is equally so, but bloodshed and insurrection would cease at once if the latter would announce that a legal, public election would take place on August 16, which is the Independence day of the country; the entire country is aroused to the necessity of a change to a government where life is secure, and it recognizes that the former Vice-President and the present pretending President is but one of the accomplices of Heureaux, and as such has no confidence in him; and there is but one man who at this time represents the people and their best interests, and that is Jiminez, and if an opportunity is given to the people they will prove it by their ballots — but if none is afforded in that way, then force will be used.
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica la parte final de una declaración sobre la situación en Santo Domingo: no hay temor de que los insurreccionistas interfieran en ninguna manera con la propiedad de los extranjeros en la isla; a pesar de las muchas revoluciones que han tenido lugar en Santo Domingo desde que alcanzó su independencia, en ningún caso ha sido tomada vida ni molestada propiedad de ningún extranjero, con la sola excepción de la acción de Heureaux, que abrió las bóvedas del banco francés por una querella personal con uno de sus directores; las mujeres y los niños están seguros en todo tiempo, pues los dominicanos nunca se rebajan a guerrear con los indefensos, ni saquean ni pillan jamás, sino que pelean por lo que creen correcto a campo abierto, como hombres y soldados deben hacer; el señor Jiminez y el general Gómez son amigos personales cálidos — de hecho, ambos residen en la misma casa en La Habana; como Heureaux fue un usurpador, el vicepresidente es igualmente eso, pero el derramamiento de sangre y la insurrección cesarían de inmediato si este último anunciara que una elección legal y pública tendría lugar el 16 de agosto, que es el día de la Independencia del país; el país entero está despertado a la necesidad de un cambio a un gobierno donde la vida sea segura, y reconoce que el anterior vicepresidente y el presente presidente pretendiente es solo uno de los cómplices de Heureaux, y como tal no tiene confianza en él; y hay un solo hombre que en este tiempo representa al pueblo y sus mejores intereses, y ese es Jiminez, y si una oportunidad es dada al pueblo ellos lo probarán por sus votos — pero si ninguna es ofrecida de esa manera, entonces se usará la fuerza.

records.headline: The Tribune prints a dispatch headed 'Figuero Takes the Reins'
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints a dispatch headed 'Figuero Takes the Reins', the Santo Domingo dispatch of August 1, in which the Vice-President, Wenceslao Figuereo, as a result of the assassination of President Heureaux on July 28, has taken charge of the Government of Santo Domingo as President, and has formed a cabinet as follows: Minister of the Interior, F. D. Morales; Minister of War and Marine, Tilo Palino; Minister of Foreign Affairs, E. Henriquez; Minister of Finance, J. de J. Alvarez; Minister of Justice, Sebastian Valverde; Minister of Agriculture, T. Cordero Bido; Minister of Posts and Telegraphs, Jaime R. Vidal; Sub-Secretary of the Interior, Braulio Alvarez; and Sub-Secretary of Justice, Pedro T. Perez. The country is quiet, and no fears of disturbances are entertained. This place was visited during the afternoon of July 27 by a severe tornado, which blew at the rate of forty miles an hour; three coasting vessels loaded with produce and anchored in the outer harbor were wrecked, and about fifteen men perished; and the damage done ashore was not of much importance. The dispatch also opens the latest story of the assassination of President Heureaux received here, which agrees with previously published accounts in nearly all particulars: according to advices just at hand, President Heureaux was with the Administrator of Finances in Moca, when a beggar presented himself and requested a gratuity, and the President went to the door of the house in answer to the appeal.
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica un despacho titulado «Figuero Takes the Reins», el despacho de Santo Domingo del 1 de agosto, en el cual el vicepresidente, Wenceslao Figuereo, a resultado del asesinato del presidente Heureaux el 28 de julio, ha tomado a su cargo el Gobierno de Santo Domingo como Presidente, y ha formado un gabinete como sigue: ministro del Interior, F. D. Morales; ministro de Guerra y Marina, Tilo Palino; ministro de Relaciones Exteriores, E. Henriquez; ministro de Finanzas, J. de J. Alvarez; ministro de Justicia, Sebastián Valverde; ministro de Agricultura, T. Cordero Bido; ministro de Correos y Telégrafos, Jaime R. Vidal; subsecretario del Interior, Braulio Alvarez; y subsecretario de Justicia, Pedro T. Pérez. El país está quieto, y no se albergan temores de disturbios. Este lugar fue visitado durante la tarde del 27 de julio por un tornado severo, que sopló a razón de cuarenta millas por hora; tres buques costeros cargados de productos y anclados en el puerto exterior fueron destruidos, y unos quince hombres perecieron; y el daño hecho en tierra no fue de mucha importancia. El despacho también abre la última historia del asesinato del presidente Heureaux recibida aquí, que concuerda con las versiones previamente publicadas en casi todos los particulares: según avisos recién a mano, el presidente Heureaux estaba con el Administrador de Finanzas en Moca, cuando un mendigo se presentó y pidió una gratificación, y el Presidente fue a la puerta de la casa en respuesta al llamamiento.

records.headline: The Tribune prints part of a letter written in defense of General Gomez
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints part of a letter written in defense of General Gomez: in it, he strove to obtain independence for the island for thirty years, and his efforts have been little recognized; the sweat on the horse is hardly dry when the rage of those who did not dare to take the field by his side falls upon him; insults will not affect him more than if they were directed against the Czar of Russia by a person with whom he had no connecting links; what, however, is irritating and painful, and has no logical explanation, is the desire to injure him, to despise the Dominican, to insult the stranger who believes he has done much for Cuba — they would insult the old Dominican Republic, which has brilliantly served the Cuban cause more than any Latin people, with money, love and blood; the Dominicans are called savages because their President was killed by the angered hands of vengeance — why then not call other nations savages on account of assassinations committed in them? In this connection the writer cites the instances of the killing of President Garfield of the United States, Señor Canovas del Castillo, the Spanish Premier, and President Carnot, of the French Republic; and, continuing, the writer says that some Cubans think they can get at him by means of this unfortunate occurrence, accusing him of aspiring to fill the place made vacant by the act of the assassin, forgetting that he aspires still higher; and the history of his life proves that he prefers liberating those writing things against him — if Cuba cannot see a position to offer him after all his efforts, how could he see one in Santo Domingo?
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica parte de una carta escrita en defensa del general Gómez: en ella, él se esforzó por obtener la independencia de la isla por treinta años, y sus esfuerzos han sido poco reconocidos; el sudor en el caballo apenas está seco cuando la rabia de aquellos que no se atrevieron a tomar el campo a su lado cae sobre él; los insultos no lo afectarán más que si fueran dirigidos contra el Czar de Rusia por una persona con quien él no tuviera lazos de conexión; lo que, sin embargo, es irritante y doloroso, y no tiene explicación lógica, es el deseo de herirlo, de despreciar al dominicano, de insultar al extraño que cree que ha hecho mucho por Cuba — insultarían a la vieja República Dominicana, que ha servido brillantemente la causa cubana más que ningún pueblo latino, con dinero, amor y sangre; los dominicanos son llamados salvajes porque su Presidente fue muerto por las manos enojadas de la venganza — ¿por qué entonces no llamar salvajes a otras naciones por razón de asesinatos cometidos en ellas? records.headline: The Tribune completes the assassination dispatch with a sketch of President Heureaux
records.summary_en: The Tribune completes the assassination dispatch with a sketch of President Heureaux: the assassination was at half past four o'clock Wednesday afternoon; the name of the murderer is Ramon Caceros; he succeeded in making his escape, but an energetic pursuit was at once begun; Vice President Gen. Wenceslao Figuereo, immediately upon the announcement of the president's death, assumed the direction of affairs; at present calmness prevails everywhere in the republic; and the remains of President Heureaux will probably be taken to Santo Domingo for the funeral services. Ulysses Heureaux, the late president of Santo Domingo, was born about 1838; little is known of his early life except that he was a power in the politics of the little West Indian republic when he was a young man; his first real prominence was attained during the war with the Spaniards in 1866, when he commanded the Santo Domingo army; after the cessation of hostilities he became very prominent in politics; he held several positions of trust and honor, and finally, in 1882, he was elected president; he served one term; in 1887 he again was placed in the presidential chair, and has been elected continuously ever since; and Heureaux faced dozens of revolutions during his long period of office holding, but he always came out victorious.
records.summary_es: El Tribune completa el despacho del asesinato con un bosquejo del presidente Heureaux: el asesinato fue a las cuatro y media de la tarde del miércoles; el nombre del asesino es Ramón Caceros; logró escapar, pero se inició de inmediato una persecución enérgica; el vicepresidente gen. Wenceslao Figuereo, inmediatamente después del anuncio de la muerte del presidente, asumió la dirección de los asuntos; en el presente prevalece la calma en todas partes de la república; y los restos del presidente Heureaux probablemente serán llevados a Santo Domingo para los servicios fúnebres. Ulysses Heureaux, el difunto presidente de Santo Domingo, nació cerca de 1838; poco se sabe de su vida temprana excepto que era un poder en la política de la pequeña república de las Indias Occidentales cuando era un hombre joven; su primera prominencia real fue alcanzada durante la guerra con los españoles en 1866, cuando comandó el ejército de Santo Domingo; después de la cesación de hostilidades llegó a ser muy prominente en la política; ocupó varias posiciones de confianza y honor, y finalmente, en 1882, fue elegido presidente; sirvió un término; en 1887 fue de nuevo puesto en la silla presidencial, y ha sido elegido continuamente desde entonces; y Heureaux enfrentó docenas de revoluciones durante su largo período de tenencia del cargo, pero siempre salió victorioso.

records.headline: The Journal prints part of a letter written in defense of General Gomez
records.summary_en: The Journal prints part of a letter written in defense of General Gomez: the letter names the killing of President Garfield, of the United States; Señor Canovas del Castillo, the Spanish premier, and President Carnot, of the French Republic. Continuing, the writer says: 'Some Cubans think they can get at him by means of this unfortunate occurrence, accusing him of aspiring to fill the place made vacant by the act of the assassin, forgetting that he aspires still higher. The history of his life proves that he prefers liberating those writing things against him. If Cuba cannot see a position to offer him after all his efforts, how could he see one in Santo Domingo? Besides, he is not accustomed to live by filling such positions. He is more inclined to a work which dignifies than to a post that enslaves. Those make a mistake who think he aspires to anything in Santo Domingo or Cuba. God forbid that he should be even an employe of high rank. He thinks it a veritable misfortune to be President, as on the field of battle a brave man exposes his life, while in the presidential chair he exposes his honor also, even if he has no valor. Jiminez is the man he hopes will be President of the Dominican Republic.'

records.headline: The Journal completes the Fort de France assassination dispatch
records.summary_en: The Journal completes the Fort de France assassination dispatch, prints President McKinley's message of condolence, and opens the July 28 details dispatch: the president's friends fired at the assassins, but it is not known whether any of them were wounded; the body of the president was taken to the palace of the governor of Moca; President Heureaux's death has caused a panic; it is said that Juan Isidoro Jimines, who took part in the attempted insurrection of June, 1898, is a candidate for the presidency, and that General Maximo Gomez, formerly president of the Cuban insurrectionists, a native of San Domingo, also aspires to the presidency; and the father of Caceres, the assassin, was put to death by order of President Heureaux in 1884. President McKinley's message, sent by direction through the State Department, offers to President Figuereo and the Dominican nation the most sincere condolences of the American people and his own. Wenceslao Figuereo is the officer next in line to President Heureaux and succeeds to the office of president. The July 28 dispatch says a financial crisis having arisen in San Domingo, and an insurrection being feared owing to the number of malcontents, President Heureaux went to the north and west of the island to prepare for all eventualities; he was about to leave Moca for Santiago de las Caballeros when he was killed.
records.summary_es: El Journal completa el despacho del asesinato de Fort de France, publica el mensaje de condolencia del presidente McKinley y abre el despacho de detalles del 28 de julio: los amigos del presidente dispararon contra los asesinos, pero no se sabe si alguno de ellos fue herido; el cuerpo del presidente fue llevado al palacio del gobernador de Moca; la muerte del presidente Heureaux ha causado pánico; se dice que Juan Isidoro Jimenes, quien tomó parte en la intentona insurreccional de junio de 1898, es candidato a la presidencia, y que el general Máximo Gómez, anteriormente presidente de los insurrectos cubanos, nativo de Santo Domingo, también aspira a la presidencia; y el padre de Cáceres, el asesino, fue ejecutado por orden del presidente Heureaux en 1884. El mensaje del presidente McKinley, enviado por su dirección a través del Departamento de Estado, ofrece al presidente Figuereo y a la nación dominicana las más sinceras condolencias del pueblo estadounidense y las suyas propias. Wenceslao Figuereo es el oficial que sigue en línea al presidente Heureaux y le sucede en el cargo de presidente. El despacho del 28 de julio dice que, habiendo surgido una crisis financiera en Santo Domingo, y temiéndose una insurrección por el número de descontentos, el presidente Heureaux fue al norte y al oeste de la isla para prepararse ante cualquier eventualidad; estaba a punto de salir de Moca hacia Santiago de los Caballeros cuando fue asesinado.

records.headline: The Tribune prints an editorial on Santo Domingo: the national debt of the Dominican republic
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints an editorial on Santo Domingo: the national debt of the Dominican republic has for some time been under the financial control of a company dominated by New York financiers, who bought it in cheaply from a syndicate in Holland, which had been unable to collect the interest; this American company took prompt possession of the Dominican custom houses and is now virtually the controlling power in the island; in addition to that, the leading steamship line is an American one, so that no matter what form of government exists down there, there is always a strong reason for American watchfulness. Under the Monroe doctrine, not likely since the Spanish war to be challenged by any European power, the only government which could intervene for purposes of pacification is that of the United States; the sending of warships and marines to the vicinity of Puerto Plata means that if a responsibility of this kind shall come through native chaos it will not be shirked; the United States is not aching for any more tropical wards, but if a further paternal oversight shall fall to it in the line of unsought duty the job will be accepted and completed with, let us hope, neatness and dispatch.
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica un editorial sobre Santo Domingo: la deuda nacional de la República Dominicana ha estado durante algún tiempo bajo el control financiero de una compañía dominada por financieros de Nueva York, quienes la compraron barata a un sindicato en Holanda, el cual no había podido cobrar los intereses; esta compañía estadounidense tomó pronta posesión de las aduanas dominicanas y es ahora virtualmente el poder controlador en la isla; además de eso, la línea de vapores principal es estadounidense, de modo que no importa qué forma de gobierno exista allí, siempre hay una fuerte razón para la vigilancia estadounidense. Bajo la doctrina Monroe, no siendo probable que desde la guerra española la desafíe ninguna potencia europea, el único gobierno que podría intervenir con fines de pacificación es el de los Estados Unidos; el envío de buques de guerra e infantes de marina a las cercanías de Puerto Plata significa que si una responsabilidad de este tipo llega a través del caos nativo no será eludida; los Estados Unidos no ansían más pupilos tropicales, pero si una adicional tutela paternal le corresponde en la línea del deber no buscado, el trabajo será aceptado y completado con, esperemos, pulcritud y rapidez.

records.headline: The Avalanche completes the assassination dispatch with a sketch of the late President Heureaux
records.summary_en: The Avalanche completes the assassination dispatch with a sketch of the late President Heureaux: the announcement of the president's death brought Vice-President Gen. Wenceslao Figuereo to the control of the government. Several attempts have been made before to take the life of President Heureaux, but they were frustrated: on one occasion, while passing through the arched entrance to the palace between lines of guards, his quick eye caught one of the soldiers, who appeared to lower his rifle in his direction; quickly pulling a revolver he shot the man dead in his tracks, passed on to his private office, where he gave orders to remove a dead man lying at the main entrance. Gen. Heureaux was born in Puerto Plata in 1840 and served in the war against Spain from 1868 to 1874; later he was put at the head of the advanced Dominicans, who sought to improve their country by inducing foreign capital to locate on the island; as he advanced all the wealthy inhabitants joined his forces, and when he arrived at the gates of the historic city of Santo Domingo he was chosen president of the republic and served his term of four years; at the expiration of every four years an electoral college assembles in the city to vote for a president for the following term, but owing to Gen. Heureaux's popularity and ability he has always been unanimously re-elected, and was serving his fifth term.

El gen. Heureaux nació en Puerto Plata en 1840 y sirvió en la guerra contra España desde 1868 hasta 1874; más tarde fue puesto a la cabeza de los dominicanos avanzados, que buscaban mejorar su país induciendo al capital extranjero a establecerse en la isla; a medida que avanzaba, todos los habitantes ricos se unieron a sus fuerzas, y cuando llegó a las puertas de la histórica ciudad de Santo Domingo fue elegido presidente de la república y sirvió su término de cuatro años; al expirar cada cuatro años un colegio electoral se reúne en la ciudad para votar por un presidente para el siguiente término, pero debido a la popularidad y habilidad del gen. Heureaux siempre ha sido reelecto por unanimidad, y estaba sirviendo su quinto término.

records.headline: The Democrat prints a Cape Haitien dispatch of July 30 and the Moscoso statement
records.summary_en: The Democrat prints a Cape Haitien dispatch of July 30 and the Moscoso statement from New York: the funeral of President Heureaux of San Domingo took place at 5 o'clock last evening in Santiago de las Caballeros; the population was panic stricken, but there was no disorder; a report has been received here to the effect that the adversaries of the government attacked Moca last night; the news of the death of the president was hardly credited here by the people generally until last evening, when undoubted confirmation was received, and then there was great rejoicing among the Dominican exiles, many of whom live in and around Cape Haitien; these exiles, who were driven out of their country by Heureaux, are now preparing to arm themselves and enter San Domingo, where they expect their chief, Don Juan Isidor Jiminez, to join them; and the Dominican government is making preparations on a large scale to maintain itself. Gen. Abelardo A. Moscoso, an exiled leader of the Liberal party of San Domingo, now living in New York, said last night: 'The death of President Heureaux will, I think, surely be followed by a long state of disorder and revolution. I want to emphasize this prophecy — that the United States will eventually be compelled to interfere to establish peace in the island, just as she did in Cuba. I favor the policy of peace. I shall be glad to return to my country and support such a policy if it is inaugurated by Gen. Figuera, the vice-president, who succeeds to the head of the government.'

records.headline: The Journal prints part of an editorial on Santo Domingo and annexation
records.summary_en: The Journal prints part of an editorial on Santo Domingo and annexation: Congress authorized the president to appoint a commission to investigate conditions and inclinations in the Dominican republic; this commission reported in 1871 that the people preferred independence, but believed that permanent independence was impossible, and therefore favored annexation; owing to radical differences of opinion, however, the subject was dropped with the printing of the report. There is probably no political significance in the sending of the cruisers New Orleans and Machias to Santo Domingo, as such action is entirely in accordance with precedent and is a prudential measure whenever American interests are threatened by such local disturbances; at the same time, in view of possible events, it may prove advantageous in more ways than one to have naval representation at hand in case of revolution. To say the least, the people of Santo Domingo would not ask in vain at this time for annexation to the United States; at the same time there is not the slightest possibility that they shall ever be annexed against their will.

records.summary_en: The Pioneer completes the assassination dispatch with a sketch of President Heureaux: the murderer is Ramon Caceros; he succeeded in making his escape, but an energetic pursuit was at once begun; Vice President Gen. Wenceslao Figuereo, immediately upon the announcement of the president's death, assumed the direction of affairs; at present calmness prevails everywhere in the republic; the remains of President Heureaux will probably be taken to Santo Domingo for the funeral services. Ulysses Heureaux, the late president of Santo Domingo, was born about 1838; little is known of his early life except that he was a power in the politics of the little West Indian republic when he was a young man; his first real prominence was attained during the war with the Spaniards in 1866, when he commanded the Santo Domingo army; after the cessation of hostilities he became very prominent in politics; he held several positions of trust and honor, and finally, in 1882, he was elected president; he served one term; in 1887 he again was placed in the presidential chair, and has been elected continuously ever since; Heureaux faced dozens of revolutions during his long period of office holding, but he always came out victorious.

records.headline: The Press-Journal prints part of an item on the crisis in Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The Press-Journal prints part of an item on the crisis in Santo Domingo and a Havana item headed 'Gomez on His Dignity': of the conspiracy which resulted in the assassination of President Heureaux, it is believed to be probable that it was planned and executed by partisans of Jiminez, the revolutionary leader; it is known that Heureaux had lived in fear of assassination for many months, and had frankly announced that he proposed to continue in the presidency as long as he lived; German interests in the republic are considerable, and President Heureaux was strongly backed by them; the future of the republic may depend largely upon the course taken by the foreign element in this crisis, and the course of the German government in the present crisis will be watched with considerable interest by the American government; the finances of San Domingo are in a bad way, and merchants doing business there have little hope of any material improvement, unless this government in some way takes control of matters. In the Havana item, General Gomez declared that a majority of the alleged interviews with him, published in the local papers, were entirely without foundation, and that he has decided to write himself anything he may hereafter have to say to the press: 'I believe all papers lie,' said Gomez, 'and that those of one country are in this respect no better than those of another. In future I will give over my own signature, or through the Associated Press alone, anything intended for publication.' General Gomez refused to discuss the presidency of the Dominican republic.

records.headline: The Courier completes a sketch of President Heureaux, with an account of the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: The Courier completes a sketch of President Heureaux, with an account of the Dominican Republic: Heureaux, after the cessation of hostilities, became very prominent in politics; he held several positions of trust and honor, and finally, in 1882, he was elected president; he served one term; in 1887 he again was placed in the presidential chair, and has been elected continuously ever since; Heureaux faced dozens of revolutions during his long period of office holding, but he always came out victorious. Last year, when the war between Spain and the United States was at its height, an expedition of filibusters was fitted out in the United States against Heureaux's government; it was given out that the expedition was intended for Cuba, but after the Americans had ceased to watch it a straight course was laid for the Dominican republic; Heureaux, however, had been apprised of the expedition, and when it reached Santo Domingo he was prepared to give it a warm reception; the filibusters were defeated. Under the head 'The Dominican Republic,' the paper says the republic occupies the eastern portion of the island of Hayti, which next to Cuba is the largest of the West Indian islands; its inhabitants are of Spanish, African and Indian descent and use the Spanish language; the president is assisted by a cabinet, and the legislative body is composed of 22 deputies elected by indirect popular vote; the population is estimated at between 416,000 and 610,000; the capital, Santo Domingo, has a population of 25,000; there are about 3,000 schools in the republic, and 40 newspapers are published.
records.summary_es: El Courier completa un bosquejo del presidente Heureaux, con una relación de la República Dominicana: Heureaux, después de la cesación de hostilidades, llegó a ser muy prominente en la política; ocupó varias posiciones de confianza y honor, y finalmente, en 1882, fue elegido presidente; sirvió un término; en 1887 fue de nuevo puesto en la silla presidencial, y ha sido elegido continuamente desde entonces; Heureaux enfrentó docenas de revoluciones durante su largo período de tenencia del cargo, pero siempre salió victorioso. El año pasado, cuando la guerra entre España y los Estados Unidos estaba en su apogeo, una expedición de filibusteros fue equipada en los Estados Unidos contra el gobierno de Heureaux; se dio a entender que la expedición estaba destinada a Cuba, pero después de que los estadounidenses dejaron de vigilarla se puso rumbo directo a la República Dominicana; Heureaux, sin embargo, había sido advertido de la expedición, y cuando esta llegó a Santo Domingo él estaba preparado para darle una cálida recepción; los filibusteros fueron derrotados. Bajo el título «The Dominican Republic», el periódico dice que la república ocupa la porción oriental de la isla de Haití, que junto a Cuba es la mayor de las islas de las Indias Occidentales; sus habitantes son de ascendencia española, africana e india y usan el idioma español; el presidente es asistido por un gabinete, y el cuerpo legislativo se compone de 22 diputados elegidos por voto popular indirecto; la población se estima entre 416,000 y 610,000; la capital, Santo Domingo, tiene una población de 25,000; hay unas 3,000 escuelas en la república, y se publican 40 periódicos.

records.headline: The Avalanche prints a Washington item on the warship orders
records.summary_en: The Avalanche prints a Washington item on the warship orders and the situation in Santo Domingo: Secretary Long Friday issued orders detaching the cruiser New Orleans from the North Atlantic squadron at Newport and directing her to proceed at once to Santo Domingo city; orders were issued also to the Machias at St. Thomas, to proceed to the same point via San Juan; these orders were made at the instance of the State Department and as a precautionary measure owing to the disturbed conditions following the assassination of President Heureaux of San Domingo. The trouble between the Government of San Domingo and its creditors has reached an acute stage; the creditors, who are almost entirely Americans, have begun to clamor for an American protectorate, which would necessarily be the first step in the direction of annexation. Political plots are already shaping themselves: the adherents of Gen. Jiminez seek to put him at the head of affairs, while the friends of Gen. Maximo Gomez are talking of making him the ruler of the republic; it is said by officers who have recently been in San Domingo that interference by this Government would be welcomed by a large proportion of the inhabitants of the island.

records.headline: The Observer prints part of an editorial on the San Domingo Improvement Company
records.summary_en: The Observer prints part of an editorial on the San Domingo Improvement Company: a company incorporated in New Jersey, known as the 'San Domingo Improvement Company of New York,' has acquired a concession in the republic; in 1888 the fiscal agents of the Dominican republic entered into convention with an Amsterdam firm for a loan of about $3,760,000, and to meet the payments on the loan the Holland company was given the right to collect directly the receipts from all custom houses in the republic, and the indebtedness was made a mortgage upon all the revenues of the country; in 1893 the rights of the Amsterdam bankers were transferred to the New York company, and by act of the Santo Domingo Congress the right of the Americans to collect the customs and port dues was reaffirmed. In the event of a revolution it will require the presence of several American warships to preserve the interest of the American company, and as a civil war would seriously reduce the revenues the administration may feel warranted to extend its protection to the extent of exerting force to maintain peace.

records.headline: The Gazette prints a Puerto Plata assassination dispatch of July 28
records.summary_en: The Gazette prints a Puerto Plata assassination dispatch of July 28 and part of a sketch of President Heureaux: President Ulysses Heureux of the republic was assassinated at Moca, a town in the interior, at 4:30 o'clock this afternoon; the murderer, whose name is Roman Caceros, succeeded in escaping, but an energetic pursuit has begun by the authorities, and it is possible that he will be captured; Vice-President Wenceslao Figuereo, immediately upon the announcement of the President's death, assumed the direction of affairs; at present calmness prevails everywhere in the republic; the body of President Heureux will probably be taken to San Domingo for the funeral services. The sketch says Gen. records.headline: The Gazette prints an account of the republic it calls Dominica
records.summary_en: The Gazette prints an account of the republic it calls Dominica and the details of the murder received at Cape Haytien: Dominica is the eastern part of the island, the western part being Haiti; it has been under French, Spanish and English domination at times, but has been a republic since 1841; the population is of mixed white, Indian and African descent, with few pure blacks; in November 1868, Bonaventura Baez, then president of Dominica, signed with President Grant a treaty for the annexation of the country to the United States, but the Senate at Washington refused to ratify it, though a commission which visited the island reported favorably. The details of the murder, received at Cape Haytien July 27, are to the effect that President Heureaux of Santo Domingo was assassinated as he was about to leave on horseback for Santiago de las Caballeros; the assassin, Ramon Caceros, surrounded by several accomplices, approached the President as he was talking with some friends and fired twice with a revolver; the first bullet struck the President in the left side and penetrated the heart, causing instant death; the second bullet killed an old man who was standing near the President; the assassin and his accomplices then fled to avoid the shots fired at them by the President's friends, and it is not known whether any of them was wounded; the body of the President was taken to the palace of the governor of Moca; President Heureaux's death has caused a panic.

records.headline: The Tribune prints a correction headed 'Grullon Not with the Firm'
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints a correction headed 'Grullon Not with the Firm' and a Washington item of August 2: Señor Adrianno Grullon, the representative in the United States of the revolutionary party in San Domingo and the former business partner of Señor J. Y. Jimenez, the leader of the insurrectionists, in making a statement on Tuesday night of the reasons why President Heureaux was assassinated, gave the impression that he was connected with the firm of Huttlinger Vivié, of No. 101 Pearl-st.; what he evidently intended to say was that he might be reached through this firm; the firm last night denied that Señor Grullon was identified in any way with their business, or that they represent Señor Jimenez and his followers in this country; they say, however: 'We, in common with the houses trading with San Domingo, are in full sympathy with the efforts to bring about reform in the deplorable administration of affairs in that republic.' The Washington item prints the report of Commander Logan of the Machias, which arrived at Santo Domingo City yesterday: the United States Consul says that the report of the death of the President of Santo Domingo is believed not to have any political significance; the motive of the assassin is supposed to be personal revenge; the Vice-President of Santo Domingo has succeeded without political disturbance and reappointed the former Cabinet; no disorder exists; and the commander requests permission to delay sailing five days to repair boiler. A further head reports Minister Powell's action approved by the State Department.
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica una corrección titulada «Grullon Not with the Firm» y una nota de Washington del 2 de agosto: el señor Adrianno Grullon, representante en los Estados Unidos del partido revolucionario en Santo Domingo y antiguo socio comercial del señor J. Y. Jimenes, el líder de los insurrectos, al hacer una declaración el martes por la noche sobre las razones por las que el presidente Heureaux fue asesinado, dio la impresión de que estaba conectado con la firma de Huttlinger Vivié, del No. 101 de Pearl-st.; lo que evidentemente quiso decir fue que se le podía localizar a través de esta firma; la firma negó anoche que el señor Grullon estuviera identificado de modo alguno con su negocio, o que ellos representen al señor Jimenes y sus seguidores en este país; dicen, sin embargo: «Nosotros, en común con las casas que comercian con Santo Domingo, simpatizamos plenamente con los esfuerzos por lograr una reforma en la deplorable administración de los asuntos en esa república». La nota de Washington publica el informe del comandante Logan del Machias, que llegó ayer a la ciudad de Santo Domingo: el cónsul de los Estados Unidos dice que se cree que el reporte de la muerte del presidente de Santo Domingo no tiene ningún significado político; se supone que el móvil del asesino fue venganza personal; el vicepresidente de Santo Domingo ha sucedido sin perturbación política y ha vuelto a nombrar al gabinete anterior; no existe desorden; y el comandante solicita permiso para demorar la salida cinco días para reparar la caldera. Un título adicional reporta la acción del ministro Powell aprobada por el Departamento de Estado.

records.headline: The Register completes a cable item on the revolution in Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The Register completes a cable item on the revolution in Santo Domingo and prints the Puerto Plata dispatch of July 31 headed 'The Situation Is Critical': the private cablegram says demoralization is growing through the death of the president; in the event of the revolution succeeding still, it is probable that Jiminez and the other reputed leaders of the revolution will agree to retire, offering the presidency to Gen. Maximo Gomez, who would prove acceptable to all parties; a deputation, it is reported, is going to Cuba to confer with Gen. Gomez. The Puerto Plata dispatch says the situation is critical and an outbreak is momentarily expected; the friends of the government are under arms and ready for action to protect property and preserve the peace; a feeble attempt was made to seize the body of President Heureaux by the assassins Ramon Caceres, Manuel Caceres, Horacio Vasquez and Domingo Pichardo, who are in the country about Moca with their followers; the burial of President Heureaux was conducted with fitting honors; Gov. Pepin has assembled troops in Moca, and the governor of La Vega has 1,000 men; the minister of the treasury has arrived at Moca in hot haste; the government is taking steps for the protection of business and the finance of the country, and expects to carry out the contemplated cancellation of the state bank notes; in Puerto Plata there is an urgent demand that the government send a sufficient force to Moca to hunt down the assassins of the president.

records.headline: The Press completes the assassination dispatch, prints a Washington item of July 27
records.summary_en: The Press completes the assassination dispatch, prints a Washington item of July 27 headed 'Not Officially Notified,' and opens a sketch headed 'Heureaux's Career': the remains of President Heureaux will probably be taken to Santo Domingo for the funeral services. The Washington item says no information was received up to half past nine o'clock Wednesday night from the consular representatives of the United States in Santo Domingo regarding the assassination there Wednesday of President Heureaux; pending official advices of the assassination, no formal action will be taken by this government; Hon. William F. Powell, the minister to Hayti, is also chargé d'affaires to Santo Domingo, and this government is directly represented in the republic in the person of Campbell L. Maxwell, who is consul general, and John A. Read, who is vice consul; officials here recall that attempts have been made heretofore on the life of Mr. Heureaux. The sketch says Ulysses Heureaux, the late president of Santo Domingo, was born about 1838; little is known of his early life except that he was a power in the politics of the little West Indian republic when he was a young man; his first real prominence was attained during the war with the Spaniards in 1866, when he commanded the Santo Domingo army; after the cessation of hostilities he became very prominent in politics; he held several positions of trust and honor, and finally was elected president; he served one term; he was again placed in the presidential chair, and has been elected continuously ever since; Heureaux faced dozens of revolutions during his long period of office holding, but he always came out victorious.
records.summary_es: El Press completa el despacho sobre el asesinato, publica una nota de Washington del 27 de julio titulada «Not Officially Notified» y abre un retrato titulado «Heureaux's Career»: los restos del presidente Heureaux probablemente serán llevados a Santo Domingo para los servicios fúnebres. La nota de Washington dice que hasta las nueve y media de la noche del miércoles no se había recibido información de los representantes consulares de los Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo respecto al asesinato allí el miércoles del presidente Heureaux; a la espera de noticias oficiales del asesinato, este gobierno no tomará ninguna acción formal; el honorable William F. Powell, ministro en Haití, es también encargado de negocios ante Santo Domingo, y este gobierno está representado directamente en la república en la persona de Campbell L. Maxwell, cónsul general, y John A. Read, vicecónsul; los funcionarios aquí recuerdan que anteriormente se han hecho atentados contra la vida del señor Heureaux. El retrato dice que Ulises Heureaux, difunto presidente de Santo Domingo, nació hacia 1838; poco se sabe de su vida temprana, salvo que era una potencia en la política de la pequeña república antillana cuando era joven; su primera prominencia real la alcanzó durante la guerra con los españoles en 1866, cuando comandó el ejército de Santo Domingo; tras el cese de las hostilidades se volvió muy prominente en la política; ocupó varios cargos de confianza y honor, y finalmente fue elegido presidente; cumplió un período; fue colocado de nuevo en la silla presidencial, y ha sido elegido continuamente desde entonces; Heureaux enfrentó docenas de revoluciones durante su largo período en el cargo, pero siempre salió victorioso.

records.headline: The Republican prints the Grullon statement issued at New York
records.summary_en: The Republican prints the Grullon statement issued at New York, headed 'The Assassination of Heureaux': Adrianno Grullon, of Huttlinger Vivié, New York, the representative in the United States of the San Domingo revolutionists, and formerly the business partner of Señor Jiminez, leader of the insurrection, Tuesday night made public at New York a statement, which in part is as follows: 'The assassination of President Heureaux was not an act of revenge for the murder of Caceres's father, but the signal for the commencement of the uprising against the existing government there. Caceres is the cousin of Gen. Horacio Vasquez, and was with him at the time of the shooting. Gen. Vasquez is a member of one of the best families of Moca. Neither Mr. Caceres nor Gen. Vasquez can be considered common assassins, as their motives were not personal, but patriotic. They attacked the president in broad daylight, in an open space, and not from ambush, although their little party was outnumbered two to one by the president and his body guard. For 14 years Heureaux has held power by a system of terrorizing: citizens were sent to prison without the slightest process of law, and more than 300 were clandestinely shot, without any trial whatever or without even being given a reason for their incarceration. There has been no legal election of any kind since 1889, and then Heureaux retained power through a fraudulent count.'

Cáceres es primo del general Horacio Vásquez y estaba con él en el momento del tiroteo. El general Vásquez es miembro de una de las mejores familias de Moca. Ni el señor Cáceres ni el general Vásquez pueden ser considerados asesinos comunes, pues sus motivos no fueron personales, sino patrióticos. Atacaron al presidente a plena luz del día, en un espacio abierto y no desde una emboscada, aunque su pequeño grupo era superado dos a uno por el presidente y su guardia. Durante 14 años Heureaux ha mantenido el poder mediante un sistema de terror: ciudadanos fueron enviados a prisión sin el menor proceso legal, y más de 300 fueron fusilados clandestinamente, sin juicio alguno ni siquiera una razón para su encarcelamiento. No ha habido elección legal de ninguna clase desde 1889, y entonces Heureaux retuvo el poder mediante un conteo fraudulento».

records.headline: The Chronicle prints the funeral dispatch from Fort de France
records.summary_en: The Chronicle prints the funeral dispatch from Fort de France on the burial of President Heureaux, under the heads 'Murdered President Buried' and 'Revolution Threatened on Island of Santo Domingo': advices from Fort de France, Martinique, state that the funeral services over the remains of President Heureaux, which took place at Santiago de las Caballeros at 5 o'clock Thursday evening, were attended by a large number of people and were conducted with great solemnity; the body, which had lain in state throughout the day, was buried in the cathedral; the governor of the province superintended the public mourning; throughout the island cannon were fired hourly, and flags were placed at half mast on all public buildings; the government has issued a decree ordering a period of national mourning for nine days; the city of Santo Domingo is in a state of great unrest and business is entirely suspended, and the people fear an outbreak; Thursday night a band of armed men attacked Moca, where President Heureaux was killed, and fired a number of shots; it is reported that the forces supporting the assassin have been augmented considerably; the government has taken measures to put down the threatened insurrection; William F. Powell, United States minister to Hayti and American diplomatic representative to the republic of Santo Domingo, sent a telegram to Vice President Figuereo, who assumed the presidency, expressing the keen regret of the United States government at the assassination of President Heureaux; and the latest news from Santo Domingo is that all is quiet.
records.summary_es: El Chronicle publica el despacho fúnebre desde Fort-de-France sobre el entierro del presidente Heureaux, bajo los títulos «Murdered President Buried» y «Revolution Threatened on Island of Santo Domingo»: noticias procedentes de Fort-de-France, Martinica, afirman que los servicios fúnebres por los restos del presidente Heureaux, celebrados en Santiago de los Caballeros a las cinco de la tarde del jueves, contaron con la asistencia de gran número de personas y se realizaron con gran solemnidad; el cuerpo, que había estado expuesto todo el día, fue enterrado en la catedral; el gobernador de la provincia supervisó el duelo público; en toda la isla se dispararon cañones cada hora y las banderas se colocaron a media asta en todos los edificios públicos; el gobierno ha emitido un decreto que ordena un período de luto nacional de nueve días; la ciudad de Santo Domingo se encuentra en un estado de gran agitación y los negocios están totalmente suspendidos, y el pueblo teme un estallido; el jueves por la noche una banda de hombres armados atacó Moca, donde fue asesinado el presidente Heureaux, y disparó numerosos tiros; se informa que las fuerzas que apoyan al asesino han aumentado considerablemente; el gobierno ha tomado medidas para sofocar la insurrección amenazante; William F. Powell, ministro de los Estados Unidos en Haití y representante diplomático estadounidense ante la república de Santo Domingo, envió un telegrama al vicepresidente Figuereo, que asumió la presidencia, expresando la profunda pena del gobierno de los Estados Unidos por el asesinato del presidente Heureaux; y las últimas noticias de Santo Domingo son que todo está en calma.

records.summary_en: The Journal prints the closing words of a dispatch on the revolution in Santo Domingo — 'with several other generals, each commanding fairly important forces' — and a Kingston item of August 3 headed 'Curb America's Ambition': owing to the efforts of the government of Santo Domingo to suppress news and information about the recent assassination of President Heureaux, and the reported revolution in Santo Domingo, the facts in the case are difficult to obtain; but a dispatch received by a passenger who has passed through Hayti indicates that the assassination of President Heureaux was not on the programme, the purpose of the revolutionists being to capture Moca with the president, thus decapitating the Dominican government at the first blow.

records.headline: The Bee prints an editorial on Santo Domingo: the Dominican republic
records.summary_en: The Bee prints an editorial on Santo Domingo: the Dominican republic has very little in common with the United States; its population of about 600,000 people is composed of a mixed race of Spanish, Indian and African descent; its government is nominally republican, but its late president, who has just fallen by the hand of an assassin, was in reality a cruel tyrant, who scrupled at nothing to rid himself of political rivals; a country so governed, with frequent attempts at revolution, with financial affairs in a low condition, and with a population entirely alien to American institutions and ideas — what greater folly would there be than to annex Santo Domingo to the United States? We certainly do not want the Dominican republic upon our hands.
records.summary_es: El Bee publica un editorial sobre Santo Domingo: la república dominicana tiene muy poco en común con los Estados Unidos; su población de unas 600,000 personas está compuesta por una raza mixta de ascendencia española, india y africana; su gobierno es nominalmente republicano, pero su difunto presidente, que acaba de caer por mano de un asesino, era en realidad un tirano cruel, que no reparaba en nada para deshacerse de sus rivales políticos; un país así gobernado, con frecuentes intentos de revolución, con sus asuntos financieros en baja condición y con una población enteramente ajena a las instituciones e ideas estadounidenses: ¿qué mayor locura habría que anexar Santo Domingo a los Estados Unidos? Ciertamente no queremos la república dominicana sobre nuestras manos.

records.headline: A Puerto Plata dispatch dated August 1 calls the situation in Santo Domingo critical after President Heureaux's
records.summary_en: A Puerto Plata dispatch dated August 1 calls the situation in Santo Domingo critical after President Heureaux's assassination, with an outbreak expected at any moment and friends of the government under arms to protect property and preserve the peace. It says the assassins, Ramón Cáceres, Manuel Cáceres, Horacio Vásquez and Domingo Pichardo, were in the country about Moca with their followers, that the president was buried with military honors, and that troops were being assembled at Moca and La Vega.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Puerto Plata fechado el 1 de agosto califica de crítica la situación en Santo Domingo tras el asesinato del presidente Heureaux, con un estallido esperado en cualquier momento y los amigos del gobierno en armas para proteger la propiedad y preservar la paz. Dice que los asesinos, Ramón Cáceres, Manuel Cáceres, Horacio Vásquez y Domingo Pichardo, estaban en el campo cerca de Moca con sus seguidores, que el presidente fue enterrado con honores militares, y que se estaban reuniendo tropas en Moca y La Vega.

Gomez Will Be Offered the Presidency. Puerto Plata, Santo Domingo, Aug. [illegible]—The situation is critical. An [illegible] is momentarily expected. A feeble attempt was made to seize the body of President Heureaux the assassins, Ramon Caceres, Manuel Caceres, Horacio Vasquez and Domingo [Pichardo?] who are in the country, about [Macoris?] with their followers. The minister of the treasury has arrived at Cuba to confer with Gen. Gomez.

records.headline: News from Puerto Plata reports an urgent demand that the government send a sufficient force to Moca to hunt down the assassins of President Heureaux.
records.summary_en: News from Puerto Plata reports an urgent demand that the government send a sufficient force to Moca to hunt down the assassins of President Heureaux. A private cable dispatch received at Kingston, Jamaica, on August 1 says the revolution in San Domingo is progressing favorably, that Heureaux's body was held and buried at Santiago because the country between Santiago and Puerto Plata is occupied by insurgents who are concentrating to attack the feebly garrisoned Puerto Plata, and that if the revolution succeeds Jiminez and his fellow leader will likely retire and offer the presidency to General Maximo Gomez.
records.summary_es: Noticias desde Puerto Plata informan de una exigencia urgente de que el gobierno envíe una fuerza suficiente a Moca para perseguir a los asesinos del presidente Heureaux. Un despacho privado por cable recibido en Kingston, Jamaica, el 1 de agosto dice que la revolución en Santo Domingo avanza favorablemente, que el cadáver de Heureaux fue retenido y enterrado en Santiago porque el territorio entre Santiago y Puerto Plata está ocupado por insurgentes que se concentran para atacar Puerto Plata, escasamente guarnecida, y que si la revolución triunfa Jiminez y su compañero líder probablemente se retirarán y ofrecerán la presidencia al general Maximo Gomez.

Gen. [Gomez?] for President. Kingston, Jam., Aug. 1.—A private cable dispatch received here by way of Cape Haitien reports that the revolution in San Domingo is progressing favorably. The dispatch says that the real reason for the holding of Heureaux's body at Santiago, and its interment there, was that the country between Santiago and Porto Plata is occupied by the insurgents, who, abandoning their plan of occupying Moca as a base of operations, are concentrating to attack Porto Plata, which is feebly garrisoned. Great excitement prevails owing to the fact that the government has not been able to ascertain the extent of the ramifications of the revolution and is growing demoralized through the death of the president. records.headline: The Journal completes the Kingston dispatch, prints the Gleaner's comment
records.summary_en: The Journal completes the Kingston dispatch, prints the Gleaner's comment on American intervention, and prints a Cape Haytien dispatch of August 3: the insurgents not possessing the means of prosecuting a protracted conflict, the premature departure of President Heureaux threatened to frustrate this scheme, whereupon an enthusiast, who was watching the President's movements, committed the act; a subsequent attack on Moca being repulsed, the insurgents withdrew into the fastnesses between Moca and Porto Plata, hoping to secure sufficient accessions of men and arms to attack Porto Plata and prosecute the movement in spite of its initial failure. Commenting on a London cablegram relative to possible American intervention in Santo Domingo, the Gleaner, under the head 'Would Curb America's Ambition,' to-day says it anticipates the 'finding of an excuse to add the island of Hayti to the string of Antillian gems on the new colonial diadem,' and invokes the powers to 'curb America's ambition.' The Cape Haytien dispatch says it has just become known that an armed insurrection has broken out at La Vega, a town seventy-eight miles northwest of Santo Domingo, in favor of Jiminez, who aspires to the presidency in succession to the late President Heureaux; later advices from the Dominican Republic indicate that the revolution is growing in strength; at Santiago de la Cruz five hundred well-armed men have risen, under the command of General Ramon Pacheco, and General P. Reyes, who is very influential in those districts, has joined the insurgents with several other generals, each commanding fairly important forces.
records.summary_es: El Journal completa el despacho de Kingston, publica el comentario del Gleaner sobre la intervención estadounidense y publica un despacho de Cabo Haitiano del 3 de agosto: al no poseer los insurrectos los medios para sostener un conflicto prolongado, la partida prematura del presidente Heureaux amenazó con frustrar este plan, ante lo cual un entusiasta, que vigilaba los movimientos del presidente, cometió el acto; rechazado un ataque posterior contra Moca, los insurrectos se retiraron a las asperezas entre Moca y Puerto Plata, con la esperanza de conseguir suficientes refuerzos de hombres y armas para atacar Puerto Plata y proseguir el movimiento a pesar de su fracaso inicial. Al comentar un cablegrama de Londres relativo a una posible intervención estadounidense en Santo Domingo, el Gleaner, bajo el título «Would Curb America's Ambition», dice hoy que anticipa «que se encontrará una excusa para añadir la isla de Haití a la cuerda de gemas antillanas en la nueva diadema colonial», e invoca a las potencias a «frenar la ambición de América». El despacho de Cabo Haitiano dice que se ha sabido que ha estallado una insurrección armada en La Vega, pueblo situado a setenta y ocho millas al noroeste de Santo Domingo, a favor de Jiménez, que aspira a la presidencia en sucesión del difunto presidente Heureaux; noticias posteriores procedentes de la República Dominicana indican que la revolución crece en fuerza; en Santiago de la Cruz se han levantado quinientos hombres bien armados, bajo el mando del general Ramón Pacheco, y el general P. Reyes, muy influyente en esos distritos, se ha unido a los insurrectos, con varios otros generales, cada uno al mando de fuerzas bastante importantes.
