records.headline: The Eagle opens a narrative feature on Don Juan Isidro Jiminez
records.summary_en: The Eagle opens a narrative feature on Don Juan Isidro Jiminez, the present aspirant to the presidential chair, who was the leading opponent of the late President Heureaux: it accounts for some hitherto mysterious movements of the steamship Fanita, which was libeled in Mobile, liberated and sailed, ostensibly for Cuba with arms for the insurgents, but in reality made a daring dash for San Domingo to take the island by storm, only to meet with defeat and flight; it explains the interest the War Department took in the trial of Jiminez on British soil, in the Bahamas, and how the United States settled with the little island republic; and, on the whole, considering the present unsettled condition of San Domingo, and the possibility of Jiminez gaining the ascendency, the recital will be of interest. San Domingo, the feature says, is a very beautiful, fruitful, but not a very big island; in fact, there is room for but one big man there at a time — this was the conviction of the late President Heureaux, who was the one big man; there was another, however, Don Juan Isidro Jiminez, a rich merchant with immense plantations on the island, great warehouses and commercial branches in New York, Hamburg and other cities of the world, and a great traveler, which contributed to his longevity; but every time he landed the island sagged considerably in that direction, and this displeased President Heureaux, whose palace was in the interior, and who rarely went to the shore for fear that the island would capsize with his weight.
records.summary_es: The Eagle abre un reportaje narrativo sobre don Juan Isidro Jiminez, el actual aspirante a la silla presidencial, quien fue el principal opositor del fallecido presidente Heureaux: da cuenta de algunos movimientos hasta ahora misteriosos del vapor Fanita, que fue embargado en Mobile, liberado y zarpó, ostensiblemente hacia Cuba con armas para los insurgentes, pero en realidad hizo una audaz carrera hacia San Domingo para tomar la isla por asalto, solo para encontrarse con la derrota y la huida; explica el interés que el Departamento de Guerra tomó en el juicio de Jiminez en suelo británico, en las Bahamas, y cómo los Estados Unidos se arreglaron con la pequeña república isleña; y, en conjunto, considerando la actual situación inestable de San Domingo y la posibilidad de que Jiminez alcance el ascendiente, el relato será de interés. San Domingo, dice el reportaje, es una isla muy hermosa y fértil, pero no muy grande; de hecho, allí solo hay espacio para un gran hombre a la vez: esa era la convicción del fallecido presidente Heureaux, quien era el gran hombre; había otro, sin embargo, don Juan Isidro Jiminez, un rico comerciante con inmensas plantaciones en la isla, grandes almacenes y sucursales comerciales en Nueva York, Hamburgo y otras ciudades del mundo, y un gran viajero, lo que contribuyó a su longevidad; pero cada vez que desembarcaba, la isla se hundía considerablemente en esa dirección, y eso disgustaba al presidente Heureaux, cuyo palacio estaba en el interior y que rara vez iba a la costa por temor a que la isla volcara con su peso.

records.headline: The Eagle continues its narrative feature with the island trade
records.summary_en: The Eagle continues its narrative feature with the island trade and the dinner at which President Heureaux warns General Jiminez against his growing popularity: the trade runs from the exportation of logwood to the French wine growers to the importation of Ansonia clocks, which were quite recherché among the Dominican elite as neck ornaments. 'General Jiminez,' the president said gravely, 'it is with interesting apprehension that the presidential prerogative views your growing popularity. You are a rich man, a benevolent man, and a just man, so far as you can judge by foreign standards. You are well liked at the custom house, so I understand, and it seems to be mutual.' General Don Juan smiled proudly. 'Now General, while you are growing richer, the presidential prerogative regrets to say the island is growing poorer. I am going to perform a grand coup. I am going to float a many million dollar loan with the Americans, and I am going to rebond the customs of San Domingo as security. I am going to allow the foreigner to sit in the seat of customs, and you know, General Jiminez, these people have riches back of their heads. Take heed, then. Make yourself less popular. Popularity is a growing disease on the island. Check yours in the incipient stage or it will be fatal. Remember, during my sixteen years of divine prerogative gentlemen of the island have been picked off because of these growing pains of popularity.'

records.headline: The Eagle prints, in a later part of its narrative feature
records.summary_en: The Eagle prints, in a later part of its narrative feature, a statement in behalf of Jiminez: the revolutionists will not interfere in any way with the property of foreigners on the island; notwithstanding the many revolutions which have taken place in San Domingo since it attained its independence, in no instance has either life been taken or property molested of any foreigner, with the single exception of the action of Heureaux, who opened the vaults of the French bank because of a personal quarrel with one of its directors; women and children are safe at all times, as the Dominicans never stoop to war with the helpless, nor do they ever sack or pillage, but fight for what they believe to be right in the open, as men and soldiers should do. 'The entire country is aroused to the necessity of a change to a government where life is secure, and it recognizes that the former vice president and the present pretending president is but one of the accomplices of Heureaux, and as such has no confidence in him. There is but one man who at this time represents the people and their best interests, and that is Jiminez, and if an opportunity is given to the people they will prove it by their ballots. But if none is accorded in that way, then force will be used.'
records.summary_es: The Eagle publica, en una parte posterior de su reportaje narrativo, una declaración a favor de Jiminez: los revolucionarios no interferirán en modo alguno con la propiedad de los extranjeros en la isla; a pesar de las muchas revoluciones que han tenido lugar en San Domingo desde que alcanzó su independencia, en ningún caso se ha quitado la vida ni se ha molestado la propiedad de ningún extranjero, con la única excepción de la acción de Heureaux, quien abrió las bóvedas del banco francés por una disputa personal con uno de sus directores; las mujeres y los niños están seguros en todo momento, pues los dominicanos nunca se rebajan a hacer la guerra a los indefensos, ni saquean ni pillan, sino que luchan por lo que creen justo a campo abierto, como deben hacerlo los hombres y los soldados. 'Todo el país está despertado ante la necesidad de un cambio hacia un gobierno donde la vida esté segura, y reconoce que el exvicepresidente y el actual presidente pretendiente no es más que uno de los cómplices de Heureaux, y como tal no tiene confianza en él. Solo hay un hombre que en este momento representa al pueblo y sus mejores intereses, y ese es Jiminez, y si se le da una oportunidad al pueblo, lo probará con sus votos. Pero si no se le concede de esa manera, entonces se usará la fuerza'.

records.headline: The Silver State prints the close of a dispatch on the revolution
records.summary_en: The Silver State prints the close of a dispatch on the revolution, a Puerto Plata dispatch of August 9 headed 'Arms Seized', and a Philadelphia item of August 9 headed 'Don't Like Sam': the forces of Don Juan Isidro Jiminez, the leader of the revolution, are being augmented every day, and news from every part of the Dominican Republic is favorable to him. The Puerto Plata dispatch says the Haytien government has seized at Fort Liberte arms and ammunition destined for Dominican insurgents; several Dominicans in Hayti have been arrested for violating the neutrality laws, among them Francisco Deetjen, in whose keeping arms were found; President Sam of Hayti has wired the Dominican government that insurgents will not be permitted to use Haytien territory as a base of operations; and the force for the government under the command of Minister Cordero has encountered insurgents led by General Pablo Reyes. The Philadelphia item says three officers representing the insurgents of San Domingo and two civilians, representing those who do not like the manner in which President Sam manages affairs in Hayti, have been here three days endeavoring to find vessels to carry munitions of war recently purchased in New Haven; to avoid suspicion, all the members of the party crossed the Windward passage in small boats and embarked on a steamship at Guantanamo, landing last week in New York; those from San Domingo were delayed by the capsizing of a boat; and they claim that there is little danger in landing contraband war material anywhere on the coast of either country, except near the principal ports, as the coasts are not patrolled.
records.summary_es: The Silver State publica el cierre de un despacho sobre la revolución, un despacho de Puerto Plata del 9 de agosto titulado 'Arms Seized', y una nota de Filadelfia del 9 de agosto titulada 'Don't Like Sam': las fuerzas de don Juan Isidro Jiminez, el líder de la revolución, aumentan cada día, y las noticias de todas partes de la República Dominicana le son favorables. El despacho de Puerto Plata dice que el gobierno haitiano ha incautado en Fuerte Libertad armas y municiones destinadas a los insurgentes dominicanos; varios dominicanos en Haití han sido arrestados por violar las leyes de neutralidad, entre ellos Francisco Deetjen, en cuyo poder se encontraron armas; el presidente Sam, de Haití, ha cablegrafiado al gobierno dominicano que no se permitirá a los insurgentes usar el territorio haitiano como base de operaciones; y la fuerza del gobierno bajo el mando del ministro Cordero se ha encontrado con insurgentes dirigidos por el general Pablo Reyes. La nota de Filadelfia dice que tres oficiales que representan a los insurgentes de San Domingo y dos civiles, que representan a quienes no les gusta la manera en que el presidente Sam maneja los asuntos en Haití, llevan tres días aquí tratando de encontrar buques para transportar municiones de guerra compradas recientemente en New Haven; para evitar sospechas, todos los miembros del grupo cruzaron el Paso de los Vientos en pequeños botes y se embarcaron en un vapor en Guantánamo, desembarcando la semana pasada en Nueva York; los de San Domingo se retrasaron por el vuelco de un bote; y afirman que hay poco peligro en desembarcar material de guerra de contrabando en cualquier punto de la costa de cualquiera de los dos países, excepto cerca de los puertos principales, pues las costas no son patrulladas.

records.headline: The State Journal prints the close of a dispatch on the revolution
records.summary_en: The State Journal prints the close of a dispatch on the revolution, a New York item of August 9 headed 'Can't Land in Hayti', and a Philadelphia item of August 9 headed 'Filibusters Active': the forces of Don Juan Isidro Jiminez, leader of the revolution, are being augmented every day and the news from all parts of the Dominican republic is favorable to him. The New York item, a Herald dispatch from Port Au Prince, Hayti, says word comes from Monte Christi that Dominican troops have been hurried there; the Haytien government is prepared to prevent Jiminez from landing on Haytien territory; all is quiet in Port Au Prince; and suspects are being interrogated by the authorities. The Philadelphia item, from a morning paper, says three officers representing the insurgents of San Domingo and two civilians, representing those who do not like the manner in which President Sam manages affairs in Hayti, have been here three days endeavoring to find vessels to carry munitions of war recently purchased in New Haven; to avoid suspicion, all the members of the party crossed the Windward passage in small boats and embarked on a steamship at Guantanamo, landing last week in New York; those from San Domingo were delayed by the capsizing of a boat; and they claim that there is little danger in landing contraband war material anywhere on the coast of either country, except near the principal ports, as the coasts are not patrolled, because neither of the governments has war vessels to do the work.

records.headline: Ties can be paid In American sold or national silver
records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Journal* reported on Dominican fiscal measures requiring a portion of customs duties to be paid in paper currency, which would be publicly burned each month to retire the circulating paper notes. Concurrently, Dominican revolutionary forces crossed from Ouanaminthe, Haiti, and captured the border town of Dajabon, forcing the local garrison to retreat to Fort Belair. The report noted expectations that rebel leader General Jimenes would soon land to take direct command, despite Haitian efforts to prevent his transit.
records.summary_es: El *Indianapolis Journal* informó sobre las medidas fiscales dominicanas que exigían el pago de una porción de los aranceles aduaneros en papel moneda, el cual se quemaría públicamente cada mes para retirar los billetes en circulación. Al mismo tiempo, fuerzas revolucionarias dominicanas cruzaron desde Ouanaminthe, Haití, y tomaron la localidad fronteriza de Dajabón, obligando a la guarnición local a replegarse hacia Fort Belair. El informe señalaba la expectativa de que el líder rebelde general Jimenes desembarcara en breve para asumir el mando directo, pese a los esfuerzos haitianos por impedir su paso.
records.passage: ties can be paid in American gold or national silver or paper money, but [illegible] per cent. of the same must be paid in paper money to a special commission named by the government in the different ports. This commission will be instructed to burn publicly the amount received during each month. The law is to remain in force until all paper money in circulation shall have been taken up. According to a former law now in force a certain part of the export dues is applied for the same purpose. A favorable change in the financial situation is expected if the government bill is approved by Congress. Judging by the latest news received from the interior of the republic the country is quiet. PORT-AU-PRINCE, Haiti, Aug. 8. — The revolutionary Dominican troops which assembled at Ouanaminthe have crossed the frontier and have taken possession of Dajabon. The garrison at that place retired to Fort Belair, a strategic position commanding the town. The foreign population and the Haitian consul left the place. records.full_text:
GENERALS DECLARE FOR JIMINEZ.

Havana, Aug. 8.—General Juan Isidro Jiminez, the aspirant to the Presidency of the Dominican Republic, says that several Dominican generals have already declared in his favor, in spite of his advice to them to delay definite action. He denies that the Dominican Government has 3,700 troops under arms, and asserts that the present Executive will not be able to make an effective resistance, owing to the scarcity of resources and sympathizers.

FILIBUSTERS General Brooke Has Issued Orders to Suppress Them

WASHINGTON, Aug 9.—General Brooke has been given instructions to prevent, at all hazards, any filibustering expedition by Jiminez in the interest of people living in Cuba.

According to the views of officials here, and evidently also those of the president and Secretary Root, the United States is as much obligated to prevent a violation of the neutrality laws in Cuba as in the United States.

records.summary_en: The paper reports that Dominican revolutionary troops assembled at Ouanaminthe crossed the frontier and took Dajabón, while its garrison retired to Fort Belair and the foreign population and Haitian consul left. It says leader Jiménez was expected to land to join them, and Haiti was taking measures to prevent him landing there.
records.summary_es: El periódico informa que tropas revolucionarias dominicanas reunidas en Ouanaminthe cruzaron la frontera y tomaron Dajabón, mientras su guarnición se retiraba a Fort Belair y la población extranjera y el cónsul haitiano abandonaban el lugar. Dice que se esperaba que el líder Jiménez desembarcara para unirse a ellos, y que Haití tomaba medidas para impedir su desembarco allí.

records.headline: The Eagle prints the closing words of a dispatch on the revolution
records.summary_en: The Eagle prints the closing words of a dispatch on the revolution, a Puerto Plata dispatch of August 9, and two New York items of August 9: the news from all parts of the Dominican republic is favorable to Jiminez. The Puerto Plata dispatch says the Haytien government has seized at Fort Liberte arms and ammunition destined for Dominican insurgents; several Dominicans in Hayti have been arrested for violating the neutrality laws, among them Francisco Deetjen, in whose keeping arms were found; President Sam, of Hayti, has wired the Dominican government that insurgents will not be permitted to use Haytien territory as a base of operations; and the force for the government under the command of Minister Cordero has encountered insurgents led by General Pablo Reyes. A special to the Herald from Washington says General Brooke was given instructions today to prevent at all hazards any filibustering expedition in Jiminez's interests leaving Cuba; the charge d'affaires of the Dominican republic in this country has called the attention of the authorities to the contemplated expedition and he was assured that everything possible would be done to prevent any such proceedings. A dispatch to the Herald from Port Au Prince, Hayti, says word comes from Monte Christi that Dominican troops have been hurried there; the Haytien government is prepared to prevent Jiminez from landing on Haytien territory; all is quiet in Port Au Prince; and suspects are being interrogated by the authorities.
records.summary_es: El Eagle publica las palabras finales de un despacho sobre la revolución, un despacho de Puerto Plata del 9 de agosto y dos noticias de Nueva York del 9 de agosto: las noticias de todas partes de la república dominicana son favorables a Jiménez. El despacho de Puerto Plata dice que el gobierno haitiano ha incautado en Fuerte Libertad armas y municiones destinadas a los insurgentes dominicanos; varios dominicanos en Haití han sido arrestados por violar las leyes de neutralidad, entre ellos Francisco Deetjen, en cuyo poder se encontraron armas; el presidente Sam, de Haití, ha telegrafiado al gobierno dominicano que no se permitirá a los insurgentes usar el territorio haitiano como base de operaciones; y la fuerza del gobierno bajo el mando del ministro Cordero se ha encontrado con insurgentes dirigidos por el general Pablo Reyes. Una nota especial al Herald desde Washington dice que el general Brooke recibió hoy instrucciones de impedir a toda costa que cualquier expedición filibustera en interés de Jiménez salga de Cuba; el encargado de negocios de la república dominicana en este país ha llamado la atención de las autoridades sobre la expedición proyectada y se le aseguró que se haría todo lo posible para impedir tales procedimientos. Un despacho al Herald desde Puerto Príncipe, Haití, dice que llegan noticias de Monte Cristi de que tropas dominicanas han sido enviadas allí con urgencia; el gobierno haitiano está preparado para impedir que Jiménez desembarque en territorio haitiano; todo está tranquilo en Puerto Príncipe; y los sospechosos están siendo interrogados por las autoridades.

records.headline: The Democrat prints the closing part of the interview with General Jiminez
records.summary_en: The Democrat prints the closing part of the interview with General Jiminez, opening with followings of 800 men: Dominican government paper, General Jiminez says, is unsalable; men of all colors in Santo Domingo are joining his cause, but most of his generals are colored; when questioned regarding a dispatch from Cape Haitien published by the Discusion, representing that the Haitian government is unfavorable to his pretensions and is prepared to prevent him from landing on Haitian territory, General Jiminez replied that the Haitian government was in a 'very rotten condition'; he estimates the revenue of the Dominican republic under a good government at not less than 2,500,000, an amount more than enough to meet governmental expenses and the interest on the public debt; when he attains to the presidency, he hopes to go ahead promptly with public works and to carry on other necessary improvements, but he insists that 'the first necessity of Santo Domingo is honest men in her administration'; and as to the possibility that the existing government may prevent his entering the country, he ridicules it, as, to quote his words, 'Santo Domingo is practically mine.'
records.summary_es: El Democrat publica la parte final de la entrevista con el general Jiménez, que se abre con partidarios de 800 hombres: el papel del gobierno dominicano, dice el general Jiménez, no tiene venta; hombres de todos los colores en Santo Domingo se están uniendo a su causa, pero la mayoría de sus generales son de color; al ser interrogado sobre un despacho de Cabo Haitiano publicado por la Discusión, que representa que el gobierno haitiano es desfavorable a sus pretensiones y está preparado para impedirle desembarcar en territorio haitiano, el general Jiménez respondió que el gobierno haitiano estaba en una «condición muy podrida»; estima los ingresos de la república dominicana bajo un buen gobierno en no menos de 2,500,000, una cantidad más que suficiente para cubrir los gastos del gobierno y los intereses de la deuda pública; cuando alcance la presidencia, espera avanzar prontamente con las obras públicas y llevar a cabo otras mejoras necesarias, pero insiste en que «la primera necesidad de Santo Domingo son hombres honestos en su administración»; y en cuanto a la posibilidad de que el gobierno existente le impida entrar al país, se burla de ella, pues, para citar sus palabras, «Santo Domingo es prácticamente mío».

records.headline: The Tribune prints part of an editorial item on the San Domingo Improvement Company
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints part of an editorial item on the San Domingo Improvement Company: the American interest at stake in the republic, the item says, is due to a concession which a company incorporated in New Jersey and known as the 'San Domingo Improvement Company of New York' has acquired in the republic; in 1888 the fiscal agents of the Dominican republic entered into convention with an Amsterdam firm for a loan, and to meet the payments on the loan the Holland company was given the right to collect directly the receipts from all custom houses in the republic, and the indebtedness was made a mortgage upon all the revenues of the country; in 1893 the rights of the Amsterdam bankers were transferred to the New York company, and by act of the Santo Domingo Congress the right of the Americans to collect the customs and port dues was reaffirmed; and in the event of a revolution it will require the presence of several American warships to preserve the interest of the American company, and as a civil war would seriously reduce the revenues the administration may feel warranted to extend its protection to the extent of exerting force to maintain peace.

Government troops commanded by General Francisco Tiriano deserted en masse upon confronting rebel General Ramon Pacheco at Dajabon, giving the insurgents control of the Yaque River crossings and isolating Monte Cristi. Washington. Aug. 9.—The hurricane

burg, Va., of old age.

records.headline: The Journal and Courier prints the close of General Jiminez's interview
records.summary_en: The Journal and Courier prints the close of General Jiminez's interview: he said to-day that funds are being daily placed to his credit in Paris and that he had refused over 800 tenders of service on the part of the Cubans and Americans who were ready to pay their expenses; in reply to these offers he had asserted that he had neither need nor desire to organize expeditions; to-day, he continued, he had received advices that two more Dominican generals had declared themselves in his favor, with followings of 800 men; and as to the possibility that the existing government may prevent his entering the country, he ridicules it, as, to quote his words, 'Santo Domingo is practically mine.'
records.summary_es: El Journal and Courier publica el cierre de la entrevista del general Jiménez: dijo hoy que diariamente se están colocando fondos a su crédito en París y que ha rechazado más de 800 ofertas de servicio de parte de cubanos y estadounidenses que estaban listos para pagar sus gastos; en respuesta a esas ofertas había asegurado que no tenía necesidad ni deseo de organizar expediciones; hoy, continuó, había recibido noticias de que dos generales dominicanos más se habían declarado a su favor, con partidarios de 800 hombres; y en cuanto a la posibilidad de que el gobierno existente le impida entrar al país, se burla de ella, pues, para citar sus palabras, «Santo Domingo es prácticamente mío».

Thousands May Settle in Newfoundland
Deputation Examining Island.
St. Johns, N. F., Aug. 9. A deputa
tion of Finlanders is here inspecting the
country with a view to arranging for
the immigration of thousands of Fin-
landers who are emigrating because of
the tyranny of the Russian government.
Joseph Chamberlain, British secretary
of state for the colonies, sent with them
a Hpeeial re.mest to the governor of
Newfoundland Sir Hugh McCullum,
that all assistance practicable be ren
dered them. To-day the deputation
started on a. tour of inspection of the
various sections of the island which
seem adaptable to their needs.

records.summary_en: The *Houston Daily Post* reported that the Dominican rebellion against the government was expanding, with the province of La Vega in open revolt. Haitian authorities arrested several Dominicans and seized weapons destined for the insurgents, with President Sam declaring Haiti would not allow its territory to serve as an insurgent base. Meanwhile, Dominican government troops sent to confront rebel leader General Ramon Pacheco at Dajabon deserted to the insurgent side, cutting communications with Monte Cristi.
records.summary_es: El *Houston Daily Post* informó que la rebelión dominicana contra el gobierno continuaba expandiéndose, hallándose la provincia de La Vega en abierta insurrección. Autoridades haitianas arrestaron a varios dominicanos e incautaron armas destinadas a los insurgentes, declarando el presidente Sam que Haití no permitiría que su territorio sirviera de base para los sublevados. Mientras tanto, las tropas del gobierno dominicano enviadas para enfrentar al líder rebelde general Ramón Pacheco en Dajabón desertaron al bando insurgente, cortando las comunicaciones con Monte Cristi.

records.headline: The Herald prints, in heavily degraded type, the Cape Haytien dispatch

The Philadelphia item says a morning paper reports that three officers representing the insurgents of San Domingo and two civilians representing those who do not like the manner in which President Sam manages affairs in Hayti have been here three days endeavoring to find vessels to carry munitions of war recently purchased in New Haven; to avoid suspicion, all the members of the party crossed the Windward passage in small boats and embarked on a steamship at Guantanamo, landing last week in New York; those from San Domingo were delayed by the capsizing of a boat; they claim that there is little danger in landing contraband war material anywhere on the coast of either country except near the principal ports, as the coasts are not patrolled, because neither of the governments has war vessels to do the work; and what they claim are needed are small steam tugs to take out their purchases and remove cargoes landed on the eastern shores of Cuba some months ago.

records.headline: The Bee prints the closing part of the Puerto Plata dispatch
records.summary_en: The Bee prints the closing part of the Puerto Plata dispatch: the Haytien government has seized at Fort Liberte arms and ammunition destined for Dominican insurgents; several Dominicans in Hayti have been arrested for violating the neutrality laws, among them Francisco Deetjen, in whose keeping arms were found; President Sam of Hayti has wired the Dominican government that insurgents will not be permitted to use Haytien territory as a base for operations; and the force for the government under the command of Minister Cordero has encountered insurgents led by General Pablo Reyes. A dispatch to the Herald from Port au Prince, Hayti, says word was received from Monte Christo that Dominican troops had been hurried there, that the Haytien government is prepared to prevent Jiminez from landing on Haytien territory, that all is quiet in Port au Prince, and that suspects are being interrogated by the authorities. A special to the Herald from Washington says General Brooke was given instructions today to prevent at all hazards any filibustering expedition in Jiminez's interests leaving Cuba, and that the charge d'affaires of the Dominican republic in this country has called the attention of the authorities to the contemplated expedition and was assured that everything possible would be done to prevent any such proceedings. The Port au Prince dispatch begins a report that the latest news from Santo Domingo says the revolutionary movement is extending and that the province of Vega is in arms, and that it is impossible to obtain any details here; the city is calm.
records.summary_es: El Bee publica la parte final del despacho de Puerto Plata: el gobierno haitiano ha incautado en Fuerte Libertad armas y municiones destinadas a los insurgentes dominicanos; varios dominicanos en Haití han sido arrestados por violar las leyes de neutralidad, entre ellos Francisco Deetjen, en cuyo poder se encontraron armas; el presidente Sam de Haití ha telegrafiado al gobierno dominicano que no se permitirá a los insurgentes usar el territorio haitiano como base de operaciones; y la fuerza del gobierno bajo el mando del ministro Cordero se ha encontrado con insurgentes dirigidos por el general Pablo Reyes. Un despacho al Herald desde Puerto Príncipe, Haití, dice que se recibió noticia de Monte Cristi de que tropas dominicanas habían sido enviadas allí con urgencia, que el gobierno haitiano está preparado para impedir que Jiménez desembarque en territorio haitiano, que todo está tranquilo en Puerto Príncipe, y que los sospechosos están siendo interrogados por las autoridades. Una nota especial al Herald desde Washington dice que el general Brooke recibió hoy instrucciones de impedir a toda costa que cualquier expedición filibustera en interés de Jiménez salga de Cuba, y que el encargado de negocios de la república dominicana en este país ha llamado la atención de las autoridades sobre la expedición proyectada y se le aseguró que se haría todo lo posible para impedir tales procedimientos. El despacho de Puerto Príncipe comienza un informe de que las últimas noticias de Santo Domingo dicen que el movimiento revolucionario se extiende y que la provincia de La Vega está en armas, y que es imposible obtener detalles aquí; la ciudad está tranquila.

records.headline: The Sun prints part of an item on the San Domingo Improvement Company
records.summary_en: The Sun prints part of an item on the San Domingo Improvement Company: the American interest at stake in the republic, the item says, is due to a concession which a company incorporated in New Jersey and known as the 'San Domingo Improvement Company of New York' has acquired in the republic; in 1888 the fiscal agents of the Dominican republic entered into convention with an Amsterdam firm for a loan of about $3,750,000, and to meet the payments on the loan the Holland company was given the right to collect directly the receipts from all custom houses in the republic, and the indebtedness was made a mortgage upon all the revenues of the country; in 1893 the rights of the Amsterdam bankers were transferred to the New York company, and by act of the Santo Domingo Congress the right of the Americans to collect the customs and port dues was reaffirmed; and in the event of a revolution it will require the presence of several American warships to preserve the interest of the American company, and as a civil war would seriously reduce the revenues the administration may feel warranted to extend its protection to the extent of exerting force to maintain peace.

records.headline: The Times prints the Dajabon dispatch and a Havana dispatch of August 9
records.summary_en: The Times prints the Dajabon dispatch and a Havana dispatch of August 9: the Dominican revolutionary troops which assembled at Ouanaminthe have crossed the frontier and taken possession of Dajabon; the garrison retired to Fort Belair, a strategic position commanding the town; the foreign population has left the place; it is considered probable that Jiminez, who leads the revolution, will attempt landing on the island shortly, join the revolutionary troops at Dajabon and take the direction of their movements; and the Haytien government is taking measures to prevent Jiminez from landing in its territory. The Havana dispatch says General Juan Isidro Jiminez, who was interviewed yesterday, said he was in daily receipt of about twenty-five cablegrams from Santo Domingo, where all was going well; to the interviewer he exhibited a letter, which he said was from a person of influence, advising him not to risk participancy in an expedition, as the result was assured and was only a matter of time; according to the writer, if anything happened to Jiminez the people of Santo Domingo would regard it as a great loss, inasmuch as their ideals and hopes regarding good government were bound up in him; and moreover, the writer holds, the system needed a man in some respects like Heureaux, whereas the present executive, Figuereo, though trying to work on the lines followed by Heureaux, was mean, unpopular and incapable of carrying on the administration with the necessary vigor.

records.headline: The Transcript prints the close of the Cape Haytien dispatch
records.summary_en: The Transcript prints the close of the Cape Haytien dispatch and two New York items of August 10: the government commander sent from Monte Cristo to attack General Ramon Pacheco at Dajabon, the headquarters of the revolutionists, was abandoned when he arrived in front of the enemy by his troops, who, without firing a shot, deserted and entered the camp of General Pacheco; the advanced posts of the latter are at Las Aguas, and the revolutionists are masters of the fords across the river Yaque, thus cutting off communication between Monte Cristo and the interior; and the forces of Don Juan Isidro Jiminez, leader of the revolution, are being augmented every day and the news from all parts of the Dominican republic are favorable to him. The first New York item says the Haytien government has seized at Fort Liberte arms and ammunition destined for Dominican insurgents, and that several Dominicans in Hayti have been arrested for violating the neutrality laws, among them Francisco Deetjen, in whose keeping arms were found. records.headline: The Silver Star prints part of an item on the San Domingo Improvement Company
records.summary_en: The Silver Star prints part of an item on the San Domingo Improvement Company: the American interest at stake in the republic, the item says, is due to a concession which a company incorporated in New Jersey and known as the 'San Domingo Improvement Company of New York' has acquired in the republic; in 1888 the fiscal agents of the Dominican republic entered into convention with an Amsterdam firm for a loan of about $3,750,000, and to meet the payments on the loan the Holland company was given the right to collect directly the receipts from all custom houses in the republic, and the indebtedness was made a mortgage upon all the revenues of the country; in 1893 the rights of the Amsterdam bankers were transferred to the New York company, and by act of the Santo Domingo Congress the right of the Americans to collect the customs and port dues was reaffirmed; and in the event of a revolution it will require the presence of several American warships to preserve the interest of the American company, and as a civil war would seriously reduce the revenues the administration may feel warranted to extend its protection to the extent of exerting force to maintain peace.

records.headline: A Washington dispatch of August 10 in the Omaha Daily Bee reports
records.summary_en: A Washington dispatch of August 10 in the Omaha Daily Bee reports that the Navy Department has received no further news of the West Indian hurricane and considers all American naval vessels in those waters safe, with the New Orleans the only vessel still out. Regarding ships in Dominican ports, the dispatch notes that the vessel printed as "Machlas" is at San Pedro de Macoris, San Domingo, while the New Orleans steamed out of Santo Domingo harbor the previous Tuesday in anticipation of the storm. A brief fragment at the top of the column also notes a disrupted link to Santo Domingo and adds that the hurricane eventually swept over Cape Haytien with less violence and correspondingly reduced damage.

Un breve fragmento al inicio de la columna menciona además una conexión interrumpida hacia Santo Domingo y añade que el huracán pasó finalmente sobre Cape Haytien con menor violencia y daños proporcionalmente menores.

records.headline: A dispatch from Puerto Plata, Santo Domingo, dated August 10
records.summary_en: A dispatch from Puerto Plata, Santo Domingo, dated August 10, in The New York Journal and Advertiser states that the full severity of the cyclone on the island cannot yet be determined because communication with the interior is cut off and even the railway from Puerto Plata to San Domingo City has been disabled. The report asserts that the northern part of the Dominican Republic was largely laid waste and predicts that accurate accounts, once received, will likely show heavy loss of life, ruined growing crops, and families left homeless and starving. With apparently diminishing violence, the storm passed from Cape Haytien toward eastern Cuba on a track pointing toward the southern coast of the United States.

records.headline: Commenting editorially on Dominican affairs, The Age-Herald describes
records.summary_en: Commenting editorially on Dominican affairs, The Age-Herald describes the island between Cuba and Porto Rico as fertile, well watered, and suited to tropical crops, while characterizing its population in racial terms as divided between the Black inhabitants of Hayti and the mulatto population of San Domingo, claiming it would become one of the richest countries in the world if occupied exclusively by white people. Turning to the rebellion, the paper states that General Jiminez is organizing expeditions abroad while Generals Pocheco and Reyes and a dozen other home generals lead the internal movement, adding that Figuero will be fortunate to withstand the Jiminez faction's attacks. The editorial concludes that the United States does not want the island no matter how strongly Dominicans again seek annexation, unless as an agricultural destination for a million Black emigrants from the American South alongside Liberia, Hayti, and San Domingo.
records.summary_es: En un comentario editorial sobre los asuntos dominicanos, The Age-Herald describe la isla situada entre Cuba y Porto Rico como fértil, húmeda y apta para cultivos tropicales, al tiempo que caracteriza racialmente a su población como dividida entre los habitantes negros de Hayti y los mulatos de San Domingo, afirmando que sería uno de los países más ricos del mundo si estuviera ocupada exclusivamente por personas blancas. Respecto a la rebelión, el periódico señala que el general Jiminez organiza expediciones en el exterior mientras los generales Pocheco y Reyes y una docena más de generales locales encabezan el movimiento interno, y añade que Figuero tendrá suerte si logra resistir los ataques de la facción de Jiminez. El editorial concluye que los Estados Unidos no desean la isla por más que los dominicanos soliciten nuevamente la anexión, salvo que se busque un destino agrícola para un millón de emigrantes negros del sur estadounidense junto con Liberia, Hayti y San Domingo.

records.headline: A Havana special dispatch in The Savannah Tribune reports a Wednesday interview
records.summary_en: A Havana special dispatch in The Savannah Tribune reports a Wednesday interview with General Juan Isidro Jiminez, whom the paper describes as the aspirant to the presidency of the "Republic of Dominica" (the Dominican Republic). Jiminez stated that funds were being placed daily to his credit in Paris and that he had declined more than 800 offers of service from Cubans and Americans ready to pay their own expenses. Ridiculing the possibility that the incumbent government of the Dominican Republic could prevent him from entering the country, he declared, "Santo Domingo is practically mine."
records.summary_es: Un despacho especial desde La Habana en The Savannah Tribune recoge una entrevista del miércoles con el general Juan Isidro Jiminez, a quien el periódico describe como aspirante a la presidencia de la "Republic of Dominica" (la República Dominicana). Jiminez afirmó que diariamente se depositaban fondos a su favor en París y que había rechazado más de 800 ofrecimientos de servicio por parte de cubanos y estadounidenses dispuestos a pagar sus propios gastos. Al ridiculizar la posibilidad de que el gobierno vigente de la República Dominicana impida su entrada al país, declaró: "Santo Domingo es prácticamente mío".

records.headline: Advices from Kingston, Jamaica, dated August 11 in The Scranton Tribune cite
records.summary_en: Advices from Kingston, Jamaica, dated August 11 in The Scranton Tribune cite an August 3 mail dispatch from Santo Domingo via Hayti confirming cable reports on the spread and significance of the revolution across the Dominican Republic. Prominent civil and military figures are taking the field on the understanding that Jiminez is the prime mover and will soon arrive with munitions of war, while Generals Ramon Pacheco and Pablo Reyes, leading armed followers that include regular soldiers, are marching rapidly westward to cut off Monte Christi from reinforcements and link up with insurgents from Hayti ahead of Jiminez's expedition. The dispatch attributes the uprising's popularity to the name of Gomez and notes that if he declines the presidency or Jiminez ultimately opposes his election, prominent leaders are already considering a plebiscite on renewing an earlier vote for American annexation or an American protectorate.

El parte atribuye la popularidad de la revolución al nombre de Gomez y señala que, si este declina la presidencia o Jiminez finalmente se opone a su elección, líderes destacados ya contemplan un plebiscito sobre renovar una votación anterior a favor de la anexión estadounidense o de un protectorado estadounidense.

records.headline: Two Dominican items appear in this column of the New-York Tribune
records.summary_en: Two Dominican items appear in this column of the New-York Tribune, opening with the close of a dispatch stating that arrivals from an armed steamer departed immediately with their staffs for Santiago de los Caballeros, and that the government will permit foreign money to enter and circulate freely without restriction while beginning the retirement of banknotes on August 17. Under the heading "Plans of the Revolutionists," an August 11 Kingston, Jamaica, dispatch relays an August 3 mail report from San Domingo via Hayti describing prominent civil and military men taking the field behind Jiminez, who is expected shortly from Cuba with munitions of war, while Generals Ramon Pacheco and Pablo Reyes march westward with armed followers including regular soldiers to cut off Monte Christi from reinforcements and join insurgents from Hayti. The dispatch adds that the revolution owes its popularity to Gomez's name and that if he declines the presidency or Jiminez finally opposes his election, leaders are considering a plebiscite to renew the 1871 vote for American annexation or an American protectorate rather than elect another dictator.
records.summary_es: Dos notas dominicanas aparecen en esta columna del New-York Tribune, comenzando con el cierre de un despacho según el cual recién llegados de un vapor armado partieron de inmediato con sus estados mayores hacia Santiago de los Caballeros, y el gobierno permitirá la libre entrada y circulación de moneda extranjera sin restricciones e iniciará el retiro de billetes bancarios el 17 de agosto. Bajo el título "Plans of the Revolutionists", un parte desde Kingston, Jamaica, del 11 de agosto transmite un informe por correo desde San Domingo del 3 de agosto vía Hayti que describe a hombres prominentes civiles y militares saliendo a campaña tras Jiminez, a quien se espera pronto desde Cuba con pertrechos de guerra, mientras los generales Ramon Pacheco y Pablo Reyes marchan hacia el oeste con seguidores armados que incluyen soldados regulares para aislar a Monte Christi de refuerzos y unirse a los insurgentes de Hayti. El despacho añade que la revolución debe su popularidad al nombre de Gomez y que, si este declina la presidencia o Jiminez se opone finalmente a su elección, los líderes contemplan un plebiscito para renovar el voto de 1871 por la anexión estadounidense o un protectorado estadounidense antes que elegir a otro dictador.

records.headline: Advices in Foster's Daily Democrat, from Kingston, Jamaica
records.summary_en: Advices in Foster's Daily Democrat, from Kingston, Jamaica, dated August 12, report that a mail dispatch from Santo Domingo confirms cable accounts of the spread and significance of the revolution throughout the Dominican Republic. Prominent civil and military men are taking the field on the understanding that Jiminez is the prime mover and will arrive shortly from Cuba with munitions of war, while Generals Ramon Pacheco and Pablo Reyes are advancing westward by forced marches with armed followers, including regular soldiers, to cut off Monte Christo from reinforcements and unite with insurgent forces from Hayti ahead of the Jiminez expedition. Attributing the movement's popularity to the name of Gomez, the dispatch states that if he declines the presidency or Jiminez finally opposes his election, prominent leaders are considering a plebiscite on renewing the 1871 vote for American annexation or an American protectorate rather than elect another dictator.
records.summary_es: Informes en Foster's Daily Democrat, desde Kingston, Jamaica, fechados el 12 de agosto, señalan que un despacho por correo desde Santo Domingo confirma las noticias por cable sobre la extensión e importancia de la revolución en toda la República Dominicana. Hombres prominentes de los círculos civiles y militares están saliendo a campaña bajo el entendido de que Jiminez es el principal promotor y llegará pronto desde Cuba con pertrechos de guerra, mientras los generales Ramon Pacheco y Pablo Reyes avanzan hacia el oeste a marchas forzadas con seguidores armados, incluidos soldados regulares, para aislar a Monte Christo de refuerzos y unirse con las fuerzas insurgentes procedentes de Hayti a fin de abrir paso a la expedición de Jiminez. Al atribuir la popularidad del movimiento al nombre de Gomez, el parte indica que, si este declina la presidencia o Jiminez finalmente se opone a su elección, líderes destacados contemplan un plebiscito sobre renovar el voto de 1871 por la anexión estadounidense o un protectorado estadounidense antes que elegir a otro dictador.

records.headline: In an item in the New-York Tribune, Jiminez, described as aspirant
records.summary_en: In an item in the New-York Tribune, Jiminez, described as aspirant to the presidency of the Dominican Republic, denies all knowledge of any expedition of his having been captured off Jamaica and asserts that there are no Dominicans there. Regarding Pedro Lluberas, former Minister of the Interior and Police under the late President Heureaux, Jiminez states that despite Lluberas's claims of friendship he doubts his loyalty and considers him to have a bad record as a member of the Heureaux clique. Jiminez believes Lluberas has gone to San Domingo to try to save the incumbent government, which Jiminez remains confident cannot survive the current month.
records.summary_es: En una nota publicada en el New-York Tribune, Jiminez, descrito como aspirante a la presidencia de la República Dominicana, niega todo conocimiento sobre la captura de expedición alguna suya frente a Jamaica y asegura que allí no hay dominicanos. Respecto a Pedro Lluberas, antiguo ministro de Interior y Policía bajo el difunto presidente Heureaux, Jiminez afirma que, pese a sus muestras de amistad, duda de su lealtad y sostiene que tiene malos antecedentes como integrante de la camarilla de Heureaux. Jiminez cree que Lluberas ha ido a San Domingo para intentar salvar al gobierno actual, el cual Jiminez sigue seguro de que no podrá sobrevivir al presente mes.

A stop of an hour or two will be made in Ogden, and at other towns on the line to give the people a chance to greet the returning heroes. Arriving in Salt Lake City, the boys will march through the principal streets to Liberty Park, where a program will be carried out. records.headline: Under the heading "Passes Over San Domingo," The Semi-Weekly Messenger reports
records.summary_en: Under the heading "Passes Over San Domingo," The Semi-Weekly Messenger reports that the West Indian hurricane crossed Porto Plata and appears to have ravaged the north of the Dominican Republic. Because all communication between Porto Plata and the interior, not including San Domingo, is interrupted, no accurate account of the damage can yet be obtained, although it is believed to be substantial. The railroad from Porto Plata to San Domingo is out of operation, and the storm eventually passed over Cape Haytien with reduced violence and correspondingly light damage.
records.summary_es: Bajo el título "Passes Over San Domingo", The Semi-Weekly Messenger informa que el huracán antillano cruzó Porto Plata y parece haber devastado el norte de la República Dominicana. Debido a que toda comunicación entre Porto Plata y el interior, sin incluir a San Domingo, está interrumpida, aún no es posible obtener un recuento exacto de los daños, aunque se cree que son importantes. El ferrocarril de Porto Plata a San Domingo dejó de funcionar y la tormenta pasó finalmente sobre Cape Haytien con menor violencia y daños proporcionalmente leves.

records.headline: The Dominican uprising: two sections of The Houston Daily Post address
records.summary_en: The Dominican uprising: two sections of The Houston Daily Post address it, beginning with a report that the establishment of a Jiminez junta in New York to encourage revolution against the recognized government of Santo Domingo is viewed with little official concern at present, although a sharp watch will be kept over its headquarters to prevent breaches of neutrality. Recalling authorities' efforts against filibustering expeditions during the Cuban insurrection, the item indicates that no special action is expected against Jiminez's friends so long as they commit no unlawful overt acts against the Dominican president recognized by President McKinley. Separately, the paper's foreign news summary states that residents of Puerto Plata, San Domingo, are in wild panic as revolutionists gain ground beyond the government forces' ability to cope with them, and adds that filibustering expeditions are believed to have already left Santiago for San Domingo.
records.summary_es: La insurrección dominicana: dos secciones de The Houston Daily Post la abordan, comenzando con un informe según el cual el establecimiento de una junta de Jiminez en Nueva York para alentar la revolución contra el gobierno reconocido de Santo Domingo se ve por ahora con poca preocupación oficial, aunque se mantendrá una estrecha vigilancia sobre su sede para impedir violaciones de la neutralidad. Al recordar la actuación de las autoridades frente a las expediciones filibusteras durante la insurrección cubana, la nota indica que no se prevé prestar atención especial a los partidarios de Jiminez mientras no violen la ley mediante actos abiertos contra el presidente dominicano reconocido por el presidente McKinley. Por separado, el resumen de noticias extranjeras del diario señala que la población de Puerto Plata, San Domingo, presa de pánico desbordado, ve avanzar a los revolucionarios sin que las fuerzas gubernamentales puedan contenerlos, y añade que se cree que ya han partido expediciones filibusteras desde Santiago rumbo a San Domingo.

records.headline: Reporting on Dominican exiles in New York, the Barre Evening Telegram quotes
records.summary_en: Reporting on Dominican exiles in New York, the Barre Evening Telegram quotes General Moscoso as stating that the revolutionary junta already possesses all the arms and money it needs and that within a few days an expedition will sail secretly from a U.S. port other than New York to join insurgents fighting the existing government of the Dominican Republic. Moscoso expects to lead the expedition into the field alongside the three other junta members, while 21 additional Dominicans in New York have declared themselves ready to go to Santo Domingo and fight. According to Moscoso, every Dominican in New York actively backs the revolution except the Dominican consul there, who is listed as neutral, and local revolutionists in contact with the island expect an important development in Santo Domingo at any moment. Predicting that the government will be overthrown within 30 days unless division among the revolutionists thwarts them, Moscoso condemns the regime as an ignorant despotism resting solely on execution and exile and characterizes Heureaux's successor, Figuero, as nothing more than a good fighter.
records.summary_es: Al informar sobre los exiliados dominicanos en Nueva York, el Barre Evening Telegram cita al general Moscoso, quien afirma que la junta revolucionaria ya cuenta con todas las armas y el dinero necesarios y que en pocos días partirá en secreto una expedición desde algún puerto de los Estados Unidos distinto de Nueva York para unirse a quienes combaten al gobierno actual de la República Dominicana. Moscoso espera encabezar la expedición en campaña junto con los otros tres miembros de la junta, mientras que otros 21 dominicanos en Nueva York han manifestado su disposición de ir a Santo Domingo a luchar. Según Moscoso, todos los dominicanos en Nueva York apoyan activamente la revolución salvo el cónsul dominicano en esa ciudad, considerado neutral, y los revolucionarios locales en contacto con la isla aguardan en cualquier momento un suceso de importancia en Santo Domingo. Al pronosticar que el gobierno será derrocado en un plazo de 30 días a menos que las divisiones internas frustren su propósito, Moscoso condena al régimen como un despotismo ignorante sustentado únicamente en el poder de matar y exiliar, y describe a Figuero, sucesor de Heureaux, tan solo como un buen combatiente.

records.headline: In an account of Dominican revolutionary preparations in New York
records.summary_en: In an account of Dominican revolutionary preparations in New York, The Evening Times reports that General Moscoso is joined in the junta by Father Charles Philip Morales, a Catholic priest who escaped from Santo Domingo the week President Heureaux was assassinated. Moscoso stated that the junta already holds all necessary arms and funds for a secret expedition expected to sail within a few days from a U.S. port other than New York, led by himself and the three other junta members, while twenty other Dominicans in New York have volunteered to go to Santo Domingo and fight. Every Dominican in New York actively favors the revolution except Consul Woz y Gil, who is listed as neutral, and local revolutionists in contact with the island anticipate a major event in Santo Domingo momentarily. Declaring success certain unless internal divisions intervene, Moscoso remarked that no monarch holds more absolute power than the Dominican president and that Heureaux wielded it tyrannically by exiling and killing his enemies.
records.summary_es: En una crónica sobre los preparativos revolucionarios dominicanos en Nueva York, The Evening Times informa que junto al general Moscoso integra la junta el padre Charles Philip Morales, sacerdote católico que escapó de Santo Domingo la semana en que fue asesinado el presidente Heureaux. Moscoso declaró que la junta ya dispone de todas las armas y fondos necesarios para una expedición secreta que zarpará en pocos días desde un puerto estadounidense distinto de Nueva York, encabezada por él mismo y los otros tres miembros de la junta, mientras que otros veinte dominicanos en Nueva York se han ofrecido para ir a Santo Domingo a combatir. Todos los dominicanos en Nueva York apoyan activamente la revolución salvo el cónsul Woz y Gil, tenido por neutral, y los revolucionarios locales en contacto con la isla aguardan de un momento a otro un acontecimiento importante en Santo Domingo. Tras asegurar el triunfo salvo que surjan divisiones internas, Moscoso afirmó que ningún rey ejerce un poder tan absoluto como el presidente de Santo Domingo y que Heureaux lo empleó como tirano al exiliar y matar a sus enemigos.

records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Journal* reported that a Dominican revolutionary junta in New York was coordinating with General Juan Isidro Jimenes in Havana to organize expeditions against the Dominican government. Agents Adriano and Maximiliano Grullon worked to mobilize Dominican diaspora communities in New York, Philadelphia, and Boston to back the insurrection. Meanwhile, officials in Santo Domingo reported general tranquillity, though the sixteen conspirators who killed President Heureaux remained at large and the national economy remained paralyzed by currency difficulties.
records.summary_es: El *Indianapolis Journal* informó que una junta revolucionaria dominicana en Nueva York se coordinaba con el general Juan Isidro Jimenes en La Habana para organizar expediciones contra el gobierno dominicano. Los agentes Adriano y Maximiliano Grullón trabajaban para movilizar a las comunidades de la diáspora dominicana en Nueva York, Filadelfia y Boston en apoyo a la insurrección. Entretanto, las autoridades en Santo Domingo informaban de una tranquilidad general, aunque los dieciséis conspiradores que mataron al presidente Heureaux seguían prófugos y la economía nacional permanecía paralizada por dificultades monetarias.

records.headline: Advices from Cape Haitien dated August 15 in The Times report
records.summary_en: Advices from Cape Haitien dated August 15 in The Times report that a defeat of the Jiminez forces in Santo Domingo by government troops under General Escoboza is considered unlikely to end the insurrection. Losses on both sides were reportedly heavy, and government authorities claim the rebels' fight turned into a massacre, while two thousand government soldiers are expected at Monte Cristi and insurgents continue forwarding money, arms, and ammunition. The Dominican warship Independencia visited Cape Haitien that day and reported quiet everywhere, while Haitian authorities barred Generals Candelario de las Rosas and Avido from landing off the German steamer Venetia arriving from St. Thomas.
records.summary_es: Informes fechados en Cabo Haitiano el 15 de agosto en The Times señalan que una derrota sufrida por las fuerzas de Jiminez en Santo Domingo ante las tropas del gobierno al mando del general Escoboza difícilmente pondrá fin a la insurrección. Se informa de cuantiosas bajas en ambos bandos y, según las autoridades gubernamentales, el combate de los rebeldes se convirtió en una masacre, mientras se esperan dos mil soldados del gobierno en Monte Cristi y los insurgentes continúan enviando dinero, armas y municiones. El buque de guerra dominicano Independencia estuvo ese día en Cabo Haitiano y reportó calma en todas partes, en tanto que las autoridades haitianas impidieron el desembarco de los generales Candelario de las Rosas y Avido del vapor alemán Venetia, procedente de St. Thomas.

records.summary_en: Under a headline referring to the Dominican Republic as 'Dominica,' The Beatrice Daily Express prints August 16 dispatches from Havana and New York on revolutionary preparations. From Havana, it reports that the collector of customs at Baracoa seized 143 carbines and 18,000 rounds of ammunition evidently destined for San Domingo, where twenty-five Cubans and Dominicans who arrived at Baracoa on Friday aboard the Mortera are apparently planning to carry arms. A companion New York dispatch states that a San Domingo junta formed there is believed to communicate daily by cable with Jiminez in Havana, where he directs the revolutionary forces, while plans are underway to dispatch expeditions from the West Indies and possibly the United States against the existing Dominican government.

The closing paragraphs of an earlier report note enormous numbers of wounded on both sides in a battle regarded as decisively ending the Jiminez uprising, while adding that the government's plan for gradually withdrawing paper money has restored confidence, short-term bills of exchange on Europe sell at 300 per cent silver, and Dominicans almost unanimously favor using American currency. records.headline: In an interview published by The Times, Father Morales and General Moscoso express
records.summary_en: In an interview published by The Times, Father Morales and General Moscoso express firm Dominican opposition to surrendering national autonomy or accepting U.S. annexation. Moscoso states that while Dominicans admire the United States and wish to adopt American ideas, they do not need American control to achieve stability; once the remnant of Heureaux's misgovernment is swept away, the 400 exiles representing Santo Domingo's education, intelligence, and civilization will return to establish settled rule and lasting peace rather than burden the United States with a 'white elephant.' Both Moscoso and Morales, however, enthusiastically endorse a U.S. protectorate—which Moscoso claims a majority of Dominicans favor—explaining that it would back a civilized established government, by force if necessary, against tyrants like Heureaux while defending Santo Domingo against foreign aggression.
records.summary_es: En una entrevista publicada por The Times, el padre Morales y el general Moscoso expresan la firme oposición dominicana a ceder su autonomía nacional o aceptar la anexión a los Estados Unidos. Moscoso afirma que, aunque los dominicanos admiran a la república estadounidense y desean adoptar sus ideas, no necesitan su dominio para lograr un gobierno estable; tan pronto sea barrido el resto del mal gobierno de Heureaux, los 400 exiliados que representan la educación, la inteligencia y la civilización de Santo Domingo regresarán para instaurar una administración ordenada y una paz duradera en vez de cargar a los Estados Unidos con un «elefante blanco». No obstante, tanto Moscoso como Morales respaldan con entusiasmo un protectorado estadounidense —apoyado, según Moscoso, por la mayoría del pueblo—, explicando que sostendría, incluso por la fuerza, a un gobierno civilizado frente a tiranos como Heureaux y defendería a Santo Domingo de agresiones extranjeras.

records.headline: Writing editorially, the Bridgeton Pioneer rejects as historically
records.summary_en: Writing editorially, the Bridgeton Pioneer rejects as historically unwarranted commentary treating assassination in what critics termed the 'Black Republic' as a routine occurrence. The paper points out that since the Dominican Republic came into existence, two U.S. presidents and one French president have been assassinated, other French chief executives have faced murderous assaults or threats, a Russian czar and an Austrian empress have been murdered, and attempts have been made on the lives of the first German emperor and Queen Victoria of England. Observing that Santo Domingo now mourns a murdered chief of state for the first time, the editorial concludes that other nations should offer sympathy rather than derision.
records.summary_es: En un comentario editorial, el Bridgeton Pioneer rechaza por carecer de fundamento histórico las opiniones que presentaban el magnicidio en la llamada «República Negra» como un suceso cotidiano. El periódico señala que, desde que existe la República Dominicana, han sido asesinados dos presidentes de los Estados Unidos y un presidente de Francia, otros jefes de Estado franceses han sufrido atentados o amenazas de muerte, fueron asesinados un zar ruso y una emperatriz austríaca, y se atentó contra el primer emperador de Alemania y la reina Victoria de Inglaterra. Al destacar que Santo Domingo llora ahora por primera vez a un jefe de Estado asesinado, el editorial concluye que a las demás naciones les corresponde solidarizarse con la pequeña república en vez de vituperarla.

records.headline: A Havana dispatch of August 16 in the New-York Tribune reports
records.summary_en: A Havana dispatch of August 16 in the New-York Tribune reports that General Juan Isidro Jiminez, aspirant to the presidency of San Domingo, will probably depart Havana for the island the following day via a south coast steamer from Batabano, traveling unarmed with two friends. Believing the moment has arrived to place himself at the head of the movement, Jiminez construes a dispatch from a former Dominican interior minister in Santiago urging revolutionists to deny the uprising's success as merely a device to deter Cuban and American adventurers eager to sail for San Domingo, and he likewise dismisses as probably false a telegram received that day reporting a rebel defeat, citing uniformly favorable reports from his own representatives. Jiminez adds that although he wished to leave long ago, he remained in Havana on his friends' advice until his presence was needed at the scene of action, and having cabled his intention, he expects to start the next day unless advised otherwise.
records.summary_es: Un despacho fechado en La Habana el 16 de agosto en el New-York Tribune informa que el general Juan Isidro Jiminez, aspirante a la presidencia de San Domingo, probablemente partirá de La Habana hacia la isla al día siguiente en un vapor de la costa sur desde Batabanó, viajando desarmado en compañía de dos amigos. Convencido de que ha llegado el momento de ponerse al frente del movimiento, Jiminez interpreta un despacho enviado desde Santiago por un exministro dominicano del Interior que instaba a negar la prosperidad de la revuelta tan solo como un medio para frenar a los aventureros cubanos y estadounidenses deseosos de embarcarse hacia San Domingo, y del mismo modo descarta por probablemente falso un telegrama recibido ese día sobre una derrota rebelde, alegando que los informes personales de sus representantes solo hablan de éxitos. Jiminez añade que, aunque deseaba partir desde hacía mucho tiempo, permaneció en La Habana por consejo de sus amigos hasta que su presencia fue necesaria en el teatro de los hechos y, tras cablegrafiar su intención, prevé salir al día siguiente salvo aviso en contrario.

records.headline: Reporting on efforts to overthrow the Dominican government
records.summary_en: Reporting on efforts to overthrow the Dominican government, The Topeka State Journal notes that General Jiminez remains in Havana directing revolutionary forces while arrangements proceed to send expeditions from points in the West Indies and possibly the United States. About 14 months earlier, Jiminez's close friend Adriano Grullon came to New York as representative of the revolutionary party, building ties with local Dominicans as well as natives of Santo Domingo in Boston and Philadelphia, and about a week ago his cousin Maximillian Grullon arrived in New York from Havana on a secret mission from Jiminez. Together with Rev. Father Charles Phillip Morales—brother of the late General Morales, whom President Heureaux had executed a year earlier, and an arrival from Santo Domingo around the first of the month—and longtime New York resident General A. A. Moscoso, Grullon has held several meetings to oversee U.S. work backing Jiminez.
records.summary_es: Al informar sobre los esfuerzos para derrocar al gobierno dominicano, The Topeka State Journal señala que el general Jiminez permanece en La Habana dirigiendo las fuerzas revolucionarias mientras avanzan los preparativos para enviar expediciones desde puntos de las Antillas y posiblemente desde los Estados Unidos. Unos 14 meses antes, Adriano Grullon, amigo íntimo de Jiminez, llegó a Nueva York como representante del partido revolucionario, estrechando vínculos con los dominicanos locales así como con nativos de Santo Domingo en Boston y Filadelfia, y hace alrededor de una semana su primo Maximillian Grullon arribó a Nueva York desde La Habana en misión secreta de Jiminez. Junto con el reverendo padre Charles Phillip Morales —hermano del difunto general Morales, ejecutado por orden del presidente Heureaux un año atrás, y llegado de Santo Domingo hacia el primero del mes en curso— y el general A. A. Moscoso, residente en Nueva York desde hace varios años, Grullon ha sostenido varias reuniones para dirigir en los Estados Unidos las labores en apoyo de Jiminez.

records.summary_en: According to the Waterbury Evening Democrat, Dominican presidential aspirant Isidro Jimenez will probably leave Havana for Santo Domingo that day aboard a south coast steamer from Batabano, accompanied by two friends and unarmed. Judging the time ripe to take personal command of his movement, he interprets a dispatch sent from Santiago by former Dominican interior minister Pedro Lluberas—urging revolutionists to deny the movement's prosperity—as merely a measure to hold back Cuban and American adventurers eager to sail for Santo Domingo. On the same basis, Jimenez dismisses as probably false a telegram received the previous day reporting the revolutionary forces' defeat, stating that his own representatives report only successes and that having remained in Havana only on his friends' counsel, his presence is now required at the scene of action.
records.summary_es: Según el Waterbury Evening Democrat, el aspirante a la presidencia dominicana Isidro Jimenez probablemente saldrá ese día de La Habana rumbo a Santo Domingo en un vapor de la costa sur desde Batabanó, acompañado por dos amigos y desarmado. Al considerar llegado el momento de ponerse al frente de su movimiento, interpreta un despacho enviado desde Santiago por el exministro dominicano del Interior Pedro Lluberas —en el que instaba a los revolucionarios a negar la prosperidad de la causa— tan solo como un recurso para contener a los aventureros cubanos y estadounidenses ansiosos por embarcarse hacia Santo Domingo. Con el mismo criterio, Jimenez descarta por probablemente falso un telegrama recibido el día anterior sobre la derrota de las fuerzas revolucionarias, afirmando que sus propios representantes solo comunican éxitos y que, tras haber permanecido en La Habana únicamente por consejo de sus amigos, su presencia es ya necesaria en el lugar de los hechos.

records.headline: An August 12 dispatch from Kingston, Jamaica, in the Gilpin Observer reports
records.summary_en: An August 12 dispatch from Kingston, Jamaica, in the Gilpin Observer reports that letters dated August 3 confirm cable accounts of the revolution's spread across the Dominican Republic, with prominent civil and military figures taking the field in the expectation that Jimenez is the prime mover and will soon arrive from Cuba with war munitions. Generals Ramon Pacheco and Pablo Reyes, leading armed followings that include regular soldiers, are advancing westward by forced marches to cut off Monte Cristi from reinforcements and link up with insurgents from Hayti so as to clear a path for Jimenez's expedition. Attributing the revolt's popularity to the use of the name of Gomez, the dispatch adds that if Gomez declines the presidency or Jimenez opposes his election, prominent leaders are already considering a plebiscite on renewing the 1871 vote for U.S. annexation or an American protectorate rather than electing another dictator.
records.summary_es: Un despacho fechado en Kingston, Jamaica, el 12 de agosto en el Gilpin Observer informa que cartas del 3 de agosto confirman los cables sobre la propagación de la revolución en toda la República Dominicana, donde destacadas figuras civiles y militares han salido a campaña bajo el entendido de que Jimenez es el principal promotor y llegará pronto desde Cuba con pertrechos de guerra. Los generales Ramon Pacheco y Pablo Reyes, al frente de contingentes armados que incluyen soldados regulares, avanzan hacia el oeste mediante marchas forzadas para aislar de refuerzos a Monte Cristi y enlazar con las fuerzas insurgentes procedentes de Haití a fin de abrir paso a la expedición de Jimenez. Tras atribuir la popularidad de la revuelta al uso del nombre de Gomez, el despacho añade que, si este rechaza la presidencia o Jimenez se opone a su elección, importantes dirigentes ya contemplan convocar un plebiscito para renovar la votación de 1871 a favor de la anexión a los Estados Unidos o de un protectorado estadounidense antes que elegir a otro dictador.

records.headline: Commenting editorially, The Columbian remarks that the recent
records.summary_en: Commenting editorially, The Columbian remarks that the recent assassination of President Heureaux of the Dominican Republic and the disputed succession are likely to confront the United States with new problems. Noting allegations that a powerful American syndicate practically controls the country's finances and affairs and that two warships have been ordered to San Domingo to protect American interests, the paper observes ironically that syndicates have been well cared for by the McKinley administration. If seizing the Philippines can be justified, the editorial concludes sarcastically, there is no reason not to take in San Domingo as well, since all territorial syndicates ought to look alike to Mr. McKinley and 'manifest destiny' should not discriminate between friends.
records.summary_es: En un comentario editorial, The Columbian señala que el reciente asesinato del presidente Heureaux de la República Dominicana y la disputada sucesión probablemente plantearán nuevos problemas a los Estados Unidos. Tras recoger versiones de que un poderoso sindicato estadounidense controla prácticamente las finanzas y los asuntos del país y de que se han enviado dos buques de guerra a San Domingo para proteger los intereses estadounidenses, el periódico observa con ironía que el gobierno actual ha cuidado muy bien de los sindicatos. Si puede justificarse la toma de las Filipinas, concluye sarcásticamente el editorial, no hay razón para no incorporar también a San Domingo, pues todos los sindicatos territoriales deberían parecerle iguales al señor McKinley y el «destino manifiesto» no debería discriminar entre amigos.

records.headline: Two brief dispatches in The San Juan Islander report on fighting
records.summary_en: Two brief dispatches in The San Juan Islander report on fighting along the Haitian-Dominican frontier. According to the first item, revolutionary Dominican troops assembled at Munaminthe crossed the border and occupied Dajabon, prompting the garrison to withdraw to the commanding position of Fort Belair and the foreign residents and Haytian consul to leave the town, while the Haytian government is taking active steps to prevent Jiminez from landing on its territory. A second dispatch from Fort de France, Martinique, dated August 10 notes that although news from the Dominican Republic is difficult to obtain, exiled Dominicans gathered at Munaminthe, Hayti, are reported to have crossed the Santo Domingo frontier and captured Dajabon.
records.summary_es: Dos breves despachos en The San Juan Islander informan sobre las operaciones en la frontera dominico-haitiana. Según la primera nota, tropas revolucionarias dominicanas concentradas en Munaminthe cruzaron la línea fronteriza y ocuparon Dajabon, lo que llevó a la guarnición a replegarse hacia la posición estratégica de Fort Belair y a la población extranjera y al cónsul haitiano a abandonar la localidad, mientras el gobierno de Haití adopta medidas activas para impedir que Jiminez desembarque en su territorio. Un segundo despacho fechado en Fort-de-France, Martinica, el 10 de agosto señala que, aunque resulta muy difícil obtener noticias sobre lo que ocurre en la República Dominicana, se informa que dominicanos exiliados reunidos en Munaminthe, Haití, cruzaron la frontera de Santo Domingo y tomaron Dajabon.

records.headline: The Springfield Weekly Republican, accompanying a map drawn
records.summary_en: The Springfield Weekly Republican, accompanying a map drawn at about 60 miles to an inch, distinguishes the two republics sharing the island: French-speaking Hayti in the west, occupying slightly less than a third of the territory after French settlement from 1665, colony-wide prosperity until 1790, proclaimed independence in 1800, and the expulsion of the French in 1803; and Spanish-speaking San Domingo in the east. According to the paper's historical sketch, San Domingo threw off Spanish rule in 1821, was governed under the Haytian republic from 1803 to 1806 and again from 1822 to 1844, expelled a temporary Spanish occupation lasting from 1863 to 1865, and voted nearly unanimously in 1871 for U.S. annexation, which was declined. Alongside Haytian coastal towns, the article identifies the southern port city of San Domingo as the Dominican capital, together with Samana on the east coast and Santiago de Los Caballeros in the northern interior, before breaking off as it begins discussing the current presidential contest.
records.summary_es: El Springfield Weekly Republican, junto a un mapa trazado a una escala aproximada de 60 millas por pulgada, distingue las dos repúblicas que comparten la isla: Haití en el oeste, de habla francesa criolla, que ocupa algo menos de un tercio del territorio tras el asentamiento francés desde 1665, el auge colonial hasta 1790, la proclamación de independencia en 1800 y la expulsión de los franceses en 1803; y San Domingo en el este, de lengua española. Según el resumen histórico del periódico, San Domingo se libró del dominio español en 1821, estuvo bajo la república haitiana de 1803 a 1806 y nuevamente de 1822 a 1844, expulsó una ocupación española temporal entre 1863 y 1865, y votó casi por unanimidad en 1871 a favor de su anexión a los Estados Unidos, solicitud que no fue aceptada. Además de los puertos haitianos, el artículo señala a la ciudad sureña de San Domingo como capital dominicana, junto con Samaná en la costa oriental y Santiago de Los Caballeros en el interior norte, antes de cortarse cuando empieza a abordar la contienda presidencial del momento.
