records.headline: Dispatches in The Daily Morning Journal and Courier announce
records.summary_en: Dispatches in The Daily Morning Journal and Courier announce that the capital of the Dominican Republic has surrendered to insurgent forces. President Jiminez is reported to have sought protection at the French consulate in Santo Domingo, with communications remaining heavily disrupted. A referenced dispatch from Puerto Plata dated April 26 notes that Vice President Horatio Vasquez, the leader of the uprising, had been marching directly against the capital to depose Jiminez.
records.summary_es: Despachos en The Daily Morning Journal and Courier anuncian que la capital de la República Dominicana se ha rendido ante las fuerzas insurgentes. Se informa que el presidente Jimenes ha buscado protección en el consulado francés de Santo Domingo, mientras las comunicaciones permanecen gravemente interrumpidas. Un despacho citado de Puerto Plata con fecha del 26 de abril señala que el vicepresidente Horacio Vásquez, líder del levantamiento, había estado marchando directamente hacia la capital para deponer a Jimenes.

records.summary_en: Vice President Horacio Vasquez has overthrown the government of President Juan I. Jiminez, an article in The Beatrice Daily Express reports, after field operations of less than two weeks. Friends of Vasquez claim he tried to support Jiminez until the president signed contracts financially harmful to the republic. In Puerto Plata, Governor Deschamps arrested Norwegian vice consul Charles H. Loinaz for allegedly conspiring against Jiminez, though foreign consuls secured his release. Deschamps commands a small troop detachment and a warship in port, but the town is expected to fall soon, while the 40-year-old Dominican-born Vasquez is expected to assume power immediately.

Jiminez, informa un artículo en The Beatrice Daily Express, tras operaciones militares de menos de dos semanas. Los allegados de Vasquez afirman que intentó respaldar a Jiminez hasta que el presidente firmó contratos financieramente perjudiciales para la república. En Puerto Plata, el gobernador Deschamps arrestó al vicecónsul noruego Charles H. Loinaz por supuestamente conspirar contra Jiminez, aunque los cónsules extranjeros lograron su liberación. Deschamps comanda un pequeño destacamento de tropas y un buque de guerra en el puerto, pero se espera que la ciudad caiga pronto, mientras que Vasquez, dominicano de 40 años de edad, asumirá el poder de inmediato.

records.headline: President Juan Jiminez has been overthrown by Vice President Horacio Vasquez
records.summary_en: President Juan Jiminez has been overthrown by Vice President Horacio Vasquez in field operations lasting under two weeks, The Indianapolis Journal reports. Until recently, relations between the two leaders appeared cordial, but Vasquez's associates state he turned against Jiminez over government contracts that damaged national finances. In Puerto Plata, Governor Deschamps arrested Charles H. Loinaz, the Norwegian vice consul, on conspiracy charges before foreign consuls intervened to secure his release. Deschamps maintains a small garrison and a small warship in port, but the town is expected to fall quickly, clearing the way for the Dominican-born Vasquez to assume power.
records.summary_es: El presidente Juan Jiminez ha sido derrocado por el vicepresidente Horacio Vasquez, con operaciones de campaña de menos de dos semanas, informa The Indianapolis Journal. Hasta hace poco, las relaciones entre ambos líderes parecían cordiales, pero los allegados a Vasquez afirman que se volvió contra Jiminez debido a contratos gubernamentales perjudiciales para las finanzas públicas. En Puerto Plata, el gobernador Deschamps arrestó a Charles H. Loinaz, vicecónsul noruego, bajo cargos de conspiración antes de que los cónsules extranjeros intervinieran para asegurar su liberación. Deschamps mantiene una pequeña guarnición y un pequeño buque de guerra en el puerto, pero se espera que la ciudad caiga rápidamente, allanando el camino para que Vasquez, nacido en el país, asuma el poder.

The capital surrendered to rebels led by Vice President Horacio Vasquez, while President Juan I. Jiminez sought refuge in the French consulate. Vasquez, a Dominican described as progressive and honorable, began his campaign about two weeks ago following disputes over presidential contracts, and Puerto Plata's resisting garrison is expected to surrender soon.

Vasquez, un dominicano calificado de progresista y honorable, comenzó su campaña hace unas dos semanas tras discrepancias sobre contratos presidenciales, y se espera que la guarnición de Puerto Plata, que aún resiste, se rinda pronto.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that foreign diplomats led by United States Minister Powell intervened during General Horacio Vásquez's advance on Santo Domingo to ensure civilian safety under the rules of war. Although Vásquez initially agreed to a temporary truce, insurgent troops occupied positions along the Ozama River to control the harbor. Finding the insurgents in effective control of the city, the diplomatic corps facilitated negotiations between Vásquez and the Jimenes administration for a formal capitulation.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que diplomáticos extranjeros encabezados por el ministro estadounidense Powell intervinieron durante el avance del general Horacio Vásquez sobre Santo Domingo para garantizar la seguridad de los civiles conforme a las leyes de la guerra. Aunque Vásquez aceptó inicialmente una tregua provisional, las tropas insurgentes ocuparon posiciones a lo largo del río Ozama para dominar el puerto. Al constatar que los sublevados tenían el control efectivo de la ciudad, el cuerpo diplomático facilitó las negociaciones entre Vásquez y el gobierno de Jimenes para una capitulación formal.

A messenger was then dispatched to Gen. Vasquez. asking him to select the time and place for an Interview with the delegation. The messenger returned with the reply that the revolutionary general had appointed the following morning for the interview, adding that, in the meanwhile, he would suspend all hostilities If the government would agree to adopt the same course. During that evening, however. Gen. Vasquez informed the government that he was shipping munitions of war, on a gunboat, to San Domingo, and that he had sent troops to the river Ozama, to take possession of the port and prevent steamers from leaving San Domingo. Mr. Powell was advised of these movements, and he dispatched another messenger to General Vasquez, demanding that his troops retire, according to the agreement that he would suspend all hostilities. records.summary_en: A Monte Cristo dispatch in The Portland Daily Press reports that the provisional government established by Horatio Vasquez will remain in power until elections can be held. Vasquez, the former vice president, led a successful uprising against President Jiminez, and his forces occupied Santo Domingo City last week following its capitulation. Peace is described as fully restored in the southern part of the republic, and an order suspending hostilities has been signed to facilitate discussion of surrender terms.

Vasquez, el exvicepresidente, lideró una exitosa sublevación contra el presidente Jiminez, y sus fuerzas ocuparon la ciudad de Santo Domingo la semana pasada tras su capitulación. Se describe que la paz ha quedado totalmente restablecida en la parte sur de la república, y se ha firmado una orden de suspensión de hostilidades para facilitar la discusión de los términos de rendición.

Later in the day, Puerto Plata capitulated to the revolutionists, who occupied the town and its fort, while the former governor, General Deschamps, embarked on a French steamer bound for Hayti. Following the earlier surrender of San Domingo city to Vice President Vasquez, President Jiminez sought refuge in the local French consulate.

Tras la previa rendición de la ciudad de Santo Domingo ante el vicepresidente Vásquez, el presidente Jiminez buscó refugio en el consulado francés local.

records.headline: The Adams County news analyzes the rapid overthrow of Dominican President Juan I. Jiminez
records.summary_en: The Adams County news analyzes the rapid overthrow of Dominican President Juan I. Jiminez by Vice President Vasquez after field operations of less than two weeks, explaining that Vasquez turned against Jiminez over contracts alleged to have harmed the republic financially. Although Puerto Plata's governor, Deschamps, holds a warship and a small garrison and may offer determined resistance, the town is expected to fall quickly, and Vasquez, having spent nearly all of his forty years in the country, is prepared to assume the reins of government. A Monte Cristi dispatch of May 7 adds that flag-of-truce messengers confirmed the capital's capitulation and Jiminez's flight to the French consulate, while surrender negotiations with Deschamps collapsed over his refusal to yield without government orders.
records.summary_es: El Adams County news analiza el rápido derrocamiento del presidente dominicano Juan I. Jiminez por parte del vicepresidente Vásquez tras operaciones militares de menos de dos semanas, explicando que Vásquez se enemistó con Jiminez debido a contratos que supuestamente perjudicaron las finanzas de la república. Aunque el gobernador de Puerto Plata, Deschamps, dispone de un buque de guerra y una pequeña guarnición y podría ofrecer una enérgica resistencia, se espera que la plaza caiga pronto, y Vásquez, quien ha vivido casi todos sus cuarenta años en el país, se encuentra preparado para asumir las riendas del poder. Un despacho de Montecristi del 7 de mayo añade que emisarios bajo bandera de tregua confirmaron la capitulación de la capital y el refugio de Jiminez en el consulado francés, mientras que las negociaciones de rendición con Deschamps fracasaron porque este se negó a entregarse sin órdenes gubernamentales.

A Santo Domingo dispatch of May 2 recounts that victorious troops under General Vasquez entered the capital quietly with no public enthusiasm after two days of heavy combat that inflicted many casualties on both sides. Meanwhile, Washington advices of May 7 confirm that Jiminez signed a relinquishment of his claims to the presidency, whereupon Horatio Vasquez granted amnesty to adherents of the late government and assumed executive office.

Mientras tanto, informes del 7 de mayo desde Washington confirman que Jiminez firmó la renuncia a sus reclamos a la presidencia, tras lo cual Horatio Vasquez concedió una amnistía a los partidarios del gobierno anterior y asumió la jefatura del Estado.

El despacho señala además que el congreso dominicano ha sido disuelto y que se ha organizado un gobierno provisional bajo la dirección del general Horacio Vasquez.

records.headline: The Houston daily post reports that the provisional government
records.summary_en: The Houston daily post reports that the provisional government under Vice President Vasquez will hold power in Santo Domingo until new elections are conducted, with peace fully reestablished in the south. At Puerto Plata, the crew of the Dominican war vessel sided with the insurgents and delivered a surrender order to General Deschamps, leading to a temporary suspension of hostilities to arrange terms of capitulation. Following the prior surrender of Santo Domingo City, where President Jiminez sought refuge in the French consulate, Puerto Plata capitulated to the revolutionists, who occupied the town and fort while Deschamps departed aboard a French steamer for Hayti.
records.summary_es: The Houston daily post informa que el gobierno provisional bajo el vicepresidente Vásquez mantendrá el poder en Santo Domingo hasta que se efectúen nuevas elecciones, habiéndose restablecido plenamente la paz en el sur. En Puerto Plata, la tripulación del buque de guerra dominicano se puso del lado de los insurgentes y entregó una orden de rendición al general Deschamps, lo que propició una suspensión temporal de las hostilidades para fijar las bases de capitulación. Tras la rendición previa de la ciudad de Santo Domingo, donde el presidente Jiminez buscó refugio en el consulado francés, Puerto Plata capituló ante los revolucionarios, quienes ocuparon la localidad y el fuerte mientras Deschamps partía hacia Haití en un vapor francés.

records.headline: Regarding the arrangements made to protect the lives and property of foreigners here
records.summary_en: The *Evening Times-Republican* reported that United States Minister Powell convened the diplomatic corps in Santo Domingo to safeguard foreign nationals and establish terms of engagement as insurgent forces approached. Despite an agreed temporary pause in hostilities, General Vásquez advanced his troops to command the Ozama River and secure the city. Concurrently, President Jimenes notified foreign ministers that he would agree to capitulate provided that full safety guarantees were granted to government officials and defenders.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Times-Republican* informó que el ministro de los Estados Unidos Powell convocó al cuerpo diplomático en Santo Domingo para salvaguardar a los ciudadanos extranjeros y acordar normas de beligerancia ante la aproximación de las fuerzas insurgentes. A pesar de una suspensión temporal de las hostilidades pactada, el general Vásquez avanzó sus tropas para dominar el río Ozama y asegurar la plaza. Al unísono, el presidente Jimenes comunicó a los ministros extranjeros que aceptaría capitular siempre que se otorgaran plenas garantías de seguridad a los funcionarios y defensores del gobierno.
records.passage: regarding the arrangements made to protect the lives and property of foreigners here, adding that in case no precautions were taken he would consider It his duty to take such measures to provide for their safety as the situa tion demanded. The nature of the reply of the government was not made public. When the revolutionists were sighted, Minister Powell called a meeting of the diplomatic and consular bodies at the United States legation, with the result that a delegation, composed of the United States minister, the French minister and the Spanish, German, Italian and British consuls, was appointed to wait upon General Vasquez and inform him that no attack could be made on the capital, under the rules of war, until due notice had been given to the diplomatic and consular corps here. Vasquez appointed the following morning for an interview, adding that in the meanwhile he would suspend all hostilities. During that evening, however, Vasquez Informed the government that he was shipping munitions of war on a gunboat to San Domingo, and that he had sent troops to the River Ozama. Mr. Powell was advised of these movements and he dispatched another messenger to General Vasquez, demanding that his troops retire. records.headline: San Domingo, capital of Santo Domingo, surrendered the previous Friday
records.summary_en: San Domingo, capital of Santo Domingo, surrendered the previous Friday to revolutionary forces commanded by Vice President Vasquez, dispatches from Monte Cristi dated May 7 in the Atlanta semi-weekly journal confirm. The provisional government established there is to retain power until new elections can be held. A later dispatch reports that Puerto Plata likewise capitulated to the revolutionists, who took possession of the town and fort, while the former governor, General Deschamps, boarded a French steamer bound for Hayti, leaving Puerto Plata quiet.
records.summary_es: Santo Domingo, capital dominicana, se rindió el viernes anterior ante las fuerzas revolucionarias comandadas por el vicepresidente Vásquez, confirman despachos de Montecristi fechados el 7 de mayo en el Atlanta semi-weekly journal. El gobierno provisional allí constituido retendrá el poder hasta que puedan realizarse nuevas elecciones. Un despacho posterior señala que Puerto Plata capituló de igual modo ante los revolucionarios, quienes se apoderaron del poblado y del fuerte, mientras que el exgobernador, el general Deschamps, abordó un vapor francés rumbo a Haití, quedando Puerto Plata en completa calma.

records.headline: A Monte Cristi dispatch of May 7 in The Princeton union reports
records.summary_en: A Monte Cristi dispatch of May 7 in The Princeton union reports that the provisional government established by Horatio Vasquez will remain in power until elections take place. Vasquez, the former vice president of the Dominican Republic, led a successful revolution against President Jiminez, his forces occupying Santo Domingo city the previous week after the capital capitulated. Peace has been fully reestablished in the southern part of the republic, and an order suspending hostilities between revolutionary and government forces has been signed to enable discussions over terms of surrender.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Montecristi del 7 de mayo en The Princeton union informa que el gobierno provisional establecido por Horatio Vasquez continuará en el poder hasta que se celebren elecciones. Vasquez, exvicepresidente de la República Dominicana, encabezó una revolución victoriosa contra el presidente Jiminez, ocupando sus fuerzas la ciudad de Santo Domingo la semana anterior tras capitular la capital. La paz se ha restablecido plenamente en la región sur de la república, y se ha firmado una orden de suspensión de hostilidades entre las fuerzas revolucionarias y gubernamentales para permitir deliberaciones sobre las condiciones de rendición.

records.headline: President of the Dominican Republic Has Retired.
records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Journal* reported that the Dominican capital surrendered to General Horacio Vásquez on May 2 following two days of severe combat outside the city. President Jimenes took refuge in the French consulate, while other officials sought asylum in the American and French legations as rebel troops occupied the capital without public demonstrations. The report added that Puerto Plata, the final stronghold loyal to Jimenes, had also capitulated, leaving Vásquez in full control of the country.
records.summary_es: El *Indianapolis Journal* informó que la capital dominicana se rindió al general Horacio Vásquez el 2 de mayo tras dos días de encarnizados combates en las afueras de la urbe. El presidente Jimenes se refugió en el consulado francés, mientras otros funcionarios solicitaron asilo en las legaciones estadounidense y francesa cuando las tropas rebeldes ocuparon la capital sin manifestaciones públicas. El informe agregó que Puerto Plata, el último bastión leal a Jimenes, también había capitulado, dejando a Vásquez con el control absoluto del país.

records.full_text:
PRESIDENT OF THE DOMINICAN REPUBLIC HAS RETIRED.

Horacio Vasquez, Leader of the Successful Revolutionary Movement, Now at Head of the Government.

SURRENDER OF PUERTO PLATA

LAST CITY THAT WAS HELD BY THE EX-PRESIDENT'S TROOPS.

New Government Probably Will Be Promptly Recognized by the United States—The Looting of a Town.

WASHINGTON, May 7.—Cable advices received here state that President Jimenez, of the Dominican Republic, has signed a relinquishment of his claims to the presidency and on his part Horacio Vasquez, the late Vice President, has granted amnesty to the adherents of the late government and assumed the presidential office.

Senor Don Foo Leonte Vasquez, the charge of the Dominican Republic, has received cable advices from home announcing the success of the revolution. It is probable that he will now become a resident minister here. Naturally the charge is desirous that the United States shall recognize at once the new government. This is a matter, however, that is by custom left to the United States minister resident, but it is not doubted that Mr. Powell will, as he has heretofore done, soon put himself in communication with the de facto government.

Puerta Plaza, the last place held by the Jimenez adherents, has capitulated.

Advices from San Domingo, under date of May 2, say the Dominican capital capitulated to-day to the revolutionary forces commanded by Gen. Horatio Vasquez, the Vice President of the republic. President Jimenez sought refuge in the French consulate and many government officers obtained shelter in the French and United States legations. The revolutionary troops entered the capital quietly. There was no enthusiasm shown by the population here at the entry of the victorious army. The approach of the revolutionists to the capital was announced after two days of heavy fighting between the government troops and the forces of General Vasquez, during which many were killed or wounded on both sides. When it became known here that General Vasquez threatened to attack Santo Domingo, the United States minister, J. S. Powell, as dean of the diplomatic corps, requested the Dominican government to inform him regarding the arrangements made to protect the lives and property of foreigners here, adding that in case no precautions were taken he would consider it his duty to take measures to provide for their safety as the situation demanded. The reply was satisfactory.

records.summary_en: The *Age-Herald* reported that General Horacio Vásquez established a provisional government in Santo Domingo after the capital capitulated following two days of intense combat. President Jimenes took refuge in the French consulate, and victorious insurgent troops occupied the capital without public celebration. On the northern coast, the crew of a Dominican war vessel mutinied in support of the revolution, forcing Governor Deschamps at Puerto Plata to negotiate surrender terms.

El presidente Jimenes se refugió en el consulado francés y las victoriosas tropas insurgentes ocuparon la capital sin celebraciones públicas. En la costa norte, la tripulación de un buque de guerra dominicano se amotinó en apoyo a la revolución, obligando al gobernador Deschamps en Puerto Plata a negociar las condiciones de capitulación.

records.headline: Vasquez from President Jiminez consenting to the drawing up of a treaty of capitulation
records.summary_en: The *Age-Herald* detailed the formal capitulation terms accepted by President Jimenes, which guaranteed the security of state officials, the protection of private property, and the immediate liberation of political prisoners. Insurgent troops took possession of government buildings in Santo Domingo under terms monitored by the foreign diplomatic corps, while the cruiser *Cincinnati* was en route to the island. Meanwhile, Puerto Plata surrendered to the revolutionists, and its deposed governor, General Deschamps, boarded a French steamer for Haiti.
records.summary_es: El *Age-Herald* detalló las condiciones de capitulación formal aceptadas por el presidente Jimenes, las cuales garantizaban la seguridad de los funcionarios del Estado, la protección de la propiedad privada y la liberación inmediata de los presos políticos. Tropas insurgentes tomaron posesión de los edificios gubernamentales en Santo Domingo bajo condiciones supervisadas por el cuerpo diplomático extranjero, mientras el crucero *Cincinnati* navegaba rumbo a la isla. Mientras tanto, Puerto Plata se rindió ante los revolucionarios y su depuesto gobernador, el general Deschamps, abordó un vapor francés con destino a Haití.
records.passage: Vasquez from President Jiminez consenting to the drawing up of a treaty of capitulation, which was to provide a full guarantee for the safety of the officials, employers and defenders of the government as well as for the security of per sonal property. The President and Ministers, it was further agreed, were not to leave the country before the submission of all the authorities of the different districts of San Domingo had been received and all political prisoners were to be liberated. Diplomats Meet. When the revolutionists were sighted. Minister Powell called a meeting of the diplomats and consular bodies at the United States legation for the purpose of deciding upon the best means for protecting life and property and to prevent injury to non-combatants in case of an assault being made on San Domingo, with the result that a delegation was appointed. The revolutionary army entered San Domingo at 11 a. m. the same day, Friday, and took possession of the government buildings. The form of the new government of San Domingo has not been decided. As this dispatch is sent no foreign war ships have arrived here. The United States cruiser Cincinnati left Norfolk for San Domingo May 4 and should arrive here tomorrow (Thursday.) Monte Christi, Santo Domingo, May 7.— Later in the day it became known here that Puerto Plata had capitulated to the revolutionists, who today took possession of the town and the fort. General Deschamps, the former Governor, embarked aboard a French steamer bound for Hayti. All is quiet at Puerto Plata.

records.headline: All intercourse with the revolutionary government has been suspended
records.summary_en: All intercourse with the revolutionary government has been suspended by United States Minister Powell, a dispatch from San Domingo in the Evening times-Republican reports, owing to local conditions. Powell is preparing to depart for Hayti, where he is also accredited, due to grave difficulties and a reported revolution in that country. The dispatch further notes that the Dominican congress has been dissolved and that a provisional government headed by General Horacio Vasquez has been formed.
records.summary_es: Toda relación con el gobierno revolucionario ha sido suspendida por el ministro de los Estados Unidos Powell, informa un despacho desde San Domingo en el Evening times-Republican, debido a las condiciones locales. Powell se prepara para partir hacia Hayti, donde también está acreditado, debido a graves dificultades y a una supuesta revolución en ese país. El despacho señala además que el congreso dominicano ha sido disuelto y que se ha formado un gobierno provisional encabezado por el general Horacio Vasquez.

El despacho añade que la comunicación telegráfica sigue interrumpida y que las noticias se obtienen con dificultad.

records.headline: A New York dispatch in the Oakes Republican, citing a Herald dispatch
records.summary_en: A New York dispatch in the Oakes Republican, citing a Herald dispatch from Puerto Plata, reports that insurgents have seized the entire republic except Puerto Plata, having taken the capital on Sunday. Governor Deschamps declared he will not surrender Puerto Plata without official notification from the government. The dispatch reports that Vice President Horacio Vasquez has overthrown President Juan I. Jiminez after field operations lasting less than two weeks, having turned against him over contracts alleged to be financially detrimental to the republic. Vasquez is expected to take charge of the government immediately.

Jiminez tras operaciones de campaña que duraron menos de dos semanas, habiéndose vuelto contra él debido a contratos que supuestamente causaron perjuicio financiero a la república. Se espera que Vasquez asuma el control del gobierno de inmediato.

records.headline: The Forrest City times reports that the Dominican capital surrendered
records.summary_en: The Forrest City times reports that the Dominican capital surrendered on the previous Friday to revolutionary forces commanded by the vice president, whose name appears garbled as usque/. A provisional government established in the capital is to retain power until new elections take place, with peace completely reestablished in southern Santo Domingo. Meanwhile, at Puerto Plata on the north coast, the crew of a Dominican warship joined the insurgents and ordered Governor Deschamps to surrender, with revolutionists occupying the town and fort on Wednesday as the former governor sailed for Hayti.
records.summary_es: The Forrest City times informa que la capital dominicana se rindió el viernes anterior ante las fuerzas revolucionarias comandadas por el vicepresidente, cuyo apellido aparece mutilado como usque/. Un gobierno provisional establecido en la capital retendrá el poder hasta que se celebren nuevas elecciones, con la paz completamente restablecida en el sur de Santo Domingo. Mientras tanto, en Puerto Plata, en la costa norte, la tripulación de un buque de guerra dominicano se unió a los insurgentes y ordenó la rendición al gobernador Deschamps, ocupando los revolucionarios el pueblo y el fuerte el miércoles mientras el exgobernador zarpaba hacia Hayti.

records.headline: An aspirant to the presidency opposed to the revolution caused
records.summary_en: An aspirant to the presidency opposed to the revolution caused the arrest of Charles H. Loinaz, Norwegian vice consul in Puerto Plata, on charges of conspiring against the Jiminez government, The Iola register reports, though consular representatives secured his release. A dispatch from Monte Cristi dated May 6 confirms that messengers arriving under a flag of truce at Puerto Plata corroborated the capitulation of San Domingo on Friday and President Jiminez's flight to the French consulate. Surrender negotiations at Puerto Plata have collapsed, however, because Governor General Deschamps refused to yield without an order from the Dominican government.

records.headline: Messengers under a flag of truce confirmed the capitulation of the Dominican capital
records.summary_en: Messengers under a flag of truce confirmed the capitulation of the Dominican capital on Friday at Puerto Plata, The Berne witness reports, and President Jiminez's flight to the French consulate. Vice-President Horacio Vasquez has overthrown President Juan Jiminez after less than two weeks of field operations, having turned against him over contracts alleged to be financially detrimental to the government. Vasquez, described by friends as progressive, intelligent, and honorable, is a forty-year-old native Dominican who is expected to assume the reins of government immediately.
records.summary_es: Emisarios bajo bandera de tregua confirmaron la capitulación de la capital dominicana el viernes en Puerto Plata, informa The Berne witness, y la huida del presidente Jiminez al consulado francés. El vicepresidente Horacio Vasquez ha derrocado al presidente Juan Jiminez tras menos de dos semanas de operaciones de campaña, habiéndose vuelto en su contra debido a contratos supuestamente perjudiciales para las finanzas del gobierno. Vasquez, a quien sus allegados describen como progresista, inteligente y honorable, es un dominicano nativo de cuarenta años que se espera que asuma las riendas del gobierno de inmediato.

records.headline: A dispatch from Santo Domingo in the Richmond dispatch reports
records.summary_en: A dispatch from Santo Domingo in the Richmond dispatch reports that United States Minister William F. Powell has suspended relations with the revolutionary government and is preparing to leave for Haiti, where a revolution is reportedly underway. Powell's departure halts negotiations to settle the claims of the Dominican Improvement Company of New York against Santo Domingo, which had been receiving favorable consideration from the overthrown government. The report lists the dissolution of Congress and the formation of a provisional cabinet under General Horacio Vasquez as Supreme Chief of the Revolution, with Juan Francisco Sanchez, Emiliano Tejera, Miguel A. Pichardo, and Casimiro Cordero among the ministers. Existing local laws and decrees are to remain in force under a revolutionary decree.
records.summary_es: Un despacho desde Santo Domingo en el Richmond dispatch informa que el ministro de los Estados Unidos William F. Powell ha suspendido las relaciones con el gobierno revolucionario y se prepara para partir hacia Haití, donde según informes se desarrolla una revolución. La partida de Powell detiene las negociaciones para solucionar las reclamaciones de la Dominican Improvement Company de Nueva York contra Santo Domingo, que recibían consideración favorable del gobierno derrocado. El informe detalla la disolución del Congreso y la conformación de un gabinete provisional bajo el general Horacio Vasquez como jefe supremo de la revolución, con Juan Francisco Sanchez, Emiliano Tejera, Miguel A. Pichardo y Casimiro Cordero entre los ministros. Por decreto revolucionario, las leyes y decretos locales existentes permanecerán en vigor.

records.headline: Revolutionary forces led by Vice President Horacio Vasquez are advancing
records.summary_en: Revolutionary forces led by Vice President Horacio Vasquez are advancing on Santo Domingo, The Emmons County record reports, which the government is taking active measures to defend despite severed telegraph lines with the interior. Vasquez reached Guerra near the capital, with the fall of President Jiminez's government anticipated the following day, leaving only the capital and Puerto Plata outside insurgent hands. At Puerto Plata, large numbers of government troops supported by Dominican warships have concentrated under Governor Gen. Deschamps, who has resolved to defend the port.
records.summary_es: El Emmons County record informa que fuerzas revolucionarias lideradas por el vicepresidente Horacio Vasquez avanzan hacia Santo Domingo, ciudad que el gobierno toma medidas activas para defender a pesar del corte de las líneas telegráficas con el interior. Vasquez llegó a Guerra, cerca de la capital, previéndose la caída del gobierno del presidente Jiminez al día siguiente, lo que deja únicamente a la capital y a Puerto Plata fuera del control insurgente. En Puerto Plata, numerosos efectivos gubernamentales respaldados por buques de guerra dominicanos se han concentrado bajo el mando del gobernador general Deschamps, quien ha resuelto defender el puerto.

records.headline: The Dominican vice president turned against the president, The Kootenai herald
records.summary_en: The Dominican vice president turned against the president, The Kootenai herald reports, over contracts alleged to be financially detrimental to the republic, while Governor Deschamps at Puerto Plata, supported by troops and a warship, may offer the stiffest resistance before the town is taken. The article notes that Vasquez is prepared to assume the reins of government at once, describing the forty-year-old native Dominican as progressive, intelligent, and honorable. A subsequent Monte Cristi dispatch confirms that San Domingo capitulated on Friday with President Jiminez taking refuge in the French consulate, but notes that surrender negotiations at Puerto Plata failed when the governor refused to yield without an order from the Dominican government.
records.summary_es: El vicepresidente dominicano se volvió contra el presidente, informa The Kootenai herald, debido a contratos que supuestamente causaron perjuicio financiero a la república, mientras que el gobernador Deschamps en Puerto Plata, respaldado por tropas y un buque de guerra, podría ofrecer la resistencia más enconada antes de que la ciudad sea tomada. El artículo señala que Vasquez está preparado para asumir las riendas del gobierno de inmediato, describiendo al dominicano nativo de cuarenta años como progresista, inteligente y honorable. Un despacho posterior de Monte Cristi confirma que San Domingo capituló el viernes y que el presidente Jiminez se refugió en el consulado francés, pero añade que las negociaciones de rendición en Puerto Plata fracasaron cuando el gobernador se negó a ceder sin una orden del gobierno dominicano.

records.headline: The Springfield Weekly Republican reports news reached Monte Christi
records.summary_en: The Springfield Weekly Republican reports news reached Monte Christi from Santo Domingo: the provisional government established by Horatio Vasquez will remain in power until elections are held. Vasquez, formerly vice-president of the Dominican Republic, led a successful revolution against President Jiminez, with forces under his command taking possession of Santo Domingo city last week after the capital capitulated. Peace has been fully re-established in the southern part of the republic, and an order suspending hostilities has been signed while surrender terms are discussed.

La paz se ha restablecido plenamente en la parte sur de la república y se ha firmado una orden de suspensión de hostilidades mientras se discuten los términos de la rendición.

Asimismo, un despacho preliminar señala que el general Deschamps, exgobernador de Puerto Plata —el último lugar en rendirse ante los revolucionarios—, abordó un vapor francés y se refugió en Cabo Haitiano, Haití.

records.full_text:
REBELS ARE IN FULL CONTROL JIMENEZ GOVERNMENT IN SAN DOMINGO OVERTHROWN. VASQUEZ IS NOW IN POWER Provisional Government Will Remain in Effect Until Elections Are Held.

Monte Cristo, San Domingo, May 8.—Further confirmation has been received here of the surrender of San Domingo, capital of San Domingo, on Friday last to the revolutionary force commanded by Vice President Vasquez. The provisional government established there will retain power until elections have been held. Peace is completely re-established in the southern part of San Domingo.

Advices from Puerto Plata, on the north coast, announce that the crew of the Dominican war vessel at that port has sided with the insurgents and yesterday conveyed to the governor, General Deschamps, an order to surrender. An agreement providing for a suspension of hostilities at Puerto Plata was signed later in the day so as to permit the drawing up of the conditions on which the port will capitulate to the revolutionists.

During the day it became known here that Puerto Plata had capitulated to the revolutionists, who today took possession of the town and fort. General Deschamps, former governor, embarked on board a French steamer bound for Hayti. All is quiet here. When San Domingo surrendered to Vasquez, President Jimenez sought refuge in the French consulate there.

AT SAN DOMINGO.

Capitulation of the Capital Brought About Quietly.

San Domingo, Friday, May 2.—The Dominican capital capitulated today to the revolutionary forces commanded by General Vasquez, the vice president of the republic. President Jimenez sought refuge in the French consulate and many government officers obtained shelter in the French and United States legations. The revolutionary troops entered the capital quietly. There was no enthusiasm shown by the population at the entry of the victorious army.

The approach of the revolutionists to the capital was announced after two days' heavy fighting between the government troops and the forces under General Vasquez, during which many were killed or wounded on both sides. When it became known here that General Vasquez threatened to attack San Domingo the United States minister here, William Powell, as dean of the diplomatic corps, requested the Dominican government to inform him regarding the arrangements made to protect the lives and property of foreigners here, adding that in case no precautions were taken he would consider it his duty to take such measures to provide for their safety as the situation demanded. The nature of the reply of the government was not made public.

General Alejandro Wosgil was appointed minister of war at this time. Intense excitement prevailed here among the population and in government circles when the news of the approach of the revolutionary army became known. When the revolutionists were sighted Minister Powell called a meeting of the diplomatic and consular bodies at the United States legation for the purpose of deciding on the best means for protecting life and property, and to prevent injury to non-combatants in case of an assault being made on San Domingo, with the result that a delegation composed of the United States minister, the French minister, M. De Jouax; the Spanish consul, Dr. Perera Blesa; the German consul, Herr Von Krosigk; the Italian consul, Signor Cammbiaso, and the British consul, Mr. Gosling, was appointed to await on General Vasquez and inform him that no attack could be made on the capital under the rules of war until due notice had been given to the diplomatic and consular representatives here.

A messenger was then dispatched to General Vasquez, asking him to select the time and place for an interview with the delegation. The messenger returned with the reply that the revolutionary general had appointed the following morning for the interview, adding that in the meantime he would suspend all hostilities, if the government would agree to adopt the same course. The revolutionists, however, already practically had possession of the city and the diplomatic and consular delegation when it met General Vasquez, the next day, May 1, could only offer its good offices with the view of inducing General Vasquez to send a committee to San Domingo to arrange with the government the terms for the formal surrender of the capital. The general agreed to this.

Later on the same day, however, the Haytien minister, L. Borno, and the Spanish minister communicated to the revolutionary commander from President Jimenez, consenting to the drawing up of a treaty of capitulation, which was to provide a full guarantee for the safety of the officials, employes and defenders of the government, as well as for the security of personal property. The president and the ministers, it was further agreed, were not to leave the country before the submission of all the authorities of all the different divisions of San Domingo had been received, and all political prisoners were to be liberated.

The revolutionary forces entered the capital the same day. The form of the new government of San Domingo has not been decided upon. As this dispatch is sent no foreign warships have arrived here. The United States cruiser Cincinnati left Norfolk, Va., for San Domingo May 4, and should arrive today.

records.headline: In an overview of island political history, the Evening Star presents
records.summary_en: In an overview of island political history, the Evening Star presents a chronology of revolutionary movements and changes of leadership in Santo Domingo and Haiti since 1843. Following the withdrawal of Spain in 1865 and the promulgation of new constitutions, the newspaper tracks successive political convulsions in Santo Domingo, including the banishments, returns, and overthrow of President Baez alongside administrations headed by Cabral and subsequent leaders. The dispatch records concurrent insurrections, executions, and presidential successions in Haiti, underscoring decades of recurrent turmoil across both nations.
records.summary_es: En una reseña histórica sobre la política insular, el Evening Star presenta una cronología de los movimientos revolucionarios y relevos de poder en Santo Domingo y Haití a partir de 1843. Tras la retirada de España en 1865 y la promulgación de nuevas constituciones, el periódico registra las continuas convulsiones políticas en Santo Domingo, entre ellas los destierros, retornos y derrocamiento del presidente Baez junto a las administraciones de Cabral y mandatarios posteriores. El recuento consigna insurrecciones, ejecuciones y sucesiones presidenciales paralelas en Haití, subrayando décadas de agitación recurrente en ambas naciones.

records.headline: Writing editorially, The Houston Daily Post cautions against United States intervention
records.summary_en: Writing editorially, The Houston Daily Post cautions against United States intervention in Santo Domingo and Haiti, arguing that simultaneous domestic revolutions and the deposition of Dominican President Jiminez offer an easy excuse for expansionist ambitions. The editorial underscores that the financial affairs of the Dominican Republic have been largely entrusted to an American firm, the San Domingo Improvement Company, which could readily petition for military protection. The paper satirically decries establishing high-salaried governors and commissioners over newly conquered populations to expand an "American zoo," though it observes that the American minister has departed the island.
records.summary_es: En un artículo editorial, The Houston Daily Post advierte contra una intervención de los Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo y Haití, argumentando que las revoluciones internas simultáneas y el derrocamiento del presidente dominicano Jiminez brindan una excusa propicia para las ambiciones expansionistas. El editorial destaca que los asuntos financieros de la República Dominicana han estado encomendados en gran medida a una firma estadounidense, la San Domingo Improvement Company, la cual podría solicitar fácilmente protección militar. El periódico censura con ironía la designación de gobernadores y comisionados con altos sueldos sobre poblaciones recién sometidas para ampliar un «zoológico estadounidense», si bien observa que el ministro estadounidense ha salido de la isla.

records.headline: A dispatch from Santo Domingo dated May 10 in The Hood River Glacier reports
records.summary_en: A dispatch from Santo Domingo dated May 10 in The Hood River Glacier reports that ex-President Jiminez of the Dominican Republic and his ministers have vacated the foreign legation where they had sought refuge. Calm has returned to the capital, though local hospitals remain crowded with men wounded during the final engagement between Dominican revolutionists and government forces. A Red Cross hospital has been established to attend to the injured, and the United States cruiser Cincinnati has arrived at the port.

La calma ha retornado a la capital, aunque los hospitales locales continúan abarrotados de heridos del último enfrentamiento entre los revolucionarios dominicanos y las fuerzas del gobierno. Se ha establecido un hospital de la Cruz Roja para atender a los heridos y el crucero estadounidense Cincinnati ha llegado al puerto.

records.headline: Under the headline "Hayti in More Trouble," the Dakota Farmers' Leader reports
records.summary_en: Under the headline "Hayti in More Trouble," the Dakota Farmers' Leader reports under a San Domingo dateline that United States Minister Powell has suspended all diplomatic intercourse with the revolutionary government in the Dominican Republic, to which he is accredited. Powell's departure is prompted by grave disturbances in Haiti, where a revolution is said to be underway. The notice also reports that the Dominican Congress has been dissolved and a provisional government headed by General Horacio Vasquez has been established.

La partida de Powell obedece a las graves alteraciones en Haití, donde se afirma que se desarrolla una revolución. La nota añade asimismo que el Congreso dominicano ha sido disuelto y que se ha establecido un gobierno provisional encabezado por el general Horacio Vasquez.

records.headline: Former Dominican president Jiminez and the country's new executive
records.summary_en: Former Dominican president Jiminez and the country's new executive, General Horacio Vasquez, have their revolutionary careers sketched by The Citizen, opening mid-narrative. The paper recalls Jiminez sailing from Mobile for Santo Domingo under the American flag, landing at Monte Christi with eleven men where his supporters failed to assemble, leaving him the sole member of his party to escape death or capture. Jiminez subsequently organized an uprising against President Heureaux from Havana in 1899, was briefly detained at Cienfuegos, and was joyfully welcomed by the populace after Heureaux was assassinated, subsequently winning unanimous election to the presidency alongside Vasquez as vice president. Vasquez, a native Dominican about forty years of age who headed the army and organized the provisional government after Heureaux's death, had maintained friendly relations with Jiminez until disputes over contracts precipitated a breach.
records.summary_es: El expresidente dominicano Jiminez y el nuevo mandatario del país, el general Horacio Vasquez, ven reseñadas sus carreras revolucionarias por The Citizen, comenzando a mitad de relato. El periódico recuerda que Jiminez zarpó desde Mobile hacia Santo Domingo bajo bandera estadounidense y desembarcó en Monte Christi con once hombres, donde sus partidarios no lograron reunirse, dejándolo como el único de su grupo que escapó de la muerte o la captura. Posteriormente, Jiminez organizó un levantamiento contra el presidente Heureaux desde La Habana en 1899, fue detenido brevemente en Cienfuegos y fue recibido con júbilo por el pueblo tras el asesinato de Heureaux, resultando luego elegido presidente por unanimidad junto con Vasquez como vicepresidente. Vasquez, un dominicano nativo de unos cuarenta años de edad que comandaba el ejército y organizó el gobierno provisional tras la muerte de Heureaux, había mantenido relaciones amistosas con Jiminez hasta que disputas en torno a contratos provocaron una ruptura.

records.headline: The Boletín Mercantil de Puerto Rico, reporting local maritime
records.summary_en: The Boletín Mercantil de Puerto Rico, reporting local maritime arrivals, notes the morning arrival in San Juan of the steamship Julia, flying the flag of the Cuban Republic, from Cuba and Santo Domingo. Among the vessel's passengers were Don Juan Henriquez, consul general of the Dominican Republic, Francisco Cigada, baritone of an Italian opera company that had recently performed locally, and thirty-four other passengers. Cigada transferred to the steamer Montevideo bound for Spain en route to his home in Italy.

Cigada tomó pasaje en el vapor Montevideo con destino a España en viaje de regreso a su hogar en Italia.

records.headline: A San Juan dispatch dated June 28 in The Saint Paul Globe relays
records.summary_en: A San Juan dispatch dated June 28 in The Saint Paul Globe relays contents of a letter received by a Santo Domingo native residing in Puerto Rico, warning that the Dominican Republic is in a decidedly critical condition and that its new government faces momentary overthrow. According to this correspondent, President Vasquez is reported to be mentally affected and unaware of what he is doing half the time. The letter further states that the country's finances are in a deplorable state, government employees receive only half pay, the public has lost all confidence in the administration, many people are leaving the country, and the current regime cannot last beyond October.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de San Juan fechado el 28 de junio en The Saint Paul Globe transmite el contenido de una carta recibida por un nativo de Santo Domingo residente en Puerto Rico, advirtiendo que la República Dominicana se encuentra en una situación decididamente crítica y que su nuevo gobierno corre peligro momentáneo de ser derrocado. Según este corresponsal, se informa que el presidente Vasquez padece problemas mentales y que la mitad del tiempo no sabe lo que hace. La carta añade que las finanzas del país se hallan en estado deplorable, que los empleados del gobierno reciben solo la mitad de su sueldo, que la población ha perdido toda confianza en la administración, que numerosas personas están abandonando el país y que el régimen actual no podrá durar más allá de octubre.

records.headline: Reporting on military and strategic debates, The Washington Times discusses
records.summary_en: Reporting on military and strategic debates, The Washington Times discusses arguments concerning American acquisition of Haiti, which the paper defines geographically as including Santo Domingo. Under the subhead Value as Naval Base, the article observes that although the possession of Porto Rico, potential coaling stations in Cuba, and negotiations for the Danish West Indies had lessened military interest, strategists expect the next American war to be fought primarily in the Caribbean. The paper reports that the strategic roadstead of Samana Bay in Dominican territory is considered by many to provide sufficient grounds for serious consideration of annexation, noting that even the conservative Cleveland administration previously sought to acquire Samana Bay for naval purposes.
records.summary_es: Al informar sobre debates militares y estratégicos, The Washington Times analiza los argumentos en torno a la adquisición estadounidense de Haití, isla que el periódico define geográficamente como comprensiva de Santo Domingo. Bajo el subtítulo Valor como base naval, el artículo señala que, si bien la posesión de Puerto Rico, las posibles estaciones de carboneras en Cuba y las negociaciones por las Antillas danesas habían reducido el interés militar, los estrategas prevén que la próxima guerra de Estados Unidos se librará principalmente en el Caribe. El diario informa que la rada estratégica de la bahía de Samaná en territorio dominicano es considerada por muchos como justificación suficiente para sopesar seriamente la anexión, recordando que incluso la administración conservadora de Cleveland intentó previamente adquirir la bahía de Samaná con fines navales.

records.headline: General Deschamps, former governor of Porto Plata, has taken
records.summary_en: General Deschamps, former governor of Porto Plata, has taken up arms against the provisional government of Santo Domingo, The Worcester Spy reports, sparking uprisings at Monte Christi, Dajabon, Savanett, and Guayabin. The paper recalls that during Vice President Vasquez's successful revolution against President Jiminez in May, Deschamps held Porto Plata stubbornly against the insurgents from May 1 until May 7 before embarking on a French steamer bound for Haiti as Jiminez relinquished his claims to the presidency. A separate Santo Domingo dispatch dated October 13 adds that another former governor named Navarro has revolted and seized Monte Christo on the northern coast near the Haitian border, prompting the government to adopt prompt measures to restore order.
records.summary_es: El general Deschamps, exgobernador de Puerto Plata, se ha levantado en armas contra el gobierno provisional de Santo Domingo, informa The Worcester Spy, provocando alzamientos en Monte Christi, Dajabón, Savanett y Guayabín. El periódico recuerda que durante la exitosa revolución del vicepresidente Vasquez contra el presidente Jiminez en mayo pasado, Deschamps resistió tenazmente en Puerto Plata frente a los insurgentes desde el 1 hasta el 7 de mayo antes de embarcarse en un vapor francés hacia Haití cuando Jiminez renunció a sus reclamos a la presidencia. Un despacho separado de Santo Domingo fechado el 13 de octubre añade que otro exgobernador de nombre Navarro se ha sublevado y ha tomado posesión de Monte Christo en la costa norte cerca de la frontera haitiana, lo que llevó al gobierno a tomar prontas medidas para restablecer el orden.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star, opening mid-sentence, reports that the Dominican government has consented to arbitrate directly with the New York firm of J. Sala & Co. over a claim of approximately $215,000 for unpaid supplies furnished to the late President Heureaux of San Domingo. State Department officials expressed gratification that the Dominican authorities agreed to direct settlement without undue pressure from the United States, noting that the surviving head of the firm is a woman. Frederick Van Dyne, assistant solicitor of the State Department, was selected by the firm as its arbitrator because of his familiarity with the case, while Bolivian Minister Guachalla was designated by San Domingo, with the two expected to choose a third arbitrator to complete the board.

records.summary_en: Under the headline The Sala Claim, The Montgomery Advertiser publishes a San Domingo dispatch dated January 19 stating that the Dominican government has paid United States Minister Powell the balance of $60,000 (rendered in the text as (60.000) due on the Sala claim, virtually disposing of the controversy. The article explains that Sala was a Frenchman who loaned money and supplied munitions of war to the late President Heureaux of Santo Domingo, and that while the Dominican government recognized the claim after Heureaux's death, it subsequently showed a disposition to ignore it. Following Sala's death, the claim passed to his widow, an American resident of New York, leading the State Department about a year ago to prosecute her claim through Minister Powell.

records.headline: A San Domingo dispatch dated January 31 in The Birmingham Age -Herald
records.summary_en: A San Domingo dispatch dated January 31 in The Birmingham Age-Herald reports that the Dominican government has declined a request made by United States Minister Powell on behalf of the American government concerning claims of the Clyde steamship line. Dominican officials stated that if the company feels aggrieved by the government's action, it should seek redress before a tribunal of the Dominican Republic rather than appealing to Washington. In a strongly worded reply, Minister Powell notified the Dominican authorities that the United States will insist upon redress for its citizens and demands that the pending cases be settled directly by the government rather than through the courts.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Santo Domingo fechado el 31 de enero en The Birmingham Age-Herald informa que el gobierno dominicano ha rechazado una solicitud formulada por el ministro de Estados Unidos Powell en nombre del gobierno estadounidense respecto a las reclamaciones de la línea de vapores Clyde. Las autoridades dominicanas señalaron que, si la compañía se siente agraviada por la acción gubernamental, debe solicitar reparación ante un tribunal de la República Dominicana en lugar de apelar a Washington. En una enérgica respuesta, el ministro Powell notificó a las autoridades dominicanas que Estados Unidos insistirá en la reparación para sus ciudadanos y exige que los casos pendientes sean resueltos directamente por el gobierno y no mediante los tribunales.

records.headline: Observing that the United States is collecting a "little bill
records.summary_en: Observing that the United States is collecting a "little bill" owed to American citizens by what it terms "Dominica, the black republic in the West Indies," The Plymouth Tribune publishes a cable from Santo Domingo on diplomatic negotiations. The Dominican minister for foreign affairs made public a message from Secretary of State Hay stating that a Dominican envoy sent to Washington would be received and heard, but reaffirming that Minister Powell remains entrusted with negotiating and concluding the claims of American citizens. After Dominican Secretary General Sanchez informed Powell that pending cases would not be considered until the commissioner returned from Washington, Powell replied that the claims admitted no further delay and notified the secretary general that a settlement must be effected within a few days. The dispatch adds that Powell's determined stand in pressing the Clyde line and Ross cases surprised the Dominican government, which was expected to yield.
records.summary_es: Al señalar que Estados Unidos está cobrando una «pequeña factura» que se le adeuda a ciudadanos estadounidenses por lo que denomina «Dominica, la república negra de las Indias Occidentales», The Plymouth Tribune publica un cable desde Santo Domingo sobre las negociaciones diplomáticas. El ministro de Relaciones Exteriores dominicano hizo público un mensaje del secretario de Estado Hay manifestando que el enviado dominicano enviado a Washington sería recibido y escuchado, pero reafirmando que el ministro Powell seguía encargado de negociar y concluir las reclamaciones de los ciudadanos estadounidenses. Después de que el secretario general dominicano Sánchez informó a Powell que los casos pendientes no se considerarían hasta el regreso del comisionado desde Washington, Powell respondió que las reclamaciones no admitían más demoras y notificó al secretario general que debía alcanzarse un arreglo en pocos días. In the northwest, General Zeno, who holds chief command of the revolutionists' operations, has captured Guayubin and is advancing toward Porto Plata at the head of a large body of insurgents. Meanwhile, Generals Perico Lasala and Eliseo Gratero lead approximately eight hundred revolutionists against Santiago de los Caballeros and La Vega, while General Raphael Rodriguez advances toward the capital, having reached the vicinity of Las Damas. In what the dispatch terms the eastern part of Dominica, General Candelario de la Rosa is likewise operating with a numerous force of insurgents.

records.summary_en: Under the headline The Dominican Arbitration, The New-York Tribune reports from Washington that a private arbitration board convened on March 18 to consider the claim of J. Sala & Co. against the Dominican government. The board consists of Frederick Van Dyke, assistant solicitor for the State Department, and the Bolivian minister, Señor Guachalla. The claim involves approximately $215 080 alleged to be due for supplies, provisions, and arms furnished to General Heureaux while he was president of the Dominican Republic. Consideration of the case began on the day of the dispatch, and the board scheduled its next hearing for April 16.

records.headline: Opening mid-sentence, the New-York Tribune reports that the Dominican minister
records.summary_en: Opening mid-sentence, the New-York Tribune reports that the Dominican minister in Washington has received a dispatch from his brother, President Horacio Vasquez, announcing that the revolutionary movement against him has been effectually crushed. Minister Vasquez disclosed that New York served as the conspirators' headquarters, where arms and ammunition were purchased, stored in an uptown Spanish-American hotel, and loaded onto vessels bound for West Indian ports before being smuggled into uninhabited points along the Dominican coast. In addition, Minister Vasquez obtained a letter signed by former Dominican president General Juan I. Jimenes, who is currently residing in New York, which reportedly establishes his complicity in the conspiracy to overthrow President Vasquez.
records.summary_es: Comenzando a mitad de frase, el New-York Tribune informa que el ministro dominicano en Washington ha recibido un despacho de su hermano, el presidente Horacio Vasquez, anunciando que el movimiento revolucionario en su contra ha sido efectivamente sofocado. El ministro Vasquez reveló que Nueva York sirvió como cuartel general de los conspiradores, donde se adquirieron armas y municiones, se almacenaron en un hotel hispanoamericano de la parte alta de la ciudad y se cargaron en embarcaciones con destino a puertos antillanos antes de ser introducidas clandestinamente por puntos deshabitados de la costa dominicana. Asimismo, el ministro Vasquez obtuvo una carta firmada por el expresidente dominicano general Juan I. Jimenes, quien reside actualmente en Nueva York, la cual demuestra presuntamente su complicidad en la conspiración para derrocar al presidente Vasquez.

records.headline: A Monte Cristi dispatch in The Indianapolis Journal reports
records.summary_en: A Monte Cristi dispatch in The Indianapolis Journal reports that General Alejandro Wos y Gil and his revolutionary followers are masters of Santo Domingo City, where War Minister General Miguel Pichardo and General Juan Francisco surrendered from the United States consulate with a small group of followers. The revolutionists hold two Dominican warships, the Independencia and the Colon, while President Horacio Vasquez sailed from Porto Plata to Sanchez aboard the cruiser Presidente, the sole government war vessel remaining. Vasquez is believed to be planning an attack on the capital with General Luis Maria Hernandez, governor of San Pedro de Macoris, while in the capital General Echenique, the president's chief of staff, has died of a foot wound suffered during Monday's fighting.

records.headline: Dominican revolutionists have taken possession of the cruiser
records.summary_en: Dominican revolutionists have taken possession of the cruiser Independencia and the gunboat Colon, two of the country's three war vessels, The Wichita Daily Eagle reports. President Horacio Vasquez departed Porto Plata for Sanchez on the cruiser Presidente, the government's sole remaining warship, planning an assault on Santo Domingo alongside General Luis Maria Hernandez, governor of San Pedro de Macoris, who has left to enlist recruits. A stubborn resistance is expected at the capital, where the president's chief of staff, General Echequi, died from a foot wound received during Monday's fighting, while General Lico Castello is wounded and skirmishes in the vicinity have resulted in about twenty government soldiers killed.

records.summary_en: A Monte Cristi dispatch in The Savannah Morning News, under the headline "President to Attack San Domingo City," reports that General Alejandro Wos y Gil and his revolutionary followers are masters of Santo Domingo City. Minister of War General Miguel Pichardo and Minister of Foreign Affairs General Juan Francisco Sanchez surrendered from the United States consulate with a small group of followers, while the insurgents hold two or three Dominican warships, including the Independence and the gunboat Colon. President Horacio Vasquez departed Porto Plata for Sanchez aboard the cruiser Presidente, intending to attack the capital alongside General Luis Marin Hernandez, governor of San Pedro de Macoris, following skirmishes in the vicinity that have killed about twenty government soldiers.

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo in The News &
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo in The News & Observer, under the printed heading "The War in San Domingo," reports that the city was thrown into alarm on Tuesday afternoon by renewed fighting at nearby San Carlos. To extend the uprising, a revolutionary commission departed aboard the warship Independence for Azua and Barahona to demand their surrender, while the warship Colon sailed from the capital for San Pedro de Macoris to compel that municipality to yield.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de la Associated Press desde Santo Domingo en The News & Observer, bajo el encabezado impreso "La guerra en Santo Domingo", informa que la ciudad se llenó de alarma el martes por la tarde debido a nuevos combates en la cercana localidad de San Carlos. Con el fin de extender el levantamiento, una comisión revolucionaria partió a bordo del buque de guerra Independence hacia Azua y Barahona para exigir su rendición, mientras que el buque de guerra Colón zarpó desde la capital hacia San Pedro de Macorís para forzar a dicho municipio a someterse.

The Bevolntionistß Sweeping Everything Be

San Domingo, Republic of Santo Do
mingo, Tuesday, March 24. —The inhabi

that town to surrender.

records.headline: Revolutionary commissioners returned after their mission failed
records.summary_en: Revolutionary commissioners returned after their mission failed, having been sent from Santo Domingo to Bahia Honda, Azua, and San Pedro de Macoris, dispatches published in The San Francisco Call state, leaving the capital quiet with business suspended while awaiting news from the north. From New York, the Dominican consul received word from Governor Caceres at Santiago reporting that General Horacio Vasquez captured the cruiser Independencia at Macoris, imprisoning all revolutionary chiefs aboard and confining the rebellion to besieged Santo Domingo City, while Washington reports the cruiser Atlanta departed Cap-Haitien for the Dominican capital.
records.summary_es: Los comisionados revolucionarios enviados desde Santo Domingo a Bahía Honda, Azua y San Pedro de Macorís regresaron tras fracasar su misión, señalan despachos publicados en The San Francisco Call, dejando a la capital en calma pero con el comercio paralizado a la espera de noticias del norte. Desde Nueva York, el cónsul dominicano recibió informes del gobernador Caceres en Santiago indicando que el general Horacio Vasquez capturó el crucero Independencia en Macorís, apresando a todos los jefes revolucionarios a bordo y reduciendo la rebelión a la sitiada ciudad de Santo Domingo, mientras que Washington informa que el crucero Atlanta partió de Cabo Haitiano hacia la capital dominicana.

records.headline: Former Dominican President General Penceslao Figuerero sailed
records.summary_en: Former Dominican President General Penceslao Figuerero sailed Monday night aboard the revolutionary warship Independencia, The New-York Tribune reports, for Azua de Compostella in an attempt to avert further bloodshed, with an engagement between warships feared upon her return. Cable and telegraph lines to the city remain severed, while General Pichardo arrived after being summoned from exile in Curacao and revolutionary land forces marched toward San Pedro de Macoris. The inhabitants of San Cristobal have joined the revolt, other regions remain loyal to General Vasquez's government, and the Clyde Line steamer New-York is reportedly detained at San Pedro de Macoris.
records.summary_es: El expresidente dominicano general Penceslao Figuerero zarpó el lunes por la noche a bordo del buque revolucionario Independencia, informa el New-York Tribune, hacia Azua de Compostela para intentar evitar más derramamiento de sangre, temiéndose un combate entre navíos a su regreso. Las líneas de cable y telégrafo hacia la ciudad permanecen cortadas, mientras que el general Pichardo llegó tras ser llamado del exilio en Curazao y fuerzas terrestres revolucionarias marcharon hacia San Pedro de Macorís. Los habitantes de San Cristóbal se han sumado a la revuelta, otras zonas continúan fieles al gobierno del general Vasquez, y se informa que el vapor New-York de la Clyde Line permanece retenido en San Pedro de Macorís.

records.headline: A three-hour battle between government troops and revolutionists
records.summary_en: A three-hour battle between government troops and revolutionists took place along the River Ozama near Santo Domingo, The New-York Tribune reports, leaving one hundred casualties, while President Vasquez demanded the city's surrender and insurgents pledged to resist to the end. A March 31 dispatch adds that the United States cruiser Atlanta anchored off Santo Domingo, establishing a signal station on shore prepared to land marines if necessary. Another engagement at San Antonio de Guerra resulted in 146 killed or wounded, further river fighting ensued, and the Clyde Line steamer New-York remains prevented from arriving from San Pedro de Macoris amid widespread suspension of business and communications.
records.summary_es: Se libró un combate de tres horas entre tropas gubernamentales y revolucionarios a lo largo del río Ozama cerca de Santo Domingo, informa el New-York Tribune, con un saldo de cien bajas, mientras el presidente Vasquez exigió la rendición de la ciudad y los insurgentes prometieron resistir hasta el final. Un despacho del 31 de marzo agrega que el crucero estadounidense Atlanta fondeó frente a Santo Domingo, estableciendo una estación de señales en tierra lista para desembarcar infantes de marina si fuera necesario. Otro enfrentamiento en San Antonio de Guerra dejó 146 muertos o heridos, estallaron nuevos choques en el río, y el vapor New-York de la Clyde Line sigue sin poder llegar procedente de San Pedro de Macorís en medio de una paralización generalizada del comercio y las comunicaciones.

records.summary_en: A Navy Department dispatch from Santo Domingo, via Haiti, dated April 5 reports that government forces attacked the city the day before and were repulsed, and that President Vasquez was approaching with a strong force. It says a government gunboat fired three shots the previous night without injury, that the city was fortified and determined to resist, and that marines were landed to protect the consulate.

Dice que una cañonera gubernamental disparó tres tiros la noche anterior sin causar daños, que la ciudad estaba fortificada y decidida a resistir, y que se desembarcaron marines para proteger el consulado.

records.summary_en: The *Essex County Herald* emphasized the strategic importance of Samana Bay as the naval key to the Caribbean, recalling President Grant's earlier annexation efforts. It reported that an unexpected revolution had seized the capital of Santo Domingo during the president's absence, complicating recent American diplomatic agreements compensating a U.S. steamship company. With the Dominican president on the run and the foreign minister sheltering in the American consulate, the paper suggested U.S. marine landings or intervention might follow.
records.summary_es: El *Essex County Herald* subrayó la importancia estratégica de la bahía de Samaná como la llave naval del Caribe, recordando los anteriores intentos de anexión del presidente Grant. Informó que una revolución imprevista se había apoderado de la capital de Santo Domingo durante la ausencia del presidente, complicando recientes acuerdos diplomáticos estadounidenses que indemnizaban a una compañía naviera de los Estados Unidos. Con el presidente dominicano en fuga y el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores refugiado en el consulado estadounidense, el periódico sugirió que podrían producirse desembarcos de la infantería de marina de EE. UU. o una intervención militar.

records.summary_en: A Washington dispatch in The Montgomery Advertiser, under the heading "Resting Place," reports that the forthcoming volume of foreign relations contains a note from United States Minister Powell in the Dominican Republic series. Minister Powell recounted that during a visit to Santo Domingo by Cuban General Maximo Gomez, Dominican authorities honored the general by exposing the casket containing the alleged bones of Christopher Columbus and permitting him to handle them. According to the minister, the casket measured six feet by ten inches and twelve inches deep, marking only the fiftieth time it had been shown, and contained a bullet imbedded in the explorer's leg; Powell added that he too was permitted to hold some of the relics.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Washington en The Montgomery Advertiser, bajo el encabezado "Lugar de descanso", informa que el próximo volumen de relaciones exteriores contiene una nota del ministro estadounidense Powell dentro de la serie sobre la República Dominicana. El ministro Powell relató que durante una visita a Santo Domingo del general cubano Máximo Gómez, las autoridades dominicanas homenajearon al general mostrándole la urna que contiene los supuestos restos de Cristóbal Colón y permitiéndole sostenerlos. Según el ministro, la urna medía seis pies por diez pulgadas y doce pulgadas de profundidad, constituyendo apenas la quincuagésima vez que se exhibía, y contenía una bala alojada en la pierna del explorador; Powell agregó que a él también se le permitió sostener algunas de las reliquias.

records.summary_en: The Birmingham Age-Herald reports a note, included in the Dominican Republic series of the forthcoming Foreign Relations volume, detailing the reception accorded to General Maximo Gomez during his visit to Santo Domingo. U.S. Minister Powell informed the State Department that Dominican authorities, as a mark of high esteem, permitted the Cuban soldier to view and handle the casket containing the bones of Christopher Columbus. The relics are kept in a casket measuring eighteen by ten inches and twelve inches deep, exposed to public view on this occasion for only the fifth time. The minister added that the casket contains a bullet said to have been embedded in the discoverer's leg and never extracted, which authorities cite as proof of the remains' authenticity.

Las reliquias se conservan en un cofre de dieciocho por diez pulgadas y doce pulgadas de profundidad, expuesto al público en esta ocasión por apenas quinta vez. El ministro añadió que la urna contiene una bala que presuntamente quedó incrustada en la pierna del descubridor sin haber sido extraída jamás, dato que las autoridades esgrimen como prueba de la autenticidad de los restos.

records.summary_en: The Savannah Morning News publishes an account of the forthcoming Foreign Relations volume highlighting a diplomatic communication from Mr. Powell, United States minister to the Dominican Republic. Writing to the State Department, Powell recounted that Dominican hosts paid tribute to General Maximo Gomez during the Cuban soldiers' visit to Santo Domingo by permitting him to view and handle the casket containing the bones of Christopher Columbus. The casket, measuring 18 by 10 inches and 12 inches deep, was opened for public inspection for only the fifth time. Powell noted that it contains an unextracted bullet reputedly lodged in the discoverer's leg, which Dominicans offer as evidence of the remains' identity, and added that he himself was allowed to hold some of the relics.
records.summary_es: The Savannah Morning News publica una reseña sobre el próximo volumen de Relaciones Exteriores que destaca una comunicación diplomática del señor Powell, ministro de los Estados Unidos ante la República Dominicana. En su nota dirigida al Departamento de Estado, Powell relató que las autoridades dominicanas rindieron homenaje al general Máximo Gómez durante la visita de los soldados cubanos a Santo Domingo, permitiéndole ver y sostener el cofre que guarda los restos óseos de Cristóbal Colón. El cofre, de 18 por 10 pulgadas y 12 pulgadas de profundidad, fue abierto para inspección pública por apenas quinta vez. Powell señaló que en su interior yace una bala nunca extraída, presuntamente alojada en la pierna del descubridor, lo que los dominicanos presentan como prueba de la identidad de las reliquias, y añadió que a él mismo se le permitió sostener parte de ellas.

records.headline: The Wichita Daily Eagle prints a Washington dispatch, under the dateline
records.summary_en: The Wichita Daily Eagle prints a Washington dispatch, under the dateline 'April II,' previewing diplomatic correspondence soon to appear in the 'Foreign Relations of the United States' volume. In the Dominican series, the American minister reported to the State Department on the courtesies shown to General Maximo Gomez during the Cuban soldier's visit to Santo Domingo. The minister stated that Dominicans honored Gomez by letting him inspect and handle their sacred casket containing the bones of Christopher Columbus. The casket, measuring eighteen by ten inches and twelve inches deep, was exposed to public view for the fifth time, and contains an unextracted bullet said to have been embedded in the discoverer's leg. The dispatch concludes by noting that the minister was likewise permitted to hold some of the relics in his own hands.
records.summary_es: The Wichita Daily Eagle publica un despacho de Washington, bajo la fecha 'April II', que anticipa la correspondencia diplomática que aparecerá próximamente en el volumen de «Relaciones Exteriores de los Estados Unidos». En la sección dominicana, el ministro estadounidense informó al Departamento de Estado sobre las atenciones dispensadas al general Máximo Gómez durante la visita del soldado cubano a Santo Domingo. El ministro declaró que los dominicanos agasajaron a Gómez permitiéndole inspeccionar y sostener el venerado cofre que encierra los restos óseos de Cristóbal Colón. El cofre, de dieciocho por diez pulgadas y doce pulgadas de profundidad, fue expuesto a la vista pública por quinta vez y contiene una bala nunca extraída, supuestamente incrustada en la pierna del descubridor. El despacho concluye señalando que al propio ministro también se le permitió sostener parte de las reliquias con sus propias manos.
