records.headline: The Messenger prints a Washington special dispatch and a Santo Domingo dispatch
records.summary_en: The Messenger prints a Washington special dispatch and a Santo Domingo dispatch: a cablegram received at the State Department from Minister Powell at San Domingo reports that conditions in the republic are in a state of great disturbance; the State Department is making vigorous efforts to communicate with Mr. Powell by cable, but with unsatisfactory results, owing to the fact that the insurgents appear to be in possession of the land telegraph lines connecting the capital, San Domingo, with the cable station on the east coast; incidentally, this has interrupted communication with Venezuela; to guard against any further cable lapses the State Department is sending, through the Navy Department, written instructions to Minister Powell for his guidance during the revolution, and these went forward on the Baltimore, which sailed to-day. The Santo Domingo dispatch says the political situation in this city is unchanged; quiet prevails, but serious trouble may arise here at any time and the presence of a foreign warship is desirable; the Clyde Line steamer Cherokee, from New York, has arrived here, having been prevented by the Dominican government cruiser Independencia from calling at Puerto Plata, Samana and Macoris; she reports that the whole of the northern part of the island has joined in the revolutionary movement.
records.summary_es: El Messenger publica un despacho especial de Washington y un despacho de Santo Domingo: un cablegrama recibido en el Departamento de Estado del ministro Powell en San Domingo informa que las condiciones en la república están en un estado de gran agitación; el Departamento de Estado hace esfuerzos vigorosos para comunicarse con el señor Powell por cable, pero con resultados insatisfactorios, debido a que los insurgentes parecen estar en posesión de las líneas telegráficas terrestres que conectan la capital, Santo Domingo, con la estación de cable en la costa este; incidentalmente, esto ha interrumpido también la comunicación con Venezuela; para precaverse contra nuevas interrupciones del cable, el Departamento de Estado envía, por medio del Departamento de Marina, instrucciones escritas al ministro Powell para su orientación durante la revolución, y estas salieron en el Baltimore, que zarpó hoy. El despacho de Santo Domingo dice que la situación política en esta ciudad no ha cambiado; prevalece la tranquilidad, pero pueden surgir aquí problemas serios en cualquier momento y es deseable la presencia de un buque de guerra extranjero; el vapor Cherokee, de la línea Clyde, procedente de Nueva York, ha llegado aquí, habiéndole impedido el crucero gubernamental dominicano Independencia hacer escala en Puerto Plata, Samaná y Macorís; informa que toda la parte norte de la isla se ha unido al movimiento revolucionario.

The Cape Haitian dispatch says the revolutionary leaders, Jiminez and Ramon Caceres, with thirty followers, are on board the French mail steamer St. Simon, which arrived to-day; the Haitian authorities prevented their debarkation and the vessel proceeded for Port-au-Prince.

records.headline: The Light prints a Santo Domingo dispatch of November 7: the Dominican government
records.summary_en: The Light prints a Santo Domingo dispatch of November 7: the Dominican government has issued a decree announcing that the northern ports of the republic are closed to maritime commerce; the political situation is unchanged; the arrival of foreign warships is anxiously expected. The Clyde line steamer Cherokee, which returned here from Macoris, where she went to see Minister Powell, after having been prevented from entering Puerto Plata on the north coast by a Dominican warship, has been ordered to Samana to await there the arrival of foreign warships; the situation is dangerous. The government intends to prevent the vessels from entering the northern ports, but Minister Powell has declared the blockade non-effective. The German consul has protested against the action of the Dominican government closing the ports.
records.summary_es: El Light publica un despacho de Santo Domingo del 7 de noviembre: el gobierno dominicano ha emitido un decreto que anuncia que los puertos del norte de la república están cerrados al comercio marítimo; la situación política no ha cambiado; la llegada de buques de guerra extranjeros se espera con ansiedad. El vapor Cherokee, de la línea Clyde, que regresó aquí desde Macorís, a donde fue a ver al ministro Powell, después de que un buque de guerra dominicano le impidió entrar en Puerto Plata, en la costa norte, ha recibido órdenes de dirigirse a Samaná para esperar allí la llegada de buques de guerra extranjeros; la situación es peligrosa. El gobierno tiene la intención de impedir que los buques entren en los puertos del norte, pero el ministro Powell ha declarado el bloqueo no efectivo. El cónsul alemán ha protestado contra la acción del gobierno dominicano de cerrar los puertos.

records.headline: The Star prints a Navy Department item: it is reported at the department
records.summary_en: The Star prints a Navy Department item: it is reported at the department that the Baltimore arrived at Sanchez, a port on the northern coast of Santo Domingo, on the 3d instant; Sanchez and Puerto Plata are not more than 400 miles apart, and it is not understood at the department why it took the Baltimore four days to cover that distance. Although the Baltimore may eventually be sent to Colon to reinforce the Nashville, Dixie and Atlanta, it is said at the Navy Department that no orders to that effect have been issued; in view of the fact that the situation on the isthmus is now well under control, it is believed that the Baltimore is likely to remain at Santo Domingo, where there seems to be great need for the presence of an American warship. The original report that the Baltimore was to be immediately dispatched to Colon was coupled with the statement that she would be relieved in Dominican waters by the gunboat Newport, which at that time was at Jacksonville; if such was the intention of the department, the plan has certainly been abandoned, for word was received at the department this morning that the Newport, instead of going south, left Jacksonville yesterday for Savannah, Ga., to be repaired and to take part in a local celebration.
records.summary_es: El Star publica una nota del Departamento de Marina: se informa en el departamento que el Baltimore llegó a Sánchez, un puerto en la costa norte de Santo Domingo, el día 3 del presente mes; Sánchez y Puerto Plata no están a más de 400 millas de distancia, y no se comprende en el departamento por qué el Baltimore tardó cuatro días en cubrir esa distancia. Aunque el Baltimore puede ser enviado eventualmente a Colón para reforzar al Nashville, al Dixie y al Atlanta, se dice en el Departamento de Marina que no se han emitido órdenes en ese sentido; en vista de que la situación en el Istmo está ahora bien controlada, sin perspectivas inmediatas de nuevos estallidos, se cree que el Baltimore probablemente permanecerá en Santo Domingo, donde parece haber gran necesidad de la presencia de un buque de guerra estadounidense. El informe original de que el Baltimore sería despachado de inmediato a Colón venía acompañado de la declaración de que sería relevado en aguas dominicanas por la cañonera Newport, que en ese momento estaba en Jacksonville; si tal fue la intención del departamento, el plan ciertamente ha sido abandonado, pues esta mañana se recibió en el departamento la noticia de que el Newport, en lugar de dirigirse al sur, salió ayer de Jacksonville hacia Savannah, Georgia, para ser reparado y participar en una celebración local.

records.headline: The Washington Times prints the closing part of a Washington dispatch
records.summary_en: The Washington Times prints the closing part of a Washington dispatch and two items on the German warships and Macoris: Germany has ordered two warships from St. Thomas to Santo Domingo; the German steamer Athen was refused admission to the port of San Domingo, and a report of this affair to the German government caused an order to be issued at once for the movement of the German cruisers Panther and Gazelle into Dominican waters. Under the head 'Macoris Partly Destroyed,' the paper says Minister Powell, at Santo Domingo, has advised the State Department that a gunboat in charge of revolutionists stormed Macoris, an important port on the north coast of the island, and destroyed part of the town; the dispatch was under date of November 6; it is also stated in the dispatch that American interests in Macoris are large; Macoris is an important fruit-shipping center, and is only twenty miles from Puerto Plata, which has been the stronghold of the revolutionists since the outbreak of the insurrection. Under the head 'Warships Dispatched,' the paper says that in a previous dispatch Minister Powell asked that a warship be sent to protect American interests; the cruiser Baltimore has arrived at Santo Domingo since Mr. Powell sent the request for aid, and the Newport, which is now at Savannah, is coaling preparatory to sailing to the revolutionary republic.
records.summary_es: El Washington Times publica la parte final de un despacho de Washington y dos notas sobre los buques de guerra alemanes y Macorís: Alemania ha ordenado a dos buques de guerra salir de Santo Tomás hacia Santo Domingo; al vapor alemán Athen se le negó la admisión al puerto de San Domingo, y un informe de este asunto al gobierno alemán hizo que se emitiera de inmediato una orden para el movimiento de los cruceros alemanes Panther y Gazelle hacia aguas dominicanas. Bajo el titular «Macoris Partly Destroyed», el periódico dice que el ministro Powell, en Santo Domingo, ha informado al Departamento de Estado que una cañonera en poder de revolucionarios tomó por asalto Macorís, un puerto importante en la costa norte de la isla, y destruyó parte de la población; el despacho tenía fecha del 6 de noviembre; también se declara en el despacho que los intereses estadounidenses en Macorís son grandes; Macorís es un importante centro de embarque de frutas y está a solo veinte millas de Puerto Plata, que ha sido el baluarte de los revolucionarios desde el estallido de la insurrección. Bajo el titular «Warships Dispatched», el periódico dice que en un despacho anterior el ministro Powell pidió que se enviara un buque de guerra para proteger los intereses estadounidenses; el crucero Baltimore ha llegado a Santo Domingo desde que el señor Powell envió la solicitud de ayuda, y el Newport, que está ahora en Savannah, está cargando carbón preparándose para zarpar hacia la república revolucionaria.

records.passage: A Gunboat Steams South. (By the Associated Press.) Savannah, Ga., Nov. 9. — Commander Meltz, of the United States gunboat Newport, received orders to coal at once and sail for Puerto Plata. The coaling was rushed and at 7:30 o'clock, the Newport fired a gun to summon such members of her crew as had received shore leave. records.summary_en: The Leader prints a Washington item of November 11: the State Department has received another belated dispatch from Minister Powell, at San Domingo City, dated the 6th inst., in which the minister says: 'Macoris has just been bombarded by a Dominican naval vessel and partially destroyed. The ship then returned to San Domingo City. The American interests in Macoris are very considerable.' Macoris is a fruit shipping port doing a large business with the United States, and the bombardment is supposed to have been without the required twenty-four hours' notice; if it appears that American interests have suffered by arbitrary action at the hands of the Dominican government, the State Department will demand full redress, and the cruiser Baltimore, now at Puerto Plata, undoubtedly will prevent further happenings of this kind; two German warships, which started from St. Thomas Monday morning, also are available by this time to aid in the maintenance of order. The item appears under the head 'Partially Destroyed'.

records.headline: The Forest Republican prints the Cherokee narrative from San Domingo
records.summary_en: The Forest Republican prints the Cherokee narrative from San Domingo: a Dominican warship stopped the Clyde line steamer Cherokee as she was nearing Puerto Plata and informed the captain that he could not enter that port; the Cherokee then proceeded for Samana and was also prevented from entering that port, the minister of war ordering the captain of the Cherokee to proceed direct to the capital. On the arrival of the vessel at San Domingo the government demanded that the cargo intended for Puerto Plata and Samana be landed at that port; the agent of the company and the captain of the Cherokee refused to comply with this demand and appealed to Minister Powell for protection. When the Cherokee was ready to leave for Azua clearance papers were refused, and it was again demanded that she land her cargo at that port; Minister Powell wrote a sharp note to the government demanding a permit for the Cherokee to depart; the government refused to allow a pilot to board the vessel, and Minister Powell then instructed Captain Archibald to take his ship out and proceed for Azua, keeping his cargo aboard and landing it at the ports of destination. The energetic action of Minister Powell has caused a great sensation, especially as his proceeding lacked the support of an American warship; the Cherokee left the harbor without a pilot.
records.summary_es: El Forest Republican publica el relato del Cherokee desde San Domingo: un buque de guerra dominicano detuvo al vapor Cherokee, de la línea Clyde, cuando se acercaba a Puerto Plata e informó al capitán que no podía entrar en ese puerto; el Cherokee se dirigió entonces a Samaná y también se le impidió entrar en ese puerto, ordenando el ministro de Guerra al capitán del Cherokee dirigirse directamente a la capital. A la llegada del buque a San Domingo el gobierno exigió que el cargamento destinado a Puerto Plata y Samaná se desembarcara en ese puerto; el agente de la compañía y el capitán del Cherokee se negaron a cumplir esta demanda y apelaron al ministro Powell en busca de protección. Cuando el Cherokee estaba listo para partir hacia Azua se le negaron los papeles de despacho y se exigió de nuevo que desembarcara su cargamento en ese puerto; el ministro Powell escribió una nota enérgica al gobierno exigiendo un permiso para que el Cherokee partiera; el gobierno se negó a permitir que un piloto subiera a bordo del buque, y el ministro Powell instruyó entonces al capitán Archibald a sacar su barco y dirigirse a Azua, conservando su cargamento a bordo y desembarcándolo en los puertos de destino. La enérgica acción del ministro Powell ha causado gran sensación, especialmente porque su proceder carecía del apoyo de un buque de guerra estadounidense; el Cherokee salió del puerto sin piloto.

records.headline: The Journal prints two belated cables from Minister Powell and a Washington item
records.summary_en: The Journal prints two belated cables from Minister Powell and a Washington item: the State Department received a cablegram from Minister Powell, dated San Domingo, November 6, 11 p. m.: 'Insurgents have reached the city. Attacked to-night on three sides. City being shelled. No damage.' Another belated dispatch under the same date said: 'Macoris has just been bombarded by a San Domingan naval vessel and partially destroyed. The ship then returned to San Domingo city. The American interests in Macoris are very considerable.' Macoris is a fruit-shipping port, doing a large business with the United States, and the bombardment is supposed to have been without the required twenty-four hours' notice; if it appears that American interests have suffered by arbitrary action at the hands of the Dominican government, the State Department will demand full redress, and the cruiser Baltimore, now at Puerto Plata, undoubtedly will prevent further happenings of this kind; two German warships which started from St. Thomas yesterday morning are also available by this time to aid in the maintenance of order. Late to-night Assistant Secretary Loomis, of the State Department, called at the executive offices of the White House and spent some time in the telegraph room; he refused to admit that he was cabling fresh instructions to Minister Powell, although he said that late in the afternoon he had notified the minister that the cruiser Baltimore was now on her way to that city and would probably reach there some time during the night; the dispatch reporting the capitulation of the city of San Domingo to the revolutionists was shown to Mr. Loomis.
records.summary_es: El Journal publica dos cables atrasados del ministro Powell y una nota de Washington: el Departamento de Estado recibió un cablegrama del ministro Powell, fechado en San Domingo el 6 de noviembre, a las 11 p. m.: «Los insurgentes han llegado a la ciudad. Atacada esta noche por tres lados. La ciudad está siendo bombardeada. Ningún daño». Otro despacho atrasado bajo la misma fecha decía: «Macorís acaba de ser bombardeado por un buque de guerra de San Domingo y parcialmente destruido. El buque regresó entonces a la ciudad de San Domingo. Los intereses estadounidenses en Macorís son muy considerables». Macorís es un puerto de embarque de frutas, que hace un gran negocio con los Estados Unidos, y se supone que el bombardeo fue sin el aviso requerido de veinticuatro horas; si resulta que los intereses estadounidenses han sufrido por la acción arbitraria del gobierno dominicano, el Departamento de Estado exigirá plena reparación, y el crucero Baltimore, ahora en Puerto Plata, sin duda impedirá nuevos hechos de esta clase; dos buques de guerra alemanes que salieron de Santo Tomás ayer por la mañana también están disponibles a estas horas para ayudar en el mantenimiento del orden. Tarde esta noche el subsecretario Loomis, del Departamento de Estado, se presentó en las oficinas ejecutivas de la Casa Blanca y pasó algún tiempo en la sala de telégrafos; se negó a admitir que estaba cablegrafiando nuevas instrucciones al ministro Powell, aunque dijo que a última hora de la tarde había notificado al ministro que el crucero Baltimore ya venía en camino hacia esa ciudad y probablemente llegaría allí en algún momento durante la noche; el despacho que informaba de la capitulación de la ciudad de Santo Domingo ante los revolucionarios fue mostrado al señor Loomis.

records.headline: The Advertiser prints a sketch of Jiminez's career: Jiminez landed
records.summary_en: The Advertiser prints a sketch of Jiminez's career: Jiminez landed in Santo Domingo and was received joyfully by the people; after the death of Heureaux a provisional government was formed by General Horatio Vasquez; an election was ordered and Jiminez became president. Vasquez turned against Jiminez and led a successful revolution; Jiminez fled to New York. Early this year the Vasquez government was routed by the former friends of Jiminez, with General Woss y Gil at their head; Jiminez went to Santo Domingo, but Woss y Gil was made president. Now Jiminez is reported to have won the reins of power from those who headed a revolution while posing as his friends and ostensibly in his interests. The sketch adds that in 1898 he got possession of the American steamship Fanita, armed and equipped it for an expedition against the Spaniards in Cuba, and sailed from Mobile.
records.summary_es: El Advertiser publica una semblanza de la carrera del general Jiménez: Jiménez desembarcó en Santo Domingo y fue recibido jubilosamente por el pueblo; después de la muerte de Heureaux se formó un gobierno provisional por el general Horatio Vásquez; se ordenó una elección y Jiménez se convirtió en presidente. Vásquez se volvió contra Jiménez y encabezó una revolución exitosa; Jiménez huyó a Nueva York. Temprano este año el gobierno de Vásquez fue derrotado por los antiguos amigos de Jiménez, con el general Woss y Gil a la cabeza; Jiménez fue a Santo Domingo, pero Woss y Gil fue hecho presidente. La semblanza añade que en 1898 se apoderó del vapor estadounidense Fanita, lo armó y lo equipó para una expedición contra los españoles en Cuba, y zarpó de Mobile.

records.headline: The Call prints a San Domingo dispatch of November 11: the insurgents
records.summary_en: The Call prints a San Domingo dispatch of November 11: the insurgents, having officially notified the foreign consuls yesterday that they contemplated a heavy bombardment on the capital, made an all night attack with shells and small arms; the attack was repulsed; the city government refused the rebels' demand to surrender. The special dispatch says General Paul Cabrera, at the head of 590 revolutionists, with six pieces of artillery and a treasure chest containing $4,000, arrived yesterday before the city; the guard for the German consulate, which was landed from the cruisers of Germany now in port, keeps in instant communication with the latter by means of a signal station which has been erected over the consulate; last night's artillery duel resulted in no damage, as the insurgents' shells failed to explode; both sides express confidence; the general idea is that the capital cannot be taken by assault, although the government forces have been bottled up since the last sortie. The German cruiser Gazelle, accompanied by the merchantman Athen, has returned from St. Thomas to force the blockade at Sanchez, Macoris, Puerto Plata and Samana. The foreign consuls held a two-hour conference yesterday and decided to ignore the insurgents.

records.headline: Hundred revolutionists, with six pieces of artillery and a treasure
records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported that 800 insurgents with artillery laid siege to the capital of Santo Domingo, prompting German warships *Panther* and *Gazelle* to land armed guards and escort the merchant steamer *Athen*. Dominican exiles in New York received reports that insurgent forces had proclaimed General Juan Isidro Jimenes president of the republic. Jimenes had previously resigned as Dominican fiscal agent to organize the armed movement to reclaim the presidency from which he had been ousted.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó que 800 insurgentes con artillería sitiaron la capital de Santo Domingo, lo que motivó a los buques de guerra alemanes *Panther* y *Gazelle* a desembarcar destacamentos armados y escoltar al vapor mercante *Athen*. Exiliados dominicanos en Nueva York recibieron informes de que las fuerzas insurgentes habían proclamado presidente de la república al general Juan Isidro Jimenes. Jimenes había renunciado previamente a su cargo de agente fiscal dominicano con el propósito de organizar el movimiento armado para recuperar la presidencia de la cual había sido desalojado.

records.headline: The Times-Recorder prints a San Domingo dispatch on the bombardment of the capital
records.summary_en: The Times-Recorder prints a San Domingo dispatch on the bombardment of the capital: the German cruiser Gazelle arrived Monday and landed marines; the German cruiser Panther arrived the preceding day; no other foreign war vessels are here. Previous to the beginning of the bombardment of San Domingo the revolutionists notified the diplomatic corps and the consular officers that they had previously served notice on the Dominican government that the forces of the revolution intended to adopt all means, including a bombardment, in their efforts to capture the city; the representatives of the powers met to-day and decided that they could only hold communication with the legally established government of the country. Paul Cabrera, at the head of 800 revolutionists, with six pieces of artillery and a treasure chest containing $4,000, arrived yesterday before the city. The situation here is becoming very critical, and the presence of more warships at San Domingo is urgently required. The guard for the German consulate, which was landed from the cruisers of Germany now in port, is in constant communication with the latter by means of a signal station which has been erected over the consulate. The German steamer Athen, which was prevented some days ago from landing her cargo at San Pedro de Macoris, under the protection of the German cruiser succeeded in landing her freight at that port, and has proceeded to the northern ports of Santo Domingo, for which she has cargo and passengers; the Athen has a German escort with her in order to facilitate the discharging of her freight.
records.summary_es: El Times-Recorder publica un despacho de San Domingo sobre el bombardeo de la capital: el crucero alemán Gazelle llegó el lunes y desembarcó infantes de marina; el crucero alemán Panther llegó el día anterior; no hay otros buques de guerra extranjeros aquí. Antes del comienzo del bombardeo de San Domingo, los revolucionarios notificaron al cuerpo diplomático y a los oficiales consulares que previamente habían notificado al gobierno dominicano que las fuerzas de la revolución tenían la intención de adoptar todos los medios, incluido un bombardeo, en sus esfuerzos por capturar la ciudad; los representantes de las potencias se reunieron hoy y decidieron que solo podían mantener comunicación con el gobierno legalmente establecido del país. Paul Cabrera, al frente de 800 revolucionarios, con seis piezas de artillería y un cofre del tesoro que contiene $4,000, llegó ayer frente a la ciudad. La situación aquí se está volviendo muy crítica, y la presencia de más buques de guerra en San Domingo se requiere con urgencia. La guardia del consulado alemán, que fue desembarcada de los cruceros de Alemania ahora en puerto, está en comunicación constante con estos últimos por medio de una estación de señales que ha sido erigida sobre el consulado. El vapor alemán Athen, al que se le impidió hace algunos días desembarcar su cargamento en San Pedro de Macorís, bajo la protección del crucero alemán logró desembarcar su flete en ese puerto, y ha proseguido hacia los puertos del norte de Santo Domingo, para los que tiene cargamento y pasajeros; el Athen tiene una escolta alemana con él para facilitar la descarga de su flete.

records.headline: The Savannah Morning News prints a San Domingo dispatch, a Washington item
records.summary_en: The Savannah Morning News prints a San Domingo dispatch, a Washington item under the head 'Baltimore to Stop It,' and an item under the head 'Won't Recognize Them': the revolutionists notified the diplomatic corps and the consular officers that they had previously served notice on the Dominican government that the forces of the revolution intended to adopt all means, including a bombardment, in their efforts to capture the city; the representatives of the powers met to-day and decided that they could only hold communication with the legally established government of the country; Gen. Paul Cabrera, at the head of 8,000 revolutionists, with six pieces of artillery and a treasure chest containing $4,000, arrived yesterday before the city. The Washington item, of November 11, says Capt. Briggs, commanding the cruiser Baltimore, telegraphed the Navy Department to-day from Puerto Plata that the Baltimore left there this morning for Macoris and San Domingo City; it is said at the State Department that the instructions to the American naval officers are of a character to prevent any further bombardment by either government or insurgent forces of any San Dominican port where American interests are involved without the notice required by international law. The third item, from San Domingo, November 11, says the revolutionists have addressed a letter to Minister Powell, informing him that engagements entered into with the United States by the government presided over by President Woss y Gil will not be recognized by them; the letter requests that Minister Powell recognize the revolutionists, but the minister has refused to hold communication with them; the political situation here is unchanged.

records.headline: The Star prints an account of the Cherokee's voyage: after some parley
records.summary_en: The Star prints an account of the Cherokee's voyage: after some parley the Cherokee was allowed to go into Puerto Plata, land her cargo and mails and reload cargo; off Macoris, on November 3, the Cherokee was stopped by the same vessel and again permitted to proceed; at Samana, November 5, the war vessel ordered the Cherokee away; the Cherokee waited until after dark, when the man-of-war sailed out of port without lights, and then went in and landed her cargo and mails; she succeeded in making schedule time at all her usual ports except Monte Cristi. Macoris was evacuated by the government forces November 3, the day of sailing, and all the ports except San Domingo City were in the hands of the insurgents when she finally sailed; at Puerto Plata, November 6, a French and a Cuban steamer were ordered away by the Dominican warship. The Dominican government officials refused the Cherokee clearance papers to leave San Domingo, and also refused to allow a pilot to take her out of the harbor; Minister Powell protested to the Dominican government and instructed the captain of the Cherokee to take his ship out without clearance papers or pilot. records.headline: The Tribune prints an account of the Cherokee's outward voyage
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints an account of the Cherokee's outward voyage: on her outward voyage the Cherokee was stopped off Puerto Plata by a Dominican man-of-war, which fired several shots across her bow; after some trouble the Cherokee was allowed to proceed to Puerto Plata; there the customs officials ordered Captain Archibald to discharge all his cargo and mail, forbidding him to enter any other Dominican ports; this Captain Archibald refused to do. The next day he sailed for Macoris, expecting to find the Baltimore there; the cruiser was not at this port, but Minister Powell went aboard and conferred for half an hour with the captain of the Cherokee. From that port the Cherokee steamed for Samana; at the entrance to the harbor the Cherokee was again stopped by the Dominican gunboat El Presidente and Captain Archibald told that he could not proceed because of the blockade; the Cherokee waited until after dark, and when the gunboat sailed away she went into the harbor and discharged her cargo and mails. At Monte Christi, her next port, she was met again by the omnipresent El Presidente, which threatened to blow her out of the water if she evaded the blockade again; the Cherokee had to lay off Monte Christi all night. One of the passengers on the Cherokee, in discussing the revolution which was responsible for the vessel's troubles and the political situation in general, said that not only was there an absolute absence of animosity to Americans in the country, but that on the contrary there existed a strong sentiment in favor of the establishment of a protectorate over the republic.
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica un relato del viaje de ida del Cherokee: en su viaje de ida el Cherokee fue detenido frente a Puerto Plata por un buque de guerra dominicano, que disparó varios tiros sobre su proa; después de alguna dificultad se permitió al Cherokee proseguir a Puerto Plata; allí los oficiales de aduana ordenaron al capitán Archibald descargar todo su cargamento y correo, prohibiéndole entrar en cualquier otro puerto dominicano; esto el capitán Archibald se negó a hacer. Al día siguiente zarpó hacia Macorís, esperando encontrar allí al Baltimore; el crucero no estaba en este puerto, pero el ministro Powell subió a bordo y conferenció durante media hora con el capitán del Cherokee. Desde ese puerto el Cherokee se dirigió a Samaná; a la entrada del puerto el Cherokee fue detenido de nuevo por la cañonera dominicana El Presidente y se dijo al capitán Archibald que no podía proseguir a causa del bloqueo; el Cherokee esperó hasta que oscureció, y cuando la cañonera se alejó entró en el puerto y descargó su cargamento y correo. En Monte Cristi, su puerto siguiente, fue recibido de nuevo por el omnipresente El Presidente, que amenazó con volarlo fuera del agua si evadía el bloqueo otra vez; el Cherokee tuvo que permanecer frente a Monte Cristi toda la noche. Uno de los pasajeros del Cherokee, al discutir la revolución que fue responsable de los problemas del buque y la situación política en general, dijo que no solo había una ausencia absoluta de animosidad hacia los estadounidenses en el país, sino que, por el contrario, existía un fuerte sentimiento a favor del establecimiento de un protectorado sobre la república.

records.headline: The Forrest City Times prints the closing part of a San Domingo dispatch
records.summary_en: The Forrest City Times prints the closing part of a San Domingo dispatch: the forces of the revolution intended to adopt all means, including a bombardment, in their efforts to capture the city; the representatives of the powers met and decided that they could only hold communications with the legally-established government of the country. Gen. Paul Cabrera, at the head of 800 revolutionists, with six pieces of artillery and a treasure chest containing $4,000, arrived Tuesday before the city. The situation here is becoming very critical, and the presence of more warships at San Domingo is urgently required. The guard for the German consulate, which was landed from the cruisers of Germany now in port, is in constant communication with the latter by means of a signal station which has been erected over the consulate. The German steamer Athen, which was prevented, some days ago, from landing her cargo at San Pedro de Macoris, has, under protection of a German cruiser, succeeded in landing her freight at that port, and has proceeded to the northern ports of Santo Domingo, for which she has cargo and passengers; the Athen has a German escort with her in order to facilitate the discharging of her freight.

records.headline: The Inter Mountain prints a Port-au-Prince dispatch: General Jiminez
records.summary_en: The Inter Mountain prints a Port-au-Prince dispatch: General Jiminez, head of the Dominican revolution, has left Port Au Prince, Hayti, on board the St. Simon, with the intention, according to report, of forcing the blockade of Puerto Plata on the northern coast of Santo Domingo; the Haytien authorities formally opposed the landing in Hayti of General Jiminez, in spite of his strong insistence upon being permitted to do so; it is said that if the St. Simon is interfered with she will ask for the assistance of the German cruiser Gazelle or other foreign ships which may be in Dominican waters; the French cruiser Jurien de la Graviere, which was in these waters recently, is understood to have returned to Martinique. Telegraphic communication with the interior of Santo Domingo was re-established yesterday morning, but now it is again interrupted, and it is reported that severe fighting must have occurred before San Domingo.
records.summary_es: El Inter Mountain publica un despacho de Puerto Príncipe: el general Jiménez, jefe de la revolución dominicana, ha salido de Puerto Príncipe, Haití, a bordo del St. Simon, con la intención, según se informa, de forzar el bloqueo de Puerto Plata en la costa norte de Santo Domingo; las autoridades haitianas se opusieron formalmente al desembarco en Haití del general Jiménez, a pesar de su fuerte insistencia en que se le permitiera hacerlo; se dice que si el St. Simon es interferido pedirá la ayuda del crucero alemán Gazelle o de otros buques extranjeros que puedan estar en aguas dominicanas; el crucero francés Jurien de la Graviere, que estuvo recientemente en estas aguas, se entiende que ha regresado a Martinica. La comunicación telegráfica con el interior de Santo Domingo fue restablecida ayer por la mañana, pero ahora está de nuevo interrumpida, y se informa que debe haber ocurrido una lucha severa frente a San Domingo.

records.headline: The Sentinel prints part of a San Domingo dispatch: the revolutionists
records.summary_en: The Sentinel prints part of a San Domingo dispatch: the revolutionists had served notice on the Dominican government that the forces of the revolution intended to adopt all means, including a bombardment, in their efforts to capture the city; the representatives of the powers met and decided that they could only hold communications with the legally-established government of the country. Gen. Paul Cabrera, at the head of 800 revolutionists, with six pieces of artillery and a treasure chest containing $4,000, arrived Tuesday before the city. The situation here is becoming very critical, and the presence of more warships at San Domingo is urgently required. The guard for the German consulate, which was landed from the cruisers of Germany now in port, is in constant communication with the latter by means of a signal station which has been erected over the consulate. The German steamer Athen, which was prevented, some days ago, from landing her cargo at San Pedro de Macoris, has, under protection of a German cruiser, succeeded in landing her freight at that port, and has proceeded to the northern ports of Santo Domingo, for which she has cargo and passengers; the Athen has a German escort with her, in order to facilitate the discharging of her freight.
records.summary_es: El Sentinel publica parte de un despacho de San Domingo: los revolucionarios habían notificado al gobierno dominicano que las fuerzas de la revolución tenían la intención de adoptar todos los medios, incluido un bombardeo, en sus esfuerzos por capturar la ciudad; los representantes de las potencias se reunieron y decidieron que solo podían mantener comunicaciones con el gobierno legalmente establecido del país. El general Paul Cabrera, al frente de 800 revolucionarios, con seis piezas de artillería y un cofre del tesoro que contiene $4,000, llegó el martes frente a la ciudad. La situación aquí se está volviendo muy crítica, y la presencia de más buques de guerra en San Domingo se requiere con urgencia. La guardia del consulado alemán, que fue desembarcada de los cruceros de Alemania ahora en puerto, está en comunicación constante con estos últimos por medio de una estación de señales que ha sido erigida sobre el consulado. El vapor alemán Athen, al que se le impidió, hace algunos días, desembarcar su cargamento en San Pedro de Macorís, ha logrado, bajo la protección de un crucero alemán, desembarcar su flete en ese puerto, y ha proseguido hacia los puertos del norte de Santo Domingo, para los que tiene cargamento y pasajeros; el Athen tiene una escolta alemana con él para facilitar la descarga de su flete.

records.headline: The Age-Herald prints a Cherokee voyage account: after the Dominican warship
records.summary_en: The Age-Herald prints a Cherokee voyage account: after the Dominican warship fired several shots across her bow and stopped her, and after some parley, the Cherokee was allowed to go into Puerto Plata, land her cargo and mails and reload cargo; off Macoris, on November 3, the Cherokee was stopped by the same vessel and again permitted to proceed; at Samana, on November 5, the war vessel ordered the Cherokee away, and the Cherokee waited until after dark, when the man-of-war sailed out of port without lights, and then went in and landed her cargo and mails; she succeeded in making schedule time at all her usual ports except Monte Cristi. Macoris was evacuated by the government forces on November 3, the day of sailing, and all the ports except San Domingo City were in the hands of the insurgents when she finally sailed; at Puerto Plata, on November 6, a French and a Cuban steamer were ordered away by the Dominican warship. The Dominican officials refused the Cherokee clearance papers to leave San Domingo, and also refused to allow a pilot to take her out of the harbor; Minister Powell protested to the Dominican government and instructed the captain of the Cherokee to take his ship out without clearance papers or pilot. The Cherokee brought nineteen cabin passengers from San Domingo, but no refugees.

Macorís fue evacuado por las fuerzas del gobierno el 3 de noviembre, el día de la partida, y todos los puertos excepto la ciudad de Santo Domingo estaban en manos de los insurgentes cuando finalmente zarpó; en Puerto Plata, el 6 de noviembre, un vapor francés y uno cubano fueron alejados por orden del buque de guerra dominicano. Los oficiales dominicanos negaron al Cherokee los papeles de despacho para salir de San Domingo y también se negaron a permitir que un piloto lo sacara del puerto; el ministro Powell protestó ante el gobierno dominicano e instruyó al capitán del Cherokee a sacar su barco sin papeles de despacho ni piloto. El Cherokee trajo diecinueve pasajeros de cabina desde San Domingo, pero ningún refugiado.

Jiminez has been proclaimed president of the republic. On Monday, November 2, the Clyde line steamer Cherokee was fired upon by the Dominican cruiser Presidente while the steamer was running the blockade of Samana and returned to the capital; the United States cruiser Baltimore reported to Minister Powell at the capital, and three hours later she left to convoy the Cherokee. On Wednesday the government forces abandoned Macoris, and the following day the Dominican cruiser Independencia bombarded the town.

records.headline: The Star prints part of a discussion of the island: the island
records.summary_en: The Star prints part of a discussion of the island: the island has an area of 28,000 square miles, and upon it are the two republics of Hayti and Santo Domingo; Santo Domingo itself is not thickly populated, and the paper says the business of the republic is conducted by the whites, who number about 20 per cent of the population, and as a rule hold the offices. The paper argues that both republics have retrograded steadily, that both are financially wrecked, and that the Monroe doctrine gives the United States control of the island so far as any European power is concerned. Under the head 'Strategic Value of Samana Bay,' the paper describes Samana Bay, thirty-one miles long, at the eastern extremity of the island, just across from Porto Rico, as one of the most beautiful and valuable bays in the West Indies, and says the United States has sought possession of this bay as a strategic point in the Caribbean Sea for almost one hundred years, Gen. Jackson having first recommended the purchase in a message to Congress.

El periódico sostiene que ambas repúblicas han retrocedido constantemente, que ambas están financieramente arruinadas, y que la doctrina Monroe da a los Estados Unidos el control de la isla en lo que concierne a cualquier potencia europea. Bajo el titular «Strategic Value of Samana Bay», el periódico describe la bahía de Samaná, de treinta y una millas de largo, en el extremo oriental de la isla, justo frente a Puerto Rico, como una de las bahías más hermosas y valiosas de las Indias Occidentales, y dice que los Estados Unidos han buscado la posesión de esta bahía como punto estratégico en el mar Caribe durante casi cien años, habiendo recomendado el general Jackson por primera vez la compra en un mensaje al Congreso.

records.summary_en: The Constitution prints the closing part of a Port-au-Prince dispatch: the French steamer St. Simon, with General Jiminez aboard, has left Port-au-Prince, Hayti, with the intention, according to report, of forcing the blockade of Puerto Plata, on the northern coast of Santo Domingo; the Haitian authorities formally opposed the landing in Hayti of General Jiminez, in spite of his strong insistence upon being permitted to do so; it is said that if the St. Simon is interfered with she will ask for the assistance of the German cruiser Gazelle, or any other foreign warship which may be in Dominican waters; the French cruiser Jurien de la Graviere, which was in these waters recently, is understood to have returned to the island of Martinique. Telegraphic communication with the interior of Santo Domingo was re-established yesterday, but now is again interrupted, and it is reported that severe fighting must have occurred before San Domingo.

records.headline: The Star prints a New York item: the agents here of the Clyde line
records.summary_en: The Star prints a New York item: the agents here of the Clyde line steamer Cherokee, which had trouble with the Dominican government authorities on her last trip to that island, declared to-day that the Cherokee will sail next Wednesday on her regular schedule and will pursue her regular itinerary, stopping at Samana Bay, Monte Christi, Sanchez, Puerto Plata and Macoris. Manuel de J. Galvan, consul general from San Domingo to New York, said to-day that the Cherokee will surely be sunk if she attempts to enter the five harbors named; he says that the entire San Domingan navy, the gunboats El Presidente and Independencia, are on guard to maintain the blockade of those ports, now in the hands of the rebels, under Jiminez. 'If the Cherokee attempts to enter any of those ports the gunboats will not parley with her this time,' said Mr. Galvan. 'They will surely sink her.' The item appears under the head 'Hostile Threats Made Against Steamer Cherokee'.

records.headline: The Star prints part of an account of the exiles' expedition
records.summary_en: The Star prints part of an account of the exiles' expedition from Cuba: the exiles decided to co-operate with a general uprising along the frontier of Haiti, taking in the towns of Monte Cristy, Dajabon and Guayubin, and extending to the towns of Santiago de los Caballeros and La Vega, having received notification from the governor of Puerto Plata, Gen. and ex-Priest Don Carlos Morales, of the result of their plans. Then they prepared to take the Cuban steamer Maria Herrera with a view of landing in Puerto Plata, which was held by Gen. Carlos Morales, and so join the revolutionary movement. Unfortunately the Dominican consul in Cuba became aware of their movements and applied to the Cuban authorities to have them prevented from embarking, but he was informed by them that as there was no evidence that these men were taking arms and war stores, and as they were leaving the country as peaceable citizens, they could not be interfered with. The Dominican consul then telegraphed to the president of the Dominican republic at the city of Santo Domingo informing him of their having embarked for some port of the republic, presumably Puerto Plata. Under the head 'Took Passage for San Juan,' the account continues: the Dominican exiles, being perfectly aware of the uncertainty of such uprisings, took passage for San Juan, Porto Rico, intending to disembark in Puerto Plata if all were well, but if not to continue to Porto Rico and join ex-President Jiminez. Upon arriving off the port of Puerto Plata a Dominican warship was sighted, but no attention was paid to her, and they continued their course.
records.summary_es: El Star publica parte de un relato de la expedición de los exiliados desde Cuba: los exiliados decidieron cooperar con un levantamiento general a lo largo de la frontera de Haití, que abarcaba las poblaciones de Monte Cristi, Dajabón y Guayubín, y se extendía a las poblaciones de Santiago de los Caballeros y La Vega, habiendo recibido notificación del gobernador de Puerto Plata, el general y ex sacerdote don Carlos Morales, del resultado de sus planes. Entonces se prepararon para tomar el vapor cubano María Herrera con miras a desembarcar en Puerto Plata, que estaba en poder del general Carlos Morales, y unirse así al movimiento revolucionario. Desafortunadamente el cónsul dominicano en Cuba se enteró de sus movimientos y solicitó a las autoridades cubanas que les impidieran embarcar, pero fue informado por ellas de que, como no había evidencia de que estos hombres llevaran armas y pertrechos de guerra, y como salían del país como ciudadanos pacíficos, no se podía interferir con ellos. El cónsul dominicano telegrafió entonces al presidente de la república dominicana en la ciudad de Santo Domingo informándole que habían embarcado hacia algún puerto de la república, presumiblemente Puerto Plata. Bajo el titular «Took Passage for San Juan», el relato continúa: los exiliados dominicanos, perfectamente conscientes de la incertidumbre de tales levantamientos, tomaron pasaje para San Juan, Puerto Rico, con la intención de desembarcar en Puerto Plata si todo iba bien, pero si no, continuar a Puerto Rico y unirse al ex presidente Jiménez. Al llegar frente al puerto de Puerto Plata se avistó un buque de guerra dominicano, pero no se le prestó atención, y continuaron su rumbo.

records.headline: The Star prints a further part of its account of the Dominican exiles
records.summary_en: The Star prints a further part of its account of the Dominican exiles and of President Woss y Gil: the account speaks of a warrior priest, brother of a renowned soldier who perished in the attack upon that town, as a man of great energy and high aspiration, determined to equal his brother in fame. All the exiles are confident of the fall of the government, as they say that Puerto Plata and Santiago de los Caballeros together form the keystone of the republic, and these towns are asserted to be in the hands of the rebels. President Alejandro Woss y Gil is a man of considerable worth as a statesman and soldier; he is a well-educated man and has lived abroad for a considerable time, representing the Dominican republic at Washington for quite a number of years during the presidency of General Heureaux. Under the head 'Second Presidential Term,' the account continues: this is his second presidential term, having occupied that position for the first time when he was about twenty-six or twenty-seven years of age, being the first Dominican to occupy that high post at such an early age; he was the intimate friend of President Heureaux, and is said to be a man of his school, that is to say, a man who does not hesitate to give his troublesome adversaries six feet of good Dominican soil whenever he can get hold of them, and a tenacious fighter, who is not to be daunted by either the large number or superior strategic position of the enemy.
records.summary_es: El Star publica otra parte de su relato de los exiliados dominicanos y del presidente Woss y Gil: el relato habla de un sacerdote guerrero, hermano de un renombrado soldado que pereció en el ataque contra esa población, como un hombre de gran energía y alta aspiración, decidido a igualar la fama de su hermano. Todos los exiliados confían en la caída del gobierno, pues dicen que Puerto Plata y Santiago de los Caballeros juntas forman la piedra angular de la república, y se afirma que estas poblaciones están en manos de los rebeldes. El presidente Alejandro Woss y Gil es un hombre de considerable valor como estadista y soldado; es un hombre bien educado y ha vivido en el extranjero por un tiempo considerable, representando a la república dominicana en Washington durante bastantes años durante la presidencia del general Heureaux. Bajo el titular «Second Presidential Term», el relato continúa: este es su segundo período presidencial, habiendo ocupado esa posición por primera vez cuando tenía unos veintiséis o veintisiete años de edad, siendo el primer dominicano en ocupar ese alto puesto a una edad tan temprana; fue el amigo íntimo del presidente Heureaux, y se dice que es un hombre de su escuela, es decir, un hombre que no vacila en dar a sus adversarios problemáticos seis pies de buena tierra dominicana siempre que puede echarles mano, y un luchador tenaz, que no se deja amedrentar ni por el gran número ni por la posición estratégica superior del enemigo.

records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported that Dominican Consul General Galván threatened that government gunboats would sink any vessel, including the Clyde Line steamer *Cherokee*, attempting to enter rebel-controlled ports. New York customs authorities refused to deny clearances to American merchantmen, stating that the United States had not recognized the blockade as effective. The report also noted that President Wos y Gil had agreed to arbitrate the San Domingo Improvement Company's four-million-dollar claim regarding railroad construction.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó que el cónsul general dominicano Galván amenazó con que los cañoneros del gobierno hundirían cualquier embarcación, incluido el vapor *Cherokee* de la Clyde Line, que intentara ingresar a puertos bajo control rebelde. Las autoridades aduaneras de Nueva York se negaron a denegar el despacho a los mercantes estadounidenses, alegando que los Estados Unidos no habían reconocido el bloqueo como efectivo. El informe señaló asimismo que el presidente Wos y Gil había aceptado someter a arbitraje la reclamación de cuatro millones de dólares de la San Domingo Improvement Company relativa a la construcción del ferrocarril.

records.headline: The Democrat prints part of a New York item on the sailing of the Cherokee
records.summary_en: The Democrat prints part of a New York item on the sailing of the Cherokee, opening with the Clyde line's answer: 'Well, you may say that the Clyde line is attending to its own business and that a part of that business is to touch at Dominican ports, and that is what we are going to do.' Senor Galvan, consul general for Santo Domingo, who is a godson of General Jiminez, the head of the rebels, said: 'Well, the gunboats will not parley with her this time. If the Independencia does not sink her El Presidente certainly will.' The offices of the consul general were besieged with anxious shippers who wanted to know what the government was going to do about it; one of them informed Senor Galvan that the Clyde line had informed him that it would carry his goods to Puerto Plata and that two United States gunboats were to convoy the Cherokee; the consul general snapped his fingers. 'My instructions are that the cargo of any vessel entering rebel ports will be confiscated and the crew treated as pirates. Now, you can take your chances if you wish, but I am telling you what will happen.' The Cherokee is the ship that ran the Dominican blockade some days ago.

Galvan, consul general from San Domingo to New York, said to-day that the Cherokee will surely be sunk if she attempts to enter the five harbors named; he says the entire San Dominican navy, the gunboats El Presidente and Independencia, are on guard to maintain the blockade of those ports, now in the hands of the rebels under Jiminez. Consul Galvan continued: 'Acting on orders from my government, I have notified the collector of the port that the ports of Samana Bay, Sanchez, Puerto Plata, Monte Cristi and Macoris are closed and that the Clyde steamers cannot be cleared for them. I think they will find they are mistaken if they think anything of that sort.'

New York, November 16.—More trouble seems to be in store for the steamer Cherokee which arrived here last week from Dominican ports after several thrilling experiences. The agents of the Clyde line steamers In this city declared today that the Cherokee will sail next Wednesday on her regular schedule and will pursue her regular itinerary, stopping at Samana Bay, Monte Christi, Sanchez, Puerto Plata and Macoris. Manuel De J. Galvan, consul general from San Domingo to New York, said today that the Cherokee will certainly be sunk if she attempts to enter the five harbors named. He says that the entire San Domingoan navy the gunboats El Presidente and Independence are on guard to maintain the blockade of those ports, now in the hands of the rebels under Jiminez. “If the Cherokee attempts to enter any of those ports the gunboats will not parley with her this time,” said Mr. Galvan. "They will surely sink her.' JIMINEZ IN COMMAND. San Juan, P. R., November 16.—Official advices received at the San Domingo consulate here say General Jiminez Is in supreme command of the revolutionists and that General Deschamps, the vice president of the republic, is to join Jiminez with the best of the supporters of President Wos y Gil.

El despacho aparece bajo el titular «To Attack San Domingo».

records.headline: The Tribune prints a Port-au-Prince dispatch: the French steamer
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints a Port-au-Prince dispatch: the French steamer St. Simon, with General Jiminez aboard, has left Port-au-Prince, Hayti, with the intention, according to report, of forcing the blockade of Puerto Plata, on the northern coast of Santo Domingo; the Haytien authorities formally opposed the landing in Hayti of Gen. Jiminez, in spite of his strong insistence upon being permitted to do so; it is said that if the St. Simon is interfered with she will ask for the assistance of the German cruiser Gazelle, or any other foreign warship which may be in Dominican waters; the French cruiser Jurien de la Graviere, which was in these waters recently, is understood to have returned to the island of Martinique. Telegraphic communication with the interior of Santo Domingo was re-established Friday morning, but now is again interrupted, and it is reported that severe fighting must have occurred before San Domingo.

records.headline: The Advertiser prints the closing part of a San Domingo dispatch
records.summary_en: The Advertiser prints the closing part of a San Domingo dispatch and a Washington item of November 17: General Woss y Gil refuses to capitulate and it is believed the fighting will be severe; the situation is desperate and fighting in the streets is liable to occur at any moment; the United States cruiser Baltimore has been compelled to leave to re-coal, and United States Minister Powell is endeavoring to protect American interests with the limited means at his disposal; a German naval vessel is ready to land troops at a moment's notice; the insurgents endeavored to have Minister Powell recognize them, but the minister refused to do so; the revolutionists fired on the Clyde Line steamer New York as she was entering the port of Samana, but the vessel was uninjured; the Dominican government has appointed Minister of Foreign Relations Galvan and Judge George Gray of Delaware as commissioners to arbitrate the Santo Domingo Improvement matter, as the result of Minister Powell's effort to compel the carrying out of the terms of the protocol, and Commissioner Galvan will leave for the United States tomorrow, though it is possible the insurgents may endeavor to capture him. The Washington item says the revolutionists of San Domingo applied to the State Department today for recognition by the United States, the application being presented by J. M. Giordan, who represented himself as the provisional agent of the revolutionary government of which General Jiminez is the head, and that the State Department declined the recognition.

records.headline: The News and Observer prints a New York item of November 16
records.summary_en: The News and Observer prints a New York item of November 16: the agents here of the Clyde Line steamer Cherokee, which had trouble with the Dominican government authorities on her last trip to that island, declared today that the Cherokee will sail next Wednesday on her regular schedule and will pursue her regular itinerary, stopping at Samana Bay, Monte Cristi, Sanchez, Puerto Plata and Macoris. Manuel de J. Galvan, consul general from San Domingo to New York, said today that the Cherokee will surely be sunk if she attempts to enter the five harbors named; he says that the entire San Dominican navy, the gunboats El Presidente and Independencia, are on guard to maintain the blockade of those ports, now in the hands of the rebels under Jiminez. 'If the Cherokee attempts to enter any of those ports the gunboats will not parley with her this time,' said Mr. Galvan. 'They will surely sink her.'

records.summary_en: The *Daily Kennebec Journal* reported that the United States government formally refused to recognize the Dominican naval blockade as effective and instructed port collectors to issue clearances for all Dominican harbors. In Dominican waters, insurgents fired unsuccessfully on the American steamer *New York* at Samana, while Minister Powell rejected rebel appeals for diplomatic recognition. In response to American diplomatic pressure, the Dominican government named Foreign Minister Galván and Judge Gray as arbitrators to resolve the San Domingo Improvement Company claim.

En aguas dominicanas, insurgentes dispararon infructuosamente contra el vapor estadounidense *New York* en Samaná, al tiempo que el ministro Powell desestimaba las peticiones rebeldes de reconocimiento diplomático. En respuesta a la presión diplomática estadounidense, el gobierno dominicano designó al ministro de Relaciones Exteriores Galván y al juez Gray como árbitros para resolver la reclamación de la San Domingo Improvement Company.

records.headline: The Pacific Commercial Advertiser prints a Washington dispatch of November 18 under the head 'Dominican Rebels Fire on Clyde Liner'
records.summary_en: The Pacific Commercial Advertiser prints a Washington dispatch of November 18 under the head 'Dominican Rebels Fire on Clyde Liner': the government has refused to recognize the Dominican revolutionists and has protested against the blockade; San Domingo is completely invested and is now being bombarded, and a general attack is expected momentarily; the revolutionists fired on the American Clyde liner as she was entering Samana Bay, but the vessel was uninjured. The Clyde line of steamers running from New York to Dominican ports are unpopular with a portion of the people of the country; the Clyde line had a claim against the Dominican government for $350,000 for refund of wharfage and other port dues, and, unable to get satisfaction from the government, finally secured a presentation of their claim through the United States government; Minister Powell demanded the settlement of the claim, but the matter was still in the air at the time the present revolution broke out; the port of Samana, in which the New York was fired upon, is being greedily watched by European powers that wish to secure it for a coaling station.

La línea Clyde de vapores que corren desde Nueva York a puertos dominicanos es impopular entre una parte de la población del país; la línea Clyde tenía una reclamación contra el gobierno dominicano por $350,000 por reembolso de derechos de muelle y otros derechos portuarios, y, al no poder obtener satisfacción del gobierno, finalmente logró la presentación de su reclamación por medio del gobierno de los Estados Unidos; el ministro Powell exigió la liquidación de la reclamación, pero el asunto estaba aún en el aire al momento de estallar la presente revolución; el puerto de Samaná, en el que el New York fue tiroteado, está siendo codiciosamente vigilado por potencias europeas que desean asegurarlo para una estación de carbón.

records.headline: The Advertiser prints part of a New York item on the Cherokee's sailing
records.summary_en: The Advertiser prints part of a New York item on the Cherokee's sailing: C. I. Maxwell, consul general to San Domingo, sailed in the Cherokee; he said he would not be surprised to find the revolution ended when he reached there, and that in a way he has orders to advise the captain of the ship what to do in certain contingencies, though he cannot say what his advice will be until they reach the spot and he sees what confronts them. He thinks the Baltimore will be at Monte Cristi, their first port of call, before they get there, and in that event the officers will decide what they are to do; if the Dominican officials establish a blockade and can maintain it, of the five ports named, or any one of them, they cannot enter, but to make the blockade effectual it must be perpetual, the gunboats which meet them at Monte Cristi and prevent their entering that harbor being unable to follow them to another port and keep them out there. The Dominican government has two gunboats, capable of maintaining a blockade of two ports at the same time, but he does not think they could effectively blockade more than that; he has heard a rumor that the government has armed two sailing vessels as supplementary warships for this blockade service, but does not know that it is true. Consul Galvan said he understood several cases of arms were offered for shipment on the Cherokee to Puerto Plata, but the Clyde people would not take them unless he certified his consent; the shippers did not come to him for approval, and he does not know who they were.

records.summary_en: The Advertiser prints a San Juan dispatch of November 18: the French steamer St. Simon arrived there today from Hayti and San Domingo; she touched at Puerto Plata, on the north coast of Santo Domingo, and reports that all the Dominican republic, except the capital, San Domingo, was in the hands of the revolutionists; the St. Simon also reported that General Jiminez, leader of the Dominican revolutionists, left Hayti on November 16 and was due to arrive Friday next before San Domingo and assume direction of the siege of that city; General Caceres was assisting in the military operations of the revolutionists. records.headline: There was a heavy artillery duel between government troops and the insurgents at Santo Domingo City on the night of November
records.summary_en: There was a heavy artillery duel between government troops and the insurgents at Santo Domingo City on the night of November 17, and the United States cruiser Baltimore landed a force of marines for the protection of American interests. Minister Powell's despatches to the State Department call the situation desperate: the city is constantly under fire, shells are falling in it, it is surrounded on three sides, an assault is momentarily expected, and it is believed the Dominican government cannot much longer hold out against the revolutionists.
records.summary_es: Hubo un intenso duelo de artillería entre las tropas del gobierno y los insurgentes en la ciudad de Santo Domingo la noche del 17 de noviembre, y el crucero estadounidense Baltimore desembarcó una fuerza de infantes de marina para proteger los intereses estadounidenses. Los despachos del ministro Powell al Departamento de Estado califican la situación de desesperada: la ciudad está constantemente bajo fuego, caen proyectiles en ella, está rodeada por tres lados, se espera un asalto de un momento a otro y se cree que el gobierno dominicano no podrá resistir mucho más contra los revolucionarios.

Santo Domingo is still holding out against the attacks of the Dominican insurgents, but dispatches from the capital indicate that it cannot withstand the bombarding of the attacking forces much longer; all cities of importance, with the exception of Santo Domingo, are said to be under the control of the insurgents; the United States cruiser Baltimore is now at San Juan coaling, and in its absence from Santo Domingo the Newport went from Puerto Plata to look after American interests. The Clyde liner Cherokee, which forced the blockade at Dominican ports two weeks ago, left New York yesterday for another visit to Santo Domingo; Consul General Galvan, the Dominican representative in New York, refused to issue clearance papers for the vessel to enter any ports excepting Santo Domingo and Azua, but in spite of the refusal the Cherokee will attempt to enter Macoris, Puerto Plata, and other ports at which Santo Domingo is attempting to establish a blockade; the State Department does not recognize this blockade as effective; C. L. Maxwell, the United States consul general at Santo Domingo, is on the Cherokee and will advise the captain concerning his entrance into harbors where the blockade is supposed to be maintained.

records.full_text:
WOULD CEDE REPUBLIC. REPORT ABOUT WOZ Y GIL. U. S. Consul General Sails with Cherokee to Advise Her Captain.

Amid shouts of "Good luck to you!" and "Don't get shot!" the Clyde Line steamer Cherokee left her pier in the East River yesterday afternoon, for the ports in San Domingo. On the bridge stood Captain Daniel Archibald, who paid no attention to the warnings and good wishes hurled at him by the people on the pier. Great interest attaches to this voyage of the Cherokee to Dominican waters on account of the decision of the Clyde Line officials that she shall enter the ports of Sanchez, Samana, Porto Plata, Macoris and Monte Cristi, despite the blockade placed on them by the government of San Domingo.

There were eighteen passengers on the Cherokee, among them Charles L. Maxwell, United States Consul General at San Domingo City. Consul General Maxwell, who has been spending his leave of absence of three months at his home, in Xenia, Ohio, goes in the capacity of adviser to Captain Archibald, should the Dominicans try to make good their threat to sink the vessel if she insists on entering the blockaded ports. He had still a month to his credit, but the seriousness of the situation caused the State Department to curtail his furlough and order him to accompany the Cherokee.

"Yes," said Mr. Maxwell just before the steamer sailed, "I have instructions from the State Department as to how the situation should be handled, but I cannot discuss them.

"The revolution might be over before we get there. Anyway. I don't think the gunboats of San Domingo will fire on us. According to my construction, a blockade is effective when the war vessels of the blockading nation are actually and permanently on the spot, and able to prevent physically vessels from entering the closed ports. If the warships move from port to port then the blockade is not effective. I shall do what I can to prevent trouble."

Captain Archibald was perhaps the coolest man on the Cherokee when she sailed. The fate that it is said threatens him if he attempts to run the blockade, as he did on the last voyage south, did not seem to trouble him. Captain Archibald has been the commander of the Cherokee for several years. He does not look the part of a blockade runner. His trousers are carefully creased and he wears narrow, pointed shoes. But his square jaw and piercing eyes presage trouble for any one who stands in the way of the performance of his duty.

"I am not looking for a fight," he said yesterday. "If the Dominican gunboats are at Monte Cristi, where we touch first, I shall not try to force my way in, for they can easily sink us. My actions will to a great extent depend upon the advice of Consul General Maxwell."

It was said that the real mission of Mr. Maxwell was to learn for the State Department whether the blockade on the several ports is really effective. So far as is known now it is not, and, acting under instructions from the Treasury Department, Collector Stranahan yesterday issued clearance papers to the Cherokee. She was lightly laden, however, the merchants here having decided to withhold shipments until the trouble subsides.

Consul Galvan was among those who saw the vessel off. Two others were General F. Leonte Vasquez, ex-consul general and a brother of ex-President Horacio Vasquez, and ex-Consul General Emilio Joubert, who served under President Jiménez, leader of the present revolt.

General Vasquez said: "I want to correct certain reports. My brother is out of politics. He is an agriculturist in Cuba, and is neutral in this affair. As to myself, I have not participated in this revolution, although they have sent for me. I have some feeling in the matter, though, as President Gil, when he overthrew my brother, decreed that I should not return to my country. I have business interests there, so—well, you can understand my position."

Consul General Galvan, it was said, went to the steamer to see whether several cases of arms offered for shipment to the rebels were on board the Cherokee. He received assurances that they were not on board.

Señor J. N. Jiordaini, a Corsican, who has been appointed by the revolutionary government as confidential agent in this city, received advices yesterday from General Carlos Morales, at Santiago de los Caballeros, a leader in the revolution, telling of the reason for the rebellion.

records.headline: The Clyde Line steamer Cherokee sailed from New York for San Domingo ports, with United States Consul General Charles J. Maxwell aboard
records.summary_en: The Clyde Line steamer Cherokee sailed from New York for San Domingo ports, with United States Consul General Charles J. Maxwell aboard to advise Captain Archibald, after the Dominican government blockaded Sanchez, Samana, Puerto Plata, Macoris and Monte Cristi and threatened to sink the vessel if she entered them. Maxwell said he did not think the Dominican gunboats would fire, and that a blockade is effective only when warships are actually and permanently on the spot to prevent vessels entering. According to General Morales's advices, President Gil had offered to cede the republic to the United States, and negotiations looking toward this end were under way between the two governments; Senor Giordani, the revolutionary government's confidential agent in New York, said he would protest against it. Senor Galvan said yesterday that a large shipment of war material was expected to arrive at San Domingo City yesterday from Germany for the government.
records.summary_es: El vapor Cherokee de la Clyde Line zarpó de Nueva York hacia puertos de Santo Domingo, con el cónsul general de los Estados Unidos Charles J. Maxwell a bordo para asesorar al capitán Archibald, después de que el gobierno dominicano bloqueó Sánchez, Samaná, Puerto Plata, Macorís y Monte Cristi y amenazó con hundir el barco si entraba en ellos. Maxwell dijo que no creía que las cañoneras dominicanas dispararan, y que un bloqueo solo es efectivo cuando los buques de guerra están real y permanentemente en el lugar para impedir la entrada de barcos. Según los informes del general Morales, el presidente Gil había ofrecido ceder la república a los Estados Unidos, y las negociaciones con ese fin estaban en curso entre los dos gobiernos; el señor Giordani, agente confidencial del gobierno revolucionario en Nueva York, dijo que protestaría contra ello. El señor Galván dijo ayer que se esperaba la llegada ayer a la ciudad de Santo Domingo de un gran cargamento de material de guerra procedente de Alemania para el gobierno.

records.headline: The Journal prints a Santo Domingo item: Commander Briggs's reports
records.summary_en: The Journal prints a Santo Domingo item: Commander Briggs's reports indicate that the bombardments of San Domingo by the insurrectionists have been hot; having stated that his coal supply was running low, Commander Briggs was authorized to take the Baltimore to San Juan for coal and then return to San Domingo city, and, in order that the interests of the United States in that city should not be left unprotected in the absence of the cruiser Baltimore, orders were telegraphed to Commander Diehl, commanding the gunboat Newport, at Puerto Plata, on the north coast of San Domingo, to proceed at once to San Domingo city, on the southern coast; it is stated it will not take the Baltimore more than a day or two to make the run to San Juan and back. A Cape Haytien dispatch of November 18 adds that information has been received at Monte Cristi from Santo Domingo that United States Minister Powell, accompanied by Minister of Foreign Relations Galvan, has gone aboard the United States cruiser Baltimore, the object of their visit to the warship being unknown, and that the arrival of the United States gunboat Newport is anxiously awaited, she being believed to be still at Puerto Plata. A New York item adds that Consul General Galvan, of San Domingo, refused to sign clearance papers for the Clyde Line steamer Cherokee to the five Dominican ports in the hands of insurgents, for which the Cherokee sailed today, but granted clearance papers for the ports of San Domingo and Azua.

Un despacho de Cabo Haitiano del 18 de noviembre añade que se ha recibido información en Monte Cristi desde Santo Domingo de que el ministro estadounidense Powell, acompañado por el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores Galván, ha subido a bordo del crucero estadounidense Baltimore, siendo desconocido el objeto de su visita al buque de guerra, y que la llegada de la cañonera estadounidense Newport es esperada con ansiedad, creyéndose que aún está en Puerto Plata. Una nota de Nueva York añade que el cónsul general Galván, de San Domingo, se negó a firmar papeles de despacho para el vapor Cherokee, de la línea Clyde, hacia los cinco puertos dominicanos en manos de los insurgentes, por los que el Cherokee zarpó hoy, pero concedió papeles de despacho para los puertos de San Domingo y Azua.

records.headline: The Messenger prints the closing part of a San Domingo dispatch
records.summary_en: The Messenger prints the closing part of a San Domingo dispatch: a general attack is expected within the next few days; General Woss y Gil refuses to capitulate and it is believed the fighting will be severe; the situation is desperate and fighting in the streets is likely to occur at any moment; the United States cruiser Baltimore has been compelled to leave to re-coal; United States Minister Powell is endeavoring to protect American interests with the limited means at his disposal; a German naval vessel is ready to land troops at a moment's notice; the insurgents endeavored to have Minister Powell recognize them, but the minister refused to do so; the revolutionists fired on the Clyde Line steamer New York as she was entering the port of Samana, but the vessel was uninjured; the Dominican government has appointed Minister of Foreign Relations Galvan and Judge George Gray of Delaware as commissioners to arbitrate the Santo Domingo Improvement matter, as the result of Minister Powell's effort to compel the carrying out of the terms of the protocol, and Commissioner Galvan will leave for the United States tomorrow, though it is possible the insurgents may endeavor to capture him.

records.headline: The Capital prints a feature under the head 'San Domingo's Queer Soldiers'
records.summary_en: The Capital prints a feature under the head 'San Domingo's Queer Soldiers': some of the queerest soldiers in the world are to be found in San Domingo, or the Dominican Republic, as it is officially called; an Englishman who ran a steamship business in San Domingo City says there were four or five generals among the hundred coal carriers he employed, who coaled the steamers by carrying big baskets on their heads at 25 cents a day, and now and then would take a day off to review their armies, conduct manoeuvres or fight revolutionists; one of these generals, who had no uniform, stole a pair of gold-laced 'pants' from a shop, was caught with the goods and punished by being paraded around town on a donkey, face toward the tail, with the 'pants' tied around his neck; the soldiers are not volunteers, for when the government wants troops it simply sends into the country districts and seizes the laborers in the fields and the travelers on the roads, and though at first naturally discontented, they like the new job when they find that soldiers have no work to do; they are furnished with a suit of clothes every year, but it does not last them long, for they are inveterate gamblers and after they have lost all their money they gamble away their uniform, keeping nothing save their rifles, an old pair of trousers and a ragged shirt.
