records.headline: Should the insurgents succeed in effecting an entrance to the city
records.summary_en: The *New-York Tribune* reported that the besieged Dominican provisional government was unable to raise a $20,000 loan for city defense, leaving the capital vulnerable to insurgent assault and street fighting. With the gunboat *Newport* remaining as the only foreign warship in port, concerns grew over the safety of foreign residents. Meanwhile, insurgent leader Juan Isidro Jimenes scored a decisive victory at Moca against 500 government troops under General Ramón Cáceres, who was wounded, clearing the path for an advance on Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: El *New-York Tribune* informó que el asediado gobierno provisional dominicano fue incapaz de obtener un préstamo de 20.000 dólares para la defensa de la ciudad, dejando a la capital expuesta a asaltos insurgentes y combates callejeros. Siendo el cañonero *Newport* el único buque de guerra extranjero en el puerto, creció la inquietud por la seguridad de los residentes extranjeros. Mientras tanto, el caudillo rebelde Juan Isidro Jimenes logró una victoria decisiva en Moca contra 500 soldados gubernamentales al mando del general Ramón Cáceres, quien resultó herido, despejando el camino para avanzar sobre Santo Domingo.

records.headline: The Tribune prints a San Domingo dispatch of December 22 with a report
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints a San Domingo dispatch of December 22 with a report that General Pelletier has formed a provisional government at Azua de Compostela, presided over by himself; that the inhabitants of Barahona have joined in the movement, and that the two forces are jointly marching on this city. The Tribune notes that the foregoing dispatch was delayed in transmission, and prints an Associated Press dispatch dated San Domingo, December 25, saying that the greater part of the Republic of San Domingo had declared in favor of General Jiménez, the former President of the republic, who was said to be marching on the city of San Domingo at the head of a large body of insurgents, and that the provisional government was making active preparation for defence. The Tribune also prints an item under the head 'Jimenez to March on Capital': a cable dispatch received yesterday from General Jiménez, the leader of the present San Domingan rebellion, by a friend in this city, sent the revolutionists' stock up several points at the Hotel Muro; the message, dated at Santiago de los Caballeros, read: 'Success assured. Will march on capital.'
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica un despacho de Santo Domingo del 22 de diciembre con un informe de que el general Pelletier ha formado un gobierno provisional en Azua de Compostela, presidido por él mismo; de que los habitantes de Barahona se han unido al movimiento, y de que las dos fuerzas marchan juntas sobre esta ciudad. El Tribune señala que el despacho anterior se retrasó en la transmisión y publica un despacho de la Associated Press fechado en Santo Domingo el 25 de diciembre, según el cual la mayor parte de la República de Santo Domingo se había declarado a favor del general Jiménez, el expresidente de la república, de quien se decía que marchaba sobre la ciudad de Santo Domingo al frente de un numeroso cuerpo de insurgentes, y que el gobierno provisional hacía activos preparativos de defensa. El Tribune publica también una nota bajo el titular «Jimenez to March on Capital»: un despacho por cable recibido ayer del general Jiménez, el jefe de la actual rebelión dominicana, por un amigo en esta ciudad, hizo subir varios puntos las acciones de los revolucionarios en el Hotel Muro; el mensaje, fechado en Santiago de los Caballeros, decía: «Éxito asegurado. Marcharé sobre la capital».

Well Known Novelist Expires from Con

London, Dec. 23.--George Gissing, the novelist,
died from consumption to-day at St. Jean-de-Luz,
in the Pyrenees. He was born at Wakefield, Eng
land, November 22, 1857.

records.headline: The Tribune prints the closing part of a Santo Domingo dispatch
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints the closing part of a Santo Domingo dispatch: the minister, who has been living in the suburbs, has been compelled to move the legation inside the city boundaries; President Morales returned here last night — he found it impossible to land on the northern part of the island, but bombarded Puerto Plata, and the damage done is not known; Morales is taking all possible steps to defend San Domingo; many arrests have been made; the South and East have joined in the Northern revolution; the situation is complicated and serious; the government troops are preparing to leave here and attack the rebels at San Cristobal, two hours from here; much excitement prevails at this place, and the arrival of another American warship, to reinforce the gunboat Newport, is anxiously desired. The Tribune also prints a Washington item of December 29 under the head 'Hurry Call for a Warship': with three revolutions raging on the island, the forces of Jiménez within four hours of San Domingo City, and excitement prevailing, Minister Powell thinks the situation in San Domingo demands the presence of an additional warship, and in a cable message dated yesterday appeals to the State Department for aid; in anticipation of the crisis the State Department had already taken steps to send another warship to San Domingo, and at its request Secretary Moody yesterday ordered Rear Admiral Lamberton, commanding the South Atlantic Squadron, now at Trinidad, to dispatch one of his vessels to San Domingo at full speed to assist the gunboat Newport.

El Tribune publica también una nota de Washington del 29 de diciembre bajo el titular «Hurry Call for a Warship»: con tres revoluciones asolando la isla, las fuerzas de Jiménez a cuatro horas de la ciudad de Santo Domingo y prevaleciendo la agitación, el ministro Powell considera que la situación en Santo Domingo exige la presencia de un buque de guerra adicional, y en un mensaje por cable fechado ayer apela al Departamento de Estado en busca de ayuda; en previsión de la crisis, el Departamento de Estado ya había tomado medidas para enviar otro buque de guerra a Santo Domingo, y a petición suya el secretario Moody ordenó ayer al contralmirante Lamberton, comandante de la Escuadra del Atlántico Sur, ahora en Trinidad, que despachara uno de sus buques a Santo Domingo a toda velocidad para ayudar a la cañonera Newport.

records.headline: The Press prints a Santo Domingo dispatch of Saturday, December 26
records.summary_en: The Press prints a Santo Domingo dispatch of Saturday, December 26 reporting that the city of San Domingo is again being barricaded, this time against the forces of the new provisional government founded at Azua de Compostela by Gen. Pelletier, which are marching on the capital; the financial position of the Morales government is bad, and the officials find it difficult to obtain rations for the soldiers; the American minister, Mr. Powell, who has been living in the suburbs, has been compelled to move the legation inside the city boundaries; President Morales returned here last night — he found it impossible to land on the northern part of the island but bombarded Puerto Plata, and the damage done is not known; Morales is taking all possible steps to defend San Domingo; many arrests have been made; the south and east have joined in the northern revolution; the situation is complicated and serious; the government troops are preparing to leave here and attack the rebels at San Cristobal, two hours' distant from here; much excitement prevails at this place, and the arrival of another American warship to reinforce the gunboat Newport is anxiously desired. The Press also prints a Washington item of December 29 under the head 'Scorpion Sent': Admiral Lamberton has cabled to the Navy Department from Trinidad that he has sent the Scorpion to reinforce the Newport in Dominican waters.
records.summary_es: La Prensa publica un despacho de Santo Domingo del sábado 26 de diciembre que informa que la ciudad de Santo Domingo está siendo atrincherada de nuevo, esta vez contra las fuerzas del nuevo gobierno provisional fundado en Azua de Compostela por el general Pelletier, que marchan sobre la capital; la posición financiera del gobierno de Morales es mala, y los funcionarios encuentran difícil obtener raciones para los soldados; el ministro estadounidense, el Sr. Powell, que ha estado viviendo en las afueras, se ha visto obligado a trasladar la legación dentro de los límites de la ciudad; el presidente Morales regresó aquí anoche: le fue imposible desembarcar en la parte norte de la isla, pero bombardeó Puerto Plata, y se desconoce el daño causado; Morales toma todas las medidas posibles para defender Santo Domingo; se han hecho muchos arrestos; el sur y el este se han unido a la revolución del norte; la situación es complicada y seria; las tropas del gobierno se preparan para salir de aquí y atacar a los rebeldes en San Cristóbal, a dos horas de aquí; prevalece mucha agitación en este lugar, y se desea con ansias la llegada de otro buque de guerra estadounidense para reforzar la cañonera Newport. La Prensa publica también una nota de Washington del 29 de diciembre bajo el titular «Scorpion Sent»: el almirante Lamberton ha cablegrafiado al Departamento de la Marina desde Trinidad que ha enviado el Scorpion para reforzar al Newport en aguas dominicanas.

records.headline: The Republican prints the closing part of a Santo Domingo dispatch
records.summary_en: The Republican prints the closing part of a Santo Domingo dispatch: the city is being defended by the troops of the provisional government; the Clyde line steamer Cherokee arrived in port today; the government authorities demanded that a portion of the Cherokee's cargo destined for Azua de Compostela be discharged here — this demand was resisted by the steamship agents, who notified the government that the Cherokee would proceed to Azua de Compostela; in case of aggression on the part of the government authorities the steamship agent will ask United States Minister Powell for protection; a commission from San Pedro de Macoris, which has declared in favor of the insurgents, arrived here today and is demanding the surrender of San Domingo to the insurgent forces; General Morales, provisional president, is determined to resist to the limit all attacks by the insurgents, and left last night on the Dominican gunboat Independencia with the intention of attacking the insurgents in the ports to the south.

records.summary_en: The Journal prints a San Juan dispatch of December 29 and a San Domingo dispatch of Sunday, December 27: the Cuban steamer which touched here, via Puerto Plata, Santo Domingo, has ceased to call at San Juan, thus severing the line of communication of Gen. Woss y Gil, formerly president of Santo Domingo, with the seat of war in that republic; the Gil party openly announced that they will sail for Santo Domingo in January to co-operate with General Jiminez; the gathering of war munitions continues in Porto Rico; Governor Hunt still refuses to recognize the Morales consulate here, which has appealed to the French consul to prevent the sailing of Gen. Woss y Gil for Santo Domingo on a French steamer. In the San Domingo dispatch the insurgents are attacking this city, which is being defended by the troops of the provisional government, who are now fighting in force; the Clyde Line steamer Cherokee arrived in port today; the government authorities demanded that that portion of the Cherokee's cargo destined for Azua de Compostela be discharged here — this demand was resisted by the steamship agents, who notified the government that the Cherokee would proceed to Azua de Compostela; in case of aggression on the part of the government authorities the steamship company will ask Minister Powell for protection; a commission from San Pedro de Macoris, which has declared in favor of the insurgents, arrived here today and is demanding the surrender of San Domingo to the insurgent forces.

records.headline: The Age-Herald prints a San Juan, P. R., dispatch of January 3
records.summary_en: The Age-Herald prints a San Juan, P. R., dispatch of January 3 under the head 'Wos y Gil Is Active': thirty of the followers of General Woss y Gil, former president of Santo Domingo, including all the Dominican revolutionary generals now here, will sail tomorrow on the French steamer St. Simon, going direct to Puerto Plata; from there they will hasten to join General Jiminez before San Domingo; they declare themselves confident that they will be able to overthrow the government of President Morales. The St. Simon will carry a good supply of ammunition and stores, as well as a number of horses secured in Porto Rico; other Porto Ricans recruited by the revolutionists will sail Tuesday on the schooner Mayaguez. General Woss y Gil says he will remain in San Juan for three weeks more on the advice of his friends, who fear he will be assassinated should he return to Santo Domingo now.
records.summary_es: El Age-Herald publica un despacho de San Juan, P. R., del 3 de enero bajo el titular «Wos y Gil Is Active»: treinta de los seguidores del general Woss y Gil, expresidente de Santo Domingo, incluidos todos los generales revolucionarios dominicanos que están ahora aquí, zarparán mañana en el vapor francés San Simón, con rumbo directo a Puerto Plata; desde allí se apresurarán a unirse al general Jiménez ante Santo Domingo; se declaran confiados en que podrán derrocar al gobierno del presidente Morales. El San Simón llevará un buen suministro de municiones y pertrechos, así como varios caballos conseguidos en Puerto Rico; otros puertorriqueños reclutados por los revolucionarios zarparán el martes en la goleta Mayaguez. El general Woss y Gil dice que permanecerá en San Juan tres semanas más por consejo de sus amigos, que temen que sea asesinado si regresa ahora a Santo Domingo.

records.headline: The Graphic prints a biographical sketch of Juan Isidro Jiminez
records.summary_en: The Graphic prints a biographical sketch of Juan Isidro Jiminez, whose portrait it publishes under the caption 'Santo Domingan General Who Heads the Latest Revolution': it has been known since Jiminez left here a few months ago for Porto Rico that he was anxious to return to the office from which he was deposed by Gen. Horacio Vasquez about a year and a half ago; he resigned the place of fiscal agent of Santo Domingo to the United States and Europe, to which President Woz Gil had appointed him, that he might be free to take part in a rebellion and return to the presidency; it was not expected that his hopes would be realized, as Gen. Carlos Morales, governor of Porto Plata, a former priest, who started the movement, has also aspirations for the place, and the Vasquez element is opposed to him. Before his appearance as an 'insurrecto' Jiminez was a merchant in this city; he was proclaimed president of Santo Domingo on the overthrow of President Heureaux in 1898, although, as in the present instance, he took no part in the fighting, and he was in turn deposed by Gen. Vasquez, who was then vice president; his one ambition since then has been to regain the office of chief executive; Jiminez is about 60 years old, unusually tall for a Dominican.
records.summary_es: El Graphic publica una semblanza biográfica de Juan Isidro Jiménez, cuyo retrato publica bajo el pie «Santo Domingan General Who Heads the Latest Revolution»: se ha sabido desde que Jiménez salió de aquí hace unos meses para Puerto Rico que estaba ansioso por volver al cargo del que fue depuesto por el general Horacio Vásquez hace aproximadamente un año y medio; renunció al puesto de agente fiscal de Santo Domingo ante los Estados Unidos y Europa, para el que lo había nombrado el presidente Woss y Gil, para poder participar libremente en una rebelión y volver a la presidencia; no se esperaba que sus esperanzas se realizaran, pues el general Carlos Morales, gobernador de Puerto Plata, ex sacerdote, que inició el movimiento, también tiene aspiraciones al puesto, y el elemento de Vásquez se le opone. Antes de su aparición como «insurrecto», Jiménez era comerciante en esta ciudad; fue proclamado presidente de Santo Domingo al ser derrocado el presidente Heureaux en 1898, aunque, como en la presente ocasión, no tomó parte en los combates, y a su vez fue depuesto por el general Vásquez, que entonces era vicepresidente; su única ambición desde entonces ha sido recuperar el cargo de jefe del Ejecutivo; Jiménez tiene unos 60 años, inusualmente alto para ser dominicano.

records.headline: The Graphic prints an editorial discussion of the Santo Domingo revolutions
records.summary_en: The Graphic prints an editorial discussion of the Santo Domingo revolutions: as soon as one faction grows more powerful than the one controlling the government for the time being, there is a revolution, and one set of rascals is turned out to make room for a worse. It quotes the argument that 'the latest revolution brings into prominence the question of forcibly annexing Santo Domingo and Hayti as the best means of preventing them from embroiling us sooner or later with one or the other of the European powers; at least we could compel them to maintain a stable and strong government, of whose friendship we could be certain.'
records.summary_es: El Graphic publica una discusión editorial sobre las revoluciones de Santo Domingo: en cuanto una facción se vuelve más poderosa que la que controla el gobierno en ese momento, hay una revolución, y un grupo de bribones es expulsado para dejar paso a otro peor. Cita el argumento de que «la última revolución pone de relieve la cuestión de anexar por la fuerza Santo Domingo y Haití como el mejor medio de evitar que tarde o temprano nos enreden con una u otra de las potencias europeas; al menos podríamos obligarlos a mantener un gobierno estable y fuerte, de cuya amistad podríamos estar seguros».

records.headline: San Domingo, Sunday, Janl 3.—The gun boat Independence arrived here last
records.summary_en: The *Montgomery Advertiser* reported that the Dominican gunboat *Independencia* captured two armed insurgent schooners and shelled suburban districts of the capital to dislodge revolutionary fighters. Government forces successfully retook Baní and San Cristóbal and repelled a major assault on Santo Domingo following an engagement at Haina. To isolate the insurrection, the government issued a decree closing six major coastal ports to foreign shipping, supported by naval patrols.
records.summary_es: El *Montgomery Advertiser* informó que el cañonero dominicano *Independencia* capturó dos goletas insurgentes armadas y cañoneó distritos suburbanos de la capital para desalojar a los combatientes revolucionarios. Las fuerzas del gobierno recuperaron con éxito Baní y San Cristóbal y repelieron un asalto de envergadura contra Santo Domingo tras un combate en Haina. Para aislar la insurrección, el gobierno emitió un decreto clausurando seis puertos costeros principales al comercio marítimo exterior, apoyado por patrullajes navales.
records.passage: San Domingo, Sunday, Jan. 3.—The gun boat Independence arrived here last night with two captured Dominican schooners In tow. The schooners carried arms and munitions of war Intended for coast defense. The Independence bombarded the suburbs of the city today with the object driving the revolutionists out. It is officially reported that [Bani?] and San Cristobal have been retaken by the government troops. There was a severe encounter between the government troops and the revolutionists at [Haina?], [with?] result favorable to the government. The government has issued a decree closing the ports of Asua de Compostella, San Pedro de Macoris, Samana, Sanches, Puerto Plata and Monte Cristo to take effect within twenty days. In the case of vessels coming from the Antilles within thirty days for vessels from American ports and within forty-five days for vessels from European ports. Armed schooners and gunboats will guard the closed ports. There was a severe attack on the city this evening but the troops managed to repulse the revolutionists. Commerce Is completely at a standstill. News from the interior cannot be obtained. Moody Changes Estimates. records.headline: The Journal prints a Washington item of January 6, making public Commander Dillingham's report
records.summary_en: The Journal prints a Washington item of January 6, making public Commander Dillingham's report from Puerto Plata: the Washington government will from now on protect American life and property in the island of Santo Domingo; Commander Dillingham, commanding the Detroit, reports: 'In this vicinity anarchy prevails and business is at a standstill. Puerto Plata is quiet at present. The Jiminez authorities are collecting duties and dues. Jiminez is at Santiago. The revolution is not one of principle, but of factions. Will not allow interruption of commerce. Went to Sousa on the morning of Jan. 3 and returned to Puerto Plata yesterday afternoon to see the Cherokee out of the port. Will coal here to-day and return to Sousa. The fighting at Sousa Dec. 26, between Morales and Jiminez troops took place on United Fruit Company's property. Without notice houses were looted, the lives of United States citizens were absolutely disregarded, women and children had to flee for safety, and property was destroyed. Have forbidden any fighting or any armed force of any party within certain limits necessary to protect the lives of United States citizens at Sousa. Commanding officers in the field near Sousa have been so instructed. Left one officer, sixteen marines, Colt automatic gun and steam launch at Sousa to see my instructions carried out until my return.'
records.summary_es: El Diario publica una nota de Washington del 6 de enero, dando a conocer el informe del comandante Dillingham desde Puerto Plata: el gobierno de Washington protegerá de ahora en adelante la vida y los bienes estadounidenses en la isla de Santo Domingo; el comandante Dillingham, al mando del Detroit, informa: «En esta vecindad impera la anarquía y los negocios están paralizados. Puerto Plata está tranquilo en la actualidad. Las autoridades de Jiménez están cobrando derechos y cuotas. Jiménez está en Santiago. La revolución no es de principios, sino de facciones. No permitiré la interrupción del comercio. Fui a Sousa la mañana del 3 de enero y regresé a Puerto Plata ayer por la tarde para ver salir del puerto al Cherokee. Haré carbón aquí hoy y regresaré a Sousa. Los combates en Sousa el 26 de diciembre, entre las tropas de Morales y las de Jiménez, tuvieron lugar en terrenos de la United Fruit Company. Sin aviso, las casas fueron saqueadas, las vidas de los ciudadanos estadounidenses fueron absolutamente despreciadas, las mujeres y los niños tuvieron que huir para ponerse a salvo, y los bienes fueron destruidos. He prohibido todo combate y toda fuerza armada de cualquier partido dentro de ciertos límites necesarios para proteger las vidas de los ciudadanos estadounidenses en Sousa. Los oficiales al mando en el campo cerca de Sousa han sido instruidos en ese sentido. Dejé un oficial, dieciséis infantes de marina, una ametralladora automática Colt y una lancha de vapor en Sousa para velar por el cumplimiento de mis instrucciones hasta mi regreso».

records.headline: The Call prints, under the head 'Puerto Plata in Peace Zone'
records.summary_en: The Call prints, under the head 'Puerto Plata in Peace Zone', a San Domingo dispatch of January 8 and the closing lines of Commander Dillingham's report: San Pedro de Macoris has been recaptured by the government forces and again declared an open port; the insurgent troops in the suburbs of this city to-day sent a message to the authorities here proposing a compromise on honorable terms — the messenger was arrested and the proposition was not answered; the news received from the interior is apparently more favorable to the government. In the closing lines of his report Commander Dillingham states that the two sides have agreed, the one not to bombard and the other not to fire on gunboats, that all fighting will be confined to the land side of town in future, and that he has small parties landed at Sosua and at the consulate in Puerto Plata.

records.headline: The Journal prints the closing part of a San Domingo dispatch
records.summary_en: The Journal prints the closing part of a San Domingo dispatch and a Washington item under the head 'Americans Are Safe': the central part of the republic is now in the hands of the government, which has nearly complete control in Samana also; three overtures for peace made by the insurgents have been rejected; a Dominican schooner en route to San Pedro de Macoris has been captured; General Morales, the acting president, has formed a volunteer company, a thing no other president has been able to accomplish. Commander Mertz, commanding the gunboat Newport, cables the Navy Department from San Domingo, under date of yesterday, as follows: 'Revolution continues. Nothing menacing Americans. Legation guard withdrawn to-day.'

El comandante Mertz, al mando de la cañonera Newport, cablegrafía al Departamento de Marina desde Santo Domingo, con fecha de ayer, lo siguiente: «La revolución continúa. Nada amenaza a los estadounidenses. La guardia de la legación fue retirada hoy».

Jiminez a speedy termination will be put to the suicidal strife now going on in the Dominican republic; the department has come to no determination as to the recognition of any of the parties in San Domingo — the last advice is that there are no less than two provisional governments and one revolutionary government in full sway at this moment — and it is disposed to continue to trust to the discretion of Minister Powell; as a further protection to American interests, the cruiser Columbia, of the training squadron, has left Guantanamo for Santo Domingo city, increasing the United States naval representation in those waters to three ships, the other vessels being the Detroit and Newport, though it is probable that the Newport will be transferred to duty in Haitian waters.

records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Journal* reported that the State Department withheld diplomatic recognition from Dominican factions despite claims by General Jimenes's followers that they controlled nearly the entire country outside the capital. United States officials observed that three rival governing authorities were contending for power simultaneously, leaving policy implementation to Minister Powell's judgment. To protect American interests, the Navy dispatched the cruiser *Columbia* from Guantanamo to reinforce the warships *Detroit* and *Newport* at Santo Domingo.

Funcionarios de los Estados Unidos observaron que tres autoridades de gobierno rivales se disputaban el poder de forma simultánea, dejando la ejecución de la política al criterio del ministro Powell. Para resguardar los intereses estadounidenses, la Armada envió el crucero *Columbia* desde Guantánamo para reforzar a los buques de guerra *Detroit* y *Newport* en Santo Domingo.

records.summary_en: The Tribune prints an item under the head 'Hearing on Claim Begun': the Dominican Arbitration Commission appointed to hear the claim of J. Sala Co. of this city against the Republic of San Domingo met yesterday at the office of J. M. Ceballos, at No. 27 William-st., who is the arbitrator for San Domingo; Frederick Van Dyne, assistant solicitor of the State Department, appeared; H. T. Kingsbury is counsel for the claimants, while Henry G. K. Heath represents the Dominican government in the same capacity; the claim of J. Sala Co., an export firm of this city, is for $250,000 for merchandise sold to San Domingo during the administration of the late President Heureaux; an adjournment was taken yesterday to three months hence, when it is expected that the matter will be finally disposed of.

records.headline: The Times prints the closing part of a Puerto Plata dispatch
records.summary_en: The Times prints the closing part of a Puerto Plata dispatch and two further items: perfect order is said to prevail; business of port is expected to begin tomorrow morning; there were no casualties among noncombatants, and no destruction of property; the surrender and arrangements of terms was conducted with order in presence of Captain Robertson and Commander Dillingham; Captain Robertson is an English naval officer who has been co-operating with Commander Dillingham in protecting foreign interests at Puerto Plata; the stronghold of the Jiminez forces has been at Puerto Plata, and the fall of that city is regarded as the end of the stubborn fight Jiminez has made against the Morales government. Under the head 'Spanish Cruiser Sails' the Times prints that the Spanish cruiser Rio de la Plata has sailed from New Orleans for Santo Domingo, where it will look after the interests of Spanish citizens threatened by the revolution. President Morales will make another appeal to the United States to recognize the temporary government he has established; Señor Sanchez, the Morales minister of foreign affairs, is now on his way to Washington, to solicit the recognition of the Dominican provisional government. Minister Powell is still resisting the alleged blockade established by the Morales government; he recently refused to allow President Morales to interfere with the movements of the Clyde steamer New York.
records.summary_es: El Washington Times publica la parte final de un despacho de Puerto Plata y dos notas más: se dice que impera un orden perfecto; se espera que la actividad del puerto comience mañana por la mañana; no hubo bajas entre los no combatientes, ni destrucción de bienes; la rendición y la concertación de los términos se realizaron con orden en presencia del capitán Robertson y del comandante Dillingham; el capitán Robertson es un oficial naval inglés que ha estado cooperando con el comandante Dillingham en la protección de los intereses extranjeros en Puerto Plata; el baluarte de las fuerzas de Jiménez ha estado en Puerto Plata, y la caída de esa ciudad se considera el fin de la tenaz lucha que Jiménez ha sostenido contra el gobierno de Morales. Bajo el titular «Spanish Cruiser Sails», el Times publica que el crucero español Río de la Plata ha zarpado de Nueva Orleans hacia Santo Domingo, donde velará por los intereses de los ciudadanos españoles amenazados por la revolución. El presidente Morales hará un nuevo llamamiento a los Estados Unidos para que reconozcan el gobierno provisional que ha establecido; el señor Sánchez, ministro de Relaciones Exteriores de Morales, está ahora de camino a Washington, para solicitar el reconocimiento del gobierno provisional dominicano. El ministro Powell sigue resistiendo el alegado bloqueo establecido por el gobierno de Morales; recientemente se negó a permitir que el presidente Morales interfiriera con los movimientos del vapor New York, de la línea Clyde.

records.headline: The commander of the United States steamer Detroit reports from Puerto Plata on January 17 that, after a fight
records.summary_en: The commander of the United States steamer Detroit reports from Puerto Plata on January 17 that, after a fight outside the city limits, the Jimenez forces occupying Puerto Plata surrendered unconditionally to President Morales's forces. He says perfect order prevails, the port's business will begin the next morning, there were no casualties among non-combatants and no destruction of property, and he calls the surrender a severe blow to Jimenez.
records.summary_es: El comandante del vapor estadounidense Detroit informa desde Puerto Plata el 17 de enero que, tras un combate fuera de los límites de la ciudad, las fuerzas de Jiménez que ocupaban Puerto Plata se rindieron incondicionalmente a las fuerzas del presidente Morales. Dice que reina un orden perfecto, que el comercio del puerto comenzará a la mañana siguiente, que no hubo víctimas entre los no combatientes ni destrucción de propiedades, y califica la rendición de un golpe severo para Jiménez.

records.headline: Reports from St. Thomas say
records.summary_en: Reports from St. Thomas say the Dominican minister of foreign affairs has left San Domingo for Washington to try to arrange a United States protectorate over the republic, while Jiminez's forces continue bombarding the capital. A Puerto Plata report adds that seven hundred government soldiers are marching on San Domingo, the rebel stronghold, in what is expected to be the most important battle of the Jiminez revolution, and gives details of the recent recapture of Puerto Plata, where the commander of an American vessel in the harbor practically managed the battle within a fighting zone fixed by the American and British warship commanders.
records.summary_es: Informes desde St. Thomas dicen que el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores dominicano ha salido de Santo Domingo hacia Washington para tratar de acordar un protectorado de los Estados Unidos sobre la república, mientras las fuerzas de Jiménez continúan bombardeando la capital. Un informe de Puerto Plata añade que setecientos soldados del gobierno marchan sobre Santo Domingo, el bastión rebelde, en lo que se espera sea la batalla más importante de la revolución de Jiménez, y da detalles de la reciente reconquista de Puerto Plata, donde el comandante de una embarcación estadounidense en el puerto dirigió prácticamente la batalla dentro de una zona de combate fijada por los comandantes de los buques de guerra estadounidense y británico.
records.passage: APPEAL TO UNCLE SAM. Dominican Minister of Foreign Affairs Reported on His Way to Arrange Protectorate.
records.chapter_es: Colapso y la cuestión de las aduanas
records.full_text:
APPEAL TO UNCLE SAM Dominican Minister of Foreign Affairs Reported on His Way to Arrange Protectorate. TROOPS ON THE MARCH Government Soldiers Advancing Toward San Domingo the Rebel Stronghold.

St. Thomas, D. W. I., Jan. 20—It is reported here that the Dominion minister of foreign affairs has left San Domingo for Washington to attempt to make arrangements with the United States to establish a protectorate over the republic of Santo Domingo. Bombardments of the capital continue by the forces of Jiminez.

Important Battle Predicted.

Puerto Plata, San Domingo, Jan. 20—Seven hundred government soldiers are on the march to San Domingo, the rebel stronghold. It is believed that this battle will be the most important in the Jiminez revolution. Details of the recapture of Puerto Plata, a few days ago by the government forces, show that the commander of an American vessel in the harbor practically managed the battle and that the fighting zone, demarked by the commander of the United States and British warships, was accepted by the contending forces.

Chicago, Jan. 21. — As the result of a storm train service on the South Side elevated road was paralyzed for nearly two hours during the day, endangering life and discommoding hundreds of passengers. Rain soaking the wood superstructure of the road caused the moisture to communicate to a defective third rail support near a network of switches. The electric current deserted the car motors and flowed through the ironwork of the structure to the ground. The entire structure for a considerable distance was electrified and menaced the safety of horses and men below, until the current was shut off at the powerhouse. Trains on the road were crowded. Passengers on the stalled trains, after waiting for some time for signs of life in the motors, took surface lines and reached their work downtown after long delay.

records.full_text:
Dishonest Bankers Held.

The government finally refuses to set at liberty the officials of the national bank charged with participation in the issuance of $200,000 in fraudulent securities early last year.

It was announced from Port au Prince January 7 that the French minister to Hayti had made an amicable demand that the arrested French officials of the national bank be provisionally released, basing his request on the ground of humanity and unhealthy condition of the prison. The government, however, refuses to comply with the demand, saying that the Haytien laws prevented such action.

records.headline: The Tribune prints a Washington item on Mr. Powell's recognition of the Morales government
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints a Washington item on Mr. Powell's recognition of the Morales government: Mr. Powell has sent to the State Department confirmation of the press report that he has recognized the provisional government of General Morales and that Puerto Plata is now in the government's possession; the recognition took place on the 20th, and it is expected that the other diplomatic representatives in San Domingo will follow Mr. Powell's initiative, thus terminating the chaotic condition of affairs which has caused suspension of business in San Domingo; Mr. Sanchez, the Secretary of State under the Morales government, who is on his way to Washington, will be recognized here in his official capacity, thus confirming Mr. Powell's action.
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica una nota de Washington sobre el reconocimiento del gobierno de Morales por el Sr. Powell: el Sr. Powell ha enviado al Departamento de Estado la confirmación de la noticia de prensa de que ha reconocido al gobierno provisional del general Morales y de que Puerto Plata está ahora en posesión del gobierno; el reconocimiento tuvo lugar el día 20, y se espera que los demás representantes diplomáticos en Santo Domingo sigan la iniciativa del Sr. Powell, poniendo así fin a la caótica situación que ha causado la suspensión de los negocios en Santo Domingo; el Sr. Sánchez, secretario de Estado bajo el gobierno de Morales, que está de camino a Washington, será reconocido aquí en su calidad oficial, confirmando así la acción del Sr. Powell.

records.summary_en: The Star prints the closing part of an account from the republic: the inhabitants of the city of Santo Domingo have declared that they will stand by President Morales and will under no consideration permit Jimenez to assume the presidency; the greatest suffering prevails throughout the entire republic, and at the time the French steamer left Puerto Plata for San Juan on the 10th one of the Dominican gunboats was shelling Cangrejo, a few miles from Puerto Plata. A Dominican colonel now residing in San Juan received a letter by the French steamer from his mother in Puerto Plata, telling him that the greater part of the town was destroyed by the bombardment of the Dominican gunboat on the 4th instant; that all letters coming into the republic are subject to the severest censorship from the post office authorities, who deliver none of those bearing unfavorable information or instructions, and have such persons to whom they are addressed immediately arrested, and that the greatest want and misery prevail, as the people are actually starving.

records.headline: The Star prints an item: Gen. Juan Francisco Sanchez, the minister of foreign affairs of the Morales party
records.summary_en: The Star prints an item: Gen. Juan Francisco Sanchez, the minister of foreign affairs of the Morales party and clothed with special powers as a minister to Washington, arrived at New York two days ago, and signalized his entry by installing Emilio Joubert as Dominican consul general at New York, in place of Mr. Galvan, who occupied that office under the Woss y Gil administration in San Domingo; Mr. Joubert accompanied Gen. Sanchez from New York to Washington, and there was also an interpreter with the party in the person of Abraham Leon. During the course of half an hour's interview with Acting Secretary Loomis of the State Department, Gen. Sanchez, through his interpreter, proffered the request for the recognition of the Morales government, explaining recent events in the Dominican republic and maintaining that the Morales party was in undoubted possession of the country and was the only de facto government, according to the rules governing recognitions heretofore followed by the United States government in its dealings with revolutionary movements in the south. Under the head 'Mr. Loomis Prefers to Wait' the Star adds that Mr. Loomis was non-committal, having in mind the most recent disturbance at Macoris, which has occurred since the Dominican contingent sailed for the United States; Minister Powell had reported that American interests were unfavorably affected by these disturbances, and the Navy Department had been obliged to hurry the big triple-screw cruiser Columbia to San Domingo from Guantanamo.
records.summary_es: El Star publica una nota: el general Juan Francisco Sánchez, ministro de Relaciones Exteriores del partido de Morales y revestido de poderes especiales como ministro ante Washington, llegó a Nueva York hace dos días, y señaló su entrada instalando a Emilio Joubert como cónsul general dominicano en Nueva York, en lugar del Sr. Galván, que ocupaba ese cargo bajo la administración de Woss y Gil en Santo Domingo; el Sr. Joubert acompañó al general Sánchez de Nueva York a Washington, y también iba con el grupo un intérprete, Abraham Leon. En el curso de una entrevista de media hora con el secretario interino Loomis, del Departamento de Estado, el general Sánchez, por medio de su intérprete, presentó la solicitud de reconocimiento del gobierno de Morales, explicando los acontecimientos recientes en la república dominicana y sosteniendo que el partido de Morales estaba en posesión indudable del país y era el único gobierno de facto, según las reglas que han regido los reconocimientos seguidos hasta ahora por el gobierno de los Estados Unidos en sus relaciones con los movimientos revolucionarios del sur. Bajo el titular «Mr. Loomis Prefers to Wait», el Star añade que el Sr. Loomis no se comprometió, teniendo en cuenta la más reciente perturbación en Macorís, ocurrida desde que el grupo dominicano zarpó hacia los Estados Unidos; el ministro Powell había informado que los intereses estadounidenses se veían desfavorablemente afectados por estas perturbaciones, y el Departamento de Marina se había visto obligado a enviar con urgencia el gran crucero Columbia, de tres hélices, a Santo Domingo desde Guantánamo.

records.headline: The Republic prints a Cape Haytien dispatch of January 28: the Presidente
records.summary_en: The Republic prints a Cape Haytien dispatch of January 28: the Presidente, a Dominican gunboat, arrived last Tuesday, and her captain asked the Haytien Government for munitions of war; President Nord made no response. After the installation of the new Dominican consul here, the Presidente sailed for Monte Cristi to attempt to prevent a German steamer from entering Monte Cristi. Word has been received from General Deschamps, a partisan of General Jiminez, who was taken to Guantanamo, Cuba, by the United States cruiser Hartford for the shipping of munitions of war; he and numerous followers of Jiminez will soon return to Santo Domingo. Leopold Espaillat, formerly Minister of War, has arrived at Monte Cristi to help Jiminez.

records.headline: The Republic prints the closing part of a Santo Domingo dispatch
records.summary_en: The Republic prints the closing part of a Santo Domingo dispatch: Jiminez is advised to retake Puerto Plata by blood and fire, to have his troops pillage the city and to exile foreign merchants refusing to advance funds to the revolutionists. Jiminez is unable to recruit troops in Monte Cristi. Hayti has recognized the Morales government and is supplying ammunition. One hundred and fifty of the troops of Jiminez, commanded by General Polin Espaillat, appeared in the vicinity of Santiago yesterday; thirty-five of them stopped and searched a railroad train, and, finding no ammunition on board, they allowed the train to proceed. Jose Bordas, governor of Santiago, reports that he has sufficient force to control the situation; every one in the city is helping him, as all fear pillage if the insurgents enter the place. A train carrying ammunition, guarded by 150 men, which left here last night, entered Santiago without resistance. The American government is closely following the Dominican situation, and yesterday instructed Consul Simpson to cable the situation in Puerto Plata; he answered that everything was quiet, and he will await developments before making another report. Strangers are especially menaced by Jiminez.
records.summary_es: El Republic publica la parte final de un despacho de Santo Domingo: se aconseja a Jiménez retomar Puerto Plata a sangre y fuego, hacer que sus tropas saqueen la ciudad y desterrar a los comerciantes extranjeros que se nieguen a adelantar fondos a los revolucionarios. Jiménez no puede reclutar tropas en Monte Cristi. Haití ha reconocido al gobierno de Morales y está suministrando municiones. Ciento cincuenta de las tropas de Jiménez, mandadas por el general Polin Espaillat, aparecieron ayer en las cercanías de Santiago; treinta y cinco de ellos detuvieron y registraron un tren de ferrocarril, y, al no encontrar municiones a bordo, permitieron que el tren continuara. José Bordas, gobernador de Santiago, informa que tiene fuerza suficiente para controlar la situación; todos en la ciudad lo están ayudando, pues todos temen el saqueo si los insurgentes entran en la plaza. Un tren que transportaba municiones, custodiado por 150 hombres, que salió de aquí anoche, entró en Santiago sin resistencia. El gobierno estadounidense sigue de cerca la situación dominicana, y ayer instruyó al cónsul Simpson que cablegrafiara la situación en Puerto Plata; respondió que todo estaba tranquilo, y que esperará los acontecimientos antes de hacer otro informe. Los extranjeros están especialmente amenazados por Jiménez.

records.headline: The Republican prints the closing part of an editorial on German designs
records.summary_en: The Republican prints the closing part of an editorial on German designs in Santo Domingo: this is not the first intimation that the ambitious kaiser has his covetous eye on the island and may at almost any time, if not restrained by the United States, make a determined grab for it; his anxiety to gain some foothold in America is of common knowledge, and toward the end of the presidential term of Wos y Gill he began open negotiations for the occupation of Samana Bay. At that time the State Department at Washington sent a vigorous message to the Dominican government, putting an emphatic prohibition on the proposed arrangement, and in consequence the initiated deal fell through; but the Dominicans maintain that they are a free and independent nation, at liberty to negotiate with whom they please, and there are several reasons, now that their political and economic conditions have become still more unendurable, why they may accede to German solicitations. Rather close relations between the two countries already exist: their mutual commerce is next in importance to that between the Dominican republic and the United States; Germany has large interests in the island, and many Germans live there, having succeeded in making themselves agreeable to the islanders in both commercial and social relations; there have been intermarriages between the German settlers and the natives, and many of the Dominican young men are graduates of German schools. These conditions afford a favorable basis for successful negotiations looking to the ultimate establishment of a German protectorate.
records.summary_es: El Republican publica la parte final de un editorial sobre los designios alemanes en Santo Domingo: no es esta la primera indicación de que el ambicioso káiser tiene su ojo codicioso puesto en la isla y puede en casi cualquier momento, si los Estados Unidos no lo refrenan, hacer un intento decidido por apoderarse de ella; su ansiedad por ganar algún punto de apoyo en América es de conocimiento común, y hacia el fin del período presidencial de Woss y Gil comenzó negociaciones abiertas para la ocupación de la bahía de Samaná. En esa época el Departamento de Estado en Washington envió un enérgico mensaje al gobierno dominicano, poniendo una enfática prohibición al arreglo propuesto, y en consecuencia el trato iniciado se vino abajo; pero los dominicanos sostienen que son una nación libre e independiente, en libertad de negociar con quien les plazca, y hay varias razones, ahora que sus condiciones políticas y económicas se han vuelto aún más insoportables, por las que pueden acceder a las solicitaciones alemanas. Ya existen relaciones bastante estrechas entre los dos países: su comercio mutuo es el siguiente en importancia al que existe entre la república dominicana y los Estados Unidos; Alemania tiene grandes intereses en la isla, y muchos alemanes viven allí, habiendo logrado hacerse agradables a los isleños tanto en las relaciones comerciales como en las sociales; ha habido matrimonios entre los colonos alemanes y los nativos, y muchos de los jóvenes dominicanos son graduados de escuelas alemanas. Estas condiciones ofrecen una base favorable para negociaciones exitosas con miras al establecimiento final de un protectorado alemán.

records.headline: The Optic prints three items: a Denver dispatch of February 6
records.summary_en: The Optic prints three items: a Denver dispatch of February 6 reports a special to the Times from Washington: it is believed that the insult to the American flag in San Domingo will be seized upon by the administration as a pretext to seize territory in that country and absorb it; the project was once under way during President Grant's term. Under the head 'Supplies of Leader Seized', a Cape Haytien dispatch of February 6 reports that munitions of war intended for General Jiminez, Dominican revolutionary leader, were seized at Puerto Plata after having been landed January 30 from New York. Under the head 'Uncle Sam's Position', a Washington item of February 6 reports that 'Full particulars about assassination of Johnson' is the substance of a cablegram Secretary Moody dispatched to Commander Lewis C. Heilner, commanding the gunboat Yankee at Santo Domingo City; when details of the assassination arrive the secretary will be in a position to give specific instructions as to the course to be followed, and if the press dispatches are confirmed, it can be stated that the naval commanders will be instructed to demand and obtain the fullest reparation.
records.summary_es: El Optic publica tres notas: un despacho de Denver del 6 de febrero da cuenta de un especial al Times desde Washington: se cree que el insulto a la bandera estadounidense en Santo Domingo será aprovechado por la administración como pretexto para apoderarse de territorio en ese país y absorberlo; el proyecto estuvo una vez en marcha durante el período del presidente Grant. Bajo el titular «Supplies of Leader Seized», un despacho de Cabo Haitiano del 6 de febrero informa que municiones de guerra destinadas al general Jiménez, líder revolucionario dominicano, fueron incautadas en Puerto Plata después de haber sido desembarcadas el 30 de enero procedentes de Nueva York. Bajo el titular «Uncle Sam's Position», una nota de Washington del 6 de febrero informa que «Full particulars about assassination of Johnson» es la sustancia de un cablegrama que el secretario Moody despachó al comandante Lewis C. Heilner, al mando de la cañonera Yankee en la ciudad de Santo Domingo; cuando lleguen los detalles del asesinato, el secretario estará en posición de dar instrucciones específicas en cuanto al curso a seguir, y si los despachos de prensa se confirman, puede afirmarse que los comandantes navales serán instruidos para exigir y obtener la más completa reparación.

records.headline: The Herald prints a biographical sketch of General Jiminez
records.summary_en: The Herald prints a biographical sketch of General Jiminez, whose portrait it publishes: he is to be favored as president of the Dominican republic, but the provisional government that recently ousted Wos y Gil is strongly opposing him; he has twice been president of Santo Domingo, the last time succeeding Heureaux, whom Jiminez's agents are said to have assassinated. Jiminez is well known in American cities, especially in New York, where he planned many of his operations affecting the Dominican government and people. In 1898, at the outbreak of the Spanish war, Jiminez attempted an invasion of the island and made a landing at Monte Christi, but was driven off and narrowly escaped with his life.

Jiménez es bien conocido en las ciudades estadounidenses, especialmente en Nueva York, donde planeó muchas de sus operaciones que afectaban al gobierno y al pueblo dominicanos. En 1898, al estallar la guerra española, Jiménez intentó una invasión de la isla y efectuó un desembarco en Monte Cristi, pero fue rechazado y escapó por poco con vida.

records.headline: The Spy prints the closing part of a Washington item: a cablegram
records.summary_en: The Spy prints the closing part of a Washington item: a cablegram was dispatched to Rear Admiral Wise, commanding the training squadron now at Guantanamo, instructing that officer to take immediate and effective steps for the adequate protection of American life and property in the Dominican republic, limiting his course of action at all times to the recognized tenets of international law; upon the receipt of this dispatch Rear Admiral Wise is expected to proceed at once, in his flagship, the Minneapolis, to Dominican waters and make a personal investigation. The Columbia already has been ordered to return to San Domingo from Guantanamo, where she went for coal, and the Hartford will be ordered back from the same place. The San Isidro plantation is owned by the Bartram Brothers of New York; it is managed by an American named Bass; the plantation is on the Ozama river about 11 miles inland; only steam tugs can navigate the river, and it is expected that Rear Admiral Wise will send one or more tugs with marines to guard the plantation. Admiral Wise is not instructed regarding the killing of Machinist Johnson, pending the receipt of full particulars telegraphed for today by Secretary Moody. Gen. Sanchez, the Dominican minister, has been informed of the firm policy adopted by the Washington government; he is cabling his government tonight regarding the feeling in official circles. It is apparent that the long pending Dominican problem is reaching a crisis that will demand immediate attention.

records.headline: The Review prints the closing part of a Washington item on the complaints of Americans
records.summary_en: The Review prints the closing part of a Washington item on the complaints of Americans in San Domingo: their property had been besieged, and appeals were made for immediate relief. Other Americans having interests in San Domingo have made similar complaint. Moody, secretary of the navy, and Loomis, acting secretary of state, held a conference with the President today on the subject; upon his return to the navy department from the White House Secretary Moody held a conference with Rear Admiral Taylor, chief of the bureau of navigation, and a cablegram was dispatched to Rear Admiral Wise, commanding the training squadron now at Guantanamo, instructing that officer to take immediate and effective steps for the adequate protection of American lives and property in the Dominican Republic, limiting his action at all times to the recognized tenets of international law. It is apparent that the long pending Dominican problem is reaching a crisis that will demand immediate attention: the German government has well nigh reached the limit of its patience in dealing with San Domingo, and the London and Paris governments show equal impatience with affairs there; all these governments have bided their time in the hope that the Washington government would meet the obligations placed upon it by the Monroe Doctrine, and put an end to the unsatisfactory state of affairs; if the United States had not acted, it can be stated that the European nations would call the situation to its attention. The German ambassador had a brief conference with the President today.
records.summary_es: El Review publica la parte final de una nota de Washington sobre las quejas de los estadounidenses en Santo Domingo: sus propiedades habían sido sitiadas, y se hicieron llamamientos pidiendo auxilio inmediato. Moody, secretario de Marina, y Loomis, secretario de Estado interino, celebraron hoy una conferencia con el Presidente sobre el asunto; a su regreso al Departamento de Marina desde la Casa Blanca, el secretario Moody celebró una conferencia con el contraalmirante Taylor, jefe de la oficina de navegación, y se despachó un cablegrama al contraalmirante Wise, al mando de la escuadra de instrucción ahora en Guantánamo, instruyendo a ese oficial a tomar medidas inmediatas y eficaces para la adecuada protección de las vidas y los bienes estadounidenses en la República Dominicana, limitando su acción en todo momento a los principios reconocidos del derecho internacional. Es evidente que el problema dominicano, pendiente desde hace tiempo, está llegando a una crisis que demandará atención inmediata: el gobierno alemán ha llegado casi al límite de su paciencia en su trato con Santo Domingo, y los gobiernos de Londres y París muestran igual impaciencia con los asuntos allí; todos estos gobiernos han esperado pacientemente con la esperanza de que el gobierno de Washington cumpliera las obligaciones que le impone la Doctrina Monroe, y pusiera fin al insatisfactorio estado de cosas; si los Estados Unidos no hubieran actuado, puede afirmarse que las naciones europeas habrían llamado su atención sobre la situación. El embajador alemán tuvo hoy una breve conferencia con el Presidente.

records.headline: The Tribune prints part of an editorial on the United States
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints part of an editorial on the United States and Santo Domingo: the United States cares little whether Jiménez or Morales or Hoochi Koochi is President of the Dominican Republic; what it does care for, and does demand, is that its flag shall be treated with courtesy, that the lives and property of its citizens shall be secure, and that the Dominican Republic, under one government or another, shall conduct itself in a manner befitting a State that wants to be recognized as independent and sovereign; if the Dominican Republic will comply with such reasonable requirements, the United States will jealously safeguard its sovereignty; if it either will not or cannot do so, it must suffer the consequences. The ordinary rights and duties of the United States in Santo Domingo are greatly reinforced by the relations sustained for many years with that country: more than three-quarters of a century ago the United States proclaimed to the world practically a protectorate over Santo Domingo against all European interference; during all these years that protectorate has been kept valid, without, of course, even the slightest interference with the island's entire independence; many a time in those years some European power would have achieved the conquest of the island had it not been for the American warning; there would now be European intervention, and probably subjection of the republic within twenty-four hours, were it not for the United States; the fact of having exercised such protection in Santo Domingo's behalf gives the United States peculiar moral rights.

records.headline: The Times prints an item on the long-pending indemnity claims
records.summary_en: The Times prints an item on the long-pending indemnity claims, under the head 'Millions Due': for years this government has been attempting to collect an indemnity of several million dollars, growing out of the injury to the property of American industries there, but each time, as a final settlement seemed probable, the Dominican government was overthrown and the negotiations had to be begun anew. The Morales government, now in control, has been striving to secure recognition from the United States. Minister Powell recently advised the Department of State that he had recognized the existing government as the de facto government; it was fully understood that the recognition was conditional upon a guarantee of settlement for the pending claims. Under the head 'Annexation Possible', the Times adds: negotiations looking to this end have been in progress, the secretary of war of the provisional government having come here to expedite the settlement; the killing of Johnson, although caused by the insurgents, is believed sufficient to warrant the government in enforcing peace on the island; there are those that declare that another change in the map of the Western Hemisphere is probable; it is significant that on the day the American seaman lost his life Senator Heyburn of Idaho advocated upon the floor of the Senate, during the discussion of the Panama question, the passage of his bill providing for the purchase and annexation of Haiti and Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: El Times publica una nota sobre las reclamaciones de indemnización pendientes desde hace tiempo, bajo el titular «Millions Due»: durante años este gobierno ha estado tratando de cobrar una indemnización de varios millones de dólares, derivada del daño a los bienes de industrias estadounidenses allí, pero cada vez que un arreglo final parecía probable, el gobierno dominicano era derrocado y las negociaciones tenían que comenzar de nuevo. El gobierno de Morales, ahora en control, ha estado esforzándose por lograr el reconocimiento de los Estados Unidos. El ministro Powell informó recientemente al Departamento de Estado que había reconocido al gobierno existente como el gobierno de facto; se entendió plenamente que el reconocimiento estaba condicionado a una garantía de arreglo para las reclamaciones pendientes. Bajo el titular «Annexation Possible», el Times añade: han estado en curso negociaciones con miras a ese fin, habiendo venido aquí el secretario de Guerra del gobierno provisional para acelerar el arreglo; la muerte de Johnson, aunque causada por los insurgentes, se cree suficiente para justificar que el gobierno imponga la paz en la isla; hay quienes declaran que es probable otro cambio en el mapa del hemisferio occidental; es significativo que el día en que el marino estadounidense perdió la vida, el senador Heyburn, de Idaho, defendió en el pleno del Senado, durante la discusión de la cuestión de Panamá, la aprobación de su proyecto de ley que dispone la compra y anexión de Haití y Santo Domingo.

records.headline: The Star prints the closing part of a Washington item: an appeal
records.summary_en: The Star prints the closing part of a Washington item: an appeal is made for immediate relief, their property having been besieged; other Americans having interests in San Domingo have made similar complaints. A cablegram was dispatched to Rear Admiral Wise, commanding the training squadron at Guantanamo, instructing that officer to take immediate and effective steps for the protection of American life and property in the Dominican republic, limiting his course of action at all times to the recognized tenets of international law; upon the receipt of this dispatch Rear Admiral Wise is expected to proceed at once in his flagship, the Minneapolis, to Dominican waters and make a personal investigation. The Columbia already has been ordered to return to San Domingo from Guantanamo, where she went for coal, and the Hartford will be ordered back from the same place. It is apparent that the long pending Dominican problem is reaching a crisis that will demand immediate attention: the German government has well nigh reached the limit of its patience in dealing with San Domingo, and the London and Paris governments show an equal impatience with affairs there; all these governments have bided their time in the hope that the Washington government would put an end to the unsatisfactory state of affairs there; if the United States had not acted, it can be stated, European nations would have called the situation to its attention.

records.headline: The Journal prints the closing part of a Washington item and a Monte Cristi dispatch
records.summary_en: The Journal prints the closing part of a Washington item and a Monte Cristi dispatch under the head 'Blow to Jiminez': at the close of the discussion, it was decided that the best solution of the problem was to turn affairs over to the navy and have Admiral Wise insure the absolute protection of American interests; it is believed here that he has already taken steps to obtain apology and full reparation for the firing on the New York. The dispatch, dated Saturday, February 6, reports: the Clyde Line steamer New York, from New York, January 30, arrived here this morning, followed by the Dominican gunboat Presidente; lighters were sent alongside the New York to bring ashore some ammunition which formed part of her cargo; when the lighters had nearly reached the steamer the gunboat fired on them and the revolutionists on shore replied with cannon and Mausers. The New York, being in danger, thereupon left Monte Cristi for Porto Plata; the firing continued for half an hour, after which the gunboat sailed for Porto Plata; she was hit twice by round shot and apparently by hundreds of bullets, for she stopped and lowered boats evidently to plug the holes made in her hull. The failure to land the ammunition is a serious blow to General Jiminez, for whom it was intended, and may cause him to lose the ground he had already gained; an attack on Santiago de los Caballeros had been fixed for Sunday. The German steamer Aiternberg was here on Monday; the revolutionists did not permit her to discharge at this port.
records.summary_es: El Diario publica la parte final de una nota de Washington y un despacho de Monte Cristi bajo el titular «Blow to Jiminez»: al cierre de la discusión, se decidió que la mejor solución del problema era entregar los asuntos a la marina y hacer que el almirante Wise asegurara la protección absoluta de los intereses estadounidenses; se cree aquí que ya ha tomado medidas para obtener disculpas y reparación completa por los disparos contra el New York. El despacho, fechado el sábado 6 de febrero, informa: el vapor New York, de la línea Clyde, procedente de Nueva York, del 30 de enero, llegó aquí esta mañana, seguido por la cañonera dominicana Presidente; se enviaron lanchones junto al New York para traer a tierra algunas municiones que formaban parte de su cargamento; cuando los lanchones casi habían llegado al vapor, la cañonera disparó contra ellos y los revolucionarios en la costa respondieron con cañones y fusiles Máuser. El New York, al estar en peligro, salió entonces de Monte Cristi hacia Puerto Plata; los disparos continuaron durante media hora, tras lo cual la cañonera zarpó hacia Puerto Plata; fue alcanzada dos veces por balas de cañón y aparentemente por cientos de balas, pues se detuvo y bajó botes, evidentemente para tapar los agujeros hechos en su casco. El fracaso en desembarcar las municiones es un golpe serio para el general Jiménez, a quien estaban destinadas, y puede hacerle perder el terreno que ya había ganado; un ataque a Santiago de los Caballeros había sido fijado para el domingo. El vapor alemán Aiternberg estuvo aquí el lunes; los revolucionarios no le permitieron descargar en este puerto.

TO HAVE DIAMOND BELT AT ST. LOUIS EXPOSITION. John L. Sullivan, world's pugilistic champion for many years, and a willing performer, whose achievements are well known, will be at the St. Louis Exposition, in charge of the diamond belt won by him. Mr. Sullivan, who is appearing at the Park Theatre this week, will be in Cuba before making the trip west. James F. Murray, manager of John L., has arranged for the Cuban tour. They will start the latter part of next month. Upon their return the diamond belt, which was presented to John L. in Boston Theatre in 1887, will be shown at the World's Fair. Since the case on 42d Street, New York, formerly owned by John L., changed hands, the diamond belt, valued at [illegible], has been in the hands of Jere Donahue of Philadelphia. John L. doesn't like the account of the Paddy Ryan fight, recently recalled in a Boston paper. Sullivan says that at the first in Mississippi City he wasn't knocked down by Ryan, despite the statement crediting Ryan with such a feat.

records.passage: the cruisers Montgomery and Detroit, now at Culebra, have been ordered from there to Porto Plata. The Clyde Liner New-York Fails to Land Cargo at Monte Christi. Monte Christi, Santo Domingo, Feb. 6. — The Clyde Line steamship New-York, which sailed from New-York on January 30, arrived here this morning. It was followed by the Dominican gunboat Presidente. Lighters were sent alongside the New-York, to bring ashore some ammunition, which formed part of her cargo. When the lighters had nearly reached the steamship the gunboat fired on them, and the revolutionists on shore replied with cannon and Mausers. Being in danger, the New-York thereupon left Monte Christi for Porto Plata. The firing continued for half an hour, after which the gunboat sailed for Porto Plata. She was hit twice by round shot, and apparently by many bullets, for she stopped and lowered boats, evidently to plug the holes made in her hull. The failure to land the ammunition is a serious blow to General Jiménez, for whom it was intended, and may cause him to lose the ground he had already gained. An attack on Santiago de los Caballeros had been fixed for Sunday.

The island is about 450 miles long, Hayti holding the western one-third, and the Dominicans the balance; it seems a mass of mountains from the sea, but the island contains many beautiful valleys. In Hayti the French tongue is spoken, but the Dominicans speak Spanish; as a rule the Dominicans are a mixture of Spaniards, Indians and negroes in about equal proportions. The republic was established in 1843, and it has been the scene of many revolutions and insurrections since that time. The United States minister, Mr. Powell, considers the present situation chaotic and an invitation to this country to intervene and restore order. As the United States will not permit any other country to become peacemaker and order restorer, the responsibility seems to rest upon it to do something in Santo Domingo, and doubtless the murder of the machinist will be all the excuse it needs for a degree of intervention that will restore order, or at least enough authority to grant it reparation for the firing on an American gunboat, and the killing on it of an American citizen.

records.headline: The Tribune prints an item on the arrival of the steamer New York
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints an item on the arrival of the steamer New York and a statement by Consul Thomas Simpson: the steamer called at all her ports en route except Monte Christi, the captain being told by Minister Powell that the Dominican government had established a blockade there. Thomas Simpson, United States consul at Puerto Plata, and Frank H. Sampson, superintendent of the San Domingo Southern Railroad, were among the passengers. Mr. Simpson was yesterday quoted as saying: 'There was no fighting in the Cibao when I left. The Morales party has been in possession of Puerto Plata since January 17, and while several provinces in the south are still unsubdued, I think the government will win in the end. We had a pretty lively time when the government troops attacked Puerto Plata. The fort held out after the town had surrendered, and a detachment of marines from the Detroit had to be sent to the insurgents in command to convince them that they were beaten. I was in doubt how to treat the Morales government and sent for advice. I received a reply saying that the United States was dealing with the government, and asking what the condition of affairs was at Puerto Plata. I was further informed by Minister Powell of the recognition of the government by our country and wrote a letter accordingly to Captain Marmion, of the New-York, advising him not to attempt to land stores at Monte Christi, as that port was being blockaded by a legitimate government.'
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica una nota sobre la llegada del vapor New York y una declaración del cónsul Thomas Simpson: el vapor hizo escala en todos sus puertos de ruta excepto Monte Cristi, habiendo sido informado el capitán por el ministro Powell de que el gobierno dominicano había establecido un bloqueo allí. Thomas Simpson, cónsul de los Estados Unidos en Puerto Plata, y Frank H. Sampson, superintendente del San Domingo Southern Railroad, estaban entre los pasajeros. El Sr. Simpson fue citado ayer diciendo: «No había combates en el Cibao cuando salí. El partido de Morales está en posesión de Puerto Plata desde el 17 de enero, y aunque varias provincias del sur aún no han sido sometidas, creo que el gobierno ganará al final. Pasamos un tiempo bastante agitado cuando las tropas del gobierno atacaron Puerto Plata. El fuerte resistió después de que la ciudad se hubo rendido, y hubo que enviar un destacamento de infantes de marina del Detroit a los insurgentes al mando para convencerlos de que estaban derrotados. Estuve en duda sobre cómo tratar al gobierno de Morales y pedí consejo. Recibí una respuesta diciendo que los Estados Unidos estaban tratando con el gobierno, y preguntando cuál era la situación en Puerto Plata. Fui informado además por el ministro Powell del reconocimiento del gobierno por nuestro país y escribí en consecuencia una carta al capitán Marmion, del New-York, aconsejándole que no intentara desembarcar provisiones en Monte Cristi, ya que ese puerto estaba siendo bloqueado por un gobierno legítimo».

records.summary_en: The Republican prints the closing part of a Santo Domingo dispatch and a Washington item under the head 'Orders Sent Admiral Wise': the body was escorted to its grave in the Santa Barbara cemetery by a detachment of marines, bluejackets and officers from the Yankee, headed by the ship's band; United States Minister Powell, the American consul and vice-consul and nearly all the diplomatic and consular representatives at San Domingo went to the funeral. All the houses outside the city walls have been pillaged; the insurgents are desperate, and are destroying foreign property wherever they find it; Mr. Powell has received urgent appeals to protect foreign property against this pillaging, and the Columbia may be compelled to land marines to do so. In the Washington item, specific instructions have been cabled Rear-Admiral Wise, commanding the training squadron in Dominican waters, regarding the protection of American shipping interests there: the firing on lighters attempting to land a part of the cargo of the Clyde line steamer New York at Monte Cristi by a government gunboat, as reported in cable dispatches published Wednesday morning, has aroused indignation in official circles at Washington; the probable course of action after such an outrage would be the seizure of the government gunboat by Rear-Admiral Wise, in which event it probably would be carried to Guantanamo. Drastic measures will be taken by this government to end the anarchy in San Domingo.

El gobierno tomará medidas drásticas para poner fin a la anarquía en Santo Domingo.

records.headline: The Sentinel prints a biographical sketch of Juan Isidro Jiminez
records.summary_en: The Sentinel prints a biographical sketch of Juan Isidro Jiminez, who left here a few months ago for Porto Rico, anxious to return to the office from which he was deposed by Gen. Horacio Vasquez about a year and a half ago; in fact he resigned the place of fiscal agent of Santo Domingo to the United States and Europe, to which President Wos y Gil had appointed him, that he might be free to take part in a rebellion and return to the presidency. It was not expected, however, that his hopes would be realized, as Gen. Carlos Morales, governor of Porto Plata, a former priest, who started the movement, has also aspirations for the place; another reason for believing that Gen. Jiminez would not again become president was the opposition to him of the Vasquez element. Gen. records.headline: The Globe prints a Washington dispatch of February 16: the rebels
records.summary_en: The Globe prints a Washington dispatch of February 16: the rebels in San Domingo have committed another breach of international law, which, added to those preceding, are making up a formidable case that may justify the United States in intervening to restore order and protect property in the distracted island. Minister Powell reported to the State Department today that he had received belated advices from Jean Villain, the vice consular agent at Samana, dated Feb. 9, to this effect: 'Insurgents entered our consulate at Samana with armed force and took two refugees out.' The State Department communicated this information to the Navy Department, with a request that proper action be taken by the naval authorities to protect the United States consulate; this was transmitted to Admiral Wise, and it is the belief that he will not only protect the consulate, but will demand the punishment of the perpetrators of this outrage, and if the provisional government is not able to do this he will employ the United States naval force to chastise the insurgents. The dispatch appears under the head 'Violate the Flag'.
records.summary_es: El Globe publica un despacho de Washington del 16 de febrero: los rebeldes en Santo Domingo han cometido otra violación del derecho internacional, que, sumada a las precedentes, está formando un caso formidable que puede justificar que los Estados Unidos intervengan para restablecer el orden y proteger los bienes en la atribulada isla. El ministro Powell informó hoy al Departamento de Estado que había recibido despachos tardíos de Jean Villain, agente consular adjunto en Samaná, fechados el 9 de febrero, en estos términos: «Los insurgentes entraron en nuestro consulado en Samaná con fuerza armada y se llevaron a dos refugiados». El Departamento de Estado comunicó esta información al Departamento de Marina, con la solicitud de que las autoridades navales tomaran las medidas adecuadas para proteger el consulado de los Estados Unidos; esto fue transmitido al almirante Wise, y se cree que no solo protegerá el consulado, sino que exigirá el castigo de los perpetradores de este ultraje, y si el gobierno provisional no puede hacerlo, empleará la fuerza naval de los Estados Unidos para castigar a los insurgentes. El despacho aparece bajo el titular «Violate the Flag».
