records.headline: The Tribune prints a syndicated description and history of Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints a syndicated description and history of Santo Domingo: in Samana Bay it possesses one of the finest natural harbors in the world; it was this port which President Grant was especially anxious to secure as a coaling station. The oldest settlement in the new world was on this island, the great discoverer himself having founded it; here the great discoverer was buried, and here for a number of years was the capital of the Spanish possessions in the new world. At the end of the eighteenth century Spain ceded the eastern half of the island to France, which held the western half. Soon after, the paper says, the entire country under Toussaint L'Ouverture gained its independence. In 1844 came the rebellion of the eastern portion of the island, resulting in the formation of the present Dominican Republic.
records.summary_es: El Tribune publica una descripción e historia sindicada de Santo Domingo: en la bahía de Samaná posee uno de los mejores puertos naturales del mundo; fue este puerto el que el presidente Grant estaba especialmente ansioso de asegurar como estación carbonera. El asentamiento más antiguo del nuevo mundo estaba en esta isla, habiéndolo fundado el propio gran descubridor; aquí fue enterrado el gran descubridor, y aquí estuvo por varios años la capital de las posesiones españolas en el nuevo mundo. A fines del siglo dieciocho España cedió la mitad oriental de la isla a Francia, que poseía la mitad occidental. Poco después, dice el periódico, todo el país bajo Toussaint L'Ouverture ganó su independencia. En 1844 vino la rebelión de la porción oriental de la isla, resultando en la formación de la actual República Dominicana.

records.headline: The Bee prints a history feature on Santo Domingo's civil wars
records.summary_en: The Bee prints a history feature on Santo Domingo's civil wars: when the Spaniards had gone, the country was little more than a thinly peopled desert, and most of the evidence of Spanish civilization had been swept away. Then, instead of trying to build up the country in peace, the Dominicans indulged in a long series of civil wars; warfare had bred a crew of soldiers of fortune and of ambitious politicians, eager to carve their way to the best places by the sword, and scarcely would one ruler, whether elected by the people or foisted upon them by armed upheaval, become seated in the executive chair than busy plotters began to arrange for his downfall. Under the head 'A Long List of Revolutions', the feature continues: revolution followed revolution, and as many as three revolutions have been harassing the unhappy islanders at the same time. When the Spaniards finally evacuated Santo Domingo, Baez became president, but was driven out the following year and succeeded by Cabral. The latter, confronted by an uprising, fled, and Baez again assumed the reins of government, which he held until 1873. It was he who opened negotiations with President Grant looking to the annexation of Santo Domingo by the United States; this proposition was defeated in the Senate at Washington by a very narrow vote. From 1873 to 1879 Gonzales was at the head of the government and managed to hold his seat despite several formidable revolutionary jolts.
records.summary_es: El Bee publica un reportaje histórico sobre las guerras civiles de Santo Domingo: cuando los españoles se habían ido, el país era poco más que un desierto escasamente poblado, y la mayor parte de la evidencia de la civilización española había sido barrida. records.full_text:
DOMINGO IN SENATE.

Senator Morgan Made Sensational Charges Against W. N. Cromwell.

WASHINGTON, March 17.—Senator Morgan occupied practically the entire time of the discussion of the Santo Domingo treaty in executive session of the senate. He made a sensational speech in which he charged that William Nelson Cromwell of New York, who was prominently connected with the sale of the Panama canal property to the United States, was the prime mover in a scheme to influence the United States in the financial affairs of the Dominican government. He asserted that Mr. Cromwell was actuated by a desire to frustrate a plan of a Mr. and Mrs. Reader, natives of Alabama, who are operating under the name of the Reader syndicate, to get certain concessions from the Dominican government and to promote the interests of a syndicate he represented, which it is alleged holds a mass of claims against Latin-American republics, including a large part of the debts against the Dominican government.

Among the senate leaders a new plan was advanced in regard to Santo Domingo, to be dealt with at the next session of congress. It has been suggested that if the whole matter is allowed to go over a joint resolution might be passed by congress to authorize the president to do the very things that are proposed by the treaty. If this course were pursued a majority vote is all that would be required to place the entire matter in the hands of the president. It is understood that the plan found favor when it was suggested at the White House by senators who called there lately. Some doubt was expressed as to the constitutionality of dealing with this question except by treaty, but the case of the annexation of Hawaii, which was done by joint resolution, was used as a precedent, and Republican leaders believe it to be feasible.

Adjournment of the session cannot be had until Saturday because of the situation in relation to nominations for judgeships in Illinois, which cannot be determined before that time. Treaty discussion will go on for the two days the session is expected to continue, and something more may be expected of the charges made by Senator Morgan.

records.headline: The Globe prints a New York item, under the heads 'Readers Tell of Dominican Snarl'
records.summary_en: The Globe prints a New York item, under the heads 'Readers Tell of Dominican Snarl' and 'Plans of Bustling Business Woman and Her Husband Upset by Roosevelt': Athole B. Reader and his wife, mentioned by Senator Morgan in the Santo Domingo treaty discussion as composing the Reader syndicate which had in hand a plan for raising the debts of the Dominican republic and the sale of a naval port in the island to the American government, are in this city. Mrs. Reader was formerly Miss Ella Rawls of Alabama, a stenographer, who came to New York in 1891 to seek her fortune; in five years she had become owner of a large stenographic bureau in Wall Street and did considerable work for the Venezuelan boundary commission. Later she went to London and, representing a prominent English banking firm, procured from the sultan of Johore a $5,000,000 railroad contract; while in London she married Reader, a native of New Zealand, who traveled widely and acted as confidential secretary to well known persons. The couple claim later to have taken charge of a big Peruvian mining deal and, by the diplomatic efforts of Mrs. Reader, to have averted a revolution in that country. Under the head 'Spoiled by Dillingham', the item adds that in a long statement the Readers set forth their scheme for relieving the Santo Domingo situation, which fell through when Commander Dillingham arrived on the scene, and that they claim to have been engaged in the matter by one Perez, a secret agent here of President Morales.
records.summary_es: El Globe publica una nota de Nueva York, bajo los títulos «Readers Tell of Dominican Snarl» y «Plans of Bustling Business Woman and Her Husband Upset by Roosevelt»: Athole B. Reader y su esposa, mencionados por el senador Morgan en la discusión del tratado de Santo Domingo como los que componen el sindicato Reader que tenía en mano un plan para recaudar las deudas de la república dominicana y la venta de un puerto naval en la isla al gobierno estadounidense, están en esta ciudad. Se dice que la señora Reader fue antes la señorita Ella Rawls, de Alabama, una taquígrafa, que vino a Nueva York en 1891 a buscar su fortuna; en cinco años se había convertido en propietaria de una gran oficina taquigráfica en Wall Street e hizo un trabajo considerable para la comisión de límites de Venezuela. Más tarde fue a Londres y, representando a una prominente firma bancaria inglesa, procuró del sultán de Johore un contrato ferroviario de $5,000,000; mientras estaba en Londres se casó con Reader, un nativo de Nueva Zelanda, que viajó ampliamente y actuó como secretario confidencial de personas bien conocidas. La pareja afirma haber tomado luego a su cargo un gran negocio minero peruano y, por los esfuerzos diplomáticos de la señora Reader, haber evitado una revolución en ese país. Bajo el título «Spoiled by Dillingham», la nota añade que en una larga declaración los Reader exponen su esquema para aliviar la situación de Santo Domingo, que fracasó cuando el comandante Dillingham llegó a la escena, y que afirman haber sido contratados en el asunto por un tal Pérez, un agente secreto aquí del presidente Morales.

records.headline: The Banner prints a New York item about the Reader syndicate
records.summary_en: The Banner prints a New York item about the Reader syndicate: Mr. and Mrs. Athole B. Reader, the South American mine owners whose plans to get concessions from President Morales, Senator Morgan said, were frustrated by the intervention of this country, have turned up in New York and elaborated on Senator Morgan's story, adding that Mr. Cromwell had been their legal adviser with respect to their Dominican enterprises, the failure of which followed the arrival of Commander Dillingham and the signing of the now famous Dillingham-Sanchez agreement. Mr. Cromwell on his part issued a general denial of any connection with Dominican affairs. It was arranged that Mrs. Reader should be fiscal agent in this country for President Morales, that Mr. Reader should take hold of the Santo Domingo end of the negotiations, and that President Morales should hand over to the Readers the bay of Samana, which the Readers might or might not hand over to President Roosevelt as a coaling station. Mrs. Reader relates that Mr. Perez and Mr. Reader arrived at Santo Domingo on the 10th of December, 1904, and were met on the boat by General Morales, and that Perez called on Morales on Friday evening, as arranged, and returned to her husband about 11 o'clock with the news that everything was most satisfactory and that President Morales was ready to keep his promise and had agreed generally to everything Mr. Reader required.

records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* reported statements from President Morales warning that the Dominican government was powerless to resist European debt enforcement unless the United States intervened to delay creditor demands. Following the United States Senate's failure to ratify the customs treaty, fears spread in Santo Domingo that European nations would seize ports to satisfy unpaid claims. The report noted that while multiple American warships patrolled the coast, local observers argued that European seizures would effectively undermine the Monroe Doctrine.

Tras la falta de ratificación del tratado aduanero por el Senado de los Estados Unidos, se extendió en Santo Domingo el temor de que las naciones europeas incautaran puertos para saldar las reclamaciones pendientes. El informe señalaba que, mientras varios buques de guerra estadounidenses patrullaban la costa, observadores locales sostenían que las incautaciones europeas socavarían de hecho la Doctrina Monroe.

It is utterly impossible for the government to pay the sums due foreign nations unless the United States can procure from foreign powers a postponement of their demands. Otherwise these demands will be pressed. I have no physical or moral force to resist them. With the customs-houses in,the control of the United States, the resources of the island will develop speedily, and all demands will be paid, with the result that the country will be educated to peace and permanent prosperity.” With two Dominican ports now in the hands of the United States and the failure of the treaty, Dominicans believe that a "grab game" by foreign powers will begin at once. An Italian cruiser was at San Domingo a few days ago, but with drew to Kingston. The American gun boat Castine is at San Domingo with 150 men; the cruiser Chattanooga is at Samana bay: the Detroit is at Puerto Plata, and the Dixie is at Monte Cristi. Rear-Admiral Sigsbee has gone to Guantanamo for a consultation with Rear-Admiral Barker. With the seizure of Dominican ports by foreign powers, it is argued at San Domingo that the Monroe doctrine will be nullified as regards the Dominican republic. With the United States in the possession of two ports, it would not be logical, it is argued, to oppose the seizure of her ports by foreign powers. At the same time the only hope of President Morales is that in some way the United States can secure a postponement of seizure by European powers. No steps to this end have been initiated at San Domingo.

records.headline: The Herald prints an item on the Dominican fiscal situation
records.summary_en: The Herald prints an item on the Dominican fiscal situation: foreign creditors, principally Italy and Belgium, are taking advantage of the deferring of the proposed convention between the United States and San Domingo, and of the Venezuela situation, to demand payment of their claims. In order to meet the situation it has been proposed by the Dominican government that an American be designated as commissioner for the collection of all customs at southern ports, 45 per cent of which collection shall be set apart for the expenses of the government, and that 65 per cent, less expenses of collection, be deposited in an American bank until the Sanchez-Dillingham convention is either ratified or repealed; should the convention be ultimately rejected, the money is to be divided in just proportion to all creditors, including the Santo Domingo Improvement company of New York. It is also suggested that the American government take charge of the custom houses at Sanchez and Samana under the arbitral award in the Santo Domingo Improvement company case. It is understood that the Improvement company, claiming prior rights, demands that 55 per cent of the moneys collected at the northern ports be also deposited in an American bank to await the final disposition of the convention; it is doubtful if such a proposition will be accepted. Thus far nothing has been decided.
records.summary_es: El Herald publica una nota sobre la situación fiscal dominicana: los acreedores extranjeros, principalmente Italia y Bélgica, están aprovechando el aplazamiento del convenio propuesto entre los Estados Unidos y Santo Domingo, y de la situación de Venezuela, para demandar el pago de sus reclamaciones. Para atender la situación se ha propuesto por el gobierno dominicano que se designe a un estadounidense como comisionado para el cobro de todas las aduanas en los puertos del sur, el 45 por ciento de cuyo cobro se apartará para los gastos del gobierno, y que el 65 por ciento, menos los gastos de cobro, se deposite en un banco estadounidense hasta que el convenio Sánchez-Dillingham sea ratificado o derogado; si el convenio fuera finalmente rechazado, el dinero ha de dividirse en proporción justa entre todos los acreedores, incluyendo la Santo Domingo Improvement Company de Nueva York. También se sugiere que el gobierno estadounidense se haga cargo de las aduanas de Sánchez y Samaná bajo el laudo arbitral en el caso de la Santo Domingo Improvement Company. Se entiende que la Improvement Company, reclamando derechos anteriores, demanda que el 55 por ciento de los dineros cobrados en los puertos del norte también se deposite en un banco estadounidense para esperar la disposición final del convenio; es dudoso que tal proposición sea aceptada. Hasta ahora nada se ha decidido.

records.summary_en: The *Washington Times* reported on the private negotiations conducted by Mr. Reader, whose wife had sought to act as Dominican fiscal agent to negotiate the sale of Samana Bay and settle foreign debts. Although President Morales initially favored the private proposals, United States Minister Dawson instructed Dominican authorities on January 9 to terminate talks with Reader and deal exclusively with Washington. Following the arrival of Commander Dillingham on an American gunboat, official state negotiations commenced, prompting Reader to abandon his mission and return to New York.
records.summary_es: El *Washington Times* informó sobre las negociaciones privadas llevadas a cabo por el señor Reader, cuya esposa había intentado actuar como agente fiscal dominicana para negociar la venta de la bahía de Samaná y saldar las deudas exteriores. Aunque el presidente Morales favoreció en un principio las propuestas privadas, el ministro estadounidense Dawson instruyó a las autoridades dominicanas el 9 de enero para que cesaran las conversaciones con Reader y trataran exclusivamente con Washington. Tras la llegada del comandante Dillingham en un cañonero estadounidense, comenzaron las negociaciones oficiales entre estados, lo que motivó a Reader a abandonar su misión y regresar a Nueva York.

records.summary_en: The News and Observer prints, for the Dominican southern ports, the terms proposed: 45 per cent of the customs collections are to be set apart for the expenses of the government and 45 per cent, less expenses of collection, deposited in an American bank until the Sanchez-Dillingham convention is either ratified or rejected; should the convention be ultimately rejected, the money is to be divided in just proportion to all creditors, including the Santo Domingo Improvement Company of New York. It is also suggested that the American government take charge of the custom houses at Sanchez and Samana under the arbitral award in the Santo Domingo Improvement Company case. It is understood that the Improvement company, claiming prior rights, demands that 55 per cent of the moneys collected at the northern ports be also deposited in an American bank to await the final disposition of the convention; it is doubtful if any such proposition will be accepted. Thus far nothing has been decided; the government is desirous of an agreement being reached, in order to prevent difficulties with European creditors which might lead to intervention.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Times-Republican* published President Roosevelt's directive instructing Minister Dawson to implement an interim modus vivendi for collecting Dominican customs revenues while the treaty awaited Senate approval. Under the executive plan, the Secretary of War would nominate port collectors, with unexpended revenues deposited in New York banks pending final legislative action. Concurrently, American warships monitored political movements in Monte Cristi, including the departure of General Barba from Puerto Rico, to prevent revolutionary disruption.

records.headline: The Courier prints a Washington item on the movement against President Morales
records.summary_en: The Courier prints a Washington item on the movement against President Morales: the affair is not giving the officials here any uneasiness, as they feel free in President Roosevelt's acceptance of the Santo Domingo proposal to control its financial situation. It is understood that General Barba and those who are with him have been in the island of Porto Rico; their movements were known to the State Department, and when they left that place several days ago their departure was promptly reported to Washington. The district of Monte Cristi is to be the hotbed of the revolutionists in Santo Domingo, and it was believed Barba and his associates would head for that section; their reported arrival there consequently caused no great surprise to the Washington officials. The Navy Department has several vessels in Dominican waters and, under directions from the State Department, if requested to do so by President Morales, will lend its cooperation in preserving the peace of the country, so that its finances may be restored to a settled condition. Under the head 'Appoints Collector', the paper adds a Baltimore item of March 29: J. records.headline: The Gazette prints an item under the head 'All Creditors Have Not Agreed': Mr. Dawson's cablegram
records.summary_en: The Gazette prints an item under the head 'All Creditors Have Not Agreed': Mr. Dawson's cablegram seemed to indicate to the mind of the officials here that the proposed arrangement for the collection of customs revenues by a foreign fiscal agent may apply only to the ports not covered by the arbitral award in the case of the San Domingo Improvement company, namely, Puerto Plata, Monte Cristi, Sanchez and Samana. The minister's report was to the effect that two foreign creditor governments have not yet formally signified their willingness to enter into this agreement, though their agents and chargés have done so. The San Domingo Improvement company's representatives have declined to express an opinion as to the practicability of the agreement, though this may be because they do not feel that the company's interests are involved, their ports being excepted. It was said at the close of the day that the point now at issue was whether or not the president may legally designate a fiscal agent to collect these island revenues, and the decision on that point is expected within a day or two.
records.summary_es: El Gazette publica una nota bajo el título «All Creditors Have Not Agreed»: el cablegrama del Sr. Dawson parecía indicar a la mente de los oficiales aquí que el arreglo propuesto para el cobro de los ingresos aduaneros por un agente fiscal extranjero puede aplicar solo a los puertos no cubiertos por el laudo arbitral en el caso de la Santo Domingo Improvement Company, a saber, Puerto Plata, Monte Cristi, Sánchez y Samaná. El informe del ministro era en el sentido de que dos gobiernos acreedores extranjeros aún no han significado formalmente su disposición de entrar en este acuerdo, aunque sus agentes y encargados lo han hecho. Los representantes de la Santo Domingo Improvement Company han declinado expresar una opinión en cuanto a la practicabilidad del acuerdo, aunque esto puede ser porque no sienten que los intereses de la compañía estén envueltos, estando exceptuados sus puertos. Se dijo al cierre del día que el punto ahora en cuestión era si el presidente puede o no legalmente designar a un agente fiscal para cobrar estos ingresos de la isla, y la decisión sobre ese punto se espera dentro de un día o dos.

records.headline: It is said that the next step in the execution of the department’s plans
records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* reported that the implementation of the Dominican customs receivership awaited President Morales concluding agreements with European creditor nations. The Secretary of War prepared to nominate customs collectors, with President Roosevelt recommending William E. Gould of Baltimore, a linguist and financial editor, for a collectorship. It was also anticipated that George R. Colton, formerly an American revenue collector in the Philippines, would be appointed to assist in administering the Dominican customs service.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield Weekly Republican* informó que la implementación de la administración de aduanas dominicanas dependía de que el presidente Morales concluyera acuerdos con las naciones acreedoras europeas. El secretario de Guerra se preparaba para nombrar a los recaudadores de aduanas, habiendo recomendado el presidente Roosevelt a William E. Gould, de Baltimore, lingüista y editor financiero, para una recaudaduría. Asimismo, se preveía la designación de George R. Colton, antiguo recaudador de rentas estadounidense en Filipinas, para colaborar en la administración del servicio de aduanas dominicano.

When the president has secured the necessary signatures to his agreement, and has so informed Washington, the secretary of war will nominate to President Morales the person who is to act as chief collector, and perhaps the subcollectors at the minor ports, though it is possible the designation of these will be left to the chief collector. William E. Gould to be Collector. The president has decided to recommend the selection of William E. Gould of Baltimore as one of the collectors of customs at San Domingo. It has not yet been determined whether Mr Gould shall have general charge of the collections at all ports or whether other persons will be appointed. The details are still under consideration. It is stated that in addition to Mr Gould it is quite likely that G. R. Colton, formerly collector of internal revenue at Iloilo, Philippine islands, will be named as one of the collectors. The cruiser Yankee, which had been at Monte Cristi for some weeks with 350 marines on board, had gone to Sanchez, and it was thought the revolutionists grew bold after its departure; Commander Leiper, the American fiscal agent in charge of the custom house at Monte Cristi, had made no report.

records.headline: The Globe reviews a San Domingo comic opera: the piece presents
records.summary_en: The Globe reviews a San Domingo comic opera: the piece presents the blustering governor of Puerto Plata, Joseph P. Ratliff as a sufficiently martial Capt. Leopoldo of the Dominican army, and J. E. Hazzard, who exhibits a funny Teutonic dialect as the governor's secretary. The ensembles, comprising assemblages of Spanish students, mosquito girls, señoritas, Spanish dancers and soldiers, present constantly changing pictures glowing with light, life and color. Among the musical numbers are the military duet between Capt. Leopoldo and Papinta, 'I'd Like to Be a Soldier', 'The Mosquito and the Midge', 'My San Domingo Maid', 'We Come of Castilian Blood', and 'In Days of Old', by Abijah Booze and chorus, the catchiest composition in the opera.

records.headline: The Republican prints a Washington item: an outline of Col. Colton's plan of organization
records.summary_en: The Republican prints a Washington item: an outline of Col. Colton's plan of organization, which has been agreed to by the Dominican government, was received at Washington Saturday from Col. Colton, chief customs collector in San Domingo. The plan organizes the customs service of the Dominican republic. Col. Colton will be in control; J. H. Edwards, Jr., deputy collector, traveling inspector and auditor; H. W. Smith, cashier, auditor and deputy collector; H. F. Worley, additional deputy collector in charge of the Haytien frontier; M. D. Carroll, chief statistician, and J. Schwartz, special agent. All the present Dominican collectors of customs are to be deputies under personal bonds and will receive extra compensation. The plan provides that, beginning April 1, 45 per cent of the customs receipts are to be paid to the Dominican government; the remainder, after the expenses of administering the customs have been subtracted, is to be deposited in a general fund.

Todos los actuales recaudadores de aduanas dominicanos han de ser adjuntos bajo fianzas personales y recibirán compensación extra. El plan provee que, comenzando el 1 de abril, el 45 por ciento de los ingresos aduaneros ha de pagarse al gobierno dominicano; el resto, después de restados los gastos de administrar las aduanas, ha de depositarse en un fondo general.

Herbert Wright, of Des Moines, was originally appointed to Puerto Plata, but never qualified; he will be given another post, subject to examination. The announcement of Wright's selection recently precipitated a storm of protest to the department from the Rev. Frank W. Lomack, a minister of Des Moines, who forwarded to the department headquarters a series of legal documents showing that he had prosecuted Wright because of alleged intimacy between Wright and Mrs. Lomack. Wright is a lawyer.

records.headline: The Astorian prints an item of July 27: an unwritten chapter
records.summary_en: The Astorian prints an item of July 27: an unwritten chapter in last year's insurrection in Santo Domingo is revealed in a circular issued yesterday by Collector Stranahan, announcing that the government will sell by public auction 30,000 cartridges confiscated by agents of the Treasury Department. It seems that early last October 30 cases of merchandise marked 'axes' were left at the Clyde Line pier for shipment to the Dominican republic. The only other marks appearing on the cases were 'U A P., 15,' and 'U U, 15.' What first aroused the suspicions of the steamship agents is not divulged, but it is said that the Clyde Line officials notified Mr. Stranahan of the war material in the cases. An investigation followed, with the result that the cartridges were seized for violation of the neutrality laws.

records.headline: The Times prints the findings of a naval court of inquiry into the death of R. Cohen
records.summary_en: The Times prints the findings of a naval court of inquiry into the death of R. Cohen, whose death is thought to have been caused by a blow received when he was knocked against a post by Johnson. The findings are as follows: '1. That an athletic entertainment was given on board the U.S.S. Yankee, at Monte Cristi, Dominican Republic, on the evening of July 8, 1905, in accordance with Article 83 of the Fleet Regulations for the North Atlantic fleet, dated June 15, 1905, and Article 3982, paragraph 2, U.S. Navy Regulations, 1905. This entertainment was attended by a large number of officers and enlisted men from the various ships of the squadron in port. 2. That a feature of said entertainment was a boxing contest between J. R. Johnson, seaman, U.S. Navy, and R. Cohen, coal passer, U.S. Navy, for a prize of fifty dollars, which was subscribed by the officers of the U.S.S. Yankee.'

records.headline: The Times prints Porto Rico advices of revolutionary movements
records.summary_en: The Times prints Porto Rico advices of revolutionary movements in Santo Domingo: it is rumored that Panchito Detchen, a prominent Dominican, who has resided for the last few months in a secluded part of the suburbs of San Juan in order to escape undue attention, has gone north for the purpose of raising a loan; the money, if obtained, is for the purchase of arms and ammunition. General Demetrio Rodriguez, governor of the Monte Cristi district, has been joined by General Cespedes and his brothers. General Cespedes was one of the principal factors in placing General Morales in the presidential chair of Santo Domingo. Cespedes has, however, quarreled with Morales on account of the latter's transactions with the Americans, and has hastened to join forces with those of the enemies of the Dominican government and American intervention in Santo Domingo.

records.headline: A travel narrative follows the old Camino Real, the royal road running 150 miles north from Santo Domingo City to Cotui
records.summary_en: A travel narrative follows the old Camino Real, the royal road running 150 miles north from Santo Domingo City to Cotui, La Vega and Moca, describing the ancient Spanish roads as broad paths cut a hundred feet wide through the forest, with no ditching, drainage, macadam or bridges, and the Isabella River crossed in native dugout canoes while the horses swim. It describes the savanna country of red clay loam and an inland town, Savanna Grande, as a row of one-story palm-wood huts thatched with palm leaves around a green central square, and the travelers' night stop at the home of Don Emiliano Tejera, a wealthy power in Dominican politics housed in thatched native houses with dirt floors.
records.summary_es: Una crónica de viaje sigue el viejo Camino Real, la vía real que corre 150 millas al norte desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo hasta Cotuí, La Vega y Moca, describiendo los antiguos caminos españoles como senderos anchos abiertos de cien pies a través del bosque, sin zanjas, drenaje, macadán ni puentes, y el río Isabela cruzado en canoas nativas de un solo tronco mientras los caballos nadan. Describe la región de sabana de arcilla roja y un pueblo del interior, Sabana Grande, como una fila de chozas de un piso de madera de palma techadas con hojas de palma alrededor de una plaza central verde, y la parada nocturna de los viajeros en la casa de don Emiliano Tejera, un hombre rico y poderoso en la política dominicana alojado en casas nativas de techo de palma y piso de tierra.

records.summary_en: A travel narrative through the interior describes riding into La Vega, in the Vega Real, the royal meadow of Columbus, and looking over a fertile valley stretching between blue mountains. It praises the valley's inexhaustibly fertile soil, its mighty forests of valuable trees, and its cacao, which it calls the best in the world and says has made the island fourth in the world's production.

records.headline: A feature calls Santo Domingo the garden of the western tropics, with soil for cocoa, tobacco, tropical fruits
records.summary_en: A feature calls Santo Domingo the garden of the western tropics, with soil for cocoa, tobacco, tropical fruits, sugar cane, coffee, vanilla and rubber, mahogany forests in its mountainous interior, and constant verdure, and says that freed from its financial incubus it need not lag behind its sister republics. It then traces the career of President Carlos F. Morales, born at Puerto Plata to a prosperous merchant's family, ordained a priest after seminary study, who renounced the priesthood after eight years, edited an opposition newspaper, was arrested and narrowly escaped being shot, lived through revolt and exile, served in Congress and as governor of Puerto Plata, and last year headed the movement that drove out Jiminez and Wos y Gil and assumed control, proclaiming an election for next June.
records.summary_es: Un reportaje llama a Santo Domingo el jardín de los trópicos occidentales, con suelo para cacao, tabaco, frutas tropicales, caña de azúcar, café, vainilla y caucho, bosques de caoba en su interior montañoso y verdor constante, y dice que libre de su peso financiero no tiene por qué quedarse atrás de sus repúblicas hermanas. Después recorre la carrera del presidente Carlos F. Morales, nacido en Puerto Plata en la familia de un comerciante próspero, ordenado sacerdote tras estudiar en un seminario, quien renunció al sacerdocio después de ocho años, editó un periódico de oposición, fue arrestado y escapó por poco de ser fusilado, vivió entre revueltas y exilios, sirvió en el Congreso y como gobernador de Puerto Plata, y el año pasado encabezó el movimiento que expulsó a Jiminez y a Wos y Gil y asumió el control, proclamando una elección para el próximo junio.

records.headline: The Tribune prints a Portsmouth dispatch of September 15, under the head
records.summary_en: The Tribune prints a Portsmouth dispatch of September 15, under the head 'Galveston Makes Record Run': the cruiser Galveston arrived in Hampton Roads today, ninety hours from Santo Domingo. The cruiser made the run of 1,330 miles in record time, averaging 14 knots an hour on the run. This is considered the best time made yet by a vessel of this class. Professor J. H. Hollander, representative of this government, who went to Santo Domingo to investigate the financial affairs of the Dominican republic, returned aboard the Galveston and will file his report in Washington at once.

El crucero hizo la travesía de 1,330 millas en tiempo récord, promediando 14 nudos por hora en la travesía. Esto se considera el mejor tiempo hecho hasta ahora por un buque de esta clase. El profesor J. H. Hollander, representante de este gobierno, que fue a Santo Domingo a investigar los asuntos financieros de la república dominicana, regresó a bordo del Galveston y presentará su informe en Washington enseguida.

records.headline: The Republican prints an item on Professor Hollander, the adviser of President Roosevelt
records.summary_en: The Republican prints an item on Professor Hollander, the adviser of President Roosevelt in dealing with the fiscal affairs of the island: he is now preparing his report for Congress. He said Saturday: 'I found the island quiet and undisturbed. The finances of the island are in good shape, and I believe San Domingo is entering upon a new era of prosperity.' Prof. Hollander has collected a vast amount of data, by direction of the president, respecting the character of the foreign indebtedness of San Domingo, and has been particularly diligent in looking into the merits of certain claims, some held by American citizens, preferred against the Dominican republic, which, it is alleged, have been very much inflated. This data is regarded as necessary for the guidance of the United States Senate. He also made an investigation into the financial conditions of some of the West Indian islands adjacent to San Domingo, with the purpose of getting suggestions for the improvement of the present customs service in the island.
records.summary_es: El Republican publica una nota sobre el profesor Hollander, el asesor del presidente Roosevelt en el manejo de los asuntos fiscales de la isla: ahora está preparando su informe para el Congreso. Dijo el sábado: «Encontré la isla tranquila y sin disturbios. Las finanzas de la isla están en buena forma, y creo que Santo Domingo está entrando en una nueva era de prosperidad». Prof. Hollander ha reunido una vasta cantidad de datos, por dirección del presidente, respecto al carácter de la deuda extranjera de Santo Domingo, y ha sido particularmente diligente en investigar los méritos de ciertas reclamaciones, algunas en poder de ciudadanos estadounidenses, presentadas contra la república dominicana, que, se alega, han sido muy infladas. Estos datos se consideran necesarios para la guía del Senado de los Estados Unidos. También hizo una investigación sobre las condiciones financieras de algunas de las islas antillanas adyacentes a Santo Domingo, con el propósito de obtener sugerencias para el mejoramiento del servicio de aduanas actual en la isla.

records.headline: The Star prints an item on Mr. Worley's border custom houses
records.summary_en: The Star prints an item on Mr. Worley's border custom houses, which were established in the interior between the two countries: goods were carried over the border by mule trains, and some of the largest mercantile houses in Monte Cristi had their warehouses far inland, where these goods were smuggled across the border. Mr. Worley was sent down there to establish custom houses, and he was warned that if he attempted to carry out his instructions he was liable to assassination, so determined are the smugglers to continue their traffic. But custom houses have been established, and others will be established until it will be impossible to continue the smuggling. Much of the border consists of an impassable mountain range with an occasional pass, but there are other regions where the smuggling is rendered easy unless official barriers are erected. There is no doubt that, acting upon the report of Mr. Worley, the department will send enough men to Santo Domingo to protect the revenues of the government. The tariff in Santo Domingo, according to estimates made by Mr. Worley, is so high ad valorem as to be a great inducement to smugglers.
records.summary_es: El Star publica una nota sobre las aduanas de Worley en la frontera, que fueron establecidas en el interior entre los dos países: las mercancías eran llevadas a través de la frontera en trenes de mulas, y algunas de las casas mercantiles más grandes de Monte Cristi tenían sus almacenes muy tierra adentro, donde estas mercancías eran pasadas de contrabando a través de la frontera. El Sr. Worley fue enviado allá para establecer aduanas, y se le advirtió que si intentaba llevar a cabo sus instrucciones estaba expuesto a ser asesinado, tan determinados están los contrabandistas de continuar su tráfico. Pero se han establecido aduanas, y se establecerán otras hasta que sea imposible continuar el contrabando. Gran parte de la frontera consiste en una cordillera impasable con un paso ocasional, pero hay otras regiones donde el contrabando se facilita a menos que se erijan barreras oficiales. No hay duda de que, actuando sobre el informe del Sr. Worley, el departamento enviará suficientes hombres a Santo Domingo para proteger los ingresos del gobierno. La tarifa en Santo Domingo, según estimados hechos por el Sr. Worley, es tan alta ad valorem como para ser un gran aliciente para los contrabandistas.

records.headline: The Sun prints an item on the new Dominican minister's presentation
records.summary_en: The Sun prints an item on the new Dominican minister's presentation to President Roosevelt: Señor Joubert made a brief speech when he handed to the President a letter from President Morales of Santo Domingo accrediting him to this country as a minister extraordinary and envoy plenipotentiary. He said that by exalting the rank of its diplomatic establishment in this country his government wished to give expression to the intense sympathy which draws it to the American nation, whose friendship Santo Domingo earnestly desires to cultivate. In closing, Señor Joubert said he had been especially charged to convey the best wishes of the President of his country. President Roosevelt responded in the usual manner, thanking Señor Joubert as the representative of Santo Domingo for the action which had been taken and the earnest wishes expressed: 'I desire for my part to assure you of the great interest felt by this Government and people in the welfare of the Dominican Republic and to declare that it is the wish and intention of this Government to maintain firmly and cordially the bonds of friendship which now unite the two countries. It gives me pleasure, Mr. Minister, to congratulate you on your well deserved promotion.'
records.summary_es: El Sun publica una nota sobre la presentación del nuevo ministro dominicano al presidente Roosevelt: el Sr. Joubert hizo un breve discurso cuando entregó al Presidente una carta del presidente Morales de Santo Domingo que lo acreditaba ante este país como ministro extraordinario y enviado plenipotenciario. Dijo que al exaltar el rango de su establecimiento diplomático en este país su gobierno deseaba dar expresión a la intensa simpatía que lo atrae a la nación estadounidense, cuya amistad Santo Domingo desea encarecidamente cultivar. Al cerrar, el Sr. Joubert dijo que se le había encargado especialmente transmitir los mejores deseos del Presidente de su país. El presidente Roosevelt respondió de la manera acostumbrada, agradeciendo al Sr. Joubert como representante de Santo Domingo por la acción tomada y los deseos encarecidos expresados: «Deseo por mi parte asegurarle el gran interés que sienten este Gobierno y pueblo por el bienestar de la República Dominicana y declarar que es el deseo e intención de este Gobierno mantener firme y cordialmente los lazos de amistad que ahora unen a los dos países. Me da placer, Sr. Ministro, felicitarlo por su bien merecida promoción».

records.headline: A Washington dispatch reports that, to thwart a revolutionary movement at Macoris against President Morales of Santo
records.summary_en: A Washington dispatch reports that, to thwart a revolutionary movement at Macoris against President Morales of Santo Domingo, the State Department has asked the Navy Department to send a warship to that port, and instructions were telegraphed to Rear Admiral Bradford at Guantanamo. It describes Bradford as the American policeman delegated to see that Morales's rule is not disturbed while the Senate acts on the proposed protectorate, and says the department believes the disturbance is fomented by New York interests opposed to the Dominican treaty.

Describe a Bradford como el policía estadounidense delegado para velar por que el gobierno de Morales no sea perturbado mientras el Senado decide sobre el protectorado propuesto, y dice que el departamento cree que la alteración es fomentada por intereses de Nueva York opuestos al tratado dominicano.

records.headline: The Star prints a correspondent's letter from Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The Star prints a correspondent's letter from Santo Domingo, under the head 'Discourtesy to American Commanders': commanders of American warships stationed at Monte Cristi or visiting that port on police duty have repeatedly paid official visits of courtesy to the governor of the province, which have not been returned. A short time ago Admiral Bradford, commanding operations in these waters, when at Monte Cristi desired to pay an official visit to the governor; fearing to be treated with the same discourtesy as his captains, he requested the American consul there to notify the governor of his intention and to inquire if the visit would be returned, but the governor categorically refused to return the visit, so the admiral did not call on him. The governor of Puerto Plata and President Morales were immediately notified of the fact, and the former wired the governor of Monte Cristi requesting him to be diplomatic in his relations with the Americans and desired him to receive and return the visit of Admiral Bradford, but the governor of Monte Cristi simply ignored the request and continued to boldly exhibit his hostility to American officials. United States officials have received gross and repeated insults from the Monte Cristi authorities, which have so far been tolerated with stoicism. Anti-American sentiment in Santo Domingo has reached fever heat.
records.summary_es: El Star publica una carta de un corresponsal desde Santo Domingo, bajo el título «Discourtesy to American Commanders»: los comandantes de los buques de guerra estadounidenses estacionados en Monte Cristi o que visitan ese puerto en servicio de policía han pagado repetidamente visitas oficiales de cortesía al gobernador de la provincia, que no han sido correspondidas. Hace poco, el almirante Bradford, que manda las operaciones en estas aguas, deseó, estando en Monte Cristi, pagar una visita oficial al gobernador; temiendo ser tratado con la misma descortesía que sus capitanes, pidió al cónsul estadounidense allí que notificara al gobernador su intención y preguntara si la visita sería correspondida, pero el gobernador se negó categóricamente a corresponderla, por lo que el almirante no lo visitó. El gobernador de Puerto Plata y el presidente Morales fueron informados de inmediato del hecho, y el primero telegrafió al gobernador de Monte Cristi pidiéndole que fuera diplomático en sus relaciones con los estadounidenses y deseando que recibiera y correspondiera la visita del almirante Bradford, pero el gobernador de Monte Cristi simplemente ignoró la petición y continuó exhibiendo audazmente su hostilidad hacia los funcionarios estadounidenses. Los funcionarios de Estados Unidos han recibido insultos groseros y repetidos de las autoridades de Monte Cristi, que hasta ahora han sido tolerados con estoicismo. El sentimiento antiestadounidense en Santo Domingo ha llegado a un punto febril.

records.headline: The Star prints a further portion of the correspondent's letter
records.summary_en: The Star prints a further portion of the correspondent's letter: most of the information sent from Santo Domingo to the United States, unless sent by competent American officials, is misleading in the extreme, and the very statistics furnished are far from being correct; the furnishers of information are either afraid to give correct data, are unable to obtain them, or are incompetent men and do not know their business. Under the head 'Morales' Power Melting Away', the letter says that further information just received tends to show that President Morales' power is melting like snow in the sun; he is now practically a broken reed leaning on Minister Dawson for support, and were it not for this American official not only would Morales be no longer president, but it is more than probable that he would be at this moment a dead man. His few supporters are daily abandoning him, and it is extremely likely that within a very short time he will need more than Minister Dawson's moral support; American military support will probably be needed soon. Ex-President Horacio Vasquez is practically the ruler of four-fifths of the Dominican republic.

Bajo el título «Morales' Power Melting Away», la carta dice que información adicional recién recibida tiende a mostrar que el poder del presidente Morales se está derritiendo como la nieve al sol; ahora es prácticamente una caña quebrada que se apoya en el ministro Dawson para sostenerse, y de no ser por este funcionario estadounidense, Morales no solo ya no sería presidente, sino que es más que probable que en este momento sería un hombre muerto. Sus pocos partidarios lo abandonan a diario, y es sumamente probable que dentro de muy poco tiempo necesite más que el apoyo moral del ministro Dawson; probablemente pronto se necesitará apoyo militar estadounidense. El expresidente Horacio Vásquez es prácticamente el gobernante de las cuatro quintas partes de la República Dominicana.

records.headline: The News prints an account of the flight: the whereabouts of the fugitive president
records.summary_en: The News prints an account of the flight: the whereabouts of the fugitive president is not known; it is generally supposed that he endeavored to gain the coast and embark on board a sloop with the object of reaching Puerto Plata, on the north coast of Santo Domingo, and there join Governor Perez, who has been dismissed by the government from the post of governor of Puerto Plata but refuses to surrender his office. On the other hand, there are those who believe that the president is endeavoring to cross Santo Domingo by land and reach Monte Cristi, on the north coast and west of Puerto Plata, from which port it is not far distant. The account recalls that Señor Juan E. Sanchez, the former foreign minister of Santo Domingo, with the American special commissioners, Commander Albert Dillingham, and former Minister Thomas Dawson, and Frederico Valasquez, minister of finance, signed the agreement between the United States and Santo Domingo providing for the fiscal protectorate of the United States over Santo Domingo. The paper also prints a Washington item: the secretary of war received the following cablegram from Edwards, acting comptroller and receiver of the Dominican customs, dated at San Domingo: 'Carlos F. Morales, dissatisfied with cabinet support, left the capital last night with few followers. His intention is said to be to join the Jimenistas in opposition to the Horacistas. Conflict between the two forces is imminent, probably in the vicinity of San Juan or vicinity of Puerto Plata. Carlos F. Morales may make an attempt to establish a new capital and create a new cabinet. Political excitement but without disturbance here. Receivership is not affected yet. George R. Colton should be Monte Cristi Tuesday.'
records.summary_es: El News publica un relato de la fuga: se desconoce el paradero del presidente fugitivo; se supone en general que trató de ganar la costa y embarcar a bordo de una balandra con el objeto de llegar a Puerto Plata, en la costa norte de Santo Domingo, y unirse allí al gobernador Pérez, que ha sido destituido por el gobierno del cargo de gobernador de Puerto Plata pero se niega a entregar su puesto. Por otra parte, hay quienes creen que el presidente está tratando de cruzar Santo Domingo por tierra y llegar a Monte Cristi, en la costa norte y al oeste de Puerto Plata, puerto del que no dista mucho. El relato recuerda que el señor Juan E. Sánchez, exministro de Relaciones Exteriores de Santo Domingo, con los comisionados especiales estadounidenses, el comandante Albert Dillingham, y el exministro Thomas Dawson, y Frederico Valasquez, ministro de Hacienda, firmó el acuerdo entre Estados Unidos y Santo Domingo que provee el protectorado fiscal de Estados Unidos sobre Santo Domingo. El periódico publica también una nota de Washington: el secretario de Guerra recibió el siguiente cablegrama de Edwards, contralor interino y receptor de las aduanas dominicanas, fechado en Santo Domingo: «Carlos F. Colton debe estar en Monte Cristi el martes».

records.headline: The Leader prints advices from Santo Domingo: following the announcement
records.summary_en: The Leader prints advices from Santo Domingo: following the announcement today that the president of the republic, General Carlos Morales, had left the capital for an unknown destination, troops were sent in pursuit of the chief magistrate. Later a fight occurred ten miles from the capital. Under the head 'Serious Condition of Affairs', the paper prints a Washington item of December 26: advices from Santo Domingo indicate a serious condition of affairs there; the captain of the port of Puerto Plata has been shot and killed during the insurrectionary movement; the governor of that province has defied the general government and barricaded the town; the Dominican government has issued a decree removing the governor; the State Department will not intervene at this stage.

The account recalls that Señor Juan E. Sanchez, the former foreign minister of Santo Domingo, with the American special commissioners, Commander Albert C. Dillingham and former Minister Thomas C. Dawson, and Frederico Velasquez, minister of finance, on January 20 last signed the agreement between the United States and Santo Domingo providing for the fiscal protectorate of the United States over Santo Domingo. Under the head 'The Official News', the paper prints the cablegram received by the secretary of war from the acting comptroller and receiver of the Dominican customs, dated at Santo Domingo: 'Charles F. Morales, disappointed with cabinet support, left the capital last night with few followers. His intention is said to be to join Jimenistas in opposition to Horacistas. A conflict between the two forces is imminent, probably in the vicinity of San Juan.'
records.summary_es: El Democrat publica un relato de la fuga: se desconoce el paradero del presidente fugitivo; se supone en general que trató de ganar la costa y embarcar a bordo de una balandra con el objeto de llegar a Puerto Plata, en la costa norte de Santo Domingo, y unirse allí al gobernador Pérez, que ha sido destituido por el gobierno del cargo de gobernador de Puerto Plata pero se niega a entregar su puesto. Por otra parte, hay quienes creen que el presidente está tratando de cruzar Santo Domingo por tierra y llegar a Monte Cristi, en la costa norte y al oeste de Puerto Plata, puerto del que no dista mucho. El relato recuerda que el señor Juan E. Sánchez, exministro de Relaciones Exteriores de Santo Domingo, con los comisionados especiales estadounidenses, el comandante Albert C. Dillingham y el exministro Thomas C. Dawson, y Frederico Velasquez, ministro de Hacienda, firmó el 20 de enero pasado el acuerdo entre Estados Unidos y Santo Domingo que provee el protectorado fiscal de Estados Unidos sobre Santo Domingo. Bajo el título «The Official News», el periódico publica el cablegrama recibido por el secretario de Guerra del contralor interino y receptor de las aduanas dominicanas, fechado en Santo Domingo: «Charles F. Morales, decepcionado con el apoyo del gabinete, salió de la capital anoche con unos pocos seguidores. Se dice que su intención es unirse a los jimenistas en oposición a los horacistas. Un conflicto entre las dos fuerzas es inminente, probablemente en las cercanías de San Juan».

records.headline: The Call prints a dispatch from Santo Domingo: Perico Lasala
records.summary_en: The Call prints a dispatch from Santo Domingo: Perico Lasala has marched on La Vega with a force of about 100 men; General Deschamps, former vice president of Santo Domingo, will leave here shortly on board a sailing vessel to operate against Puerto Plata; it is rumored that President Morales is a prisoner in irons at the capital, San Domingo. Under the head 'America Holds Aloof', the paper prints a Washington dispatch of December 26: for the present there will not be any interference by the United States in the difficulty which has arisen in Santo Domingo; the trouble is regarded by the State Department officials as entirely an internal one, and so long as outside interests are not menaced this attitude of non-intervention will be maintained; if, however, conditions should change materially and lawless acts should be committed against Americans and American interests or involve the collection of the Dominican customs by this Government, or other violence occur which in the opinion of the officials here would make it proper for this Government to interfere, this step will be taken and measures will be adopted to quell the trouble. This decision was reached by the State Department officials during the day and was confirmed at a conference at the White House late this afternoon, in which the President and Secretaries Taft, Root and Bonaparte participated.

Morales, dissatisfied with cabinet support, left the capital last night with a few followers. His intention is said to be to join Jimenistas in opposition to Horacistas. Morales may make an attempt to establish a new capital and to create a new Cabinet. Political excitement but without disturbance here. Receivership is not affected yet. George R. Colton should be Monte Cristi Tuesday.'

records.summary_en: The *Birmingham Age-Herald* criticized President Roosevelt for enforcing the unratified Dominican customs treaty through executive action, using warships to protect Customs Receiver George R. Colton. The editorial argued that neither Roosevelt nor President Morales held constitutional authority to bind their nations without legislative approval, and warned the policy risked committing the United States to guaranteeing debts throughout Spanish America. The article predicted that Senate Democrats would firmly oppose ratification, noting rumors that the administration might seek a congressional joint resolution to validate the receivership.
records.summary_es: El *Birmingham Age-Herald* criticó al presidente Roosevelt por aplicar el tratado aduanero dominicano no ratificado mediante una acción ejecutiva, empleando buques de guerra para proteger al receptor de aduanas George R. Colton. El editorial sostenía que ni Roosevelt ni el presidente Morales tenían autoridad constitucional para comprometer a sus naciones sin aprobación legislativa, y advertía del riesgo de que esta política comprometiera a los Estados Unidos a garantizar deudas en toda Hispanoamérica. El artículo vaticinaba que los demócratas en el Senado se opondrían con firmeza a la ratificación, señalando rumores de que el gobierno intentaría obtener una resolución conjunta del Congreso para validar la administración aduanera.

The treaty has never been ratified by the Senate, and It Is repudiated by the people of Santo Domingo. It Is still hung up, but President Roosevelt has proceeded without right or precedent to enforce It. George B. The revolution, or rather revolutions, In Santo Domingo, have not affected Receiver Colton, because the guns of our ships are pointed shoreward, and the administration proposes, it appears, to let the revolutions in Santo Domingo proceed unchecked while Colton stands unharmed. records.summary_en: The *Free Lance* reported on the repressive governance of Dominican President Morales, stating he had executed approximately 200 political opponents and maintained a coded blacklist of prominent citizens. Meanwhile, the State Department in Washington announced a policy of non-intervention in internal Dominican strife, regarding the conflict as domestic as long as foreign interests remained safe. Officials cautioned, however, that the United States would intervene militarily if violence threatened American lives or interfered with customs collections.
records.summary_es: El *Free Lance* informó sobre la gobernanza represiva del presidente dominicano Morales, afirmando que había ejecutado a cerca de 200 opositores políticos y mantenía una lista negra cifrada de ciudadanos prominentes. Entretanto, el Departamento de Estado en Washington anunció una política de no intervención en las disputas internas dominicanas, considerando el conflicto como doméstico mientras los intereses extranjeros estuvieran a salvo. No obstante, los funcionarios advirtieron que los Estados Unidos intervendrían militarmente si la violencia amenazaba vidas estadounidenses o interfería con la recaudación de aduanas.

records.summary_en: Dispatches in the Ottumwa Tri-Weekly Courier report that government troops pursued Dominican President Morales after he fled the capital for an unknown destination, clashing about ten miles away with rebel commander General Plmental. The fugitive executive is believed to be seeking to reach the north coast by sloop to join Governor Perez, who was dismissed as governor of Puerto Plata but refused to surrender his office and barricaded the town. A Washington dispatch dated December 26 adds that cable advices report the port captain of Puerto Plata has been killed during the uprising, though the State Department regards the conflict as internal and will not intervene at this stage.

Se cree que el mandatario fugitivo busca llegar a la costa norte en una balandra para unirse al gobernador Pérez, quien fue destituido como gobernador de Puerto Plata pero se negó a entregar su cargo y atrincheró la ciudad. Un despacho de Washington fechado el 26 de diciembre añade que avisos por cable comunican que el capitán del puerto de Puerto Plata murió durante el levantamiento, aunque el Departamento de Estado considera el conflicto como interno y no intervendrá en esta etapa.

records.headline: A Washington dispatch in The San Francisco Call reports that Dominican Minister Joubert conferred
records.summary_en: A Washington dispatch in The San Francisco Call reports that Dominican Minister Joubert conferred with Secretary Root at the State Department following a cable from Foreign Minister Tejera. The message announced that Vice President General Caceres, who was at Puerto Plata when Morales fled the capital, is expected in Santo Domingo City to assume the presidential office. Joubert stated he had no information indicating Morales had been wounded and discounted reports of serious fighting near Jaima on Tuesday, adding that the customs modus vivendi should remain undisturbed because the dominant cabinet party remains strongly committed to the arrangement.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Washington en The San Francisco Call informa que el ministro dominicano Joubert conferenció con el secretario Root en el Departamento de Estado tras recibir un cable del ministro de Relaciones Exteriores Tejera. El mensaje anunció que el vicepresidente general Cáceres, quien se encontraba en Puerto Plata cuando Morales huyó de la capital, es esperado en la ciudad de Santo Domingo para asumir la presidencia. Joubert afirmó que no tenía datos que indicaran que Morales hubiera sido herido y desestimó los informes sobre combates graves cerca de Jaima el martes, añadiendo que el modus vivendi aduanero no debería verse afectado dado que el partido dominante del gabinete sigue firmemente comprometido con el acuerdo.

records.summary_en: The Iowa State Bystander reports the departure of General Deschamps, former vice president of Santo Domingo, on a sailing vessel to operate against Puerto Plata, amid local rumors that President Morales is held prisoner in irons at the capital. Troops were sent in pursuit of the chief executive, General Charles F. Morales, after he fled for an unknown destination, with a clash occurring about ten miles away against rebel commander General Plmentel. The fugitive president is believed to be attempting to reach the north coast by sloop to join Governor Perez, who was dismissed as governor of Puerto Plata but refuses to surrender his command.

Se enviaron tropas en persecución del mandatario, general Charles F. Morales, tras su huida hacia un destino desconocido, registrándose un combate a unas diez millas de distancia contra el comandante rebelde general Plmentel (según se imprime). Se cree que el presidente fugitivo intenta llegar a la costa norte en balandra para unirse al gobernador Pérez, quien fue destituido como gobernador de Puerto Plata pero se niega a entregar su mando.

records.summary_en: A dispatch in the Vilas County News reports that Carlos F. Morales may attempt to establish a new capital and cabinet following anticipated clashes near San Juan or Puerto Plata, though local political excitement remains peaceful and the customs receivership unaffected, with George R. Colton expected at Monte Cristi on Tuesday. A following Washington dispatch of December 27 states that the United States will not intervene at present, viewing the conflict as internal so long as foreign interests are not threatened. However, should lawless acts endanger Americans or the collection of Dominican customs, the United States will intervene to quell the disturbance, a determination affirmed at a White House conference attended by President Roosevelt and Secretaries Root, Taft, and Bonaparte.

Un despacho de Washington del 27 de diciembre añade que los Estados Unidos no intervendrán en el presente, considerando el conflicto como interno mientras los intereses extranjeros no se vean amenazados. records.headline: General Prez, governor of Puerto Plata, has surrendered to revolutionists
records.summary_en: General Prez, governor of Puerto Plata, has surrendered to revolutionists in Monte Cristi, a Turks Island dispatch dated December 31 in The Birmingham Age-Herald reports, citing mail advices from Monte Cristi. The dispatches add that the Dominican cruiser Independence, laden with ammunition, was turned over to General Deschamps, who sailed for Puerto Plata alongside Generals Demetrio and Rodriguez with 23Q men on board. In addition, General Barber is reported stationed with 200 men at Altamira, a village fifteen miles from Puerto Plata.

Los despachos añaden que el crucero dominicano Independence, cargado de municiones, fue entregado al general Deschamps, quien zarpó hacia Puerto Plata junto a los generales Demetrio y Rodríguez con 23Q hombres (según se imprime) a bordo. Además, se informa que el general Barber está apostado con 200 hombres en Altamira, una aldea situada a quince millas de Puerto Plata.

records.headline: A report in the Aberdeen Herald outlines an official determination
records.summary_en: A report in the Aberdeen Herald outlines an official determination by State Department and cabinet officials at the White House to intervene in Santo Domingo if circumstances require, though the meeting was called primarily before President Roosevelt departed for Virginia. The Secretary of War received a cablegram from Santo Domingo sent by Acting Comptroller and Receiver of Customs Edwards, reporting that Carlos F. Morales abandoned the capital with a few followers after losing cabinet support, allegedly intending to join the followers of Jimminez against the followers of Horacio. Edwards warns that conflicts are imminent near San Juan or Puerto Plata and that Morales may attempt to establish a new government, though order prevails locally and Receiver of Customs George R. Colton is scheduled to arrive at Monte Cristi on Tuesday.
records.summary_es: Un informe en el Aberdeen Herald describe la determinación oficial de las autoridades del Departamento de Estado y del gabinete en la Casa Blanca de intervenir en Santo Domingo si las circunstancias lo exigen, aunque la reunión se convocó principalmente antes de la partida del presidente Roosevelt a Virginia. El secretario de Guerra recibió un cablegrama desde Santo Domingo enviado por el interventor interino y receptor de aduanas Edwards, informando que Carlos F. Morales abandonó la capital con unos pocos seguidores tras perder el apoyo del gabinete, supuestamente con la intención de unirse a los partidarios de Jimminez contra los partidarios de Horacio. Edwards advierte que los enfrentamientos son inminentes cerca de San Juan o Puerto Plata y que Morales podría intentar constituir un nuevo gobierno, aunque prevalece el orden a nivel local y está prevista la llegada del receptor de aduanas George R. Colton a Monte Cristi el martes.

records.summary_en: The Dominican gunboat Independencia at Puerto Plata was warned that bombardment of the town would not be permitted, a Washington dispatch in The Paducah Sun reports; the warning came from the American naval vessels Nashville and Scorpion, under Commander Sutherland, and any fighting was to take place beyond city limits. The dispatch notes that the 322-ton Dominican vessel is heavily outmatched by the 1370-ton Nashville and 850-ton Scorpion, citing Navy Department precedents established at Monte Cristi by Admiral Sigsbee and a commander printed as Dllllngfinm. In Washington, the action is regarded as the exercise of a protectorate to safeguard American customs collections regardless of whether Morales, Caceres, or another leader heads the Dominican government.

El despacho señala que la nave dominicana de 322 toneladas está ampliamente superada por el Nashville de 1370 toneladas y el Scorpion de 850 toneladas, citando precedentes del Departamento de la Marina sentados en Monte Cristi por el almirante Sigsbee y un comandante impreso como Dllllngfinm. En Washington, la acción es considerada como el ejercicio de un protectorado para salvaguardar la recaudación aduanera estadounidense, sin importar si Morales, Cáceres u otro líder encabeza el gobierno dominicano.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that revolutionary forces under General Guellito united outside Puerto Plata to attack Santiago, where provisional President Ramón Cáceres was concentrating government forces. A cable from Customs Receiver Colonel George R. Colton confirmed that President Morales had fled the capital to join the Monte Cristi insurrection, prompting the Dominican Congress to initiate impeachment proceedings. Colton reported that despite the acute political crisis, the customs receivership continued to operate without interference from any faction.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que las fuerzas revolucionarias bajo el mando del general Güellito se unieron en las afueras de Puerto Plata para atacar Santiago, donde el presidente provisional Ramón Cáceres concentraba las fuerzas gubernamentales. Un cable del receptor de aduanas, coronel George R. Colton, confirmó que el presidente Morales había huido de la capital para sumarse a la insurrección de Monte Cristi, lo que llevó al Congreso dominicano a iniciar un juicio político en su contra. records.summary_en: The Albuquerque Morning Journal reports advices brought by a messenger stating that Dominican revolutionists have encamped along the Santiago-Puerto Plata road and are besieging Puerto Plata, blocking all ingress and egress except for American warships and persons under their protection. Bombardment of the port by the revolutionary gunboat Independencia will not take place, presumably due to representations made by foreign consuls. The messenger also reports that forces under General Guellito, the former governor of Monte Cristi, are cooperating with the insurgents to attack Santiago, where temporary President General Caceres is massing his troops for an anticipated decisive engagement. Meanwhile, reports reaching Cape Haitien state that fugitive President Morales is acting on behalf of General Jiminez, whose attempt to regain the presidency was defeated in 1903.

Furthermore, reports reaching Cape Haitien state that fugitive President Morales is acting in the interest of General Jiminiz, the former president whose attempt to regain the presidency was previously defeated.

An American observer arriving from Monte Cristi, Hugh M. Creighton, asserted that the United States should sustain Morales, arguing the conflict erupted because Morales refused financial demands from Cáceres's political faction. Creighton señaló que el 45 por ciento de los ingresos de aduanas asignado por la administración estadounidense cubría adecuadamente los gastos legítimos del Estado, pero no dejaba fondos para el clientelismo político.

TALE ON SANTO DOMINGO. “Morales Represents Best Element on Island,” Says Observer. Hugh M. Creighton arrived on the steamer [Seminole?], from Monte Cristi, Santo Domingo. Mr. Creighton said:

I was in Santo Domingo three weeks, and was in constant contact with all classes of Dominicans. I became convinced that, unless the government at Washington asserts itself promptly, and with a firm hand sustains President Morales, who is still the constitutional head of the government, the prestige of the United States, with the best element on the island, which is being dissipated by delay, will entirely disappear. The present trouble, as I learned from business men, grows out of the inability of President Morales to respond to the demands made on him by the faction headed by Vice-President Caceres for money. The 4 per cent that is derived from the customs collections, under the supervision of the United States agent, is sufficient for all the legitimate needs of the government, but it affords no margin out of which to pay levies that may be made by political ‘‘grafters.”

records.summary_en: Through representations of foreign consuls, a threatened bombardment of Puerto Plata by the revolutionary gunboat Independencia was averted, Dispatches in The Salt Lake Tribune report, while insurgents besieging the port have joined forces with troops under General Guellito, former governor of Monte Cristi. The combined forces intend to attack Santiago, where temporary President General Caceres is marshalling his troops for an anticipated decisive engagement. Dispatches from Cape Haitien add that fugitive President Morales is operating in the interest of former President Jiminiz, while a Washington dispatch of January 2, citing a December 30 cable from Santo Domingo, reports that Morales is within twenty miles of the capital without troops, facing impending impeachment by Congress and expected capture, with United States customs operations continuing uninterrupted.

records.headline: The Times-Dispatch reports an interview with a Mr. Coulter
records.summary_en: The Times-Dispatch reports an interview with a Mr. Coulter, an American resident in Santo Domingo representing extensive timber interests, who stopped in Richmond en route to confer with President Roosevelt regarding the Dominican revolution. Having taken an active part alongside United States Consul-General Thomas C. Dawson in diplomatic discussions on the island, Coulter stated that prior to his departure an open breach existed between President Morales and his cabinet, leaving Morales in office only on sufferance. Coulter explained that the dominant Horacio or Vasquez faction exercises practical control of affairs, prompting Morales to ally with the opposing Jiminez party in the expectation of obtaining active United States support as the constitutional executive.
records.summary_es: The Times-Dispatch informa sobre una entrevista con el señor Coulter, un residente estadounidense en Santo Domingo representante de amplios intereses madereros, quien se detuvo en Richmond camino a conferenciar con el presidente Roosevelt sobre la revolución dominicana. Habiendo participado activamente junto al cónsul general de los Estados Unidos Thomas C. Dawson en las discusiones diplomáticas en la isla, Coulter declaró que antes de su partida existía una ruptura abierta entre el presidente Morales y su gabinete, lo que mantenía a Morales en el cargo solo por tolerancia. Coulter explicó que la facción dominante de Horacio o Vásquez ejerce el control práctico de la situación, lo que llevó a Morales a aliarse con el partido rival de Jiminez ante la expectativa de obtener el apoyo activo de los Estados Unidos como mandatario constitucional.

records.headline: A news report in The Madison Daily Leader states that Dominican insurgents
records.summary_en: A news report in The Madison Daily Leader states that Dominican insurgents have blockaded Puerto Plata against all entry and exit except for American warships and individuals under foreign consular protection. A threatened bombardment of the port by the revolutionary gunboat Independencia was averted following protests by foreign consuls. A messenger reports that forces commanded by General Guellito, former governor of Monte Cristi, have joined the rebels before Puerto Plata with plans to attack Santiago, where temporary President General Caceres is massing government forces for an expected decisive engagement. Meanwhile, reports reaching Cape Haitien state that fugitive President Morales is operating in the interest of General Jiminez, whose 1903 bid for the presidency was defeated.
records.summary_es: Una noticia en The Madison Daily Leader afirma que insurgentes dominicanos han bloqueado Puerto Plata impidiendo toda entrada y salida salvo para los buques de guerra estadounidenses y las personas bajo protección consular extranjera. El amenazado bombardeo del puerto por la cañonera revolucionaria Independencia fue evitado tras protestas de los cónsules extranjeros. Un mensajero informa que fuerzas comandadas por el general Guellito, exgobernador de Monte Cristi, se han unido a los rebeldes frente a Puerto Plata con planes de atacar Santiago, donde el presidente provisional, general Cáceres, concentra tropas gubernamentales para un enfrentamiento decisivo previsto. Mientras tanto, informes recibidos en Cabo Haitiano indican que el presidente fugitivo Morales actúa en favor del general Jiminez, cuya tentativa de alcanzar la presidencia en 1903 fue derrotada.

The united forces plan to attack Santiago, where temporary President General Caceres is marshalling his troops for an anticipated decisive engagement, while dispatches from Cape Haitien indicate that fugitive President Morales is acting on behalf of former President Jiminiz, whose campaign to regain power was defeated in 1003 as printed. A following Washington dispatch of January 2, citing a December 30 cable from Santo Domingo, reports that Morales is within twenty miles of the capital without troops, facing impending impeachment by Congress and expected capture, with American customs operations continuing undisturbed.
