records.headline: A Washington dispatch in The Washington Times reports that the Dominican minister
records.summary_en: A Washington dispatch in The Washington Times reports that the Dominican minister views conditions in Santo Domingo as exceedingly alarming after conferring with State Department officials, while telegraph communication across the republic is badly crippled. Delays of up to twenty-four hours between Santo Domingo City and Puerto Plata are also affecting French cable relays to South America connected through the theater of hostilities. A companion dispatch from Port-au-Prince adds that General Demetrio Rodriguez was killed after his Morales troops were repulsed and defeated outside Puerto Plata by General Cespedes and the Caceres forces.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Washington en The Washington Times informa que el ministro dominicano considera que la situación en Santo Domingo es sumamente alarmante tras reunirse con funcionarios del Departamento de Estado, mientras que la comunicación telegráfica en toda la república se encuentra gravemente paralizada. Los retrasos de hasta veinticuatro horas entre la ciudad de Santo Domingo y Puerto Plata también afectan las retransmisiones del cable francés hacia Sudamérica conectadas a través del teatro de las hostilidades. Un despacho complementario desde Puerto Príncipe añade que el general Demetrio Rodríguez murió luego de que sus tropas leales a Morales fueran rechazadas y derrotadas en las afueras de Puerto Plata por el general Céspedes y las fuerzas de Cáceres.

records.headline: The Audubon Republican reports the departure of General Deschamps
records.summary_en: The Audubon Republican reports the departure of General Deschamps, former vice president of Santo Domingo, on a sailing vessel to operate against Puerto Plata, while rumors circulate that President Morales is held prisoner in irons at the capital. Following the announcement that Gen. Charles F. Morales had fled the capital for an unknown destination, government troops were sent in pursuit, and a clash took place about ten miles away where rebel commander General Pimentel was supposedly attacked. The fugitive president is believed to be attempting to reach the coast to board a sloop for Puerto Plata, hoping to join Governor Perez, who refuses to surrender his command despite being dismissed by the government.
records.summary_es: El Audubon Republican informa la partida del general Deschamps, exvicepresidente de Santo Domingo, en una embarcación de vela para operar contra Puerto Plata, en medio de rumores de que el presidente Morales está prisionero con grilletes en la capital. Tras anunciarse que el general Charles F. Morales había salido de la capital hacia un destino desconocido, tropas gubernamentales fueron enviadas en su persecución y se produjo un combate a unas diez millas de distancia, donde el comandante rebelde, el general Pimentel, fue supuestamente atacado. Se presume que el presidente prófugo intenta llegar a la costa para abordar un balandro hacia Puerto Plata, con la esperanza de unirse al gobernador Pérez, quien rehúsa entregar su mando a pesar de haber sido destituido por el gobierno.

records.headline: The Evening Star reports that Caceres forces commanded by General Cespedes attacked
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reports that Caceres forces commanded by General Cespedes attacked the Morales troops outside Puerto Plata, defeating and dispersing them after stubborn fighting that left many casualties on both sides. Among the dead was General Demetrio Rodriguez, the former governor of Monte Cristi, who had reportedly intended to proclaim himself a candidate for the presidency of Santo Domingo if his assault succeeded. Stores in Puerto Plata are closed and streets deserted, while Dominican exiles authorized by the Morales party are arriving at Monte Cristi. Direct advices to the State Department were delayed by wire interruptions across the island, which also created twenty-four-hour delays on French cable communication with Venezuela.
records.summary_es: The Evening Star informa que fuerzas de Cáceres comandadas por el general Céspedes atacaron a las tropas de Morales en las afueras de Puerto Plata, derrotándolas y dispersándolas tras un encarnizado combate que dejó numerosas bajas en ambos bandos. Entre los muertos figuró el general Demetrio Rodríguez, exgobernador de Monte Cristi, quien según informes planeaba proclamarse candidato a la presidencia de Santo Domingo si su asalto tenía éxito. Las tiendas de Puerto Plata están cerradas y las calles desiertas, mientras exiliados dominicanos autorizados por la facción de Morales llegan a Monte Cristi. Los informes directos al Departamento de Estado sufrieron demoras debido a interrupciones telegráficas en la isla, lo que también causó retrasos de veinticuatro horas en la comunicación del cable francés con Venezuela.

records.headline: A serious situation in Santo Domingo is described in cable advices
records.summary_en: A serious situation in Santo Domingo is described in cable advices received by the State and Navy Departments, The Washburn Leader reports, where the captain of the port of Puerto Plata was killed during an insurrectionary uprising. The provincial governor has barricaded the town in defiance of the general government, and fighting between government forces and rebels is also reported near Santo Domingo City. Off Puerto Plata, the Dominican gunboat Independencia has anchored under the command of Captain Catrain, who demanded the surrender of the town to the legitimate government of President Morales within twenty-four hours under threat of bombardment.
records.summary_es: Una grave situación en Santo Domingo es descrita en informes recibidos por cable por los Departamentos de Estado y de Marina, informa The Washburn Leader, donde el capitán del puerto de Puerto Plata murió durante un levantamiento insurreccional. El gobernador provincial atrincheró la ciudad en desafío al gobierno general, y también se reportan enfrentamientos entre fuerzas del gobierno y rebeldes cerca de la ciudad de Santo Domingo. Frente a Puerto Plata, el cañonero dominicano Independencia fondeó bajo el mando del capitán Catrain, quien exigió la rendición de la ciudad al gobierno legítimo del presidente Morales en un plazo de veinticuatro horas bajo amenaza de bombardeo.

records.headline: The Mitchell Capital reports official Washington views that the Dominican situation
records.summary_en: The Mitchell Capital reports official Washington views that the Dominican situation is serious and a clash between contending factions is probable, even though conditions remain temporarily quiet. Both sides are reported anxious to protect American property and avoid any interference with United States interests, while telegrams across the island are being subjected to censorship. A dispatch from Turks Island relays mail advices from Monte Cristi stating that General Perez, governor of Puerto Plata, surrendered to revolutionists, and that the cruiser Independencia was surrendered to General Deschamps, who departed for Puerto Plata with 250 men alongside Generals Demetrio and Rodriguez. General Barba is also reported in Altimira, fifteen miles from Puerto Plata, with 200 men.
records.summary_es: The Mitchell Capital informa sobre la opinión oficial en Washington de que la situación dominicana es grave y que es probable un choque entre las facciones en disputa, aun cuando reine una calma momentánea. Se reporta que ambos bandos están ansiosos por proteger las propiedades estadounidenses y evitar interferencias con los intereses de los Estados Unidos, mientras que los telegramas en toda la isla son sometidos a censura. Un despacho desde las islas Turcas transmite avisos por correo desde Monte Cristi señalando que el general Pérez, gobernador de Puerto Plata, se rindió a los revolucionarios, y que el crucero Independencia fue entregado al general Deschamps, quien partió hacia Puerto Plata con 250 hombres junto a los generales Demetrio y Rodríguez. Asimismo, se informa que el general Barba se encuentra en Altamira, a quince millas de Puerto Plata, con 200 hombres.

General Rodriguez, the former governor of Monte Cristi, was among those killed after reportedly stating that he would proclaim himself a candidate for the presidency of Santo Domingo if his assault succeeded. In Puerto Plata, business is at a standstill with closed stores and streets largely deserted, while Dominican exiles authorized by the Morales party to return are landing at Monte Cristi.

records.headline: Cable advices received by the State Department indicate the Dominican revolution
records.summary_en: Cable advices received by the State Department indicate the Dominican revolution is practically at an end, The Lewiston Evening Teller features dispatches reporting, with troops dispersing to their homes. A Cape Haitien dispatch reports, however, that surviving Morales followers sailed aboard the gunboat Independencia to Monte Cristi, where former governor General Guellito resolved to fight on his own behalf to attack Santiago, and former president General Jiminez arrived to seek the presidency with Morales's assistance. In addition, an official proclamation in Santo Domingo announces that Congress has decided to impeach President Morales, who remains a fugitive.
records.summary_es: Informes por cable recibidos por el Departamento de Estado indican que la revolución dominicana prácticamente ha concluido y que las tropas se están dispersando a sus hogares, según despachos presentados en el Lewiston Evening Teller. Sin embargo, un despacho desde Cabo Haitiano informa que los partidarios sobrevivientes de Morales zarparon a bordo del cañonero Independencia hacia Monte Cristi, donde el exgobernador general Guellito decidió combatir por cuenta propia para atacar Santiago, y el expresidente general Jimínez llegó para buscar la presidencia con el apoyo de Morales. Además, una proclama oficial en Santo Domingo anuncia que el Congreso decidió procesar en juicio político al presidente Morales, quien permanece prófugo.

records.summary_en: The Idaho Republican reports that following the departure of the Dominican chief magistrate, a fight took place about ten miles away where rebel commander General Pimentel was supposedly attacked by government forces. The whereabouts of the fugitive president remain unconfirmed, but he is widely thought to be traveling by sloop to Puerto Plata to join Jiminez partisans against the followers of Horacio. Furthermore, former foreign minister Juan F. Sanchez has left the capital; the report notes that Sanchez, along with Finance Minister Frederico Velasquez and American commissioners Albert C. Dillingham and Thomas C. Dawson, had signed the agreement of January 20 providing for a United States fiscal protectorate over Santo Domingo.

El paradero del presidente prófugo sigue sin confirmarse, pero se presume ampliamente que viaja en balandro hacia Puerto Plata para unirse a los partidarios de Jimínez frente a los seguidores de Horacio. Asimismo, el exministro de Relaciones Exteriores Juan F. Sánchez abandonó la capital; la nota recuerda que Sánchez, junto con el ministro de Hacienda Federico Velázquez y los comisionados estadounidenses Albert C. Dillingham y Thomas C. Dawson, había suscrito el acuerdo del 20 de enero que establecía un protectorado fiscal de los Estados Unidos sobre Santo Domingo.

records.headline: The Morris Tribune reports that Caceres troops commanded by General Cespedes attacked
records.summary_en: The Morris Tribune reports that Caceres troops commanded by General Cespedes attacked Morales forces outside Puerto Plata on Wednesday following an earlier repulse, defeating and dispersing them after stubborn fighting with casualties on both sides. Among the killed was General Demetrio Rodriguez, former governor of Monte Cristi, who had announced that he would seek the presidency of Santo Domingo if his assault succeeded. Business in Puerto Plata is at a standstill with closed stores and deserted streets, while Dominican exiles authorized by the Morales faction are landing at Monte Cristi. A Washington dispatch adds that Dominican representative Mr. Joubert informed Secretary Root that fighting had lasted three days, but reported that the country was quiet and conditions expected to clear shortly.
records.summary_es: El Morris Tribune informa que las tropas de Cáceres comandadas por el general Céspedes atacaron a las fuerzas de Morales en las afueras de Puerto Plata el miércoles tras un rechazo previo, derrotándolas y dispersándolas luego de un tenaz combate con bajas en ambos bandos. Entre los muertos figuró el general Demetrio Rodríguez, exgobernador de Monte Cristi, quien había anunciado que aspiraría a la presidencia de Santo Domingo si su asalto tenía éxito. El comercio en Puerto Plata está paralizado con tiendas cerradas y calles desiertas, mientras exiliados dominicanos autorizados por la facción de Morales desembarcan en Monte Cristi. Un despacho de Washington añade que el representante dominicano, el señor Joubert, informó al secretario Root que los combates duraron tres días, pero reportó que el país estaba en calma y que se esperaba una pronta clarificación de la situación.

records.summary_en: The Omaha Daily Bee reports that Morales followers boarded the gunboat Independence for Monte Cristi, following the fighting near Puerto Plata, where former governor General Guellito resolved to fight on his own behalf to attack Santiago upon learning of General Rodriguez's death. In addition, former president General Jiminez left Puerto Plata for Monte Cristi to compete for the presidency with Morales's assistance, backed by a large part of northern Santo Domingo. A Washington dispatch reports that the Secretary of War received a cablegram from Colonel Colton, general receiver of Dominican customs, stating that Carlos F. Morales was legally impeached by Congress and that Raymond Caceres is acting in accordance with the constitution pending court proceedings, leaving the legality of the Caceres government unquestioned.

Asimismo, el expresidente general Jimínez partió de Puerto Plata hacia Monte Cristi para competir por la presidencia con el respaldo de Morales, contando con el apoyo de gran parte del norte de Santo Domingo. Un despacho de Washington informa que el secretario de Guerra recibió un cablegrama del coronel Colton, receptor general de aduanas dominicanas, comunicando que Carlos F. Morales fue sometido a juicio político por el Congreso y que Raymond Cáceres ejerce el poder conforme a la constitución a la espera de los procesos judiciales, dejando incuestionada la legalidad del gobierno de Cáceres.

records.headline: Following the impeachment and elimination of Carlos F. Morales
records.summary_en: Following the impeachment and elimination of Carlos F. records.headline: The Grand Rapids Herald-Review reports that President Morales warned
records.summary_en: The Grand Rapids Herald-Review reports that President Morales warned the governor of Puerto Plata that the cruiser Independencia would attack by sea and land unless the port surrendered within twenty-four hours. American warships stationed off the port announced they would not interfere with naval operations, though they would take aboard non-combatants seeking refuge under the United States flag. A Washington dispatch of January 3 indicates that a bombardment remains unlikely, reporting that United States gunboats Nashville and Scorpion are in the harbor and negotiations are underway to ensure that both Dominican factions make their fight outside the town, in accordance with the arrangement made by Captain Dillingham at Monte Cristi two years earlier.
records.summary_es: El Grand Rapids Herald-Review informa que el presidente Morales advirtió al gobernador de Puerto Plata que el crucero Independencia atacaría por mar y tierra si el puerto no se rendía en un plazo de veinticuatro horas. Los buques de guerra estadounidenses apostados frente al puerto anunciaron que no interferirían en las operaciones navales, aunque recibirían a bordo a los no combatientes que buscaran refugio bajo la bandera de los Estados Unidos. Un despacho de Washington del 3 de enero indica que un bombardeo sigue siendo improbable, señalando que los cañoneros estadounidenses Nashville y Scorpion se encuentran en el puerto y que se negocia para que ambas facciones dominicanas libren su combate fuera de la ciudad, de acuerdo con el arreglo concertado por el capitán Dillingham en Monte Cristi dos años antes.

records.headline: Fugitive president General Morales was completely defeated on January 3
records.summary_en: Fugitive president General Morales was completely defeated on January 3 before Puerto Plata by troops loyal to temporary president General Caceres, a Cape Haytien dispatch published in The Madison Daily Leader reports. Morales commander General Demetrio Rodriguez was killed and about 150 men were killed or wounded, with the surviving insurgents embarking on the gunboat Independence for Monte Cristi. General Guellito, the former governor of Monte Cristi, decided upon learning of Rodriguez's death to fight independently and prepare an attack on Santiago. Meanwhile, former president General Jiminez left Puerto Plata for Monte Cristi to enter the presidential contest with Morales's assistance, backed by a large portion of northern Santo Domingo. A supplementary New York dispatch cites a cable to the Herald reporting that five generals were killed during the battle at Puerto Plata.
records.summary_es: El presidente prófugo, el general Morales, fue completamente derrotado el 3 de enero frente a Puerto Plata por tropas leales al presidente provisional, el general Cáceres, según un despacho de Cabo Haitiano publicado en The Madison Daily Leader. El comandante de Morales, el general Demetrio Rodríguez, murió en combate y cerca de 150 hombres resultaron muertos o heridos, tras lo cual los insurgentes sobrevivientes abordaron el cañonero Independence rumbo a Monte Cristi. El general Guellito, exgobernador de Monte Cristi, decidió al enterarse de la muerte de Rodríguez combatir por cuenta propia y preparar un asalto contra Santiago. Mientras tanto, el expresidente, general Jiménez, partió de Puerto Plata hacia Monte Cristi para competir por la presidencia con el respaldo de Morales, contando con el apoyo de gran parte del norte de Santo Domingo. Un despacho complementario de Nueva York cita un cable al Herald que reporta la muerte de cinco generales durante la batalla en Puerto Plata.

records.headline: A news item in The Laclede Blade recounts that revolutionists
records.summary_en: A news item in The Laclede Blade recounts that revolutionists besieging Puerto Plata held positions cutting off all passage except for American naval vessels and individuals protected by foreign consuls. Intervention by foreign consuls reportedly averted a planned naval bombardment by the revolutionary gunboat Independencia. Forces led by General Guellito, former governor of Monte Cristi, were collaborating with the besiegers and preparing a joint assault on Santiago, where temporary president General Caceres was assembling government troops for an anticipated decisive battle. Advices received at Cape Haytien added that fugitive president Morales was acting on behalf of former president General Jiminez, who had previously failed to regain executive power in 1903.
records.summary_es: Una nota de prensa en The Laclede Blade relata que los revolucionarios que sitiaban Puerto Plata ocupaban posiciones que impedían todo tránsito, salvo para buques de la armada estadounidense y personas protegidas por los cónsules extranjeros. La intervención de los cónsules extranjeros evitó presuntamente el proyectado bombardeo naval por parte del cañonero revolucionario Independencia. Tropas comandadas por el general Guellito, exgobernador de Monte Cristi, colaboraban con los sitiadores y preparaban un ataque conjunto contra Santiago, donde el presidente provisional, el general Cáceres, concentraba tropas gubernamentales para una batalla decisiva prevista. Despachos recibidos en Cabo Haitiano añadían que el presidente prófugo Morales actuaba en interés del expresidente, general Jiménez, quien previamente había fracasado en recuperar el poder ejecutivo en 1903.

Intensos combates se prolongaron durante toda la jornada hasta las 5 de la tarde, momento en que las tropas sitiadoras se retiraron.

records.headline: A Cape Haytien dispatch in The Salt Lake Herald reports that forces of temporary president
records.summary_en: A Cape Haytien dispatch in The Salt Lake Herald reports that forces of temporary president General Caceres won a complete victory over the insurgent army of fugitive president General Morales before Puerto Plata on January 3. Morales's field commander, General Demetrio Rodriguez, was killed during the action, and about one hundred and fifty men were killed or wounded. Following the defeat, the remaining Morales partisans embarked on the gunboat Independencia off Puerto Plata and sailed for Monte Cristi. The dispatch notes that Carlos F. Morales had not yet been heard from, while General Guellito, the former governor of Monte Cristi, had previously declared his troops in Morales's favor.

El comandante de campo de Morales, el general Demetrio Rodríguez, murió durante la acción militar y cerca de ciento cincuenta hombres resultaron muertos o heridos. Tras la derrota, los partidarios restantes de Morales abordaron el cañonero Independencia frente a Puerto Plata y zarparon hacia Monte Cristi. El despacho señala que aún no se tenían noticias de Carlos F. Morales, mientras que el general Guellito, exgobernador de Monte Cristi, se había pronunciado previamente con sus tropas a favor de Morales.

records.headline: The Evening Star reports that Senator Rayner delivered his maiden
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reports that Senator Rayner delivered his maiden Senate speech on United States relations with the Dominican Republic and the true nature of the Monroe Doctrine. Rayner commanded the close attention of a rapidly filling chamber, also digressing to denounce the persecution of Jews in Russia. Colleagues from both political parties, including Senator Gorman, congratulated him following the address. Rayner emphasized that he adhered strictly to the original text of the Monroe Doctrine established over three-quarters of a century earlier, repudiating modern revisions as counterfeit presentments.
records.summary_es: El Evening Star informa que el senador Rayner pronunció su discurso inaugural en el Senado sobre las relaciones de los Estados Unidos con la República Dominicana y la verdadera naturaleza de la Doctrina Monroe. Rayner captó la atención de un recinto que se llenó con rapidez, apartándose también del tema para denunciar la persecución de judíos en Rusia. Colegas de ambos partidos políticos, entre ellos el senador Gorman, lo felicitaron al término de su intervención. Rayner subrayó que se atenía estrictamente al texto original de la Doctrina Monroe proclamado hacía más de tres cuartos de siglo, rechazando las interpretaciones modernas por considerarlas versiones adulteradas.

When the departing steamer sailed, a renewed assault by the insurgent general Pedro Alverz was momentarily expected to compel the surrender of local authorities. Inland, insurgent generals Guellito and Navarro were defeated on January 6 during their assault on Santiago, which was defended by General Caceres's troops. Furthermore, General lift Sala, campaigning in support of General Jiminez, was reported preparing to attack La Vega, located about seventy-five miles northwest of Santo Domingo.

Al zarpar el barco de vapor, se aguardaba por momentos un nuevo asalto del general insurgente Pedro Alverz que obligaría a las autoridades locales a rendirse. En el interior, los generales insurgentes Guellito y Navarro sufrieron una derrota el 6 de enero durante su ataque contra Santiago, plaza defendida por las tropas del general Cáceres. Además, se informaba que el general lift Sala, en campaña a favor del general Jiménez, se disponía a atacar La Vega, situada a unas setenta y cinco millas al noroeste de Santo Domingo.

records.summary_en: According to dispatches brought by the steamer Cherokee from Puerto Plata under date of January 6, sharp combat near that harbor caused 150 casualties among the 800 men engaged, with corpses remaining in the city streets for two days. An imminent attack by insurgent general Pedro Alvarez was expected to force the surrender of Puerto Plata's authorities as the steamer departed. Meanwhile, insurgent generals Guillito and Navarro were defeated on January 5 while attacking Santiago against government forces loyal to General Caceres. In another sector, General La Salla was preparing to strike La Vega, about 75 miles northwest of Santo Domingo, on behalf of General Jiminez.
records.summary_es: Según despachos traídos por el vapor Cherokee desde Puerto Plata con fecha del 6 de enero, los violentos combates cerca de ese puerto causaron 150 bajas entre los 800 hombres enfrentados, permaneciendo cadáveres en las calles de la ciudad durante dos días. Al partir el vapor, se preveía que un inminente ataque del general insurgente Pedro Álvarez obligaría a las autoridades de Puerto Plata a capitular. Entre tanto, los generales insurgentes Guillito y Navarro fueron derrotados el 5 de enero al atacar Santiago frente a las fuerzas gubernamentales leales al general Cáceres. En otro sector, el general La Salla se disponía a acometer contra La Vega, a unas 75 millas al noroeste de Santo Domingo, en nombre del general Jiménez.

records.headline: Recent combat near Puerto Plata's port was exceptionally fierce
records.summary_en: Recent combat near Puerto Plata's port was exceptionally fierce, leaving 150 of the 800 men engaged on both sides killed or wounded, according to reports carried by the steamer Cherokee and relayed in a Turks Island dispatch in the Arizona Republican. Dead bodies lay in the streets of Puerto Plata for two days, and a renewed assault by insurgent general Pedro Alvarez was expected to compel the authorities' surrender shortly after the vessel sailed. The report also announces that insurgent generals Guellito and Lavarro were defeated on January 5 in an assault on Santiago defended by Caceres's troops. Furthermore, General Lasala, fighting on behalf of General Jiminez, was poised to attack the interior town of La Vega, located about seventy-five miles northwest of Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: Los recientes enfrentamientos cerca del puerto de Puerto Plata fueron sumamente intensos y dejaron 150 muertos o heridos entre los 800 hombres trabados en combate, según informes transportados por el vapor Cherokee desde Puerto Plata y transmitidos en un despacho de las islas Turcas en el Arizona Republican. Los cadáveres permanecieron en las calles de Puerto Plata durante dos días y se anticipaba que un nuevo asalto del general insurgente Pedro Álvarez obligaría a la rendición de las autoridades poco después de zarpar la nave. El informe anuncia además que los generales insurgentes Guellito y Lavarro fueron derrotados el 5 de enero en un asalto contra Santiago defendido por las tropas de Cáceres. Por último, el general Lasala, en armas a favor del general Jiménez, se disponía a atacar la población interior de La Vega, situada a unas setenta y cinco millas al noroeste de Santo Domingo.

records.headline: A dispatch in The Star reports that insurgent forces at Puerto Plata suffered
records.summary_en: A dispatch in The Star reports that insurgent forces at Puerto Plata suffered an utter rout, losing 120 men killed and wounded, including Generals Rodriguez, Lino, and Peres, while General Perdo Vanega and Antonio Calderon were killed among Caceres's defenders. United States cruisers prevented the insurgent gunboat from bombarding and forbade the local fort from using artillery, compelling the revolutionaries to re-embark. In Washington, Dominican minister Emilio Joubert received a cablegram confirming Rodriguez's death after three days of fighting and shared the information with Secretary Root. Furthermore, cables received by the State Department from Santo Domingo indicated that the revolution had practically ended as troops dispersed and quiet returned across the country.
records.summary_es: Un despacho en The Star informa que las fuerzas insurgentes sufrieron una completa derrota en Puerto Plata, perdiendo 120 hombres entre muertos y heridos, incluidos los generales Rodríguez, Lino y Peres, mientras que en las filas defensoras de Cáceres murieron el general Perdo Vanega y Antonio Calderón. Cruceros de los Estados Unidos impidieron que el cañonero insurgente bombardeara y prohibieron al fuerte utilizar artillería, forzando a los revolucionarios a reembarcarse. En Washington, el ministro dominicano Emilio Joubert recibió un cablegrama confirmando la muerte de Rodríguez tras tres días de combate y transmitió dicha información al secretario Root. Asimismo, despachos recibidos por el Departamento de Estado desde Santo Domingo señalaban que la revolución había concluido prácticamente al dispersarse las tropas y restablecerse la calma en el país.

records.summary_en: The Weekly Arizona Journal-Miner publishes a Turks Island dispatch reporting news delivered by the steamer Cherokee from Puerto Plata. The dispatch, dated January 0 as printed in the text, relates that recent fighting at the port was very sharp, resulting in 150 killed or wounded out of the 800 men engaged on both sides. Corpses had remained in the streets of Puerto Plata for two days, and conditions across the country were described as threatening further combat in several areas.

El despacho, con fecha del 0 de enero según el texto impreso, señala que los recientes combates en el puerto fueron sumamente intensos y dejaron 150 muertos o heridos entre los 800 hombres trabados en lucha en ambos bandos. Los cadáveres habían quedado abandonados en las calles de Puerto Plata durante dos días, y se describía que las condiciones del país amenazaban con desatar nuevos combates en diversas zonas.

records.headline: Recent developments establishing the constitutional legitimacy of Raymond Caceres's administration
records.summary_en: Recent developments establishing the constitutional legitimacy of Raymond Caceres's administration removed Carlos F. Morales from the presidency, advices compiled in the Pierre Weekly Free Press note. State Department naval reports confirmed that hostilities ceased around Puerto Plata after desultory skirmishes that left thirty dead and sixty wounded on Caceres's side, while the insurgent gunboat Independencia hovered offshore. An additional Cape Haitien dispatch dated January 7 recounts Morales's complete defeat before Puerto Plata on January 3, which cost the life of insurgent commander Demetrio Rodriguez and resulted in about 150 casualties. In the aftermath, former president General Jiminez proceeded toward Monte Cristi to launch a presidential campaign with Morales's assistance and northern backing.
records.summary_es: Los recientes acontecimientos que consolidaron la legitimidad constitucional de la administración de Raymond Cáceres apartaron a Carlos F. Morales de la presidencia, indican despachos compilados en el Pierre Weekly Free Press. Informes navales del Departamento de Estado confirmaron el cese de las hostilidades en torno a Puerto Plata tras escaramuzas dispersas que dejaron treinta muertos y sesenta heridos en el bando de Cáceres, mientras el cañonero insurgente Independencia permanecía mar adentro. Un despacho adicional de Cabo Haitiano del 7 de enero relata la total derrota de Morales ante Puerto Plata el 3 de enero, que costó la vida al comandante insurgente Demetrio Rodríguez y causó cerca de 150 bajas. Tras estos hechos, el expresidente, general Jiménez, marchó hacia Monte Cristi para lanzar su candidatura presidencial con el auxilio de Morales y el respaldo del norte.

records.headline: The Wahpeton Times carries dispatches reporting that the downfall of Carlos F. Morales confirmed
records.summary_en: The Wahpeton Times carries dispatches reporting that the downfall of Carlos F. Morales confirmed the legality of Raymond Caceres's government under the national constitution. Naval messages to the State Department announced that hostilities ceased at Puerto Plata, recording thirty men killed and sixty wounded on Caceres's side, with rebel losses unstated and the gunboat Independencia cruising nearby. A Cape Haitien cable of January 7 adds that Morales suffered an absolute defeat outside Puerto Plata on January 3, suffering the death of General Demetrio Rodriguez and about 150 men killed or wounded. Meanwhile, former president General Jiminez journeyed from Puerto Plata to Monte Cristi to seek the presidency with Morales's support and widespread favor in northern districts.
records.summary_es: The Wahpeton Times publica despachos informando que la caída de Carlos F. Morales ratificó la legalidad del gobierno de Raymond Cáceres al amparo de la constitución nacional. Comunicaciones navales remitidas al Departamento de Estado anunciaron el fin de los combates en Puerto Plata, contabilizando treinta hombres muertos y sesenta heridos en las filas de Cáceres, sin detallar las bajas rebeldes y con el cañonero Independencia patrullando en las inmediaciones. Un cable de Cabo Haitiano del 7 de enero añade que Morales sufrió una derrota absoluta a las afueras de Puerto Plata el 3 de enero, registrándose la muerte del general Demetrio Rodríguez y cerca de 150 bajas. Mientras tanto, el expresidente, general Jiménez, viajó de Puerto Plata a Monte Cristi para aspirar a la presidencia con el respaldo de Morales y amplio favor en los distritos del norte.

records.headline: The Bowbells Tribune reports that Supreme Court proceedings
records.summary_en: The Bowbells Tribune reports that Supreme Court proceedings and constitutional procedures confirmed the authority of Raymond Caceres's government while completely eliminating Carlos F. Morales from the political scene. Naval cables transmitted to the State Department announced that hostilities had ceased around Puerto Plata after intermittent firing, leaving thirty dead and sixty wounded among Caceres's forces. A dispatch from Cape Haitien dated January 7 describes Morales's total rout before Puerto Plata on January 3, where insurgent commander General Demetrio Rodriguez died and about 150 men were killed or wounded. In the wake of the defeat, former president General Jiminez proceeded toward Monte Cristi to seek the presidency with Morales's assistance.
records.summary_es: The Bowbells Tribune informa que las actuaciones de la Suprema Corte y los procedimientos constitucionales confirmaron la autoridad del gobierno de Raymond Cáceres, apartando por completo a Carlos F. Morales de la escena política. Cables navales remitidos al Departamento de Estado anunciaron el cese de las hostilidades en los alrededores de Puerto Plata tras tiroteos intermitentes, dejando un saldo de treinta muertos y sesenta heridos en las fuerzas de Cáceres. Un despacho desde Cabo Haitiano con fecha del 7 de enero describe la derrota total de Morales frente a Puerto Plata el 3 de enero, donde falleció el comandante insurgente general Demetrio Rodríguez y cerca de 150 hombres resultaron muertos o heridos. A raíz de la derrota, el expresidente, general Jiménez, marchó hacia Monte Cristi para disputar la presidencia con el apoyo de Morales.

records.headline: Dispatches in the Evening Times-Republican report that fugitive president
records.summary_en: Dispatches in the Evening Times-Republican report that fugitive president Carlos F. Morales, suffering from a broken leg, entered the United States legation at Santo Domingo accompanied by an envoy from the Monte Cristi revolutionists. Dominican authorities initiated negotiations to secure his formal resignation and departure from the country, anticipating that his surrender would effectively terminate the island's civil unrest. In Washington, Secretary of War Taft received a confirmatory cable from George R. Colton, receiver of Dominican customs, stating that Morales had sought American diplomatic protection the previous evening and was expected to resign that day.
records.summary_es: Despachos en el Evening Times-Republican informan que el presidente prófugo Carlos F. Morales, con una pierna fracturada, ingresó en la legación de los Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo acompañado por un emisario de los revolucionarios de Monte Cristi. Las autoridades dominicanas entablaron negociaciones para obtener su renuncia formal y su salida del país, anticipando que su rendición pondría fin efectivo a los disturbios civiles en la isla. En Washington, el secretario de Guerra Taft recibió un cable confirmatorio de George R. Colton, receptor de aduanas dominicanas, comunicando que Morales había solicitado protección diplomática estadounidense la noche anterior y se esperaba su renuncia durante la jornada.

records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* reported that former President Juan Isidro Jimenes traveled to Monte Cristi to seek the presidency with the backing of fugitive President Morales and broad northern support. The paper profiled insurgent leader General Demetrio Rodríguez, an American-educated commander who had previously controlled customs revenues in Monte Cristi before being defeated by General Céspedes. It noted that Céspedes, originally a key supporter of Morales, had turned against the president in fierce opposition to the fiscal convention with the United States.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield Weekly Republican* informó que el expresidente Juan Isidro Jimenes viajó a Monte Cristi para aspirar a la presidencia con el respaldo del presidente prófugo Morales y un amplio apoyo en el norte. El periódico reseñó al líder insurgente, general Demetrio Rodríguez, un militar educado en los Estados Unidos que anteriormente había controlado los ingresos de aduanas en Monte Cristi antes de ser derrotado por el general Céspedes. Señaló además que Céspedes, quien en un principio fue un firme partidario de Morales, se volvió contra el mandatario en feroz oposición a la convención fiscal con los Estados Unidos.

Gen Jiminez, the former president of San Domingo, has left Puerto Plata for Monte Cristi, and, it is understood, will, with the assistance of Morales, compete for the presidency of the republic against the other candidates for that office. According to the reports brought to Cape Haytien by messengers, a large part of the population of northern San Domingo is in Favor of Gen Jiminez. Gen Demetrio Rodriguez had long been a prominent factor in the affairs of San Domingo. He was a graduate of Fordham college. New York, spoke English fluently, and was described as an affable and scholarly man and a born leader of men. He resided about 25 miles from Monte Christi; and was considered to be one of the most formidable of Morales's opponents. At the close of the last revolution Rodriguez only consented to lay down his arms under the promise of being allowed to collect the customs and other revenues in the province of Monte Christi. Gen Cespedes, who defeated Gen Rodriguez, was one of the leading men in the movement which placed Morales in the presidential chair of San Domingo, but Cespedes quarreled with Morales on account of the latter's transactions with the American government, and when the enemies of Morales became active Cespedes hastened to join issue with them in their opposition to the Morales government and the fiscal agreement between the United States and San Domingo.

records.headline: Dispatches received by the War and State Departments confirmed
records.summary_en: Dispatches received by the War and State Departments confirmed the acceptance of Former President Morales's resignation as chief executive of the Dominican Republic, The Washington Times reports. Immediately following the action, Morales embarked from Santo Domingo City aboard the United States gunboat Dubuque, bound for San Juan, Puerto Rico. His departure marked his formal exit into exile under United States naval auspices.

Inmediatamente después de este hecho, Morales zarpó de la ciudad de Santo Domingo a bordo del cañonero estadounidense Dubuque con destino a San Juan de Puerto Rico. Su salida selló su partida formal hacia el exilio bajo custodia naval de los Estados Unidos.

records.headline: A Washington report in The Sun details the submission of President Carlos F. Morales's resignation
records.summary_en: A Washington report in The Sun details the submission of President Carlos F. Morales's resignation to the Dominican Congress in Santo Domingo City prior to his departure for exile in Puerto Rico. Before sailing, Morales transmitted a dispatch to the rebellious authorities of the Monte Cristi district urging that circumstances required sacrifice for the sake of peace and advising them to accept government guarantees. Commander W. H. H. Southerland of the gunboat Yankee forwarded Morales's conciliatory message to the Navy Department, while Dominican customs collector Colonel Colton informed the War Department that Morales's resignation had been accepted by Congress, predicting an early restoration of peace.

Southerland, desde el cañonero Yankee, remitió el mensaje pacificador de Morales al Departamento de la Armada, en tanto que el recaudador de aduanas dominicanas, coronel Colton, informó al Departamento de Guerra que el Congreso había admitido la renuncia de Morales, pronosticando un pronto restablecimiento de la paz.

records.headline: The Beatrice Daily Express reports that the insurgent gunboat
records.summary_en: The Beatrice Daily Express reports that the insurgent gunboat Independence and the governor of Monte Cristi prepared to surrender to the Dominican government under safety guarantees, complying with counsel from former president General Morales. From a hospital cot in San Juan, Puerto Rico, where he arrived on the USS Dubuque, former president General Carlos F. Morales asked the Associated Press to convey his heartfelt gratitude to President Roosevelt and the American people for their support during his presidency. Morales asserted that the republic's future salvation depended entirely upon the ratification of the pending convention by the United States Senate and the Dominican Congress, warning that continued revolutionary turmoil would ensure ongoing ruination.

Morales aseveró que la salvación futura de la república dependía por entero de la ratificación de la convención pendiente por el Senado de los Estados Unidos y el Congreso dominicano, advirtiendo que la constante agitación revolucionaria significaba la ruina continua del país.

Colton announces that the Monte Cristi district, which had been in a state of rebellion since 1904, surrendered today, with revolutionary leaders permitted to leave the country. The dispatch adds that the revolution has collapsed, the Dominican government possesses entire control of the situation, and peace prevails.

records.headline: Monte Cristi capitulated to Dominican government forces under guarantees
records.summary_en: Monte Cristi capitulated to Dominican government forces under guarantees protecting the lives and property of the rebels, a Santo Domingo dispatch of January 15 in The San Francisco Call reports. The Dominican gunboat Independencia, which had supported former President General Morales, also surrendered after its commander sought refuge on an American warship. The dispatch concludes that the revolution has ended and all is quiet.

El cañonero dominicano Independencia, que había apoyado al expresidente general Morales, también se rindió después de que su comandante buscara refugio en un buque de guerra estadounidense. El despacho concluye que la revolución ha terminado y todo está en calma.

Morales, who affirmed that national salvation depended on the ratification of the pending customs convention by both nations. Morales noted that while provisional President Cáceres and various rebel factions had come to endorse the convention, political stability remained precarious under Cáceres's minority government. Morales recounted suffering a fractured ankle when a vine rope broke while scaling a cliff during his escape from the Dominican capital.

Former president Morales, interviewed at San Juan, said the future salvation of Santo Domingo depends entirely on ratification of the pending convention by the United States Senate and the Dominican congress.

El expresidente Morales, entrevistado en San Juan, dijo que la salvación futura de Santo Domingo depende enteramente de la ratificación de la convención pendiente por el Senado de los Estados Unidos y el congreso dominicano.

records.headline: Advices from Monte Cristi published by The Frontier from a Cape Haytien dispatch
records.summary_en: Advices from Monte Cristi published by The Frontier from a Cape Haytien dispatch report that the Dominican gunboat Independencia declared for fugitive President General Morales, but is immobilized without coal and unable to engage in further hostile operations. General Morales was recently wounded in an engagement with forces under temporary President General Caceras, whose troops captured a doctor from Morales's army and are pursuing the former president. Meanwhile, recruiting is being actively conducted in the northern provinces of San Domingo to march against General Ouellito, a presidential aspirant preparing an assault on the capital.

El general Morales resultó herido recientemente en un enfrentamiento con fuerzas leales al presidente provisional general Caceras, cuyas tropas capturaron a un médico del ejército de Morales y persiguen al expresidente. Mientras tanto, se realiza un reclutamiento activo en las provincias del norte de San Domingo para marchar contra el general Ouellito, un aspirante presidencial que prepara un asalto a la capital.

records.summary_en: The *Stark County Democrat* reported on a Senate speech by Senator Benjamin Tillman condemning President Roosevelt's Dominican policy and the enforcement of the unratified customs treaty. Tillman criticized the administration for prioritizing European bondholders and ridiculed the executive *modus vivendi* as an unconstitutional usurpation of Senate authority. Warning against imperial expansion, Tillman asserted that unless the Senate firmly rejected the administration's actions, the United States would permanently dominate and occupy Santo Domingo.

Tillman criticó al gobierno por priorizar a los tenedores de bonos europeos y ridiculizó el *modus vivendi* ejecutivo como una usurpación inconstitucional de la autoridad del Senado. Al advertir contra la expansión imperialista, Tillman aseveró que, a menos que el Senado rechazara firmemente las acciones del gobierno, los Estados Unidos dominarían y ocuparían de forma permanente a Santo Domingo.

El informe confirma que la revolución ha llegado a su fin y se ha restablecido la tranquilidad.

records.headline: Signed "Inquirer," a letter to the editor of the New-York Tribune warns
records.summary_en: Signed "Inquirer," a letter to the editor of the New-York Tribune warns that Santo Domingo will be forced to seek European financial assistance if the Senate and Executive fail to compromise on preserving the Roosevelt Doctrine's core arrangements. The correspondent recalls a 1903 pamphlet by the Minister of Interior Relations under President Wos y Gil proposing to lease Samana Bay to Germany to settle the republic's foreign debt. The writer notes that a modified version of that plan is already being contemplated in Santo Domingo as a possible alternative should negotiations with the United States collapse completely.
records.summary_es: Firmada por "Inquirer", una carta al director del New-York Tribune advierte que Santo Domingo se verá obligado a buscar auxilio financiero europeo si el Senado y el Ejecutivo no logran un acuerdo para preservar los puntos fundamentales de la Doctrina Roosevelt. El autor recuerda un folleto de 1903 elaborado por el ministro de Relaciones Interiores bajo la presidencia de Wos y Gil, en el cual se proponía arrendar la bahía de Samaná a Alemania para saldar la deuda externa de la república. El firmante señala que en Santo Domingo ya se contempla una versión modificada de ese plan como posible alternativa en caso de que las negociaciones con Estados Unidos fracasen por completo.

records.headline: The Evening Star reviews the executive history of Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reviews the executive history of Santo Domingo, characterizing it as a sequence of self-enriching politicians who attained and surrendered power through force and conspiracy. The article notes that despite adopting a constitution, presidency, congress, and electoral college modeled after the United States, twenty-five or more presidents have held power during the last forty years without a single honest election taking place. A chronological table is presented showing the Dominican chief executives since the evacuation of the Spanish army and the revolutionary or constitutional circumstances under which each entered and vacated office.
records.summary_es: El Evening Star examina la historia del poder ejecutivo en Santo Domingo, caracterizándola como una sucesión de políticos enriquecidos a costa del erario que obtuvieron y dejaron el mando mediante la fuerza y la conspiración. El artículo señala que, a pesar de haber adoptado una constitución, presidencia, congreso y colegio electoral inspirados en los de Estados Unidos, veinticinco o más presidentes han gobernado durante los últimos cuarenta años sin que se haya realizado una sola elección honesta. Se presenta una tabla cronológica que muestra a los mandatarios dominicanos desde la evacuación del ejército español y las circunstancias revolucionarias o constitucionales en las que cada uno asumió y abandonó el cargo.

records.headline: The Evening Star recounts the political collapse in Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The Evening Star recounts the political collapse in Santo Domingo, beginning when Admiral Bradford caused alarm in the capital by sending naval sailors ashore for exercise, which frightened residents mistook for an impending siege. Soon afterward, President Morales fled into the woods, and government forces dispersed following a battle near Puerto Plata where Gen. Rodriguez, commander of the army, was killed. Under an agreement negotiated by revolutionists with an intermediary identified as Mr. Daweon, Morales was granted safe departure to Porto Rico on condition of leaving permanently, while Vice President Caceres assumed the presidency and agreed to continue the customs modus vivendi.
records.summary_es: El Evening Star relata el colapso político en Santo Domingo, iniciado cuando el almirante Bradford alarmó a la capital al enviar marineros a tierra para ejercicios, maniobra que los atemorizados pobladores confundieron con un asedio inminente. Poco después, el presidente Morales huyó a los montes y las fuerzas del gobierno se dispersaron tras una batalla cerca de Puerto Plata en la que murió el general Rodríguez, comandante del ejército. Conforme a un acuerdo negociado por los revolucionarios con un intermediario identificado como el señor Daweon, se le concedió a Morales la salida segura hacia Puerto Rico a condición de marcharse definitivamente, mientras que el vicepresidente Cáceres asumió la presidencia y aceptó continuar el modus vivendi aduanero.

records.headline: Power in the region is divided between Morales in the capital
records.summary_en: Power in the region is divided between Morales in the capital and northern leaders, an analysis in the Watertown Republican describes, focusing on Demetrio Rodriguez, the local chieftain of Monte Christi. After fierce fighting two years earlier, Morales had pacified Rodriguez by appointing him administrator of the Monte Christi customhouse. This arrangement collapsed when the United States sent a cruiser to seize the customhouse by force under the arbitral "laudo" awarded to the Santo Domingo Improvement Company, cutting off Rodriguez's revenue and converting Monte Christi into a persistent center of revolutionary activity.
records.summary_es: El poder en la región se divide entre Morales en la capital y los caudillos norteños, describe un análisis en el Watertown Republican, centrándose en Demetrio Rodríguez, el jefe local de Monte Cristi. Tras encarnizados combates dos años antes, Morales había pacificado a Rodríguez nombrándolo administrador de la aduana de Monte Cristi. Este arreglo colapsó cuando Estados Unidos envió un crucero para tomar posesión de la aduana por la fuerza en virtud del "laudo" arbitral concedido a la Santo Domingo Improvement Company, privando a Rodríguez de sus ingresos y convirtiendo a Monte Cristi en un foco constante de actividad revolucionaria.

records.headline: Intelligence from Monte Cristi is reported in a Cape Haytien dispatch
records.summary_en: Intelligence from Monte Cristi is reported in a Cape Haytien dispatch in The Frontier: the Dominican gunboat Independencia, allied with fugitive President General Morales, is stranded without coal and incapable of further military operations. The dispatch states that General Morales was wounded during a clash with forces commanded by temporary President General Caceras, whose troops captured a doctor from Morales's army and are actively tracking him. It adds that recruitment is progressing rapidly in northern San Domingo to counter General Gueliito, who has declared his candidacy for the presidency and is plotting an attack on the capital.
records.summary_es: Noticias de Monte Cristi se dan a conocer en un despacho de Cabo Haitiano en The Frontier: el cañonero dominicano Independencia, aliado del presidente prófugo general Morales, se encuentra varado sin carbón e incapacitado para más operaciones militares. El despacho señala que el general Morales fue herido durante un combate contra fuerzas mandadas por el presidente provisional general Caceras, cuyas tropas capturaron a un médico del ejército de Morales y le siguen la pista activamente. Añade que el reclutamiento avanza con rapidez en el norte de San Domingo para frenar al general Gueliito, quien proclamó su candidatura a la presidencia y planea un ataque sobre la capital.

records.headline: An editorial in The News-Herald considers public opinion on Dominican
records.summary_en: An editorial in The News-Herald considers public opinion on Dominican affairs, asserting that informed American voters overwhelmingly agree with President Theodore Roosevelt's policy. The piece contends that Roosevelt's course is necessary both to avert European armed intervention and to protect the honest creditors of the Dominican Republic. It claims that a popular referendum on the struggle between the President and his congressional critics would produce an overwhelming victory that would silence his opponents for years.
records.summary_es: Un editorial en The News-Herald reflexiona sobre la opinión pública respecto a los asuntos dominicanos, afirmando que los votantes estadounidenses informados respaldan abrumadoramente la política del presidente Theodore Roosevelt. El texto sostiene que la actuación de Roosevelt es indispensable tanto para evitar una intervención armada europea como para proteger a los acreedores legítimos de la República Dominicana. Asegura que un referéndum popular sobre la contienda entre el presidente y sus críticos en el Congreso resultaría en una victoria aplastante que silenciaría a sus adversarios durante años.

records.headline: A treaty of peace between the insurgent generals at Monte Cristi
records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* reported that a peace treaty ending the Dominican insurrection was signed aboard the United States cruiser *Yankee* at Monte Cristi. Foreign Minister Emiliano Tejera stated that the rapid restoration of peace was made possible by decisive military action and the American financial *modus vivendi*, which deprived the insurgents of customs revenues. Under the capitulation terms, Monte Cristi returned to government control, rebel General Desiderio Arias was permitted to go into exile in Puerto Rico, and remaining insurgents were granted amnesty.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield Weekly Republican* informó que se firmó a bordo del crucero estadounidense *Yankee*, en Monte Cristi, un tratado de paz que puso fin a la insurrección dominicana. El ministro de Relaciones Exteriores Emiliano Tejera declaró que el rápido restablecimiento de la paz fue posible gracias a la enérgica acción militar y al *modus vivendi* financiero estadounidense, que privó a los insurgentes de las rentas aduaneras. Bajo los términos de la capitulación, Monte Cristi volvió al control del gobierno, se le permitió al general rebelde Desiderio Arias exiliarse en Puerto Rico y se concedió amnistía a los insurgentes restantes.
records.passage: TREATY OF PEACE SIGNED. [illegible] of the Failure of the San Domingo Revolution. A treaty of peace between the insurgent generals at Monte Cristi and the government was signed Wednesday last week on board the American cruiser Yankee, says a dispatch from San Domingo. Monte Cristi is now in the hands of the constitutional government forces. Emiliano [Tejera?], minister of foreign affairs, said to the Associated Press Wednesday: “I attribute the prompt collapse of the insurrection to the vigor of the government's military operations, to the financial modus vivendi which restrained the revolutionists from seizing the custom-houses, and to the fact that the government is a constitutional one.” The Dominican government in receiving the surrender of Monte Cristi permitted the revolutionary governor, Gen Arias, to depart for Porto Rico, and granted general amnesty to the other revolutionists. records.headline: The Albuquerque Morning Journal's telegraphic congressional
records.summary_en: The Albuquerque Morning Journal's telegraphic congressional coverage takes up a Senate debate regarding Moroccan and Dominican diplomacy. Senator Money spoke for over two hours against the administration, arguing that American interests in Santo Domingo were insufficient to justify the current intervention and asserting that the President had exceeded his constitutional authority. In contrast, Senator Heyburn addressed the chamber in favor of annexing Santo Domingo to the United States.
records.summary_es: La cobertura telegráfica del Congreso en el Albuquerque Morning Journal aborda un debate en el Senado relativo a la diplomacia en Marruecos y Santo Domingo. El senador Money intervino durante más de dos horas contra la administración, argumentando que los intereses estadounidenses en Santo Domingo eran insuficientes para justificar la intervención actual y sosteniendo que el presidente se había extralimitado en sus atribuciones constitucionales. Por el contrario, el senador Heyburn habló ante la cámara a favor de anexar Santo Domingo a Estados Unidos.

records.headline: The Salt Lake Tribune reports Senate speeches on foreign policy
records.summary_en: The Salt Lake Tribune reports Senate speeches on foreign policy, highlighting addresses by Senators Money and Heyburn. Senator Money argued that the United States has no sufficient concern in Santo Domingo to warrant its intervention, maintained that the President had exceeded executive powers, and pointed out conflicting justifications offered by the administration and its allies. While Money insisted that the Senate must guard its constitutional authority, Senator Heyburn spoke before the chamber in support of annexing Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: The Salt Lake Tribune informa sobre intervenciones en el Senado acerca de la política exterior, destacando los discursos de los senadores Money y Heyburn. El senador Money sostuvo que Estados Unidos no tiene interés suficiente en Santo Domingo que justifique su intervención, afirmó que el presidente se había extralimitado en sus facultades ejecutivas y señaló las justificaciones contradictorias ofrecidas por la administración y sus aliados. Mientras Money insistía en que el Senado debe preservar su autoridad constitucional, el senador Heyburn habló ante el pleno en apoyo a la anexión de Santo Domingo.

records.headline: An editorial in The Billings Gazette supports Senator Heyburn's proposal
records.summary_en: An editorial in The Billings Gazette supports Senator Heyburn's proposal to annex Santo Domingo, noting that General Grant similarly pursued annexation while president before the Senate rejected the measure. The editorial argues that geographical proximity dictates that the island should belong to the United States and warns that Dominican independence will remain an enduring source of friction. It depicts the Dominican people as temperamentally unsuited for self-government, claiming that power-seeking demagogues continuously foment revolutions to plunder the national treasury.
records.summary_es: Un editorial en The Billings Gazette apoya la propuesta del senador Heyburn de anexar Santo Domingo, recordando que el general Grant promovió igualmente la anexión cuando fue presidente antes de que el Senado rechazara la medida. El editorial argumenta que la cercanía geográfica determina que la isla deba pertenecer a Estados Unidos y advierte que la independencia dominicana seguirá siendo un motivo constante de fricción. Describe al pueblo dominicano como temperamentalmente incapaz para el autogobierno, alegando que demagogos ávidos de poder fomentan continuas revoluciones para saquear el tesoro nacional.

records.headline: The News and Herald reports heated debate in the United States Senate
records.summary_en: The News and Herald reports heated debate in the United States Senate over Dominican policy, led by Senator Money, who declared that he cared nothing for Santo Domingo and concurred with Senator Lodge that annexation was undesirable. Money warned that absorbing overseas territories and inferior populations would cause the republic to sink of its own weight unless the form of government changed. In response, a senator identified as Mr. Hepburn advocated annexation by arguing the inhabitants would become Americanized and ultimately supplanted by whites, leading Senator Tillman to remark ironically that negotiations could proceed with the Dominican president currently harbored in American territory.
records.summary_es: The News and Herald relata un acalorado debate en el Senado de Estados Unidos sobre la política hacia Santo Domingo, encabezado por el senador Money, quien declaró que no le importaba en lo absoluto Santo Domingo y coincidió con el senador Lodge en que la anexión era indeseable. Money advirtió que absorber territorios de ultramar y poblaciones inferiores haría sucumbir a la república por su propio peso a menos que se cambiara la forma de gobierno. En respuesta, un senador identificado como el señor Hepburn defendió la anexión aduciendo que los habitantes se americanizarían y finalmente serían reemplazados por blancos, lo que llevó al senador Tillman a comentar irónicamente que se podría negociar con el presidente dominicano actualmente refugiado en territorio estadounidense.

records.summary_en: The Dominican gunboat Indopencla arrived from Barahona with troops dispatched there to restore tranquility, a dispatch from San Domingo in The Courier-Journal announces. Insurgents at Barahona recently surrendered after accepting terms and guarantees tendered by the Dominican government. With government forces having seized the rebels' weapons and munitions, the report asserts that the entire republic is at peace and that further disturbances are unlikely for some time.

records.headline: The Evening Star reports that General Neney, commanding a numerous body of troops
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reports that General Neney, commanding a numerous body of troops, attacked and seized the Haitian border town of Dajabon. Neney is described as a staunch supporter of former President General Jimenez, and his insurrection is widely regarded as an effort to restore Jimenez and prevent the Dominican government from holding scheduled elections. In Washington, Secretary of State Root received a naval cable from Commander Southerland at Monte Cristi describing the uprising as a small force at Dajabon and reassuring that no danger exists if the de facto government takes prompt action.

Se describe a Neney como un firme partidario del expresidente general Jiménez, y se considera que su insurrección busca restablecer a Jiménez e impedir que el gobierno dominicano celebre las elecciones previstas. En Washington, el secretario de Estado Root recibió un cable naval del comandante Southerland desde Monte Cristi en el que califica el levantamiento como una pequeña fuerza en Dajabón y asegura que no existe peligro si el gobierno de facto actúa con rapidez.

records.summary_en: Rumors of a major uprising at Monte Cristi are dismissed in a San Domingo dispatch in The San Francisco Call, reporting that the country is exceptionally tranquil. It explains that the skirmish at Dajabon was initiated by a small band of outlaws who were repulsed in their bid to take the town and fled into the mountains under pursuit by government forces. With President Caceres having retracted his resignation, the dispatch portrays the political situation as highly satisfactory and free from revolutionary threats.

Habiendo retirado el presidente Cáceres su renuncia, el despacho describe la situación política como muy satisfactoria y libre de amenazas revolucionarias.

General Neney, leading a sizable force, attacked and captured the border town of Dajabon. Neney is identified as an adherent of former President General Jiminez, and the offensive is understood to support Jiminez's return while disrupting forthcoming government elections.

Se identifica a Neney como partidario del expresidente general Jimenes, y se entiende que la ofensiva busca respaldar el regreso de Jimenes e impedir las próximas elecciones del gobierno.

records.headline: The Milk River Valley News outlines recent Dominican political factions
records.summary_en: The Milk River Valley News outlines recent Dominican political factions under the heading "Recent Revolutionary History," distinguishing the rival Jiminista and Horacista movements. The Jiministas, comprising largely illiterate masses loyal to exiled former President General Jiminez, direct anti-administration operations against Carlos Morales from British-controlled Turk's Island using Clyde Line steamers Cherokee and Seminole. Conversely, the Horacistas, led by former President Horacio Vasquez and drawing from the educated classes, rely on civilian leader Emiliano Tejera and General Ramon Caceres, the faction's idolized military chief.
records.summary_es: El Milk River Valley News describe las facciones políticas dominicanas recientes bajo el epígrafe "Historia revolucionaria reciente", distinguiendo entre los movimientos rivales jimenista y horacista. Los jimenistas, formados en gran parte por masas analfabetas leales al expresidente general Jimenes en el exilio, dirigen operaciones contra la administración de Carlos Morales desde la isla de Turcas, bajo dominio británico, utilizando los vapores Cherokee y Seminole de la Clyde Line. En contraste, los horacistas, liderados por el expresidente Horacio Vásquez y nutridos de las clases letradas, se apoyan en el dirigente civil Emiliano Tejera y en el general Ramón Cáceres, el idolatrado jefe militar de la facción.

records.headline: The role of Demetrio Rodriguez, the local chief of Monte Christi
records.summary_en: The role of Demetrio Rodriguez, the local chief of Monte Christi, in Dominican political strife is examined in a feature in the Milk River Valley News. After prolonged conflict, President Morales conciliated Rodriguez by assigning him the revenues of the Monte Christi customhouse. However, when the United States dispatched a cruiser to take armed control of the customhouse under the arbitral "laudo" favoring the Santo Domingo Improvement Company, Rodriguez resumed revolutionary plotting in Monte Christi, located across the bay from the railway terminal of Puerto Plata.
records.summary_es: El papel de Demetrio Rodríguez, el caudillo de Monte Cristi, en las luchas políticas dominicanas es examinado en un artículo especial en el Milk River Valley News. Tras un prolongado conflicto, el presidente Morales concilió a Rodríguez asignándole los ingresos de la aduana de Monte Cristi. No obstante, cuando Estados Unidos despachó un crucero para tomar control armado de la aduana bajo el "laudo" arbitral a favor de la Santo Domingo Improvement Company, Rodríguez reanudó las conspiraciones revolucionarias en Monte Cristi, situada al alcance del terminal ferroviario de Puerto Plata.

records.headline: The political standing of General Ramon Caceres, the Horacista leader
records.summary_en: The political standing of General Ramon Caceres, the Horacista leader who became a hero to his supporters after fatally shooting the dictator General Ulysses Heureaux, is outlined in a feature article in The Western News. Caceres is identified as a brother-in-law of Horacio Vasquez and a relation of Francisco Leonte Vasquez, formerly Dominican consul general in New York under Morales. Following Morales's rise over rival factions, Caceres entered the government as Vice President and Minister of the Interior, establishing his base in Santiago to control unrest along the north coast while Morales held executive authority in the capital city of Santo Domingo.

Tras el ascenso de Morales sobre las facciones rivales, Cáceres ingresó al gobierno como vicepresidente y ministro de lo Interior, estableciendo su sede en Santiago para controlar los disturbios en la costa norte mientras Morales ejercía la autoridad ejecutiva en la ciudad capital de Santo Domingo.

records.headline: Special correspondence in The Grit-Advocate depicts conditions
records.summary_en: Special correspondence in The Grit-Advocate depicts conditions across San Domingo, noting that rural inhabitants dwell in palm-thatched huts and cultivate yams, plantains, cacao, or tobacco. The writer challenges popular estimates of San Domingo's population at 600,000, arguing that half that number would be closer to the truth, while observing that Haiti has four or five times as many people. From an international standpoint, the report highlights Samana Bay as the country's greatest asset, describing it as a magnificent harbor offering immense strategic value as the key to the Caribbean Sea in light of the Panama canal.
records.summary_es: Una correspondencia especial en The Grit-Advocate describe las condiciones de San Domingo, señalando que los habitantes del campo habitan en chozas techadas con palmas y cultivan ñames, plátanos, cacao o tabaco. El autor pone en duda las estimaciones populares que sitúan la población de San Domingo en 600.000 habitantes, alegando que la mitad de esa cifra se aproximaría más a la verdad, al tiempo que observa que Haití cuenta con cuatro o cinco veces más habitantes. Desde una perspectiva internacional, el informe resalta la bahía de Samaná como el mayor activo del país, describiéndola como un puerto magnífico de inmenso valor estratégico y la clave del mar Caribe a la luz del canal de Panamá.

records.headline: A feature article in The Kendrick Gazette reviews General Ramon Caceres's leadership of the Horacista faction
records.summary_en: A feature article in The Kendrick Gazette reviews General Ramon Caceres's leadership of the Horacista faction after killing the dictator General Ulysses Heureaux, who had governed San Domingo with an iron rod. The article notes that Caceres is a brother-in-law of Horacio Vasquez and related to Francisco Leonte Vasquez, formerly Dominican consul general in New York under the Morales administration. By aligning with Morales, Caceres secured the offices of Vice President and Minister of the Interior, remaining in Santiago to monitor unrest across the interior and the north coast while Morales governed from the capital city of Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: Un artículo en The Kendrick Gazette pasa revista al liderazgo del general Ramón Cáceres al frente de la facción horacista tras dar muerte al dictador general Ulises Heureaux, quien había gobernado San Domingo con vara de hierro. El artículo señala que Cáceres es cuñado de Horacio Vásquez y pariente de Francisco Leonte Vásquez, quien fuera cónsul general dominicano en Nueva York bajo el gobierno de Morales. Al aliarse con Morales, Cáceres asumió los cargos de vicepresidente y ministro de lo Interior, permaneciendo en Santiago para vigilar la agitación en el interior y la costa norte mientras Morales gobernaba desde la ciudad capital de Santo Domingo.

records.headline: A Santo Domingo dispatch in The Providence News reports on the overthrow of President Morales
records.summary_en: A Santo Domingo dispatch in The Providence News reports on the overthrow of President Morales and the elevation of former vice president General Ramon Caceres to the executive office. The correspondent states that few citizens understood the true gravity of events, as no official account had been published and prevailing rumors proved misleading. The arrival of three United States warships—the Olympia, the Des Moines, and the Scorpion—prompted fears that guns would be turned on the capital, though bloodshed was averted through composed leadership before an angry mob.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Santo Domingo en The Providence News informa sobre el derrocamiento del presidente Morales y el ascenso del exvicepresidente general Ramón Cáceres a la jefatura del ejecutivo. El corresponsal manifiesta que pocos ciudadanos comprendieron la verdadera gravedad de los sucesos, dado que no se había publicado ninguna versión oficial y los rumores dominantes resultaban equívocos. La presencia de tres buques de guerra estadounidenses —el Olympia, el Des Moines y el Scorpion— despertó temores de que sus cañones apuntaran hacia la capital, aunque el derramamiento de sangre se evitó mediante un liderazgo sereno frente a una multitud enardecida.

records.headline: A dispatch in The New York Herald reports that President Caceres
records.summary_en: A dispatch in The New York Herald reports that President Caceres has temporarily postponed his intended resignation after learning of a border revolt in Monte Cristi province led by General Navarro. The provincial governor took the field with troops to confront Navarro, who reportedly commands only about thirty-five men and is driven primarily by plans to engage in large-scale smuggling. Caceres is anticipated to remain in office through the opening of the Chamber's legislative session, while foreign observers remark that former dictator Heureaux represents the only type of ruler capable of governing the country.
records.summary_es: Un despacho en The New York Herald informa que el presidente Cáceres ha postergado temporalmente su renuncia prevista tras conocerse un levantamiento fronterizo en la provincia de Monte Cristi encabezado por el general Navarro. El gobernador provincial se puso en marcha con tropas para enfrentar a Navarro, quien según informes solo cuenta con unos treinta y cinco hombres y persigue principalmente dedicarse al contrabando en gran escala. Se prevé que Cáceres continúe en el cargo durante la apertura del período de sesiones de la Cámara, mientras que observadores extranjeros comentan que el exdictador Heureaux representa el único perfil de gobernante capaz de regir el país.

records.headline: A dispatch illustrates former president Heureaux's strong methods with the example of horsemen who shot at the glass
records.summary_en: A dispatch illustrates former president Heureaux's strong methods with the example of horsemen who shot at the glass insulators of the telegraph line between Puerto Plata and Santiago: Heureaux decreed that whoever indulged in the sport should be shot. It also reports that Ricardo Limardo resigned last week as Governor of Puerto Plata after finding the principal posts under him were to be filled at the dictation of a military officer with men he judged unfit, and his protests were ignored.
records.summary_es: Un despacho ilustra los métodos enérgicos del expresidente Heureaux con el ejemplo de los jinetes que disparaban a los aisladores de cristal de la línea telegráfica entre Puerto Plata y Santiago: Heureaux decretó que quien se entregara a ese deporte sería fusilado. También informa que Ricardo Limardo renunció la semana pasada como gobernador de Puerto Plata tras descubrir que los principales cargos bajo su mando serían ocupados por imposición de un oficial militar con hombres que él juzgaba incapaces, y que sus protestas fueron ignoradas.
records.passage: into execution. Heureaux's Strong Methods. Heureaux's methods may be judged by one or two examples. When the telegraph was strung between Puerto Plata and Santiago it used to amuse passing horsemen to shoot at the glass knobs to the detriment of the service. When Heureaux learned of the practice he decreed that whoever indulged in the sport should be shot. It is interesting to note that when Ricardo Limardo announced his resignation as Governor of Puerto Plata last week the two persons who had been very prominent in the revolution deemed it wise to expatriate themselves, on the theory that the pledges of immunity which Limardo would not violate might not hold good under a successor. Governor Limardo's resignation illustrates the danger of a partisan administration. He has been a consistent Horacist, believing that to be the party representing honesty in politics. After taking office he found that the principal positions under him were to be filled at the dictation of a military officer and in his judgment the men named were notoriously unfit for the duties assigned to them. As his protests were ignored he decided to resign. Few men have more personal friends than he and the administration can hardly afford to lose many such supporters. New President of Brazil. records.headline: A correspondent in The New York Herald disputes references in the American press
records.summary_en: A correspondent in The New York Herald disputes references in the American press designating Santo Domingo as the 'Black Republic.' The author argues that the Dominican population descends predominantly from the indigenous inhabitants found by Columbus, mixed with Spanish blood, asserting that persons of African descent are confined largely to four or five coastal ports. Noting colloquial comparisons of native ancestry and comparing racial perceptions to the use of English in seaports, the writer uses these theories to explain why rural Dominicans are drawn into frequent revolutions.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal en The New York Herald refuta las menciones en la prensa estadounidense que denominan a Santo Domingo como la 'República Negra'. El autor sostiene que la población dominicana desciende predominantemente de los habitantes indígenas encontrados por Colón, mezclados con sangre española, afirmando que las personas de ascendencia africana se concentran casi exclusivamente en cuatro o cinco puertos costeros. Al señalar expresiones populares sobre la ascendencia nativa y comparar las percepciones raciales con el uso del inglés en los puertos marítimos, el redactor se vale de estas teorías para explicar por qué los dominicanos del interior se ven arrastrados a frecuentes revoluciones.
