records.headline: Mineral treasures in Santo Domingo are reported on by an observer
records.summary_en: Mineral treasures in Santo Domingo are reported on by an observer in an article concluding in The New York Herald, stating that women washing gold in wooden bowls recovered garnets, amethysts, emeralds, and diamonds. The writer relates that the largest diamond among the crown jewels of Spain was discovered in the River Verde between Santiago de los Caballeros and La Vega. Reflecting on the republic's condition, the correspondent attributes its retarded development to foreign investors' neglect and ignorance of its natural resources alongside local factors.
records.summary_es: Los tesoros minerales en Santo Domingo son informados por un observador en un artículo que concluye en The New York Herald, afirmando que mujeres que lavaban oro en bateas recuperaron granates, amatistas, esmeraldas y diamantes. El autor relata que el diamante más grande de las joyas de la corona de España se descubrió en el río Verde, entre Santiago de los Caballeros y La Vega. Al reflexionar sobre la situación de la república, el corresponsal atribuye su rezagado desarrollo a la negligencia y el desconocimiento de los recursos naturales por parte de los inversionistas extranjeros, junto con factores locales.

records.headline: 'Rebels killed in Santo Domingo': Nené Cepín, one-armed revolutionary general, and six followers were killed at Guayubín
records.summary_en: 'Rebels killed in Santo Domingo': Nené Cepín, one-armed revolutionary general, and six followers were killed at Guayubín, where he had gone to confer with Governor Camacho of Monte Cristi after taking the field in the Dajabón smuggling district.
records.summary_es: «Rebeldes muertos en Santo Domingo»: Nené Cepín, general revolucionario manco, y seis seguidores fueron muertos en Guayubín, adonde había ido a conferenciar con el gobernador Camacho de Monte Cristi tras alzarse en la zona de contrabando de Dajabón.
records.passage: Cepin was one of the most noted revolutionists in the island. He took sides with Morales in the last outbreak. After the latter's defeat he received guaranty of safety, but with Navarro, took the field in the Monte Christi district with a small party, presumably to assist smugglers at Dajabon, on the Haitian frontier. No duties ever had been paid at Dajabon, tho large quantities of merchandise are received by the customs officers. Cepin visited the town and declared all goods there contraband. While Cepin and his party were fighting many goods were removed inland. After negotiations lasting some days Cepin and Navarro agreed to lay down arms. Cepin was promised the office of military commandant at Dajabon. He went to Guanyubin on a friendly visit to arrange terms. 24th Annual Reduced-Price Sale. The Great Plymouth Clothing House. MILLIONAIRE'S SON TO BECOME A CLERK. Journal Special Service. Chicago, March 10. — Stuyvesant Fish, president of the Illinois Central railroad, and his son, Stuyvesant Fish, Jr., are in Chicago. The son has announced his intention of taking a clerkship in the Illinois Central offices at $60 a month. He purposes to learn the railroad business from the ground up. Young Mr. Fish arrived from New York with his father in a palatial private car. He put up in one of the finest suites on the parlor floor of the Annex and took breakfast yesterday at the Chicago club. This is not the usual program of a working man.

records.headline: A feature in The New York Herald reports on the intervention of Mrs. Reader
records.summary_en: A feature in The New York Herald reports on the intervention of Mrs. Reader, who claims authority to resolve the Dominican financial crisis outside the influence of the Jiminezist, Horacist, or Morales-Caceres factions. Interviewed at her Wall Street office, Mrs. Reader explained that she was letting Secretary of State Root do the talking, having sent him a certified copy of credentials from the 'Central Patriotic Committee of Monte Cristi.' Her formal notification claims powers to seek international recognition for the committee and announces plans to call an international committee regarding Dominican foreign debts.
records.summary_es: Un reportaje en The New York Herald informa sobre la intervención de la señora Reader, quien afirma tener autoridad para resolver la crisis financiera dominicana al margen de las facciones jimenista, horacista o de Morales y Cáceres. Entrevistada en su oficina de Wall Street, la señora Reader explicó que dejaba hablar al secretario de Estado Root, habiéndole enviado una copia certificada de credenciales del 'Comité Patriótico Central de Monte Cristi'. Su notificación formal asegura tener poderes para buscar el reconocimiento internacional del comité y anuncia planes para convocar una comisión internacional sobre las deudas externas dominicanas.

records.headline: Mrs. Ella Rawls Reader's persistent involvement in Dominican affairs
records.summary_en: Mrs. Ella Rawls Reader's persistent involvement in Dominican affairs is reviewed in an article in The New York Herald, following the thwarting of her earlier plans, which included proposing the sale of Samana Bay to the United States to settle foreign debts. The dispatch notes that following the implementation of the customs modus vivendi, a revolution ousted President Morales and placed Ramon Caceres in temporary custody of the palace, leaving revenue control disputed among Morales, Caceres, and General Jimenez. In the meantime, Mrs. Reader is considering travel to Santo Domingo, though associates express concern that rivals could plant dynamite with clockwork detonators aboard her vessel.
records.summary_es: La continua participación de la señora Ella Rawls Reader en los asuntos dominicanos es examinada en un artículo en The New York Herald, tras el fracaso de sus planes anteriores, que incluían proponer la venta de la bahía de Samaná a los Estados Unidos para saldar deudas exteriores. El despacho señala que, tras la aplicación del modus vivendi aduanero, una revolución despojó del poder al presidente Morales y entregó el palacio a la custodia temporal de Ramón Cáceres, dejando el control de los ingresos en disputa entre Morales, Cáceres y el general Jiménez. Mientras tanto, la señora Reader evalúa viajar a Santo Domingo, aunque sus allegados temen que rivales coloquen dinamita con detonadores de relojería a bordo de su embarcación.

records.headline: The envisioned pacification of Santo Domingo is portrayed in a satirical feature
records.summary_en: The envisioned pacification of Santo Domingo is portrayed in a satirical feature in The New York Herald, once Mrs. Reader takes charge as the representative of the Central Committee of Patriotic Citizens of Monte Cristi. Under the section heading 'President Not Yet Chosen,' the report describes how partisan factions will surrender weapons at polling places, enabling Mrs. Reader and the Dominican populace to select a consensus president without interference from the incumbent executive. Following the inauguration, the narrative envisions arms smugglers being imprisoned, typewriters deployed to issue declarations, and Mrs. Reader personally supervising customs revenue tallies.
records.summary_es: La proyectada pacificación de Santo Domingo es retratada en un artículo satírico en The New York Herald, una vez que la señora Reader tome el mando como representante del Comité Central de Ciudadanos Patriotas de Monte Cristi. Bajo el acápite 'Aún no se ha elegido presidente', la crónica relata cómo las facciones partidistas depondrán sus armas ante las mesas de votación, permitiendo que la señora Reader y la población dominicana elijan a un presidente de consenso sin interferencias del mandatario en funciones. Tras la toma de posesión, el relato vislumbra el encarcelamiento de los contrabandistas de armas, el despliegue de máquinas de escribir para lanzar proclamas y a la propia señora Reader supervisando el recuento de los ingresos aduaneros.

records.headline: An article in The Providence News reports on credentials submitted
records.summary_en: An article in The Providence News reports on credentials submitted to the Secretary of State by Mrs. Reader, who claims authorization from the 'central patriotic committee of Monte Cristi' to represent Santo Domingo globally and reorganize its public finances. The notice announces her intention to convoke an international committee to address relations between the Dominican Republic and its foreign creditors. Commenting on her past career running a typewriting office in the city's Mills building, the piece compares her little-known Monte Cristi committee to legendary petitioners claiming to speak on behalf of an entire nation.
records.summary_es: Un artículo en The Providence News informa sobre las credenciales presentadas al secretario de Estado por la señora Reader, quien asegura contar con autorización del 'comité patriótico central de Monte Cristi' para representar a Santo Domingo en el mundo y reorganizar sus finanzas públicas. La notificación anuncia su intención de convocar una comisión internacional encargada de regular las relaciones entre la República Dominicana y sus acreedores externos. Al comentar su trayectoria anterior al frente de una oficina de mecanografía en el edificio Mills de la ciudad, el artículo equipara a su desconocido comité de Monte Cristi con peticionarios legendarios que pretendían hablar en nombre de toda una nación.

records.headline: The prolonged festivities of Dominican Independence Day, February 27
records.summary_en: The prolonged festivities of Dominican Independence Day, February 27, brought local economic hardship into sharp focus, special correspondence from Santo Domingo in The New York Herald reports. The dispatch notes that scarce employment, minimal currency circulation, and steep import duties on basic provisions—including rates based on $1 a quintal for rice, $3 for cod, $12 for lard, and 15 cents a gallon for kerosene—have driven up living costs and left laborers' homes virtually bare. Although prevailing conditions are depressed, observers note that Colonel George R. Colton has remitted nearly one million dollars to New York over the preceding ten months.
records.summary_es: Las prolongadas festividades del Día de la Independencia dominicana, el 27 de febrero, hicieron aún más evidentes las penurias económicas locales, según una correspondencia especial desde Santo Domingo en The New York Herald. El despacho relata que la escasez de empleo, la mínima circulación monetaria y los elevados gravámenes de importación sobre provisiones básicas —con bases arancelarias de 1 dólar por quintal para el arroz, 3 para el bacalao, 12 para la manteca y 15 centavos por galón para el queroseno— encarecieron el costo de vida y dejaron los hogares obreros prácticamente vacíos. Pese a la difícil situación reinante, observadores destacan que el coronel George R. Colton ha remitido casi un millón de dólares a Nueva York durante los diez meses precedentes.

records.headline: Racial commentary on Santo Domingo is offered in an article
records.summary_en: Racial commentary on Santo Domingo is offered in an article in The National Tribune, asserting that political instability stems from racial diversity and a perceived lack of unity. The author highlights Don Emiliano Tehera, termed the grand old man of the island, and Santiago Governor Miguel A. Roman as prominent figures consulted for guidance when factional disputes reach an impasse. Turning to the island's black population, the writer characterizes former ruler General Hereaux as a fearless, energetic tyrant whose forceful authority none of his successors has matched.
records.summary_es: Un comentario racial sobre Santo Domingo es ofrecido en un artículo en The National Tribune, afirmando que la inestabilidad política obedece a la diversidad racial y a una pretendida falta de unidad. El autor destaca a don Emiliano Tehera, denominado el gran anciano de la isla, y al gobernador de Santiago, Miguel A. Román, como figuras prominentes consultadas en busca de consejo cuando las disputas facciosas llegan a un callejón sin salida. Al referirse a la población negra de la isla, el redactor califica al exgobernante general Hereaux como un tirano intrépido y enérgico, cuya autoridad contundente no ha sido igualada por ninguno de sus sucesores.

records.headline: Herald correspondence from Santo Domingo, dated March 3, reports that General Ramon Caceres will not resign the presidency
records.summary_en: Herald correspondence from Santo Domingo, dated March 3, reports that General Ramon Caceres will not resign the presidency, because a change of administration would involve internal disturbances, and that the demand for him to remain was almost universal. His cousin Horacio Valdez, head of the Horacist party and the man in whose favor Caceres wished to withdraw, was the first to urge him to reconsider, and after petitions and a mass meeting in Columbus plaza a crowd marched to Caceres's house, where he told them he would postpone his resignation until the danger to the republic ceased, later issuing a public address accepting what he called the new sacrifice.
records.summary_es: Una correspondencia del Herald desde Santo Domingo, fechada el 3 de marzo, informa que el general Ramón Cáceres no renunciará a la presidencia, porque un cambio de administración implicaría disturbios internos, y que la demanda de que permaneciera fue casi universal. Su primo Horacio Valdez, jefe del partido horacista y la persona en cuyo favor Cáceres deseaba retirarse, fue el primero en instarlo a reconsiderarlo, y tras las peticiones y una reunión masiva en la plaza Colón una multitud marchó a la casa de Cáceres, donde les dijo que pospondría su renuncia hasta que cesara el peligro para la república, y después emitió un mensaje público aceptando lo que llamó el nuevo sacrificio.

records.headline: An analytical article in the Bonners Ferry Herald examines Dominican
records.summary_en: An analytical article in the Bonners Ferry Herald examines Dominican political unrest through the career of Rodriguez, the Monte Cristi chieftain who fought against Morales. After being conciliated with control of the Monte Cristi custom house, Rodriguez resumed revolutionary plotting when an American naval vessel seized the port under the arbitral award favoring the Santo Domingo Improvement Company. The dispatch also outlines the country's strategic terrain, explaining that northern revolts typically move from Monte Cristi or Puerto Plata against the Caceres base at Santiago before utilizing mountain passes to march against the capital city of Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: Un artículo analítico en el Bonners Ferry Herald examina las tensiones políticas dominicanas a través de la trayectoria de Rodríguez, el caudillo de Monte Cristi que combatió a Morales. Tras haber sido apaciguado con el control de la aduana de Monte Cristi, Rodríguez retomó las conspiraciones revolucionarias cuando un buque de guerra estadounidense se incautó del puerto en virtud del laudo arbitral a favor de la Santo Domingo Improvement Company. El despacho describe además la geografía estratégica del país, explicando que las revueltas norteñas avanzan típicamente desde Monte Cristi o Puerto Plata hacia el bastión de Cáceres en Santiago antes de utilizar los pasos de montaña para marchar contra la ciudad capital de Santo Domingo.

records.headline: Minor non-political disturbances continue in the countryside
records.summary_en: Minor non-political disturbances continue in the countryside while general peace prevails in populous districts, special correspondence from Santo Domingo in The New York Herald reports. General Carlos Ginebra, Minister of War and Navy, departed the capital for Barahona to collaborate with Governor General Zenon Ovando in quelling an uprising led by Candelario de la Rosa. The insurgency is characterized as strictly financial, ignited after Candelario was denied an anticipated payout from the national treasury overseen by Minister Federico Velazquez.
records.summary_es: Persisten disturbios menores no políticos en el campo si bien prevalece la paz general en los distritos poblados, según una correspondencia especial desde Santo Domingo en The New York Herald. El ministro de Guerra y Marina, general Carlos Ginebra, partió de la capital hacia Barahona para colaborar con el gobernador general Zenón Ovando en sofocar una revuelta encabezada por Candelario de la Rosa. La insurgencia se define como estrictamente financiera, desatada luego de que se negara a Candelario un pago previsto del tesoro nacional custodiado por el ministro Federico Velázquez.

records.headline: The New York Herald, in special correspondence from Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The New York Herald, in special correspondence from Santo Domingo, describes the grand official reception accorded to former president Horacio Vasquez, delegate to the Cibao, upon his arrival in the capital. President Caceres led five hundred horsemen twenty-five miles along the road toward La Vega to escort Vasquez, accompanied by musical bands, festive city decorations, and a seventeen-gun salute from the fort matched by the United States steamer Newport. The correspondent notes that although Caceres had previously intended to step aside in favor of Vasquez, the president has resolved to maintain his post as long as transition poses peril to the country.
records.summary_es: The New York Herald, en una correspondencia especial desde Santo Domingo, describe el gran recibimiento oficial brindado al expresidente Horacio Vásquez, delegado en el Cibao, a su llegada a la capital. El presidente Cáceres encabezó a quinientos jinetes a lo largo de veinticinco millas por el camino hacia La Vega para escoltar a Vásquez, entre bandas de música, adornos festivos en la ciudad y una salva de diecisiete cañonazos de la fortaleza correspondida por el vapor estadounidense Newport. El corresponsal observa que, aunque Cáceres tenía previsto apartarse en favor de Vásquez, el mandatario ha resuelto conservar su puesto mientras cualquier transición represente un peligro para el país.

records.headline: In a letter published by The New York Herald, Leonte G. Franco rejects
records.summary_en: In a letter published by The New York Herald, Leonte G. Franco rejects Mrs. Reader's schemes for Santo Domingo, characterizing them as fanciful illusions that will be viewed by Dominicans like the 'Arabian Nights.' Franco acknowledges the need for political and financial reforms but insists that the republic is capable of resolving its internal challenges without the interference of foreign politicians. He emphasizes that the country requires foreign capital to develop its rich mineral resources and fertile soil, cautioning that outsiders who travel there to foment revolution will face prosecution as disturbers of public order.
records.summary_es: En una carta publicada por The New York Herald, Leonte G. Franco rechaza los planes de la señora Reader para Santo Domingo, calificándolos de ilusiones extravagantes que los dominicanos verán como 'Las mil y una noches'. Franco reconoce la necesidad de reformas políticas y financieras, pero insiste en que la república es capaz de resolver sus dificultades internas sin la intromisión de políticos extranjeros. Subraya que el país requiere capital foráneo para explotar sus ricos recursos minerales y su suelo fértil, advirtiendo que los forasteros que viajen allí a fomentar revoluciones serán procesados como perturbadores del orden público.

records.headline: Insurgent leader Candelario de la Rosa has crossed into Haiti
records.summary_en: Insurgent leader Candelario de la Rosa has crossed into Haiti under the guidance of two Dominican officers, special correspondence from Santo Domingo in The New York Herald reports, with the government receiving a telegram announcing his arrival at Port-au-Prince. His chief lieutenant, Manuel Torres, was taken to the Barahona cemetery and executed by shooting, ending disturbances along the southwestern frontier. The report notes that Candelario left the republic without a dollar of official funds, having engaged in persistent local warfare against changing administrations—including the recent Morales revolution—primarily to obtain money for his followers and himself before quitting.
records.summary_es: El líder insurgente Candelario de la Rosa cruzó hacia Haití bajo la guía de dos oficiales dominicanos, según una correspondencia especial desde Santo Domingo en The New York Herald, recibiendo el gobierno un telegrama que anunció su llegada a Puerto Príncipe. Su principal lugarteniente, Manuel Torres, fue conducido al cementerio de Barahona y ejecutado por fusilamiento, poniendo fin a los disturbios a lo largo de la frontera suroccidental. La crónica señala que Candelario abandonó la república sin un solo dólar de fondos oficiales, habiendo librado una rebelión constante frente a sucesivas administraciones —incluida la reciente revolución de Morales— principalmente para conseguir dinero para sus seguidores y para sí mismo antes de deponer las armas.

records.summary_en: Cable dispatches received at the State and Navy Departments indicate that a serious condition of affairs exists in Santo Domingo. The captain of the port of Puerto Plata was shot and killed during an insurrectionary movement, while the provincial governor defied the general government and barricaded the town, alongside reports of fighting near Santo Domingo City. The Dominican gunboat Independencia has anchored off Puerto Plata, and its commander, Captain Catrain, has threatened to bombard the town unless it surrenders within twenty-four hours to the legitimate government of President Morales.

records.headline: Writing editorially, the New-York Tribune strongly commends
records.summary_en: Writing editorially, the New-York Tribune strongly commends official efforts to suppress the smuggling of contraband munitions of war into the Dominican Republic. The editorial argues that the reprobation previously directed at illicit trade with Cuba must be applied with equal vigor to Santo Domingo and Haiti, calling it both wicked and foolish for Americans to assist insurrections or tolerate filibustering operations by refugees. It distinguishes these recurring Caribbean uprisings from the Cuban revolution, describing Dominican conflicts not as righteous struggles against oppression, but as recurring rivalries between ambitious politicians and military dictators.
records.summary_es: En un artículo editorial, el New-York Tribune elogia firmemente los esfuerzos oficiales para reprimir el contrabando de municiones de guerra hacia la República Dominicana. El editorial sostiene que la reprobación dirigida con anterioridad al comercio ilícito con Cuba debe aplicarse con igual vigor a Santo Domingo y Haití, calificando de perverso e insensato que los estadounidenses apoyen insurrecciones o toleren operaciones filibusteras de refugiados. Asimismo, distingue estos recurrentes alzamientos caribeños de la revolución cubana, describiendo los conflictos dominicanos no como luchas legítimas contra la opresión, sino como rivalidades recurrentes entre políticos ambiciosos y dictadores militares.

records.summary_en: According to dispatches received at the Navy Department from Commander Southerland of the Yankee at Santo Domingo, more trouble has broken out in Santo Domingo at Samana. Southerland's cablegram announced that another revolution has broken out, the Dubuque is on the scene, and American interests are not involved. Dominican Minister Joubert called upon Secretary Root at the State Department but possessed no independent news regarding the outbreak, which is not regarded as serious despite the government's historical difficulty in firmly establishing authority in that northern quarter.

board of the National Council of Wom

records.summary_en: In an interview published in the New-York Tribune, Mrs. Perry discusses her past financial and political backing of a Dominican revolutionary expedition. She denies contributing $250,000, stating her monetary support was much smaller and nearer to $300, alongside using influence in Washington. She recounts that the expedition sailed on the steamship Fanita in May (given in print as 18%.) to Monte Cristi, where the governor was captured, but President Heureaux met the landing party and General Morales, whom she backed, was shot and killed. Following Morales's death, she severed ties with General Jiménez's expedition, adding that her former name, Mrs. Fisher, surfaced in court because she had loaned $2000 on a sealed envelope containing the revolutionary contract disputed by Mr. Cunningham.
records.summary_es: En una entrevista publicada en el New-York Tribune, la señora Perry aborda el respaldo financiero y político que brindó en el pasado a una expedición revolucionaria dominicana. Niega haber aportado 250.000 dólares y afirma que su contribución monetaria fue mucho menor y más próxima a los 300 dólares, además de haber recurrido a influencias en Washington. Relata que la expedición zarpó en el vapor Fanita en mayo rumbo a Monte Cristi, donde el gobernador fue capturado, pero el presidente Heureaux enfrentó al contingente de desembarco y el general Morales, a quien ella respaldaba, murió por disparos. Tras la muerte de Morales, rompió todo vínculo con la expedición del general Jiménez, añadiendo que su antiguo nombre, señora Fisher, surgió en los tribunales debido a que había prestado 2.000 dólares sobre un sobre lacrado que contenía el contrato revolucionario demandado por el señor Cunningham.

records.summary_en: Former President Morales is at the head of a formidable revolutionary movement being organized among Dominican refugees in Porto Rico, preparing to sweep into the northern part of Santo Domingo with a large force, aided by Sanchez, his former minister of foreign affairs. Advices received at the State Department indicate a revolution brewing that could be greater than any disturbance since the American customs receivership was first inaugurated, and the Navy will take precautions to protect American interests.
records.summary_es: El expresidente Morales está al frente de un formidable movimiento revolucionario que se organiza entre refugiados dominicanos en Puerto Rico, preparándose para invadir la parte norte de Santo Domingo con una fuerza numerosa, ayudado por Sánchez, su exministro de Relaciones Exteriores. Informes recibidos en el Departamento de Estado indican que se gesta una revolución que podría ser mayor que cualquier disturbio desde que se inauguró la receptoría aduanera estadounidense, y la Armada tomará precauciones para proteger los intereses estadounidenses.

records.headline: Naval authorities have granted full discretion to Commander Southerland of the Yankee
records.summary_en: Naval authorities have granted full discretion to Commander Southerland of the Yankee to enforce neutrality laws along the Dominican coast, a dispatch in the Twice-a-Week Plain Dealer states. The concentration of American warships at Dominican ports, particularly near Monte Cristi where rebels are reported in nearby mountains, indicates that Southerland is acting strictly to prevent the landing of munitions of war. Former president Jiminez is taking an active role in these movements and has addressed several letters to Secretary Root arguing that his party should be allowed to regain control of the Dominican government unimpeded. Dispatches from Puerto Rico's acting governor note that Jiminez is being closely watched there, while munitions destined for an expedition against Santo Domingo are being shipped from St. Thomas, British West Indies, to a location called Ba Jabon near the Dominican boundary.
records.summary_es: Las autoridades navales otorgaron plenas facultades al comandante Southerland del Yankee para aplicar las leyes de neutralidad a lo largo de la costa dominicana, señala un despacho en el Twice-a-Week Plain Dealer. La concentración de buques de guerra estadounidenses en puertos dominicanos, especialmente cerca de Monte Cristi donde se reporta la presencia de rebeldes en las montañas próximas, indica que Southerland actúa con rigor para impedir el desembarco de municiones bélicas. El expresidente Jiminez desempeña un papel activo en estos movimientos y ha enviado varias cartas al secretario Root argumentando que debe permitirse a su partido recuperar el control del gobierno dominicano sin trabas. Avisos del gobernador interino de Puerto Rico señalan que Jiminez es vigilado de cerca allí, mientras que se están embarcando municiones destinadas a una expedición contra Santo Domingo desde St. Thomas, Indias Occidentales Británicas, hacia un lugar denominado Ba Jabon, cerca de la frontera dominicana.

records.headline: The Evening Star reports that Dominican insurgents led by Mauricio Jimenez attacked
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reports that Dominican insurgents led by Mauricio Jimenez attacked Guayubin, killed town commander General Mongo, and retreated into the interior. Revolutionists acting on behalf of former president General Isidoro Jimenez have cut all telegraphic communication between Monte Cristi and Santiago de los Caballeros, joined by partisans of his predecessor, General Morales. The uprising is believed to confirm that a schooner carrying arms and ammunition from St. Thomas succeeded in landing its cargo between Puerto Plata and Monte Cristi.
records.summary_es: El Evening Star informa que insurgentes dominicanos liderados por Mauricio Jiménez atacaron Guayubín, mataron al comandante de la plaza, general Mongo, y se retiraron hacia el interior. Revolucionarios alzados en favor del expresidente general Isidoro Jiménez cortaron toda comunicación telegráfica entre Monte Cristi y Santiago de los Caballeros, sumándose a ellos partidarios de su predecesor, el general Morales. Se cree que el levantamiento confirma que una goleta con armas y municiones procedente de St. Thomas logró desembarcar su cargamento entre Puerto Plata y Monte Cristi.

records.summary_en: An account in the Arizona Republican describes a rebel attack on Guayubin that left town commander General Mongo dead before the insurgents retired into the interior. Telegraphic lines connecting Monte Cristi and Santiago de los Caballeros were cut by revolutionists rising in support of former president General Isidoro Jiminez, joined by partisans of General Morales, the predecessor of President General Caceres. The outbreak indicates that a schooner loaded with arms and ammunition from St. Thomas successfully landed its cargo along the northern Dominican coast between Puerto Plata and Monte Cristi.

El estallido indica que una goleta cargada con armas y municiones procedente de St. Thomas desembarcó con éxito su cargamento a lo largo de la costa norte dominicana entre Puerto Plata y Monte Cristi.

records.headline: Contraband arms were landed between Puerto Plata and Monte Cristi
records.summary_en: Contraband arms were landed between Puerto Plata and Monte Cristi by a schooner from St. Thomas, an uprising on the northern Dominican coast suggests, a report in The Salt Lake Herald notes. Meanwhile, a New York dispatch quoting the Tribune reports that Dominican Consul General Fabio Fiallo denied rumors of an insurrection in his country, asserting that no rebellion was likely. Fiallo declared that the only military chiefs opposing President Caceres who have any following are currently imprisoned. He characterized those seeking to depose the Dominican chief executive as adventurers scheming to seize the 1500000 deposited in the National City Bank for bond payments.

records.headline: Naval accidents are reviewed by Representative Weeks of Massachusetts
records.summary_en: Naval accidents are reviewed by Representative Weeks of Massachusetts, speaking before the House of Representatives, who notes that the U.S.S. Detroit ran aground twice while departing Puerto Plata on May 17, 1905. He states that the warship's captain was tried by court-martial and dismissed from the naval service following the Dominican harbor incident. The case is cited among naval mishaps that presumably should have been avoided, alongside other vessel losses due to natural disasters and navigational errors.

Afirma que el capitán del buque fue juzgado en consejo de guerra y expulsado del servicio naval tras el incidente en el puerto dominicano. El caso se cita entre los percances navales que debieron haberse evitado, junto con otras pérdidas de embarcaciones causadas por desastres naturales y errores de navegación.

records.headline: A naval movement column in the New-York Tribune details the stations
records.summary_en: A naval movement column in the New-York Tribune details the stations and departures of United States warships in Dominican waters. On June 21, the gunboat Paducah was stationed at Macoris, while the Dubuque sailed from Macoris and arrived at Santo Domingo City. On June 22, the Scorpion was reported at Monte Cristi after sailing from Puerto Plata, and the Nashville departed Santo Domingo City bound for San Juan.
records.summary_es: Una columna de movimientos navales en el New-York Tribune detalla las estaciones y salidas de buques de guerra de Estados Unidos en aguas dominicanas. El 21 de junio, el cañonero Paducah se hallaba fondeado en Macorís, mientras que el Dubuque zarpó de Macorís y arribó a la ciudad de Santo Domingo. El 22 de junio, se informó del Scorpion en Monte Cristi tras haber zarpado de Puerto Plata, y el Nashville partió de la ciudad de Santo Domingo con destino a San Juan.

records.headline: General Berroa, an exiled opponent of President Ramon Caceres
records.summary_en: General Berroa, an exiled opponent of President Ramon Caceres, has arrived in New York, an Associated Press dispatch in the San Antonio Daily Light reports. Berroa, formerly governor of Macoris, had just arrived from Turks Island following imprisonment, and stated that the Dominican insurrection is growing daily and will overthrow the Caceres government. Announcing a meeting of opposition leaders in New York next month, he described conditions in Santo Domingo as terrible, citing daily political executions, packed jails, denial of constitutional rights, starvation, and suppressed suffrage. Calling the revolution a Christian uprising against barbarism, Berroa stated that while American guarantees of free elections would end the rebellion, insurgents are compelled to protest with arms.
records.summary_es: El general Berroa, opositor exiliado del presidente Ramón Cáceres, ha llegado a Nueva York, según un despacho de la Associated Press en el San Antonio Daily Light. Berroa, quien fuera gobernador de Macorís, acababa de llegar de las islas Turcas tras sufrir prisión, y declaró que la insurrección dominicana cobra fuerza a diario y derrocará al gobierno de Cáceres. Al anunciar una reunión de dirigentes de la oposición en Nueva York para el próximo mes, describió las condiciones en Santo Domingo como terribles, citando ejecuciones políticas cotidianas, prisiones repletas, privación de derechos constitucionales, hambruna y supresión del sufragio. Al calificar la revolución como un levantamiento cristiano contra la barbarie, Berroa afirmó que, aunque las garantías estadounidenses de elecciones libres pondrían fin a la rebelión, los insurgentes se ven obligados a protestar con las armas.

records.headline: In a New York interview in the Americus Times-Recorder, General Q. Berroa discusses
records.summary_en: In a New York interview in the Americus Times-Recorder, General Q. Berroa discusses the Dominican insurrection and plans for an opposition conference. Berroa, formerly governor of Macoris, arrived from exile on Turks Island and asserted that the insurrection against President Ramon Caceres is growing daily and will overthrow the regime. He announced an upcoming conference in New York between opposition leaders, including former presidents General Jeminez and General Morales, who have set aside their differences to cooperate, along with former vice president General des Champs and former foreign minister Dr. Francesco Sanchez. Denouncing conditions in Santo Domingo as terrible due to daily political killings, full jails, starvation, and dead-letter suffrage, Berroa called the revolution a Christian uprising against barbarism that could end only if the United States guarantees free elections.
records.summary_es: En una entrevista en Nueva York en el Americus Times-Recorder, el general Q. Berroa analiza la insurrección dominicana y los planes para una conferencia de la oposición. Berroa, exgobernador de Macorís, llegó tras su exilio en las islas Turcas y afirmó que la insurrección contra el presidente Ramón Cáceres se fortalece a diario y derrocará al régimen. Anunció una próxima conferencia en Nueva York entre líderes opositores, incluidos los expresidentes general Jeminez y general Morales, quienes han dejado a un lado sus diferencias para colaborar, junto con el exvicepresidente general des Champs y el exministro de Relaciones Exteriores Dr. Francesco Sánchez. Al denunciar las condiciones en Santo Domingo como terribles debido a ejecuciones políticas diarias, cárceles repletas, hambruna y un sufragio convertido en letra muerta, Berroa calificó la revolución de levantamiento cristiano contra la barbarie que solo podría terminar si Estados Unidos garantiza elecciones libres.

records.summary_en: The Evening Times published a statement from Dominican revolutionists detailing their aims to reform land taxes, modify tariffs, eliminate export duties, and establish habeas corpus protections. The statement asserted that Generals Morales and Jimenez had reached an understanding, while former President Horacio Vasquez had deserted President Caceres. It also alleged that Dominican Minister of Finance Federico Velasquez was seeking to secure half of the $1,300,000 deposited for foreign creditors to fund government war expenses.
records.summary_es: The Evening Times publicó una declaración de revolucionarios dominicanos en la que detallaban sus objetivos de reformar los impuestos sobre la tierra, modificar los aranceles, suprimir los derechos de exportación y establecer garantías de habeas corpus. El manifiesto aseguraba que los generales Morales y Jimenes habían alcanzado un entendimiento, mientras que el expresidente Horacio Vásquez había abandonado al presidente Cáceres. Alegaba además que el ministro de Hacienda dominicano Federico Velásquez procuraba asegurarse la mitad de los 1.300.000 dólares depositados para los acreedores extranjeros con el propósito de costear los gastos bélicos del gobierno.

It is our purpose, if we are victorious, as I am certain we shall be, to establish land taxes, modify the tariff and remove the pernicious export duties, which retard the progress of our industries. We also want the right of habeas corpus, which is unknown in our country. As matters are, the government puts in Jail and exiles citizens without any process of law. The revolution was started without the consent or advice of General Jimenez. General Morales and General Jimenez have come to an understanding. The government has suspended payment of the army and civil employes and seeks to pay preferred creditors, which cannot be done according to the modus vivendi. Of course we recognize the Santo Domingo treaty, and we are anxious for an even better one. It is probably not generally known in this country, but I know that Federico Velasquez, minister of finance, who is now in this city, has come here to get, if possible, half of the $1,300,000 on deposit for the payment of Santo Domingo's foreign creditors, that the money might be used for the expenses of the war. If the United States could guarantee us free elections the revolution would end, but as we are without help we were compelled to protest with arms. records.headline: A San Juan dispatch of June 27 in the Evening Star reports the arrival
records.summary_en: A San Juan dispatch of June 27 in the Evening Star reports the arrival on French and Cuban steamers of numerous Dominican exiles, including wounded fighters who had clashed with government troops. The refugees report that towns including Barahona, San Cristobal, Azua, San Pedro de Macoris, Hato Mayor, Sabana de la Mar, La Vega, Puerto Plata, and Monte Cristi are constantly harassed by insurgents, with rebellion active along the northwest line. The movement has reportedly captured most of its arms from government forces but suffers from a shortage of war supplies and unified leadership. A letter from Santo Domingo to an exile in Puerto Rico asserts that public opinion overwhelmingly desires the return of former president Morales to lead anti-Horacista forces against the current administration.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de San Juan del 27 de junio en el Evening Star informa sobre la llegada en vapores franceses y cubanos de numerosos exiliados dominicanos, incluidos combatientes heridos en choques con tropas del gobierno. Los refugiados informan que poblaciones como Barahona, San Cristóbal, Azua, San Pedro de Macorís, Hato Mayor, Sabana de la Mar, La Vega, Puerto Plata y Monte Cristi son hostigadas constantemente por insurgentes, con la rebelión en pleno desarrollo a lo largo de la línea noroeste. Según afirman, el movimiento ha capturado la mayor parte de sus armas a las fuerzas gubernamentales, pero padece escasez de pertrechos y de un liderazgo unificado. Una carta enviada desde Santo Domingo a un exiliado en Puerto Rico sostiene que la opinión pública anhela unánimemente el regreso del expresidente Morales para encabezar a las fuerzas antihoracistas contra la administración actual.

records.headline: A Puerto Rico dispatch in the New-York Tribune reports that Dominican exiles
records.summary_en: A Puerto Rico dispatch in the New-York Tribune reports that Dominican exiles describe widespread insurgent attacks against towns including Barahona, Azua, San Pedro de Macoris, Puerto Plata, and Monte Cristi. At a mass meeting held in Mayaguez on June 12 under the chairmanship of former president Jimenez, exiles adopted resolutions to unite Jimenez and Morales against the Dominican administration. The agreement stipulates that Jimenez would resume the presidency to complete the term for which he was elected in 1000, as printed in the dispatch, with Morales serving as Vice President and succeeding him as candidate for the following presidential term. Under the pact, Morales is assigned full military command of the campaign while Jimenez directs the collection of funds.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Puerto Rico en el New-York Tribune informa que exiliados dominicanos describen ataques insurgentes generalizados contra localidades como Barahona, Azua, San Pedro de Macorís, Puerto Plata y Monte Cristi. En una asamblea general celebrada en Mayagüez el 12 de junio bajo la presidencia del expresidente Jiménez, los exiliados adoptaron resoluciones para unir las fuerzas de Jiménez y Morales contra la administración dominicana. El acuerdo estipula que Jiménez reasumiría la presidencia para completar el mandato para el cual fue elegido en 1000, según consta textualmente en el despacho, correspondiendo a Morales ocupar la vicepresidencia y sucederlo como candidato para el período presidencial siguiente. Conforme al pacto, Morales asumirá el mando militar completo de la campaña, mientras que Jiménez dirigirá la recaudación de fondos.

records.headline: A Washington report in the Evening Star announces that several United States warships
records.summary_en: A Washington report in the Evening Star announces that several United States warships have been ordered to Dominican waters to reinforce the naval patrol maintained since American authorities assumed control of Dominican finances. Newly dispatched vessels include the cruiser Columbia carrying a battalion of 400 marines, the presidential yacht Mayflower, the auxiliary cruiser Tacoma, and the supply ship Culgoa. They join naval vessels already stationed across Dominican ports of entry, including the Yankee, Scorpion, and Dixie at Monte Cristi, the Paducah at Macoris, the Dubuque at Santo Domingo, the Don Juan de Austria at Samana, the Marietta at Puerto Plata, and the Newport at Sanchez. While naval observers consider the existing fleet sufficient to control the island, the deployment is widely understood as an effort by the United States to preserve the status quo and protect Dominican funds.
records.summary_es: Un informe de Washington en el Evening Star anuncia que varios buques de guerra de Estados Unidos recibieron órdenes de zarpar hacia aguas dominicanas para reforzar la patrulla naval que se mantiene desde que las autoridades estadounidenses asumieron el control de las finanzas dominicanas. Entre los buques recientemente despachados figuran el crucero Columbia, que transporta un batallón de 400 infantes de marina, el yate presidencial Mayflower, el crucero auxiliar Tacoma y el buque de suministros Culgoa. Estas naves se suman a las unidades ya apostadas en los distintos puertos dominicanos de entrada: el Yankee, el Scorpion y el Dixie en Monte Cristi, el Paducah en Macorís, el Dubuque en Santo Domingo, el Don Juan de Austria en Samaná, el Marietta en Puerto Plata y el Newport en Sánchez. Aunque analistas navales estimaban suficiente la flota ya reunida, el despliegue se percibe ampliamente como una medida de Estados Unidos para preservar el statu quo y proteger los fondos dominicanos.

records.headline: Advices from the Navy Department published in the Bismarck Daily Tribune disclose
records.summary_en: Advices from the Navy Department published in the Bismarck Daily Tribune disclose that Commander Southerland, head of American naval forces in Dominican waters, reported on the revolutionary movement in northern Santo Domingo. Southerland stated that a Dominican government representative was in Monte Cristi negotiating with insurgent leaders in an attempt to reach a peaceful settlement. The rebel leadership insisted on retaining absolute control over the city and province of Monte Cristi. These demands were completely rejected by the government, and orders were issued by President Caceres directing troops to attack the insurgents.
records.summary_es: Informes del Departamento de la Armada publicados en el Bismarck Daily Tribune revelan que el comandante Southerland, jefe de las fuerzas navales estadounidenses en aguas dominicanas, informó sobre el movimiento revolucionario en el norte de Santo Domingo. Southerland comunicó que un representante del gobierno dominicano se encontraba en Monte Cristi negociando con los cabecillas insurgentes en un intento por alcanzar un arreglo pacífico. La dirigencia rebelde insistió en retener el control absoluto sobre la ciudad y provincia de Monte Cristi. Estas exigencias fueron rechazadas de plano por el gobierno, y el presidente Cáceres impartió órdenes para que las tropas atacaran a los insurgentes.

records.summary_en: A dispatch in the Bismarck Daily Tribune reports that peace negotiations between the Dominican government and insurgent leaders have failed, prompting President Caceres to order an immediate assault. The government force comprises about 300 men enlisted in Monte Cristi and an equal number brought from the interior, totaling 600 soldiers preparing to attack 500 rebels with the assistance of a government gunboat. A high official indicated that in the event of armed conflict in Santo Domingo, the United States will ensure that the Marquis of Queensberry rules are observed. The United States government is not expected to intervene unless the financial interests protected under the existing modus vivendi are disturbed.

La fuerza del gobierno comprende unos 300 hombres reclutados en Monte Cristi y un número similar traído del interior, sumando 600 soldados que se preparan para acometer contra 500 rebeldes con el apoyo de un cañonero gubernamental. Un alto funcionario indicó que, en caso de conflicto armado en Santo Domingo, Estados Unidos se encargará de que se respeten las reglas del marqués de Queensberry. Se colige que el gobierno estadounidense no intervendrá a menos que se vean afectados los intereses que se siente obligado a proteger bajo el modus vivendi vigente.

records.headline: Hollander, the representative of this government, who has charge of the collection of customs In San Domingo
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Dominican representative Mr. Joubert conferred in Washington with Dr. Hollander and other U.S. officials regarding the situation in Santo Domingo. Joubert dismissed reports of a major revolutionary uprising at Monte Cristi as rumors from enemies of President Caceres and denied claims that customs funds held by the United States would be divided before treaty ratification. Joubert and Dominican Finance Minister Velasquez planned to travel to New York, where Velasquez would study American institutions.
records.summary_es: The Evening Star informó que el representante dominicano, el señor Joubert, conferenció en Washington con el Dr. Hollander y otros funcionarios estadounidenses sobre la situación en Santo Domingo. Joubert desestimó los informes sobre un gran levantamiento revolucionario en Monte Cristi calificándolos de rumores de los enemigos del presidente Cáceres, y negó que los fondos de aduanas custodiados por los Estados Unidos fueran a dividirse antes de la ratificación del tratado. Joubert y el ministro de Hacienda dominicano Velásquez planeaban viajar a Nueva York, donde Velásquez estudiaría las instituciones estadounidenses.

No change In the government Is anticipated by Mr. Joubert, who says the negotiations now pending for a settlement eventually of claims against the Dominican government do not contemplate any expenditure of the money the United States Is now holding for the little republic until after the ratification of the Dominican treaty. "Reports that an attempt Is being made to get a division of the funds derived from customs collections are without founda tion," said Mr. Joubert. "The negotiations now pending are for preliminary arrangements, which will make It possible to pay out the money without delay when the treaty shall be ratified. The adjudication of claims and other preliminary work might well be done immediately, and then the funds could be disbursed more speedily when proper authority is granted." records.headline: Trade opportunities in Santo Domingo are detailed in a commercial survey
records.summary_en: Trade opportunities in Santo Domingo are detailed in a commercial survey published in the New-York Tribune, noting that sugar exports reached 100,972,400 pounds valued at $3,292,470, of which about 99 percent was consumed in the United States. Santo Domingo contains eleven ports of entry, including northern and southern coastal harbors such as Monte Cristi, Puerto Plata, Macoris, and Azua, alongside the western frontier land ports of Tierra Nueva, Commendador, and Dajabon bordering Haiti. American citizens and capital have taken a leading role in national development, holding at least half the investment in sugar plantations, the majority of the banana industry, and one of the country's two operational railroads running sixty-eight miles between Puerto Plata and Santiago. Dominican sentiment is described as friendly toward American investors, offering promising trade opportunities for United States exporters.
records.summary_es: Las oportunidades de intercambio en Santo Domingo son detalladas en un estudio comercial publicado en el New-York Tribune, señalando que las exportaciones de azúcar alcanzaron 100.972.400 libras valoradas en 3.292.470 dólares, de las cuales cerca del 99 por ciento fue consumido en Estados Unidos. Santo Domingo cuenta con once puertos de entrada, incluidos puertos marítimos en las costas norte y sur como Monte Cristi, Puerto Plata, Macorís y Azua, junto con los puestos terrestres fronterizos occidentales de Tierra Nueva, Comendador y Dajabón en el límite con Haití. Los ciudadanos y el capital estadounidenses han asumido un papel protagónico en el desarrollo nacional, concentrando al menos la mitad de la inversión en las plantaciones de azúcar, la mayor parte de la industria bananera y uno de los dos ferrocarriles en servicio en el país, que cubre sesenta y ocho millas entre Puerto Plata y Santiago. Se describe una actitud dominicana amistosa hacia los inversionistas estadounidenses, lo que ofrece prometedoras perspectivas comerciales para los exportadores norteamericanos.

records.summary_en: An executive dispatch from Oyster Bay in the Evening Star lists appointments announced by President Roosevelt on July 18. Among consular designations, William H. Gale of Virginia was appointed consul at Puerto Plata in the Dominican Republic, alongside George Bucklin of Oklahoma named to Glauchau, Saxony. President Roosevelt additionally signed proclamations creating the Heppner Forest Reserve in Oregon and the Pinnacles Forest Reserve in California.

El presidente Roosevelt firmó además proclamaciones que crean la Reserva Forestal Heppner en Oregón y la Reserva Forestal Pinnacles en California.

records.headline: A Washington dispatch in the Alexandria Gazette reports that the indebtedness of Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: A Washington dispatch in the Alexandria Gazette reports that the indebtedness of Santo Domingo is to be settled under an adjustment plan formulated by Dominican minister Señor Velazquez and Dr. Hollander of Baltimore. Calling at the State Department, both representatives indicated that the outlook for financial settlement is highly favorable. They expressed confidence that the arrangement for paying foreign claims will satisfy all interested parties, including external creditors, the Dominican government, and the United States.

Al visitar el Departamento de Estado, ambos representantes indicaron que las perspectivas para un acuerdo financiero son altamente favorables. Manifestaron su confianza en que el arreglo para el pago de las reclamaciones extranjeras satisfará a todas las partes interesadas, incluidos los acreedores externos, el gobierno dominicano y Estados Unidos.

records.headline: A biographical article in The Kennewick Courier identifies Emiliano Tejera
records.summary_en: A biographical article in The Kennewick Courier identifies Emiliano Tejera as a political leader and highlights General Ramon Caceres as the foremost soldier of the Horacista faction, acclaimed after killing the dictator General Ulysses Heureaux. Caceres is described as a brother-in-law of Horacio Vasquez and related to Francisco Leonte Vasquez, formerly Dominican consul general in New York under the Morales administration. Following Morales's rise to power, Caceres joined the coalition government as Vice President and Minister of the Interior. He remained stationed in the interior city of Santiago to maintain control over the north coast while Morales directed national administration from the capital city of Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: Un artículo biográfico en The Kennewick Courier identifica a Emiliano Tejera como líder político y destaca al general Ramón Cáceres como el principal soldado de la facción horacista, aclamado tras dar muerte al dictador general Ulises Heureaux. Se describe a Cáceres como cuñado de Horacio Vásquez y emparentado con Francisco Leonte Vásquez, quien fuera cónsul general dominicano en Nueva York bajo la administración de Morales. Tras la llegada de Morales al poder, Cáceres se incorporó al gobierno de coalición como vicepresidente y ministro de lo Interior. Permaneció apostado en la ciudad interior de Santiago para mantener el control sobre la costa norte mientras Morales dirigía la administración nacional desde la ciudad capital de Santo Domingo.

records.headline: Escalating military and diplomatic crises in the republic are described
records.summary_en: Escalating military and diplomatic crises in the republic are described in accounts from travellers arriving from Santo Domingo, published in the New-York Tribune. J. T. Smith, an American merchant from Wilmington doing business there, reported that the revolutionary alliance backing Jimenez and Morales is growing rapidly, with nearly the entire province of Monte Cristi held by insurgents. General Ricardo Limardo remains besieged in the town of Monte Cristi, holding out with repeated government reinforcements but unable to gain any advantage over the rebels. Meanwhile, deep consternation is reported in Dominican government circles over the inability of Ministers Joubert and Vasquez to obtain authorization from Washington to release funds in the National City Bank of New York to pay Dominican creditors.
records.summary_es: La intensificación de las crisis militar y diplomática en la república es descrita en relatos de viajeros llegados de Santo Domingo, publicados en el New-York Tribune. J. T. Smith, comerciante estadounidense de Wilmington con negocios allí, informó que la alianza revolucionaria que respalda a Jiménez y Morales cobra fuerza rápidamente, encontrándose casi toda la provincia de Monte Cristi en manos de los insurgentes. El general Ricardo Limardo permanece sitiado en la ciudad de Monte Cristi, resistiendo con continuos refuerzos del gobierno pero sin lograr ventaja alguna sobre los rebeldes. Entre tanto, se reporta profunda consternación en los círculos gubernamentales dominicanos por la imposibilidad de los ministros Joubert y Vásquez de obtener autorización de Washington para liberar los fondos en el National City Bank de Nueva York destinados al pago de los acreedores dominicanos.

records.headline: The Nezperce Herald reviews the shifting alliances of Dominican
records.summary_en: The Nezperce Herald reviews the shifting alliances of Dominican politics, noting that Morales, in his present emergency, appears to seek a coalition with Rodrigues, the petty chief of Monte Cristi. Rodrigues had previously fought Morales bitterly before being placated with the administration of the Monte Cristi custom house, but resumed plotting after a United States cruiser seized the custom house under the arbitral agreement known as the laudo on behalf of the Santo Domingo Improvement Company. Consequently, Monte Cristi has served as a focal point of revolutionary sentiment, while Puerto Plata remains connected by railway to the Caceres stronghold at Santiago.
records.summary_es: The Nezperce Herald examina las cambiantes alianzas de la política dominicana, señalando que Morales, ante su actual emergencia, parece buscar una coalición con Rodrigues, el caudillo local de Monte Cristi. Rodrigues había combatido encarnizadamente a Morales antes de ser apaciguado con la administración de la aduana de Monte Cristi, pero volvió a conspirar luego de que un crucero de los Estados Unidos tomara posesión de la aduana en virtud del acuerdo arbitral conocido como el laudo a favor de la Santo Domingo Improvement Company. Por consiguiente, Monte Cristi ha sido centro de agitación revolucionaria, mientras que Puerto Plata se mantiene conectada por ferrocarril con el bastión de Cáceres en Santiago.

records.headline: A Washington dispatch in the New-York Tribune reports that State Department advices
records.summary_en: A Washington dispatch in the New-York Tribune reports that State Department advices anticipate further revolutionary outbreaks in Santo Domingo, where unrest around Monte Cristi and other northern ports threatens the government. Commander Southerland, commanding the American fleet patrolling the island against insurgent expeditions, has been alerted to intercept hostile forces expected from Puerto Rico and neighboring islands. Puerto Rico serves as the haven for banished adversaries of the Caceres administration, and the departure of former President Jiménez from that island for New York is viewed in Washington as an attempt to recruit American support against Caceres.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Washington en el New-York Tribune informa que informes recibidos por el Departamento de Estado prevén nuevos brotes revolucionarios en Santo Domingo, donde el descontento en Monte Cristi y otros puertos del norte amenaza al gobierno. El comandante Southerland, al mando de la flota estadounidense que patrulla la isla contra expediciones insurgentes, ha sido alertado para interceptar contingentes hostiles que se esperan desde Puerto Rico e islas vecinas. Puerto Rico sirve de refugio a los adversarios desterrados del gobierno de Cáceres, y la salida del expresidente Jiménez desde esa isla con destino a Nueva York se interpreta en Washington como un intento de reclutar apoyo estadounidense contra Cáceres.

records.headline: Reporting from Washington, the New-York Tribune states that Colonel Colton dismissed
records.summary_en: Reporting from Washington, the New-York Tribune states that Colonel Colton dismissed rumors of serious insurrections in Santo Domingo, though noting persistent unrest around Monte Cristi and reports that former President Jiménez sought funds in New York to finance a revolt. Colton reported that American capital regards revolutionary threats with optimism, noting recent arrivals acquiring land for cocoa cultivation. He also deplored the killing of Thurston, an American revenue collector for the Dominican government, and his Puerto Rican associate, who were shot in their hammocks by smugglers after seizing eight loads of contraband, while native guards sleeping on the ground escaped.
records.summary_es: En un despacho desde Washington, el New-York Tribune señala que el coronel Colton desestimó los rumores de insurrecciones graves en Santo Domingo, aunque constató la persistente agitación en torno a Monte Cristi y las versiones de que el expresidente Jiménez buscaba fondos en Nueva York para financiar una revuelta. Colton indicó que el capital estadounidense observa el riesgo revolucionario con optimismo y mencionó la llegada reciente de personas interesadas en adquirir tierras para el cultivo de cacao. Asimismo, lamentó la muerte de Thurston, un estadounidense empleado en la recaudación de rentas del gobierno dominicano, y de su compañero puertorriqueño, quienes fueron baleados en sus hamacas por contrabandistas tras incautar ocho cargas de contrabando, mientras los guardias nativos que dormían en el suelo escaparon ilesos.

records.headline: A recently intercepted filibustering expedition was bound for Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: A recently intercepted filibustering expedition was bound for Santo Domingo and not for Cuba, according to rumors among guests of hotels near Union Square reported in The New-York Tribune. With an active insurrection underway in the Dominican Republic intended to restore former President Juan Isidro Jiménez to power, numerous sympathizers are present in New York. While General Jiménez stated upon his arrival from Puerto Rico three weeks ago that he had avoided Dominican politics for two years and was traveling on private business, his local followers are suspected of knowing more about the expedition than they admit.
records.summary_es: Una expedición filibustera recientemente interceptada se dirigía a Santo Domingo y no a Cuba, según rumores entre huéspedes de hoteles cercanos a Union Square de los que da cuenta el New-York Tribune. En momentos en que una insurrección activa se desarrolla en la República Dominicana con el propósito de devolver al poder al expresidente Juan Isidro Jiménez, numerosos partidarios se encuentran en Nueva York. Aunque el general Jiménez declaró a su llegada desde Puerto Rico hace tres semanas que se había mantenido apartado de la política dominicana durante dos años y que viajaba por negocios privados, se sospecha que sus seguidores locales saben más sobre la expedición de lo que admiten.

records.summary_en: This profile presents Ramon Caceres, the present dictator-president of the Dominican Republic, as a big man of fully six feet and over 250 pounds whose word is law but who rules with a laugh, even, the writer says, when he shot down his predecessor, Ulysses Heureaux, and who is known throughout the land simply as Mon. It relates that Caceres put Morales in the presidential chair because he did not want the job himself, kept him there against his will, and that Morales, feeling himself virtually a prisoner in his own capital, negotiated with the revolutionists and precipitated a revolution against his own government.

RAMON CACERES is a big man, fully six feet in height, and weighs considerably over 250 pounds. records.headline: A correspondent writing in The Washington Times portrays Dominican President Ramón Cáceres
records.summary_en: A correspondent writing in The Washington Times portrays Dominican President Ramón Cáceres as a leader who takes nothing seriously, not even having shot down his predecessor, Ulysses Heureaux. Recounting an interview during an uprising when an army division was routed and the minister of war killed, the author relates that Cáceres received him with laughter and resumed laughing immediately after the minister was buried beneath the church floor beside the slain Heureaux. Throughout the country he is addressed neither by military or presidential titles nor by his surname, but universally by his childhood nickname, 'Mon.'
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal en The Washington Times retrata al presidente dominicano Ramón Cáceres como un gobernante que nada se toma en serio, ni siquiera el haber ultimado a tiros a su predecesor, Ulises Heureaux. Al relatar una entrevista mantenida durante una sublevación en que una división del ejército fue derrotada y el ministro de guerra muerto, el autor refiere que Cáceres lo recibió entre risas y volvió a reírse inmediatamente después del entierro del ministro bajo el suelo de la iglesia junto al difunto Heureaux. En todo el país no se le llama por títulos militares ni presidenciales ni por su apellido, sino universalmente por su apodo de infancia, «Mon».

The retreating rebels subsequently assaulted the town of Dajabón, compelling government troops to retreat into the fort, where they mounted a courageous defense. The government commander at Monte Cristi was awaiting promised reinforcements of 400 men before pursuing the insurgents, with combat at Dajabón still underway when the courier left.

El comandante del gobierno en Monte Cristi aguardaba refuerzos prometidos de 400 hombres antes de iniciar la persecución de los insurgentes, mientras los combates en Dajabón continuaban cuando partió el mensajero.

records.headline: In an article on Dominican political life, the Yorkville Enquirer sketches
records.summary_en: In an article on Dominican political life, the Yorkville Enquirer sketches President Ramón Cáceres, noting that he received a correspondent with laughter, attended the burial of his minister of war beside the former president Cáceres had shot down, and resumed laughing immediately afterward. The account observes that he is universally known as 'Mon,' the name used by his family and playmates in childhood, rather than by any official title. Illustrating the fierce pride of Dominicans, the writer adds that when Morales ordered the execution of prisoners General Mansuetta and Commander Gillheaux, Gillheaux casually asked to be spared in honor of the inauguration, to which Morales calmly replied that the death warrants were already signed.
records.summary_es: En un artículo sobre la vida política dominicana, el Yorkville Enquirer describe al presidente Ramón Cáceres, señalando que recibió a un corresponsal entre risas, asistió al entierro de su ministro de guerra junto al expresidente al que Cáceres había ultimado y volvió a reírse de inmediato. El relato hace notar que se le conoce en todo el país como «Mon», el apelativo con el que lo llamaban sus familiares y compañeros de juego de niño, y no por título oficial alguno. Para ilustrar el indomable orgullo dominicano, el autor añade que cuando Morales ordenó el fusilamiento de los prisioneros general Mansuetta y comandante Gillheaux, este último le pidió con naturalidad ser perdonado en honor a la investidura, a lo que Morales respondió con serenidad que las sentencias de muerte ya estaban firmadas.

records.headline: Dominican President Ramón Cáceres's personal background is sketched
records.summary_en: Dominican President Ramón Cáceres's personal background is sketched by The Yorkville Enquirer, describing him as owning weapons rather than books, possessing Caucasian ancestry, and laughing off past revolutionary perils. His father, a minister under Luperón, was shot in cold blood in Santo Domingo while holding a newly baptized infant as Ulysses Heureaux was rising to power. Left without income at his family's rural home near Moca, young Ramón supported his mother by managing a freight mule train, an occupation in which he learned patience, marksmanship, and expert horsemanship.
records.summary_es: Los antecedentes personales del presidente dominicano Ramón Cáceres son reseñados por el Yorkville Enquirer, que lo describe como un hombre provisto de armas pero desprovisto de libros, de ascendencia caucásica y que relata entre risas los peligros de pasadas revoluciones. Su padre, ministro bajo el régimen de Luperón, fue asesinado a sangre fría en Santo Domingo mientras sostenía a un infante recién bautizado, en momentos en que Ulises Heureaux ascendía al poder. Al quedar sin ingresos en la finca familiar cerca de Moca, el joven Ramón sostuvo a su madre conduciendo un convoy de mulas de carga, oficio en el que aprendió paciencia, puntería y una extraordinaria destreza como jinete.

records.headline: The Evening Times reports that an insurrection is underway in the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: The Evening Times reports that an insurrection is underway in the Dominican Republic to restore former President Juan Isidro Jiménez to power, with numerous supporters active in New York. Although General Jiménez maintained upon arriving from Puerto Rico three weeks earlier that he had abstained from Dominican politics for two years and was in the city on private business, his local followers are suspected of possessing inside knowledge regarding an ill-fated filibustering expedition. The article contrasts this Dominican movement with the formal headquarters recently opened on Water Street by the Cuban insurgent junta.
records.summary_es: The Evening Times informa que una insurrección está en desarrollo en la República Dominicana con el fin de restaurar en el poder al expresidente Juan Isidro Jiménez, contando con numerosos partidarios activos en Nueva York. A pesar de que el general Jiménez sostuvo tras arribar desde Puerto Rico tres semanas antes que se había mantenido al margen de la política dominicana durante dos años y se hallaba en la ciudad por asuntos privados, se sospecha que sus simpatizantes locales poseen información reservada sobre una frustrada expedición filibustera. El artículo contrasta este movimiento dominicano con la sede formal inaugurada recientemente en Water Street por la junta insurgente cubana.

records.headline: Captain Southerland commands American naval forces in Dominican waters
records.summary_en: Captain Southerland commands American naval forces in Dominican waters and has cabled that the situation has grown critical and that a revolution is possible, a Washington dispatch in the New-York Tribune reports. Southerland warns that the Dominican government's assembly of 400 men at Monte Cristi leaves other sections of the republic unprotected, creating conditions for a broader insurrection, while communication between Puerto Plata and Monte Cristi has been severed. In view of these developments, he urges that no further naval vessels be transferred away from Dominican waters.

Southerland advierte que la concentración de 400 hombres dispuesta por el gobierno dominicano en Monte Cristi deja desguarnecidas otras regiones de la república, propiciando un alzamiento mayor, al tiempo que la comunicación entre Puerto Plata y Monte Cristi ha quedado cortada. Ante estos hechos, insta a no retirar más buques de guerra de las aguas dominicanas.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star's Washington report states that Professor Hollander, of Hopkins University in Baltimore, will sail for Antwerp to confer with Frederico Valasquez, the minister of foreign affairs and commerce of Santo Domingo. Their conference will relate to a bond issue plan devised by Minister Valasquez for the adjustment of Santo Domingo's foreign indebtedness. El profesor Hollander ha actuado con anterioridad en calidad de asesor de Santo Domingo y como representante del presidente Roosevelt en las negociaciones con la República Dominicana.

records.headline: After spending two months in the United States as special commissioner
records.summary_en: After spending two months in the United States as special commissioner adjusting his country's finances, Federico Velasquez, minister of finance and commerce of Santo Domingo, departed for home aboard the steamer Cherokee, a New York dispatch in the Abilene Weekly Reflector reports. Before leaving, Velasquez announced that the Dominican republic intends to settle its public debt directly with creditors on equitable terms within its resources, rather than asking the United States to supervise the adjustment. The republic will then request that the United States government administer Dominican customs to service a loan to liquidate established obligations. He stated that Kuhn, Loeb & Co. have engaged to purchase an issue of $20,000,000 of sinking fund gold bonds, with the Morton Trust Company also participating.
records.summary_es: Tras permanecer dos meses en Estados Unidos como comisionado especial para arreglar las finanzas dominicanas, Federico Velásquez, ministro de Hacienda y Comercio de Santo Domingo, partió de regreso a su país a bordo del vapor Cherokee, según un despacho de Nueva York en el Abilene Weekly Reflector. Antes de partir, Velásquez anunció que la República Dominicana pretende saldar su deuda pública directamente con los acreedores en condiciones equitativas y dentro de sus recursos, en lugar de solicitar a Estados Unidos que supervise el ajuste. Posteriormente, la república pedirá al gobierno estadounidense que administre las aduanas dominicanas para atender el servicio de un empréstito destinado a liquidar las obligaciones reconocidas. Declaró además que la firma Kuhn, Loeb & Co. se comprometió a comprar una emisión de $20.000.000 en bonos de oro de fondo de amortización, con la participación adicional de la Morton Trust Company.

records.headline: The siege of Monte Cristi, Santo Domingo, by Dominican revolutionists
records.summary_en: The siege of Monte Cristi, Santo Domingo, by Dominican revolutionists is reported in a dispatch from Cape Haitien in the Albuquerque Morning Journal. President Peres, at the head of 12,000 men, attacked the revolutionists, lifted the siege, and pursued the besiegers, dispersing them and capturing prisoners. Twenty-four of the captured revolutionists were executed and their property was destroyed. Later dispatches indicated that the revolutionists had rallied and were preparing to mount another assault on Monte Cristi.
records.summary_es: El asedio de Monte Cristi, Santo Domingo, por revolucionarios dominicanos es informado en un despacho desde Cabo Haitiano en el Albuquerque Morning Journal. El presidente Peres, al frente de 12.000 hombres, atacó a los revolucionarios, levantó el sitio y persiguió a los sitiadores, dispersándolos y capturando prisioneros. Veinticuatro de los revolucionarios capturados fueron ejecutados y sus propiedades destruidas. Informes posteriores indicaron que los revolucionarios se habían reagrupado y se disponían a emprender otro ataque contra Monte Cristi.

records.headline: The article reports a Dominican government proclamation for Monte Cristi province, countersigned by President
records.summary_en: The article reports a Dominican government proclamation for Monte Cristi province, countersigned by President Caceres, declaring that peace negotiations having failed, the government will end the war however violent and severe the means, placing the district under siege and threatening summary shooting even for women found carrying cartridges. Exiled revolutionist General Berroa, speaking in New York alongside ex-President Jiminez, called the decree simply despotic, said 700 to 1,000 well-armed revolutionists were in the field, and said the revolution would stop only when constitutional rights, political prisoners and the exiles were dealt with justly.
records.summary_es: El artículo informa de una proclama del gobierno dominicano para la provincia de Monte Cristi, refrendada por el presidente Cáceres, que declara que, habiendo fracasado las negociaciones de paz, el gobierno terminará la guerra por violentos y severos que sean los medios, pone el distrito en estado de sitio y amenaza con fusilamiento sumario incluso para las mujeres a las que se encuentren cartuchos. El general revolucionario exiliado Berroa, hablando en Nueva York junto al expresidente Jiménez, calificó el decreto de simplemente despótico, dijo que había entre 700 y 1,000 revolucionarios bien armados en campaña, y afirmó que la revolución solo cesaría cuando los derechos constitucionales, los presos políticos y los exiliados fueran tratados con justicia.

Government Proclaims a War of Extermination in Monte Cristi Province. Exiled revolutionists of Santo Domingo and their sympathizers here were discussing yesterday a proclamation issued recently by Ricardo Limardo, Government Delegate in the province of Monte Cristi, and countersigned by Gov. Camacho of the province and President Caceres of the republic. The proclamation states that all negotiations for harmony and peace having proved futile, the Government has resolved to retaliate with like measures. The Government will end the war no matter how violent and severe the means. The document declares the district in a state of siege and prohibits travel to natives and foreigners alike. Even women caught with cartridges on their persons will be summarily shot. Anyone attempting to smuggle ammunition or war stores into the country will meet the same fate. records.summary_en: Monte Cristi is described, in an account in the Evening Star, as a smuggling center near the Haitian boundary where recent revolutionary movements have originated. Because national laws were seldom enforced there in the past, the city functioned virtually as an independent province until American administration of Dominican customs brought strict enforcement. Smugglers, irritated by border posts and responsible for the killing of two customs employees several months earlier, seek to overthrow President Caceres because his administration cooperates with American collectors. The smugglers calculate that replacing the government or fomenting revolutionary disorder will enable them to continue their illicit trade.

records.summary_en: A dispatch in the Grant County Herald reports that revolutionary leaders in the Dominican Republic have failed to enter an agreement to surrender and preserve peace. Monte Cristi is characterized as the headquarters for smugglers and the center of recent revolutionary activity near the Haitian boundary, across which merchants formerly smuggled large quantities of merchandise. The city long functioned as an independent province because Dominican laws were seldom enforced until the United States undertook customs collections. Smugglers have been harassed by border collectors, and relations have grown intense following the murder of two customs office employees several months earlier.
