La ciudad operó durante largo tiempo como una provincia independiente debido a que las leyes dominicanas casi no se aplicaban, hasta que Estados Unidos asumió la recaudación aduanera. Los contrabandistas se han visto obstaculizados por los inspectores fronterizos y la situación se ha vuelto tensa tras el asesinato de dos empleados de aduanas meses antes.

records.summary_en: The Morning Tribune reported that Dominican government forces under President Caceres had completely defeated revolutionists near Monte Cristi, leading most rebels to surrender and accept pardons. Several rebel leaders fled across the frontier into Haiti to join General Navarro at Cape Haitien, where they were required to depart for a foreign country because the Haitian government prohibited their stay. The excerpt noted that the uprising had been motivated by border smugglers and that the Monte Cristi district had returned to quiet.

Varios cabecillas rebeldes huyeron cruzando la frontera hacia Haití para unirse al general Navarro en Cabo Haitiano, donde se les exigió partir hacia un país extranjero debido a que el gobierno haitiano prohibió su permanencia. La nota señaló que el levantamiento había sido impulsado por contrabandistas fronterizos y que el distrito de Monte Cristi había recobrado la tranquilidad.

records.headline: A report in The Montgomery Advertiser relays statements from United States Minister Thomas C. Dawson
records.summary_en: A report in The Montgomery Advertiser relays statements from United States Minister Thomas C. Dawson, who reports that internal conditions in Santo Domingo are now peaceful. Dawson characterizes recent disturbances as insignificant, noting that only one fight worthy of the name occurred during the strife around Monte Cristi, and adds that he will return to Santo Domingo in November. A companion dispatch datelined New York announces that Emilio C. Joubert, Minister Resident of the Dominican Republic at Washington, is ill at the Westminster Hotel after falling sick during his return from the Pan-American Conference in Rio de Janeiro.

Un despacho complementario fechado en Nueva York anuncia que Emilio C. Joubert, ministro residente de la República Dominicana en Washington, se halla enfermo en el Hotel Westminster tras haber caído indispuesto durante su regreso de la Conferencia Panamericana en Río de Janeiro.

records.headline: A Washington report in The National Tribune states that Thomas C. Dawson
records.summary_en: A Washington report in The National Tribune states that Thomas C. Dawson, United States Minister to Santo Domingo, held an extensive conference at the State Department with Assistant Secretary Bacon regarding Dominican affairs. Minister Dawson reported that internal affairs in Santo Domingo are now quite peaceful, characterizing recent disturbances as insignificant with only one fight worthy of the name occurring throughout the unrest centered about Monte Cristi on the north shore. Dawson is currently in the United States on leave and is not scheduled to return to Santo Domingo until November.
records.summary_es: Un informe de Washington en The National Tribune señala que Thomas C. Dawson, ministro de Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo, mantuvo una extensa conferencia en el Departamento de Estado con el subsecretario Bacon acerca de los asuntos dominicanos. El ministro Dawson informó que los asuntos internos en Santo Domingo son ahora bastante pacíficos, calificando los recientes disturbios de insignificantes, con un solo combate digno de mención en todos los conflictos librados alrededor de Monte Cristi, en la costa norte. Dawson se encuentra actualmente de permiso en Estados Unidos y no tiene previsto regresar a Santo Domingo hasta noviembre.

records.headline: A report in The Times Dispatch announces that San Domingo will participate
records.summary_en: A report in The Times Dispatch announces that San Domingo will participate in the Jamestown Exposition celebrating the three hundredth anniversary of the landing at Jamestown Island. In an official letter to Hon. St. George Tucker, president of the exposition company, President Ramon Caceres accepted the invitation and pledged that the republic will erect its own building constructed from its precious woods. The Dominican exhibit will display native island products including cocoa, coffee, minerals, and timber, with the pavilion surrounded by Dominican palms and tropical foliage. The dispatch notes that native islanders may also travel to the exposition to demonstrate the manufacture of hats, mats, and pottery.
records.summary_es: Un informe en The Times Dispatch anuncia que San Domingo participará en la Exposición de Jamestown para conmemorar el tricentenario del desembarco en la isla de Jamestown. En una carta oficial dirigida al honorable St. George Tucker, presidente de la compañía de la exposición, el presidente Ramón Cáceres aceptó la invitación y aseguró que la república construirá su propio pabellón de maderas preciosas. La muestra dominicana exhibirá productos típicos de la isla, como cacao, café, minerales y madera, y el edificio estará rodeado de palmeras dominicanas y follaje tropical. El despacho añade que aborígenes de la isla podrían viajar a la exposición para mostrar la confección de sombreros, esteras y cerámica.

records.headline: A detailed account in the New-York Tribune traces a failed revolutionary expedition
records.summary_en: A detailed account in the New-York Tribune traces a failed revolutionary expedition to the northern coast of Santo Domingo led by Generals Enrique Jiménes and Pedro Lasala. Originally organized to deliver arms to Generals Andrés Picharde and Mavriclo Jiménez, the force learned at Turks Island that the frontier had been pacified and those leaders expelled. Jiménes and Lasala nevertheless landed a small party not exceeding twenty persons at a cove near Blanco and marched inland toward Santiago de los Caballeros. While passing through General Lasala's possessions near San José de las Matas, the insurgents were surrounded by government troops in a skirmish that left Lasala mortally wounded, two or three men killed, and the remainder captured.
records.summary_es: Un pormenorizado relato en el New-York Tribune describe una fallida expedición revolucionaria a la costa norte de Santo Domingo liderada por los generales Enrique Jiménes y Pedro Lasala. Organizada inicialmente para entregar armas a los generales Andrés Picharde y Mavriclo Jiménez, la fuerza se enteró en las islas Turcas de que la frontera había sido pacificada y dichos caudillos expulsados. A pesar de ello, Jiménes y Lasala desembarcaron una pequeña partida de no más de veinte personas en una caleta cerca de Blanco y avanzaron tierra adentro hacia Santiago de los Caballeros. Mientras transitaban por posesiones del general Lasala cerca de San José de las Matas, los insurgentes fueron cercados por tropas gubernamentales en una refriega que dejó a Lasala mortalmente herido, dos o tres hombres muertos y al resto capturados.

records.headline: A dispatch in the Evening Star reports that a revolutionary band
records.summary_en: A dispatch in the Evening Star reports that a revolutionary band not exceeding twenty persons pushed inland toward Santiago de los Caballeros before being intercepted by government forces. While traversing the possessions of General Lasala near San Jose de las Matas, the group was encircled by government troops, resulting in a skirmish where General Lasala was mortally wounded, two or three companions fell, and the survivors were captured. Although the prisoners were ordered sent to the city of Santo Domingo, rumors widely circulated that General Enrique Jimenez and one of his prominent followers were executed.
records.summary_es: Un despacho en el Evening Star informa que una partida revolucionaria de no más de veinte personas avanzó hacia el interior rumbo a Santiago de los Caballeros antes de ser interceptada por fuerzas del gobierno. Al cruzar las propiedades del general Lasala cerca de San José de las Matas, el grupo fue cercado por tropas gubernamentales, lo que derivó en una refriega donde el general Lasala resultó herido de muerte, cayeron dos o tres compañeros y los sobrevivientes fueron capturados. Si bien se ordenó enviar a los prisioneros a la ciudad de Santo Domingo, circularon insistentes rumores de que el general Enrique Jiménez y uno de sus partidarios prominentes habían sido ejecutados.

records.headline: A report in the Evening Star details agreements reached by House
records.summary_en: A report in the Evening Star details agreements reached by House and Senate conferees on the diplomatic and consular appropriation bill. Among the contested provisions, the Senate receded from an amendment that had substituted 'Santo Domingo' for 'the Dominican republic,' leading the conferees to adopt the designation 'the Dominican republic' as originally passed by the House. The conferees also established salary scales for consular clerks beginning July 1, 1907, and set specific appropriations for clerk allowances across foreign consulates.
records.summary_es: Un informe en el Evening Star detalla los acuerdos adoptados por los comités de conferencia de la Cámara de Representantes y el Senado sobre la ley de asignaciones diplomáticas y consulares. Entre las disposiciones debatidas, el Senado desistió de una enmienda que reemplazaba 'the Dominican republic' por 'Santo Domingo', lo que llevó a los comisionados a adoptar la designación 'the Dominican republic' conforme a lo aprobado por la Cámara. La comisión fijó además escalas de sueldos para el personal consular a partir del 1 de julio de 1907 y determinó partidas específicas para empleados en los consulados extranjeros.

records.headline: A Washington dispatch published in The Courier-Journal outlines
records.summary_en: A Washington dispatch published in The Courier-Journal outlines conference agreements on diplomatic legislation. The Senate receded from an amendment that had altered the country's designation from 'the Dominican republic'—as approved by the House—to 'Santo Domingo,' thereby adopting 'the Dominican republic' as the designation ratified by the conferees. The measure also authorizes the President at his discretion to elevate the ranks of United States diplomatic representatives when foreign governments reciprocate by increasing the ranks of their envoys.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Washington publicado en The Courier-Journal resume los acuerdos de la comisión mixta sobre la legislación diplomática. El Senado desistió de una enmienda que había alterado la designación del país de 'the Dominican republic'—según lo aprobado por la Cámara—a 'Santo Domingo', con lo cual se adoptó 'the Dominican republic' como la fórmula ratificada por los delegados. La norma autoriza asimismo al presidente a elevar a su discreción el rango de los representantes diplomáticos estadounidenses cuando los gobiernos extranjeros correspondan incrementando el de sus enviados.

records.summary_en: The Courier-Journal reported that President Roosevelt transmitted a new treaty with the Dominican Republic to the U.S. Senate concerning the administration of Dominican revenues. Under the agreement, contingent on debt arrangements with creditors, the U.S. President would appoint a receiver general to collect Dominican customs funds. Senate leaders aimed for action before congressional adjournment, and while several Democratic senators signaled support, Senator Bacon of Georgia had not yet fully assented.
records.summary_es: The Courier-Journal informó que el presidente Roosevelt remitió al Senado de los Estados Unidos un nuevo tratado con la República Dominicana relativo a la administración de las rentas dominicanas. En virtud del acuerdo, supeditado a los arreglos de deuda con los acreedores, el presidente estadounidense nombraría a un receptor general para recaudar los fondos aduaneros dominicanos. Los líderes del Senado procuraban actuar antes del receso del Congreso, y si bien varios senadores demócratas manifestaron su respaldo, el senador Bacon de Georgia aún no había dado su total consentimiento.
records.passage: [illegible]er county Arnet Mitchell The House to-day passed a bill providing for a United States Judge for the Northern district of Alabama SENT TO SENATE That Body Now Has New Treaty With Santo Domingo Washington, Feb. 12— The President to-day sent to the Senate the new treaty with the Republic of Santo Domingo relative to the revenues of that country. The new agreement sets forth In the preamble the fact that Santo Domingo has entered on an agreement with her creditors which is made contingent on the fact that this country shall collect the money and It is then agreed that the President of the United States shall appoint a representative of the Government as receiver general to take charge of all the funds collected and provide means for their collection. The treaty will go direct to the Committee on Foreign Relations and there will be a determined effort to have it reported and acted on before the adjournment of the present session of Congress. Many of the Democratic Senators have Indicated their willingness that this should be done but Senator Bacon of Georgia who is the leading Democratic member of the Senate Committee on Foreign Relations has not yet given his full assent to this programme

records.headline: An editorial analysis in The Sun examines the financial framework of the new Dominican
records.summary_en: An editorial analysis in The Sun examines the financial framework of the new Dominican treaty, under which customs revenues will be collected with 45 per cent turned over to the Dominican Republic and the remaining 55 per cent allocated to the sinking fund and interest of a 20,000,000 loan. The banking firm of Kuhn, Loeb & Co. has agreed to finance the loan to liquidate foreign indebtedness, which has been ascertained at approximately 17,000,000 on an equitable basis. Citing the operational experience of the preceding eighteen months during which customs revenues were provisionally collected and apportioned by the Federal Government, the analysis projects that the debt will be fully paid off in less than twenty years.
records.summary_es: Un análisis editorial en The Sun examina la estructura financiera del nuevo tratado dominicano, conforme al cual se recaudarán los ingresos aduaneros entregando el 45 por ciento a la República Dominicana y reservando el 55 por ciento restante para el fondo de amortización y los intereses de un empréstito de 20.000.000. La firma bancaria Kuhn, Loeb & Co. ha acordado financiar el préstamo para liquidar la deuda con acreedores extranjeros, determinada en unos 17.000.000 sobre una base equitativa. Con base en la experiencia operativa de los dieciocho meses previos en que los ingresos aduaneros fueron provisionalmente recaudados y distribuidos por el gobierno federal, el análisis proyecta que la deuda quedará totalmente saldada en menos de veinte años.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star detailed the financial provisions of the proposed Dominican treaty, outlining how customs revenues would cover receivership expenses, interest, bond amortization, and payments to the Dominican government. Collection costs were capped at five percent, with $100,000 monthly allocated to the loan's fiscal agent and annual collections over $3,000,000 applied to the sinking fund. The terms also prohibited the Dominican Republic from increasing its public debt or modifying import duties without the consent of the U.S. President.
records.summary_es: The Evening Star detalló las disposiciones financieras del propuesto tratado dominicano, explicando cómo los ingresos aduaneros cubrirían los gastos de la receptoría, los intereses, la amortización de los bonos y los pagos al gobierno dominicano. Los costos de recaudación quedaron limitados a un tope del cinco por ciento, con 100.000 dólares mensuales destinados al agente fiscal del empréstito y la aplicación al fondo de amortización de las recaudaciones anuales que superaran los 3.000.000 de dólares. Los términos prohibían asimismo a la República Dominicana incrementar su deuda pública o modificar los derechos de importación sin el consentimiento del presidente de los Estados Unidos.

The remainder of the previous month's collections is to be turned over to the Dominican government or be applied to the sinking fund for the redemption of bonds. records.summary_en: The Morning Tribune reported that ratification of the treaty in the Dominican Republic remained uncertain despite support from President Caceres and his cabinet. Severe opposition had arisen in the Dominican Congress and among the public, with opponents threatening lawmakers and alleging the treaty would give the United States an unshakable grip on the nation. The article argued that the treaty would protect Dominican independence and curb revolutionists, hoping the Dominican Congress would ultimately approve it.
records.summary_es: The Morning Tribune informó que la ratificación del tratado en la República Dominicana continuaba siendo incierta a pesar del respaldo del presidente Cáceres y su gabinete. Una severa oposición se había desatado en el Congreso dominicano y entre la ciudadanía, amenazando los opositores a los legisladores y alegando que el tratado otorgaría a los Estados Unidos un dominio inquebrantable sobre la nación. El artículo argumentaba que el tratado protegería la independencia dominicana y frenaría a los revolucionarios, manifestando la esperanza de que el Congreso dominicano terminara por aprobarlo.

records.headline: The United States has several gunboats patrolling both coasts of the warring Central American countries
records.summary_en: The New-York Tribune reported on Caribbean and Central American developments, noting U.S. naval patrols in Honduras and widespread Dominican discontent over the newly approved U.S. treaty. Dominican citizens reportedly feared the United States was turning their debt-burdened republic into a fief, preferring multiple foreign creditors over a single American power. Due to this popular backlash, expectations grew that the Dominican Congress might reject the treaty.
records.summary_es: The New-York Tribune informó sobre los acontecimientos en el Caribe y Centroamérica, señalando los patrullajes navales estadounidenses en Honduras y el descontento generalizado de los dominicanos ante el tratado recién aprobado por los Estados Unidos. Según se comunicó, los ciudadanos dominicanos temían que los Estados Unidos estuvieran convirtiendo su endeudada república en un feudo, prefiriendo múltiples acreedores extranjeros a un único poder estadounidense. Debido a este rechazo popular, crecieron las expectativas de que el Congreso dominicano pudiera rechazar el tratado.

records.headline: Not only did it lead to the deposit in New York
records.summary_en: The New-York Tribune reported that the Dominican modus vivendi proved financially beneficial, resulting in $3,000,000 deposited in New York, increased revenues, four U.S.-built coastguard cutters, and reduced smuggling. Following Secretary Root's revision of the pending treaty, an agreement was reached between Finance Minister Federico Velasquez and foreign creditors to reduce claims by 50 percent for cash settlement. A New York banking house agreed to advance funds against $20,000,000 in fifty-year 5 percent bonds to consolidate Dominican debts.
records.summary_es: The New-York Tribune informó que el modus vivendi dominicano resultó económicamente provechoso, acumulando 3.000.000 de dólares depositados en Nueva York, un alza en los ingresos, cuatro guardacostas construidos en los Estados Unidos y la reducción del contrabando. Tras la revisión del tratado pendiente por el secretario Root, el ministro de Hacienda Federico Velásquez y los acreedores extranjeros alcanzaron un acuerdo para reducir las reclamaciones en un 50 por ciento mediante pago al contado. Una casa bancaria de Nueva York acordó adelantar fondos contra 20.000.000 de dólares en bonos a cincuenta años con un interés del 5 por ciento para consolidar las deudas dominicanas.
records.passage: The modus vivendi, however, resulted beneficially, as far as the little republic's finances were concerned. Not only did it lead to the deposit in New York of [illegible], which will now be placed to the credit of the Dominican government, but that government has had more available money during the period of its operation than at any other time in its history. This state of affairs resulted from a more economical administration, the suppression of smuggling and the encouragement of business. The Dominican government also finds itself in possession of four fine coastguard cutters, built in the United States, forming an effective force for the protection of the customs revenues and avail able for all public uses. The substance of the modus vivendi, in the shape of a treaty, was pending before the United States Senate when Secretary Root assumed office. Recognizing the force of the objections which developed to its ratification, he set about recasting the document, and on February 13 last the treaty which has just been ratified was submitted to the Senate. records.summary_en: The Birmingham Age-Herald reported that the 1905 modus vivendi deposited 55 percent of Dominican customs receipts in New York, accumulating $3,000,000 despite the overthrow of President Morales and the elevation of General Caceres. Secretary Root later recast the pending treaty after Dominican Finance Minister Federico Velasquez negotiated a 50 percent cash settlement reduction with foreign creditors. A New York banking firm agreed to advance the necessary funds by accepting $20,000,000 in 50-year 5 percent bonds, consolidating all foreign debts into a single entity.
records.summary_es: The Birmingham Age-Herald informó que el modus vivendi de 1905 depositaba el 55 por ciento de los ingresos de aduanas dominicanos en Nueva York, acumulando 3.000.000 de dólares a pesar del derrocamiento del presidente Morales y la asunción del general Cáceres. Más tarde, el secretario Root reformuló el tratado pendiente después de que el ministro de Hacienda dominicano, Federico Velásquez, negociara con los acreedores extranjeros una quita del 50 por ciento mediante pago en efectivo. Una firma bancaria de Nueva York acordó adelantar los fondos necesarios aceptando 20.000.000 de dólares en bonos a 50 años al 5 por ciento, consolidando todas las deudas externas en una sola obligación.

records.full_text:
TREATY RATIFIED BY SAN DOMINGO

Departure in United States' Relations to Small Republics

CONTROLS CUSTOM HOUSE

United States Now Becomes Legally a Trustee In a Financial Sense.

Will Discourage Revolutions.

Santo Domingo, May 3.—The new treaty between the United States and Santo Domingo intended to replace the treaty which has been pending before the United States Senate for the last two years was ratified by the Dominican congress today.

The Dominican treaty marks a new departure from the relations of the United States to the smaller republics of the western hemisphere, for in the case of Santo Domingo the United States now becomes legally a trustee in a financial sense, and must go so far in the preservation of order and the accompanying discouragement of revolutions as is incident to the control of the custom house.

The treaty really had its birth in a revolution. While the American government was pressing for a settlement of the claims of its citizens against Santo Domingo in December, 1904, President Morales being beset by revolutionists in the hope of securing the moral support of the United States, entered into an agreement with Captain Dillingham of the American navy by which the Dominican custom houses were to be occupied by the Americans and the foreign indebtedness of the country discharged from the receipts. Rejected at Washington, this agreement gave place March 31, 1905, to a modus vivendi which has operated up to this time. This placed an American collector in charge and provided for the deposit in New York of 55 per cent of the customs receipts for the benefit of the Dominican creditors. The modus vivendi did not save Morales from political destruction, as he was deported by the revolutionists and his vice president, General Caceres, installed as president. But the modus vivendi did lead to the deposit in New York of $3,000,000 which will now be placed to the credit of the Dominican government. That government has had more available money since the modus vivendi was established than any other time in its history. The Dominican government also finds itself in possession of four coast guard cutters built in the United States.

The modus vivendi was formed after a treaty pending before the United States Senate when Secretary Root assumed office. He recast the document, and February 19, last, the treaty which has just been ratified was submitted to the Senate. The way had been paved by an agreement between Federico Velasquez, the Dominican minister of finance, and the creditors of the republic whereby the latter agreed to a 50 per cent reduction in their claims if these were settled in cash.

A New York banking house undertook to advance the money for this purpose, accepting $20,000,000 5 per cent fifty-year bonds, which will now be promptly issued. Thus all of the creditors of Santo Domingo will be embodied in this New York firm.

The new treaty provides in its first article for the appointment by the President of a receiver of customs to collect the Dominican revenues as long as the bonds are outstanding, a period estimated at twenty to forty years. This collector is to pay the expenses of receivership, the interest on the bonds and the annual sums required for a mortization of the bonds, and then turn the balance over to the Dominican government. On the first day of each month he is to pay $100,000 to the fixed agent of the loan. When the customs receipts exceed $3,000,000 annually, then one-half of the surplus shall be applied to the sinking fund.

records.summary_en: The New-York Tribune reported on an interview with the former Dominican president, who described being detained in a palace during a visit to Port-au-Prince. He asserted that the era of Dominican revolutions had ended, praised President Caceres and the American customs receivership, but expressed firm opposition to annexation by the United States. He also stated his desire to return to Santo Domingo once a general amnesty was granted and recounted how political betrayal had forced his past flight.

Declaró además su deseo de regresar a Santo Domingo tan pronto se concediera una amnistía general y relató cómo la traición política había forzado su huida en el pasado.

records.headline: The suppression of an alleged revolutionary conspiracy in Cuba
records.summary_en: The suppression of an alleged revolutionary conspiracy in Cuba is detailed in a Havana dispatch in the New-York Tribune, noting that three Dominicans well known for their past revolutionary records arrived in port simultaneously with the conspirator Parra. The authorities also learned that other Dominican agitators were active in Eastern Cuba, and that General Jiménez, the former president of Santo Domingo, had recently visited Santiago de Cuba, though his connection to the conspiracy remained unconfirmed. Morning arrests reportedly thwarted the movement, while Provisional Governor Magoon stood prepared with 5,000 American soldiers and 5,000 rural guards to crush any further uprising.

Las autoridades supieron además que otros agitadores dominicanos operaban en el oriente de Cuba y que el general Jiménez, expresidente de Santo Domingo, había visitado recientemente Santiago de Cuba, aunque su vínculo con la conspiración no estaba confirmado. records.headline: The government on the charge of complicity in the revolutionary movement
records.summary_en: The New-York Tribune reported Consul General Medina's statement announcing the surrender of Dominican insurgent General Candelario de la Rosa and the pacification of refractory districts. Medina asserted that American revenue administration had restored national credit, enabling debt payments and attracting American capital into central pine forestry and railroad construction. He maintained that the government was fully prepared to counter any revolutionary efforts from Dominican exiles in Puerto Rico.
records.summary_es: The New-York Tribune informó sobre la declaración del cónsul general Medina en la que anunciaba la rendición del general insurgente dominicano Candelario de la Rosa y la pacificación de distritos rebeldes. Medina afirmó que la administración aduanera estadounidense había restaurado el crédito nacional, posibilitando el pago de deudas y atrayendo capital estadounidense hacia la explotación forestal de pinares centrales y la construcción de ferrocarriles. Sostuvo que el gobierno estaba plenamente preparado para contrarrestar cualquier tentativa revolucionaria proveniente de los exiliados dominicanos en Puerto Rico.

The consul general says that he has just received dispatches from Santo Domingo informing him of the surrender of General Candelario de la Rosa, who had for some time been giving the government trouble. He says that the hopes of the revolutionists are vain: that the government is prepared to meet every contingency, and that he is keeping a sharp watch on the Dominican exiles residing in Porto Rico. In referring to the actual condition in Santo Domingo, Consul General Medina makes the following statement:

At no time has the Dominican Republic been in such a favorable condition as at present. The fact that honest, strong and intelligent men are at the head of public affairs has raised the credit of the country. American control of the revenues has been the means of insuring a steady income, thus enabling the government not only to attend to its own needs but also to pay off the heavy debt that weighed down the country. With the assurance of lasting peace, capital is flowing into the republic. Within the last five or six months American companies have undertaken the tapping of the vast pine forests which cover the centre of the island, and the turpentine and lumber obtained will be a source of increased revenue. records.headline: A Washington report describes a new plan to settle the Dominican Republic's debt after the original bond sale to a New York firm
records.summary_en: A Washington report describes a new plan to settle the Dominican Republic's debt after the original bond sale to a New York firm fell through because of the money market. Foreign creditors recognized in the original project would receive an immediate pro rata cash payment from the $3,500,000 accumulated in the National City Bank from 55 per cent of the republic's customs revenues over two years, with the bond sale postponed or bonds issued directly by the Dominican government for the remainder, in a settlement to be discussed with Senor Velasquez at the State Department.
records.summary_es: Un informe de Washington describe un nuevo plan para saldar la deuda de la República Dominicana después de que la venta original de bonos a una firma de Nueva York fracasara por la situación del mercado monetario. Los acreedores extranjeros reconocidos en el proyecto original recibirían un pago inmediato en efectivo, a prorrata, del fondo de $3,500,000 acumulado en el National City Bank procedente del 55 por ciento de las rentas aduaneras de la república durante dos años, y la venta de bonos se pospondría o los bonos serían emitidos directamente por el gobierno dominicano por el resto, en un acuerdo que se discutiría con el señor Velásquez en el Departamento de Estado.
records.passage: public who were recognized in the original project and are willing to agree to accept the other features of the new scheme will receive an immediate cash payment of part of the money owing to them by a division on a pro rata basis of the fund of $3,500,000 which has accumulated in the National City Bank of New York as the result of the segregation of 55 per cent of the republic's customs revenues for the last two years. In consideration of this payment the sale of the bonds of the republic to some syndicate which will advance the cash to settle the remainder of the debt will be postponed until a more opportune time. A variation of this plan, which also will be considered by a conference to-morrow at the State Department between the officials and Senor Velasquez, the Dominican Secretary of Commerce and Finance, looks to the distribution of the accumulated cash as in the first case, but provides for the immediate issue to the creditors of bonds for the remainder of the obligation, which will be issued directly by the Dominican government. In either case it is contemplated that the Morton Trust Company and Speyer Co., who have acted as the fiscal agents for the Dominican government, will continue in that capacity and aid in carrying out the terms of the new agreement. records.summary_en: The New-York Tribune reported that the U.S. Secret Service arrested Giordani in New York, uncovering his role as the financial agent of a Haitian revolutionary movement under General Fermin. Giordani had previously contracted the printing of 1,500,000 "Deux Gourdes" banknotes, half of which had been stored in a New York warehouse after an earlier failed uprising. Federal authorities intervened to prevent the remaining currency from being shipped to finance active insurgent forces in Haiti.
records.summary_es: The New-York Tribune informó que el Servicio Secreto de los EE. records.headline: Senor Frederico Velasquez, minister of finance of Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: Senor Frederico Velasquez, minister of finance of Santo Domingo, and Senor Joubert, Dominican minister to the United States, held a conference yesterday with Secretary of State Root concerning the settlement of the Dominican Republic's foreign and internal debt, The Washington Herald reports. Velasquez is scheduled to return to Santo Domingo shortly, his mission regarding the amortization of the debt in the United States being practically completed. A fund of $4,000,000, representing 55 per cent of customs collections accumulated under American auspices, has been transferred from the National City Bank of New York to the Morton Trust Company for payment to creditors. The settlement will provide creditors with 20 per cent in cash and the remainder in bonds, with full distribution anticipated within several months.
records.summary_es: El señor Frederico Velásquez, ministro de Hacienda de Santo Domingo, y el señor Joubert, ministro dominicano ante los Estados Unidos, sostuvieron ayer una conferencia con el secretario de Estado Root, informa The Washington Herald, sobre la liquidación de la deuda externa e interna de la República Dominicana. Está previsto que Velásquez regrese pronto a Santo Domingo, habiendo concluido prácticamente su misión relativa a la amortización de la deuda en los Estados Unidos. La suma de $4.000.000, correspondiente al 55 por ciento de las recaudaciones aduaneras acumuladas bajo administración estadounidense, fue transferida del National City Bank de Nueva York a la Morton Trust Company para el pago a los acreedores. La liquidación otorgará a los acreedores el 20 por ciento en efectivo y el resto en bonos, previéndose la conclusión total de los pagos en pocos meses.

records.headline: The Washington Herald states that Dominican courts have sentenced
records.summary_en: The Washington Herald states that Dominican courts have sentenced Pedro Santiago and Mateo Garcia to twenty years' imprisonment at hard labor for the murder of customs receivership employees Charles B. Thurston and John Milbourne. The crime occurred on August 6, 1906 near the town of Las Matas on the Haitian frontier, after Thurston and Milbourne took custody of contraband goods seized by frontier guards. Santiago, principal owner of the cargo and then vice president of Las Matas, and Garcia, a municipal councilman with an interest in the contraband, led between thirty and forty men in attacking the customs party, killing Milbourne, mortally wounding Thurston, and seriously wounding a Dominican guard. Other participants in the smuggling group who failed to appear in court received identical sentences of imprisonment by default.
records.summary_es: The Washington Herald señala que los tribunales dominicanos sentenciaron a Pedro Santiago y Mateo García a veinte años de prisión con trabajos forzados por el asesinato de Charles B. Thurston y John Milbourne, empleados de la receptoría aduanera. El crimen se perpetró el 6 de agosto de 1906 cerca de la localidad de Las Matas, en la frontera con Haití, luego de que Thurston y Milbourne tomaran custodia de mercancías de contrabando decomisadas por la guardia fronteriza. Santiago, dueño principal del cargamento y en ese entonces vicepresidente de Las Matas, y García, regidor del ayuntamiento con participación en el contrabando, encabezaron a entre treinta y cuarenta hombres en un asalto contra los aduaneros, matando a Milbourne, hiriendo mortalmente a Thurston e hiriendo de gravedad a un guardia dominicano. Los demás integrantes de la partida de contrabandistas que no acudieron ante la justicia recibieron idénticas condenas de prisión en rebeldía.

records.headline: The Washington Herald reports that a new tariff schedule for Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The Washington Herald reports that a new tariff schedule for Santo Domingo will be submitted to the Dominican Congress within a few weeks. The existing customs schedule is described as antiquated and ill-suited to economic conditions, requiring a general revision that will considerably lower duties across many schedules to stimulate industry without overtaxing the population. The article observes that the Dominican Republic has enjoyed unusual prosperity under American customs supervision and administration of government finances. In accordance with an agreement with the republic, foreign creditors are being settled with 20 per cent in cash and the remainder in bonds, with $100,000 to be set aside annually for bond redemption.
records.summary_es: The Washington Herald informa que en pocas semanas se someterá al Congreso dominicano un nuevo arancel de aduanas para Santo Domingo. Se describe el régimen arancelario actual como anticuado y perjudicial para las condiciones económicas, haciéndose necesaria una reforma general que rebajará sustancialmente los derechos en diversos renglones a fin de incentivar las industrias sin abrumar a la población con cargas impositivas. El artículo destaca que la República Dominicana ha gozado de una prosperidad poco común bajo la supervisión aduanera y la administración fiscal estadounidense. Conforme a un acuerdo suscrito con la república, se abona a los acreedores extranjeros un 20 por ciento en efectivo y el saldo restante en bonos, consignándose anualmente una suma de $100.000 para amortizar los títulos de deuda.

records.summary_en: The Washington Times reports that Dr. Jacob H. Hollander, professor of political economy at Johns Hopkins University and financial adviser to the Dominican Republic, has approached the Department of Agriculture to find a scientific agricultural expert. The expert is required to instruct Dominicans in modern farming methods, with the Dominican government offering ample compensation and Secretary Wilson working to identify a candidate. Dr. Hollander stated that promoting agricultural modernization is essential both for the Dominican Republic and for American commercial interests, emphasizing that every effort should be made toward the economic rejuvenation of Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: The Washington Times informa que el doctor Jacob H. Hollander, profesor de economía política de la Universidad Johns Hopkins y asesor financiero de la República Dominicana, recurrió al Departamento de Agricultura para conseguir un experto científico en agronomía. Dicho especialista deberá instruir a los dominicanos en las más recientes técnicas de cultivo, ofreciendo el gobierno dominicano una atractiva retribución mientras el secretario Wilson se esfuerza por hallar al postulante adecuado. El doctor Hollander declaró que promover la modernización agrícola reviste gran importancia tanto para la República Dominicana como para el comercio estadounidense, destacando que debe hacerse cuanto sea posible por el resurgimiento económico de Santo Domingo.

records.summary_en: The Washington Times reports that the Department of Agriculture is seeking a qualified scientific agriculturist willing to reside in Santo Domingo to instruct local inhabitants in modern cultivation methods. Officials in Secretary Wilson's office revealed that the inquiry has thus far proven futile, as no applicant interested in the assignment has been found. Dr. Jacob H. Hollander, professor of political economy at Johns Hopkins University and financial adviser to the Dominican Republic, had turned to Secretary Wilson after an exhaustive nationwide search, but despite assurances of generous pay, he has been unable to attract an American agricultural expert to accept the position.

records.summary_en: The New-York Tribune reported on Major McIntyre's inspection of the Dominican customs receivership for the U.S. Bureau of Insular Affairs, noting steadily increasing revenues despite economic downturns. Under Receiver W. E. Pulliam, the receivership paid $100,000 monthly to the Morton Trust Company in New York while transferring the remainder to the Dominican government. McIntyre reported that nearly $5,000,000 had been deposited since 1905, with approximately $2,000,000 already distributed from the sinking fund to settle creditor claims.

Pulliam, la receptoría abonaba 100.000 dólares mensuales a la Morton Trust Company en Nueva York, transfiriendo el resto al gobierno dominicano. McIntyre comunicó que se habían depositado casi 5.000.000 de dólares desde 1905, habiéndose distribuido ya cerca de 2.000.000 de dólares del fondo de amortización para liquidar reclamaciones de acreedores.

records.headline: An official letter of June 25, sent to General Clarence R. Edwards of the Bureau of Insular Affairs
records.summary_en: An official letter of June 25, sent to General Clarence R. Edwards of the Bureau of Insular Affairs by W. E. Pulliam, United States receiver of customs in Santo Domingo, is outlined in a Washington dispatch in The Topeka State Journal. Pulliam writes that the inauguration of President Caceres signals a new era for the Dominican Republic and effectively discourages revolutionary movements. Highlighting significant gains in public revenues, Pulliam reports that General Ramon Caceres, who assumed office in January 1906 following the flight and deportation of President Morales, has been elected to a full six-year constitutional term beginning July 1.

Pulliam manifiesta que la toma de posesión del presidente Cáceres inaugura una nueva época para la República Dominicana y neutraliza eficazmente las tentativas revolucionarias. Tras subrayar los notables avances en las arcas públicas, Pulliam resalta que el general Ramón Cáceres, quien asumió el mando en enero de 1906 tras la fuga y destierro del presidente Morales, fue electo para un mandato constitucional de seis años a partir del 1 de julio.

records.headline: Public works appropriations in Santo Domingo are reported by The Daily Telegram
records.summary_en: Public works appropriations in Santo Domingo are reported by The Daily Telegram, including a budget allocation for an experimental agricultural school to better exploit the country's rich soil and climate. The dispatch lists an appropriation of $75,000 to extend irrigation in the Monte Cristi district and an outlay of 119.200 for two wireless telegraph stations, with the station in the capital more than half completed to secure independent external communication. A Director General of Public Works has been instituted and filled by an experienced foreign engineer to supervise national improvements. In addition, the Dominican government has taken over the Puerto Plata and Santiago railway, designated as the Ferrocarril Central Dominicano, from the Santo Domingo Improvement Company.
records.summary_es: Diversas partidas destinadas a obras públicas en Santo Domingo son informadas por The Daily Telegram, incluyendo fondos para una escuela práctica de agricultura a fin de sacar mayor provecho de la fertilidad del suelo y del clima favorable. El despacho enumera una partida de $75.000 para ampliar los regadíos en el distrito de Monte Cristi y una dotación de 119.200 (según el texto) para dos estaciones de radiotelegrafía, hallándose la estación de la capital avanzada en más de la mitad para dotar al país de comunicación exterior autónoma. Asimismo, se creó la Dirección General de Obras Públicas, confiada a un ingeniero foráneo experimentado para coordinar las obras de fomento. Además, el gobierno dominicano asumió la explotación del ferrocarril de Puerto Plata a Santiago, conocido como el Ferrocarril Central Dominicano, retirándolo de manos de la Santo Domingo Improvement Company.

Edwards of the Bureau of Insular Affairs. Pulliam conveys that the inauguration of President Ramon Caceres initiates a new era in which revolutionary movements have been effectively discouraged. The dispatch emphasizes extraordinary revenue growth, with fiscal income beginning July 1 estimated at $3,048,300, the largest in Dominican history. After reserving $1,200,000 payable in monthly allotments of $100,000 for bond interest and amortization, the remaining funds available for government expenditures surpass the nation's total federal receipts of four years ago.

records.headline: Official correspondence from American customs receiver W. E. Pulliam
records.summary_en: Official correspondence from American customs receiver W. E. Pulliam is pointed to by the New-York Tribune, writing editorially, as evidence of remarkable fiscal and political progress in Santo Domingo. The editorial argues that this record confirms the transformative impact of American assistance, which has established a new era in Dominican history. The paper strongly rejects the label "Black Republic" applied by uninformed writers, maintaining that while such a term might accurately describe neighboring Haiti, the Dominican Republic has historically maintained a substantial majority of white inhabitants.
records.summary_es: La correspondencia oficial del receptor aduanero estadounidense W. E. Pulliam es destacada por el New-York Tribune, en sus columnas editoriales, como demostración de un notable avance financiero y político en Santo Domingo. La nota argumenta que estos resultados confirman el impacto transformador del respaldo norteamericano, el cual ha dado origen a una nueva etapa en la historia dominicana. El rotativo desestima tajantemente el calificativo de "República Negra" empleado por autores desinformados, sosteniendo que si bien tal término podría adecuarse al vecino Haití, la República Dominicana ha contado históricamente con una considerable mayoría de habitantes blancos.

records.headline: The New-York Tribune details Santo Domingo government appropriations
records.summary_en: The New-York Tribune details Santo Domingo government appropriations aimed at promoting immigration and economic development, noting a fund voted to settle agricultural workers along the frontier with Haiti after the pattern of Spanish immigration into Cuba and Puerto Rico. An additional $40,000 was appropriated for an experimental agricultural school to increase crop returns from the republic's fertile soil. The dispatch notes an appropriation to sustain Monte Cristi irrigation works and an allotment for two wireless telegraph stations, the capital installation being more than half completed. The report also highlights a significant appropriation creating the office of director general of public works.
records.summary_es: El New-York Tribune detalla las partidas presupuestarias del gobierno en Santo Domingo destinadas al fomento de la inmigración y el desarrollo económico, señalando un fondo para asentar trabajadores agrícolas en la frontera con Haití siguiendo el modelo de la inmigración española en Cuba y Puerto Rico. Se aprobaron otros $40.000 para una escuela práctica de agricultura orientada a elevar el rendimiento de los fértiles suelos de la república. El despacho consigna una asignación para continuar los regadíos de Monte Cristi y una partida para dos estaciones radiotelegráficas, hallándose la de la capital avanzada en más de la mitad. Asimismo, la crónica resalta una asignación significativa que crea la Dirección General de Obras Públicas.

The paper also noted reports from Haiti that insurgent leader General Jean Jumeau was alive and preparing an insurrection against President Nord Alexis.

records.headline: The Daily Press reports on public appropriations in Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The Daily Press reports on public appropriations in Santo Domingo, including $40,000 for an experimental agricultural school to enhance crop yields from the island's fertile soil and favorable climate. An appropriation of $75,000 was approved to extend irrigation works in the Monte Cristi district, while $19,200 was made available for two wireless telegraph stations, with the station at the capital over half finished. The dispatch notes that a Director General of Public Works has been appointed to supervise national improvements. Furthermore, the Dominican government has taken over the railway between Puerto Plata and Santiago, known as the Ferrocarril Central Dominicano, from the Santo Domingo Improvement Company.
records.summary_es: The Daily Press da cuenta de las partidas presupuestarias en Santo Domingo, entre ellas $40.000 para una escuela práctica de agricultura con el propósito de optimizar los rendimientos agrícolas del fértil suelo y clima de la isla. Se aprobó una partida de $75.000 para extender las obras de irrigación en el distrito de Monte Cristi, en tanto que se asignaron $19.200 para dos estaciones radiotelegráficas, encontrándose la de la capital terminada en más de la mitad. El despacho añade que se designó un director general de Obras Públicas para coordinar el plan de obras públicas. Además, el gobierno dominicano asumió la administración directa del ferrocarril entre Puerto Plata y Santiago, conocido como Ferrocarril Central Dominicano, tras retirárselo a la Santo Domingo Improvement Company.

records.headline: A report in The Freeman states that General Clarence K. Edwards
records.summary_en: A report in The Freeman states that General Clarence K. Edwards, chief of the Bureau of Insular Affairs of the War Department, has received a letter from M. E. Pulliam, United States receiver of customs of Santo Domingo. Pulliam expresses the belief that with the inauguration of President Caceres, the Dominican Republic entered upon a new era and the last vestige of formidable revolutionary tendencies has been effectively discouraged. The letter highlights immense financial improvement, estimating income for the fiscal year beginning July 1 at $3,948,300, the largest in Dominican history. Pulliam adds that after deducting $1,200,000 in monthly installments of $100,000 for bond interest and amortization, available funds for government expenditures will exceed the entire federal income of four years ago.

La carta resalta una inmensa mejora financiera y estima los ingresos para el año fiscal iniciado el 1 de julio en 3,948,300 dólares, la mayor cifra en la historia dominicana. records.headline: The career and financial activities of Mrs. Reader are described
records.summary_en: The career and financial activities of Mrs. Reader are described in an article in The Virginia Enterprise; Mrs. Reader maintains an office at 45 Broadway. The report states that she came prominently before the public after visiting the State Department in Washington with letters claiming full authority to negotiate international agreements between Santo Domingo and any foreign nation. She sued capitalist J. B. Haggin for $3,150,000 damages for alleged slander and accused the United States government of conspiring to defeat her plans for re-establishing the Dominican Republic. The piece notes her previous work as a soda fountain attendant and stenographer, as well as an unpaid grocery debt to Butler that resulted in a court judgment against her.

records.headline: A report in The Evening World outlines allegations in a complaint
records.summary_en: A report in The Evening World outlines allegations in a complaint by Gaylord regarding Wall Street firm A. O. Brown & Co. prior to its collapse. Gaylord claims that the brokerage firm's Wall Street coup was minor compared to the heaps of gold—estimated at an amount printed as HSOOOOMOOOO—expected from their interests in the San Domingo Company in the Dominican Republic. The complaint charges that Gaylord paid 120 per share for his stock, while firm member Edward V. Buchanan acquired large blocks at a far lower price, and the firm sold stock to third parties at a rate printed as M per share. Gaylord further asserts that the Dominican gold properties are practically worthless and that the defendants never owned them.

La demanda señala que Gaylord pagó 120 por acción, mientras que Edward V. Gaylord asevera además que los yacimientos auríferos dominicanos carecen prácticamente de valor y que los demandados nunca fueron sus legítimos propietarios.

records.summary_en: The Semi-Weekly Herald reviewed the outcome of the 1905 Dominican customs arrangement instituted by President Roosevelt to avert foreign military intervention over unpaid debts. Despite initial domestic controversy and Senate delays over Roosevelt's executive authority, the system transferred 45 percent of collections to the Dominican government and 55 percent to debt liquidation. The paper noted that the policy achieved a total transformation in the country, stabilizing public finances and virtually eliminating civil insurrections.
records.summary_es: The Semi-Weekly Herald analizó los resultados del arreglo aduanero dominicano de 1905 instituido por el presidente Roosevelt para eludir una intervención militar extranjera por deudas impagas. Pese a la controversia nacional inicial y las demoras en el Senado en torno a las atribuciones ejecutivas de Roosevelt, el sistema transfirió el 45 por ciento de la recaudación al gobierno dominicano y el 55 por ciento a la liquidación de la deuda. El periódico destacó que esta política logró una transformación total en el país, estabilizando las finanzas públicas y eliminando prácticamente las insurrecciones civiles.

San Domingo was deeply in debt, and as it had for some time previous ceased to meet obligations, its foreign creditors were clamoring for a settlement and were threatening to collect their claims by force. Realizing that something would have to be done to avert the dangerous complications which were manifestly impending, Mr. Roosevelt instituted negotiations which resulted in the execution in February, 1905, of an agreement whereby officials appointed by the United States government were to collect the customs' receipts and after paying 45 per cent of the same to the Dominican authorities were to apply the remaining [illegible] per cent to the liquidation of the outstanding indebtedness. It will not have been forgotten how bitterly the president was criticised for his action in the premises. records.headline: A detailed survey in The Sun reviews substantial transportation
records.summary_en: A detailed survey in The Sun reviews substantial transportation and security developments across the Dominican Republic. Railroad projects include a projected line of eighty-five miles connecting Monte Cristi to Santiago, an inland extension of the private Sanchez and Samana Railroad, and government plans for a railway along the southern coast. The Dominican government has also acquired the concession of the Clyde Steamship Company, eliminating its monopolistic port fees and opening harbors to competing steamship lines and sailing vessels. Additionally, the administration has erected two wireless telegraph stations, works to improve postal communication and reduce rates to the United States, and has replaced irregular militia with the well-equipped and strictly disciplined Guardia Republicana.
records.summary_es: Una reseña detallada en The Sun examina importantes adelantos en materia de transporte y seguridad en la República Dominicana. Entre los proyectos ferroviarios figuran una línea proyectada de ochenta y cinco millas que conectará Monte Cristi con Santiago, la extensión hacia el interior del ferrocarril privado de Sánchez y Samaná, y planes gubernamentales para una vía férrea a lo largo de la costa sur. El gobierno dominicano también adquirió la concesión de la Clyde Steamship Company, suprimiendo sus tasas portuarias monopólicas y abriendo los puertos a navieras competidoras y buques de vela. Asimismo, la administración ha instalado dos estaciones radiotelegráficas, busca mejorar el servicio postal reduciendo las tarifas hacia los Estados Unidos y ha sustituido a las milicias irregulares por una disciplinada y bien equipada Guardia Republicana.

records.headline: An article reprinted from Leslie's Weekly in The Birmingham Age-Herald cites
records.summary_en: An article reprinted from Leslie's Weekly in The Birmingham Age-Herald cites observations by Consul R. J. Totten of Puerto Plata concerning music in the Dominican Republic. Totten notes that the Dominican people are very fond of music, with municipal bands playing in public plazas, most men playing the mandolin and guitar, and well-to-do homes possessing pianos and graphophones. The report highlights an opening for American enterprise, observing that the nation possesses only a single regular music store, located in Santo Domingo city. As a consequence, inhabitants of the northern districts order instruments through commission merchants, with most orders placed in Europe because American manufacturers have neglected the trade.
records.summary_es: Un artículo reproducido de Leslie's Weekly en The Birmingham Age-Herald cita comentarios del cónsul R. J. Totten en Puerto Plata sobre la música en la República Dominicana. Totten destaca la gran afición de los dominicanos por la música, con bandas municipales que ofrecen conciertos en las plazas públicas, la mayoría de los hombres ejecutando la mandolina y la guitarra, y familias acomodadas que cuentan con pianos y grafófonos. El informe resalta una oportunidad comercial para empresas estadounidenses, indicando que la república posee una única tienda formal de música, ubicada en la ciudad de Santo Domingo. En consecuencia, los habitantes de la región norte solicitan sus instrumentos a través de comisionistas, enviándose la mayor parte de los pedidos a Europa ante el descuido del mercado por parte de los fabricantes norteamericanos.

records.headline: The widespread appreciation of music throughout the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: The widespread appreciation of music throughout the Dominican Republic is described in a dispatch credited to Leslie's Weekly in The Newark Star and Newark Advertiser. Municipal bands perform regularly in central town plazas, men from all walks of life play the mandolin and guitar, and pianos and graphophones are common in prosperous homes. The piece emphasizes that the country has only one regular music store, situated in the capital city of Santo Domingo, obliging consumers in the north to place orders through commission merchants. Because American manufacturers have failed to cultivate this market, European firms supply most of the demand for guitars, banjos, mandolins, pianos, and graphophones.
records.summary_es: La extendida apreciación musical en toda la República Dominicana es descrita en un despacho atribuido a Leslie's Weekly en The Newark Star and Newark Advertiser. Bandas municipales tocan habitualmente en las plazas centrales de los pueblos, hombres de diversos estratos tocan la mandolina y la guitarra, y los pianos y grafófonos son frecuentes en las casas acomodadas. La crónica subraya que el país solo cuenta con una tienda formal de música, situada en la capital, Santo Domingo, lo que compele a los consumidores del norte a formular sus pedidos mediante intermediarios comisionistas. Debido a que las firmas manufactureras estadounidenses no han atendido este mercado, las casas europeas abastecen la mayor parte de la demanda de guitarras, banjos, mandolinas, pianos y grafófonos.

records.headline: A Cape Haitien dispatch of May 23 in The San Francisco Call
records.summary_en: A Cape Haitien dispatch of May 23 in The San Francisco Call, transmitted by courier from Monte Cristi, reports that the revolutionary movement against the Dominican government is spreading. Forces under General Camacho, former governor of Monte Cristi, operating in unison with General Quirito Felice, have attacked and captured Guayubin and Dajabon along the Haitian frontier at the Dajabon River. Clashes have occurred between insurgents and loyal forces at Monte Cristi, while the fate of Puerto Plata Governor Jose Bordas remains uncertain amid reports that he is either dead or imprisoned. With overland communications severed, Dominican government troops are expected to reach the disturbed districts by sea.
records.summary_es: Un despacho del 23 de mayo desde Cabo Haitiano en The San Francisco Call, enviado por mensajero desde Monte Cristi, informa que el movimiento revolucionario contra el gobierno dominicano se extiende. Fuerzas al mando del general Camacho, exgobernador de Monte Cristi, actuando en conjunto con el general Quirito Felice, han atacado y tomado Guayubín y Dajabón a lo largo de la frontera haitiana en el río Dajabón. Se han registrado enfrentamientos entre insurgentes y fuerzas leales en Monte Cristi, mientras que la suerte del gobernador de Puerto Plata, José Bordas, sigue siendo incierta entre informes de que está muerto o prisionero. Al hallarse interrumpidas las comunicaciones terrestres, se espera que las tropas gubernamentales lleguen por mar a las zonas sublevadas.

records.headline: A Cape Haitien dispatch of May 24 in The Richmond Palladium
records.summary_en: A Cape Haitien dispatch of May 24 in The Richmond Palladium and Sun-Telegram reports that the Dominican revolution is gaining strength, prompting the government to dispatch troops by sea because overland communications are cut. Insurgents under General Camacho, former governor of Monte Cristi, and General Quirito Felice have occupied Guayubin and Dajabon along the Haitian frontier. The dispatch adds that Puerto Plata Governor Jose Bordas was captured during fighting between government troops and revolutionists at Monte Cristi and is feared dead.
records.summary_es: Un despacho del 24 de mayo desde Cabo Haitiano en The Richmond Palladium and Sun-Telegram informa que la revolución dominicana cobra fuerza, lo que obligó al gobierno a despachar tropas por mar debido a que las comunicaciones terrestres se encuentran cortadas. Insurgentes comandados por el general Camacho, exgobernador de Monte Cristi, y el general Quirito Felice han ocupado Guayubín y Dajabón a lo largo de la frontera haitiana. El despacho agrega que el gobernador de Puerto Plata, José Bordas, fue hecho prisionero durante los combates librados entre fuerzas del gobierno y revolucionarios en Monte Cristi y se teme que haya muerto.

records.headline: A Cape Haitien cable of May 23 in The Birmingham Age-Herald
records.summary_en: A Cape Haitien cable of May 23 in The Birmingham Age-Herald, transmitted via courier from Monte Cristi, reports that internal conflict is spreading across Santo Domingo. Rebel forces led by General Camacho, former governor of Monte Cristi, and General Quirito Felice have captured the frontier towns of Guayubin and Dajabon along the Dajabon River bordering Haiti. Fighting has taken place at Monte Cristi between government loyalists and revolutionists seeking to overthrow the administration. Puerto Plata Governor Jose Bordas is reported either dead or a prisoner, and government reinforcements are expected to travel by sea because land communications are cut off.
records.summary_es: Un cable del 23 de mayo desde Cabo Haitiano en The Birmingham Age-Herald, transmitido por mensajero desde Monte Cristi, informa que el conflicto interno se extiende por Santo Domingo. Fuerzas rebeldes encabezadas por el general Camacho, exgobernador de Monte Cristi, y el general Quirito Felice han tomado las localidades fronterizas de Guayubín y Dajabón a lo largo del río Dajabón, en el límite con Haití. Se han registrado combates en Monte Cristi entre fuerzas leales al gobierno y revolucionarios que buscan deponer a la administración. Se reporta que el gobernador de Puerto Plata, José Bordas, se encuentra muerto o prisionero, y se prevé que refuerzos gubernamentales viajen por mar al encontrarse cortadas las comunicaciones terrestres.

records.headline: A New York dispatch of July 1 in The Citizen reports that the British steamship
records.summary_en: A New York dispatch of July 1 in The Citizen reports that the British steamship Ethelwold has been denied clearance papers by order of the secretary of commerce and labor on suspicion of outfitting a filibustering expedition to Santo Domingo. The vessel had been moored near Francis Bannerman's firearms warehouse, prompting Haitian minister Senor Sannon to alert the State Department because Haiti shares the island with the Dominican Republic. Captain Brown of the Ethelwold is believed to be acting in conjunction with two Dominican politicians in the United States, named in print as Glordania and Jlmluez, to transport munitions to sea for transfer to another vessel.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Nueva York del 1 de julio en The Citizen informa que al vapor británico Ethelwold se le han denegado los documentos de despacho por orden del secretario de Comercio y Trabajo, bajo sospecha de equipar una expedición filibustera a Santo Domingo. La nave había permanecido amarrada cerca del almacén de armas de fuego de Francis Bannerman, lo que llevó al ministro haitiano, el señor Sannon, a alertar al Departamento de Estado debido a que Haití comparte la isla con la República Dominicana. Se cree que el capitán Brown del Ethelwold actuaba de concierto con dos políticos dominicanos en los Estados Unidos, identificados en el texto como Glordania y Jlmluez, para transportar pertrechos a alta mar y transbordarlos a otra nave.

records.headline: A Washington dispatch of October 7 in The Sun announces that Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: A Washington dispatch of October 7 in The Sun announces that Santo Domingo is preparing to revise its customs tariff downward, with a special session of the Dominican Congress called for October 15 to enact the changes. Since the United States began supervising Dominican customs collections, annual receipts have exceeded $3,000,000. As this amount surpasses what is needed to cover government operating expenses and public debt amortization, several burdensome schedules in the existing tariff will be reduced.

Desde que los Estados Unidos comenzaron a supervisar la recaudación aduanera dominicana, los ingresos anuales han superado los 3 000 000 de dólares. En vista de que esta suma sobrepasa lo necesario para cubrir los gastos corrientes del gobierno y la amortización de la deuda pública, se reducirán varias partidas gravosas del arancel vigente.

records.summary_en: A dispatch in the Evening Star indicates that political unrest near the Haitian frontier is intensifying according to advices from Santo Domingo. A Dominican cutter arrived to receive instructions from the government after communication with Monte Cristo was interrupted. The crew reported that a cruiser from Puerto Plata had reached Monte Cristo carrying troops with orders to disembark at Port Liberte on the Haitian coast and attack rebel forces led by General Andre Navarro, who are concentrated at Dajabon.

La tripulación informó que un crucero procedente de Puerto Plata había llegado a Monte Cristo transportando tropas con órdenes de desembarcar en Port Liberté, en la costa haitiana, y atacar a las fuerzas rebeldes comandadas por el general André Navarro, concentradas en Dajabón.

records.headline: In a Cape Haitien dispatch of October 14, The Newark Star and Newark Advertiser reports
records.summary_en: In a Cape Haitien dispatch of October 14, The Newark Star and Newark Advertiser reports that political disturbance near the Haitian frontier is growing increasingly serious, following earlier fighting in which several men were killed on either side and others wounded. A Dominican cutter reached Cape Haitien to seek instructions from the Santo Domingo government due to interrupted communications with Monte Cristo. The cutter's crew stated that a cruiser had arrived at Monte Cristo from Puerto Plata bearing troops ordered to land at Port Liberte on the Haitian coast to engage revolutionary forces assembled at Dajabon under General Andre Navarro.
records.summary_es: En un despacho de Cape Haitien del 14 de octubre, The Newark Star and Newark Advertiser informa que los disturbios políticos cerca de la frontera haitiana se agravan, tras combates previos en los que murieron varios hombres en ambos bandos y otros resultaron heridos. Un guardacostas dominicano llegó a Cape Haitien en busca de instrucciones del gobierno de Santo Domingo debido a la interrupción de las comunicaciones con Monte Cristo. La tripulación del guardacostas declaró que un crucero había arribado a Monte Cristo procedente de Puerto Plata con tropas bajo órdenes de desembarcar en Port Liberté, en la costa haitiana, para combatir a las fuerzas revolucionarias reunidas en Dajabón bajo el mando del general André Navarro.

records.headline: Tariff revision has become central before the Dominican Congress
records.summary_en: Tariff revision has become central before the Dominican Congress, which convened today, a Santo Domingo dispatch of October 15 in The Laramie Republican reports. The legislature is approximately evenly split between revisionists and 'stand-patters,' setting the stage for a sharp political confrontation. Apprehensions are voiced that the dispute could provoke an armed revolution and topple the administration, while President Ramon Caceres preserves a neutral stance.
records.summary_es: La revisión arancelaria se ha convertido en asunto central ante el Congreso dominicano, que se reunió hoy, según un despacho de Santo Domingo del 15 de octubre en The Laramie Republican. El poder legislativo se encuentra dividido casi en partes iguales entre revisionistas y partidarios del statu quo, configurando el escenario para una dura confrontación política. Se expresan temores de que la disputa pueda desencadenar una revolución armada y derrocar a la administración, mientras el presidente Ramón Cáceres conserva una postura neutral.

While concerns exist that the conflict could precipitate a revolution and the fall of the government, President Ramon Caceres remains neutral.

Aunque existen temores de que el conflicto pueda precipitar una revolución y la caída del gobierno, el presidente Ramón Cáceres permanece neutral.

records.headline: An educational feature in The Washington Herald details how
records.summary_en: An educational feature in The Washington Herald details how land tenure originated in the Dominican Republic, noting that practically all land grants date back to the early part of the fifteenth century. The Spanish portion of the island was partitioned by natural landmarks into extensive tracts bestowed by the Spanish crown upon prominent leaders and nobles. These holdings were subsequently divided into parcels of 1,000 to 100,000 acres—known as communes—and granted to retainers or sold to incoming settlers, forming the legal foundation for all modern land titles.
records.summary_es: Una crónica divulgativa en The Washington Herald detalla el origen de la tenencia de la tierra en la República Dominicana, señalando que prácticamente todas las concesiones territoriales se remontan a principios del siglo XV (según se consigna en el despacho). La parte española de la isla fue delimitada mediante accidentes naturales en extensas extensiones otorgadas por la corona española a nobles y caudillos prominentes. Estas propiedades fueron posteriormente fraccionadas en parcelas de 1 000 a 100 000 acres —conocidas como comunes— y concedidas a allegados o vendidas a colonos recién llegados, formando la base jurídica de todos los títulos de propiedad modernos.

Attempts are being made to charter a steamer to make a descent on Santo Domingo with a President Designate and his staff.

Kingston, Jamaica, Nov. 5.—A revolutionary Santo Domingo junta has established headquarters here, and this morning a sloop belonging to it took out clearance papers for Hayti. Her destination, however, is believed to be some point on the Dominican coast. On board the sloop are some of the principal revolutionary leaders. Attempts are being made here to charter a steamer in order to make a descent on Santo Domingo with a President Designate and his staff. ESTRADA DEFEATED. Zelaya's Forces Reported Moving on Rama.

Managua, Nicaragua, Nov. 4 (Delayed in transmission).—Government troops defeated the revolutionists in a sharp engagement to-day, many of General Estrada's followers being killed, wounded or captured. The government lost fifteen men, including General Castillo [Chamorro?]. President Zelaya's forces attacked the rebel general, Fornos Diaz, at Paso las Lajas, capturing that point, which had been defended by four hundred men. The rebels fled in the direction of Rama and were pursued. The above dispatch, which the correspondent was unable to get through yesterday, refers doubtless to the battle of Thursday, concerning which conflicting reports reached New Orleans and Washington. MOVING ON DOMINGO. Efforts in Jamaica to Aid the Insurrection.

Kingston, Jamaica, Nov. 5.—A revolutionary Santo Domingo junta has established headquarters here, and this morning a sloop belonging to it took out clearance papers for Hayti. Her destination, however, is believed to be some point on the Dominican coast. On board the sloop are some of the principal revolutionary leaders.

Attempts are being made here to charter a steamer in order to make a descent on Santo Domingo with a President Designate and his staff.

records.headline: A commercial report in the Evening Journal cites Ralph J. Totten
records.summary_en: A commercial report in the Evening Journal cites Ralph J. Totten, United States consul at Puerto Plata, stating that the island of Haiti and specifically the Santo Domingo republic could assume a prominent position among cotton-producing territories. Although cotton farming is still experimental, tree cotton grows wild throughout northern parts of the island, yielding a coarse, short, but bright white fiber used locally for bedding. Deliberate cultivation for export began in Monte Cristi province in the spring of 1907, where landowners and merchants planted experimental plots with imported sea-island seed, native seed, and mixed varieties, producing plants that yield for at least three years.
records.summary_es: Un informe comercial en el Evening Journal cita a Ralph J. Totten, cónsul de los Estados Unidos en Puerto Plata, señalando que la isla de Haití y en particular la república de Santo Domingo podrían asumir un papel destacado entre los territorios productores de algodón. Si bien el cultivo algodonero es aún experimental, el algodón arbóreo crece silvestre en el norte de la isla, produciendo una fibra áspera y corta pero de gran blancura utilizada localmente para colchonería. El cultivo sistemático para exportación comenzó en la provincia de Monte Cristi en la primavera de 1907, donde hacendados y comerciantes sembraron parcelas de prueba con semilla importada sea-island, nativa y variedades mixtas, obteniendo plantas que rinden cosechas durante al menos tres años.

Champaign, Ill., Nov. 18 — Aversion to babies and domestic life is ascribed as the cause for the suicide today of Prof. Wilfred C. Wheeler, first assistant in chemistry in the engineering experiment station of the university of Illinois. The chemist's body was found on the university campus. He took a large quantity of cyanide of potassium. It was said tonight that Professor Wheeler took his meals away from home after a baby came into the household. records.headline: The government has purchased several onerous wharf and warehouse concessions, and has reduced the port charges
records.summary_en: The Evening Star detailed extensive public works and infrastructure projects advancing in the Dominican Republic, including the purchase and expansion of the Puerto Plata-Santiago railroad and new branch lines. The Dominican government reduced port fees, dredged the Ozama River, surveyed irrigation systems in Monte Cristi and Azua, and initiated macadamized highway construction between the capital and San Cristobal. The report lauded the country's economic potential, civic improvements, and the hospitality of its citizens.
records.summary_es: The Evening Star detalló los amplios proyectos de obras públicas e infraestructura que avanzaban en la República Dominicana, incluyendo la adquisición y ampliación del ferrocarril de Puerto Plata a Santiago y nuevos ramales. El gobierno dominicano redujo las tasas portuarias, dragó el río Ozama, realizó estudios para sistemas de irrigación en Monte Cristi y Azua, e inició la construcción de una carretera macadamizada entre la capital y San Cristóbal. El informe alabó el potencial económico del país, sus mejoras urbanas y la hospitalidad de sus habitantes.

JOUBERT'S RANK RAISED.

The Dominican republic now has an envoy extraordinary and minister plenipotentiary in Washington. Emilio C. Joubert presented his credentials raising his rank to President Taft yesterday.

records.headline: An article in the Evening Star recounts the establishment of the first Christian church
records.summary_en: An article in the Evening Star recounts the establishment of the first Christian church in the New World, built on the north coast of Santo Domingo by Christopher Columbus. Returning on his second voyage in 1493 to find Fort Navidad destroyed and its garrison slain, Columbus withdrew to a harbor near Monte Cristi and founded the settlement of Isabella. There he constructed a stone church dedicated to St. Michael, supplied with a bell presented by King Ferdinand, along with a stone royal storehouse and governor's palace. After the discovery of gold in the interior prompted Isabella's abandonment, surviving cut stone from the ruins was collected by the warship Enterprise and brought to the United States.
records.summary_es: Un artículo en el Evening Star relata la fundación de la primera iglesia cristiana en el Nuevo Mundo, levantada en la costa norte de Santo Domingo por Cristóbal Colón. Al regresar en su segundo viaje en 1493 y hallar el fuerte de La Navidad destruido y su guarnición aniquilada, Colón se retiró hacia un fondeadero cerca de Monte Cristi y fundó el poblado de La Isabela. Allí erigió una iglesia de piedra consagrada a San Miguel, provista de una campana obsequiada por el rey Fernando, además de un almacén real y un palacio de gobierno también de piedra. Tras el hallazgo de oro en el interior que provocó el abandono de La Isabela, los sillares labrados que subsistían en las ruinas fueron recogidos por el buque de guerra Enterprise y llevados a los Estados Unidos.
