records.headline: The Washington Herald reports that renewed revolutionary outbreaks
records.summary_en: The Washington Herald reports that renewed revolutionary outbreaks have occurred at Puerto Plata in the Dominican Republic, prompting the gunboat Nashville to proceed to that port to monitor the situation. U.S. officials believe the warship's presence will go far toward restoring order following several months of brewing revolt in the region, where Haitians are accused in some quarters of stirring up unrest near their territory. The Nashville had previously maintained a watch at Santo Domingo City from midwinter until the preceding month, when naval authorities required the vessel's presence at Guantanamo and Santiago.
records.summary_es: The Washington Herald informa que se han producido nuevos brotes revolucionarios en Puerto Plata, República Dominicana, lo que motivó el envío del cañonero Nashville a dicho puerto para vigilar la situación. Las autoridades estadounidenses confían en que la presencia del buque de guerra contribuirá en gran medida a restablecer el orden tras varios meses de creciente revuelta en la región, donde en algunos sectores se acusa a los haitianos de fomentar disturbios cerca de su territorio. El Nashville había permanecido previamente vigilando la ciudad de Santo Domingo desde mediados del invierno hasta el mes anterior, cuando las autoridades navales requirieron la presencia del buque en Guantánamo y Santiago.

records.headline: Minister Furniss left Santo Domingo City for the Haitian-Dominican frontier
records.summary_en: Minister Furniss left Santo Domingo City for the Haitian-Dominican frontier to assist in establishing a proposed neutral zone between the two republics, The Washington Herald reports, pending settlement of their long-standing boundary dispute. Dispatches received by the State Department describe conditions along the border as deeply disturbing. Meanwhile, revolutionary disturbances are also taking place at Puerto Plata, identified as a Dominican port near the Haitian border.
records.summary_es: El ministro Furniss partió de la ciudad de Santo Domingo hacia la frontera domínico-haitiana para colaborar en el establecimiento de una proyectada zona neutral entre ambas repúblicas, según informa The Washington Herald, en espera de la solución de su prolongada disputa limítrofe. Los despachos recibidos por el Departamento de Estado califican la situación a lo largo de la frontera como sumamente inquietante. Entre tanto, también se están produciendo disturbios revolucionarios en Puerto Plata, identificado como un puerto dominicano cercano a la frontera haitiana.

records.headline: A report in The Sun states that State Department advices describe
records.summary_en: A report in The Sun states that State Department advices describe conditions along the Haitian-Dominican border as disturbing, with revolutionary disturbances occurring at Puerto Plata and allegations that Haiti is encouraging Dominican insurgents while the U.S. gunboat Nashville remains stationed at Puerto Plata. The mutual boundary has been a source of friction for years as densely populated Haiti presses against the line maintained by Santo Domingo and each government accuses the other of encroaching on alien territory. Haiti is charged with using its low import tariff to permit the importation and smuggling of arms into Santo Domingo, where high tariffs prevail, delivering weapons to rebels on easy terms. In response, it has been proposed that the Dominican Republic retaliate by allowing Haitians to export coffee through Dominican ports under low duties, which would severely impair Haitian government revenues that depend almost entirely on coffee export taxes.
records.summary_es: Un informe en The Sun señala que los despachos del Departamento de Estado describen la situación a lo largo de la frontera domínico-haitiana como inquietante, con disturbios revolucionarios en Puerto Plata y denuncias de que Haití alienta a los insurrectos dominicanos mientras el cañonero estadounidense Nashville permanece apostado en Puerto Plata. La frontera mutua ha sido fuente de fricciones durante años a medida que un Haití densamente poblado presiona sobre la línea fijada por Santo Domingo y cada gobierno acusa al otro de invadir territorio ajeno. Se acusa a Haití de utilizar sus bajos aranceles de importación para permitir la entrada y el contrabando de armas hacia Santo Domingo, donde rigen aranceles elevados, entregando armamento a los rebeldes en condiciones favorables. En respuesta, se ha propuesto que la República Dominicana tome represalias permitiendo a los haitianos exportar café a través de puertos dominicanos bajo bajos gravámenes, lo que afectaría gravemente las rentas del gobierno haitiano, dependientes casi por completo de los impuestos a la exportación de café.

records.summary_en: The Washington Herald addresses rumors that an American yacht in a Brooklyn shipyard was sought by Minister of War General Alfredo Victoria for a planned escape from Santo Domingo with his uncle, President Eladio Victoria. The paper explains that Dominican Minister Peynado had actually sought a vessel suitable for conversion into a gunboat with the advice of two U.S. naval officers designated by the State Department. Although the yacht Rheclair in Brooklyn was considered the most suitable purchase, Minister Peynado suddenly abandoned negotiations under instructions from his government. The vessel had been intended to assist the Dominican gunboat Independencia in suppressing the insurrection in the Puerto Plata district near the Haitian border.
records.summary_es: The Washington Herald aborda los rumores de que un yate estadounidense en un astillero de Brooklyn era buscado por el ministro de Guerra, general Alfredo Victoria, para una planeada huida de Santo Domingo junto con su tío, el presidente Eladio Victoria. El diario explica que, en realidad, el ministro dominicano Peynado había buscado un barco adecuado para su conversión en cañonero con el asesoramiento de dos oficiales navales estadounidenses designados por el Departamento de Estado. Aunque el yate Rheclair en Brooklyn fue considerado la opción más conveniente, el ministro Peynado canceló repentinamente las negociaciones por instrucciones de su gobierno. El navío estaba destinado a prestar auxilio al cañonero dominicano Independencia en la sofocación de la insurrección en el distrito de Puerto Plata, cerca de la frontera haitiana.

records.headline: The expulsion of Washington Lithgow from the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: The expulsion of Washington Lithgow from the Dominican Republic has been averted following the intercession of U.S. Minister Russell, The Washington Herald reports; Lithgow is an American citizen. The Dominican government had ordered Lithgow's expulsion from Puerto Plata on charges of political activity, accusing him of transmitting sensationalized accounts of revolutionary fighting to a New York newspaper that opposed the American receivership. Lithgow appealed to the commander of the U.S. gunboat Nashville, who alerted Washington, leading to instructions for Minister Russell to investigate and successfully obtain the rescission of the expulsion decree.
records.summary_es: La expulsión de Washington Lithgow de la República Dominicana fue evitada tras la intercesión del ministro de Estados Unidos, Russell, según informa The Washington Herald; Lithgow es un ciudadano estadounidense. El gobierno dominicano había ordenado la expulsión de Lithgow desde Puerto Plata bajo cargos de actividad política, acusándolo de transmitir relatos sensacionalistas sobre los combates revolucionarios a un periódico neoyorquino opuesto a la receptoría estadounidense. Lithgow acudió al comandante del cañonero estadounidense Nashville, quien alertó a Washington, lo que motivó que el ministro Russell recibiera instrucciones de investigar y lograra la anulación del decreto de expulsión.

records.headline: State Department dispatches reported in The Washington Herald indicate
records.summary_en: State Department dispatches reported in The Washington Herald indicate that war between Haiti and the Dominican Republic appeared imminent following increased movements of Haitian troops toward the mutual frontier. American diplomatic efforts to mediate an adjustment have failed thus far, with the U.S. gunboat Petrel stationed at Puerto Plata and the gunboat Nashville held at Guantanamo, Cuba, pending developments. The report notes that while treaties grant the United States authority to intervene in the Dominican Republic, no such arrangement exists with Haiti, compelling Washington to observe non-interference out of fairness to both nations.
records.summary_es: Despachos del Departamento de Estado reseñados en The Washington Herald indican que la guerra entre Haití y la República Dominicana parecía inminente tras el incremento de movimientos de tropas haitianas hacia la frontera común. Las gestiones diplomáticas estadounidenses para mediar en un arreglo han fracasado hasta ahora, encontrándose el cañonero estadounidense Petrel apostado en Puerto Plata y el cañonero Nashville retenido en Guantánamo, Cuba, en espera de acontecimientos. El informe señala que, si bien los tratados otorgan a Estados Unidos autoridad para intervenir en la República Dominicana, no existe un convenio semejante con Haití, lo que obliga a Washington a observar la no intervención por equidad hacia ambas naciones.

records.headline: The Manitowoc Pilot reports that the governor of Puerto Plata warned
records.summary_en: The Manitowoc Pilot reports that the governor of Puerto Plata warned Commander Morgan that every patriotic Dominican would offer armed opposition to any landing of American bluejackets or marines. Commander Morgan lodged a sharp protest and appealed to the central government in Santo Domingo to restrain the provincial governor, forwarding reports of the confrontation to the Navy and State Departments. State Department officials declined to disclose what measures would follow if the Dominican government did not resolve the controversy promptly. The item adds that the gunboat Nashville had been sent to Puerto Plata from Guantanamo, Cuba, underscoring that the United States will not tolerate revolutionary activity that disrupts the administration of Dominican customs receipts.
records.summary_es: The Manitowoc Pilot informa que el gobernador de Puerto Plata advirtió al comandante Morgan de que todo dominicano patriota opondría resistencia armada a cualquier desembarco de marineros o infantes de marina estadounidenses. El comandante Morgan presentó una enérgica protesta y apeló al gobierno central en Santo Domingo para que contuviera al gobernador provincial, remitiendo informes de la confrontación a los departamentos de Marina y de Estado. Los funcionarios del Departamento de Estado se negaron a revelar qué medidas se tomarían en caso de que el gobierno dominicano no resolviera la controversia prontamente. La nota añade que el cañonero Nashville había sido enviado a Puerto Plata desde Guantánamo, Cuba, subrayando que Estados Unidos no tolerará actividades revolucionarias que perturben la administración de las rentas aduaneras dominicanas.

records.summary_en: The Washington Times reported that the presence of U.S. gunboats *Petrel* and *Nashville* served to deter war between the Dominican Republic and Haiti, with U.S. officials prepared to land marines to protect foreign interests if conflict erupted. Concurrently, customs receivership reports showed robust fiscal health, with June collections reaching $334,791.27 and eleven-month receipts totaling $3,317,973.17. Both import and export duties posted significant annual increases under American supervision.

Al mismo tiempo, los informes de la receptoría aduanera mostraron una sólida salud fiscal, alcanzando la recaudación de junio 334.791,27 dólares y los ingresos de once meses un total de 3.317.973,17 dólares. Tanto los derechos de importación como de exportación registraron considerables aumentos anuales bajo la supervisión estadounidense.

records.headline: Much fear is felt for Americans and their interests in the interior
records.summary_en: The Richmond Virginian reported that war appeared imminent between Haiti and the Dominican Republic amid revolutions in both countries, following the assassination of Haiti's President Leconte and rebel capture of the border town Dajabon. Santo Domingo prepared to declare war after hundreds of Haitians allegedly assisted Dominican insurgents, massing 4,000 troops along the border. The region also faced severe agricultural drought and famine, while civil strife escalated concurrently in Nicaragua.
records.summary_es: The Richmond Virginian informó que la guerra parecía inminente entre Haití y la República Dominicana en medio de revoluciones en ambos países, tras la muerte del presidente haitiano Leconte y la toma por los rebeldes de la localidad fronteriza de Dajabón. Santo Domingo se preparaba para declarar la guerra luego de que cientos de haitianos presuntamente auxiliaran a los insurgentes dominicanos, concentrando 4.000 soldados a lo largo de la frontera. La región padecía además una severa sequía agrícola y hambruna, mientras la guerra civil se intensificaba a la par en Nicaragua.

records.headline: An editorial in The Washington Herald contrasts conditions in Haiti
records.summary_en: An editorial in The Washington Herald contrasts conditions in Haiti and the Dominican Republic, noting that while Haiti's last three presidents—Nord Alexis, Simon, and Leconte—were elevated through revolutions, Santo Domingo has enjoyed continued peace and progress. The editorial credits an American receiver with teaching an enforced lesson in financial management by overseeing the customs revenues. It maintains that for the first time since the Dominican population arose from the amalgamation of Spanish, Black, and Indigenous peoples, the country is recognizing the benefits of peace and honest government. Concluding that this improvement may become permanent, the paper queries whether the United States might eventually introduce similar financial schooling in Haiti.
records.summary_es: Un editorial en The Washington Herald contrasta la situación de Haití y la República Dominicana, señalando que mientras los tres últimos presidentes de Haití —Nord Alexis, Simon y Leconte— fueron encumbrados mediante revoluciones, Santo Domingo ha disfrutado de continua paz y progreso. El editorial atribuye este logro a un receptor estadounidense que imparte una lección forzada de administración financiera mediante la supervisión de las rentas aduaneras. Sostiene que, por primera vez desde que la población dominicana surgió de la amalgama de españoles, negros e indígenas, el país reconoce los beneficios de la paz y de un gobierno honesto. Al concluir que esta mejoría podría resultar permanente, el diario plantea la interrogante de si Estados Unidos podría llegar a implementar una tutela financiera similar en Haití.

Rebels Take Haytian City.

Washington, D. C.—Hajabon, Santo Domingo, has been captured by rebels, from Haytian territory, according to State department advices from Port Au Prince. The fight which resulted in the capture lasted 14 hours. The wounded numbered 200. The rebels, it is said, crossed from Ouanaminthe, Hayti. The Dominican government asserts the defeat of the rebels, with great losses. Rights of foreigners and nations are being respected.

records.headline: The outbreak is said to be promoted by the prime movers
records.summary_en: The Birmingham Age-Herald reported that an ongoing Dominican insurrection, centered between Puerto Plata and Sanchez, had rekindled following previous fighting at Dajabon. General Horacio Vasquez, former cabinet minister and defeated presidential candidate against President Victoria, was identified as a key leader linked to a New York revolutionary junta. With government claims of victory contradicted by continued rebel strength, the U.S. Navy prepared warships and marines to deploy within three days.
records.summary_es: The Birmingham Age-Herald informó que una continua insurrección dominicana, concentrada entre Puerto Plata y Sánchez, se había reavivado tras los combates previos en Dajabón. El general Horacio Vásquez, exministro y candidato presidencial derrotado por el presidente Victoria, fue señalado como un cabecilla clave vinculado a una junta revolucionaria en Nueva York. Al contradecirse los partes de victoria gubernamentales con la persistente pujanza rebelde, la Armada de los EE. UU. preparó buques de guerra y tropas de desembarco para actuar en un lapso de tres días.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the seizure of Dominican border custom houses by rebels operating near Haiti prompted U.S. officials to consider establishing a formal protectorate. The closures interrupted treaty debt collections and enabled rampant contraband arms smuggling, leading State Department authorities to assert their legal obligation to use military force to retake the posts. Returning American customs officials attributed the renewed unrest to changing Dominican interpretations of American authority.

Las clausuras interrumpieron la recaudación estipulada en los tratados para el servicio de la deuda y facilitaron un desmedido contrabando de armas, lo que condujo a los funcionarios del Departamento de Estado a afirmar su obligación jurídica de emplear la fuerza armada para recuperar los puestos. The one element above all others which may determine the United States to assume a protectorate over Santo Domingo is the reported seizure by the rebels of some of the customhouses on the border between Haiti and Santo Domingo, which were being operated by American officials. The closing of these customhouses not only cuts off the revenue which under the treaty is to be collected to meet the interest charges and other indebtedness of the Dominican government, but opens the door to wholesale smuggling from Haiti, including consignments of arms and ammunition for the rebels, which is making the revolutionary movement difficult to suppress. So explicit are the treaty provisions regarding the customhouses that State Department officials feel it is not only the right but the duty of the American government to use any degree of force necessary to regain possession of the buildings. records.full_text:
Mexico, Santo Domingo, Nicaragua.

It appears that the criticism of Senor Didapp, the representative of the Mexican revolutionists in Washington, and former Mexican Consul General to Spain, Turkey, and later at Norfolk, Va., is pretty well founded when, in his public utterances, he criticises Secretary Knox’s “dollar diplomacy,” which he maintains is making a mess of it in all Pan-American affairs, especially so in Mexico and Nicaragua.

As regards the former, Senor Didapp says that, unable to protect American lives and property by showing a firm attitude toward Madero, the department has been forced to the expedient of assisting the Mexican government by allowing Mexican troops to cross American territory in their attempt to get closer to the revolutionists. This, adds the senor, under the rules of international law, is equivalent to a declaration of war against the revolutionists on the part of the United States.

While The Herald believes that he is wrong in this contention, because the Mexican revolutionists are not yet recognized as belligerents by the Powers, yet it is a queer way of upholding the laws of neutrality. If this is considered fair on the part of the United States, then it would hardly be a greater violation of neutrality to throw a few brigades of United States regulars across the Rio Grande for the purpose of re-enforcing the Madero armies.

It would seem, therefore, that there is some ground for the contention of Senor Didapp that our government already has “intervened” when it allowed Mexican troops to cross American soil on their way to attack the revolutionists.

Secretary Knox, while away on a mission which an Assistant Secretary could well have fulfilled, leaves Pan-American affairs in a badly muddled condition, and the question may be permitted what good his recent trip to Central America has accomplished. His peace efforts have made a dismal failure of preserving the peace in Nicaragua.

The object of our proposed treaty with that country has been to authorize the executive branch of the United States government, with the consent of Congress, to intervene in Nicaragua, as it did in Santo Domingo in the alleged interest of the protection of American lives and property and the maintenance of public order. We know what that has meant to the Dominicans. Neither was property protected nor order maintained. The natives were overawed by the aid of the American forces. All debts of that republic, since the year one of its existence, were combined into bonds, and these exchanged for pieces of paper called Dominican-American “guaranteed national bonds.” These bonds have the interest guaranteed by the United States, but not the principal, by the collection of customs moneys.

If seriously looked into it will be found that Americans hold large blocks of the old debts of Nicaragua. The State Department had such an easy time in the Senate in the Dominican intervention deal that it also may have given assurances to Nicaraguan professional patriots with bundles of old scrip. But the Senate balked, because, were the United States to side with one faction against another, it would make it quite uncomfortable for American industrial expansionists.

It looks to The Herald that, when the smoke has cleared away, the United States will be found collecting Nicaraguan customs duties in the interest of American pioneers. This is known as “Dawsonizing the Monroe Doctrine,” for it avoids annexing the republics, while it obliterates them from the map as international factors of discord. Despite the fact that the Senate has refused to sanction the grabbing of a neighboring republic's custom-house, it would seem that those interested in the possibilities of spoil possess sufficient power to have the State Department spread United States marines over Nicaragua interior towns. This is apparently evidenced by the fact, quite palpable, that a battalion of American marines had been dispatched to Granada, which is not on the line of communication between Washington and Minister Weitzel, in order to rescue some girls alleged to be held in a French college.

What we should like to know is what these girls, this purely domestic affair, have to do with the Nicaraguan question?

The report reviewed the convention's financial terms, which scaled public debt to $17,000,000 and issued $20,000,000 in bonds through New York trusts. Increased customs revenues under American administration had enabled annual principal payments to reach $400,000, well above required minimums.

records.summary_en: The Birmingham Age-Herald reported that Insular Bureau Chief Frank McIntyre and William Doyle sailed on the transport *Prairie* with marines to inspect the Dominican frontier and reopen four customs stations closed by insurgents. Authorities declared that military force would be utilized if necessary to uphold customs obligations under the 1907 Dawson treaty, with troops prepared to march inland from coastal landings. U.S. officials expressed hope that the show of force would compel rebels to abandon the posts without bloodshed.
records.summary_es: The Birmingham Age-Herald informó que el jefe de la Oficina de Asuntos Insulares, Frank McIntyre, y William Doyle zarparon en el transporte *Prairie* con infantes de marina para inspeccionar la frontera dominicana y reabrir cuatro puestos aduaneros clausurados por los insurgentes. Las autoridades declararon que se recurriría a la fuerza armada si resultaba indispensable para hacer cumplir los compromisos aduaneros del tratado Dawson de 1907, con efectivos listos para avanzar tierra adentro tras los desembarcos costeros. Los funcionarios estadounidenses manifestaron su confianza en que la demostración de fuerza obligaría a los rebeldes a desalojar los puestos sin derramamiento de sangre.
records.passage: [illegible]action. To Probe Conditions. With the American marines will go Brigadier General Frank McIntyre, chief of the army Insular bureau, and Mr. Doyle as special commissioners to investigate conditions in Santo Domingo, particularly on the border between that country and Haiti, where the revolutionists have been most active. The Prairie will arrive at the island about October 3. Under the Dawson treaty of 1907 between the United States and the Dominican republic the United States is responsible for the collection and distribution of Santo Domingo's customs dues. Heretofore this has been accomplished peacefully, but rebels operating from Haiti have now closed all four of the border customs posts. Whatever force that may be necessary will be used by the marines to reopen the posts and continue their orderly operation. Officials here believe, however, that when made aware of the determination of the United States government the rebels will offer no resistance and that it may even be found unnecessary to disembark the marines. To Be Landed if Necessary. But if there should be any sign of resistance the force will be landed on the north and south coasts and marched directly inland over the wagon roads and trails, for there are no railroads in that section to the custom houses. records.headline: A regiment of approximately 800 marines under Colonel Franklin J. Moses
records.summary_en: A regiment of approximately 800 marines under Colonel Franklin J. Moses and Lieutenant Andrew B. Drum is being sent to Santo Domingo, The Evening Capital and Maryland Gazette reports, aboard the cruiser transport Prairie from the League Island navy yard. Detachments for the force have been assembled from naval stations at Philadelphia, Charleston, Norfolk, and other installations. The regiment's primary mission is to enforce the reopening of customhouses along the Haitian border that were recently closed by insurgent forces in the Dominican Republic.

Los destacamentos que integran el contingente fueron reunidos a partir de puestos navales en Filadelfia, Charleston, Norfolk y otras instalaciones. La misión principal del regimiento consiste en obligar a la reapertura de las aduanas a lo largo de la frontera haitiana que fueron clausuradas recientemente por fuerzas insurgentes en la República Dominicana.

records.headline: The Norwich Bulletin reports that the transport Prairie departed
records.summary_en: The Norwich Bulletin reports that the transport Prairie departed the Philadelphia navy yard with 800 marines bound for Santo Domingo to protect American interests, with detachments drawn from Atlantic coast yards. In a separate Washington dispatch, the paper announces that Senor Don Francisco J. Peynado has resigned as Dominican minister, clarifying that his resignation was forwarded to Santo Domingo a month ago and was not caused by the revolution or United States intervention. Although requested by the Dominican president to remain indefinitely, Minister Peynado agreed only to stay long enough to prepare the republic's boundary dispute with Haiti before the Hague tribunal before returning to his private law practice.

En un despacho independiente desde Washington, el periódico anuncia que el señor don Francisco J. Peynado ha renunciado como ministro dominicano, aclarando que su dimisión fue enviada a Santo Domingo un mes atrás y no obedeció a la revolución ni a la intervención de los Estados Unidos. Aunque el presidente dominicano le solicitó permanecer de manera indefinida, el ministro Peynado aceptó quedarse únicamente el tiempo necesario para preparar la disputa de límites de la república frente a Haití ante el tribunal de La Haya antes de reanudar el ejercicio privado del derecho.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Dominican border custom houses had been reopened, potentially eliminating the need for American marines to land and establish patrols. The Haitian government sought assurances from Washington that its territorial rights would be protected under the provisional boundary established by the United States. Haitian officials also inquired whether American intervention would conclude once customs operations were fully restored.

El gobierno haitiano recabó seguridades de Washington en cuanto a que sus derechos territoriales quedarían resguardados bajo la línea limítrofe provisional trazada por los Estados Unidos. Los funcionarios haitianos indagaron además si la intervención estadounidense concluiría una vez restablecidas íntegramente las operaciones aduaneras.

Haitian anxiety as to the intention of the United States in taking a hand in the Dominican revolution is shown in an interrogation received by Haitian Minister Menos from his government. The Haitian government desires to be assured that its rights in the boundary dispute with the Dominican Republic will be safeguarded in accordance with the provisional boundary between the two countries established by the United States and set forth in the note issued last week. It was said at the Haitian legation that the Haitians also are anxious to know whether the active interest of the United States will cease with the reopening of the Dominican customs houses. TRAINMEN MAY STRIKE. Unable to Settle Differences With Officials of Georgia Railway. AUGUSTA, Ga., October 1.—Three hundred trainmen of the Georgia railroad are expected to strike today. Their representatives conferred with officials of the railroad until early this morning in an effort to reach a settlement of the controversy, but no agreement resulted. The immediate cause of the men's decision to strike was the refusal of the railroad to reinstate Conductor J. T. Paschal, who was discharged for alleged violation of the hours of service law.

records.headline: Apprehension in Haiti regarding American actions matches that of the Dominicans
records.summary_en: Apprehension in Haiti regarding American actions matches that of the Dominicans, The Washington Herald reports, with dispatches from Port-au-Prince to both the Haitian Legation and the State Department reflecting widespread concern. Although the United States delivered an official note assuring Haiti that its rights in the boundary dispute with the Dominican Republic would remain unimpaired by a provisional border line established to locate and safeguard Dominican customhouses, Haitian officials continue to fear that their territorial position against Santo Domingo will be damaged.

Si bien los Estados Unidos remitieron una nota oficial asegurando a Haití que sus derechos en la disputa limítrofe con la República Dominicana no se verían menoscabados por la delimitación provisional trazada para situar y resguardar las aduanas dominicanas, las autoridades haitianas continúan temiendo que su posición territorial frente a Santo Domingo resulte perjudicada.

records.headline: A delayed Washington dispatch published in The Birmingham Age -Herald
records.summary_en: A delayed Washington dispatch published in The Birmingham Age-Herald announces that the transport Prairie has arrived safely at Santo Domingo City carrying 750 marines commanded by Colonel Moses to reopen border customhouses closed by rebels. Although the city was reported quiet, the dispatch did not state whether landing the marines would be necessary, adding that severed telegraph wires to Puerto Plata left cable communications dependent on a slow link through Bogota, Colombia. Traveling with the expedition are General Frank McIntyre, chief of the War Department's insular bureau, and Chief W. T. S. Doyle of the State Department's Latin American division, who were dispatched as special commissioners to investigate conditions in the republic.
records.summary_es: Un despacho demorado de Washington publicado en The Birmingham Age-Herald anuncia que el transporte Prairie llegó sin novedad a la ciudad de Santo Domingo llevando a 750 infantes de marina al mando del coronel Moses para reabrir las aduanas fronterizas clausuradas por rebeldes. Aunque se informó que la ciudad estaba en calma, el despacho no especificó si sería necesario el desembarco de los infantes, añadiendo que el corte de líneas telegráficas hacia Puerto Plata dejaba las comunicaciones por cable sujetas a un enlace lento a través de Bogotá, Colombia. Junto a la expedición viajan el general Frank McIntyre, jefe de la oficina insular del Departamento de Guerra, y el jefe W. T. S. Doyle, de la división latinoamericana del Departamento de Estado, quienes fueron enviados como comisionados especiales para investigar las condiciones en la república.

records.headline: The commander of the gunboat Wheeling advised from Santo Domingo City
records.summary_en: The commander of the gunboat Wheeling advised from Santo Domingo City under date of October 1 that all was quiet there, the Evening Star reports under the headline "His News Meager," though communication with the northern portion of the island had been interrupted since his arrival. No further communications had been received from the American marines and commissioners who traveled aboard the Prairie following their initial report of safe arrival. It remained unknown whether conditions in the Dominican Republic had necessitated landing the marines.
records.summary_es: El comandante del cañonero Wheeling comunicó desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo, con fecha 1 de octubre, que todo permanecía en calma allí, según informa el Evening Star bajo el titular "Sus noticias son escasas", aunque la comunicación con la parte norte de la isla se encontraba interrumpida desde su llegada. No se habían recibido nuevas comunicaciones de los infantes de marina ni de los comisionados estadounidenses que viajaron a bordo del Prairie tras su informe inicial de llegada sin novedad. Se desconocía si las condiciones en la República Dominicana habían hecho necesario el desembarco de los infantes de marina.

records.headline: Under the headline "Wants to Be President of Dominica, but State Department Won't Let Him,"
records.summary_en: Under the headline "Wants to Be President of Dominica, but State Department Won't Let Him," The Washington Herald reports that Frederico Velasquez, a political exile from the Dominican Republic who sailed from New York for Jamaica on Sunday, appealed to the State Department for backing to make himself president of the island republic. Velasquez offered himself as a substitute for the unpopular Victoria government, asserting that he could become president at any time if supported by the United States. Department officials refused to consider his proposals and requested that he not repeat the suggestion. Velasquez previously served as Minister of Finance under President Ramon Caceres until Caceres was assassinated the previous winter, having since remained in Jamaica awaiting an opportune moment to return.
records.summary_es: Bajo el titular «Wants to Be President of Dominica, but State Department Won't Let Him» (Quiere ser presidente de Dominica, pero el Departamento de Estado no se lo permite), The Washington Herald informa que Frederico Velasquez, exiliado político de la República Dominicana que zarpó de Nueva York hacia Jamaica el domingo, apeló al Departamento de Estado en busca de respaldo para proclamarse presidente de la república insular. Velasquez se ofreció como sustituto del impopular gobierno de Victoria, asegurando que podría asumir la presidencia en cualquier momento si contaba con el apoyo de Estados Unidos. Los funcionarios del departamento se negaron a considerar sus propuestas y le solicitaron no repetir la sugerencia. Velasquez se desempeñó anteriormente como ministro de Hacienda bajo el presidente Ramón Cáceres hasta que este fue asesinado el invierno anterior, permaneciendo desde entonces en Jamaica a la espera de un momento propicio para regresar.

records.headline: A Washington dispatch to The Sun reports that Frederico Velasquez
records.summary_en: A Washington dispatch to The Sun reports that Frederico Velasquez, a political exile from the Dominican Republic who departed New York for Jamaica yesterday, appealed to the State Department for backing in his project to make himself president of the island republic. Velasquez presented himself to officials as a replacement for the unpopular Victoria government, asserting he could assume the presidency at any time with the backing of the United States. Department officials refused to consider his overtures and requested that he not repeat the proposal. Velasquez formerly served as Minister of Finance under President Ramon Caceres, whose administration's unpopularity was attributed to the finance minister's influence, and fled to Jamaica following Caceres's assassination last winter to await an opportunity to return.

Los funcionarios del departamento se negaron a considerar sus propuestas y le solicitaron no reiterar su planteamiento. Velasquez ocupó anteriormente el cargo de ministro de Hacienda bajo el presidente Ramón Cáceres, a cuya influencia se atribuía la impopularidad del gobierno, y tras el asesinato de Cáceres el invierno pasado huyó a Jamaica a la espera de una oportunidad para regresar.

records.headline: Under the headline "He Got $50,000, but No O.K. to His Scheme,"
records.summary_en: Under the headline "He Got $50,000, but No O.K. to His Scheme," the Atlanta Georgian reports that Frederico Velasquez, former treasurer of the Dominican Republic, is en route back to Santo Domingo after a month spent in secret efforts to convince the State Department of his availability as president. Velasquez sailed from New York after the State Department promptly and vigorously rejected his proposition to use the department to further his political ambitions. The report adds that during his stay in New York, Velasquez induced certain persons to subscribe to a $50,000 "slush fund."

El informe añade que durante su permanencia en Nueva York, Velasquez convenció a varias personas para que aportaran a un fondo para sobornos de 50.000 dólares.

records.headline: The Daily Banner reports that the Taft administration has devised
records.summary_en: The Daily Banner reports that the Taft administration has devised a plan for virtually annexing Santo Domingo, formulated by Secretary of State Knox, Assistant Secretary Wilson, General McIntyre, Mr. Doyle, and Dominican minister Francisco J. Peynado. The dispatch explains that the ongoing revolution was instigated by political factions in Santo Domingo seeking more money after growing dissatisfied with the revenues allocated to the Dominican government by the American supervisor of customs. While the uprising initially disrupted the State Department's designs, the disturbance provided the justification to land marines and open a general investigation, advancing a broader plan to absorb Santo Domingo as a colonial possession pending congressional approval.
records.summary_es: The Daily Banner informa que el gobierno de Taft ha elaborado un plan para prácticamente anexionar Santo Domingo, formulado por el secretario de Estado Knox, el subsecretario Wilson, el general McIntyre, el señor Doyle y el ministro dominicano Francisco J. Peynado. El despacho explica que la revolución en curso fue promovida por facciones políticas en Santo Domingo que buscaban mayores fondos tras descontentarse con las rentas asignadas al gobierno dominicano por el supervisor de aduanas estadounidense. Si bien la sublevación perturbó en un principio los planes del Departamento de Estado, el conflicto brindó la justificación necesaria para desembarcar infantes de marina y abrir una investigación general, promoviendo un proyecto más amplio para absorber a Santo Domingo como posesión colonial, sujeto a la aprobación del Congreso.

records.headline: The investigations of Harriet Chalmers Adams are highlighted
records.summary_en: The investigations of Harriet Chalmers Adams are highlighted in The San Francisco Call, following her return from the Dominican Republic to study the disputed burial place of Christopher Columbus; Adams is a Latin American explorer and wife of Pan-American Union official Franklin Adams. After visiting Spain to inspect the tomb at Seville, Mrs. Adams concluded that the evidence demonstrates Columbus's bones truly rest in Santo Domingo City. The article explains that while remains removed in 1795 eventually reached Seville, the authentic remains were discovered in 1877 by Padre Billini, who summoned all the foreign consuls in port to witness and verify the find inside the cathedral.

records.headline: American special commissioners General McIntyre and Mr. Doyle
records.summary_en: American special commissioners General McIntyre and Mr. Doyle have conferred daily with the Dominican government since arriving in Santo Domingo City on October 2, a Washington dispatch to The Sun reports, though the State Department has withheld details of the negotiations. Commander Scales reported that no marines had yet landed at the capital, requesting provisions for his command and the gunboat Wheeling due to high food prices in the city. Officials emphasize that the commissioners must untangle a crisis caused by a boundary dispute with Haiti combined with a border revolution that forced the closure of Dominican frontier custom houses, with an announcement expected shortly.
records.summary_es: Los comisionados especiales estadounidenses, el general McIntyre y el señor Doyle, se han reunido a diario con el gobierno dominicano desde su llegada a la ciudad de Santo Domingo el 2 de octubre, informa un despacho de Washington para The Sun, aunque el Departamento de Estado no ha divulgado pormenores de las negociaciones. El comandante Scales informó que aún no habían desembarcado infantes de marina en la capital, solicitando víveres para su dotación y el cañonero Wheeling debido a los altos precios de la comida en la ciudad. Las autoridades subrayan que los comisionados deben resolver una crisis ocasionada por una disputa fronteriza con Haití unida a una revolución limítrofe que provocó el cierre de las aduanas dominicanas, previéndose un anuncio formal en breve.

Commander Scales reported that no marines had yet landed at Santo Domingo City and asked for supplies for his men and the gunboat Wheeling owing to elevated food costs in the capital. records.headline: In an imminent assault, Dominican rebels advancing upon Puerto Plata
records.summary_en: In an imminent assault, Dominican rebels advancing upon Puerto Plata are expected to overpower government forces, The Daily Banner reports. To protect American interests, the gunboat Wheeling and the Prairie, carrying 750 marines from Santo Domingo City, are expected to steam to Puerto Plata, where anti-American sentiment is running high. The dispatch states that negotiations carried on by American commissioners W. T. S. Doyle and Brigadier General McIntyre have provoked resentment among local Dominican officials, as the commissioners insist that the Dominican government dismiss officials guilty of dishonesty and the maladministration of public revenues.
records.summary_es: The Daily Banner informa que rebeldes dominicanos avanzan sobre Puerto Plata, donde se espera un ataque inminente que derrote a las fuerzas gubernamentales. Para resguardar los intereses estadounidenses, se prevé que el cañonero Wheeling y el Prairie, que transporta a 750 infantes de marina desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo, naveguen hacia Puerto Plata, donde el sentimiento antinorteamericano es intenso. El despacho señala que las negociaciones encabezadas por los comisionados estadounidenses W. T. S. Doyle y el general de brigada McIntyre han generado resentimiento entre los funcionarios dominicanos locales, dado que los comisionados exigen que el gobierno dominicano destituya a los funcionarios culpables de deshonestidad y malversación de fondos públicos.

records.summary_en: The Sun reported that American commissioners investigating Santo Domingo found widespread corruption and treaty violations under the unpopular Victoria administration. The commissioners reported that public funds had been misappropriated, illicit debts incurred, and government employees left unpaid while border custom houses were forced shut. The United States demanded an immediate administrative cleanup and the reopening of frontier customs posts, holding marines in readiness to provide protection.
records.summary_es: The Sun informó que los comisionados estadounidenses que investigaban en Santo Domingo constataron una corrupción generalizada y violaciones de los tratados bajo la impopular administración de Victoria. Los comisionados denunciaron que se habían malversado caudales públicos, contraído deudas ilícitas y dejado sin salario a los empleados públicos, al tiempo que se clausuraban a la fuerza las aduanas de la frontera. records.summary_en: A Washington dispatch in The San Francisco Call reports that revolutionists have captured nearly the entire province of Samana, including Sanchez and Sabana de la Mar, and that the town of Samana was bombarded by a government gunboat. The transport Prairie with 750 marines is believed to have sailed from Santo Domingo for Samana, where Colonel Franklin F. Moses is prepared to land troops under the authority of the 1907 convention protecting Dominican customs collections. The report further notes that customs houses along the Haitian frontier at Dajabon, Banica, Lieranueva, and Pedronalles have fallen into rebel hands.

Se cree que el transporte Prairie con 750 infantes de marina zarpó de Santo Domingo hacia Samaná, donde el coronel Franklin F. Moses está preparado para desembarcar tropas al amparo de la convención de 1907 que protege la recaudación aduanera dominicana. El informe agrega que las aduanas a lo largo de la frontera haitiana en Dajabón, Bánica, Lieranueva y Pedronalles han caído en manos de los rebeldes.

records.summary_en: The Washington Herald reports that State Department dispatches confirm rebels have bombarded the town of Samana and captured Sanchez and Sabana de la Mar, prompting the dispatch of the naval transport Prairie with 750 marines to investigate Samana Bay. Street fighting with numerous casualties has also broken out in Puerto Plata, where a general rebel assault is believed to have occurred, though severed communications have left details uncertain. records.headline: A Washington dispatch to The Sun reports that Dominican rebels
records.summary_en: A Washington dispatch to The Sun reports that Dominican rebels have gained control of virtually all of Samana province on the northern coast, capturing Sanchez and Sabana de la Mar and reportedly bombarding the town of Samana. The naval transport Prairie, with 750 marines aboard, has sailed to Samana Bay to investigate and will land troops if necessary to safeguard American interests. The State Department also learned that heavy fighting with many casualties has taken place in the streets of Puerto Plata, where a general assault by rebel forces is believed to have occurred.

El transporte naval Prairie, con 750 infantes de marina a bordo, ha navegado hacia la bahía de Samaná para investigar y desembarcará tropas si es preciso para salvaguardar los intereses estadounidenses. El Departamento de Estado tuvo noticia asimismo de intensos combates callejeros con abundantes bajas en Puerto Plata, donde se presume que las fuerzas rebeldes lanzaron un asalto general.

records.headline: The Washington Herald reports that Receiver General W. C. Pulliam
records.summary_en: The Washington Herald reports that Receiver General W. C. Pulliam, head of the Dominican customs service, arrived in Washington yesterday for extended conferences with Acting Secretary of State Wilson. His advice was sought regarding measures to restrain Dominicans from reckless and wrongful expenditure of their revenues, as Dominicans are unwilling to accept direct United States supervision of their spending. Meanwhile, the transport Prairie, carrying 750 marines, arrived at Puerto Plata, where a rebel attack was feared at any moment, having stopped on its way to investigate Samana following reports of rebel bombardment.
records.summary_es: The Washington Herald informa que el receptor general W. C. Pulliam, titular del servicio de aduanas dominicano, llegó ayer a Washington para mantener extensas conferencias con el secretario de Estado interino Wilson. Se solicitó su asesoramiento en relación con medidas para impedir que los dominicanos gasten sus rentas de forma imprudente e indebida, en vista de que no aceptarán una supervisión directa de sus desembolsos por parte de Estados Unidos. Entre tanto, el transporte Prairie, con 750 infantes de marina a bordo, arribó a Puerto Plata, donde se temía un asalto rebelde en cualquier momento, habiendo hecho escala previa en Samaná para investigar denuncias de bombardeos insurgentes.

records.headline: A Washington dispatch in the Omaha Daily Bee reports that conditions
records.summary_en: A Washington dispatch in the Omaha Daily Bee reports that conditions in the Dominican Republic are so precarious that officials would not be surprised if the entire administration abdicated, leaving American commissioners to establish a provisional government pending a popular election. The retirement of General Alfred Victoria, nephew of President Victoria, from the post of secretary of war was announced as a concession to the rebels, though such moves are often interpreted by Dominicans as signs of weakness. Meanwhile, the transport Prairie, carrying 750 American marines from Santo Domingo City to investigate revolutionary disturbances on the northern coast, reached Puerto Plata today.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Washington en el Omaha Daily Bee informa que las condiciones en la República Dominicana son tan precarias que los funcionarios no se sorprenderían si toda la administración abdicara, dejando a los comisionados estadounidenses la tarea de establecer un gobierno provisional a la espera de elecciones populares. La renuncia del general Alfred Victoria, sobrino del presidente Victoria, a la cartera de Guerra fue anunciada como una concesión a los rebeldes, aunque tales medidas suelen ser interpretadas por los dominicanos como señales de debilidad. En tanto, el transporte Prairie, que transportaba a 750 infantes de marina estadounidenses desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo para investigar disturbios revolucionarios en la costa norte, llegó hoy a Puerto Plata.

records.summary_en: Under the headline "Straighten Tangles of Dominican Republic," The Washington Times reports that Brigadier General McIntyre and W. S. Doyle of the State Department are in Santo Domingo City working to straighten out the financial difficulties of the Dominican republic. The transport Prairie is also stationed at the capital with 750 marines aboard. The article states that the Dominican government has contracted a number of debts considered illegal under its treaty with the United States, and it is probable that some will go unpaid. Doyle and McIntyre plan to remain in Santo Domingo until they have cleared up the situation.

El transporte Prairie se halla asimismo en la capital con 750 infantes de marina a bordo. El artículo señala que el gobierno dominicano ha contraído una serie de deudas consideradas ilegales conforme al tratado con Estados Unidos, siendo probable que algunas de ellas queden sin pagar. Doyle y McIntyre proyectan permanecer en Santo Domingo hasta esclarecer por completo la situación.

records.headline: The Washington Herald reports that American special commissioner
records.summary_en: The Washington Herald reports that American special commissioner W. T. S. Doyle informed the State Department of his return to Santo Domingo City alongside General McIntyre aboard the naval transport Prairie following a cruise along the north coast. Doyle reported that no marines had been landed at any point, noting that the Prairie observed Samana Bay and stopped for only five hours at Puerto Plata, where conditions appeared quiet despite previous insurgent threats. The commissioners expect to resolve the Dominican situation in a short time, having already announced parts of their program, including President Victoria's pledge to retire in July 1914.
records.summary_es: The Washington Herald informa que el comisionado especial estadounidense W. T. S. Doyle notificó al Departamento de Estado su regreso a la ciudad de Santo Domingo junto al general McIntyre a bordo del transporte naval Prairie tras una travesía por la costa norte. Doyle comunicó que no se desembarcó a ningún infante de marina en ninguno de los puntos visitados, señalando que el Prairie observó la bahía de Samaná y permaneció solo cinco horas en Puerto Plata, donde la situación parecía tranquila a pesar de las amenazas insurgentes previas. Los comisionados esperan solventar la crisis dominicana en poco tiempo, habiendo anunciado ya partes de su programa, entre ellas la promesa del presidente Victoria de retirarse en julio de 1914.

records.headline: The Dominican Republic is the subject of two brief Washington dispatches
records.summary_en: The Dominican Republic is the subject of two brief Washington dispatches on revolutionary developments printed in The Alaska Citizen. Under the heading "Another War," an October 24 dispatch reports that Dominican rebels are advancing upon Puerto Plata, prompting the American naval vessels Prairie and Wheeling to be dispatched to the scene of impending trouble. Under the heading "Tired of Job," an October 25 dispatch states that the president of the Dominican Republic reported his country to be in the throes of a revolution and announced his intention to retire from the presidency in July 1914.
records.summary_es: La República Dominicana es el tema de dos breves despachos de Washington sobre los acontecimientos revolucionarios publicados en The Alaska Citizen. Bajo el encabezado «Another War» (Otra guerra), un despacho del 24 de octubre informa que rebeldes dominicanos avanzan sobre Puerto Plata, lo que motivó el envío de los buques de guerra estadounidenses Prairie y Wheeling al escenario del conflicto inminente. Bajo el título «Tired of Job» (Cansado del cargo), un despacho del 25 de octubre indica que el presidente de la República Dominicana declaró que su país se encuentra en medio de una revolución y anunció su intención de retirarse de la presidencia en julio de 1914.

records.headline: The Washington Herald reports on naval orders issued by President Taft
records.summary_en: The Washington Herald reports on naval orders issued by President Taft to protect the Dominican Republic from further uprisings and safeguard American citizens and property. The Baltimore will sail from Philadelphia today while the Yankton was expected to depart New York last night to serve as a dispatch and supply ship between the Baltimore, assigned to patrol Puerto Plata, and the Prairie, stationed at Santo Domingo City. Although authorities originally intended to send a detachment of marines south on the Baltimore (the number appearing in print as "ISO marines"), naval plans were modified to transfer a portion of the marines already aboard the Prairie, with orders that no troops land unless conditions absolutely demand it.
records.summary_es: The Washington Herald informa sobre las órdenes navales emitidas por el presidente Taft para proteger a la República Dominicana de nuevas sublevaciones y salvaguardar a los ciudadanos y propiedades estadounidenses. El Baltimore zarpará hoy de Filadelfia, mientras que se esperaba que el Yankton partiera de Nueva York anoche para actuar como buque de abastecimiento y comunicaciones entre el Baltimore, asignado a patrullar Puerto Plata, y el Prairie, apostado en la ciudad de Santo Domingo. Aunque las autoridades planeaban enviar inicialmente un destacamento de infantes de marina hacia el sur en el Baltimore, los planes navales se modificaron para transferir a una parte de las tropas que ya viajaban en el Prairie, con la instrucción de que no desembarquen salvo que las circunstancias lo exijan estrictamente.

records.summary_en: Under the headline "Abdicate and Leave United States in Charge of Island," the Springfield Weekly Republican reports that conditions in the Dominican Republic are so unstable that Washington officials would not be surprised if the entire administration abdicated, leaving American commissioners to establish a provisional government pending a popular election. The retirement of General Alfred Victoria, nephew of President Victoria, from the ministry of war was announced Friday as a concession to the rebels, though Dominicans frequently interpret such changes as signs of weakness that precede wholesale withdrawals. In addition, the transport Prairie, carrying 750 American marines from Santo Domingo City to investigate northern coastal unrest, arrived at Puerto Plata on Friday.
records.summary_es: Bajo el titular «Abdicate and Leave United States in Charge of Island» (Abdicar y dejar a Estados Unidos a cargo de la isla), el Springfield Weekly Republican informa que las condiciones en la República Dominicana son tan inestables que las autoridades de Washington no se sorprenderían si toda la administración abdicara, dejando a los comisionados estadounidenses a cargo de establecer un gobierno provisional en espera de elecciones populares. El retiro del general Alfred Victoria, sobrino del presidente Victoria, de la secretaría de Guerra fue anunciado el viernes como una concesión a los rebeldes, si bien los dominicanos suelen interpretar tales cambios como muestras de debilidad que preceden a renuncias generalizadas. Además, el transporte Prairie, que transportaba a 750 infantes de marina estadounidenses desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo para investigar disturbios en la costa norte, llegó a Puerto Plata el viernes.

records.headline: Two United States naval vessels have been ordered to Dominican waters
records.summary_en: Two United States naval vessels have been ordered to Dominican waters owing to the wide territory in which Dominican revolutionists operate, a Washington dispatch dated October 31 reports. The protected cruiser Baltimore is scheduled to leave the Philadelphia navy yard at noon Friday, while the Yankton is expected to sail from New York today. State Department advices indicate that an assault on Puerto Plata, the chief northern coast city of the Dominican Republic, appears imminent, with government forces erecting street barricades in preparation.

records.headline: A Washington dispatch dated November 1 states that rebels in Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: A Washington dispatch dated November 1 states that rebels in Santo Domingo are causing severe unrest, making United States naval intervention—comparable to the occupation of Nicaragua by marines and bluejackets—appear certain within ten days. The United States government is also expected to assume full control over Dominican finances until the government proves capable of responsibility, following State Department reports of misappropriated funds and grave financial disorder under the Victoria administration. In addition, dispatches from Puerto Plata report that insurgents have besieged Monte Cristi since Sunday under near-continuous bombardment, endangering American lives and property.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Washington fechado el 1 de noviembre afirma que los rebeldes en Santo Domingo están provocando graves disturbios, por lo que una intervención naval estadounidense —comparable a la ocupación de Nicaragua por infantes de marina y marineros— parece segura en un plazo de diez días. Se prevé además que el gobierno de Estados Unidos asuma el control total de las finanzas dominicanas hasta que su gobierno demuestre capacidad de gestión, tras informes del Departamento de Estado que denuncian malversación de fondos y grave desorden financiero bajo la administración de Victoria. Asimismo, reportes de Puerto Plata indican que los insurgentes han sitiado Monte Cristi desde el domingo bajo un bombardeo casi incesante, amenazando vidas y propiedades estadounidenses.

records.summary_en: Advices forwarded to the State Department from Puerto Plata report that bombardment has been continuing since Sunday, prompting expectations that a United States warship has been sent there. The cruiser Baltimore sailed from Philadelphia at noon today for Santo Domingo City and the Yankton left New York yesterday for Puerto Plata, bringing the total United States naval presence in Dominican waters to four ships alongside the Prairie at Caldera Bay and the Wheeling at Santo Domingo City. records.headline: The Washington Times reports that a crisis has arrived in Dominican
records.summary_en: The Washington Times reports that a crisis has arrived in Dominican affairs, with expectations that rebels will decide to lay down their arms before the week ends to grant the country a period of peace. American commissioners and the Archbishop of Santo Domingo are proceeding aboard the gunboat Wheeling to confer with insurgent representatives at Samana Bay this week. Although Samana Bay and the adjoining district have been in rebel possession for some time, the insurgents are reported to have made little progress.

Los comisionados estadounidenses y el arzobispo de Santo Domingo se trasladan a bordo del cañonero Wheeling para reunirse esta semana con representantes insurgentes en la bahía de Samaná. A pesar de que la bahía de Samaná y el distrito adyacente han estado bajo dominio rebelde durante algún tiempo, se informa que los insurgentes han logrado escasos avances.

records.headline: Increasing disorder in Santo Domingo and desperate street fighting
records.summary_en: Increasing disorder in Santo Domingo and desperate street fighting in the outskirts of Puerto Plata, threatening American lives and property, led the Navy Department to order the immediate dispatch of the cruiser Baltimore and the tender Yankton to Dominican waters, a Washington dispatch dated October 31 reports. The Yankton is to sail from New York today and the Baltimore from Philadelphia on Friday, expected to arrive by midweek to reinforce the Prairie and its 700 marines. The Baltimore will carry an additional force of 150 marines.

El Yankton zarpará hoy desde Nueva York y el Baltimore el viernes desde Filadelfia, previéndose su llegada para mediados de la próxima semana a fin de reforzar al Prairie y sus 700 infantes de marina. El Baltimore transportará una fuerza adicional de 150 infantes de marina.

records.summary_en: A dispatch in The Washington Herald reports that the Dominican minister, referred to in print as Minister Ponado, will sail tomorrow from New York for Santo Domingo City to remain in close touch with developments after an arranged governmental change by Congress. Due to revolutionary operations that severed northern cable lines from Santo Domingo City, messages must travel south via Venezuela and Colombia to reach the United States, averaging seventy hours in transit to Washington. While Congress was scheduled to meet next Tuesday to accept the resignation of President Victoria and his administration, no report of the proceedings had reached the State Department.

A causa de las operaciones revolucionarias que inutilizaron el cable norte desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo, las comunicaciones deben enviarse hacia el sur pasando por Venezuela y Colombia para alcanzar los Estados Unidos, tomando un promedio de setenta horas de transmisión hacia Washington. Aunque el Congreso debía reunirse el próximo martes para aceptar la renuncia del presidente Victoria y su gabinete, ningún reporte oficial sobre la sesión había llegado aún al Departamento de Estado.

records.summary_en: According to a report in The Sun, the Dominican minister will sail from New York on Saturday for Santo Domingo city to get more closely in touch with the situation following a change of government believed to have been arranged by Congress within the last two days. Because the northern cable is unavailable due to rebel operations, dispatches must be routed south through Venezuela and Colombia before reaching the United States, resulting in an average transmission time of seventy hours from Washington to Santo Domingo city. Although the Dominican Congress was scheduled to meet on Tuesday to accept the resignation of President Victoria and his administration, the State Department has not yet received any official report of the session's action from the American commissioners.
records.summary_es: Según un informe en The Sun, el ministro dominicano zarpará desde Nueva York el sábado hacia la ciudad de Santo Domingo para mantenerse más en contacto con la situación tras un cambio de gobierno que se cree fue dispuesto por el Congreso en los últimos dos días. Debido a que el cable del norte no se encuentra disponible por las operaciones de los rebeldes, los despachos deben enviarse hacia el sur a través de Venezuela y Colombia antes de llegar a los Estados Unidos, lo que genera un tiempo promedio de transmisión de setenta horas desde Washington hasta la ciudad de Santo Domingo. Aunque estaba previsto que el Congreso dominicano se reuniera el martes para aceptar la renuncia del presidente Victoria y su administración, el Departamento de Estado aún no ha recibido ningún informe oficial sobre las medidas adoptadas en la sesión por parte de los comisionados estadounidenses.

records.headline: The New Haven Union reports that voting on the election of Archbishop Nouel proceeded
records.summary_en: The New Haven Union reports that voting on the election of Archbishop Nouel proceeded favorably in both houses, though Dominican law requires the House to vote three times with no more than one ballot per day, requiring three days to finalize the result. The election carries out a compromise program proposed by United States commissioners and accepted by the now-resigned Victoria administration and the revolutionists, with a permanent presidential election planned once normal conditions return. In a Rome dispatch dated Dec. 3, it is reported that the Pope cabled congratulations and his apostolic blessing to Archbishop Nouel on his election as provisional president of the Dominican Republic, expressing hope that it will strengthen ties with the Holy See and noting that the prelate will likely be created a cardinal upon completing his term.
records.summary_es: The New Haven Union informa que la votación para la elección del arzobispo Nouel avanzó favorablemente en ambas cámaras, aunque la ley dominicana exige que la Cámara vote tres veces a razón de no más de un sufragio por día, por lo que se requerirán tres días para finalizar el resultado. La elección responde a un programa de compromiso propuesto por los comisionados de los Estados Unidos y aceptado tanto por el ya dimitido gobierno de Victoria como por los revolucionarios, previéndose una elección presidencial permanente tan pronto como se restablezcan las condiciones normales. En un despacho de Roma con fecha del 3 de diciembre, se informa que el Papa telegrafió sus felicitaciones y su bendición apostólica al arzobispo Nouel por su elección como presidente provisional de la República Dominicana, expresando la esperanza de que fortalezca los lazos con la Santa Sede y señalando que es probable que el prelado sea nombrado cardenal al concluir su mandato.

records.headline: Archbishop Nouel has been chosen by the Dominican congress as provisional president of the republic for a term of two
records.summary_en: Archbishop Nouel has been chosen by the Dominican congress as provisional president of the republic for a term of two years, succeeding President Victorio, who has resigned. The report says the choice followed three successive unanimous votes in the Dominican house of representatives in favor of the senate's action, and that in the two-year period a free and fair election is expected to be held to choose and install a constitutional president.
records.summary_es: El arzobispo Nouel ha sido elegido por el congreso dominicano como presidente provisional de la república por un período de dos años, en sucesión del presidente Victorio, que ha renunciado. El informe dice que la elección siguió a tres votaciones sucesivas y unánimes en la cámara de representantes dominicana a favor de lo aprobado por el senado, y que en el período de dos años se espera celebrar una elección libre y justa para escoger e instalar a un presidente constitucional.
records.passage: NOUEL MADE PRESIDENT. Archbishop Chosen to Head Dominican Republic a Two Years. [illegible] Archbishop Nouel has been chosen by the Dominican congress as provisional president of the republic for a term of two years and will immediately succeed President Victoria, who has resigned. That result followed three successive and unanimous votes in the Dominican house of representatives in favor of the prelate, the senate having already acted favorably, thus complying with the constitutional requirements. In the two-year period it is believed that a free and fair election can be held and a constitutional president chosen and installed with reasonable assurance of a permanent tenure.

records.summary_en: Following the departure of United States marines from Santo Domingo city aboard the cruiser-transport Prairie for Philadelphia, the Evening Star reports that Archbishop Adolfo Alejandro Nouel has been unanimously elected provisional president of the Dominican Republic. The fifty-year-old prelate, Archbishop of Santo Domingo and Primate of America, was consecrated by his Roman classmate Cardinal Merry del Val and received special permission from Pope Pius to assume the presidency. Described as an intimate friend of Cardinal Farley, who gave him his episcopal ring, Archbishop Nouel was selected as the only compromise figure capable of restoring peace following the resignation of President Victoria. Under his administration, custom houses along the Haitian frontier are expected to be restored under United States control, eliminating the danger of financial loss to American bondholders.
records.summary_es: Tras la partida de los infantes de marina de los Estados Unidos desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo a bordo del crucero de transporte Prairie rumbo a Filadelfia, el Evening Star informa que el arzobispo Adolfo Alejandro Nouel ha sido elegido por unanimidad como presidente provisional de la República Dominicana. El prelado de cincuenta años, arzobispo de Santo Domingo y primado de América, fue consagrado por su compañero de estudios en Roma, el cardenal Merry del Val, y recibió un permiso especial del papa Pío para asumir la presidencia. Descrito como amigo íntimo del cardenal Farley, quien le obsequió el anillo episcopal que lleva puesto, el arzobispo Nouel fue seleccionado como la única figura de consenso capaz de restablecer la paz tras la renuncia del presidente Victoria. Bajo su administración, se espera que las aduanas a lo largo de la frontera haitiana sean restablecidas bajo control estadounidense, eliminando así el peligro de pérdidas financieras para los tenedores de bonos norteamericanos.

records.headline: Brig. Gen. Frank McIntyre has returned to Washington expressing
records.summary_en: Brig. Gen. Frank McIntyre has returned to Washington expressing optimism about the country's outlook, The Washington Times reports under the heading "Santo Domingo's Condition Better"; McIntyre is an American peace commissioner to the Dominican Republic. McIntyre stated that the commission regarded the election of Archbishop Nouel as a wise step. He noted that the Dominicans will likely convene a constituent assembly to arrange their national affairs, with President Nouel serving in office until that body convenes.
records.summary_es: El general de brigada Frank McIntyre regresó a Washington expresando optimismo sobre el porvenir de ese país, según informa The Washington Times bajo el encabezado "Santo Domingo's Condition Better"; McIntyre es comisionado de paz estadounidense para la República Dominicana. McIntyre afirmó que la comisión consideró la elección del arzobispo Nouel como una medida acertada. Señaló además que es probable que los dominicanos convoquen una asamblea constituyente para organizar sus asuntos nacionales, ejerciendo el presidente Nouel sus funciones hasta la instalación de dicho cuerpo.

records.summary_en: An illustration showing the west facade of the cathedral of Santo Domingo in the Dominican Republic appears in The Yale Expositor, under the title "Columbus' Bones Found Here." An accompanying caption notes that in 1877 a priest, whose name is printed as Father Bllllnl, discovered the veritable remains of Christopher Columbus in this structure. The text identifies the building as the first cathedral erected in America, begun in 1514 under the early name "do lot Indios," and adds that the first mass in the New World was celebrated on January 8, 1494, in Isabela on the northern coast of the island.

records.headline: According to Washington dispatches in The East St. Louis Daily Journal
records.summary_en: According to Washington dispatches in The East St. Louis Daily Journal, unrest resumed in the Dominican Republic almost as soon as American commissioners and United States marines departed from Santo Domingo City. Horatio Vasques, leader of the recent revolution, is reported to be preparing to challenge Archbishop Nouel, who was installed as compromise provisional president less than two weeks ago. In response, the Navy Department ordered the battleship New Hampshire to steam with all speed to Santo Domingo, with the transport Prairie prepared to return marines to protect customs houses and foreign lives and property. Special commissioners Brig. Gen. McIntyre and W. T. S. Doyle had only just arrived back in Washington after attempting to settle the tangled situation.

Se informa que Horacio Vásquez, líder de la reciente revolución, se prepara para crear dificultades al arzobispo Nouel, quien fue investido como presidente provisional de compromiso hace menos de dos semanas. En respuesta, el Departamento de la Armada ordenó al acorazado New Hampshire zarpar a toda máquina hacia Santo Domingo, disponiéndose que el transporte Prairie traslade de regreso a los infantes de marina para proteger las aduanas y las vidas y propiedades extranjeras. Los comisionados especiales, general de brigada McIntyre y W. T. S. Doyle, apenas acababan de regresar a Washington tras intentar solucionar la enredada situación.

records.summary_en: The New Hampshire, a battleship carrying a below-normal supply of coal, put to sea at midnight for San Domingo without waiting to replenish, a Norfolk dispatch in The Laramie Republican reports under the heading "Sails for South," prompted by reports of a serious uprising. The battleship New Hampshire is en route to the capital following apprehensive reports received the previous night. Officials stated that the warship is being sent purely for moral effect, with no intention at present of landing marines or bluejackets, and noted that the unrest has thus far shown no signs of escalating into armed conflict.

records.summary_en: Archbishop Adolfo Nouel presented his resignation, a San Domingo dispatch to The Montgomery Advertiser reports, after having held office for only thirteen days as provisional president of the Dominican Republic. He suspended his resignation later at the request of members of the Dominican Congress and several prominent citizens. The provisional president's future action depends upon the outcome of an interview with former Dominican president Horacio Vasquez, who arrived in the capital yesterday.

Más tarde suspendió su dimisión a petición de miembros del Congreso dominicano y de varios ciudadanos prominentes. Las medidas posteriores del presidente provisional dependen del resultado de una entrevista con el expresidente dominicano Horacio Vásquez, quien llegó ayer a la capital.

records.headline: A Santo Domingo City dispatch to The Sun reports that Archbishop Nouel resigned
records.summary_en: A Santo Domingo City dispatch to The Sun reports that Archbishop Nouel resigned as provisional president of the Dominican Republic after having been in office a little more than thirteen days, though he subsequently suspended the action. The move caused little surprise, as recent advices indicated that the archbishop had been exasperated by the struggle for office waged by Horatio Vasquez and other leaders of the recent revolution. Nouel had accepted the compromise presidency expecting that constitutional revision and general elections would follow, an arrangement demanded by revolutionists and negotiated by special United States commissioners Brigadier General Frank McIntyre and W. T. S. Doyle of the State Department.

La decisión causó escasa sorpresa, ya que despachos recientes indicaban que el prelado se hallaba exasperado por la disputa por cargos públicos librada por Horacio Vásquez y otros líderes de la reciente revolución. Nouel había asumido la presidencia de compromiso con la expectativa de que se revisaría la constitución y se celebrarían elecciones generales, acuerdo exigido por los revolucionarios y concertado por los comisionados especiales de los Estados Unidos, el general de brigada Frank McIntyre y W. records.headline: Dominican revolutionists apparently renewed their hostilities
records.summary_en: Dominican revolutionists apparently renewed their hostilities only after American commissioners and United States marines departed Santo Domingo City, according to dispatches received in Washington and published in the Potosi Journal. Horatio Vasquez, leader of the recent revolution, is reported to be preparing to create difficulties for Archbishop Nouel, who had been installed as compromise provisional president less than two weeks earlier. In response, the Navy Department ordered the battleship New Hampshire to steam at full speed to Santo Domingo, while the transport Prairie may return marines to protect customhouses and foreign lives and property. Special commissioners Brigadier General McIntyre and W. T. S. Doyle had only just returned to Washington after seeking a settlement of the tangled situation.
records.summary_es: Los revolucionarios dominicanos aparentemente reanudaron sus hostilidades solo después de que los comisionados estadounidenses y los infantes de marina de los Estados Unidos salieran de la ciudad de Santo Domingo, según despachos recibidos en Washington y publicados en el Potosi Journal. Se informa que Horacio Vásquez, líder de la reciente revolución, se dispone a causarle dificultades al arzobispo Nouel, quien había sido investido como presidente provisional de compromiso hacía menos de dos semanas. En respuesta, el Departamento de la Marina ordenó al acorazado New Hampshire zarpar a toda máquina rumbo a Santo Domingo, mientras que el transporte Prairie podría trasladar de regreso a los infantes de marina para resguardar las aduanas y las vidas y propiedades extranjeras. Los comisionados especiales, el general de brigada McIntyre y W. T. S. Doyle, acababan de regresar a Washington tras intentar solucionar la enmarañada situación.
