records.summary_en: The *daily worker* published a sharp critique of American policy in the Caribbean, condemning a peace society editorial that defended military intervention in Haiti and the Dominican Republic. The paper described the Haitian administration as a puppet regime upheld by American arms, asserting that a secret treaty extension planned to keep U.S. forces in Haiti until 1935. It similarly denounced the 1916 military takeover of the Dominican Republic, rejecting claims that financial collapse justified imperialist intervention on behalf of capitalist interests.
records.summary_es: El *daily worker* publicó una severa crítica a la política estadounidense en el Caribe, condenando el editorial de una sociedad pacifista que defendía la intervención militar en Haití y la República Dominicana. El rotativo describió al gobierno haitiano como un régimen títere sostenido por las armas estadounidenses, afirmando que una prórroga secreta de tratados contemplaba mantener tropas de Estados Unidos en Haití hasta 1935. De igual modo, denunció la toma del poder militar en la República Dominicana en 1916, rechazando el argumento de que el colapso financiero justificara una intervención imperialista en favor de intereses capitalistas.

records.headline: The bulk of the customs revenues collected by the Amer
records.summary_en: The *daily worker* criticized the $25,000,000 loan floated in the United States for the Dominican Republic, claiming that customs revenues collected by the American receiver-general served primarily to enrich Wall Street bankers. The article alleged that when Santo Domingo began retiring its debts too quickly, Secretary of State Hughes made troop withdrawal contingent on treaties that ratified military decrees, expanded receivership powers, and secured a new loan. It asserted that these treaties were secretly negotiated in 1924 prior to American military evacuation and national elections.
records.summary_es: El *daily worker* criticó el empréstito de 25 000 000 de dólares emitido en Estados Unidos para la República Dominicana, afirmando que las rentas aduaneras recaudadas por el receptor general estadounidense servían primordialmente para enriquecer a los banqueros de Wall Street. El artículo denunciaba que, cuando Santo Domingo comenzó a liquidar sus deudas con excesiva rapidez, el secretario de Estado Hughes condicionó la retirada de las tropas a tratados que ratificaban los decretos militares, ampliaban las atribuciones de la receptoría y aseguraban un nuevo préstamo. Aseguraba que estos tratados se negociaron secretamente en 1924 antes de la evacuación militar estadounidense y de las elecciones nacionales.
records.passage: loan of $25,000,000 to be floated in the United States. The bulk of the customs revenues collected by the American receiver general is applied to paying off the American bankers; only what is left is turned over to the Dominican government. The purpose of these treaties was to extend American control over the Dominican republic. America's excuse in 1904 for invading Santo Domingo was that the native government was having trouble with foreign creditors, chiefly France, which threatened to send warships to collect the debts claimed by its bondholders. In 1922, when Santo Domingo's bonds were held by American bankers, the state department thought that the Caribbean republic was paying off its debts too rapidly, and was approaching the point where it could claim complete freedom. In June 1922 Secretary of State Hughes announced that the United States would withdraw its troops, if Santo Domingo signed treaties recognizing all the acts of the American military occupation, extending the 1907 treaty until its debts to American bankers were paid off, extending the powers of the American receiver general of customs and opening the way for a new loan by American bankers. records.summary_en: The *Daily Worker* reported that recently ratified treaties confirmed all acts of the former American military government in Santo Domingo, despite the transition to a native civil government. The treaties validated a 1922 Dominican bond issue maturing in 1942, marketed through Lee, Higginson and Company. A U.S. naval officer had assured bankers that customs duties would be collected by a U.S.-appointed official and serve as a first lien on the loan.
records.summary_es: El *Daily Worker* informó que los tratados recientemente ratificados convalidaron todos los actos del anterior gobierno militar estadounidense en Santo Domingo, a pesar de la transición a un gobierno civil propio. Los convenios reconocieron la validez de una emisión de bonos dominicanos de 1922 con vencimiento en 1942, comercializada a través de Lee, Higginson and Company. Un oficial naval estadounidense había asegurado a los banqueros que los derechos arancelarios serían recaudados por un funcionario designado por Estados Unidos y constituirían un gravamen prioritario para el pago del empréstito.
records.passage: [illegible]teed "the acceptance and validation of this bond issue by any government of the Dominican republic as a legal, binding and irrevocable obligation of the Dominican republic." The 1922 loan runs until 1942. A letter to Lee, Higginson and company from the United States naval officer in charge of the department of finance and commerce in Santo Domingo assured the bankers that Dominican customs duties "shall be collected and applied by an official appointed by the president of the United States and that the loan now authorized shall have first lien upon such customs revenues." Though the American military government of Santo Domingo has given way to a native civil government, the treaties ratified this week confirm this and all other acts of the American military government. records.headline: DOMINICAN TREATIES Washington, Oct, 25.—The flotation of a loan for the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: In a brief Washington dispatch of October 25, the flotation of a loan for the Dominican Republic in the United States was expected to follow the ratification of two treaties signed Saturday between Secretary Kellogg and Minister Carmen Ariza. One treaty confirmed all the decrees issued by North Americans during the occupation of the Dominican Republic ending in 1922, and the other related to customs collections.
records.summary_es: En un breve despacho de Washington del 25 de octubre, se esperaba que la emisión de un préstamo para la República Dominicana en los Estados Unidos siguiera a la ratificación de dos tratados firmados el sábado entre el secretario Kellogg y el ministro Carmen Ariza. Un tratado confirmaba todos los decretos emitidos por los norteamericanos durante la ocupación de la República Dominicana que terminó en 1922, y el otro se refería a la recaudación de aduanas.

One treaty confirms all the decrees issued by North Americans during the occupation of the Dominican Republic ending in 1922. The other relates to customs collections. TURKEY LOOKS WESTWARD Angora, Oct. [illegible]. — Another western reform was approved today when a special government commission decided to favor the adoption of the Gregorian Calendar. The 24 hour clock will also be introduced into Turkey. TERRIBLE CYCLONE IN PERSIAN GULF Karachi, Oct. 25. — Dispatches to the Daily Gazette say that 7,000 died in the Persian Gulf in a cyclone which was accompanied by an earthquake. The pearl fishing fleet was almost entirely wiped out. Over 200 boats sank. British naval vessels lost one boat.

records.headline: The decree establishing the council of state was for a term
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported on political controversy in Haiti surrounding President Borno's eligibility, his decree extending the Council of State to secure reelection, and extended American financial control under the 1915 treaty. The article also noted heavy outward migration among Haitian farmers, with tens of thousands departing for Cuba and the Dominican Republic. An estimated 150,000 natives had emigrated since the American occupation began, resulting in a local labor scarcity.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó sobre la controversia política en Haití en torno a la elegibilidad del presidente Borno, su decreto de prórroga del Consejo de Estado para asegurarse la reelección y la extensión del control financiero estadounidense bajo el tratado de 1915. El artículo también señaló una intensa emigración de agricultores haitianos, con decenas de miles partiendo hacia Cuba y la República Dominicana. Se estimaba que unos 150 000 naturales habían emigrado desde el inicio de la ocupación estadounidense, lo que provocó escasez de mano de obra local.
records.passage: [A?] new constitution was prepared by Assistant Secretary of the Navy Franklin D. Roosevelt and adopted by Haiti, by decree of its President, acting as dictator. The council of State elected President Borno in 1922. It is claimed that he is ineligible to serve as President, since he was the son of alien French, although he was born in Haiti. The decree establishing the council of state was for a term of 10 years, which term has now expired, but President Borno, a candidate to reelect [himself?] next April 12, has decreed its extension for another 10 years, and it is alleged he has filled several vacancies on it with his own relatives and cabinet officials and expects it to reelect him. In the meanwhile the people have not been permitted to vote for a new Assembly, whose constitutional function it is to elect the President. The treaty of 1915 with the United States has been extended by presidential decree until 1936, without coming before our Senate. This extends our control over Haitian finances. The National City Bank is negotiating an additional loan of $16,000,000 to Haiti, the bids for the loan having been advertised by our State Department. In 1922 the Haitian foreign debt was $6,971,874. Haiti has a population of 3,000,000, mostly small farmers. In 1924 there was an emigration of 21,013 from Haiti to Cuba; in 1925 there were upward of 30,000 emigrated to Cuba, and many more to the Dominican Republic. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published an account describing the conditions of Haitian peasants under the American occupation. The report asserted that the occupation protected rural workers from forced military impressment and bandits, allowing them to farm and sell produce freely. It stated that peasants were better fed, clothed, and receiving medical treatment at free clinics, despite widespread illiteracy.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* publicó una crónica que describía la situación de los campesinos haitianos bajo la ocupación estadounidense. El reportaje afirmaba que la ocupación protegía a los trabajadores rurales del reclutamiento militar forzoso y de los bandoleros, permitiéndoles cultivar y vender sus productos libremente. Indicaba que los campesinos estaban mejor alimentados, mejor vestidos y recibían atención médica en dispensarios gratuitos, a pesar del analfabetismo generalizado.
records.passage: spoken language is a Creole patois, so different from the French of the small cultivated class that no Frenchman could understand them. By comparison the American Expeditionary Force doughboy, with his rudimentary vocabulary and his amazing pronunciation, would be a wizard in his understanding of French. In addition, the Creole patois rarely sees print. The word man, for instance, is "mouin," possessing not the slightest resemblance to the French word "homme." The peasant, or [illegible], as the American marine dubs him, is not only hopelessly illiterate, but equally inarticulate. Under the influence of our occupation he is no longer the helpless victim of impressment into the armies and bands of robbers who roamed through Haiti, destroying his little garden patch and burning his home while he hid in the hills, but free to work his gardens, and bring its produce into market. He is content and immeasurably better fed and THE SUNDAY STAR, WASHINGTON, D. C., MARCH 28, 1926 — PART 5, clothed, and free clinics and dispensaries administer to his ills. records.headline: The j department of public works is each year training a growing number of Haitian engineers
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported on efforts to prepare Haiti for eventual American withdrawal by training native personnel across various government departments. Haitian nationals were increasingly staffing public works, sanitary services, customs administration, and agricultural engineering, while Haitians comprised about half the commissioned officers in the gendarmerie. Concurrently, the American military presence had been reduced to an 800-man marine force.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó sobre los esfuerzos para preparar a Haití para una eventual retirada estadounidense mediante la capacitación de personal autóctono en diversos departamentos gubernamentales. Ciudadanos haitianos se incorporaban de forma creciente a las obras públicas, servicios sanitarios, administración de aduanas e ingeniería agrícola, al tiempo que conformaban cerca de la mitad de los oficiales en la gendarmería. En forma paralela, la presencia militar estadounidense se había reducido a un contingente de 800 infantes de marina.
records.passage: ultimate withdrawal, with all the elements necessary for its self-government. The yearly reports made to the State Department are eloquent in the increasing number and sphere of Haitian participation in the various fields. The department of public works is each year training a growing number of Haitian engineers, architects, artisans, office executives, hydrographic aids, steam gauge readers, telephone and telegraph operators and inspectors. The sanitary service is turning out Haitian physicians, surgeons, nurses, dentists, pharmacists and sanitary inspectors. Practically all the force of the financial adviser and general receiver of customs is purely Haitian. The recently formed office of the chief agricultural engineer is enrolling and training a Haitian personnel. In the ranks of the Haitian gendarmerie there are now approximately 60 Haitians of the best type who are either commissioned, acting or aspirant officers, or practically one-half of its commissioned strength. All these departments are organized into departments with district and subdistrict divisions, so that throughout Haiti the native Haitian is working shoulder to shoulder with Americans in the rehabilitation of the country. Coincident with this sound expansion has gone the gradual reduction of armed American forces to a minimum. The former marine brigade of full strength, with aviation and other attached special units, three years ago was stationed throughout the island. Today it numbers but 800,

records.summary_en: The *Pocahontas Times* recounted the history of U.S. intervention in Haiti, noting that seven revolutions between 1910 and 1915 culminated in the killing of President Sam and the landing of U.S. Marines. Under the 1916 treaty establishing a 20-year protectorate, the article stated that order and prosperity were established with minimal risk of revolution. By October, American military forces had been reduced to 800 marines supporting an armed native constabulary.
records.summary_es: El *Pocahontas Times* relató la historia de la intervención estadounidense en Haití, recordando que siete revoluciones entre 1910 y 1915 culminaron con la muerte violenta del presidente Sam y el desembarco de los marines estadounidenses. Bajo el tratado de 1916 que estableció un protectorado de 20 años, el artículo señalaba que se habían implantado el orden y la prosperidad con mínimo riesgo de revolución. Para octubre, las tropas militares estadounidenses se habían reducido a 800 marines que apoyaban a una fuerza policial nativa armada.
records.passage: West Virginia it is a mountain country, and like West Virginia it has mountains heavily forested clear to the top. It produces for export coffee, sugar, cotton, logwood, and [cacao?]. It is the most fertile island in the West Indies. From the year 1910 to the year 1915, Haiti had seven revolutions, and seven presidents occupied uneasy thrones in that country. The last of the seven, Gen. Sam, was inaugurated March 4, 1915. He lasted until July 26, of that year. That day he took refuge in the French legation, and on that date, 200 political prisoners were massacred in the jail. The funeral services were being held, and the temper of the crowd was so dangerous, that they dragged President Sam out and killed him. Two hours after President Sam had passed, a United States cruiser entered the harbor of Port au Prince and landed marines and restored order. In 1916, a treaty between the United States and Haiti was ratified. By the terms of that treaty, the United States undertook a political and fiscal protectorate for a period of twenty years. Since then Haiti has known a measure of peace and prosperity. At this time there seem to be no danger of revolutions. Last October, there were 800 marines in Haiti with an armed constabulary of 2688 men, and a reserve of 20,000 men. The United States as usual did a good job. It was in this work that Vincent McCarty found [illegible] in the marines. He went there in 1917, and remained thirty-seven months. records.headline: A concrete high way connecting Port-au-Prince, tho Haitian Capital, and Santa
records.summary_en: The *New Britain Herald* reported on extensive infrastructure modernization in Haiti under President Borno, including more than 1,000 miles of paved roads, new schools, hospitals, and lighthouses. A concrete highway connecting Port-au-Prince with Santo Domingo had reached the border on the Haitian side, promising to reduce travel time between the capitals from days to hours once the Dominican section was completed. The report also highlighted telephone network expansion, tariff revisions to promote trade with the United States, and the continuing presence of 800 American marines.
records.summary_es: El *New Britain Herald* informó sobre la vasta modernización de infraestructura en Haití bajo el presidente Borno, con más de 1 000 millas de carreteras pavimentadas, nuevas escuelas, hospitales y faros. Una carretera de hormigón que comunicaba Puerto Príncipe con Santo Domingo había alcanzado la frontera del lado haitiano, prometiendo reducir el tiempo de viaje entre ambas capitales de días a horas una vez concluido el tramo dominicano. El despacho destacó asimismo la ampliación de la red telefónica, modificaciones arancelarias para estimular el comercio con Estados Unidos y la continua presencia de 800 infantes de marina estadounidenses.
records.passage: In the last ten years, more than 1,000 miles of paved roads have been laid, replacing highways that had deteriorated until they were little more than trails. A concrete highway connecting Port-au-Prince, the Haitian Capital, and Santo Domingo, capital city of the Dominican Republic, has been completed by the Haitians up to the border. When the Dominican portion is completed, the trip between the two capitals may be done in hours, where formerly it took days. This progress has been particularly notable during the administration of the present chief executive, President Borno, said a report in the booklet made by the Haitian minister of public works. His administration also has seen the construction of fourteen schools, thirteen hospitals and eleven lighthouses; installation of an automatic telephone system, and material progress in irrigation and canals. Since 1921, there has been an increase of 350 per cent in the number of telephones in use and the telegraph system has been augmented and improved. In order to foster trade between the United States and Haiti, the present Haitian Import Customs Tariff is being revised. Some eight hundred American Marines still remain in Haiti, completing their work of reorganizing the native constabulary. records.headline: Evan E. Young, the American Minister to the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: Evan E. Young, the American Minister to the Dominican Republic, is in Washington on his first leave from Santo Domingo since President Coolidge appointed him the previous year, frequently visiting the State Department's Eastern European Division, which he formerly headed. Formerly a lawyer in South Dakota with 21 years in the foreign service in Russia, the Near East, and Ecuador, Young backed Secretary Hughes in maintaining U.S. non-recognition of Soviet Russia. He reports that he stays informed on American affairs by listening to the radio in Santo Domingo.

Antiguo abogado en Dakota del Sur con 21 años en el servicio exterior en Rusia, el Cercano Oriente y Ecuador, Young respaldó al secretario Hughes en mantener el no reconocimiento estadounidense de la Rusia soviética. Informa que se mantiene al tanto de los asuntos estadounidenses escuchando la radio en Santo Domingo.

records.full_text:
Hot Wave Drives Members Of Corps to Seek Resorts

The Ambassador of Spain and Senora de Riano are spending the week end out of town.

The Minister of Hungary, Count Szechenyi, had as his guest in his home on Massachusetts avenue John Cardinal Csernoch, prince primate of Hungary, who will go to New York today preparatory to sailing for his home after attending the Eucharistic Congress in Chicago.

The Minister of the Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, Dr. Ante Tresich Pavichich, will go to Williamstown, Mass., the end of this month to spend several weeks attending the Institute of Politics at Williams College. The minister will be accompanied by the new secretary of the legation, Mr. Krunoslva.

The Minister of Bolivia and Senora de Jaimes Freyre and their daughter, Senorita Yolanda Jaimes Freyre, are spending the week end in Atlantic City, where they went by motor from New York. They will stop in Philadelphia for the Sesquicentennial on their way back to Washington this week.

The retiring Minister of the Dominican Republic and Senora de Ariza are in New York for a few days before sailing Thursday for their home.

The Minister of the Irish Free State, Dr. Timothy Smiddy, joined Mrs. Smiddy in their apartment at Wardman Park Hotel last week, after a trip to Newport, R. I., where he attended the Sesquicentennial celebration and also spoke at the special exercises commemorating the services of Count Gen. Arthur Dillon with the Revolutionary Army.

The Minister of Haiti and Mme. Price will go to New York tomorrow and Mme. Price will sail Wednesday for Port au Prince. The Minister will return to Washington the end of the week.

The Minister of Egypt and Mme. Samy are spending the week end as the guests of Mr. and Mrs. Peter A. Drury in their Summer home, Valley View, on the mountain above Bluemont, Va.

The Minister of Sweden, M. W. Bostrom, who is traveling with the Crown Prince Gustavus Adolphus and Crown Princess Louise of Sweden, will not return to Washington until after they sail from San Francisco Thursday, August 5, for the Orient. The Minister will then start East arriving here about the middle August. Mme. Bostrom is in their Swedish home for the Summer.

The newly appointed Minister of the Dominican Republic, Dr. Angel Morales, accompanied by Senora de Morales, have arrived in Washington and taken an apartment at the Wardman Park Hotel. Dr. Morales, who succeeds Dr. Jose del Carmen Ariza, served as Dominican Minister to Paris for one year, and prior to that was one of the vice presidents of the League of Nations at Geneva. An attorney by profession, he has held several governmental posts in the Dominican Republic, serving as secretary of the interior for one term. The newly appointed secretary of the Dominican legation, Senor Maximo L. Vasquez, also came to Washington last week and, accompanied by Senora de Vasquez, is established at the Roosevelt Hotel. Senor Vasquez is a nephew of President Vasquez of the Dominican Republic.

The charge d'affaires of Panama and Senora de Chevalier returned Friday from Philadelphia, where they attended the Sesquicentennial and the opening there of the Panama exhibit.

The counselor of the Czechoslovakian legation and Mme. Lipova are expected to arrive Friday aboard the Mauretania, which sailed from Southampton yesterday. M. and Mme. Lipova have been on vacation in Europe for some time and will come at once to Washington on their arrival.

The secretary of the Italian embassy and Donna Anna Domville Mascia have closed their apartment at 2106 Sixteenth street and gone to Canada to spend their vacation.

The secretary of the Polish legation and Mme. Orlowska will close their apartment at Wardman Park Hotel Wednesday and leave for several weeks' trip through the White Mountains, going first to Bretton Woods and visiting other points of interest in that region.

The assistant military attache of the French embassy and Mme. Thenault are expected to return tomorrow from a fortnight's visit with the latter's mother, Mrs. Oliver M. Spencer, in her cottage on Cape Cod. Maj. and Mme. Thenault made the trip by motor.

The second secretary of the British embassy and Mrs. G. H. Thompson will start Friday or Saturday by motor for Manchester, Mass., where the embassy is established for the Summer. Mr. and Mrs. Thompson have been occupying the home of the latter's mother, Mrs. Grosvenor H. Backus, since their return from a brief wedding trip.

The retiring attache of the Egyptian legation, Abdul-el-Eneim Salem Effendi, went to New York yesterday and will sail Wednesday for England. After a brief vacation in England he will go to Czechoslovakia to take up his duties as secretary of the Egyptian legation in Prague.

The attache of the Swedish legation, Baron Lennart Rappe, is spending a few days at Spring Lake, where he went yesterday, and will return tomorrow.

records.full_text:
MRS. COOLIDGE TO ATTEND RECITAL Displays Interest in Chamber Music Festival

Mrs. Coolidge will be present this afternoon at the second recital of the music festival in the chamber music auditorium of the Library of Congress. This is an event of social as well as artistic importance, with music lovers from many cities here to attend. Mrs. Frederick Coolidge, organizer of the famous Bethlehem music festivals and donor of the auditorium has come from Massachusetts for the occasions.

President and Mrs. Coolidge have Myron T. Herrick, American Ambassador to France, as a guest at the White House.

An appointment has been made for President Coolidge to receive the new ambassador of Spain, Don Alejandro Padilla, within the next few days. The new minister of the Dominican Republic, the new minister of Siam and the new minister of Albania are also waiting the opportunity to present their credentials to the Chief Executive. The Spanish envoy was presented to Secretary Kellogg yesterday.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported on extensive hurricane devastation across Cuba, citing observations from P. A. Bonet, the Cuban consul general to the Dominican Republic. Bonet reported widespread damage to villages and the countryside along the railroad line from Santa Clara Province westward. Several large sugar factories and cigar plants were wrecked or heavily damaged, with multiple casualties reported.

Bonet, cónsul general cubano ante la República Dominicana. Bonet reportó cuantiosos daños en poblados y campos a lo largo de la vía férrea desde la provincia de Santa Clara hacia el oeste. Varios grandes ingenios azucareros y fábricas de tabaco quedaron destruidos o gravemente averiados, registrándose numerosas víctimas.

Trains running at a speed not exceeding greatly that of a walk have managed to creep into the city from the eastern section of the republic. Passengers on them reported floods as far east as Santa Clara Province. P. A. Bonet, Cuban consul general to the Dominican Republic, who was a passenger on one of the trains, said every village along the railway line, from Manaca in Santa Clara province westward, was seriously damaged. The entire countryside, as far as he was able to see on both sides of the track, was a wreck. Havana has a plentiful supply of food and medicine, and thus far has been able without difficulty to take care of refugees. Sugar Factories Wrecked. Three large sugar factories in the outlying districts were hard hit by the storm. Central Occidente, a 150-year-old cane grinding plant, was wrecked. Central Fajaro was destroyed, with a loss of eight lives, and Central Toledo was badly damaged. At La Salud [illegible] tobacco curing sheds were demolished. Among the big industries here which suffered from the storm was the Partagas Cigar factory, which was destroyed. It employed 900 cigar makers. The Aguila [illegible] Cigar factory also was destroyed. The National Manufacturing Co. was damaged to the extent of $75,000, a paper factory, $50,000, and the Tropical Brewery, $40,000.

records.headline: Arriving on the first train from Santiago since a six-hour hurricane
records.summary_en: Arriving on the first train from Santiago since a six-hour hurricane struck Cuba, Porfirio A. Bonet, the Cuban consul general to the Dominican Republic, reported that his train could travel no faster than two or three miles an hour from Manaca in Santa Clara province. Bonet stated that trees, telephone poles, and telegraph poles were knocked flat and nearly every house in the towns along the route was destroyed, with every locality reporting heavy casualties. The account continued that the destruction and loss of life in Havana city would be repeated on a smaller scale throughout the entire area: the presidential palace in Havana was invaded by the flood and the interior was badly damaged, other large buildings in the city suffered similarly, temporary shelters were being erected for the homeless, and there were many thousands of persons needing relief. Eight persons were killed and many injured at Central Fajaro, where the sugar factory was destroyed; at Guira de Melena, nine dead, 22 injured and most of the town wrecked; eight were killed at Camp Columbia, which was almost completely wrecked, with 18 army airplanes destroyed; at Punta Brava and Bauta 175 houses were razed, at Regla 15 houses wrecked, and at San Jose de las Lajas 40 injured and 204 houses destroyed, while the villages of Tapaste and Jamaica were reported to have been completely razed. A further Havana dispatch reported 300 more persons killed at Batabano, 80 perished at Bejucal, 11 dead and eight injured at Gabriel, and at Guanabacoa three dead, 150 injured and 1,500 families homeless, while Florida escaped virtually unscathed from the storm.

Bonet, cónsul general de Cuba en la República Dominicana, informó que su tren no pudo avanzar a más de dos o tres millas por hora desde Manaca, en la provincia de Santa Clara. Bonet declaró que los árboles y los postes de teléfono y telégrafo quedaron derribados y casi todas las casas de los pueblos a lo largo de la ruta fueron destruidas, reportándose numerosas víctimas en cada localidad. El relato continuaba diciendo que la destrucción y la pérdida de vidas en la ciudad de La Habana se repetirían en menor escala en toda la zona: el palacio presidencial de La Habana fue invadido por la inundación y el interior quedó gravemente dañado, otros edificios grandes de la ciudad sufrieron daños similares, se erigían refugios temporales para los sin hogar y había muchos miles de personas necesitadas de auxilio. Ocho personas murieron y muchas resultaron heridas en Central Fajaro, donde la fábrica de azúcar fue destruida; en Güira de Melena, nueve muertos, 22 heridos y la mayor parte del pueblo destruida; ocho murieron en Camp Columbia, que quedó casi completamente destruido, con 18 aviones del ejército destruidos; en Punta Brava y Bauta fueron arrasadas 175 casas, en Regla 15 casas destruidas, y en San José de las Lajas 40 heridos y 204 casas destruidas, mientras los pueblos de Tapaste y Jamaica fueron, según se informó, completamente arrasados. Un despacho adicional de La Habana informó de 300 personas más muertas en Batabanó, 80 fallecidas en Bejucal, 11 muertos y ocho heridos en Gabriel, y en Guanabacoa tres muertos, 150 heridos y 1,500 familias sin hogar, mientras Florida escapó prácticamente ilesa de la tormenta.

In the years that followed the United States securely fastened its financial tentacles upon the island, and with financial control went interference with the political life of the nation. As in Haiti, so in Santo Domingo, we find the National City Bank of New York, a Morgan-Rockefeller outfit, the dominating influence. Whenever a spark of smouldering discontent would light the fires of opposition in the island, U. S. warships were always ready to "do their stuff." One stage of this development is carefully narrated in "Dollar Diplomacy" as follows: "American financial and political interference in Santo Domingo finally led to armed intervention. In April 1916 another insurrection took place in Santo Domingo, and this time, on May 4, [illegible], United States marines were landed. Long Protectorate in Nicaragua Opposed by White House 100-Year Diaz Plan Rejected by President, but Marines Will Remain for the Present

A 100-year protectorate over Nicaragua, as proposed by President Diaz, is opposed by President Coolidge.

This government will reject such a treaty unless it is greatly modified, the White House indicated late yesterday.

Meanwhile, the U. S. will continue its intervention in Nicaragua on the present basis. There was no suggestion of withdrawing the marines.

Wholesome Effect Seen

The Coolidge announcement is expected to have a wholesome effect in Latin America and to restore some of the confidence lost thru the recent Nicaraguan developments.

The plan proposed by Diaz is not unique in Amercian diplomacy. The U. S. now, thru its own officials or American citizens recommended by the State Department, controls the finances of the Dominican Republic, Haiti and El Salvador. An American customs collector is maintained in Nicaragua under a long-standing arrangement.

Frequent Use of Troops

Virtual protectorates are maintained over Cuba, Panama, the Dominican Republic, Haiti, El Salvador and, temporarily at least, in Nicaragua.

Military intervention has been resorted to four times in the case of each of the countries except Haiti. Marines sent to Haiti in 1915 are still there.

Battle Near in Nicaragua

MANAGUA, Nicaragua—A decisive battle was believed imminent today as government troops at Boaca, under Gen. Viquezen, prepared to attack Liberal forces at Muy Muy.

records.full_text:
REPORT STATES BOSS OF HAITI FINDS ALL O. K.

By Louis R. Lautier

During the past year the American treaty officials have been directing their efforts toward increasing the productive wealth of Haiti to the ultimate end of strengthening and improving the general economic condition, Brig. Gen. John H. Russell, American High Commissioner to Haiti, declared in his fifth annual report to the Secretary of State, which was made public by the State Department Monday.

In addition, he reported, the Haitian Government and the treaty officials have continued the general governing program for the stablization of Haitian finances, the maintenance of law and order, the construction of public works, and the improvement of the public health service.

A bumper coffee crop in a period of exceptionally high and abnormal prices and the re-election

BOSS OF HAITI REPORTS EVERYTHING IS O. K.

(Continued from page 1)

of President Borno contributed to the stability and the prosperity of Haiti in 1926, General Russell stated.

Business Confidence
“Confidence among business men, which, on account of the usual sensational rumors which precede a presidential election in Haiti, had been trembling in the balance, was restored immediately upon the promulgation of the results of the election,” General Russell reports. “This fact contributed largely in making the past year the greatest in the history of the Republic from a financial and business point of view.”

As a result of the visit of President Borno to the United States in last June he returned to Haiti imbued with a stronger desire to further the progress and development of his country and to make it a republic in being as well as in name, General Russell states.

The Haitian judiciary system is in need of complete renovation. “The courts are, if such could be possible, less effective than ever and their inefficiency and incompetency more notorious,” General Russell reports. “Trials by jury are farcial.”

There has been no reduction in the United States forces in Haiti. They consist of a skeleton brigade of United States marines and a mine sweeper of 950 tons displacement. Martial law has only been exercised upon the rarest occasions, says General Russell.

The customs receipts for the past year were unprecedented. The total receipts amounted to $9,072,929.62. Of this amount the sum of $8,118,996.35 was from custom revenues.

The Public Debt
The actual debt reducing amortization was $1,384,836.90. The required reduction was only $717,218.36. The total public debt amounts to $18,849,000.

As a result of the favorable year just closed the Haitian people have been benefited materially, says General Russell. They are better fed, better clothed, and better housed than ever before.

The commerce of Haiti during the past year has been most satisfactory, it is reported. There has been a healthy growth of shipping entering the harbors of the Republic and a gradual increase in traffic across the Dominican border.

Educational Ideas
The Haitian Government believes that its educational system should be designed to furnish agricultural education to the rural and industrial education to the urban population, the American high commissioner states. He says that “the Haitian Government considers it not only essential but vital that the Haitian people be taught to use their hands.”

General Russell also states in his report:
“The efforts that have been made and are being made to foster the further increase of production in Haiti will soon show results and with the passing of an appropriate revenue law and the renovation of the Haitian judiciary, the advance toward the stabilization of government will be most marked.

“As in past years President Borno has co-operated in every way for the carrying out of the provisions of the treaty of 1915, and has made the marked improvement of last year possible.

“The treaty officials have consistently, tactfully and energetically carried out their duties and the efficient management of the respective departments under their control has largely contributed to the remarkable progress which is being made in the bringing of happiness and prosperity to the Haitian people.”

Statements Contradictory
Statements in the report of General Russell are contradictory to those made upon the floor of the Senate by Senator William H. King, Democrat, of Utah, who was recently barred by President Borno from visiting Haiti because of derogatory remarks made by the Senator concerning the Haitian president in demanding that the American forces be withdrawn from the island republic.

In a speech in the Senate on February 1 last, Senator King declared:
“First, let it be remembered that by every standard of morality and justice there was no treaty. Our forces were in possession of the country. We had destroyed the legislative branch of the government and taken possession of all governmental agencies of the country. We set up a shadow government. It was not a Haitian government. A few Haitians were put into positions, but they were named by Naval officers of the United States and they did the will of those who named them. One of them we called a President, and he was required to sign a treaty prepared by the United States.”

Senator King described the re-election of President Borno as a farce. This “shadow president,” he said, was chosen by members of an assembly which he had appointed. “The Haitian people,” he declared, “are in a condition of political servitude.”

records.headline: President Vasquez of the Dominican Republic departed on Thursday
records.summary_en: President Vasquez of the Dominican Republic departed on Thursday for Port-au-Prince, marking the first visit ever made by a Dominican president to Haiti, an Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo dated July 30 reports. Accompanied by cabinet members and high military officials, Vasquez is expected to stay about eight days, for which extensive preparations were made in Port-au-Prince. The two republics, which share an island about the size of South Carolina, are expected to discuss their boundary dispute dating back to French colonial times.
records.summary_es: El presidente Vasquez de la República Dominicana partió el jueves hacia Puerto Príncipe, marcando la primera visita jamás realizada por un presidente dominicano a Haití, según un despacho de Associated Press desde Santo Domingo fechado el 30 de julio. Acompañado por miembros del gabinete y altos oficiales militares, se espera que Vasquez permanezca unos ocho días, para lo cual se hicieron amplios preparativos en Puerto Príncipe. Se prevé que las dos repúblicas, que comparten una isla aproximadamente del tamaño de Carolina del Sur, discutan su disputa fronteriza que data de la época colonial francesa.

records.headline: Reprinting an item from the Porto Rico Progress, the St. Croix avis
records.summary_en: Reprinting an item from the Porto Rico Progress, the St. Croix avis notes that Porto Rico ranks second among Santo Domingo's foreign population, with families preferred under inducements to settle people on the land. Although Porto Ricans in rural areas quickly adopt local speech and assimilate, those in cities who know English sometimes compete for jobs desired by Dominicans, who occasionally express their feelings regarding Porto Ricans as American citizens. The article emphasizes the shared language, racial viewpoint, and early colonial history linking the two islands, recalling that Ponce de Leon sailed from Santo Domingo across the Mona Channel to settle Borinquen.
records.summary_es: Reproduciendo un artículo del Porto Rico Progress, el St. Croix avis señala que Puerto Rico ocupa el segundo lugar entre la población extranjera de Santo Domingo, prefiriéndose a las familias dentro de los incentivos para asentar personas en la tierra. Aunque los puertorriqueños en las zonas rurales adoptan rápidamente el habla local y se asimilan, aquellos en las ciudades que saben inglés a veces compiten por puestos deseados por los dominicanos, quienes en ocasiones expresan sus sentimientos respecto a los puertorriqueños como ciudadanos estadounidenses. El artículo destaca el idioma común, la perspectiva racial y la historia colonial temprana que vinculan a ambas islas, recordando que Ponce de León zarpó de Santo Domingo a través del Canal de la Mona para colonizar Borinquen.

records.headline: Knowles, former American minister to the Dominican republic and now consul
records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* reported that Horace G. Knowles, former U.S. minister to the Dominican Republic and currently a Dominican consul, strongly condemned U.S. interventions in Nicaragua, Haiti, and Santo Domingo during a speech in Northampton. Knowles told the Hampshire County Progressive Club that these military actions constituted unauthorized acts of war undertaken by the executive government without congressional approval.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield Weekly Republican* informó que Horace G. Knowles, exministro de Estados Unidos ante la República Dominicana y en ese momento cónsul dominicano, condenó enérgicamente las intervenciones estadounidenses en Nicaragua, Haití y Santo Domingo durante un discurso pronunciado en Northampton. Knowles manifestó ante el Club Progresista del Condado de Hampshire que estas acciones militares constituían actos de guerra no autorizados y emprendidos por el poder ejecutivo sin el consentimiento del Congreso.

Northampton, Nov. 20 — The policy of the government at Washington in practicing intervention on the countries of Nicaragua, Haiti, and Santo Domingo was severely criticised by Horace G. Knowles, former American minister to the Dominican republic and now consul for that country, speaking under the auspices of the Hampshire County Progressive club at Carnegie hall tonight. Mr. Knowles said that the policies and acts presented were not those of the American people, nor even of the American Congress, but of the American government, which notwithstanding the fact that only Congress can declare war, had committed acts of war in these republics by the landing of armed forces. Northampton, Nov. 21 — The two buildings occupied by J. E. Lambie Co. of Main street, and the stock of dry goods, suits and coats, were destroyed by fire this morning at 4, and there were heavy losses on the furniture stock of J. H. Quinn, and the block occupied by Quinn, owned by J. H. O'Dea, and smaller losses on the clothing stocks of M. J. Keating, on one side of the Lambie store, and Coffey Burke in the other side. The present owners of Lambie Co. are George F. Edwards and James P. Fairchild. The losses, as insurance men figure them, probably are not more than $250,000, but replacement values at present high costs of building construction might add another $50,000 to the estimate of total loss.

records.headline: A United Press dispatch from Washington reports that technical adviser
records.summary_en: A United Press dispatch from Washington reports that technical adviser Albert Kelsey announced plans for an international airport in the Dominican Republic linked to the Christopher Columbus memorial lighthouse on the Atlantic coast near Santo Domingo. Sponsored by the Pan-American Union, the project has already received land and $300,000 in contributions, may request four million dollars from nations worldwide, and will offer a top architectural prize alongside lesser prizes. Kelsey noted that the airport will serve as a halfway point on the most direct airway between the two Americas, while the lighthouse will house the tomb of Columbus at its base and project a beam visible for fifty miles.

Patrocinado por la Unión Panamericana, el proyecto ya ha recibido terrenos y $300,000 en contribuciones, podría solicitar cuatro millones de dólares a las naciones del mundo y ofrecerá un premio arquitectónico principal junto con premios menores. Kelsey señaló que el aeropuerto servirá como punto intermedio en la ruta aérea más directa entre las dos Américas, mientras que el faro albergará la tumba de Colón en su base y proyectará un haz de luz visible a cincuenta millas.

records.headline: The Pan-American Union will soon undertake the construction of a $4,000,000 memorial lighthouse
records.summary_en: The Pan-American Union will soon undertake the construction of a $4,000,000 memorial lighthouse to Christopher Columbus in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, funded by contributions from countries across Europe and America. In a worldwide architectural competition, 10 initial designs will be selected and their architects given detailed cost and measurement instructions before a final winner is chosen. The base of the lighthouse will include a chapel to house the bones of Columbus, which currently rest in a monument inside the Santo Domingo cathedral.
records.summary_es: La Unión Panamericana emprenderá pronto la construcción de un faro monumental de $4,000,000 en honor a Cristóbal Colón en Santo Domingo, República Dominicana, financiado mediante contribuciones de países de Europa y América. En un concurso arquitectónico mundial, se seleccionarán inicialmente 10 diseños y sus arquitectos recibirán instrucciones detalladas sobre medidas y costos antes de elegir al ganador final. La base del faro incluirá una capilla para albergar los restos de Colón, que actualmente reposan en un monumento dentro de la catedral de Santo Domingo.

records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* criticized President Coolidge's speech in Havana, where he asserted that nations including Haiti, Nicaragua, and the Dominican Republic were best suited to govern themselves and make their own mistakes. The editorial argued that this rhetoric contradicted the administration's active military interventions, including aerial bombing in Nicaragua and persistent intervention rights in Cuba.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield Weekly Republican* criticó el discurso del presidente Coolidge en La Habana, donde sostuvo que naciones como Haití, Nicaragua y la República Dominicana eran las más indicadas para gobernarse por sí mismas y cometer sus propios errores. El editorial argumentó que semejante retórica contradecía las intervenciones militares activas de su gobierno, incluidos los bombardeos aéreos en Nicaragua y el mantenimiento de derechos de intervención en Cuba.
records.passage: United States is sovereign in this hemisphere. In the closing passages of the address the President vaguely refers to an "international system" peculiar to this hemisphere, which imposes on each nation certain "obligations," "defined by laws which we recognize as binding on all of us." What "laws" there are of the character referred to no one may know, inasmuch as the Monroe doctrine, even with its corollaries stretched to their most extreme imperialistic implication, remains a policy of the United States like Great Britain's old claim to dominate the high seas. Ignoring the realistic bases of the policy of the United States since the Spanish war, the President found himself able to say with perfect gravity, "We are thoroughly committed to the principle that they (the Colombias, Costa Ricas, Haytis, Nicaraguas, Panamas, Dominican Republics and Cubas) are better fitted to govern themselves than anyone else is to govern them. It is better for the people to make their own mistakes than to have someone else make their mistakes for them." Why, then, do we not clear out of the Philippine islands? Even in Cuba, why do we insist on special rights of intervention? Why are our gallant marines put to such work as bombing Nicaraguan villages? There is reason to suspect that two Coolidges were struggling for expression in the Havana address. records.summary_en: In the Senate debate over Latin American policy, Senator Bingham defended the Administration by arguing that the withdrawal of American Marines from the Dominican Republic was proof that the United States had no imperialistic motives.

Las celebraciones incluyeron una recepción por la tarde en la residencia presidencial a la que asistió la élite dominicana, seguida por la noche de un concierto militar en una plaza pública, un espectáculo pirotécnico y un carnaval floral en el ayuntamiento con un modelo suspendido del Spirit of St. Louis.

records.headline: Hundreds of automobiles and thousands of spectators gathered
records.summary_en: Hundreds of automobiles and thousands of spectators gathered at the landing field in the Dominican Republic to give Colonel Lindbergh an ovation on his birthday. Escorted on arrival by the airships Santa Maria and La Nina, he was greeted with a 21-gun presidential salute from a Dominican fortress and received by President Vasquez, the American minister, and the diplomatic corps. President Vasquez presented him with a key to Santo Domingo, a gold medal on behalf of the republic, and a gold nugget from the authorities of Santiago, followed by an afternoon reception at the presidential residence and an evening military concert.
records.summary_es: Cientos de automóviles y miles de espectadores se reunieron en el campo de aterrizaje en la República Dominicana para brindar una ovación al coronel Lindbergh en su cumpleaños. Escoltado a su llegada por las aeronaves Santa Maria y La Nina, fue saludado con una salva presidencial de 21 cañonazos desde una fortaleza dominicana y recibido por el presidente Vasquez, el ministro estadounidense y el cuerpo diplomático. El presidente Vasquez le entregó una llave de Santo Domingo, una medalla de oro en nombre de la república y una pepita de oro de parte de las autoridades de Santiago, seguido de una recepción vespertina en la residencia presidencial y un concierto militar por la noche.

records.headline: I The route to Port-Au-Prince, 160 miles by airplane from here
records.summary_en: Col. Charles A. Lindbergh took off from Santo Domingo at 11 a.m. on February 6 for Port-au-Prince, Haiti, on a 160-mile route flown entirely across land, as he neared the end of his goodwill flight to the Pan American conference at Havana. The night before, he had been guest of honor at a brilliant ball at the presidential palace, attended by the diplomatic body, members of the government and prominent society figures.
records.summary_es: El coronel Charles A. Lindbergh despegó de Santo Domingo a las 11 de la mañana del 6 de febrero rumbo a Puerto Príncipe, Haití, en una ruta de 160 millas volada enteramente sobre tierra, cuando se acercaba al final de su vuelo de buena voluntad a la conferencia panamericana de La Habana. La noche anterior había sido el invitado de honor en un brillante baile en el palacio presidencial, al que asistieron el cuerpo diplomático, miembros del gobierno y destacadas figuras de la sociedad.
records.passage: By the Associated Press. SANTO DOMINGO, Dominican Republic, February 6. — Col. Charles A. Lindbergh, now nearing the end of his good will flight to the Pan American conference at Havana, took off for Port-au-Prince, Haiti, at 11 a.m., local time. The route to Port-au-Prince, 160 miles by airplane from here, led entirely across land, unless Lindbergh in his flight should venture across the inland waters of Lake Enriquillo and Lake Saumatre. The path of the lone eagle was over a country teeming with bird life, wild duck, flamingo, herons and other shore birds. The route passed over mountains and deep forests where voodooism was brought from Africa and practiced for many years. It led over a land where negro slaves by their own efforts freed themselves and set up a republic, of which Port-au-Prince is the capital. Haiti is the second country to be visited by Col. Lindbergh in his good will tour where American Marines are present. In Nicaragua he found them engaged in an active campaign against the rebel Gen. Sandino. In Haiti they are engaged in maintaining order until the new republic is considered capable of exercising in full its rights of sovereignty. Col. Lindbergh was kept busy until late last night. He was the guest of honor at a brilliant ball held at the presidential palace, which was decorated with flowers and lights. All the diplomatic body, members of the Government and prominent society figures attended. CITY WILL HONOR COSTES AND LEBRIX French Flyers, Due Here Tomorrow

records.headline: An International News Service dispatch from New York by H. C
records.summary_en: An International News Service dispatch from New York by H. C. Montee notes that Colonel Charles A. Lindbergh celebrated his 26th birthday on Saturday by flying on schedule from San Juan, Puerto Rico, to Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. That flight closed an eventful peacetime year in which Lindbergh rose from air mail carrier to world-renowned aviator, logging approximately 41,000 miles across 18 countries, colonies, or islands.
records.summary_es: Un despacho del International News Service desde Nueva York escrito por H. C. Montee señala que el coronel Charles A. Lindbergh celebró su 26.º cumpleaños el sábado volando según lo programado desde San Juan, Puerto Rico, hasta Santo Domingo, República Dominicana. Ese vuelo cerró un año lleno de acontecimientos en tiempos de paz en el que Lindbergh pasó de ser transportista de correo aéreo a aviador de renombre mundial, registrando aproximadamente 41,000 millas a través de 18 países, colonias o islas.

records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* commented on Colonel Lindbergh's reference to the shared island of Haiti and Santo Domingo, providing historical background for readers. The paper noted that the eastern republic had formally become the Dominican Republic in 1844 after twenty-one years as part of Haiti and earlier status as a Spanish colony.

records.headline: Commemoration of Great Haitian Liberator's Birth
records.summary_en: The birthday of Toussaint L'Ouverture was commemorated at a memorial meeting in New York under the auspices of the American Negro Labor Congress, with Richard B. Moore acting as chairman. Moore said that a little more than a hundred years after Haiti's triumphant struggle against Napoleon for complete independence, the island found itself under American imperialism, a foreign control he called far more menacing and crushing than the political control of one state over another. The meeting heard that L'Ouverture was born enslaved in the French colony of Haiti, then known as Santo Domingo, overthrew slavery throughout the island and carried on the struggle against Napoleon's reaction, making way for the birth of the republic of Haiti.
records.summary_es: El cumpleaños de Toussaint L'Ouverture fue conmemorado en una reunión memorial en Nueva York, bajo los auspicios del Congreso Americano de Trabajadores Negros, con Richard B. Moore como presidente del acto. Moore declaró que poco más de cien años después de la lucha triunfante de Haití contra Napoleón por su independencia completa, la isla se encontraba bajo el imperialismo estadounidense, un control extranjero que calificó de mucho más amenazante y aplastante que el control político de un Estado sobre otro. En la reunión se recordó que L'Ouverture nació esclavo en la colonia francesa de Haití, entonces conocida como Santo Domingo, abolió la esclavitud en toda la isla y continuó la lucha contra la reacción de Napoleón, abriendo el camino al nacimiento de la república de Haití.
records.passage: [illegible]cluded Richard B. Moore of the American Negro Labor congress, who acted as chairman; William Pickens, Henry Rosemond, August Bernier, J. J. Adams, Haitian representative at the Geneva conference, and others. Mr. Moore said a little more than a hundred years after Haiti's triumphant struggle against Napoleon for her complete independence, this island of the West Indies finds itself under the steel heels of American imperialism; a foreign control far more menacing and crushing and deadening than ever attended the political control of one state over another. Toussaint L'Ouverture was born a slave in the French colony of Haiti, then known as Santo Domingo. When the revolution came in France at the close of the eighteenth century the revolutionary ideas of Danton and Robespierre found ready recruits among the toiling slaves and discontented mulattoes of the oppressed island. records.headline: Following years of campaigning, the Fifth Pan-American Conference
records.summary_en: Following years of campaigning, the Fifth Pan-American Conference at Santiago, Chile, adopted a resolution in 1923 recommending that the governments and peoples of the Americas cooperate to erect a memorial lighthouse in the Dominican Republic, leading the governing board of the Pan-American Union to organize an architectural competition. The competition specifications require the reinforced-concrete and structural-steel monument to stand on a mound or terrace nearly 40 feet high, not exceed 600 feet in total height, support at least one great lantern, and include both a museum and a chapel large enough to house the Columbus monument currently in the cathedral at Santo Domingo.

records.headline: An architectural competition directed by the Pan-American Union
records.summary_en: An architectural competition directed by the Pan-American Union has invited architects from all nations to submit designs for a monumental lighthouse near Santo Domingo, with a winning entry to be chosen in the coming months. Estimated to cost about $4,000,000 and situated in a park donated by the Dominican Republic, the structure will house the world's largest and most powerful beacon, an adjoining museum for Columbus memorabilia, and a chapel to receive the monument holding Columbus's bones in the Cathedral of Santo Domingo. The Pan-American Union's foreword urges participating artists to adopt a universal perspective encompassing five centuries of world history since the discovery of America.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reviewed historical instances of U.S. supervision of Caribbean elections, citing American oversight of Dominican congressional elections in 1913 and presidential elections in 1914. Following the November 1916 military intervention, the country was occupied without elections until 1924, when voting was conducted under close American observation as troops prepared to depart.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* repasó los precedentes históricos de supervisión electoral estadounidense en el Caribe, citando la fiscalización de las elecciones legislativas de 1913 y las presidenciales de 1914 en la República Dominicana. Tras la intervención militar de noviembre de 1916, el país permaneció ocupado y sin elecciones hasta 1924, año en que se efectuaron votaciones bajo atenta observación estadounidense mientras las tropas preparaban su partida.
records.passage: forces of the United States and Senor Dartiguenave was elected president. The Marines were in charge of maintaining order in the country and of revising the electoral procedure. In 1920 this was again done, although this time the Haitian constabulary, under Marine officers, were the ones to supervise and maintain order during the period of election. In 1913 the elections for the national assembly of Santo Domingo were supervised by a North American commission. In 1914 the presidential elections were supervised by civil and military representatives. In November, 1916, the United States intervened in the affairs of the Dominican Republic to re-establish order. The republic was then occupied by military forces and no elections were held until 1924. No direct supervision was made of the 1924 elections, although there still remained a few of Uncle Sam's forces and they were observed very closely by a United States representative. In 1920 the Nicaraguan Government requested from the United States the assistance of an expert in the revision of its electoral laws. Harold W. Dodds was designated to go to Nicaragua, where he compiled a new electoral law, which was approved by the Congress of Nicaragua in 1923. Four United States Marines, dressed in civilian clothes, aided Mr. Dodds in the registration of the electoral voters. The last electoral supervision of Nicaragua has been conducted by Gen. McCoy as a result of the armed intervention which followed the civil war between the Liberal and Conservative parties

records.summary_en: The *Daily Worker* denounced U.S. imperialist expansion, asserting that American financial penetration of the Dominican Republic began with an interest-bearing loan in 1905 secured by customs control for fifty years. The article stated that U.S. Marines landed under the pretext of insurrection in 1916, declaring martial law and dismantling the Dominican constitutional government: with the government dissolved, the chief of the forces of occupation was proclaimed the supreme judge, supreme legislator and supreme executive. The military dictatorship lasted until 1924, in which year Santo Domingo was compelled to accept an arrangement whereby it became a protectorate of the United States.

records.summary_en: An article in La Sentinella describes the joint effort of the 21 American republics to build a Columbus memorial lighthouse on the coast of the Dominican Republic, noting that the international architectural design contest opened on September first after the concept was first proposed years ago following the discovery of Columbus's remains in the cathedral of Santo Domingo. The first stage of the competition closes on April 1, when the ten best designs will be chosen to enter a second stage. Preliminary requirements specify that the elevated base must be visible above neighboring trees and call on architects to go beyond academic perfection to portray Columbus's achievements in the evolution of world civilization.
records.summary_es: Un artículo en La Sentinella describe el esfuerzo conjunto de las 21 repúblicas americanas para construir un faro conmemorativo a Colón en la costa de la República Dominicana, señalando que el concurso internacional de diseño arquitectónico se abrió el primero de septiembre luego de que la idea fuera concebida hace años tras hallarse los restos de Colón en la catedral de Santo Domingo. La primera etapa del certamen cierra el 1 de abril, cuando se seleccionarán los diez mejores diseños para pasar a una segunda etapa. Los requisitos preliminares especifican que la base elevada debe ser visible por encima de los árboles vecinos e instan a los arquitectos a ir más allá de la mera perfección académica para representar los logros de Colón en la evolución de la civilización mundial.

records.headline: The Evening Star reports on the Episcopal mission work of Archdeacon Wyllie
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reports on the Episcopal mission work of Archdeacon Wyllie and his wife in the Dominican Republic ahead of a Tuesday evening talk at the parish hall of Epiphany Church at 1317 G Street. During the influenza epidemic, the Wyllies organized a hospital in Santo Domingo City that remains a flourishing institution, and they have also built schools and churches serving both the American population in the sugar industry and native inhabitants in the interior. Speaking under the title "Spreading the Kingdom in the Land of Columbus," Mrs. Wyllie will describe her life and social work in the interior of the island.

Durante la epidemia de influenza, los esposos Wyllie organizaron un hospital en la ciudad de Santo Domingo que sigue siendo una institución próspera, y también han construido escuelas e iglesias que atienden tanto a la población estadounidense en la industria azucarera como a los habitantes nativos del interior. Bajo el título «Spreading the Kingdom in the Land of Columbus», la señora Wyllie relatará su vida y obra social en el interior de la isla.

records.headline: Pan-American Airways placed 1,500 miles of new air routes into operation
records.summary_en: Pan-American Airways placed 1,500 miles of new air routes into operation following a three-day celebration of the new airport opening in Miami, Florida, forming the first major link in a projected 13,000-mile network to Central and South America. Alongside daily Miami-Havana flights and thrice-weekly flights to Nassau, the company launched a 1,440-mile thrice-weekly route from Miami via Havana to Camaguey and Santiago in Cuba, Port au Prince in Haiti, Santo Domingo City in the Dominican Republic, and San Juan, Porto Rico. Service began Wednesday when four planes departed Miami and one left San Juan, with passengers on the Miami departures including Amelia Earhart, Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Aeronautics William P. McCracken Jr., Mr. and Mrs. James Warner Bellah, Postmaster General Harry S. New, Second Assistant Postmaster General W. Irving Glover, and Mayor E. G. Sewell.
records.summary_es: Pan-American Airways puso en operación 1,500 millas de nuevas rutas aéreas tras una celebración de tres días por la inauguración del nuevo aeropuerto en Miami, Florida, formando el primer eslabón principal de una red proyectada de 13,000 millas hacia América Central y del Sur. Junto con vuelos diarios entre Miami y La Habana y vuelos tres veces por semana a Nassau, la compañía inauguró una ruta de 1,440 millas tres veces por semana desde Miami vía La Habana hacia Camagüey y Santiago en Cuba, Puerto Príncipe en Haití, la ciudad de Santo Domingo en la República Dominicana y San Juan, Puerto Rico. El servicio comenzó el miércoles cuando cuatro aviones despegaron de Miami y uno salió de San Juan, contándose entre los pasajeros que partieron de Miami a Amelia Earhart, el subsecretario de Comercio para Aeronáutica William P. McCracken Jr., el señor y la señora James Warner Bellah, el director general de Correos Harry S. New, el segundo subdirector general de Correos W. Irving Glover y el alcalde E. G. Sewell.

records.summary_en: The Indianapolis Times reports that Dominican General Gregorio Urbano Gilbert is among the revolutionary generals from Sandino's forces currently interned. According to the account, Gilbert fought against American forces at Santo Domingo in 1916, killed two American officers in San Pedro Macoris, Dominican Republic, and escaped after being captured and sentenced to death before traveling to Central America to join Sandino's forces. He is now reported to be in ill health and suffering from several wounds.

Se informa que ahora se encuentra delicado de salud y sufre de varias heridas.

records.headline: In a book review of Sumner Welles's study of the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: In a book review of Sumner Welles's study of the Dominican Republic, the Evening Star notes that Welles examines the country's turbulent history and political instability with painstaking detail, evaluating both fine and self-seeking Dominican leaders. The reviewer observes that external covetousness has repeatedly troubled the nation, culminating in the intervention of the United States, which the review compares to a Puritan "righteous Ahab" seeking to direct "Naboth" for his own good.
records.summary_es: En una reseña del estudio de Sumner Welles sobre la República Dominicana, el Evening Star señala que Welles examina con minucioso detalle la turbulenta historia y la inestabilidad política del país, evaluando tanto a los líderes dominicanos íntegros como a los interesados. El reseñador observa que la codicia externa ha perturbado repetidamente a la nación, culminando en la intervención de Estados Unidos, a la que la reseña compara con un «Acab justo» puritano que busca dirigir a «Nabot» por su propio bien.

records.summary_en: The Milwaukee Leader reports that former United States Vice President Dawes sailed the previous day aboard the Porto Rican Line steamship Coamo with 10 other members of his commission to revise the finances of the Dominican Republic. Hablando con confianza ante los periodistas sobre poner en orden las finanzas nacionales de Santo Domingo lo antes posible, Dawes explicó que la misión viajaba por invitación del presidente Vasquez para hacer recomendaciones sobre la instauración de un sistema presupuestario.

records.headline: Former Vice President General Charles G. Dawes arrived that morning
records.summary_en: Former Vice President General Charles G. Dawes arrived that morning en route to Santo Domingo with his committee of American financiers and budget experts to study the country's finances at the invitation of President Vasquez, an Associated Press dispatch from San Juan, Porto Rico, dated April 1 reports. During his stop in San Juan, Dawes visited Governor Towner and went to El Morro to review the 65th Infantry on its twenty-ninth anniversary. The party of 20 experts is due in Santo Domingo the following day, and Dawes stated before leaving New York that his mission to recommend a budget system would have nothing to do with the internal or foreign policy of the Dominican Republic.
records.summary_es: El exvicepresidente, general Charles G. Dawes, llegó esa mañana rumbo a Santo Domingo con su comité de financieros y expertos presupuestarios estadounidenses para estudiar las finanzas del país por invitación del presidente Vasquez, según un despacho de Associated Press desde San Juan, Puerto Rico, fechado el 1 de abril. Durante su escala en San Juan, Dawes visitó al gobernador Towner y acudió a El Morro para pasar revista al 65.º Regimiento de Infantería en su vigésimo noveno aniversario. La comitiva de 20 expertos debe llegar a Santo Domingo al día siguiente, y Dawes declaró antes de salir de Nueva York que su misión para recomendar un sistema presupuestario no tendría nada que ver con la política interna o exterior de la República Dominicana.

records.headline: The former vice president, who is himself a big Chicago banker
records.summary_en: The *Daily Worker* criticized former Vice President Charles G. Dawes's financial mission to Santo Domingo, characterizing it as an imperialist survey designed to secure additional American loans and control. The article noted that Dominican customs had been managed by the United States for twenty-five years to service twenty million dollars in debt, while predicting growing popular resistance against foreign financial dominance across Latin America.
records.summary_es: El *Daily Worker* criticó la misión financiera del exvicepresidente Charles G. Dawes en Santo Domingo, calificándola de estudio imperialista ideado para afianzar nuevos préstamos y un mayor control estadounidense. El artículo remarcó que las aduanas dominicanas habían sido administradas por Estados Unidos durante veinticinco años para solventar una deuda de veinte millones de dólares, al tiempo que vaticinaba una creciente resistencia popular contra la hegemonía financiera extranjera en América Latina.
records.passage: the former vice president, who is himself a big Chicago banker with a shady past, especially in the Lorimer scandal, may simply be conducting a survey to determine what further could profitably be taken under American control as security for another loan. The collection of Dominican customs revenues has already been under the control of the United States government for the past 25 years, to provide interest for the repayment of $20,000,000 rolled up in loans already extended to governments, most of which have been set up by the Wall Street-Washington regime as its pet puppets. After Lindbergh and Hoover, Dawes comes to the West Indies and Latin America to cash in on the "good will" tours of aviators and presidents. The chains of great finance, properly adjusted according to the Dawes method, are expected to make the American semi-colonials easier victims of the Yankee imperialist pickpockets. But there are many indications, as in Santo Domingo at the present time, also Nicaragua, that the workers and peasants of Latin America intend having something to say about this enslaving program of the dollar financial experts. records.summary_en: According to an article in the Evening Star, critics across several Latin American nations suspected that General Dawes's mission of American experts to the Dominican Republic concealed a political motive or a scheme for an international financial combination to tighten American economic control in the Caribbean. Upon arriving in the Dominican Republic, Dawes's first task was to counter propaganda from opposition newspapers, which claimed he had come to Santo Domingo to arrange a large American loan that would threaten the country's economic condition and political liberty.

Al llegar a la República Dominicana, la primera tarea de Dawes fue contrarrestar la propaganda de los periódicos opositores al gobierno, los cuales afirmaban que había ido a Santo Domingo para gestionar un gran préstamo estadounidense que pondría en peligro la situación económica del país y la libertad política de su pueblo.

records.headline: Dominican political parties and the public view the new budgeting
records.summary_en: Dominican political parties and the public view the new budgeting system outlined by General Charles G. Dawes and his commission of private experts as an improvement to the republic's financial methods, the Associated Press notes, reporting from Santo Domingo City on April 29. President Vasquez has received congratulations from across the island for inviting Dawes and his colleagues to examine state finances, and the Dominican government has already submitted several bills to Congress in line with the plan.
records.summary_es: Los partidos políticos y el público dominicano consideran que el nuevo sistema presupuestario trazado por el general Charles G. Dawes y su comisión de expertos privados mejora los métodos financieros de la república, según señala la Associated Press en un despacho desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo fechado el 29 de abril. El presidente Vasquez ha recibido felicitaciones de todas partes de la isla por su iniciativa de invitar a Dawes y a sus colegas a estudiar las finanzas estatales, y el gobierno dominicano ya ha sometido al Congreso varias leyes de acuerdo con el plan.

records.headline: A feature in the New Britain Herald describes the geography
records.summary_en: A feature in the New Britain Herald describes the geography and economy of the Dominican Republic, highlighting the Royal Plain, Samana Bay—which the United States once considered leasing as a West Indies naval base instead of Guantanamo Bay—and the arterial highway system begun during the United States administration from 1916, including a road linking Port au Prince, Haiti, with Santo Domingo City. The article notes that sugar is the leading crop, with last year's production bought heavily by England, Canada, and Germany, followed by cacao, yucca, corn, bananas, guavas, and coffee. It also describes a colony of emancipated American slaves established by a Florida planter on the Samana Peninsula where descendants have preserved a southern American English dialect.
records.summary_es: Un reportaje en el New Britain Herald describe la geografía y la economía de la República Dominicana, destacando la Vega Real, la bahía de Samaná —que los Estados Unidos consideraron arrendar en una ocasión como base naval en las Antillas en lugar de la bahía de Guantánamo— y la red de carreteras principales iniciada durante la administración estadounidense desde 1916, incluida una vía que conecta Puerto Príncipe, Haití, con la ciudad de Santo Domingo. El artículo señala que el azúcar es el cultivo principal, cuya cosecha del año anterior fue comprada en gran volumen por Inglaterra, Canadá y Alemania, seguido por el cacao, la yuca, el maíz, el guineo, la guayaba y el café. También describe una colonia de esclavos estadounidenses emancipados establecida por un hacendado de Florida en la península de Samaná, cuyos descendientes han conservado un dialecto del inglés del sur de los Estados Unidos.

records.headline: Dominican Minister to the United States Angel Morales confirmed
records.summary_en: Dominican Minister to the United States Angel Morales confirmed that the Dominican Republic has purchased a lot on the north side of Massachusetts Avenue between Twenty-fourth and California streets in Washington to build a legation costing approximately $150,000. The site, measuring about 100 feet in frontage and 125 feet in depth, was acquired from Mrs. Elizabeth Van R. Frazer through the office of Mayo Wright, just west of the home of Dr. Stanley M. and Mrs. Mary Roberts Rinehart. Architectural plans are to be drawn shortly, with construction scheduled to begin the following year.

El terreno, con unos 100 pies de frente y 125 pies de fondo, fue comprado a la señora Elizabeth Van R. Frazer por intermedio de la oficina de Mayo Wright, justo al oeste de la residencia del doctor Stanley M. y la señora Mary Roberts Rinehart. Los planos de la estructura se trazarán en breve y se prevé iniciar la construcción el año próximo.
