records.summary_en: The *South Bend News-Times* criticized U.S. High Commissioner General John H. Russell's pervasive authority in Haiti, citing the barring of Senator William H. King by President Borno. The piece argued that Russell tolerated the suppression of free speech and judicial independence while Borno expanded his executive powers. It noted that the dissolution of the Haitian legislature by U.S. Marines had eliminated representative checks on the commissioner's governance.
records.summary_es: El *South Bend News-Times* criticó la autoridad desmedida del alto comisionado estadounidense, general John H. Russell, en Haití, citando la prohibición de entrada al senador William H. King por parte del presidente Borno. El artículo sostuvo que Russell toleró la supresión de la libertad de expresión y de la independencia judicial mientras Borno acrecentaba sus prerrogativas ejecutivas. Destacó que la disolución del poder legislativo haitiano a manos de los infantes de marina estadounidenses había eliminado todo contrapeso representativo sobre la gestión del comisionado.
records.passage: What appeared to be a demonstration of Russell's power was given last year when Senator King of Utah, who had criticized American occupation of Haiti, was barred from visiting the country by President Borno. While it could not be shown that Russell had [illegible] inspired the ban, few failed to concede that a word from him to Borno would promptly have averted this affront to an American Senator. With the benign [illegible] tacit approval of Russell, free press and free speech in Haiti have been pretty generally suppressed and Borno has jammed through laws extending his titular dictatorship and effecting his domination of the Haitian courts, which we did not take over under the treaty. American marines long ago dissolved the Haitian congress, so Russell hasn't a representative legislative body to contend with as has our governor general in the Philippines.

records.summary_en: An article in The Daily Worker states that the Dominican Company acquired the water systems of Santiago and the electric system of San Pedro de Macoris, alongside foreign operation of the electric system in Puerto Plata. The writer criticizes President Vasquez for implementing the Dawes report's recommendation to create a new Department of War and Marine under the title of National Defense, alleging it is designed to maintain an American marine base and military forces in Santo Domingo at the expense of workers and peasants. The piece further asserts that Haitian peasants impoverished under the American occupation of Haiti are brought into the Dominican Republic to work for lower wages, and accuses American imperialism of instigating racial antagonism between Dominican mestizos and Black Haitians to divide workers.

El autor critica al presidente Vasquez por aplicar la recomendación del informe Dawes de crear un nuevo Departamento de Guerra y Marina bajo el título de Defensa Nacional, alegando que su propósito es mantener una base de infantería de marina y fuerzas militares estadounidenses en Santo Domingo a expensas de los obreros y campesinos. records.headline: Secretary of the Navy Adams awarded a cross the previous day
records.summary_en: Secretary of the Navy Adams awarded a cross the previous day to Marine Corps Lieutenant Colonel Thomas C. Turner, stationed in Washington, and First Lieutenant Hayne D. Boyden, stationed at Quantico, Virginia. Turner received the decoration for his 1921 round-trip flight between Washington and Santo Domingo City, Dominican Republic, which the citation described as the longest flight in a land plane over land and water ever completed by a naval aviator at that time.

Turner recibió la condecoración por su vuelo de ida y vuelta en 1921 entre Washington y la ciudad de Santo Domingo, República Dominicana, el cual la citación describió como el vuelo más largo en un avión terrestre sobre tierra y agua jamás realizado por un aviador naval en aquel entonces.

records.headline: Lindbergh and his party will begin the flight in a Fokker 10
records.summary_en: Lindbergh and his party will begin the flight in a Fokker 10 powered by three Wasp motors, carrying capacity for 12 passengers and a crew of four, the South Bend News-Times notes, reporting on the official opening of air mail service between the United States and Dutch Guiana. The 1,500-mile route passes through Haiti, the Dominican Republic, and Porto Rico, with scheduled stops at Havana, Camaguey, Santiago, Port-Au-Prince, Santo Domingo, and San Juan, where the party will transfer to a Sikorsky amphibian transport to continue to Trinidad and Paramaribo.
records.summary_es: Lindbergh y su comitiva iniciarán el vuelo en un avión Fokker 10 impulsado por tres motores Wasp, con capacidad para 12 pasajeros y una tripulación de cuatro personas, según señala el South Bend News-Times al informar sobre la inauguración oficial del servicio de correo aéreo entre los Estados Unidos y la Guayana Neerlandesa. La ruta de 1,500 millas atraviesa Haití, la República Dominicana y Puerto Rico, con escalas previstas en La Habana, Camagüey, Santiago, Puerto Príncipe, Santo Domingo y San Juan, donde el grupo cambiará a un transporte anfibio Sikorsky para continuar hacia Trinidad y Paramaribo.

records.headline: An Evening Star dispatch outlines the next day's approximately
records.summary_en: An Evening Star dispatch outlines the next day's approximately 700-mile flight leg from Santiago to San Juan, which includes intermediate stops at Port Au Prince, Haiti, and San Domingo. Most of the journey will be overland except for water crossings over the Windward Passage between Cuba and Haiti and the Mona Passage between the Dominican Republic and Porto Rico. Aboard the plane alongside Colonel and Mrs. Lindbergh and Mr. Curtiss are Pan-American Company President Juan T. Trippe and Mrs. Trippe, co-pilot Ed Musick, radio operator G. N. Angus, and news and newsreel correspondents T. R. Gill, Sylvester MacDowell, and Charles D. Beeland.

La mayor parte del trayecto será sobre tierra, salvo los cruces marítimos sobre el Paso de los Vientos entre Cuba y Haití y el Canal de la Mona entre la República Dominicana y Puerto Rico. A bordo del avión, junto al coronel y la señora Lindbergh y el señor Curtiss, viajan el presidente de la Pan-American Company, Juan T. records.headline: An Associated Press radio dispatch from Port au Prince, Haiti
records.summary_en: An Associated Press radio dispatch from Port au Prince, Haiti, on September 21 reports that Colonel Charles A. Lindbergh, accompanied by his wife on a flight to South America, landed in the Haitian capital at 9:30 a.m. after departing Santiago de Cuba at 6:56 a.m. After covering the 270 miles in 2 hours 34 minutes—26 minutes faster than estimated—Lindbergh planned to stop for an hour before departing for Santo Domingo, capital of the Dominican Republic, where he was expected shortly after noon. From Santo Domingo, the party is scheduled to reach San Juan at 4 o'clock in the afternoon before continuing on Sunday in an amphibian plane to Paramaribo, Dutch Guiana.
records.summary_es: Un despacho radial de la Associated Press desde Puerto Príncipe, Haití, fechado el 21 de septiembre, informa que el coronel Charles A. Lindbergh, acompañado por su esposa en un vuelo hacia Sudamérica, aterrizó en la capital haitiana a las 9:30 de la mañana tras despegar de Santiago de Cuba a las 6:56 de la mañana. Tras recorrer las 270 millas en 2 horas y 34 minutos —26 minutos menos de lo estimado—, Lindbergh planeaba detenerse una hora antes de partir hacia Santo Domingo, capital de la República Dominicana, adonde se esperaba que llegara poco después del mediodía. Desde Santo Domingo, la comitiva tiene previsto arribar a San Juan a las 4 de la tarde antes de continuar el domingo en un avión anfibio hacia Paramaribo, Guayana Neerlandesa.

records.headline: Describing the aerial journey from Port Au Prince, Haiti, across
records.summary_en: Describing the aerial journey from Port Au Prince, Haiti, across the Dominican Republic and the northern shore of Porto Rico, an article in the Evening Star recounts the scenery observed by the Lindbergh party from an altitude of 1,500 feet. After flying over mountainous terrain in the Republic of Haiti and sighting a sunken salt lake 225 feet below sea level, the passengers saw numerous wild horses in the countryside as the plane crossed the Dominican Republic toward Santo Domingo. Along the Dominican coastline, waves crashing against limestone rock fissures sent up geyser-like spouts of water.

records.headline: An article in The Ely Miner reports that the nations of the Americas
records.summary_en: An article in The Ely Miner reports that the nations of the Americas are cooperating under the auspices of the Pan-American Union to erect a four-million-dollar memorial lighthouse for sea and air navigators in the capital of Santo Domingo in honor of Christopher Columbus. The Dominican Republic has set aside 2,500 acres of waterfront land for a Pan-American park and appropriated funds for its share of the memorial, while appropriation bills have also been introduced in the United States, Cuba, and other Latin American countries. With financing in an advanced stage, the next step will be an international architectural competition to select a design.
records.summary_es: Un artículo en The Ely Miner informa que las naciones de las Américas cooperan bajo los auspicios de la Unión Panamericana para erigir un faro monumental de cuatro millones de dólares para navegantes marítimos y aéreos en la capital de Santo Domingo en honor a Cristóbal Colón. La República Dominicana ha reservado un terreno costero de 2,500 acres para un parque panamericano y ha asignado fondos para cubrir su parte del monumento, mientras que también se han presentado proyectos de ley de asignación presupuestaria en los Estados Unidos, Cuba y otros países latinoamericanos. Con el financiamiento en una etapa avanzada, el próximo paso será un concurso arquitectónico internacional para elegir el diseño.

BOLIVIA APPROVES YOUNG AS ENVOY Minister to Dominican Republic to Succeed David Kaufman at La Paz.

By the Associated Press. LA PAZ, Bolivia, November 26.—The Bolivian government has declared Evan E. Young persona grata as United States Minister to Bolivia, to succeed David E. Kaufman, resigned. Mr. Young now is Minister to Santo Domingo.

Mr. Young was born at Kenton, Ohio, and took his law degree at the University of Wisconsin in 1903. He practiced law at Sioux Falls, S. Dak., until he became American consul at Harput, Turkey, in 1905. He was Minister to Ecuador in 1911 and 1912 and American commissioner to the Baltic Provinces of Russia in 1920 and 1922. He also had filled many positions with the State Department in Washington before becoming Minister to the Dominican Republic in 1925.

records.summary_en: The *Indianapolis Times* summarized historical relations between the United States and the Dominican Republic, recalling President Grant's rejected annexation treaty and the 1906 financial commission that halved unjustified foreign debt. It stated that persistent revolutionary turmoil led to the 1916 U.S. military intervention and administrative reforms in finance, schooling, and transportation. The account noted that American military forces completed their withdrawal in July 1924 after restoring stability.

Declaró que los recurrentes conflictos revolucionarios motivaron la intervención militar estadounidense de 1916 y reformas administrativas en finanzas, educación y transportes. La reseña destacó que las fuerzas militares estadounidenses concluyeron su retirada en julio de 1924 tras restablecer la estabilidad.

records.summary_en: The *New Britain Herald* reported that 275 U.S. Marines were ordered from Quantico to Haiti following dispatches from High Commissioner John H. Russell regarding serious unrest in Aux Cayes. The reinforcements were sent to augment the 700 marines already stationed in the country, which shares an island with the Dominican Republic. The report recalled that American military forces had originally landed in Haiti in July 1915. The marines had landed in July 1915, one hundred hours after President Sam was dragged from the French legation by a mob and literally torn to pieces. Under a treaty ratified in 1916, the United States agreed to assist Haiti to establish orderly government; an American high commissioner was appointed, and Arthur C. Millspaugh, the American financial adviser, resigned last spring after an argument with High Commissioner Russell. The present difficulty began with a customs house strike, political elements took advantage of the situation and widened the strike to include industrial and civil employes, and two American customs house officials were injured slightly in disorders at Port-au-Prince. Martial law, already in effect since marines landed, was declared Thursday, and a state of watchful waiting, with quiet enforced by American marines and Haitian guards, prevailed in Port-au-Prince and other towns of the little republic where violence and disorder occurred Wednesday and Thursday.

records.full_text:
'Situation Serious,' Secretary Stimson Comments Frankly

President Sends Message to Congress Revealing Government Recognized Conditions

(Continued from Page 1)

ing the serious political situation developing in Haiti and informing Congress he had ordered dispatch of additional marines to the republic.

Hoover's message was read at the Capitol soon after a dispatch to the State Department announced the clash at Aux Cayes.

In the House it was immediately referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs.

Chairman Stephen G. Porter of the House Foreign Relations Committee said he would prepare a resolution appropriating the $50,000 which Hoover requested for a commission to investigate the Haitian situation.

The House is not organized, however, and Porter is without a committee. This situation can not be remedied before Wednesday and so the resolution can not be taken up until next Friday.

President's Message

President Hoover's message said:

"In my message to Congress of the third insant I indicated my concern as to the future of our policies in Haiti. I stated that we have there about 700 Marines, and that we are confronted with a difficult problem, the solution of which is still obscure. I further stated that if Congress approves I shall dispatch a commission to Haiti to review and study the matter in an endeavor to arrive at some more definite polisy than at present.

"Our representatives in Haiti have shown great ability and devotion, and have accomplished signal results in improvement of the material condition of that people. Yet our experience has revealed more clearly than was seen at first the difficulties of the problem, and the entire situation should be reviewed in the light of this experience.

Emphasize Need

"Since the dispatch of my message disturbances in Haiti emphasize the importance of such an investigation and determination of national policies in the immediate futuer.

"The students at the Agricultural School at Damien went on a strike on Oct. 31st as a protest against a new policy of the Haitian government. The Haitian government had heretofore allotted $10,000 per annum to this school for scholarships, but this year it withheld $2000 of the appropriation in order to make it possible for needy students to perform practical school work on the grounds.

"Sympathetic strikes were subsequently declared in the medical and law schools. President Borno appointed a committee of Haitians to inquire into the matter and it seemed probable at the time that recommendations presented by this committee and accepted by the authorities would adjust the difficulty. Unfortunately, advantage was taken of the situation by various agencies to foment disturbances against the Haitian administration, and on Dec. 3 the American High Commissioner reported that the strike movement had spread thruout the country and that it was feared that the Haitian employes of the departments under American treaty officials might become involved.

Abandoned Work

"On Dec. 4 customs house employes at Port Au Prince abandoned their work in a disorderly manner and crowds have gathered in Port Au Prince. At the same time there were reported demonstrations by crowds at Cape Haitian in sympathy with the disturbance in Port Au Prince. The American High Commissioner reported that on the morning of Dec. 4 it was feared that disorderly conditions would arise at Aux Cayes and similar disturbances were possible at other places.

"The High Commissioner has asked that additional Marines be in readiness to make sure that if the situation becomes serious American lives will be protected, and the force he has suggested has been ordered dispatched for that purpose.

"I feel that it is most desirable that the commission mentioned in my message of Dec. 3 be constituted and sent to Haiti without delay and I, therefore, request the Congress to authorize the immediate sending of such a commission and to appropriate for this purpose $50,000. It is my intention to include one or two members from each House of Congress on this commission."

273 Marines, 4 Officers

Now at Hampton Roads

A company of 273 Marines and four officers was to arrive at Hampton Roads, Va., early today from the Marine base at Quantico, to await further orders from the President.

The order for movement of troops last night came after Brig. Gen. John H. Russell, American high commissioner, had informed Secretary Stimson of the grave situation at Aux Cayes, a coffee port, where 25 Americans reside.

3000 White Foreigners

There are about 3000 white foreigners in the republic which shares an island with the Dominican republic. Marines landed in Haiti July 26, 1915, two hours after President Sam was dragged from the French legation by a mob and literally torn to pieces. The funeral of 200 political prisoners who had been massacred had just ended when Sam was lynched.

Agreed to Aid Government

Under a treaty ratified in 1926 the U. S. agreed to assist Haiti establish orderly government. An American commissioner was appointed and an American financial adviser. Arthur C. Millspaugh, financial advisor, resigned last spring after an argument with High Commissioner Russel. The State Department has refused to reveal the source of the disagreement.

Martial law, technically in effect since Marines landed in 1915, was invoked and, altho Russel feared spread of the disturbance, he reported the invocation had an excellent effect.

records.summary_en: The *Milwaukee Leader* reported that President Hoover ordered 500 marines to Haiti after widespread unrest and strikes led to martial law in Port-au-Prince. The disturbance was reportedly triggered when an American customs collector struck a Haitian employee, while High Commissioner Russell warned of dangerous unrest in Aux Cayes. The incoming troops were deployed to protect foreign residents and reinforce the 700 marines stationed in the republic, which shares an island with the Dominican Republic. President Hoover sent a special message to Congress explaining the serious political situation developing in Haiti and informing Congress he had ordered dispatch of additional marines to the republic. Just before the message was sent to the Capitol, Secretary of State Stimson announced a contingent of 500 marines will sail from Hampton Roads today. Mr. Hoover's message was read at the Capitol soon after a dispatch to the State Department announced death of five Haitians and wounding of several others in a clash with marines at Aux Cayes, a coffee port; the message was read to the House shortly after the start of its session at noon and was immediately referred to the committee on foreign affairs. The president asked authority for appointment of a commission to go to Haiti without delay and requested appropriation of $50,000 for that purpose; he said he would include members of both houses of Congress on the commission.
records.summary_es: El *Milwaukee Leader* informó que el presidente Hoover ordenó el envío de 500 infantes de marina a Haití después de que huelgas y desórdenes generalizados motivaran la declaración de la ley marcial en Puerto Príncipe. Según trascendió, el conflicto se originó cuando un recaudador aduanero estadounidense agredió a un empleado haitiano, al tiempo que el alto comisionado Russell alertaba sobre peligrosas protestas en Los Cayos (Aux Cayes). Las tropas recién despachadas fueron asignadas a resguardar a los residentes extranjeros y reforzar a los 700 marines acantonados en la república, que comparte la isla con la República Dominicana. El presidente Hoover envió un mensaje especial al Congreso explicando la grave situación política que se desarrollaba en Haití e informando al Congreso de que había ordenado el envío de más marines a la república. Justo antes de que el mensaje fuera enviado al Capitolio, el secretario de Estado Stimson anunció que un contingente de 500 marines zarparía hoy desde Hampton Roads. El mensaje del señor Hoover fue leído en el Capitolio poco después de que un despacho al Departamento de Estado anunciara la muerte de cinco haitianos y las heridas de varios más en un choque con marines en Los Cayos (Aux Cayes), un puerto cafetero; el mensaje fue leído en la Cámara poco después del inicio de su sesión al mediodía y fue remitido de inmediato al comité de asuntos exteriores. El presidente pidió autorización para nombrar una comisión que viajara a Haití sin demora y solicitó una asignación de $50,000 para ese fin; dijo que incluiría a miembros de ambas cámaras del Congreso en la comisión.

records.summary_en: The *South Bend News-Times* recalled the 1915 revolution and the mob killing of Haitian President Sam that led to the deployment of U.S. Marines under the Monroe Doctrine. The article contrasted French-speaking Haiti with the Spanish-speaking Dominican Republic, describing both nations on the shared island. It asserted that while marine forces had established order in coastal cities before being reduced to a skeleton force, unrest and voodoo sects persisted in the remote highlands.
records.summary_es: El *South Bend News-Times* rememoró la revolución de 1915 y el linchamiento del presidente haitiano Sam que condujeron al despliegue de los infantes de marina estadounidenses en virtud de la Doctrina Monroe. El artículo contrastó a Haití, de habla francesa, con la República Dominicana, de habla hispana, describiendo a ambas naciones en la isla compartida. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reviewed the history of Hispaniola, detailing how European conflicts partitioned the island into French Saint-Domingue and the Spanish eastern colony that became the Dominican Republic. It described the decimation of the indigenous population, the expansion of plantation slavery, and the revolution that culminated in Haitian independence in 1804. The account asserted that over the following century Haiti experienced chronic political instability and the decay of colonial infrastructure under successive dictators.

records.headline: The history of the Republic of Haiti, as well as the 'empire' and 'kingdom'
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reviewed the political background of Haiti and the establishment of the Dominican Republic on the shared island. The report detailed decades of political turmoil and violent depositions of Haitian executives that led to the 1915 marine intervention following the murder of President Guillaume Sam. It noted that the treaty signed with Haiti went beyond the Dominican agreement by establishing an American-led constabulary and directing urban public sanitation.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* repasó los antecedentes políticos de Haití y el establecimiento de la República Dominicana en la isla compartida. El informe detalló décadas de turbulencia política y violentas deposiciones de mandatarios haitianos que desembocaron en la intervención de los marines en 1915 tras el asesinato del presidente Guillaume Sam. Hizo notar que el tratado firmado con Haití fue más allá del acuerdo dominicano al instaurar un cuerpo policial comandado por oficiales estadounidenses y dirigir el saneamiento público urbano.
records.passage: separated from the Negro republic and established the Dominican Republic. "The history of the Republic of Haiti, as well as the 'empire' and 'kingdom,' has been a series of revolutions, assassinations of rulers and general strife between factions in control of the government and those desiring forcibly to gain control. Of [illegible] rulers of Haiti since its first 'Emperor' Dessalines, only four completed their terms of office. Five were assassinated and most of the others were driven from office and even from the country. After a particularly bloody incident in 1915, when President Guillaume Sam was taken from the French embassy and drawn and quartered in the streets of the capital by an infuriated mob, the United States has occupied the island. A treaty was entered into similar to one with the Dominican Republic, but going further in that it provided for an American-officered constabulary, regulation of matters pertaining to arms and ammunition and the appointment of an American sanitary engineer to recommend methods for cleaning up the cities of the republic. The latter were said by globe trotters to offer a greater affront to human nostrils than any other communities in existence. "The entire island of Haiti, with its two republics, has an area of approximately 28,000 square miles — slightly less than that of Ireland or the State of South Carolina. records.summary_en: According to the Evening Star, Mr. Welles and his wife, formerly Mrs. Peter Goelet Gerry and Miss Mathilde Townsend, spend three to six months each year in a seaside stone residence while he writes a comprehensive study of the Dominican Republic's politics and history. The article describes Santo Domingo as the first permanent city in the New World, noting its modern hotels, good roads, lively harbor, and winter climate. It also highlights the picturesque ruins of the stone mansion built by Diego Columbus, son of the navigator and first governor of the island.

El artículo describe a Santo Domingo como la primera ciudad permanente del Nuevo Mundo, destacando sus hoteles modernos, buenos caminos, animado puerto y clima invernal. También resalta las pintorescas ruinas de la mansión de piedra construida por Diego Colón, hijo del navegante y primer gobernador de la isla.

records.headline: Reports reaching Port-au-Prince from points along the border
records.summary_en: Reports reaching Port-au-Prince from points along the border on February 24 indicated a serious insurrection in the Dominican Republic, with commercial advices stating that insurgents had seized the fort and police stations at Santiago de los Caballeros. The commandant of the Haitian Garde reported that rebels disarmed municipal police and government partisans at Dajabon, while American travelers reported shooting in Santo Domingo that injured three or four persons, and unofficial reports claimed President Horacio Vasquez was in a fort near the capital hoping to take a ship to Jacmel, Haiti. According to information received in Port-au-Prince, the unrest stemmed from dissatisfaction over Vasquez's reported intention to seek re-election, compounded by an economic depression linked to a critical situation in the coffee industry.
records.summary_es: Informes llegados a Puerto Príncipe desde puntos a lo largo de la frontera el 24 de febrero indicaban una grave insurrección en la República Dominicana, con avisos comerciales que señalaban que los insurrectos habían tomado el fuerte y las estaciones de policía en Santiago de los Caballeros. El comandante de la Guardia Haitiana informó que los rebeldes desarmaron a la policía municipal y a los partidarios del gobierno en Dajabón, mientras que viajeros estadounidenses informaron de tiroteos en Santo Domingo con tres o cuatro personas heridas, e informes extraoficiales afirmaban que el presidente Horacio Vasquez se encontraba en un fuerte cerca de la capital esperando tomar un barco hacia Jacmel, Haití. Según la información recibida en Puerto Príncipe, los disturbios se debían al descontento por la supuesta intención de Vasquez de buscar la reelección, agravado por una depresión económica vinculada a una situación crítica en la industria cafetalera.

records.headline: In Santo Domingo, Senora de Vasquez sought refuge in the American legation
records.summary_en: In Santo Domingo, Senora de Vasquez sought refuge in the American legation while President Horacio Vasquez briefly fled to the fortress commanding the capital, though the newspaper La Opinion reported that calm returned late Monday afternoon after a promise of free elections on May 15. The unrest was attributed to Vasquez's intention to seek re-election, and Haitian Minister Leon Lejeans reported to his government that north central Santo Domingo was aflame with the counter-government movement. In Washington, the Associated Press reported no indication that the United States was preparing to send Marines, while Dominican Minister Dr. Angel Morales acknowledged that the reported revolutionary movement was serious but expressed complete faith that Vasquez could handle the situation.
records.summary_es: En Santo Domingo, la señora de Vasquez buscó refugio en la legación estadounidense mientras el presidente Horacio Vasquez huyó por un tiempo a la fortaleza que domina la capital, aunque el periódico La Opinión informó que la calma se restableció a última hora de la tarde del lunes tras la promesa de elecciones libres el 15 de mayo. Los disturbios se atribuyeron a la intención expresada por Vasquez de buscar la reelección, y el ministro haitiano Leon Lejeans informó a su gobierno que el centro-norte de Santo Domingo ardía con el movimiento antigubernamental. En Washington, la Associated Press informó que no había indicios de que el gobierno estadounidense se preparara para enviar infantes de marina, mientras que el ministro dominicano, el Dr. Angel Morales, reconoció que el movimiento revolucionario reportado era grave, pero expresó plena fe en que Vasquez podría controlar la situación.

records.headline: Dominican Rebellion Starts as Hoover Commission Departs
records.summary_en: The *Washington Daily News* reported that an uprising against Dominican President Horacio Vásquez had broken out, leading Señora Vásquez to seek refuge in the American Legation. The paper outlined treaty provisions authorizing a U.S.-appointed general receiver of customs with American protection, and recalled the 1916–1924 marine occupation under Admiral Samuel S. Robinson. The unrest coincided with the departure of the Forbes commission aboard the *Rochester* to investigate conditions in neighboring Haiti.

El diario reseñó las disposiciones del tratado que autorizaban a un receptor general de aduanas designado por Estados Unidos bajo protección norteamericana, y recordó la ocupación de los marines entre 1916 y 1924 bajo el mando del almirante Samuel S. Robison. Los disturbios coincidieron con la partida de la comisión Forbes a bordo del buque *Rochester* para investigar las condiciones en el vecino Haití.

records.full_text:
DOMINICAN REBELLION STARTS AS HOOVER COMMISSION DEPARTS

Haiti Commission Sails From Key West; Marines Available to Put Down Any Disorder

Departure of President Hoover's Haitian commission today from Key West coincided with reports of a rebellion in the Dominican Republic which shares the island of Santo Domingo with Haiti.

The U. S. has assumed responsibilities under the existing Dominican-American treaty which might be made the basis for intervention in the Dominican Republic if disorder persists.

President Hoover said today his reports of revolutionary conditions contained no information that there is any danger to the life or liberty of Americans at the present time.

Marines Ready
Marines are available in Haiti and a force could be dispatched to the other part of the island.

Treaty relations between the U. S. and the Dominican Republic are financial. Article I authorizes the President of the U. S. to appoint a General Receiver of Dominican Customs, and Article II says:

“The government of the U. S. will give to the General Receiver and his assistants such protection as it may find to be requisite for the performance of their duties.”

Natives Killed
The President ordered additional marines to Haiti after disorders last December, but subsequently recalled them. Several natives were killed by the marines. The Haitian Commission, headed by Cameron Forbes, former Governor General of the Philippines, is sailing on the U. S. S. Rochester.

Marines were sent to the Dominican republic in 1916 to quiet a serious uprising. They formed a military government which continued in office until 1924 when Rear Admiral Samuel S. Robinson, military governor turned the government over to the newly elected president, Horacio Vasquez, who still is in office.

Extent Unknown
Reports received by the State Department from Minister Charles B. Curtis indicated rebellion against the Vasquez governments and said Senora Vasquez had sought safety in the American Legation. First reports to the department did not define the origin or extent of the disorder.

Dominican affairs have been tranquil for 10 years. The present treaty relationship with the U. S. began in 1907. Between 1865 and 1904 domestic disorder contributed to the creation of a national debt of $32,000,000, much of which was represented by bonds held in European countries.

Roosevelt Acted
In 1905 there were rumors that several European governments contemplated vigorous action in behalf of the bondholders. President Roosevelt negotiated a treaty which was rejected by the Senate because one clause was interpreted as establishing a protectorate.

Roosevelt then negotiated an executive agreement which was put in force, and subsequently put in treaty form.

records.headline: United Press correspondent Harry W. Frantz reports from Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: United Press correspondent Harry W. Frantz reports from Santo Domingo that an estimated 2,000 ununiformed revolutionary forces armed with rifles entered and occupied the capital at dawn. Although heavy rifle firing broke out in the central plaza in the morning, distant cannon fire was heard, and three government gunners in the northern district were reported killed, the regular army in the capital appeared to submit without resistance as the rebels seized the public works department, the central police station, and other strategic points without attempting to take the fort. Commanding General Jose Estrella, representing the chief rebel leader at Santiago, led the forces into the city, assured United States Minister Curtiss at the American legation that American lives and property would be protected, and stated that he intended to maintain order.
records.summary_es: El corresponsal de la United Press, Harry W. Frantz, informa desde Santo Domingo que unas 2,000 fuerzas revolucionarias sin uniforme y armadas con rifles entraron y ocuparon la capital al amanecer. Aunque se produjeron intensos disparos de rifle en la plaza central por la mañana, se escucharon disparos de cañón a la distancia y se informó de la muerte de tres artilleros del gobierno en el distrito norte, el ejército regular en la capital pareció someterse sin resistencia mientras los rebeldes tomaban el departamento de obras públicas, la estación central de policía y otros puntos estratégicos sin intentar tomar el fuerte. El comandante general Jose Estrella, en representación del líder rebelde principal en Santiago, condujo a las fuerzas hacia la ciudad, aseguró al ministro estadounidense Curtiss en la legación norteamericana que las vidas y propiedades de los ciudadanos estadounidenses serían protegidas, y afirmó que tenía la intención de mantener el orden.

records.headline: In the Dominican Republic, 28-year-old diplomat John M. Cabot of Cambridge
records.summary_en: In the Dominican Republic, 28-year-old diplomat John M. Cabot of Cambridge, Massachusetts, stood between two hostile camps to ask for peace in the name of the United States, while American Minister Charles B. Curtis worked to broker a peaceful settlement. According to a February 25 dispatch from Santo Domingo, insurgents against President Horacio Vasquez's government controlled nearly all of the northern Dominican Republic, where a provisional government backed by the Dominican Guardia—which had disarmed police and government sympathizers—held the region north of the Sierra de Cibao and threatened the capital. The national assembly was scheduled to meet Thursday to consider the situation and the resignation of Vice President Dr. Jose Alfonseca, who stepped down under pressure from the anti-government movement.

Cabot, de Cambridge, Massachusetts, se interpuso entre dos bandos hostiles para pedir la paz en nombre de los Estados Unidos, mientras el ministro estadounidense Charles B. Curtis gestionaba un arreglo pacífico. Según un despacho del 25 de febrero desde Santo Domingo, los insurgentes contra el gobierno del presidente Horacio Vasquez controlaban casi todo el norte de la República Dominicana, donde un gobierno provisional respaldado por la Guardia Dominicana —que había desarmado a la policía y a los simpatizantes del gobierno— dominaba la región al norte de la Sierra de Cibao y amenazaba la capital. Estaba previsto que la asamblea nacional se reuniera el jueves para considerar la situación y la renuncia del vicepresidente, el Dr. Jose Alfonseca, quien dimitió bajo la presión del movimiento antigubernamental.

records.headline: Insurgent forces in Santo Domingo captured the capital's fortress
records.summary_en: Insurgent forces in Santo Domingo captured the capital's fortress and public buildings without bloodshed or loss of life, consolidating their control throughout the Dominican Republic after a revolt that began Sunday when the national guardia in the north revolted and occupied Monte Cristi and other towns. Although the opening fragment notes that President Horacio Vasquez denied he would resign and remained weak from a serious operation in Baltimore the previous December, the main dispatch reports that Vasquez—whose efforts to succeed himself largely prompted the revolt—took refuge in a nearby legation with Vice President Alfonseca, who had offered to resign shortly after the uprising began. The president of the Senate sheltered in the Danish consulate, though he was expected to move to a legation because insurgent leaders did not recognize the right of consulates to grant asylum.

Aunque el fragmento inicial señala que el presidente Horacio Vasquez negó que fuera a renunciar y que seguía débil tras una grave operación en Baltimore en diciembre pasado, el despacho principal informa que Vasquez —cuyos esfuerzos por sucederse a sí mismo provocaron en gran medida la revuelta— se refugió en una legación cercana con el vicepresidente Alfonseca, quien había ofrecido su renuncia poco después de comenzar el levantamiento. El presidente del Senado buscó refugio en el consulado danés, aunque se esperaba que se trasladara a una legación porque los líderes insurgentes no reconocían el derecho de los consulados a ofrecer asilo.

records.headline: President Vasquez, whose efforts to succeed himself in the upcoming
records.summary_en: President Vasquez, whose efforts to succeed himself in the upcoming elections largely sparked the anti-government uprising, took refuge in the French legation alongside Vice President Jose Alfonseca, while the president of the Senate sheltered in the Danish consulate but was expected to move to a legation because insurgent leaders did not recognize consular asylum. The Evening Star notes that today's insurgent operations caused no bloodshed or loss of life, and that while the anti-Vasquez movement held nearly all of the northern republic, American Minister Charles B. Curtis and an emissary worked to broker a peaceful settlement as rebels camped outside Santo Domingo the previous night. The insurgency began the previous Sunday when the National Guardia in the north revolted and occupied Monte Cristi, Concepcion de la Vega, Santiago, and another town, forcing Senora de Vasquez to seek refuge at the American legation on Monday while her husband fled to the capital fortress.

El Evening Star señala que las operaciones insurgentes del día no causaron derramamiento de sangre ni pérdida de vidas, y que mientras el movimiento contra Vasquez controlaba casi todo el norte de la república, el ministro estadounidense Charles B. Curtis y un emisario gestionaban un arreglo pacífico mientras los rebeldes acampaban fuera de Santo Domingo la noche anterior. La insurgencia comenzó el domingo anterior cuando la Guardia Nacional en el norte se sublevó y ocupó Monte Cristi, Concepcion de la Vega, Santiago y otra población, lo que obligó a la señora de Vasquez a buscar refugio en la legación estadounidense el lunes mientras su esposo huía a la fortaleza de la capital.

records.headline: Acting Secretary of State Joseph P. Cotton stated that he did not expect
records.summary_en: Acting Secretary of State Joseph P. Cotton stated that he did not expect the revolutionary forces in the Dominican Republic to overthrow the government. He based his view on official reports from American Minister Charles B. Curtis in Santo Domingo and on the stability shown by Dominican governments in recent years, adding that he hoped the revolutionists had not overthrown anything. Other State Department officials attributed the unrest solely to the presidential election scheduled for the following month.
records.summary_es: El secretario de Estado interino, Joseph P. Cotton, declaró que no esperaba que las fuerzas revolucionarias en la República Dominicana derrocaran al gobierno. Basó su suposición en los informes oficiales del ministro estadounidense Charles B. Curtis en Santo Domingo y en la estabilidad mostrada por los gobiernos dominicanos en los últimos años, añadiendo que esperaba que los revolucionarios no hubieran derrocado nada. Otros funcionarios del Departamento de Estado atribuyeron el malestar únicamente a la proximidad de las elecciones presidenciales previstas para el mes siguiente.

records.headline: Vice-president Jose Dolores Alfon seca announced his resignation, and president Horacio
records.summary_en: The *Daily Worker* reported that Dominican rebels seized Santiago de los Caballeros, Puerto Plata, and La Vega, leading to the resignation of Vice President Alfonseca. The paper charged that President Horacio Vásquez was being kept in power by U.S. Minister Charles B. Curtis and Customs Receiver General William E. Pulliam to protect American financial investments. Curtis reportedly urged Vásquez to reconsider resigning, while the publication denounced the regime as a tool of Wall Street and the National City Bank of New York. The continuation said Curtis urged Vásquez not to resign, to establish active resistance to the rebels, and undoubtedly promised him marine support; a battle between the troops of Vásquez and the revolutionists was threatened 12 miles from the city. John M. Cabot, secretary of the United States legation, was motoring throughout the interior aiding the Vásquez government against the revolutionists. In Washington, President Hoover was considering the matter of sending marines against the Santo Domingan revolutionists; Hoover said he was studying reports from Santo Domingo, but did not state how far he would go in supporting the Wall Street financial dictator, William E. Pulliam. The paper recounted that Horacio Vásquez was elected president during the spring of 1924, with U.S. marine support, that many loans were given Vásquez by the National City Bank of New York, and that the U.S. customs controller was appointed by Coolidge to guarantee the National City Bank loans. The peasants had been losing their land to the American-owned sugar corporations and were forced to work for miserable wages and long hours.

Según los informes, Curtis instó a Vásquez a reconsiderar su renuncia, mientras el rotativo tildaba al régimen de ser un instrumento de Wall Street y del National City Bank of New York. La continuación decía que Curtis instó a Vásquez a no renunciar, a establecer una resistencia activa contra los rebeldes y, sin duda, le prometió apoyo de los marines; una batalla entre las tropas de Vásquez y los revolucionarios se perfilaba a 12 millas de la ciudad. John M. Cabot, secretario de la legación de los Estados Unidos, recorría el interior en automóvil ayudando al gobierno de Vásquez contra los revolucionarios. En Washington, el presidente Hoover consideraba enviar marines contra los revolucionarios dominicanos; Hoover dijo que estudiaba los informes de Santo Domingo, pero no indicó hasta dónde llegaría su apoyo al dictador financiero de Wall Street, William E. Pulliam. El periódico recordaba que Horacio Vásquez fue elegido presidente en la primavera de 1924, con apoyo de los marines estadounidenses, que el National City Bank de Nueva York le concedió muchos préstamos y que el contralor de aduanas estadounidense fue nombrado por Coolidge para garantizar los préstamos del National City Bank. Los campesinos habían ido perdiendo sus tierras a manos de las corporaciones azucareras de propiedad estadounidense y se veían obligados a trabajar por salarios miserables y largas jornadas.

records.headline: A United Press dispatch from Santo Domingo dated February 26
records.summary_en: A United Press dispatch from Santo Domingo dated February 26 reports that an estimated 2,000 ununiformed revolutionary troops armed with rifles entered and occupied the capital at dawn with few casualties, seizing the public works department, the central police station, and other strategic points without attempting to take the fort. General Jose Estrella led the revolutionary army into the city as regular government troops submitted without resistance, and he visited United States Minister Curtiss at the American legation to assure him that American lives and property would be protected. By 9 a.m. the military phase of the revolution appeared complete, with the public accepting the change in government and considering the resignation of President Horacio Vasquez—whose exact whereabouts in the capital were uncertain—to be inevitable.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de la United Press desde Santo Domingo fechado el 26 de febrero informa que unas 2,000 tropas revolucionarias sin uniforme y armadas con rifles entraron y ocuparon la capital al amanecer con pocas bajas, tomando el departamento de obras públicas, la estación central de policía y otros puntos estratégicos sin intentar tomar el fuerte. El general Jose Estrella condujo al ejército revolucionario hacia la ciudad mientras las tropas regulares del gobierno se sometían sin resistencia, y visitó al ministro estadounidense Curtiss en la legación norteamericana para asegurarle que las vidas y propiedades de los ciudadanos estadounidenses serían protegidas. Hacia las 9 a. m. la fase militar de la revolución parecía haberse cumplido con éxito, aceptando el público el cambio de gobierno y considerando inevitable la renuncia del presidente Horacio Vasquez, cuyo paradero exacto en la capital era incierto.

records.headline: According to dispatches sent to the State Department by American Minister Charles B. Curtis
records.summary_en: According to dispatches sent to the State Department by American Minister Charles B. Curtis, revolutionary forces entered Santo Domingo at 5 a.m. accompanied by a brief fusillade lasting under a minute, and moderate quiet prevailed by 7 a.m. Curtis also reported that John M. Cabot, secretary of the American legation at Santo Domingo, had returned to the capital the previous night with the revolutionists' proposals after attempting to bring the opposing factions together, holding out the prospect of an agreement between the insurgents and the Dominican government. The State Department did not make public the agreement. Both the government and the opposition, Curtis said, showed every disposition to respect American lives and property. Acting Secretary of State Cotton and other officials expressed confidence today that intervention by the United States in Santo Domingo would not be necessary to bring order there. Cotton expressed the belief that the Dominican financial situation was excellent and that the plan worked out by Charles G. Dawes just before he went to London as American ambassador was still in effect. Officials attributed the revolt to the approaching elections, with the opposition clamoring for election reforms which would increase their chances of defeating the government candidates.
records.summary_es: Según los despachos enviados al Departamento de Estado por el ministro estadounidense Charles B. Curtis, las fuerzas revolucionarias entraron en Santo Domingo a las 5 a. m. acompañadas de un breve tiroteo que duró menos de un minuto, y para las 7 a. m. prevalecía una calma moderada. Curtis también informó que John M. Cabot, secretario de la legación estadounidense en Santo Domingo, había regresado a la capital la noche anterior con las propuestas de los revolucionarios tras intentar acercar a las facciones opuestas, abriendo la perspectiva de un acuerdo entre los insurgentes y el gobierno dominicano. El Departamento de Estado no hizo público el acuerdo. Tanto el gobierno como la oposición, dijo Curtis, mostraron toda disposición a respetar las vidas y propiedades estadounidenses. El secretario de Estado interino Cotton y otros funcionarios expresaron hoy su confianza en que no sería necesaria la intervención de los Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo para restablecer el orden allí. Cotton expresó su convicción de que la situación financiera dominicana era excelente y de que el plan elaborado por Charles G. Dawes justo antes de marchar a Londres como embajador estadounidense seguía en vigor. Los funcionarios atribuyeron la revuelta a la proximidad de las elecciones, con la oposición reclamando reformas electorales que aumentarían sus posibilidades de derrotar a los candidatos del gobierno.

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo dated February 26
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo dated February 26 reports that revolutionary forces were in complete control of the Dominican capital after entering that morning amid public acclaim, with their commander, General Trujillo, quartered in Ozama fort while President Horacio Vasquez took refuge in the American legation (though the closing line states that the president and Vice President Alfonseca took refuge in the French legation). Predictions indicated that within 24 hours a provisional president would be chosen and a nonpartisan government established to guarantee free voting in the May presidential elections. Meanwhile, American Minister Charles B. Curtis acted as intermediary to seek a bloodless settlement without property damage, and insurgent leaders promised to respect all lives and property, making changes only to the police force while assuring other public employees they would keep their jobs.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de la Associated Press desde Santo Domingo fechado el 26 de febrero informa que las fuerzas revolucionarias tenían el control total de la capital dominicana tras entrar esa mañana en medio de la aclamación popular, con su comandante, el general Trujillo, acuartelado en la fortaleza Ozama mientras el presidente Horacio Vasquez se refugiaba en la legación estadounidense (aunque la línea final señala que el presidente y el vicepresidente Alfonseca se refugiaron en la legación francesa). Se pronosticaba que en un plazo de 24 horas se elegiría a un presidente provisional y se establecería un gobierno no partidista para garantizar elecciones libres en los comicios presidenciales de mayo. Entretanto, el ministro estadounidense Charles B. Curtis actuaba como intermediario para lograr un pacto sin derramamiento de sangre ni daños a la propiedad, y los líderes insurgentes prometieron respetar todas las vidas y propiedades, realizando cambios únicamente en la fuerza policial mientras aseguraban a los demás empleados públicos que no perderían sus puestos.

records.summary_en: The *Daily Worker* reported that Dominican President Vásquez offered to repeal electoral amendments extending his term from four to six years as rebel forces over 1,000 strong advanced from the interior. The article stated that public rebellion was fueled by fears that Vásquez would maintain power with U.S. support, alongside severe poverty caused by falling sugar and tobacco prices. It also reported that Vásquez remained in frequent consultation with the American minister regarding marine backing.
records.summary_es: El *Daily Worker* informó que el presidente dominicano Vásquez ofreció derogar las enmiendas electorales que prolongaban su mandato de cuatro a seis años mientras fuerzas rebeldes de más de 1 000 hombres avanzaban desde el interior. El artículo indicó que el descontento popular estuvo avivado por el temor de que Vásquez se perpetuara en el poder con apoyo de Estados Unidos, unido a la extrema miseria provocada por la caída de los precios del azúcar y del tabaco. Reportó además que Vásquez celebraba continuas consultas con el ministro estadounidense en relación con un posible respaldo de la infantería de marina.

records.summary_en: A February 27 dispatch reports that with Santo Domingo and most of the country in insurgent hands, leading figures from both the insurgency and the government gathered in the capital to reach an agreement. President Horacio Vasquez, whose resignation the insurgents demanded, summoned a national assembly to present a presidential message and invited diplomats and consuls in Santo Domingo to attend. Overnight, insurgent chiefs General Rafael Estrella Urena and a co-leader arrived in the capital—held by a force of 2,000 of their followers—while General Trujillo, chief of the government army, withstood a bombardment with a small garrison in Fort Ozama and refused to surrender pending negotiations. American Minister Charles B. Curtis acted as intermediary to seek a pact without bloodshed or property damage, amid predictions that a provisional president and non-partisan government would be set up to ensure free voting in the May 15 presidential election.
records.summary_es: Un despacho del 27 de febrero informa que, con Santo Domingo y la mayor parte del país en manos insurgentes, figuras destacadas tanto de la insurgencia como del gobierno se reunieron en la capital para llegar a un acuerdo. El presidente Horacio Vasquez, cuya renuncia exigían los insurgentes, convocó a una asamblea nacional para presentar un mensaje presidencial e invitó a asistir a los diplomáticos y cónsules en Santo Domingo. Durante la noche, los jefes insurgentes general Rafael Estrella Urena y otro dirigente llegaron a la capital —controlada por una fuerza de 2,000 de sus seguidores—, mientras el general Trujillo, jefe del ejército gubernamental, resistió un bombardeo con una pequeña guarnición en la Fortaleza Ozama y se negó a rendirse en espera de las negociaciones. El ministro estadounidense Charles B. Curtis actuó como intermediario para procurar un pacto sin derramamiento de sangre ni daños a la propiedad, en medio de pronósticos de que se establecería un presidente provisional y un gobierno no partidista para garantizar una votación libre en las elecciones presidenciales del 15 de mayo.

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo dated February 24
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo dated February 24 reports that President Horacio Vasquez was obliged to assume command of soldiers in the capital fortress after disturbances over political differences connected with the forthcoming elections broke out the previous night in three north-central towns, including Santiago and La Vega. While Santo Domingo and most of the republic remained tranquil, the newspaper La Opinion reported that the situation had been calmed that afternoon by the resignation of Vice President Dr. Alfonseca. Soon afterward, the government promised to keep the elections free from political bias, and American Minister Charles B. Curtis offered his services to smooth over difficulties between the government and the opposition.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de la Associated Press desde Santo Domingo fechado el 24 de febrero informa que el presidente Horacio Vasquez se vio obligado a asumir el mando de los soldados en la fortaleza de la capital tras estallar la noche anterior disturbios por diferencias políticas relacionadas con las próximas elecciones en tres poblaciones de la parte norcentral del país, entre ellas Santiago y La Vega. Mientras Santo Domingo y la mayor parte de la república permanecían tranquilos, el periódico La Opinion informó que la situación se había calmado esa tarde con la renuncia del vicepresidente doctor Alfonseca. Poco después, el gobierno prometió mantener las elecciones libres de parcialidad política, y el ministro estadounidense Charles B. Curtis ofreció sus servicios para limar las dificultades entre el gobierno y la oposición.

records.headline: Reporting on the occupation of Santo Domingo by a revolutionary army
records.summary_en: Reporting on the occupation of Santo Domingo by a revolutionary army the previous day, The Milwaukee leader notes that former Santo Domingo lawyer Rafael Estrella Urena, described as "chief of the revolution," arrived overnight from the rebel stronghold at Santiago to take charge of the city and demand satisfaction of insurrectionist grievances. Sporadic firing continued through the night without evident bloodshed, as overall-clad rebel forces and government troops mingled in friendly fashion while approximately 1,000 insurgents occupied strategic points of the capital awaiting a decision on President Horacio Vasquez's political fate. Reinforcements were expected to hasten developments, with Vasquez's resignation and the appointment of a provisional president anticipated, while negotiations between Vasquez and Estrella Urena included rebel demands for electoral law reform and provisions for a general free election.
records.summary_es: Al informar sobre la ocupación de Santo Domingo por un ejército revolucionario el día anterior, The Milwaukee leader señala que el exabogado de Santo Domingo Rafael Estrella Urena, descrito como "jefe de la revolución", llegó durante la noche desde el bastión rebelde de Santiago para hacerse cargo de la ciudad y exigir la satisfacción de los reclamos insurreccionales. Los disparos esporádicos continuaron durante toda la noche sin derramamiento de sangre evidente, mientras las fuerzas rebeldes vestidas con overoles y las tropas gubernamentales se mezclaban amistosamente y aproximadamente 1,000 insurgentes ocupaban puntos estratégicos de la capital en espera de que se decidiera el destino político del presidente Horacio Vasquez. Se esperaba que la llegada de refuerzos acelerara los acontecimientos, anticipándose la renuncia de Vasquez y el nombramiento de un presidente provisional, mientras que las negociaciones entre Vasquez y Estrella Urena incluían demandas rebeldes de reforma de las leyes electorales y disposiciones para una elección general libre.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that insurgent troops occupied Santo Domingo while Army Commander General Trujillo held Fort Ozama before joining peace talks at the American Legation. Rebel leaders Rafael Estrella Ureña and Desiderio Arias demanded constitutional elections on May 15 without Vásquez as a candidate. U.S. Minister Charles B. Curtis stated that Washington would not recognize a de facto regime, prompting discussions to designate Trujillo or Ángel Morales as provisional president upon Vásquez's resignation.

records.headline: The Indianapolis times describes a triangular political drama
records.summary_en: The Indianapolis times describes a triangular political drama in which President Horacio Vasquez, Revolutionary Chief Rafael Estrella Urena, and General Rafael Trujillo of the regular army are wrangling over peace terms. According to the report, Vasquez's resignation is considered a foregone conclusion, and the public believes that General Trujillo, whose neutral attitude in the crisis has commended itself across the country, is a presidential possibility.
records.summary_es: The Indianapolis times describe un drama político triangular en el que el presidente Horacio Vasquez, el jefe revolucionario Rafael Estrella Urena y el general Rafael Trujillo del ejército regular disputan sobre los términos de paz. Según el informe, la renuncia de Vasquez se considera un hecho consumado, y el público cree que el general Trujillo, cuya actitud neutral en la crisis ha sido elogiada en todo el país, es una posibilidad presidencial.

records.summary_en: In a brief February 28 Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo, The Bismarck tribune reports that Rafael Estrella Urena, one of the leading figures in the revolt against President Horacio Vasquez, was designated provisional president that afternoon. No additional details on the political transition are provided in the item.

La nota no ofrece detalles adicionales sobre la transición política.

records.headline: Latest reports declared the revolutionary army was preparing
records.summary_en: Latest reports declared the revolutionary army was preparing to bombard Vasquez's palace if he did not resign, though thus far the revolutionists had been greeted by the regular army headed by General Rafael Trujillo, The daily worker states, reporting on the Dominican uprising. The paper asserts that the petty-bourgeois lawyers and politicians leading the movement are maneuvering for political leadership and using mass discontent to overthrow the Vasquez regime without pressing the demands of the peasants who form the revolutionary army, while claiming that Hoover has already threatened to send marines to Santo Domingo if the revolution assumes a mass character. A second item datelined Santo Domingo, February 27, reports that Rafael Estrella Urena —whom the paper characterizes as a betrayer of the peasant masses—was expected in the capital that day to negotiate with American Minister Curtis after 2,000 revolutionary workers and peasants marched on Santo Domingo amid land deprivation, low wages, and an acute economic crisis.
records.summary_es: Los últimos informes declaraban que el ejército revolucionario se preparaba para bombardear el palacio de Vasquez si este no renunciaba, aunque hasta ese momento los revolucionarios habían sido recibidos por el ejército regular encabezado por el general Rafael Trujillo, según señala The daily worker al informar sobre el levantamiento dominicano. El periódico afirma que los abogados y políticos pequeñoburgueses que encabezan el movimiento maniobran por el liderazgo político y utilizan el descontento de las masas para derrocar al régimen de Vasquez sin impulsar las demandas de los campesinos que integran el ejército revolucionario, al tiempo que sostiene que Hoover ya ha amenazado con enviar infantes de marina a Santo Domingo si la revolución asume un carácter de masas. Una segunda nota fechada en Santo Domingo el 27 de febrero informa que se esperaba ese día en la capital a Rafael Estrella Urena —a quien el diario califica de traidor a las masas campesinas— para negociar con el ministro estadounidense Curtis después de que 2,000 trabajadores y campesinos revolucionarios marcharan sobre Santo Domingo en medio de la privación de tierras, bajos salarios y una aguda crisis económica.

records.headline: A February 27 dispatch from Santo Domingo reports that supporters of President Horacio Vasquez
records.summary_en: A February 27 dispatch from Santo Domingo reports that supporters of President Horacio Vasquez and insurgent leaders who had completed their virtual seizure of power by marching into the capital the previous day discussed the immediate political future of the Dominican Republic. Insurgent leaders met at the American legation with General Rafael Trujillo, loyal commander of the fortress of Ozama, to seek an agreement on choosing a provisional president to guarantee unbiased presidential elections in May. According to the dispatch, Vice President Jose Alfonseca has officially resigned, and the resignation of President Vasquez is virtually taken for granted while awaiting only the selection of a provisional successor.
records.summary_es: Un despacho del 27 de febrero desde Santo Domingo informa que partidarios del presidente Horacio Vasquez y líderes insurgentes que habían completado su virtual toma del poder al marchar hacia la capital el día anterior discutieron el futuro político inmediato de la República Dominicana. Los líderes insurgentes se reunieron en la legación estadounidense con el general Rafael Trujillo, comandante leal de la fortaleza de Ozama, para intentar llegar a un acuerdo sobre la elección de un presidente provisional que garantizara elecciones presidenciales imparciales en mayo. Según el despacho, el vicepresidente Jose Alfonseca ha renunciado oficialmente, y la renuncia del presidente Vasquez se da prácticamente por descontada a la espera únicamente de la elección de un sucesor provisional.

records.headline: American Minister Charles B. Curtis informed the State Department
records.summary_en: American Minister Charles B. Curtis informed the State Department on Thursday that rebels and government authorities had signed an armistice to prevent violence in Santo Domingo, in a February 27 United Press dispatch from Washington. Curtis stated that a basis for settlement had apparently been reached. He added that although there had been some alarming developments in the rebellion, the capital was quiet and only a few incidents of violence had occurred in other towns.
records.summary_es: El ministro estadounidense Charles B. Curtis informó el jueves al Departamento de Estado que los rebeldes y las autoridades gubernamentales habían firmado un armisticio para evitar la violencia en Santo Domingo, en un despacho de la United Press fechado en Washington el 27 de febrero. Curtis indicó que aparentemente se había alcanzado una base para un acuerdo. Añadió que, aunque se habían producido algunos acontecimientos alarmantes en la rebelión, la capital estaba tranquila y solo habían ocurrido unos pocos incidentes de violencia en otras poblaciones.

records.headline: The Milwaukee leader reports that Rafael Estrella Urena had apparently
records.summary_en: The Milwaukee leader reports that Rafael Estrella Urena had apparently counted on the president's physical weakness and a show of force to bring about a rapid "abdication," but the president's stubbornness disrupted plans for an overnight revolution. Meanwhile, 2,500 well-disciplined troops under General Trujillo rested on their arms in an attitude of neutrality, with Trujillo maintaining his "loyalty and patriotism" while permitting the bloodless occupation of the capital "from motives of humanity." A Washington dispatch in the same report notes that American Minister Charles B. Curtis informed the State Department that prospects for a satisfactory adjustment of the Dominican insurrection were encouraging despite the danger of serious disorders in Santo Domingo, confirming that President Vasquez and General Estrella Urena discussed agreement terms at the American legation and noting that Great Britain had ordered the war sloop Wistaria from St. Thomas, Virgin Islands, to Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: The Milwaukee leader informa que Rafael Estrella Urena aparentemente había contado con la debilidad física del presidente y la demostración de fuerza para lograr una rápida "abdicación", pero la obstinación del mandatario frustró los planes de una revolución de la noche a la mañana. Mientras tanto, 2,500 tropas bien disciplinadas bajo el mando del general Trujillo permanecían sobre las armas en una actitud de neutralidad, manteniendo Trujillo su "lealtad y patriotismo" tras haber permitido la ocupación incruenta de la capital "por motivos de humanidad". Un despacho desde Washington en el mismo informe señala que el ministro estadounidense Charles B. Curtis informó al Departamento de Estado que las perspectivas de un arreglo satisfactorio de la insurrección dominicana eran alentadoras a pesar del peligro de graves desórdenes en Santo Domingo, confirmando que el presidente Vasquez y el general Estrella Urena discutieron los términos de un acuerdo en la legación estadounidense y señalando que Gran Bretaña había ordenado a la corbeta de guerra Wistaria dirigirse desde St. Thomas, Islas Vírgenes, a Santo Domingo.

records.headline: A March 1 dispatch from Santo Domingo reports that insurgent
records.summary_en: A March 1 dispatch from Santo Domingo reports that insurgent chief General Rafael Estrella Urena will become provisional president of the Dominican Republic upon the imminent departure of President Vasquez due to "ill health." Yielding peaceably to the six-day-old insurgent movement, Vasquez agreed the previous day to accept the resignations of most of his cabinet and appoint Urena secretary of the interior, from which post he will succeed to the presidency by law once Vasquez leaves the country; immediately afterward, Vasquez asked the national assembly for permission to leave the republic on account of ill health, his physicians having warned that following a recent flight to the United States for a major operation he could not endure the strain much longer. The constitutional arrangement apparently had the approval of American Minister Charles B. Curtis, who had previously told the insurgents the United States would not recognize a de facto regime, and the report notes that Urena is a lawyer who served in the Dominican cabinet as minister of justice and instruction and later as minister to France.
records.summary_es: Un despacho del 1 de marzo desde Santo Domingo informa que el jefe insurgente general Rafael Estrella Urena se convertirá en presidente provisional de la República Dominicana tras la inminente salida del país del presidente Vasquez por motivos de "mala salud". Cediendo pacíficamente al movimiento insurgente de seis días, Vasquez acordó el día anterior aceptar las renuncias de la mayoría de su gabinete y nombrar a Urena secretario de Interior, puesto desde el cual sucederá en la presidencia por ley tan pronto como Vasquez esté fuera del país; inmediatamente después, Vasquez solicitó permiso a la asamblea nacional para abandonar la república por problemas de salud, pues sus médicos le habían advertido que, tras haber tenido que volar recientemente a los Estados Unidos para una operación mayor, no podría soportar por mucho más tiempo la tensión de los últimos días. El arreglo constitucional contaba aparentemente con la aprobación del ministro estadounidense Charles B. Curtis, quien previamente había informado a los insurgentes que el gobierno estadounidense no reconocería un régimen de facto, y el informe señala que Urena es un abogado que ocupó el cargo de ministro de Justicia e Instrucción en el gabinete dominicano y posteriormente fue ministro en Francia.

records.headline: In a United Press dispatch from Santo Domingo, The Washington
records.summary_en: In a United Press dispatch from Santo Domingo, The Washington daily news reports that lawyer and "Supreme Chief of the Revolution" Rafael Estrella Urena became secretary of the interior that day and will ascend to the presidency as soon as President Horacio Vasquez, described as "a weary old man," leaves the country. The appointment concluded three days of conferences between administration leaders and the chieftains of 8,000 peasant soldiers who had been ready to seize the government by force, and Vasquez, a sick man, is expected to leave Santo Domingo within the week after Congress acts on his resignation. With their objective achieved, the revolutionary army began melting away—leaving only a few guards near public buildings while crowds of citizens cheered the departing insurrectionists—and all sides expressed gratification at the bloodless constitutional change, in which fewer than a dozen casualties were reported despite several thousand men having been under arms.
records.summary_es: En un despacho de la United Press desde Santo Domingo, The Washington daily news informa que el abogado y "Jefe Supremo de la Revolución" Rafael Estrella Urena se convirtió ese día en secretario de Interior y ascenderá a la presidencia tan pronto como el presidente Horacio Vasquez, descrito como "un anciano cansado", abandone el país. El nombramiento puso fin a tres días de conferencias entre los líderes de la administración y los jefes de 8,000 soldados campesinos que estaban dispuestos a tomar el gobierno por la fuerza, y se prevé que Vasquez, un hombre enfermo, abandone Santo Domingo en el transcurso de la semana después de que el Congreso actúe sobre su renuncia. Con su propósito cumplido, el ejército revolucionario comenzó a dispersarse —dejando solo unos pocos guardias cerca de los edificios públicos mientras multitudes de ciudadanos vitoreaban a los insurrectos que se retiraban—, y todas las partes expresaron satisfacción por la forma incruenta en que se efectuó el cambio constitucional, en el que se reportaron menos de una docena de bajas a pesar de haber varios miles de hombres sobre las armas.

records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo reports that Rafael Estrella Urena will assume the duties of provisional president of the Dominican Republic while President Horacio Vasquez is out of the country. Vasquez, who is traveling to Puerto Rico, will not return to Santo Domingo until after the May elections. The dispatch explains that Urena's accession follows constitutional procedure, under which Vice President Alfonseca resigned and Urena was appointed secretary of the interior, a post that grants him executive power in the vice president's absence and the right to assume the presidency.

El despacho explica que el ascenso de Urena se realiza de acuerdo con la constitución, en virtud de la cual el vicepresidente Alfonseca renunció y Urena fue nombrado secretario de Interior, un cargo que le otorga el derecho al poder ejecutivo en ausencia del vicepresidente e incluso a asumir la presidencia.

records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* reported that Rafael Estrella Ureña assumed the provisional presidency of the Dominican Republic after negotiating with Fort Ozama commander General Rafael Trujillo. Outgoing President Horacio Vásquez requested legislative permission to travel abroad due to ill health, while Trujillo declined consideration for the presidency. U.S. Minister Charles B. Curtis, who had insisted on constitutional continuity, expressed satisfaction with the arrangement as rebel forces secured political control.

El ministro estadounidense Charles B. Curtis, quien había insistido en mantener la continuidad constitucional, expresó su conformidad con el acuerdo mientras las fuerzas rebeldes consolidaban el control político.

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo dated March 3
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo dated March 3 reports that General Rafael Estrella Urena, leader of the recent insurgency against the Vasquez government and secretary of the interior appointed by the outgoing chief executive, was sworn in as provisional president of the Dominican Republic before the National Assembly in the presence of U.S. Minister Charles B. Curtis and other diplomatic and consular officials. In a brief address that made a favorable impression in political circles, Estrella Urena pledged to uphold the constitution and laws, guarantee free elections in May, and seek the cooperation of the Assembly and all citizens. With quiet prevailing across the country, the new provisional president also requested that Angel Morales, Dominican minister to Washington, withdraw his offered resignation.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de la Associated Press desde Santo Domingo fechado el 3 de marzo informa que el general Rafael Estrella Urena, líder de la reciente insurgencia contra el gobierno de Vasquez y secretario del Interior designado por el jefe ejecutivo saliente, prestó juramento como presidente provisional de la República Dominicana ante la Asamblea Nacional en presencia del ministro estadounidense Charles B. Curtis y otros funcionarios diplomáticos y consulares. En un breve discurso que causó una impresión favorable en los círculos políticos, Estrella Urena prometió respetar la constitución y las leyes, garantizar elecciones libres en mayo y solicitar la cooperación de la Asamblea y de todos los ciudadanos. Mientras reinaba la calma en todo el país, el nuevo presidente provisional también solicitó que Angel Morales, ministro dominicano en Washington, retirara su renuncia presentada.

records.headline: An editorial in The Bismarck tribune remarks that the recent
records.summary_en: An editorial in The Bismarck tribune remarks that the recent revolution in the Dominican Republic appears to have been singularly bloodless, with shots fired only into the air and the residents of Santo Domingo seemingly satisfied with the outcome. Whereas the first signs of such an upheaval once would have brought a U.S. naval squadron and Marines patrolling the capital's streets within 24 hours, the paper observes that Washington has grown more patient and concludes that there is no reason why its current hands-off policy should not continue indefinitely.
records.summary_es: Un editorial en The Bismarck tribune señala que la reciente revolución en la República Dominicana parece haber sido singularmente incruenta, con disparos hechos únicamente al aire y los habitantes de Santo Domingo aparentemente satisfechos con el resultado. Mientras que los primeros indicios de tal revuelta antes habrían atraído un escuadrón naval estadounidense e infantes de marina patrullando las calles de la capital en un plazo de 24 horas, el periódico observa que Washington ha adquirido más paciencia y concluye que no hay razón para que su actual política de no intervención no continúe indefinidamente.
