records.headline: A March 13 dispatch from Santo Domingo profiles General Rafael Estrella
records.summary_en: A March 13 dispatch from Santo Domingo profiles General Rafael Estrella Urena, describing the successor to Horacio Vasquez after a brief and virtually bloodless revolution as scarcely 40 years old and one of the Dominican Republic's foremost orators. Less than two weeks before becoming provisional president, Estrella Urena had agreed to run for the vice presidency on a coalition ticket, and the circumstances that placed him in the presidency now bar him from running for that or any other office in a regular election. In forming his eight-member cabinet, he faced immediate difficulties because at least five of the initial appointees and candidates considered are potential presidential contenders, though only one can be elected in the "free and fair" election he hopes to hold.
records.summary_es: Un despacho del 13 de marzo desde Santo Domingo perfila al general Rafael Estrella Urena, describiendo al sucesor de Horacio Vasquez tras una breve y virtualmente incruenta revolución como un hombre de apenas 40 años y uno de los principales oradores de la República Dominicana. Menos de dos semanas antes de convertirse en presidente provisional, Estrella Urena había acordado postularse a la vicepresidencia en una boleta de coalición, y las circunstancias que lo colocaron en la presidencia le impiden ahora ser candidato a ese o cualquier otro cargo en una elección regular. Al formar su gabinete de ocho miembros, enfrentó dificultades inmediatas porque al menos cinco de los primeros designados y personas consideradas son posibles aspirantes presidenciales, aunque solo uno puede ser elegido en las elecciones «libres y justas» que espera celebrar.

records.headline: The Evening star recounts how young career vice consul Cabot
records.summary_en: The Evening star recounts how young career vice consul Cabot, acting at the direction of U.S. Minister Charles Boyd Curtis, drove a runabout over rough Dominican roads to meet the invading army marching on Santo Domingo and rode back into the capital with the chief insurgent sitting quietly beside him, melting away the trouble. A graduate of Harvard and of Brasenose College, Oxford, who joined the State Department in 1927 and spent about 18 months in Washington, Cabot has ignored stage offers to appear with his battered car. His drive is highly commended at the State Department for bringing a period of law and order to the island and giving its people time to reflect before continuing the revolutionary movement.
records.summary_es: El Evening star relata cómo el joven vicecónsul de carrera Cabot, actuando por instrucciones del ministro estadounidense Charles Boyd Curtis, condujo un automóvil ligero por los caminos poco transitados de las afueras dominicanas para salir al encuentro del ejército invasor que marchaba sobre Santo Domingo y regresó a la capital con el jefe insurgente sentado tranquilamente a su lado, disipando el conflicto. Graduado de Harvard y del Brasenose College de Oxford, que ingresó al Departamento de Estado en 1927 y pasó unos 18 meses en Washington, Cabot ha desestimado ofertas teatrales para presentarse con su maltratado vehículo. Su recorrido es muy elogiado en el Departamento de Estado por traer un período de ley y orden a la isla y dar a su pueblo la oportunidad de reflexionar antes de continuar el movimiento revolucionario.

records.summary_en: Acting on recommendations from Acting Secretary of State Joseph P. Cotton, President Hoover nominated two young U.S. foreign service officers for two-grade promotions in recognition of their courageous efforts to help bring peace between contending factions without bloodshed during the recent uprising in the Dominican Republic. John M. Cabot of Cambridge, Massachusetts, legation secretary at Santo Domingo—whom Cotton noted had been exposed to grave personal danger—was nominated to become a secretary in the diplomatic service, and William A. Bickers of Culpeper, Virginia, consul at Puerto Plata, was nominated to become a class 8 foreign service officer.

records.headline: A society item in the Evening star notes that Massachusetts manufacturer
records.summary_en: A society item in the Evening star notes that Massachusetts manufacturer Godfrey Lowell Cabot and his wife recently sailed for Santo Domingo on a spring visit to their son, Dr. John Moors Cabot, secretary of legation there, who helped quell a budding revolution in the Dominican Republic several weeks earlier with the aid of an old flivver. His parents hope he will visit their summer home in Beverly Farms on the North Shore in August, and the item also recounts the elder Cabot's aviation career and the couple's diplomatic entertaining in Washington and Massachusetts.

Sus padres esperan que él visite su residencia de verano en Beverly Farms, en la Costa Norte, en agosto, y la nota también recuerda la carrera de aviación de Cabot padre y las recepciones diplomáticas ofrecidas por la pareja en Washington y Massachusetts.

records.headline: The Washington daily news reports that the presidential election
records.summary_en: The Washington daily news reports that the presidential election scheduled for that day in the Dominican Republic, following weeks of intensive campaigning, has drawn unusual interest in Washington official and diplomatic circles. International attention was focused on the country's internal politics by the February constitutional revolution that ousted President Horacio Vasquez and brought his political opponent, Rafael Estrella Urena, to the presidency, and reports indicate that the campaign was marked by partisan bitterness and more than the usual pre-election disturbances.
records.summary_es: The Washington daily news informa que la elección presidencial programada para ese día en la República Dominicana, tras semanas de intensa campaña, ha despertado un interés inusual en los círculos oficiales y diplomáticos de Washington. La atención internacional se centró en la política interna del país a raíz de la revolución constitucional de febrero que derrocó al presidente Horacio Vasquez y llevó a la presidencia a su oponente político, Rafael Estrella Urena, y los informes indican que la campaña se libró con amargura partidista y con más disturbios preelectorales de lo habitual.

records.headline: A dispatch datelined Santo Domingo, May 18, reports that the Dominican Republic's presidential
records.summary_en: A dispatch datelined Santo Domingo, May 18, reports that the Dominican Republic's presidential election is proceeding after the appellate court reserved until Saturday its decision on the legality of the new election board appointed the previous week by Provisional President Jacinto Peynado. Because the National Progressive Alliance announced it would not participate, an easy victory is expected for Confederate Party candidates General Rafael Trujillo for president and Estrella Urena for vice president. Following the March revolution that forced President Vasquez to resign, Estrella Urena had become provisional president before resigning to run in the election and being succeeded by Peynado, who named a new election board after the alliance-friendly regular board resigned amid conflicting claims over whether the alliance failed to submit party lists or whether the army was not in garrison as required by law.
records.summary_es: Un despacho fechado en Santo Domingo el 18 de mayo informa que la elección presidencial de la República Dominicana se lleva a cabo después de que la corte de apelaciones reservara hasta el sábado su decisión sobre la legalidad de la nueva junta electoral nombrada la semana anterior por el presidente provisional Jacinto Peynado. Debido a que la Alianza Nacional Progresista anunció que no participaría, se espera una fácil victoria para los candidatos del Partido Confederado, el general Rafael Trujillo para presidente y Estrella Urena para vicepresidente. Tras la revolución de marzo que obligó al presidente Vasquez a renunciar, Estrella Urena había asumido la presidencia provisional antes de dimitir para postularse en los comicios y ser sucedido por Peynado, quien nombró una nueva junta electoral luego de que la junta regular afín a la alianza renunciara en medio de versiones contrapuestas sobre si la alianza no presentó listas partidarias o si el ejército no estaba acuartelado como exige la ley.

records.summary_en: The Evening star reports that pan-American representatives have endorsed the Dominican Republic's claim that Christopher Columbus's remains rest beneath the high altar in the Cathedral of Santo Domingo, and that because Santo Domingo was the first city founded in the New World and the seat of authority delegated to Columbus by Ferdinand and Isabella, the Pan-American Columbus memorial lighthouse was placed in its harbor. Originating at the 1923 Pan-American Congress in Santiago de Chile, the international design competition drew plans from 455 architects across 46 countries, from which an international jury in Madrid last summer selected 10 architects whose worthy designs will be judged for final awards to be announced this summer from Rio de Janeiro.

records.headline: An Evening star report, opening mid-sentence with a reference
records.summary_en: An Evening star report, opening mid-sentence with a reference to intercepted word that Morales and an associate were fomenting a revolution, notes that both Valesquez and Morales withdrew from the electoral contest before balloting began on May 16. Consequently, Army Commander Rafael Trujillo and General Rafael Estrella Urena, the government party candidates, ran unopposed and were elected president and vice president, respectively. Sentries were posted on the streets leading to the American legation, apparently under orders to prevent Morales and fellow Aliancista leader Martin Mora from taking refuge there. Both Valesquez and Mora had held cabinet posts under resigned President Horacio Vasquez, who was forced from office by a movement led by Generals Trujillo and Estrella Urena.

En consecuencia, el comandante del ejército Rafael Trujillo y el general Rafael Estrella Urena, candidatos del partido de gobierno, se presentaron sin oposición y fueron elegidos presidente y vicepresidente, respectivamente. Se apostaron centinelas en las calles que conducen a la legación estadounidense, aparentemente bajo órdenes de impedir que Morales y el también líder aliancista Martin Mora se refugiaran allí. Tanto Valesquez como Mora habían ocupado cargos de gabinete bajo el presidente renunciante Horacio Vasquez, quien fue desplazado del poder por un movimiento encabezado por los generales Trujillo y Estrella Urena.

records.summary_en: According to the Springfield weekly Republican, the Aliancistas hope to have the Dominican election declared illegal by the courts to bring about new balloting, contending that members of the Junta Central Electoral were illegally appointed some time ago. The article recounts that General Trujillo, now 37, began his military career 12 years earlier when United States Marines occupying the Dominican Republic in 1918 took several native young men into their ranks to train as prospective officers for the Dominican army. Many Americans regarded the quiet Trujillo as a 'real buddy' and a 'good soldier,' and by the time the Marines withdrew in 1924 he had risen to major before becoming brigadier-general in command of the Dominican army.

records.headline: Reporting from Santo Domingo, The Milwaukee leader states that Federico
records.summary_en: Reporting from Santo Domingo, The Milwaukee leader states that Federico Velasquez, an unsuccessful presidential candidate on a coalition ticket imprisoned after Friday's election on charges of fomenting a revolution, has nevertheless been offered the treasury portfolio in the cabinet of newly elected President General Rafael Trujillo. Acting President Jacinto B. Peynado advised General Trujillo that appointing Velasquez to the most important cabinet post would help quiet the opposition. Trujillo agreed, and Peynado personally carried the offer to Velasquez.
records.summary_es: Informando desde Santo Domingo, The Milwaukee leader señala que a Federico Velasquez, candidato presidencial derrotado de una boleta de coalición que fue encarcelado tras las elecciones del viernes bajo cargos de fomentar una revolución, se le ha ofrecido no obstante la cartera de Hacienda en el gabinete del recién elegido presidente, el general Rafael Trujillo. El presidente interino Jacinto B. Peynado aconsejó al general Trujillo que nombrar a Velasquez para el cargo más importante del gabinete contribuiría a calmar a la oposición. Trujillo estuvo de acuerdo y el propio Peynado llevó personalmente la oferta a Velasquez.

records.headline: In an Associated Press dispatch from San Domingo dated June
records.summary_en: In an Associated Press dispatch from San Domingo dated June 4, President Urena told the Santo Domingo chamber of commerce that he favored extending the Dominican Republic's debt payments but opposed contracting new loans, warning that a $10,000,000 loan in the United States contracted by a previous administration jeopardized the republic's sovereignty. He urged chamber officers and provincial governors to increase production and negotiate commercial treaties with other countries to secure better markets. Urena added that if revenues became insufficient to meet the country's monthly debt payments, the United States could take over control of the republic under the conventions of 1907 and 1924.
records.summary_es: En un despacho de la Associated Press desde San Domingo fechado el 4 de junio, el presidente Urena manifestó ante la Cámara de Comercio de Santo Domingo que favorecía una prórroga en los pagos de la deuda de la República Dominicana pero se oponía a contratar nuevos préstamos, advirtiendo que un empréstito de $10,000,000 en los Estados Unidos contratado por una administración anterior ponía en peligro la soberanía de la república. Instó a los directivos de la cámara y a los gobernadores provinciales a incrementar la producción y negociar tratados comerciales con otros países para obtener mejores mercados. Urena añadió que si los ingresos resultaran insuficientes para cubrir los pagos mensuales de la deuda del país, los Estados Unidos podrían asumir el control de la república en virtud de las convenciones de 1907 y 1924.

records.headline: The Harlem news describes the itinerary of an aerial expedition
records.summary_en: The Harlem news describes the itinerary of an aerial expedition flying along the Atlantic coast to Miami and Havana and then across the West Indies, with probable landings at Santiago de Cuba, Port-au-Prince, San Pedro de Macoris in the Dominican Republic, San Juan, St. Thomas, St. John's (Antigua), Port Castries (St. Lucia), and Port of Spain, Trinidad. From there the plane is scheduled to stop at Georgetown, Paramaribo, and Cayenne before continuing through Para and numerous Brazilian coastal cities to Montevideo and Buenos Aires. Upon reaching Buenos Aires, the party's photographers will transfer to a smaller high-altitude plane to fly westward to the Andes and make aerial photographs of Mount Aconcagua, which reaches an altitude of 23,080 feet.

records.headline: Commenting on visits by Latin-American presidents-elect to the United States since
records.summary_en: Commenting on visits by Latin-American presidents-elect to the United States since Hoover's return early in 1929 from his Central and South American good will tour, the Douglas daily dispatch notes that Washington has received Enrique Olaya of Colombia, Ortiz Rubio of Mexico, and Julio Prestes of Brazil. The next visitor expected is President-elect Trujillo of the Dominican Republic, though his plans have not been officially announced. The article observes that such visits promote international friendships and commercial relations by allowing incoming leaders to discuss international affairs with officials in Washington and meet bankers and business men in New York, while contrasting the lack of popular excitement in Washington with the receptions given to Hoover's party in Latin-American capitals.
records.summary_es: Al comentar las visitas de presidentes electos latinoamericanos a los Estados Unidos desde el regreso de Hoover a principios de 1929 de su gira de buena voluntad por América Central y del Sur, el Douglas daily dispatch señala que Washington ha recibido a Enrique Olaya de Colombia, Ortiz Rubio de México y Julio Prestes de Brasil. El próximo visitante esperado es el presidente electo Trujillo de la República Dominicana, aunque sus planes no han sido anunciados oficialmente. El artículo observa que tales visitas promueven las amistades internacionales y las relaciones comerciales al permitir a los mandatarios entrantes tratar asuntos internacionales con funcionarios en Washington y reunirse con banqueros y hombres de negocios en Nueva York, a la vez que contrasta la falta de entusiasmo popular en Washington con las recepciones brindadas a la comitiva de Hoover en las capitales latinoamericanas.

records.headline: A special dispatch from Elkhart, Indiana, dated July 15 in the South Bend news-times
records.summary_en: A special dispatch from Elkhart, Indiana, dated July 15 in the South Bend news-times reports that Frederick Elvin Seibert, formerly of Elkhart, was assigned on Monday to the office of vice consul at Puerto Plata, Dominican Republic, according to Washington press dispatches. The article describes Puerto Plata as a northern coast seaport with a population of 10,000 to 15,000 and characterizes it as the second most important metropolis in the 'black republic.' It also notes that Seibert's father, Charles K. Seibert, formerly taught mathematics at Elkhart High School for about 10 years before moving to Omaha, Nebraska, and that the younger Seibert attended West Point for two years before graduating from Columbia University.
records.summary_es: Un despacho especial desde Elkhart, Indiana, fechado el 15 de julio en el South Bend news-times informa que Frederick Elvin Seibert, anteriormente de Elkhart, fue asignado el lunes al cargo de vicecónsul en Puerto Plata, República Dominicana, según despachos de prensa de Washington. El artículo describe a Puerto Plata como un puerto marítimo en la costa norte con una población de entre 10,000 y 15,000 habitantes y lo caracteriza como la segunda metrópoli más importante de la 'república negra'. También señala que el padre de Seibert, Charles K. Seibert, enseñó matemáticas en la escuela secundaria de Elkhart durante unos 10 años antes de trasladarse a Omaha, Nebraska, y que Seibert hijo cursó dos años en West Point antes de graduarse en la Universidad de Columbia.

records.summary_en: A brief filler item in the Brownsville herald states that Santo Domingo, the capital of the Dominican Republic, is the oldest city in the New World settled by Europeans. The same note adds that Panama City, founded by the Spanish in 1519, is the oldest white settlement on the mainland of the Americas.

records.headline: After commanding the Marine Barracks at the Philadelphia navy
records.summary_en: After commanding the Marine Barracks at the Philadelphia navy yard, General Fuller was detached on August 31, 1916, to command the second provisional brigade of Marines in the Dominican Republic, where he assumed command on August 21, 1918, and remained for two years, a biographical sketch in the Evening star recounts. While there, he also served on the staff of the military governor of Santo Domingo as secretary of state, interior, police, war, and navy. On December 14, 1925, he became assistant to the major general commandant at headquarters until the death of Major General Commandant Neville, when he was appointed acting commandant, holding decorations that include the Spanish, Philippine, and China campaign medals, the Expeditionary Ribbon, and the Victory Medal for service in the West Indies.
records.summary_es: Tras comandar el cuartel de infantes de marina en el astillero naval de Filadelfia, el general Fuller fue destacado el 31 de agosto de 1916 para comandar la segunda brigada provisional de infantes de marina en la República Dominicana, donde asumió el mando el 21 de agosto de 1918 y permaneció durante dos años, según relata una reseña biográfica en el Evening star. Durante su estancia allí, también sirvió en el estado mayor del gobernador militar de Santo Domingo como secretario de Estado, Interior, Policía, Guerra y Marina. El 14 de diciembre de 1925 pasó a ser asistente del mayor general comandante en el cuartel general hasta el fallecimiento del mayor general comandante Neville, cuando fue nombrado comandante interino, contando entre sus condecoraciones las medallas de las campañas de España, Filipinas y China, la Cinta Expedicionaria y la Medalla de la Victoria por su servicio en las Antillas.

records.headline: Governor Theodore Roosevelt of Porto Rico, finding 80 per cent of that island's
records.summary_en: Governor Theodore Roosevelt of Porto Rico, finding 80 per cent of that island's population undernourished, sent a representative to study the Dominican Republic as a source of beef supply, resulting in plans to erect a new packing plant in either San Pedro de Macoris or Santo Domingo, an Associated Press dispatch from San Pedro de Macoris reports. Whereas Porto Rico has 1,543,000 inhabitants—or 450 to the square mile—and only 150,000 cattle, two-thirds of which are beasts of burden, the Dominican Republic has scarcely 50 people to the square mile and ample grazing land. Governor Roosevelt believes that increasing the people's meat diet can reduce tuberculosis, rickets, and other ailments of malnutrition.

Mientras que Puerto Rico tiene 1,543,000 habitantes —o 450 por milla cuadrada— y solo 150,000 cabezas de ganado, dos tercios de las cuales son animales de carga, la República Dominicana cuenta con apenas 50 habitantes por milla cuadrada y abundantes tierras de pastoreo. El gobernador Roosevelt considera que incrementar la dieta cárnica de la población puede reducir la tuberculosis, el raquitismo y otras dolencias derivadas de la desnutrición.

records.headline: Following the inauguration of General Trujillo as president of the Dominican
records.summary_en: Following the inauguration of General Trujillo as president of the Dominican Republic, provisional president Rafael Estrella Urena, three years older than Trujillo and head of state since February's "bloodless revolution," became vice president alongside twelve new senators and 33 new deputies. Having risen through February's "youth movement," the new officials set three goals for their four-year term: lowering government expenses, reviving business prosperity, and expanding popular education. United States Minister Charles B. Curtis represented President Hoover at the ceremonies, and the report notes that Trujillo enlisted as a private in 1918 in the Dominican army organized to keep order after the withdrawal of American marines, reaching the rank of major when the occupation ended in 1924.
records.summary_es: Tras la toma de posesión del general Trujillo como presidente de la República Dominicana, el presidente provisional Rafael Estrella Urena, tres años mayor que Trujillo y jefe de Estado desde la "revolución incruenta" de febrero, asumió la vicepresidencia junto con doce nuevos senadores y 33 nuevos diputados. Habiendo ascendido mediante el "movimiento juvenil" de febrero, los nuevos funcionarios fijaron tres metas para su período de cuatro años: reducir los gastos gubernamentales, reactivar la prosperidad comercial y difundir la educación popular. El ministro estadounidense Charles B. Curtis representó al presidente Hoover en las ceremonias, y el informe señala que Trujillo se alistó como soldado raso en 1918 en el ejército dominicano organizado para mantener el orden tras el retiro de los marines estadounidenses, alcanzando el grado de mayor cuando terminó la ocupación en 1924.

records.summary_en: Describing General Trujillo as a farmer's son who began his military career during the 1916 to 1924 United States Marine Corps occupation of the Dominican Republic, the Evening Star reports that his contacts with Americans made him a friend of the United States. According to his statements, one of his first government measures will be seeking the cooperation of American businessmen and experts to address Dominican economic problems, including appointing a mixed commission of three American and three Dominican economists to encourage industrial diversification beyond sugar, coffee, cacao, and tobacco. He also plans to hire American experts to organize technical departments of the administration, and the paper compares him to newly inaugurated Colombian President Olaya Herrera as a pledge of inter-American goodwill.

records.summary_en: Reporting for the United Press from Santo Domingo, correspondent Francisco Escovar states that a Wednesday hurricane destroyed a large part of the Dominican capital, with early authoritative estimates placing the toll at about 300 dead and almost 1,000 injured. Property damage in the city was estimated at more than $15,000,000 and included the destruction of United States Minister Charles B. Curtis's home, while disrupted interior communications prevented officials from determining the island-wide toll. Officials of President Rafael L. Trujillo's administration reported great misery in the capital and called for urgent relief, while authorities also worked to recapture inmates who had escaped when an insane asylum was demolished.

records.headline: In Santo Domingo, the cable company's office was flooded and houses
records.summary_en: In Santo Domingo, the cable company's office was flooded and houses unroofed by the first violent winds were wrecked, while a Pan-American airplane flying over the city reported widespread damage. Radio advices from San Juan, Puerto Rico, reported that the hurricane had previously killed 20 persons on the British island of Dominica before striking the Dominican capital with its greatest force and veering northward over northwestern Haiti toward Cuba and Florida. The report adds that the Dominican Republic, with a population of more than 1,000,000, had not fully recovered from the previous West Indies hurricane and was already facing economic depression and a governmental transition following the February overthrow of General Horacio Vasquez. The revolutionary leader, General Rafael Leonidas Trujillo, was elected president in May. The capital, situated at the mouth of the Ozama River, has many ancient houses although some sections are sturdily built, and its great cathedral, in which the bones of Columbus rested until 1795, is one of the chief structures in the center of the city, the second oldest European city in the New World.

El líder revolucionario, el general Rafael Leonidas Trujillo, fue electo presidente en mayo. La capital, situada en la desembocadura del río Ozama, tiene muchas casas antiguas aunque algunas secciones están sólidamente construidas, y su gran catedral, en la que reposaron los huesos de Colón hasta 1795, es una de las principales construcciones del centro de la ciudad, la segunda ciudad europea más antigua del Nuevo Mundo.

records.summary_en: A dispatch from Miami on September 4 reports that radio communication with Santo Domingo remained broken, raising fears that the Dominican Republic's capital had been devastated by the previous day's hurricane. An earlier wireless message from a ship in the West Indies service provided the first direct word to break the silence surrounding the republic since the storm struck. Pan-American Airways reported that the final radio message from its Santo Domingo station arrived at 3:12 p.m. the previous afternoon, when winds of 186 miles an hour were sweeping the capital.

Un mensaje inalámbrico previo enviado desde un buque del servicio de las Indias Occidentales proporcionó la primera noticia directa en romper el silencio que rodeaba a la república desde el paso de la tormenta. records.headline: The Dominican capital of Santo Domingo was "99 per cent destroyed
records.summary_en: The Dominican capital of Santo Domingo was "99 per cent destroyed" by the tropical hurricane, the New York offices of the All America Cables Company reported on September 4; the city has over 45,000 inhabitants. Because the company's local offices were flooded, employees transmitted the first direct message to New York from an emergency station set up in a beach hut where the cables connected. Meanwhile, a dispatch from San Juan, Puerto Rico, cited Radio Corporation of America reports that at least 300 persons were killed and the capital's wireless station was completely wrecked, according to word from the steamship Lady Hawkins after it returned to port in Santo Domingo.

Entretanto, un despacho desde San Juan, Puerto Rico, citó informes de la Radio Corporation of America según los cuales al menos 300 personas murieron y la estación inalámbrica de la capital quedó completamente destruida, de acuerdo con el reporte del vapor Lady Hawkins tras regresar al puerto de Santo Domingo.

records.headline: While communication with Santo Domingo remained disrupted, weather
records.summary_en: While communication with Santo Domingo remained disrupted, weather conditions were clearing in Haiti on the western half of the island. Incomplete reports indicated considerable damage and the unroofing of houses in Santo Domingo after intense winds struck in the mid-afternoon, moving slightly south of the path of the hurricane that hit Puerto Rico and the Greater Antilles two years earlier. Dispatches from San Juan, Puerto Rico, warned that the storm remained severe at sea, and American Red Cross officials prepared to provide relief to the stricken region if further reports confirmed widespread damage and loss of life. Dominican officials in the United States were greatly concerned, especially in view of the economic depression already existing in the republic. A United Press dispatch from Santo Domingo by staff correspondent Francisco Escovar reported that the hurricane had crossed the island destroying a large part of the capital and killing many persons: the most authoritative early estimates of dead were about 300, with almost 1,000 others injured, and damage to the city, including the destruction of the home of American Minister Charles B. Curtiss, was estimated at more than $15,000,000, with an enormous number of persons homeless and communications with the interior regions disrupted. The All-America Cable Company re-established communication with Santo Domingo and received advices that the city was almost entirely destroyed — a second message said it was “fifty percent destroyed” and that food and medical aid were badly needed — while the United States Weather Bureau reported the storm moving in the direction of northern Cuba and the Florida Straits.

Los funcionarios dominicanos en Estados Unidos estaban muy preocupados, sobre todo en vista de la depresión económica ya existente en la república. Un despacho de la United Press desde Santo Domingo, del corresponsal Francisco Escovar, informó que el huracán había cruzado la isla destruyendo gran parte de la capital y matando a muchas personas: las estimaciones tempranas más autorizadas cifraban los muertos en unos 300, con casi 1,000 heridos, y los daños a la ciudad, incluida la destrucción de la residencia del ministro estadounidense Charles B. records.headline: The hurricane cut a wide swath of destruction across the Dominican
records.summary_en: The hurricane cut a wide swath of destruction across the Dominican Republic, with damage estimated in millions of dollars, a correspondent traveling from Port-au-Prince, Haiti, toward Santo Domingo City reports. After arriving 20 miles south of Azua by automobile and continuing on horseback into the stricken region, the writer observed destroyed roads, downed telegraph wires, and wrecked gardens and country estates. Resulting floods washed out many houses and reportedly forced residents in some places to take refuge on improvised rafts, while the dispatch notes that Azua lies near the southern coast about 55 miles west by south of Santo Domingo City and has a population listed at 1,500.
records.summary_es: El huracán abrió una amplia franja de destrucción a través de la República Dominicana, con daños estimados en millones de dólares, según un corresponsal en ruta desde Puerto Príncipe, Haití, hacia la ciudad de Santo Domingo. Tras llegar en automóvil a 20 millas al sur de Azua y continuar a caballo hacia la región afectada, el autor observó caminos destruidos, cables telegráficos derribados y jardines y fincas rurales arruinados. Las inundaciones resultantes arrasaron numerosas viviendas y, según los informes, obligaron a los residentes de algunos lugares a refugiarse en balsas improvisadas, mientras el despacho señala que Azua se encuentra cerca de la costa sur, a unas 55 millas al oeste-suroeste de la ciudad de Santo Domingo, y cuenta con una población registrada de 1,500 habitantes.

records.headline: The city possesses asphalt pavements, a modern water supply
records.summary_en: The city possesses asphalt pavements, a modern water supply carried from mountains 20 miles away, and rural roads, an account in the Evening Star notes, describing the approach to Santo Domingo by steamer. As a vessel rounds a point jutting into the Caribbean and enters the narrow harbor mouth where the Ozama River empties into the sea, the city rises from coral cliffs toward rolling hills, framed by central mountains to the north and the mountains dividing Haiti and the Dominican Republic. Along the harbor stand a colonial fortress still used as a national military garrison and municipal prison, the palace of the Columbus family with its medieval walls beside the old city wall, and the riverfront docks, customs houses, and intact city gates leading into the commercial quarter.
records.summary_es: La ciudad cuenta con pavimentos de asfalto, un moderno acueducto traído desde montañas a 20 millas de distancia y caminos rurales, según una reseña en el Evening Star, al describir la llegada a Santo Domingo en vapor. Cuando la embarcación dobla una punta que se adentra en el Caribe y entra por la estrecha boca del puerto donde el río Ozama desemboca en el mar, la ciudad se alza desde acantilados de coral hacia colinas onduladas, enmarcada por las montañas centrales al norte y la cordillera que divide a Haití y la República Dominicana. Junto al puerto se levantan una fortaleza colonial aún utilizada como guarnición militar nacional y prisión municipal, el palacio de la familia Colón con sus muros medievales junto a la antigua muralla, y los muelles fluviales, las aduanas y las puertas coloniales intactas que conducen al sector comercial.

records.headline: In a statement issued in Miami at 10:30 a.m. on September 4
records.summary_en: In a statement issued in Miami at 10:30 a.m. on September 4, government meteorologist R. W. Gray reported that the tropical disturbance that crossed the Dominican Republic on Wednesday afternoon with winds far exceeding 100 miles per hour was moving northwestward toward the southern Bahamas. Earlier in the afternoon, Belen Observatory reported that the hurricane was north of Baracoa in Oriente Province, Cuba, with its speed only slightly diminished, while Gray warned that the storm would likely bring strong winds to extreme South Carolina by Friday night if it maintained its course. A companion photo caption notes that Washington Weather Bureau forecasters under Charles L. Mitchell were busy plotting reports from the Caribbean hurricane, above a headline announcing that Santo Domingo City was razed.
records.summary_es: En un comunicado emitido en Miami a las 10:30 de la mañana del 4 de septiembre, el meteorólogo gubernamental R. W. Gray informó que la perturbación tropical que cruzó la República Dominicana el miércoles por la tarde con vientos muy superiores a las 100 millas por hora avanzaba hacia el noroeste en dirección al sur de las Bahamas. Más temprano esa tarde, el Observatorio de Belén informó que el huracán se encontraba al norte de Baracoa, en la provincia de Oriente, Cuba, con una velocidad apenas disminuida, mientras Gray advirtió que la tormenta probablemente causaría fuertes vientos en el extremo de Carolina del Sur el viernes por la noche si mantenía su rumbo. Un pie de foto adjunto señala que los meteorólogos del Negociado del Tiempo en Washington, bajo la dirección de Charles L. Mitchell, trabajaban intensamente trazando los informes del huracán del Caribe, sobre un titular que anunciaba que la ciudad de Santo Domingo había quedado arrasada.

records.headline: Following a hurricane with winds estimated around 150 miles
records.summary_en: Following a hurricane with winds estimated around 150 miles an hour, President Rafael Trujillo took personal charge of relief work in Santo Domingo and called out the entire army. Communications across the Dominican Republic were completely severed, bridges and roads around the capital were wrecked, and the plant of the Associated Press member newspaper La Opinion was destroyed, while three of fifteen occupants perished when an adjoining building collapsed. Soldiers and police recaptured inmates who had fled into the streets from the destroyed lunatic asylum, the districts of Villa Nueva, Duarte, and San Carlos were completely leveled, and officials and newspapers appealed to the American press and United States charities for aid as hunger and robberies began.

Las comunicaciones en toda la República Dominicana quedaron totalmente cortadas, los puentes y caminos alrededor de la capital fueron destruidos y la planta del periódico La Opinion, miembro de la Associated Press, quedó arrasada, mientras que tres de los quince ocupantes de un edificio contiguo perecieron al desplomarse el inmueble. Soldados y policías recapturaron a los internos que habían huido a las calles desde el manicomio destruido, los sectores de Villa Nueva, Duarte y San Carlos quedaron completamente arrasados, y tanto las autoridades como los periódicos pidieron ayuda a la prensa estadounidense y a las organizaciones benéficas de los Estados Unidos ante el inicio del hambre y los robos.

records.headline: After a tropical hurricane wrecked the capital, officials of President Rafael L. Trujillo's administration
records.summary_en: After a tropical hurricane wrecked the capital, officials of President Rafael L. Trujillo's administration reported great misery in Santo Domingo and called for urgent food and medical supplies. Following 18 hours without communication, restored cable service brought initial reports from All-America Cables stating that the city of approximately 50,000 inhabitants was "50 per cent destroyed" and that the American Red Cross would be asked for assistance. An insane asylum was demolished, allowing inmates to run through the city, while a Pan-American Line airplane reported heavy damage in the capital and radio dispatches from San Juan, Puerto Rico, reported 20 deaths on the British island of Dominica before the storm moved northwest. Observatories reported the storm center was likely to reach the north coast of Cuba within 24 hours and the Florida coast in 36 hours or two days. The Dominican Republic, which had not entirely recovered from the last West Indies hurricane, was already suffering from economic depression and the effect of a governmental transition when the new disaster struck: the little republic went through a bloodless revolution last February, when the regime of Gen. Horacio Vasquez was overthrown and the revolutionary leader, Gen. Rafael Leonidas Trujillo, was elected President in May. The capital city, situated at the mouth of the River Ozama and founded by Bartholomew Columbus in 1496, has many ancient houses although some sections are sturdily built, and the great cathedral in which the bones of Columbus rested until 1795 is one of the chief structures in the center of the capital. Government officials and the American Red Cross joined to provide relief for Santo Domingo: Ernest J. Swift, acting chairman of foreign operations for the American Red Cross, was called into conference with Acting Secretary of State Cotton to consider relief measures, and during the conference the State Department received a report from American Minister Charles B. Curtis, who asked the American Red Cross to rush relief to the island — the first telegram received from the hurricane section since communications were cut off — saying that while Santo Domingo city had suffered extensively, the loss of life appeared small. War Department officials announced they were ready to offer relief in the way of medical aid and supplies and tents to house those made homeless by the storm.
records.summary_es: Después de que un huracán tropical devastara la capital, funcionarios del gobierno del presidente Rafael L. Trujillo informaron de una gran miseria en Santo Domingo y solicitaron con urgencia alimentos y suministros médicos. Tras 18 horas de incomunicación, el restablecimiento del servicio de cable trajo los primeros informes de All-America Cables, según los cuales la ciudad de aproximadamente 50,000 habitantes quedó "destruida en un 50 por ciento" y se pediría ayuda a la Cruz Roja Estadounidense. Un manicomio fue demolido, lo que permitió que los internos corrieran por la ciudad, mientras que un avión de la línea Pan-American informó de graves daños en la capital y despachos radiales desde San Juan, Puerto Rico, reportaron 20 muertos en la isla británica de Dominica antes de que la tormenta avanzara hacia el noroeste. Los observatorios informaron que el centro de la tormenta probablemente llegaría a la costa norte de Cuba en 24 horas y a la costa de Florida en 36 horas o dos días. La República Dominicana, que no se había recuperado del todo del último huracán de las Indias Occidentales, ya sufría una depresión económica y el efecto de una transición gubernamental cuando sobrevino el nuevo desastre: la pequeña república pasó por una revolución incruenta el pasado febrero, cuando fue derrocado el régimen del general Horacio Vasquez y el líder revolucionario, el general Rafael Leonidas Trujillo, fue electo presidente en mayo. La capital, situada en la desembocadura del río Ozama y fundada por Bartolomé Colón en 1496, tiene muchas casas antiguas aunque algunas secciones están sólidamente construidas, y la gran catedral en la que reposaron los huesos de Colón hasta 1795 es una de las principales construcciones del centro de la capital. Funcionarios del gobierno y la Cruz Roja Estadounidense se unieron para brindar auxilio a Santo Domingo: Ernest J. Swift, presidente interino de operaciones en el exterior de la Cruz Roja Estadounidense, fue llamado a conferenciar con el secretario de Estado interino Cotton para considerar las medidas de auxilio, y durante la conferencia el Departamento de Estado recibió un informe del ministro estadounidense Charles B. Curtis, quien pidió a la Cruz Roja que enviara auxilio urgente a la isla —el primer telegrama recibido de la zona del huracán desde que se cortaron las comunicaciones—, diciendo que, aunque la ciudad de Santo Domingo había sufrido extensamente, la pérdida de vidas parecía pequeña. Funcionarios del Departamento de Guerra anunciaron que estaban listos para ofrecer auxilio en forma de ayuda médica y suministros y tiendas de campaña para albergar a los que quedaron sin hogar por la tormenta.

records.summary_en: After noting that the structure where the remains of Columbus rested until 1795 stands in the center of Santo Domingo, the second oldest European city in the New World, a Havana dispatch reports that a fierce hurricane swept northward through the West Indies on Thursday with winds estimated at 160 to 200 miles an hour. The Dominican Republic had been cut off from communication since late Wednesday and was believed to have suffered heavy property damage and loss of life after the destructive winds passed south of Puerto Rico and struck the city of Santo Domingo. Observers in Havana indicated that if the storm maintained its course it would cross eastern Cuba and head toward the Bahamas within 74 hours.

records.headline: Following State Department reports of extensive hurricane damage
records.summary_en: Following State Department reports of extensive hurricane damage, emergency funds were allocated primarily to purchase food for the stricken area, with additional money promised once total needs could be determined. After killing twenty persons on the British island of Dominica, the hurricane struck the Dominican Republic's capital with its greatest force before veering northward over extreme northwestern Haiti toward Cuba and Florida. The report notes that the Dominican Republic was still recovering from the previous West Indies hurricane and facing economic depression and governmental transition when the storm hit, demolishing many buildings in the capital and wrecking an insane asylum whose escaping inmates officials were working to recapture.
records.summary_es: Tras los informes del Departamento de Estado sobre los cuantiosos daños causados por el huracán, se destinaron fondos de emergencia principalmente para comprar alimentos para la zona afectada, con la promesa de recursos adicionales una vez que se determinaran las necesidades totales. Después de causar la muerte de veinte personas en la isla británica de Dominica, el huracán azotó la capital de la República Dominicana con su mayor violencia antes de desviarse hacia el norte sobre el extremo noroccidental de Haití en dirección a Cuba y Florida. El informe señala que la República Dominicana aún se recuperaba del anterior huracán de las Indias Occidentales y atravesaba una depresión económica y una transición gubernamental cuando golpeó la tormenta, la cual demolió numerosos edificios en la capital y destruyó un manicomio cuyos internos prófugos las autoridades trataban de recapturar.

records.headline: Writing from Azua, Dominican Republic, on September 4, Associated Press special
records.summary_en: Writing from Azua, Dominican Republic, on September 4, Associated Press special correspondent Ernest Nichols reported that Santo Domingo City lay desolate and in urgent need of water and medical supplies after Wednesday's hurricane destroyed almost the entire capital. Having struck early in the afternoon and reached its greatest fury from about 2:30 p.m. during a four-hour blow, the storm cut a wide diagonal swath northwestward across the country and caused millions of dollars in damage. A companion Port-au-Prince dispatch noted that the high mountains dividing the Dominican Republic from Haiti fended off the storm's main strength as its tail end brought heavy rain and violent wind to Haiti, while Pan-American Airways reported all its planes safe after suspending schedules.

Tras azotar a primeras horas de la tarde y alcanzar su mayor furia desde aproximadamente las 2:30 p.m. durante cuatro horas de embate, la tormenta abrió una amplia franja diagonal hacia el noroeste a través del país y causó daños por millones de dólares. Un despacho adjunto desde Puerto Príncipe señaló que las altas montañas que dividen a la República Dominicana de Haití desviaron la fuerza principal de la tormenta mientras su cola llevaba fuertes lluvias y vientos violentos a Haití, en tanto que Pan-American Airways informó que todos sus aviones estaban a salvo tras suspender sus itinerarios.

records.headline: Reporting for the United Press from Santo Domingo on September
records.summary_en: Reporting for the United Press from Santo Domingo on September 5, staff correspondent Francisco Escovar stated that officials had counted eight hundred dead in the ruins of the capital and believed a thousand more were injured following Wednesday's hurricane. Rescuers placed bodies in tiers for cremation while martial law prevailed across the devastated city, where 50,000 to 100,000 persons were left homeless. With the water supply failed, lighting lacking for night work, and food shortages growing acute, the population urgently awaited relief ships from Puerto Rico and Cuba due the following day as well as aid expected by air. The city was without light and water, and thousands of homeless persons sought to recover what they could from the debris while others went through the ruins of their homes for the bodies of missing relatives and friends. The customs house and warehouses were destroyed with a loss of great quantities of merchandise and provisions, thus cheating authorities of the hope that they might be able to feed survivors from reserve supplies. Flood waters from the River Ozama added to the damage and suffering and brought the further danger of disease and pestilence, and a small village opposite the city, on the bank of the Ozama, was entirely wiped out by the floods. Damage to the harbor, which was filled with debris, made it impossible for vessels to enter the port or leave. With rescue workers making every effort to relieve the suffering in the city itself, there was no word from the interior of the Republic, which was in the direct path of the storm, and one of the first tasks of volunteers was to clear the airplane landing field in order that planes might arrive from San Juan and Havana with medical and food supplies. It was feared that inmates of an insane asylum, which had been destroyed, were roaming through Santo Domingo and other parts of the island. Relief was urged in a message from Col. Crockett to Gov. Roosevelt: doctors and medical supplies were needed at once, and blankets, rations and funds were needed for from 50,000 to 100,000 persons. Illustrative of the suddenness with which the city was practically demolished by the hurricane, the weather cleared after the storm passed, and today a brilliant sun played upon the ruins of the capital.
records.summary_es: Informando para la United Press desde Santo Domingo el 5 de septiembre, el corresponsal Francisco Escovar señaló que las autoridades habían contado ochocientos muertos entre las ruinas de la capital y estimaban que había mil heridos más tras el huracán del miércoles. Los socorristas apilaban los cadáveres en hileras para su cremación mientras regía la ley marcial en toda la ciudad devastada, donde entre 50,000 y 100,000 personas quedaron sin hogar. Ante la falta de suministro de agua, la carencia de alumbrado para las labores nocturnas y una escasez de alimentos cada vez más aguda, la población aguardaba con urgencia la llegada de buques de socorro procedentes de Puerto Rico y Cuba prevista para el día siguiente, así como la ayuda esperada por vía aérea. La ciudad estaba sin luz ni agua, y miles de personas sin hogar trataban de recuperar lo que podían de los escombros mientras otras buscaban entre las ruinas de sus casas los cuerpos de familiares y amigos desaparecidos. La aduana y los almacenes fueron destruidos con la pérdida de grandes cantidades de mercancías y provisiones, frustrando así la esperanza de las autoridades de poder alimentar a los supervivientes con las reservas. Las aguas desbordadas del río Ozama se sumaron a los daños y al sufrimiento y trajeron el peligro adicional de enfermedades y pestilencia, y una pequeña aldea frente a la ciudad, a orillas del Ozama, fue enteramente arrasada por las inundaciones. Los daños al puerto, lleno de escombros, hicieron imposible que los buques entraran o salieran. Mientras los socorristas hacían todo lo posible por aliviar el sufrimiento en la propia ciudad, no había noticias del interior de la República, que estaba en la trayectoria directa de la tormenta, y una de las primeras tareas de los voluntarios fue despejar el campo de aterrizaje para que pudieran llegar aviones desde San Juan y La Habana con suministros médicos y alimentos. Se temía que los internos de un manicomio, que había sido destruido, deambularan por Santo Domingo y otras partes de la isla. Se urgió el socorro en un mensaje del coronel Crockett al gobernador Roosevelt: se necesitaban médicos y suministros médicos de inmediato, y se necesitaban mantas, raciones y fondos para entre 50,000 y 100,000 personas. Como muestra de la brusquedad con que la ciudad fue prácticamente demolida por el huracán, el tiempo se despejó tras el paso de la tormenta, y hoy un sol brillante brillaba sobre las ruinas de la capital.

records.headline: The hurricane moved westward over the Dominican Republic and wrecked
records.summary_en: The hurricane moved westward over the Dominican Republic and wrecked the capital city of Santo Domingo, the Douglas Daily Dispatch notes in a brief continuation report. The storm missed the Republic of Haiti on the western end of the island before swirling northward and sparing Cuba, which had previously lain in its projected path.
records.summary_es: El huracán avanzó hacia el oeste sobre la República Dominicana y destruyó la ciudad capital de Santo Domingo, según señala el Douglas Daily Dispatch en una breve nota de continuación. La tormenta no alcanzó a la República de Haití en el extremo occidental de la isla antes de girar hacia el norte y librar a Cuba, que previamente se encontraba en su trayectoria proyectada.

records.headline: Commenting on the atmospheric forces that produce tropical tempests
records.summary_en: Commenting on the atmospheric forces that produce tropical tempests, the New Britain Herald notes that winds reportedly traveling 150 miles an hour struck Santo Domingo and reduced the city to wreckage. At the time of writing, 800 known dead had been counted in the center of population, with additional fatalities in the outlying districts of the island. Expressing condolences to the citizens of the Dominican Republic, the paper remarks that the United States and Cuba may give thanks that the island's mountains appear to have broken up the storm and spared Cuba and Florida.
records.summary_es: Al comentar sobre las fuerzas atmosféricas que producen las tempestades tropicales, el New Britain Herald señala que vientos que, según los informes, viajaban a 150 millas por hora azotaron Santo Domingo y redujeron la ciudad a escombros. Al momento de redactarse la nota, se habían contabilizado 800 muertos confirmados en el centro de población, además de otras víctimas fatales en los distritos periféricos de la isla. Al expresar sus condolencias a los ciudadanos de la República Dominicana, el diario observa que los Estados Unidos y Cuba pueden dar gracias de que las montañas de la isla parecen haber desarticulado la tormenta, librando así a Cuba y a Florida.

records.headline: Following a conference with President Trujillo and Minister Curtis
records.summary_en: Following a conference with President Trujillo and Minister Curtis and a reconnaissance of Santo Domingo, a report states that three-quarters of the houses are practically destroyed, the American legation is destroyed though the American minister and all Europeans are saved, and Trujillo reports at least a hundred deaths already counted with no news yet from interior towns. The report calls for an urgent supply of doctors, medical supplies, tents, cots, blankets, clothing, Red Cross funds, and 50,000 to 100,000 rations. In a separate cablegram made public by the Dominican legation, the Dominican government states that the cyclone destroyed 90 per cent of the city with an estimated loss of at least thirty millions, and that 800 bodies have been recovered so far and must be cremated for lack of time for burials. With rivers in high flood, families sheltered in habitable churches, schools, and public buildings, and acute shortages of food, clothing, and medical supplies, the government appeals urgently to the American government, foreign representatives, the press, the Red Cross, and the American people.
records.summary_es: Tras una conferencia con el presidente Trujillo y el ministro Curtis y un reconocimiento de Santo Domingo, un informe señala que tres cuartas partes de las casas están prácticamente destruidas, la legación estadounidense está destruida aunque el ministro estadounidense y todos los europeos están a salvo, y Trujillo informa de al menos cien muertes ya contabilizadas sin noticias aún de los pueblos del interior. El informe solicita con urgencia médicos, suministros médicos, tiendas de campaña, catres, mantas, ropa, fondos de la Cruz Roja y de 50,000 a 100,000 raciones. En un cablegrama aparte hecho público por la legación dominicana, el gobierno dominicano afirma que el ciclón destruyó el 90 por ciento de la ciudad con una pérdida estimada de al menos treinta millones, y que hasta el momento se han recuperado 800 cadáveres que deben ser incinerados por falta de tiempo para los entierros. Con los ríos desbordados, las familias refugiadas en iglesias, escuelas y edificios públicos habitables, y una grave escasez de alimentos, ropa y suministros médicos, el gobierno hace un llamado urgente al gobierno estadounidense, a los representantes extranjeros, a la prensa, a la Cruz Roja y al pueblo estadounidense.

Advices cited said conditions in the stricken area were worse than first reported.

Los informes citados decían que las condiciones en la zona afectada eran peores de lo informado al principio.

records.headline: Commandant of the Coast Guard Admiral Billard offered the Red Cross
records.summary_en: Commandant of the Coast Guard Admiral Billard offered the Red Cross the use of a Coast Guard vessel at Mobile, Alabama, to transport relief supplies to Santo Domingo, while the Bull Line offered one of its vessels currently at San Juan, Porto Rico. Red Cross headquarters also announced gifts of 2000 children's dresses from the New York chapter and 1000 from the Philadelphia chapter to be shipped to Santo Domingo from New York the following day. A subsequent United Press dispatch from Miami reports that weather forecaster R. W. Gray said the Caribbean hurricane had lessened appreciably in danger since cutting a destructive path across the Dominican Republic and islands to the south.
records.summary_es: El comandante de la Guardia Costera, almirante Billard, ofreció a la Cruz Roja el uso de un buque de la Guardia Costera en Mobile, Alabama, para transportar suministros de socorro a Santo Domingo, mientras que la Bull Line ofreció uno de sus barcos actualmente en San Juan, Puerto Rico. La sede de la Cruz Roja también anunció donaciones de 2000 vestidos para niños de la filial de Nueva York y 1000 de la filial de Filadelfia para ser enviados a Santo Domingo desde Nueva York al día siguiente. Un despacho posterior de la United Press desde Miami informa que el meteorólogo R. W. Gray dijo que el peligro del huracán del Caribe había disminuido apreciablemente desde que abrió un camino destructivo a través de la República Dominicana y las islas del sur.

records.headline: Winds that were reported as exceeding 150 miles an hour over Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: Winds that were reported as exceeding 150 miles an hour over Santo Domingo were said today to be no longer damaging as they moved west-northwestward. Meanwhile, Minister Curtiss informed the State Department that the legation office and residence were unroofed and other quarters unobtainable, though supplies, recent archives, legation personnel, and the consul and his family were unharmed. Governor Roosevelt of Porto Rico advised the Red Cross of a report from his aide Major Cary I. Crockett, who flew to Santo Domingo the previous day and conferred with President Trujillo and Minister Curtiss. Crockett reported that three-quarters of the city's houses were practically destroyed, at least a hundred deaths were already counted, and doctors, medical supplies, tentage, cots, blankets, clothing, Red Cross funds, and rations were urgently needed, while a Dominican government cablegram stated that 90 per cent of the city was destroyed.
records.summary_es: Se informó hoy que los vientos que habían superado las 150 millas por hora sobre Santo Domingo ya no eran dañinos mientras avanzaban hacia el oeste-noroeste. Entretanto, el ministro Curtiss informó al Departamento de Estado que la oficina y la residencia de la legación habían perdido el techo y que era imposible conseguir otro alojamiento, aunque los suministros, los archivos recientes, el personal de la legación y el cónsul y su familia resultaron ilesos. El gobernador Roosevelt de Puerto Rico comunicó a la Cruz Roja un informe de su ayudante, el mayor Cary I. Crockett, quien voló a Santo Domingo el día anterior y se reunió con el presidente Trujillo y el ministro Curtiss. Crockett informó que tres cuartas partes de las casas de la ciudad estaban prácticamente destruidas, que ya se habían contado al menos cien muertos y que se necesitaban con urgencia médicos, suministros médicos, tiendas de campaña, catres, mantas, ropa, fondos de la Cruz Roja y raciones, mientras que un cablegrama del gobierno dominicano indicaba que el 90 por ciento de la ciudad fue destruido.

records.headline: An editorial commentary remarks that critics of the United States regime
records.summary_en: An editorial commentary remarks that critics of the United States regime in the Dominican Republic should note that relief is being rushed to the island by the U.S. Army and Navy and from Porto Rico. The writer rejects claims that the American government sought to strangle and usurp the Dominican government or that United States Marines stationed there under the Monroe Doctrine and at the Dominican Republic's request acted like butchers. Asserting that American policy in Dominican affairs has been honorable and unselfish, the editorial states that the United States is the first to answer appeals for help in times of distress, whether from Santo Domingo, Japan, or Italy.
records.summary_es: Un comentario editorial señala que para los críticos del régimen de los Estados Unidos en la República Dominicana debe resultar interesante saber que el Ejército y la Marina estadounidenses, así como Puerto Rico, están enviando ayuda con urgencia. El autor rechaza las afirmaciones de que el propósito del gobierno estadounidense haya sido estrangular y usurpar al gobierno dominicano o que los infantes de marina estadounidenses estacionados allí bajo la Doctrina Monroe y a petición específica de la República Dominicana hayan actuado como carniceros. Al afirmar que el curso del gobierno estadounidense en los asuntos dominicanos ha sido honorable y desinteresado, el editorial sostiene que los Estados Unidos son los primeros en responder a un llamado de auxilio en tiempos de angustia, ya provenga de Santo Domingo, Japón o Italia.

records.headline: A United Press dispatch from Santo Domingo dated September 5
records.summary_en: A United Press dispatch from Santo Domingo dated September 5 reports that casualties from Wednesday's hurricane were estimated at more than 1,000 killed and about 4,000 injured, with many expected to die. With roughly three-quarters of the capital's population of more than 40,000 homeless, sanitary authorities ordered the burning of wreckage to prevent pestilence. The American, British, Cuban, Mexican, Spanish, French, and Haitian legations were demolished—leaving the Haitian minister and his family in their wrecked cellar without food or clothing—along with the Bank of Nova Scotia and the Bull Insular Steamship line offices, while banks and businesses closed so relief forces could operate. The Dominican government announced that three vessels with supplies and medicine were expected early Saturday from Porto Rico, physicians and medicine were expected from Cuba, and the Haitian government had dispatched supplies and medicine by airplane and land routes.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de la United Press desde Santo Domingo fechado el 5 de septiembre informa que las víctimas del huracán del miércoles se estimaban en más de 1,000 muertos y unos 4,000 heridos, muchos de ellos de tanta gravedad que se temía su muerte. Con cerca de tres cuartas partes de la población capitalina de más de 40,000 habitantes sin hogar, las autoridades sanitarias ordenaron quemar los escombros para prevenir epidemias. Las legaciones estadounidense, británica, cubana, mexicana, española, francesa y haitiana quedaron demolidas —dejando al ministro haitiano y a su familia viviendo en el sótano en ruinas sin comida ni ropa—, junto con los edificios del Bank of Nova Scotia y las oficinas de la línea naviera Bull Insular Steamship, mientras que los bancos y comercios cerraron para permitir funcionar a las fuerzas de socorro. El gobierno dominicano anunció que se esperaban tres barcos con suministros y medicinas el sábado temprano desde Puerto Rico, que se esperaban médicos y medicinas de Cuba y que el gobierno haitiano había enviado suministros y medicinas por vía aérea y terrestre.

records.headline: Three photo and map captions accompanying coverage of the West Indian hurricane
records.summary_en: Three photo and map captions accompanying coverage of the West Indian hurricane depict scenes in Santo Domingo. The first caption describes a map showing the blast sweeping down on Santo Domingo and speeding northwesterly over the Dominican Republic. Two photographs provided by ex-Marine A. K. Group of 1207 Broadway show the headquarters camp of the Second Brigade, United States Marines at Santo Domingo, located about 600 feet from the water's edge, and the statue of Columbus in front of the cathedral at Santo Domingo City.
records.summary_es: Tres pies de foto y de mapa que acompañan la cobertura del huracán de las Indias Occidentales muestran escenas de Santo Domingo. El primer texto describe un mapa que muestra la ráfaga abatiéndose sobre Santo Domingo y avanzando en dirección noroeste sobre la República Dominicana. Dos fotografías cedidas por el ex infante de marina A. K. Group, de 1207 Broadway, muestran el campamento del cuartel general de la Segunda Brigada de Infantes de Marina de los Estados Unidos en Santo Domingo, situado a unos 600 pies de la orilla del agua, y la estatua de Colón frente a la catedral en la ciudad de Santo Domingo.

records.summary_en: An experienced disaster relief worker named Silva, who flew from San Juan, Porto Rico, to Santo Domingo the previous afternoon to survey the devastated sections of the city, cabled a report that was submitted to the White House. Silva reported that Governor-General Theodore Roosevelt of Porto Rico had sent physicians, nurses, food, tents, and cots, but declared these supplies insufficient to meet the needs of the refugees. Chairman John Barton Payne authorized Atlantic coast Red Cross chapters to accept relief contributions, while the Red Cross cabled an additional sum to Governor Roosevelt for medical supplies, bringing total expenditures to $25,000, and announced that the New York and Philadelphia chapters would ship 2,000 and 1,000 children's dresses and infants' garments on Saturday.

Silva informó que el gobernador general Theodore Roosevelt de Puerto Rico había enviado un grupo de médicos y enfermeras junto con alimentos, tiendas de campaña y catres, pero declaró que esto no bastaba para atender las necesidades de los refugiados. El presidente de la Cruz Roja, John Barton Payne, autorizó a las filiales de la costa atlántica a recibir contribuciones para el fondo de socorro, mientras que la Cruz Roja envió por cable una suma adicional al gobernador Roosevelt para suministros médicos, elevando el gasto total a $25,000, y anunció que las filiales de Nueva York y Filadelfia enviarían el sábado 2,000 y 1,000 vestidos para niños y prendas infantiles.

records.headline: The hurricane, which was the first of any consequence to strike
records.summary_en: The hurricane, which was the first of any consequence to strike Santo Domingo in more than 50 years, lost as much force traveling over the mountainous island as it would have across the Florida Peninsula, potentially sparing Cuba and the United States coast, weather forecaster Mitchell stated. Meanwhile, the devastation in the Dominican Republic caused apprehension among American commercial interests, which had already grown increasingly concerned over the island market's declining buying power during the past six months. Department of Commerce officials estimated American investments in Santo Domingo at between $90,000,000 and $110,000,000.
records.summary_es: El huracán, que fue el primero de importancia en azotar Santo Domingo en más de 50 años, perdió tanta fuerza al cruzar la isla montañosa como la que habría perdido al atravesar la península de la Florida, lo que pudo haber resultado afortunado para Cuba o la costa de los Estados Unidos, según afirmó el meteorólogo Mitchell. Entretanto, los daños causados en la República Dominicana despertaron inquietud entre los intereses comerciales estadounidenses, cuya preocupación por la situación económica allí había aumentado de forma constante durante los últimos seis meses debido a la continua caída del poder adquisitivo de ese mercado insular. Funcionarios del Departamento de Comercio estimaron las inversiones estadounidenses en Santo Domingo entre $90,000,000 y $110,000,000.

records.headline: After escaping inmates ran wild through Santo Domingo's streets
records.summary_en: After escaping inmates ran wild through Santo Domingo's streets amid widespread robberies, soldiers and police recaptured them and restored a semblance of order. With 20,000 people homeless in Santo Domingo City, the dead remain unburied and the injured suffer from a lack of medical and surgical care, while conditions in Haiti are reported normal. President Trujillo has worked without rest in the streets personally ordering the distribution of supplies and rations to forestall famine, and word arrived that two American ships carrying medicines and foodstuffs would arrive momentarily in response to Minister Curtis's appeal. Meanwhile, Associated Press correspondent Ernest Nichols, the only person to have penetrated as far as the southern coast port of Azua from Port au Prince, Haiti, continued his expedition toward the demolished Dominican capital.

El presidente Trujillo no ha descansado un solo momento desde que comenzó la tormenta, ordenando personalmente en las calles la distribución de suministros y raciones para evitar la hambruna, y se recibió la noticia de que dos barcos estadounidenses llegarían de un momento a otro con medicinas y alimentos en respuesta al llamado del ministro Curtis. Entretanto, el corresponsal de la Associated Press Ernest Nichols, la única persona que había logrado llegar hasta el puerto sureño de Azua desde Puerto Príncipe, Haití, continuó su expedición hacia la demolida capital dominicana.

records.headline: Winds exceeding 150 miles an hour unroofed and partly destroyed
records.summary_en: Winds exceeding 150 miles an hour unroofed and partly destroyed the American legation in Santo Domingo, destroyed the great bridge across the Ozama River, and blew all buildings of the Pan-American Airways to pieces. In a conference with American Minister Charles B. Curtis and Major Cary I. Crockett, representative of Governor Theodore Roosevelt of Porto Rico, President Rafael Trujillo stated that 800 dead had been counted in the city and that the toll might rise higher. Crockett radioed Governor Roosevelt that the American minister, his staff, and all Europeans were saved, but that three-quarters of the city's houses were destroyed, hundreds were injured, and physicians, medical supplies, tents, pots, blankets, clothing, Red Cross funds, and 50,000 to 100,000 rations were urgently needed. Although the All American Cable company restored exterior communications, telegraph lines to the interior vanished, leaving roads impassable and the rest of the republic cut off.

Aunque la compañía All American Cable restableció las comunicaciones con el exterior, las líneas telegráficas hacia el interior desaparecieron, dejando los caminos intransitables y al resto de la república incomunicado.

records.headline: After 18 hours without communication, restored service from All-America Cables brought
records.summary_en: After 18 hours without communication, restored service from All-America Cables brought the first definite reports that the capital city of Santo Domingo was fifty per cent destroyed by a violent tropical hurricane and urgently needed food and medical supplies. The windstorm blasted away part of the bridge spanning the river in the center of town, destroyed food supplies, and left hundreds of dazed refugees wandering through the debris in need of clothing and shelter, while the first airplane pilot to fly over the city reported that the heart of the hurricane had passed directly over it. Having moved north and west from the island of Dominica to strike the Dominican capital with its greatest violence, the storm veered northward from Haiti, on the western half of the island, toward northern Cuba and Florida.
records.summary_es: Tras 18 horas de incomunicación, el restablecimiento del servicio de All-America Cables trajo los primeros informes definitivos de que la ciudad capital de Santo Domingo había quedado destruida en un cincuenta por ciento por un violento huracán tropical y necesitaba con urgencia alimentos y suministros médicos. El temporal voló parte del puente sobre el río en el centro de la ciudad, destruyó las provisiones de alimentos y dejó a cientos de refugiados aturdidos vagando entre los escombros necesitados de ropa y abrigo, mientras que el primer piloto de avión en sobrevolar la ciudad informó que el centro del huracán había pasado directamente sobre ella. Tras avanzar hacia el norte y el oeste desde la isla de Dominica para golpear con su mayor violencia la capital dominicana, la tormenta viró hacia el norte desde Haití, en la mitad occidental de la isla, en dirección al norte de Cuba y la Florida.

records.headline: Commenting on the swift response of the U.S. government, Army
records.summary_en: Commenting on the swift response of the U.S. government, Army, Navy, and American Red Cross to the hurricane that cost more than 1,100 lives and virtually wiped out Santo Domingo, an editorial notes that relations between the Dominican Republic and the United States have long been close and friendly. The piece recalls that Dominicans approved annexation to the United States after winning freedom from Spain, though the United States rejected it, and that Washington later intervened with two civil commissions and an eight-year Marine occupation lasting until 1924. According to the editorial, the United States kept its promise to withdraw the Marines after improving politics, communications, transportation, and economics, earning Dominican friendship at a time when the country is suffering a severe depression due to low prices for sugar, its chief crop.
records.summary_es: Al comentar la rápida respuesta del gobierno, el Ejército, la Marina y la Cruz Roja de los Estados Unidos ante el huracán que cobró más de 1,100 vidas y prácticamente arrasó Santo Domingo, un editorial señala que las relaciones entre la República Dominicana y los Estados Unidos han sido durante mucho tiempo estrechas y amistosas. El texto recuerda que los dominicanos aprobaron la anexión a los Estados Unidos tras obtener su independencia de España, aunque los Estados Unidos la rechazaron, y que Washington intervino posteriormente con dos comisiones civiles y una ocupación de infantes de marina durante ocho años hasta 1924. Según el editorial, los Estados Unidos cumplieron su promesa de retirar a los infantes de marina tras mejorar la política, las comunicaciones, el transporte y la economía, ganándose la amistad de los dominicanos en un momento en que el país sufre una grave depresión debido al bajo precio del azúcar, su cultivo principal.

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo on September 6 reports that relief agencies reaching the stricken
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo on September 6 reports that relief agencies reaching the stricken city found the horror of Wednesday's hurricane worse rather than better: an estimated 1,500 to 2,000 persons dead, more than 5,000 injured, 30,000 homeless, and of 10,000 buildings only 400 left standing, with property damage to pass $20,000,000. There is no water fit to drink, the dead are being collected and burned in heaps and in concrete cisterns used as funeral pyres, relief planes have brought some supplies and doctors from Port-au-Prince, Havana, the United States and Porto Rico, and the president has stopped food profiteering by ordering all food sold at cost under pain of court martial, while Santiago, La Vega and Puerto Plata are reported undamaged.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Associated Press desde Santo Domingo del 6 de septiembre informa que las agencias de socorro que llegaron a la ciudad devastada encontraron el horror del huracán del miércoles peor en vez de mejor: se estima que murieron entre 1,500 y 2,000 personas, más de 5,000 resultaron heridas, 30,000 quedaron sin hogar y de 10,000 edificios solo 400 quedaron en pie, con daños materiales que pasarán de $20,000,000. No hay agua apta para beber, los muertos están siendo recogidos y quemados en montones y en cisternas de concreto usadas como piras funerarias, aviones de socorro han traído algunos suministros y médicos desde Puerto Príncipe, La Habana, los Estados Unidos y Puerto Rico, y el presidente ha detenido la especulación con los alimentos ordenando que toda la comida se venda al costo bajo pena de consejo de guerra, mientras se informa que Santiago, La Vega y Puerto Plata no sufrieron daños.

records.headline: Following 34 hours of storm and a 180-mile-an-hour north wind
records.summary_en: Following 34 hours of storm and a 180-mile-an-hour north wind that unroofed the legation and destroyed many homes in Santo Domingo, conservative estimates placed the death toll at 1500 and the injured at 5000, with no casualties reported among continental Americans or Europeans. President Trujillo has taken personal charge with the city under martial law, good order prevailing, and the dead being burned. Governor Theodore Roosevelt of Porto Rico sent personal representatives by airplane Thursday and is dispatching food, shelter, clothing, and medical aid, while a Marine Corps plane arrived from Port au Prince, Haiti, with representatives of a Marine colonel and is returning immediately for medical officers and supplies. Shipping cannot enter Santo Domingo port because of swift currents and a dredge sunk in the channel, and although the old cathedral and colonial monuments were practically undamaged, disabled water and electric plants and wrecked bridges have isolated the capital on the land side.
records.summary_es: Tras 34 horas de tormenta y un viento del norte de 180 millas por hora que destechó la legación y destruyó muchas casas en Santo Domingo, estimaciones conservadoras situaron el número de muertos en 1500 y el de heridos en 5000, sin que se registraran víctimas entre los estadounidenses continentales ni los europeos. El presidente Trujillo ha asumido personalmente el mando con la ciudad bajo ley marcial, donde reina el orden y se están incinerando los cadáveres.
