records.headline: Reporting from Santo Domingo on September 5 for the Associated
records.summary_en: Reporting from Santo Domingo on September 5 for the Associated Press, Rene M. Lepervanche writes that the Dominican capital lay in ruins under martial law as the bodies of almost 1,000 men, women, and children burned on funeral pyres. Wednesday's hurricane wiped out all communications between the Caribbean seaport and the interior to the north, leaving the extent of desolation outside the capital unknown. Inside the city, where only 400 of 10,000 big buildings remained standing to house the wounded and the weak, hunger began to stalk the littered streets as the plight of 5,000 injured and 30,000 homeless and destitute residents grew more critical by the hour.
records.summary_es: Informando desde Santo Domingo el 5 de septiembre para la Associated Press, Rene M. Lepervanche escribe que la capital dominicana yacía en ruinas bajo la ley marcial mientras los cuerpos de casi 1,000 hombres, mujeres y niños ardían en grandes piras funerarias. El huracán del miércoles destruyó todas las vías de comunicación entre el puerto caribeño y el interior hacia el norte, por lo que se desconocía la magnitud de la desolación fuera de la capital. Dentro de la ciudad, donde solo quedaban en pie 400 de los 10,000 grandes edificios para albergar a los heridos y a los débiles, el hambre comenzaba a recorrer las calles cubiertas de escombros mientras la situación de los 5,000 heridos y de los 30,000 habitantes sin hogar y desamparados se volvía más crítica a cada hora.

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Washington dated September 5
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Washington dated September 5 reports that while the hurricane weakened after crossing the rugged mountains of the Dominican Republic and moved leisurely toward the Florida Straits, incoming reports to the American Red Cross counted a thousand dead, 2,500 injured, 4,700 homes destroyed, and thousands homeless in Santo Domingo. Food, medicines, water, and clothing were being dispatched by airplane and ship. Red Cross officials stated that an American committee named by Minister Charles B. Curtis would direct American relief in cooperation with Dominican officials and administer $40,000 cabled to Curtis by the Red Cross, while Captain Antonio Silva, president of the Porto Rican Red Cross chapter, would take charge of immediate field relief.

Se estaban enviando alimentos, medicinas, agua y ropa en avión y en barco. Funcionarios de la Cruz Roja indicaron que un comité estadounidense nombrado por el ministro Charles B. Curtis dirigiría las labores de socorro estadounidenses en cooperación con las autoridades dominicanas y administraría los $40,000 enviados por cable a Curtis por la Cruz Roja, mientras que el capitán Antonio Silva, presidente de la filial puertorriqueña de la Cruz Roja, asumiría el mando inmediato del socorro sobre el terreno.

records.headline: A continuation of the Santo Domingo hurricane dispatch describes the capital in ruins, with the Ozama River out of its banks
records.summary_en: A continuation of the Santo Domingo hurricane dispatch describes the capital in ruins, with the Ozama River out of its banks and whole sections inundated, people left with almost no clothing, and relief planes arriving from Port au Prince, Havana, the United States and Porto Rico with food, medicines, shelters and doctors, while the river bar blocked relief ships. The president ordered all food sold at cost under pain of court-martial, the old cathedral survived winds of 180 miles an hour, Santiago, La Vega and Puerto Plata were reported undamaged, and the International Red Cross in Paris appealed worldwide for funds for the sufferers.

El presidente ordenó que todos los alimentos se vendieran al costo bajo pena de consejo de guerra, la antigua catedral sobrevivió a vientos de 180 millas por hora, Santiago, La Vega y Puerto Plata fueron reportadas sin daños, y la Cruz Roja Internacional en París hizo un llamamiento mundial de fondos para los damnificados.

While the landing field here has been cleared sufficiently to permit landing of relief planes from Port au Prince, Havana, the United States and Porto Rico, the landing of ships is not so simple. The Ozama River is a raging torrent pouring out over a bar at its entrance which effectively blocks what was the old harbor. One authority said he did not believe even a Navy launch could cross the bar. Planes Bring Supplies. The suggestion has been made — and it appears plausible — that the relief ships may disembark their cargoes and men at San Geronimo, four kilometers south of the capital, where there is a good beach. Some supplies, food, medicines and even shelters have already arrived here by airplanes which also brought doctors for treatment of the sick and injured, and it is understood others are en route here aboard ships from Porto Rico, one of which is the naval tug Grebe, due today. records.headline: An account preceding the main dispatch states that 80 percent of the residential
records.summary_en: An account preceding the main dispatch states that 80 percent of the residential district was destroyed, the San Carlos, Barahona, and Pajarito districts were nearly obliterated, and only a few sturdy buildings from the days of Columbus escaped damage in the city proper, while the army under President Trujillo maintained order and began clearing the streets. In a September 6 United Press dispatch from Santo Domingo, Red Cross Director of Relief Captain Antonio Silva describes surveying the hurricane-felled capital by plane from San Juan, Porto Rico, and walking through debris-choked streets where the shortage of volunteer workers and need for speed forced mass incineration. With water unavailable, electricity shut off, and food growing scarcer, President Trujillo has taken personal charge of efforts to resume water and food supplies and placed the capital under martial law to prevent pillaging as further outside aid is needed.
records.summary_es: Un relato que precede al despacho principal señala que el 80 por ciento del distrito residencial quedó destruido, que los distritos de San Carlos, Barahona y Pajarito quedaron prácticamente arrasados y que solo unos pocos edificios sólidos de la época de Colón escaparon a los daños en la ciudad propiamente dicha, mientras el ejército, bajo las órdenes del presidente Trujillo, mantuvo el orden y comenzó a despejar las calles. En un despacho de la United Press fechado el 6 de septiembre desde Santo Domingo, el director de socorro de la Cruz Roja, capitán Antonio Silva, describe haber inspeccionado desde el aire la capital abatida por el huracán al llegar en avión desde San Juan, Porto Rico, y haber recorrido calles obstruidas por los escombros donde la escasez de trabajadores voluntarios y la urgencia obligaron a recurrir a la incineración masiva. Sin agua disponible, con el suministro eléctrico cortado y los alimentos cada vez más escasos, el presidente Trujillo ha asumido personalmente la dirección de los esfuerzos para restablecer los suministros de agua y alimentos y ha puesto la capital bajo ley marcial para impedir el pillaje, mientras se necesita más ayuda exterior.

records.headline: United Press staff correspondent Francisco Escovar reports from Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: United Press staff correspondent Francisco Escovar reports from Santo Domingo that outside relief reached the devastated Dominican capital on Saturday as hungry, exhausted survivors worked to dispose of some 2,000 dead and clear wreckage from Wednesday's hurricane. An American transport and two American Marine planes arrived with the first outside supplies, while the S.S. Catherine, which had sailed from San Juan on Friday with two other supply ships, had to make alternative arrangements to unload her cargo because the river was still running high. Additional aid was en route by land, air, and sea, and partially restored interior communications revealed that many villages were destroyed and the city of Villa Duarte was reported entirely demolished.
records.summary_es: El corresponsal de la United Press Francisco Escovar informa desde Santo Domingo que la ayuda exterior llegó a la devastada capital dominicana el sábado, mientras los sobrevivientes hambrientos y exhaustos trabajaban para disponer de unos 2,000 muertos y retirar los escombros dejados por el huracán del miércoles. Un transporte estadounidense y dos aviones de la Infantería de Marina de los Estados Unidos llegaron con los primeros suministros del exterior, mientras que el vapor S.S. Catherine, que había zarpado de San Juan el viernes junto con otros dos buques de abastecimiento, tuvo que hacer otros arreglos para descargar su cargamento debido a que el río seguía crecido. Más ayuda estaba en camino por tierra, aire y mar, y el restablecimiento parcial de las comunicaciones con el interior reveló que muchas aldeas habían sido destruidas y que la ciudad de Villa Duarte se reportaba completamente demolida.

records.headline: An editorial in The Washington Daily News commends the prompt
records.summary_en: An editorial in The Washington Daily News commends the prompt response of the U.S. government, the Army and Navy, and the American Red Cross in sending aid and funds to the hurricane-stricken Dominican Republic, where Santo Domingo has been virtually wiped out and outlying districts are believed to have suffered heavy damage. Reviewing relations between the two countries, the paper notes that Dominicans once approved annexation after winning freedom from Spain, though the United States rejected it, and that later U.S. interventions through two civil commissions and an eight-year Marine control were followed by the promised withdrawal of forces after improvements in politics, communications, transportation, and economics. The editorial adds that the country has suffered a severe depression due to the low price of sugar, its major crop and chief source of revenue and trade, and will immediately need money and supplies.
records.summary_es: Un editorial de The Washington Daily News elogia la pronta respuesta del gobierno de los Estados Unidos, el Ejército, la Marina y la Cruz Roja Estadounidense al enviar ayuda y fondos a la República Dominicana azotada por el huracán, donde Santo Domingo ha quedado prácticamente arrasada y se cree que los distritos periféricos han sufrido graves daños. Al repasar las relaciones entre ambos países, el periódico señala que los dominicanos aprobaron en su momento la anexión tras obtener la independencia de España, aunque los Estados Unidos la rechazaron, y que las intervenciones estadounidenses posteriores mediante dos comisiones civiles y ocho años de control de la Infantería de Marina fueron seguidas por el retiro prometido de las fuerzas tras mejoras en la política, las comunicaciones, el transporte y la economía. El editorial añade que el país ha padecido una grave depresión debido al bajo precio del azúcar, su cultivo principal y fuente primordial de ingresos y comercio, y que necesitará dinero y suministros de inmediato.

records.headline: Flying over the Dominican Republic's rolling cattle country
records.summary_en: Flying over the Dominican Republic's rolling cattle country and coastal salt flats where workers shovel sun-evaporated sea salt into heaps near straw huts and fishing boats is described in a first-person aerial travel narrative in the Evening Star. Turning inland over Santo Domingo City, the writer observes the wreck of the American cruiser Memphis still piled up on the beach, the church said to hold a casket with the bones of Columbus, and the yellow flood of the Ozama River pouring into the indigo-blue sea. The flying boat then lands on the Bay of San Pedro de Macoris, where American sugar planters and Dominican officials are present.
records.summary_es: El vuelo sobre las onduladas tierras ganaderas de la República Dominicana y las salinas costeras donde los trabajadores amontonan con palas la sal marina evaporada por el sol cerca de chozas de paja y botes pesqueros es descrito en un relato de viaje aéreo en primera persona en el Evening Star. Al girar tierra adentro sobre la ciudad de Santo Domingo, el autor observa los restos del crucero estadounidense Memphis aún encallados en la playa, la iglesia donde se dice que se conserva una urna con los huesos de Colón y la corriente amarilla del río Ozama desembocando en el mar azul índigo. El hidroavión acuatiza luego en la bahía de San Pedro de Macoris, donde se encuentran hacendados azucareros estadounidenses y funcionarios dominicanos.

records.summary_en: Reporting for the Associated Press from Santo Domingo on September 6, Rene M. Lepervanche writes that funeral pyres burned across the city as the bodies of victims of Monday's hurricane, estimated at more than 4,000, were consigned to the flames. Sanitary service director Dr. Antonio Calderon's estimate of the dead is considered conservative, with fears that the final death toll will reach at least 5,000—about one-eighth of the city's population—alongside five thousand more seriously injured and property losses set at $40,000,000 to $50,000,000. Refugees from outlying towns continue to arrive with accounts of further destruction, piles of bodies still lie along muddy streets and the banks of the Ozama River, and all available houses, churches, and hospitals are filled with the wounded, including 400 in San Rafael Hospital.

records.headline: In a September 6 Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: In a September 6 Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo, Rene M. Le Pervanche reports that funeral pyres smoked over the city as the bodies of more than 4,000 victims of Monday's hurricane were burned and twenty-five percent of the populace were counted as casualties. Dr. Antonio Calderon, head of the sanitary service, gave a conservative estimate of the dead, with fears that the final total will reach at least 5,000—about one-eighth of the city's population—while five thousand more are seriously injured and expected in many cases to die. Refugees arriving from outlying towns bring reports of additional death and destruction as workers uncover more bodies while clearing debris from the streets. Along the muddy streets, the discovery of a body was announced by a pistol shot — and shots were frequent. Relief work was pushed today: the U.S.S. Grebe arrived with the first unit of medical workers, a group of 26 physicians and assistants from Puerto Rico sent through the foresight of Governor Theodore Roosevelt with the cooperation of the Red Cross. Two other relief ships arrived from San Juan, and Lieut. Petrie, commander of the Grebe, was ordered to remain here to superintend the unloading of supplies. Because of rough seas and then a swift tide in the Ozama River, the ships were not able to unload until late today.

records.summary_en: Accounts of a serious spread of typhus in Santo Domingo led Haitian government officials to consider closing the frontier between Haiti and the Dominican Republic, an Associated Press dispatch from Port au Prince, Haiti, reports. Meanwhile, the Weather Bureau warned that a second Caribbean hurricane of small diameter but considerable intensity was about 200 miles south of the city of Santo Domingo, moving west-northwestward at 12 to 14 miles per hour toward Jamaica or the southwestern tip of Haiti. Curtis reported that medical supplies from adjacent regions had been exhausted, the Red Cross arranged to send 5,000 pounds of surgical dressings, antitoxin, and anaesthetics to Santo Domingo by airplane following a conference between Red Cross Chairman John Barton Payne and Army and Navy Surgeons General Maj. records.headline: The danger of an epidemic among hurricane survivors increased
records.summary_en: The danger of an epidemic among hurricane survivors increased with rapid outbreaks of typhoid, malaria, and influenza while street clearing and relief work proceeded slowly, an International News Service dispatch from Santo Domingo reports. With the water supply still cut off, sanitary conditions desperate, and many bodies decomposing under wrecked buildings in the tropical heat, conservative observers estimated fatalities would not exceed 2,000, though official quarters conceded the death toll could prove higher and at least 6,000 people were injured. An inset appeal from the District of Columbia chapter of the American Red Cross urgently requests clean, lightweight clothing for men, women, and children suffering from the storm in Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: El peligro de una epidemia entre los sobrevivientes del huracán aumentó con la rápida propagación de numerosos casos de tifoidea, malaria e influenza, mientras la limpieza de las calles y las labores de socorro avanzaban con lentitud, según un despacho del International News Service desde Santo Domingo. Con el suministro de agua aún interrumpido, condiciones sanitarias desesperadas y muchos cadáveres descomponiéndose bajo los edificios destruidos en el calor tropical, observadores conservadores estimaron que las muertes no pasarían de 2,000, aunque en círculos oficiales se admitió que el total de fallecidos podría ser mayor y que al menos 6,000 personas resultaron heridas. Un llamado intercalado de la filial del Distrito de Columbia de la Cruz Roja Estadounidense solicita con urgencia ropa limpia y ligera para hombres, mujeres y niños afectados por la tormenta en Santo Domingo.

records.summary_en: The opening paragraph notes a Monday report by the United States Weather Bureau placing a new Caribbean storm of smaller diameter but considerable intensity about 200 miles south of Santo Domingo, heading toward Jamaica or extreme southwestern Haiti on Tuesday. Following this, United Press correspondent Francisco Escovar reports from Santo Domingo that gangrene and lockjaw were increasing the death toll hourly and threatening hundreds of injured victims as the city strove on Monday to restore its water supply and avert further pestilence. Doctors and nurses worked without sleep in overcrowded hospitals.

A continuación, el corresponsal de la United Press Francisco Escovar informa desde Santo Domingo que la gangrena y el tétanos aumentaban cada hora el número de muertos y amenazaban a cientos de heridos mientras la ciudad se esforzaba el lunes por restablecer su suministro de agua y conjurar un mayor peligro de pestilencia. Los médicos y las enfermeras trabajaban sin dormir en hospitales abarrotados.

records.headline: Fear of pestilence gripped the hurricane-flattened capital on Sunday
records.summary_en: Fear of pestilence gripped the hurricane-flattened capital on Sunday as relief workers labored to restore sanitary conditions, Francisco Escovar reports in a September 7 United Press dispatch from Santo Domingo. Director Johnson of the Haitian General Hospital stated that gangrene was spreading rapidly among thousands injured in Wednesday's storm and that an airplane shipment of antitoxin due Monday from Philadelphia would be insufficient. Burial parties burned bodies where they found them because putrefaction in the tropical heat prevented gathering them into piles, bringing the latest figure to 1,500 bodies cremated, while doctors organized vaccination stations, gave anti-typhoid inoculations at police headquarters, and frequently operated without anesthetics using butcher knives or kitchen utensils as false rumors of a new storm alarmed the populace.

El director Johnson del Hospital General haitiano declaró que la gangrena se propagaba rápidamente entre los miles de heridos por la tormenta del miércoles y que un cargamento de antitoxina esperado en avión el lunes desde Filadelfia sería insuficiente. records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Washington dated September 8 reports that the U.S. Navy responded promptly to a request from Santo Domingo for surgical instruments, particularly those used in amputations, to treat thousands of gangrenous cases spreading across the hurricane-stricken city. Reports sent to the American Red Cross by Captain Antonio Silva, representing the Red Cross at Santo Domingo, and American Minister Charles B. Curtis stated that 1000 patients had been examined for gangrenous infections and that medical supplies from adjacent regions were exhausted. records.headline: Planes bound for Santo Domingo are set to carry 2460 pounds of surgical dressings
records.summary_en: Planes bound for Santo Domingo are set to carry 2460 pounds of surgical dressings, antitoxins, and anaesthetic each, while Rear Admiral W. R. Sexton, commander of the scouting fleet destroyer squadrons, ordered the destroyer U.S.S. Gilmer from Newport, Rhode Island, to New York harbor on stand-by for further medical aid to the Dominican capital. Meanwhile, President Trujillo cabled Dominican Minister Rafael Brache that the known magnitude of the hurricane devastation was increasing hourly and that an epidemic was feared. Trujillo's cablegram stated that 2,000 dead had been buried or burned, over 5,000 were injured, and more than 30,000 were homeless.

records.headline: The arrival of a small fleet of relief ships carrying doctors
records.summary_en: The arrival of a small fleet of relief ships carrying doctors, nurses, provisions, and funds—along with relief missions from Porto Rico, Cuba, Haiti, and other points—brought workers and a steady flow of food to half-famished Santo Domingo. President Trujillo requested Ernest J. Swift, director of the American Red Cross foreign operations branch, to survey the entire situation in Santo Domingo and report to him personally with recommendations to improve and speed up relief and rehabilitation. Airplanes also flew between the storm area and Port-au-Prince, Haiti, completing an aerial survey of outlying zones, while relief workers noted the large number of serious injuries, many of them calling for the most extreme measures by the already overworked army and civilian physicians and surgeons, as no official death count had yet been made.
records.summary_es: La llegada de una pequeña flota de buques de socorro con médicos, enfermeras, provisiones y fondos —junto con misiones de auxilio procedentes de Porto Rico, Cuba, Haití y otros puntos— aportó personal y un flujo de alimentos a la semihambrienta Santo Domingo. El presidente Trujillo solicitó a Ernest J. Swift, director de la división de operaciones en el exterior de la Cruz Roja Estadounidense, que inspeccionara toda la situación en Santo Domingo y le informara personalmente con sugerencias para mejorar y acelerar las labores de socorro y rehabilitación. Asimismo, los aviones continuaron volando entre la zona de la tormenta y Port-au-Prince, Haití, completando un reconocimiento aéreo de las zonas periféricas, mientras los trabajadores de socorro destacaban el gran número de heridos graves, muchos de ellos necesitados de las medidas más extremas por parte de los ya sobrecargados médicos y cirujanos militares y civiles, a falta aún de un recuento oficial del total de muertos.

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo dated September 10
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo dated September 10 reports that British marines and the medical unit from the British cruiser Danae landed to assist Dominican authorities and relieve Dominican troops on guard since the hurricane, following arrangements between President Trujillo and British Charge d'Affaires Gallienne that also placed the warship's technicians and hospital at the President's disposal. For the first time in a week, the city's population had enough food after a small fleet of relief ships and trucks from the interior brought sufficient provisions, medicines, shelters, clothing, doctors, nurses, and relief workers to feed 10,000 or more people in the bread lines. In addition, surgical care for the injured was bolstered by the opening of the 1,000-bed Roosevelt Emergency Tent Hospital.

Por primera vez en una semana, la población de la ciudad contó con alimentos suficientes después de que una pequeña flota de barcos de socorro y camiones procedentes del interior trajeron provisiones, medicinas, refugios, ropa, médicos, enfermeras y trabajadores de auxilio suficientes para alimentar a 10,000 o más personas en las filas de reparto. From Sumter, South Carolina, on September 10, an Associated Press dispatch states that Marine Corps flier Major Roy Geiger and United States Navy pilots Lieutenant A. P. Storrs and C. F. Harper were forced down there by fog while flying a squadron of three planes to hurricane sufferers in Santo Domingo. After leaving Norfolk the previous day and making an overnight stop at Fort Bragg, North Carolina, the fliers hoped to reach Jacksonville if the weather cleared and proceed via Miami and Havana, with each plane carrying approximately 2,000 pounds of anti-toxins, anaesthetics, surgical dressings, and surgical instruments. A September 10 United Press dispatch from Washington adds that the destroyer U.S.S. Gilmer left Hampton Roads loaded with relief supplies for the Dominican Republic and is due at Santo Domingo at 8 a.m. on Saturday, September 13.

records.headline: Two telephoto captions from NEA Service depict scenes in the hurricane-wrecked
records.summary_en: Two telephoto captions from NEA Service depict scenes in the hurricane-wrecked city of Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, where a tropical storm killed 4,000 and injured many others. The upper view, taken from the customs house, shows the rehabilitation task facing the city as relief workers search for the dead and injured amid the ruins of waterfront buildings. The lower caption states that schoolhouses, churches, and other buildings that survived the storm were converted into temporary morgues and emergency hospitals, showing a nurse with two injured children orphaned by the hurricane inside a school.
records.summary_es: Dos pies de foto transmitidos por telefoto de NEA Service muestran escenas en la ciudad de Santo Domingo, República Dominicana, devastada por un huracán donde una tormenta tropical causó la muerte de 4,000 personas e hirió a muchas otras. La vista superior, tomada desde la aduana, muestra la labor de rehabilitación que enfrenta la ciudad mientras los trabajadores de socorro buscan muertos y heridos entre las ruinas de los edificios de la zona portuaria. El pie de foto inferior señala que las escuelas, iglesias y otros edificios que sobrevivieron a la tormenta fueron convertidos en morgues provisionales y hospitales de emergencia, mostrando a una enfermera con dos niños heridos que quedaron huérfanos por el huracán dentro de una escuela.

records.headline: Tonight it -was possible for the first time to drive through
records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* reported on catastrophic devastation in Santo Domingo caused by a hurricane that demolished poorer residential districts across a 160-square-mile area. President Rafael Trujillo assumed personal command of military forces to maintain order, clear debris, and organize relief before the arrival of outside assistance. Initial relief ships from Puerto Rico and commercial cable vessels landed medical units and provided emergency tents for 2,000 homeless survivors.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield Weekly Republican* informó sobre la devastación catastrófica en Santo Domingo causada por un huracán que demolió los distritos residenciales más humildes en un área de 160 millas cuadradas. El presidente Rafael Trujillo asumió el mando personal de las fuerzas militares para mantener el orden, despejar escombros y organizar el socorro antes de la llegada de ayuda exterior. Primeros barcos de auxilio procedentes de Puerto Rico y buques de tendido de cable comercial desembarcaron brigadas médicas y proveyeron tiendas de campaña de emergencia para 2 000 damnificados sin hogar.
records.passage: picks strewn over an area of 160 square miles. Tonight it was possible for the first time to drive through any of the streets of the ruined city to gain anything like an intelligent idea of the storm's wreckage. The poorer sections of the city suffered the most damage. Whole areas inhabited by thousands were completely wiped out, without a single house remaining to give shelter. President Rafael Trujillo took heroic measures in his own hands and with troops under his personal command began clearing the streets and roads. He also gave personal attention to maintaining order. Cable Ship Brings Tents When the first relief ships arrived today they found that the efforts of President Trujillo had resulted in shaping conditions so that more headway may be made than had been hoped for. But it will be next week before there are any street lights and it will still be several days before the town water can be turned on. The All-America Cable company's cable ship today brought tents for 2000 persons. Cable Engineer Judo, of the cable ship All-America, who was an eye-witness of the hurricane which hit San Juan, Porto Rico, in September, 1928, declared this afternoon that the destruction wrought by Wednesday's storm was much greater and that the storm's intensity exceeded the San Juan hurricane. A relief boat from Porto Rico also arrived today and the Porto Rican medical unit was landed. Additional supplies will be here tomorrow for the use of the doctors and nurses besides

Swift. A 1,000-bed tent hospital was established under U.S. Navy Commander L. W. Johnson to perform surgeries and treat injured residents. Dominican soldiers and armed bluejackets from the USS *Grebe* stood guard over supply trucks and wharves to prevent desperate crowds from looting incoming provisions.

Swift, de la Cruz Roja. Se levantó un hospital de campaña de 1 000 camas a cargo del comandante de la Armada de Estados Unidos L. W. Johnson para efectuar cirugías y atender a los heridos. Soldados dominicanos y marineros armados del USS *Grebe* custodiaban camiones de abastecimiento y muelles para evitar que multitudes desesperadas saquearan los víveres que arribaban.
records.passage: to the city itself, opened several rationing stations, and Director Ernest J. Swift estimated that 10,000 persons now are receiving rations daily. At one time today the crowd at a Red Cross food station became so large and so unmanageable for the civilians that Dominican soldiers were compelled to drive the crowd back before order could be restored. Food Supply Augmented Tonight for the first time in a week there were few among the city's homeless who were hungry. Imported food made possible the feeding of the thousands who had not only lost their homes and their loved ones, but also their sources of income. The food supply was greatly augmented by trucks bringing provisions from other parts of the Dominican republic. Surgical attention for the injured was greatly facilitated today with the opening of the Roosevelt emergency tent hospital, which has 1000 beds. Comdr. L. W. Johnson of the United States army was placed in charge of all the medical work in the city. Many Vessels In Port So many vessels arrived today that Capt. John Davis, chief of the port at Port-au-Prince, was delegated to the task of discharging their cargoes in an organized manner. At the same time, bluejackets from the United States ship Grebe were sent ashore to form an armed guard over food wagons passing from the wharves to the general warehouses from which relief is distributed. This latter emergency action was taken following yesterday's attempt by hungry citizens to wrest food from the handlers at the wharves. Comdr. John B. Pollard of the medi[illegible]

records.headline: In his column, Arthur Brisbane writes that an unceasing wind
records.summary_en: In his column, Arthur Brisbane writes that an unceasing wind blowing 150 miles an hour has destroyed Santo Domingo, chief city of the Dominican Republic. The wind leveled the houses of the prosperous class and picked up and carried away the lighter dwellings of the poor. According to the column, 50,000 people in Santo Domingo are menaced by hunger, thieves are operating in the ruins, and the storm continues onward toward the United States coast, though a modern airplane flying 200 or 250 miles an hour could safely fly ahead of and around it.
records.summary_es: En su columna, Arthur Brisbane escribe que un viento incesante de 150 millas por hora ha destruido Santo Domingo, ciudad principal de la República Dominicana. El viento arrasó las casas de la clase acomodada y levantó y se llevó las viviendas más ligeras de los pobres. Según la columna, 50,000 personas en Santo Domingo están amenazadas por el hambre, los ladrones operan entre las ruinas y la tormenta continúa su marcha hacia la costa de los Estados Unidos, aunque un avión moderno que vuele a 200 o 250 millas por hora podría volar con seguridad por delante y alrededor de ella.

records.headline: Two NEA Service telephoto captions dispatched to the Douglas
records.summary_en: Two NEA Service telephoto captions dispatched to the Douglas Daily Dispatch describe the aftermath of the tropical hurricane that reduced Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, to shattered lumber and uprooted trees. With fatalities estimated at some 4,000 persons and the threat of an epidemic following the storm, the first photograph, taken from the custom house looking toward the waterfront, shows workers searching the wreckage. The second caption notes that as disease swept hundreds to their death, the Hostos school in Santo Domingo was turned into an emergency hospital for thousands of sick and dying, and shows a nurse with two injured children orphaned by the disaster.
records.summary_es: Dos pies de foto transmitidos por telefoto de NEA Service y enviados al Douglas Daily Dispatch describen las secuelas del huracán tropical que redujo a Santo Domingo, República Dominicana, a madera destrozada y árboles arrancados de raíz. Con las víctimas mortales estimadas en unas 4,000 personas y la amenaza de una epidemia tras la tormenta, la primera fotografía, tomada desde la aduana mirando hacia la zona portuaria, muestra a los trabajadores registrando los escombros. El segundo pie de foto señala que, mientras las enfermedades llevaban a cientos a la muerte, la escuela Hostos en Santo Domingo fue convertida en un hospital de emergencia para miles de enfermos y moribundos, y muestra a una enfermera con dos niños heridos que quedaron huérfanos por el desastre.

records.headline: A dispatch from Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, reports that sailors
records.summary_en: A dispatch from Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, reports that sailors from the British cruiser Danae came ashore in the afternoon and significantly improved the appearance of the hurricane-stricken city's streets before nightfall. Dressed in white and wearing regulation cork helmets, the seamen were initially assigned in squads to direct local labor. They soon tired of merely directing, pitched in themselves, and removed large quantities of accumulated refuse that had been threatening to cause a serious epidemic.
records.summary_es: Un despacho desde Santo Domingo, República Dominicana, informa que marineros del crucero británico Danae desembarcaron por la tarde y mejoraron notablemente el aspecto de las calles de la ciudad azotada por el huracán antes del anochecer. Vestidos de blanco y con sus cascos de corcho reglamentarios, los marinos fueron asignados inicialmente en cuadrillas para dirigir a los trabajadores locales. Pronto se cansaron de limitarse a dirigir, pusieron manos a la obra ellos mismos y retiraron grandes cantidades de basura acumulada que amenazaba con provocar una grave epidemia.

records.headline: Rear-Admiral W. R. Sexton dispatched the destroyer U.S.S. Gilmer
records.summary_en: Rear-Admiral W. R. Sexton dispatched the destroyer U.S.S. Gilmer from Newport, Rhode Island, to New York harbor to stand by in case further medical aid is needed for Santo Domingo, acting under Navy Department orders. Meanwhile, President Trujillo cabled Dominican Minister Rafael Brache that hurricane devastation was increasing hourly, with an epidemic feared, 2,000 dead buried or burned, over 5,000 injured, and more than 30,000 homeless; he also cabled Pan-American Union director L. S. Rowe in appreciation of a suggestion that all American governments cooperate in relief. In a subsequent Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo, where 4,000 are reported dead and shelter virtually destroyed, the Legislature invested President Trujillo with all powers of the Dominican government to help save more than 1,090 badly injured hurricane victims from death by disease.
records.summary_es: El contralmirante W. R. Sexton despachó al destructor U.S.S. records.headline: Opening mid-report with figures for the capital alone placing
records.summary_en: Opening mid-report with figures for the capital alone placing the injured at about 5,000 and damages at $20,000,000, the article notes that Santo Domingo's 400-year-old cathedral and the tomb of Christopher Columbus inside it escaped destruction. Motorcycle messengers surveying the interior reported that the hurricane concentrated its fury on the capital, while the large towns of La Vega, Santiago, and Puerto Plata were undamaged. As residents took night refuge in surviving churches, schools, and public buildings, Senate President Mario Fermin Cabral, designated by President Trujillo to oversee feeding refugees and clearing debris from 10,000 destroyed buildings, began operating rolling kitchens for the hungry and homeless. A following Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo adds that the ruined capital is under martial law as the bodies of almost 1,000 men, women, and children burn on funeral pyres.
records.summary_es: Comenzando a mitad de un informe con cifras solo para la capital que sitúan a los heridos en unos 5,000 y los daños en $20,000,000, el artículo señala que la catedral de 400 años de antigüedad de Santo Domingo y la tumba de Cristóbal Colón en su interior escaparon a la destrucción. Mensajeros en motocicleta que inspeccionaron el interior informaron que el huracán concentró su furia en la capital, mientras que las grandes localidades de La Vega, Santiago y Puerto Plata no sufrieron daños. Mientras los residentes se refugiaban por la noche en las iglesias, escuelas y edificios públicos que quedaron en pie, el presidente del Senado, Mario Fermin Cabral, designado por el presidente Trujillo para supervisar la alimentación de los refugiados y la remoción de escombros de 10,000 edificios destruidos, puso en funcionamiento cocinas rodantes para los hambrientos y desamparados. Un despacho subsiguiente de la Associated Press desde Santo Domingo añade que la capital en ruinas se encuentra bajo ley marcial mientras los cuerpos de casi 1,000 hombres, mujeres y niños arden en grandes piras funerarias.

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo dated September 12
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo dated September 12 states that the Dominican Republic's need for a loan to meet the hurricane emergency will be placed before President Hoover for final approval. Under an agreement more than 25 years old, the Dominican Republic cannot increase its exterior indebtedness without the consent of the United States. The Dominican government is seeking a $3,000,000 loan, allocating $1,000,000 for government public works and reconstruction and $2,000,000 for limited private loans to individuals on first mortgages at a low interest rate.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de la Associated Press fechado el 12 de septiembre en Santo Domingo indica que la necesidad de la República Dominicana de obtener un préstamo para hacer frente a la emergencia provocada por el huracán será presentada ante el presidente Hoover para su aprobación definitiva. En virtud de un acuerdo de más de 25 años de antigüedad, la República Dominicana no puede aumentar su deuda externa sin el consentimiento de los Estados Unidos. El gobierno dominicano busca un préstamo de $3,000,000, del cual se destinarán $1,000,000 a obras públicas gubernamentales y reconstrucción, y $2,000,000 a préstamos privados limitados para particulares sobre primeras hipotecas a una baja tasa de interés.

records.headline: Under a world news roundup, the column reports that a tropical hurricane
records.summary_en: Under a world news roundup, the column reports that a tropical hurricane with winds reported as traveling 360 miles an hour at the height of its force swept Santo Domingo, capital of the Dominican Republic, on Friday, laying waste to the city of 50,000 people. The storm killed over 1,200 people, injured 5,000, and caused material damage estimated at over $20,000,000, though the ancient city's 400-year-old cathedral containing the tomb of Christopher Columbus survived. Dead bodies had to be burned in huge funeral pyres, and overland and air relief expeditions were immediately launched to address water shortages and scarce food supplies for the survivors.
records.summary_es: En un resumen de noticias mundiales, la columna informa que un huracán tropical con vientos reportados en 360 millas por hora en su punto máximo azotó el viernes Santo Domingo, capital de la República Dominicana, devastando la ciudad de 50,000 habitantes. La tormenta causó la muerte de más de 1,200 personas, dejó 5,000 heridos y provocó daños materiales estimados en más de $20,000,000, aunque la catedral de 400 años de antigüedad de la ciudad antigua, que alberga la tumba de Cristóbal Colón, sobrevivió. Los cadáveres tuvieron que ser incinerados en enormes piras funerarias, y de inmediato se enviaron expediciones de socorro por aire y tierra para atender la escasez de agua y de alimentos entre los sobrevivientes.

records.headline: After blasting across the Dominican Republic several days earlier
records.summary_en: After blasting across the Dominican Republic several days earlier and losing its force against the Dominican mountains, the hurricane wandered over Cuba, the Gulf, and Florida before regaining strength in the Atlantic. According to a September 12 United Press dispatch from Newbern, North Carolina, the full force of the renewed storm was believed to have struck the North Carolina coast on Friday afternoon. High winds and severe rains were reported at Morehead City and Beaufort before all telephone communication with towns in the disturbance's path ended at 2:45 o'clock.
records.summary_es: Tras abrirse paso de forma devastadora a través de la República Dominicana varios días antes y perder su fuerza contra las montañas dominicanas, el huracán vagó sobre Cuba, el Golfo y Florida antes de recobrar intensidad en el Atlántico. Según un despacho de la United Press fechado el 12 de septiembre en Newbern, Carolina del Norte, se creía que toda la fuerza de la renovada tormenta había golpeado la costa de Carolina del Norte el viernes por la tarde. Se registraron fuertes vientos y lluvias intensas en Morehead City y Beaufort antes de que toda comunicación telefónica con las localidades situadas en la trayectoria de la perturbación se interrumpiera a las 2:45.

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, dated September 13 reports that Major Thomas E. Watson of the United States Marines, formerly the superior officer of Rafael Trujillo, was officially assigned as naval attaché of the American legation. At the request of President Trujillo, Major Watson will serve as food administrator during the hurricane relief crisis. On the same day, three United States Marine transport airplanes commanded by Major Roy Geiger completed their journey from Newport News and landed Red Cross supplies in the city.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de la Associated Press fechado el 13 de septiembre en Santo Domingo, República Dominicana, informa que el mayor Thomas E. Watson, del Cuerpo de Marines de los Estados Unidos y antiguo oficial superior de Rafael Trujillo, fue asignado oficialmente como agregado naval de la legación estadounidense. A petición del presidente Trujillo, el mayor Watson desempeñará el cargo de administrador de alimentos durante la crisis de socorro por el huracán. Ese mismo día, tres aviones de transporte de los Marines de los Estados Unidos bajo el mando del mayor Roy Geiger completaron su viaje desde Newport News y desembarcaron suministros de la Cruz Roja en la ciudad.

records.headline: The hurricane in Santo Domingo has prompted calls for greater
records.summary_en: The hurricane in Santo Domingo has prompted calls for greater study of radio communication and Weather Bureau methods to reduce storm damage and avoid distress. Quoting editorial reactions from several newspapers, the piece cites the Zanesville Signal, which remarks that the Caribbean region and the island home of the Dominican Republic seem decreed to be a permanent home of turmoil and disaster. Additional commentary from the Columbus Ohio State Journal, the Birmingham News, and the Hamilton (Ontario) Spectator reflects on the destructive power of Caribbean hurricanes and humanity's helplessness before such tropical storms.
records.summary_es: El huracán en Santo Domingo ha motivado llamados a profundizar el estudio de las comunicaciones por radio y los métodos del Negociado del Tiempo para reducir los daños de las tormentas y evitar desgracias. Citando reacciones editoriales de varios periódicos, el texto recoge palabras del Zanesville Signal, el cual señala que la región del Caribe y la isla que alberga a la República Dominicana parecen condenadas a ser morada permanente de agitación y desastre. Comentarios adicionales del Columbus Ohio State Journal, el Birmingham News y el Hamilton (Ontario) Spectator reflexionan sobre el poder destructivo de los huracanes del Caribe y la impotencia de la humanidad ante tales tormentas tropicales.

records.headline: Dr. Isern informed the president that a 1,000-patient medical establishment
records.summary_en: Dr. Isern informed the president that a 1,000-patient medical establishment equipped with an operating tent, cook fly, and the San Juan municipal motor ambulance would be turned over to the Dominican Republic once the Porto Rican personnel withdraws after the emergency, the report states, opening mid-article. Although medical conditions have improved and British sailors and marines from the cruiser Danae continue supervising street cleaning—with the U.S. destroyer Gilmer expected the next day with medical supplies—officials fear rains could trigger influenza or other epidemics unless temporary housing is provided for those living outdoors. In a September 11 Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo, a hurricane property-loss survey committee met with President Trujillo and made preliminary plans to seek a $3,000,000 emergency loan in the United States, while the American Red Cross was reported feeding 18,000 in one section of the city and Trujillo weighed provisions for 30,000 shelterless refugees.
records.summary_es: El Dr. Isern informó al presidente que una instalación médica con capacidad para 1,000 pacientes, equipada con carpa de operaciones, toldo de cocina y la ambulancia motora municipal de San Juan, sería entregada a la República Dominicana una vez que el personal puertorriqueño se retire tras pasar la emergencia, según el informe, que comienza a mitad de artículo. Aunque la situación médica ha mejorado y los marineros e infantes de marina británicos del crucero Danae continúan supervisando la limpieza de las calles —esperándose para el día siguiente al destructor estadounidense Gilmer con suministros médicos—, existe inquietud de que las lluvias provoquen influenza u otras epidemias si no se proporciona alojamiento temporal a quienes viven a la intemperie. En un despacho de la Associated Press fechado el 11 de septiembre en Santo Domingo, un comité encargado de evaluar las pérdidas materiales del huracán se reunió con el presidente Trujillo e hizo planes preliminares para gestionar un préstamo de emergencia de $3,000,000 en los Estados Unidos, mientras se informaba que la Cruz Roja Estadounidense alimentaba a 18,000 personas en un sector de la ciudad y Trujillo consideraba necesario atender a 30,000 refugiados sin techo.

records.headline: President Rafael Trujillo personally took charge of immediate
records.summary_en: President Rafael Trujillo personally took charge of immediate relief work in the Dominican Republic, putting the entire army to work aiding sufferers while Santo Domingo officials and newspapers appealed to the United States and received a swift response from the Red Cross. American Minister Curtis cabled the State Department in Washington that although he lacked reports from the interior, loss of life there was probably small, whereas around the capital winds estimated at 150 miles an hour had wrecked all bridges, made roads impassable, and destroyed telegraph wires. As the storm moved from the southeast toward eastern Cuba and the Florida straits, disrupting regional communications, the Porto Rico liner Coamo bound for Santo Domingo passed through the center of the hurricane and had to turn back to San Juan in a battered condition.
records.summary_es: El presidente Rafael Trujillo asumió personalmente el mando de las labores inmediatas de socorro en la República Dominicana, poniendo a trabajar a todo el ejército para ayudar a los damnificados mientras funcionarios y periódicos de Santo Domingo apelaban a los Estados Unidos y recibían una rápida respuesta de la Cruz Roja. El ministro estadounidense Curtis envió un cable al Departamento de Estado en Washington indicando que, aunque carecía de informes del interior, la pérdida de vidas allí era probablemente pequeña, mientras que en los alrededores de la capital los vientos estimados en 150 millas por hora habían destrozado todos los puentes, dejado intransitables los caminos y destruido los cables telegráficos. Mientras la tormenta avanzaba desde el sureste hacia el extremo oriental de Cuba y el estrecho de Florida, interrumpiendo las comunicaciones regionales, el vapor puertorriqueño Coamo, que se dirigía a Santo Domingo, atravesó el centro mismo del huracán y tuvo que regresar a San Juan en estado maltrecho.

records.headline: President Hoover has selected Eliot Wadsworth of Boston, former Assistant Secretary of the Treasury
records.summary_en: President Hoover has selected Eliot Wadsworth of Boston, former Assistant Secretary of the Treasury and an officer of the American Red Cross, to go to Santo Domingo on a special mission to develop a financial and reconstruction program for the Dominican Republic. Announcing the appointment at the White House, the President explained that he chose Mr. Wadsworth for the task because of his familiarity with financial matters from his Treasury service and his experience in Red Cross work.
records.summary_es: El presidente Hoover ha seleccionado a Eliot Wadsworth, de Boston, ex subsecretario del Tesoro y directivo de la Cruz Roja Estadounidense, para viajar a Santo Domingo en una misión especial con el fin de elaborar un programa financiero y de reconstrucción para la República Dominicana. Al dar a conocer el nombramiento en la Casa Blanca, el presidente explicó que eligió al señor Wadsworth para esta tarea debido a su familiaridad con los asuntos financieros adquirida durante su servicio en el Tesoro y a su experiencia en las labores de la Cruz Roja.

records.headline: Reviewing the 1930 hurricane that swept across the Caribbean Sea
records.summary_en: Reviewing the 1930 hurricane that swept across the Caribbean Sea on September 1 and struck the eastern end of the island shared by the Republic of Haiti and the Dominican Republic, the Watauga Democrat reports that a population was plunged from moderate prosperity into want. Santo Domingo, capital of the Dominican Republic and a city of 40,000 people, took the full force of winds estimated at 160 miles an hour and suffered property damage estimated at more than $50,000,000. Not one person in four escaped without physical injury, and a complete count of the dead is expected to show that one out of every eight inhabitants in the city alone perished. The commentary adds that Caribbean islanders face the hurricane hazard every September and compares the storm to the 1900 hurricane at Galveston, Texas, thirty years earlier.
records.summary_es: Al repasar el huracán de 1930 que barrió el mar Caribe el 1 de septiembre y azotó el extremo oriental de la isla que comparten la República de Haití y la República Dominicana, el Watauga Democrat informa que una población quedó sumida de una prosperidad moderada en la indigencia. Santo Domingo, capital de la República Dominicana y ciudad de 40,000 habitantes, recibió toda la fuerza de vientos estimados en 160 millas por hora y sufrió daños a la propiedad calculados en más de $50,000,000. Ni una de cada cuatro personas escapó sin lesiones físicas, y se espera que el recuento completo de los muertos muestre que tan solo en la ciudad pereció uno de cada ocho habitantes. El comentario añade que los habitantes de las islas del Caribe enfrentan el peligro de los huracanes cada septiembre y compara la tormenta con el huracán de 1900 en Galveston, Texas, ocurrido treinta años atrás.

records.headline: Physicians, nurses, relief workers, and large quantities of food
records.summary_en: Physicians, nurses, relief workers, and large quantities of food, clothing, and medicines from the United States, Cuba, Haiti, and Porto Rico arrived in Santo Domingo following the storm. An army of men was put to work cleaning up the stricken capital of the Dominican Republic. Securing a water supply and clearing the streets of bodies and debris reduced the threat of pestilence.

Un ejército de hombres fue puesto a trabajar en la limpieza de la devastada capital de la República Dominicana. La obtención de un suministro de agua y el despeje de cadáveres y escombros de las calles redujeron el peligro de peste.

records.summary_en: An October 3 dispatch from Santo Domingo reports that the Dominican government and populace observed a day of national mourning one month after the hurricane, holding services in the cathedral and a pilgrimage of thousands to the Plaza Colombina for ceremonies honoring the dead buried or burned there after the catastrophe. Some emergency hospitals are concluding their work as patients recover, while provisioning and the housing of homeless men have been eased by constructing barracks in an elevated section of the city. Eliot Wadsworth, representing President Hoover, is continuing his investigation of conditions regarding a possible reconstruction loan, and it is generally believed that the storm's damage will be repaired within five years, transforming the capital into a modern city.
records.summary_es: Un despacho del 3 de octubre desde Santo Domingo informa que el gobierno y el pueblo dominicanos observaron un día de duelo nacional un mes después del huracán, celebrando oficios en la catedral y una peregrinación de miles de personas a la Plaza Colombina para ceremonias en memoria de los muertos sepultados o incinerados allí tras la catástrofe. Algunos hospitales de emergencia están concluyendo su labor a medida que los pacientes se recuperan, mientras que el aprovisionamiento y el alojamiento de los hombres sin hogar se han facilitado mediante la construcción de barracas en una parte elevada de la ciudad. Eliot Wadsworth, en representación del presidente Hoover, continúa su investigación de las condiciones en relación con un posible préstamo de reconstrucción, y se cree generalmente que los efectos del huracán serán reparados en un plazo de cinco años, transformando la capital en una ciudad moderna.

El presidente Trujillo de la República Dominicana ofreció un banquete de Estado en su honor el miércoles por la noche.

records.headline: Arriving on a steamer from the Caribbean, Texas native and World War flier
records.summary_en: Arriving on a steamer from the Caribbean, Texas native and World War flier Willard S. Wade, a former flying instructor for the insular government, brought the twisted remnants of his airplane to trade toward a new plane at a Detroit factory before flying back to Santo Domingo via Miami, with a final 900-mile hop over water. He stated that his plane, with which he had assisted General Rafael Trujillo's coup d'état in February, was wrecked in the recent island hurricane alongside two military planes, destroying all three aircraft that made up the island republic's air fleet. Serving as General Trujillo's entire aerial expeditionary force during the coup, he recounted flying over enemy bivouacs in the mountains and dropping large homemade cannon crackers, after which conciliatory foes swarmed the lowlands the next day without a single casualty.
records.summary_es: Al llegar en un vapor procedente del Caribe, el aviador de la Guerra Mundial y nativo de Texas Willard S. Wade, exinstructor de vuelo del gobierno insular, trajo consigo los restos retorcidos de su aeroplano para darlos a cuenta de un avión nuevo en una fábrica de Detroit antes de volar de regreso a Santo Domingo vía Miami, con un tramo final de 900 millas sobre el agua. Declaró que su avión, con el cual había ayudado en el golpe de Estado del general Rafael Trujillo en febrero, quedó destrozado en el reciente huracán de la isla junto con dos aviones militares, destruyéndose los tres aparatos que integraban la flota aérea de la república isleña. Habiendo constituido toda la fuerza expedicionaria aérea del general Trujillo durante el golpe, relató haber sobrevolado los vivaques enemigos en las montañas y arrojado grandes petardos de fabricación casera, tras lo cual al día siguiente las tierras bajas se llenaron de adversarios conciliadores sin que se registraran bajas.

records.summary_en: Listing Archbishop Nouel's titles—including Ex-President of the Dominican Republic, Primate of America, Knight of the Great Cross of the Constantinian Order of St. George and of the Order of the Holy Sepulchre, Assistant to the Pontifical Throne, Officer of the Legion of Honor, Commendador of the Crown of Italy, and Most Meritorious Pastor of the Arcadia of Rome—the Washington Daily News reports that he is seeking funds for the churches of Santo Domingo destroyed by the hurricane. Thus far his fundraising has not been very successful, though he has been presented with a portable altar that he carries on his travels. The paper remarks that this should interest the Dominican Republic, as there is not a single portable altar in the entire country.

records.headline: Answering the question "What is the oldest city in the new world
records.summary_en: Answering the question "What is the oldest city in the new world?", an informational item in the Milwaukee Leader states that Santo Domingo, capital of the Dominican Republic, is the oldest city in the New World settled by Europeans. It contrasts Santo Domingo with Panama City, founded by the Spanish in 1519 as the oldest white settlement on the American mainland, as well as older cities of indigenous origin such as Mexico City, settled about 1325, and Cuzco, Peru, inhabited since the 10th century.

El texto contrasta a Santo Domingo con la ciudad de Panamá, fundada por los españoles en 1519 como el asentamiento blanco más antiguo en tierra firme americana, así como con ciudades más antiguas de origen indígena como la Ciudad de México, establecida hacia 1325, y Cuzco, Perú, habitada desde el siglo X.

records.headline: Reporting on the previous day's schedule of the Archbishop of Santo
records.summary_en: Reporting on the previous day's schedule of the Archbishop of Santo Domingo, the Most Rev. Mons. Nouel, the Washington Daily News notes that he met with Secretary Stimson, laid a wreath at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, attended a luncheon hosted by Pan American Union director Dr. Leo S. Rowe, and dined with Dr. F. L. Benton, a former Marine Corps officer long stationed in the Dominican Republic. Prominent churchmen invited to meet the archbishop at luncheon included Cardinal Mundelein of Chicago, Cardinal Hayes of New York, Apostolic Delegate Pietro Fumasoni-Biondi, and Archbishop Curley and Bishop McNamara of Baltimore. Senor Don Gonzalo Galvan and Senor Don Ramon Nadal of Archbishop Nouel's suite accompanied him.

Rowe, y cenó con el Dr. F. L. Benton, exoficial del Cuerpo de Marines que estuvo destacado durante largo tiempo en la República Dominicana. Entre los destacados prelados invitados a conocer al arzobispo en el almuerzo figuraron el cardenal Mundelein de Chicago, el cardenal Hayes de Nueva York, el delegado apostólico Pietro Fumasoni-Biondi, y el arzobispo Curley y el obispo McNamara de Baltimore. Acompañaron al arzobispo Nouel los señores don Gonzalo Galvan y don Ramon Nadal, miembros de su comitiva.

records.headline: Reporting on the aftermath of the hurricane in which Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: Reporting on the aftermath of the hurricane in which Santo Domingo was almost totally wrecked, the Wolf Point Herald notes that the American Red Cross contributed $50,000 from its treasury toward relief work while other nations also sent generous aid to the republic. United States Navy and Marine aviators flew in Red Cross medical supplies and established communications, and an expert relief director was sent to assist the American committee organized by Governor Theodore Roosevelt of neighboring Porto Rico. The article adds that President Trujillo of the Dominican Republic organized the nation's forces to care for the injured and safeguard the health of survivors.
records.summary_es: Al informar sobre las secuelas del huracán en el que Santo Domingo quedó casi totalmente destruida, el Wolf Point Herald señala que la Cruz Roja Americana aportó $50,000 de su tesoro para las labores de socorro, mientras que otras naciones también enviaron generosa ayuda a la república. Aviadores de la Marina y del Cuerpo de Marines de los Estados Unidos transportaron suministros médicos de la Cruz Roja y establecieron comunicaciones, y se envió a un director experto en socorro para asistir al comité estadounidense organizado por el gobernador Theodore Roosevelt de la vecina isla de Porto Rico. El artículo añade que el presidente Trujillo de la República Dominicana organizó las fuerzas de la nación para atender a los heridos y proteger la salud de los sobrevivientes.

records.summary_en: Dr. L. S. Rowe, director general of the Pan-American Union, hosted a luncheon at the Pan-American annex in honor of members of the Dominican Republic's cabinet: Lic. Elias Brache Hijo, secretary of justice, public instruction, and fine arts; Lic. Roberto Despradel, secretary of finance; and Rafael Vidal, secretary of the presidency. Also attending were Dominican Minister to Washington Dr. Rafael Brache, Dominican legation secretary Dr. Persio C. Franco, U.S. Minister to Honduras Julius G. Lay, Pan-American Union assistant director Dr. Esteban Gil Borges, State Department officials Walter C. Thurston, H. Percival Dodge, and Dr. William R. records.headline: Santo Domingo, capital of the Dominican Republic, was destroyed
records.summary_en: Santo Domingo, capital of the Dominican Republic, was destroyed by a hurricane, with the dead numbering about 4,000, the Evening Star records under August in a chronological review of major disasters of 1930. Alongside the Santo Domingo catastrophe, the chronology lists the sinking of the British steamer Tahiti in the mid-Pacific, fatal earthquakes in Italy and the Soviet Republic of Tadjikistan, a bridge collapse at Coblenz, Germany, and a sandboat capsizing in Lake Erie.
records.summary_es: Santo Domingo, capital de la República Dominicana, fue destruida por un huracán, con un número de muertos de alrededor de 4,000, según registra el Evening Star bajo el mes de agosto en un recuento cronológico de los principales desastres de 1930. Junto a la catástrofe de Santo Domingo, la cronología enumera el hundimiento del vapor británico Tahiti en medio del Pacífico, terremotos mortales en Italia y en la República Soviética de Tadjikistán, el derrumbe de un puente en Coblenza, Alemania, y el vuelco de un barco arenero en el lago Erie.

records.headline: As a preliminary to these events there was a revolution In the Dominican republic in February
records.summary_en: The *Ronan Pioneer* reviewed Latin American political changes in 1930, noting that revolutionary upheavals began in February when Dominican President Horacio Vásquez sought reelection. Vásquez was forced from office after brief skirmishes and succeeded temporarily by General Estrella Ureña. In subsequent elections held on May 16, General Rafael Trujillo was elected president, officially taking office three months later.
records.summary_es: El *Ronan Pioneer* repasó las transformaciones políticas latinoamericanas en 1930, destacando que las conmociones revolucionarias se iniciaron en febrero cuando el presidente dominicano Horacio Vásquez pretendió reelegirse. Vásquez fue forzado a renunciar tras breves escaramuzas y sucedido transitoriamente por el general Estrella Ureña. En los comicios posteriores del 16 de mayo, el general Rafael Trujillo resultó electo presidente, asumiendo oficialmente el cargo tres meses más tarde.
records.passage: virtual dictators were ousted. Four new governments were established. As a preliminary to these events there was a revolution in the Dominican republic in February, the immediate cause being the announced intention of President Horacio Vasquez to stand for re-election. After a few skirmishes Vasquez was forced out of office, [illegible] succeeded temporarily by General Urena. Elections were held on May 16 and Gen. Rafael Trujillo was chosen president and inaugurated three months later. Bolivia was next on the list. There Dr. Hernando Siles tried, like Vasquez, to perpetuate his rule and was driven from office in May by the insurgents. He was permitted to take refuge in Chile, and his much hated right hand man, Gen. Hans Kundt of Prussia, fled back to his German home. A military junta took over the government, its chief being Gen. Carlos Blanco Galindo. Peru followed suit in August. The officers of the army led a movement against President Augusto B. Leguia, who had held the office for more than ten years and considered himself almost irremovable. He was forced to resign, turning over his powers to a military junta, and later Lieut. Col. Luis M. Sanchez Cerro was made provisional president. Leguia had been recognized as an efficient business president and Peru made great material strides during his regime, but the revolutionists accused him of "denial of civil liberties" and also of nepotism and the sale of concessions. He was imprisoned to await trial.

records.summary_en: Reviewing Latin American revolutions that ousted four virtual dictators and established four new governments, The Dermott News notes a preliminary February revolution in the Dominican Republic sparked by President Horacio Vasquez's announced intention to seek re-election. Following a few skirmishes, Vasquez was forced from office and temporarily succeeded by General Urena. General Rafael Trujillo was elected president on May 16 and inaugurated three months later.

Tras algunas escaramuzas, Vasquez fue obligado a dejar el cargo y sucedido temporalmente por el general Urena. El general Rafael Trujillo fue elegido presidente el 16 de mayo e investido tres meses después.

The chronicle also noted that General Rafael Trujillo was elected president of the country on May 16.

records.headline: Recounting how four virtual dictators were ousted and four new governments
records.summary_en: Recounting how four virtual dictators were ousted and four new governments established in Latin America, The Midland Journal reports that a preliminary revolution broke out in the Dominican Republic in February after President Horacio Vasquez announced his intention to run for re-election. After a few skirmishes, Vasquez was driven from office and temporarily succeeded by General Urena. Elections on May 16 chose General Rafael Trujillo as president, and he was inaugurated three months later.
records.summary_es: Al relatar cómo cuatro dictadores virtuales fueron derrocados y cuatro nuevos gobiernos establecidos en América Latina, The Midland Journal informa que en febrero estalló una revolución preliminar en la República Dominicana después de que el presidente Horacio Vasquez anunciara su intención de postularse a la reelección. Tras algunas escaramuzas, Vasquez fue expulsado del cargo y sucedido temporalmente por el general Urena. Las elecciones del 16 de mayo eligieron como presidente al general Rafael Trujillo, quien fue investido tres meses más tarde.

Subsequent entries note that Dominican rebels occupied the capital without bloodshed on February 26 and that a provisional government for the Dominican Republic was arranged under insurgent leader Urena on February 28.

Las entradas siguientes señalan que los rebeldes dominicanos ocuparon la capital sin derramamiento de sangre el 26 de febrero y que el 28 de febrero se organizó un gobierno provisional para la República Dominicana bajo el líder insurgente Urena.

records.summary_en: Revolt flamed in four South American republics, ousting four virtual dictators and establishing four new governments, the Nogales International reports under the heading "Latin-American Revolutions." As a preliminary to those events, a revolution broke out in the Dominican Republic in February, its immediate cause the announced intention of President Horacio Vasquez to stand for re-election. After a few skirmishes Vasquez was forced out of office and succeeded temporarily by General Urena; in elections held on May 16, General Rafael Trujillo was chosen president and inaugurated three months later.
records.summary_es: La revuelta estalló en cuatro repúblicas sudamericanas, derrocando a cuatro dictadores virtuales y estableciendo cuatro nuevos gobiernos, según el Nogales International bajo el título «Revoluciones latinoamericanas». Como preludio de esos acontecimientos, en febrero se produjo una revolución en la República Dominicana, cuya causa inmediata fue la intención anunciada del presidente Horacio Vasquez de presentarse a la reelección. Tras algunas escaramuzas, Vasquez se vio obligado a dejar el cargo y fue sucedido temporalmente por el general Urena; en las elecciones celebradas el 16 de mayo, el general Rafael Trujillo resultó elegido presidente y tomó posesión tres meses después.

records.headline: Dr. Adolfo Alejandro Nouel y Bobadilla, Archbishop of Santo
records.summary_en: Dr. Adolfo Alejandro Nouel y Bobadilla, Archbishop of Santo Domingo, made his first airplane flight to visit his friend Alden Freeman at Miami Beach, an Associated Press dispatch from Miami dated January 3 reports. The prelate, who presides over the Santo Domingo cathedral where Christopher Columbus's bones lie, called the flight enjoyable but lonesome and noisy, contrasting the modern world's hurry with Santo Domingo, where there is time to ponder and meditate. The article notes that he had previously visited New York, Washington, and other Eastern cities to seek disaster relief funds for the Dominican Republic following an autumn hurricane.
records.summary_es: El Dr. Adolfo Alejandro Nouel y Bobadilla, arzobispo de Santo Domingo, realizó su primer vuelo en avión para visitar a su amigo Alden Freeman en Miami Beach, según un despacho de la Associated Press fechado en Miami el 3 de enero. El prelado, quien preside la catedral de Santo Domingo donde reposan los restos de Cristóbal Colón, calificó el vuelo de agradable pero solitario y ruidoso, contrastando la prisa del mundo moderno con Santo Domingo, donde hay tiempo para reflexionar y meditar. El artículo señala que anteriormente había visitado Nueva York, Washington y otras ciudades del este para recaudar fondos de socorro para la República Dominicana tras un huracán otoñal.

records.headline: In a review of Latin American revolutions that ousted four virtual
records.summary_en: In a review of Latin American revolutions that ousted four virtual dictators and established four new governments, the Farmers Independent recounts a preliminary February revolution in the Dominican Republic caused by President Horacio Vasquez's announced intention to stand for re-election. After a few skirmishes, Vasquez was forced out of office and temporarily succeeded by General Urena. General Rafael Trujillo was chosen president in the May 16 elections and inaugurated three months later.
records.summary_es: En un repaso de las revoluciones latinoamericanas que derrocaron a cuatro dictadores virtuales y establecieron cuatro nuevos gobiernos, el Farmers Independent relata una revolución preliminar ocurrida en febrero en la República Dominicana, causada por la intención anunciada del presidente Horacio Vasquez de presentarse a la reelección. Tras algunas escaramuzas, Vasquez fue obligado a dejar el cargo y sucedido temporalmente por el general Urena. El general Rafael Trujillo fue elegido presidente en los comicios del 16 de mayo e investido tres meses después.

records.summary_en: The *Daily Worker* condemned U.S. support for General Trujillo's regime in the Dominican Republic, noting heavy American capital investments and the use of U.S. currency on the island. Citing declarations from the Caribbean Red Aid, the publication alleged that Dominican authorities arbitrarily arrested workers as vagrants to condemn them to forced labor in brutal prisons. The editorial demanded that U.S. officials apply the same forced-labor import bans to Dominican sugar, cocoa, and tobacco that were imposed against Soviet imports.
records.summary_es: El *Daily Worker* condenó el respaldo estadounidense al régimen del general Trujillo en la República Dominicana, resaltando las cuantiosas inversiones de capital norteamericano y el uso de la moneda de Estados Unidos en la isla. Citando declaraciones del Socorro Rojo del Caribe, el diario denunció que las autoridades dominicanas arrestaban arbitrariamente a trabajadores bajo cargos de vagancia para destinarlos a trabajos forzados en prisiones brutales. El editorial exigió a los funcionarios de Washington aplicar al azúcar, cacao y tabaco dominicanos las mismas restricciones de importación por trabajo forzado impuestas a los productos soviéticos.

Yet what do we hear about forced labor — not in the Soviet Union — but right here at America's doorstep and under its control? The workers' defense organization known as the Caribbean Red Aid, in a recent statement on conditions in Santo Domingo, protests at the terror against the Dominican working class, and says: "The troops stop and question workers in the streets of all the cities of the country and after brief questions and replies declare the passers-by 'vagrants' and take them off under arrest. records.headline: A mail dispatch from Santo Domingo reports that forced labor
records.summary_en: A mail dispatch from Santo Domingo reports that forced labor is growing in the Dominican Republic, where workers are systematically arrested for "vagrancy" and made to work without pay so the government can obtain free labor to repair the republic's bridges. According to the correspondent, 300 workers were recently arrested on vagrancy charges, and the next day in pouring rain soldiers held 500 more in the public square before hundreds of inhabitants, asking if they were employed and forcing them to join the prisoners without waiting for an answer. The article adds that a boy supporting his mother by selling bread from a pushcart was forced to abandon his cart and join the captives, leaving his mother destitute, while soldiers wait for quitting time to seize employed workers.
records.summary_es: Un despacho por correo desde Santo Domingo informa que el trabajo forzado va en aumento en la República Dominicana, donde los trabajadores son arrestados sistemáticamente bajo cargos de «vagancia» y obligados a laborar sin paga para que el gobierno obtenga mano de obra gratuita destinada a reparar los puentes de la república. Según el corresponsal, recientemente fueron arrestados 300 trabajadores por vagancia y, al día siguiente, bajo una lluvia torrencial, los soldados retuvieron a otros 500 en la plaza pública ante cientos de habitantes, preguntándoles si tenían empleo y obligándolos brutalmente a unirse a los detenidos sin esperar respuesta. El artículo añade que un joven que mantenía a su madre vendiendo pan en una carretilla fue obligado a abandonarla y a sumarse a los cautivos, dejando a su madre en la indigencia, mientras los soldados esperan la hora de salida del trabajo para abordar a los obreros empleados.

records.headline: A critic who had consistently denounced the crimes of the Dominican Republic's dictator
records.summary_en: A critic who had consistently denounced the crimes of the Dominican Republic's dictator was recently attacked in the newspaper Listin Diario, this fragment reports, opening mid-sentence. The writer asserts that American imperialists willingly assist in creating forced labor in the Dominican Republic because they receive the profits. According to the passage, the Listin Diario article was written by Manuel Pazos, secretary of the Dominican Federation of Labor, whom the paper characterizes as a paid lackey of the Santo Domingo government who declared himself "satisfied" with the government while remaining silent about the forced labor of Dominican workers.

El articulista afirma que los imperialistas estadounidenses ayudan gustosamente a crear el trabajo forzado en la República Dominicana porque obtienen las ganancias. Según el pasaje, el artículo del Listín Diario fue escrito por Manuel Pazos, secretario de la Federación Dominicana del Trabajo, a quien el diario califica de lacayo a sueldo del gobierno de Santo Domingo que se declaró «satisfecho» con dicho gobierno mientras guarda silencio sobre el trabajo forzado de los obreros dominicanos.

records.summary_en: A business report listing communities where utilities are operated by a Chicago firm and companies affiliated with Central Public Service includes Santiago and San Pedro in the Dominican Republic alongside numerous municipalities in the United States and the Philippine Islands. BELGRADE, Jugoslavia, September 3. — Jugoslavia, Kingdom of the Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, returned to constitutional government today after more than two years of dictatorship under the iron fist of King Alexander. Gen. Peter Zivkovitch, president of the Jugoslavian cabinet, today handed King Alexander his resignation and that of his ministry in conformance with the King's decree returning the country to constitutional government after two years of dictatorship. The King immediately gave him a mandate to form a new government, and the general reconstituted a cabinet of the same members, who were sworn in forthwith. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that American naval assistance was dispatched to Belize following a hurricane that killed between 150 and 200 people. Meanwhile, officials monitored a second storm advancing across Puerto Rico toward Haiti and the Dominican Republic. That cyclone had already caused one death and torn roofs from 200 homes in San Juan while tracking westward across the Caribbean.

Paralelamente, las autoridades monitoreaban una segunda tormenta que cruzaba Puerto Rico hacia Haití y la República Dominicana. Dicho ciclón ya había dejado una víctima mortal y desprendido los techos de 200 viviendas en San Juan en su avance hacia el oeste a través del Caribe.
