records.headline: In a column in the San Antonio Light, former Dominican Republic minister
records.summary_en: In a column in the San Antonio Light, former Dominican Republic minister to Washington Angel Morales predicts revolution in the Dominican Republic, stating that the republic of colored citizens covering two-thirds of the island of Haiti is in danger. According to the column, the Santo Domingo republic spends $6,000,000 a year, half of which goes to maintain an army whose sole function is to keep President Trujillo in absolute power. Morales reports that President Trujillo appointed his five-year-old son Rafael a full-fledged lieutenant colonel in the army, with the pay of that rank, for "eminent service to the country," and also changed the constitution to permit industrial monopolies.
records.summary_es: En una columna en el San Antonio Light, el exministro de la República Dominicana en Washington, Ángel Morales, predice una revolución en la República Dominicana y afirma que la república de ciudadanos de color que abarca dos tercios de la isla de Haití está en peligro. Según la columna, la república de Santo Domingo gasta $6,000,000 al año, la mitad de los cuales se destina a mantener un ejército cuya única función es conservar al presidente Trujillo en el poder absoluto. Morales informa que el presidente Trujillo nombró a su hijo de cinco años, Rafael, teniente coronel efectivo del ejército, con el sueldo correspondiente a ese rango, por «eminentes servicios al país», y además modificó la constitución para permitir monopolios industriales.

records.summary_en: The vessel sailed across the Atlantic, after stopping for supplies at Charleston, where his passengers remained below decks, to the crooked channel passage in the Bahamas and then to the northern coast of the Dominican Republic, the master of the ship Boreas, Captain Scott, recounted. According to Scott, former Cuban President Machado stated that he would be safe in Santo Domingo because of the many horses, guns, ammunition, and uniforms he had sent to the Dominican Republic while serving as president of Cuba. The captain also exhibited a rifle and pistol that he said Machado had presented to him, while the Boreas underwent minor repairs in Miami before an expected Friday departure for New York.

records.headline: The Evening Star reports the account of Scott, captain of the vessel
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reports the account of Scott, captain of the vessel Boreas, who stated that after taking former Cuban President Machado aboard at Cape Henlopen on May 16, he landed him 10 days later at Monte Cristi, a small port on the opposite side of the Caribbean island from Santo Domingo City. Two other Cubans—Fred Villapol, Machado's secretary, and a valet named Andre —also made the voyage, with Villapol subsequently returning to the United States aboard the Boreas. Although Machado had promised to make him independently rich for life for transporting him to Santo Domingo, Scott said he never saw Machado again after a Dominican coast guard boat met the Boreas at Monte Cristi and took the Machado party to Manzanillo Bay, from which they departed with friends to a house high in the mountains.

records.headline: In The Washington Daily News, Scott, captain of the schooner Boreas
records.summary_en: In The Washington Daily News, Scott, captain of the schooner Boreas, recounted how he transported former Cuban President Gerardo Machado—wanted in Cuba on various charges—from Lewes, Delaware, to a Dominican Republic Coast Guard boat off Monte Cristi, Santo Domingo, on June 26. Accompanying Machado as passengers were his secretary, Fred Villapol, and his valet, known to Scott only as "Andre." Scott related that Machado had promised to make him wealthy for life if he landed him safely in Santo Domingo, “but I never saw him again after the small boat took him off my ship,” and that Villapol came back to Miami with them but had gone north. The entire party, particularly Machado, were badly frightened as the small craft made the trip, and members of the party were heavily armed. The identity of his passengers was not revealed to Scott when they first boarded the boat: Scott knew Machado at first as “Cohen” and Villapol as “Estes,” understanding they were starting on a deep-sea fishing trip, and not until he left Lewes was he told who the men were. Machado then told him to make all speed and said that if he were stopped at any time by a U.S. Coast Guard boat he and his party intended to start firing; Scott told him there would be no shooting on his boat and took their arms and ammunition away and locked them up. Scott claimed that Machado had been in hiding in a house in Rehoboth, Delaware, for 10 days before boarding the Boreas at Lewes; when Scott stopped at Charleston for supplies his passengers stayed below decks. The ship's master said the trip from Charleston was across the Atlantic to the crooked channel passage in the Bahamas, then to the northern coast of the Dominican Republic. Scott said Machado told him he would be safe in Santo Domingo “because of the many horses, guns, ammunition and uniforms I sent to the Dominican Republic while I was president of Cuba.” The ship's captain exhibited a rifle and pistol which he said Machado had presented to him. The Boreas was making minor repairs in Miami and expected to sail for New York Friday.
records.summary_es: En The Washington Daily News, Scott, capitán de la goleta Boreas, relató cómo transportó al expresidente cubano Gerardo Machado —reclamado en Cuba por diversos cargos— desde Lewes, Delaware, hasta un barco guardacostas de la República Dominicana frente a Monte Cristi, Santo Domingo, el 26 de junio. Acompañaban a Machado como pasajeros su secretario, Fred Villapol, y su ayuda de cámara, conocido por Scott únicamente como «Andre». Scott relató que Machado le había prometido hacerlo rico de por vida si lo desembarcaba a salvo en Santo Domingo, «pero nunca lo volví a ver después de que la pequeña embarcación lo recogió de mi barco», y que Villapol regresó con ellos a Miami pero ya se había marchado al norte. Todo el grupo, en particular Machado, estaba muy asustado durante la travesía de la pequeña embarcación, y sus miembros iban fuertemente armados. La identidad de sus pasajeros no le fue revelada a Scott cuando embarcaron: conoció a Machado al principio como «Cohen» y a Villapol como «Estes», entendiendo que emprendían un viaje de pesca en alta mar, y no supo quiénes eran los hombres hasta después de salir de Lewes. Machado le dijo entonces que navegara a toda velocidad y que, si un guardacostas estadounidense los detenía en algún momento, él y su grupo pensaban empezar a disparar; Scott le dijo que en su barco no habría tiroteo y les quitó las armas y la munición y las guardó bajo llave. Scott afirmó que Machado había estado escondido en una casa de Rehoboth, Delaware, durante 10 días antes de embarcar en el Boreas en Lewes; cuando Scott se detuvo en Charleston para abastecerse, sus pasajeros permanecieron bajo cubierta. El capitán del barco dijo que el viaje desde Charleston fue a través del Atlántico hasta el sinuoso paso de canal de las Bahamas, y luego hasta la costa norte de la República Dominicana. Scott dijo que Machado le contó que estaría seguro en Santo Domingo «por los muchos caballos, armas, municiones y uniformes que envié a la República Dominicana cuando era presidente de Cuba». El capitán del barco exhibió un rifle y una pistola que, según dijo, Machado le había regalado. El Boreas hacía reparaciones menores en Miami y esperaba zarpar hacia Nueva York el viernes.

records.headline: Trujillo began life as a private in the constabulary forces in the island
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published a profile of Dominican President Rafael Trujillo, noting his rise from private to captain in the Marine-trained constabulary and his disciplined administrative methods. The article detailed his measures eliminating government automobiles for legislators and dropping 500 redundant employees from the state payroll. Despite the depression cutting government revenues by more than half, the piece credited Trujillo and his financial adviser with balancing the national budget and maintaining civic order.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* publicó una semblanza del presidente dominicano Rafael Trujillo, destacando su ascenso de soldado raso a capitán en la guardia entrenada por los marines y sus métodos de disciplina administrativa. El artículo detalló sus medidas para suprimir los automóviles oficiales para legisladores y dar de baja a 500 empleados innecesarios de la nómina estatal. A pesar de que la depresión redujo los ingresos fiscales a más de la mitad, la nota atribuyó a Trujillo y a su consejero financiero el haber equilibrado el presupuesto nacional y preservado el orden cívico.
records.passage: sidelights respecting Gen. Rafael Leonides Trujillo, the President of the republic. Trujillo began life as a private in the constabulary forces in the island, long operated by the United States Marines; rose to be captain of it, and is now running the country in the thoroughly efficient, if somewhat hard-boiled, fashion of a marine. Trujillo's first act when he took office was to take away from all the members of the Dominican House and Senate their free government automobiles; his next act to drop 500 supernumeraries off the official pay roll. The depression in Santo Domingo cut the state's revenue in half—from $15,000,000 to $7,000,000, and Trujillo found an empty treasury. But now, thanks to Trujillo and to the advice of his financial adviser, the republic has a balanced budget and is sweet, sanitary and safe. [illegible] The historic United States mint at San Francisco is now antiquated and to all intents and purposes obsolete. It might have gone on and on in genteel decay but for the fact that with the rise in the paper money price of gold and the resultant boom in gold mining and boom in the gold melting pots for gold teeth and wedding rings the Government mints have had a new lease on life. And the San Francisco mint physically has been quite unequal to the strain. This mint's gold hoard is being shifted to the Denver mint and funds have been allotted and plans are afoot for the construction of a brand-new, up-to-date mint in the city of the Golden Gate.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported on the accelerated withdrawal of U.S. Marines from Haiti, advancing their final departure two months ahead of schedule following President Roosevelt's visit to Cap-Haïtien. The article recalled the nineteen-year military occupation initiated under Woodrow Wilson in 1915 to suppress rebel factions. It observed that the departing marines left behind an efficient native constabulary, modern barracks, and improved municipal conditions in Port-au-Prince.

El artículo recordó los diecinueve años de ocupación militar iniciada bajo Woodrow Wilson en 1915 para sofocar facciones rebeldes. Observó que los marines en retirada dejaban tras de sí un eficiente cuerpo policial nativo, cuarteles modernos y mejores condiciones municipales en Puerto Príncipe.

records.headline: The Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, headed by Reuben Clark, jr
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that the Dominican government and the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council agreed to extend the maturity dates of two $10,000,000 bond issues to ease debt repayment. Under the plan, 5.5 percent bonds maturing in 1942 were extended twenty years, while 1940 bonds were extended to 1970, reestablishing the 1924 financial accord. Acting Secretary of State Phillips praised the Dominican Republic's determination to meet its debt obligations despite worldwide economic distress.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el gobierno dominicano y el Foreign Bondholders Protective Council acordaron extender las fechas de vencimiento de dos emisiones de bonos de 10.000.000 de dólares para facilitar el pago de la deuda. Conforme al plan, los bonos al 5,5 por ciento con vencimiento en 1942 se prorrogaron veinte años, mientras que los de 1940 se extendieron hasta 1970, restableciendo el acuerdo financiero de 1924. El secretario de Estado interino Phillips elogió la determinación de la República Dominicana de cumplir con sus obligaciones de deuda a pesar de la crisis económica mundial.

Of this total amount $4,000,000 already had been repaid. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that ousted Cuban dictator Gerardo Machado was preparing to leave his refuge in the Dominican Republic after President Rafael Trujillo advised him to depart. Trujillo had previously granted Machado an extensive estate and extraterritorial status protected by 130 Cuban guards, but faced threats of retaliation from the Cuban government. Machado was reportedly seeking a new haven in Venezuela under President Gómez.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el derrocado dictador cubano Gerardo Machado se preparaba para abandonar su refugio en la República Dominicana luego de que el presidente Rafael Trujillo le aconsejara marcharse. Trujillo le había otorgado previamente a Machado una extensa finca y estatus extraterritorial custodiado por 130 guardias cubanos, pero enfrentaba amenazas de represalias por parte del gobierno cubano. Según trascendió, Machado buscaba un nuevo asilo en Venezuela bajo el gobierno del presidente Gómez.
records.passage: is In a hot spot again. After many peregrinations he finally found haven in the Dominican Republic. President Trujillo, a close friend of Machado, offered him a huge domain in the island and gave him extraterritorial privileges. Machado settled down with his family and got himself a guard of 130 Cuban uniformed henchmen to form his personal guard. Neither the Dominican police nor the army was allowed to trespass on Machado's property. But the Cuban government threatened Trujillo with reprisals if he refused to surrender his old friend. The President of San Domingo got scared and advised Machado to clear out as soon as possible. Machado is looking now toward Venezuela, where his friend Gen. Gomez rules with an iron hand. He expects to find a place somewhere near [Caracas?], where he can settle down in peace and enjoy the millions he has been able to salt away while he was Cuba's dictator. records.full_text:
WASHINGTON OBSERVATIONS

The happily concluded negotiations for the adjustment of the foreign dollar bonds of the tiny Dominican Republic as announced last week is a new laurel crown for the Honorable Joseph E. Davies, whose prominent place in the Washington picture dates back to the days of the Wilson administration, when “Joe” Davies was first chairman of the Federal Trade Commission. Now in the private practice of law, though boomed for a place in the Roosevelt cabinet, Mr. Davies numbers the Dominican Republic among his clients and piloted the island’s government through the tortuous channel of debt negotiations with the Foreign Bondholders’ Protective Council. Friends of Mr. Davies are in receipt of copies of his brief in these proceedings, a magnus opus of 200 pages, in which the facts and the law and the argument are skillfully intertwined.

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo dated October 19 reports that Dominican Republic authorities believed they had blocked an assassination plot against exiled former Cuban President Gerardo Machado
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo dated October 19 reports that Dominican Republic authorities believed they had blocked an assassination plot against exiled former Cuban President Gerardo Machado by barring eight supposed University of Havana students at Puerto Plata the previous day. The eight unidentified students arrived at Puerto Plata aboard the S. S. Cuba and were not permitted to disembark. The report notes that University of Havana students were among the leaders of the revolution that overthrew Machado.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de la Associated Press desde Santo Domingo fechado el 19 de octubre informa que las autoridades de la República Dominicana creían haber bloqueado un complot de asesinato contra el expresidente cubano exiliado Gerardo Machado al impedir la entrada el día anterior en Puerto Plata a ocho supuestos estudiantes de la Universidad de La Habana. Los ocho estudiantes no identificados llegaron a Puerto Plata a bordo del vapor Cuba y no se les permitió desembarcar. El informe señala que los estudiantes de la Universidad de La Habana estuvieron entre los líderes de la revolución que derrocó a Machado.

records.headline: The Evening star reports that recent highway developments have opened
records.summary_en: The Evening star reports that recent highway developments have opened both the Dominican Republic and Haiti to motor tourism, with a highway running northward from Santo Domingo City through La Vega and Santiago to Puerto Plata, as well as southern and northern motor routes connecting the Dominican and Haitian capitals. The article credits United States Marines formerly stationed in the two republics with building the core road networks that both nations subsequently extended. Regular airplanes flying between Miami and San Juan, Puerto Rico, also call at Havana, Santiago, Port-au-Prince, and Santo Domingo City in both directions.
records.summary_es: El Evening star informa que el reciente desarrollo vial ha abierto tanto a la República Dominicana como a Haití al turismo automovilístico, con una carretera que se extiende hacia el norte desde la ciudad de Santo Domingo pasando por La Vega y Santiago hasta Puerto Plata, así como rutas automovilísticas del sur y del norte que conectan las capitales dominicana y haitiana. El artículo atribuye a los infantes de marina de los Estados Unidos anteriormente destacados en las dos repúblicas la construcción de las redes viales básicas que ambas naciones ampliaron posteriormente. Asimismo, aviones regulares que vuelan entre Miami y San Juan, Puerto Rico, hacen escala en La Habana, Santiago, Puerto Príncipe y la ciudad de Santo Domingo en ambas direcciones.

records.summary_en: According to the Evening star, exiled Cuban politician Gerardo Machado slipped into the Dominican Republic from the United States some weeks earlier, and once his presence became known, President Trujillo flatly refused to surrender him to Havana. Despite receiving Dominican hospitality, Machado recently crossed the border into Haiti, found it inhabited by Cuban terrorists, and has couriers reportedly investigating a haven on the South American mainland pending his return to the Dominican Republic. The article adds that rumor credits Machado with presenting President Trujillo with several submarine chasers and naval equipment out of gratitude for Dominican asylum.

A pesar de recibir la hospitalidad dominicana, Machado cruzó recientemente la frontera hacia Haití, encontró que estaba habitado por terroristas cubanos y cuenta con mensajeros que, según se informa, investigan un refugio en el continente suramericano mientras aguarda su regreso a la República Dominicana. El artículo añade que los rumores atribuyen a Machado haber obsequiado al presidente Trujillo varios cazasubmarinos y equipos navales en agradecimiento por el asilo dominicano.

records.headline: A United Press dispatch from Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: A United Press dispatch from Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, dated November 20 reports that former Cuban President Gerardo Machado, wanted in Cuba on murder and other charges, was hiding in the Dominican Republic and reportedly preparing to move to Europe. According to the dispatch, Machado may seek asylum in Germany following threats by Cubans to seize him and return him to Havana for trial.

De acuerdo con el despacho, Machado podría buscar asilo en Alemania tras las amenazas de cubanos de capturarlo y llevarlo de vuelta a La Habana para ser juzgado.

records.summary_en: Former Cuban ruler Gerardo Machado is practically recovered from the attack of indigestion that sent him to a hospital in Santo Domingo two weeks ago and is preparing to sail for Italy. Machado fled Cuba on August 12, 1933, and lived in Canada and the United States while Cuban governments sought his return for trial. His friends denied a version that his illness in Santo Domingo was poisoning, and in the Dominican Republic he was granted refuge by President Rafael Trujillo, long a friend of Machado.
records.summary_es: El exgobernante cubano Gerardo Machado está prácticamente recuperado del ataque de indigestión que lo llevó a un hospital en Santo Domingo hace dos semanas y se prepara para zarpar hacia Italia. Machado huyó de Cuba el 12 de agosto de 1933 y vivió en Canadá y Estados Unidos mientras los gobiernos cubanos buscaban su devolución para juzgarlo. Sus amigos negaron una versión de que su enfermedad en Santo Domingo fue un envenenamiento, y en la República Dominicana recibió refugio del presidente Rafael Trujillo, amigo de Machado desde hacía tiempo.

records.headline: A special bulletin from Santo Domingo in the Atlanta daily world
records.summary_en: A special bulletin from Santo Domingo in the Atlanta daily world reports that goodwill aviators Dr. Albert C. Forsythe of Atlantic City and C. Alfred Anderson of Bryn Mawr arrived in the Dominican capital on Tuesday aboard a Dominican Republic air service plane piloted by Captain Felix. Their own monoplane, the Booker T. Washington, had been damaged on Sunday during a forced landing. An accompanying dispatch from Port-au-Prince by Sylvio Cator notes that the aviators had previously arrived in Haiti from Kingston, Jamaica, on Thursday afternoon and stayed through part of Sunday.

Un despacho adjunto desde Puerto Príncipe por Sylvio Cator señala que los aviadores habían llegado previamente a Haití procedentes de Kingston, Jamaica, el jueves por la tarde y permanecieron allí hasta parte del domingo.

records.headline: In an Associated Negro Press dispatch from Santo Domingo, Dominican
records.summary_en: In an Associated Negro Press dispatch from Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, Pan-American goodwill flyer Dr. Albert E. Forsythe describes a forced landing made with fellow aviator Anderson on Sunday morning, half an hour after departing Port-au-Prince, Haiti, where they had been received by President Stenio Vincent and had circled the presidential palace twenty-one times in salute. Around nine o'clock, just as the goodwill plane crossed the Haitian-Dominican border and flew over Lake Enriquillo, a valve stem broke and forced the valve head through the piston head, causing engine failure. Anderson turned the aircraft sharply and executed a landing near the edge of the lake without damaging the plane itself. The flyers walked part of the way and rode donkeys the balance, it not being possible to communicate with Santo Domingo or any other large city or town either by telephone or other means. When the plane did not reach Santo Domingo on scheduled time, a message was sent to Porto Rico asking whether the ship had landed there, and on a negative answer the Dominican government ordered out army planes to search for them, but poor visibility made it impossible for the army planes to reach the vicinity where they were forced down. In the meantime they were well taken care of by Lieutenant Estrella, who was in charge of the military outpost at Descubierta, the nearest village, who provided a military guard for the plane and attended to their personal wants. A message was put through to Santo Domingo Sunday evening, and the following morning a military detachment under the command of Captain Felix was sent with a mechanic to aid them; on Tuesday morning, it being impossible to repair the engine sufficiently to fly into the capital, the military plane came again and carried the flyers and the mechanic back to Santo Domingo. At the military airport they were met by Mr. Brown, secretary of the American legation, taken to the American consul, and later received by Rudolph Schoenfeld, United States minister to the Dominican Republic; Forsythe talked with members of his family in Jamaica, he and Anderson delivered radio addresses, and the flyers expected to be in Santo Domingo for several days awaiting parts for the plane to be sent from the United States by air express — “undaunted by this misfortune,” though “down in the pocket.”
records.summary_es: En un despacho de la Associated Negro Press desde Santo Domingo, República Dominicana, el aviador de buena voluntad panamericano Dr. Albert E. Forsythe describe un aterrizaje forzoso realizado junto a su compañero aviador Anderson el domingo por la mañana, media hora después de partir de Puerto Príncipe, Haití, donde habían sido recibidos por el presidente Stenio Vincent y habían volado en círculos sobre el palacio presidencial veintiuna veces en señal de saludo. Alrededor de las nueve en punto, justo cuando el avión de buena voluntad cruzaba la frontera domínico-haitiana y volaba sobre el lago Enriquillo, se rompió el vástago de una válvula y empujó la cabeza de la válvula a través de la cabeza del pistón, provocando una falla en el motor. Anderson giró bruscamente la aeronave y ejecutó un aterrizaje cerca de la orilla del lago sin que el avión sufriera daños en su estructura. Los aviadores caminaron parte del camino y recorrieron el resto en burros, sin que fuera posible comunicarse con Santo Domingo ni con ninguna otra ciudad o población grande, ni por teléfono ni por otro medio. Cuando el avión no llegó a Santo Domingo a la hora prevista, se envió un mensaje a Puerto Rico preguntando si la nave había aterrizado allí, y ante la respuesta negativa el gobierno dominicano envió aviones del ejército a buscarlos, pero la escasa visibilidad hizo imposible que los aviones llegaran a las cercanías del lugar donde habían descendido. Entretanto, fueron bien atendidos por el teniente Estrella, a cargo del puesto militar de Descubierta, la aldea más cercana, quien proporcionó una guardia militar para el avión y atendió sus necesidades personales. El domingo por la noche se logró comunicar con Santo Domingo, y a la mañana siguiente se envió un destacamento militar al mando del capitán Félix con un mecánico para auxiliarlos; el martes por la mañana, al ser imposible reparar el motor lo suficiente para volar a la capital, el avión militar volvió y llevó a los aviadores y al mecánico de regreso a Santo Domingo. En el aeropuerto militar fueron recibidos por el Sr. Brown, secretario de la legación estadounidense, llevados ante el cónsul americano y recibidos después por Rudolph Schoenfeld, ministro de Estados Unidos en la República Dominicana; Forsythe habló con miembros de su familia en Jamaica, él y Anderson pronunciaron alocuciones por radio, y los aviadores esperaban permanecer en Santo Domingo varios días a la espera de las piezas del avión, que serían enviadas desde Estados Unidos por correo aéreo exprés: «sin desanimarse por esta desgracia», aunque «con los bolsillos vacíos».

records.headline: Señor Don Rafael Brache, the new Minister of the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: Señor Don Rafael Brache, the new Minister of the Dominican Republic, is traveling to New York to meet Señora de Trujillo, wife of the Dominican President, upon her arrival the following day for a short stay en route to Europe, The Evening star reports; Brache presented his credentials at the end of the week. Accompanying Minister Brache to New York is Señora de Espaillat, widow of the counselor of the Dominican legation and a resident of Washington. Brache is staying at the Hotel Roosevelt until Señora de Brache and their children join him later in the season.
records.summary_es: El señor don Rafael Brache, el nuevo ministro de la República Dominicana, viaja a Nueva York para recibir a la señora de Trujillo, esposa del presidente dominicano, a su llegada al día siguiente para una breve estadía rumbo a Europa, según informa el Evening star; Brache presentó sus credenciales a finales de la semana. Acompaña al ministro Brache a Nueva York la señora de Espaillat, viuda del consejero de la legación dominicana y residente en Washington. Brache se hospeda en el Hotel Roosevelt hasta que la señora de Brache y sus hijos se reúnan con él más adelante en la temporada.

records.headline: According to The Washington times, Señora de Trujillo is making
records.summary_en: According to The Washington times, Señora de Trujillo is making a short stay in the United States on her way from Santo Domingo to Europe and is being met in New York by the new Dominican Minister, Señor Don Rafael Brache, who presented his credentials at the White House on Friday, along with Señora de Espaillat, widow of the former Chargé d'Affaires of the legation. Señora de Espaillat had previously met Señora de Trujillo while staying as a guest at the Presidential Palace in Santo Domingo with her late husband. The paper also notes that the former Dominican Minister, Señor Don Roberto Despradel, departed on Thursday to take up his new post as Secretary of Justice in President Trujillo's Cabinet.
records.summary_es: Según The Washington times, la señora de Trujillo realiza una breve estadía en los Estados Unidos en su viaje desde Santo Domingo hacia Europa y es recibida en Nueva York por el nuevo ministro dominicano, el señor don Rafael Brache, quien presentó sus credenciales en la Casa Blanca el viernes, junto con la señora de Espaillat, viuda del antiguo encargado de negocios de la legación. La señora de Espaillat había conocido previamente a la señora de Trujillo mientras se hospedaba como invitada en el Palacio Presidencial en Santo Domingo con su difunto esposo. El periódico también señala que el exministro dominicano, el señor don Roberto Despradel, partió el jueves para asumir sus nuevas funciones como secretario de Justicia en el gabinete del presidente Trujillo.

records.headline: Pan-American goodwill aviators Dr. E. Forsythe and C. Alfred
records.summary_en: Pan-American goodwill aviators Dr. E. Forsythe and C. Alfred Anderson, flying the plane Booker T. Washington on a tour of 25 Central and South American countries, departed Santo Domingo, capital of the Dominican Republic, the previous Sunday for Puerto Rico after an unfortunate three-week delay, an Associated Negro Press dispatch in The Gary American reports. Upon landing at the Pan American airport in San Juan, the flyers received a cheering welcome from cultural and institutional representatives, were greeted with the national anthem and the Tuskegee hymn, and were escorted by automobile to the Municipal Theater, where Puerto Rican aviator LeCompte welcomed them.
records.summary_es: Los aviadores de buena voluntad panamericanos Dr. E. Forsythe y C. Alfred Anderson, que volaban en el avión Booker T. Washington en una gira por 25 países de América Central y del Sur, partieron de Santo Domingo, capital de la República Dominicana, el domingo anterior hacia Puerto Rico tras un desafortunado retraso de tres semanas, según un despacho de la Associated Negro Press en The Gary American. Al aterrizar en el aeropuerto de Pan American en San Juan, los aviadores recibieron una entusiasta bienvenida por parte de representantes culturales e institucionales, fueron saludados con el himno nacional y el himno de Tuskegee, y fueron escoltados en automóvil hasta el Teatro Municipal, donde el aviador puertorriqueño LeCompte les dio la bienvenida.

records.headline: The Washington times reports that Señora de Trujillo is arriving
records.summary_en: The Washington times reports that Señora de Trujillo is arriving in Washington that evening to stay for several days as the house guest of Mr. and Mrs. Joseph Davies on Massachusetts Avenue, who will host a dinner for her the next evening and a luncheon on Tuesday. She arrived in the United States on December 17 accompanied by her brother, Señor Leonida Ricardo, for a short visit prior to traveling to Europe. Upon her arrival in New York, she was met by the new Dominican Minister, Señor Don Rafael Brache, and Señora de Espaillat, widow of the former chargé d'affaires of the legation, who stayed several days with her at the Waldorf-Astoria.
records.summary_es: The Washington times informa que la señora de Trujillo llega a Washington esa noche para permanecer varios días como invitada de los esposos Joseph Davies en su residencia de Massachusetts Avenue, quienes ofrecerán una cena en su honor la noche siguiente y un almuerzo el martes. Ella llegó a los Estados Unidos el 17 de diciembre acompañada por su hermano, el señor Leonida Ricardo, para una breve visita antes de viajar a Europa. A su llegada a Nueva York, fue recibida por el nuevo ministro dominicano, el señor don Rafael Brache, y la señora de Espaillat, viuda del antiguo encargado de negocios de la legación, quienes permanecieron varios días con ella en el Waldorf-Astoria.

records.summary_en: The Evening star reports that Señora de Trujillo, wife of the President of the Dominican Republic, arrived in Washington the previous night to stay for several days with Mr. and Mrs. Joseph E. Davies at their home on Massachusetts Avenue, where she will be honored at a dinner that evening and a luncheon on Tuesday. Earlier, the new Dominican Minister, Señor Don Rafael Brache, and Señora de Espaillat, widow of the former chargé d'affaires of the legation, had traveled to New York to meet Señora de Trujillo upon her arrival and stayed several days with her at the Waldorf-Astoria.

records.summary_en: The Washington times reports that Mrs. Charles J. Linthicum, widow of the late Representative from Maryland, hosted a luncheon that day in the presidential room at the Mayflower in honor of Señora de Trujillo, wife of the President of the Dominican Republic. Also attending the luncheon were Dominican Minister Señor Rafael Brache, Mr. and Mrs. Joseph E. Davies, Mrs. Aldace Walker, and Señora de Espaillat. Later that afternoon, Señora de Trujillo was scheduled to be the guest of Mrs. Roosevelt at tea at the White House.

También asistieron al almuerzo el ministro dominicano, el señor Rafael Brache, los esposos Joseph E. Davies, la Sra. Aldace Walker y la señora de Espaillat. Más tarde esa misma tarde, estaba previsto que la señora de Trujillo fuera invitada de la Sra. Roosevelt para tomar el té en la Casa Blanca.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that First Lady Eleanor Roosevelt was scheduled to receive Señora de Trujillo, wife of the President of the Dominican Republic, for afternoon tea at the White House. The engagement was listed alongside other events on the First Lady's weekly social schedule, including a Senate luncheon and musical performances.

El compromiso figuraba junto a otros actos de la agenda social semanal de la primera dama, entre ellos un almuerzo en el Senado y presentaciones musicales.

records.headline: Mr. and Mrs. Joseph Davies hosted a midday dinner the previous day
records.summary_en: Mr. and Mrs. Joseph Davies hosted a midday dinner the previous day at their home on Massachusetts Avenue honoring their house guest, Señora de Trujillo, wife of the President of the Dominican Republic, who had arrived in Washington on Saturday from New York, the Evening star reports. Guests included the Dominican Minister, Don Rafael Brache, and the hosts' daughter, Mrs. Aldace Walker, who accompanied Señora de Trujillo to Washington for a stay of several days. Mrs. Davies will also host a ladies' luncheon for Señora de Trujillo the following day.

Aldace Walker, quien acompañó a la señora de Trujillo a Washington para una estadía de varios días. La Sra. Davies también ofrecerá un almuerzo de damas en honor a la señora de Trujillo al día siguiente.

records.headline: Dominican Minister Rafael Brache will host an informal dinner
records.summary_en: Dominican Minister Rafael Brache will host an informal dinner for 16 at the Shoreham this evening in honor of Senora de Trujillo, wife of the President of the Dominican Republic. Senora de Espaillat, widow of the legation's former chargé d'affaires, will serve as hostess, with guests comprising legation staff members and a few close friends of Senora de Trujillo. The item also notes that Minister Brache entertained at the Madrillon dinner dance the previous evening.
records.summary_es: El ministro dominicano Rafael Brache ofrecerá una cena informal para 16 personas en el Shoreham esta noche en honor de la Señora de Trujillo, esposa del presidente de la República Dominicana. La Señora de Espaillat, viuda del ex encargado de negocios de la legación, actuará como anfitriona, y los invitados incluirán a miembros del personal de la legación y a algunos amigos íntimos de la Señora de Trujillo. La nota añade que el ministro Brache agasajó a invitados la noche anterior en la cena bailable del Madrillon.

records.headline: The Washington Times reports on an informal dinner hosted by Dominican Minister
records.summary_en: The Washington Times reports on an informal dinner hosted by Dominican Minister Brache, with Senora de Espaillat, widow of the late chargé d'affaires, acting as hostess in honor of Senora de Trujillo, wife of the President of the Dominican Republic and house guest of Mr. and Mrs. Joseph E. Davies on Massachusetts Avenue. Attendees included legation staff, Senator and Mrs. William H. King, Dr. Leo S. Rowe, Mr. and Mrs. Davies, Mrs. Aldace Walker, Senorita Battle of New York, and the guest of honor's brother and sister-in-law, Senor Leonida Ricardo and Senora de Ricardo. The item adds that Minister Brache will be joined on Monday by Senora de Brache, currently traveling from Santo Domingo, and will take possession on Saturday of an apartment at 2633 Sixteenth St., where the legation offices will occupy the first floor.

records.headline: Profiling Senora de Trujillo on her third visit to the United States
records.summary_en: Profiling Senora de Trujillo on her third visit to the United States, The Washington Times notes her praise for American hospitality, scenery, and clothing design, as well as her interests in aviation, knitting, and opera and symphonic music. According to the article, she defers to her husband's disapproval of her flying. Accompanied by her brother and sister-in-law, Senor Don Leonida Ricardo and Senora de Ricardo, she is scheduled to sail from New York on January 19 aboard the Ile de France for a stay of several months in Europe, including London and France, before rejoining President Trujillo in Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: En una semblanza de la Señora de Trujillo durante su tercera visita a los Estados Unidos, The Washington Times destaca sus elogios a la hospitalidad, los paisajes y el diseño de ropa estadounidenses, así como su interés por la aviación, el tejido y la música de ópera y sinfónica. Según el artículo, ella acata la desaprobación de su esposo respecto a que vuele. Acompañada por su hermano y su cuñada, el señor Don Leonida Ricardo y la Señora de Ricardo, tiene previsto zarpar de Nueva York el 19 de enero a bordo del Ile de France para una estancia de varios meses en Europa, incluyendo Londres y Francia, antes de reunirse nuevamente con el presidente Trujillo en Santo Domingo.

records.summary_en: A February 6 dispatch from San Juan, Puerto Rico, reports that twenty-four United States Navy planes from the Panama Canal Zone departed in squadron formation for Samana Bay in the Dominican Republic as part of a Caribbean tour. El escuadrón tiene previsto realizar ejercicios durante una semana en la bahía de Samaná antes de continuar hacia Guantánamo y Jamaica y regresar posteriormente a Coco Solo.

records.headline: In making this announcement, the j Dominican Legation said President i
records.summary_en: The Dominican Legation announced that the boundary dispute between the Dominican Republic and Haiti had been settled. President Trujillo Molina of the Dominican Republic and President Vincent of Haiti had conferred in Haiti recently, settling all five of the principal boundary questions, in a dispute dating back to when Haiti was French territory and Santo Domingo was under Spanish rule. After the two countries agreed in 1930 to a peaceful solution by arbitration, President Vincent paid an official visit to Santo Domingo City the previous week, when the frontier treaty was signed.
records.summary_es: La Legación Dominicana anunció que la disputa fronteriza entre la República Dominicana y Haití había quedado resuelta. El presidente Trujillo Molina, de la República Dominicana, y el presidente Vincent, de Haití, se habían reunido recientemente en Haití y resolvieron las cinco cuestiones fronterizas principales, en una disputa que se remontaba a cuando Haití era territorio francés y Santo Domingo estaba bajo dominio español. Después de que ambos países acordaron en 1930 una solución pacífica por arbitraje, el presidente Vincent realizó la semana anterior una visita oficial a la ciudad de Santo Domingo, cuando se firmó el tratado fronterizo.
records.passage: the Dominican Republic and Haiti has been settled. In making this announcement, the Dominican Legation said President Trujillo Molina of the Dominican Republic, and President Vincent of Haiti, conferred in Haiti recently, settling all five of the principal boundary questions. The dispute, which dates back to the time when Haiti was French territory and Santo Domingo under Spanish rule, never did reach battle pitch. Haiti became Independent In 1804, and the Dominican Republic was released from Spain 40 years later. The only outbreaks over the boundary question were from minor guerilla warfare engagements shortly before 1920. In 1930 the two countries agreed to a peaceful solution by arbitration. Last week. President Vincent was in Santo Domingo City on an official visit to the Dominican President, when the frontier treaty was signed and the two island republics settled their political difficulties. ITALIAN CONSUL GIVEN RELEASE

Santo Domingo, May 16.—(UP)—The court to-day announced release of Amadeo Barletta, Italian consul, on ball in connection with an alleged assassination plot which caused Italy to threaten to send a warship to Dominican waters.

Barletta had been held on charges that he was involved in a plot against President Rafael Trujillo. The Italian minister at Washington is en route here to confer with the president and Italy had said a warship would be sent if necessary. Strong representations were made in Washington to Secretary of State Cordell Hull.

Ball for Barletta was set at $50,000.

The U. S. government was brought into the case when it developed that Barletta represents important American commercial interests in Santo Domingo, including General Motors Corp, and the Penn Tobacco company.

records.headline: The United States will raise no objections if Italy decides
records.summary_en: The United States will raise no objections if Italy decides to dispatch a warship to Santo Domingo over the imprisonment of honorary Italian consul Amadeo Barletta, who is held on charges of subversive activities against the dictatorship of President Rafael Trujillo. Italian Ambassador Augusto Rosso informed Secretary of State Cordell Hull that Premier Benito Mussolini was growing impatient and might send a naval vessel unless Barletta was promptly released. Mussolini's advance notice was attributed to respect for the Monroe Doctrine and the State Department's existing interest in the case, as Barletta represents American motor and tobacco enterprises in the Dominican Republic. Secretary Hull has already made representations to Dominican authorities on the grounds that Barletta's detention injures American business interests.
records.summary_es: Los Estados Unidos no presentarán objeciones si Italia decide enviar un buque de guerra a Santo Domingo ante el encarcelamiento del cónsul honorario italiano Amadeo Barletta, detenido bajo cargos de actividades subversivas contra la dictadura del presidente Rafael Trujillo. El embajador italiano Augusto Rosso informó al secretario de Estado Cordell Hull que el primer ministro Benito Mussolini se estaba impacientando y podría enviar un buque naval a menos que Barletta fuese puesto en libertad con prontitud. El aviso previo de Mussolini se atribuyó al respeto por la Doctrina Monroe y al interés previo del Departamento de Estado en el asunto, ya que Barletta representa a empresas estadounidenses de motores y tabaco en la República Dominicana. El secretario Hull ya ha presentado gestiones ante las autoridades dominicanas bajo el argumento de que la detención de Barletta perjudica los intereses comerciales norteamericanos.

records.summary_en: The *Springfield Weekly Republican* reported that Dominican President Rafael Trujillo maintained total control over national elections, running his Dominican Party unopposed and suppressing domestic opposition with an iron hand. Meanwhile, Dominican exiles in Cuba under former Vice President Rafael Estrella Ureña were reportedly organizing an expedition against Trujillo, with some Cuban youths attempting to join their cause. Opposition actions abroad had thus far been limited to minor incidents such as the mobbing of three diplomats in Havana.

Entretanto, según se reportó, exiliados dominicanos en Cuba bajo la dirección del exvicepresidente Rafael Estrella Ureña organizaban una expedición contra Trujillo, y algunos jóvenes cubanos intentaban sumarse a su causa. Hasta entonces, las acciones opositoras en el exterior se habían limitado a incidentes menores, como la agresión a tres diplomáticos en La Habana.

records.full_text:
An Absolute Dictatorship European Autocrats Mere Upstarts Compared With Ruler of Dominican Republic, According to Exile Here

By WILLIAM PHILIP SIMMS

WHAT is now perhaps the world's most absolute dictatorship is not in Europe, Asia or Africa, as Americans might casually suppose, but right at Uncle Sam's front door—in the Dominican Republic.

Its lord and master is Gen. Rafael Leonidas Trujillo-Molina, commonly called Trujillo (pronounced Trooh-ee-yo). There is a cabinet, but its members are his men. And a congress, but it votes unanimously what he tells it to vote.

"My life may pay for it if I tell you these things," said Angel Morales, Dominican attorney now in exile in this country. "A friend of mine was recently shot in New York when mistaken for me. But I will not hide. Nor will I keep silent. I am not afraid.

'PRESS MUZZLED'

"A complete censorship has been clamped down on the island. There is no such thing there as a free press or free speech. No Dominican newspaper would dare print anything hostile to the regime. The editor would pay for his indiscretion with his life.

"From Cuba sometimes the radio broadcasts criticisms of the dictator. People in Santo Domingo, like people in this country, love to listen in. But the moment the name Trujillo is heard coming thru, they don't wait to hear more. They spring up and shut it off, or switch to another station.

"It isn't that they are fond of the dictator. They are afraid neighbors or passersby might hear an anti-Trujillo speech coming out of the house and report its inmates as enemies. And that might bring fatal consequences.

CHILD GETS COLONEL'S PAY

"The dictator is the law of the land. He has a 5-year-old son named after him. Trujillo made him a full-fledged colonel of the army or constabulary—not just an honorary colonel such as the Czar made the little Czarevitch, but a regular one.

"The 'Little Colonel's' appointment was published in the official gazette. He receives $400 a month salary, wears a full colonel's uniform, and wherever he goes soldiers and junior officers click their heels and salute him."

President Trujillo rose from obscurity. He was a sergeant of constabulary when the American Marines were in occupation. Later he rose to captain, colonel, and second in command. In 1930, by a coup d'etat, he put a temporary president in office, then held an election and made himself chief of state.

"There are no longer any political parties in Santo Domingo," said Morales. "There is only one party and that is Trujillo's. So, when Trujillo ran for re-election last year, no one else received a vote. He was re-elected unanimously. He doubtless will continue to be, every four years hereafter.

AIDED BY NEW DEAL

"It was the 'Old Deal' that put Trujillo in power. But it is the 'New Deal' that keeps him there. The American policy of 'the good neighbor' is splendid. But in this particular case Washington's determination not to intervene in any way is playing into the hands of a tyrant."

The republic occupies the eastern two-thirds of the Island of Santo Domingo, second largest of the Greater Antilles group. It is in the Caribbean between Cuba and Puerto Rico. Haiti occupies the western end.

In size it is about 19.000 square miles, twice as big as Vermont, and it is very fertile. Its population is estimated at 1,200,000, of mixed European, Indian and Negro races. Spanish is spoken.

Today, over that corner of the southern sea hovers an ominous silence. Almost no news comes out. Nothing critical of the regime goes in. But in New York, Havana, Europe and elsewhere hundreds of exiles are waiting and wondering when a turn will come and they can go home.

records.headline: Political exiles from the Dominican Republic residing in the United States
records.summary_en: Political exiles from the Dominican Republic residing in the United States have been offered a general amnesty and invited to return home at government expense. Emilio Garcia Godoy, Dominican chargé d'affaires in Washington, announced the pardon and stated that the Dominican Republic would pay the expenses incurred on the return trip. The initiative was described as another move toward stability by the government of President Trujillo Molina.

Emilio Garcia Godoy, encargado de negocios dominicano en Washington, anunció el indulto y declaró que la República Dominicana sufragará los gastos originados por el viaje de retorno. La iniciativa fue descrita como otra medida en favor de la estabilidad por parte del gobierno del presidente Trujillo Molina.

records.headline: Dominican School System Placed on Modern Basis
records.summary_en: This feature describes the modernization of the Dominican school system under President Trujillo's reconstruction program: in the last year a thousand new rural school buildings have been constructed as part of an intense campaign against illiteracy, built with native materials by the Dominican Party. The program includes a Dominican edition of 20,000 copies of a reading and writing primer by the Catalan educator Eladio Homs, distributed by the President at his own expense to 20,000 rural schoolboys, and a book of the President's own maxims, published for training in citizenship. The article also reports the conversion of the Admiral's Mansion, home of Columbus's son, into a National Museum and home of the Dominican Academy of History, and state support for the Dominican Athenaeum and for the Lovers of Light, a literary club of Santiago de los Caballeros.

records.headline: A syndicated feature entry describes the "Columbus Tree," situated
records.summary_en: A syndicated feature entry describes the "Columbus Tree," situated a few yards from the west bank of the Ozama River in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. The gnarled castor bean tree, measuring about ten feet in diameter at the base, is venerated as the first hitching post of the New World because Columbus reputedly moored his vessel there on one of his voyages of discovery. Already several hundred years old during the era of Columbus, the tree is noted as still hale and hearty, expected to continue producing castor beans for another few centuries.
records.summary_es: Una nota de prensa sindicada describe el "Árbol de Colón", situado a pocas yardas de la margen occidental del río Ozama en Santo Domingo, República Dominicana. Este nudoso árbol de higuereta, que mide unos diez pies de diámetro en su base, es venerado como el primer punto de amarre del Nuevo Mundo debido a que, según la tradición, Colón amarró allí su nave durante uno de sus viajes de descubrimiento. Con varios cientos de años de antigüedad ya en la época de Colón, se afirma que el árbol continúa lozano y vigoroso, y se espera que siga produciendo semillas de higuereta durante otros cuantos siglos más.

Dominican Republic Envoy and Wife in New York Attending Ceremony and Reception

The Minister of the Dominican Republic and Senora de Brache are in New York where this morning at 9 o'clock the Minister acted as best man at the marriage of Senorita Irma Maria Levy and the Assistant General Consul in New York, Senor Manuel de Moya.

The ceremony took place in the Central Church of the Disciples and was followed by a wedding breakfast and reception at the home of the bride's mother, Senora Milaeros Levy, at 222 West Seventy-seventh St.

Due to the absence from the city of the Minister and his wife, there will be no celebration at the Legation in honor of the forty-third anniversary of the birth of the President of the Dominican Republic, Senor Rafael Leonidas Trujillo.

The Minister and Senora de Brache will return to the Capital on Saturday.

records.headline: Described as one of Latin America's most powerful political figures
records.summary_en: Described as one of Latin America's most powerful political figures, President Rafael L. Trujillo of the Dominican Republic will soon visit the United States according to advices from Santo Domingo. Trujillo put into effect two decrees transferring control of the civil administration and the army to the vice president and the president's brother during his absence. Trujillo, 44, who has never left his country except for a visit to neighboring Haiti during the past year, indicated he would depart Santo Domingo next month after preparing the 1936 budget.
records.summary_es: Calificado como una de las figuras políticas más poderosas de América Latina, el presidente Rafael L. Trujillo de la República Dominicana visitará próximamente los Estados Unidos según despachos procedentes de Santo Domingo. Trujillo puso en vigor dos decretos que transfieren el control de la administración civil y del ejército al vicepresidente y al hermano del mandatario durante su ausencia. Trujillo, de 44 años, quien nunca ha salido de su país excepto por una visita al vecino Haití durante el último año, indicó que saldría de Santo Domingo el próximo mes tras preparar el presupuesto de 1936.

records.headline: The Washington Daily News reports that news of the impending
records.summary_en: The Washington Daily News reports that news of the impending marriage of Mrs. Eleanor Davies Cheeseborough to Maryland's bachelor senator, Millard Tydings, has stirred unusual interest in diplomatic circles and throughout Central America and the West Indies. In Santo Domingo, capital of the Dominican Republic, cables detailing the event are avidly read because the name Joe Davies is as well known on the island as that of President-Dictator Rafael Trujillo. In addition to business and political connections, Davies served for many years as legal adviser to the Trujillo government, leading the public there to follow all social gossip involving their American adviser.

En Santo Domingo, capital de la República Dominicana, los cables sobre el acontecimiento se leen con avidez debido a que el nombre de Joe Davies es tan conocido en la isla como el del presidente-dictador Rafael Trujillo. The family plans to spend a week or 10 days in New York before traveling to the capital. records.headline: Following his reception by President Roosevelt at the White House
records.summary_en: Following his reception by President Roosevelt at the White House on Christmas Eve, a biographical profile outlines the background of the Dominican Republic's new minister, Andres Pastoriza. He is noted as well known in Washington from prior missions and business trips, having served as secretary of state for agriculture and labor in the cabinet of President Trujillo, on the National Council of Education, and as president of the Chamber of Commerce, Industry and Agriculture in Santiago and Santo Domingo. Pastoriza matriculated at Peekskill Military Academy in 1901 and graduated from the Pierce College of Business Administration in Philadelphia in 1905. The article highlights his distinguished family ties as the son of business leader Tomas Pastoriza, nephew of former Dominican President Gen. Desiderio Valverde, and husband of the granddaughter of former President and national hero Ulises F. Espaillat.

Pastoriza se matriculó en la Academia Militar de Peekskill en 1901 y se graduó en el Pierce College of Business Administration en Filadelfia en 1905. records.headline: Telephone communication between this city and Santo Domingo, capital of the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: The *Worcester Democrat and the Ledger-Enterprise* reported the inauguration of direct telephone communication between Washington, D.C., and Santo Domingo in an exchange between U.S. Secretary of State Cordell Hull and Dominican Foreign Minister Elías Brache, Hijo. Secretary Hull expressed hope that direct telephone service would foster better understanding and conveyed well-wishes to President Trujillo Molina and the Dominican people. Foreign Minister Brache agreed with Hull's sentiments and reciprocated the Dominican President's felicitations to the American public.
records.summary_es: El *Worcester Democrat and the Ledger-Enterprise* informó sobre la inauguración de la comunicación telefónica directa entre Washington D.C. y Santo Domingo mediante una conversación entre el secretario de Estado estadounidense Cordell Hull y el canciller dominicano Elías Brache, hijo. El secretario Hull manifestó su esperanza de que el servicio telefónico directo fomentara un mejor entendimiento y transmitió sus mejores votos al presidente Trujillo Molina y al pueblo dominicano. El canciller Brache coincidió con las apreciaciones de Hull y retribuyó las felicitaciones del mandatario dominicano al público estadounidense.

records.headline: President Trujillo, the statement says: "With a will that brought comment
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published a statement praising President Trujillo for directing the rebuilding of Santo Domingo following its destruction, modernizing the city without incurring new debt or defaulting on bonded interest payments. The report highlighted extensive nationwide public works, including new roads, schools, hospitals, Latin America's largest suspension bridge, and a nearly completed $3,000,000 artificial port at Trujillo City. It added that despite public efforts to rename the capital in his honor, Trujillo had initially opposed the proposal.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* publicó una declaración en la que elogiaba al presidente Trujillo por dirigir la reconstrucción de Santo Domingo tras su destrucción, modernizando la urbe sin contraer nueva deuda ni suspender el pago de intereses sobre los bonos. El informe destacó amplias obras públicas en todo el territorio nacional, como nuevas carreteras, escuelas, hospitales, el puente colgante más grande de América Latina y un puerto artificial de 3.000.000 de dólares a punto de concluirse en Ciudad Trujillo. Añadió que, pese a las gestiones públicas para rebautizar la capital en su honor, Trujillo se había opuesto inicialmente a dicha propuesta.
records.passage: President Trujillo, the statement says: "With a will that brought comment from the entire world, the 39-year-old Chief Executive personally directed the task of saving the impoverished population from starvation and epidemics. and then of constructing a new city to replace the old one. Rapidly new streets, buildings, homes and parks appeared, until Santo Domingo became a new metropolis in gleaming white, far surpassing the city it had replaced. "Without defaulting or postponing Interest payments on bonded indebtedness. and without incurring new indebtedness. President Trujillo conducted a vast program of public works throughout the nation, financed entirely from current revenue. New highways were laid into every corner of the country; great bridges were swung across rivers, among them the largest suspension bridge in Latin America; new schools, hospitals, libraries. were erected everywhere. Agricultural development mounted to new all-time highs and industry leaped from a handful of manufacturing establishments to more than 1,200. After his re-election in 1934. President Trujillo began an even more impressive public works program, the climax of which is the creation of an artificial port at Trujillo City, now nearly completed. At a cost of $3,000,000 this new port permits for the first time actual entry to the docks of the harbor. records.headline: A feature article depicts the Dominican Republic as an enchanting
records.summary_en: A feature article depicts the Dominican Republic as an enchanting destination combining tropical scenery with centuries of history. Santo Domingo, now called Trujillo City and identified as the oldest capital in the Americas, was founded on August 4, 1496, by Bartolome Columbus, brother of the discoverer, and named because its first stone was laid on a Sunday that fell on the day of Saint Domingo. Nearly four centuries later, visitors can walk streets and view scenes little changed since the earliest European adventurers arrived. Surveying the city's historic edifices, the account highlights the Holy Cathedral, begun in 1514 and completed in 1541, which holds the crypt of Christopher Columbus, replicates the arches of the Cathedral at Sevilla, and preserves a solid shot embedded in its roof from Sir Francis Drake's occupation in 1586.
records.summary_es: Un artículo especial retrata a la República Dominicana como un destino encantador que combina paisajes tropicales con siglos de historia. Santo Domingo, ahora llamada Ciudad Trujillo e identificada como la capital más antigua de América, fue fundada el 4 de agosto de 1496 por Bartolomé Colón, hermano del descubridor, y nombrada así porque su primera piedra se colocó un domingo que coincidió con el día de Santo Domingo. Casi cuatro siglos después, los visitantes pueden recorrer calles y contemplar escenarios poco cambiados desde la llegada de los primeros aventureros europeos. Al reseñar los edificios históricos de la ciudad, el relato destaca la Santa Catedral, iniciada en 1514 y concluida en 1541, que alberga la cripta de Cristóbal Colón, reproduce los arcos de la Catedral de Sevilla y conserva una bala de cañón incrustada en su techo desde la ocupación de Sir Francis Drake en 1586.

records.headline: The Harlem News reports that Santo Domingo, the oldest European settlement
records.summary_en: The Harlem News reports that Santo Domingo, the oldest European settlement in the Western Hemisphere, has been renamed Ciudad Trujillo (Trujillo City) after nearly four and a half centuries. Founded in 1496 by Bartholomew Columbus, brother of Christopher, the capital was rechristened in honor of the Dominican Republic's president and dictator, General Rafael Leonidas Trujillo Molina. The article quotes a National Geographic Society bulletin highlighting the historic port at the mouth of the Ozama River on the south coast of Hispaniola, from which Columbus, Pizarro, Ponce de Leon, Velazquez, and Narvaez once sailed on voyages of discovery. The bulletin observes that while ancient ruins and city walls still stand among modern structures, historic monuments suffered over generations as stones were reused for city repairs and even as harbor fill toward the end of the last century.
records.summary_es: The Harlem News informa que Santo Domingo, el asentamiento europeo más antiguo del hemisferio occidental, ha sido renombrado como Ciudad Trujillo (Trujillo City) tras casi cuatro siglos y medio. Fundada en 1496 por Bartolomé Colón, hermano de Cristóbal, la capital fue rebautizada en honor al presidente y dictador de la República Dominicana, el general Rafael Leonidas Trujillo Molina. El artículo cita un boletín de la National Geographic Society que destaca el puerto histórico en la desembocadura del río Ozama, en la costa sur de La Española, desde donde Colón, Pizarro, Ponce de León, Velázquez y Narváez zarparon en viajes de descubrimiento. El boletín señala que, si bien aún quedan ruinas antiguas y murallas entre las construcciones modernas, los monumentos históricos sufrieron durante generaciones debido a que sus piedras se reutilizaron para reparaciones urbanas e incluso como relleno portuario hacia finales del siglo pasado.

TRUJILLO TIDINGS

Hot-haste to present the compliments of President Trujillo of the Dominican Republic, to Secretary of State Hull, came a big, affable man yesterday afternoon.

He is Senor Don Ernesto Bonetti Burgos, new Foreign Minister of the Republic, en route from Berlin to Santo Domingo. He received a wire from Trujillo to accept personally President Roosevelt's Pan-American peace conference offer.

"We are old friends," said Burgos, as he and able Minister Andres Pastoriza of the Dominican Republic, arrived arm-in-arm at the State Department.

Dominican Republic Honors Washington by New Boulevard Name

TRUJILLO CITY, Dominican Republic, Feb. 22.—The national congress has declared George Washington's birthday a national holiday.

With an opening salute of 21 guns from the batteries of Ozama Fortress, the Dominican Republic today inaugurated the most extensive and elaborate celebration of Washington's birthday ever held outside the United States.

In a gesture of friendship and admiration for the United States and its first President, George Washington, Pres. Gen. Rafael L. Trujillo recently suggested that the name of Trujillo City's most beautiful boulevard, until today called Avenida Presidente Trujillo, be changed to Avenida George Washington. Acting on this suggestion the national congress approved an ordinance to that effect and named February 22, 1936, as the date for the official inaugural ceremonies.

Solemn dedication ceremonies were held here, including an address by President Trujillo, and another by the American Minister Hans P. Arthur Schoenfeld. A commemorative bronze plaque of large dimensions, suitably inscribed, was unveiled. Band concerts and other festivities were attended by many thousands celebrating this great event.

Other guests included the Minister of Bolivia and Senora de Finot, the Minister of Ecuador and Senora de Alfaro, Pan-American Union Director General Dr. Leo S. Rowe, Dr. Alfredo B. Cuellar, and Senoritas Piedad Castillo Levi and Davila.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that in accepting President Roosevelt's invitation to a Pan-American conference in Buenos Aires, the Dominican Republic, Colombia, and Guatemala proposed establishing an American league of nations. Dominican President Rafael Trujillo and Colombian President Alfonso López argued that an American league would serve regional purposes more effectively than the League of Nations in Geneva. Guatemala additionally proposed a mutual assistance pact providing for joint action under the Monroe Doctrine against non-American aggression.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que, al aceptar la invitación del presidente Roosevelt a la conferencia panamericana en Buenos Aires, la República Dominicana, Colombia y Guatemala propusieron la creación de una liga de naciones americanas. El mandatario dominicano Rafael Trujillo y el presidente colombiano Alfonso López sostuvieron que una liga continental respondería mejor a las necesidades de la región que la Sociedad de Naciones en Ginebra. Guatemala propuso además un pacto de asistencia mutua que contemplaba acciones conjuntas al amparo de la Doctrina Monroe frente a agresiones extracontinentales.

The Hull reciprocal tariff program produced trade treaties with six Latin American states and launched negotiations with several others. As the fitting aftermath of these constructive developments came President Roosevelt's project for an extraordinary conference of Pan-American states to be convened at Buenos Aires this year for the purpose of laying still deeper the foundations of inter-American fraternity. That there is a cordial desire to knit ever more closely the ties of common interest is indicated by the views of Colombia, Guatemala and the Dominican Republic, which propose, while accepting Mr. Roosevelt's invitation, the formation of a league of nations for the Americas. Guatemala also suggests a multilateral pact of mutual assistance, which would provide for joint Pan-American action under the Monroe Doctrine in case of aggression by any non-American power. President Lopez of Colombia and President Trujillo of the Dominican Republic emphasize that a league of American nations would be more efficacious for purely American purposes than the Geneva League. Some of the Latin American governments think a Western league might in some degree advantageously supplement the World organization. President Ubico of Guatemala favors an American international court of justice in addition to a league or association concerned exclusively with Western Hemisphere affairs. records.headline: Two values of a Dominican postage series planned by Congress
records.summary_en: Two values of a Dominican postage series planned by Congress to contain 13 denominations have appeared, bearing inscriptions for the national library and archives. The items received are a 3c purple stamp portraying President R. L. Trujillo and a 7c grayish-blue stamp depicting General Antonio Duverge. An Associated Press report states that collecting experts understand all stamp proceeds will form a national treasury fund to construct a national library and archives building. While available for regular postage, the issue is intended primarily to raise construction funds, differing somewhat from standard semi-postals.
records.summary_es: Han aparecido dos valores de una serie postal dominicana que el Congreso proyectó en 13 denominaciones, con inscripciones destinadas a la biblioteca y archivos nacionales. Las piezas recibidas son un sello morado de 3c con el retrato del presidente R. L. Trujillo y uno azul grisáceo de 7c que representa al general Antonio Duvergé. Un despacho de Associated Press señala que los expertos filatélicos entienden que toda la recaudación de los sellos creará un fondo en el tesoro nacional para construir el edificio de la biblioteca y archivos nacionales. Aunque pueden usarse para franqueo ordinario, los sellos tienen el propósito primordial de recaudar fondos para la construcción, diferenciándose en parte de los sellos semipostales habituales.

records.headline: An announcement from Trujillo City reports that the Dominican Republic succeeded
records.summary_en: An announcement from Trujillo City reports that the Dominican Republic succeeded in living within its national revenue without incurring debts in 1935. The dispatch notes that not more than two other nations in the world balanced their budgets during that period, and that the republic closed the year with a surplus. In addition, more public works were carried out than in any previous 13-month period. The achievement was credited to strict operating economy, careful planning, the elimination of graft, and general employment conditions.
records.summary_es: Un anuncio desde Trujillo City comunica que la República Dominicana logró vivir dentro de sus ingresos nacionales sin contraer deudas en 1935. El despacho señala que no más de otras dos naciones en el mundo equilibraron sus presupuestos durante ese período y que la república cerró el año con superávit. Además, se llevaron a cabo más obras públicas que en cualquier período previo de 13 meses. El logro se atribuyó a una rigurosa economía de operaciones, una cuidadosa planificación, la erradicación del soborno y las condiciones generales del empleo.

records.headline: Ahead of the forthcoming inter-American peace conference, three
records.summary_en: Ahead of the forthcoming inter-American peace conference, three Latin American nations have proposed forming a league of American nations to preserve peace in the Western Hemisphere. The suggestion was submitted by Presidents Alfonso Lopez of Colombia, Jorge Ubico of Guatemala, and Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic. The leaders believe the proposed league would not only prevent war in the New World, but would also serve as an effective adjunct to worldwide organizations working to preserve global peace.
records.summary_es: De cara a la próxima conferencia de paz interamericana, tres naciones latinoamericanas han propuesto formar una liga de naciones americanas para preservar la paz en el hemisferio occidental. La sugerencia fue presentada por los presidentes Alfonso López de Colombia, Jorge Ubico de Guatemala y Rafael Trujillo de la República Dominicana. Los mandatarios consideran que la liga propuesta no solo evitaría la guerra en el Nuevo Mundo, sino que también serviría como un complemento eficaz para las organizaciones mundiales que trabajan por la paz global.

records.headline: Preparatory to the forthcoming inter-American peace conference
records.summary_en: Preparatory to the forthcoming inter-American peace conference, three Latin American nations have proposed creating a league of American nations to maintain peace in the Western Hemisphere. The recommendation came from Presidents Alfonso Lopez of Colombia, Jorge Ubico of Guatemala, and Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic, who believe such a league would prevent conflicts in the New World and assist global peace organizations. President Ubico specifically proposed naming the agency the Association of American Nations, pledging mutual assistance against non-American aggression. He also suggested establishing a permanent inter-American court of justice, modeled after the World Court at The Hague, to settle disputes through arbitration.
records.summary_es: En vísperas de la próxima conferencia de paz interamericana, tres naciones latinoamericanas han propuesto crear una liga de naciones americanas para mantener la paz en el hemisferio occidental. La recomendación provino de los presidentes Alfonso López de Colombia, Jorge Ubico de Guatemala y Rafael Trujillo de la República Dominicana, quienes consideran que dicha liga evitaría conflictos en el Nuevo Mundo y ayudaría a las organizaciones de paz mundiales. El presidente Ubico propuso específicamente llamar al organismo Asociación de Naciones Americanas, comprometiendo asistencia mutua frente a agresiones no americanas. Sugirió además establecer una corte permanente de justicia interamericana, inspirada en el Tribunal Mundial de La Haya, para resolver disputas mediante arbitraje.

records.headline: Three Latin American governments have proposed the creation of a league of American nations
records.summary_en: Three Latin American governments have proposed the creation of a league of American nations to preserve peace across the Western Hemisphere ahead of the upcoming inter-American peace conference. The plan was advanced by Presidents Alfonso Lopez of Colombia, Jorge Ubico of Guatemala, and Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic. The leaders expressed conviction that such an organization would prevent wars in the New World while serving as an effective adjunct to international institutions working for peace.

Los mandatarios expresaron su convicción de que dicha organización prevendría guerras en el Nuevo Mundo y serviría como un complemento eficaz para las instituciones internacionales que trabajan por la paz.

records.headline: Addressing George Washington University students at Corcoran
records.summary_en: Addressing George Washington University students at Corcoran Hall, Andres Pastoriza, Minister of the Dominican Republic to the United States, reported that his country is one of three nations that balanced their budgets during the depression. Pastoriza attributed this financial achievement to the policies of President Rafael L. Trujillo. He stated that millions have been spent on public works and funded from current income since the Trujillo administration took office, adding that unemployment has been eliminated.

Pastoriza atribuyó este logro financiero a las políticas del presidente Rafael L. Trujillo. Declaró que se han gastado millones en obras públicas costeadas con ingresos corrientes desde que la administración de Trujillo asumió el cargo, agregando que el desempleo ha sido eliminado.

records.headline: A review discusses Lawrence De Besault's 'President Trujillo
records.summary_en: A review discusses Lawrence De Besault's 'President Trujillo, His Work and the Dominican Republic,' published by the Washington Publishing Company. The account outlines major public works undertakings, including a massive breakwater and harbor improvement scheduled for completion this year to permit large steamships to dock near the capital. It also recounts that President Trujillo began his career as a telegrapher before entering the military, where his rapid rise led him to become commander of the army prior to assuming the presidency. The review concludes that the work offers clear insight into the factors behind the republic's successful development.
records.summary_es: Una reseña comenta la obra de Lawrence De Besault, «President Trujillo, His Work and the Dominican Republic», publicada por la Washington Publishing Company. El relato describe importantes proyectos de obras públicas, entre ellos un enorme rompeolas y mejoras portuarias que concluirán este año para permitir el atraque de grandes vapores cerca de la capital. También relata que el presidente Trujillo inició su carrera como telegrafista antes de ingresar al ejército, donde su rápido ascenso lo llevó a comandar las fuerzas armadas antes de asumir la presidencia. La reseña concluye señalando que la obra ofrece una perspectiva clara sobre los factores detrás del exitoso desarrollo de la república.

records.summary_en: An illustrated report highlights the rebuilding of the historic capital of the Dominican Republic under President and dictator Gen. Rafael Leonidas Trujillo Molino. Founded in 1496 by Christopher Columbus's brother Bartholomew, the city became one of the most historic in the region, serving as the departure point for Columbus, Cortez, Pizarro, Ponce de Leon, and other explorers, and standing near the site where white men first found gold in America. The account cites the great George Washington Avenue as an example of the modernization, describing it as a wide, tree-lined coastal boulevard offering a magnificent harbor view. A recently issued postage stamp, one of four commemorating the thoroughfare's completion, portrays the new boulevard alongside President Trujillo.
records.summary_es: Una reseña ilustrada destaca la reconstrucción de la histórica capital de la República Dominicana bajo el presidente y dictador general Rafael Leonidas Trujillo Molino. Fundada en 1496 por Bartolomé Colón, hermano de Cristóbal, la ciudad se convirtió en una de las más históricas de la región, sirviendo como punto de partida para Colón, Cortés, Pizarro, Ponce de León y otros en sus exploraciones, y ubicándose cerca del lugar donde los hombres blancos hallaron oro por primera vez en América. El informe cita la gran avenida George Washington como ejemplo de la modernización, describiéndola como un bulevar costero amplio y arbolado con una magnífica vista del puerto. Un sello postal emitido recientemente, uno de los cuatro que conmemoran la finalización de la vía, muestra el nuevo bulevar junto al presidente Trujillo.
