records.summary_en: An illustrated syndicated feature notes that the Dominican capital has received a new name, Ciudad Trujillo (Trujillo City), in honor of the Dominican Republic's president and dictator, Gen. Rafael Leonidas Trujillo Molino. Founded in 1496 by Bartholomew Columbus, brother of Christopher, the historic city served as the departure point for Columbus, Cortez, Pizarro, Ponce de Leon, and other explorers, and was situated near where white men first found gold in America. The account reports that the newly named ancient city is being rebuilt, citing as an example the great George Washington Avenue, a wide, tree-lined boulevard along the coast with a magnificent view of the harbor. A featured postage stamp, one of four issued recently upon completion of the thoroughfare, portrays the new boulevard and President Trujillo.

Fundada en 1496 por Bartolomé Colón, hermano de Cristóbal, la histórica ciudad sirvió de punto de partida para Colón, Cortés, Pizarro, Ponce de León y otros exploradores, y estuvo situada cerca del lugar donde los hombres blancos hallaron oro por primera vez en América. La nota informa que la antigua ciudad recién nombrada está siendo reconstruida, citando como ejemplo la gran avenida George Washington, un bulevar amplio y arbolado a lo largo de la costa con una magnífica vista del puerto. records.headline: An article examining international conflicts sparked by postage
records.summary_en: An article examining international conflicts sparked by postage stamps recalls that in 1900 a map stamp issued by the government of the Dominican Republic—commonly known as San Domingo—provoked a violent reaction in neighboring Haiti. Enraged by the stamp's depiction of the island they share in the West Indies, Haitians reportedly armed themselves with shooting irons and marched from a hundred jungle villages into Port au Prince. According to the account, the marching Haitians cried out for San Dominguan blood over the controversial stamp displayed on the page.
records.summary_es: Un artículo que examina los conflictos internacionales provocados por sellos postales recuerda que en 1900 un sello con mapa emitido por el gobierno de la República Dominicana —conocida comúnmente como Santo Domingo— provocó una reacción violenta en la vecina Haití. Enfurecidos por la representación del sello sobre la isla de las Indias Occidentales que comparten, los haitianos se armaron con rifles y marcharon desde un centenar de aldeas selváticas hacia Puerto Príncipe. Según el relato, los haitianos en marcha clamaban por la sangre de los dominicanos a causa del polémico sello mostrado en la página.

records.headline: A feature caption and narrative explain that while land on the island
records.summary_en: A feature caption and narrative explain that while land on the island was roughly equally divided between the Dominican Republic and Haiti, a Dominican stamp depicted the frontier in a way that squeezed the Haitians into the western tip. Although several thousand Haitian soldiers stood ready for war and several minor clashes between troops occurred, cool heads persuaded the warriors to wait a day or two while a courier was sent to the other end of the island to demand an explanation from San Domingo. The dispute was ultimately averted when the Dominican government apologized and blamed the map's boundary error on an artist who was deficient in geography.
records.summary_es: El pie de foto y el relato explican que, aunque la tierra de la isla estaba dividida casi en partes iguales entre la República Dominicana y Haití, un sello dominicano trazó la frontera de modo que los haitianos quedaron apretados en el extremo occidental. Aunque varios miles de soldados haitianos estaban listos para la guerra y se produjeron varios enfrentamientos menores entre las tropas, la sensatez persuadió a los combatientes de esperar uno o dos días mientras se enviaba un mensajero al otro extremo de la isla para exigir una explicación a Santo Domingo. El conflicto se evitó finalmente cuando el gobierno dominicano se disculpó y atribuyó el error en los límites del mapa a un artista con escasos conocimientos de geografía.

records.headline: According to the Dominican Republic News Service in Washington
records.summary_en: According to the Dominican Republic News Service in Washington, the Dominican Republic is holding its second celebration this year honoring the United States with a concert and festivities in Trujillo City commemorating the American Declaration of Independence. President Rafael L. Trujillo is scheduled to deliver a congratulatory message to America during ceremonies centered around a laurel tree planted in Independence Park during the 1932 Washington Bicentennial. The report notes that the republic previously declared Washington's birthday a national holiday this year, and that President Trujillo named the capital's principal thoroughfare George Washington Avenue.
records.summary_es: Según el Servicio de Noticias de la República Dominicana en Washington, la República Dominicana celebra este año su segundo festejo en honor de los Estados Unidos con un concierto y festividades en Ciudad Trujillo para conmemorar la Declaración de Independencia estadounidense. Está previsto que el presidente Rafael L. Trujillo pronuncie un mensaje de felicitación a los Estados Unidos durante ceremonias centradas en torno a un árbol de laurel plantado en el Parque Independencia con motivo del bicentenario de Washington en 1932. La nota añade que la república declaró anteriormente este año el natalicio de Washington como día feriado nacional, y que el presidente Trujillo nombró la principal avenida de la capital como avenida George Washington.

records.summary_en: A July 4 dispatch from Trujillo City reports that the Dominican Republic marked the United States Independence Day with President Rafael L. Trujillo delivering a message of congratulations to the United States on its birthday. records.headline: A motion picture review describes a new issue of the newsreel
records.summary_en: A motion picture review describes a new issue of the newsreel series "March of Time," distributed through RKO Distributing Corporation, which includes a segment on the Dominican Republic. The episode portrays President-Dictator Rafael Trujillo maintaining his dictatorship over the country despite the efforts of exiled political foes in the United States, including the Nationalist Morales. The film presents reports that Trujillo has become nervous about his position, allegedly keeping steam up on his yacht day and night in case he is forced to flee.

records.headline: The Washington Times reports that Dominican government representatives
records.summary_en: The Washington Times reports that Dominican government representatives are continuing protests against the exhibition of a current motion picture that they contend portrays President Trujillo of the Dominican Republic as a dictator. Minister Pastoriza raised the matter yesterday in diplomatic discussions with the State Department, protesting the screening of "The March of Time" in American theaters and characterizing it as a misrepresentation of present-day Dominican political conditions that casts an unwarranted reflection on President Trujillo's administration. No action had been taken up to an early hour today toward the withdrawal of the film.

El ministro Pastoriza planteó ayer el asunto en conversaciones diplomáticas con el Departamento de Estado, protestando por la proyección de "The March of Time" en los cines estadounidenses y calificándola de tergiversación de las condiciones políticas dominicanas actuales que supone un reflejo injustificado sobre la administración del presidente Trujillo. Hasta primeras horas de hoy no se había tomado ninguna medida orientada al retiro del filme.

records.summary_en: The *Washington Daily News* reported that Dominican Minister Andrés Pastoriza lodged an unofficial complaint with Assistant Secretary of State Sumner Welles regarding a "March of Time" film depicting President Trujillo. The column commented on the diplomatic challenge Pastoriza faced representing a dictator in the United States while maintaining poise. It also recounted a humorous anecdote about a Cuban sugar expert who became intoxicated on Dominican rum during a picnic on Chesapeake Bay.

La columna comentó el desafío diplomático que enfrentaba Pastoriza al representar a un dictador en Estados Unidos preservando la compostura. Relató asimismo una anécdota humorística sobre un perito azucarero cubano que se embriagó con ron dominicano durante un pícnic en la bahía de Chesapeake.

records.headline: An article reviewing assassinations and attacks on national leaders
records.summary_en: An article reviewing assassinations and attacks on national leaders compiles a historical roster of heads of state to whom death has come since 1900. Among the international leaders enumerated is President Ramon Caceres of the Dominican Republic, listed for 1911. The list also includes figures such as King Humbert of Italy in 1900, President William McKinley in 1901, Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary in 1914, and Austrian Chancellor Engelbert Dollfuss in 1934.

Entre los mandatarios internacionales enumerados figura el presidente Ramón Cáceres de la República Dominicana, registrado en 1911. La lista incluye además a personalidades como el rey Humberto de Italia en 1900, el presidente William McKinley en 1901, el archiduque Francisco Fernando de Austro-Hungría en 1914 y el canciller austríaco Engelbert Dollfuss en 1934.

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that the ashes of Christopher Columbus
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that the ashes of Christopher Columbus were deposited that day in a new rock-crystal urn, replacing the original lead casket. The receptacle was presented by President Rafael Trujillo in observance of his birthday, with high diplomatic officials attending the ceremonies at the Columbus tomb. The president asserted that the transfer was the first step in a program to culminate six years later with a lighthouse memorial on the 450th anniversary of the discovery of America.

El receptáculo fue obsequiado por el presidente Rafael Trujillo en conmemoración de su cumpleaños, con la asistencia de altos funcionarios diplomáticos a las ceremonias en la tumba de Colón. El presidente afirmó que el traslado constituía el primer paso de un programa que culminaría seis años después con un faro conmemorativo en el 450.º aniversario del descubrimiento de América.

records.summary_en: The Minister of the Dominican Republic and Senora de Pastoriza entertained at a luncheon today at their legation on Sixteenth Street in honor of the Mexican Minister to Santo Domingo and Senora de Alvarez del Castillo. records.headline: Joseph Davies promised the Dominican Republic much easier terms
records.summary_en: Joseph Davies promised the Dominican Republic much easier terms for adjusting Trujillo's foreign debt of about $15,000,000, a syndicated Washington dispatch in the Imperial Valley Press reports. When the State Department opposed the proposal, Davies took it to the White House, where President Roosevelt intervened to conclude the arrangement. The item notes that Davies had been promised a fee of $450,000 from a nation whose annual budget is only about six millions. Although Davies received an initial sum followed by $150,000 more, Trujillo retained the other $200,000 after Davies failed to secure an expected new loan.

La nota señala que a Davies se le habían prometido honorarios de $450,000 de una nación cuyo presupuesto anual es de apenas unos seis millones. Aunque Davies recibió una suma inicial seguida de otros $150,000, Trujillo retuvo los otros $200,000 después de que Davies no lograra conseguir un nuevo préstamo previsto.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reports that newly appointed United States Ambassador to the Soviet Union Joseph E. Davies and Mrs. Davies were guests of honor at a dinner tendered them the previous evening by a group of their friends. Seated at the head table with the honorees were Attorney General Homer S. Cummings, the Soviet Ambassador and Mme. Troyanovsky, and the Minister of the Dominican Republic and Senora de Pastoriza, alongside prominent members of the organizing committee. Approximately 150 guests attended the function, which included a reception in the hotel's Chinese room followed by dinner in the presidential dining room.

records.headline: A dispatch from San Pedro de Macoris dated January 19 reports that Commodore William K. Vanderbilt's luxurious $150,000
records.summary_en: A dispatch from San Pedro de Macoris dated January 19 reports that Commodore William K. Vanderbilt's luxurious $150,000 plane, the Baby Clipper, arrived that night, ending the first leg of a projected 14,000-mile unofficial good-will air tour of South America. The plane, carrying five passengers and a crew of two, including Commodore and Mrs. Vanderbilt, Mr. and Mrs. Robert D. Huntington and Captain Earl F. White, landed at the Pan-American Airways airport for an overnight stop in the Dominican Republic.
records.summary_es: Un despacho desde San Pedro de Macoris fechado el 19 de enero informa que el lujoso avión de $150,000 del comodoro William K. Vanderbilt, el Baby Clipper, llegó esa noche, completando la primera etapa de una gira aérea no oficial de buena voluntad por Sudamérica proyectada en 14,000 millas. El avión, con cinco pasajeros y una tripulación de dos, entre ellos el comodoro y la señora Vanderbilt, el señor y la señora Robert D. Huntington y el capitán Earl F. White, aterrizó en el aeropuerto de Pan-American Airways para una escala nocturna en la República Dominicana.

records.summary_en: According to Pan American Airways reports, New York capitalist William K. Vanderbilt and his party of six landed Monday at San Pedro de Macoris in the Dominican Republic. The group had departed Miami Beach at 6:45 a.m. yesterday on a 13,385-mile goodwill flight across Central and South America aboard a luxuriously refitted 'baby clipper.' The party, consisting of Mr. and Mrs. Vanderbilt, Mr. and Mrs. Robert D. Huntington of New York, a pilot, and a mechanic, spent the night at San Pedro de Macoris.

records.summary_en: In a letter to the editor of the Evening Star, Dominican Charge d'Affaires ad Interim Emilio Garcia Godoy states that despite the hurricane that nearly destroyed Santo Domingo, the world economic crisis, and an ongoing public works program in the Dominican Republic, the government of President Trujillo Molina has made special efforts to pay both interest and amortization on its external debt punctually. To illustrate the government's attitude toward its foreign obligations, Garcia Godoy quotes an August 1934 statement by Secretary Hull praising the Dominican government for maintaining prompt payment of full interest during the world depression and setting an example worthy of emulation.

records.headline: Opening mid-article, The Washington Daily News quotes a man
records.summary_en: Opening mid-article, The Washington Daily News quotes a man named Hall whose yacht was attached by the Dominican government at Puerto Plata for a $55 food and liquor bill. Hall explained that he had recruited two crew members and five partners in Miami last June to share in a mining expedition, and that after they sailed on June 6 to meet him at Puerto Plata, he arrived on July 15 to find they had gotten drunk and incurred the debt. Fearing the bill against the vessel might now reach $600 if the Dominican Republic is feeding his penniless former partners and charging the yacht, Hall declared the expedition off and said he hopes to find new partners and raise money to release the boat for gold prospecting in Venezuela.

records.headline: Good-will airplane flights to mark the October 12 anniversary of the discovery of America
records.summary_en: Good-will airplane flights to mark the October 12 anniversary of the discovery of America were announced by Cuban Ambassador Pedro Martinez Fraga and Dominican Minister Andres Pastoriza. Four planes bearing the names of the vessels in Christopher Columbus' discovery fleet are scheduled to depart from Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic, on October 12 and return there on December 18 after flying across South America and north to Canada, with a stopover in Washington.
records.summary_es: Vuelos de buena voluntad para conmemorar el aniversario del descubrimiento de América el 12 de octubre fueron anunciados por el embajador de Cuba, Pedro Martinez Fraga, y el ministro de la República Dominicana, Andres Pastoriza. Cuatro aviones con los nombres de las naves de la flota descubridora de Cristóbal Colón despegarán de Ciudad Trujillo, República Dominicana, el 12 de octubre y regresarán allí el 18 de diciembre tras volar hacia América del Sur y al norte hasta Canadá, incluyendo una escala en Washington.

records.headline: An Evening Star feature recounts the 1916 operations of the U.S. Marine Corps 4th
records.summary_en: An Evening Star feature recounts the 1916 operations of the U.S. Marine Corps 4th Regiment in the Dominican Republic, noting the occupation of Santiago and the appointment of Rear Admiral Harry S. records.headline: Continuing an account of the U.S. Marine Corps Fourth Regiment
records.summary_en: Continuing an account of the U.S. Marine Corps Fourth Regiment in the northern district of the Dominican Republic—covering Monte Cristi, Santiago, Puerto Plata, Espaillat, La Vega, Pacificador, and Samana until troop concentration was ordered in 1922—the Evening Star notes that Col. Dion Williams relieved Gen. Pendleton in 1919 due to the latter's ill health. By June 1924, Fourth Regiment officers reported to Washington that banditry was practically wiped out in the Dominican Republic, with the regiment concentrated at Monte Cristi, Sanchez, and San Francisco de Macoris. In July 1924 the unit received orders to return to the United States and was reorganized at San Diego that September.

Para junio de 1924, los oficiales del Cuarto Regimiento informaron a Washington que el bandolerismo estaba prácticamente erradicado en la República Dominicana, concentrándose el regimiento en Monte Cristi, Sanchez y San Francisco de Macoris. records.headline: A good-will flight promoting the construction of a memorial
records.summary_en: A good-will flight promoting the construction of a memorial lighthouse to Christopher Columbus at Punta Torrecilla in the Dominican Republic was planned, Cuban Ambassador Dr. Pedro Martinez Fraga and Dominican Minister Andres Pastoriza announced. Three Cuban airplanes will depart Havana on October 10 for Trujillo City and join a Dominican plane to form the "Columbine Squad," which will take off from the Dominican capital on October 12—marking 455 years since the discovery of America—on a tour outlined in a Buenos Aires Peace Conference resolution. The squadron is scheduled to visit Washington on December 5–6 and New York on December 6–7.
records.summary_es: Un vuelo de buena voluntad para promover la construcción de un faro conmemorativo a Cristóbal Colón en Punta Torrecilla, en la República Dominicana, fue planificado, según anunciaron el embajador de Cuba, Dr. Pedro Martinez Fraga, y el ministro de la República Dominicana, Andres Pastoriza. Tres aviones cubanos saldrán de La Habana el 10 de octubre hacia Trujillo City y se unirán allí a un avión dominicano para formar la «Columbine Squad», que despegará de la capital dominicana el 12 de octubre —conmemorando 455 años del descubrimiento de América— en una gira trazada en una resolución de la Conferencia de Paz de Buenos Aires. La escuadrilla tiene previsto visitar Washington el 5 y 6 de diciembre y Nueva York el 6 y 7 de diciembre.

records.headline: The Evening star recounts that Rafael Trujillo began his career
records.summary_en: The Evening star recounts that Rafael Trujillo began his career as a telegraph operator in his hometown of San Cristobal and rose to colonel at the head of the United States Marine-trained constabulary. Now 46, he is credited with executing a large program of public improvements—including road repairs, new highways and bridges, and port improvements—without foreign loans or an increase in public debt, while the capital, Trujillo City (formerly Santo Domingo), is described as one of the cleanest cities in the Caribbean. The column also lists a three-day Cuban special stamp issue sold from October 13 to 15 in 22 denominations totaling $1.72, which includes a 5-cent stamp for the Dominican Republic alongside issues for Haiti, the United States, and other American nations.
records.summary_es: El Evening star relata que Rafael Trujillo inició su carrera como operador de telégrafo en su pueblo natal de San Cristobal y ascendió a coronel al frente de la guardia entrenada por la Infantería de Marina de los Estados Unidos. Ahora con 46 años, se le atribuye la ejecución de un amplio plan de mejoras públicas —incluyendo reparaciones de caminos, nuevas carreteras y puentes, y mejoras portuarias— sin préstamos extranjeros ni aumento de la deuda pública, mientras que la capital, Trujillo City (anteriormente Santo Domingo), es descrita como una de las ciudades más limpias del Caribe. La columna también enumera una emisión especial de sellos cubanos de tres días vendida del 13 al 15 de octubre en 22 denominaciones por un valor nominal total de $1.72, que incluye un sello de 5 centavos para la República Dominicana junto con emisiones para Haití, los Estados Unidos y otras naciones americanas.

records.headline: The U.S. Administration has ordered Norweb to leave the international
records.summary_en: The U.S. Administration has ordered Norweb to leave the international radio conference in Havana, Cuba, and return immediately to his post, a move that lent credence to reports that soldiers of President General Trujillo had slaughtered 1000 Haitians near the Dominican border early in October. In New York, Haitian Foreign Minister Georges Leger confirmed dispatches from Santiago, Cuba, regarding the killings and is scheduled to travel to Washington on Monday to confer with President Roosevelt. The report attributes the massacre to unsatisfactory economic conditions and overcrowding in Haiti, noting that thousands of Haitians had reportedly crossed the Dominican border to take jobs at very low wages, reputedly provoking resentment among Dominicans.
records.summary_es: El gobierno estadounidense ha ordenado a Norweb abandonar la conferencia internacional de radio en La Habana, Cuba, y regresar de inmediato a su puesto, una medida que dio credibilidad a los informes de que los soldados del presidente general Trujillo habían matado a 1000 haitianos cerca de la frontera dominicana a principios de octubre. En Nueva York, el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores de Haití, Georges Leger, confirmó los despachos procedentes de Santiago de Cuba sobre la matanza y tiene previsto viajar a Washington el lunes para conferenciar con el presidente Roosevelt. El informe atribuye la masacre a las condiciones económicas insatisfactorias y a la sobrepoblación en Haití, señalando que miles de haitianos habrían cruzado la frontera dominicana para aceptar empleos con salarios sumamente bajos, lo que supuestamente provocó resentimiento entre los dominicanos.

records.headline: An order to return at once to the Dominican Republic on Sunday's
records.summary_en: An order to return at once to the Dominican Republic on Sunday's first available plane lent credence to reports that soldiers of President General Trujillo had slaughtered 1,000 Haitians near the border early in October. In New York, Haitian Foreign Minister Georges Leger confirmed United Press dispatches from Santiago, Cuba, reporting the killings, and the United Press learned he is scheduled to go to Washington on Monday to confer on Tuesday with President Roosevelt and Assistant Secretary of State Sumner Welles regarding the crisis. Recent developments appeared to substantiate weeks of unconfirmed diplomatic reports of massacres on the Haitian-Dominican border and rising tension in both nations, with news of the killings having reached Haitian officials in Port au Prince slowly due to the remoteness of the district.

Los recientes acontecimientos parecían corroborar los informes diplomáticos no confirmados durante varias semanas sobre masacres en la frontera domínico-haitiana y el aumento de la tensión en ambos países, habiendo llegado lentamente la noticia a los funcionarios haitianos en Port au Prince debido a la lejanía del distrito.

Dominican Republic Says Haiti Incident Is Closed

By United Press

CIUDAD TRUJILLO, Dominican Republic, Nov. 8—A government statement said today that the recent frontier "incident" in which more than 1000 Haitian persons were reported killed had been closed.

The incident was not of international character, the statement said, but was a private dispute between individuals on both sides of the frontier. It also denied troops had been sent to the border.

"The Dominican Republic continues its peaceful intentions as always," the statement concluded.

records.headline: The United Press reports that President Roosevelt offered the good
records.summary_en: The United Press reports that President Roosevelt offered the good offices of the United States, together with Mexico and Cuba, to mediate the crisis between the Dominican Republic and Haiti stemming from the alleged slaughter of 5000 Haitians the previous month. According to the State Department, Cuba had already tendered its good offices and Mexico was set to make a parallel offer immediately. In separate telegrams to Haitian President Stenio Vincent and Dominican President Rafael Trujillo, Roosevelt stated the desire of the United States to help achieve an early, satisfactory settlement in the spirit of the peace treaties adopted at the Buenos Aires Conference the previous year.
records.summary_es: La United Press informa que el presidente Roosevelt ofreció los buenos oficios de los Estados Unidos, conjuntamente con México y Cuba, para mediar en la crisis entre la República Dominicana y Haití desencadenada por la supuesta matanza de 5000 haitianos el mes anterior. Según el Departamento de Estado, Cuba ya había extendido sus buenos oficios y México haría una oferta similar de inmediato. En telegramas separados dirigidos al presidente haitiano Stenio Vincent y al presidente dominicano Rafael Trujillo, Roosevelt expresó el deseo de los Estados Unidos de ayudar a alcanzar un arreglo satisfactorio lo antes posible dentro del espíritu de los tratados de paz adoptados en la Conferencia de Buenos Aires el año anterior.

records.headline: The times-news reports that President Trujillo rose to high
records.summary_en: The times-news reports that President Trujillo rose to high office from the post of railroad telegraph operator and has accumulated a personal fortune estimated at several million dollars. records.headline: Reports published in The Washington daily news state that Haitians
records.summary_en: Reports published in The Washington daily news state that Haitians were slaughtered on successive days and nights over a wide area well inside Dominican territory rather than in border clashes. An October 16, 1937 communication from the Dominican Republic recounts that while President Trujillo was attending a dance in his honor during a trip to the Cibao District, he was informed of cattle stealing by Haitians from Dominican ranches and delivered a strong speech indicating that drastic steps would be taken to stop it. During the following week, Dominican National Police and army members reportedly visited Haitian families to serve deportation orders and herded hundreds to the border, with authentic sources reporting up to 1300 dead men, women, and children, travelers describing the area from Dajabon north to Monte Cristi as looking like a battlefield, and further killings and disappearances reported in San Francisco de Macoris and Santiago.
records.summary_es: Informes publicados en The Washington daily news señalan que ciudadanos haitianos fueron masacrados durante días y noches sucesivos en una amplia zona bien adentro del territorio dominicano, y no en enfrentamientos fronterizos. Una comunicación fechada el 16 de octubre de 1937 desde la República Dominicana relata que, mientras el presidente Trujillo asistía a un baile en su honor durante un viaje al distrito del Cibao, fue informado sobre el robo de ganado por parte de haitianos en haciendas dominicanas y pronunció un enérgico discurso indicando que se tomarían medidas drásticas para detenerlo. Durante la semana siguiente, miembros de la Policía Nacional Dominicana y del ejército habrían visitado a familias haitianas para entregarles órdenes de deportación y arreado a cientos hacia la frontera, informando fuentes auténticas de hasta 1300 muertos entre hombres, mujeres y niños, mientras viajeros describieron la zona desde Dajabon hacia el norte hasta Monte Cristi como un campo de batalla y se reportaron más muertes y desapariciones en San Francisco de Macoris y Santiago.

records.headline: The Waterbury Democrat reports that population pressure on the island
records.summary_en: The Waterbury Democrat reports that population pressure on the island shared by Haiti and Santo Domingo, or the Dominican Republic, has driven Haitians across the border in search of work, provoking resentment among Dominicans who want the jobs for their own people. According to the article, Dominican prisons were reportedly packed with prisoners who were all assassinated, and an American correspondent described the massacres as one of history's major crimes, reporting that rural police rounded up Haitians in bands of about 150 and brought them to Dajabon. Barred from crossing by the bridge, the Haitians were reportedly led six at a time into a forest belt south of the customs house, where men armed with clubs, bayonets, machetes, and three-pointed daggers killed the men, women, and children, with five thousand reported slaughtered in this and other ways.
records.summary_es: The Waterbury Democrat informa que la presión demográfica en la isla compartida por Haití y Santo Domingo, o la República Dominicana, ha impulsado recientemente a los haitianos a cruzar la frontera en busca de trabajo, provocando resentimiento entre los dominicanos que desean los empleos para su propio pueblo. Según el artículo, las prisiones dominicanas habrían estado repletas de prisioneros que fueron todos asesinados, y un corresponsal estadounidense describió las masacres como uno de los mayores crímenes de la historia, informando que la policía rural reunió a los haitianos en grupos de unos 150 y los llevó a Dajabon. Impedidos de cruzar por el puente, los haitianos habrían sido conducidos de seis en seis hacia una franja boscosa al sur de la aduana, donde hombres armados con garrotes, bayonetas, machetes y dagas de tres puntas mataron a hombres, mujeres y niños, informándose de cinco mil muertos de esta y otras maneras.

records.full_text:
Massacre Stories Assailed as Lies

By LOUIS JAY HEATH
United Press Staff Correspondent

Haitian and Dominican politicians and revolutionists were charged with malicious distortion of a “small incident” which took place early in October near the Dominican-Haitian border, in a formal communique issued by Dominican Minister Andres Pastoriza here today.

Haitian officials have charged that the so-called “small incident” referred to by Pastoriza consisted of “brutal killings of from 3000 to 5000 Haitian nationals by Dominican soldiers and police.” At the request of the Haitian government the United States, Mexico and Cuba have tendered their good offices to mediate the incident. To date the Dominican government has not accepted the tender and has sent special envoys to all three capitols to present the Dominican case.

The Pastoriza communique, addressed to editors, stated that the Dominican government already considered the “incident closed.”

USED BY ENEMIES
“The small incident . . . between Dominican citizens and Haitian citizens who were maintaining illegal residence in certain zones of the Dominican Republic, or who were violently entering the Dominican Republic,” the communique said, “is being used by political enemies of President Trujillo (of the Dominican Republic) and by Haitian elements interested in covering up the political unrest existing for some time in the Republic of Haiti. . . .”

“The bloody encounters which took place near the Dominican-Haitian border as a consequence of the illegal

(Continued on Page 32)

Haiti

(Continued From Page 1)

penetration of Haitian citizens into Dominican territory have been described and, apparently, believed as such in certain circles, as 'mass slaughter' of women and children and as orgies of boundless savagery. Of course any person even half informed, who has read the news published up to this time in connection with those 'massacres' will have realized that such news are based on rumors and clearly show the falsehoods invented by those interested elements to whom we have previously referred.

GROSS EXAGGERATION

“To speak of thousands of deaths in the clashes between small groups of Dominican civilians and Haitian citizens involved in an illegal and undesirable immigration is simply a gross exaggeration. And to affirm that the Haitians who were residing near Dajabon were taken to Monte Christy to be placed aboard a boat and returned to their country, is either an unpardonable evidence of ignorance of geography or proof of patent bad faith. Between the city of Dajabon and the Haitian territory there is only a small and narrow river.

“The alleged 'massacres' took place, according to the rumors received by the newspapers, in the vicinity of Dajabon during the first days of October. Across the river from Dajabon lies the Haitian city of Juana Mendez, which has telephonic communications and good highways with the principal cities of Haiti. Obviously it is illogical to suppose that the reports of a 'massacre' of the nature described by 'unidentified correspondents' did not reach the city of Juana Mendez until more than a month after its occurrence.

“There are more than 60,000 Haitians who reside legally in the Dominican Republic. They are protected by the laws of the country, and are working in peace and appreciation of the hospitality which they are receiving. This fact is very well known to the revolutionists of New York as well as to their friends, the Haitian politicians, who are attempting by means of ridiculous and fantastic exaggerations, and in furtherance of ill-concealed ambitions, to make this incident, already considered as closed by the Dominican Government, an international incident.”

records.headline: Comparing the two republics sharing the island, The daily Alaska empire
records.summary_en: Comparing the two republics sharing the island, The daily Alaska empire notes that Spanish-speaking Santo Domingo broke away from Spain before the U.S. Civil War, whereas French-speaking Haiti broke away from France around the French Revolution. The article states that although the Dominican Republic has experienced many revolutions, it has had far less race bitterness than Haiti, resulting in greater prosperity and a more inviting environment to live. According to the paper, this disparity is a major reason why Haitians have drifted across the border, which in most places is marked only on a map or by simple barriers such as a wooden gate across a highway.
records.summary_es: Al comparar las dos repúblicas que comparten la isla, The daily Alaska empire señala que Santo Domingo, de habla española, se independizó de España antes de la Guerra Civil estadounidense, mientras que Haití, de habla francesa, se separó de Francia hacia la época de la Revolución Francesa. El artículo afirma que, aunque la República Dominicana ha tenido numerosas revoluciones, ha experimentado mucho menos rencor racial que Haití, lo que se ha traducido en una mayor prosperidad y en un lugar más atractivo para vivir. Según el periódico, esta disparidad es una razón principal por la que los haitianos han cruzado hacia el otro lado de la frontera, la cual en la mayoría de los lugares solo está marcada en un mapa o mediante barreras simples como un portón de madera en una carretera.

records.summary_en: Emissaries of President Trujillo of Santo Domingo reportedly recruited Negro League baseball players—prompting strong complaints from the Pittsburgh Crawfords—after the dictator learned fighting and baseball during eight years with the United States Marines prior to the end of the occupation in 1924. According to the White Bluffs spokesman, after rising from private to brigadier general and taking over the country in 1930—which his enemies said he accomplished by double-crossing President Horacio Vasquez —he made baseball a major part of his planned economy, helped build up the Central American league, hosted parties for visiting teams at his palace in Ciudad Trujillo, and jailed a strong opposition in 1933. The article adds that several thousand exiles have maintained a junta in New York City led by former Dominican Minister to Washington Dr. Angel Morales, accusing Trujillo of wholesale killings and the suppression of political and civil rights, while referencing the April 1935 murder in New York of former secretary of war Sergio Bencosme.

Having learned fighting and baseball during eight years with the United States Marines until the occupation ended in 1924, the Santo Domingo dictator rose from farm boy and army private to brigadier general, took power in 1930—by double-crossing President Horacio Vasquez, according to his enemies—and made baseball a central feature of his planned economy, hosting large parties for visiting teams at his palace in Ciudad Trujillo. After he jailed a strong opposition in 1933, several thousand exiles maintained a New York City junta led by former Dominican Minister to Washington Dr. Angel Morales, accusing Trujillo of wholesale killings and the suppression of political and civil rights, while the passage also notes the April 1935 murder in New York of former secretary of war Sergio Bencosme.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published an analysis attributing cross-border tensions between Haiti and the Dominican Republic to acute hunger and agricultural underproduction resulting from Haiti's dense population. The writer argued that food shortages drove impoverished Haitians across the frontier to steal livestock and farm animals. In turn, isolated Dominican homesteaders strongly resented these cattle thefts and feared for their lives and families.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* publicó un análisis que atribuía las tensiones fronterizas entre Haití y la República Dominicana al hambre aguda y al déficit de producción agrícola causados por la alta densidad demográfica haitiana. El autor sostenía que la escasez de alimentos empujaba a haitianos desposeídos a cruzar la frontera para robar ganado y animales de labranza. Por su parte, los campesinos dominicanos de zonas aisladas resentían profundamente esos robos pecuarios y temían por la integridad de sus familias y vidas.
records.passage: cattle and farm animals. Haiti's teeming population literally cannot subsist on what is produced by their country's backward agriculture. Considerably greater production would be possible in Haiti, despite the fact that the soil has been treated villainously ever since the French were expelled, if it were not for a racial trait which is characteristic of the island. Well does the Haitian peasant know this weakness of his fellow-countrymen. Of what use for him—or, more accurately, for his wife—to work hard and produce an abundance if some one else is to reap the benefit? In Haiti, the prudent peasant never allows fruit to ripen on his trees—if he does, his neighbors, on the first dark night that comes along, will pick it for him. Thus the situation in Haiti is a combination of dense population with underproduction of food. When such a situation comes into being in any country it means trouble—trouble within the country and trouble for the neighbors without. Hunger Basic Cause. In a word, it is hunger, and not just a propensity for vicious thievery, that drives the poverty-stricken Haitians to commit depredations. records.headline: In a surprise raid, a band of 30 Haitian farmers armed with machetes
records.summary_en: In a surprise raid, a band of 30 Haitian farmers armed with machetes struck the frontier town of Capotillo, near the border of the Dominican Province of Monte Cristi, killing or wounding a large number of Dominicans and carrying off livestock and farm produce, a December 4 government announcement from the Dominican Republic stated. According to the secretary of interior and police, this was the first border clash officially reported at Ciudad Trujillo, whereas Haitian officials had stated the previous month that between 3,000 and 5,000 Haitians had been killed by Dominican armed forces during troubles stemming from the wholesale expulsion of Haitian workers. Meanwhile, diplomatic discussions have continued in Washington aimed at reaching an eventual settlement of the controversy.
records.summary_es: En un ataque sorpresivo, una banda de 30 campesinos haitianos armados con machetes atacó el poblado fronterizo de Capotillo, cerca de la frontera de la provincia dominicana de Monte Cristi, matando o hiriendo a un gran número de dominicanos y llevándose ganado y productos agrícolas, según afirmó un anuncio gubernamental del 4 de diciembre desde la República Dominicana. Según el secretario de Interior y Policía, este fue el primer choque fronterizo reportado oficialmente en Ciudad Trujillo, mientras que funcionarios haitianos habían declarado el mes anterior que entre 3,000 y 5,000 haitianos habían sido muertos por las fuerzas armadas dominicanas en disturbios derivados de la expulsión masiva de trabajadores haitianos. Entretanto, han continuado las conversaciones diplomáticas en Washington con miras a lograr un eventual arreglo de la controversia.

records.headline: Ernesto Bonetti Burgos, 43, Dominican secretary of state for foreign affairs
records.summary_en: Ernesto Bonetti Burgos, 43, Dominican secretary of state for foreign affairs since 1936, died on Friday in Trujillo City, Dominican Republic, word received at the Dominican Legation in Washington reported. Bonetti Burgos had been treated for several months at Johns Hopkins University Hospital in Baltimore before leaving about a month earlier. Earlier in his career, he served as private secretary to his uncle, Dominican President J. B. Vicini Burgos, was Speaker of the House of the Dominican Republic from 1924 to 1930, and served as Dominican Minister to Germany in 1935.

records.full_text:
MINISTER OF HAITI DEPLORES CLASHES Lescot Says "Nothing Can Blot Out Unfortunate Events" in Border Dispute.

By the Associated Press.

Haitian Minister Elie Lescot said yesterday "nothing can blot out the tragic and unfortunate events already well known" in connection with the dispute between his country and the Dominican Republic.

The Minister's statement was issued after publication of reports from Ciudad Trujillo quoting Dominican authorities to the effect "a large number" of Dominican farmers had been killed or wounded in an attack by Haitians on a Dominican frontier community.

The statement said it was prompted by "certain news given out by the press, which seems to have its source in an organized propaganda." At the Haitian Legation an official said the Minister was absent, but added he understood the statement referred "not only to the latest reports from Ciudad Trujillo, but to other news as well."

It has been the Haitian government's contention that unprovoked attacks by Dominicans on Haitian citizens residing in Dominican territory were the cause of the tension on the West Indies island which both republics occupy. Haitian Foreign Minister Georges Leger, during a recent visit here, said "at least" 3,000 Haitians had been slain in "wholesale massacres."

PORT-AU-PRINCE, Haiti, Dec. 6 (AP).—Minister of Interior Duvigneaud yesterday declared the Haitian government had no knowledge of new Haiti-Dominican frontier outbreaks reported officially by the Dominican government.

records.headline: President Vincent asserted that the border question which once existed had
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Haitian President Sténio Vincent estimated 8,000 Haitians were assassinated in the Dominican Republic, maintaining that the border dispute had already been settled by treaty two years prior. Vincent asserted that the Dominican government should have used standard diplomatic channels to repatriate undesirable foreigners, rather than resorting to violence without warning. While Vincent requested mediation from the United States, Cuba, and Mexico, President Trujillo expressed surprise at the appeal, pointing to existing bilateral accords.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el presidente haitiano Sténio Vincent estimó en 8.000 los haitianos asesinados en la República Dominicana, sosteniendo que la disputa de límites ya había quedado resuelta mediante tratado hacía dos años. Vincent aseveró que el gobierno dominicano debió recurrir a los canales diplomáticos habituales para repatriar a los extranjeros indeseables en lugar de acudir a la violencia sin previo aviso. Mientras Vincent solicitaba la mediación de Estados Unidos, Cuba y México, el presidente Trujillo expresó sorpresa ante dicha apelación señalando la vigencia de los acuerdos bilaterales.
records.passage: President Vincent asserted that the border question which once existed had been settled, largely at the initiative of the Haitian government two years ago when a treaty was signed by the two nations. He said there had been no border question since then. Usual Channels Open. "If the Dominican government wanted to expel foreigners they believed for one reason or another undesirable. they could have used the usual channels, the same as Cuba did when it repatriated thousands of Haitians from Cuba recently," President Vincent said. "I vow that this government has never received the slightest indications that Haitians, many of whom resided in the Dominican Republic for many -years, suddenly had become undesirable, until I heard of the assassinations." President Vincent's estimate of 8.000 slain was higher even than reports circulating on the streets of this sultry little mountain capital, where the populace is clamoring for strong measures in dealing with the Dominican Republic. The United States State Department on November 13 announced it had received a request from President Vincent for the United States to offer its good offices, together with Cuba and Mexico, toward seeking a solution of the Haitian-Dominican controversy. When President Rafael Leonidas Trujillo of the Dominican Republic learned of President Vincent's action, he expressed surprise that the United States, Cuba and Mexico had been asked to mediate. He mentioned a diplomatic accord which exists between the two governments.

records.headline: Following claims the previous month that Dominican armed forces
records.summary_en: Following claims the previous month that Dominican armed forces had killed between 3,000 and 5,000 Haitians during the wholesale expulsion of Haitian workers, Dominican officials acknowledged clashes had occurred, admitted the Dominican consul in Cape Haitien had been withdrawn, and called the Haitian reports "fantastic," while Dominican Minister to the United States Andres Pastoriza charged that political enemies of Haitian President Stenio Vincent and Dominican President Trujillo had exaggerated the border troubles to embarrass both administrations. Conferences have taken place among representatives of the two West Indian republics and the mediating nations of the United States, Mexico, and Cuba. In Port-au-Prince, Haiti, Minister of Interior Duvigneaud declared on Monday that the Haitian government had no knowledge of new frontier outbreaks after the Dominican government officially reported that a raid by 30 Haitian farmers across the border had killed or wounded a large number of Dominicans.
records.summary_es: Tras las afirmaciones del mes anterior de que las fuerzas armadas dominicanas habían matado a entre 3,000 y 5,000 haitianos durante la expulsión masiva de trabajadores haitianos, funcionarios dominicanos admitieron que habían ocurrido enfrentamientos y que el cónsul dominicano en Cape Haitien había sido retirado, pero calificaron los informes haitianos de «fantásticos», mientras que el ministro dominicano en los Estados Unidos, Andres Pastoriza, acusó a los enemigos políticos del presidente haitiano Stenio Vincent y del presidente dominicano Trujillo de exagerar los problemas fronterizos para crear dificultades a ambos gobiernos. Se han celebrado conferencias entre representantes de las dos repúblicas antillanas y los países mediadores: Estados Unidos, México y Cuba. En Port-au-Prince, Haití, el ministro del Interior Duvigneaud declaró el lunes que el gobierno haitiano no tenía conocimiento de nuevos brotes fronterizos luego de que el gobierno dominicano anunciara oficialmente que una incursión de 30 campesinos haitianos a través de la frontera había matado o herido a un gran número de dominicanos.

records.headline: Commenting on efforts to arbitrate the Dominican dispute with Haiti
records.summary_en: Commenting on efforts to arbitrate the Dominican dispute with Haiti, an editorial notes that Trujillo is accused of causing the slaughter of 8,000 Haitians yet refuses arbitration. The writer argues that a "sound spanking" may be in order and warns that Pan-American peace machinery, the Good Neighbor policy, and the contest between dictatorship and democracy are at stake if the United States lets itself be stepped on by an "upstart dictator in its own backyard." The piece recalls that when Trujillo previously imprisoned an Italian citizen illegally, Mussolini dispatched a destroyer toward the Dominican Republic and the prisoner was quickly freed.

El texto recuerda que cuando Trujillo encarceló ilegalmente a un ciudadano italiano tiempo atrás, Mussolini envió un destructor rumbo a la República Dominicana y el prisionero fue liberado de inmediato.

records.headline: A geographical survey of the Dominican-Haitian border traces
records.summary_en: A geographical survey of the Dominican-Haitian border traces the frontier from the Copotillo River over West Indies mountain peaks covered in pines and oaks, down into the desert trough near Manneville and Lake Enriquillo—150 feet below sea level—and southward over the mile-high Sierra de Bahoruco and along the Rio Pedernales to the Caribbean. Although no railroad crosses the border, two motor roads link the two nations—one crossing the Rio Copotillo at Dajabon in the north and another running midway between Lascahobas in Haiti and the Dominican village of Las Matas—while a narrow-gauge railway from Port-au-Prince nears the border at Manneville, where an unimproved road leads to Ciudad Trujillo. Despite sharp social contrasts, both countries share similar scenery and economic resources, exporting sugar, tobacco, coffee, and cacao.
records.summary_es: Una reseña geográfica de la frontera dominico-haitiana traza el límite desde el río Copotillo a través de picos montañosos de las Indias Occidentales cubiertos de pinos y robles, descendiendo hacia la depresión desértica cerca de Manneville y el lago Enriquillo —a 150 pies bajo el nivel del mar— y hacia el sur sobre la Sierra de Bahoruco, de más de una milla de altura, y a lo largo del río Pedernales hasta el Caribe. Aunque ningún ferrocarril cruza la frontera, dos carreteras unen a ambas naciones —una que cruza el río Copotillo en Dajabon en el norte y otra a mitad de camino entre Lascahobas en Haití y el poblado dominicano de Las Matas—, mientras que un ferrocarril de vía estrecha desde Puerto Príncipe se acerca a la frontera en Manneville, donde un camino sin mejorar conecta con Ciudad Trujillo. Pese a los marcados contrastes sociales, ambos países comparten paisajes y recursos económicos similares, exportando azúcar, tabaco, café y cacao.

records.headline: Reporting on the slaying of Haitian citizens on Dominican soil
records.summary_en: Reporting on the slaying of Haitian citizens on Dominican soil—which President Trujillo termed a "local incident"—this dispatch surveys explanations ranging from alleged Dominican annexation designs or a fabricated "foreign crisis" to Haitian squatters taking Dominican property, while pointing to traditional hatreds and economic rivalry as more likely causes. The writer contrasts French-speaking Haiti with the Spanish-speaking Dominican Republic, where Trujillo rules two-thirds of the island and some 1,500,000 citizens compared with Haiti's double population on one-third, and notes three past Haitian invasions and a 22-year occupation (dating the last invasion in the text to 1922). According to the article, the October outbreaks were linked to pre-season plans for the Dominican sugar harvest, in which Haitian laborers are annually authorized to work long hours in the canefields for 20 to 25 cents a day, though it remains unclear whether Dominicans sought those jobs for themselves or whether Haitians committed any acts of provocation.
records.summary_es: Al informar sobre la matanza de ciudadanos haitianos en suelo dominicano —que el presidente Trujillo calificó de "incidente local"—, este despacho examina explicaciones que van desde supuestos planes dominicanos de anexión o una "crisis exterior" fabricada hasta ocupantes ilegales haitianos que tomaban propiedades dominicanas, aunque señala los odios tradicionales y la rivalidad económica como causas más probables. El autor contrasta al Haití de lengua francesa con la República Dominicana de habla hispana, donde Trujillo gobierna dos tercios de la isla y a unos 1,500,000 ciudadanos frente al doble de población de Haití en un tercio del territorio, y menciona tres invasiones haitianas pasadas y una ocupación de 22 años (fechando en el texto la última invasión en 1922). Según el artículo, los disturbios de octubre estuvieron vinculados con los planes previos a la zafra azucarera dominicana, en la que anualmente se autoriza a braceros haitianos a trabajar largas jornadas en los cañaverales por 20 a 25 centavos diarios, aunque no está claro si los dominicanos quisieron esos empleos para sí o si hubo actos de provocación por parte de los haitianos.

records.full_text:
Haiti Charges Troops Bashed Babies to Death

By LOUIS J. HEATH

Copyright, 1937, by United Press

An estimated 10,000 Haitians, terrified by alleged ruthless attacks by Dominican rural police and soldiery which cost the lives of "thousands" of their fellow countrymen in the Dominican Republic, have fled to their homeland, it was reported here today.

A report from an American resident in northern Haiti, dated Dec. 18, said more than 5000 Haitians had crossed the border and the flow of refugees was continuing.

Meanwhile Elie Lescot, Haitian minister to the United States, in an official communique issued here, fixed the number of Haitian victims of the alleged mass killings at 12,168.

The communique charged that mass killings had taken place in more than 65 Dominican localities almost simultaneously and at a given signal. The document alleges that victims were slain without distinction as to age or sex, that pregnant women were shot and that children were stabbed and their heads beaten against walls.

Lescot's estimate of the number of dead was the highest thus far. President Stenio Vincent of Haiti recently placed the figure at 8000. The communique was issued at the order of the Haitian government.

CITES PRESIDENT'S SPEECH

The American's report said stories of wounded refugees, substantiated by Father Robert, a priest of Ouanaminthe, convinced the American that "several thousand Haitians were killed."

The American reported that he went to Ouanaminthe Oct. 7 to investigate reports that 212 Haitians had crossed the border on the previous day at that point and that he found a large crowd of refugees awaiting word from relatives from whom they had become separated in flight. The refugees, the writer said, reported that President Rafael Leonidas Trujillo Molena made a speech at a ball at Dajabon on Oct. 3 and that the attacks on the Haitians began immediately thereafter.

HURLED INTO SEA

"I saw the Haitian consul, who closed his office in Dajabon on Oct. 7 on the grounds that the attitude of the Dominican authorities was so threatening he felt his life was in danger," the report continued. "He had seen four murdered Haitians on Oct. 5 in a house in Dajabon but had not been permitted to make any investigation — or even to bury the dead. The civil authorities told him that it was a matter for the local military commander to handle, and when he appealed to the commander he was advised that the Sanitary Service would take care of the matter and that he could not guarantee the life of any Haitian."

The report described the arrival of a group of refugees who had been hiding at Monte Christi.

"These people stated that on Sunday night a group of 50 Haitians had been marched to the wharf at Monte Christi by a number of Guardia (Dominican rural police) and thrown into the sea and drowned," the writer reported.

WHOLESALE ARRESTS

"On the following day wholesale arrests began of all Haitians unable to hide themselves or flee during the night."

The Haitian government, it was reported, provided trucks and a small motor vessel to aid the flight of their nationals. Fourteen Haitians were brought to one border hospital, all suffering from knife or machete wounds.

"In most cases they insisted that they were the only survivors of their groups and had escaped by feigning death after being wounded," the report went on.

A report from J. M. Jan, French Bishop of Cape Haitian, quoted President Trujillo as having said substantially that he had investigated complaints of Dominicans against "depredations of Haitians in their midst" and said, "I can settle that."

FED TO SHARKS

" 'We have begun to settle the question; already 300 Haitians are dead at Banica and the settlement must continue,'" the bishop quotes Trujillo as saying.

The prelate records that he questioned a Frenchman refugee who escaped because of his nationality and who reported that Haitians were herded into Monte Christi, thrown into the sea as food for sharks, "led into the woods near the city to be massacred and told of nameless savageries which the pen cannot describe."

records.headline: In a December 1937 message from Ciudad Trujillo addressed to the President of the Dominican
records.summary_en: In a December 1937 message from Ciudad Trujillo addressed to the President of the Dominican Senate, President Trujillo states that Law No. 1203 of November 4, 1936, on the repression of communism and similar doctrines has lost its reason for existence because the causes behind its enactment have disappeared. He explains that the law was originally passed to prevent communist outcroppings—driven by personal political ambition rather than social justice—from taking hold through imitation and hampering his government's efforts on behalf of the Republic's working classes. When he initiated the measure under his constitutional prerogatives, Trujillo adds, he believed that terroristic violence and subversive, anarchical aims could plunge the country into a bloody class struggle between capital and labor.
records.summary_es: En un mensaje de diciembre de 1937 desde Ciudad Trujillo dirigido al presidente del Senado dominicano, el presidente Trujillo afirma que la Ley No. 1203 del 4 de noviembre de 1936, sobre la represión del comunismo y doctrinas similares, ha perdido su razón de ser porque han desaparecido las causas que motivaron su promulgación. Explica que la ley fue aprobada originalmente para evitar que ciertos brotes de comunismo —inspirados en la ambición política personal más que en la justicia social— arraigaran por imitación y obstaculizaran los esfuerzos de su gobierno en beneficio de las clases trabajadoras de la República. Trujillo añade que, cuando inició la medida en virtud de sus prerrogativas constitucionales, consideraba que la violencia terrorista y los fines subversivos y anárquicos podían sumir al país en una sangrienta lucha de clases entre el capital y el trabajo.

records.headline: Following a parenthetical note that President Trujillo came
records.summary_en: Following a parenthetical note that President Trujillo came to power in the 1930 revolution, sent many political opponents into exile, imposed strict press censorship, and later accepted the "good offices" of United States, Mexican, and Cuban arbitrators, this profile describes him seated on the porch of his farmhouse 20 miles west of Ciudad Trujillo. Rather than discuss charges that Dominicans were killing Haitians, Trujillo preferred to speak of his 2,500 head of Holstein cattle and his government's public works program, calling the border affair a "purely local incident" under judicial investigation. Turning to political philosophy, the former farmer and soldier declared that a leader in his position must show no fear lest he and his people be lost.
records.summary_es: Tras una nota entre paréntesis que señala que el presidente Trujillo llegó al poder en la revolución de 1930, envió a muchos opositores políticos al exilio, impuso una estricta censura de prensa y más tarde aceptó los "buenos oficios" de árbitros de Estados Unidos, México y Cuba, esta semblanza lo describe sentado en el pórtico de su casa de campo a 20 millas al oeste de Ciudad Trujillo. En lugar de hablar sobre las acusaciones de que los dominicanos estaban matando a haitianos, Trujillo prefirió conversar sobre sus 2,500 cabezas de ganado Holstein y el programa de obras públicas de su gobierno, calificando el asunto fronterizo de "incidente puramente local" bajo investigación judicial. Pasando a la filosofía política, el exagricultor y militar declaró que un gobernante en su posición no debe mostrar miedo alguno, pues de lo contrario él y su pueblo estarían perdidos.

records.headline: A December 27 dispatch reports that the presidents of the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: A December 27 dispatch reports that the presidents of the Dominican Republic and Haiti exchanged Christmastide pledges to avoid war over recent border incidents in which thousands of Haitians were reportedly killed. According to an official announcement made the previous day, President Rafael Trujillo proposed the voluntary peace accord to Haitian President Stenio Vincent on December 22, noting that the lamented events of October had raised the possibility of war. The article adds that official estimates of Haitians slain on Dominican soil since October have reached up to 12,000, and attributes the dispute to a large influx of Haitians taking jobs in the Dominican Republic at wages below those paid to native workers.
records.summary_es: Un despacho del 27 de diciembre informa que los presidentes de la República Dominicana y de Haití intercambiaron compromisos navideños para evitar la guerra por los recientes incidentes fronterizos en los que se informó de la muerte de miles de haitianos. Según un anuncio oficial hecho el día anterior, el presidente Rafael Trujillo propuso el acuerdo voluntario de paz al presidente haitiano Stenio Vincent el 22 de diciembre, señalando que los lamentables sucesos de octubre habían planteado la posibilidad de una guerra. El artículo añade que las estimaciones oficiales de haitianos muertos en suelo dominicano desde octubre han llegado hasta 12,000, y atribuye la disputa a una afluencia masiva de haitianos que aceptaban empleos en la República Dominicana con salarios inferiores a los pagados a los trabajadores nativos.

records.headline: Three Cuban aircraft—the Nina, Santa Maria, and "La Planta"—collided
records.summary_en: Three Cuban aircraft—the Nina, Santa Maria, and "La Planta"—collided and crashed in flames in a mountainous jungle region 12 miles west of Cali during a four-plane air cruise of Latin American capitals promoting the Columbus memorial lighthouse proposed for the harbor of Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic. The fourth plane in the squadron, piloted at high altitude by Maj. Frank Miranda of the Dominican army, landed safely at Paitilla Field in Panama. Seven men perished in the crash: Cuban army pilot Lieut. Feliciano Riseche and mechanic Roberto Perez aboard the Nina; Cuban army pilot Lieut. Antonio Menendez Peleaz, mechanic Manuel Ramos, and newspaperman Ruy Lugovina aboard the Santa Maria; and pilot Lieut. Alfredo Jimenez and mechanic Pedro Castillo aboard the third plane.
records.summary_es: Tres aeronaves cubanas —la Nina, la Santa Maria y "La Planta"— colisionaron y se estrellaron en llamas en una región montañosa y selvática a 12 millas al oeste de Cali durante una gira aérea de cuatro aviones por las capitales latinoamericanas en favor del faro monumental a Colón propuesto para el puerto de Ciudad Trujillo, República Dominicana. El cuarto avión del escuadrón, pilotado a gran altura por el mayor Frank Miranda del ejército dominicano, aterrizó a salvo en el campo Paitilla de Panamá. Siete hombres perecieron en el accidente: el piloto del ejército cubano teniente Feliciano Riseche y el mecánico Roberto Perez a bordo de la Nina; el piloto del ejército cubano teniente Antonio Menendez Peleaz, el mecánico Manuel Ramos y el periodista Ruy Lugovina a bordo de la Santa Maria; y el piloto teniente Alfredo Jimenez y el mecánico Pedro Castillo a bordo del tercer aparato.

records.headline: An N.N.P.A. report states that following Tuesday's official
records.summary_en: An N.N.P.A. report states that following Tuesday's official announcement, Dominican President Rafael Trujillo proposed a voluntary peace accord on December 22 to Haitian President Stenio Vincent to avoid war over recent border incidents. Official estimates place the number of Haitians slain on Dominican soil since October at up to 12,000, in a dispute attributed to a large influx of Haitians accepting lower wages than native laborers in the Dominican Republic. Trujillo invited Vincent to proclaim a "pact of honor" declaring that the October events in Dominican territory would never cause war between the two neighbors, and Vincent replied with pleasure as an Inter-American conciliation commission in Washington seeks a settlement.
records.summary_es: Un informe de la N.N.P.A. señala que, tras el anuncio oficial del martes, el presidente dominicano Rafael Trujillo propuso el 22 de diciembre un acuerdo voluntario de paz al presidente haitiano Stenio Vincent para evitar la guerra por los recientes incidentes fronterizos. Las estimaciones oficiales sitúan en hasta 12,000 el número de haitianos muertos en suelo dominicano desde octubre, en una disputa atribuida a una afluencia masiva de haitianos que aceptaban salarios más bajos que los trabajadores nativos en la República Dominicana. Trujillo invitó a Vincent a proclamar un "pacto de honor" declarando que los sucesos de octubre en territorio dominicano jamás serían causa de guerra entre ambos vecinos, y Vincent respondió complacido mientras una comisión interamericana de conciliación en Washington procura un arreglo.

records.headline: Flying at a higher altitude, a faster Dominican plane escaped
records.summary_en: Flying at a higher altitude, a faster Dominican plane escaped a storm and reached Panama safely while the other three aircraft in its four-plane squadron touring Latin America crashed in high mountains about 12 miles away. The three destroyed Cuban planes—the Nina, Pinta, and Santa Maria, which had departed Havana on November 10—were heading to Panama on a flight to raise funds for the Columbus memorial to be erected in the harbor of Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic. Killed in the crash were Cuban navy Lieut. Antonio Menendez, mechanic Manuel Naranjo, and writer Ruy de Lugo Vina aboard the Santa Maria; Cuban naval Lieut. Feliciano Risech and mechanic Roberto Medina aboard the Nina; and Cuban army Lieut. Alfredo Jiminez and mechanic Pedro Castillo aboard the Pinta.
records.summary_es: Volando a mayor altitud, un avión dominicano más veloz escapó de una tormenta y llegó a salvo a Panamá mientras las otras tres aeronaves de su escuadrón de cuatro aparatos que recorría América Latina se estrellaron en altas montañas a unas 12 millas de distancia. Los tres aviones cubanos destruidos —el Nina, el Pinta y el Santa Maria, que habían partido de La Habana el 10 de noviembre— se dirigían a Panamá en un vuelo para recaudar fondos para el monumento a Colón que se erigiría en el puerto de Ciudad Trujillo, República Dominicana. En el accidente murieron el teniente de la marina cubana Antonio Menendez, el mecánico Manuel Naranjo y el escritor Ruy de Lugo Vina a bordo del Santa Maria; el teniente naval cubano Feliciano Risech y el mecánico Roberto Medina a bordo del Nina; y el teniente del ejército cubano Alfredo Jiminez y el mecánico Pedro Castillo a bordo del Pinta.

records.headline: The State Department hopes Ambassador Davies will accept a temporary appointment
records.summary_en: The State Department hopes Ambassador Davies will accept a temporary appointment to chair the commission investigating the dispute between the Republic of Haiti and the Dominican Republic, with Davies remaining in the United States until July. Davies is regarded as especially qualified to settle the controversy because he served as President Trujillo's counsel in Washington prior to entering the diplomatic service.

Se considera que Davies está especialmente calificado para resolver la controversia porque se desempeñó como abogado del presidente Trujillo en Washington antes de ingresar al servicio diplomático.

records.summary_en: A caption in The Washington Times describes the winning worldwide competition design by J. L. Sleave of Nottingham, England, for a $4,000,000 Christopher Columbus memorial lighthouse to serve as the centerpiece of a 2,000-acre park overlooking the capital of the Dominican Republic. The accompanying article attributes the nation's transformation to the administrative ability of President Rafael Leonidas Trujillo, noting the construction of modern highways, bridges, and schools, the dredging of harbors and expansion of piers, and agricultural advancement. According to the paper, the Dominican Republic has maintained sound finances through seven years of global turbulence without incurring obligations that would threaten its national liberty, independence, or economic balance.

El artículo adjunto atribuye la transformación del país a la capacidad administrativa del presidente Rafael Leonidas Trujillo, señalando la construcción de carreteras modernas, puentes y escuelas, el dragado de puertos y la ampliación de muelles, así como el adelanto agrícola. Según el periódico, la República Dominicana ha mantenido sus finanzas en excelente estado durante siete años de turbulencia mundial sin contraer obligaciones que pusieran en peligro su libertad nacional, independencia o equilibrio económico.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Dominican Minister Andrés Pastoriza announced President Trujillo would not seek reelection, instead endorsing Dr. Jacinto B. Peynado for president and Dr. Manuel de Jesús Troncoso de la Concha for vice president, though Trujillo remained ready to serve if needed. The announcement came amid ongoing diplomatic friction with Haiti, which alleged that over 12,000 Haitians were massacred on Dominican soil. Dominican officials denied the accusations, attributing the reports to political enemies and citing economic strain caused by illegal Haitian migration.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el ministro dominicano Andrés Pastoriza anunció que el presidente Trujillo no buscaría la reelección, respaldando en su lugar al Dr. Jacinto B. Peynado para la presidencia y al Dr. Manuel de Jesús Troncoso de la Concha para la vicepresidencia, si bien Trujillo permanecía dispuesto a servir de ser necesario. El anuncio se produjo en medio de continuas fricciones diplomáticas con Haití, que alegaba la masacre de más de 12.000 haitianos en suelo dominicano. Las autoridades dominicanas rechazaron las acusaciones, atribuyendo los informes a enemigos políticos y señalando la carga económica provocada por la inmigración clandestina haitiana.
records.passage: statement to the press, said President Trujillo in a radio address recommended Dr. Jacinto B. Peynado for President and Dr. Manuel de Jesus Troncoso de la Concha for Vice President. Dr. Troncoso, who is rector of the University of Santo Domingo, has been in Washington since the middle of November on a special mission connected with the Haitian Dominican controversy. Minister Pastoriza said that although President Trujillo would not be a candidate for re-election, the latter had stated he "always would be ready to answer the nation's call if necessity arose." The Minister's statement made no mention of the controversy between his country and Haiti, which grew out of clashes early in October. The Haitian government, through its Legation here, has charged more than 12,000 Haitians were "massacred" on Dominican soil. TRUJILLO DECIDES NOT TO MAKE RACE President of Dominican Republic Will Always Be 'Ready to Answer Call.'

By the Associated Press.

The Dominican Legation said last night President Rafael L. Trujillo had announced his decision "not to accept nomination for the next term as President of the Dominican Republic."

Minister Andres Pastoriza, in a statement to the press, said President Trujillo in a radio address recommended Dr. Jacinto B. Peynado for President and Dr. Manuel de Jesus Troncoso de la Concha for Vice President. Dr. Troncoso, who is rector of the University of Santo Domingo, has been in Washington since the middle of November on a special mission connected with the Haitian-Dominican controversy.

Minister Pastoriza said that although President Trujillo would not be a candidate for re-election, the latter had stated he "always would be ready to answer the nation's call if necessity arose."

The Minister's statement made no mention of the controversy between his country and Haiti, which grew out of clashes early in October. The Haitian government, through its Legation here, has charged more than 12,000 Haitians were "massacred" on Dominican soil.

Dominican authorities have denied these assertions, charging in reply that many Haitians illegally entered the Dominican Republic, aggravating economic conditions there. Dominican officials have said the reports of the alleged "massacres" were spread by enemies of the present regime for political purposes.

records.headline: The killing of Haitians who sought work in the neighboring Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: The killing of Haitians who sought work in the neighboring Dominican Republic is characterized by writer Reynolds as the "most horrible unprovoked massacre of modern times," for which Dominican President Trujillo is blamed, an editorial in the Imperial Valley Press cites. Suggesting that the dispute may be left to the two republics directly involved, the paper argues that the episode illustrates how intelligent leadership cannot arise from an unintelligent public. The editorial characterizes the Dominican population as uneducated and untrained in thinking by United States standards, contending that this enabled a stern dictator like the Dominican president to take power.

Al sugerir que el asunto quizás deba resolverse entre las dos repúblicas directamente involucradas, el periódico sostiene que el episodio demuestra que un liderazgo inteligente no puede surgir de un público no inteligente. El editorial califica a la población dominicana como carente de educación y de formación para pensar según los estándares de los Estados Unidos, argumentando que esto permitió que un dictador severo como el presidente dominicano ascendiera al poder.

records.headline: The boundary passes near Lake Enriquillo—150 feet below sea
records.summary_en: The boundary passes near Lake Enriquillo—150 feet below sea level—before crossing the mile-high Sierra de Bahoruco and following the Rio Pedernales to the Caribbean, The Gazette notes in its description of the boundary across Hispaniola. While no railroad crosses the frontier, two motor roads link the nations—one in the north crossing the Rio Capotillo at Dajabon and another running between the Haitian town of Lascahobas and the Dominican village of Las Matas—while a narrow-gauge railway from Port-au-Prince reaches near the border at Manneville to meet an unimproved road to Ciudad Trujillo. Although the two countries display sharp social contrasts, both export sugar, tobacco, coffee, and cacao and possess largely unexploited mineral deposits, with the Dominican Republic having less rainfall for crops but more cattle-grazing land and greater timber resources, including mahogany, cedar, lignum vitae, and satinwood.

records.headline: Massacre river and chop sugar cane for wealthier Santo Domingo planters
records.summary_en: The *Times-News* reported that economic hardship and falling sugar prices exacerbated animosity toward thousands of Haitian laborers living in the Dominican Republic, culminating in nocturnal massacres where hundreds of Haitians were butchered with machetes along the Massacre River. Rather than retaliating militarily, Haitian President Sténio Vincent submitted the conflict to the Permanent Committee of Inter-American Conciliation under the 1923 Gondra Treaty. The resulting settlement required the Dominican government to pay a $750,000 indemnity, continue investigating the killings with full publicity, and cooperate to prevent future occurrences.
records.summary_es: El *Times-News* informó que las dificultades económicas y la caída del precio del azúcar avivaron la hostilidad hacia miles de braceros haitianos radicados en la República Dominicana, culminando en matanzas nocturnas donde cientos de haitianos fueron degollados a machetazos a lo largo del río Masacre. En lugar de tomar represalias militares, el presidente haitiano Sténio Vincent sometió la disputa a la Comisión Permanente de Conciliación Interamericana al amparo del Tratado Gondra de 1923. El acuerdo resultante obligó al gobierno dominicano a pagar una indemnización de 750.000 dólares, proseguir las investigaciones judiciales con amplia difusión pública y cooperar para prevenir hechos semejantes en el futuro.
