records.full_text:
MEDIATION INSTEAD OF BATTLE FRONTS

(By BRUCE CATTON)

The Dominican Republic has agreed to pay its neighboring country of Haiti $750,000 indemnification for the wholesale massacre of Haitians several months ago, and civilization inches forward another notch.

It is not particularly important that actual money is paid to Haiti. Presumably $750,000 wouldn't go very far even if it could be accurately distributed among the survivors of the wholesale machete killings in which from three to ten thousand Haitians were reported to have died.

But the fact that Santo Domingo, with its comparatively superior military strength, is paying vastly weaker Haiti the money, thereby confessing and agreeing to amends, is most important.

Dark, wood-fringed Massacre river separates the two republics on the island of Hispaniola. Santo Domingo has long raised sugar for an American market, thriving with the high prices. Haiti had no such industry, but Haitians were willing to cross Massacre river and chop sugar cane for wealthier Santo Domingo planters for 20 cents a day—and Santo Domingo planters were eager to have them. Then the price of sugar dropped and production fell off. But already thousands of Haitians were in Santo Domingo, married, rearing families, residents of as long as 20 years.

That was the seat of the trouble—that and the blending of French and Negro blood—and when hard times struck the island, Santo Domingo grumbled about the Haitians on the wrong side of Massacre river and what to do with them. Apparently the solution was found, if peculiarly, for by night, according to survivors, the Haitians were hauled from their tiny homes and butchered with machetes, butchered by the hundreds, and the bodies left along the banks of Massacre river.

When these facts came out of the interior and reached the seaport, foreigners looked at Haiti's president Stenio Vincent for warring retaliation. But instead he placed the matter before the Permanent Committee of Inter-American Conciliation, under the Gondra Treaty of 1923, which guaranteed amiability between the two nations.

The committee investigated and fixed the blame. An accord was reached and laid before the Congresses of both nations. Both agreed to the proposal that Santo Domingo pay the $750,000 indemnification. The Dominican government agreed to continue investigations and give the affair full publicity. Both governments agreed to prevent future like occurrences.

It was as simple as that. Even with a tongue-in-cheek view of the Dominican investigations and further action against its people, the result thus far so justifies the mediation method that it seems almost a miraculous happening. Especially in this day, when no aggressor ever seems actually to blame for aggression.

records.summary_en: The *Waterbury Democrat* reported that economic distress following a drop in sugar prices led to anti-Haitian hostility in the Dominican Republic, resulting in the nighttime slaughter of hundreds of Haitian residents along the Massacre River. Haitian President Sténio Vincent avoided war by submitting the dispute to the Permanent Committee of Inter-American Conciliation under the 1923 Gondra Treaty. Under the negotiated agreement, the Dominican Republic agreed to pay a $750,000 indemnification, continue criminal investigations with publicity, and work to prevent recurrences.
records.summary_es: El *Waterbury Democrat* informó que la crisis económica provocada por el desplome de los precios del azúcar desató la hostilidad antihaitiana en la República Dominicana, desembocando en la matanza nocturna de cientos de residentes haitianos a orillas del río Masacre. El presidente de Haití, Sténio Vincent, eludió el conflicto bélico sometiendo la querella a la Comisión Permanente de Conciliación Interamericana en virtud del Tratado Gondra de 1923. Conforme al arreglo pactado, la República Dominicana convino en pagar una indemnización de 750.000 dólares, mantener las investigaciones penales bajo escrutinio público y aunar esfuerzos para evitar nuevos brotes de violencia.

records.summary_en: In its "Cranium Crackers" quiz column, The Waterbury Democrat poses the question "Where is the Dominican Republic?" as item 5. The accompanying answer section states that the Dominican Republic (Santo Domingo) occupies the eastern two-thirds of the Island of Hispaniola, while Haiti occupies the western portion.
records.summary_es: En su columna de preguntas «Cranium Crackers», The Waterbury Democrat plantea la pregunta «¿Dónde está la República Dominicana?» en el punto 5. La sección de respuestas adjunta indica que la República Dominicana (Santo Domingo) ocupa los dos tercios orientales de la isla de La Española, mientras que Haití ocupa la porción occidental.

records.headline: According to a Washington dispatch in the Atlanta Daily World
records.summary_en: According to a Washington dispatch in the Atlanta Daily World, the four-month-old controversy between Haiti and Santo Domingo ended the previous Monday when representatives of the two countries signed an agreement. The accord specifies that the Dominican Republic will pay Haiti $750,000 as indemnity, with one-third paid in a lump sum and the remainder in five equal installments starting January 31, 1939. Haitian officials had charged that their nationals in the Dominican Republic were victims of a "wholesale massacre."
records.summary_es: Según un despacho desde Washington en el Atlanta Daily World, la controversia de cuatro meses entre Haití y Santo Domingo terminó el lunes anterior cuando representantes de los dos países firmaron un acuerdo. El convenio especifica que la República Dominicana pagará a Haití $750,000 como indemnización, un tercio en un pago único y el resto en cinco cuotas iguales a partir del 31 de enero de 1939. Funcionarios haitianos habían denunciado que sus nacionales en la República Dominicana fueron víctimas de una «masacre a gran escala».

records.headline: A sports column in the Evening Star reports that Indian Spring golf
records.summary_en: A sports column in the Evening Star reports that Indian Spring golf professional George Diffenbaugh has been offered a club position at Santo Domingo, though he does not plan to accept it for the time being. While a Washington golfer wants him to take the post in the Dominican Republic, Diffenbaugh noted that he had heard nothing further about it recently and doubted it would materialize into a firm offer. Diffenbaugh added jokingly that he feared being placed up against a wall for target practice if he missed a short putt.
records.summary_es: Una columna deportiva en el Evening Star informa que al profesional de golf de Indian Spring, George Diffenbaugh, se le ha ofrecido un puesto profesional en Santo Domingo, aunque por el momento no piensa aceptarlo. Si bien un golfista de Washington quiere que ocupe el cargo en la República Dominicana, Diffenbaugh señaló que no había tenido noticias recientes al respecto y dudaba que llegara a convertirse en una oferta formal. Diffenbaugh añadió en tono de broma que temía que lo pusieran contra un paredón para practicar tiro al blanco si fallaba un putt corto.

records.headline: The Washington Daily News reports that Dominican Minister Dr
records.summary_en: The Washington Daily News reports that Dominican Minister Dr. Andres Pastoriza will return to Washington in the middle of the week following a brief stay in Trujillo City. The previous week, the President of the Dominican Republic decorated both the minister and his wife with the medal of the Order of Merit. Senora de Pastoriza, who stayed in Washington during her husband's trip, will receive her decoration upon his return.
records.summary_es: The Washington Daily News informa que el ministro de la República Dominicana, Dr. Andrés Pastoriza, regresará a Washington a mediados de la semana tras una breve estadía en Ciudad Trujillo. La semana anterior, el presidente de la República Dominicana condecoró tanto al ministro como a su esposa con la medalla de la Orden del Mérito. La señora de Pastoriza, quien permaneció en Washington durante el viaje de su esposo, recibirá su condecoración cuando el ministro regrese.

records.headline: Opening with a reference to outgoing Dominican leadership retaining
records.summary_en: Opening with a reference to outgoing Dominican leadership retaining party influence, promoting agricultural betterment, and pointing to a balanced budget, debt reduction, educational improvements, and land distribution to the poor, an article in the Evening Star profiles sixty-year-old candidate Dr. Peynado and his running mate, Dr. de la Concha. Educated at the Normal School of Santo Domingo and the Professional Institute before graduating in law in 1889 at age 21, Dr. Peynado became a professor of civil law at the University of Santo Domingo in 1912, served as minister of justice and public instruction under Dr. Ramon Baez and Juan Isidro Jimenez, and was acting president during the 1930 election when Trujillo ran for the presidency. Dr. de la Concha, formerly managing editor of the Listin Diario and dean of the University of Santo Domingo, previously served as a judge in Santo Domingo, secretary to President Carlos Morales Languasco, Supreme Court justice, attorney general, secretary of justice and public education under President Caceres, and secretary of the interior.

records.headline: The Evening Star reports that the Minister of the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reports that the Minister of the Dominican Republic and Senora de Pastoriza entertained members of the Archaeological Society the previous evening, assisted in receiving by society president Wade H. Ellis, Mrs. Ellis, and program organizer Mrs. Mitchell Carroll. During the gathering, the minister delivered an illustrated lecture titled "Santo Domingo, the Land that Columbus Loved," and Pan American Union Director General Dr. Leo S. Rowe spoke on the "Columbus Memorial Light House." The Dominican minister also presented the medal of the Order of Juan Pablo Duarte to retired U.S. Navy Medical Corps Rear Admiral Frederick L. Benton on behalf of the Dominican government in recognition of his sanitation work in the Dominican Republic, where Mrs. Benton assisted him.
records.summary_es: El Evening Star informa que el ministro de la República Dominicana y la señora de Pastoriza agasajaron a los miembros de la Sociedad Arqueológica la noche anterior, asistidos en la recepción por el presidente de la sociedad, Wade H. Ellis, la señora Ellis y la organizadora de programas, la señora Mitchell Carroll. Durante la velada, el ministro dictó una conferencia ilustrada titulada «Santo Domingo, the Land that Columbus Loved», y el director general de la Unión Panamericana, Dr. Leo S. Rowe, habló sobre el «Columbus Memorial Light House». El ministro dominicano también entregó la medalla de la Orden de Juan Pablo Duarte al contralmirante retirado del Cuerpo Médico de la Marina de los Estados Unidos, Frederick L. Benton, en nombre del gobierno dominicano y en reconocimiento a su labor sanitaria en la República Dominicana, donde la señora Benton colaboró con él.

records.summary_en: During his fishing cruise near the British island of Sombrero, after embarking from Charleston the previous Saturday, the U.S. President spent part of the previous afternoon attending to official radio dispatches, the Evening Star notes. During that time, he exchanged radio greetings with President Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic while declining several official and private invitations to go ashore.

Durante ese tiempo, intercambió saludos por radio con el presidente Rafael Trujillo de la República Dominicana, al tiempo que declinó varias invitaciones oficiales y privadas para bajar a tierra.

records.summary_en: A steamship advertisement in the Evening Star promotes eleven-day all-expense West Indies cruises sailing every Thursday from New York aboard the cruise liners Borinquen or Coamo. The itinerary features a loop trip through the Puerto Rican mountains, a dinner dance at a San Juan resort, and sightseeing and luncheon in Trujillo City, Dominican Republic, along with maintenance and entertainment aboard ship. records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo dated May 18 reports that Dr. Jacinto B. Peynado, having gone through the formalities of an unopposed presidential election, is ready to take office on August 16
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo dated May 18 reports that Dr. Jacinto B. Peynado, having gone through the formalities of an unopposed presidential election, is ready to take office on August 16. Backed by President Rafael Trujillo, described as the island republic's political "strong man," Dr. Peynado received the support of 92 per cent of the registered voters in Monday's election, winning 318,779 out of a possible 345,174 votes. His running mate, Dr. Manuel J. Troncoso de la Concha, will also take office as vice president on August 16.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de la Associated Press fechado en Ciudad Trujillo el 18 de mayo informa que el Dr. Jacinto B. Peynado, tras cumplir las formalidades de una elección presidencial sin oposición, está listo para asumir el cargo el 16 de agosto. Con el respaldo del presidente Rafael Trujillo, descrito como el "hombre fuerte" político de la república isleña, el Dr. Peynado recibió el apoyo del 92 por ciento de los votantes inscritos en los comicios del lunes, obteniendo 318,779 de un total posible de 345,174 votos. Su compañero de fórmula, el Dr. Manuel J. Troncoso de la Concha, también asumirá la vicepresidencia el 16 de agosto.

records.headline: The Minister of the Dominican Republic and Senora de Pastoriza
records.summary_en: The Minister of the Dominican Republic and Senora de Pastoriza have cancelled their social engagements following the death in Santo Domingo of the Minister's brother-in-law, Senor Rafael de Pierrot, whose wife is the Minister's sister. Consequently, a luncheon that Senora de Pastoriza had planned in honor of Senora de Recinos, wife of the Guatemalan Minister who recently returned from a visit to her homeland, has been postponed indefinitely.

En consecuencia, el almuerzo que la señora de Pastoriza había planeado en honor de la señora de Recinos, esposa del ministro de Guatemala que regresó recientemente de una visita a su patria, ha sido pospuesto indefinidamente.

records.headline: A column in the St. Croix Avis notes that Carleton Beals wrote
records.summary_en: A column in the St. Croix Avis notes that Carleton Beals wrote in The Reader's Digest that the Dominican Republic is rapidly coming under the influence of Germany, which seeks it as a base near the Panama Canal. The columnist observes that the Dominican Senate had considered a plan to settle Germans in the country when Horacio Vasquez was President of the Republic, making the idea not as new as Beals indicated. With Germany now attempting to take an active part in the governments of other nations, the column states it is believed that the United States, whose friendship the Dominican Republic cannot afford to lose, will use its influence to prevent such a move.
records.summary_es: Una columna en el St. Croix Avis señala que Carleton Beals escribió en The Reader's Digest que la República Dominicana está cayendo rápidamente bajo la influencia de Alemania, país que la pretende como base cerca del Canal de Panamá. El columnista observa que el Senado dominicano ya había considerado un plan para establecer colonos alemanes en el país cuando Horacio Vasquez era presidente de la República, por lo que la idea no resulta tan nueva como indicó el autor. Ahora que Alemania intenta tomar parte activa en el gobierno de otros países, la columna afirma que se cree que los Estados Unidos, cuya amistad la República Dominicana no puede permitirse perder, emplearán su influencia para impedir tal medida.

records.headline: In a July 9 Associated Press dispatch from the thirty-two-nation
records.summary_en: In a July 9 Associated Press dispatch from the thirty-two-nation refugee conference at Evian-les-Bains, France, the Dominican Republic, Mexico, and Peru offered to open their doors to German and Austrian refugees after other countries stated they could not permit mass immigration. Following Mexico's pledge of asylum and work opportunities, the Dominican Republic and Peru followed suit, although Peru excluded refugee intellectuals. Dominican delegate Virgilio Trujillo Molina announced that the Dominican Republic would accept both agricultural and professional men, stating that large areas suitable for farming were available and that the republic would provide seed and technical advice.
records.summary_es: En un despacho de la Associated Press fechado el 9 de julio desde la conferencia sobre refugiados de treinta y dos naciones en Evian-les-Bains, Francia, la República Dominicana, México y el Perú ofrecieron abrir sus puertas a los refugiados alemanes y austríacos después de que otros países declararan que no podían permitir la inmigración masiva. Tras la promesa mexicana de asilo y oportunidades de trabajo, la República Dominicana y el Perú siguieron el ejemplo, aunque este último excluyó a los intelectuales refugiados. El delegado dominicano Virgilio Trujillo Molina anunció que la República Dominicana aceptaría tanto a agricultores como a profesionales, afirmando que había grandes extensiones aptas para el cultivo y que la república proporcionaría semillas y asesoramiento técnico.

records.full_text:
Dominican President Goes Mr. Coolidge One Better

By EVELYN PEYTON GORDON

Well, once we had a President who "did not choose to run." For a good many years that pronouncement of the late Calvin Coolidge has been rather unique. Presidents today don't so easily give up the job. But down in the Dominican Republic another man has made the same statement—only in many more words.

The other day Rafael Trujillo Molina, who has served two terms as President and dictator of the island republic, announced to "the nation" that he "would renounce public office in order to enjoy once more the peaceful quiet of private life." Now there's a smart man. He has had all the glory—if there be any—in twice serving as President of his country. He has—according to all accounts—accomplished many things during his eight-year tenure of office. Even the capital of the republic is now called Trujillo City—Ciudad Trujillo in Spanish. But unlike Mr. Coolidge, who merely wrote those six historical words on a slip of paper. Mr. Trujillo delivered a 12-page speech to his fellow citizens.

WILL RETAIN POWER

So on Aug. 16, Strongman Trujillo will retire from office. He will retire to his fabulous home in the mountains near Ciudad Trujillo "to the peaceful quiet of private life." But the bets are even that he will still remain the strong man of Dominican politics.

Here in Washington we know a good deal about Mr. Trujillo. Some years back there came to the Capital a pretty brunet, smartly gowned and gay of smile—Mme. Trujillo. She was officially received at the White House as the wife of a foreign president. She was officially called upon by State Department big-wigs. And then she settled down to enjoy the remainder of her stay—it was some weeks—as the guest of Mr. and Mrs. Joseph E. Davies. At the time Mr. Davies, who is now our Ambassador to Brussels, was a local attorney and among other things, counsel to the President of the Dominican Republic—that was Mme. Trujillo's husband.

Now Mr. Trujillo has another wife and so has Mr. Davies, but there is still a close friendship between the two families. Mrs. Aldace Walker, a daughter of Mr. Davies, spent some weeks in Trujillo City and was thrilled with the charm of the place. Of course she stayed at the Presidential Palace, and that does make a trip just a little different.

MINISTER RETURNING

Today the Minister of the Dominican Republic, Andres Pastoriza, will return from New York where he has been to speed his wife and family on their way to Trujillo City—the Minister himself forgets sometimes, and speaks of Santo Domingo City, but hastily corrects himself. And on his return Mr. Pastoriza will begin to make plans for an imminent visit of the erstwhile President.

Just when Mr. Trujillo will come to this country is not yet known, but it will be some time shortly after his retirement. He has never been here and is probably agog at the thrilling tales his wife and Ministers have brought back to him. So Mr. Pastoriza is preparing to "give him the works"; take him thru the country on a coast-to-coast tour; show him how things are run in our modest little republic.

Meantime down in the Dominican Republic there is none of the uproar that would be attendant to the emphatic retirement of our Chief Executive. There is no scurrying around looking for two noble candidates to fight, fight, fight, for the coveted office.

While President Roosevelt has been touring the country dropping a word here and a smile there by way of endorsement for his candidates for various public offices, Mr. Trujillo simply said "to the nation" that he wished to recommend to his fellow citizens the mutual advantages of unifying electoral action by nominating Dr. J. B. Peynado for the Presidency. The retiring Chief Executive continued "This is my candidate and as such I recommend him favorably to my fellow citizens."

HE'S QUITE FRANK

No beating around the bush there. Mr. Trujillo just told 'em and they went to work and elected Mr. Peynado, a distinguished lawyer. Didn't even bother to nominate an opponent. Simple as that.

Now, of course, Mr. Trujillo may return to Trujillo City after his visit in this country, so filled with new ideas of government—many of the Latin American republics have been patterned after ours—that he will want to execute them himself again. That remains to be seen four years from now when Mr. Peynado has done his job.

records.headline: The Washington Times reports that the Rev. Charles Raymond Barnes
records.summary_en: The Washington Times reports that the Rev. Charles Raymond Barnes, an Episcopal missionary who was slain the previous day in the library of his home at Ciudad Trujillo, had been a popular rector of the Church of Our Saviour in Woodridge. Detective Sergt. David G. Fletcher told reporters that he had served as a vestryman of the church when the slain cleric was its pastor four years ago, and that Barnes had stayed as his house guest two years ago while en route to the Dominican Republic. Dominican authorities are holding a chef employed by the rector as a suspect in the murder.
records.summary_es: The Washington Times informa que el reverendo Charles Raymond Barnes, misionero episcopal que fue asesinado el día anterior en la biblioteca de su residencia en Ciudad Trujillo, había sido un apreciado rector de la iglesia Church of Our Saviour en Woodridge. El sargento detective David G. Fletcher declaró a los periodistas que había sido miembro de la junta parroquial de la iglesia cuando el clérigo asesinado era su pastor cuatro años atrás, y que Barnes se había alojado en su casa como invitado hacía dos años cuando se dirigía a la República Dominicana. Las autoridades dominicanas mantienen detenido como sospechoso del asesinato a un cocinero empleado por el rector.

records.headline: The Evening Star reports that Dominican Minister Don Andres Pastoriza held
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reports that Dominican Minister Don Andres Pastoriza held an informal champagne party and luncheon at the Dominican Legation to mark the double celebration in Santo Domingo of the seventy-fifth anniversary of the Dominican Republic's independence and the inauguration of the new President, Dr. Jacinto Peynado. Senora de Pastoriza, who had been in Santo Domingo for over a month, participated on Monday in the dedication of the capital's new $6,000,000 port and expected to attend a grand ball at the National Palace given by former President Gen. Trujillo in Dr. Peynado's honor. At the Legation, which was decorated with red, white, and blue flowers, Senor Pastoriza was assisted in receiving guests by the wife of the new counselor, Dr. Luis Logrono, while luncheon guests included Ecuadorian Ambassador Senor Alfaro, Dr. Oscar Albertini, former United States Minister to Bolivia Abbot Maginniss, and Miss Elsa Maguire. Senora de Pastoriza will return to Washington in two weeks accompanied by her sons, Andres and Thomas Pastoriza, and her daughter, Senorita Mathilde Pastoriza.

records.headline: Under a headline referring to the country as "Dominica," a September 1
records.summary_en: Under a headline referring to the country as "Dominica," a September 1 dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic, in The Washington Daily News reports that Jose Manuel Diaz was sentenced the previous day to seven years at hard labor for the murder of the Rev. Charles Raymond Barnes, formerly of Camden, N. J. Barnes, pastor of the English-speaking Episcopal Church, was struck over the head with an iron bar and slain on July 28 in the library of his home in Ciudad Trujillo. records.headline: The Key West Citizen recounts the maritime adventure of Tracy
records.summary_en: The Key West Citizen recounts the maritime adventure of Tracy A. Bader and Brian Mozier of Illinois, who had been digging for gold in the mountains of Puerto Plata, Dominican Republic. They teamed up with Jose Julio Nunez Fernandez, a local newspaper writer whose father owned farmland and houses. After officials at Monte Christi refused them clearance papers and confiscated their charts and compass, the trio bypassed neighboring Haiti, where Nunez Fernandez was out of favor, and sailed for Cuba. On their fifth day at sea, the three youths navigated through a severe storm under a reefed muslin sail mounted on a short 15-foot mast.
records.summary_es: The Key West Citizen relata la aventura marítima de Tracy A. Bader y Brian Mozier de Illinois, quienes habían estado buscando oro en las montañas de Puerto Plata, República Dominicana. Ambos se asociaron con José Julio Núñez Fernández, un redactor de prensa local cuyo padre poseía tierras y casas. Luego de que las autoridades en Monte Cristi les negaran los papeles de despacho y les confiscaran sus cartas de navegación y brújula, el trío esquivó la vecina Haití, donde Núñez Fernández no era bien visto, y navegó con rumbo a Cuba. En su quinto día en el mar, los tres jóvenes sortearon una fuerte tormenta bajo una vela de muselina tomada con rizos montada en un mástil corto de 15 pies.

records.headline: A United Press dispatch reports that Tracey Bader, 27, and Bryant
records.summary_en: A United Press dispatch reports that Tracey Bader, 27, and Bryant Morgan, 23, of Hamburg, Illinois, alongside Jose Julio Nunez, 19, of the Dominican Republic, ran into legal trouble after completing a hazardous 1000-mile voyage in an 18-foot dory. The trio faced probable charges for entering the United States without clearance papers or a bill of health. Customs officers at Puerto Plata had refused them sailing authorization after deeming their craft unseaworthy, prompting them to slip out on Oct. 15 and navigate for nearly a month before landing at Duck Key, 35 miles north of Key West.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de United Press informa que Tracey Bader, de 27 años, y Bryant Morgan, de 23, de Hamburg, Illinois, junto con José Julio Núñez, de 19, de la República Dominicana, tuvieron problemas legales tras completar una peligrosa travesía de 1000 millas en un bote de 18 pies. El trío enfrentó posibles cargos por ingresar a los Estados Unidos sin documentos de despacho ni certificado de sanidad. Los funcionarios de aduanas en Puerto Plata les habían negado la autorización para zarpar al considerar que la embarcación no era apta para navegar, lo que los impulsó a zarpar a escondidas el 15 de octubre y navegar durante casi un mes antes de desembarcar en Duck Key, a 35 millas al norte de Cayo Hueso.

records.headline: Despradel’s visit to Hitler caused vague rumors last night that the German government was negotiating with Latin American countries for placing Jews
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that the Dominican Legation and German sources dismissed rumors that Germany was negotiating with Latin American nations to resettle Jewish refugees in the Dominican Republic following a meeting between Adolf Hitler and new Dominican Minister Roberto Despradel. The Dominican Legation in Washington stated it had no knowledge of any such discussions. Despradel had previously served in Washington earlier in the year helping negotiate the settlement of the Haitian-Dominican dispute under the Gondra Treaty.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported on the competing diplomatic proposals heading into the Pan-American conference in Lima, Peru, noting Dominican dictator Rafael L. Trujillo's plan to create a Pan-American league of nations. Other key dynamics included Mexican President Lázaro Cárdenas's policy on foreign naturalization and Argentine Foreign Minister José María Cantilo's resistance to President Roosevelt's collective defense initiative. The U.S. delegation under Secretary of State Cordell Hull was expected to navigate these differing hemispheric positions.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* reseñó las propuestas diplomáticas contrapuestas con miras a la conferencia panamericana de Lima, Perú, señalando el plan del dictador dominicano Rafael L. Trujillo de instaurar una liga de naciones panamericana. Otros factores clave abarcaban la política sobre naturalización de extranjeros del presidente mexicano Lázaro Cárdenas y la renuencia del canciller argentino José María Cantilo a la iniciativa de defensa colectiva del presidente Roosevelt. Se esperaba que la delegación estadounidense, encabezada por el secretario de Estado Cordell Hull, sorteara estas divergencias hemisféricas.

records.headline: A political analysis in the Evening Star ahead of the Lima conference
records.summary_en: A political analysis in the Evening Star ahead of the Lima conference asserts that Rafael Trujillo's proposed Pan-American league of nations appears destined for the pigeonhole. The column states that Colombia is the only Latin American nation likely to support the proposal. It characterizes the league, alongside the Christopher Columbus Memorial Lighthouse at Santo Domingo City (now called Trujillo City), as a personal project of the Dominican dictator, who continues to rule through a straw president and a rubber-stamp Congress.
records.summary_es: Un análisis político en el Evening Star previo a la conferencia de Lima afirma que el proyecto de liga panamericana propuesto por Rafael Trujillo parece destinado al olvido. La columna señala que Colombia es la única nación latinoamericana que probablemente apoyará la propuesta. Califica dicha liga, junto con el faro conmemorativo a Cristóbal Colón en la ciudad de Santo Domingo (ahora llamada Ciudad Trujillo), como un proyecto personal del dictador dominicano, quien continúa gobernando a través de un presidente títere y un Congreso sumiso.

records.headline: The Washington Daily News reports that Senor Rafael Leonidas
records.summary_en: The Washington Daily News reports that Senor Rafael Leonidas Trujillo, ex-president and "strong man" of the Dominican Republic, has contributed a personal check for $5000 to Spanish Ambassador Senor de los Rios. The funds are designated for the relief of widows and orphans in Loyalist Spain. Trujillo, who is planning a journey to the United States while temporarily out of office, expressed his desire to see Spain enjoy peace under democratic ideals worthy of its history. Meanwhile, Dominican Minister Senor Andres Pastoriza and his family are preparing to transfer from Washington to London.

records.headline: An Adventurers' Club story tells of Charley, who worked six months for a sugar concern at La Romana and, while on vacation
records.summary_en: An Adventurers' Club story tells of Charley, who worked six months for a sugar concern at La Romana and, while on vacation in Santo Domingo City, received orders transferring him to a new project at Barahona, but found every steamer tied up by a steamship strike and no road to take him there. He took a small sailing vessel for what should have been an overnight trip, but a storm blew the boat ten miles off course and disabled its steering gear, leaving him becalmed for days with forty Haitian passengers, no food and hot drinking water, as the only white man aboard, paying the captain ten dollars for protection and sleeping lashed to the rail. On the third night he woke to see two men creeping toward him with machetes in their mouths and shot both dead as the ship erupted in uproar.
records.summary_es: Un relato del Club de Aventureros cuenta la historia de Charley, que trabajó seis meses para una empresa azucarera en La Romana y, estando de vacaciones en la ciudad de Santo Domingo, recibió órdenes de traslado a un nuevo proyecto en Barahona, pero encontró todos los vapores detenidos por una huelga naviera y ningún camino que lo llevara allí. Se embarcó en un pequeño velero para lo que debía ser un viaje de una noche, pero una tormenta desvió el barco diez millas de su rumbo y averió su timón, dejándolo en calma durante días con cuarenta pasajeros haitianos, sin comida y con el agua potable caliente, siendo el único hombre blanco a bordo, pagando al capitán diez dólares por protección y durmiendo atado a la barandilla. En la tercera noche despertó y vio a dos hombres acercándose a él arrastrándose con machetes en la boca, y les disparó a ambos hasta matarlos mientras el barco estallaba en alboroto.
records.passage: was hot and humid. Hunger gnawed at his innards, but he had to make the best of it. The natives were getting more and more restless. They eyed Charley's clothes with covetous looks that became more and more insolent and apparent. And still there was no sign of the wind that would blow them into Barahona. That night, worn out by two days and nights of wakefulness, Charley fell asleep. Sometime in the dark hours he woke up suddenly, by sheer instinct. In the dim light of a tropic moon he saw two dark figures creeping along the deck toward him — two natives — great, husky blacks with machetes in their mouths! "They didn't know my eyes were open," he says, "if they had known it I wouldn't be alive today. But their ignorance gave me an opportunity to draw my guns." Charley got those guns out just as the natives were taking their machetes from their mouths. He whipped up one gun and fired twice. In an instant, two men were dead on the deck and the whole ship was in an uproar. Dark figures came swarming toward him. The captain was a big, powerful fellow. Charley says he was built on the style of Harry Wills in his prime. He picked Charley up with one hand, threw him into his cabin head first, and then, with the aid of a revolver and his powerful physique, held that furious mob at bay. Captain Threatens to Sink the Ship. records.headline: A cruising narrative in the Evening Star quotes a yacht's log
records.summary_en: A cruising narrative in the Evening Star quotes a yacht's log recording the conclusion of a 62-hour run of 450 miles from Ciudad Trujillo in the Dominican Republic to Kingston, Jamaica. The account recalls sleepless nights and repeated engine failures, noting that power failed no less than 10 times over three days due to inferior fuel purchased in Trinidad. Reflecting on the voyage, the skipper emphasizes that dependable auxiliary power is indispensable when sailing through West Indian waters.
records.summary_es: Una crónica de navegación en el Evening Star cita el diario de a bordo de un yate al concluir una travesía de 62 horas y 450 millas desde Ciudad Trujillo en la República Dominicana hasta Kingston, Jamaica. El relato recuerda noches en vela y continuas averías del motor, señalando que la propulsión falló no menos de 10 veces durante tres días debido a un combustible de mala calidad adquirido en Trinidad. Al reflexionar sobre el viaje, el capitán subraya que contar con fuerza motriz auxiliar confiable es indispensable para navegar por las aguas de las Indias Occidentales.

records.headline: The Evening Star reports that retiring Dominican Minister Senor Don Andres Pastoriza
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reports that retiring Dominican Minister Senor Don Andres Pastoriza has flown to Santo Domingo for a brief visit before returning to Washington to take official leave. Senora de Pastoriza and their children will travel to New York, where the minister will rejoin them to sail for England following his diplomatic transfer to London, with Legation Counselor Senor Dr. Don Luis Logrono serving as Charge d'Affaires. Meanwhile, the newly appointed Dominican Minister and Senora de Urena are due to arrive in New York on Sunday, January 15, on their way to Washington, trading diplomatic posts with Pastoriza.
records.summary_es: El Evening Star informa que el ministro dominicano saliente, señor don Andrés Pastoriza, viajó en avión a Santo Domingo para una breve visita antes de regresar a Washington a despedirse oficialmente. La señora de Pastoriza y sus hijos viajarán a Nueva York, donde el ministro se reunirá con ellos para zarpar hacia Inglaterra tras su traslado diplomático a Londres, quedando como encargado de negocios el consejero de la legación, señor doctor don Luis Logroño. Entretanto, está prevista la llegada a Nueva York del nuevo ministro dominicano y de la señora de Ureña el domingo 15 de enero con destino a Washington, intercambiando puestos diplomáticos con Pastoriza.

records.headline: An editorial in the Evening Star commemorates Eugenio Maria de Hostos
records.summary_en: An editorial in the Evening Star commemorates Eugenio Maria de Hostos on his one hundredth birthday anniversary, recounting his extensive achievements throughout Latin America, including founding the first normal school in the Dominican Republic. The article records that De Hostos died in Santo Domingo in 1903 at sixty-four years of age, having lived his final years away from Puerto Rico following its annexation by the United States. To celebrate his hemispheric legacy as a "Citizen of America," the Pan-American Union in Washington organized an afternoon ceremony to receive a bust of the educator presented by Puerto Rico.
records.summary_es: Un editorial en el Evening Star conmemora a Eugenio María de Hostos en el centenario de su nacimiento, recordando sus amplios logros en toda América Latina, entre ellos la fundación de la primera escuela normal de la República Dominicana. El artículo señala que De Hostos falleció en Santo Domingo en 1903 a la edad de sesenta y cuatro años, tras haber vivido sus últimos años lejos de Puerto Rico a raíz de su anexión por parte de los Estados Unidos. Para celebrar su legado continental como "Ciudadano de América", la Unión Panamericana en Washington organizó una ceremonia vespertina para recibir un busto del educador obsequiado por Puerto Rico.

records.full_text:
Refugees Pin Hope On Santo Domingo

Buried in the news yesterday was a story that may mean new hope, new life in a new world to 100,000 Jewish refugees fleeing persecution in Europe.

The Dominican Republic, twice the size of Palestine (19,332 square miles, about the area of Vermont and New Hampshire together), has offered to open its doors to 100,000 Jews.

It has a population of only 1,500,000 persons now, the same as Palestine, but its land is much more fertile, three-quarters of it being suited for cultivation. It exports sugar, tobacco and coffee. Half its trade is with the United States.

The Dominican Republic, dictated by Rafael Leonidas Trujillo, occupies two-thirds of the Caribbean's second largest island.

It was discovered by Columbus, who is buried there. Its capital city, Santo Domingo, the oldest white settlement in the New World, was named after the patron saint of the father of Columbus—until Trujillo came along. He dubbed it Ciudad Trujillo.

Trujillo's past record with immigrants isn't so good.

The Dominican Republic was originally a Spanish colony and felt French rule for a time.

In 1869 it negotiated a treaty for annexation to the United States, but Washington refused to ratify the pact.

During the World War, civil war flared, and the United States intervened to maintain order and establish a government. American troops were withdrawn after peace was restored.

records.headline: An Adventurers' Club story tells of Charley, who had worked for a sugar concern at La Romana and, while on vacation
records.summary_en: An Adventurers' Club story tells of Charley, who had worked for a sugar concern at La Romana and, while on vacation in Santo Domingo City, was transferred to a new project at Barahona; with steamers tied up by a strike, he booked passage on a sailing vessel for what was supposed to be an overnight trip. A storm blew the little craft off course and broke its steering gear, leaving it becalmed without food, and on the third night Charley woke to see two men creeping toward him with machetes in their mouths and drew his guns and fired twice, killing both.
records.summary_es: Un relato del Adventurers' Club cuenta la historia de Charley, que había trabajado para una empresa azucarera en La Romana y, mientras estaba de vacaciones en la ciudad de Santo Domingo, fue transferido a un nuevo proyecto en Barahona; con los vapores detenidos por una huelga, compró pasaje en un velero para lo que debía ser un viaje de una noche. Una tormenta desvió la pequeña embarcación de su rumbo y rompió su timón, dejándola en calma y sin alimentos, y a la tercera noche Charley despertó y vio a dos hombres arrastrándose hacia él con machetes en la boca, sacó sus pistolas y disparó dos veces, matando a ambos.
records.passage: was hot and humid. Hunger gnawed at his innards, but he had to make the best of it. The natives were getting more and more restless. They eyed Charley's clothes with covetous looks that became more and more insolent and apparent. And still there was no sign of the wind that would blow them into Barahona. That night, worn out by two days and nights of wakefulness, Charley fell asleep. Sometime in the dark hours he woke up suddenly, by sheer instinct. In the dim light of a tropic moon he saw two dark figures creeping along the deck toward him — two natives — great, husky blacks with machetes in their mouths! "They didn't know my eyes were open," he says, "if they had known it I wouldn't be alive today. But their ignorance gave me an opportunity to draw my guns." Charley got those guns out just as the natives were taking their machetes from their mouths. He whipped up one gun and fired twice. In an instant, two men were dead on the deck and the whole ship was in an uproar. Dark figures came swarming toward him. The captain was a big, powerful fellow. Charley says he was built on the style of Harry Wills in his prime. He picked Charley up with one hand, threw him into his cabin head first, and then, with the aid of a revolver and his powerful physique, held that furious mob at bay. records.summary_en: The Washington Daily News reports that diplomats expect President Roosevelt to return from Caribbean fleet maneuvers with new proposals for continental defense. Among the measures under consideration is the possible requirement for permanent naval facilities at Samana Bay in the Dominican Republic, where temporary naval privileges were granted during recent exercises. The report adds that Roosevelt may also consider expanding the Guantanamo naval base and advancing military development in Puerto Rico.

El informe añade que Roosevelt también podría evaluar la ampliación de la base naval de Guantánamo y el fomento del desarrollo militar en Puerto Rico.

records.headline: A society feature in The Washington Daily News reflects on a diplomatic
records.summary_en: A society feature in The Washington Daily News reflects on a diplomatic reception celebrating Dominican independence and the first anniversary of the inauguration of the Port of Trujillo City, instigated by former President Leonidas Trujillo. Speculating on Caribbean naval strategy as President Roosevelt cruises nearby waters, the writer suggests the United States might seek fleet harbor privileges at strategic Samana Bay similar to Guantanamo Bay in Cuba. However, the author emphasizes that the gathering was purely social, drawing approximately 800 guests between 5 and 7 o'clock to greet Minister Andres Pastoriza and Senora de Pastoriza and raise toasts to independence alongside relatives of Trujillo.
records.summary_es: Una crónica de sociedad en The Washington Daily News reflexiona sobre una recepción diplomática en la que se celebró la independencia dominicana y el primer aniversario de la inauguración del puerto de Ciudad Trujillo, promovido por el expresidente Leónidas Trujillo. Al especular sobre la estrategia naval en el Caribe mientras el presidente Roosevelt navega por aguas cercanas, el autor sugiere que los Estados Unidos podrían procurar privilegios de fondeadero de flota en la estratégica bahía de Samaná, semejantes a los de la bahía de Guantánamo en Cuba. No obstante, el articulista recalca que el encuentro fue meramente social, reuniendo a unos 800 invitados entre las 5 y las 7 en punto para saludar al ministro Andrés Pastoriza y a la señora de Pastoriza y brindar por la independencia junto a familiares de Trujillo.

records.headline: A commission of seven United States experts has departed for Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: A commission of seven United States experts has departed for Santo Domingo to investigate the potential settlement of 100,000 German refugees in the Dominican Republic. The mission is composed not of diplomats, but of specialists in soil, forestry, and public health tasked with identifying crops that would avoid competing with existing Dominican agriculture and determining safe areas for settlement. The delegation is led by Dr. H. D. Barker of the Bureau of Plant Industry, accompanied by Dr. William Kramer of the Forest Service and Dr. Arthur Kocher of the Soil Conservation Service.

records.full_text:
The Dominican Dictator Rumored En Route Here

By EVELYN PEYTON GORDON

Some weeks ago a popular New York shop received an order for smart luggage amounting to $7500. Even the New York shop was staggered! Today, with the luggage, will arrive in New York Senora de Trujillo, wife of the "strong man" of Santa Domingo. La Senora and her "suite," which includes her young son, Rafael, her 75-year-old mother, her stepdaughter, Senora Flor Trujillo de Brea, and her brother, Senor Francisco Martinez Alba, are aboard the liner Santa Paula.

Now all that is interesting enough. But what makes the event more interesting is the fact that there are rumors abroad that Gen. Trujillo himself, is on the Santa Paula with the party. Nobody, not even the Grace Line, has been able to confirm or deny the presence of the dictator of the Dominican Republic on that ship. The party, traveling incognito, embarked at Cape Haitien, and not in their own country.

But, just to cinch things if the General is along, Andres Pastoriza, Dominican Minister to Washington, and several consular officials from New York, will hustle out to Quarantine early this morning. Then, whether Gen. Trujillo is aboard or not, the fireworks of entertaining will start. Mayor LaGuardia will be on hand to welcome the party, and thence they will go to the Waldorf, where an entire floor of the Towers has been reserved for them.

EN ROUTE TO GERMANY?

The reason there is so much importance attached to this arrival, is because the word goes forth that Gen. Trujillo and his family are en route to Germany. Some time ago, the Dominican Legation went to great pains to announce that Gen. Trujillo "was not going to visit Hitler." In denying the report that the generalissimo would not pay a visit to Der Fuehrer, there was no denial that he was not going to Germany!

And why shouldn't he go to see Hitler? No reason except perhaps it would be better if the Reichschancellor didn't wind up a deal on that same Samana Bay of which we spoke the other day. President Roosevelt didn't do any negotiating for the use of Samana Bay as a marine base when he was in southern waters. At least we haven't heard that he did. But Herr Hitler has long thought Samana Bay would be an excellent submarine base for himself!

LENGTHY VISIT HERE?

Last autumn, when Gen. Trujillo finished his term as President of the Dominican Republic, it was reported that he was coming to this country for a tour. No more has been heard of that visit, and to date no immediate plans have been made for it. Perhaps on his return from Europe he will see fit to pay us a lengthier visit.

With Senora de Trujillo's party there are also Dr. Jose Roman, private doctor; Joaquin Montero Monteagudo and Juan Antonio Perrota, listed, without rank, as "officers of the Dominican Army"; Emilia Tapia, maid; Felipa Nunez, maid, and J. M. Bonetti Burgos, secretary to Gen. Trujillo. Note those military aides, the private physician and Senor Bonetti make us very sure that the General himself is on that boat. Today will tell.

Meantime plans have been hurriedly, but carefully, made for the entertainment of the ladies of the party anyhow. Secret Service men and a police detail have been placed at their disposal during the stay; a motorcycle escort will precede them to the hotel; the 12-room suite with servants' quarters has been filled with flowers; arrangements have been made for Rafael—he's about 12 years old—to be made an honorary captain in the famous Knickerbocker Greys (that group to which all aristocratic little New York boys aspire to belong).

ROUND OF PARTIES

This evening, Mr. and Mrs. Reginald Lanier, Mr. and Mrs. James Lenox Banks, Virginia French (sister of young Mrs. John Jacob Astor), and other members of society will give a reception for the visitors. Later this week, Miss French will give a large luncheon for the General's daughter, Senora de Brea. Tomorrow Senora de Brea will be entertained by Mrs. Lanier and members of the New York Junior League, following a visit to Girl Scout headquarters, where she will be greeted by Mrs. Lyman Delano. International Girl Scout chairman. Senora de Brea is head of the organization in her own country.

Now, this visit isn't supposedly an official visit. Some years ago, another Senora de Trujillo, first wife of the General, officially visited the Capital and was entertained at the White House as the wife of a foreign president. But aside from the fact that it is not announced as such, the entire visit seems to have all the earmarks of a very official mission. We'll see!

records.summary_es: Esta columna recoge los rumores de que el propio general Trujillo viaja a bordo del Santa Paula con el grupo de su familia, que viajó de incógnito y embarcó en Cabo Haitiano, y de que el ministro dominicano Andrés Pastoriza y funcionarios consulares recibirán el barco en la cuarentena, con el alcalde LaGuardia para dar la bienvenida al grupo a un piso del Waldorf en Nueva York. Se hace eco de la especulación de que el grupo va rumbo a Alemania, señalando que la legación dominicana solo había negado que Trujillo visitaría a Hitler, y que Hitler ha pensado durante mucho tiempo que la bahía de Samaná sería una excelente base de submarinos.

Senora de Brea is head of the organization in her own country. Now, this visit isn't supposedly an official visit. Some years ago, another Senora de Trujillo, first wife of the General, officially visited the Capital and was entertained at the White House as the wife of a foreign president. But aside from the fact that it is not announced as such, the entire visit seems to have all the earmarks of a very official mission. We'll see! THE ARTIST. By BLAINE W. LANE. He did not look like an artist. And he certainly did not look like the greatest artist of them all. He was a big, clumsy man whose heavy, spatulate hands appeared more adapted to grasping a shovel than a camel's hair brush. His eyes alone were a clue to his eminence; keen gray eyes which seemed to be able to survey the world — and more. Those gray eyes were narrowed as they turned first to the young man and then lingered on the girl seated opposite him. They were nervous, those two. The young man plucked at the frayed edge of his cuff. His sensitive mouth twitched spasmodically. The girl was tense. Her finely molded face was unnaturally pale. She drew up the collar of her shabby coat as tho she were suddenly cold. Finally, the great man spoke. "It has been hard going, I understand." He smiled sympathetically. records.headline: Dominican Minister and Senora de Pastoriza are staying at the Waldorf-Astoria
records.summary_en: Dominican Minister and Senora de Pastoriza are staying at the Waldorf-Astoria in New York to welcome visitors from their homeland and participate in scheduled festivities. George Djamgaroff hosted an apartment reception at the Waldorf-Astoria Towers for Senora de Trujillo and her daughter, along with a luncheon honoring Senora de Brea, honorary head of the Dominican Girl Scouts, attended by diplomatic and prominent social guests. Senora de Brea is also being entertained at functions hosted by Mrs. Lyman Delano, Mrs. Reginald Lanier, and Miss Virginia French before the Dominican minister and his wife return to Washington.
records.summary_es: El ministro dominicano y la señora de Pastoriza se hospedan en el Waldorf-Astoria de Nueva York para recibir a visitantes procedentes de su patria y participar en las festividades programadas. George Djamgaroff ofreció una recepción en su apartamento de las Torres del Waldorf-Astoria para la señora de Trujillo y su hija, además de un almuerzo en honor de la señora de Brea, jefa honoraria de las Girl Scouts dominicanas, con la asistencia de diplomáticos y distinguidas personalidades de la sociedad. La señora de Brea también está siendo agasajada en reuniones ofrecidas por la señora de Lyman Delano, la señora de Reginald Lanier y la señorita Virginia French antes de que el ministro dominicano y su esposa regresen a Washington.

records.headline: The counselor of the Legation of the Dominican Republic and Senora de Logroño
records.summary_en: The counselor of the Legation of the Dominican Republic and Senora de Logrono have announced the birth of twins, a boy and a girl, on Thursday, March 9, in Washington. The newborn infants are the first children for the couple, who arrived in Washington in July and were married little more than a year ago. Senor and Senora de Logrono were joined on Tuesday by her parents, Senor Santiago Ricart and Senora de Ricart of San Domingo, who are visiting for an extended stay.
records.summary_es: El consejero de la legación de la República Dominicana y la señora de Logroño han anunciado el nacimiento de mellizos, un niño y una niña, el jueves 9 de marzo en Washington. Los recién nacidos son los primeros hijos de la pareja, que llegó a Washington en julio y contrajo matrimonio hace poco más de un año. El señor y la señora de Logroño recibieron el martes la visita de los padres de ella, el señor Santiago Ricart y la señora de Ricart, procedentes de Santo Domingo, quienes permanecerán algún tiempo.

records.headline: A United States delegation headed by Senator Green, Democrat of Rhode
records.summary_en: A United States delegation headed by Senator Green, Democrat of Rhode Island, and Representative Fish, Republican of New York, is traveling to the Dominican Republic to witness the opening of Christopher Columbus's casket. The party will travel by train to Miami and by airplane to Ciudad Trujillo, where they will also inspect the site for the proposed pan-American Columbus memorial. The ceremonies are scheduled to take place in the Cathedral of Santo Domingo, with the National Broadcasting Company arranging a shortwave broadcast to North and South America.
records.summary_es: Una delegación de los Estados Unidos encabezada por el senador Green, demócrata de Rhode Island, y el representante Fish, republicano de Nueva York, viaja a la República Dominicana para presenciar la apertura del féretro de Cristóbal Colón. La comitiva viajará en tren hacia Miami y en avión a Ciudad Trujillo, donde además inspeccionará el terreno destinado al proyectado monumento panamericano a Colón. Las ceremonias están programadas para celebrarse en la catedral de Santo Domingo, y la National Broadcasting Company coordina una transmisión por onda corta hacia Norteamérica y Sudamérica.

records.headline: The Minister of the Dominican Republic and Senora de Pastoriza
records.summary_en: The Minister of the Dominican Republic and Senora de Pastoriza are hosting a supper party at the legation this evening in honor of Senora de Brea, daughter of former Dominican President Trujillo. Meanwhile, Representative and Mrs. Hamilton Fish, along with their son Hamilton Jr. and Richard Chatfield-Taylor, are departing at the end of the week for a brief visit to attend Sunday's Columbus memorial celebration in Santo Domingo. Senator Theodore Green, currently in Miami, will fly to Santo Domingo on Saturday to take part in the event and plans to return to Washington on March 21.
records.summary_es: El ministro de la República Dominicana y la señora de Pastoriza ofrecen esta noche una cena en la legación en honor de la señora de Brea, hija del expresidente dominicano Trujillo. Entre tanto, el representante Hamilton Fish y su esposa, acompañados por su hijo Hamilton Jr. y por Richard Chatfield-Taylor, partirán a fines de semana en una breve visita para asistir a la celebración del memorial de Colón el domingo en Santo Domingo. El senador Theodore Green, actualmente en Miami, volará a Santo Domingo el sábado para incorporarse al evento y planea regresar a Washington el 21 de marzo.

records.headline: The Dominican Minister and Senora de Pastoriza hosted a buffet
records.summary_en: The Dominican Minister and Senora de Pastoriza hosted a buffet supper honoring members of Congress departing on a mission to the Dominican Republic. Led by Senator Theodore F. Green and Representative Hamilton Fish of the congressional foreign affairs committees, the party of 16 is traveling by train to Miami and by chartered clipper to Ciudad Trujillo. The delegation will inspect the site designated by the Dominican government for a proposed Columbus memorial symbolizing peace and unity among the 21 American nations.
records.summary_es: El ministro dominicano y la señora de Pastoriza ofrecieron una cena bufé en honor de los miembros del Congreso que partían en misión hacia la República Dominicana. Encabezada por el senador Theodore F. Green y el representante Hamilton Fish, de las comisiones parlamentarias de relaciones exteriores, la comitiva de 16 personas viaja en tren a Miami y en un hidroavión fletado hacia Ciudad Trujillo. La delegación inspeccionará el terreno asignado por el gobierno dominicano para el proyectado monumento a Colón que simbolizará la paz y la unidad entre las 21 naciones americanas.

records.headline: Writing from aboard a Pan-American clipper ship bound for the Dominican
records.summary_en: Writing from aboard a Pan-American clipper ship bound for the Dominican Republic, a correspondent describes joining a 16-person delegation traveling from Washington to Trujillo City. The group is attending events connected to the proposed Christopher Columbus memorial, conceived to symbolize peace and unity among the 21 Pan-American nations. The traveler notes that the official party includes Senator Theodore Green, Representative Matthew Merritt, Representative Hamilton Fish Jr., travel author Eleanor Early, young Hammy Fish, Dicky Chatfield-Taylor, and George Djamgaroff.
records.summary_es: Escribiendo a bordo de un hidroavión de Pan-American rumbo a la República Dominicana, una corresponsal relata su integración a una comitiva de 16 personas que viaja desde Washington a Ciudad Trujillo. El grupo asistirá a los actos vinculados al proyectado monumento a Cristóbal Colón, concebido para simbolizar la paz y la unidad entre las 21 naciones panamericanas. La viajera señala que la delegación oficial incluye al senador Theodore Green, al representante Matthew Merritt, al representante Hamilton Fish Jr., a la autora de libros de viajes Eleanor Early, a los jóvenes Hammy Fish y Dicky Chatfield-Taylor, y a George Djamgaroff.

records.headline: A dispatch in The Washington Daily News details the upcoming
records.summary_en: A dispatch in The Washington Daily News details the upcoming schedule for the visiting American delegation arriving in Trujillo City after stops in Cuba and Haiti. The party expects to be officially received in Santo Domingo by the president and former president General Trujillo, followed by evening cocktail parties and a ball. On the following morning, the visitors plan to attend ceremonies in the cathedral for the opening of Christopher Columbus's casket, accompanied by an international radio broadcast at 11:30, before attending a special parliamentary session on Monday morning and departing for home on Tuesday.
records.summary_es: Una crónica en The Washington Daily News detalla el programa previsto para la delegación estadounidense que llega a Ciudad Trujillo tras escalas en Cuba y Haití. La comitiva espera ser recibida oficialmente en Santo Domingo por el presidente y el expresidente general Trujillo, seguido por recepciones de cóctel y un baile esta noche. A la mañana siguiente, los visitantes prevén asistir a ceremonias en la catedral para presenciar la apertura del ataúd de Cristóbal Colón, acompañadas por una transmisión radial internacional a las 11:30, antes de presenciar una sesión parlamentaria especial el lunes por la mañana y emprender el regreso el martes.

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Miami reports that an official
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Miami reports that an official party of 16 representing the United States government flew today aboard a Pan American Clipper to Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic. The delegation travels to witness the disinterment of Christopher Columbus's casket during ceremonies in the cathedral and to inspect the site of a proposed memorial to be erected by 21 pan-American nations. The monument is scheduled to be constructed and dedicated in 1942. The delegation includes Senator Green, Democrat of Rhode Island, of the Foreign Relations Committee, and Representative Fish, Republican of New York, of the corresponding House committee.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de la Associated Press desde Miami informa que una delegación oficial de 16 personas en representación del gobierno de los Estados Unidos voló hoy a bordo de un hidroavión de Pan American hacia Ciudad Trujillo, República Dominicana. La comitiva viaja para presenciar la exhumación del féretro de Cristóbal Colón durante ceremonias en la catedral e inspeccionar el terreno para el proyectado monumento conmemorativo que erigirán 21 naciones panamericanas. La obra está programada para construirse y dedicarse en 1942. La delegación incluye al senador Green, demócrata de Rhode Island, de la Comisión de Relaciones Exteriores, y al representante Fish, republicano de Nueva York, de la comisión correspondiente de la Cámara de Representantes.

records.headline: The Evening Star reports that the tomb revered in Ciudad Trujillo
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reports that the tomb revered in Ciudad Trujillo as containing the bones of Christopher Columbus is being opened for the third time, marking the first occasion that photographs of the coffin and its contents have been permitted. Unofficial United States representatives invited to attend include Senator Theodore P. Green, Representative Matthew J. Merritt, and Representative Hamilton Fish, who were also invited by the Dominican Republic to address the Dominican Congress on Monday. The article notes that after more than four centuries of removals and reburials, the final resting place remains disputed: Dominicans and many historians maintain that the Ciudad Trujillo Cathedral holds the true remains, while Seville, Spain, and Genoa, Italy, also claim to enshrine the explorer's body.

Entre los representantes oficiosos de los Estados Unidos invitados al acto figuran el senador Theodore P. Green, el representante Matthew J. records.headline: En route to San Pedro, an American correspondent reflects on the history of the Dominican
records.summary_en: En route to San Pedro, an American correspondent reflects on the history of the Dominican capital, formerly Santo Domingo de Guzman, which was founded on Aug. 4, 1496, by Christopher Columbus's brother and subsequently renamed for Generalissimo Trujillo after he gained power. The author observes that Trujillo dislikes references to the city's former name, with mail addressed to Santo Domingo reportedly returned as "place unknown," while noting that the settlement claims the oldest cathedral and university in the hemisphere, as well as the introduction of the first horse in 1551 and the first cow in 1554. Upon arriving at San Pedro, 30 miles from Trujillo City, the party was hosted at the Kilbourne sugar plantation and welcomed with royal fanfare by seven dignitaries, including Arturo Logrono, "Secretario de Estada de la Presidencia."
records.summary_es: En ruta hacia San Pedro, una corresponsal estadounidense reflexiona sobre la historia de la capital dominicana, antiguamente Santo Domingo de Guzmán, fundada el 4 de agosto de 1496 por el hermano de Cristóbal Colón y posteriormente rebautizada con el nombre del generalísimo Trujillo tras su ascenso al poder. La autora comenta que a Trujillo le disgustan las referencias al antiguo nombre y que el correo dirigido a Santo Domingo se devuelve con la leyenda de "lugar desconocido", destacando además que la urbe cuenta con la catedral y la universidad más antiguas del hemisferio, así como con la llegada del primer caballo en 1551 y la primera vaca en 1554. Al llegar a San Pedro, a 30 millas de Ciudad Trujillo, el grupo fue agasajado en la plantación azucarera de Kilbourne y recibido con gran pompa por siete dignatarios, entre ellos Arturo Logroño, "Secretario de Estada de la Presidencia".

records.headline: United States and Dominican officials held formal ceremonies
records.summary_en: United States and Dominican officials held formal ceremonies in the oldest cathedral of the New World, laying wreaths on a coffin reputed to hold the bones of Christopher Columbus. Scheduled plans to open the coffin for a third time and photograph its contents were cancelled at the last moment due to what authorities termed "technicalities," leaving the casket sealed as it had been since its discovery in 1877, when an identifying plate indicated it contained only part of the discoverer's skeleton. Former President General Rafael L. Trujillo opened cathedral ceremonies by welcoming the 16-member American delegation headed by Senator Theodore D. Green, who received the keys to the city at a banquet, visited the site for a Columbus memorial lighthouse to be erected by 21 American nations, and praised Columbus as a symbol of American unity against overseas division.

Los planes previstos para abrir el ataúd por tercera vez y fotografiar su interior se cancelaron a última hora debido a lo que las autoridades calificaron de "tecnicismos", permaneciendo sellado tal como ocurrió tras su hallazgo en 1877, cuando una placa identificatoria consignó que solo contenía parte del esqueleto del descubridor. El expresidente general Rafael L. Trujillo abrió los actos en la catedral dando la bienvenida a la delegación estadounidense de 16 personas encabezada por el senador Theodore D. records.headline: Observing what she describes as an impressive, theatrical environment
records.summary_en: Observing what she describes as an impressive, theatrical environment shaped by General Trujillo, correspondent Evelyn Peyton Gordon spent two days en route home from Santo Domingo, she recounts. She notes that the clean streets, ancient architecture, and picturesque populace combine with the lavish estates of the Dominican ruler, arguing that substantial achievements underlie the spectacle. Gordon describes Trujillo's seaside country residence, Sans Souci, noting its Moorish design, luxurious swimming pool, mosaic terraces, and lavish hospitality, as well as the ceremonial entrances of the generalissimo amid glitter of uniforms, medals, and playing of the national anthem.
records.summary_es: Observando lo que describe como un entorno imponente y teatral forjado por el general Trujillo, la corresponsal Evelyn Peyton Gordon relata su estancia de dos días en una crónica enviada de regreso desde Santo Domingo. Señala que las calles limpias, la arquitectura antigua y la pintoresca población se combinan con las suntuosas residencias del gobernante dominicano, sosteniendo que detrás del espectáculo existen obras de verdadera envergadura. Gordon describe la residencia campestre de Trujillo junto al mar, Sans Souci, destacando su diseño morisco, su lujosa piscina, sus terrazas de mosaicos y su fastuosa hospitalidad, así como las entradas ceremoniales del generalísimo en medio del brillo de uniformes, medallas y la interpretación del himno nacional.

records.full_text:
Trujillo Working on Plans to Provide Refugee Homes

By EVELYN PEYTON GORDON

This fellow Trujillo, dictator of the Dominican Republic, has some pretty constructive ideas and plans up his sleeve. As you know, there has been for some time a good deal of talk about the Dominican Republic receiving some thousands of refugees from Europe. The number has not been specified, nor has it been determined whether the refugees will be only of the Semitic race.

The plan now afoot is to bring to the little republic anywhere up to 100,000 homeless people. They must, of course, bring with them $500. They will be given small land grants and it is hoped they will be of the farmer type. In this good-sized country there are little over a million and a half people, so there is room for them all.

IT'S PRETTY HOT

Will these people work in the fields where in summer the climate is so hot that to date nobody but Negroes have been able to labor successfully? Will they work in the fields in a country where there is a class feeling that members of the white race should not work in the fields? That is to be seen. Labor is cheap in the Dominican Republic. Each of the refugees will have a chance to become, in a small way, a country squire. He will eventually be expected to take his part in the government of the country.

Perhaps all the refugees will not be of an agrarian nature. Perhaps there will be among them doctors who will find a place in the new hospitals which Gen. Trujillo has built there. There may be scientists, engineers who will add their knowledge to the future construction of an even better equipped country. There may be musicians who will organize orchestras, perhaps even an opera. The Dominican people—and we speak of the mass of the people as guided by the leaders—are open to culture.

MEETS REFUGEE AGENT

While we were in Trujillo City we met a delightful gentleman from New York named Houston. He was visiting in the city on just this problem of refugees. He was sent there by the American Jewish Distribution Committee. Mr. Houston, who has lived for many years in South America, consulted with Gen. Trujillo about the plans.

Their decisions were, of course, not announced, nor any information as to when the migration to Trujillo City is to take place. As in most things which transpire there, there will be little done until the plans are all in good working order.

ANENT SAMANA BAY

Now, once more anent Samana Bay. The other day it was reported that Gen. Trujillo had negotiated with Germany for the lease of that strategic body of water as a submarine base. The report emanated from Puerto Rico, where there are a number of exiled enemies of the Generalissimo. It does seem that in view of the fact the General desires only the friendliest relations with this country, he would be smarter than to enter into any such negotiations. Especially when he had so recently entertained a number of prominent Americans in his own house.

The lease of the bay to the Nazis would not only be an unfriendly act to the United States, but a hostile one. And, also in view of this same friendliness, it is certain that at any emergency the General would permit the United States Navy the use of Samana Bay or any other Dominican port, as a submarine base or any other military facility.

These aren't direct quotes from the Generalissimo, but they are very definitely the impression received during our visit. The General knows that we are friendly to his country, but he also knows that we expect him to play ball with us.

SOME MORE ITEMS

Here are just a few more facts about our visit. The General was the best of hosts. For young Ham Fish and young Dick Chatfield-Taylor, he arranged endless amusement. The night before we left Trujillo City he asked the boys if they'd like to see a Wild West movie. Such fun. But little did the boys know, until they arrived at the theater, that it was the private theater of young Ramfis Trujillo, and that Ramfis' private operator was on hand to grind out the excitement of the bad men of the West.

On the streets of Trujillo City we, honored visitors, stopped to have our shoes shined. "Is it 10 cents?" we asked the small urchin who knelt to deal us a good polish. "Please, ma'am. Nothing," he answered. "It is with the compliments of the benefactor!" So it goes every place. And the "benefactor" sees that the urchin gets his dime.

Among the people of Trujillo City one rarely hears the name Trujillo. It is "general," "generalissimo" or "Mr. Jones." Does "Mr. Jones" speak English, you'll want to know? Everybody says no. But we have a suspicion that he is somewhat in a class with the so-called deaf-mutes who drive Intourist cars in Soviet Russia—they hear keenly and speak fluently any number of languages!

records.headline: The Key West Citizen reviews the historical controversy surrounding
records.summary_en: The Key West Citizen reviews the historical controversy surrounding Christopher Columbus's burial in connection with the planned five million dollar memorial supported by New World nations. Although conventional accounts record that Columbus died at Valladolid in 1506, was moved to Seville, was transferred to the cathedral of San Domingo in 1542, and was supposedly moved to Havana in 1795 and back to Seville in 1898, Dominicans insist the body was never removed. They maintain that in 1877, eighty-two years after the purported transfer to Havana, a lead coffin marked with Columbus's name was discovered near the altar of the San Domingo cathedral, indicating the Spaniards evacuated the wrong casket. The article concludes that the remains preserved in the Dominican Republic will occupy the place of honor in the new memorial regardless of competing historical claims.
records.summary_es: The Key West Citizen examina la controversia histórica en torno al sepulcro de Cristóbal Colón con motivo del proyectado monumento de cinco millones de dólares financiado por naciones del Nuevo Mundo. Aunque las versiones tradicionales señalan que Colón falleció en Valladolid en 1506, fue trasladado a Sevilla, llevado a la catedral de Santo Domingo en 1542 y supuestamente conducido a La Habana en 1795 y de regreso a Sevilla en 1898, los dominicanos sostienen que el cuerpo jamás salió de la isla. Afirman que en 1877, ochenta y dos años después del supuesto traslado a La Habana, se halló junto al altar de la catedral de Santo Domingo un féretro de plomo con una inscripción que indicaba contener los restos de Colón, sugiriendo que los españoles evacuaron el ataúd equivocado. La crónica concluye que los restos conservados en la República Dominicana ocuparán el lugar de honor en el nuevo monumento sin importar las disputas historiográficas.

records.headline: An anti-Roosevelt campaign in the German newspaper Völkischer Beobachter (cited
records.summary_en: An anti-Roosevelt campaign in the German newspaper Völkischer Beobachter (cited as the Beobachter) ridiculed President Roosevelt's peace proposal requesting non-aggression guarantees for 31 nations. Accusing the American president of concealing his own territorial ambitions while imputing plans of conquest to others, the organ challenged Roosevelt to pledge that he would not launch any attack against Haiti, San Domingo (the Dominican Republic), or Dutch Caribbean territories. The report indicates that the German publication's claims were apparently linked to a proposal by Senator Lundeen of Minnesota urging United States acquisition of European possessions in the Western Hemisphere for defense bases.
records.summary_es: Una campaña contra Roosevelt difundida por el periódico alemán Völkischer Beobachter (citado como el Beobachter) ridiculizó la propuesta de paz del presidente Roosevelt que solicitaba garantías de no agresión para 31 naciones. Tras acusar al mandatario estadounidense de ocultar sus propias ambiciones territoriales mientras imputa planes de conquista a otros países, el órgano retó a Roosevelt a comprometerse a no perpetrar ningún ataque contra Haití, Santo Domingo (la República Dominicana) o las posesiones holandesas del Caribe. La información señala que los señalamientos de la publicación alemana se vinculaban aparentemente a una iniciativa del senador Lundeen de Minnesota en la que sugería la adquisición estadounidense de posesiones europeas en el hemisferio occidental como bases defensivas.

records.headline: A young German fugitive who faced imminent deportation to Germany
records.summary_en: A young German fugitive who faced imminent deportation to Germany and execution by a Nazi firing squad is en route to the Dominican Republic after securing asylum, Attorney Frank Buckley announced. Through the diplomatic intervention of Dominican Minister Andres Pastoriza, the young man was granted entry without payment of the customary immigrant head tax. Accompanied by his American bride, Mary Wells of Tuscaloosa, Alabama, the youth had deserted a German vessel at New Orleans last July before being apprehended in Miami, eventually obtaining legal representation and a deportation stay through American supporters including State Department official Stuart Fuller.

Gracias a las gestiones diplomáticas del ministro dominicano Andrés Pastoriza, se autorizó el ingreso del joven sin exigir el pago del impuesto de entrada acostumbrado para los inmigrantes. Acompañado por su esposa estadounidense, Mary Wells de Tuscaloosa (Alabama), el muchacho había desertado de un barco alemán en Nueva Orleans en julio pasado antes de ser capturado en Miami, logrando finalmente representación legal y una suspensión de la deportación con la ayuda de partidarios estadounidenses, entre ellos el funcionario del Departamento de Estado Stuart Fuller.
