records.headline: Dominican Minister Andres Pastoriza announced the establishment of a $50,000 annual international peace prize
records.summary_en: Dominican Minister Andres Pastoriza announced the establishment of a $50,000 annual international peace prize in the name of former President Dr. Rafael L. Trujillo at the opening of the Dominican Pavilion at the New York World's Fair. Designated officially as the Trujillo Peace Prize, the award will honor the individual or institution making the most outstanding yearly contribution toward re-establishing and maintaining peace among nations, with the initial presentation scheduled for October 24. Pastoriza stated that the prize, created by the Dominican government, pays tribute to Trujillo's devotion to international peace principles, adding that nominations may be submitted by executive, legislative, and diplomatic figures worldwide, members of the Permanent Court of Arbitration at The Hague, and university faculty.

Denominado oficialmente Premio de la Paz Trujillo, el galardón distinguirá a la persona o institución que realice la contribución más sobresaliente cada año al restablecimiento y mantenimiento de la paz entre las naciones, con una primera entrega programada para el 24 de octubre. Pastoriza afirmó que el galardón, instituido por el gobierno dominicano, rinde homenaje a la devoción de Trujillo hacia los principios de paz internacional, y precisó que las candidaturas podrán ser presentadas por miembros del poder ejecutivo, legislativo y diplomático de todas las naciones, jueces del Tribunal Permanente de Arbitraje de La Haya y catedráticos universitarios.

records.headline: The Hamburg-Amerika liner St. Louis, carrying German Jewish refugees
records.summary_en: The Hamburg-Amerika liner St. Louis, carrying German Jewish refugees barred from landing in Havana, sailed slowly as an offer of refuge from the Dominican Republic remained pending with details under negotiation. Luis Clasing, the shipping line's Havana representative, reported that the company gave the Dominican government until noon to radio whether arrangements could be made to land the passengers at Santo Domingo, failing which the ship would return to Hamburg. Dominican Secretary of State Arturo de Spradel instructed Havana Consul Nestor Pou to offer asylum on condition that each refugee pay a fee for residence permission, though ship officials doubted the liner would alter its course because most refugees could not afford the sum.

Luis Clasing, representante de la línea naviera en La Habana, informó que la empresa otorgó al gobierno dominicano hasta el mediodía para comunicar por radio si se podían hacer arreglos para desembarcar a los pasajeros en Santo Domingo, de lo contrario el buque regresaría a Hamburgo. El secretario de Estado dominicano, Arturo de Spradel, instruyó al cónsul en La Habana, Néstor Pou, a ofrecer asilo con la condición de que cada refugiado pagara una tarifa para obtener el permiso de residencia, aunque los oficiales del barco dudaban de que el transatlántico cambiara su rumbo porque la mayoría de los refugiados no podía pagar dicha suma.

records.headline: A bust of Christopher Columbus sculpted by Aristide Fortano
records.summary_en: A bust of Christopher Columbus sculpted by Aristide Fortano was recently discovered in a garage in Deal, New Jersey, where it had been stored for years after belonging to the late John J. Cone, Supreme Knight of the Knights of Columbus in 1898. The bust is to be exhibited near the model of the $5,000,000 Columbus Memorial in the Hall of Peace, being built by the 21 Pan-American nations. Following the exhibition, the sculpture will be shipped to the Dominican Republic to be placed before the tomb of Columbus in the Cathedral of Santo Domingo.

records.headline: When the Dominican Republic agreed to participate in the New York World's
records.summary_en: When the Dominican Republic agreed to participate in the New York World's Fair, commissioners arranged to dedicate a section of their pavilion to Christopher Columbus, whose remains lie in the Cathedral of Santo Domingo. Seeking a bust by Fortano, investigators learned that the Knights of Columbus had presented one 40 years earlier to John J. Cone, then supreme knight of the order. After discovering that Cone had died, they located the sculpture in a garage belonging to relatives at 232 Ocean Avenue in Deal, New Jersey. The bust will be exhibited at the fair, shipped to the Dominican Republic to stand before Columbus's cathedral tomb, and ultimately placed alongside the tomb in the Columbus memorial planned for 1942.

records.headline: Dr. Logrono, counselor at the Dominican Legation, has departed
records.summary_en: Dr. Logrono, counselor at the Dominican Legation, has departed Washington with his wife and two children to return to Trujillo, where he will serve as a judge of the Supreme Court. Prior to his diplomatic post, he served eight years as an appellate court judge in his native country and earned distinction as a noted lawyer possessing one of the finest libraries in Trujillo. The Logronos were widely known in Washington diplomatic society for their hospitality, with both hailing from prominent old families in the Dominican Republic.
records.summary_es: El Dr. Logroño, consejero de la legación dominicana, partió de Washington junto a su esposa y dos hijos para regresar a Trujillo, donde fungirá como juez de la Suprema Corte. Antes de su cargo diplomático, se desempeñó durante ocho años como juez del tribunal de apelaciones en su país natal y se distinguió como un notable abogado poseedor de una de las mejores bibliotecas de Trujillo. Los señores de Logroño eran ampliamente conocidos en la sociedad diplomática de Washington por sus agasajos, perteneciendo ambos a destacadas familias tradicionales de la República Dominicana.

records.full_text:
Military to Have Charge of Reception for Molina

By EVELYN PEYTON GORDON

Invitations for the last of the summer official entertaining—a reception to be given next Saturday evening at the Pan American Union by the Dominican Minister and Senora de Pastoriza in honor of the former President of the Dominican Republic, Gen. Rafel Trujillo Molina—arrived several days ago. But when inquiries were made as to the date of the arrival of the Generalissimo himself, not a thing could be learned.

Now that may seem a little backwards. But really it isn't. When a diplomat is planning for the several days entertainment of one of the head men of his government, well, that diplomat—if he's smart—waits until every detail of the plan is perfect, and then he begins to talk about it. So only just now have I been able to worm out of the legation the date of the actual arrival of our neighbor from the Caribbean island.

Having visited in Trujillo City last spring and been royally entertained, I am perhaps more interested in this prospective visit of Gen. Trujillo than a good many other people. For almost a year the general has been planning to come to Washington. And for him, as well as for the Capital, it is a momentous trip. For it is the first time Gen. Trujillo has been away from his native land—excepting a brief visit to Haiti.

SCHEDULE UNCERTAIN

Gen. Trujillo is a military man and as such he will be received in Washington when he arrives next Thursday. The exact time is not yet certain. In fact much of this schedule is tentative and subject to change if the general chooses to spend more time seeing people than sightseeing.

As a former member of the United States Marine Corps—during the Marine occupation of the Dominican Republic some years ago, Rafael Trujillo served with them—the general has been invited to Washington by the Maj. Gen. Commandant of the Marine Corps, Gen. Thomas Holcomb. And as such a guest many of his activities during his several days in Washington will be with the military.

On Thursday the visitor will go to Mt. Vernon, and Arlington where he will lay wreathes on the tombs of George Washington and the Unknown Soldier. He will then visit the CCC camp at Fort Hunt, following much the same schedule that the King and Queen followed on their recent visit. On Friday morning Gen. Trujillo will call on the Secretary of State, and later on President Roosevelt and will then be entertained at luncheon at the Senate by a group of senators, probably including Sen. Theodore Green of Rhode Island who was among the delegates who went to Trujillo City for the dedication of the Christopher Columbus Memorial site.

BUSY SCHEDULE

That afternoon the general will visit the United States gun factory, the Navy Yard and the Marine Barracks, and that evening will be the dinner guest of Gen. Holcomb. July 8, will be devoted to a visit to Fort Meade followed by luncheon at the Army-Navy Club, and an afternoon of sightseeing preliminary to the reception that evening at 10 o'clock.

On Sunday, July 9, past differences will be forgotten when the Haitian Minister, Elie Lescot, entertains at a luncheon for the general. That afternoon there will be visits to Greenbelt and other Federal Housing Projects nearby, and on June 10, a visit to Fort Myer with a review of the troops and luncheon with Maj. Gen. Breckinridge. That evening the new Chief of Staff of the United States Army, Gen. Marshall will fete the visiting general at dinner, and the next day Gen. Trujillo will go to New York where he will whip thru another long program.

The general will be accompanied by his secretary, Mr. Bonnetti and his physician.

records.full_text:
Society Again Gets Breath With Departure of Royalty And Summer Season Here Arrival of Gen. Rafael Trujillo, However, Will Revive Interests; Harriet Dawley Makes Debut

By MARGARET HART,

Society Editor.

Washington society is settling down to normalcy again after weeks marked with excitement and brilliant festivities for royal visitors. And, may it be said that the National's Capital liked royalty and for many years to come stories will be retold of the pleasant informality of these persons of royal birth. To those who had never met royalty before, the natural and wholesome manner in the royal visitors' conversations and the sincere interest displayed in all with whom they came in contact, was a revelation.

The visits of their Britannic Majesties, King George VI and Queen Elizabeth; the Crown Prince Frederik and Crown Princess Ingrid of Denmark and Iceland and the Crown Prince Olav and Crown Princess Martha of Norway all added indelibly to the pages of history of society in the Capital of our country, as well as furthering the bonds between this Nation and the kingdoms across the sea.

Queen and Princesses

Leave Fashion Impressions.

Fashion played no minor party in the happy impressions left behind by the visiting Queen and the two Princesses. On each and every occasion these royal ladies wore costumes that delighted the eyes of not only the fashioned-minded woman but, as well, the men who know not one color or material from another. Little is the doubt that the trend of style will be greatly swayed by the costumes and accessories selected by the lovely visitors for their stay in this country. Memory recalls the dainty parasols carried by the gracious Queen Elizabeth during her daytime appearances; the beautiful fan of ostrich feathers which complemented the striking ensemble worn by Princess Martha at one of the dinners in her honor as well as the fetching veiling effect which formed the crown of one of the Princess Ingrid's becoming picture hats.

Another Foreign Visitor

Is Due in Capital.

It never is quite safe to state that the curtain has been dropped on all formal entertaining in this town. For just when the social calendar appears absolutely blank something is just bound to happen. Members of society who are still lingering in the city will find the latter part of the week not quiet socially, but gay with festive parties for distinguished visitors.

The former President of the Dominican Republic, Gen. Rafael L. Trujillo, and now commander in chief of his country's army, will arrive in Washington Thursday. While he will spend much of his time visiting service posts around the Capital, several interesting social events will center around his stay here. Gen. Trujillo will have luncheon at the Senate Friday, in the afternoon will visit the Navy Yard and the Marine Barracks and that night will be the honor guest at dinner of Maj. Gen. Commandant of the Marine Corps Thomas Holcomb. The following day the visitor will visit Fort Meade, have luncheon at the Army Navy Club and in the evening will be feted at a reception at the Pan-American Union, with the Minister of his republic and Senora de Pastoriza as hosts.

Sunday, July 9, the army chief will be the guest in whose honor the Haitian Minister, Mr. Elie Lescot, will give a luncheon and the following day Gen. Trujillo will visit Quantico, where the commandant, Gen. James C. Breckinridge, will entertain him at luncheon after a review of the troops. The last event on the program for the visitor, who will leave the Capital Tuesday, will be the dinner Monday night given for him by the Chief of Staff, U. S. A., Maj. Gen. George C. Marshall. Also included on Gen. Trujillo's schedule will be a visit to Mount Vernon, Arlington National Cemetery and Federal housing projects in and near the Capital.

Another visitor who will arrive on the scene this week is Gen. Goes Monteiro, commander in chief of the Brazilian Army. Gen. Goes Monteiro is no stranger to Washington and during his last visit he was much feted. His wife, Senhora de Goes Monteiro, arrived in the city yesterday from New York, where she was met upon her arrival by the Brazilian Ambassador and Senhora de Martins. There undoubtedly will be parties for her as well as her husband. Included among the festivities planned for the Brazilian general is a dinner Friday night, with the Undersecretary of State, Mr. Sumner Welles as host, and a luncheon the following day given by the Assistant Secretary of War, Mr. Louis Johnson.

Miss Harriet Webster Dawley

Made Debut Yesterday.

The ranks of all circles of society in Washington are considerably depleted over this week end, with many planning to remain away until after the holiday. Many deferred their departure until late yesterday in order to attend the debut of Miss Harriet Webster Dawley, daughter of Mrs. M. Webster Dawley.

records.headline: Even if he is denounced as a tyrant and accused of the massacre of thousands of Haitians two years ago
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* profiled General Rafael Trujillo, noting that despite being denounced as a tyrant and accused of the massacre of thousands of Haitians two years earlier, he was recognized for administrative energy and public works. Having taken power in 1930 under the slogan "God and Trujillo," he oversaw road construction, school expansion, and the rebuilding and renaming of the capital before handing the presidency to Dr. Jacinto Bienvenido Peynado. The article noted that Trujillo continued to direct Dominican governance while being celebrated by sympathetic biographers as an inspired leader.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* perfiló al general Rafael Trujillo, señalando que, a pesar de haber sido denunciado como un tirano y acusado de la matanza de miles de haitianos dos años antes, se le reconocía por su empuje administrativo y sus planes de obras públicas. Habiendo tomado el poder en 1930 bajo el lema «Dios y Trujillo», dirigió la construcción de caminos, la expansión de escuelas y la reedificación y cambio de nombre de la capital antes de traspasar la presidencia formalmente al Dr. Jacinto Bienvenido Peynado. El artículo consignaba que Trujillo seguía conduciendo las riendas del gobierno dominicano mientras biógrafos afines lo ensalzaban como un líder providencial.
records.passage: come and who plan to come. Even if he is denounced as a tyrant and accused of the massacre of thousands of Haitians two years ago, during a border struggle along the boundary between the Dominican Republic and Haiti, there is no doubt that he is a forceful leader with a certain genius in public finance. He has an extraordinary concept of himself as a child of destiny When he was still a boy, he resolved to be the president of the Dominican Republic, where storm and strife in politics and insecurity of tenure for presidents was the classical political situation. He won the post in 1930, when he was 39, after a campaign whose slogan was "God and Trujillo." He relinquished it last August to a devoted follower. Dr. Jacinto Bienvenido [Peynado?], who still follows his wishes devotedly. Gen. Trujillo's biographer suggests that in his governing he is guided by an "electric force" from Heaven. He has built roads and pursued other public works, increased the number of public schools, reconstructed the ancient capital of the republic, Santo Domingo, after the 1930 hurricane (and renamed it in his own honor) and enhanced the lot of those persons in his country who are willing to accept his leadership. He is energetic, industrious and a born leader. An inspired biography of him published as a panegyric is revealing for all its encomiums. Progress Through Discipline. records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that General Rafael Trujillo hosted a lavish reception at the New York World's Fair aboard his yacht *Ramfis*, formerly owned by American millionaire Julius Fleischmann, before the vessel steamed toward Washington. The article noted Trujillo's fondness for military attire and listed dozens of high foreign orders and medals bestowed upon him across Europe and the Americas. Observers commented that Trujillo possessed more decorations than nearly any other anticipated foreign visitor.

La nota hizo hincapié en la predilección de Trujillo por las galas militares y enumeró decenas de condecoraciones y medallas extranjeras que le habían sido otorgadas en Europa y América. Los observadores comentaron que Trujillo ostentaba más preseas que casi cualquier otro visitante distinguido del exterior.

records.full_text:
Trujillo Defended By Dominican C. of C.

The Dominican Chamber of Commerce today defended Gen. Rafael Leonidas Trujillo, former president of the Dominican Republic, whose invitation from President Roosevelt to tea at the White House was attacked by the "Committee for Dominican Democracy."

"As Americans, we strongly resent any criticism of the President of the United States from such a source, insulting his distinguished guest," the chamber declared in a statement for the press. It added:

"We members of the Dominican Chamber of Commerce in the United States, composed of American business men, know that the accomplishments achieved by Gen. Trujillo during his administration have far exceeded any social welfare program ever instituted in his country."

The general, who will be here until Tuesday, when he departs by yacht for New York, went to Fort George G. Meade, Md., today to see the troops there. A reception at the Pan American Union which had been planned for tonight in the general's honor by Minister Pastoriza of the Dominican Republic has been canceled out of respect to the late Secretary Swanson.

records.headline: Out of respect for the late Secretary of the Navy Claude A. Swanson
records.summary_en: Out of respect for the late Secretary of the Navy Claude A. Swanson, General Rafael Leonidas Trujillo requested the cancellation of a large reception planned in his honor by Dominican Minister and Señora de Pastoriza, setting aside all formal events surrounding his visit until after Swanson's funeral services. Because preparations for the reception were already complete, Trujillo directed that the food prepared for the function be distributed to a Washington home for orphaned children and to the Little Sisters of the Poor.
records.summary_es: Por respeto al difunto secretario de la Marina Claude A. Swanson, el general Rafael Leonidas Trujillo solicitó la cancelación de una gran recepción planeada en su honor por el ministro dominicano y la señora de Pastoriza, posponiendo todos los eventos formales en torno a su visita hasta después de los servicios fúnebres de Swanson. Debido a que los preparativos para la recepción ya estaban concluidos, Trujillo dispuso que los alimentos preparados para la velada fueran distribuidos a un hogar para niños huérfanos de Washington y a las Hermanitas de los Pobres.
records.passage:
Joining in with Washington in showing respect for the late cabinet
officer was the noted visitor from the Dominican Republic, Gen. Rafael
Leonidas Trujillo, commander in chief of his country's army and former
President of the republic. Gen. Trujillo was to have met many prominent
personages last night at a brilliant reception planned in his honor by the
Dominican Minister and Senora de Pastoriza. When word reached the
visitor of the death of Mr. Swanson he requested that the party honoring
him be canceled out of deference to the departed member of the Presi
dent's official family. All other formal parties centered around the visit
of the Dominican Army chief were cast aside until after the service for
Mr. Swanson tomorrow.
Food for Reception Given
To Less Fortunate.

tribution of the food, prepared for the reception last evening, to those less
fortunate. Everything was in readiness for the large reception, only the
finishing touches having to be added. So a home for orphaned children
in Washington and the Little Sisters of the Poor saw the silver lining
to the cloud that spread over Washington society.
Many are the hearts saddened over the loss of Secretary Swanson and
sympathy goes out to his widow from all circles of society in the Nation's
Capital. While in the past few years the cabinet officer made few ap
pearances at social functions he delighted in the stories of the social
whirl brought home to him by his petite and popular wife. Mrs. Swanson

Clapper cited first-hand reporting by Quentin Reynolds of *Collier's*, who investigated the border atrocities and observed victims mutilated by Dominican forces. Clapper maintained that any prosperity Trujillo claimed was purchased through the murder of thousands of obscure Haitian peasants.

records.full_text:
It Seems to Me

THERE is consistency in the Ham who talks like a Fish.

The gentleman from Duchess County takes his dictators straight and manifests the same enthusiasm for the home-grown kind as he has for those in foreign lands. When Hitler made his reply to the peace proposals of President Roosevelt who was first and foremost in this country to praise the Fuehrer on the air? Who but Ham? And the policy of Mr. Fish, as he functions in the House—has it not been to oppose all measures which would in any way discourage the ambitions of the Axis powers?

Ham Fish has repeatedly declared himself a true neutral and has argued that his votes have been motivated by his abhorrence of bloodshed. How, then does he explain the fact that he has just taken occasion to shake the hand of Gen. Rafael Leonidas Trujillo y Molina, the dictator from the Dominican Republic? Mr. Fish is quoted as having said at a dinner to Trujillo in New York on Wednesday, "You have created a golden age for your country." But if Trujillo has brought any treasure to his country it certainly was compounded out of the blood of many thousands. Quentin Reynolds was sent by Collier's several months ago to make a first-hand examination of the Trujillo massacres along the border.

I KNOW Reynolds well, and he is a reliable reporter of high competence. He came back from the Dominican Republic having actually seen many of those who were mutilated by Trujillo's ruffians. Nobody knows the full toll of the dead. There were obscure Haitian peasants who were murdered under the fury of the Dominican dictator. Reynolds thought that 20,000 was about the closest estimate anybody could make concerning the dead. There might be more, and right down to this day I have seen no denial of the mass murders which occurred in the land of Trujillo.

And this is the man and the hand which Ham Fish delights to honor. This is no dictator across the water. These are not outrages concerning which there is any fundamental dispute in testimony. Here upon our own doorstep lies the land of Trujillo and the earth stained by the blood of simple people. "You have created a golden age for your people," said Ham Fish. And two strong men reach across a dark puddle to shake hands.

This is the same Ham Fish who shouts "war mongers" at all who strive to bring about European peace. Is it truly better many should die in order that the few should profit very much?

HITLER, like Trujillo, has been cruel and brutal in his treatment of those in Germany who oppose him. And some he has allowed to live under the forced labor of concentration camps. But if he can create treasure it may be that Mr. Fish will overlook many things and once again hail the creation of another golden age. Raise up the goblet! Drink deep, oh Ham and Hitler and Trujillo! Here's a cup to the next man who dies.

The murdered men and women at our doorsteps were Negroes of Haiti. The persecuted folks of Germany are Jewish. And it seems that such things can be overlooked by certain statesmen. Perhaps it is just an optical illusion if one sees a shade more somber than that of yellow metal upon the surface of the golden age. Soap may remove it, and those who are content to close their eyes will see no ugly stains.

There is treasure. What matter the price paid by the poor and humble to the fury of dictators?

There is gold in those same hells.

records.headline: During his visit to Washington, the Dictator of the Dominican
records.summary_en: During his visit to Washington, the Dictator of the Dominican Republic, General Rafael Trujillo, received extraordinary protection not provided by U.S. officials. Following his arrival, the Dominican Legation was transformed under strict suspicion, with detectives examining grocery deliveries and inspecting camera cases for hidden bombs. Although Trujillo displays a mild manner and ingratiating smile in public, Dominican exiles in Puerto Rico and the United States remember him differently, and a detective hired from the New York police force guards his bedroom door at night.
records.summary_es: Durante su visita a Washington, el dictador de la República Dominicana, general Rafael Trujillo, recibió una protección extraordinaria que no fue proporcionada por funcionarios estadounidenses. Tras su llegada, la legación dominicana se transformó bajo rigurosa sospecha, con detectives que examinaban las entregas de víveres e inspeccionaban estuches de cámaras en busca de bombas ocultas. Aunque Trujillo muestra modales apacibles y una sonrisa cautivadora en público, los exiliados dominicanos en Puerto Rico y Estados Unidos lo recuerdan de otra manera, y un detective contratado de la policía de Nueva York vigila la puerta de su dormitorio por la noche.

records.summary_en: The column discusses social plans for General Rafael Trujillo, noting that midsummer lethargy and the death of Secretary Swanson contributed to the cancellation of an earlier reception at the Pan American Union. Dominican Minister Andres Pastoriza, who has been showing his chief around New York, is scheduled to return to Washington early next week to oversee informal social gatherings for the General. Following this return visit to the capital, Trujillo plans to sail for Europe to join Señora de Trujillo in Paris and meet his infant daughter born there some weeks ago. The item also reports that when Trujillo left his country early in July, he bought the large yacht Camargo, renamed it Ramfis after his young son, and sailed to Miami before proceeding to New York.

El ministro dominicano Andrés Pastoriza, quien ha estado acompañando a su jefe por Nueva York, tiene previsto regresar a Washington a principios de la próxima semana para supervisar las reuniones sociales informales del general. Tras esta nueva visita a la capital, Trujillo planea zarpar hacia Europa para reunirse con la señora de Trujillo en París y conocer a su pequeña hija nacida allí hace unas semanas. La nota también informa que cuando Trujillo salió de su país a principios de julio, compró el gran yate Camargo, lo rebautizó Ramfis en honor a su hijo menor y navegó a Miami antes de continuar hacia Nueva York.

records.full_text:
Gen. Trujillo to Be Feted by Dominican Minister

By EVELYN PEYTON GORDON

Oh, ye of little faith! Yes, you were disappointed when the reception in honor of the Dominican Republic's Gen. Rafael Trujillo was cancelled, weren't you? But it's all right now. All those who had accepted the invitation to the Pan American reception the Dominican Minister and Senora de Pastoriza planned for July 8, will get in on the party to be given Thursday afternoon at the Legation.

In lieu of those terrifyingly formal invitations which summoned several hundred guests to that fete at the Pan American Union, the Minister and his wife have sent out just normal big white invites. It's to be an informal cocktail party and just across the top of the card is written by hand, "In honor of Gen. Trujillo." That's all. No R. S. V. P. about it. No decorations and medals. Just a chance to say hello to the Strong Man of the Dominican Republic.

Now that is a very smart move. Washington is too far sunk in mid-summer lethargy to haul out the old white ties and tails again. Some people say that's one reason the reception of two weeks ago was cancelled—that, and of course, the fact that Secretary Swanson died. But there just weren't enough people in town to make a big showing in the huge rooms of the Pan American Union. And there weren't enough people who were willing to deck themselves in formal winter attire on a hot evening.

So it's all working out for the best. The General will have a chance to talk to the people he has known and everybody will have a good time. The Minister, Andres Pastoriza, who has been in New York giving his chief a whirl, will be back the early part of next week to see that things run smoothly.

After his return visit to the Capital, Gen. Trujillo will sail for Europe to join Senora de Trujillo in Paris, and to make the acquaintance of his small daughter born in the French capital some weeks ago. The General doesn't do things by halves. When he left his island republic for the first time early in July, he didn't content himself with merely a jaunt to Washington. No indeed. He bought one of the biggest yachts afloat, "Junky" Fleischman's Camargo, renamed it Ramfis for his young son, and sailed over to Miami.

Since then the yacht has been in New York and the General has been doing his traveling around those parts aboard her. But for his first trip to Europe—whew, what a thrill to be on your very first voyage across the ocean!—Trujillo has chosen the Normandie. But the Ramfis will follow close behind to be on hand for any European cruising the owner wants to do.

Paris, among other places, is on the schedule. To date no mention has been made of a visit to Germany and a chat with Der Fuehrer about that famous Samana Bay business. Last spring, when it was rumored that Gen. Trujillo was en route to this country, it was simultaneously reported that he was en route to Germany! Well, he has been to Washington, met our President, sowed whatever seeds of business he had to sow. Maybe he is really a bargainer and wants to put his proposition to Mr. Hitler! Anyhow, there won't be any politics or business at the party Thursday afternoon.

records.headline: General Rafael L. Trujillo Molina, former President of the Dominican
records.summary_en: General Rafael L. Trujillo Molina, former President of the Dominican Republic, returned to Washington yesterday for a brief visit and extensive entertainment. A reception in his honor is scheduled for tomorrow afternoon at the Dominican Legation, hosted by Dominican Minister and Madame Pastoriza. In addition, Dr. and Mrs. Frederick Benton are hosting an informal garden tea for him this afternoon at their home overlooking the Potomac. Accompanying the General from New York were Dr. Francisco Benzo, minister of public health of Santo Domingo, Dr. Emilio Garcia Godoy, Dominican Minister to Cuba, and Minister Pastoriza.
records.summary_es: El general Rafael L. Trujillo Molina, expresidente de la República Dominicana, regresó ayer a Washington para una breve visita y extensos agasajos. Mañana por la tarde se celebrará una recepción en su honor en la legación dominicana, ofrecida por el ministro dominicano y la señora Pastoriza. Además, el Dr. y la señora Frederick Benton ofrecerán una merienda informal en el jardín de su residencia con vista al Potomac esta tarde. Acompañaron al general desde Nueva York el Dr. Francisco Benzo, ministro de Salud Pública de Santo Domingo, el Dr. Emilio García Godoy, ministro dominicano en Cuba, y el ministro Pastoriza.

records.headline: General Rafael Trujillo was honored at several social gatherings
records.summary_en: General Rafael Trujillo was honored at several social gatherings in Washington prior to his departure for New York immediately following a legation reception given by the Dominican Minister and Señora de Pastoriza. Dr. and Mrs. Frederick Benton entertained the visitor yesterday at a cocktail party at their Reservoir Road home. Earlier that afternoon, Senator and Mrs. Ernest Lundeen held a small reception to enable Trujillo to renew acquaintances with members of Congress who visited Santo Domingo last year.
records.summary_es: El general Rafael Trujillo fue agasajado en varios encuentros sociales en Washington antes de su partida hacia Nueva York inmediatamente después de una recepción en la legación ofrecida por el ministro dominicano y la señora de Pastoriza. El Dr. y la señora Frederick Benton agasajaron al visitante ayer con un cóctel en su residencia de Reservoir Road. Más temprano esa tarde, el senador Ernest Lundeen y su esposa ofrecieron una pequeña recepción para permitirle a Trujillo renovar el trato con miembros del Congreso que visitaron Santo Domingo el año pasado.

records.headline: The wife of the incumbent President of the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: The wife of the incumbent President of the Dominican Republic, Señora de Peynado, arrived quietly in New York yesterday with her children to spend several weeks abroad, The Washington Daily News reports; the name is printed 'Peynada'. General Trujillo stated that he is not going to Germany at all, but will travel to Paris to join Señora de Trujillo and meet their newborn daughter. In Washington society notes, the Ambassador of Ecuador hosted a luncheon yesterday in honor of General Rafael Trujillo.

El general Trujillo declaró que no irá a Alemania en absoluto, sino que viajará a París para reunirse con la señora de Trujillo y conocer a su pequeña hija. En las notas de sociedad de Washington, el embajador de Ecuador ofreció un almuerzo ayer en honor al general Rafael Trujillo.

records.headline: The Evening Star reports on a Washington farewell reception
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reports on a Washington farewell reception given at the Dominican Legation in honor of former Dominican President General Trujillo. The gathering, hosted by Señora de Pastoriza, featured cakes iced in Dominican colors and was attended by prominent figures including Secretary of State Cordell Hull, Mrs. Hull, and several congressional wives. General Trujillo's daughter, Señora Brea Messena, who flew from Santo Domingo with her husband on Wednesday, also attended and accompanied her father to New York to visit the World's Fair.
records.summary_es: El Evening Star informa sobre una recepción de despedida en Washington ofrecida en la legación dominicana en honor al expresidente dominicano, general Trujillo. El encuentro, organizado por la señora de Pastoriza, incluyó pasteles decorados con los colores dominicanos y contó con la asistencia de figuras prominentes, entre ellos el secretario de Estado Cordell Hull, la señora Hull y varias esposas de congresistas. La hija del general Trujillo, la señora Brea Messena, quien voló desde Santo Domingo con su esposo el miércoles, también asistió y acompañó a su padre a Nueva York para visitar la Feria Mundial.

records.headline: The column recounts two incidents during General Rafael Trujillo's visit
records.summary_en: The column recounts two incidents during General Rafael Trujillo's visit to Washington. At a dinner given in his honor by U.S. Chief of Staff Marshall, Trujillo barred two of his aides from attending because they arrived at the Legation at 7:55 instead of the ordered 7:45, informing Marshall they were unable to come and threatening to court-martial them upon their return to Santo Domingo. In addition, the paper claims that the death of Secretary of the Navy Swanson provided a convenient excuse to cancel a planned reception for Trujillo at the Pan American Union ballroom, after only 400 of the 2,000 invited guests accepted.
records.summary_es: La columna relata dos incidentes ocurridos durante la visita del general Rafael Trujillo a Washington. Además, el periódico afirma que la muerte del secretario de Marina Swanson sirvió de conveniente pretexto para cancelar una recepción prevista para Trujillo en el salón de baile de la Unión Panamericana, después de que solo 400 de los 2,000 invitados aceptaran.

records.summary_en: Nearly 200 Washington homing pigeons had returned to their home lofts after taking part in the Santo Domingo-to-New York relay flight, an Associated Press dispatch from Richmond, Virginia, reports. Released in Richmond yesterday morning, each bird carried a copy of the goodwill message from the President of the Dominican Republic to Mayor La Guardia of New York. The flight to Washington represented the ninth lap of the relay, with the first pigeon completing the 100-mile trip in approximately 2 hours and 11 minutes.

records.summary_en: In a historical filler item comparing early colonial cities, The Ely Miner notes that Santo Domingo, capital of the Dominican Republic, was founded in 1496 and represents the oldest settlement of white people in the New World. records.headline: The Washington Daily News reports that after Señora de Trujillo
records.summary_en: The Washington Daily News reports that after Señora de Trujillo and their infant daughter sailed on a passenger liner, General Rafael Trujillo was unable to secure passage for himself and his entourage, prompting him to prepare his yacht Ramfis for an Atlantic crossing. On September 4, Trujillo sailed from Lisbon carrying a capacity load of guests, including several American refugees who joined him after a brief delay. The columnist remarks that although the Dominican Republic remains neutral, Trujillo's gesture of transporting American refugees counters rumors of pro-Nazi sympathies. The yacht is expected to take 10 or 12 days to reach New York, where Trujillo is said to be planning another tour of the country that will include Washington.
records.summary_es: The Washington Daily News informa que, después de que la señora de Trujillo y su pequeña hija zarparan en un barco de pasajeros, el general Rafael Trujillo no pudo conseguir pasaje para él ni para su comitiva, lo que lo llevó a preparar su yate Ramfis para cruzar el Atlántico. El 4 de septiembre, Trujillo zarpó desde Lisboa con el yate a su máxima capacidad de pasajeros, incluidos varios refugiados estadounidenses que se unieron a él tras una breve espera. La columnista observa que, aunque la República Dominicana permanece neutral, el gesto de Trujillo de transportar refugiados estadounidenses desmiente los rumores sobre simpatías pronazis. Se calcula que el yate tardará entre 10 o 12 días en llegar a Nueva York, donde según se informa Trujillo planea realizar otra gira por el país que incluirá a Washington.

records.headline: Mr. and Mrs. Robert McClintock are staying briefly at the Mayflower Hotel
records.summary_en: Mr. and Mrs. Robert McClintock are staying briefly at the Mayflower Hotel in Washington before departing for New York, the Evening Star reports under the headline "McClintocks Here for Few Days." Mr. McClintock, who recently returned to the United States from Trujillo in the Dominican Republic where he was assigned as third secretary and vice consul, will sail for Finland to take up duties at the legation in Helsingfors. Due to wartime conditions abroad, Mrs. McClintock will not accompany him to Europe and will temporarily divide her time between New York and Washington.

El señor McClintock, quien regresó recientemente a los Estados Unidos desde Trujillo, en la República Dominicana, donde estuvo asignado como tercer secretario y vicecónsul, zarpará hacia Finlandia para asumir funciones en la legación en Helsingfors. Debido a las condiciones bélicas en el extranjero, su esposa no lo acompañará a Europa y dividirá temporalmente su tiempo entre Nueva York y Washington.

records.headline: Former Dominican President Gen. Rafael Trujillo arrived in Washington accompanied
records.summary_en: Former Dominican President Gen. Rafael Trujillo arrived in Washington accompanied by the Dominican Minister to the United States, Andres Pastoriza, who met him in New York upon his return from Europe. His wife, Senora de Trujillo, had been staying with Senora de Pastoriza at the Dominican Legation in Washington awaiting his arrival. On Sunday, she hosted Senora de Pastoriza and members of the legation staff and their wives aboard the general's yacht anchored in the Potomac for an afternoon cruise and tea.

Su esposa, la señora de Trujillo, había permanecido como huésped de la señora de Pastoriza en la legación dominicana en Washington a la espera de su llegada. El domingo, la señora de Trujillo ofreció una recepción a la señora de Pastoriza y a los miembros del personal de la legación y sus esposas a bordo del yate del general, anclado en el Potomac, para un breve paseo y té sobre cubierta.

records.headline: A Washington columnist reflects on Gen. Rafael Trujillo's development
records.summary_en: A Washington columnist reflects on Gen. Rafael Trujillo's development programs, including harbor dredging and proposing Samana Bay as an American submarine base, which have brought the Dominican Republic international attention. The writer highlights a recent inquiry in the British House of Commons regarding reports that Dominican vessels were refueling German U-boats in the Caribbean. Although the report has been officially denied, the rumor has caused discomfort while Trujillo undergoes medical attention at the Mayo Clinic ahead of a planned visit to Washington and casts doubt over the planned 1942 Columbus Memorial celebration in Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: Un columnista de Washington reflexiona sobre los programas de desarrollo del general Rafael Trujillo, que incluyen el dragado de puertos y la propuesta de la bahía de Samaná como base de submarinos estadounidenses, lo que ha dado relevancia internacional a la República Dominicana. El autor destaca una reciente interpelación en la Cámara de los Comunes británica sobre informes de que embarcaciones dominicanas estaban abasteciendo de combustible a submarinos alemanes en el Caribe. Aunque la noticia ha sido desmentida formalmente, el rumor ha causado inquietud mientras Trujillo recibe atención médica en la clínica Mayo antes de su prevista visita a Washington y arroja dudas sobre la proyectada conmemoración del Faro a Colón de 1942 en Santo Domingo.

records.summary_en: The column reports that original plans for the 1942 celebration commemorating Columbus have fallen through. The elaborate program had envisioned a massed assembly of warships from the world's major naval powers in Samana Bay, with commanders-in-chief bringing their flagships into the new harbor at Trujillo City, and Italian leader Benito Mussolini having promised to attend. The author concludes that even if Dominican vessels were entirely innocent of wartime refueling allegations, overcoming the resulting suspicion remains difficult.

El articulista concluye que, aun si los barcos dominicanos fuesen completamente inocentes de las acusaciones de abastecimiento en tiempos de guerra, resulta difícil disipar la sospecha creada.

records.headline: Officials of the Dominican Legation announced that Gen. Rafael L. Trujillo
records.summary_en: Officials of the Dominican Legation announced that Gen. Rafael L. Trujillo has virtually completed arrangements to construct a horse race track in the Dominican Republic, with an American expert slated to supervise the work once final details are settled. Trujillo returned to Washington from Louisville, Kentucky, and was scheduled to confer with Secretary of State Cordell Hull before departing by train for Miami. From Florida, he will board his yacht to sail home after spending several months traveling in the United States and Europe.

records.headline: Yes, the race track will be built with Dominican money
records.summary_en: In an interview, General Trujillo said the race track would be built with Dominican money and run by the government, that he had not bought any horses in the United States, and that he hoped an island breed might work out as race horses and private owners would bring their strings to his track. records.full_text:
Trujillo Departs, Promising Great Things for Republic

By EVELYN PEYTON GORDON

Well, our dictator visitor, Gen. Rafael Trujillo, who has been touring in this country, off and on, since early July, slipped away rather quietly yesterday. Bound for Miami, the general will board his yacht there and cruise to Havana, pick up his wife and family, and thence go to Trujillo City, where, no doubt, a riotous and joyous welcome awaits him.

As you know, the general had never ventured from his native island before. But once away, he didn't miss a thing.

Yesterday, before attending a huge luncheon at the Carlton, Trujillo held a press conference and got a lot of things off his chest.

Most interesting to Washington is the announcement that the Dominican Legation will soon have a residence all its own. Senor and Senora de Pastoriza have been living in a big apartment, but the general decided at first sight he wanted something better for his envoy. So-o-o—within the next few months building will start on Massachusetts-av, where an advantageous property has been purchased. It's not far from the new Venezuelan Embassy, right in the heart of "embassy row."

PLANS RACING PLANT

Next the general announced that during his recent trip to Kentucky, where he visited at the governor's mansion with Mrs. "Happy" Chandler, wife of Kentucky's new senator, and a gay house party, his idea to build a race track in Trujillo City ripened. He attended races at Lexington, looked over hundreds of fine horses, and the outcome will be a course and Jockey Club which, he says, will rival the finest in the Caribbean countries.

The general looks very well since his sojourn at the Mayo Clinic. Yesterday he wore a light brown suit, natty striped shirt of beige and brown, and a foulard tie to match. He's rather shy with the press, but with the aid of an interpreter, he answered all questions. Yes, the race track will be built with Dominican money and will be run by the government—like most things in that country. No, he didn't buy any horses here. He has a breed on the island which he hopes may work out as race horses, and he hopes that private owners will bring their strings to his track.

NEW HOTEL, TOO

There's going to be a new and modern hotel at Trujillo City, and since the harbor has been dredged from 14 feet to 35, cruise ships will now include Trujillo City as a port of call on Caribbean trips.

When the tourist trade down there begins to boom, I can personally tell you it's a fine place for a vacation.

The general further elaborated on his refugee plans which were outlined last year. Refugees will not have to pay $500, a sum established by the Dominican law of immigration. Because they will not be immigrants. They will be considered as refugees working on colonization plans. In accordance with plans which are being worked out by the Committee for Refugees in New York, 500 families will be admitted to the Dominican Republic.

And for two years the general will be personally responsible for their upkeep and education. After that they should have a good start and be able to support themselves.

CONCERNING WAR RUMORS

And, finally, the general got around to answering all those rumors about Dominican ships aiding and refueling German submarines. And, because I recently picked on the Dominican government about that same thing, I'll quote the general: "I consider that the statements made in this regard by Secretary of State Hull, as well as the categoric reports made by the French Legation and Santo Domingo and the British Admiralty, are ample denials of the charge. Furthermore, they all expressed their complete satisfaction with the manner in which the Dominican government maintains its neutrality.

"Our government was the first to request the co-operation of the United States for the patrol of the surrounding seas."

records.headline: The Dominican Republic has become the first nation to open its borders
records.summary_en: The Dominican Republic has become the first nation to open its borders to the colonization of European refugees under intergovernmental auspices. Former President Rafael L. Trujillo, commander-in-chief of the Dominican Army, announced in Washington that five hundred families would be admitted immediately, with the Dominican government waiving its standard head tax. Trujillo affirmed that the refugees would be welcomed under colonization plans with humanitarian goodwill, pledging personal responsibility for two years for the upkeep and education of unmarried young men and women among the settlers, who will be selected from sixty thousand refugees currently sheltered in the Netherlands, Switzerland, Belgium, and Scandinavia.

La tripulación informó de que esperaba navegar con sus propios medios hacia el puerto haitiano más cercano a lo largo de la costa.

records.headline: Priateness of endorsing home-grown dictators while condemning the European variety
records.summary_en: The *Gazette* contrasted the lavish military honors previously accorded to Latin American dictators like Trujillo with the restrained, informal reception given to visiting Haitian President Sténio Vincent in Washington. Despite Vincent being the sitting president of a nation of 2.6 million, he received no 21-gun salute, fanfare, or military parade, meeting only Undersecretary of State Sumner Welles and a small delegation at the station. Critics questioned the appropriateness of celebrating authoritarian figures while giving a chilly welcome to the head of a neighboring constitutional republic.

A pesar de que Vincent ejercía la presidencia en funciones de un país de 2,6 millones de habitantes, no se le rindieron salvas de 21 cañonazos, fanfarrias ni desfiles de tropas, siendo recibido en la estación ferroviaria únicamente por el subsecretario de Estado Sumner Welles y una reducida comitiva. Quienes criticaron la actitud oficial cuestionaron la idoneidad de exaltar a mandatarios autócratas mientras se brindaba una fría acogida al gobernante de una vecina república constitucional.

records.summary_en: Explorer and author Capt. John D. Craig exhibited underwater motion picture footage of sunken seventeenth-century Spanish galleons during a lecture before the National Geographic Society. According to historical records cited by Craig, sixteen vessels sank in a hurricane in 1642 off Silver Shoals, yielding millions of dollars in recovered treasure to Sir William Phipps in 1686. Craig revealed that former Dominican President Gen. Rafael Trujillo offered the assistance of his government to help salvage the remaining treasure upon learning of the discovery, though Craig noted the gold and silver remain embedded under coral and sand awaiting improved electrical detection equipment.

records.full_text:
Dominicans to Admit
100,000 Refugees

By the Associated Press.

CIUDAD TRUJILLO, Jan. 31.—A contract signed here between the Dominican government and the Dominican Republic Settlement Association provides for the immediate admission of some 500 European political refugee families and aims at the establishment of 100,000 refugees over a period of years.

Most of the first group are German Jewish refugees, but the contract does not specify nationalities.

The settlement association will pay for establishing them and is to be reimbursed by income from their lands once they have regained their financial feet.

records.headline: A settlement contract signed in the presence of James N. Rosenberg
records.summary_en: A settlement contract signed in the presence of James N. Rosenberg, president of the Dominican Republic Settlement Association, establishes terms for Jewish and non-Jewish refugees to colonize land near Sosua. The agreement waives entry fees, permits duty-free importation of tools and equipment, and guarantees full Dominican citizenship to the newcomers. While project organizers envision providing haven for up to one hundred thousand refugees, economic experts suggest the country can comfortably accommodate twenty-five thousand. The dispatch also surveys the republic's agricultural exports, mineral potential, and population of 1,500,000, tracing Rafael Trujillo's rise to dictatorial rule, his title of Benefactor, and the conclusion of his second presidential term in 1938.
records.summary_es: Un contrato de colonización firmado en presencia de James N. Rosenberg, presidente de la Dominican Republic Settlement Association, establece los términos para que refugiados judíos y no judíos colonicen tierras cercanas a Sosúa. El acuerdo exonera las tarifas de entrada, permite la importación libre de aranceles de herramientas y maquinaria y garantiza la plena ciudadanía dominicana a los recién llegados. Aunque los organizadores del proyecto prevén ofrecer refugio a un máximo de cien mil personas, expertos en economía calculan que el país puede acoger cómodamente a veinticinco mil. El despacho reseña además las exportaciones agrícolas de la república, su potencial minero y su población de 1.500.000 habitantes, repasando el ascenso de Rafael Trujillo al poder dictatorial, su título de Benefactor y la conclusión de su segundo mandato presidencial en 1938.

records.headline: Welles to the Dominican Republic as his special representative to prepare
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* recounted the diplomatic career of Undersecretary of State Sumner Welles, noting his mission under President Harding to arrange the withdrawal of U.S. Marines from the Dominican Republic. Welles also returned to Santo Domingo alongside Charles G. Dawes to examine Dominican national finances. These Caribbean experiences helped Welles formulate the non-interventionist diplomatic approach later known as the "Good Neighbor" policy.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* rememoró la trayectoria diplomática del subsecretario de Estado Sumner Welles, recordando la encomienda asumida bajo la presidencia de Harding para organizar la retirada de los marines estadounidenses de la República Dominicana. Welles también volvió a Santo Domingo junto a Charles G. Dawes para examinar las finanzas públicas de la nación caribeña. Aquellas vivencias en las Antillas contribuyeron a que Welles articulara la doctrina diplomática no intervencionista conocida después como la política del «Buen Vecino».

records.headline: A profile in The Frontier contrasts critics comparing Rafael Trujillo
records.summary_en: A profile in The Frontier contrasts critics comparing Rafael Trujillo to Adolf Hitler with his recent signing of a contract admitting five hundred refugee families from Germany and Poland, accompanied by a personal donation of twenty-four thousand acres and projected provision for one hundred thousand additional settlers. The article traces Trujillo's emergence from farm boy and baseball shortstop learning fighting with the United States Marines through the 1924 withdrawal, his rapid military promotion from private to general, and his 1930 overthrow of President Horacio Vasquez. As complete dictator, Trujillo has jailed political rivals, boasted of eliminating crime and unemployment, mandated the slogan "Viva Trujillo!" on automobile license plates, and secured the official title "benefactor of the fatherland."
records.summary_es: Un perfil en The Frontier contrasta a los críticos que comparan a Rafael Trujillo con Adolfo Hitler con su reciente firma de un contrato que admite a quinientas familias de refugiados de Alemania y Polonia, acompañada de una donación personal de veinticuatro mil acres y la previsión para cien mil colonos adicionales. El artículo reseña los orígenes de Trujillo como muchacho de campo y campocorto de béisbol que aprendió combate con la Infantería de Marina estadounidense hasta el retiro de 1924, su rápido ascenso militar de soldado raso a general y el derrocamiento en 1930 del presidente Horacio Vásquez. Como dictador absoluto, Trujillo encarceló a sus rivales políticos, se jactó de haber erradicado la delincuencia y el desempleo, ordenó el lema "¡Viva Trujillo!" en las placas de los automóviles y aseguró el título oficial de "benefactor de la patria".

records.headline: A syndicated feature in the Coulee City Dispatch examines Rafael Trujillo's paradox
records.summary_en: A syndicated feature in the Coulee City Dispatch examines Rafael Trujillo's paradox as an authoritarian ruler who nonetheless signed an accord admitting five hundred exiled families from Germany and Poland, donated twenty-four thousand acres of land, and opened the door to one hundred thousand future settlers with full citizenship. The account recounts how Trujillo acquired military and baseball skills under United States Marines before the occupation concluded in 1924, rose through the ranks from private to general, and seized the government in 1930 by displacing President Horacio Vasquez. Governing as an absolute ruler who imprisoned the political opposition, Trujillo boasts that Santo Domingo has eliminated crime and unemployment, while enforcing public adulation through "Viva Trujillo!" license plate slogans and his formal title as benefactor of the fatherland.
records.summary_es: Una crónica sindicada en el Coulee City Dispatch examina la paradoja de Rafael Trujillo como gobernante autoritario que, no obstante, suscribió un acuerdo para admitir a quinientas familias exiliadas de Alemania y Polonia, donó veinticuatro mil acres de tierra y abrió la puerta a cien mil futuros colonos con plena ciudadanía. El relato cuenta cómo Trujillo adquirió destrezas militares y deportivas bajo la Infantería de Marina estadounidense antes de concluir la ocupación en 1924, ascendió en el escalafón desde soldado raso hasta general y tomó el gobierno en 1930 al desplazar al presidente Horacio Vásquez. Gobernando como mandatario absoluto que encarceló a la oposición política, Trujillo se jacta de que Santo Domingo carece de delincuencia y desempleo, al tiempo que impone la adulación pública mediante el lema "¡Viva Trujillo!" en las placas de vehículos y su designación formal como benefactor de la patria.

records.headline: An editorial in the Springfield Weekly Republican reviews the refugee
records.summary_en: An editorial in the Springfield Weekly Republican reviews the refugee colonization plan as a preliminary report of progress, noting that although negotiators have agreed on terms and Gen. Rafael Trujillo has pledged a twenty-five-thousand-acre tract, neither the Dominican Congress nor the settlement association has formally ratified the pact. James N. Rosenberg recalled that during the thirty-two-nation Evian conference, Trujillo extended the sole practical offer of haven, prompting the newspaper to observe that difficulties deterring thirty-one other countries might also affect the Dominican Republic. Under the pending terms, the settlement association would enjoy complete tax exemption provided it avoids commercial or competitive enterprises, reflecting Dominican efforts to alleviate Europe's wartime displacement crisis.
records.summary_es: Un editorial en el Springfield Weekly Republican analiza el plan de colonización de refugiados como un informe preliminar de avance, señalando que, aunque los negociadores han acordado los términos y el general Rafael Trujillo prometió una extensión de veinticinco mil acres, ni el Congreso dominicano ni la asociación de asentamiento han ratificado formalmente el pacto. James N. Rosenberg recordó que durante la conferencia de Evian, integrada por treinta y dos naciones, Trujillo presentó la única oferta práctica de asilo, lo que lleva al periódico a reflexionar que las dificultades que disuadieron a otros treinta y un países podrían también repercutir en la República Dominicana. Bajo los términos pendientes, la asociación de colonización gozaría de total exención tributaria con la condición de evitar empresas comerciales o competitivas, reflejando el interés dominicano por aliviar la crisis provocada por la guerra en Europa.

records.headline: A parenthetical editorial note reports that through the end of January
records.summary_en: A parenthetical editorial note reports that through the end of January, the extensive U.S. air patrol operating for months in the Caribbean failed to spot a single submarine. This coincided with a period of frequent rumors, including a report that submarines were being refueled out of Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic. However, no factual basis for the claim was ever found.

Esto coincidió con un período de frecuentes rumores, incluido un informe de que los submarinos se estaban reabasteciendo desde Ciudad Trujillo, República Dominicana. Sin embargo, nunca se encontró ninguna base fáctica para dicha afirmación.

records.headline: The column characterizes newly appointed United States Ambassador
records.summary_en: The column characterizes newly appointed United States Ambassador to Peru Henry Norweb as a "building envoy." records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo dated March 8
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo dated March 8 reports that the Dominican Republic began a nine-day period of national mourning for President Jacinto B. Peynado, who died last night at age 62 following a leg amputation that failed to halt an infection. He is to be buried with military honors in the National Cathedral. The article outlines Dr. Peynado's political career under late President Ramon Baez and General Rafael L. Trujillo, noting his succession to the presidency in 1938 with nearly 92 per cent of the vote, and reports that Vice President Manuel de J. Troncoso de la Concha becomes President.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Associated Press desde Ciudad Trujillo fechado el 8 de marzo informa que la República Dominicana inició un período de nueve días de duelo nacional por el presidente Jacinto B. Peynado, quien falleció anoche a los 62 años tras una amputación de pierna que no logró frenar una infección. Será sepultado con honores militares en la Catedral Nacional. El artículo reseña la carrera política del Dr. Peynado bajo el mandato del difunto presidente Ramón Báez y del general Rafael L. Trujillo, destacando su ascenso a la presidencia en 1938 con casi el 92 por ciento de los votos, e informa que el vicepresidente Manuel de J. Troncoso de la Concha asume la presidencia.

records.headline: Thirty-seven survivors of the 5,600-ton German steamer Hannover arrived
records.summary_en: Thirty-seven survivors of the 5,600-ton German steamer Hannover arrived there after the vessel was scuttled and burned upon approach by a British cruiser in the American neutrality zone, a United Press dispatch from Trujillo, Dominican Republic, dated March 11 reports. The fate of 67 other crewmen and the captain remained uncertain. The ship, which had sailed from Willemstad, Netherlands West Indies, carrying ore and other supplies to run the blockade, was set on fire, had its sea cocks opened, and was abandoned in the 75-mile-wide Mona Channel.

La suerte de otros 67 tripulantes y del capitán permanecía incierta. El barco, que había zarpado de Willemstad, Antillas Neerlandesas, con un cargamento de mineral y otros pertrechos para burlar el bloqueo, fue incendiado, se le abrieron las válvulas de fondo y fue abandonado en el canal de la Mona, de 75 millas de ancho.

records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo dated March 11 reports that thirty-seven seamen from the scuttled German freighter Hannover arrived there after traveling in small boats to the Dominican coast. The 5,600-ton freighter was fired by its crew after being overtaken by enemy warships Thursday night, and Captain Wahn Schaffe believed 55 other crew members had been captured. One crew member reported that a British destroyer and a French cruiser, probably the Jeanne d’Arc, intercepted the freighter 40 miles offshore between Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic, differing from London's report of a lone British cruiser.

Uno de los marineros relató que un destructor británico y un crucero francés, probablemente el Jeanne d’Arc, interceptaron la embarcación a 40 millas de la costa entre Puerto Rico y la República Dominicana, lo que contrastaba con el informe de Londres que atribuía la interceptación a un solo crucero británico.

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo dated March 10
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo dated March 10 reports that sailors from a German merchant vessel, destroyed after encountering a British cruiser, landed today on the eastern Dominican coast. Although unnamed in the local dispatch, the British Admiralty in London identified the vessel as the 5,600-ton German steamer Hannover, intercepted last Thursday night between the Dominican Republic and Puerto Rico, and set on fire and abandoned by its crew. Authorities were also investigating reports that a second, unnamed German ship was seized by a British cruiser off Cape Engano on the eastern coast.

Aunque el barco no fue identificado en el despacho local, el Almirantazgo británico en Londres informó que se trataba del vapor alemán Hannover, de 5,600 toneladas, interceptado el jueves por la noche entre la República Dominicana y Puerto Rico, e incendiado y abandonado por su tripulación. Las autoridades investigaban asimismo informes sobre la captura de un segundo barco alemán, tampoco identificado, por parte de un crucero británico frente a cabo Engaño, en la costa oriental.

records.headline: The article profiles New York bankruptcy attorney John N. Rosenberg
records.summary_en: The article profiles New York bankruptcy attorney John N. Rosenberg, who serves as president of the Dominican Resettlement Association and is co-partnering with General Trujillo to establish European refugees in an island haven under the Trujillo plan. The initiative is described as an unprecedented undertaking to provide 500 refugees with a new beginning in the Western world, supplied with houses, roads, land, cattle, and farm implements. The profile highlights Rosenberg's long-standing involvement in European famine and war relief since the World War, alongside his varied creative accomplishments as an author, painter, printmaker, and playwright.
records.summary_es: El artículo reseña al abogado neoyorquino especialista en quiebras John N. La iniciativa se presenta como una labor sin precedentes para brindar a 500 refugiados un nuevo comienzo en el hemisferio occidental, dotados de viviendas, caminos, tierras, ganado e implementos agrícolas. El perfil destaca la prolongada participación de Rosenberg en obras de auxilio contra el hambre y la guerra en Europa desde la Guerra Mundial, así como sus polifacéticas realizaciones artísticas como escritor, pintor, grabador y dramaturgo.

Rosenberg, a lawyer specializing in bankruptcy proceedings, has joined General Trujillo of the Dominican Republic in settling European refugees on the island under the Trujillo plan. Acting as head of the Dominican Resettlement Association, Rosenberg is assisting in a distinctive program to establish 500 refugees in the Western Hemisphere with land, livestock, roads, houses, and farming equipment. La crónica señala que, además de gestionar reorganizaciones financieras y auxilios de posguerra internacional, Rosenberg participa activamente en las bellas artes como pintor, escritor y mecenas teatral.

records.summary_en: A music notice reports that during her tour last season, concert singer Madame Evanti was honored in Haiti and subsequently visited the Dominican Republic, where Generalissimo Trujillo presented her with the keys to the capital. Following an appearance at the Club Ateneo in Venezuela, she is scheduled to give a farewell concert in Washington at the Asbury M. E. Church on the evening of May 27 at 8:45 before departing for South America. Her performance will feature Spanish vocal works alongside selections in English and other languages.

E. la noche del 27 de mayo a las 8:45 antes de partir hacia América del Sur. Su repertorio incluirá composiciones vocales en español junto con piezas en inglés y otros idiomas.

records.headline: Under the heading "Acclimated," the report mentions Generalissimo Trujillo's offer
records.summary_en: Under the heading "Acclimated," the report mentions Generalissimo Trujillo's offer to admit 1,000 refugee children and youths to the Dominican Republic, noting that 37 colonists have been settled on the Sosua tract since May 10. Representing the vanguard of an anticipated community of 500 families, the 37 settlers are reported to be thoroughly acclimated, with none having lost weight despite hard labor under unusual climatic conditions. The group includes Danny Herzberg, a stowaway under two years of age, while Mrs. Joseph A. Rosen is scheduled to depart New York on June 27 to join her husband at Sosua.

Representando la vanguardia de una comunidad proyectada de 500 familias, se informa que los 37 colonos se encuentran totalmente aclimatados, sin que ninguno haya perdido peso a pesar de las duras faenas bajo condiciones climáticas poco habituales. El grupo incluye a Danny Herzberg, un polizón menor de dos años de edad, mientras que la señora de Joseph A. Rosen tiene previsto salir de Nueva York el 27 de junio para unirse a su esposo en Sosúa.

records.headline: The column discusses a controversy concerning Jewish refugees
records.summary_en: The column discusses a controversy concerning Jewish refugees establishing an agricultural settlement in the Dominican Republic. The United States Navy has asserted that these refugees are Nazi spies expelled from Germany to operate as fifth columnists. Conversely, the column reports that the settlers were thoroughly screened by the Jewish Refugee Committee as reputable former property owners in Germany, though naval advisers to President Roosevelt could potentially impede the settlement in Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: La columna examina una controversia relativa a los refugiados judíos que están estableciendo un asentamiento agrícola en la República Dominicana. La Armada de los Estados Unidos ha afirmado que estos refugiados son espías nazis expulsados de Alemania para desempeñarse como quintacolumnistas. Por el contrario, la crónica informa que los colonos fueron rigurosamente evaluados por el Comité de Refugiados Judíos como respetables antiguos propietarios en Alemania, si bien los asesores navales del presidente Roosevelt podrían obstaculizar el asentamiento en Santo Domingo.

records.headline: A special "Christopher Columbus" stamp or series of stamps is scheduled
records.summary_en: A special "Christopher Columbus" stamp or series of stamps is scheduled to appear the coming October 12, Columbus Day, to raise funds for the construction of a lighthouse memorial to Columbus at Ciudad Trujillo in the Dominican Republic. Some participating nations reportedly plan to sell the stamps at a price slightly above their postage value, with the surplus allocated to the memorial fund. The United States, Cuba, Haiti, the Dominican Republic, Colombia, Ecuador, El Salvador, Honduras, Guatemala, Bolivia, and Panama have reportedly indicated their willingness to join the program.

Según se informa, algunas naciones participantes planean vender los sellos a un precio ligeramente superior a su valor de franqueo, destinando la diferencia al fondo del faro. Se tiene entendido que Estados Unidos, Cuba, Haití, la República Dominicana, Colombia, Ecuador, El Salvador, Honduras, Guatemala, Bolivia y Panamá han manifestado su disposición de unirse al programa.

records.headline: Twenty-five British sailors from the Davisian were landed today
records.summary_en: Twenty-five British sailors from the Davisian were landed today by the Norwegian freighter Leif, a wire dispatch datelined Samana, Dominican Republic, July 21, reports. The Davisian was one of two British merchant ships sunk the previous week by a German raider operating in the West Indies. The Norwegian freighter rescued the seamen northeast of the island republic in what the dispatch describes as the deepest known waters of the Atlantic Ocean.

El Davisian fue uno de dos buques mercantes británicos hundidos la semana anterior por un atacante corsario alemán que operaba en las Antillas. El carguero noruego rescató a los tripulantes al noreste de esta república antillana en las aguas más profundas conocidas del océano Atlántico.

records.headline: A five-story hotel featuring 120 rooms, most planned with views
records.summary_en: A five-story hotel featuring 120 rooms, most planned with views over the Caribbean, is currently under construction in Trujillo City, Dominican Republic. Situated between Independence and George Washington avenues, the location is described as one of the finest sites in the capital. Aiming to attract American tourist trade, the establishment will offer private baths for each suite, electrical outlets for razors and curlers, a large swimming pool, a sun deck, and a gymnasium.

Ubicado entre las avenidas Independencia y George Washington, el emplazamiento se describe como uno de los mejores de la ciudad. Con el propósito de atraer al turismo estadounidense, el establecimiento contará con baño privado en cada suite, tomas eléctricas para afeitadoras y rizadores, una amplia piscina, terraza para tomar sol y un gimnasio.

records.headline: A published dispatch charges that the German Third Reich has employed
records.summary_en: A published dispatch charges that the German Third Reich has employed European subversive tactics against the sovereignty and liberty of the Western Hemisphere, centering its conspiracy and Adolf Hitler's regional plans in the Dominican Republic. According to the report, the Dominican Republic lies within the defense perimeter being developed by the United States to protect the Panama Canal, extending from Guantanamo, Cuba, to Bermuda with Puerto Rico at its center. The dispatch asserts that a German fifth column has operated in the Dominican Republic for more than four years through the Dominican-German Scientific Institute, founded in 1937 under the cover of scientific study. While ostensibly established to investigate tropical conditions, the dispatch claims that Santo Domingo is subtropical and that German researchers have focused primarily on identifying potential military bases.
records.summary_es: Un despacho publicado denuncia que el Tercer Reich alemán ha empleado tácticas subversivas europeas contra la soberanía y la libertad del hemisferio occidental, concentrando su conspiración y los planes regionales de Adolf Hitler en la República Dominicana. Según el informe, la República Dominicana se encuentra dentro de la línea de defensa desarrollada por Estados Unidos para proteger el canal de Panamá, la cual se extiende desde Guantánamo, Cuba, hasta las Bermudas, teniendo como centro a Puerto Rico. El despacho afirma que una quinta columna alemana ha operado en la República Dominicana durante más de cuatro años a través del Instituto Científico Dominico-Alemán, fundado en 1937 bajo apariencia de investigación científica. Aunque ostensiblemente se estableció para examinar condiciones tropicales, el texto sostiene que Santo Domingo es un país subtropical y que los investigadores alemanes se han concentrado principalmente en posibles bases militares.

Badillo's dispatch stated that a German fifth column had been active in the republic for more than four years, operating primarily through the Dominican-German Scientific Institute founded in 1937 under the pretext of scientific research. Although officially established to study tropical conditions, the dispatch noted that Santo Domingo is a subtropical country and contended that scientific investigations had centered largely on potential military sites.

records.headline: Dominican Republic Boss Bans Discussion of War
records.summary_en: NEA correspondent Thomas J. B. Wenner reports from Ciudad Trujillo that members of the Dominican Republic's only legal political party have been ordered not to discuss the European war, a decree of Generalissimo Rafael Leonidas Trujillo Molina, the country's virtual dictator. Party director Paino Pichardo explained that Trujillo, an ardent advocate of Pan-Americanism and a friend of the United States, does not wish his work to be made more difficult by sentiments at variance with the country's declared policy, and insisted the agreement applies to party members, not to the population at large. The article profiles Trujillo, 49, president since 1930, whose name the capital bears, and describes the armed forces he has modernized: a standing army of about 4,000 men, a navy of one military transport and several coast guard vessels, and an air force of about 25 planes.
records.summary_es: El corresponsal de NEA Thomas J. B. Wenner informa desde Ciudad Trujillo que a los miembros del único partido político legal de la República Dominicana se les ha ordenado no hablar de la guerra europea, por decreto del generalísimo Rafael Leónidas Trujillo Molina, dictador virtual del país. El director del partido, Paino Pichardo, explicó que Trujillo, ardiente defensor del panamericanismo y amigo de los Estados Unidos, no desea que su labor se vea dificultada por sentimientos contrarios a la política declarada del país, e insistió en que el acuerdo se aplica a los miembros del partido, no a toda la población. El artículo perfila a Trujillo, de 49 años, presidente desde 1930, cuyo nombre lleva la capital, y describe las fuerzas armadas que ha modernizado: un ejército permanente de unos 4.000 hombres, una marina de un transporte militar y varias naves guardacostas, y una fuerza aérea de unos 25 aviones.
