Bernardino asistió junto a la escritora boliviana Carmen B. de Lozada y otras corresponsales latinoamericanas pertenecientes a la Comisión Interamericana de Mujeres. La reunión fue presidida por la señora McLean junto a las presidentas de los clubes, Alice Eversman del Evening Star y Christine Sadler del Washington Post.

records.summary_en: An illustrated profile described the Dominican Republic as about the size of Vermont and New Hampshire combined, occupying about two-thirds of the island of Santo Domingo, with 1,654,000 people governed by President General Rafael Trujillo, a Senate and a Chamber of Deputies. It noted that Columbus is said to be buried in the cathedral, showed the old walls at the entrance to the modern capital, Ciudad Trujillo, and cited 1,000 miles of modern highways. Coffee was described as a source of income for thousands of small farmers and as helping to supply United States needs, with sugar, cocoa and tobacco listed as other exports.

Señalaba que, según se dice, Colón está enterrado en la catedral, mostraba las antiguas murallas a la entrada de la capital moderna, Ciudad Trujillo, y mencionaba 1.000 millas de carreteras modernas. El café era descrito como fuente de ingresos para miles de pequeños agricultores y como un producto que ayuda a abastecer las necesidades de los Estados Unidos, con el azúcar, el cacao y el tabaco como otras exportaciones.

records.summary_en: The *Wilmington Morning Star* described the geography and population of the Dominican Republic, noting its varied climate ranging from jungles and 10,000-foot peaks to Lake Enriquillo, located 150 feet below sea level. The article reported that the nation's population of roughly 1.75 million was primarily concentrated in northern valleys and around the southern capital of Trujillo City.

La publicación indicó que el millón setecientos cincuenta mil habitantes con que contaba el país se concentraba principalmente en los fértiles valles del Cibao y en el entorno meridional de Ciudad Trujillo.

Haiti also exports an unusual variety of commercial crops. Of these, coffee is well in the lead, followed, normally, by bananas, sisal, cotton, sugar, and cacao. Although the war has brought its usual quota of shipping and trade problems. Haitian economy has been stabilized by recent shipments of coffee and sugar; by cotton crop agreements with the United States, and other financial and trade assistance from the big continental neighbor. Particularly welcome have been orders from the U. S. War Department for Haitian coffee. Haitian sisal, too. is proving a valuable fiber to take the place of some of this lost raw material of the Orient, while rubber planting there also is expected to help meet war needs. A significant indication of increased interest in the United States is seen in a recent decree making English a required subject in Haitian schools. In an area about half the size of Virginia, the Dominican Republic presents samples of some of the world's most varied climate and scenery—from humid jungle to cactus-dotted desert, from ten thousand-foot mountain heights to the Lake de Enriquillo, 150 feet below sea level and saltier than sea water. Most of the Dominicans, who number roughly a million and three-quarters, are concentrated either in the lowlands and valleys of the north, or around the capital, Trujillo City, in the south. records.summary_en: The *Daily Monitor Leader* reported that President Roosevelt nominated incumbent ministers across the Caribbean and Central America to become ambassadors, including Avra M. Warren in the Dominican Republic and John Campbell White in Haiti. Under the White House plan, the elevated envoys would continue receiving their ministerial salaries of $10,000 instead of the usual $17,500 ambassadorial pay. Other diplomats nominated for ambassadorial rank included Boaz Long, Robert M. Scotten, and James B. Stewart.

The White House announced that the elevated envoys would retain their $10,000 ministerial salaries rather than receive standard ambassadorial compensation.

Belisario Porras, Jr., May Be Envoy Here

PANAMA, March 31. — Usually reliable sources reported today that Belisario Porras, jr., Panama's present Minister to Cuba, would be named Ambassador to Washington to succeed Ernesto Jaen Guardia, who resigned yesterday because of ill health.

He is a son of the late Dr. Belisario Porras, sr., who served three terms as President of the republic and was affectionately known as "the grand old man of Panamanian politics."

The younger Porras previously had been minister to Portugal, Spain, Ecuador and the Dominican Republic.

records.headline: S. decided, with the five republics of Central America, Haiti, and the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: The *Washington Daily News* reported on the diplomatic elevation of missions between the United States and seven Caribbean and Central American nations, including the Dominican Republic and Haiti, from legations to full embassies. Under reciprocal agreements, the respective ministers were elevated to ambassadors, leaving Canada as the only Western Hemisphere mission remaining at ministerial rank. Latin American diplomats gathered in Washington to celebrate the confirmations and exchange congratulations.

Conforme a convenios de reciprocidad, los respectivos ministros pasaron a ser embajadores extraordinarios, quedando Canadá como la única sede diplomática continental que conservaba rango de legación. Los dignatarios hispanoamericanos se congregaron en Washington para festejar las acreditaciones e intercambiar salutaciones de estilo.

records.full_text:
Minister Bids Minister to Party, but They Are Ambassadors on Meeting

By EVELYN PEYTON GORDON

The invitations were issued from "the Minister of Nicaragua and Mme. De Bayle in honor of the U. S. Minister to Nicaragua James B. Stewart." But by the time the guests arrived the legation had changed to an embassy and the Ministers were bona fide Ambassadors!

What a world in which we live! It all came about because the U. S. decided, with the five republics of Central America, Haiti, and the Dominican Republic, to exchange ambassadors instead of ministers. Soooo—the works went thru yesterday. James B. Stewart, one of the men longest in our own foreign service, was confirmed by the Senate. When he leaves shortly for Managua he will be the first ambassador in history to go from Washington to that capital.

And by reciprocal action youthful Leon De Bayle will soon present his credentials to the President as the first Nicaraguan Ambassador. The other day I remarked that a "H'ya, Mr. Ambassador" is a safer greeting these days than any lesser salutation. It's about true.

ONLY ONE MINISTER NOW

On this whole vast Western Hemisphere there remains only one diplomatic chief of mission who is of ministerial rank—Leighton McCarthy, the Canadian Minister. The representative of a dominion larger than the United States, with a population of 13,000,000 people, hasn't yet been elevated to top rank. He's outranked by 20 envoys from this side of the world!

Well, anyhow, all the envoys of the Latin American republics were on hand yesterday to congratulate their popular host and to receive good wishes themselves.

"No, I'm still just Maria Recinos to my friends," laughed pretty Senora de Recinos, wife of the Guatemalan Min—, no, Ambassador, when I greeted her as "Madame l'Ambassadrice."

The De Bayles have recently moved into the George Garrett house on New Hampshire-av, and a very excellent spot it is for an embassy. The house was decorated with huge sprays of fruit blossoms, and with pretty, little Mme. De Bayle, who has been named one of the best-dressed women in the Capital. She wore a floor-length frock of pale gray embroidered with white braid and fashioned with a short, long-sleeved jacket.

On the wall of the dining room hung a new portrait of the hostess—a beautiful painting done by a young American artist, George Quintas—picturing the lady in a bouffant gown of white net, holding in her hand a spray of the deep purple orchids she wears so frequently.

The De Bayles had what I consider a perfect wartime buffet. There were plenty of tiny hot finger rolls filled with sliced turkey. There were platters of hot fried shrimps with bowls of spicy tartar sauce. There were salted nuts and two big cakes. And then there was a bar. No frills and no folderol.

Hundreds of guests came to welcome Mr. Stewart and to congratulate the host. Our own Ambassador to Nicaragua, who was born in Philadelphia in 1882, started his career in 1915 when he went to Pernambuco, Brazil, as vice consul. Thence he went to Chihuahua, Mexico, and to Tampico, Mexico. He knows South and Central Americas well.

His tours of duty in Europe have been brief, but effective. He was Consul General in Budapest in 1933, and later was "exchanged" to the foreign service to become counselor of our legation there. Back to Mexico he went, and then to Zurich, Switzerland, from which place he was sent to Nicaragua last March, 1942.

James B. Stewart is sandy and ruddy in coloring. He's genial and well liked. His colleagues call him "a helluva good fellow," which means a lot in any business or profession. He's older than Leon De Bayle, who was first known to Washington, when he came here in 1937, as "Dr. Henri De Bayle's baby brother."

LONG REPRESENTED HERE

The De Bayle "tribe" has been representing Nicaragua in Washington for a good many years. First came "big brother" Luis, as charge d'affaires, in 1932. In 1933, with the Roosevelt dynasty, came brother Henri, and then young Leon.

A De Bayle without an M. D. after his name is almost a rarity. Leon De Bayle is a doctor. But a doctor of political science and economics rather than of medicine, which almost makes him an apostate. His father was a physician and both older brothers, but Leon's tastes ran to government and finance rather than anatomy and the cardio-vascular system.

I looked around the crowded embassy yesterday and saw all the distinguished representatives from south of the border. All of them were smiling. Hemispheric unity seems to be waiting only the decisions of Argentina. When he first came to Washington, Leon De Bayle thought no world war was in the offing. Yet even in those days he believed in a more closely knit America—North, South, and Central.

Yesterday, with a world war raging, the young envoy was happy that knitting had been so well achieved. It was a great day for the De Bayle family.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Flor de Oro Trujillo, daughter of Dominican President Rafael Trujillo, arrived en route to Washington to assume duties as first secretary of the Dominican Embassy. Miss Trujillo, whose husband Captain Maurice Berck died in an accident four months prior, expressed her desire to study international law, pursue diplomacy, and observe American women's customs to introduce them to her home country. She noted that she was fluent in Portuguese, German, French, and English in addition to Spanish.

La señorita Trujillo, cuyo cónyuge, el capitán Maurice Berck, pereciera en un infortunio cuatro meses antes, exteriorizó su inclinación hacia el estudio del derecho internacional, el ejercicio diplomático y el conocimiento de las costumbres cívicas de la mujer estadounidense para aplicarlas en su tierra natal. Añadió que dominaba a la perfección el portugués, alemán, francés e inglés, además de su castellano natal.

Miss Trujillo, daughter of the President of the Dominican Republic, arrived yesterday en route to Washington, where she will assume her post as first secretary to the Dominican Embassy. "This is a big chance my father has given me." the attractive brunette declared, "and I am going to study hard so that I will not disappoint him." The young diplomat has spent the last two years, until the past month, in the United States, as the wife of Capt. Maurice Berck. Capt. Berck. she said, was killed in an accident In Washington four months ago. Miss Trujillo, who was educated abroad, said she plans to pursue a diplomatic career and will study international law. She already speaks four languages in addition to Spanish—Portuguese, German, French and English. She was to leave today by plane for New York, where she will spend a week before assuming her post. records.headline: In an interview accompanied by a staff photo, Señora Flor de Oro Trujillo
records.summary_en: In an interview accompanied by a staff photo, Señora Flor de Oro Trujillo describes expanding opportunities for women in the Dominican Republic following her appointment to the embassy in Washington. She recalls that Dominican women secured the vote in January 1942 and voted in their first election the following May, resulting in one woman senator and two women representatives entering the legislature. Beyond teaching, 150 women have entered professional careers in medicine, law, dentistry, and engineering after graduating from the University of Santo Domingo. The twenty-six-year-old diplomat, who speaks four languages, praises the nation's constitution and asserts that utilizing women equally with men will greatly benefit a country of less than 2,000,000 people.
records.summary_es: En una entrevista acompañada por una fotografía, la señora Flor de Oro Trujillo describe las crecientes oportunidades para las mujeres en la República Dominicana tras su nombramiento en la embajada en Washington. Recuerda que las mujeres dominicanas lograron el sufragio en enero de 1942 y participaron en sus primeras elecciones en el mes de mayo siguiente, lo que permitió el ingreso de una senadora y dos representantes mujeres al cuerpo legislativo. Más allá del magisterio, 150 mujeres han ingresado a carreras profesionales en medicina, derecho, odontología e ingeniería tras egresar de la Universidad de Santo Domingo. La diplomática, de 26 años de edad y hablante de cuatro idiomas, elogia la constitución nacional y sostiene que emplear a las mujeres a la par de los hombres beneficiará notablemente a un país de menos de 2,000,000 de habitantes.

The report noted her interest in philosophy, jewelry, and writing articles about the Dominican Republic for a New York magazine. Señorita Minerva Bernardino, Dominican delegate and vice chairman of the Inter-American Commission of Women, praised the appointment, highlighting that the Dominican Republic had granted women full civil and political rights.

El reportaje aludía a sus aficiones por la filosofía, el coleccionismo de alhajas y la preparación de artículos descriptivos sobre la República Dominicana para un magacín de Nueva York. La señorita Minerva Bernardino, delegada dominicana y vicepresidenta de la Comisión Interamericana de Mujeres, ensalzó el nombramiento resaltando la vocación artística de Flor de Oro y su versatilidad para expresarse fluidamente en diversas lenguas europeas.

Senora Trujillo's fondness for lovely clothes and jewels is evident, but she has many serious interests. with a study of philosophy probably in the lead, she said. records.summary_en: Dictator Trujillo of the Dominican Republic harbors intense bitterness toward U.S. Undersecretary of State Sumner Welles and bars Welles's name from Dominican newspapers, a syndicated dispatch printed in the Daily Alaska Empire reports. Los discursos de Welles se divulgan en el país, pero su identidad es sistemáticamente suprimida. El informe explica que Welles, en su antiguo cargo de alto comisionado de la República Dominicana, se había opuesto a la revolución de Trujillo para acceder al poder presidencial.

records.headline: A biographical feature in the Evening Star profiles Dominican feminist
records.summary_en: A biographical feature in the Evening Star profiles Dominican feminist leader Minerva Bernardino, who presented the Inter-American Commission of Women's report at the Eighth Pan-American Conference in Lima. In the Dominican Republic, Bernardino served as head of educational statistics, section chief in the agriculture department, and supervisor of vocational schools in the Santo Domingo district, while also holding the presidency of the Committee of Inter-American Cooperation. Now in Washington, she advises prominent international women's organizations and recently joined the American Newspaper Women's Club. She is writing two books, including an account of the Inter-American Commission of Women and a directory of distinguished women across the twenty-one American republics.
records.summary_es: Una semblanza biográfica en el Evening Star presenta a la líder feminista dominicana Minerva Bernardino, quien expuso el informe de la Comisión Interamericana de Mujeres en la Octava Conferencia Panamericana en Lima. En la República Dominicana, Bernardino ocupó cargos como jefa de estadísticas de educación, jefa de sección en el departamento de agricultura y supervisora de escuelas vocacionales en el distrito de Santo Domingo, ejerciendo además la presidencia del Comité de Cooperación Interamericana. Establecida en Washington, asesora a destacadas organizaciones femeninas internacionales y se incorporó recientemente al American Newspaper Women's Club. Actualmente escribe dos libros, entre ellos una reseña sobre la Comisión Interamericana de Mujeres y un directorio de mujeres distinguidas de las 21 repúblicas americanas.

records.headline: A choral group from the three West Potomac Park residence halls
records.summary_en: A choral group from the three West Potomac Park residence halls has produced what is believed to be the first English recording of the Dominican Republic's national anthem. The record is scheduled to be played at the West Potomac Park Community Center before being presented to the Dominican President through Ambassador Dr. J. M. Troncoso. Choral director Ramona Blunt announced that Enrique De Marchena, a Dominican pianist, composer, and director of radio station HIN in Ciudad Trujillo, will perform as guest soloist on the program.

El disco se reproducirá en el Centro Comunitario de West Potomac Park antes de ser presentado al presidente dominicano a través del embajador doctor J. M. Troncoso. La directora del coro, Ramona Blunt, anunció que Enrique De Marchena, pianista y compositor dominicano y director de la emisora HIN en Ciudad Trujillo, participará como solista invitado en el programa.

records.headline: An obituary remembers 62-year-old metalworker Mr. Luskey as an expert
records.summary_en: An obituary remembers 62-year-old metalworker Mr. Luskey as an expert in ornamental forging and leaf work with the Fred S. Gichner Iron Works. In addition to installations for embassies and the Mayflower ballroom, he forged gates for United States legations in Nicaragua, Haiti, and Ciudad Trujillo in the Dominican Republic. He is survived by his widow, five daughters, and seven grandchildren, with funeral services scheduled for Thursday afternoon and burial in Cedar Hill Cemetery.
records.summary_es: Una esquela recuerda al obrero metalúrgico de 62 años, el señor Luskey, como experto en forja ornamental y motivos de hojas en la empresa Fred S. Gichner Iron Works. Además de realizar trabajos para embajadas y el salón de baile del Mayflower, forjó las verjas de las legaciones de Estados Unidos en Nicaragua, Haití y Ciudad Trujillo en la República Dominicana. Le sobreviven su viuda, cinco hijas y siete nietos; los servicios fúnebres están fijados para el jueves por la tarde y el sepelio en el cementerio de Cedar Hill.

records.headline: A commentary on refugee resettlement recalls that at the Evian conference
records.summary_en: A commentary on refugee resettlement recalls that at the Evian conference in 1938, the Dominican Republic offered to accept up to 100,000 European refugees. A Settlement Association organized by American sponsors established subsistence homesteads, placing an initial contingent of approximately 300 at Sosua in the northwestern part of the republic before wartime conditions suspended further immigration. The writer characterizes the colony in Santo Domingo as a failure, pointing to an investigation by the Brookings Institution and arguing that organizations pursuing mass colonization outside Palestine overlook the limited availability of suitable lands.
records.summary_es: Un comentario sobre el reasentamiento de refugiados recuerda que en la conferencia de Evian de 1938, la República Dominicana ofreció admitir hasta 100.000 refugiados europeos. Una Asociación de Asentamiento organizada por promotores estadounidenses estableció granjas de subsistencia, ubicando a un contingente inicial de aproximadamente 300 personas en Sosúa, en el noroeste de la república, antes de que las circunstancias de la guerra suspendieran la inmigración adicional. El autor califica la colonia de Santo Domingo como un fracaso, señalando una investigación del Brookings Institution y argumentando que las organizaciones que buscan la colonización masiva fuera de Palestina pasan por alto la escasa disponibilidad de tierras aptas.

records.headline: Czechoslovak Ambassador Vladimir Hurban departed Washington yesterday
records.summary_en: Czechoslovak Ambassador Vladimir Hurban departed Washington yesterday for Ciudad Trujillo to present his credentials as Czechoslovak Minister to the Dominican Republic, the Evening Star reports under the headline "Hurbans Leave for Few Weeks." He will subsequently visit Port-au-Prince to present credentials as minister to that country and stop in Havana before returning to Washington. While the embassy counselor acts as chargé d'affaires during the ambassador's absence, Mme. Hurban has traveled to New York to visit her mother.
records.summary_es: El embajador checoslovaco Vladimir Hurban partió ayer de Washington hacia Ciudad Trujillo para presentar sus credenciales como ministro checoslovaco ante la República Dominicana, informa el Evening Star bajo el titular «Los Hurban parten por unas semanas». Posteriormente visitará Puerto Príncipe para presentar credenciales como ministro ante ese país y hará escala en La Habana antes de regresar a Washington. Mientras el consejero de la embajada ejerce como encargado de negocios durante la ausencia del embajador, la señora Hurban ha viajado a Nueva York para visitar a su madre.

records.headline: A musical program featuring works from the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: A musical program featuring works from the Dominican Republic will take place this afternoon at 4 o'clock in the Hall of the Americas at the Pan American Union, the Evening Star reports under the headline "Dominican Music Played at Union." Dominican folklorist Jose G. Ramirez Peralta will demonstrate native rhythms on the guiro and tambora, and 17-year-old soprano Anita de Palma will sing popular Dominican songs. American violinist Mary Ann Kullmer, accompanied by pianist Frederick H. Block, will premiere compositions by Luis A. Mena and Enrique de Marchena, followed by Block's solo performance of a selection by Enrique Mejia Arredondo.
records.summary_es: Un programa musical dedicado a obras de la República Dominicana tendrá lugar esta tarde a las 4 en punto en el Salón de las Américas de la Unión Panamericana, informa el Evening Star bajo el titular «Música dominicana interpretada en la Unión». El folclorista dominicano José G. Ramírez Peralta ofrecerá una demostración de ritmos autóctonos con el güiro y la tambora, y la soprano de 17 años Anita de Palma cantará canciones populares dominicanas. La violinista estadounidense Mary Ann Kullmer, acompañada por el pianista Frederick H. Block, estrenará composiciones de Luis A. Mena y Enrique de Marchena, seguido por la interpretación solista de Block de una pieza de Enrique Mejía Arredondo.

records.headline: A profile features Luis Galvan Jr., an American-born candidate
records.summary_en: A profile features Luis Galvan Jr., an American-born candidate for an Army commission whose late father served as Dominican Minister in Washington during the United States Marine occupation of Santo Domingo. The young man explains that his father died in Washington in 1920 and that he chose never to visit Santo Domingo or use a Dominican passport to protect his American citizenship, even while employed at the Dominican Consulate in New York. Having preserved his citizenship, he is now preparing to enter the United States Army alongside his two brothers.

El joven explica que su padre murió en Washington en 1920 y que prefirió no visitar nunca Santo Domingo ni usar un pasaporte dominicano para no comprometer su ciudadanía estadounidense, aun cuando estuvo empleado en el consulado dominicano en Nueva York. Tras haber conservado su ciudadanía, ahora se prepara para ingresar en el ejército de los Estados Unidos junto con sus dos hermanos.

records.headline: The party was given in the Pan-American Union Annex in honor
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Pan-American Union Director General Dr. Leo S. Rowe hosted a luncheon honoring the new Dominican Ambassador, Dr. Anselmo Copello, following his formal reception by President Roosevelt. Copello succeeded Dr. Jesús María Troncoso, who had served as minister and subsequently as the republic's first ambassador after the legation was elevated in May 1943. Distinguished guests included Attorney General Francis Biddle, Assistant Secretary of State Adolf A. Berle, Jr., and several Pan-American Union and State Department officials.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* dio cuenta de un almuerzo servido por el director general de la Unión Panamericana, Dr. Leo S. Rowe, en agasajo al nuevo embajador dominicano Dr. Anselmo Copello, con posterioridad a la ceremonia oficial de recepción de credenciales por el mandatario Roosevelt. Copello sustituía al Dr. Jesús María Troncoso, quien había ejercido como ministro y más tarde como primer embajador formal de la república tras la jerarquización de la legación en mayo de 1943. Entre los convidados de honor asistieron el fiscal general Francis Biddle, el subsecretario de Estado Adolf A. Berle, Jr., y altos funcionarios de la Unión Panamericana y del Departamento de Estado.

records.headline: An analytical article notes that following the end of political assassinations
records.summary_en: An analytical article notes that following the end of political assassinations, the Dominican Republic instituted economic and social reforms comparable to those in Mexico. In 1932 during the world depression, the republic established a chain of agricultural colonies and cooperatives for landless farmers, which by 1944 produced ample quantities of rice and other staples while shielding the population from wartime shipping shortages. Although the American Sugar Trust controls much of the land and sugar represents 90 per cent of exports, the government aims to develop self-sustaining independent growers and align public education with agriculture.
records.summary_es: Un artículo analítico señala que, tras el fin de los asesinatos políticos, la República Dominicana instituyó reformas económicas y sociales comparables a las de México. En 1932, durante la depresión mundial, la república estableció una cadena de colonias agrícolas y cooperativas para campesinos sin tierras, las cuales para 1944 producían abundantes cantidades de arroz y otros productos básicos protegiendo a la población de la escasez de transporte en tiempos de guerra. Aunque el American Sugar Trust controla gran parte de las tierras y el azúcar representa el 90 por ciento de las exportaciones, el gobierno aspira a formar agricultores independientes y autosuficientes y a orientar la educación pública hacia el agro.

records.headline: A feature article describes social developments in the Dominican
records.summary_en: A feature article describes social developments in the Dominican Republic, noting that domestic science schools train young women in nutrition and housekeeping in accordance with President Trujillo's statement that equal preparation makes woman the equal of man. While acknowledging that class equality remains distant and that political freedom faces criticism, the text credits the administration with building hospitals and clinics and subsidizing literature for needy authors. The article also highlights three modern Dominican authors deserving of English translation and notes that Santo Domingo had proposed a league of American nations prior to Roosevelt's hemispheric unity plan.
records.summary_es: Un artículo examina los avances sociales en la República Dominicana y señala que las escuelas de ciencias domésticas capacitan a las jóvenes en nutrición y labores del hogar, de acuerdo con la afirmación del presidente Trujillo de que la preparación igualitaria hace a la mujer igual al hombre. Si bien reconoce que la igualdad entre clases aún está distante y que la falta de libertades políticas genera críticas, el texto elogia a la administración por construir hospitales y clínicas y conceder subsidios literarios a autores necesitados. El artículo también destaca a tres autores dominicanos modernos merecedores de ser traducidos al inglés y recuerda que Santo Domingo había propuesto una liga de naciones americanas con anterioridad al plan de unidad hemisférica de Roosevelt.

records.headline: A society column reports personnel changes and movements within
records.summary_en: A society column reports personnel changes and movements within the Dominican Embassy in Washington. Flor Trujillo, former First Secretary, has been appointed Minister Counselor, while Dr. J. M. Sanz has been promoted from Second Secretary to First Secretary, and Chancellor Otto Vega has been named Second Secretary. The report also notes that Second Secretary Carlos Alberto Ricart is spending the weekend in New York, and Manuel de Moya, a special presidential representative staying at the Statler, plans to return to Ciudad Trujillo within a week after a month-long visit.

records.headline: A diplomatic society column reports that Flor Trujillo, newly
records.summary_en: A diplomatic society column reports that Flor Trujillo, newly appointed Minister-Counselor of the Dominican Embassy, departed Washington for her homeland following a farewell party given in her honor on Friday by the Second Secretary and Señora de Guerra. Miss Trujillo is traveling to Ciudad Trujillo to participate in celebrations marking the 100th anniversary of Dominican independence, commemorating the founding date of February 27, 1844, with festivities scheduled from February 23 through March 3. The column identifies her as the daughter of the former president of the Dominican Republic.
records.summary_es: Una crónica de sociedad diplomática informa que Flor Trujillo, recién nombrada ministra consejera de la embajada dominicana, partió de Washington hacia su patria tras una fiesta de despedida ofrecida en su honor el viernes por el segundo secretario y la señora de Guerra. La señorita Trujillo viaja a Ciudad Trujillo para participar en los actos del centenario de la independencia dominicana, que conmemoran la fecha de fundación del 27 de febrero de 1844, con festividades programadas del 23 de febrero al 3 de marzo. La columna la identifica como hija del expresidente de la República Dominicana.

records.headline: A news report states that Djamgaroff admitted receiving $50
records.summary_en: A news report states that Djamgaroff admitted receiving $50,000 annually in 1939 and 1940 as a registered agent in the United States for the Dominican Republic. While serving in that role, he arranged a visit to the republic by a congressional delegation that included Representative Fish, Republican of New York. Later developments revealed that President Trujillo had deposited $25,000 in a New York bank to Fish's credit, with Fish's office stating that the congressman returned $12,500 and invested the remaining $12,500 on Trujillo's behalf in a Texas wildcat oil venture. Djamgaroff noted that Trujillo was not president while he served as registered agent.
records.summary_es: Un informe de prensa señala que Djamgaroff admitió haber recibido $50,000 anuales en 1939 y 1940 como agente registrado de la República Dominicana en los Estados Unidos. Mientras desempeñaba esa función, organizó una visita a la república para una delegación del Congreso que incluyó al representante Fish, republicano de Nueva York. Revelaciones posteriores indicaron que el presidente Trujillo había depositado $25,000 en un banco de Nueva York a crédito de Fish, explicando la oficina de Fish que el congresista devolvió $12,500 e invirtió los $12,500 restantes en nombre de Trujillo en un proyecto de prospección petrolera en Texas. Djamgaroff señaló que Trujillo no era presidente mientras él fungía como agente registrado.

records.headline: Marking the centennial of Dominican independence, a feature
records.summary_en: Marking the centennial of Dominican independence, a feature reviews educational progress and the public role of women in the republic. The nation boasts over 3,000 schools and the University of Santo Domingo, founded in 1538 as the oldest institution of higher learning in the Americas, which has graduated over 300 professional women including seven physicians, six dentists, over 100 pharmacists, and many lawyers. The article profiles Dr. Consuelo Bernardino, sister of Inter-American Commission of Women chairman Minerva Bernardino, who completed postgraduate training at Johns Hopkins Hospital and in 1940 became the university's first female professor at age 30. It also notes that women participate in the national legislature, holding one seat in the Senate and two in the lower house of Congress.
records.summary_es: Con motivo del centenario de la independencia dominicana, un reportaje repasa los avances educativos y el papel público de las mujeres en la república. La nación cuenta con más de 3.000 escuelas y la Universidad de Santo Domingo, fundada en 1538 como la institución de educación superior más antigua de América, que ha graduado a más de 300 profesionales mujeres, entre ellas siete médicas, seis odontólogas, más de 100 farmacéuticas y numerosas abogadas. El artículo destaca a la doctora Consuelo Bernardino, hermana de la presidenta de la Comisión Interamericana de Mujeres Minerva Bernardino, quien realizó estudios de posgrado en el Hospital Johns Hopkins y en 1940 se convirtió a los 30 años en la primera profesora de la universidad. También señala que las mujeres participan en la legislatura nacional, ocupando un escaño en el Senado y dos en la cámara baja del Congreso.

records.headline: Miss Bernardino departed for Miami en route to the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: Miss Bernardino departed for Miami en route to the Dominican Republic to participate in the centennial celebration of national independence as a guest of her government in Ciudad Trujillo. She had originally planned to remain in Washington for a Sunday afternoon reception hosted by the Dominican Ambassador and Señora de Copello before receiving instructions to return home. Following a one-week stay at her Dominican home, she is scheduled to fly on March 4 to Havana for conferences on women's welfare and political advancement before returning to Washington in mid-March.

Tras una estancia de una semana en su hogar dominicano, tiene programado volar el 4 de marzo a La Habana para asistir a conferencias sobre bienestar y progreso político de las mujeres antes de retornar a Washington a mediados de marzo.

records.headline: Senhor Cyro de Freitas Valle, newly appointed as Brazil's first ambassador
records.summary_en: Senhor Cyro de Freitas Valle, newly appointed as Brazil's first ambassador to Canada, is visiting Ciudad Trujillo to represent his nation at the centenary celebration of Dominican independence. He is scheduled to arrive in Miami early next week before traveling to Washington. Freitas Valle previously served in Washington as embassy counselor and later represented Brazil as minister in Bolivia, Cuba, and Romania, as well as ambassador in Berlin at the outbreak of the German invasions.

Freitas Valle se desempeñó anteriormente en Washington como consejero de embajada y más tarde representó a Brasil como ministro en Bolivia, Cuba y Rumania, además de ejercer como embajador en Berlín al comienzo de las invasiones alemanas.

records.headline: Marking a week of centennial festivities in Ciudad Trujillo
records.summary_en: Marking a week of centennial festivities in Ciudad Trujillo, a historical feature surveys the development of the Dominican Republic since achieving independence from Haiti in 1844. The column recalls the nation's colonial origin, Columbus's arrival nearly 500 years earlier, and a brief return to Spanish rule during the 1860s under Queen Isabella II. It also portrays the country as a lush tropical land with historic sites such as the ancient cathedral holding Columbus's remains and the palace of Bartolomeo Columbus, noting that Generalissimo Trujillo renamed the capital after himself.
records.summary_es: Con motivo de una semana de festejos centenarios en Ciudad Trujillo, una crónica histórica examina la trayectoria de la República Dominicana desde que logró su independencia de Haití en 1844. La columna rememora los orígenes coloniales del país, la llegada de Colón casi quinientos años antes y un breve retorno a la soberanía española durante la década de 1860 bajo la reina Isabel II. Asimismo, describe el territorio como una fértil tierra tropical con monumentos históricos como la antigua catedral que guarda los restos de Colón y el palacio de Bartolomé Colón, destacando que el generalísimo Trujillo rebautizó la capital con su propio nombre.

records.full_text:
Gen. Holcomb Is Named Envoy to South Africa

Gen. Thomas Holcomb, who recently retired as Marine Corps commandant, was nominated today by President Roosevelt to be Minister to the Union of South Africa.

The President also named Leland B. Morris, now Minister to Iceland, to be the first American Ambassador to Iran. The diplomatic establishment in that country recently was raised from a ministry, and Louis G. Dreyfus, who has been serving as Minister there, will take over Mr. Morris' post in Iceland.

Other nominations included:

Avra M. Warren, now Ambassador to the Dominican Republic, to be Ambassador to Panama.

Ellis O. Briggs, counsellor of Embassy at Havana, to be Ambassador to the Dominican Republic.

records.headline: An educational feature profiles the Dominican Republic, noting
records.summary_en: An educational feature profiles the Dominican Republic, noting that its capital, Santo Domingo, founded in 1496 by Bartholomew Columbus and now renamed Ciudad Trujillo after President Trujillo, was the earliest permanent European settlement in the New World. The item describes the fertile Vega Real plain nestled among four mountain ranges as a major producer of tobacco, cacao, sugar, and fruits. It adds that the republic pledged full moral and material support to the United Nations war effort, expanding its output of vital tropical war supplies including tannin, mahogany, and rope fibers.
records.summary_es: Una sección educativa describe a la República Dominicana señalando que su capital, Santo Domingo, fundada en 1496 por Bartolomé Colón y ahora rebautizada Ciudad Trujillo en honor al presidente Trujillo, constituyó el primer asentamiento europeo permanente en el Nuevo Mundo. La nota resalta el fértil valle de la Vega Real, enclavado entre cuatro cordilleras, como un gran centro productor de tabaco, cacao, azúcar y frutas. Agrega que la república comprometió su pleno respaldo moral y material al esfuerzo bélico de las Naciones Unidas, aumentando la producción de insumos tropicales estratégicos como tanino, caoba y fibras para cuerdas.

Inter-American Group Plans Meeting Here

Delegates from 14 of the 21 American republics will gather here April 14, for the fourth general assembly of the Inter-American Commission of Women, at the Pan-American Union, it was announced today.

Opening on Pan-American Day, the assembly will continue to April 20, under chairmanship of Miss Minerva Bernadino, delegate from the Dominican Republic.

records.headline: A commentary highlighting the integration of leaders of African descent
records.summary_en: A commentary highlighting the integration of leaders of African descent across Latin America contrasts their status with prevailing racial attitudes in the United States. The column asserts that Dominican leader Rafael Trujillo and President Elie Lescot of Haiti are men of color who will always be viewed as such by Southern politicians regardless of attempts to lighten their complexions with cosmetics. It also points to former Brazilian president Nilo Pecanha, Cuban president Fulgencio Batista, and numerous Black legislators throughout Latin America as evidence of substantial political achievement.
records.summary_es: Un comentario que resalta la integración de gobernantes de ascendencia africana en América Latina contrasta su posición con los prejuicios raciales imperantes en los Estados Unidos. La columna afirma que el mandatario dominicano Rafael Trujillo y el presidente Elie Lescot de Haití son hombres de color que siempre serán considerados como tales por los políticos del sur estadounidense, a pesar de cualquier intento por aclarar su tez con cosméticos. Asimismo, señala al expresidente brasileño Nilo Pecanha, al presidente cubano Fulgencio Batista y a numerosos legisladores afrodescendientes en toda Latinoamérica como testimonio de notables logros políticos.

records.headline: Theodore C. Weber, who previously served as United States consul
records.summary_en: Theodore C. Weber, who previously served as United States consul at Ciudad Trujillo in the Dominican Republic, died Thursday night at his home in Arlington, Virginia. The State Department announced his passing, noting that he had recently been reassigned to department headquarters in Washington. The announcement also reported the death of Clayson W. Aldridge, another foreign service officer recently reassigned to Washington after serving as consul in Sydney, Australia.

El Departamento de Estado anunció su fallecimiento e indicó que había sido reasignado recientemente a la sede del departamento en Washington. El comunicado informó asimismo sobre la muerte de Clayson W. Aldridge, otro funcionario consular trasladado hace poco a Washington tras haber servido en Sídney, Australia.

In embassy activities, Señorita Flor Trujillo, Minister Counselor of the Dominican Embassy, will travel to St. Louis for the convention of the General Federation of Women's Clubs. records.headline: Diplomatic officials of the Dominican Embassy in Washington hosted
records.summary_en: Diplomatic officials of the Dominican Embassy in Washington hosted multiple social functions for delegates attending international gatherings. Embassy Minister Counselor Flor Trujillo planned a buffet supper in honor of Dr. Luis F. Thomen, Undersecretary of State for Sanitation and Public Welfare and delegate to the International Health Conference, along with Señora de Thomen, having already entertained the embassy staff earlier in the week. Additionally, Minister Counselor and Señora de Moya held a reception introducing Salvatore A. Cocco, Dominican delegate to the International Labor Conference in Philadelphia, and Señora de Cocco, with Dr. Rodriguez serving as delegation adviser.

records.headline: Señorita Flor Trujillo, daughter of the Dominican president
records.summary_en: Señorita Flor Trujillo, daughter of the Dominican president and first secretary of the Dominican Embassy, hosted an informal reception at her Massachusetts Avenue residence for members of the M. Eleanor Brackenridge Club. The organization had sponsored Dominican student Carmen Lara during the previous year to pursue studies in the United States. La señorita Trujillo elogió este respaldo educativo transfronterizo, mientras que la señorita Marnee Thomas, presidenta del comité de la República Dominicana del club, transmitió la gratitud de la institución.

records.summary_en: A wire service account details the widespread public reaction to a premature news bulletin falsely reporting Allied landings in France. In Ciudad Trujillo, capital of the Dominican Republic, newspaper sirens sounded and crowds gathered in the streets, only to express keen disappointment when the report was retracted. The Associated Press explained from London that the erroneous bulletin was transmitted inadvertently by a novice teletype operator during an unauthorized test on a perforator.

Associated Press explicó desde Londres que el boletín erróneo fue transmitido por descuido por una operadora de teletipo principiante durante una prueba no autorizada con una perforadora.

records.headline: A news report describes the excitement and subsequent disappointment
records.summary_en: A news report describes the excitement and subsequent disappointment caused by an erroneous wire flash announcing Allied invasion landings in France before an official kill order was issued. In Ciudad Trujillo, capital of the Dominican Republic, newspaper sirens blared and crowds gathered, reacting with audible dismay when the mistake was corrected. The article notes that wire editors caught the error quickly enough that the false flash never appeared in print. In New York and elsewhere, newspaper and radio station switchboards were almost instantly swamped with inquiries from persons who had heard the original and incorrect flash but not the “kill.” The London bureau of the Associated Press cabled this explanation: the flash erroneously stating Eisenhower had announced Allied landings in France was transmitted by a new teletype operator in a wholly unauthorized test of a perforator; it moved without authority of censors and without knowledge of the editorial staff, which had no such copy on hand. Experienced operators saw the flash on the printer and immediately notified New York and the editors, who sent a “kill.” Joan Ellis, the young operator who erred, said she had been practicing on a disconnected machine and thought she had torn up all that tape and thrown it away; however, before transmitting the first “take” of the Russian communiqué, she inadvertently ran through part of the tape that she thought she had destroyed. Miss Ellis is 22 and had been with the Associated Press since January 1944, with four years' experience as a teletype operator in the WAAF (Women's Auxiliary Airforce). The big American radio chains — NBC, CBS, Blue Network and Mutual — all interrupted programs to carry the erroneous flash, and again to announce the correction, which they repeated at intervals during the evening. By coincidence, the British Broadcasting Company was at the time broadcasting a dramatic reenactment of the Dunkerque epic of four years ago; the BBC did not receive the false flash, but anyone who had tuned in on its program might easily have gained the impression that an invasion was in progress.
records.summary_es: Una crónica periodística describe el entusiasmo y la posterior desilusión provocados por un teletipo erróneo que anunció desembarcos de invasión aliados en Francia antes de que se emitiera una orden oficial de anulación. En Ciudad Trujillo, capital de la República Dominicana, sonaron las sirenas de los diarios y se agruparon muchedumbres, reaccionando con evidente desaliento cuando se corrigió el error. El artículo añade que los redactores de la agencia detectaron el fallo a tiempo para que la falsa noticia no llegara a publicarse en papel. En Nueva York y en otros lugares, las centralitas de los periódicos y las emisoras de radio se vieron inundadas casi al instante de consultas de personas que habían oído el teletipo original e incorrecto pero no la orden de anulación. La oficina de Londres de la Associated Press cablegrafió esta explicación: el teletipo que afirmaba erróneamente que Eisenhower había anunciado desembarcos aliados en Francia fue transmitido por una nueva operadora de teletipo en una prueba totalmente no autorizada de una perforadora; circuló sin autoridad de los censores y sin conocimiento de la redacción, que no tenía tal texto en su poder. Operadores experimentados vieron el teletipo en la impresora y avisaron de inmediato a Nueva York y a los redactores, que enviaron la orden de anulación. Joan Ellis, la joven operadora que cometió el error, dijo que había estado practicando en una máquina desconectada y creía haber roto toda la cinta y haberla tirado; sin embargo, antes de transmitir la primera entrega del comunicado ruso, pasó inadvertidamente parte de la cinta que creía destruida. La señorita Ellis tiene 22 años y trabajaba en la Associated Press desde enero de 1944, con cuatro años de experiencia como operadora de teletipo en la WAAF (Fuerza Aérea Auxiliar Femenina). Las grandes cadenas de radio estadounidenses —NBC, CBS, Blue Network y Mutual— interrumpieron sus programas para transmitir el falso teletipo, y de nuevo para anunciar la corrección, que repitieron a intervalos durante la noche. Por coincidencia, la British Broadcasting Company transmitía en ese momento una dramatización de la epopeya de Dunkerque de cuatro años atrás; la BBC no recibió el falso teletipo, pero cualquiera que hubiera sintonizado su programa podría haber tenido fácilmente la impresión de que una invasión estaba en curso.

records.headline: Following an erroneous wire transmission announcing Allied landings
records.summary_en: Following an erroneous wire transmission announcing Allied landings in France, cities worldwide experienced sudden waves of excitement and disillusionment. In Ciudad Trujillo, capital of the Dominican Republic, newspaper sirens sounded and crowds assembled, only to voice disappointment when authorities clarified that no invasion had begun. The Associated Press reported that the unauthorized message was sent during a machine test by an inexperienced teletype operator in London, though the error was halted before reaching printed newspapers.

En Ciudad Trujillo, capital de la República Dominicana, sonaron las sirenas de los periódicos y el público se congregó, solo para manifestar decepción cuando se aclaró que ninguna invasión había comenzado. Associated Press informó que el mensaje no autorizado fue enviado durante una prueba de equipo por una operadora novata de teletipo en Londres, si bien el error se interceptó antes de llegar a los periódicos impresos.

records.headline: Señor Luis Enrique Franco, editor of La Información in Santiago
records.summary_en: Señor Luis Enrique Franco, editor of La Información in Santiago, Dominican Republic, visited Washington as part of a Latin American journalists' delegation invited by the National Press Club and the Office of the Coordinator of Inter-American Affairs. During their week-long stay in the capital, the visiting newspapermen attended presidential and State Department press conferences with Secretary of State Cordell Hull. Their schedule featured informal gatherings with American journalists and officials, an excursion to the Naval Academy, and a luncheon hosted by Library of Congress leaders.

Durante su semana de estancia en la capital, los comunicadores visitantes asistieron a conferencias de prensa presidenciales y del Departamento de Estado con el secretario Cordell Hull. Su programa incluyó reuniones informales con periodistas y funcionarios estadounidenses, una excursión a la Academia Naval y un almuerzo ofrecido por directivos de la Biblioteca del Congreso.

records.headline: According to an Associated Press dispatch from Miami dated August
records.summary_en: According to an Associated Press dispatch from Miami dated August 18, gale winds whipped the Caribbean Sea as a tropical disturbance bypassed Puerto Rico and moved steadily over open water far from land. The San Juan weather bureau station reported that at 4 p.m. the disturbance was centered about 300 miles south-southeast of Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic, moving west-northwestward. The bureau declared that all danger to Puerto Rico had passed, noting that the storm center lay about 1,000 miles southeast of Miami in one of the broadest areas of the Caribbean.
records.summary_es: Según un despacho de Associated Press fechado el 18 de agosto en Miami, vientos de galerna azotaron el mar Caribe mientras una perturbación tropical pasaba de largo por Puerto Rico y avanzaba de forma constante sobre aguas abiertas lejos de tierra. La estación de la oficina meteorológica de San Juan informó que a las 4 p. m. la perturbación estaba centrada a unas 300 millas al sur-sureste de Ciudad Trujillo, República Dominicana, desplazándose con rumbo oeste-noroeste. records.full_text:
Don Anselmo Copella, Dominican Envoy, Dies

Don Anselmo Copella, Ambassador to the United States from the Dominican Republic, died in Doctors Hospital today from a heart attack which followed pneumonia. Don Anselmo was 65 years old.

The Ambassador, who came here a year ago, became ill two days ago. He entered the hospital yesterday.

His wife, Senora Copello, and five children are in the Capital.

Don Anselmo was president of the principal tobacco company of the Dominican Republic. Except for several honorary posts he had never served as a Government official until he was appointed Ambassador in November, 1943. His credentials were received by President Roosevelt on December 20, 1943.

records.headline: Don Anselmo Copello
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published tributes mourning the death of Dominican Ambassador Anselmo Copello, praising his distinction as a diplomat and cooperative spirit on matters of mutual concern. Copello, head of the Dominican Republic's main tobacco company based in Santiago, had returned to Washington only days before his death following three months of official business in his home country. Minister Counselor Dr. J. R. Rodríguez was designated to direct embassy affairs until a successor was appointed.

Copello, directivo de la compañía tabacalera radicada en Santiago de los Caballeros, había retornado a Washington escasos días antes de su partida terrenal luego de permanecer tres meses atendiendo gestiones de Estado en su patria. El ministro consejero Dr. J. R. Rodríguez quedó a cargo de los despachos de la misión hasta la designación de un sucesor titular.

Don Anselmo Copello
Funeral Arranged
For Tomorrow

Members of the diplomatic corps and high Government officials will attend funeral services for Don Anselmo Copello, Ambassador from the Dominican Republic, at 11 a.m tomorrow at the Sacred Heart Church, Sixteenth street and Park road N.W. After temporary burial in Arlington Cemetery, the body will be taken to the Dominican Republic.

The Ambassador, who was 65, died yesterday in Doctors Hospital of a heart attack which followed pneumonia. He had been ill two days.

His work was praised in the following statement made yesterday by Secretary of State Stettinius:

“I have been greatly grieved to learn of the death of the distinguished Ambassador of the Dominican Republic. His excellency Anselmo Copella. In my association with him in dealing with the problems of mutual interest, I have come to know his outstanding qualities as a diplomat and as a friend.

“He has represented his country with distinction and has always evinced a most helpful spirit of cooperation in dealing with matters of common concern. The Dominican people will rightly mourn the passing of a gifted statesman and his many friends in this country will sincerely share their sorrow.”

Senor Copello returned to Washington Monday from the Dominican Republic, where he had been on official business for three months. He was accompanied by his only son, Jeronimo.

Before his appointment as Ambassador to this country in November, 1943, Senor Copello had never served as a government official except for several honorary posts. His credentials were received by President Roosevelt on December 20, 1943. He succeeded Dr. J. M. Troncoso, now Secretary of the Treasury of the Dominican Republic.

President of the principal tobacco company of the Dominican Republic, Senor Copello’s home was in Santiago.

Besides his widow, Senora de Copello, and his son, he is survived by four daughters, Adelina, Argentina, Ileana and Margarita. The family lives at the Embassy, 4530 Sixteenth street N.W.

Dr. J. R. Rodriguez, Minister Counselor, will direct the affairs of the Embassy until further arrangements are made by his government.

records.headline: A Washington obituary records the death of Dr. Consuelo Bernardino
records.summary_en: A Washington obituary records the death of Dr. Consuelo Bernardino, a 33-year-old Dominican physician who died last Thursday in Ciudad Trujillo. She was the sister of Minerva Bernardino, chairman of the Inter-American Commission of Women in Washington. Having studied at the Women's Medical College of Philadelphia, Johns Hopkins University, and Columbia University, Dr. Bernardino was the first woman appointed professor of gynecology at the University of Santo Domingo Medical School and served on a Dominican government committee for the protection of mothers and children. Having departed Washington for Ciudad Trujillo in late December, she is survived by three brothers and two sisters.
records.summary_es: Una nota necrológica de Washington registra el fallecimiento de la doctora Consuelo Bernardino, médica dominicana de 33 años que murió el jueves pasado en Ciudad Trujillo. Era hermana de Minerva Bernardino, presidenta de la Comisión Interamericana de Mujeres en Washington. Habiendo cursado estudios en el Women's Medical College de Filadelfia, la Universidad Johns Hopkins y la Universidad de Columbia, la doctora Bernardino fue la primera mujer nombrada profesora de ginecología en la Escuela de Medicina de la Universidad de Santo Domingo y formó parte de un comité del gobierno dominicano para la protección de madres y niños. Tras partir de Washington hacia Ciudad Trujillo a fines de diciembre, le sobreviven tres hermanos y dos hermanas.

records.full_text:
18 Nations Ratify Pact On World Food Unit; Two More Needed

By the Associated Press.

The United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization provided for at the Hot Springs (Va.) Conference of 1943 will come into being with the ratification of only two more nations, it was revealed today. Eighteen nations have approved the agreement. Twenty ratifications are required.

Ambassador L. B. Pearson of Canada, chairman of the United Nations interim commission on food and agriculture, said that acceptances of membership had been received from the following countries:

Australia, Belgium, China, Czechoslovakia, Dominican Republic, Egypt, Guatemala, Haiti, Honduras, Iceland, India, Mexico, the Netherlands, Nicaragua, Norway, Philippines, Poland and the United Kingdom.

Acceptance for Poland came from the Polish government in exile in London, Mr. Pearson told a questioner. He added: "This occurred last October."

The plan has not yet been submitted to Congress for approval, although President Roosevelt indicated in his February 2 message on the Bretton Woods proposals that it soon will be.

Mr. Pearson said action is "pending" in "a number of other countries."

All 44 United Nations participating in the Hot Springs Conference a year and a half ago have been represented on Mr. Pearson's interim commission.

The proposed constitution provides for the FAO to "become a part of any general world organization which may be established," Mr. Pearson declared.

records.headline: A Washington diplomatic column reports that Dr. Garland is preparing
records.summary_en: A Washington diplomatic column reports that Dr. Garland is preparing to assume new duties in Bolivia after serving at his embassy in Washington for more than a year following his post as minister in the Dominican Republic. Dr. Garland's diplomatic tour of duty in Ciudad Trujillo came after several years on the embassy staff in Washington, where he had originally succeeded Dr. Juan Mendosa as counselor. The diplomat plans to depart in mid-May for a fortnight in his homeland before proceeding to La Paz, while Señora de Garland and their children remain in the capital until the close of the school year.
records.summary_es: Una columna diplomática de Washington informa que el Dr. Garland se prepara para asumir nuevas funciones en Bolivia tras desempeñarse en su embajada en Washington durante más de un año después de haber ocupado el cargo de ministro en la República Dominicana. El período de servicio diplomático del Dr. Garland en Ciudad Trujillo se produjo tras varios años en el personal de la embajada en Washington, donde originalmente había sucedido al Dr. Juan Mendosa como consejero. El diplomático planea partir a mediados de mayo para pasar una quincena en su patria antes de dirigirse a La Paz, mientras que la señora de Garland y sus hijos permanecerán en la capital hasta la clausura del año escolar.

records.summary_en: The Key West Citizen reports that K. N. Dahle of Key West has been appointed section radio technician for the Latin American Division of Pan American World Airways. Stationed in Miami, Dahle oversees the maintenance of company radio stations in Miami, Port-au-Prince in Haiti, Ciudad Trujillo in the Dominican Republic, Kingston, Nassau, San Juan, St. Thomas, Brownsville, and Glendale. He also supervises station mechanics and inspects new sets and equipment, having joined the airline in 1940 and served in Surinam and French Guiana.

records.headline: A Washington society column recounts that Betty Byrne married
records.summary_en: A Washington society column recounts that Betty Byrne married Luis on April 26 at the church in the Dominican Monastery in the Dominican Republic, where Luis had a close friend serving as Spanish minister. The newlyweds honeymooned at a magnificent new hotel built at the ocean's edge, which the bride praised enthusiastically. Writing of Trujillo City, she described it as a place where visitors could readily buy radios, electric clocks, and plentiful steaks, although she had to leave behind a $2.75 hand-embroidered pink linen dress when Pan American Airways secured their return travel.

Los recién casados pasaron su luna de miel en un magnífico nuevo hotel construido a la orilla del mar, al cual la novia elogió con entusiasmo. Al escribir sobre Ciudad Trujillo, la describió como un lugar donde los visitantes podían adquirir con facilidad radios, relojes eléctricos y abundantes filetes de carne, aunque tuvo que dejar atrás un vestido de lino rosa bordado a mano de $2.75 cuando Pan American Airways aseguró su pasaje de regreso.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported on U.S. wartime cooperation and mutual aid programs established across Latin America. Cooperative health programs to control malaria were launched in eighteen nations, including the Dominican Republic and Haiti, to sustain the production of vital war materials. The article emphasized that these initiatives, along with agricultural and technical assistance, were mutually beneficial cooperative efforts rather than unilateral handouts.

El informe recalcó que estos planes, junto al respaldo técnico y agrícola, obedecían a esquemas bilaterales equitativos de beneficio común y no a dádivas discrecionales unilaterales.

records.summary_en: The State Department made public a lengthy March 1930 report by American Minister C. B. Curtis on the Dominican revolution, in papers relating to foreign relations for 1930. Curtis said General Trujillo was disloyal to President Vasquez from the first moment after his return on January 6, was in league with the revolutionists from the very beginning, and that if Trujillo had been truly loyal the revolution could not have succeeded and would probably not have broken out. The release added that although the American government was strongly opposed to his coming to power, and discreetly did all it could to prevent it, Trujillo nevertheless was elected through ballot box stuffing and has remained in office since. As stated in the papers, one of the reasons which lent weight to the causes for the revolution was that “the country has always opposed the reelection of its chief magistrates.” It is significant to note that although Trujillo has enjoyed the recognition of this government, he is one of the few Latin American chiefs of state who during the life of President Roosevelt had not been invited to make an official visit to the United States.
records.summary_es: El Departamento de Estado hizo público un extenso informe de marzo de 1930 del ministro estadounidense C. B. Curtis sobre la revolución dominicana, en los documentos de relaciones exteriores de 1930. Curtis dijo que el general Trujillo fue desleal al presidente Vásquez desde el primer momento después de su regreso el 6 de enero, estuvo aliado con los revolucionarios desde el principio, y que si Trujillo hubiera sido verdaderamente leal la revolución no podría haber triunfado y probablemente no habría estallado. La publicación añadió que, aunque el gobierno estadounidense se oponía firmemente a su llegada al poder e hizo discretamente todo lo posible por impedirla, Trujillo fue no obstante elegido mediante el relleno fraudulento de urnas y ha permanecido en el cargo desde entonces. Como se afirma en los documentos, una de las razones que dieron peso a las causas de la revolución fue que «el país siempre se ha opuesto a la reelección de sus magistrados supremos». Es significativo notar que, aunque Trujillo ha disfrutado del reconocimiento de este gobierno, es uno de los pocos jefes de Estado latinoamericanos que durante la vida del presidente Roosevelt no había sido invitado a realizar una visita oficial a los Estados Unidos.

records.headline: A slight tropical disturbance is centered near latitude 17.4
records.summary_en: A slight tropical disturbance is centered near latitude 17.4 north and longitude 70.2 west, roughly 75 to 100 miles south-southwest of Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic, a weather bulletin published in The Key West Citizen reports. The disturbance was moving west-northwest or northwest at about 12 miles per hour, generating maximum winds estimated at 40 to 50 miles per hour over a small area near its center. Forecasters warned that the storm would skirt the southern coast of Hispaniola and might move inland, urging continued caution from Hispaniola westward to Jamaica.
records.summary_es: Una leve perturbación tropical se localiza cerca de los 17.4 grados de latitud norte y 70.2 grados de longitud oeste, aproximadamente a unas 75 a 100 millas al sur-suroeste de Ciudad Trujillo, República Dominicana, según informa un boletín meteorológico publicado en The Key West Citizen. La perturbación avanzaba con rumbo oeste-noroeste o noroeste a unas 12 millas por hora, con vientos máximos estimados entre 40 y 50 millas por hora en una reducida área cercana a su centro. Los pronosticadores advirtieron que la tormenta bordearía la costa sur de La Española y podría penetrar en tierra firme, instando a mantener la precaución desde La Española hacia el oeste hasta Jamaica.

records.headline: Americas Plan Slap at Franco
records.summary_en: Consultations are under way among the foreign offices of the American nations over a simultaneous diplomatic break with the government of Generalissimo Francisco Franco in Spain, after the Uruguayan Senate forwarded a recommendation for a break and both houses of the Peruvian Congress approved one. In Central America and the Caribbean, Guatemala, Honduras, Panama, the Dominican Republic and Haiti have already broken relations with Franco, and Mexico never recognized his dictatorship. A State Department spokesman in Washington denied a report that the United States and other American nations had agreed on a collective break, but other sources predicted that further diplomatic breaks with Spain could be expected.
records.summary_es: Se celebran consultas entre las cancillerías de las naciones americanas sobre una ruptura diplomática simultánea con el gobierno del generalísimo Francisco Franco en España, después de que el Senado uruguayo remitiera una recomendación de ruptura y ambas cámaras del Congreso peruano aprobaran una. En Centroamérica y el Caribe, Guatemala, Honduras, Panamá, la República Dominicana y Haití ya han roto relaciones con Franco, y México nunca reconoció su dictadura. Un portavoz del Departamento de Estado en Washington negó que los Estados Unidos y otras naciones americanas hubieran acordado una ruptura colectiva, pero otras fuentes previeron que podrían esperarse nuevas rupturas diplomáticas con España.
records.passage: Two days ago, both houses of the Peruvian Congress approved a recommendation to the executive that Peru sever diplomatic and commercial ties with Franco. Liberal legislators and newspapers in Cuba, Colombia and Venezuela have urged a break. WASHINGTON DENIES REPORT OF AGREEMENT WASHINGTON, Aug. 9.— ([U.P.?]) A State Department spokesman tonight described as "untrue" a report that the United States and other American nations are consulting on a collective move to break relations with the Franco government of Spain. He would not elaborate on the statement. Other sources predicted, however, that diplomatic breaks with Spain can be expected by additional Latin American nations. A Spanish republican source said the movement was strongest in Chile, Cuba, Uruguay, Colombia and Venezuela. Nicaragua, Panama, Guatemala, the Dominican Republic and Haiti already have broken with the Franco regime. Mexico never has maintained diplomatic relations with it. records.headline: A correspondent's firsthand travel account in the California Eagle examines
records.summary_en: A correspondent's firsthand travel account in the California Eagle examines racial attitudes and social practices in the Dominican Republic. The author observes that while Dominican law does not enforce the racial segregation seen in parts of the United States, upper-class whites maintain clear social distance and openly boast of pure-blood ancestry. During a week in Ciudad Trujillo, the correspondent observed no Black or visibly mixed-race guests mingling with white patrons in hotel dining rooms or recreational spaces such as swimming pools, despite assurances that the Spanish-operated Ciudad Trujillo Hotel would not turn away Black visitors. Traveling to Santiago, the country's second largest city, the writer noted a mestizo family dining separately from Spanish-blooded guests, while remarking that Black and mestizo residents shape the broader life and character of the colonial city.
records.summary_es: Una crónica de viaje de primera mano de un corresponsal en el California Eagle examina las actitudes raciales y las prácticas sociales en la República Dominicana. El autor observa que, si bien la ley dominicana no impone la segregación racial imperante en zonas de los Estados Unidos, los blancos de clase alta mantienen una marcada distancia social y alardean abiertamente de su ascendencia de sangre pura. Durante una semana de permanencia en Ciudad Trujillo, el corresponsal no vio a huéspedes negros ni visiblemente mestizos conviviendo con clientes blancos en comedores de hoteles o espacios recreativos como piscinas, a pesar de las afirmaciones de que el Hotel Ciudad Trujillo, administrado por españoles, no rechazaría a visitantes negros. Al trasladarse a Santiago, la segunda ciudad del país, el autor observó a una familia mestiza cenando apartada de los comensales de ascendencia española, al tiempo que remarcó que los habitantes negros y mestizos definen la vida y el carácter general de la urbe colonial.

records.headline: The Dominican ambassador and his wife hosted an afternoon reception
records.summary_en: The Dominican ambassador and his wife hosted an afternoon reception at the embassy on Sixteenth Street in honor of Maj. Gen. F. E. Watson, U.S.M.C., and Mrs. Watson. The hosts and guests of honor first met in Ciudad Trujillo during General Watson's tour of duty and renewed their friendship in Washington and the Dominican Republic. General Watson recently arrived for duty at Marine Corps headquarters after serving in the Pacific theater, while the ambassador had recently returned from his homeland. Guests included Latin American diplomats and numerous fellow officers who had also served in the Dominican Republic.

Los anfitriones y los invitados de honor se conocieron en Ciudad Trujillo durante el servicio del general Watson y reanudaron su amistad en Washington y en la República Dominicana. El general Watson se incorporó recientemente a la comandancia de la Infantería de Marina tras prestar servicio en el teatro del Pacífico, mientras que el embajador acababa de regresar de su país de origen. Entre los asistentes figuraron diplomáticos latinoamericanos y numerosos compañeros de armas que también habían servido en la República Dominicana.

records.summary_en: The Dominican Embassy in Washington announced that wartime censorship on mail communications, telegraphic, cable, and telephone messages has been officially rescinded in the Dominican Republic. The lifting was enacted under an order issued by President Trujillo on August 25. The restrictions had remained in force throughout the duration of the war.

El levantamiento fue dispuesto mediante una orden emitida por el presidente Trujillo el 25 de agosto. Las restricciones se habían mantenido vigentes durante toda la duración de la guerra.

The dispatch notes that the country is peopled predominantly by colored people.

El 4 de septiembre, el gobierno dominicano depositó ante el Departamento de Estado su instrumento de ratificación de la Carta y del anexo Estatuto de la Corte Internacional de Justicia. El despacho señala que el país está habitado predominantemente por personas de color.

records.headline: Venezuelan Cabinet Post Goes to Ex-GI
records.summary_en: Luis Valmore Rodríguez, a 45-year-old former United States Army sergeant and editor of El País, will be sworn in as interior minister in Venezuela's new revolutionary government, which seized power in a four-day uprising that overthrew President Isaías Medina Angarita. Named to the post by his friend, revolutionary president Rómulo Betancourt, he will oversee the government's relations with American oil companies and other foreign investors, and has assured them he will respect their rights. Interim foreign minister Carlos Morales said the junta would meet all international obligations undertaken by the previous government and was seeking foreign recognition; asked about future relations with Franco's Spain, Trujillo's Dominican Republic and the Argentine regime, he made no commitment but said his people were not in favor of such regimes.

Nombrado por su amigo, el presidente revolucionario Rómulo Betancourt, supervisará las relaciones del gobierno con las compañías petroleras estadounidenses y otros inversionistas extranjeros, y les aseguró que respetará sus derechos. records.full_text:
Venezuela's New Regime Seeks Recognition of the Americas

By United Press

CARACAS, Oct. 23—Venezuela's new revolutionary government bid for diplomatic recognition by the rest of the world today.

Carlos Morales, Foreign Minister of the military junta, told a press conference that diplomatic representatives of all American nations in Caracas had been informed of the constitution of the new government.

Representatives of the American republics conferred at the American Embassy yesterday on the situation and will meet again tomorrow at the home of the Papal Nuncio.

HINTS SPAIN BREAK

Morales said he expected recognition because of the popularity of the revolution abroad. He said the junta would comply with all international commitments entered into by previous Venezuelan governments.

He suggested that the junta might break relations with Spain and the Dominican Republic on grounds they were Fascist-controlled.

CHURCH BACKS IT

The government already had won internal support from the Catholic Church and the Venezuelan Chamber of Commerce. A spokesman said the government was preparing for election of delegates to a convention to draw up a new constitution.

The government issued a decree prohibiting any member of the present interim junta from being a candidate for president in the April election. The junta also froze the bank accounts of all persons having more than $30,000 on deposit.

The government announced that it intends to try all officials who were believed to have enriched themselves in the last 50 years, including deposed President Isaias Medina.

records.headline: An art review highlights an exhibition by Ernesto Lothar at the Whyte Gallery featuring
records.summary_en: An art review highlights an exhibition by Ernesto Lothar at the Whyte Gallery featuring portraits and figures of residents living near Sosua, alongside tropical landscapes of the Dominican Republic. The text describes the local subjects as descendants of the island's indigenous inhabitants and of the Spanish and African settlers who arrived after Columbus. The reviewer notes that Lothar's work reflects conventions reminiscent of Modigliani, including elongated features and stylized eyes, combined with a distinct palette and depictions of hillside villages in Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: Una reseña artística destaca una exposición de Ernesto Lothar en la Galería Whyte que presenta retratos y figuras de habitantes de las cercanías de Sosúa, junto con paisajes tropicales de la República Dominicana. El texto describe a los pobladores locales como descendientes de los habitantes indígenas de la isla y de los colonos españoles y africanos llegados después de Colón. El crítico señala que la obra de Lothar refleja convenciones que recuerdan a Modigliani, entre ellas rasgos alargados y ojos estilizados, combinados con una paleta particular y representaciones de aldeas en las colinas de Santo Domingo.

records.headline: A five-member trade delegation from the Dominican Republic arrived
records.summary_en: A five-member trade delegation from the Dominican Republic arrived in New Orleans, predicting an increase in commercial traffic between their nation and the Louisiana port. The delegates anticipated that much of the Dominican trade routed through eastern ports during the war would shift to the Mississippi Valley due to lower operating costs compared to New York. Hosted by International House and the Association of Commerce, the group is led by Manuel Resumil Aragunde, president of the Ciudad Trujillo Chamber of Commerce.
records.summary_es: Una delegación comercial integrada por cinco representantes de la República Dominicana llegó a Nueva Orleans, anticipando un incremento en el tráfico mercantil entre su país y el puerto de Luisiana. Los delegados previeron que gran parte del comercio dominicano canalizado por puertos del este durante la guerra se trasladaría al valle del Misisipi debido a los costos operativos más bajos en comparación con Nueva York. Atendida por la International House y la Asociación de Comercio, la comitiva está encabezada por Manuel Resumil Aragunde, presidente de la Cámara de Comercio de Ciudad Trujillo.
