records.headline: Travelers arriving from Port-au-Prince described civil disturbances
records.summary_en: Travelers arriving from Port-au-Prince described civil disturbances that precipitated the collapse of the Haitian cabinet and the arrest of anti-government demonstrators, an Associated Press dispatch datelined Ciudad Trujillo reports. In a radio broadcast monitored in the Dominican capital, Haitian President Élie Lescot confirmed that he had accepted the resignations of his ministers. The unrest reportedly commenced on January 4 with the suppression of the youth journal La Ruche and the arrest of its editorial staff.
records.summary_es: Viajeros llegados de Puerto Príncipe describieron disturbios civiles que precipitaron la caída del gabinete haitiano y el arresto de manifestantes contrarios al gobierno, según un despacho de Associated Press con fecha de Ciudad Trujillo. En una transmisión radial captada en la capital dominicana, el presidente haitiano Élie Lescot confirmó que había aceptado la dimisión de sus ministros. Según se informó, los desórdenes comenzaron el 4 de enero con la clausura de la publicación juvenil La Ruche y la detención de su equipo editorial.

records.headline: According to Pan American Airways, former United States Ambassador

records.headline: An article in the California Eagle sharply criticizes dictator
records.summary_en: An article in the California Eagle sharply criticizes dictator Rafael Leonidas Trujillo, alleging that he acts against the interests of the Dominican Republic's predominantly colored majority by discouraging non-white immigration. The commentary accuses Trujillo of denying his African lineage by claiming ancestry from the early Spanish conquerors. It also refers to his past ties to the United States Marines who facilitated his rise to power.
records.summary_es: Un artículo en el California Eagle censura con dureza al dictador Rafael Leonidas Trujillo, alegando que actúa en contra de los intereses de la mayoría predominantemente de color de la República Dominicana al desalentar la inmigración no blanca. El comentario acusa a Trujillo de negar su linaje africano al atribuirse ascendencia de los antiguos conquistadores españoles. También hace referencia a sus vínculos pasados con los infantes de marina estadounidenses que facilitaron su llegada al poder.

records.headline: A commentary highlights star pitcher Leroy 'Satchel' Paige
records.summary_en: A commentary highlights star pitcher Leroy 'Satchel' Paige, recalling that his All-Stars team claimed the 1937 championship of the Dominican Republic and later won the Denver Post tournament wearing uniforms denoting their Trujillo title. The author emphasizes that Latin American leagues offered fairer conditions and higher compensation to Black ballplayers than the major leagues in the United States. Paige is quoted asserting that he would sooner reside in South America than return to playing under domestic Jim Crow restrictions.
records.summary_es: Un comentario destaca al célebre lanzador Leroy 'Satchel' Paige, recordando que su novena de Estrellas conquistó el campeonato de 1937 de la República Dominicana y más tarde ganó el torneo del Denver Post vistiendo uniformes alusivos a su título trujillista. El autor subraya que las ligas latinoamericanas ofrecían condiciones más justas y mayor compensación a los peloteros negros que las Grandes Ligas de los Estados Unidos. Se cita a Paige afirmando que preferiría residir en América del Sur antes que volver a jugar bajo las restricciones de segregación racial vigentes en el país.

records.headline: The United Nations General Assembly, during its London session
records.summary_en: The United Nations General Assembly, during its London session, approved plans for a memorial to Christopher Columbus to be constructed on the coast of the Dominican Republic at Ciudad Trujillo. The initiative was begun earlier by the Pan-American Union, with the 21 American republics expected to supply estimated funds of about $4,000,000. Designed by a young British architect whose model was shown in London, the project features a 100-foot central pile of masonry topped by a powerful beacon for ships and planes, with site clearing reported well under way.
records.summary_es: La Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas, durante su período de sesiones en Londres, aprobó los planos de un monumento conmemorativo a Cristóbal Colón que se construirá en la costa de la República Dominicana en Ciudad Trujillo. La iniciativa fue iniciada anteriormente por la Unión Panamericana, y se espera que las 21 repúblicas americanas aporten fondos estimados en unos $4,000,000. Diseñado por un joven arquitecto británico cuya maqueta se exhibió en Londres, el proyecto cuenta con una estructura central de mampostería de 100 pies rematada por una potente baliza para barcos y aviones, con el desmonte del terreno ya muy avanzado.

records.headline: Secretary of the Presidency of Nicaragua, and Senor Leopoldo Arguello Gil
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Dr. Sevilla of Nicaragua was scheduled to fly to the Dominican Republic to present his credentials to President Rafael Trujillo as the Nicaraguan Minister in Ciudad Trujillo. Sevilla was staying at the Roosevelt Hotel in Washington alongside legal adviser Leopoldo Arguello Gil before departing. The report also covered social and diplomatic activities involving Cuban and Venezuelan embassy officials.

Previo a su despegue, Sevilla se alojaba en el Roosevelt Hotel de Washington junto a su consultor jurídico Leopoldo Argüello Gil. La nota también pasó revista a reuniones de carácter social protagonizadas por diplomáticos adscritos a las embajadas de Cuba y Venezuela.

records.full_text:
Embassy Staff Changes Made In Corps Here

By Betty Milliken

Not for a long time has there been such an exodus of ambassadors and ministers from the Capital scene as there was during the past week. The occasion for this general departure was the dedication of Hyde Park, the late President Roosevelt's private residence, as a national shrine. Every foreign envoy in Washington who was able to be present at the ceremony was on hand for the occasion, most of them brought along their wives and many are remaining in New York over the week end.

The dean of the corps, Mr. Carlos Martins, with Mme. Martins, headed the foreign representation at the ceremony, and the Nicaraguan Ambassador, Dr. Guillermo Sevilla Sacasa, newly elected chairman of the governing board of the Pan American Union, not only represented his country but the Union as well.

Dr. Sevilla returned in time to be host at a stag cocktail party today from 5:30 to 7:30 o'clock at the embassy, when he will entertain in honor of two Nicaraguan government officials visiting Washington. Senor Jose Benito Ramirez, Secretary of the Presidency of Nicaragua, and Senor Leopoldo Arguello Gil, legal adviser to the Nicaraguan government, are accompanied by their wives and are staying at the Roosevelt Hotel until their departure Thursday.

Dr. Sevilla will leave by plane Tuesday for the Dominican Republic, to present his credentials to President Trujillo as Nicaraguan Minister in Ciudad Trujillo. He will return April 26.

The Cuban Ambassador and Senora de Belt have returned from the Hyde Park ceremonies, and while in New York were guests of honor at a luncheon given at the Waldorf-Astoria by the Pan-American Society and the Cuban Chamber of Commerce.

The Venezuelan Ambassador, Dr. Alfredo Machado-Hernandez, and Senora de Machado-Hernandez have with them at the Embassy their son and daughter-in-law, Dr. Alfredo Machado-Gomez and Senora de Machado-Gomez. Dr. Machado-Gomez has been appointed Second Secretary of the Embassy and he and his bride of eight months will be an attractive addition to the younger married set in the Capital.

Morgan, who performed numerous charitable operations for the underprivileged in the Dominican Republic without accepting payment. Dr. Morgan commended the Dominican government for its cooperation and health advancements, noting the presence of government hospitals in Trujillo City and Santiago prior to the construction of Morgan Hospital. Dr. W. T. Sanger of the Medical College of Virginia accompanied him to arrange personnel exchanges with the new Dominican institution.

El Dr. Morgan encomió la asistencia brindada por las autoridades dominicanas y las mejoras sanitarias del país, haciendo alusión a la existencia de nosocomios estatales en Ciudad Trujillo y Santiago de los Caballeros antes de la erección del Hospital Morgan. El Dr. W. T. Sanger, del Colegio Médico de Virginia, lo secundó para coordinar programas de intercambio de galenos y enfermeras con la flamante institución asistencial dominicana.

records.headline: Consumers can buy new Nash automobiles immediately from a local dealer
records.summary_en: Consumers can buy new Nash automobiles immediately from a local dealer instead of waiting on lengthy customer lists in the United States, correspondent John A. Thale reports, writing from Ciudad Trujillo. The dealership offered an 84-horsepower 4 door model selling for $2,200 and a 112-horsepower model at $2,500 from a first shipment of 15 cars, of which six had not yet been sold. Bringing a vehicle back to the United States would cost about $125 in boat shipping to New York plus an American embassy-advised customs duty of 42 per cent.

El concesionario ofrecía un modelo de 4 puertas y 84 caballos de fuerza a la venta por $2,200 y uno de 112 caballos de fuerza a $2,500 de un primer envío de 15 vehículos, de los cuales seis aún no se habían vendido. Llevar un vehículo de regreso a los Estados Unidos costaría unos $125 de flete marítimo a Nueva York más un arancel aduanero del 42 por ciento indicado por la embajada estadounidense.

records.headline: Dispatches from correspondent Mr. Thale describe travelers comparing
records.summary_en: Dispatches from correspondent Mr. Thale describe travelers comparing conditions in the Dominican Republic to prewar Germany, noting that Dominicans viewed President Trujillo with careful awe and were reluctant to discuss politics or mention the president's name in public. While crediting the Trujillo administration with hospital construction, slum clearance, and an efficient corps of officials, the reports highlighted stringent domestic censorship protecting Trujillo from criticism. Foreign periodicals carrying even mildly critical remarks about El Benefactor were reportedly confiscated upon reaching Dominican ports of entry.
records.summary_es: Despachos del corresponsal señor Thale señalan que varios viajeros comparaban las condiciones de la República Dominicana con las de la Alemania previa a la guerra, observando que los dominicanos miraban al presidente Trujillo con un temor cuidadoso y evitaban hablar de política o pronunciar el nombre del gobernante en público. Aunque se reconocía al gobierno de Trujillo la construcción de hospitales, la erradicación de tugurios y un cuerpo eficiente de funcionarios, los informes destacaban una rigurosa censura interna que protegía a Trujillo de cualquier crítica. Las publicaciones periódicas extranjeras con comentarios siquiera levemente críticos sobre El Benefactor eran presuntamente confiscadas al llegar a los puertos dominicanos de entrada.

records.summary_en: The Midland Journal reported on upcoming celebrations marking the 450th anniversary of the founding of Santo Domingo, featuring a historic pageant and an address by President Rafael Trujillo. The article noted that the capital was rebuilt along modern lines following a devastating hurricane in 1930 and subsequently renamed Ciudad Trujillo by its citizens despite Trujillo's objections. It also praised the republic's fertile agriculture and highlighted its strong standing in Washington following its early war declarations against Japan and Germany in December 1941.
records.summary_es: El *Midland Journal* informó sobre los preparativos para conmemorar el 450.º aniversario de la fundación de la ciudad de Santo Domingo, programa que comprendería una representación alegórica de valor histórico y el discurso del mandatario Rafael Trujillo. El artículo consignó que la capital había renacido bajo directrices modernas luego del desolador huracán de 1930, siendo rebautizada como Ciudad Trujillo por voluntad popular no obstante la renuencia inicial de Trujillo. Destacó asimismo la fecunda fertilidad agrícola nacional y el sólido predicamento de que gozaba el régimen en Washington tras su pronta declaración de guerra a Japón y Alemania en diciembre de 1941.

records.headline: A commentary details plans for the New World's largest monument
records.summary_en: A commentary details plans for the New World's largest monument to Christopher Columbus, situated on a 2,000-acre site near Ciudad Trujillo at the mouth of the Ozama River. The mile-long memorial will comprise a recumbent cross of pink-yellow stone bearing a 1,200-foot cruciform structure that combines a shrine for Columbus's remains with a revolving beacon for ships and aircraft. Estimated to cost around $5,000,000, the undertaking is to be funded jointly by the governments and peoples of the Americas, with financing proposed through special commemorative stamps.
records.summary_es: Un comentario detalla los planes para erigir el monumento más grande del Nuevo Mundo en honor a Cristóbal Colón, situado en un predio de 2,000 acres cerca de Ciudad Trujillo, en la desembocadura del río Ozama. El monumento de una milla de longitud constará de una cruz yacente de piedra amarillo-rosácea sobre la que se levantará una estructura cruciforme de 1,200 pies que combinará un santuario para los restos de Colón con una baliza giratoria para barcos y aeronaves. Con un costo calculado en alrededor de $5,000,000, la obra será financiada de manera conjunta por los gobiernos y pueblos de las Américas, proponiéndose su recaudación mediante sellos postales conmemorativos especiales.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported on an interview with President Rafael Trujillo in which he announced plans to encourage a two- or three-party system with free elections during the 450th anniversary of Santo Domingo. Trujillo denied operating as a dictator, asserting that his critics had private motives, and pledged to grant amnesty to all political refugees to allow their safe return. He stated that the nation had achieved stability ahead of the presidential election scheduled for May 16, 1947.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* reprodujo una entrevista concedida por el presidente Rafael Trujillo en la cual hizo pública su intención de promover un sistema bipartidista o tripartidista con sufragio irrestricto en el marco del 450.º aniversario de Santo Domingo. Trujillo negó tachaduras de autócrata sosteniendo que sus detractores obedecían a móviles inconfesables, y prometió conceder indulto y amnistía general a los refugiados políticos para garantizar su retorno al terruño. Afirmó enfáticamente que el país gozaba de sosiego institucional ante las elecciones presidenciales convocadas para el 16 de mayo de 1947.

records.headline: A diplomatic affairs column reports that a new weekly bulletin
records.summary_en: A diplomatic affairs column reports that a new weekly bulletin from the Dominican embassy announces the upcoming celebration of Ciudad Trujillo's 450th anniversary next Sunday. The writer describes personal visits to the capital founded by the brother of Columbus in 1496, recalling its cathedral containing Christopher Columbus's bones and the 15th Century castle where his brother resided when Santo Domingo was among the earliest permanent Western settlements. While acknowledging that some American officials criticize Rafael Trujillo as a dictator, the author notes that Trujillo points to extensive material progress and seeks to establish the republic as a Caribbean winter resort.
records.summary_es: Una columna de asuntos diplomáticos informa que un nuevo boletín semanal de la embajada dominicana anuncia la próxima conmemoración del 450.º aniversario de Ciudad Trujillo el domingo siguiente. El articulista relata visitas personales a la capital fundada por el hermano de Colón en 1496, recordando su catedral que alberga los restos de Cristóbal Colón y el alcázar del siglo XV donde residió su hermano cuando Santo Domingo era uno de los primeros asentamientos permanentes de Occidente. Si bien reconoce que algunos funcionarios estadounidenses critican a Rafael Trujillo como dictador, el autor señala que Trujillo resalta un gran progreso material y busca posicionar a la república como un destino invernal caribeño.

records.headline: Travelers arriving by air and sea gather to mark the anniversary of the founding of Ciudad
records.summary_en: Travelers arriving by air and sea gather to mark the anniversary of the founding of Ciudad Trujillo, originally established in 1496 by Bartolome Columbus as Santo Domingo. Program events include a reenactment of Columbus's landing, the blessing of a commemorative plaque by Archbishop Ricardo Pittini at a replica of the tree where Bartolome Columbus landed, and an exhibition of church relics including an altar bell designed by Benvenuto Cellini and the original cross from the battle of Santo Cerro. The article adds that two million Dominican citizens take pride in their capital, which was rebuilt along modern lines and renamed after President Trujillo following its complete demolition by a 1930 hurricane.
records.summary_es: Viajeros llegados por aire y mar se congregan para conmemorar el aniversario de la fundación de Ciudad Trujillo, establecida originalmente en 1496 por Bartolomé Colón como Santo Domingo. Los actos previstos incluyen una recreación del desembarco de Colón, la bendición de una placa conmemorativa por parte del arzobispo Ricardo Pittini en una réplica del árbol donde desembarcó Bartolomé Colón, y una muestra de reliquias eclesiásticas que exhibe una campana de altar diseñada por Benvenuto Cellini y la cruz original de la batalla de Santo Cerro. El artículo añade que dos millones de ciudadanos dominicanos se enorgullecen de su capital, que fue reconstruida con criterios modernos y rebautizada en honor al presidente Trujillo tras haber sido destruida por completo por un huracán en 1930.

records.headline: Trujillo’s Accomplishments Yet the task of modernizing the birthplace of the New World
records.summary_en: The Springfield Weekly Republican reported on the extensive modernization of the Dominican Republic under President Rafael Trujillo over a sixteen-year span achieved without foreign loans. Improvements included a twenty percent decrease in illiteracy, hundreds of newly built schools, seventy new bridges, and irrigation projects reclaiming 85,000 acres. The article noted that the rebuilt capital, renamed Ciudad Trujillo by citizens, was growing into a major Caribbean tourist destination.
records.summary_es: El *Springfield Weekly Republican* reportó las profundas transformaciones de progreso material logradas por la República Dominicana bajo el mandato de dieciséis años del presidente Rafael Trujillo, realizadas sin necesidad de préstamos extranjeros. Los adelantos abarcaban una reducción del veinte por ciento en el analfabetismo, centenares de escuelas recién levantadas, setenta puentes nuevos e infraestructuras de regadío que recuperaron 85.000 acres de tierra. El informe agregaba que la reconstruida capital, rebautizada Ciudad Trujillo por la población, se afianzaba como un emporio turístico caribeño de primer orden.
records.passage: capital were unpaved. Agriculture and industry were languishing under a moral as well as economic depression. Trujillo's Accomplishments Yet the task of modernizing the birthplace of the New World was accomplished in the brief span of 16 years without once resorting to foreign loans. Illiteracy dropped 20 per cent due to the building of hundreds of new schools and the allotment of 13 per cent of the national budget to furthering education. Beautifully paved roads and 70 new bridges put formerly isolated regions into easy communication with one another and with the capital. Vast irrigation projects brought 85,000 acres of land under cultivation. Factories employ twice as many people and produce three times as many exportable items as previously. New hospitals. clothing manufacture, water works, schools and public buildings transformed an ancient city of ruins into a modern metropolis. Little wonder that a grateful people over-rode the protests of their president and gave Santo Domingo the name it bears today—Ciudad Trujillo. Home of Columbus The Dominican Republic occupies the eastern three-quarters of the island of Santo Domingo- an area slightly larger than Kentucky. Ciudad Trujillo, its capital, straddles the mouth of the Ozama river and is only four hours by air from Miami. The city threatens to rival Rio de Janiero, Havana and Miami as a year-round playground for American tourists. records.headline: A major Caribbean earthquake that produced tremors for two hours
records.summary_en: A major Caribbean earthquake that produced tremors for two hours after the initial shock struck five Dominican communities: Puerto Plata, Santiago, Moca, Macoris, and San Francisco. In Moca, the municipal hall and church collapsed in ruins, with extensive destruction among commercial stores and residences. While southern Ciudad Trujillo reported only slight tremors, seismographs at the United States naval base at Guantanamo, Cuba, approximately 300 miles west of Puerto Plata, were disabled by the force of the upheaval.

records.headline: Seismologists evaluating a powerful Caribbean earthquake suggested
records.summary_en: Seismologists evaluating a powerful Caribbean earthquake suggested that its epicenter lay north of Santo Domingo and northwest of Puerto Rico in what they hoped was an uninhabited area. Father Joseph Lynch reported the temblor was the largest recorded during the 36 years since his observatory's instrument was installed, with the force also dislodging the seismograph pointer at Weston College in Massachusetts. The report discusses the regional geology of the West Indies and notes the Turks and Caicos islands located north of the island of Santo Domingo, which includes Haiti and the Dominican Republic.
records.summary_es: Sismólogos que evaluaron un potente terremoto en el Caribe indicaron que su epicentro se situó al norte de Santo Domingo y al noroeste de Puerto Rico, en lo que esperaban fuera una zona deshabitada. El padre Joseph Lynch informó que el temblor fue el mayor registrado durante los 36 años transcurridos desde la instalación del instrumento de su observatorio, y su fuerza también desplazó la aguja del sismógrafo del Weston College en Massachusetts. El informe analiza la geología regional de las Antillas y menciona las islas Turcas y Caicos situadas al norte de la isla de Santo Domingo, que comprende a Haití y la República Dominicana.

records.headline: Preliminary reports indicate that a major Caribbean earthquake
records.summary_en: Preliminary reports indicate that a major Caribbean earthquake spanning a 600-mile area generated a towering tidal wave that swept into Puerto Plata, a northern Dominican seaport of 4500, traveling a considerable distance inland. Five northern towns suffered severe destruction from the initial quake at 1:49 p. m. Sunday, with damage extending across northern Santo Domingo Island in both the Dominican Republic and Haiti. In Ciudad Trujillo on the southern coast, where afternoon shaking was slight, a renewed tremor at 10 p. m. sparked public panic.

Cinco localidades del norte sufrieron graves destrozos por el sismo inicial registrado a la 1:49 p. m. del domingo, con daños que se extendieron a lo largo del norte de la isla de Santo Domingo tanto en la República Dominicana como en Haití. En Ciudad Trujillo, en la costa sur, donde la sacudida diurna fue leve, un nuevo temblor a las 10 p. m. desató el pánico público.

records.summary_en: Following a violent regional earthquake, reports indicated that five separate tremors shook Ciudad Trujillo, the capital of the Dominican Republic, with one shock lasting 45 seconds. Pan American Airways reported that its airport at Ciudad Trujillo recorded a morning tremor of slight intensity. Dr. Marion Gilmore suggested the epicenter lay in the Milwaukee Deep, located 30,246 feet below sea level and 50 miles off the Dominican Republic's northeastern coast. The temblor was sufficiently severe to disable seismographs in St. Louis, Puerto Rico, Cuba, and Trinidad.

El doctor Marion Gilmore sugirió que el epicentro se ubicaba en la fosa Milwaukee Deep, situada a 30,246 pies bajo el nivel del mar y a 50 millas de la costa noreste de la República Dominicana. records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that a violent
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that a violent earthquake and exceptionally high waves inflicted widespread destruction across 11 Dominican towns on Sunday, claiming at least two lives. The coastal town of Matanzas was reported completely flooded by sea waves, while Nagua and Miches were partly inundated. In Moca, the municipal palace and market were destroyed, while San Francisco de Macoris suffered the collapse of 25 to 35 private homes with one death, Santiago sustained severe damage to institutional buildings, and the Cibao agricultural region incurred thousands of dollars in property losses.

records.headline: Eye witness reports received today from Matanzas on the North Coast
records.summary_en: Eyewitness reports from Matanzas, on the north coast, said a tidal wave from Sunday's earthquake swept as much as a mile inland, catching even a party fleeing by automobile, and left only eight of the town's 300 houses standing. Residents had taken refuge in trees and high places, and reports from Matanzas and Nagua said frightened inhabitants in the forests were suffering from hunger, with authorities considering dropping food from airplanes, as wrecked communications made the damage across more than 11 towns hard to assess.
records.summary_es: Testimonios desde Matanzas, en la costa norte, decían que un maremoto provocado por el terremoto del domingo penetró hasta una milla tierra adentro, alcanzó incluso a un grupo que huía en automóvil y dejó en pie solo ocho de las 300 casas del pueblo. Los vecinos se habían refugiado en árboles y lugares altos, y los informes de Matanzas y Nagua decían que habitantes asustados en los bosques padecían hambre, mientras las autoridades consideraban lanzar alimentos desde aviones y las comunicaciones destruidas dificultaban evaluar los daños en más de 11 pueblos.
records.passage: range, stricken Sunday by an earthquake and tidal wave which took a toll of at least two dead and damaged more than 11 towns in this Carribean Republic. Eye witness reports received today from Matanzas on the North Coast, said a tidal wave swept inland as much as a mile so swiftly that it caught a party fleeing in an automobile. The eyewitness said the residents had been forewarned and had taken refuge in trees and high places. Only eight of the 300 houses in Matanzas were reported left standing. Wrecked telegraph and communication facilities made it difficult to get a clear picture of the damage wrought by the quake which apparently centered in the deepest point in the Atlantic ocean, approximately 50 miles off the east coast of the Dominican Republic. Reports from the Matanzas and Nagua regions said that frightened inhabitants had taken refuge in the forests and were suffering from hunger. Authorities were considering dropping food from airplanes. Meanwhile apprehension gripped the Republic as new tremors shook the ground here yesterday and blacked out radio communications for several hours. records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that President Rafael Trujillo directed relief operations across the Dominican Republic following a severe earthquake, deploying the military, police, and Red Cross to stricken communities including Matanzas, Nagua, Moca, and San Francisco de Macoris. Santiago suffered extensive building damage and one death, while another casualty occurred in San Francisco de Macoris. Neighboring Haiti reported minor effects in Port-au-Prince but significant destruction across northern border towns.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el mandatario Rafael Trujillo encabezó personalmente las labores de rescate en toda la República Dominicana a raíz del feroz terremoto, comisionando tropas del ejército, agentes policiales y brigadas de la Cruz Roja a las poblaciones más flageladas, entre ellas Matanzas, Nagua, Moca y San Francisco de Macorís. En Santiago se verificaron serios derrumbes y una víctima fatal, registrándose otro muerto en San Francisco de Macorís. En el colindante territorio de Haití se sintieron efectos menores en Puerto Príncipe, pero se reportaron considerables averías en los distritos de la frontera norte.
records.passage: hard hit by Sunday's catastrophe Most of the suffering was reported to be in the interior of the country. Chambers of Commerce of the Spanish and Dominican colonies and the Association of Architects and Engineers have offered their co-operation to the government in saving and reconstructing damaged buildings. Advices from Haiti, where communications have been reestablished, said Sunday's quake did little damage to Port au Prince, but caused considerable damage in the smaller towns. In the northern section of Haiti nearest the Dominican Republic more than 50 houses were reported badly damaged and several churches were devastated. In the village of Le Borgne, nine houses were wrecked with a loss of approximately $25,000. Services Stand By to Aid. In the Dominican capital President Raphael Trujillo Molina directed the dispatching of aid to the stricken regions, while officials of the army, police force, Fire department and Red Cross stood by in Mosa, San Francisco de Macoris. Matanzas and the Nagua regions to aid the populace. Another severely hit section was Santiago, which, with a population of 50.000, was the largest city in the affected area. records.headline: An editorial note discusses a submarine Caribbean earthquake
records.summary_en: An editorial note discusses a submarine Caribbean earthquake powerful enough to disable seismographs in St. Louis and New Orleans, noting that it caused its principal damage in Puerto Rico and Santo Domingo. A massive tidal wave struck landward, raising fears of heavy casualties that could not be verified because of disrupted communications. Seismologists calculated that the tremor originated in the Atlantic's area of greatest depth, approximately fifty miles off the Dominican Republic.
records.summary_es: Una nota editorial analiza un terremoto submarino en el Caribe con intensidad suficiente para inutilizar los sismógrafos en St. Louis y Nueva Orleans, observando que causó sus principales estragos en Puerto Rico y Santo Domingo. Un enorme maremoto avanzó hacia la costa, despertando temores de numerosas víctimas que no podían confirmarse debido al colapso de las comunicaciones. records.headline: Official reports state that a tidal wave in Bahia Escocesa leveled
records.summary_en: Official reports state that a tidal wave in Bahia Escocesa leveled the Dominican communities of Matanzas, Nagua, Arroyo Salado, and El Bajio, bringing the confirmed death toll in those four towns to 28. To counter severe food shortages following the disaster, President Trujillo issued a prohibition against the export of any foodstuffs. Further aftershocks struck Cabrera and Bajio, where floodwaters reached a depth of two feet, while renewed tremors were also reported in Puerto Plata and Las Lianas.

Con el propósito de enfrentar la grave escasez de alimentos provocada por el desastre, el presidente Trujillo decretó la prohibición de exportar cualquier tipo de víveres. Nuevas réplicas sacudieron Cabrera y Bajío, donde las aguas alcanzaron dos pies de profundidad, mientras que se registraron otros temblores en Puerto Plata y Las Lianas.

records.summary_en: A photo caption reports on the aftermath of an earthquake and tidal wave that caused extensive damage across the Dominican Republic. The image shows a crowd on a street in Ciudad Trujillo pointing out a large fracture that opened in a building during the tremors. The notice mentions that adjacent Caribbean islands and coastal sectors of northern South America also felt the impact of the shocks and high water.

La nota agrega que las islas caribeñas vecinas y los sectores costeros del norte de Sudamérica también experimentaron el impacto de los temblores y las grandes olas.

records.headline: An earth tremor struck Ciudad Trujillo at 8:30 a.m. on August
records.summary_en: An earth tremor struck Ciudad Trujillo at 8:30 a.m. on August 8, sending residents fleeing in search of safer places. The tremor was part of a series that began the previous weekend, with a spokesman measuring its intensity at two-thirds that of the original quake on Aug. 4. An accompanying note indicated that the dispatch had arrived before United States quake reports, leaving it uncertain whether the tremor was followed by another.
records.summary_es: Un temblor de tierra sacudió Ciudad Trujillo a las 8:30 a. m. del 8 de agosto, lo que provocó que los residentes huyeran en busca de lugares más seguros. El sismo formaba parte de una serie iniciada el fin de semana anterior, y un portavoz calculó su intensidad en dos tercios de la del sismo original del 4 de agosto. Una nota complementaria indicaba que el despacho había llegado antes que los informes sísmicos de Estados Unidos, por lo que no se tenía certeza de si al temblor le había seguido otro.

records.headline: President Rafael Trujillo decreed an immediate ban on the export of all
records.summary_en: President Rafael Trujillo decreed an immediate ban on the export of all foodstuffs on Wednesday as the nation began repairing destruction caused by three days of earthquakes and tidal waves. The seismic disasters had killed 30 persons across the country. Official authorities issued the food restriction to address acute shortages resulting from the catastrophe.
records.summary_es: El presidente Rafael Trujillo decretó el miércoles la prohibición inmediata de exportar cualquier alimento, mientras la nación comenzaba las tareas de reparación de los daños causados por tres días de terremotos y maremotos. Los desastres sísmicos habían provocado la muerte de 30 personas en el país. Las autoridades oficiales emitieron la orden sobre alimentos con el fin de enfrentar la aguda escasez provocada por la catástrofe.

records.headline: In the wake of Sunday's devastating earthquake, rescue teams
records.summary_en: In the wake of Sunday's devastating earthquake, rescue teams rushed toward the valley south of the Monte Christi range, where early reports indicated at least two dead. Disrupted telephone, telegraph, and radio communications left stricken interior communities entirely cut off from the outside world for many hours. Meanwhile, a Pan American Airways pilot arriving in Miami reported that two towns on the north coast had been completely wiped out by the initial quake and tidal wave, while observatory records located the epicenter in the Atlantic Ocean approximately 50 miles off the northeast coast.
records.summary_es: Tras el devastador terremoto del domingo, equipos de rescate se apresuraron hacia el valle situado al sur de la cordillera de Monte Christi, donde los primeros informes indicaban al menos dos muertos. La interrupción de las comunicaciones telefónicas, telegráficas y de radio mantuvo a las comunidades del interior incomunicadas por completo del mundo exterior durante muchas horas. Entretanto, un piloto de Pan American Airways que llegó a Miami informó que dos pueblos de la costa norte habían sido totalmente arrasados por el terremoto y el maremoto iniciales, mientras que los registros de los observatorios ubicaron el epicentro en el océano Atlántico, aproximadamente a 50 millas de la costa noreste.

records.headline: Earthquakes and accompanying tidal waves battered northeastern
records.summary_en: Earthquakes and accompanying tidal waves battered northeastern Dominican coastal communities for a third straight day, bringing the known death toll to 22 as terrified residents fled into interior forests. Twenty deaths occurred in the adjoining settlements of Bajio and Cabrera on Scotch Bay, where Bajio was inundated under two feet of water, adding to earlier single fatalities reported in Santiago and San Francisco de Macoris. Government airplanes dropped food and clothing to refugees from Matanzas sheltering in nearby woods, where an eight-foot wall of water had destroyed 424 houses.
records.summary_es: Terremotos y maremotos acompañantes azotaron las comunidades de la costa noreste dominicana por tercer día consecutivo, lo que elevó la cifra conocida de muertos a 22 mientras los residentes aterrorizados huían hacia los bosques del interior. Veinte muertes ocurrieron en las poblaciones contiguas de Bajio y Cabrera, en la bahía Escocesa, donde Bajio quedó anegada bajo dos pies de agua, sumándose a víctimas individuales reportadas anteriormente en Santiago y San Francisco de Macorís. Aviones gubernamentales lanzaron alimentos y ropa a refugiados de Matanzas que se resguardaban en bosques cercanos, donde una muralla de agua de ocho pies había destruido 424 casas.

records.headline: Seismologists and United States naval observers described a fresh
records.summary_en: Seismologists and United States naval observers described a fresh earthquake affecting the Dominican Republic as the second major crustal slippage of the week, matching the intensity of Sunday's convulsion. Geophysicist Marion H. Gilmore stated that the tremor broke the galvanometer at the Guantanamo Bay naval weather station in Cuba, leaving the device disabled after 9:34 a.m. EDT. Continued tremors were logged in the region late Thursday by the naval hurricane service through 2:36 p.m. EDT, while airline pilot William Karraker landed in Ciudad Trujillo nine minutes after the initial shock.
records.summary_es: Sismólogos y observadores navales de Estados Unidos calificaron un nuevo terremoto que afectó a la República Dominicana como el segundo gran desplazamiento terrestre de la semana, igualando en intensidad la sacudida del domingo. El geofísico Marion H. Gilmore afirmó que el temblor rompió el galvanómetro en la estación meteorológica naval de la bahía de Guantánamo, en Cuba, dejando el aparato inutilizado desde las 9:34 a. m. EDT. El servicio de huracanes de la Armada continuó registrando sismos en la zona hasta la tarde del jueves a las 2:36 p. m. EDT, mientras que el piloto de aerolínea William Karraker aterrizó en Ciudad Trujillo nueve minutos después de la primera sacudida.

records.headline: Panic-stricken residents leapt from balconies into the streets
records.summary_en: Panic-stricken residents leapt from balconies into the streets after a 40-second tremor rattled the Dominican Republic yesterday morning, with many refusing to spend the night indoors. In Ciudad Trujillo, the American Embassy requested doctors and nurses from San Juan naval headquarters, while 15 physicians arrived from Curaçao and the Red Cross erected emergency relief camps. Aerial observers surveying the battered northern coast noted that collapsing cliffs had slid into the sea to reshape the shoreline, while the course of a river between Julia Molina and Cabrera was visibly altered.
records.summary_es: Residentes presas del pánico saltaron desde balcones hacia las calles después de que un temblor de 40 segundos sacudiera la República Dominicana la mañana de ayer, y muchos se negaron a pasar la noche bajo techo. En Ciudad Trujillo, la Embajada de Estados Unidos solicitó médicos y enfermeras a la comandancia naval de San Juan, al tiempo que 15 médicos llegaban desde Curazao y la Cruz Roja instalaba campamentos de socorro de emergencia. records.headline: Receding coastal waters heralded another destructive tidal wave
records.summary_en: Receding coastal waters heralded another destructive tidal wave that battered the devastated town of Matanzas yesterday, sending residents fleeing as they cleared debris from Sunday's disaster. The cumulative death toll from sea and earth tremors since Sunday reached at least 66, while United States Navy patrol bombers flew in emergency relief supplies. In Ciudad Trujillo, false rumors of an approaching tidal wave caused three thousand people at a thanksgiving mass meeting to bolt in panic, during which one man was killed after being struck by a truck.

El saldo acumulado de muertos por los sismos y el oleaje desde el domingo llegó al menos a 66, al tiempo que bombarderos de patrulla de la Armada de Estados Unidos trasladaban provisiones de socorro. En Ciudad Trujillo, falsos rumores sobre la aproximación de un maremoto hicieron que tres mil personas reunidas en una misa de acción de gracias huyeran presas del pánico, suceso en el que un hombre murió atropellado por un camión.

records.headline: Fresh earth shocks jolted the Dominican Republic at 3:20 and 8:05 a.m.
records.summary_en: Fresh earth shocks jolted the Dominican Republic at 3:20 and 8:05 a.m., as authorities attributed the ongoing upheaval to a shifting seabed in the Atlantic Ocean 50 miles northeast of the island at a depth of 28,680 feet. President Rafael L. Trujillo Molina urgently contacted seismologists at Fordham University to trace the progression of the shocks while disrupted communications impeded damage assessments in northern provinces. Meanwhile, a Red Cross brigade arrived along the northern coast to distribute food, and five churches in Ciudad Trujillo were ordered closed after sustaining structural damage.

records.headline: Continuing earthquakes and towering waves devastated the northern
records.summary_en: Continuing earthquakes and towering waves devastated the northern Dominican Republic, leaving at least 73 persons dead and 20,000 homeless since the initial shocks on Sunday. Mild tremors recurred across most of the republic approximately every five minutes, driving intense terror throughout the region surrounding Scotch Bay (Bahia Escocesa). Coastal towns including Matanzas, Puerto Plata, Batey, Samana, and Sanchez were entirely deserted, as displaced populations took refuge in trees, caves, and nearby hills.
records.summary_es: Continuos terremotos y olas gigantescas devastaron el norte de la República Dominicana, dejando al menos 73 personas muertas y 20 000 sin hogar desde los sismos iniciales del domingo. Temblores leves se repetían en la mayor parte de la república aproximadamente cada cinco minutos, desatando un intenso terror en toda la región circundante a la bahía Escocesa. Localidades costeras como Matanzas, Puerto Plata, Batey, Samaná y Sánchez quedaron totalmente desiertas, mientras las poblaciones desplazadas se refugiaban en árboles, cuevas y colinas cercanas.

records.headline: Two additional shocks renewed severe terror across northern
records.summary_en: Two additional shocks renewed severe terror across northern Dominican provinces on August 10, compounding disaster tolls of 73 persons dead and 20,000 homeless over a six-day ordeal. Swollen streams washed out critical bridges and roadways, severely obstructing government operations to deliver desperately needed food to affected populations. Shortages of food, clothing, and medicine were particularly desperate around Scotch Bay (Bahia Escocesa), where ongoing tremors and persistent false alarms further intensified local panic. The government threatened punishment for those guilty of spreading the false reports, and more than 80 persons had already been prosecuted for relaying them. The new tremors were felt at 4 a.m. and 6:50 a.m., but they did not add appreciably to the damage inflicted throughout the week. In one of the hardest hit communities, the northern city of Bajio, a revised death toll showed that 39 persons had been killed by the tidal wave and that 139 had been injured; previously the toll for the town had been reported at 50 dead. In the Almacious section, an entire rice field was uprooted and carried several miles. The series of shocks began last Sunday and brought a devastating tidal wave in their wake; they were believed caused by a shift in the bed of the Atlantic at its deepest point, 50 miles northeast of the island. Every inhabitant of the shattered coastal towns of Matanzas, Puerto Plata, Batey Samaná and Sánchez had been evacuated; many refugees from these destroyed towns live in trees and caves in the hills nearby, and the Red Cross refugee camps in the northern provinces were not sufficient for the thousands of homeless. Travelers from the Dominican Republic in San Juan, Puerto Rico, said virtually all the houses in Matanzas, which had a population of 1,000, were washed away in the tidal wave, and the destruction was equally as severe in Julia Molina and San Francisco de Macorís. The government had sent 10 planes across country to drop medical supplies and food to more than 20,000 homeless refugees camping in the hills along the quake and tidal wave stricken north coast. The only casualty in Ciudad Trujillo from the quakes resulted when a man hid under a truck during a minor tremblor and the truck ran over him and killed him.
records.summary_es: Dos sacudidas adicionales reavivaron el intenso terror en las provincias del norte dominicano el 10 de agosto, agravando un balance de 73 personas muertas y 20 000 damnificados a lo largo de seis días de tragedia. Crecidas de arroyos arrasaron puentes y caminos fundamentales, obstaculizando gravemente las tareas del gobierno para transportar alimentos indispensables a las poblaciones afectadas. La escasez de comida, ropa y medicamentos era especialmente crítica en los alrededores de la bahía Escocesa, donde las continuas réplicas y los insistentes falsos rumores agravaron aún más el pánico colectivo. El gobierno amenazó con castigar a los culpables de difundir los falsos informes, y más de 80 personas ya habían sido procesadas por transmitirlos. Los nuevos temblores se sintieron a las 4 a.m. y a las 6:50 a.m., pero no aumentaron apreciablemente los daños infligidos durante la semana. En una de las comunidades más castigadas, la ciudad norteña de Bajio, un balance revisado mostró que 39 personas habían muerto por el maremoto y 139 habían resultado heridas; antes se había informado de 50 muertos en la población. En la sección de Almacious, un campo de arroz entero fue arrancado de raíz y arrastrado varias millas. La serie de sacudidas comenzó el domingo anterior y trajo en su estela un maremoto devastador; se creía que fueron causadas por un desplazamiento del lecho del Atlántico en su punto más profundo, a 50 millas al noreste de la isla. Todos los habitantes de las destrozadas poblaciones costeras de Matanzas, Puerto Plata, Batey Samaná y Sánchez habían sido evacuados; muchos refugiados de esas poblaciones destruidas viven en árboles y cuevas de las colinas cercanas, y los campamentos de refugiados de la Cruz Roja en las provincias del norte no eran suficientes para los miles de damnificados. Viajeros procedentes de la República Dominicana en San Juan, Puerto Rico, dijeron que prácticamente todas las casas de Matanzas, que tenía una población de 1,000, fueron arrasadas por el maremoto, y que la destrucción fue igualmente severa en Julia Molina y San Francisco de Macorís. El gobierno había enviado 10 aviones a través del país para lanzar suministros médicos y alimentos a más de 20,000 refugiados sin hogar acampados en las colinas a lo largo de la costa norte azotada por el terremoto y el maremoto. La única víctima en Ciudad Trujillo a causa de los temblores fue un hombre que se escondió bajo un camión durante un temblor menor y el camión lo atropelló y lo mató.

records.summary_en: Total evacuation was carried out across the devastated northern coastal communities of Matanzas, Puerto Plata, Batey, Samana, and Sanchez, forcing thousands of homeless residents to shelter in caves and trees. In Puerto Rico, arriving travelers reported that an immense tidal wave had destroyed almost every structure in Matanzas, which had a population of 1,000, with comparable destruction hitting Julia Molina and San Francisco de Macoris. Associated Press correspondent Roger Greene stated that the Dominican government dispatched 10 planes carrying food and medical supplies to over 20,000 displaced persons along the coast, while the only casualty in Ciudad Trujillo occurred when an individual hiding beneath a truck was accidentally run over.

records.headline: Upon arriving in Miami from Ciudad Trujillo, New Orleans international
records.summary_en: Upon arriving in Miami from Ciudad Trujillo, New Orleans international relations director Rafael Urruela maintained that recent earthquake damage had been greatly overstated, insisting the greatest toll was to public morale rather than infrastructure. Urruela surveyed damaged zones alongside New Orleans businessmen and estimated the total number of homeless at no more than 3,000, asserting that destroyed dwellings were mostly frail structures and that destruction in major cities was nonexistent. Meanwhile, the American Red Cross prepared to execute emergency relief measures once field director H. Edward Russel completed his tour of the affected areas from San Juan.
records.summary_es: Al llegar a Miami procedente de Ciudad Trujillo, el director de relaciones internacionales de Nueva Orleans, Rafael Urruela, sostuvo que los daños del reciente terremoto habían sido sumamente exagerados, afirmando que el mayor perjuicio afectó a la moral ciudadana más que a las construcciones. Urruela recorrió las zonas damnificadas junto a empresarios de Nueva Orleans y calculó que el número de personas sin hogar no superaba las 3000, asegurando que las viviendas destruidas eran en su mayoría edificaciones endebles y que la destrucción en las grandes urbes fue nula. Mientras tanto, la Cruz Roja estadounidense preparaba la ejecución de operativos de auxilio en cuanto su director de campo H. Edward Russel concluyera su recorrido por las zonas afectadas desde San Juan.

records.headline: Although an earth tremor was felt at 4:31 a.m. on August 12
records.summary_en: Although an earth tremor was felt at 4:31 a.m. on August 12, seismic activity across the Dominican Republic showed a marked decrease in frequency and strength over the previous 48 hours. The most recent shock caused no reported destruction after eight days of terror inaugurated by the August 4 earthquake and tidal waves. Restoration of communication lines with northern and northeastern districts progressed, allowing the government to intensify emergency relief operations delivering food and medicine to 20,000 homeless individuals.
records.summary_es: A pesar de que se percibió un temblor de tierra a las 4:31 a. m. del 12 de agosto, la actividad sísmica en la República Dominicana mostró una notable disminución en frecuencia e intensidad durante las 48 horas previas. La sacudida más reciente no ocasionó daños tras ocho días de pánico desatados por el terremoto y los maremotos del 4 de agosto. Las labores de restablecimiento de las líneas de comunicación con las regiones del norte y noreste avanzaron, permitiendo al gobierno intensificar las tareas de socorro y distribuir víveres y medicinas a 20 000 damnificados sin hogar.

records.headline: The American Red Cross dispatched a planeload of emergency medical supplies
records.summary_en: The American Red Cross dispatched a planeload of emergency medical supplies from San Juan, Puerto Rico, to the earthquake and tidal wave disaster zone along the northern coast of the Dominican Republic. Red Cross representative H. E. Russell stated that the shipment included hundreds of pounds of antitoxin, vaccine, tetanus toxoids, sulfa drugs, and quinine to combat disease outbreaks threatening thousands of homeless refugees. In one camp of 500 refugees, more than 75 persons were reported ill with paratyphus, malaria, or intestinal ailments. The dispatch added that the village of Matanzas was virtually wiped out by two tidal waves following the August 4 earthquake, with native huts swept 250 yards into the jungle.

El representante de la Cruz Roja, H. E. Russell, declaró que el cargamento incluía cientos de libras de antitoxinas, vacunas, toxoides tetánicos, sulfamidas y quinina para combatir los brotes de enfermedades que amenazaban a miles de refugiados sin hogar. En un campamento de 500 refugiados, se informó que más de 75 personas estaban enfermas de paratifoidea, malaria o afecciones intestinales. El despacho agregó que la aldea de Matanzas quedó prácticamente destruida por dos maremotos tras el terremoto del 4 de agosto, y que las chozas nativas fueron arrastradas 250 yardas hacia la selva.

records.headline: Renewed terror followed two new shocks in a six-day series of earthquakes
records.summary_en: Renewed terror followed two new shocks in a six-day series of earthquakes and tidal waves in the northern provinces of the Dominican Republic, an Associated Press dispatch states under a headline reporting earthquakes felt in Dominica. The disasters left 73 persons dead and 20,000 homeless throughout the region. Government attempts to rush food to stricken communities were seriously hampered by washed-out roads and bridges along swollen streams. Apprehension was reported highest near Bahía Escocesa (Scotch Bay), where severe food shortages developed and clothing and medical supplies were nearly exhausted.
records.summary_es: Un renovado terror siguió a dos nuevos temblores en una serie de terremotos y maremotos de seis días en las provincias del norte de la República Dominicana, según señala un despacho de Associated Press bajo un titular que informa sobre sismos sentidos en Dominica. Los desastres dejaron 73 personas muertas y 20,000 sin hogar en toda la región. Los intentos del gobierno por enviar alimentos de urgencia a las comunidades afectadas se vieron gravemente obstaculizados por caminos y puentes arrasados a lo largo de corrientes desbordadas. Se informó que la inquietud era mayor cerca de la bahía Escocesa (Scotch Bay), donde la escasez de alimentos era aguda y la ropa y los suministros médicos estaban casi agotados.

records.headline: The Chicago Star reports from Ciudad Trujillo that American big
records.summary_en: The Chicago Star reports from Ciudad Trujillo that American big business is bolstering the dictatorship of General Rafael L. Molina Trujillo and promoting his regime internationally through aggressive publicity. The paper states that Trujillo is allied with executives of the American Hotel Corp., which operates the government-owned $3,000,000 Hotel Jaragua and plans to manage 12 additional hotels under a $20,000,000 resort development program. Corporate officials are portrayed as promoting the Dominican Republic as a tourist destination for commercial profit, even as the country recovers from a series of severe earthquakes.
records.summary_es: The Chicago Star informa desde Ciudad Trujillo que las grandes empresas estadounidenses están respaldando la dictadura del general Rafael L. Molina Trujillo y promoviendo su régimen a nivel internacional mediante una agresiva publicidad. El periódico afirma que Trujillo está aliado con ejecutivos de la American Hotel Corp., empresa que administra el Hotel Jaragua, propiedad del gobierno y valorado en $3,000,000, y que planea operar 12 hoteles adicionales bajo un programa de complejos turísticos de $20,000,000. Se retrata a los directivos corporativos promocionando a la República Dominicana como un destino turístico con fines de lucro comercial, aun mientras el país se recupera de una serie de graves terremotos.

records.summary_en: The Chicago Star quotes publicity director Harry Klemfuss asserting that Trujillo has performed miracles for the Dominican Republic and comparing him favorably to Benito Mussolini. The article contrasts this promotional rhetoric with the stance of liberal Dominicans, recalling that Trujillo's armed forces carried out a three-day massacre in 1937 against thousands of Haitians working in the Dominican borderlands. Forced into exile, these Dominican patriots announced intentions to bring Trujillo's regime before the United Nations. The report adds that Trujillo has maintained power since 1930.

records.summary_en: The Daily Alaska Empire reported that a strong earthquake shook the Dominican Republic, causing widespread panic but no casualties or significant damage. The tremor was identified as the strongest in thirteen days amidst an ongoing series of quakes across the country. Other brief dispatches covered a hunting fatality in Alaska and mechanical delays in German rocket testing in New Mexico.

Otras gacetillas del despacho reseñaron un mortal accidente de cacería en Alaska e inconvenientes mecánicos en el ensayo con cohetes alemanes en Nuevo México.

records.headline: The seismograph at Georgetown University recorded an earthquake
records.summary_en: The seismograph at Georgetown University recorded an earthquake in the vicinity of the Dominican Republic, commencing at 9:50 a.m. and reaching maximum motion at the same minute. Associated Press dispatches from Ciudad Trujillo stated that a tremor of moderate intensity was registered in the capital at 9:55 a.m. No damage of consequence was reported in the city, though information was still lacking from the interior of the country.

Despachos de Associated Press desde Ciudad Trujillo señalaron que se registró un temblor de intensidad moderada en la capital a las 9:55 a.m. No se reportaron daños de importancia en la ciudad, aunque todavía faltaban informaciones procedentes del interior del país.

records.headline: A cable from Manuel de Moya, secretary to Dominican President
records.summary_en: A cable from Manuel de Moya, secretary to Dominican President Trujillo, alleges that armed Communists initiated rioting and attempted a coup d'état in Ciudad Trujillo on Saturday night, an Associated Press dispatch quoting a Miami Herald report relays. De Moya stated that organizers notified authorities of a meeting but distributed knives, machetes, and clubs before attacking foreigners and unarmed citizens at 10 p.m. The message claimed disturbances erupted across the capital, the Mexican Embassy was violated, and senior Communist leaders avoided the gathering after orchestrating the unrest.
records.summary_es: Un cablegrama de Manuel de Moya, secretario del presidente dominicano Trujillo, denuncia que comunistas armados iniciaron disturbios e intentaron un golpe de Estado en Ciudad Trujillo el sábado por la noche, según transmite un despacho de Associated Press que cita un reporte del Miami Herald. De Moya afirmó que los organizadores notificaron a las autoridades sobre una reunión, pero distribuyeron cuchillos, machetes y garrotes antes de atacar a extranjeros y ciudadanos desarmados a las 10 p.m. El mensaje aseguró que estallaron desórdenes en toda la capital, se violó la embajada de México y altos dirigentes comunistas evitaron asistir a la concentración tras haber orquestado los disturbios.

records.headline: A dispatch from Bunnell, Florida, reports that a deputy sheriff shot and killed a 20-year-old Dominican, an adopted
records.summary_en: A dispatch from Bunnell, Florida, reports that a deputy sheriff shot and killed a 20-year-old Dominican, an adopted nephew of President Rafael Trujillo, mistaking him for a colored American insisting upon his civil rights, as the young man, on terminal leave from the United States Army after two years of service, was driving from New York to Miami on Friday night. Dominican Consul Jose M. Noel hurried to Florida on Saturday night under direct orders of President Trujillo to determine why the young man was killed, and Sheriff Henry Wells said the shooting was done by Deputy Miller Teeter. A coroner's jury found that Mr. Teeter fired in self-defense. The youth was adopted as a child by Anibal Trujillo; prior to the adoption, the youth was named Seijas, which he continued to use in his formal signature. A State Department official in Florida reportedly had been advised of the shooting; however, Walter W. Walters, representing the State Department at Miami, was away on vacation. The men had argued that they should be served, and the sheriff was called; Deputy Teeter was sent to the scene and found Mr. Trujillo seated in his car with Mr. Todd standing nearby. Mr. Teeter testified at the inquest that Mr. Trujillo drew a pistol, was told twice to put it away, and then was shot through the chest; he died instantly. Bunnell is 25 miles northwest of Daytona Beach.
records.summary_es: Un despacho desde Bunnell, Florida, informa que un ayudante del sheriff disparó y mató a un dominicano de 20 años, sobrino adoptivo del presidente Rafael Trujillo, confundiéndolo con un americano de color que insistía en sus derechos civiles, cuando el joven, con licencia terminal del Ejército de los Estados Unidos tras dos años de servicio, viajaba en automóvil de Nueva York a Miami el viernes por la noche. El cónsul dominicano José M. Noel viajó apresuradamente a Florida el sábado por la noche por órdenes directas del presidente Trujillo para averiguar por qué fue muerto el joven, y el sheriff Henry Wells dijo que el disparo lo hizo el ayudante Miller Teeter. Un jurado del forense determinó que el señor Teeter disparó en defensa propia. El joven había sido adoptado de niño por Aníbal Trujillo; antes de la adopción se llamaba Seijas, nombre que siguió usando en su firma formal. Un funcionario del Departamento de Estado en Florida habría sido informado del tiroteo; sin embargo, Walter W. Walters, representante del Departamento de Estado en Miami, estaba de vacaciones. Los hombres habían argumentado que debían ser atendidos, y se llamó al sheriff; el ayudante Teeter fue enviado al lugar y encontró al señor Trujillo sentado en su automóvil, con el señor Todd de pie cerca. El señor Teeter testificó en la pesquisa que el señor Trujillo sacó una pistola, se le ordenó dos veces guardarla y entonces recibió un disparo en el pecho; murió al instante. Bunnell está a 25 millas al noroeste de Daytona Beach.

records.headline: The State Department disclosed that it has twice apologized
records.summary_en: The State Department disclosed that it has twice apologized to Dominican Republic officials regarding the fatal shooting of Jose Adrian Trujillo Seijas, nephew of President Rafael Trujillo. records.summary_en: A Washington report states that the United States Government has twice apologized to Dominican Republic representatives over the fatal shooting of Jose Adrian Trujillo Seijas, nephew of Dominican President Rafael Trujillo, who was mistaken by a deputy sheriff for a colored man while insisting upon service. The State Department requested Governor Millard F. records.headline: An account reports that a deputy sheriff fatally shot Jose Adrian Trujillo
records.summary_en: An account reports that a deputy sheriff fatally shot Jose Adrian Trujillo last week. Traveling to Miami by automobile, Trujillo and a Jamaican companion stopped in Brunell, Florida, where they were refused service after being mistaken for Negroes. In the ensuing argument, deputy sheriff Teeter arrived and claimed he shot Trujillo in self-defense after Trujillo drew a gun, though the companion's statement was not published. The paper suggests the Dominican Republic could demand financial retribution, observing that the killing of the nephew of a neighboring country's president could produce international repercussions.
records.summary_es: Una crónica informa que un alguacil adjunto mató a tiros a Jose Adrian Trujillo la semana pasada. Durante un viaje en automóvil hacia Miami, Trujillo y un acompañante jamaiquino se detuvieron en Brunell, Florida, donde se les negó el servicio tras ser confundidos con negros. En la discusión subsiguiente, el alguacil adjunto Teeter se presentó en el lugar y afirmó haber disparado en defensa propia luego de que Trujillo empuñara un arma, aunque la declaración del acompañante no fue publicada. El periódico sugiere que la República Dominicana podría exigir una compensación económica, observando que la muerte del sobrino del presidente de un país vecino podría acarrear repercusiones internacionales.

records.headline: Young Trujillo was shot and killed on Saturday night near Bunnell, Florida, after he and his companion Louis Henry Todd
records.summary_en: Young Trujillo was shot and killed on Saturday night near Bunnell, Florida, after he and his companion Louis Henry Todd were refused service at a cafe because they were thought to be American Negroes and argued that they should be served. Deputy Sheriff Tetter testified at the inquest that Trujillo, seated in his car, drew a pistol and was shot through the chest when he refused to put it away; the dead youth, generally called Trujillo but named Seijas, was the adopted son of Anibal Trujillo, brother of President Trujillo, and was on terminal leave from the United States Army on his way home.
records.summary_es: El joven Trujillo fue muerto a tiros el sábado por la noche cerca de Bunnell, Florida, después de que a él y a su compañero Louis Henry Todd se les negara el servicio en un café porque se les creyó negros estadounidenses y de que discutieran que debían ser atendidos. El alguacil adjunto Tetter declaró en la pesquisa que Trujillo, sentado en su automóvil, sacó una pistola y recibió un tiro en el pecho cuando se negó a guardarla; el joven fallecido, llamado generalmente Trujillo pero de nombre Seijas, era hijo adoptivo de Aníbal Trujillo, hermano del presidente Trujillo, y estaba con licencia terminal del Ejército de los Estados Unidos de camino a su hogar.

records.headline: An editorial commentary argues that the death of Trujillo, sacrificed
records.summary_en: An editorial commentary argues that the death of Trujillo, sacrificed to Southern tradition, will affect race relations within the United States as well as relations with foreign neighbors. With the United Nations currently examining the plight of global minority groups and the Dominican Republic participating as a member, the paper expects the Trujillo affair will undergo intense scrutiny. The article notes that while the United Nations cannot take direct action, this public discussion will compromise the position of democratic world leadership assumed by the United States.
records.summary_es: Un comentario editorial sostiene que la muerte de Trujillo, sacrificado ante las tradiciones del sur, afectará las relaciones raciales dentro de los Estados Unidos así como los vínculos con sus vecinos extranjeros. Al hallarse las Naciones Unidas examinando la situación de las minorías en todo el mundo y participando la República Dominicana como Estado miembro, el diario prevé que el caso Trujillo sea objeto de un intenso escrutinio. El artículo observa que, si bien las Naciones Unidas no pueden adoptar medidas directas, este debate público perjudicará la posición de liderazgo mundial democrático que los Estados Unidos han asumido.

records.headline: An account reports on the fatal shooting of young Trujillo by deputy
records.summary_en: An account reports on the fatal shooting of young Trujillo by deputy Teters, who claimed Trujillo pointed a German automatic pistol at him and refused two pleas to lower the weapon. A coroner's jury concluded that Trujillo's death was caused by a bullet from Teters's pistol and ruled that the officer acted justifiably in self-defense. The article questions how Trujillo, who had served three years in the United States Army, could have allowed Teters to draw and fire if Trujillo was already holding a weapon. At the time of the shooting, Trujillo and his companion were traveling from New York City to his home in the Dominican Republic.

Un jurado de instrucción forense dictaminó que la muerte de Trujillo fue causada por un disparo de la pistola de Teters y concluyó que el oficial actuó de manera justificada en defensa propia. El artículo cuestiona cómo Trujillo, quien había servido tres años en el ejército de los Estados Unidos, pudo permitir que Teters desenfundara y disparara si Trujillo ya tenía un arma en la mano. Al momento del incidente, Trujillo y su acompañante viajaban desde la ciudad de Nueva York hacia su hogar en la República Dominicana.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported on an escalating banana trade war in Haiti between the Standard Fruit Company and independent exporters following the overthrow of President Elie Lescot. President Dumarsais Estime's administration reportedly prepared to revoke the export license of Habanex due to its owner's family ties to Lescot. Meanwhile, independent shippers accused Standard Fruit of aggressive price competition that threatened to price American importers out of the market.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó sobre la encarnizada pugna por el negocio bananero en Haití entre la Standard Fruit Company y firmas exportadoras autónomas a raíz del derrocamiento del presidente Élie Lescot. Trascendió que la administración del presidente Dumarsais Estimé se disponía a revocar los permisos comerciales de la compañía Habanex a causa del parentesco de su titular con Lescot. Paralelamente, los consignatarios independientes acusaban a la Standard Fruit de prácticas de competencia desleal en precios destinadas a expulsar a los importadores norteamericanos de plaza.

records.summary_en: In a question-and-answer column, a reader inquires about the identity of the oldest city in the Western Hemisphere. The response states that Ciudad Trujillo, the capital of the Dominican Republic, is the oldest city founded by white men in the hemisphere. The item adds that the city is celebrating its 450th anniversary this year.

La nota agrega que la ciudad conmemora su 450.º aniversario este año.

records.summary_en: The East Hartford Gazette reviewed major news highlights of late 1946, noting that the Dominican Republic suffered severe losses from a violent earthquake and tidal wave in August. The retrospective also cited international incidents including the desertion of the steamship *American Farmer* and the Yugoslav shootdown of two American airplanes. Additional domestic events covered labor strikes, price controls, and the anniversary of the U.S. Army Air Forces.
records.summary_es: El *East Hartford Gazette* presentó una recopilación de los sucesos más descollantes de finales de 1946, destacando que la República Dominicana sufrió desastrosas pérdidas a consecuencia del terremoto y maremoto registrados en agosto. La síntesis informativa rememoró también episodios internacionales como el abandono del vapor *American Farmer* y el derribo por fuerzas yugoslavas de dos aeronaves militares estadounidenses. En el ámbito interno, recapituló jornadas de huelga obrera, controversias por los controles de precios y el aniversario de las Fuerzas Aéreas del Ejército norteamericano.

The Year 1946 —

(Continued from page 2)

MAY. On May 11 the miners accepted a two-week truce. The King of Italy had already abdicated in favor of his son Humbert, later to be voted out of office by the Italian plebiscite. On May 14 an American Military Court sentenced 58 operators of the Mathausen Concentration Camp to be hanged. In Alcatraz prison we witnessed the two-day insurrection with the inmates fortifying themselves in the main building.

The railroad strike began on May 24. In the Far East the Chinese recaptured Changchung.

Then JUNE made its entry. On the second day of the month the McMahon Bill for national, civilian control of atomic energy was passed. In Europe Antonescu and some of his associates were executed on the same day.

June 5 saw the disastrous Hotel La Salle fire in Chicago, followed on the 10th day by the second great hotel fire in Dubuque, Iawo, when the Canfield hotel burned down.

June 7th Secretary of the Treasury Fred M. Vinson was appointed Chief Justice of the United States Supreme Court.

The month of June also witnessed the disappearance of the famous Hesse Crown jewels in Germany from Kronberg Castle near Frankfurt. At home the maritime strike was settled by the middle of the month.

Disorders occurred on a large scale in Palestine as Jewish extremists blew up five bridges, virtually isolating Transjordan from Palestine. And here in East Hartford we remember the Willimantic incident when on June 19 a Constellation plane made an emergency landing in Connecticut without injury to any of its 42 occupants.

June 24 saw the Pacific Coast earthquake with damage reported from Oregon to Canada. A star of the silent films passed away with the death of William S. Hart, famous for his portrayals in Western films of earlier movie days.

The month ended with the great atomic tests at the Bikini atoll in the Pacific. Thus we moved on into

JULY. The first day of the month brought injury to five American soldiers in Trieste when a hand grenade was thrown during a demonstration. Mass violence occurred on July 2 in the movie studio strike in Hollywood. Great religious riots took place in India with scores of dead and injured.

July 4th saw the Stars and Stripes lowered in Manila with the end of U. S. control. President Truman signed the Hobbs anti-racketeering bill.

The National Education Association at its meeting in Buffalo, New York, reported the loss of a million teachers in the ranks of the profession, due to poor wages and working conditions.

Major Alexander De Seversky predicted future missiles, making a trip to the moon in three and a half hours at speeds of 139,000 miles per hour. (That's better than 23 miles a second, folks, or about four seconds from East Hartford to New York. Want to climb aboard and take a ride?) Another oddity of the month came when Jinjiro Mizuno, member of the Japanese House of Peers, declared that all Jap males were guilty of waging war and the only solution would be an all-women government for Japan.

The Arab High Commission wrote to President Truman, suggesting to open America to the Jews indiscriminately. Milk, petroleum and other products went off price control.

The pope read a message to the Japanese Catholics, the first of its kind in the history of the Church.

The second atomic test (submarine) at the Bikini atoll came off on July 25. On July 29, four days later, the first Peace Conference opened in Paris. And time moved on into

AUGUST. August 2nd was the 39th birthday of the United States Army Air Forces. On August 4th Protestant leaders from eight nations, gathered in England, favored joint action with the Catholics on world problems.

Athens, Tennessee, saw ex-GIs drive the sheriff elect out of town and seize control of the government.

The Dominican Republic suffered great loss in a tidal wave and violent earthquake. The steamship American Farmer was deserted at sea and became a problem for international litigation.

Channing Pollock, famous playwright, died August 18.

The Yugoslavs shoot down two American planes. The State Department sent violent protest. Severe rioting occurred in Calcutta. The Norwalk, Connecticut, schools teachers go on strike for wage relief.

President Truman vacationed in Bermuda. New England scientists from M. I. T. studied cosmic rays at 40,000 feet altitude. Fifteen German spies were arrested in the American zone of occupation. Those were some of the August headlines and then

SEPTEMBER. Price control went on a spree on such items as canned fruits and vegetables and many other items. The truck strike was hitting New York. An Army jet plane did 578 miles per hour at the Cleveland races.

Marshal Tito apologized to the United States for the shooting down of our planes. A musicians' strike silenced the dining rooms of the New York hotels.

The Queen Mary arrived on September 4th with art treasures, valued at seven million dollars, for exhibition in the U. S. A. A shipping strike tied up all ports with 3,000 ships moored at their docks and 400,000 workers idle.

September 6. A two-year-old child is the only survivor of a transcontinental plane crash in Navada, with all 21 passengers killed. The Nazi top war criminals are sentenced to hang.

OCTOBER. The high spot of the month of October to most people possibly was the execution of the Nazi war criminals. When Master Sergeant John C. Woods of San Antonio, Texas, said: "I've hung my last man. I'm through," a tale of human brutality and barbariism came to an end.

Two tragic plane crashes in Newfoundland also made the headlines in October. We balked plenty at the high cost of living again because we had expected a leveling off to nearer pre-war prices. With the world slowly trying to emerge from its great illness of the war we began to concentrate at home on the coming November elections. We do not remember a year in which we saw more political prophets hit the zero mark for accuracy.

NOVEMBER and DECEMBER are really just like yesterday and might be looked at together in retrospect.

First attention came on the outcome of the elections and the many new angles of government reaction to the nation's needs and its ills. The Republican sweep came unheralded like the summer storm. The last two months of 1946 saw another coal strike, another tragic hotel fire in Atlanta, Georgia, and also the passing of Damon Runyon, one of America's greatest and most beloved newspaper men, and Governor-elect Talmadge of Georgia.

Then in December we went to work on the German war factories, destroying twenty-five plants for the manufacture of explosives and the sprawling underground installations of the Messerschmitt airplane works. We have found a permanent site for the home of the United Nations and are marching on to 1947 with many good promises ahead. We are about to make our customary New Year's resolutions and envisage a year of growth and expansion.

We become more mass-conscious of our needs and we are realizing more fully that we must look on our human accomplishments in the light of cooperation effort. Just as we do not wish to repeat our personal mistakes of yesterday or last week, we become conscious that the whole aggregate of the human race must also be made aware not to repeat its blunders and failures of the past.

And so we have looked at 1946 in retrospect and lived through the changes and happenings that the historians of tomorrow will record as the history of our land. We hope we haven't bored you with this little review. It is nice sometimes to sit down together and reminesce. It has been like a journey we all made together through the year with its laughs and its tragedies that make up life.

Thus, in conclusion, there is no better wish than to say to all our readers the one real wish we repeat so faithfully each time December hands its scepter to young January:

"A VERY HAPPY AND PROSPEROUS NEW YEAR TO YOU!"
