records.headline: A maritime travel report announces that the cruise ship Polaris
records.summary_en: A maritime travel report announces that the cruise ship Polaris, currently anchored in Nassau harbor, is returning from its first postwar South American cruise and departs New York on January 13 for New Orleans. After an initial 22-day voyage visiting 11 ports, the vessel will embark on February 20 on the first of five 16-day cruises. The itinerary includes stops at Havana, Cuba; Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic; La Guaira, Venezuela; Willemstad, Curaçao; and Kingston, Jamaica.
records.summary_es: Una crónica de viajes marítimos anuncia que el buque de crucero Polaris, fondeado actualmente en el puerto de Nasáu, se encuentra de regreso de su primer crucero de posguerra por América del Sur y zarpa de Nueva York el 13 de enero rumbo a Nueva Orleans. Tras una travesía inicial de 22 días que recorrerá 11 puertos, la nave iniciará el 20 de febrero el primero de cinco cruceros de 16 días. El itinerario incluye escalas en La Habana, Cuba; Ciudad Trujillo, República Dominicana; La Guaira, Venezuela; Willemstad, Curazao; y Kingston, Jamaica.

records.headline: A Washington diplomatic column reports that Dr. Julio Ortega
records.summary_en: A Washington diplomatic column reports that Dr. Julio Ortega Frier, the newly appointed Dominican Republic Ambassador to the United States, is scheduled to arrive within the next couple of weeks. Appointed by Dominican President Rafael L. Trujillo, Dr. Ortega Frier formerly served as rector of the University of Santo Domingo and previously held office as Secretary of State. His wife, daughter Maruja, and son Rafael have already arrived in Washington and are residing at the embassy.
records.summary_es: Una columna diplomática de Washington informa que el Dr. Julio Ortega Frier, recién nombrado embajador de la República Dominicana ante los Estados Unidos, tiene previsto llegar en el transcurso de las próximas dos semanas. Designado por el presidente dominicano Rafael L. Trujillo, el Dr. Ortega Frier se desempeñó anteriormente como rector de la Universidad de Santo Domingo y años atrás ocupó el cargo de secretario de Estado. Su esposa, su hija Maruja y su hijo Rafael ya han llegado a Washington y se encuentran hospedados en la embajada.

records.headline: A Washington columnist reports on educational administration
records.summary_en: A Washington columnist reports on educational administration in the Dominican Republic, observing that compulsory education is strictly enforced through heavy fines levied against parents whose children miss school without bona fide excuses. Whenever local authorities identify a group of 20 children lacking a nearby school, a teacher is sent to establish an emergency school, with twelve hundred such schools reported in operation. The column notes that under President Trujillo, described as the virtual dictator for a score of years, illiteracy has been reduced to 35 per cent compared to an estimated 75 per cent fifteen years earlier. The passage opens on a reference to a Dominican cabinet minister who previously served as an ambassador during the arbitration of the Dominican-Haitian problem.
records.summary_es: Un columnista de Washington comenta sobre la administración educativa en la República Dominicana, señalando que la educación obligatoria se cumple con rigor mediante fuertes multas impuestas a los padres cuyos hijos falten a la escuela sin una justificación válida. Siempre que las autoridades locales notifican la existencia de un grupo de 20 niños sin escuela cercana, se envía un maestro para abrir una escuela de emergencia, registrándose mil doscientas de estas escuelas en funcionamiento. La columna añade que bajo el presidente Trujillo, calificado como el dictador virtual durante una veintena de años, el analfabetismo se ha reducido al 35 por ciento frente a un 75 por ciento estimado quince años atrás. El texto se abre con una referencia a un ministro del gabinete dominicano que actuó como embajador durante el arbitraje del conflicto dominico-haitiano.

records.headline: A travel correspondent recounts driving from Haiti across the border
records.summary_en: A travel correspondent recounts driving from Haiti across the border into the Dominican Republic and continuing directly to Trujillo City, where a modern building program was underway. Traveling from the capital to inspect damage caused by a recent earthquake, the writer received extensive cooperation from the Dominican Government, which provided an American two-seater fighter plane for aerial photography. Piloted by Lieutenant Perez, the aircraft flew with its plexiglass cockpit opened into the windstream before encountering a heavy rainstorm aloft.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal de viajes relata haber cruzado en automóvil la frontera desde Haití hacia la República Dominicana y continuado directamente hacia Ciudad Trujillo, donde se desarrollaba un moderno programa de construcción. Al trasladarse desde la capital para examinar los daños causados por un reciente terremoto, el autor recibió una amplia cooperación del gobierno dominicano, que puso a su disposición un avión de combate biplaza estadounidense para tomar fotografías aéreas. Pilotada por el teniente Pérez, la nave voló con la cubierta de plexiglás abierta contra el viento antes de toparse en el aire con una fuerte tormenta de lluvia.

records.headline: Under the headline "Have Returned from the Dominican Republic,"
records.summary_en: Under the headline "Have Returned from the Dominican Republic," a local report states that Mr. and Mrs. Charles P. Gillespie returned Sunday night from a six-week trip to the Dominican Republic. During their travels, they were the guests of Señor and Señora Eduardo León in Santiago and of Mrs. Huston in Monte Cristi. The item notes that Mrs. Huston, a native of Virginia, teaches a private school for the Grenada Fruit Company. The Gillespies were accompanied on the journey by Dr. John McGuire of Bluefield, West Virginia, and visited friends in Delray Beach and Miami on their return.

Durante su estadía, fueron huéspedes del señor Eduardo León y su esposa en Santiago y de la señora Huston en Monte Cristi. La nota destaca que la señora Huston, oriunda de Virginia, imparte clases en una escuela privada para la Grenada Fruit Company. Los Gillespie estuvieron acompañados durante el viaje por el Dr. John McGuire, de Bluefield, Virginia Occidental, y de regreso visitaron a amigos en Delray Beach y Miami.

records.summary_en: The Key West Citizen reported that Haiti's application for an Export-Import Bank loan remained pending amid growing criticism from local Communists over past American occupation debts. Concurrently, Haitian President Dumarsais Estime moved toward closer ties with Argentina, with President Juan Domingo Peron reportedly extending credit and diplomatic overtures. The report also referenced the neighboring Dominican Republic under President Rafael Trujillo sharing the island of Hispaniola.

Local factions criticized long-standing American financial controls dating to the 1922 occupation, while Argentina sought commercial influence by offering loans and exchanging ambassadors. The account highlighted geopolitical dynamics involving Haitian President Dumarsais Estime and Dominican President Rafael Trujillo on Hispaniola.

records.headline: A travel report states that the Dominican Republic is launching
records.summary_en: A travel report states that the Dominican Republic is launching a campaign for all-year-round vacationing this summer under the promotional slogan, "20 degrees south of New York and 20 degrees cooler." Dominican Tourist Bureau Director H. W. Goeggel attributes this climate to trade winds and mountain breezes. To encourage recreational travel, President Rafael L. Trujillo recently approved the construction of 14 modern hotels across 12 cities. The new facilities are scheduled to open for the 1947-8 winter travel season under the management of the American Hotels Corporation.
records.summary_es: Un informe de viajes señala que la República Dominicana está lanzando una campaña de vacaciones para todo el año este verano bajo el lema promocional: «20 grados al sur de Nueva York y 20 grados más fresco». El director de la Oficina de Turismo Dominicana, H. W. Goeggel, atribuye este clima a los vientos alisios y a las brisas de la montaña. Para fomentar los viajes de recreo, el presidente Rafael L. Trujillo aprobó recientemente la construcción de 14 hoteles modernos en 12 ciudades. Las nuevas instalaciones tienen previsto abrir para la temporada turística de invierno de 1947-8 bajo la administración de la American Hotels Corporation.

records.headline: The medical work of Dr. William A. Morgan, a Washington, D.C
records.summary_en: The medical work of Dr. William A. Morgan, a Washington, D.C., nose and throat specialist who traveled to the Dominican Republic for the dedication of a large modern hospital named in his honor, is recounted in a feature article. Dr. Morgan had visited the country ten years earlier on a hunting and fishing trip, but after seeing afflicted children across rural hamlets, he offered President Trujillo to perform free surgery on any child requiring nose or throat care. Following initial operations on orphanage children, demand grew rapidly, prompting Dr. Morgan to organize what he described as an assembly line using half a dozen operating tables and anaesthetists to remove tonsils.
records.summary_es: La labor médica del Dr. William A. Morgan, especialista en nariz y garganta de Washington, D.C., quien viajó a la República Dominicana para la inauguración de un gran hospital moderno bautizado en su honor, es relatada en un artículo especial. El Dr. Morgan había visitado el país diez años antes en un viaje de caza y pesca, pero al observar a niños enfermos en aldeas rurales, ofreció al presidente Trujillo operar gratuitamente a cualquier niño que necesitara atención de nariz o garganta. Tras las primeras intervenciones a niños de un orfanato local, la demanda creció rápidamente, lo que llevó al Dr. Morgan a organizar lo que describió como una línea de ensamblaje con media docena de mesas de operaciones y anestesistas para extirpar amígdalas.

records.headline: Speaking before local Rotarians, retired U.S. Coast Guard Captain Carl
records.summary_en: Speaking before local Rotarians, retired U.S. Coast Guard Captain Carl Hilton, a former member of the United States Naval Mission to the Dominican Republic from February, 1943, to September, 1944, expressed his conviction that the bones of Christopher Columbus are buried in Santo Domingo. Hilton recounted that when authorities excavated the floor of the cathedral, they identified an old break in Columbus's leg, convincing him that the explorer's body rests there. Hilton also described the Dominican Navy, explaining that the government had acquired eight U.S. Coast Guard vessels that operated effectively with a mixed crew of Spaniards and native sailors.
records.summary_es: En una intervención ante los rotarios locales, el capitán retirado de la Guardia Costera de EE. UU. Carl Hilton, antiguo integrante de la Misión Naval de los Estados Unidos en la República Dominicana desde febrero de 1943 hasta septiembre de 1944, expresó su convicción de que los restos de Cristóbal Colón descansan en Santo Domingo. Hilton relató que cuando las autoridades excavaron el suelo de la catedral, identificaron una antigua fractura en la pierna de Colón, lo que le convenció de que el cuerpo del navegante yace allí. Hilton también describió la marina dominicana, explicando que el gobierno había adquirido ocho embarcaciones de la Guardia Costera estadounidense que operaban con eficacia gracias a una tripulación mixta de españoles y marineros nativos.

Trujillo obtuvo una victoria aplastante en su campaña de reelección. De acuerdo con la Junta Central Electoral, ambos candidatos rivales —Rafael Espailiat, del Partido Demócrata Nacional, y Francisco Plats-Ramirez, del Partido Laborista Nacional— reconocieron la elección de Trujillo.

records.headline: On the one hand the Communists threatened to dominate his government
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Brazil, Venezuela, and Haiti were moving aggressively to purge communist influence in hopes of securing financial favor from the United States. In Haiti, President Dumarsais Estime dissolved the Communist Party by decree after Washington withheld a $20,000,000 loan needed for debt retirement and agricultural development. Similar anti-communist actions were noted in Brazil under President Dutra and Venezuela under President Betancourt.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que Brasil, Venezuela y Haití emprendían severas purgas anticomunistas con miras a captar auxilios y beneficios crediticios de los Estados Unidos. En Haití, el gobernante Dumarsais Estimé ilegalizó el Partido Comunista mediante decreto luego de que Washington suspendiera una partida financiera de 20.000.000 de dólares vital para redimir deuda y financiar planes agrarios. Represalias ideológicas similares fueron adoptadas en el Brasil presidido por Dutra y en la Venezuela del presidente Betancourt.

records.headline: Reporting from Ciudad Trujillo for The Star and the Chicago
records.summary_en: Reporting from Ciudad Trujillo for The Star and the Chicago Daily News, a foreign correspondent observes that food supplies remain abundant and prices low, with local peasants voicing no complaints despite slight price increases over the previous nine months. Five gallons of shrimp can still be purchased for 20 cents, one nickel buys a lobster, and avocado pears sell for 2 cents a dozen. The correspondent notes that Dominican currency maintains parity with the United States dollar, with American paper dollars circulating throughout the country. While the government has a project underway to issue its own paper pesos, only Dominican small change is currently available.
records.summary_es: En un despacho desde Ciudad Trujillo para The Star y el Chicago Daily News, un corresponsal extranjero señala que los suministros de alimentos se mantienen abundantes y los precios bajos, sin que los campesinos locales expresen quejas a pesar de leves alzas en los últimos nueve meses. Se pueden comprar cinco galones de camarones por 20 centavos, una moneda de cinco centavos compra una langosta y los aguacates se venden a 2 centavos la docena. El corresponsal observa que la moneda dominicana mantiene la misma paridad que el dólar de los Estados Unidos y que los billetes estadounidenses circulan por todo el país. Aunque el gobierno tiene en marcha un proyecto para emitir sus propios pesos de papel, por el momento solo se dispone de moneda fraccionaria dominicana.

records.headline: Dominican officials questioned about the 1937 deaths of 12,000
records.summary_en: Dominican officials questioned about the 1937 deaths of 12.000 Haitians along the border dismissed the killings, stating that many Dominicans had died as well. When asked about allegations that opponents of his government were imprisoned and persecuted, President Rafael Trujillo replied that anyone was welcome to visit the country's prisons and ask inmates if they were political prisoners. The dispatch reports that the Dominican Party maintains authority through thorough organization rather than political despotism. In addition, Trujillo is promoting an industrialization program along the sparsely settled frontier, seeking to contract Haitian laborers individually for factory work while subjecting anyone involved in unauthorized union organizing to deportation.
records.summary_es: Los funcionarios dominicanos interrogados acerca de la muerte de 12.000 haitianos a lo largo de la frontera en 1937 restaron importancia a las matanzas, afirmando que también habían muerto muchos dominicanos. Al ser preguntado sobre las denuncias de que opositores a su gobierno eran encarcelados y perseguidos, el presidente Rafael Trujillo respondió que cualquiera podía visitar las prisiones del país y preguntar a los reclusos si eran presos políticos. El despacho señala que el Partido Dominicano mantiene su autoridad mediante una organización meticulosa y no por despotismo político. Además, Trujillo promueve un programa de industrialización a lo largo de la frontera escasamente poblada, con el propósito de contratar obreros haitianos individualmente para labores fabriles, disponiendo que quien participe en actividades sindicales no autorizadas quedará sujeto a deportación.

records.headline: A diplomatic incident arose in Buenos Aires when audiences were suspended
records.summary_en: A diplomatic incident arose in Buenos Aires when audiences were suspended at the Presidential Palace for two hours and thirty minutes, leaving the incoming ambassadors of Czechoslovakia, Brazil, and the Dominican Republic waiting to present their credentials to President Juan Perón. Argentine protocol representatives and the three diplomats waited without explanation while Perón conducted an uninterrupted conference. When an aide was sent at 12:30 p.m. to apologize, the envoy of Czechoslovakia accepted with good grace, but the ambassadors of Brazil and Santo Domingo were furious and announced they would protest to their home governments.
records.summary_es: Un incidente diplomático se produjo en Buenos Aires cuando las audiencias fueron suspendidas en el Palacio Presidencial durante dos horas y treinta minutos, dejando a los nuevos embajadores de Checoslovaquia, Brasil y la República Dominicana a la espera de presentar sus cartas credenciales ante el presidente Juan Perón. Los representantes de protocolo argentinos y los tres diplomáticos aguardaron sin explicaciones mientras Perón sostenía una reunión sin interrupciones. Cuando un ayudante fue enviado a las 12:30 p.m. para ofrecer disculpas, el enviado de Checoslovaquia las aceptó de buen grado, pero los embajadores de Brasil y Santo Domingo se mostraron furiosos y anunciaron que protestarían ante sus respectivos gobiernos.

records.headline: The Embassy of the Dominican Republic in Washington is awaiting
records.summary_en: The Embassy of the Dominican Republic in Washington is awaiting the arrival of its new First Secretary, Señor Miguel A. Herrera. Meanwhile, the Dominican Ambassador and Señora de Ortega Frier departed for Princeton, New Jersey, where the envoy will represent the University of Santo Domingo at Princeton University's bicentennial celebration. Following a three-day stay in Princeton, the ambassador and his wife will travel to New York as part of a two-week absence from the capital.
records.summary_es: La embajada de la República Dominicana en Washington aguarda la llegada de su nuevo primer secretario, el señor Miguel A. Herrera. En tanto, el embajador dominicano y la señora de Ortega Frier salieron rumbo a Princeton, Nueva Jersey, donde el enviado representará a la Universidad de Santo Domingo en la celebración del bicentenario de la Universidad de Princeton. Después de una estancia de tres días en Princeton, el embajador y su esposa viajarán a Nueva York como parte de una ausencia de dos semanas de la capital.

records.headline: Dominican President Rafael Trujillo is credited with formulating
records.summary_en: Dominican President Rafael Trujillo is credited with formulating a plan to assist Haiti in overcoming its financial difficulties, anticipating improved relations once the neighboring republic is freed of debts. During conferences in the Dominican Republic regarding local irrigation construction, contractor Rosoff was told by Trujillo at luncheon that a $14,000,000 loan could rehabilitate the Haitian economy. However, Haitian President Dumarsais Estimé contends that approximately $20,000,000 is required for his country's affairs, including $8,000,000 to repay the United States and $3,000,000 to liquidate an attempt to grow rubber in Haiti.

Durante conferencias celebradas en la República Dominicana acerca de la construcción de obras locales de irrigación, Trujillo manifestó en un almuerzo al contratista Rosoff que un préstamo de $14,000,000 podría rehabilitar la economía haitiana. Sin embargo, el presidente haitiano Dumarsais Estimé sostiene que se necesitan aproximadamente $20,000,000 para los asuntos de su país, incluidos $8,000,000 para saldar la deuda con Estados Unidos y $3,000,000 para liquidar el intento de cultivar caucho en Haití.

records.headline: A Dominican ambassador informed a reporter that a boatload of 1,000 men
records.summary_en: A Dominican ambassador informed a reporter that a boatload of 1,000 men was scheduled to depart Friday night from the eastern Cuban port of Antillas to stage an invasion. The envoy reported that the entire Dominican army had been fully alerted to confront the threatened attack. In response, the Cuban naval commander at Antillas stated that he investigated reports of revolutionaries assembling there and found no substantiation, reporting only sugar vessels in the harbor.

El enviado comunicó que todo el ejército dominicano se encontraba plenamente alertado para hacer frente al ataque previsto. En respuesta, el comandante naval cubano en Antillas declaró que investigó las versiones sobre revolucionarios concentrados en el lugar y no halló confirmación alguna, informando que solo había barcos azucareros en el puerto.

Dominicans' Report Invaders Are on Way Lacks Confirmation

Charges by the Dominican Embassy here that a three-ship expedition had left Cuba to invade the Dominican Republic could not be confirmed in Cuba.

Jose Vega, secretary to the Dominican Ambassador here, told reporters last night that two landing barges and one corvette equipped with cannon and machine guns had sailed from Cuba yesterday morning or the night before.

Officials Disclaim Knowledge.

Cuban government officials, the Associated Press reported, said they had no knowledge of any revolutionary activity directed from Cuba against the Dominican Republic. These officials would not be quoted by name.

Efforts of the Associated Press to check independently on reports that a three-ship expedition had left a northeastern Cuban port were difficult because of the many small harbors and inlets which are so isolated from interior towns by lack of communications.

Mr. Vega placed the point of departure between Antilla and Barracoa on the eastern tip of Cuba. He had no estimate of the number of men aboard the vessels.

Dominican Ambassador Julio Ortega Frier told reporters last week that 3,000 men recruited from Cuba, Guatemala, Venezuela and Puerto Rico were poised in Cuba to attack his country. He described the men as "Communist revolutionaries" aiming at overthrowing Dominican President Rafael Trujillo.

His charges were denied by officials of Guatemala, Venezuela and Cuba.

A State Department spokesman said the department had heard about "rumors" that an army of Communists was preparing to invade the Dominican Republic from Cuba, but that its information was insufficient to warrant any comment.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Dominican Ambassador Julio Ortega Frier claimed an invasion expedition comprising two landing craft and a corvette had sailed from Cuba, accompanied by at least seven aircraft. While the Dominican government maintained air patrols and reported internal calm, travelers arriving in Haiti described heavy Dominican troop movements. The implicated foreign governments continued to deny involvement in any organized expedition targeting Rafael Trujillo's regime.

A search started, and airports along both Florida coasts were checked without success, as were other Gulf areas. Meanwhile no Washington agency could be found that would admit ordering the alert.

Then, yesterday afternoon, the State Department acknowledged it had heard the rumor and said it had relayed it to the Customs Bureau and other agencies for investigation.

The statement disclosed that the State Department has had in effect for months a general alert, based on “general rumors of revolutionary plotting,” to make sure that “United States territory would not be used for conspiracy.”

Rumor Involves 7 Planes.

The statement, issued by Press Officer Reginald Mitchell, said the State Department has been receiving “rumors” and “fragmentary reports” of impending trouble in the Caribbean area but has declined to comment because of their unsubstantial nature. The statement continued:

“One such rumor was to the effect that there were seven combat planes at an airfield in Florida ready to depart for a Caribbean destination. The department Friday immediately communicated this rumor to the Customs Bureau and other United States Government agencies concerned and requested that an investigation be made and that these alleged planes be prevented from leaving the United States.

“The department has been informed that the Customs Bureau promptly notified its Florida headquarters office at Tampa which in turn alerted its subordinate customs offices at Miami, Jacksonville, West Palm Beach and elsewhere in Florida. The department has received no further information in this particular matter.

“The department heard general rumors of revolutionary plotting in the Caribbean area as long ago as January of this year and in an effort to make sure that United States territory would not be used for conspiracy alerted the appropriate law enforcement agencies, which since that date have kept a scrupulous watch.”

Easy Flight for Fighters.

At least some of the rumors were based on reports in Haitian and Dominican newspapers.

The P38 Lightning and the P51 Mustang, Army fighter planes extensively used in the war, would easily be able to fly from Florida to the Dominican Republic. The shortest airline distance is a little over 650 miles. There are the Bahama Islands and the tip of Cuba in between.

A War Department official said some Lightnings and Mustangs have been sold as surplus and may be in the hands of civilians.

records.headline: An informal supper party was held at an embassy in Washington
records.summary_en: An informal supper party was held at an embassy in Washington in honor of the Military Governor of the Canary Islands, General García Escámez, and Señora de Escámez. The visitors arrived in the city before proceeding to New York on their way to the Dominican Republic, where General Escámez will serve as a special envoy for the ceremonies inaugurating General Rafael Trujillo as President. More than one hundred guests attended the gathering, including diplomats, officials, and officers of the United States military services.
records.summary_es: Se celebró una cena informal en una embajada en Washington en honor del gobernador militar de las Islas Canarias, el general García Escámez, y la señora de Escámez. Los visitantes llegaron a la ciudad antes de continuar hacia Nueva York en ruta a la República Dominicana, donde el general Escámez fungirá como enviado especial en las ceremonias de investidura del general Rafael Trujillo como presidente. Más de cien invitados asistieron a la reunión, entre ellos diplomáticos, funcionarios y oficiales de las fuerzas armadas de Estados Unidos.

records.headline: Key details regarding the Dominican Republic are outlined in a profile
records.summary_en: Key details regarding the Dominican Republic are outlined in a profile titled "U.N. Facts and Faces," noting that it covers 19,332 square miles on the eastern end of the island of Hispaniola and has a population of 1,826,400. The Spanish-speaking nation shares the fertile island with French-speaking Haiti, with agriculture and stock raising serving as its primary industries. Ciudad Trujillo, formerly called Santo Domingo, is the capital and chief port. The nation is a member of the United Nations General Assembly, represented at U.N. Headquarters by Dr. Max Henriquez-Urena, and flies a red and blue flag with a white cross and a central seal.

La nación de habla hispana comparte la fértil isla con su vecino francófono, Haití, constituyendo la agricultura y la ganadería sus principales industrias. Ciudad Trujillo, antes llamada Santo Domingo, es la capital y puerto principal. El país es miembro de la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas, está representado en la sede de la ONU por el Dr. Max Henriquez-Urena, y enarbola una bandera roja y azul con una cruz blanca y un escudo central.

records.summary_en: Argentine Ambassador Dr. Oscar Ivanissevich and Naval Attaché Lt. Comdr. Ricardo P. Anzorena are traveling to Ciudad Trujillo as special envoys to attend the inauguration of General Rafael Trujillo as President of the Dominican Republic. Also attending the inaugural ceremonies as special envoy of his government will be Paraguayan Ambassador Dr. Don Guillermo Enciso Velloso, accompanied by his wife, Señora de Enciso Velloso. Both visiting delegations plan to return immediately following the festivities.

Anzorena viajan a Ciudad Trujillo como enviados especiales para asistir a la investidura del general Rafael Trujillo como presidente de la República Dominicana. También asistirá a las ceremonias inaugurales como enviado especial de su gobierno el embajador paraguayo Dr. Don Guillermo Enciso Velloso, acompañado por su esposa, la señora de Enciso Velloso. Ambas delegaciones visitantes tienen previsto regresar inmediatamente después de las festividades.

records.summary_en: A historical account traces the United States customs receivership to the Dominican resolution of March 31, 1905, known as the Modus Vivendi, which conceded to the United States the same rights over customs income as an earlier pact. It states that the Dominican-American Covenant signed February 8, 1907, gave the United States President the right to name a General Receiver of Customs to collect all Dominican customs taxes until government bonds issued to settle debts were paid and retired.
records.summary_es: Un recuento histórico atribuye la receptoría aduanera estadounidense a la resolución dominicana del 31 de marzo de 1905, conocida como Modus Vivendi, que concedió a Estados Unidos los mismos derechos sobre los ingresos aduaneros que un pacto anterior. Señala que el Convenio domínico-estadounidense firmado el 8 de febrero de 1907 dio al presidente de Estados Unidos el derecho de nombrar un Receptor General de Aduanas para recaudar todos los impuestos aduaneros dominicanos hasta que se pagaran y retiraran los bonos gubernamentales emitidos para saldar deudas.

records.headline: An explanatory note reports that a bill unanimously passed and signed
records.summary_en: An explanatory note reports that a bill unanimously passed and signed by President Trujillo authorized payment to Oliver P. Newman, representing American bondholders, to redeem Dominican bonds of 1922 and 1926 on September 1 and October 1, 1947. Alongside this financial notice, a travel advertisement placed by the Information Center of the Dominican Republic promotes the country as a blend of modernity and historical landmarks. The notice invites prospective vacationers to write to the Director of Tourism in Ciudad Trujillo for descriptive literature detailing tours, countryside scenery, and hotels.
records.summary_es: Una nota explicativa informa que un proyecto de ley aprobado unánimemente y promulgado por el presidente Trujillo autorizó el pago a Oliver P. Newman, en representación de los tenedores de bonos estadounidenses, para amortizar los bonos dominicanos de 1922 y 1926 el 1 de septiembre y el 1 de octubre de 1947. Junto a este aviso financiero, un anuncio turístico publicado por el Centro de Información de la República Dominicana promociona el país como una combinación de modernidad y monumentos históricos. El aviso invita a los turistas a escribir al Director de Turismo en Ciudad Trujillo para solicitar folletos descriptivos con pormenores sobre excursiones, paisajes rurales y hoteles.

records.headline: President Rafael Trujillo was inaugurated before foreign diplomats
records.summary_en: President Rafael Trujillo was inaugurated before foreign diplomats and members of the National Assembly in the Senate following his May 17 re-election with a 30-to-1 lead over two opponents. In his inaugural address, Trujillo pledged to maintain the established democratic order and protect the country against anti-American ideology, before leading officials and diplomats in a march to the cathedral of Santo Domingo for a Te Deum service. The report observes that Trujillo has retained power since 1930 except for the period between 1938 and 1942, and notes that his two rivals had conceded defeat prior to the election.
records.summary_es: El presidente Rafael Trujillo fue juramentado ante diplomáticos extranjeros y miembros de la Asamblea Nacional en el Senado tras su reelección del 17 de mayo por una ventaja de 30 a 1 sobre dos opositores. En su discurso inaugural, Trujillo se comprometió a preservar el orden democrático establecido y a defender al país de ideologías antinorteamericanas, antes de encabezar una marcha de funcionarios y diplomáticos hacia la catedral de Santo Domingo para un tedeum. La nota señala que Trujillo retiene el poder desde 1930, salvo por el periodo entre 1938 y 1942, y destaca que sus dos contendientes habían admitido la derrota con anterioridad a los comicios.

records.headline: The Dominican government would welcome an international commission
records.summary_en: The Dominican government would welcome an international commission to investigate reports that an international brigade of communist revolutionaries was mobilizing in Cuba to invade the Dominican Republic, it announced in Ciudad Trujillo. The statement noted that the government felt it should solicit the good offices of another American nation to persuade Cuba to permit such an inquiry. The article adds that the initial reports originated from the Dominican ambassador in Washington, who alleged that a 3,000-man communist force from Cuba, Guatemala, Venezuela, and Puerto Rico was assembling to overthrow the Trujillo administration, charges that Cuban authorities subsequently denied.
records.summary_es: El gobierno dominicano recibiría con beneplácito una comisión internacional para investigar las denuncias de que una brigada internacional de revolucionarios comunistas se organizaba en Cuba para invadir la República Dominicana, según anunció en Ciudad Trujillo. El comunicado señaló que el gobierno consideraba oportuno solicitar los buenos oficios de otra nación americana a fin de persuadir a Cuba de autorizar dicha pesquisa. El despacho agrega que los primeros reportes procedían del embajador dominicano en Washington, quien afirmó que una fuerza comunista de 3,000 hombres de Cuba, Guatemala, Venezuela y Puerto Rico se concentraba para derrocar a la administración de Trujillo, acusaciones que las autoridades cubanas desmintieron con posterioridad.

records.headline: Cuban President Grau San Martin informed President Rafael Trujillo
records.summary_en: Cuban President Grau San Martin informed President Rafael Trujillo by cable that he was investigating allegations of a revolutionary army mobilizing in Cuba to invade the Dominican Republic, the Dominican Information Bureau announced. The message came in response to a cable sent 24 hours earlier by Trujillo, who requested that steps be taken to halt an international brigade gathering in Cuba to overthrow his regime. Cuban officials had previously maintained that the frequently repeated Dominican accusations were unfounded.
records.summary_es: El presidente cubano Grau San Martin comunicó por cable al presidente Rafael Trujillo que investigaba las denuncias sobre un ejército revolucionario que se concentraba en Cuba para invadir la República Dominicana, según informó la Oficina de Información Dominicana. El mensaje respondió a un cable enviado 24 horas antes por Trujillo, quien solicitó medidas para poner fin a las actividades de una brigada internacional reunida en Cuba con el fin de derrocar a su régimen. Los funcionarios cubanos habían sostenido con anterioridad que las acusaciones dominicanas formuladas con frecuencia carecían de base.

records.headline: The newspaper said its investigation of State Department detention
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that federal customs authorities in Baltimore detained the *Patria*, a converted infantry landing craft suspected of involvement in anti-Trujillo activities. An investigation revealed the vessel was manned largely by affluent Dominican exiles and had been acquired by Cuban Cruz Alonso, though a search found no weapons or ammunition. The State Department stated the action enforced strict policy prohibiting the use of United States territory to launch civil strife in foreign nations.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que la policía aduanera federal destacada en Baltimore aprehendió al *Patria*, un buque de desembarco de infantería modificado sospechoso de involucramiento en actividades conspirativas contra Trujillo. Las pesquisas comprobaron que la dotación estaba formada mayoritariamente por acaudalados desterrados dominicanos y que la nave había sido adquirida por el cubano Cruz Alonso, si bien el registro ocular no arrojó hallazgo de municiones ni fusiles. El Departamento de Estado aclaró que la retención obedecía a la estricta política neutral de proscribir la utilización del suelo estadounidense para fraguar expediciones bélicas contra Estados soberanos.
records.passage: The newspaper said its investigation of State Department detention of a converted infantry landing craft in Baltimore Harbor disclosed the ship's "crew” was composed largely of Dominican exiles who “hated” Rafael L. Trujillo, for 17 years President of the republic. Customs officials ordered the 153 foot landing craft detained yesterday. A State Department spokesman said in Washington the action was in line with its instructions to the Federal Bureau of Investigation and other Government agencies to prevent the use of territory in this country as a possible base of operations to promote civil strife elsewhere. The Evening Sun said its investigation disclosed that nearly 40 men were aboard the LCI at one time, although a normal crew is 12 or 14, and that most of them “looked like college boys” and were either exiles or sons of exiles who had lost large land holdings under the Trujillo regime. Most of the "crew" had left “by last night.” the paper reported, and conversations aboard indicated many of them were from fairly wealthy families" and “were not Communists." Customs authorities announced yesterday that a search of the vessel for arms and ammunition had been fruitless. Workers at the ship repair yard where she was tied up were preparing today to seal her doors. The Evening Sun said the ship, called the Patria. originally was sold to a Cuban named Cruz Alonso by a New York ship broker and moved here for repairs from an anchorage on the James River in Virginia. records.summary_en: The Evening Star published a letter from Dominican exile Persio C. Franco criticizing former Secretary of State Cordell Hull for congratulating President Rafael Trujillo on paying off the Dominican foreign debt. Franco condemned Hull's praise as inappropriate, accusing Trujillo of seizing power through treason in 1930 and maintaining control through terror and murder. Franco appealed to democratic nations to support the Dominican people in reclaiming their freedom rather than endorsing the dictatorship.

Franco tildó de imprudente el encomio de Hull, denunciando que Trujillo se entronizó en el poder mediante la traición en 1930 y sojuzgaba a la nación mediante el crimen y el terror estatal. Franco exhortó a los pueblos democráticos del orbe a amparar a la ciudadanía dominicana en su anhelo libertario en lugar de convalidar la tiranía.

records.headline: The consulate of the Dominican Republic announced that tobacco
records.summary_en: The consulate of the Dominican Republic announced that tobacco heiress Miss Duke, a fashion correspondent for Harper's Bazaar, is planning to marry Porfirio Rubirosa, former son-in-law of Dominican President Rafael Trujillo. A consulate spokesman stated that the wedding would take place either on Monday or early in the coming week. Rubirosa, an honorary chargé d'affaires for the Trujillo regime, was previously married to Flor de Oro Trujillo and was divorced last May from actress Danielle Darriew. Miss Duke was formerly married to James H. R. Cromwell, former American minister to Canada.
records.summary_es: El consulado de la República Dominicana anunció que la señorita Duke, heredera del tabaco y corresponsal de modas para Harper's Bazaar, planea casarse con Porfirio Rubirosa, exyerno del presidente dominicano Rafael Trujillo. Un portavoz del consulado declaró que la ceremonia se celebraría el lunes o a principios de la próxima semana. Rubirosa, encargado de negocios honorario del régimen de Trujillo, estuvo casado anteriormente con Flor de Oro Trujillo y se divorció en mayo pasado de la actriz Danielle Darriew. La señorita Duke estuvo casada previamente con James H. R. Cromwell, exministro estadounidense en Canadá.

records.summary_en: Dominican Consul General Dr. Salvador E. Paradas officiated at the civil marriage of Miss Duke and Rubirosa in his second-floor consulate office so the ceremony would take place on Dominican soil. records.headline: In a personal account of surviving severe Caribbean storms
records.summary_en: In a personal account of surviving severe Caribbean storms, the devastation of three major hurricanes is described, including the 1928 hurricane in Puerto Rico and the 1932 storm that struck the capital of the Dominican Republic—then called Santo Domingo—and took 10,000 lives. The author notes that winds exceeding 100 miles per hour demolished houses and scattered zinc roofing for miles, leaving only concrete structures standing.

El autor señala que vientos de más de 100 millas por hora demolieron casas y esparcieron planchas de zinc a lo largo de millas, dejando en pie únicamente las estructuras de concreto.

records.full_text:
Cuban Senators Link Grau With Abortive Dominican Invasion

By the Associated Press

HAVANA, Cuba, Oct. 1.—Two Cuban Senators accused President Grau San Martin last night of complicity in the organization of an expeditionary force which intended—before it was broken up by the Cuban Army and Navy—to overthrow the government of the Dominican Republic.

Senator Eduardo Chibas, an aspirant for the presidency in the June, 1948, elections, declared in a statement published in the newspaper Prensa Libre that the Cuban President "betrayed the cause of Dominican liberty after having offered hospitality and refuge to the political exiles of this sister republic."

Move for Dictatorship Charged.

"Grau, upon the pretext of liberating the Dominican Republic from the dictator (President Rafael) Trujillo, was conspiring to suspend the forthcoming elections and convert himself into the dictator of Cuba," Senator Chibas' statement said.

The Senator previously had been considered one of the President's staunchest defenders.

Senator Aurelio Alvarez, leader of the opposition, accused President Grau of having "armed gangs which sought to invade the Dominican Republic, in order to create an atmosphere of violence in Cuba and thus perpetuate himself in power."

The army announced Monday that it had crushed the ambitious expeditionary force—numbering about 1,500 men with four vessels and a considerable amount of arms, ammunition and explosives—which had been organized in Cuba in July to invade the Dominican Republic.

360 Detained in Prison.

Some 360 alleged members of the expedition were detained in the prison at Camp Columbia, army headquarters in Havana, and 781 other men described as members of the expedition were reported en route here by train from Antilla, where they surrendered aboard two of the expedition's ships yesterday.

Some of the expedition's leaders were reported to be among this latter group:

Col. Oscar Diaz, who made the army's announcement concerning the crushing of the expedition Monday, was quoted under banner headlines in the Cuban press as having said the expedition also had sought to stage "a revolutionary coup (in Cuba) to prevent the elections."

President Grau summoned reporters to the presidential palace yesterday and informed them that Col. Diaz had denied making this statement.

records.headline: Cuban military authorities reported that a 1,900-man expeditionary force
records.summary_en: Cuban military authorities reported that a 1,900-man expeditionary force organized to overthrow President Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic had been broken up. Col. Oscar Diaz, the army's chief investigator, stated that some conspirators turned against the Cuban government after their invasion failed, prompting a Senate inquiry and leading Diaz to submit documents to the Supreme Tribunal. Diaz stated that 360 unarmed men from the expedition were recovered on Quinchos Cay, 50 miles off the north Cuban coast and 300 miles east of Havana, after refusing their commander's orders to attack the Cuban navy, while 11 bombing planes were seized and two expedition ships surrendered at Antilla.
records.summary_es: Las autoridades militares cubanas informaron que una fuerza expedicionaria de 1,900 hombres organizada para derrocar al presidente Rafael Trujillo de la República Dominicana había sido desarticulada. El coronel Oscar Díaz, jefe de investigaciones del ejército, declaró que algunos conspiradores se volvieron contra el gobierno cubano tras el fracaso de su invasión, lo que motivó una investigación del Senado y llevó a Díaz a entregar documentos al Tribunal Supremo. Díaz afirmó que 360 hombres desarmados de la expedición fueron rescatados en Cayo Quinchos, a 50 millas de la costa norte de Cuba y a 300 millas al este de La Habana, tras negarse a acatar las órdenes de su comandante de atacar a la marina cubana, al tiempo que se incautaron 11 aviones bombarderos y dos barcos expedicionarios se rindieron en Antilla.

Un diario de bitácora ocupado y divulgado por el diario *Hoy* detalló los adiestramientos castrenses en Holguín y las precarias penalidades sufridas en Cayo Confites, donde los reclutas padecieron motines internos, ahogamientos accidentales y severos descalabros de abasto a bordo de los barcos *Aurora*, *Berta* y *Angelita*. records.full_text:
Cuba Cabinet Member Quits After Link to Dominican Invasion

By the Associated Press

HAVANA, Cuba, Oct. 2.—Education Minister Jose Manuel Aleman, whose name has been mentioned in connection with a recently smashed expedition organized in Cuba to invade the Dominican Republic, quit his job last night under fire.

The Cuban Senate had voted "no confidence" in Mr. Aleman on the ground that arms were found at his home and that he allegedly had on his payroll persons not connected with his ministry.

Mr. Aleman resigned at once. President Ramon Grau San Martin immediately appointed him a minister without portfolio and elevated Undersecretary Carlos F. Arazosa to the Education Ministry. Mr. Aleman had held the education post since May, 1946.

Col. Oscar Diaz of the Cuban Army charged at a news conference Monday that Mr. Aleman was implicated in the organization of the expedition plotted to overthrow the Dominican Republic government of President Rafael Trujillo.

The diary of one of the troopers in the 1,500-man expedition, published yesterday in the newspaper Hoy, said he had been given rifle practice for 13 days at the military and civic institute at Holguin, in Eastern Cuba. The institute is under control of the Cuban Education Ministry.

Senators, in voting nonconfidence in Mr. Aleman, said that arms, including depth bombs, were seized by Cuban soldiers September 20 at the ranch home which Mr. Aleman rents. Other Cuban officials have linked this arms seizure to the Dominican expedition.

In the meantime, Magistrate Evelio Tabio of the supreme tribunal of the Criminal Court announced that only the purported leaders of the expeditionary force would be kept in custody after today. Nearly 1,200 others now being held will be released.

About 725 members of the expedition who surrendered Tuesday at the port of Antilla arrived here last night by train to join 360 others who were picked up earlier from Guinchos Cay, a sandspit off the Cuban coast.

Mr. Tabio did not disclose the names of those he considered to be the leaders, nor their number.

Hoy withheld the name of the trooper who wrote the diary. The diary's account:

The volunteer enlisted July 20 for the campaign against President Rafael Trujillo, was trained at Holguin and then transferred with other revolutionaries from a coastal point to Confites Key. The diary said the men were moved aboard the ships Aurora and Berta and a Dominican schooner registered as the Angelita, which the expeditionary force captured near Confites Keys.

Two volunteers drowned while being disembarked. One was a Cuban, the other a Venezuelan. One man was killed and some others were wounded in fighting among themselves.

The troops became discontented over delays in action against the Dominican Republic. On August 16, which was D-day, a ship expected to arrive with war material and food did not make port. The diary said the troops showed distrust afterwards upon learning there had been fighting among members of their high command. Food and water also were short.

records.headline: Heavily armed troops guarded 500 bedraggled members of the abortive revolutionary expedition
records.summary_en: Heavily armed troops guarded 500 bedraggled members of the abortive revolutionary expedition against the Dominican Republic as they awaited release at Camp Columbia following a grueling 32-hour boxcar journey from Antilla. Claiming they had been 'sold' to the 17-year dictatorship of Generalissimo Rafael Leonidas Trujillo, the men shouted denouncements against Cuban army chief Gen. Genovevo Perez Damera. Although the criminal branch of the Cuban Supreme Court ordered the immediate release of the rank and file while holding top leaders, observers doubted authorities would discharge 900 penurious men into the city without feeding and clothing them first.
records.summary_es: Tropas fuertemente armadas custodiaban a 500 exhaustos miembros de la fallida expedición revolucionaria contra la República Dominicana mientras esperaban su liberación en el campamento militar Columbia tras un agotador viaje de 32 horas en vagones de carga desde Antilla. Alegando que habían sido «vendidos» a la dictadura de 17 años del generalísimo Rafael Leónidas Trujillo, los hombres vociferaron consignas contra el jefe del ejército cubano, general Genovevo Pérez Dámera. Aunque la sala de lo penal del Tribunal Supremo cubano ordenó la liberación inmediata de los subordinados reteniendo a los principales cabecillas, los observadores dudaban que las autoridades soltaran en la ciudad a 900 hombres indigentes sin antes alimentarlos y vestirlos.

Special Magistrate Evelio Tabio of the Supreme Tribunal accepted the bonds from a security company, which refused to say for whom it was acting Judge Tabio had ordered the 26 men charged with “having jeopardized the peace of the state” and having taken enlistments “without legal authorization of the Cuban government.” The group, mostly Dominicans and Cubans, included eight generals. Waddel, 27, and Thomas Sawyer, 26, both of New York city. The force surrendered to Cuban authorities early last week on Guinchos Cay off the North Cuban coast and at the port of Antilla.

records.headline: President Branch Rickey of the Brooklyn Dodgers announced in New York
records.summary_en: President Branch Rickey of the Brooklyn Dodgers announced in New York that the baseball club will conduct spring training next year in Ciudad Trujillo, capital city of the Dominican Republic. records.full_text:
Cuban Blames Trujillo For Arms Plot Charges

By the Associated Press

JACKSONVILLE, Fla., Dec. 9.—Manolo Castro, director of the Cuban Sports Commission, charged yesterday that enmity of Rafael Trujillo was responsible for his implication in an alleged plot to export arms to Cuba for use in an unsuccessful revolt against the Dominican Republic President last summer.

Castro, who came to Jacksonville for arraignment on an indictment charging illegal exportation of arms and high explosives from the United States, pleaded not guilty before Federal Judge Louie W. Strum.

The case was set for trial January 5.

Not guilty pleas also were entered by Chester L. Miller and Percy H. Cyr, both airplane pilots of Hasbrouck Heights, N. J. Hollis B. Smith, Palisades Park, N. J., who is alleged to have purchased the arms, pleaded guilty.

Smith was permitted to remain under bond pending disposition of the charges against the other defendants.

records.headline: DIPLOMATIC NOTES FOR DREW PEARSON A plot by the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: A White Paper circulated by the Venezuelan Embassy charged that the Dominican Republic was plotting to send an armed invasion against Venezuela, accusing dictator Trujillo of harboring Venezuelan enemies and purchasing arms for them in Brazil. As proof it attached a photostat of an intercepted letter from Trujillo's private secretary to Dominican foreign offices around the world, instructing them to attend to exiled Venezuelans, enemies of Caracas, and to tell them they would find in the Dominican Republic refuge, hospitality and protection, personal as well as political. The White Paper added that the Venezuelan government had concrete proof the Dominican Republic had long sponsored an armed movement against Venezuela. The paper went on that the movement was composed of exiled Venezuelans training at Dominican airports, that its agents traveled on Dominican diplomatic passports, and that Trujillo had purchased vast stores of arms in Brazil, using the Presidential yacht to ship them — one shipment assertedly included 10,000 rifles, 30,000,000 rounds of ammunition, and 800 machine guns — more than Dominican defense required, and a "serious preoccupation for all the American Governments." Venezuela could break relations, the paper said, but would not lift a finger to disturb the peace of the Dominican Republic unless obliged to defend her own rights, sovereignty, and institutions.
records.summary_es: Un Libro Blanco distribuido por la Embajada de Venezuela acusó a la República Dominicana de tramar el envío de una invasión armada contra Venezuela, señalando al dictador Trujillo de albergar a enemigos venezolanos y comprar armas para ellos en Brasil. Como prueba adjuntaba una fotocopia de una carta interceptada del secretario privado de Trujillo a las oficinas dominicanas en el exterior, con instrucciones de atender a los venezolanos exiliados, enemigos de Caracas, y decirles que en la República Dominicana encontrarían refugio, hospitalidad y protección, tanto personal como política. El Libro Blanco añadía que el gobierno venezolano tenía pruebas concretas de que la República Dominicana auspiciaba desde hacía tiempo un movimiento armado contra Venezuela. El documento proseguía que el movimiento estaba compuesto por venezolanos exiliados que se entrenaban en aeropuertos dominicanos, que sus agentes viajaban con pasaportes diplomáticos dominicanos y que Trujillo había comprado en Brasil grandes cantidades de armas, usando el yate presidencial para transportarlas —un cargamento, según se afirmaba, incluía 10,000 fusiles, 30,000,000 de cartuchos y 800 ametralladoras—, más de lo que requería la defensa dominicana y una «seria preocupación para todos los gobiernos americanos». Venezuela podía romper relaciones, decía el documento, pero no movería un dedo para perturbar la paz de la República Dominicana a menos que se viera obligada a defender sus propios derechos, su soberanía y sus instituciones.
records.passage: DIPLOMATIC NOTES FOR DREW PEARSON A plot by the Dominican Republic to send an armed invasion against Venezuela is charged in a "White Paper" circulated among Latin American Ambassadors here by the Venezuelan Embassy. Written in Spanish, the paper accuses dictator Trujillo of harboring Venezuelan enemies and purchasing arms for them in Brazil. At proof, a photostat is attached of an intercepted letter from Trujillo's private secretary to the Dominican foreign offices around the world. Translated, the letter declares: "The Honorable President Trujillo has charged me to communicate to you that it is his wish that you attend to the exiled Venezuelans, enemies of the Caracas, who are residing in or who pass through your jurisdiction. Inform them that they will find in the Dominican Republica a good refuge, hospitality and protection, personal as well as political. Do all that is possible to convince them that they should come to reside in our country." records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that thirty-one persons were killed on Sunday when a commercial transport plane crashed in Rio Verde while flying from Barahona to Santiago in the Dominican Republic. Burial services were held the following day for the three crew members and 28 passengers, most of whom were baseball players returning from a game in Barahona. The aircraft was operated by Compania Nacional, a Dominican airline.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de la Associated Press desde Ciudad Trujillo informa que treinta y una personas perecieron el domingo cuando un avión de transporte comercial se estrelló en Río Verde mientras volaba de Barahona a Santiago, en la República Dominicana. Al día siguiente se celebraron las honras fúnebres para los tres tripulantes y los 28 pasajeros, la mayoría de los cuales eran jugadores de béisbol que regresaban de un partido en Barahona. El avión era operado por la Compañía Nacional, una aerolínea dominicana.

records.headline: A Hollywood entertainment column reports that actress Laraine Day
records.summary_en: A Hollywood entertainment column reports that actress Laraine Day and Leo Durocher are considering marrying in Santo Domingo to escape crowds of reporters and photographers wanting to attend their ceremony in the United States. The couple plans to leave shortly for the Dominican Republic, where Durocher will direct spring training for the Brooklyn Dodgers. Day plans to film a movie in New York in August to remain near her husband during the baseball season.

La pareja planea viajar en breve a la República Dominicana, donde Durocher dirigirá los entrenamientos de primavera de los Brooklyn Dodgers. Day tiene previsto rodar una película en Nueva York en agosto para permanecer junto a su marido durante la temporada de béisbol.

records.headline: A book review examining an analysis of political forces in the Americas
records.summary_en: A book review examining an analysis of political forces in the Americas by Mr. Tomlinson discusses three main categories of regional dictatorship. The author places Trujillo of the Dominican Republic, alongside Gomez of Venezuela and Somoza of Nicaragua, into a category of individualistic, swashbuckling dictators who seized power to satisfy personal greed or ambition rather than an ideological doctrine. While noting the danger posed by such rulers to freedom, the review contrasts them with what Tomlinson views as the far graver threat of communist and ultranationalist movements across Latin America.
records.summary_es: Una reseña literaria sobre el análisis de las fuerzas políticas en las Américas realizado por el Sr. Tomlinson comenta tres categorías principales de dictaduras en la región. El autor ubica a Trujillo de la República Dominicana, junto a Gómez de Venezuela y Somoza de Nicaragua, dentro de una categoría de dictadores individualistas y pintorescos que tomaron el poder para colmar su codicia o ambición personal antes que una doctrina ideológica. Si bien advierte el peligro que estos mandatarios entrañan para la libertad, la reseña los distingue de lo que Tomlinson considera la amenaza mucho más grave de los movimientos comunistas y ultranacionalistas en América Latina.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that tobacco heiress Doris Duke Rubirosa arrived by airplane in New York from Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic. She was noted as the wife of Porfirio Rubirosa, the Dominican Ambassador to Argentina. Other brief items in the issue covered a Supreme Court labor ruling regarding foremen and President Truman's request for additional aid to Greece and Turkey.

Otras informaciones sucintas del despacho reseñaron un dictamen laboral emitido por el Tribunal Supremo con respecto a los capataces y la solicitud presupuestaria formulada por el presidente Truman en auxilio de Grecia y Turquía.

President to Ask More Money for Greece, Turkey Reports to Congress On Aid Already Given Against Guerrillas EATON WILLING to cut foreign aid fund to get passage. Page A-4 President Truman notified Congress today that he intends to ask more money, for military aid, for Greece and Turkey. He gave no indication of how much new assistance will be needed, however, in transmitting to Congress a report on use of the $400,000,000 voted last year to help Greece and Turkey resist Communism. Mr. Truman declared in a letter accompanying the report that Greece has been under “ever increasing pressure by the communist minority” drawing support from “foreign influences” since his last report in November. The communist obstruction, he added, makes it clear that "economic recovery in Greece must await establishment of internal security." Way Open for More Direct Aid.

records.headline: A baseball survey notes that major league teams will play a total of 378 grapefruit league exhibition games
records.summary_en: A baseball survey notes that major league teams will play a total of 378 Grapefruit League exhibition games during spring training, with all sixteen squads training in the United States except the Brooklyn Dodgers. The Dodgers are preparing for their National League season at Ciudad Trujillo in the Dominican Republic. Florida remains the favorite conditioning site with five American and four National League clubs, while other teams are based in California and Arizona.
records.summary_es: Un informe de béisbol señala que los equipos de las Grandes Ligas disputarán un total de 378 juegos de exhibición de la Liga de la Toronja durante los entrenamientos de primavera, preparándose todas las escuadras en los Estados Unidos con la sola excepción de los Brooklyn Dodgers. Los Dodgers se alistan para su temporada de la Liga Nacional en Ciudad Trujillo, República Dominicana. Florida se mantiene como la sede predilecta con cinco novenas de la Liga Americana y cuatro de la Liga Nacional, mientras que otros conjuntos se ubican en California y Arizona.

records.headline: Jackie Robinson has become the center of attention for spectators
records.summary_en: Jackie Robinson has become the center of attention for spectators attending the Brooklyn Dodgers' spring workouts in the Dominican Republic, an Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports under the heading 'Robinson Intrigues Fans.' After arriving in camp the previous day and joining team drills, the first baseman lined three pitches to deep left center and worked around first base despite carrying 15 pounds of excess weight.
records.summary_es: Jackie Robinson se ha convertido en el centro de atención para los espectadores que concurren a los entrenamientos de primavera de los Brooklyn Dodgers en la República Dominicana, según informa un despacho de la Associated Press desde Ciudad Trujillo bajo el encabezado «Robinson Intrigues Fans». Luego de llegar al campamento el día previo e incorporarse a los ejercicios del equipo, el primera base conectó con contundencia tres lanzamientos a lo profundo del jardín izquierdo-central y se ejercitó alrededor de la primera almohadilla a pesar de presentar 15 libras de sobrepeso.

records.summary_en: A baseball dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that minor ailments have disrupted workouts for the Brooklyn Dodgers in the Dominican Republic, with pitcher Ralph Branca sidelined by a pulled thigh muscle, Rex Barney suffering from grippe, Duke Snider recovering from an intestinal disturbance, and Al Gionfriddo recuperating after being struck on the head by a pitch from rookie Johnny Van Cuyk on his 26th birthday. Jackie Robinson Now Working Out With Brooklyn

CUIDAD TRUJILLO, Dominican Republic—(NNPA)—Jackie Robinson, the Brooklyn Dodgers' first baseman, arrived in training camp here last Thursday and went thru his first workout with the team.

Regarded here as a baseball hero, every move Jackie made on the field was applauded by the natives. School kids, eating their lunch in the grandstand, shouted when they spied Jackie in the dugout, applauded him when he took his turn at batting practice, and cheered every time he hit the ball.

Jackie reported over weight by fifteen pounds. He hit .297 last season and figures to better that mark this year. He worked out at first base.

records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that Brooklyn Dodgers pitcher Dan Bankhead, formerly of the Memphis Negro League, is receiving an opportunity to demonstrate his ability in the outfield. Bankhead contributed a single that helped Brooklyn score four runs during the second inning of an exhibition contest against the Montreal Royals, which the Dodgers won by a score of 8-2. El mánager Leo Durocher comentó que Bankhead es un atleta formidable en todos los sentidos y recordó que bateó un cuadrangular en su primer turno al bate el año anterior.

records.headline: NEA sports editor Harry Grayson reports from Ciudad Trujillo
records.summary_en: NEA sports editor Harry Grayson reports from Ciudad Trujillo that Brooklyn Dodgers manager Leo Durocher is exhibiting conspicuously subdued behavior following his yearlong banishment from baseball. Accompanied by Laraine Day at the Presidente Trujillo High School Stadium and the Hotel Jaragua, Durocher is abstaining from alcohol and tobacco while using unusually mild language. Although Durocher insists he has not changed and will continue to argue aggressively with umpires to shield his key players from ejection, Grayson writes that the manager's present decorum stands in marked contrast to his former temperament.
records.summary_es: El editor deportivo de NEA, Harry Grayson, informa desde Ciudad Trujillo que el mánager de los Dodgers de Brooklyn, Leo Durocher, muestra un comportamiento visiblemente moderado tras cumplir su año de suspensión del béisbol. Acompañado por Laraine Day en el Estadio de la Escuela Secundaria Presidente Trujillo y en el Hotel Jaragua, Durocher se abstiene del alcohol y el tabaco a la vez que emplea un lenguaje inusualmente templado. Aunque Durocher insiste en que no ha cambiado y continuará discutiendo enérgicamente con los árbitros para proteger a sus peloteros clave de las expulsiones, Grayson escribe que el decoro actual del mánager contrasta notablemente con su temperamento anterior.

records.headline: An NNPA dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that defensive shifts
records.summary_en: An NNPA dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that defensive shifts in the Brooklyn Dodgers' training camp indicate Jackie Robinson will become the regular second baseman, while Roy Campanella will share catching duties with Bruce Edwards. Following the trade of Eddie Stanky to Boston, manager Leo Durocher tested outfielders Pete Reiser and Dick Whitman at first base, clearing the way for Robinson to return to his natural position at second. The club also experimented by playing Campanella in right field and at third base, and used pitcher Dan Bankhead in the outfield. During Tuesday's 13 to 4 victory over the Montreal Royals, Robinson batted in the leadoff spot and dispelled suggestions that he lacked hustle.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de la NNPA desde Ciudad Trujillo informa que las variantes defensivas en el campamento de entrenamiento de los Dodgers de Brooklyn indican que Jackie Robinson será el segunda base titular, mientras que Roy Campanella compartirá la receptoría con Bruce Edwards. Tras el traspaso de Eddie Stanky a Boston, el mánager Leo Durocher probó a los jardineros Pete Reiser y Dick Whitman en la primera base, abriendo el camino para que Robinson volviera a su posición natural en la intermedia. El club también experimentó alineando a Campanella en el jardín derecho y en la tercera base, y colocó al lanzador Dan Bankhead en los jardines. Durante la victoria del martes por 13 a 4 sobre los Reales de Montreal, Robinson bateó como primer bate y disipó las versiones de que carecía de entrega.

records.headline: The Costa Rican government has renewed appeals to Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the Costa Rican government appealed to Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic for military assistance against insurgent forces led by Jose Figueres. Rebel troops sabotaged electrical installations at Brazil and launched surprise assaults at Quepos, threatening the advance toward Cartago. The armed conflict arose following the disputed presidential election of Otilio Ulate, which the government-controlled Congress had annulled in favor of Rafael Calderon Guardia.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el gobierno constitucional de Costa Rica recabó socorro de armas a Nicaragua y a la República Dominicana con el propósito de combatir a las columnas rebeldes acaudilladas por José Figueres. Los destacamentos insurrectos sabotearon redes de energía en la localidad de Brasil y acometieron asaltos sorpresivos en Quepos, poniendo en jaque el avance hacia Cartago. La contienda intestina estalló a raíz de los controvertidos sufragios presidenciales que ungieron a Otilio Ulate, los cuales fueron anulados por el Congreso oficialista para beneficiar al candidato Rafael Calderón Guardia.

Costa Rica Asks Aid From Two Republics By the Associated Press SAN JOSE, Costa Rica, Mar. 27.— The Costa Rican government has renewed appeals to Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic for help in fighting the Figueres revolutionary forces, reliable sources said tonight, What the response would be no one could say. Nicaraguan troops have been fighting on the government's side and some are still here, although an order for their return home has been issued. Rebel troops, led by Jose Figueres, slipped through government lines this morning and dynamited power plant installations at Brazil on the Pacific Coast. They also began a surprise attack against government troops at Quepos north of Dominical which the government has been trying to hold since last week. To the south Figueres soldiers moved down the side of Cerro de la Muerte Mountain toward Cartago and apparently were ready to storm that ancient capital of Costa Rica. The fighting which began 17 days ago is the outgrowth of last month's turbulent and disputed presidential election in which Otilio Ulate was elected. On March 1, the government-controlled Congress annulled the election, upholding fraud charges brought by Rafael Calderon Guardia, government-backed candidate. [illegible] [illegible]

records.headline: A dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that the Brooklyn Dodgers prepared
records.summary_en: A dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that the Brooklyn Dodgers prepared to depart for Florida following the completion of their spring training camp. Team president Branch Rickey indicated that the organization planned to return to the Dominican Republic for training in 1949. The Dodgers finished their stay undefeated, winning 14 exhibition contests without a loss against minor league and amateur opponents.
records.summary_es: Un despacho desde Ciudad Trujillo informa que los Dodgers de Brooklyn se preparaban para viajar a Florida tras concluir su campamento de entrenamientos de primavera. El presidente del equipo, Branch Rickey, indicó que la organización planeaba regresar a la República Dominicana para entrenar en 1949. Los Dodgers terminaron su estadía de manera invicta, ganando 14 partidos de exhibición sin derrota alguna frente a rivales de ligas menores y aficionados.

records.headline: An SNS dispatch from Vero Beach reports that the Brooklyn Dodgers
records.summary_en: An SNS dispatch from Vero Beach reports that the Brooklyn Dodgers are scheduled to arrive in Florida after completing a month of spring training in Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic. The report notes that the organization received a guarantee of $65,000 to utilize the island's facilities and stayed at the Jaragua. In their final game in Ciudad Trujillo, an alternate Brooklyn squad defeated the Montreal Royals 6-4 before approximately 400 spectators while the regular lineup competed in Santiago.

En su último partido en Ciudad Trujillo, una escuadra alternativa de Brooklyn derrotó a los Reales de Montreal por 6-4 ante unos 400 espectadores, mientras la alineación titular competía en Santiago.

records.headline: A sports report notes that the Brooklyn Dodgers arrived in Florida
records.summary_en: A sports report notes that the Brooklyn Dodgers arrived in Florida on Tuesday aboard a Pan-American Clipper following the close of their training camp in Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic. On Wednesday, the team inaugurated Dodgertown's Ebbets Field No. 2 by defeating their Montreal Royals farm club for the tenth consecutive time. The main Dodger squad subsequently headed for Texas to begin an exhibition tour at Fort Worth, with Jackie Robinson and Roy Campanella playing with the primary roster rather than the secondary squad appearing in Atlanta.

El miércoles, el conjunto inauguró el Ebbets Field No. 2 de Dodgertown al derrotar a su filial de los Reales de Montreal por décima vez consecutiva. La plantilla principal de los Dodgers partió seguidamente hacia Texas para comenzar una gira de exhibición en Fort Worth, con Jackie Robinson y Roy Campanella integrando la escuadra titular en lugar del equipo secundario que se presentaba en Atlanta.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star analyzed strategic vulnerabilities in Caribbean defenses, warning of potential submarine threats to the Panama Canal and regional bases. The analysis noted ongoing armed conflict in Costa Rica, where government forces reportedly received backing from Dominicans, Nicaraguans, and Hondurans against rebels supporting Otilio Ulate. The author cautioned that a communist victory would leave American defense lines bordered by hostile regimes, with the unsympathetic Dominican government positioned centrally in the region.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* examinó las vulnerabilidades operativas en el dispositivo de seguridad caribeño, previniendo acerca de posibles amenazas submarinas contra el canal de Panamá y las bases tácticas comarcanas. La crónica reparó en las hostilidades fratricidas de Costa Rica, señalando que las tropas gobiernistas contaban presuntamente con el apoyo de efectivos dominicanos, nicaragüenses y hondureños para contrarrestar a los alzados que secundaban a Otilio Ulate. El redactor alertó de que una victoria de cuño comunista dejaría el cordón defensivo estadounidense flanqueado por regímenes antagonistas, con el desconfiado gobierno dominicano afianzado en el corazón del espacio antillano.

records.summary_en: An aviation feature reports that Pan American has introduced special summer excursion rates effective through September 30, providing discounts of more than 30 per cent from southern United States cities. Seventeen itineraries have been arranged offering reduced airfares to Caribbean and Latin American destinations including Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic, and Port-au-Prince, Haiti. records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that President Truman nominated Ralph H. Ackerman, a career Foreign Service officer from California, to serve as Ambassador to the Dominican Republic. The President also appointed Ambassador Henry F. Grady to an additional post on the United Nations Economic Commission for Asia and the Far East. Domestically, Michigan state police were dispatched to suburban Detroit to control picket line violence during a Chrysler auto strike.

Michigan Police Called to Quell Auto Pickets CIO Union Threatens To Call Out 225,000 At GM in Two Weeks By the Associated Press DETROIT, May 17.—Special squads of State police were rushed into suburban Highland Park today to cope with an outbreak of picket line violence around one of 16 strikebound Chrysler Corp. plants. They were dispatched into the Detroit area by Gov. Kim Sigler at the request of Mayor Norman Patterson of Highland Park. Mayor Patterson said local police were unable to quell a disturbance started by CIO united Auto Workers “goon squads." Two policemen were reported sent to the hospital by the outbreak of fist fighting and rock throwing. Gov. Sigler also disclosed he was preparing to alert the National Guard if necessary. First Violence in Strike This first major violence in the 6-day-old Chrysler strike came as the auto-union threatened to call a strike of 225.000 General Motors workers and replied tartly to an unexpected plea from the Ford Motor Co. to cut wages. T. A. Johnstone, acting director of the UAW's General Motors department, said there is "a very good possibility" of a walkout in 90 GM
records.full_text:
Henry Grady Nominated To Asia Economic Unit

President Truman today nominated Ambassador to India Henry F. Grady as United States representative on the Economic Commission for Asia and the Far East.

Mr. Grady will hold the post along with his job as Ambassador and as Minister to Nepal.

The Economic Commission was established by the Economic and Social Council of the United Nations on March 28, 1947.

The President also nominated Ralph H. Ackerman to be Ambassador to the Dominican Republic.

Mr. Ackerman, a Californian, is a Foreign Service career man.

records.headline: A geographical note reports that the Dominican Republic occupies
records.summary_en: A geographical note reports that the Dominican Republic occupies approximately two-thirds of the island of Santo Domingo, which Columbus named Hispaniola upon discovering it during his first voyage in 1492, while Haiti occupies the remaining third. The item explains that the republic's president is nominally elected every five years by popular vote with female participation. However, the text adds that the chief executive remains eligible for indefinite re-election.
records.summary_es: Una nota geográfica informa que la República Dominicana ocupa cerca de dos tercios de la isla de Santo Domingo, bautizada como La Española por Colón tras descubrirla en su primer viaje de 1492, mientras que Haití ocupa el tercio restante. La nota explica que el presidente de la república es elegido nominalmente cada cinco años mediante sufragio popular con participación femenina. No obstante, el texto añade que el mandatario permanece habilitado para la reelección indefinida.
