records.headline: 80 in Dominican Village Reported Dead in Flood by the Associated
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that an unconfirmed news dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo indicated that eighty residents of Tres Puntos, a sugar-growing village in southwestern Dominican Republic, were drowned in torrential floods. In international developments, British Foreign Secretary Ernest Bevin urged Arabs and Jews to accept a United Nations cease-fire in Palestine. Bevin refrained from a full parliamentary statement while sensitive Anglo-American diplomatic talks continued.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que un cablegráfico extraoficial desde Ciudad Trujillo daba cuenta de que ochenta habitantes de Tres Puntos, un poblado cañero del sudoeste dominicano, perecieron ahogados víctimas de devastadoras riadas e inundaciones. En el escenario mundial, el canciller británico Ernest Bevin instó formalmente a árabes y judíos a someterse a la tregua dispuesta por las Naciones Unidas en Palestina. Bevin declinó pronunciar una declaración parlamentaria pormenorizada mientras proseguían delicadas tratativas diplomáticas conjuntas con los Estados Unidos.
records.passage: 80 in Dominican Village Reported Dead in Flood By the Associated Press CIUDAD TRUJILLO, Dominican Republic, May 25.—An unconfirmed newspaper dispatch said yesterday that all the inhabitants of the sugar growing Dominican village of Tres Puntos, in the southwestern part of the republic, have been drowned in floods caused by torrential rains.

records.headline: A Washington society report describes a late-afternoon reception
records.summary_en: A Washington society report describes a late-afternoon reception held by Mr. and Mrs. Cummings at their Forest Lane home honoring Dominican Ambassador and Señora de Thomen. In tribute to the Dominican guests, the hosts displayed in their entrance hall a portrait of President Rafael Trujillo flanked by the Dominican and United States flags. The ambassador's daughter, Señorita Lourdes de Thomen, stood briefly in the receiving line alongside Señorita Margarita Pizano, and the gathering was attended by foreign diplomats including Chinese Ambassador Dr. V. K. Wellington Koo and envoys from Honduras, El Salvador, Mexico, and Bolivia.

En homenaje a los invitados dominicanos, los anfitriones exhibieron en su vestíbulo de entrada un retrato del presidente Rafael Trujillo flanqueado por las banderas de la República Dominicana y los Estados Unidos. La hija del embajador, la señorita Lourdes de Thomen, acompañó brevemente la línea de recepción junto a la señorita Margarita Pizano, y al encuentro asistieron diplomáticos extranjeros como el embajador chino, Dr. V. K. Wellington Koo, y representantes de Honduras, El Salvador, México y Bolivia.

records.full_text:
OFFICIAL SEEKS DUEL OR APOLOGY FROM ARGENTINE Dominican Claims He Was Insulted by Ambassador

OTTAWA, June 16. (AP)—The Consul General of the Dominican Republic wants the Argentine ambassador to Canada to meet him on the field of honor or apologize for what the Dominican insists is a double insult.

Julio Ricart, the Dominican, sent a challenge to Dr. Juan-Carlos Rodriguez, the Argentine, suggesting the duel be held in the Argentine Embassy, technically outside Canada, and urging the ambassador to choose his weapons.

The Argentine will send a reply—to Cuidad Trujillo, capital of the Dominican Republic.

Here is how it started according to Ricart: The Argentine Embassy recently was visited by the Humane Society after it was reported two dogs at the Embassy had been beaten to death. At an Embassy reception, Ricart said he made "some pleasantry" about dogs, not meaning to be nasty. The ambassador's wife "made what I thought was an offensive answer," Ricart said.

records.headline: Arlington Cemetery was announced as the burial site for former American customs
records.summary_en: Arlington Cemetery was announced as the burial site for former American customs collector Mr. Orme, age 72, who passed away Sunday at his home in Asheville, North Carolina. Orme had lived in Asheville since retiring five years earlier from his position as customs collector at San Domingo in the Dominican Republic. A veteran of Theodore Roosevelt's Rough Riders who was severely wounded at San Juan Hill in July 1898, he served the government in Washington and abroad for decades.

Orme había vivido en Asheville desde su jubilación cinco años antes de su cargo como colector de aduanas en Santo Domingo, en la República Dominicana. Veterano de los Rough Riders de Theodore Roosevelt que resultó gravemente herido en San Juan Hill en julio de 1898, sirvió al gobierno en Washington y en el extranjero durante décadas.

records.headline: Photographers visiting the Dominican Republic are advised to capture
records.summary_en: Photographers visiting the Dominican Republic are advised to capture historic colonial architecture in Trujillo City, including the sixteenth-century Church of St. Nicolas, the Convent of San Francisco, and the 1510 house of Don Diego Colon on the waterfront. Modern local scenes include the Jaragua Hotel with its pool and dance patio, alongside coastal vistas along George Washington Avenue. For inland travel, the route leads past the 1494 ruins of La Vega and extends northward toward Samana Bay, noted for its fine harbor, beaches, and hills.

Las escenas modernas locales comprenden el Hotel Jaragua con su piscina y patio de baile, junto con vistas costeras por la avenida George Washington. Para excursiones al interior, la ruta pasa por las ruinas de 1494 de La Vega y se prolonga hacia el norte rumbo a la bahía de Samaná, célebre por su magnífico puerto, playas y colinas.

records.summary_en: Obituary notices announce Washington funeral services for career diplomat Mr. Scherer, whose diplomatic postings included service in Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic. Over his Foreign Service career, Scherer also served in Ciudad Juarez, Havana, Bogota, and Buenos Aires, in addition to heading the Cuban desk at the State Department for two years. A graduate of Groton, Yale, and the National War College, he is survived by his wife, a five-year-old son, and three brothers.

Graduado de Groton, Yale y el Colegio Nacional de Guerra, le sobreviven su esposa, un hijo de cinco años y tres hermanos.

records.headline: A Dominican government communique announced the suicide on Thursday of General Trujillo
records.summary_en: A Dominican government communique announced the suicide on Thursday of General Trujillo, age 55, a former senator, diplomat, and chief of staff of the Dominican Republic's army. The announcement stated that the general suffered from a nervous breakdown aggravated by the fatal shooting two years earlier of his adopted son, Jose Adrian Trujillo, by a deputy sheriff in Bunnell, Florida. While the communique attributed the killing to the youth defending a wartime companion, a Florida coroner's jury had ruled the deputy acted in self-defense during an altercation at a cafe. General Trujillo had refused medical evacuation to the United States and was being attended by Dr. Foster Kennedy of New York when he took his life.
records.summary_es: Un comunicado del gobierno dominicano anunció el suicidio ocurrido el jueves del general Trujillo, de 55 años de edad, exsenador, diplomático y jefe del Estado Mayor del ejército de la República Dominicana. El anuncio manifestaba que el general padecía un colapso nervioso agravado por la muerte a tiros dos años antes de su hijo adoptivo, José Adrián Trujillo, a manos de un ayudante del alguacil en Bunnell, Florida. Si bien el comunicado atribuyó el homicidio a la defensa del joven hacia un compañero de guerra, un jurado de instrucción de Florida dictaminó que el oficial actuó en defensa propia durante un altercado en un café. El general Trujillo había rechazado la evacuación médica a Estados Unidos y era atendido por el doctor Foster Kennedy de Nueva York cuando se quitó la vida.

records.headline: A Caribbean travel report features the chalk-white Hotel Jaragua
records.summary_en: A Caribbean travel report features the chalk-white Hotel Jaragua in Ciudad Trujillo, noting that the Dominican government designed the lavish resort to cater to American tastes. Guests enjoy tiled terraces overlooking gardens and a swimming pool, alongside nightly dancing beneath palm trees. Exploring the capital city, visitors encounter hospitable local merchants who treat American travelers courteously, before potentially flying onward to Haiti, which shares the island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic.
records.summary_es: Una crónica de viajes por el Caribe reseña el blanquísimo Hotel Jaragua en Ciudad Trujillo, señalando que el gobierno dominicano diseñó el lujoso complejo para complacer los gustos estadounidenses. Los huéspedes disfrutan de terrazas de baldosas con vista a jardines y una piscina, junto con baile nocturno bajo las palmeras. Al explorar la capital, los visitantes encuentran comerciantes locales hospitalarios que tratan cortésmente a los viajeros estadounidenses, antes de proseguir eventualmente su viaje en avión hacia Haití, país que comparte la isla de La Española con la República Dominicana.

records.headline: On a tour of the West Indies, J. Leslie Kincaid, president of the American Hotels
records.summary_en: On a tour of the West Indies, J. Leslie Kincaid, president of the American Hotels Corporation, visited the Dominican Republic to assess conditions for pleasure travel. While admiring the agreeable climate and scenic mountain valleys running down to the sea, Kincaid told President Trujillo that local hostelries fell short of American travelers' expectations and indicated he would not return. President Trujillo promised that the deficiencies would be remedied and that a prominent New York architectural firm would be engaged.

Aunque admiró el clima agradable y los pintorescos valles montañosos que descienden hacia el mar, Kincaid manifestó al presidente Trujillo que los establecimientos locales no satisfacían las expectativas de los viajeros estadounidenses e indicó que no regresaría. El presidente Trujillo le aseguró que esas deficiencias serían corregidas y que se contrataría a una destacada firma de arquitectos de Nueva York.

records.headline: New excursion airline fares include a discounted $198 circuitous Caribbean tour
records.summary_en: New excursion airline fares include a discounted $198 circuitous Caribbean tour offering stops in Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic, alongside Cuba, Jamaica, Haiti, and Puerto Rico. Airline official Mr. Lipscomb detailed the routing options, explaining that travelers from Eastern seaboard centers like Atlanta or New York can tour the Antilles before connecting back through mainland cities. A separate direct round-trip between the Eastern coast and San Juan was scheduled at $180.

El funcionario de las aerolíneas señor Lipscomb detalló las alternativas de ruta, explicando que los pasajeros de centros de la costa este como Atlanta o Nueva York pueden recorrer las Antillas antes de conectar de regreso a través de ciudades del territorio continental. Un viaje redondo directo separado entre la costa este y San Juan fue fijado en $180.

records.headline: A squadron of Marine Corps jet aircraft flying toward Puerto Rico
records.summary_en: A squadron of Marine Corps jet aircraft flying toward Puerto Rico from North Carolina faced multiple engine failures shortly after crossing over Hispaniola. Following an engine stall at 20,000 feet, Master Sergeant Lytten Blass executed an emergency landing on a narrow beach without injury or damage to his aircraft. Two companion planes assigned to locate an emergency landing site consumed extensive fuel during low-altitude maneuvers and were directed by radio to land at Ciudad Trujillo.
records.summary_es: Una escuadrilla de aviones a reacción de la Infantería de Marina que volaba hacia Puerto Rico desde Carolina del Norte enfrentó varias fallas de motor poco después de cruzar sobre La Española. Tras apagarse su motor a 20.000 pies de altura, el sargento mayor Lytten Blass realizó un aterrizaje de emergencia en una estrecha playa sin sufrir lesiones ni averiar su aeronave. Dos aviones acompañantes asignados a buscar un punto de aterrizaje de emergencia consumieron abundante combustible en maniobras a baja altitud y fueron orientados por radio para aterrizar en Ciudad Trujillo.

Entre los invitados que asistieron a la recepción figuraron el embajador dominicano y la señora de Thomen, junto con representantes diplomáticos y funcionarios del Departamento de Estado.

records.headline: Communications written by Roland and captured by the Haitian government
records.summary_en: The Ohio Daily-Express reported that captured correspondence revealed former Haitian diplomat Col. Astrel Roland conspired with Dominican President Rafael Trujillo and Interior Minister Alvarez Paulino to orchestrate an invasion of Haiti. A Belgian woman named Lady Verbracken, operating as an ethnologist, gathered Haitian military intelligence and coordinated strategy meetings in New York with Dominican officials. Following his dismissal from the diplomatic service in January, Roland launched subversive radio broadcasts targeting the Haitian government.
records.summary_es: El *Ohio Daily-Express* informó que correspondencia confidencial incautada puso al descubierto que el exdiplomático y coronel haitiano Astrel Roland confabulaba con el mandatario dominicano Rafael Trujillo y el ministro de Interior Álvarez Paulino para organizar una invasión armada contra Haití. Una dama belga apodada Lady Verbracken, amparada en una presunta labor de etnóloga, recopiló secretos de inteligencia militar haitiana y articuló reuniones operativas en Nueva York con dignatarios dominicanos. Tras su exoneración del escalafón exterior en enero, Roland comenzó a emitir arengas de agitación subversiva por las ondas radiales hostigando al gobierno de su patria.
records.passage: Communications written by Roland and captured by the Haitian government reveal that he worked with Lady Verbracken, the president of the Dominican Republic, referred to as Desire in his letters the Dominican minister of interior, Alvarez Paulino, referred to as P. in his letters, and other Dominican officials. The most important person to the success of Roland's plans evidently was the Belgian lady, with whom Roland was reported to be in love. Originally, she went to Haiti as an ethnologist with aim of destroying those named as Roland's enemies. In July and August of 1948, she failed in this mission and left Haiti for Brazil. She returned to Haiti in December, but this time was trailed by the police. She sought information on the nation's military strength and setup, and promised that Col. Roland would return to Haiti soon. She left Haiti December 29 and met Roland two days later in Quito, R. D. Two weeks later she met with [illegible] Roland, Paulino, and another person in New York at the Hotel Martinique. There they discussed an invasion of Haiti. During this time Roland was a Haitian official, councillors of legation in Quito, D. R. His job was dropped by Haiti January 19. Col. Roland Plotted With Dominican Leaders To Revolt

WASHINGTON, March 9. (ANP)—A vicious plot to overthrow the Haitian government was revealed here last week by Joseph D. Charles, ambassador from Haiti to the U. S.

This complex scheme involved Col. Astrel Roland, former Haitian diplomat and military leader, his sweetheart, a Johanna Verbracken of Belgium, and several officials of the Dominican Republic including President Trujillo.

According to the ambassador, the government of Haiti considers the support given Roland by the Dominican government is an act of hostility toward Haiti. He said his nation also considers the broadcasts of Col. Roland from the Dominican Republic as subversive.

News of the various Roland plots became public recently when Roland attacked the Haitian government from the radio station of the Dominican Republican president's brother, Col. Arismendi Trujillo, from the R. D. He promised to liberate the Haitian people.

Latest developments in the situation have been a protest against the R. D. by Haiti before the Council of the Organization of American States and the capture of Lady Verbracken by the D. R.

Roland's campaign against the Haitian administration began in 1947. As blocks to his success in Haiti he named the president of Haiti, the chief of staff, Gen. Lavaud; the colonel of the presidential guard, Col. Magloire, and the director of the military academy, Col. Levelt.

Communications written by Roland and captured by the Haitian government reveal that he worked with Lady Verbracken, the president of the Dominican Republic, referred to as Desire in his letters; the Dominican minister of interior, Aluvarez Paulino, referred to as P. in his letters, and other Dominican officials.

The most important person to the success of Roland's plans evidently was the Belgian lady, with whom Roland was reported to be in love. Originally, she went to Haiti as an thnologist with aim of destroying those named as Roland's enemies. In July and August of 1948, she failed in this mission and left Haiti for Brazil.

She returned to Haiti in December, but this time was trailed by the police. She sought information on the nation's military strength and setup, and promised that Col. Roland would return to Haiti soon. She left Haiti December 29 and met Roland two days later in Quito, R. D.

Two weeks later she met with Roland, Paulino, and another person in New York at the Hotel Martinique. There they discussed an invasion of Haiti. During this time Roland was a Haitian official, councillor of legation in Quito, D. R. His job was dropped by Haiti January 19.

Not long after the loss of his job Roland began his propaganda broadcasts against Haiti.

The Haitian ambassador to the U. S. revealed that his government had a number of letters written by Roland showing his connection with plots to overthrow the government.

What may develop now that Haiti has filed protest against its sister nation can only be speculated.

records.headline: Branch Rickey's spring training setup highlights the Brooklyn Dodgers' preference
records.summary_en: Branch Rickey's spring training setup highlights the Brooklyn Dodgers' preference for their current facility over their previous season in the Caribbean, a report notes under the heading It's Preferred Over Ciudad Trujillo. Farm system director Fresco Thompson declared that the players were far happier than during the previous year at Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic. Thompson explained that in Ciudad Trujillo the food was cooked in rancid grease, the water tasted strange, and many players disliked flying to exhibition games.
records.summary_es: El esquema de entrenamiento primaveral de Branch Rickey resalta la preferencia de los Dodgers de Brooklyn por sus instalaciones actuales en comparación con su temporada anterior en el Caribe, según una crónica bajo el epígrafe Se prefiere sobre Ciudad Trujillo. El director del sistema de granjas, Fresco Thompson, declaró que los peloteros estaban mucho más contentos que durante el año previo en Ciudad Trujillo, República Dominicana. Thompson explicó que en Ciudad Trujillo la comida se preparaba en grasa rancia, el agua sabía extraña y a muchos jugadores les disgustaba viajar en avión a los partidos de exhibición.

records.headline: Enraged Dominicans attempted to seize three American sailors
records.summary_en: Enraged Dominicans attempted to seize three American sailors last week for molesting a Dominican girl, nearly causing an international incident for the second time in two weeks. In Ciudad Trujillo, local police held back the crowd until a U.S. Navy shore patrol rescued the sailors by arresting them and taking them out to sea. Following the disturbance, Police Chief Col. Luis Arzeno Colón visited the American vessel Mount Olympus, warning naval authorities that all American sailors should be kept off the streets to prevent further disorder.

records.headline: During wartime relief operations, medicines and other necessities
records.summary_en: During wartime relief operations, medicines and other necessities shipped from Florida were transported across Cuba, ferried to Haiti, and trucked from Haiti to the Dominican Republic before being carried by boat to Puerto Rico. From Puerto Rico, the cargo was distributed among various Caribbean islands under a project launched with an initial United States revolving fund of $25,000,000. In 1946, this cooperative wartime agency was transformed into the regional Caribbean Commission.

Desde Puerto Rico, la carga se distribuyó entre varias islas del Caribe en el marco de un proyecto iniciado con un fondo rotatorio de los Estados Unidos de $25,000,000. En 1946, esta agencia cooperativa de tiempos de guerra se transformó en la Comisión del Caribe regional.

records.headline: The council politely referred the matter to "the Inter American
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the Organization of American States referred the dispute between Haiti and the Dominican Republic over Col. Astrel Roland's subversive broadcasts to a peace commission, which advised direct bilateral negotiations. Haitian diplomats stated the broadcasts caused widespread unrest that necessitated declaring a state of siege to maintain public order. While Dominican authorities defended the broadcasts under free speech on a private station, Haitian officials contended the station was controlled by President Trujillo's brother.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que la Organización de los Estados Americanos remitió a una comisión de paz la disputa suscitada entre Haití y la República Dominicana por las transmisiones sediciosas del coronel Astrel Roland, encomendando dicho organismo la apertura de negociaciones directas de cancillería. El cuerpo diplomático haitiano adujo que las emisiones agitaron graves conmociones que forzaron a la promulgación del estado de sitio para restablecer la paz pública. Si bien las autoridades dominicanas escudaron las transmisiones amparándose en la libre expresión ejercida en una emisora particular, los voceros haitianos arguyeron que la referida estación estaba supeditada al hermano del gobernante Trujillo.

records.headline: An analysis of Latin American press conditions observes that authoritarian
records.summary_en: An analysis of Latin American press conditions observes that authoritarian regimes suppress domestic press freedom and restrict the outward flow of news. The commentary cites unquestioned government control over the press, radio, and other information agencies under the iron-fisted rule of General Trujillo in the Dominican Republic, alongside comparable controls in Nicaragua and Argentina.
records.summary_es: Un análisis sobre las condiciones de la prensa en América Latina señala que los regímenes autoritarios suprimen la libertad de prensa interna y restringen el flujo de noticias hacia el exterior. El artículo cita el incuestionable control gubernamental sobre la prensa, la radio y otras agencias de información bajo el mandato de mano dura del general Trujillo en la República Dominicana, junto con controles comparables en Nicaragua y Argentina.

records.full_text:
THE DOMINICAN DICTATOR

O. Henry wrote several tales about "banana republics", which seemed at the time to be exaggerated, but what he said was mild compared with the truth about the Dominican Republic which squirms under the ruthless heel of President Rafael J. Trujillo.

News yesterday told of three Miami flyers who had been tracked down in the hills of Trujillo's "republic" and shot to death. They and several other Americans had joined in an abortive attempt to drive Dictator Trujillo out of power.

Many stories have appeared in newspapers, and magazines in the United States about the arbitrary way Trujillo runs the affairs of his country. No such thing as freedom exists in the Dominican Republic. Natives are afraid to denounce Trujillo because they know that what has happened to a good many hardy citizens, who expressed their resentment against the dictator, may happen to them. Those objectors disappeared overnight and have never been seen again.

Trujillo, fearful of losing his life, seldom appears in public, and when he does he rides in an armored car, protected in the front and rear by contingents from the army riding in other automobiles. No other dictator in modern times has used for his own purposes, without a pretence of secretion, so much of the money collected presumably for the operation and maintenance of government. Actually, the entire country is working to make him richer and richer.

Those stories evidently appealed to adventurous Americans to join in an 'invasion' that was designed to rid the Dominican Republic of Trujillo. But the "invasion" was poorly planned and turned out to be a fiasco.

It was thought at the time that Porfirio Diaz in Mexico was the kingpin of dictatorships, but he at least worked hard to help his country as well as himself. Trujillo, however, is unconcerned by the hardships and misery that are common throughout the Dominican Republic. His only aim is to help himself, members of his family and his minions in the army.

records.headline: The State Department released the text of an air transport agreement
records.summary_en: The State Department released the text of an air transport agreement signed on July 19 by the United States and the Dominican Republic. Together with an annex, the accord establishes terms described by officials as fair and equal competition between both countries in commercial airline operations. Under the pact, the United States receives blanket authorization to carry passenger, cargo, and mail air traffic through the Dominican Republic, while the Dominican Republic obtains comparable rights for flights to Miami, Florida, and San Juan, Puerto Rico.

En virtud del pacto, los Estados Unidos reciben autorización general para transportar tráfico aéreo de pasajeros, carga y correo a través de la República Dominicana, mientras que la República Dominicana obtiene derechos comparables para vuelos hacia Miami, Florida, y San Juan, Puerto Rico.

records.headline: A career retrospective within an obituary notes that customs
records.summary_en: A career retrospective within an obituary notes that customs official Mr. Pulliam was appointed receiver-general of customs in the Dominican Republic in 1907, serving in that post until his retirement. In 1914, Pulliam conceived the concept of a memorial lighthouse to Christopher Columbus, for which ground was broken in Ciudad Trujillo in 1946 following international approvals. In recognition of his efforts on behalf of the project, the Dominican Republic awarded Pulliam the Order of Juan Pablo Duarte in 1935.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported on regional political polarization pitting Cuba, Guatemala, and Costa Rica against the authoritarian regimes of Rafael Trujillo in the Dominican Republic and Anastasio Somoza in Nicaragua. While the United States maintained a policy of non-intervention, diplomats debated proposals by Panama's Ricardo J. Alfaro urging the Organization of American States to deny recognition to regimes seizing power through coups. Observers emphasized that enduring democratic stability in the Caribbean would require addressing deep-seated socioeconomic grievances.

Mientras Estados Unidos mantenía una política de no intervención, los diplomáticos debatían las propuestas del panameño Ricardo J. Alfaro, quien instaba a la Organización de los Estados Americanos a negar el reconocimiento a los regímenes que tomaran el poder mediante golpes de Estado. Los observadores enfatizaron que una estabilidad democrática duradera en el Caribe requeriría abordar profundos reclamos socioeconómicos.

Somoza, Nicaragua's Minister of Defense. The United States, despite obvious interest in the Caribbean, has adopted a “hands off” policy in recent years. Within the State Department, however, there has been some support for a formula proposed by former President Ricardo J. Alfaro of Panama, who is his nation's U. N. representative. Dr. Alfaro has urged that the Organization of American States withhold recognition from any government which comes to power as a result of a military coup. Recognition would be given only after a free and fair election to determine public preference. The ambitions of political and military leaders, the intervention of Central American countries in the internal affairs of their neighbors and some Communist Influence are factors in the constant turmoil. But more pressing are the social and economic factors that have led to revolt. The United States has taken the lead in bettering conditions in the Caribbean. Some progress has been reported already. But observers see little hope for stability and for a real trial of democratic principles until social and economic measures succeed. records.summary_en: The marriage of Miss Francisca Angelica Romero to Mr. Warren Joseph Bilkey took place at St. Mathew's Cathedral. The bride, daughter of Mrs. Angelica Beltre Vda. El novio posee títulos de posgrado de la Universidad de Harvard y formará parte del cuerpo docente de la Universidad de Connecticut.

records.headline: In the mountains of the Dominican Republic, a small tropical hurricane
records.summary_en: In the mountains of the Dominican Republic, a small tropical hurricane dissipated after degenerating into squalls with strong gusty winds. Before dying out, the storm caused the deaths of eight men, who drowned before an estimated 4,000 spectators at the port entrance of Ciudad Trujillo. The victims included the captain of the sailboat Puerto Plata and his crew of four, along with three young men who plunged into the mountainous waves in a futile rescue attempt.

Antes de extinguirse, la tormenta provocó la muerte de ocho hombres, quienes se ahogaron ante unos 4,000 espectadores en la entrada del puerto de Ciudad Trujillo. Entre las víctimas se encontraban el capitán del velero Puerto Plata y su tripulación de cuatro hombres, junto con tres jóvenes que se lanzaron a las olas montañosas en un intento infructuoso de rescate.

records.summary_en: A foreign policy analysis notes that the United States government's refurbished Good Neighbor policy strongly condemns Latin American dictators and militarists whose actions promote unrest. The report highlights that leaders such as Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic and Anastasio Somoza of Nicaragua can find no encouragement in Washington's recent declaration, even though it also condemns those conspiring against them. Quoting Secretary of State Dean Acheson's assertion that Washington is waging peace in the hemisphere, the commentary details continuing selective economic assistance alongside President Truman's proposed Point Four program.

records.headline: The Dominican Republic has opened the Montana, an ultramodern
records.summary_en: The Dominican Republic has opened the Montana, an ultramodern hotel located in the mountain resort town of Jarabacoa, 90 miles from Ciudad Trujillo. Situated at an elevation of 3,000 feet overlooking the Royal Valley, the 32-room establishment features a swimming pool, cocktail lounge, dining room, and improved access roads. The property represents the fourth in a planned chain of 14 modern hotels built to attract American tourists and will be operated by the American Hotels Corp.

El inmueble representa el cuarto de una proyectada cadena de 14 hoteles modernos erigidos para atraer turistas estadounidenses y será administrado por la American Hotels Corp.

records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that the Dominican Republic has accused conspirators of hatching a new invasion plot in Cuba. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced in a communiqué that no formal protest had been sent to Havana because past experience demonstrated it would produce no results. Declaring that the nation's only alternative is to prepare to repel any new attack by force, the ministry asserted that the republic is already prepared to defend itself. In New York, the Dominican Republic information center reported that men and war material were assembling in Cuba's Guantanamo Province near an airport under construction.

records.full_text:
Trujillo Held Threat To Peace by Guatemala

By the Associated Press

GUATEMALA CITY, Guatemala, Dec. 15.—Foreign Minister Gonzales Arevalo yesterday accused President Rafael Leonidas Trujillo of the Dominican Republic of "a threat to continental peace."

He said this threat was contained in Gen. Trujillo's call Monday to the congress of his island nation, in the Caribbean 1,100 miles east of Guatemala, for power to declare war against any country "aiding or protecting" revolutionary forces intending to invade the republic.

Guatemala and Cuba were accused of assisting exiled Dominican conspirators. Mr. Arevalo denied this, as the Cuban foreign office did Tuesday.

A dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo, the Dominican capital, said a joint House-Senate committee continued its consideration of the president's message. A committee spokesman said the Foreign Ministry was asked "for fuller information on all attempts against the Dominican Republic prepared at Cayo Confites (Cuba)," where an expeditionary force was broken up by Cuban authorities last year.

A United States Air Force pilot told a Guatemala newsman yesterday that United States planes operating in the Caribbean have been buzzed in recent weeks off the Dominican coasts by Dominican fighters evidently checking on the identification of the planes.

records.summary_en: Under the headline "U.S. Frowns," the paper reports United States disapproval of statements by President Trujillo concerning potential military action. A United States spokesman expressed hope that the Dominican Republic was not contemplating the use of armed forces contrary to inter-American commitments. Emphasizing that Washington deplores raising the prospect of armed forces for war, the official characterized such terminology as entirely inappropriate among American nations and pledged that the United States would exert its greatest efforts to prevent aggression.

Al enfatizar que Washington lamenta que se plantee la posibilidad de utilizar fuerzas armadas con fines bélicos, el funcionario calificó dicha terminología de absolutamente inapropiada entre las naciones americanas y aseguró que Estados Unidos dedicará sus máximos esfuerzos a impedir cualquier agresión.

records.headline: In an address thanking Congress, President Rafael Trujillo promised
records.summary_en: In an address thanking Congress, President Rafael Trujillo promised that extraordinary powers granted to him would never be used in acts of aggression, while directing bitter accusations against Cuba, Guatemala, and Costa Rica. Trujillo claimed that a new invasion of the Dominican Republic was being organized in Cuba with the assistance of the Cuban Red Cross, and that Havana had refused direct negotiations over previous damages. He asserted that 1,600 men were mobilized and trained in Cuba for the failed 1947 invasion attempt, alleging that Cuban authorities acted only after public opinion exposed their complicity. The Dominican president also cited an interview in Bohemia Magazine in which former Cuban President Grau San Martin allegedly admitted active participation in the plot.
records.summary_es: En un discurso de agradecimiento al Congreso, el presidente Rafael Trujillo prometió que los poderes extraordinarios que le fueron concedidos nunca se utilizarían en actos de agresión, al tiempo que lanzó duras acusaciones contra Cuba, Guatemala y Costa Rica. Trujillo denunció que una nueva invasión contra la República Dominicana se estaba organizando en Cuba con el auxilio de la Cruz Roja Cubana, y que La Habana se había negado a sostener negociaciones directas sobre los perjuicios ocasionados anteriormente. Afirmó que 1.600 hombres fueron movilizados y adiestrados en Cuba para el frustrado intento de invasión de 1947, alegando que las autoridades cubanas solo actuaron una vez que la opinión pública dejó al descubierto su complicidad. El mandatario dominicano citó además una entrevista en la revista Bohemia en la que el expresidente cubano Grau San Martín supuestamente admitió su participación activa en la conjura.

records.summary_en: A diplomatic note reminding the Dominican Republic that American republics have formally renounced war was sent by an inter-American peace committee composed of the United States, Brazil, Mexico, Argentina, and Cuba. The communication urged peaceful methods of dispute resolution after Dominican President Trujillo sought and received authorization from congress to declare war on any country harboring plotters against his regime. While Trujillo claimed a new invasion effort was being prepared in Cuba, Havana flatly denied the accusation. Furthermore, Secretary of State Dean Acheson denounced Trujillo's initiative as entirely inappropriate for settling issues among Western Hemisphere nations.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that an inter-American peace committee urged Dominican President Rafael Trujillo to refrain from force unless attacked, citing commitments under the Rio Mutual Defense Treaty. Dominican Secretary of State Virgilio Diaz Ordonez defended the government's stance against alleged invasion preparations in Cuba but expressed readiness to accept conciliatory recommendations. The committee's ongoing efforts followed repeated crises involving the 1947 Cayo Confites expedition, a failed airborne invasion in 1949, and recurring friction with Haiti.

records.full_text:
Dominican Republic
Asks New Airing of
Dispute With Cuba

By the Associated Press

A long-standing feud between Cuba and the Dominican Republic was spotlighted yesterday when the Dominican government formally asked for another airing of troubles between the two countries.

The development occurred in an exchange of notes between the Dominican government and the five-nation Inter-American Peace Committee.

The latter group was set up by the 21 hemisphere foreign ministers in 1940 to seek peaceful settlement of Inter-American disputes. The United States, Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Cuba are members.

After three weeks of discussion the committee Thursday night sent a note to the Dominican government expressing concern over special war powers granted to President Rafael Trujillo. The Dominican Republic replied that they resulted from a “profound state of emergency” in the Caribbean.

War Powers Granted.

Trujillo got from the Dominican Congress this month power to declare war on any country which he considers is harboring plotters working against him.

The move was directed to Cuba where Mr. Trupillo charged a new attempt to mount an invasion of the Dominican Republic is going on. This was strongly denied by Cuba.

The committee’s note asked Mr. Trujillo not to use force unless under armed attack in accordance with terms of the Rio mutual defense treaty.

In reply, Dominican Secretary of State Virgilio Diaz Ordonez said “no other country or government would fail to act in the same way as we are doing now.” But he added that the republic would respond to any conciliatory gesture to end the “abnormality with which we are confronted.”

His note added the government is ready to receive recommendations from the committee.

The feud between the two Caribbean nations is an old story to the committee. In 1948, the group got the two nations to agree to settle their differences through diplomatic channels. The Dominican charge then was based on an unsuccessful attempt in 1947 by various groups of exiles to create an invasion force in Cuba to overthrow Mr. Trujillo.

The following year the Dominicans went before the committee with the assertion the same group was being outfitted anew in Cuba.

A few months ago the committee issued a 14-point statement designed to calm Caribbean tension after an airborne invasion of the Dominican Republic failed.

In the meantime, it settled a flareup between the neighboring Dominican Republic and Haiti when the latter charged Mr. Trujillo was personally involved in a plot to ove-thorw the Port-au-Prince government.

records.headline: An analytical article surveying inter-American peacekeeping
records.summary_en: An analytical article surveying inter-American peacekeeping reviews past conflicts and the mediation role of the Organization of American States. The account notes that an earlier tragedy in which Haitians on Dominican territory were brutally massacred was prevented from erupting into open warfare between the two neighbors. Over the past 12 months, the machinery of the OAS has also contained two minor disputes, including one between the Dominican Republic and Haiti. Additionally, the OAS Peace Committee is currently handling tensions arising from Dictator-President Trujillo's charges that Cuba and Guatemala are plotting to overthrow him.
records.summary_es: Un artículo analítico que examina el mantenimiento de la paz interamericana repasa los conflictos del pasado y la función mediadora de la Organización de los Estados Americanos. El relato señala que una tragedia previa en la que haitianos en territorio dominicano fueron brutalmente masacrados logró contenerse para no derivar en una guerra abierta entre ambos vecinos. Durante los últimos 12 meses, la estructura de la OEA también contuvo dos controversias menores, incluida una entre la República Dominicana y Haití. Asimismo, la Comisión de Paz de la OEA atiende en la actualidad las tensiones surgidas por las acusaciones del presidente y dictador Trujillo de que Cuba y Guatemala conspiran para derrocarlo.

Recent mutual accusations involved Haiti charging the Dominican Republic with plotting to overthrow its government, while the Dominican government alleged that Haiti, Cuba, and Guatemala had long harbored conspiracies against President Rafael Trujillo. U. S. Asks Caribbean Peace

The United States yesterday made a diplomatically worded appeal to Caribbean nations to quit quarreling. The appeal was made by Robert Butler, United States Ambassador to Cuba, whose Embassy is host to the three-day meeting in Havana of 12 United States Ambassadors in Caribbean countries.

Mr. Butler said the Organization of American States has machinery for the settlement of disputes and that this machinery ought to be understood and used fully to prevent conflicts.

Haiti recently charged the Dominican Republic with a plot to overthrow the Haitian government. The Dominican government replied that Haiti, Cuba, Guatemala and some other Caribbean countries had for many months fostered plots to overthrow Dominican President Rafael Trujillo.—A. P.

records.summary_en: The Nome Nugget reported on widespread regional and American protests after the Dominican congress granted President Rafael Trujillo authority to declare war on nations harboring hostile forces. Trujillo frequently accused Cuba, Guatemala, and Venezuela of sponsoring plots against his government while state-controlled Dominican media publicized invasion rumors. Observers questioned whether the legislation foreshadowed foreign aggression or merely served as domestic propaganda to justify military expenditures.
records.summary_es: El *Nome Nugget* informó sobre las amplias protestas regionales y estadounidenses surgidas luego de que el congreso dominicano otorgara al presidente Rafael Trujillo autorización para declarar la guerra a las naciones que albergaran fuerzas hostiles. Trujillo acusaba con frecuencia a Cuba, Guatemala y Venezuela de patrocinar complots contra su gobierno, mientras los medios estatales dominicanos difundían rumores de invasión. Los observadores cuestionaban si la legislación presagiaba una agresión exterior o si servía simplemente como propaganda interna para justificar gastos militares.

When the law was passed there were protests from the United States and from countries throughout the Caribbean area. President Trujillo has frequently accused Cuba, Guatemala, Venezuela and other nations of harboring enemies and plotting attacks upon his regime. The Dominican press, which is not at all free, often publishes reports of alleged mobilizations designed for the invasion of the republic. Just why the dictator wanted his congress to pass such a law is uncertain. Whether it means a possible attack on some other nation or represents nothing but propaganda to justify heavy expenditures for Trujillo's army is not known. WHAT EXPLAINS SUCCESS? An idea seems to be spreading throughout the land that men and women achieve success through the operation of government rather than by their own patient persistence in honest endeavor. The readers of the NUGGET, especially young (men and women, should not be misled in this respect. They should realize that worthwhile success in life is achieved almost exclusively through personal endeavor. After all is said and done, the vast majority of business successes owe their growth to one or more rare individuals who give to the enterprise a contribution that includes, not only physical effort, but superior intelligence and the wisdom that arises from the intangible thing that we call “character”.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that an OAS five-nation fact-finding committee departed Washington to conduct on-site investigations in Haiti, Cuba, the Dominican Republic, and Guatemala. The inquiry aimed to defuse regional crises ignited by Rafael Trujillo's war-power request and a reported conspiracy to assassinate Haitian President Dumarsais Estime. The investigating mission comprised delegates from the United States, Uruguay, Colombia, Bolivia, and Ecuador operating under the Rio Treaty.

Las pesquisas buscaban desactivar las crisis regionales encendidas por la solicitud de poderes de guerra de Rafael Trujillo y una supuesta conspiración para asesinar al presidente haitiano Dumarsais Estimé. La misión investigadora estaba compuesta por delegados de Estados Unidos, Uruguay, Colombia, Bolivia y Ecuador que operaban al amparo del Tratado de Río.

On December 19, Haiti announced it had broken up a plot aimed at assassinating President Dumarsais Estime and other officials. The Haitians said the plot Included an invasion of Haiti by the Dominican Republic. As charges mounted between the two countries, the council of the Organization of American States invoked the Rio treaty, a Latin American mutual defense pact similar to the North Atlantic Pact, and decided to get to the bottom of the feuding in the Caribbean. records.headline: A political commentary argues that the current crop of authoritarian
records.summary_en: A political commentary argues that the current crop of authoritarian rulers in Latin America is of purely domestic origin rather than the creation of United States imperialism. The writer characterizes President Rafael Trujillo, who treats the Dominican Republic as his private and exclusive domain, as an indigenous product of Hispaniola where Columbus founded the first European settlement. Similar indigenous roots are attributed to Anastasio Somoza of Nicaragua, along with governing figures in Panama, Venezuela, and Colombia. The article maintains that claims portraying Yankee exploiters as responsible for these regimes have become complete anachronisms.
records.summary_es: Un comentario político argumenta que la actual generación de gobernantes autoritarios en América Latina es de origen netamente nacional y no una creación del imperialismo estadounidense. El articulista describe al presidente Rafael Trujillo, quien trata a la República Dominicana como su dominio privado y exclusivo, como un producto autóctono de La Española, donde Colón fundó el primer asentamiento europeo. Raíces locales semejantes se atribuyen a Anastasio Somoza en Nicaragua, junto con figuras de gobierno en Panamá, Venezuela y Colombia. El texto sostiene que las afirmaciones que presentan a los explotadores yanquis como responsables de estos regímenes se han vuelto anacronismos totales.

records.headline: An analysis of United States policy observes that the firmly
records.summary_en: An analysis of United States policy observes that the firmly entrenched dictatorships in the Dominican Republic and Nicaragua arose in nations previously occupied by American forces. The article notes that Generalissimos Trujillo and Somoza were trained by the United States Marines and seized control of their respective governments almost immediately after the occupying troops withdrew. United States diplomats and field experts recommend a dual policy of withholding direct financial assistance, loans, and military armaments from strong-arm rulers. Concurrently, they advise protecting legitimate American business investments and assisting in developing regional natural resources and technical knowledge.
records.summary_es: Un análisis sobre la política de Estados Unidos observa que las férreas dictaduras arraigadas en la República Dominicana y Nicaragua surgieron en naciones previamente ocupadas por fuerzas norteamericanas. El artículo señala que los generalísimos Trujillo y Somoza fueron entrenados por la infantería de marina de Estados Unidos y tomaron el control de sus respectivos gobiernos casi de inmediato tras la retirada de las tropas de ocupación. Diplomáticos y expertos de campo estadounidenses recomiendan una política dual de denegar asistencia financiera directa, préstamos y pertrechos militares a los gobernantes de mano dura. Simultáneamente, aconsejan respaldar las inversiones comerciales legítimas de ciudadanos norteamericanos y prestar apoyo en el desarrollo de los recursos naturales y la pericia técnica de la región.

records.headline: A report on diplomatic developments in the Caribbean notes concerns
records.summary_en: A report on diplomatic developments in the Caribbean notes concerns among Organization of American States officials regarding potential accusations of interference in the domestic affairs of member countries. The dispatch points out that the alleged plotting Haiti accuses Trujillo of conducting took place with disgruntled Haitians in Trujillo City rather than within Haiti itself. A seasoned diplomat quoted in the piece argues that direct intervention by outsiders accomplishes little and suggests that the only effective method to counter regional strongmen is to maintain public scrutiny by exposing their maneuvers to the world.
records.summary_es: Un informe sobre acontecimientos diplomáticos en el Caribe señala la preocupación de funcionarios de la Organización de los Estados Americanos ante posibles acusaciones de intromisión en los asuntos internos de los países miembros. El despacho puntualiza que la supuesta conspiración de la que Haití acusa a Trujillo no se realizó en Haití, sino con haitianos descontentos en Trujillo City. Un veterano diplomático citado en la nota argumenta que la intervención directa de agentes externos rinde escasos frutos y sugiere que la única vía efectiva contra los gobernantes autoritarios radica en mantener el escrutinio público, exponiendo sus maniobras ante la opinión mundial.

records.headline: A syndicated column reports that the Babb Company of Newark
records.summary_en: A syndicated column reports that the Babb Company of Newark, New Jersey, purchased three surplus B-17 bombers from educational institutions and sold one of the planes to Dictator Trujillo of the Dominican Republic. While the original military contracts restricted the bombers to scrap or educational use, the company asserts that the State Department granted approval for the export. The column notes that Babb Company secures prices as high as $25,000 for each improved B-17, despite purchasing the surplus aircraft from the Army for $350.

Si bien los contratos militares originales restringían los bombarderos para fines educativos o chatarra, la compañía sostiene que el Departamento de Estado autorizó la exportación. La columna destaca que Babb Company percibe precios de hasta $25,000 por cada B-17 mejorado, a pesar de comprar las aeronaves excedentes al ejército por $350.

records.headline: Former world heavyweight boxing champion Joe Louis is traveling
records.summary_en: Former world heavyweight boxing champion Joe Louis is traveling to Haiti and the Dominican Republic to fight a series of exhibition matches. The Brown Bomber departed Miami for Port-au-Prince on a Pan American World Airways flight alongside his manager Marshall Miles and trainer Manny Seaman. After contesting an eight-round exhibition against a local opponent in Haiti, Louis will fly to Ciudad Trujillo for a four-round bout on Sunday, February 12. The fighter plans to return to Miami on February 13 to resume his Florida exhibition tour.
records.summary_es: El ex campeón mundial de boxeo de peso pesado Joe Louis viaja a Haití y a la República Dominicana para disputar una serie de peleas de exhibición. El Bombardero de Detroit salió desde Miami hacia Puerto Príncipe en un vuelo de Pan American World Airways junto con su manejador Marshall Miles y su entrenador Manny Seaman. Tras celebrar un combate de exhibición a ocho asaltos contra un rival local en Haití, Louis volará a Ciudad Trujillo para una pelea a cuatro asaltos el domingo 12 de febrero. El púgil prevé regresar a Miami el 13 de febrero para continuar su gira de exhibición por Florida.

records.headline: An Associated Press report from Ciudad Trujillo states that the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: An Associated Press report from Ciudad Trujillo states that the Dominican Republic has conferred its highest decoration upon Ambassador Warren R. Austin, the United States representative to the United Nations. Foreign Minister Virgilio Diaz Ordonez presented the Grand Cross of the Order of Juan Pablo Duarte to Austin during a reception attended by President Rafael Trujillo. The award was presented while the United States ambassador was conducting a goodwill tour of the Caribbean area.

records.headline: Joe Louis, retired heavyweight boxing champion, is touring Haiti
records.summary_en: Joe Louis, retired heavyweight boxing champion, is touring Haiti and the Dominican Republic for exhibition bouts. Accompanied by his manager, Marshall Miles, and his trainer, Manny Seaman, the fighter is scheduled to fly Thursday from Miami to Port-au-Prince aboard a Pan American World Airways Clipper. Miles stated that Louis would box an eight-round exhibition against a local opponent in the Haitian capital on Thursday, followed by a four-round exhibition in Ciudad Trujillo on Sunday. Louis intends to return to Miami on Feb. 13 to resume his Florida exhibition tour.

records.headline: Lester Schwartz, acting manager for heavyweight boxer Jersey Joe
records.summary_en: Lester Schwartz, acting manager for heavyweight boxer Jersey Joe Walcott, is conducting a Caribbean tour to evaluate prospects for scheduling exhibition bouts for the Camden, New Jersey, veteran. Schwartz departed Miami on a Pan American World Airways Clipper for Havana, the initial stop on an itinerary including Panama City, Barranquilla, Maracaibo, Caracas, San Juan, Port-au-Prince, and Ciudad Trujillo in the Dominican Republic. Walcott, who previously lost a disputed decision to Joe Louis before suffering a knockout in their rematch, plans to undertake the exhibition tour in late February and early March.

records.summary_en: A correspondent reports that serious political discussion throughout the Caribbean has shifted away from rumors of war between the Dominican Republic and Haiti toward Puerto Rico's first elected chief executive. A Jamaican journalist commented that developments in Puerto Rico hold far greater significance for the region than the martial exhibitionism of Dictator Trujillo or the swashbuckling antics of Nicaragua's Somoza. Costa Rican leader Jose Figueres expressed similar admiration, indicating his intention to visit San Juan to examine firsthand what Munoz and his democratic government have to offer neighboring nations.

records.full_text:
Trujillo Eases Jitters

President Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic has eased combat jitters in the Caribbean by asking his Congress to revoke his extraordinary powers to declare war.

He had requested these powers last month after he had accused Cuba, Haiti and Guatemala of harboring plotters against his country. The three nations denied his charges. Now he said he was asking that the powers be withdrawn to facilitate discussion as a means of solving Caribbean disputes.—AP.

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that the Dominican Congress voted
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that the Dominican Congress voted yesterday to revoke President Rafael Trujillo's extraordinary powers to declare war. The repeal was requested by the president himself to encourage the use of consultative procedures in resolving Caribbean political disputes. Congress had originally granted Trujillo war-declaring authority on January 6, following his request for emergency defense powers for his regime.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de la Associated Press desde Ciudad Trujillo informa que el Congreso dominicano votó ayer la revocación de las facultades extraordinarias del presidente Rafael Trujillo para declarar la guerra. La derogación fue solicitada por el propio mandatario con el propósito de fomentar el uso de procedimientos de consulta para dirimir las controversias políticas en el Caribe. El Congreso había concedido inicialmente a Trujillo la potestad de declarar la guerra el 6 de enero, tras su solicitud de poderes de defensa de emergencia para su régimen.

records.summary_en: In a published letter to the editor, Harry C. Klemfuss, director of the Dominican Republic Information Center, criticizes commentator Mr. Tomlinson for alleged prejudice against President Trujillo and irresponsible presentation of Caribbean affairs. Klemfuss contends that Tomlinson published distorted claims prior to the official release of the report prepared by the Investigating Committee of the Organization of American States. Highlighting Tomlinson's references to the document now before the OAS Council, Klemfuss expresses surprise and concern, stating that the committee had not yet made its findings public or shared them with the nations involved.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the OAS investigating committee issued recommendations to preserve peace in the Caribbean under threat of Rio Treaty sanctions. The committee urged the Dominican government to halt official support for seditious movements against neighboring states and adhere strictly to its 1949 pact with Haiti. Additionally, Cuba and Guatemala were instructed to dismantle armed exile expeditions on their soil and halt illicit arms trafficking by the Caribbean Legion.

records.headline: An investigating committee found that in 1947, 1,000 men along
records.summary_en: An investigating committee found that in 1947, 1,000 men along with substantial numbers of aircraft and munitions moved across Cuba with official knowledge and naval observation before assembling at Cayo Confites to invade and overthrow President Trujillo. The committee identified Cuban Education Minister Jose Manuel Aleman and sports director Manolo Castro as intimately involved, noting that former Cuban President Ramon Grau San Martin later confirmed these facts in a magazine article. Turning to Dominican allegations of a renewed plot involving the Cuban Red Cross, investigators reached no definitive conclusion but deemed a halted airstrip at L'Amelie unsuitable for an invasion of the Dominican Republic due to its short runway. Red Cross president Rodolfo Henriquez had asserted that the landing strip was intended strictly for emergency relief.
records.summary_es: Una comisión investigadora determinó que en 1947, 1,000 hombres junto con una cantidad considerable de aviones y municiones se desplazaron por Cuba con conocimiento oficial y bajo observación naval antes de concentrarse en Cayo Confites para invadir y derrocar al presidente Trujillo. La comisión señaló la íntima participación del ministro cubano de Educación, José Manuel Alemán, y del director de deportes, Manolo Castro, añadiendo que el expresidente de Cuba Ramón Grau San Martín confirmó posteriormente estos hechos en un artículo de revista. En cuanto a las acusaciones dominicanas de una nueva tentativa a través de la Cruz Roja Cubana, los investigadores no llegaron a una conclusión definitiva, pero declararon que una pista aérea paralizada en L'Amelie no era apta para una invasión de la República Dominicana debido a la escasa longitud de su pista. El presidente de la Cruz Roja, Rodolfo Henríquez, había afirmado que la pista estaba destinada estrictamente a prestar socorro de emergencia.

The committee exonerated Haiti while censuring the Dominican Republic, Cuba, and Guatemala for treaty violations and support of subversive exile plots. records.full_text:
Caribbean Turmoil

The report of the Investigating Committee of the Organization of American States on disturbed conditions in the Caribbean area is a forthright exposure of a bad situation.

With one or two fortunate exceptions, the political history of the small republics bordering the Caribbean has been an unhappy chronicle of revolutions usually resulting in the supplanting of one dictatorship by another. Each such revolution spawns a group of exiles who take refuge in neighboring republics. These exiles not only plot continuously against their home regimes, but are also tempting instruments for troublemaking by their hosts—or against neighboring governments with whom they are not on good terms.

This sort of thing has embroiled several Caribbean countries during the past three years, producing an explosive situation with dangerous possibilities. The storm center has been General Trujillo, the dictatorial ruler of the Dominican Republic. He appears to have fomented trouble in the neighboring republic of Haiti through the use of Haitian exiles, but at the same time to have been the object of revolutionary plots by Dominican exiles assisted by high-ranking officials in Cuba and Guatemala. Some months ago, this imbroglio led to a complaint lodged by Haiti with the Organization of American States, the body set up under the Rio Treaty to maintain peace and security in the New World. Haiti’s action was quickly followed by a similar complaint by Trujillo against Cuba, Guatemala and Haiti. Thereupon, the OAS appointed a committee to make a thorough investigation of all the charges. After two months of intensive work, including visits to all the countries involved and interrogations of all parties concerned, the committee has submitted a report of the highest significance. From it, only Haiti emerges with a clean bill of health. The three others are vigorously taken to task for their actions, which violate the Rio Pact, together with other treaties and accepted international comity. They are bidden to desist under threat of the application of sanctions provided for by the Rio Treaty.

It is to be hoped that the OAS will act upon its committee's report, which includes the setting up of a "watchdog committee" to prevent future infractions. The peace of the Caribbean could thereby be safeguarded.

President Estime expressed a desire to attract African American entrepreneurs and capital to build domestic enterprises like sugar refineries, canning plants, and cement factories. records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the OAS investigating committee led by Dr. Jose A. Mora issued unprecedented findings condemning state-sponsored subversion in the Caribbean. The report found President Rafael Trujillo's regime guilty of aiding plots to overthrow the Haitian government, while finding Cuban and Guatemalan officials complicit in Caribbean Legion expeditions against Trujillo. The committee urged the OAS Council to actively enforce its authority by invoking Rio Treaty sanctions against future violators.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que la comisión investigadora de la OEA, presidida por el Dr. José A. Mora, emitió conclusiones sin precedentes que condenaban la subversión patrocinada por estados en el Caribe. El informe declaró culpable al régimen del presidente Rafael Trujillo de colaborar en planes para derrocar al gobierno haitiano, al tiempo que determinó la complicidad de funcionarios cubanos y guatemaltecos en expediciones de la Legión del Caribe contra Trujillo. La comisión instó al Consejo de la OEA a ejercer enérgicamente su autoridad invocando las sanciones del Tratado de Río contra futuros infractores.

It declared the Dominican Republic. through henchmen of President Rafael Trujillo, guilty of harboring and giving aid to revolutionary plot ters seeking the overthrow of the government of Haiti. It also established that officials and prominent citizens of Cuba and Guatemala had abetted "the Caribbean Legion” and other sub versive groups in repeated plans to invade the Dominican Republic and unseat Dictator Trujillo. Stronger Council Urged The stinging report of the fact finders is not only an innovation, but unprecedented in hemisphere relations. But the Mora commit tee feels that it is not enough merely to turn the spotlight of publicity upon the would-be ag gressors. Exposing the culprits will not be enough to put an end to political bickering and back biting in the American neigh borhood. The committee has called upon the Council to take steps to make itself more positive, not to say more powerful, in enforcing its decisions against such trouble makers. It recommends that the Rio defense treaty, which pro vides for all sorts of political and economic sanctions in case of ag gression, or threatened aggression, either from within or from with out the hemisphere, be invoked without delay against any and all who persist in creating disturb ances in the American family of nations. records.headline: A diplomatic analysis of the OAS investigating committee's findings
records.summary_en: A diplomatic analysis of the OAS investigating committee's findings reports that while Haiti was cleared of Trujillo's countercharges, investigators urged Haiti to enter into a new bilateral pact with the Dominican Republic pledging peaceful resolution of disputes. Haitian diplomats reacted with skepticism, recalling that barely six days after signing an OAS agreement on June 9 of last year, Haitian exiles were given access to government radio in Trujillo City to incite an uprising against President Dumarsais Estime. The dispatch notes an absence of serious public interest or editorial support for the report across major South American capitals, including Rio, Santiago, and Mexico City. By contrast, the state-controlled press in the Dominican Republic published the entire 18,000-word report without editorial commentary.
records.summary_es: Un análisis diplomático sobre los resultados de la comisión investigadora de la OEA informa que, aunque Haití fue exonerado de las contraacusaciones de Trujillo, los investigadores instaron a Haití a suscribir un nuevo pacto bilateral con la República Dominicana comprometiéndose a una resolución pacífica de sus controversias. Los diplomáticos haitianos reaccionaron con escepticismo, recordando que apenas seis días después de firmar un acuerdo de la OEA el 9 de junio del año pasado, se facilitó a exiliados haitianos el acceso a la radio gubernamental en Ciudad Trujillo para incitar un alzamiento contra el presidente Dumarsais Estimé. El despacho señala una falta de interés público o respaldo editorial significativo hacia el informe en las principales capitales sudamericanas, entre ellas Río, Santiago y Ciudad de México. Por el contrario, la prensa controlada por el Estado en la República Dominicana publicó el informe completo de 18,000 palabras sin comentarios editoriales.

records.headline: The 21-nation Council of the Organization of American States called
records.summary_en: The 21-nation Council of the Organization of American States called upon Cuba, Guatemala, and the Dominican Republic to cease their Caribbean feuds immediately or face intervention by armed force. Haitian Foreign Minister Vilfort Beauvoir submitted a resolution requesting that the Dominican government reduce armaments alongside Haiti to preserve a balance of forces between both nations, while also urging the expulsion of two Haitian exiles from Dominican territory. Following review of an investigating committee's findings, the OAS cleared Haiti of charges brought by the Dominican Republic, while ordering 'Dominica,' Cuba, and Guatemala to halt their feuds.
records.summary_es: El Consejo de 21 naciones de la Organización de los Estados Americanos conminó a Cuba, Guatemala y la República Dominicana a poner fin de inmediato a sus desavenencias en el Caribe o afrontar una intervención armada. El ministro de Asuntos Exteriores de Haití, Vilfort Beauvoir, presentó una resolución pidiendo que el gobierno dominicano disminuya sus armamentos a la par con Haití para mantener el equilibrio de fuerzas entre ambos países, solicitando además la expulsión de dos exiliados haitianos de territorio dominicano. Luego de evaluar las conclusiones de una comisión investigadora, la OEA exoneró a Haití de las acusaciones presentadas por la República Dominicana, a la vez que ordenó a «Dominica», Cuba y Guatemala que suspendan sus disputas.

records.headline: A feature article highlights the arrival and resettlement in the Dominican Republic of Russian refugees
records.summary_en: A feature article highlights the arrival and resettlement in the Dominican Republic of Russian refugees fleeing Stalin's regime. Pending permanent occupational placement across various trades, the Dominican government housed 190 refugees in the dormitories and faculty residences of the new state agricultural college in San Cristobal, 20 miles from Ciudad Trujillo. Government departments are coordinating to secure positions for the arrivals, whose members include doctors, electricians, machinists, miners, and teachers. The text notes Christopher Columbus's historical praise for the fertile island, accompanied by a photograph of young sons of the refugees visiting Columbus's tomb in the cathedral at Ciudad Trujillo.
records.summary_es: Un artículo especial reseña la llegada y reasentamiento en la República Dominicana de refugiados rusos que escaparon del régimen de Stalin. Mientras se concreta su colocación laboral definitiva en diversos oficios, el gobierno dominicano alojó a 190 refugiados en los dormitorios y residencias para profesores del nuevo colegio agrícola estatal en San Cristóbal, a 20 millas de Ciudad Trujillo. Las dependencias gubernamentales coordinan la consecución de empleos para los recién llegados, entre quienes figuran médicos, electricistas, maquinistas, mineros y maestros. El texto evoca los elogios históricos de Cristóbal Colón hacia la fertilidad de la isla y se acompaña con una fotografía de hijos pequeños de los refugiados visitando la tumba de Colón en la catedral de Ciudad Trujillo.

8 Held in Conspiracy to Use Bogus Money for Caribbean Revolt

By the Associated Press

NEW YORK, May 26.—Seven men and an attractive blond have been seized in a crackdown on an alleged $3 million counterfeit smuggling ring supposedly linked to a Caribbean revolution plot.

The fantastic scheme, according to an authoritative source, was to sneak $3 million in bogus United States bills into Cuba's national treasury, exchange them for good Cuban money and then finance a revolt in the Dominican Republic.

The blond and four men were arrested here and one man was apprehended in Miami yesterday. Two Cubans were held in that country.

An indictment returned by a Federal grand jury here alleged a conspiracy to buy money from a big American counterfeit ring. The jury did not mention the reported Dominican revolution connection. The indictment named the two Cubans as plotters.

Five Prisoners Arraigned.

The alleged plan to milk the Cuban treasury was revealed before United States Commissioner Edward W. McDonald here as five prisoners were arraigned.

"What was to be done with the $3 million in Cuban money?" the commissioner asked. "That's enough to start a revolution."

Assistant United States Attorney Roy M. Cohn replied: "There has been speculation." But he added that his boss, United States Attorney Irving H. Saypol, "will not comment on that."

The speculation to which Mr. Cohn referred was about a revolution plot.

Those arrested here were: Charlotte Whitehurst, 25; Jesus M. Roland, 39, restaurant worker; Henry Chavarria, 55; Jose Antonio Roche, 50, and Roudolph Schmidt, 53.

Roche's brother, Oscar Roche, 50, was seized in Miami. The Cubans are Dr. Jose Manuel Fernandez Hernandez, 60, said by Mr. Cohn to be prominent in Cuban politics, and Jesus Mon, 38.

Held in High Bail.

All the United States defendants were charged either with passing or conspiring to pass counterfeit money. All were held in high bail. All eight suspects were bagged by United States Secret Service men and Cuban secret police.

The alleged plot, according to Mr. Saypol, was to work this way:

The ring planned to get in advance a batch of old Cuban currency destined to be burned, and substitute the counterfeit American bills, which presumably would be burned instead of the valid but aged Cuban money.

The switch was to be made by Cuban government workers with access to the treasury at Havana.

records.summary_en: A short dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo outlines language instruction policies in the Dominican Republic. While Spanish remains the country's official and native language, English is taught in schools across the republic. Under educational regulations, every Dominican student is required to study English for a minimum of eight years.

records.headline: A dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that a new Dominican Republic law
records.summary_en: A dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that a new Dominican Republic law has been enacted to encourage foreign investments. Under its provisions, 20-year tax exemptions may be granted to individuals who establish themselves in the country to cultivate crops, raise livestock, or manufacture raw materials derived from agricultural and animal-product industries. Beneficiaries will receive full exemption from all taxes, contributions, or charges, as well as any future tax increases imposed by the state, municipalities, or other entities.
records.summary_es: Un despacho desde Ciudad Trujillo informa que se ha promulgado una nueva ley en la República Dominicana para fomentar las inversiones extranjeras. Bajo sus disposiciones, se pueden otorgar exenciones fiscales de 20 años a personas que se establezcan en el país con el propósito de cultivar tierras, criar ganado o manufacturar materias primas derivadas de las industrias agrícolas y de productos pecuarios. Los beneficiarios recibirán exención total de todo impuesto, contribución o gravamen, así como de cualquier aumento tributario establecido por el Estado, los municipios u otras entidades.

records.headline: The Evening Star reports that the White House received messages of support
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reports that the White House received messages of support from foreign leaders backing United Nations action to protect South Korea against aggression. Among them, President Rafael L. Trujillo Molina of the Dominican Republic congratulated President Truman for backing up the U.N. with arms. Colombian President Mariano Ospina Perez likewise offered cooperation in the international effort.
records.summary_es: El Evening Star informa que la Casa Blanca recibió mensajes de apoyo de líderes extranjeros que respaldan la acción de las Naciones Unidas para proteger a Corea del Sur frente a la agresión. Entre ellos, el presidente Rafael L. Trujillo Molina de la República Dominicana felicitó al presidente Truman por respaldar a la ONU con armas. Asimismo, el presidente colombiano Mariano Ospina Pérez ofreció cooperación en el esfuerzo internacional.

records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that geologists from the Dominican Bureau of Mining have discovered a million-ton deposit of lignite in Samana Province. Al describir el lignito como un combustible intermedio entre la turba y el carbón, el informe señala que se prevé que este hallazgo abra nuevas posibilidades para la generación de electricidad y gasolina sintética en la República Dominicana.

records.summary_en: A dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that construction has begun on the second large textile mill in the Dominican capital in less than a year. The Dominican Republic government announced that once operational, the facility will make Ciudad Trujillo the seat of the most complete textile industry in the Caribbean. The plant will specialize in processing domestically grown cotton into threads and fabrics.

La instalación se especializará en procesar algodón cultivado localmente para transformarlo en hilos y telas.

records.headline: The Chapel Hill Weekly profiles a local naval reservist, Nettles
records.summary_en: The Chapel Hill Weekly profiles a local naval reservist, Nettles, who traveled to New Orleans in June to embark on a summer training cruise aboard the U.S. destroyer Compton. Working in the ship's radio room, he traveled on an itinerary that included a one-day stop at Guantanamo, Cuba, and a port visit to Ciudad Trujillo in the Dominican Republic. The vessel subsequently conducted maneuvers with three other destroyers on its return voyage to New Orleans.
records.summary_es: The Chapel Hill Weekly reseña la trayectoria de un reservista naval local de apellido Nettles, quien viajó a New Orleans en junio para embarcarse en un crucero de instrucción de verano a bordo del destructor estadounidense Compton. Asignado a labores en la sala de radio del buque, formó parte de un itinerario que incluyó una escala de un día en Guantánamo, Cuba, y una visita al puerto de Ciudad Trujillo en la República Dominicana. Posteriormente, la embarcación realizó maniobras junto a otros tres destructores durante su travesía de regreso a New Orleans.

records.headline: The Evening Star reports that on October 12, Ciudad Trujillo
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reports that on October 12, Ciudad Trujillo will host one of the most impressive ceremonies in the West Indies when the casket containing the remains of Christopher Columbus is opened for public inspection. The Archbishop of Santo Domingo, Ricardo Pittini, will lead the rites of homage in the Dominican Republic's Cathedral of Santo Domingo, with tourists from across the hemisphere expected to attend. Four separate keys will unlock the casket of wrought iron, lead, and rock crystal, allowing thousands to view the remains of the navigator.
records.summary_es: El Evening Star informa que el 12 de octubre Ciudad Trujillo acogerá una de las ceremonias más solemnes de las Antillas cuando se abra a la inspección pública el féretro con los restos de Cristóbal Colón. El arzobispo de Santo Domingo, Ricardo Pittini, encabezará los ritos de homenaje en la Catedral de Santo Domingo de la República Dominicana, a los que se prevé que asistan turistas de todo el hemisferio. Cuatro llaves distintas abrirán el féretro de hierro forjado, plomo y cristal de roca, permitiendo a miles de personas contemplar los restos del navegante.
