records.headline: A society report in the Evening Star details a Washington luncheon
records.summary_en: A society report in the Evening Star details a Washington luncheon hosted by Dominican Ambassador and Senora de Thomen in honor of the Spanish Ambassador to the Dominican Republic, Manuel Aznar, and Senora de Aznar. Following a stay at the Spanish Embassy on Sixteenth Street, the Spanish envoy and his wife departed for New York en route to Madrid for a leave of two months or more before returning to Ciudad Trujillo early next year. The guest list included Spanish Ambassador-at-Large and Senora de Lequerica, Spanish embassy attachés, and senior Dominican diplomatic officials including Minister-Counselor and Senora de Vega, Military Attaché and Senora de Espaillat, and First Secretary and Senora de Hoepelman.
records.summary_es: Una crónica social en el Evening Star reseña un almuerzo en Washington ofrecido por el embajador dominicano y la señora de Thomen en honor del embajador de España en la República Dominicana, Manuel Aznar, y la señora de Aznar. Tras alojarse en la embajada española en Sixteenth Street, el enviado español y su esposa partieron hacia Nueva York en ruta a Madrid para una licencia de dos meses o más antes de regresar a Ciudad Trujillo a principios del próximo año. La lista de invitados incluyó al embajador plenipotenciario español y la señora de Lequerica, agregados de la embajada española y altos funcionarios diplomáticos dominicanos, entre ellos el ministro consejero y la señora de Vega, el agregado militar y la señora de Espaillat, y el primer secretario y la señora de Hoepelman.

He subsequently returned to the Nogales border in 1928 to assist the Mexico-Arizona Trading Company.

records.headline: In the first meeting between the heads of Haiti and the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: In the first meeting between the heads of Haiti and the Dominican Republic in nine years, Presidents Magloire and Trujillo agreed to conduct a vigorous and unrelenting fight against communism. According to Haitian Secretary of State Luc Fouché, the leaders proposed treaties covering four points: confirming the February 1928 Havana convention on political asylum, protecting migratory workers, regulating export-import tariffs, and advancing cultural, touristic, and political solidarity. Observers in both countries viewed the agreement as fostering a progressive future.
records.summary_es: En la primera reunión celebrada en nueve años entre los mandatarios de Haití y la República Dominicana, los presidentes Magloire y Trujillo acordaron llevar a cabo una lucha enérgica e implacable contra el comunismo. De acuerdo con el secretario de Estado haitiano Luc Fouché, los gobernantes propusieron tratados sobre cuatro aspectos: ratificar la convención de La Habana de febrero de 1928 sobre asilo político, amparar a los trabajadores migratorios, regular los aranceles de exportación e importación y promover la solidaridad cultural, turística y política. Observadores de ambos países valoraron el acuerdo como un paso hacia un futuro de progreso.

20 Demonstrate Against Trujillo Near Conference

About 20 political refugees, nearly all from the Dominican Republic, today began displaying placards urging moves against the Trujillo regime about one block away from the Pan American Conference.

Extra police details, called out in case of a serious disturbance, told the group it must not parade closer than 500 feet from the premises of the Pan American Union, where President Auriol of France was addressing the conference.

records.headline: In a dispatch from Buenos Aires on Mar. 31, President Juan Perón
records.summary_en: In a dispatch from Buenos Aires on Mar. 31, President Juan Perón offered to share the benefits of Argentina's reported discovery of cheap atomic power with the Dominican Republic. Perón extended the offer in a cabled reply to President Rafael Trujillo, who had congratulated the Argentine leader on the atomic development. Thanking Trujillo for his noble gesture, Perón pledged to place at the disposal of the Dominican people whatever achievements might assist their happiness and greatness.
records.summary_es: En un despacho fechado el 31 de marzo en Buenos Aires, el presidente Juan Perón ofreció compartir con la República Dominicana las ventajas del anunciado hallazgo argentino de energía atómica económica. Perón formuló el ofrecimiento en una respuesta cablegráfica al presidente Rafael Trujillo, quien lo había felicitado por el desarrollo atómico. Tras agradecer el noble gesto de Trujillo, Perón se comprometió a poner a disposición del pueblo dominicano cuanto resultado pudiera favorecer su felicidad y grandeza.

records.headline: Executive Secretary Louis S. Law announced that the Caribbean Interim Tourism Committee
records.summary_en: Executive Secretary Louis S. Law announced that the Caribbean Interim Tourism Committee will hold its third annual general meeting in Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic, from September 17 to 21. The principal agenda item is the formation of the Caribbean Tourist Development Association, as the interim committee will terminate on December 31, 1951. The session will also include the judging of the Caribbean Poster Competition, featuring two entries submitted by each territory and displayed by number only. An afternoon would be devoted to selecting the winners of the first, second and third prizes. Mr. Law, who left Port of Spain a few days ago, would hold discussions with the Netherlands Antilles Tourism Committee; from there he would go directly to Ciudad Trujillo to preside at the meeting.

El tema primordial de la agenda es la constitución de la Asociación para el Desarrollo Turístico del Caribe, dado que el comité interino concluirá sus labores el 31 de diciembre de 1951. La asamblea incluirá asimismo la evaluación del Concurso de Carteles del Caribe, en el que se expondrán dos obras por territorio identificadas únicamente con números. Se dedicaría una tarde a seleccionar a los ganadores del primer, segundo y tercer premios. El señor Law, que había salido de Puerto España unos días antes, sostendría conversaciones con el Comité de Turismo de las Antillas Neerlandesas; desde allí iría directamente a Ciudad Trujillo para presidir la reunión.

records.headline: At a conference of the Caribbean Interim Tourist Commission held
records.summary_en: At a conference of the Caribbean Interim Tourist Commission held in Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic, from September 17th to 21st, Harry W. Goeggel was chosen as chairman of the newly formed Caribbean Interim Tourist Association. The meeting was attended by delegates from Trinidad, Haiti, Puerto Rico, Grenada, St. Vincent, Aruba, Curaçao, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Saba, Saint Martin, the Virgin Islands, and the Dominican Republic. The assembled representatives participated as guests of the Dominican Republic. The new association will be concerned with coordinating the efforts of the various individual areas in the promotion of tourism to the Caribbean area, and the importance of additional transportation facilities to the islands, and particularly inter-island surface and air transportation, was stressed. The next meeting of the CITA will be held in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, in May 1952 at the invitation of the Haitian government.
records.summary_es: En una conferencia de la Comisión Interina de Turismo del Caribe celebrada en Ciudad Trujillo, República Dominicana, del 17 al 21 de septiembre, Harry W. Goeggel fue elegido presidente de la recién constituida Asociación Interina de Turismo del Caribe. La asamblea contó con delegados de Trinidad, Haití, Puerto Rico, Granada, San Vicente, Aruba, Curazao, Guadalupe, Martinica, Saba, San Martín, las Islas Vírgenes y la República Dominicana. Los representantes congregados asistieron en calidad de huéspedes de la República Dominicana. La nueva asociación se ocupará de coordinar los esfuerzos de las diversas áreas individuales en la promoción del turismo hacia el área del Caribe, y se subrayó la importancia de facilidades adicionales de transporte hacia las islas, y en particular el transporte interinsular de superficie y aéreo. La próxima reunión de la CITA se celebrará en Puerto Príncipe, Haití, en mayo de 1952, por invitación del gobierno haitiano.

records.headline: Photographs from Santo Domingo illustrate the resting place of Christopher
records.summary_en: Photographs from Santo Domingo illustrate the resting place of Christopher Columbus, where his body lies in accordance with his desire to remain in the land he loved best. The Columbus Memorial Lighthouse, scheduled for completion in the Dominican Republic in 1954, will house his ashes, historical relics, a library, and sections for 21 American nations. In the cathedral at Ciudad Trujillo, Archbishop Ricardo Pittini, Primate of the West Indies, unlocks the casket containing the bones twice a year to verify the republic's greatest historical treasure.
records.summary_es: Fotografías tomadas en Santo Domingo ilustran la sepultura de Cristóbal Colón, donde reposa su cuerpo según su deseo de permanecer en la tierra que más amó. El Faro Conmemorativo de Colón, cuya finalización en la República Dominicana está prevista para 1954, guardará sus cenizas, reliquias históricas, una biblioteca y secciones para 21 países de América. En la catedral de Ciudad Trujillo, el arzobispo Ricardo Pittini, primado de las Indias Occidentales, abre dos veces al año con una llave dorada el cofre con los restos para verificar el mayor tesoro histórico de la república.

records.headline: Archival searches across Europe and Washington have failed to uncover
records.summary_en: Archival searches across Europe and Washington have failed to uncover architectural plans or settler descriptions of the early settlement of La Isabela. Historians first investigated the site in 1893 ahead of the Columbian Exposition, dispatching a commissioner to Dominica to collect surviving materials, though many building stones had already been removed. Settled by Spanish farmers and artisans who complained of the local climate, the outpost was abandoned in 1496 after gold was discovered along the Ozama River near the site of Ciudad Trujillo.
records.summary_es: Las pesquisas archivísticas realizadas en Europa y Washington no han logrado descubrir planos arquitectónicos ni relatos de los colonos sobre el primitivo asentamiento de La Isabela. Los historiadores examinaron el lugar por vez primera en 1893 con vistas a la Exposición Colombina, comisionando a un enviado a Dominica para recuperar restos materiales, aunque gran parte de las piedras de las construcciones ya habían sido retiradas. Poblada por agricultores y artesanos españoles descontentos con el clima local, la colonia fue abandonada en 1496 a raíz del hallazgo de oro junto al río Ozama, cerca del actual emplazamiento de Ciudad Trujillo.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the United States concluded a ten-year bilateral pact with the Dominican Republic authorizing guided missile monitoring stations to close the observation gap between the Bahamas and Puerto Rico. Under the agreement, unarmed test missiles launched from Florida would fly over Dominican coastal waters rather than over the mainland. U.S. military personnel operating the tracking sites were capped at 300 individuals, expandable up to 500 under exceptional circumstances.

En virtud del acuerdo, los misiles de prueba desarmados lanzados desde Florida sobrevolarían aguas costeras dominicanas en lugar de territorio continental. El personal militar estadounidense que operaría los puestos de seguimiento tenía un límite máximo de 300 efectivos, ampliable hasta 500 en circunstancias excepcionales.

records.full_text:
Turkey, Dominicans Sign Friendship Treaty Here

The Republic of Turkey and the Dominican Republic today signed a friendship treaty here, guaranteeing "perpetual peace" between the two countries and paving the way for treaties on commerce and navigation, consular rights and privileges, copyrights and patents and extradition.

Dr. Luis Francisco Thomen, Dominican Ambassador to the United States, signed for his country, and the signature for Turkey was affixed by Feridun C. Erkin, the Turkish Ambassador. The treaty was signed at the Turkish Embassy.

Officials said the treaty will go into effect upon exchange of ratifications at a still undermined date.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Cuban Foreign Minister Aureliano Sanchez Arango denounced the Dominican seizure of a vessel and the subsequent 30-year hard-labor sentences imposed on its crew for alleged subversive plotting. Sanchez Arango accused the ship's captain, Brito, of acting as a Dominican spy who delivered the craft and kidnapped its crew under shifting pretenses before being convicted alongside them. Because diplomatic protests proved futile, Cuba appealed the maritime incident to the Inter-American Peace Commission.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Cuban Foreign Minister Aureliano Sanchez Arango planned to present evidence to the OAS Peace Committee demonstrating that the Dominican interception of the unarmed vessel *Quetzal* constituted high-seas piracy. Sanchez Arango argued that the ship was seized near Cape San Antonio, far from Dominican territory, and threatened to take the case to the United Nations and the World Court if Cuban crewmen were not freed. Dominican Foreign Minister Virgilio Diaz Ordonez prepared to argue the Dominican case before the committee, amidst reports that Guatemalan prisoners might soon be released.

records.headline: Representatives of Cuba and the Dominican Republic convened
records.summary_en: Representatives of Cuba and the Dominican Republic convened at the Pan-American Union Building under the Inter-American Peace Committee to settle the Quetzal dispute. Crew members of the Quetzal, including five Cubans, had received 20 years' imprisonment on charges of conspiracy against the Dominican Republic, while Cuba accused the Dominicans of high-seas piracy and abduction. Cuban Ambassador Gonzales Guell signed the declaration only after receiving official word that the Cuban nationals were released in Ciudad Trujillo. The controversy followed years of deteriorating relations over Dominican accusations that Cubans assisted exiles seeking to overthrow Generalissimo Trujillo.

El embajador cubano Gonzales Guell firmó la declaración únicamente tras recibir aviso oficial de que los ciudadanos cubanos habían sido liberados en Ciudad Trujillo. PHYSICIANS AND FRIENDS TO TOUR CARIBBEAN

CHICAGO — (ANP) — A group of physicians, their families, friends and other interested tourists are planning a good-will tour of the West Indies early next May. Invited initially by the l'Association Medicale d'Haiti to spend some time in the land of Toussaint L'Ouverture, where a series of clinics will be held, the trip which will be a sight seeing and pleasure tour as well will include a number of the Caribbean islands.

Besides Haiti, the party will visit Peurto Rico, Jamaica, the Dominican Republic and Cuba.

Dr. Joseph G. Gathings of Washington, D. C., president of the National Medical Association will head the group along with Claude A. Barnett of Chicago.

The tour which will be made in Pan American Constellations will last approximately two weeks. Details are being handled by the travel expert, John L. Kooreman, 110 S. Dearborn St., Chicago.

SERVICE BY KEFAUVER

For a long time, I have been wondering about that Kefauver television show. Did it really accomplish something constructive? Obviously, it made Rudolph Halley a figure in New York politics and encouraged Estes Kefauver himself to run for President on the Democratic side.

Was that all?

Apparently, it is not so. I have received a circular from the Dominican Republic Information Center which is devoted to advertising the aforesaid Republic where Christopher Columbus is buried. According to the circular, the Dominican Republic is progressive and takes advantage of every opportunity. Therefore, as Kefauver drove gambling out of the United States, the Dominican Republic made gambling the cultural tie between the United States and the other Republic. The circular says:

“Gambling-in-the-sky via slot machines will feature a four-hour plane flight by the ‘Sportsmen’s Special,’ between Miami and Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic—the ‘Monte Carlo of the Caribbean’ where four legal gambling casinos flourish, if final flight negotiations are completed this week. Three of the casinos have opened since the Kefauver Crime Investigation closed many illegal gambling places in the U.S.

“Service by the 50-passenger chartered plane ‘Lady Luck’ is scheduled to commence on or about March 7 from Miami. The plane, though owned by the (CDA) Compania Dominicana de Aviacion, a Pan-American subsidiary, would be chartered to a sponsoring promotion group to begin the week-end round-trips between Miami and the West Indies country. The Dominican Government itself is not sponsoring the project but approves of it.”

In addition to approving of the slot-machines and other devices, the Dominican Government sends me this circular through the mails. If any American sent a similar circular through the mails, he would probably go to jail. But then Americans no longer count in the United States except to pay taxes and to have their sons conscripted for United Nations police actions.

I forgot to save the envelope in which this circular came and therefore I cannot tell you whether it used a paid-for stamp or came as diplomatic mail, free of charge. I get a lot of that kind of mail, all free, the object of which is always to educate me to love some foreign country. But if anyone wants to send some mail about loving America, a paid-for stamp is essential. It is a fine point, this business of who pays to have mail delivered advocating love.

ZETAS CROWN SEPIA LADY

Ship Ahoy — the theme.

Beta Tau Zeta chapter of Zeta Phi Beta sorority, presented its annual ball, March 28 in the beautiful. spacious Harlem Square Crystal Room. The theme for the setting was "Ship Ahoy." The ballroom, improvised as a deck, was lavishly adorned with palms, minute ship and life preservers, all of which gave a beautiful tropical setting.

CROWNING OF SEPIA LADY

The special feature of the evening was the crowning of the Sepia Lady. which title was won by Mrs. Corinne L. Anton. Mrs. Anton was attractively attired in a glimmering white evening gown; the crown was presented by Mrs. Portia Bannister, Sepia Lady of 1949-50. Mrs. Bannister was attired in a light lavendar heavily sequined dress that was quite stunning. The regal robe of royal blue velvet with white satin lining was gracefully thrown around Mrs. Anton and a queen's bouquet of white roses was presented her by the retiring "Lady."

LADIES IN WAITING

Mrs. Nancy Collins, Miss Betty Gaitor and Mrs. Marjorie Adams were ladies in waiting. Each wore evening gowns of pastel shades, and the charm and poise with which they ambulated about the ballroom easily made them the belles of the ball. The throne of blue and white backround, with a regal silver lined chair for the queen, was graced by each of the ladies in waiting on either side.

Mr. Charles L. Williams, principal of Booker T. Washington high school was Master of Ceremonies. He presented the queen and her court and Mrs. H. D. Thompson, basileus of the chapter presented a first prize to Mrs. Anton of an 11½ inch engraved loving cup; an 11-day all expense cruise in the Caribbean (Dominican Republic, Trujillo, Haiti, Cuba, Jamaica.) The second prize to Mrs. Nancy Collins, a loving cup and Samsonite luggage. Each of the other ladies received loving cups engraved.

All who witnessed the "ship ahoy" ball and the crowning declared it the most outstanding event of the year and of the history of social events of this kind in the city.

Members of the chapter were all dressed in gorgeous shades of blue and white. Sorors visited from West Palm Beach.

records.summary_en: The Key West Citizen reported that the Dominican government announced plans to construct a $1,000,000 factory to manufacture newsprint from bagasse, the fibrous waste of sugarcane. With imported paper costing $240 per ton, domestic production was projected to lower newsprint costs for local publishers to approximately $160 per ton. The article also discussed tests conducted by the U.S. Bureau of Standards validating a similar bagasse paper-making process developed by engineer Joaquin de la Roza.

Frente al costo del papel importado de 240 dólares por tonelada, se proyectaba que la producción nacional reduciría los costos de papel prensa para las editoras locales a aproximadamente 160 dólares por tonelada. In some other countries, the price of newsprint is much higher —around $156 a ton in England, for example. In the Dominican Republic, where the price of imported newsprint is $240 a ton, the government announced it will build a million dollar plant to make newsprint from sugar cane waste, called bagasse. The process, similar to those in S use elsewhere for many years. will supply paper for the Dominican papers at around $160 a ton, the government says. A newer process for making paper from the cane waste—the fibrous residue after the mills have ground all the sugar from the cane—has been given the approval of Secretary of Commerce Sawyer. He reported to Congress that the Bureau of Standards had made paper from Louisiana cane waste that was “satisfactory” in all important respects and superior in some to newsprint now currently in use.” Joaquin de la Roza, engineer and paper technologist, who holds a U. records.full_text:
HE LOCKED HIS STABLE

Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo, former president of the Dominican Republic and presently Ambassador-at-large and delegate to the United Nations, was a guest of honor at a dinner the other night at Tregaron, the fabulous Washington home of former Ambassador and Mrs. Joseph E. Davies—where the Generalissimo was described by Chief Justice Fred M. Vinson as a latter day George Washington.

Trujillo, the Chief Justice told the dinner group, which included General Omar Bradley, Seantor Estes Kefauver and Justice Stanley Reed, is one of the great personalities of our time, and the man who lighted the torch of civilization for his country.

Which reminds us, that besides giving his country a stable government and a sound economy, the Generalissimo may also have provided an example of enlightenment to the United States. We have on our desk a translation of Dominican "Law No. 1443" signed by Trujillo on June 14, 1947, outlawing the communist party as representing "doctrines and platforms that are incompatible with the civil, republican, democratic and representative nature of the Government of the Republic."

But in this country of ours, the number one target of the Kremlin, there is today no Federal ban on the Communist Party, which is openly and avowedly devoted to the destruction of our Constitution. Neighbor Trujillo reminds us that we are stretching the intent of this document and the mantle of freedom in sheltering a criminal ideology.

records.headline: Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic was picketed last night
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that seven demonstrators from New York picketed outside a Washington office building during a diplomatic reception held by General Rafael Trujillo at the nearby Mayflower Hotel. Police enforced regulations barring demonstrations within 500 feet of the hotel, and the peaceful picketers displayed placards accusing Trujillo of political murders during his presidency. Trujillo was serving as Dominican minister of finance and chief United Nations delegate, while his brother Hector B. Trujillo held the presidency.

La policía aplicó la normativa que prohibía manifestaciones a menos de 500 pies del hotel, y los piqueteros pacíficos portaban pancartas acusando a Trujillo de asesinatos políticos durante su presidencia. Trujillo ejercía como ministro de Hacienda dominicano y delegado principal ante las Naciones Unidas, mientras su hermano Héctor B. Trujillo ocupaba la presidencia.

records.full_text:
Dominican Republic Accuses U. S. Official Of Inciting Trouble

CIUDAD TRUJILLO, Dominican Republic, May 20.—The Dominican Republic government has accused the United States Undersecretary of State for Latin American Affairs, John Moors Cabot, of stirring up trouble in the Caribbean area against the Dominican Republic.

(In Washington a State Department spokesman said the Dominican statement was "too ridiculous to comment upon.")

A Dominican War Department statement yesterday said that as a result of Mr. Cabot's activity on his recent tour of the Caribbean area, the Dominican Republic may not send a contingent of troops to join United Nations forces fighting in Korea. The statement said the troops may be needed at home.

Gen. Felix Hermida, chief of the army's intelligence service, said in a statement that "through secret documents obtained by the army intelligence service, the Dominican Republic government has confirmed that during . . . Cabot's tour of the Caribbean area, he devoted a large part of his time talking and discussing plans with Communists enemies of the Venezuelan, Cuban, Salvadoran, Dominican Republic, Honduran and Peruvian governments."

Gen. Hermida added that "Cabot invited known agitators to visit the United States, promising them entrance visas, a fact which is known through a letter written by the well-known Dominican Marxist Jose Ricardo Roques Martinez, which was addressed to intimate friends in Lima, Maiquetia, Guantanamo and Miami."

records.full_text:
McDermott Named Envoy to El Salvador To Succeed Duke

President Eisenhower today nominated Michael J. McDermott, a veteran State Department career officer, to be Ambassador to the Republic of El Salvador.

Mr. McDermott, now special assistant to the Secretary for press relations, will succeed Angier Biddle Duke, who is retiring.

Gen. Eisenhower also asked the Senate to approve these appointments:

1. R. Douglas Stuart of Lake Forest, Ill., to be Ambassador to Canada, succeeding Stanley Woodward. Mr. Stuart, 67, is vice chairman of the board of Quaker Oats Co.

2. William T. Pheiffer, New York attorney, to be Ambassador to the Dominican Republic, succeeding Phelps Phelps, resigned. Mr. Pheiffer, a former member of Congress, is 62 and is also a former law partner of White House Secretary Thomas E. Stephens.

3. Joseph E. Talbot for reappointment to a six-year term on the United States Tariff Commission. Mr. Talbot, a former Republican member of Congress from Connecticut, was appointed to an unexpired term on the commission several weeks ago.

4. William V. Mitchell, Denver, assistant to the President of the Quick-Way Truck Shovel Corp., to be administrator of the Small Defense Plants Administration. He succeeds Yngvar Brynildssen.

Was "Dean" of Press Officers.

Mr. McDermott, 58, who is known affectionately by his newspaper friends around the world as "Mac" or "Mike," long has been the dean of United States Government press officers.

During his more than 32 years with the State Department, he has helped interpret to the public the policies of 11 Secretaries of State—Secretaries Lansing, Colby, Hughes, Kellogg, Stimson, Hull, Stettinius, Byrnes, Marshall, Acheson, and Dulles.

Started as Clerk

Born in Peabody, Mass., about 10 years after his parents immigrated from Ireland, he began working for the Government here in 1917 as a clerk in the War Department. After World War I service as a confidential clerk at the Supreme War Council in Paris, he joined the State Department in 1920.

He was made assistant chief of the department's old Current Information Division in 1924 and chief in 1927. Since then he has been the chief spokesman to newspaper reporters for one Secretary of State after another and their adviser on what they should say in their own news conferences.

Was Special Assistant.

Since a 1944 departmental re-organization, his title has been special assistant to the Secretary of State for press relations.

His name has become widely known to newspaper readers only since 1945 when Mr. McDermott began letting reporters quote him by name when he made announcements or answered questions. Previously, he had insisted on anonymity

For many years, Mr. McDermott has looked older than his age because of a thatch of snow-white hair. His hair became white since soon after, as a boy of 10, he saw a bolt of lightning shoot through his home.

Mr. McDermott intends to keep his home here at 1855 Upshur street N.W.

records.headline: Dutch aviators Toni and Henni Tromm made an emergency landing
records.summary_en: Dutch aviators Toni and Henni Tromm made an emergency landing at Catalina Island, southeast of Ciudad Trujillo, while attempting to refuel their seaplane without contacting Dominican authorities. Rough six-foot waves broke the wire stays supporting the floats, compelling the flyers to lash the pontoons with rope and taxi to the coastal settlement of La Rommana. After a local pilot boat towed the craft upriver, radio reports of a forced landing at Catalina caused authorities to dispatch four American mechanics attached to the Dominican air force, mistakenly believing a large PBY Catalina aircraft required assistance.

Olas picadas de seis pies rompieron los tirantes de alambre que sostenían los flotadores, obligando a los tripulantes a atar los pontones con cuerdas y navegar hasta el poblado costero de La Rommana. Luego de que una lancha piloto remolcara la aeronave río arriba, los avisos radiales sobre un amerizaje forzoso en Catalina motivaron que las autoridades enviaran a cuatro mecánicos estadounidenses adscritos a la fuerza aérea dominicana, bajo la falsa creencia de que un gran hidroavión PBY Catalina requería auxilio.

records.headline: During an interview on Italian emigration, a spokesperson cites
records.summary_en: During an interview on Italian emigration, a spokesperson cites an offer by General Trujillo to settle 100,000 Italian immigrants in the Dominican Republic. The reference is discussed alongside American legislative proposals to admit an extra quota of some 100,000 Italians over two years. The discussion examines broader international avenues for absorbing surplus Italian agricultural labor.

El diálogo examina vías internacionales más amplias para absorber los excedentes de mano de obra agrícola italiana.

records.headline: According to Dominican sources, a priest named Toledano, former vice-rector
records.summary_en: According to Dominican sources, a priest named Toledano, former vice-rector for four years at the University of Santo Domingo and deputy for Archbishop Ricardo Pittini, will serve under the direct instructions of Generalissimo Trujillo. The dispatch notes Trujillo's secret defense agreement with the Eisenhower administration and references ongoing construction of a secret long-range missile base in the Dominican Republic to safeguard Caribbean waterways and the Panama Canal. In addition, Trujillo plans to demand United Nations action to free Spanish prisoners held in the Soviet Union while arranging to bring 100,000 agricultural laborers from Italy.
records.summary_es: Según fuentes dominicanas, un sacerdote de apellido Toledano, exvicerrector durante cuatro años de la Universidad de Santo Domingo y representante del arzobispo Ricardo Pittini, actuará bajo las instrucciones directas del generalísimo Trujillo. El despacho menciona el acuerdo militar secreto de Trujillo con el gobierno de Eisenhower y alude a la construcción en curso de una base secreta de proyectiles de largo alcance en la República Dominicana para resguardar las rutas caribeñas y el canal de Panamá. Además, Trujillo proyecta exigir gestiones ante las Naciones Unidas para liberar a prisioneros españoles retenidos en la Unión Soviética y coordina el traslado de 100,000 trabajadores agrícolas desde Italia.

records.headline: Señorita Bernadino, a delegate to the United Nations from the Dominican
records.summary_en: Señorita Bernadino, a delegate to the United Nations from the Dominican Republic, is in Geneva attending a conference of one of the organization's branches. Her brother, embassy first secretary Luis Bernadino, has traveled to London on a special mission for his government. Another brother, Felix Bernadino, sailed last week for his new post as Dominican Ambassador to Venezuela following a farewell party in New York attended by friends, including Paul Murphy of the Organization of American States. Señorita Bernadino, formerly a Washington correspondent for La Nacion in Ciudad Trujillo, continues her reporting from New York as a non-resident member of the American Newspaper Women’s Club.
records.summary_es: La señorita Bernadino, delegada de la República Dominicana ante las Naciones Unidas, se encuentra en Ginebra asistiendo a una conferencia de una de las ramas del organismo. Su hermano, el primer secretario de embajada Luis Bernadino, viajó a Londres en una misión especial para su gobierno. Otro hermano, Félix Bernadino, zarpó la semana pasada hacia su nuevo destino como embajador dominicano en Venezuela tras una reunión de despedida en Nueva York a la que asistieron amigos, entre ellos Paul Murphy, de la Organización de los Estados Americanos. La señorita Bernadino, anteriormente corresponsal en Washington de La Nación en Ciudad Trujillo, continúa sus labores periodísticas desde Nueva York como miembro no residente del American Newspaper Women’s Club.

records.summary_en: Msgr. Oscar Robles Toledano, 41, has been appointed as the newest Dominican Republic delegate to the United Nations. He previously served for a number of years offering Mass and preaching sermons at the cathedral in Ciudad Trujillo, described as the oldest cathedral in the Western Hemisphere. In his new diplomatic post, he will serve under Gen. Rafael L. Trujillo on the country's UN delegation.

En su nuevo cargo diplomático, prestará servicios bajo el mando del general Rafael L. Trujillo en la delegación del país ante la ONU.

records.headline: Trujillo, is leaving office temporarily to take over management of a large sugar producing firm
records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that Dominican President Hector B. Trujillo nominated Brigadier General Manuel de Moya Alonzo to succeed Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo as Ambassador to the United Nations. The announcement stated that the generalissimo was temporarily relinquishing his diplomatic post and military command to manage a large sugar enterprise. De Moya had previously served on multiple Dominican trade and diplomatic missions across the United States and Europe.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el presidente dominicano Héctor B. Trujillo designó al general de brigada Manuel de Moya Alonzo para suceder al generalísimo Rafael L. Trujillo como embajador ante las Naciones Unidas. El anuncio señalaba que el generalísimo dejaba temporalmente su cargo diplomático y el mando militar para administrar una gran empresa azucarera. De Moya había participado previamente en múltiples misiones comerciales y diplomáticas dominicanas por Estados Unidos y Europa.
records.passage: As Ambassador to U. S. By the Associated Press TRUJILLO, Dominican Republic, Aug. 19.—President Hec tor B. Trujillo announced today he is nominating Brig. Gen. Manuel Demoya Alonzo to suc ceed his brother, the Dominican Republic’s strong man since 1930, as Ambassador to the United Nations. The outgoing Ambassador, Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo, is leaving office temporarily to take over management of a large sugar producing firm. He also is giving up his posts as commander in chief of his country's armed forces. Gen. Demoya has represented his country on diplomatic and trade missions in Europe and the United States. The generalissimo turned over the Dominican presidency to his brother last year after holding it almost continuously since 1930.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported on the impending departure of Dominican Ambassador Luis Francisco Thomen and his wife following the succession of President Hector Trujillo. Although Dr. Thomen had initially tendered his routine resignation and was briefly asked to remain, Brigadier General Manuel de Moya Alonzo was appointed as his successor. De Moya was well known in Washington diplomatic circles, having previously served as Minister Counselor at the embassy.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó sobre la inminente partida del embajador dominicano Luis Francisco Thomen y su esposa tras la asunción del presidente Héctor Trujillo. Aunque el Dr. Thomen había presentado inicialmente su renuncia de rigor y se le pidió brevemente permanecer en funciones, el general de brigada Manuel de Moya Alonzo fue nombrado su sucesor. De Moya era bien conocido en los círculos diplomáticos de Washington, habiéndose desempeñado con anterioridad como ministro consejero en la embajada.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star detailed extensive personnel rotations within the Dominican diplomatic mission in Washington following the appointment of Ambassador Manuel de Moya Alonzo. records.headline: Jewels of Queen Isabella of Spain have been placed on public display
records.summary_en: Jewels of Queen Isabella of Spain have been placed on public display in Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic, in preparation for the celebration of Columbus Day on Oct 12. The items belong to a five million dollar collection of Christopher Columbus mementos housed in the city's cathedral, identified as the oldest cathedral in the New World where the explorer is entombed. The exhibition has attracted young tourists visiting the historic site.

Las piezas forman parte de una colección de recuerdos de Cristóbal Colón valorada en cinco millones de dólares y conservada en la catedral de la ciudad, descrita como la más antigua del Nuevo Mundo donde reposan los restos del explorador. La muestra ha concitado la atención de jóvenes turistas que visitan el recinto histórico.

records.headline: Lobbying efforts by Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo in Washington secured
records.summary_en: Lobbying efforts by Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo in Washington secured an increase for Dominican sugar in United States import quotas over recent years. Operating through several foreign agents who distributed substantial sums and propaganda, Trujillo obtained an important concession for himself and his family, who own much of the Dominican Republic's sugar industry. The increase was achieved at the expense of Cuba, prompting the Cuban sugar industry to retain former United States Senators James P. Kem of Missouri and Joseph C. O’Mahoney of Wyoming to protect its quota.

records.headline: Located twenty-five miles outside Ciudad Trujillo, the seaside
records.summary_en: Located twenty-five miles outside Ciudad Trujillo, the seaside village of Boca Chica is attracting American tourists visiting the Dominican Republic. The village features the Hamaca Hotel-Casino, an ultrasmart 28-room resort built as part of a chain of 14 hotels planned by the Dominican government to offer North American travelers modern comforts. Visitors can enjoy a private walled-in beach, ocean and hill views, and recreational boating and fishing, with skiffs and outboards available for rent at about $5 and about $8 per day.

La localidad cuenta con el hotel-casino Hamaca, un elegante complejo de 28 habitaciones erigido como parte de una cadena de 14 hoteles proyectada por el gobierno dominicano para ofrecer comodidades modernas a los viajeros norteamericanos. Los visitantes disfrutan de una playa protegida, vistas al mar y a las colinas, y paseos en bote y pesca deportiva, con alquiler de botes de remo y fuera de borda por unos $5 y unos $8 al día.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported that the Dominican government stripped Porfirio Rubirosa of his diplomatic post as embassy counselor in Paris and revoked his diplomatic status citing scandalous personal conduct. Rubirosa's dismissal followed his naming as co-respondent in high-profile divorce litigation in London and the United States. His history of celebrity marriages included unions with Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo's daughter Flor de Oro, French actress Danielle Darrieux, and American heiress Doris Duke.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el gobierno dominicano despojó a Porfirio Rubirosa de su cargo diplomático como consejero de embajada en París y revocó su estatus diplomático alegando una conducta personal escandalosa. La destitución de Rubirosa se produjo luego de ser señalado como codemandado en sonados litigios de divorcio en Londres y Estados Unidos. Su historial de matrimonios con celebridades incluía enlaces con la hija del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo, Flor de Oro, la actriz francesa Danielle Darrieux y la heredera estadounidense Doris Duke.

Mr. Rubirosa was most re cently in the news when he was named as the other man in a divorce suit brought by Million aire Golfer Robert Sweeney in London last month against his wife, the former Joanne Connelly of New York. records.headline: Welcoming representatives of the Pan American Medical Association
records.summary_en: Welcoming representatives of the Pan American Medical Association, the President of the United States extended greetings to members participating in an upcoming convention cruise aboard the Nieuw Amsterdam scheduled for next January. The cruise itinerary includes visits to Ciudad Trujillo in the Dominican Republic, Caracas, Saint Thomas, San Juan, and Havana. The President commended the association's 26-year program promoting hemispheric medical knowledge and cooperation, affirming his support for widening its professional scholarship initiatives.
records.summary_es: Al recibir a representantes de la Asociación Médica Panamericana, el presidente de los Estados Unidos saludó a los miembros que participarán en el próximo crucero de convenciones a bordo del Nieuw Amsterdam programado para el próximo enero. El itinerario del viaje contempla escalas en Ciudad Trujillo en la República Dominicana, Caracas, Santo Tomás, San Juan y La Habana. El mandatario encomió el programa de 26 años de la entidad en favor del intercambio científico y la amistad médica continental, manifestando su respaldo a la ampliación de sus becas de formación profesional.

records.headline: Two new ecclesiastical jurisdictions carved out of the Archdiocese of Ciudad Trujillo
records.summary_en: Two new ecclesiastical jurisdictions carved out of the Archdiocese of Ciudad Trujillo have been erected in the Dominican Republic, according to a Vatican announcement. The new entities are the Diocese of Santiago de los Caballeros y de la Vega and the Prelacy Nullius of San Juan de la Magifana. Archbishop Ottavio Beras will govern the Diocese of Santiago de los Caballeros as apostolic administrator, assisted by Auxiliary Bishop Ugo Edoardo Polanco Brito. No appointment has yet been announced to head the newly created prelature.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported on an embassy social gathering where guests were entertained with demonstrations of the Dominican Republic's national dance. The dance was demonstrated by Beatrice Rodriguez, daughter of the Dominican OAS Ambassador, and Senora Eva Finkel, accompanied by music provided by musicians visiting from New York. The article noted that the dance, originally practiced by rural peasants, was introduced to elite Dominican society twenty-four years earlier by President Rafael Trujillo.

El artículo señaló que el baile, practicado originariamente por campesinos, fue introducido en la alta sociedad dominicana veinticuatro años antes por el presidente Rafael Trujillo.

records.summary_en: Prior to departing Los Angeles, Mr. Rubirosa announced his marriage plans to reporters. The Dominican Republic Foreign Office in Ciudad Trujillo disclosed that Mr. Rubirosa and Miss Hutton would marry at the Dominican consulate general in New York. According to the Foreign Office, Mr. Rubirosa will be restored to his former diplomatic post, and Miss Hutton will become a Dominican citizen. Mr. Rubirosa had recently been dismissed from his assignment as minister plenipotentiary in Paris for what the government termed misconduct.
records.summary_es: Antes de salir de Los Ángeles, el señor Rubirosa anunció sus planes de matrimonio a la prensa. La cancillería de la República Dominicana en Ciudad Trujillo comunicó que el señor Rubirosa y la señorita Hutton contraerían matrimonio en el consulado general dominicano en Nueva York. De acuerdo con el ministerio, el señor Rubirosa será restituido en su antiguo cargo diplomático y la señorita Hutton adquirirá la nacionalidad dominicana. El señor Rubirosa había sido separado recientemente de sus funciones como ministro plenipotenciario en París debido a lo que el gobierno calificó de mala conducta.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported on the wedding of Woolworth heiress Barbara Hutton and Dominican diplomat Porfirio Rubirosa, with Dominican Air Force chief Major General Rafael Trujillo Martinez among the attendees. Hutton became a Dominican citizen immediately prior to the nuptials in order to wed under Dominican law utilizing Rubirosa's diplomatic status as minister plenipotentiary to France. The report reviewed both individuals' previous high-society marriages, including Rubirosa's prior union with Flor Trujillo.

Hutton adquirió la ciudadanía dominicana inmediatamente antes de las nupcias para casarse bajo la ley dominicana aprovechando el estatus diplomático de Rubirosa como ministro plenipotenciario en Francia. records.summary_en: On Jan. 2, the Dominican Republic federal health department ordered padlocked nine of 12 housing developments operated by Central Barahona. records.summary_en: Charges alleging Dominican complicity in an invasion conspiracy against Guatemala were rejected by the Dominican Republic Foreign Office as an invention of atheistic communism. The Dominican government declared that it had no relations with Guatemalans either as friends or enemies of the Arbenz administration. An official Guatemalan communique had alleged intercepted correspondence showing that anti-government plotters were supported by the governments of Santo Domingo, El Salvador, Venezuela, and Nicaragua, with the acquiescence of the United States.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reported international reactions to Guatemalan accusations alleging a foreign conspiracy against President Jacobo Arbenz's government. The Dominican Foreign Ministry dismissed the charges as communist fabrications, denying any involvement with Guatemala or the Arbenz regime. Other accused figures, including Nicaraguan Colonel Anastasio Somoza Debayle and General Miguel Ydigoras Fuentes, ridiculed the conspiracy claims, while Panama dismissed an attache named in the Guatemalan communique.

Otras figuras señaladas, como el coronel nicaragüense Anastasio Somoza Debayle y el general Miguel Ydígoras Fuentes, ridiculizaron las denuncias de conspiración, mientras que Panamá destituyó a un agregado mencionado en el comunicado guatemalteco.

records.headline: Dominican claims that neighboring republics have harbored political refugees
records.summary_en: Dominican claims that neighboring republics have harbored political refugees plotting armed invasions were reported as an issue for the upcoming Inter-American conference. Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo charged that remnants of the Caribbean Legion are currently operating in Costa Rica to plot against his government. The conference is slated to consider a supplementary protocol to strengthen the 1928 Convention on Duties and Rights of States in Event of Civil Strife, which required signatory nations to prevent armed expeditions from forming on their soil.
records.summary_es: Reclamos dominicanos que señalan que repúblicas vecinas han albergado a refugiados políticos que conspiran para realizar invasiones armadas figuraban en la agenda de la próxima conferencia interamericana. El generalísimo Rafael L. Trujillo denunció que remanentes de la Legión del Caribe operan actualmente en Costa Rica para conspirar contra su gobierno. La reunión prevé evaluar un protocolo complementario para reforzar la Convención sobre Deberes y Derechos de los Estados en Caso de Guerra Civil de 1928, tratado que obligaba a los Estados signatarios a impedir la formación de expediciones armadas en su suelo.

records.headline: Celebration of the 110th anniversary of Dominican independence
records.summary_en: Celebration of the 110th anniversary of Dominican independence at the Pan American Union was accompanied by an anti-Trujillo picket line outside the building. While Dominican Ambassador Manuel deMoya Alonzo hosted a reception for American diplomats and attaches in the Hall of the Americas, exiled members of three Dominican organizations in New York paraded nearby carrying signs protesting the dictatorship alongside a funeral wreath on a black coffin. Police required the pickets to maintain a distance of 500 feet from the building, prompting them to march along Seventeenth Street in front of the Daughters of the American Revolution Building.
records.summary_es: La conmemoración del 110.º aniversario de la independencia dominicana en la Unión Panamericana estuvo acompañada por un piquete de protesta antitrujillista en el exterior del edificio. Mientras el embajador dominicano Manuel deMoya Alonzo ofrecía una recepción a diplomáticos y agregados americanos en el Salón de las Américas, miembros exiliados de tres organizaciones dominicanas de Nueva York marcharon en las inmediaciones portando carteles contra la dictadura junto a una corona fúnebre colocada sobre un ataúd negro. La policía ordenó a los manifestantes mantenerse a 500 pies del recinto, por lo que desfilaron por la calle Diecisiete frente a la sede de las Hijas de la Revolución Americana.

records.summary_en: The Tribune recounted a travelogue by visiting members of the Pan American Medical Association touring historic and medical sites across Ciudad Trujillo, including the Alcazar de Colon and the Cathedral of Santa Maria la Menor. records.full_text:
Caribbean Cruise --- Part Five

By MRS. L. C. DOWNING

Early the next morning after our visit to Puerto Rico, we anchored in the harbor of Ciudad Trujillo, capital of the Dominican Republic. In 1930, the city had been almost entirely destroyed by a hurricane. To-day, the city has been almost entirely rebuilt thanks to President Rafael Leonidas Trujilloy Molina who has spared no money in building new highways, hospitals, markets and public buildings. As a monument to his endeaors, the capital was named for him. Cuidad is the Spanish for city.

Upon reaching land in the tenders, we were met by guides who took us sight-seeing in their cars. Our first stop was at the ruins of the San Nichols de Bari Hospital, the first hospital built in America in 1503. Governor Ovando had been instructed at that time to "build where he thought most needed, houses to take care of the poor, both Christians and Indians." Before this, a pious Negro woman had been taking care of the sick. From the ruins of the first hospital, we drove to the very latest modern hospital where a meeting was held with physicians of the cruise and the physicians of the Dominican Republic. The place was in a long patio between two parts of the hospital. After the meeting, we went on to the President's palace. On the way, along the banks of the Ozama River, we passed the Tower of Homage, the oldest stone fortress in the Americas; it is now a prison. Farther on, we saw Alcazar de Colon, a castle built in 1512 by Don Diego in honor of his father, Christopher Columbus. Next, we visited the Basilica of Santa Maria la Menor, the oldest cathedral in the world where the remains of Columbus are supposed to be buried. Some of the jewels of Queen Isabella are on display there. By this time we reached the palace.

In a Spanish address, President Trujillo welcomed the members of the Pan-American Medical Association; we received copies of his speech in Spanish and English. After thanking the group for the Diploma of Honor presented to him by the group for his work toward the health of the population, he spoke of the policy of his government, and, I quote: "The health and social welfare policy of the Dominican government has been inspired in the conviction that the fate of American civilization depends largely upon the success of the measures taken in that field. To ward off Communism, to keep our institutions from falling into its clutches, the working classes must feel protected by the government and realize that under a constructive government they will gain greater and more stable advantages than those Communism offers them through its deceiving theories. To render Communism unconvincing, it would be enough to show the worker of the democratic countries the real conditions in the nations behind the Iron Curtain, where the exploitation of the working is even worse than during the Middle Ages when slavery was still a common way of life. But to completely eradicate this doctrine from our free world, it is necessary for the working man to be absolutely sure that he can obtain within the capitalistic system greater advantages than those offered to him in theory by regimes contrary to Christian democracy." He ended his speech saying that the government is "dedicating itself each day with greater vigor to the task of forever banishing from its frontiers these two great enemies of Western civilization: poverty and ignorance." Then, he shook hands with us with a smile and a word for each one. The reception line led to a table where liquid refreshments of all kinds were served. From there, we were escorted to the banquet room where a buffet luncheon, consisting of an abundance of meats, salads, and deserts were waiting. The silverware, linens and dishes were what one would expect in such a magnificent executive mansion.

After enjoying the hospitality of the government of the Dominican Republic, we drove back to the harbor. On the way, we passed the University of St. Thomas Aquinas, the oldest university in this hemisphere and the very beautiful modern Hotel Jaragua. An ideal playground for children is the Ramfis Park on the shores of the Caribbean. The largest lighthouse in the world is being built as a shrine and memorial to Columbus. It will be called Columbus Lighthouse. Soon after boarding our ship, the Nieuw Amsterdam, we sailed away from the oldest city in the new world, the spot where Columbus landed and is buried.

Next week, our cruise will take you to Havana, Cuba.

records.headline: Opening mid-sentence, a news item highlights findings from a survey
records.summary_en: Opening mid-sentence, a news item highlights findings from a survey released by Reinhold P. Wolff, director of the Bureau of Business and Economic Research of the University of Miami. The report indicates that while regional tourism surpassed its pre-war peak, the Caribbean's full tourist potential has hardly been tapped. In 1953, an estimated 880,000 tourists visited the Bahamas, Cuba, Curacao, the Dominican Republic, Haiti, Jamaica, Puerto Rico, and the Virgin Islands, generating $40,000,000 in expenditures exclusive of transportation costs, compared to 203,900 visitors and $20,100,000 in 1937. Linked by Pan American World Airways, the West Indies are described as lying within a few flying hours of an estimated market of some 200 million people in North and Middle America.

records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Madrid reports that Spanish chief of state General Francisco Franco and former Dominican president Rafael Leonidas Trujillo observed military exercises demonstrating how Madrid could be defended if an enemy army attacked the capital. General Trujillo, who was in Spain on a 12-day official visit, watched maneuvers of the Spanish Army alongside Franco at Carabanchel Camp on the outskirts of the capital. The military units participating in the war games were equipped with jeeps, bazookas, Sherman medium tanks, and Patton heavy tanks supplied to Spain by the United States under a bilateral military pact.

Trujillo stated that the treaty affirmed his government's dedication to the Catholic Church as the bulwark of order and Christian civilization.

records.summary_en: Quoting a Vatican City newspaper, the article highlights the Dominican Republic's recognition of the religious and social mission of the Catholic Church, noting government assistance for Church works and the enactment of favorable legislative reforms. Formerly known as Santo Domingo, the Dominican Republic occupies the eastern two-thirds of the island named La Espanola by Columbus, with the remaining third belonging to Haiti. The report notes an almost exclusively Catholic population of around 2,167,000 and observes that Mass was probably first celebrated in the New World on January 6, 1494, in Santo Domingo, which later became the seat of the first metropolitan see and the University of St Thomas Aquinas.

records.summary_en: The Evening Star reviewed the history of Caribbean political conflicts, tracing how Venezuelan exiles and Romulo Betancourt helped form the Caribbean Legion to invade Rafael Trujillo's Dominican Republic. Following the collapse of those invasion attempts, legion remnants aided Jose Figueres in establishing power in Costa Rica during the 1948 revolution. Dictators Trujillo and Anastasio Somoza accused Figueres of harboring communist conspirators and reforming the legion to attack their regimes, charges Figueres dismissed as dictatorial paranoia.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* repasó la historia de los conflictos políticos del Caribe, reseñando cómo los exiliados venezolanos y Rómulo Betancourt colaboraron en la formación de la Legión del Caribe para invadir la República Dominicana de Rafael Trujillo. Tras el fracaso de aquellas intentonas de invasión, los remanentes de la legión ayudaron a José Figueres a afianzarse en el poder en Costa Rica durante la revolución de 1948. Los dictadores Trujillo y Anastasio Somoza acusaron a Figueres de cobijar a conspiradores comunistas y reorganizar la legión para atacar a sus regímenes, señalamientos que Figueres desestimó considerándolos paranoia dictatorial.

When the old military regime was overthrown, its leaders obtained territorial asylum in the Dominican Republic. There, under the tutelage of President Rafael Trujillo Molina, they plotted a counter-revolution. Learning about this, Betancourt and party helped organize an expedi tionary force of asylees from Carib bean totalitarian regimes to invade the Dominican Republic. This force, named the Caribbean Legion, trained in Cuba and failed at two attempts to invade Trujillo's land. It then disintegrated. Costa Rican Adventure Remnants of the legion figured in a revolution that broke out in Costa Rica late in 1948. A conserva tive invalidated the free election of a liberal president. Jose Figueres mobilized a group of young liberals and forced the Conservative-Com munist coalition out, set himself up as provisional president, and even tually turned the government over to the constitutionally elected presi dent. Betancourt is in Costa Rica, with his friend, Figueres. records.summary_en: A regional news report outlines external diplomatic pressures directed against President Jose Figueres of Costa Rica by neighboring Latin American leaders. Among these critics, President Hector B. Trujillo of the Dominican Republic accuses Figueres of being a Communist, while President Anastasio Somoza of Nicaragua blames him for an assassination attempt the preceding April. The article also highlights hostility from Venezuelan President Marcos Perez Jimenez, whose political opponent Romulo Betancourt received asylum in Costa Rica and became an advisor to Figueres.

El artículo destaca igualmente la hostilidad del mandatario venezolano Marcos Pérez Jiménez, cuyo opositor político Rómulo Betancourt halló asilo en Costa Rica y pasó a desempeñarse como asesor de Figueres.

records.headline: A new concordat with the Holy See has abolished the traditional
records.summary_en: A new concordat with the Holy See has abolished the traditional patronage system permitting Latin American heads of state to name bishops in the Dominican Republic, a National Catholic news dispatch datelined Ciudad Trujillo reports. Signed on June 16 and recently published, the treaty is the Vatican's second concordat within a year with a Spanish-speaking nation, following an agreement signed with Spain on August 27, 1953. Under its terms, the Dominican state guarantees full civil recognition to Catholic marriages while invalidating subsequent recourse to civil divorce, respects Church holy days of obligation, and affirms Church rights to operate seminaries and provide spiritual care to the armed forces and welfare institutions.
records.summary_es: Un nuevo concordato con la Santa Sede ha abolido el tradicional sistema de patronato que facultaba a los jefes de Estado latinoamericanos a nombrar obispos en la República Dominicana, según informa un despacho noticioso de National Catholic con fecha de Ciudad Trujillo. Suscrito el 16 de junio y publicado recientemente, el tratado constituye el segundo concordato firmado por el Vaticano con una nación hispanohablante en menos de un año, tras el acuerdo rubricado con España el 27 de agosto de 1953. Conforme a sus disposiciones, el Estado dominicano otorga pleno reconocimiento civil al matrimonio católico invalidando el recurso posterior al divorcio civil, respeta los días de precepto de la Iglesia y ratifica los derechos eclesiásticos para dirigir seminarios y brindar atención espiritual a las fuerzas armadas e instituciones de beneficencia.

records.headline: In a comparative survey assessing democratic development across
records.summary_en: In a comparative survey assessing democratic development across the Americas, the Dominican Republic receives an evaluation of two points under the rule of Rafael Leonidas Trujillo. The feature notes that while friends style Trujillo a savior, enemies condemn him as the worst dictator since Nero, adding that unlike other authoritarian rulers he does not bother maintaining the trappings of democracy. The analysis further contends that private enterprise does not genuinely exist in the Dominican Republic because Trujillo and his family own so much of the nation's wealth.
records.summary_es: En un estudio comparativo que evalúa el desarrollo democrático en las Américas, la República Dominicana recibe una calificación de dos puntos bajo el régimen de Rafael Leonidas Trujillo. La reseña señala que, mientras sus allegados apodan a Trujillo como un salvador, sus detractores lo condenan como el peor dictador desde Nerón, añadiendo que a diferencia de otros gobernantes autoritarios no se molesta en mantener las apariencias de la democracia. El análisis sostiene además que la libre empresa no existe verdaderamente en la República Dominicana debido a que Trujillo y su familia acaparan gran parte de la riqueza nacional.

records.summary_en: Opening mid-report, a dispatch indicates that an examiner has recommended approving San Juan, Puerto Rico, as an intermediate stop and permitting Iberia to inaugurate two flight routes originating from the city. Gen. Trujillo Is Here on Short Visit

Visiting Washington unofficially is the former president of the Dominican Republic, Gen. Rafael L. Trujillo, now Dominican delegate to the United Nations.

The Generalissimo arrived in the Capital Wednesday, en route to his homeland from Europe. After spending several days here at the Mayflower, he expects to leave for New York tomorrow.

He was accompanied by his son, Gen. Rafael Trujillo, jr., who is staying with his family at the Dominican Embassy.

The visiting official was the guest of honor yesterday at a stag luncheon given by Assistant Secretary of State Henry F. Holland at Blair House.

Guests included the Dominican Ambassador, Senor de Moya; the Minister, Dr. Horacio Vicioso; Plinio B. Pina Chevalier, Minister and Commercial Counselor of the Embassy, and Jose R. Rodriguez, Dominican Ambassador to the Organization of American States.

Members of the visitor's party included Gen. Trujillo, jr., and Gen. Anselmo Paulino, minister without portfolio.

Among others were Gen. Nathan F. Twining, Chief of Staff of the Air Force; Maj. Gen. Robert Webster, chairman of the United States delegation to the Inter-American Defense Board; Homer Cummings, Dr. William Morgan, Charles Burrows, director of the State Department's Office of Middle American Affairs, and William B. Connett, officer in charge of Dominican affairs.

records.headline: Following several days in Miami after arriving from Washington
records.summary_en: Following several days in Miami after arriving from Washington, Generalissimo Rafael Leonidas Trujillo Molina is scheduled to depart today for the Dominican Republic aboard the yacht Moineau. The newspaper reports that Trujillo had recently concluded an extended vacation in Spain as the special guest of Generalissimo Francisco Franco, and was subsequently feted by numerous hosts in the United States capital. The article notes that Trujillo is currently serving as the Dominican foreign minister and his nation's representative to the United Nations General Assembly.

El periódico informa que Trujillo concluyó recientemente unas prolongadas vacaciones en España como invitado especial del generalísimo Francisco Franco, siendo posteriormente homenajeado por numerosos anfitriones en la capital de Estados Unidos. La nota destaca que Trujillo se desempeña en la actualidad como ministro de Relaciones Exteriores dominicano y representante de su país ante la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas.

Tourist Cards Debated

CIUDAD TRUJILLO, Dominican Republic, Aug. 18 (AP).—The Dominican Senate began debate yesterday on a bill to permit tourists to visit the Dominican Republic on a simple tourist card which could be issued by air or steamship lines. Backed by President Hector Trujillo, the bill would do away with passports and visas.

records.headline: After nine years of work, a 200-foot-high marble and stone structure
records.summary_en: After nine years of work, a 200-foot-high marble and stone structure has been completed on a 1,200-foot promontory overlooking Santiago, described as the tallest man-made monument in the Western Hemisphere south of the United States. Funded by public contributions to honor the achievements for peace and progress of former four-term president Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo, the monument is scheduled for dedication the following year during the 25th anniversary of the "Era of Trujillo." The five-story base of Ionian style supports a marble tower rising roughly 125 feet above it, and visitors will take an elevator rising 180 feet to a veranda providing views of the 10,890-foot Trujillo Peak, the highest mountain in the Antilles.
records.summary_es: Tras nueve años de labores, una estructura de mármol y piedra de 200 pies de altura ha quedado concluida sobre una elevación de 1,200 pies con vista a Santiago, siendo descrita como el monumento artificial más alto del hemisferio occidental al sur de Estados Unidos. Financiado mediante suscripciones del pueblo dominicano para honrar los logros de paz y progreso del expresidente de cuatro mandatos, el generalísimo Rafael L. Trujillo, el monumento será inaugurado al año siguiente durante el 25 aniversario de la "Era de Trujillo". La base de cinco pisos y estilo jónico sustenta una torre de mármol de unos 125 pies de altura sobre ella, y los visitantes utilizarán un ascensor que sube 180 pies hasta una terraza con vistas al pico Trujillo, de 10,890 pies, la montaña más alta de las Antillas.

records.headline: A travel advertisement in the Evening Star urges vacationers
records.summary_en: A travel advertisement in the Evening Star urges vacationers to visit the Dominican Republic, praising the spotless cleanliness of its cities, the friendliness of its people, and its colorful carnival of tropical flowers and birds. The advertisement highlights the affordability of the country's luxury hotels and describes the nation as a wonderland accessible by airliner or cruise ship. Prospective travelers are invited to consult local travel agents or write to the Director of Tourism in Ciudad Trujillo and the Dominican Republic Tourist Office in New York.
records.summary_es: Un anuncio de viajes en el Evening Star exhorta a los turistas a visitar la República Dominicana, elogiando la impecable limpieza de sus ciudades, la cordialidad de sus habitantes y su vistoso espectáculo de flores y aves tropicales. La publicidad destaca las accesibles tarifas de los hoteles de lujo del país y presenta a la nación como un paraíso accesible mediante aviones de pasajeros o barcos de crucero. Se sugiere a los potenciales visitantes consultar a sus agencias de viajes o escribir a la Dirección de Turismo en Ciudad Trujillo y a la Oficina de Turismo de la República Dominicana en Nueva York.

records.headline: In her syndicated column, Lillian Cox Athey highlights mahogany
records.summary_en: In her syndicated column, Lillian Cox Athey highlights mahogany as both an exceptionally useful and beautiful wood prized in housing, furniture, and shipbuilding since the days of Columbus. The people of Santo Domingo appreciate the importance of the mahogany tree to their country and have adopted its flower as their national floral emblem. The municipal government of Ciudad Trujillo has planted mahogany trees for ornamental shade along city streets, where residents enjoy the fragrance of its dainty greenish-white blossoms from April to June. The trees can reach 60 feet in height, require 30 years of growth before cutting, and yield lumber sold in lengths running from 4 to 16 feet.
records.summary_es: En su columna sindicada, Lillian Cox Athey destaca la caoba como una madera sumamente útil y hermosa, apreciada para la construcción de viviendas, muebles y buques desde los tiempos de Colón. El pueblo de Santo Domingo valora la trascendencia del árbol de caoba para su país y ha adoptado su flor como emblema floral nacional. El gobierno municipal de Ciudad Trujillo ha plantado árboles de caoba para brindar sombra ornamental en sus calles, donde los habitantes disfrutan de la fragancia de sus delicadas flores verde-blanquecinas de abril a junio. Los árboles pueden alcanzar 60 pies de altura, requieren 30 años de crecimiento antes de la tala y producen madera vendida en longitudes que van de 4 a 16 pies.

records.headline: Opening mid-article, the report notes that mahogany lumber brings
records.summary_en: Opening mid-article, the report notes that mahogany lumber brings up to $250 per thousand board feet. Mahogany grows scattered among other hardwoods across nearly all parts of the Dominican Republic, with principal stands situated in Barahona and Azua in the south, Seibo in the east, and a few in Monte Cristi in the northwest. While an American authority once estimated that 4,000,000 board feet could be cut annually over 20 years, Dominican officials place sustainable yields at 500,000 board feet based on the preceding 15 years. To preserve the resource for future centuries, Dominican law prohibits cutting any mahogany tree unless 20 replacement trees are planted for each one felled.

Para preservar el recurso para los siglos venideros, la ley dominicana prohíbe cortar cualquier árbol de caoba a menos que se planten 20 árboles de reposición por cada uno que se tale.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Rafael Trujillo proposed that anti-Communist nations establish their own "United Nations for Peace" headquartered in Washington to combat Communist aggression. Simultaneously, Manuel de Moya announced his resignation as Dominican Ambassador to the United States in order to accept a cabinet post in Ciudad Trujillo.

Al mismo tiempo, Manuel de Moya anunció su renuncia como embajador dominicano en Estados Unidos para aceptar un cargo de gabinete en Ciudad Trujillo.

records.headline: Continuing an interview, pitcher Ruben Gomez recalls buying
records.summary_en: Continuing an interview, pitcher Ruben Gomez recalls buying out his contract from Kansas City for $3,000 to play baseball in the Dominican Republic. He explains that he was paid $2,000 a month in the republic, which led him to demand comparable pay and a bonus when Brooklyn scout Al Campanis approached him. Gomez subsequently signed with Tom Sheehan of the New York Giants for big-league play and a $6,000 bonus. Managed by Leo Durocher, Gomez became the club's leading winner and improved upon his 1953 record to finish the 1954 season with a 17-9 mark.
records.summary_es: Al continuar una entrevista, el lanzador Rubén Gómez recuerda haber comprado su contrato a Kansas City por $3,000 para jugar béisbol en la República Dominicana. Explica que en la república le pagaban $2,000 al mes, por lo que exigió una remuneración semejante y una bonificación cuando el cazatalentos de Brooklyn Al Campanis habló con él. Gómez firmó más tarde con Tom Sheehan de los Gigantes de Nueva York para jugar directamente en las Grandes Ligas con una bonificación de $6,000. Bajo la dirección de Leo Durocher, Gómez se consagró como el lanzador más ganador del equipo y superó su rendimiento de 1953 al culminar la temporada de 1954 con una marca de 17-9.

records.headline: A converted Canadian frigate used as a private yacht by the dictator of the Dominican Republic arrived
records.summary_en: A converted Canadian frigate used as a private yacht by the dictator of the Dominican Republic arrived in Washington for an indefinite stay, docking at Municipal Pier 5 at 8:30 a.m. with an 80-man crew under Captain Luis A. Facundo. The vessel was met by Commander Luis H. Lajara, naval attaché at the Dominican embassy, who explained that the ship was brought to port because General Rafael Trujillo is in New York and may decide to return home aboard her. Lajara stated the visit might last three days or a week or more. While named Presidente Trujillo after the republic's current president, Hector B. Trujillo, the vessel serves as the personal ship of his brother and predecessor, Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo, who is described as the actual head of the country.
records.summary_es: Una fragata canadiense transformada y empleada como yate privado por el dictador de la República Dominicana atracó en Washington para una estancia indefinida, amarrando en el muelle municipal 5 a las 8:30 a.m. con una tripulación de 80 hombres al mando del capitán Luis A. Facundo. La nave fue recibida por el comandante Luis H. Lajara, agregado naval de la embajada dominicana, quien explicó que el barco fue trasladado a dicho puerto porque el general Rafael Trujillo se encuentra en Nueva York y podría resolver regresar a su país a bordo de él. records.summary_en: Dominican Ambassador Manuel de Moya, whose resignation takes effect at the end of November, clarifies rumors regarding Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo's impending visits to Washington. De Moya states that the Generalissimo is too busy to serve as ambassador himself, but intends to visit frequently because he loves the city. The ambassador explains that a newly purchased residence was acquired to host important guests, potentially including Trujillo and his son, rather than displacing embassy activities from Edgevale Terrace. Later in the column, Generalissimo Trujillo and his wife are reported attending a diplomatic gathering in Washington alongside Ambassador de Moya.

El diplomático explica que la nueva residencia fue adquirida para alojar a huéspedes distinguidos, entre ellos posiblemente Trujillo y su hijo, y no para sustituir la sede de la embajada en Edgevale Terrace. Más adelante en la columna, se informa que el generalísimo Trujillo y su esposa asistieron a una recepción diplomática en Washington en compañía del embajador de Moya.
