records.full_text:
Exclusively Yours—By Betty Beale Generalissimo Trujillo Entertains Fifty at Luncheon On His 300-Foot Yacht; Plans Big Party in January

Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, who admits he's a dictator—a benevolent dictator, that is—dispensed benevolent hospitality yesterday on his luxurious yacht that left his Washington guests wide-eyed.

Two of my columnist colleagues leaned back on a divan on the aft-erdeck. Overhead was a deep blue canvas to keep off the hot sun, underfoot was a deep pile specially designed carpet. Balmy river breezes swept through the glistening white 300-foot yacht and caressed their brows; tall drinks were carried to them from the super special mahogany bar.

"You two never had it so good," someone quipped. "No, and we're getting paid for it," they grinned back, looking at it from the esthetic side as usual.

The luncheon aboard the Canadian-built frigate, El Presidente Trujillo, drew about 50 guests down to Pier 5, Maine avenue, at the early hour of 11 a.m. Nobody objected though. Sitting on a yacht that sports a crew of 85 is so much better than sitting at a typewriter.

It was mostly newsmen and women who walked up the gangplank and were ushered by the Generalissimo's aides into the richly paneled dining lounge where he and Ambassador Manuel de Moya were receiving. The latter did the interpreting for his boss, who doesn't speak English as well as his wife, Mme. Trujillo arrived later and mingled with the guests on the deck.

They say she's not overly fond of the yacht—gets a bit of mal de mer on it. Their 15-year-old daughter Angelita and 11-year-old son Ramades were also on board. And there was a huge photograph of their 25-year-old son who is already chief of staff of the air corps.

Non-press people invited included General Trujillo's old friend, former Ambassador Joe Davies and his daughter, Rachel Fitch; Dr. William Morgan, for whom the hospital in Ciudad Trujillo is named, and his wife Elizabeth; and from the State Department—Chief of Protocol Jack Simmons, Director of the Middle American Division and Mrs. Robert Newbegin, his deputy, Jack Neal, and his wife, and Charles Whittaker, who has to do with Dominican affairs.

Gen. and Mrs. Wade Hampton Haislip, Mr. and Mrs. Samuel H. Kauffmann, Dennie Rumbough, the Robert LeBarons and the Bill Hapleys were also in the group that helped themselves to a buffet luncheon on the upper deck. Lamb chops, turkey, ham, vegetable salad, rice and quantities of other dishes ornamented the big table.

Yours truly wandered below to see what was cooking and found the Generalissimo and the Ambassador having a bite alone in the paneled dining lounge. They drew up another chair and next thing you knew there was merengue music emanating from the victrola and yours truly was twirling first with the Ambassador and then with Gen. Trujillo. Both are expert hoofers, even on a plush carpet. And who would have thought yesterday morning that by mid-day I'd be cutting a rug with a dictator?

Who would be the next ambassador here? It might be Joaquim Salazar, now consul general in New York and former Ambassador to the U. N. At least he would like to have the post, indicated his boss.

When he returns, Trujillo will stay at the embassy on Edgevale terrace, but his wife doesn't like it, he said; she wants to be closer to town. On January 27, he and Ambassador de Moya will have a huge, gay party at the Embassy. "You mean Manuel is not leaving the end of November after all but will still be here in January?" "Yes." . . . Believe me, dictators are as unpredictable as women are supposed to be.

Intermittent press conferences held before lunch was served informed us that a world's fair of free nations will open in Ciudad Trujillo on its namesake's birthday, October 24, 1955; that invitations to participate went out to envoys of other nations here this week; that the Dominican Republic owes nary a cent to any country in the world; that the Generalissimo's confidential files on communism in Latin America have been offered to the House Investigating Committee, and so forth.

There's no question about it. The boss of the little Caribbean republic is setting about to remove the American stigma on dictators. Another party on that yacht would probably do it.

records.headline: A Washington diplomatic report explains that a reception at the Dominican Embassy originally
records.summary_en: A Washington diplomatic report explains that a reception at the Dominican Embassy originally scheduled for the 27th was moved to the 29th to avoid conflicting with a major function given by the Haitian ambassador for the President of Haiti and Mme. Magloire. Because relations between Haiti and the Dominican Republic have been strained, hosting events on the same day would have appeared as a deliberate slight, though the Dominicans sent invitations first without knowledge of the Haitian plans. The rescheduled reception on the 29th will serve as the farewell appearance for Dominican Ambassador Manuel de Moya, who departs Washington three days later to take up his new post as secretary of state without portfolio. The report notes that Generalissimo Trujillo is not expected to attend, and his successor as ambassador has not yet been announced.
records.summary_es: Una crónica diplomática desde Washington explica que la recepción de la embajada dominicana fijada en principio para el día 27 se trasladó al 29 para no coincidir con un gran agasajo ofrecido por el embajador haitiano en honor del presidente de Haití y la señora de Magloire. Dado que las relaciones entre Haití y la República Dominicana han sido tirantes, celebrar actos el mismo día habría parecido un desaire deliberado, pese a que la delegación dominicana remitió sus invitaciones con anterioridad sin tener noticia del festejo haitiano. La velada reprogramada para el 29 marcará la despedida del embajador dominicano Manuel de Moya, quien saldrá de Washington tres días después para asumir su nuevo cargo de secretario de Estado sin cartera. El informe añade que no se espera la asistencia del generalísimo Trujillo y que todavía no se ha dado a conocer a su sucesor en la embajada.

records.headline: Vice President and Mrs. Nixon are scheduled to depart on February 6
records.summary_en: Vice President and Mrs. Nixon are scheduled to depart on February 6 for a four-week goodwill tour that includes stops in Central America, Cuba, Haiti, Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, and the Dominican Republic. In light of the itinerary, Generalissimo Trujillo is expected to postpone his planned visit to Washington until after he hosts the United States Vice President. The tour was discussed following an official White House state dinner given in the Nixons' honor by President and Mrs. Eisenhower.
records.summary_es: El vicepresidente y la señora de Nixon tienen previsto partir el 6 de febrero en una gira de cuatro semanas que contempla escalas en Centroamérica, Cuba, Haití, Puerto Rico, las Islas Vírgenes y la República Dominicana. A la luz de este itinerario, se espera que el generalísimo Trujillo posponga su proyectada visita a Washington hasta después de haber recibido al vicepresidente de los Estados Unidos. La gira se dio a conocer tras una cena de gala oficial ofrecida en honor de los Nixon en la Casa Blanca por el presidente y la señora de Eisenhower.

records.headline: Haiti President
records.summary_en: This is the continuation of the published itinerary of Haitian President Paul E. Magloire's North American tour: after official activity in Washington from January 26 to 28, a visit to the United States Military Academy at West Point and five days in New York, the party travels to Chicago, Boston and Ottawa, Canada. The itinerary lists receptions, luncheons and visits day by day, and ends with the party leaving Canada on February 14 for Kingston, Jamaica, then continuing by boat to Ciudad Trujillo in the Dominican Republic and on to Port-au-Prince. The members of the presidential party, Haitian and American, are named in full, including Secretary of State Mauclair Zephirin, Ambassador Jacques Leger and the United States ambassador to Haiti, Roy Tasco Davis.

Se nombran en su totalidad los miembros de la comitiva presidencial, haitianos y estadounidenses, entre ellos el secretario de Estado Mauclair Zephirin, el embajador Jacques Leger y el embajador de los Estados Unidos en Haití, Roy Tasco Davis.

Medics Say Smoking Bad For Heart;Whiskey No Antidote BY EDWIN DIAMOND CHICAGO—(I N S)—The American Medical Association declared on Thursday “there seems to be direct evidence” that smoking cigarettes causes heart damage. And the long-held notion that drinking whiskey “protects” the heart against the effects of ciga rettes was rejected as “purely an il lusion.” Two articles and an editorial were devoted to the effects of smoking and drinking in the current Journal of the AMA. Timothy V. Hartnett, chairman of the Tobacco Industry Research Committee, commented: “From time to time, reports can be expected that may seem either favorable or unfavorable to the use of tobacco. It is impossible to at tempt to evaluate each specific re port as it appears in the scientific or lay press. The Tobacco Industry Research Committee is convinced the vast majority of the American public agree that all questions of tobacco in relation to human health need much more thorough and com plete investigation than has been made up to now.”

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that Dominican playboy
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that Dominican playboy diplomat Rubirosa initiated divorce proceedings against dime-store heiress Barbara Hutton on grounds of incompatibility. Rubirosa's attorney, Eneas Savinon, published legal notice in the newspaper El Caribe requiring Hutton to advise the court of her current address, which Dominican law mandates when the person sued resides abroad. Savinon stated that if no communication is received from her, he will notify the district attorney on February 21 ahead of a March court hearing. Hutton and Rubirosa were married in New York on December 30, 1953, and separated in March following a Florida honeymoon.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Associated Press fechado en Ciudad Trujillo informa que el diplomático y playboy dominicano Rubirosa inició trámites de divorcio contra la heredera de tiendas por departamentos Barbara Hutton por motivos de incompatibilidad. El abogado de Rubirosa, Eneas Savinon, publicó una notificación legal en el periódico El Caribe requiriendo a Hutton comunicar su domicilio actual al tribunal, requisito obligatorio según la legislación dominicana cuando el demandado reside en el exterior. Savinon indicó que si no recibe respuesta de ella, notificará al fiscal de distrito el 21 de febrero con miras a una vista judicial en marzo. Hutton y Rubirosa contrajeron matrimonio en Nueva York el 30 de diciembre de 1953 y se separaron en marzo tras una luna de miel en Florida.

records.headline: Dominican diplomat Porfirio Rubirosa requested a divorce from dime
records.summary_en: Dominican diplomat Porfirio Rubirosa requested a divorce from dime store heiress Barbara Hutton through his attorney before a civil court judge in Ciudad Trujillo, asserting that their characters were incompatible. Rubirosa did not appear at the brief hearing because he was in Miami preparing for a sports car race and was represented by Eneas Savinon, while Hutton was neither present nor represented. Judge Anibal Sosa Ortiz took under advisement Savinon's brief and the testimony of two witnesses, with Dominican law requiring divorce proceedings to take place behind closed doors.
records.summary_es: El diplomático dominicano Porfirio Rubirosa solicitó el divorcio de la heredera Barbara Hutton a través de su abogado ante un juez civil en Ciudad Trujillo, manifestando que sus caracteres eran incompatibles. Rubirosa no compareció a la breve audiencia debido a que se encontraba en Miami preparándose para una carrera de coches deportivos y estuvo representado por Eneas Savinon, mientras que Hutton no estuvo presente ni representada. El juez Aníbal Sosa Ortiz dejó en estudio el escrito de Savinon y la declaración de dos testigos, disponiendo la legislación dominicana que los procesos de divorcio se efectúen a puerta cerrada.

records.headline: Ciudad Trujillo is preparing for mass tourism through significant
records.summary_en: Ciudad Trujillo is preparing for mass tourism through significant hotel expansion projects. A 100-room annex is being added to the Jaragua Hotel, while the Dominican government is constructing a 150-room hotel scheduled to open November 3. Another fully air-conditioned $2.5 million hotel featuring a swimming pool, nightclub, and 18-hole golf course will open December 20 for the inauguration of the Dominican Republic's International Fair. In addition, travel agents are offering a four-day tour of Haiti and the Dominican Republic for $66 plus airfare, providing two days and nights in each country.
records.summary_es: Ciudad Trujillo se prepara para recibir turismo masivo mediante importantes proyectos de expansión hotelera. Se construye un anexo de 100 habitaciones en el Hotel Jaragua, mientras que el gobierno dominicano edifica un hotel de 150 habitaciones cuya apertura está prevista para el 3 de noviembre. Otro hotel de 2,5 millones de dólares, completamente climatizado y dotado de piscina, club nocturno y campo de golf de 18 hoyos, se inaugurará el 20 de diciembre con motivo de la apertura de la Feria Internacional de la República Dominicana. Asimismo, las agencias de viajes ofrecen una excursión de cuatro días por Haití y la República Dominicana por 66 dólares más pasaje aéreo, que incluye dos días y dos noches en cada país.

records.headline: A photograph caption published in connection with an upcoming
records.summary_en: A photograph caption published in connection with an upcoming Washington embassy tour features Señora Lourdes de Salazar of the Dominican Republic posing with her four-year-old daughter, Bernadette. The mother and daughter are pictured beneath a portrait of her uncle, Generalissimo Trujillo, which visitors will view during the tour. The goodwill event is sponsored by the Goodwill Guild to benefit the rehabilitation program of Davis Memorial Goodwill Industries.

Madre e hija aparecen retratadas bajo un cuadro de su tío, el generalísimo Trujillo, que los asistentes podrán observar durante el recorrido. La actividad benéfica está patrocinada por el Goodwill Guild en beneficio del programa de rehabilitación de Davis Memorial Goodwill Industries.

records.headline: Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo is restoring the ruins of the historic
records.summary_en: Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo is restoring the ruins of the historic Columbus Palace in Ciudad Trujillo, from which explorers including Balboa and Ponce de León sailed forth to discover the Pacific, Florida, and other lands. The refurbished castle will be dedicated as an international museum of Columbiana when the Dominican Fair for Peace and Progress opens in December, 1958. Twenty-eight free world nations are scheduled to participate in the ceremonies.

El castillo acondicionado se consagrará como museo internacional de objetos colombinos cuando se inaugure la Feria Dominicana por la Paz y el Progreso en diciembre de 1958. Veintiocho naciones del mundo libre tienen programado participar en las ceremonias.

records.headline: Fifty-nine naval reserve seamen and officers from the Washington area
records.summary_en: Fifty-nine naval reserve seamen and officers from the Washington area will depart on a two-week training cruise aboard the destroyer USS Robert F. Keller. Leaving from the Naval Gun Factory, the vessel will sail to Ciudad Trujillo, capital of the Dominican Republic, where it will dock during Armed Forces weekend before returning to Washington the following Friday. Under the command of Lieutenant Commander L. E. Voorhees, the trip marks the ship's first cruise since undergoing extensive repairs in Baltimore.
records.summary_es: Cincuenta y nueve marineros y oficiales de la reserva naval del área de Washington partirán en un crucero de adiestramiento de dos semanas a bordo del destructor USS Robert F. Keller. Tras zarpar de la Fábrica de Cañones Navales, el buque navegará hacia Ciudad Trujillo, capital de la República Dominicana, donde atracará durante el fin de semana de las Fuerzas Armadas antes de regresar a Washington el viernes siguiente. Bajo el mando del teniente comandante L. E. Voorhees, la travesía representa el primer viaje del barco desde que se le realizaron extensas reparaciones en Baltimore.

records.headline: The National Safety Council has cited Caribair for a perfect
records.summary_en: The National Safety Council has cited Caribair for a perfect safety record during 1954, marking the sixth consecutive year the carrier has received the safety award. The airline has operated 66,992,000 passenger miles without mishap across its network, which links St. Thomas, St. Croix, Ciudad Trujillo in the Dominican Republic, and San Juan, Ponce, and Mayagüez in Puerto Rico. The article attributes this success to thorough daily maintenance and the competence of the company's personnel.

La aerolínea ha operado 66.992.000 millas de pasajeros sin accidente alguno a través de su red de rutas, que enlaza Santo Tomás, Saint Croix, Ciudad Trujillo en la República Dominicana, y San Juan, Ponce y Mayagüez en Puerto Rico. El artículo atribuye este logro al exhaustivo mantenimiento diario y a la competencia del personal de la compañía.

records.headline: A report on a five-day Caribbean institute highlights regional
records.summary_en: A report on a five-day Caribbean institute highlights regional cooperative progress, noting 25,000 credit union members in the Dominican Republic alongside cooperatives in Honduras, Costa Rica, Jamaica, Mexico, Dominica, and Puerto Rico. Participants affirmed that mutual aid and cooperation offer the primary solution to poverty across the Caribbean area. The gathering concluded that developing trained leadership through specialized centers is the essential first step to overcome illiteracy and foster community confidence.
records.summary_es: Un informe sobre un instituto caribeño de cinco días resalta los progresos de las cooperativas en la región, señalando la existencia de 25.000 miembros de cooperativas de crédito en la República Dominicana junto a cooperativas en Honduras, Costa Rica, Jamaica, México, Dominica y Puerto Rico. Los participantes coincidieron en que la ayuda mutua y la cooperación constituyen la solución primordial frente a la pobreza en el Caribe. El encuentro concluyó que la formación de líderes capacitados mediante centros especializados representa el primer paso indispensable para superar el analfabetismo y consolidar la confianza comunitaria.

records.headline: A travel dispatch reports on tourist infrastructure and historic
records.summary_en: A travel dispatch reports on tourist infrastructure and historic landmarks in the Dominican Republic, where a coastal highway is under construction connecting Ciudad Trujillo with the beach resort of Boca Chica and the Hotel Hamaca. Within the capital, sightseers can visit the site of Christopher Columbus's mooring tree and inspect the ruins of the Alcázar de Colón, built by Diego Columbus and slated for accurate restoration and furnishings. The account also notes the carvings and Columbus Cross inside the Basilica of Santa María la Menor, as well as early work across the Ozama River on the Columbus Memorial Lighthouse designed to house Columbus's tomb.
records.summary_es: Una crónica de viajes informa sobre la infraestructura turística y los monumentos históricos de la República Dominicana, donde se construye una carretera costera que conecta Ciudad Trujillo con el balneario de Boca Chica y el Hotel Hamaca. En la capital, los turistas pueden visitar el sitio del árbol de amarre de Cristóbal Colón e inspeccionar las ruinas del Alcázar de Colón, edificado por Diego Colón y proyectado para una fiel restauración y amueblamiento. La reseña destaca igualmente los tallados y la Cruz de Colón en la Basílica de Santa María la Menor, así como los primeros trabajos al otro lado del río Ozama en el Faro a Colón, concebido para albergar la tumba de Colón.

records.headline: The dean of women and piano teacher Miss Anne Gamble, both of Fisk University
records.summary_en: The dean of women and piano teacher Miss Anne Gamble, both of Fisk University in Nashville, Tennessee, were houseguests of Dr. K. L. Pharr during the week following an extended Caribbean tour. Their travels took them to Port-au-Prince, Haiti; Kingston, Jamaica; San Juan, Puerto Rico; and Ciudad Trujillo in the Dominican Republic. During the tour, Gamble, described as an accomplished pianist, gave a command performance for Haitian President Paul Magloire and also played for Jamaican Prime Minister Norman Manley.

Durante la gira, Gamble, calificada como una consumada pianista, ofreció una función por invitación especial para el presidente haitiano Paul Magloire y también tocó para el primer ministro jamaicano Norman Manley.

records.summary_en: A Bethesda naval reception hosted by Vice Admiral and Mrs. Matthias B. Gardner honored Dominican Admiral Richardson during his nationwide inspection tour of United States naval installations. Lieutenant August Schirmer of the Navy's Pan American Affairs Division flew to Ciudad Trujillo to escort Admiral Richardson to Washington, where he was welcomed at the airport by Dominican Ambassador Dr. Joaquin E. Salazar and Naval Attache Commander Luis Lajara Burgos. records.full_text:
Island Mountains Knock Power Out Of Katie's Wind

MIAMI, Fla. (AP)—Hurricane Katie beat a path across the Dominican Republic today and had much of the wind knocked of her by the towering mountains of the tropical island of Hispaniola.

The Dominican Republic shares the island with Haiti. Both countries are rugged and the interior is sparsely populated.

Katie slammed into the south shore of the island last night with 115-mile winds, but her encounter with the mountains distorted the storm and weakened her winds to about 40 or 50 miles an hour. She was expected to regain hurricane force after reaching the open sea during the afternoon.

Her northeastward course pointed her toward the open Atlantic and barring some unexpected development the 12th tropical storm of the year was not expected to threaten the U.S. mainland.

The storm's center at noon was near latitude 19.7 north, longitude 70.3 west, or near the town of Puerto Plata in the Dominican Republic. It was moving northeastward at about 14 miles an hour.

records.headline: Preparations for the agricultural exhibition at the International Fair
records.summary_en: Preparations for the agricultural exhibition at the International Fair for Peace and Progress are detailed in a Florida report, noting that the fair will run from December 20 through February, 1956, in Ciudad Trujillo, capital of the Dominican Republic. Entries from 18 cattle associations across five countries have already been registered, with beef and dairy cattle, sheep, horses, swine, goats, and poultry set to be exhibited from January 5 to 10, 1956. American university professors will judge the competitions, which will culminate in an auction allowing breeders to sell their stock. The presentation represents the first major livestock show staged by the country since building up its own cattle industry, with entry arrangements coordinated through Dominican Consul Dr. Miguel A. Herrera in Miami under an eight dollar registration fee.
records.summary_es: Los preparativos para la exhibición agropecuaria en la Feria Internacional por la Paz y el Progreso se detallan en un informe de Florida, que señala que la feria se extenderá desde el 20 de diciembre hasta febrero de 1956 en Ciudad Trujillo, capital de la República Dominicana. Ya se han registrado inscripciones de 18 asociaciones ganaderas de cinco países, y se exhibirán ejemplares de ganado vacuno de carne y leche, ovejas, caballos, cerdos, cabras y aves de corral del 5 al 10 de enero de 1956. Profesores universitarios estadounidenses juzgarán las competencias, que culminarán con una subasta que permitirá a los criadores vender sus animales. La presentación constituye la primera gran exposición ganadera organizada por el país desde que desarrolló su propia y próspera industria pecuaria, con gestiones de inscripción coordinadas a través del cónsul dominicano Dr. Miguel A. Herrera en Miami bajo una tarifa de registro de ocho dólares.

European artisans supplied the marble statues and furnishings for the Santo Domingo Cathedral, a structure commenced in 1514 and completed in 1540.

records.headline: A travel feature examines hotel and recreational expansions
records.summary_en: A travel feature examines hotel and recreational expansions in Ciudad Trujillo preparing for the international exposition, highlighting the newly constructed 310-room El Embajador hotel perched on a knoll overlooking the fairgrounds and the Caribbean Sea. New York's Ambassador Hotel chain will manage the new property and has recently taken over operation of the Hotel Jaragua, which added a new wing to accommodate visitors after a decade of luxury service. The capital forms the centerpiece of the island's elite dining, entertainment, and social activities, offering access to a new $3.5 million sports stadium where baseball interest runs high. The Milwaukee Braves are scheduled to hold spring training at the venue, while the nearby Santo Domingo Country Club combines social life with golf and other sports.

La cadena Ambassador Hotel de Nueva York administrará la nueva propiedad y recientemente asumió la gestión del Hotel Jaragua, que construyó una nueva ala para albergar visitantes tras una década de servicio de lujo. La capital constituye el núcleo de la vida social, gastronómica y de entretenimiento de la élite de la isla, y ofrece acceso a un nuevo estadio deportivo de $3.5 millones donde el entusiasmo por el béisbol es notable. Los Bravos de Milwaukee tienen programado realizar sus entrenamientos de primavera en dicho recinto, mientras que el cercano Santo Domingo Country Club combina la vida social con el deporte.

records.headline: Highway construction and mountain tourism in the Dominican interior
records.summary_en: Highway construction and mountain tourism in the Dominican interior are surveyed by a travel correspondent, beginning with an evening terrace where society gatherings from both the capital and Santiago congregate for music and dancing. Motorists currently undertake a three-hour drive between the two cities over rough surfaces, but heavy earthmoving equipment is actively leveling and straightening the road to reduce travel distance by virtually a third. Inland travelers also benefit from highway improvements leading to the government-built New Swiss Hotel at Constanza's 4,800-foot elevation, which has cut the former road journey from the capital by approximately half despite brief interruptions caused by summer rainstorms.
records.summary_es: Un corresponsal de viajes examina las obras viales y el turismo de montaña en el interior dominicano, comenzando en una terraza nocturna donde concurren círculos sociales de la capital y de Santiago para veladas de música y baile. Los automovilistas realizan actualmente un trayecto de tres horas entre ambas ciudades sobre terreno irregular, pero maquinaria pesada de movimiento de tierras se encuentra nivelando y rectificando la ruta para acortar el kilometraje en prácticamente un tercio. Los viajeros hacia el interior también se benefician de las mejoras viales hacia el New Swiss Hotel, edificado por el gobierno en Constanza a 4,800 pies de altitud, que ha reducido el antiguo viaje por carretera desde la capital a cerca de la mitad, a pesar de breves interrupciones provocadas por lluvias de verano.

records.headline: An advertisement placed by the Dominican Republic Tourist Office invites
records.summary_en: An advertisement placed by the Dominican Republic Tourist Office invites travelers to visit the international exposition in Ciudad Trujillo running through spring, 1956. The notice, titled in Spanish as the Fair of Peace and Fraternity of the Free World, highlights extensive exhibits gathered from across the globe. records.headline: Reporting from Ciudad Trujillo, the National Negro Publishers Association highlights
records.summary_en: Reporting from Ciudad Trujillo, the National Negro Publishers Association highlights 24-year-old infielder Charley Neal, who is playing winter baseball with the local Escondido club and aiming for the regular second base position with the Brooklyn Dodgers next season. Neal's standing will be decided during spring camp at Vero Beach, Florida, where he faces competition from Jim Gilliam and Don Zimmer. Originally from Longview, Texas, Neal has progressed through Dodger farm teams in Hornell, Lancaster, Elmira, Newport News, and St. Paul, earning high praise from Brooklyn farm managers while rival organizations declined to meet a six-figure asking price.

La situación de Neal se decidirá durante los entrenamientos de primavera en Vero Beach, Florida, donde deberá competir frente a Jim Gilliam y Don Zimmer. records.headline: The Dominican Republic opened its $30,000,000 International Peace
records.summary_en: The Dominican Republic opened its $30,000,000 International Peace and Progress Fair in Ciudad Trujillo, drawing about 20,000 visitors to the opening day. Omero Caton of Teaneck, New Jersey, known internationally as "Mr. First," waited 14 hours at the gate to purchase the first ticket from an official. The fairgrounds encompass 79 pavilions spread over a 125-acre tract centered on a winged-globe theme, with the exposition scheduled to continue for the next six months.
records.summary_es: La República Dominicana inauguró su Feria Internacional de la Paz y el Progreso, valorada en $30,000,000, en Ciudad Trujillo, atrayendo a unos 20,000 visitantes el día de la apertura. Omero Caton, de Teaneck, Nueva Jersey, conocido internacionalmente como "Mr. First", esperó 14 horas en la puerta para comprar la primera entrada a un funcionario. El recinto ferial abarca 79 pabellones distribuidos en un terreno de 125 acres centrado en el lema de un globo alado, y la exposición está programada para continuar durante los próximos seis meses.

records.headline: Two American baseball players photographed at Trujillo stadium
records.summary_en: Two American baseball players photographed at Trujillo stadium in the Dominican Republic have been reported as prospects for major league clubs next season. records.headline: A pilot named Fred recounts flying into a severe tropical storm
records.summary_en: A pilot named Fred recounts flying into a severe tropical storm while traveling with fellow pilot Walt Crissey from Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic, to Guantanamo, Cuba. Encountering seventy-mile-an-hour winds that tossed the plane like a cork, the aviators flew at 20 feet along a twisting, cliff-lined coast using the breaker line as their sole guide. The two pilots alternated controls of the dual-controlled plane for 90 minutes until the storm broke, allowing them to climb to 300 feet.
records.summary_es: Un piloto llamado Fred relata haberse topado con una fuerte tormenta tropical mientras viajaba con su colega aviador Walt Crissey desde Ciudad Trujillo, República Dominicana, hacia Guantánamo, Cuba. Al enfrentar vientos de setenta millas por hora que sacudían el avión como un corcho, los aviadores volaron a 20 pies a lo largo de una costa sinuosa y acantilada utilizando la línea de rompientes como única guía. Los dos pilotos alternaron los mandos del avión de control dual durante 90 minutos hasta que la tormenta amainó, permitiéndoles ascender a 300 pies.

records.headline: An account describes the Dominican Republic as encompassing
records.summary_en: An account describes the Dominican Republic as encompassing an area of 19,332 square miles, occupying the eastern three-fourths of the island of Santo Domingo and slightly exceeding Vermont and New Hampshire combined. Located less than a thousand miles from Miami, the nation is separated from Puerto Rico by the Mona Channel on the east and from Cuba by the Windward Passage on the west. The report characterizes the country as a Caribbean anomaly marked by clean streets, safety for women walking alone at night, and an absence of beggars.

Situada a menos de mil millas de Miami, la nación está separada de Puerto Rico por el canal de la Mona al este y de Cuba por el paso de los Vientos al oeste. El informe califica al país como una anomalía caribeña caracterizada por calles limpias, seguridad para las mujeres que caminan solas de noche y ausencia de mendigos.

records.headline: A letter to the editor highlights the record of the Inter-American Peace Committee of the Organization of American States
records.summary_en: A letter to the editor highlights the record of the Inter-American Peace Committee of the Organization of American States in resolving disputes between member nations. It notes that in 1950, the year of its creation, the committee expedited the resolution of a dispute arising from charges made by President Trujillo of the Dominican Republic against Haiti and Cuba that threatened Caribbean tranquility. The writer emphasizes that adequate treaties exist for the peaceful settlement of all disputes in the Americas.
records.summary_es: Una carta al director resalta la trayectoria de la Comisión Interamericana de Paz de la Organización de los Estados Americanos en la solución de controversias entre países miembros. Señala que en 1950, año de su creación, la comisión agilizó la resolución de una disputa surgida por acusaciones formuladas por el presidente Trujillo de la República Dominicana contra Haití y Cuba que amenazaban la tranquilidad del Caribe. El autor subraya que existen tratados adecuados para la solución pacífica de todas las disputas en las Américas.

records.headline: During deliberations on maritime boundaries at an inter-American
records.summary_en: During deliberations on maritime boundaries at an inter-American legal conference, Temistocles Messina of the Dominican Republic stated that the three-mile rule is uniform only in the sense that no nation recognizes a smaller limit. Messina urged that the upcoming Ciudad Trujillo conference should approve a flexible rule governing territorial waters. Representatives from Haiti and Uruguay also supported extending territorial limits beyond three miles to protect coastal resources.
records.summary_es: Durante las deliberaciones sobre fronteras marítimas en una conferencia jurídica interamericana, Temístocles Messina, de la República Dominicana, afirmó que la norma de las tres millas solo es uniforme en el sentido de que ningún país reconoce un límite menor. Messina instó a que la próxima conferencia de Ciudad Trujillo apruebe una norma flexible que regule las aguas territoriales. Representantes de Haití y Uruguay respaldaron igualmente la ampliación de los límites territoriales más allá de las tres millas para proteger los recursos costeros.

records.headline: Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo was declared in excellent health
records.summary_en: Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo was declared in excellent health following an examination by Dr. Paul Dudley White of Boston, heart specialist to President Eisenhower. Dr. White traveled to Ciudad Trujillo over the weekend to conduct a routine checkup, finding the former Dominican president in perfect condition before returning to the United States on Sunday. Following the examination, Trujillo attended a reception honoring delegates to the Inter-American Conference on Conservation of Natural Resources.

Tras el examen, Trujillo asistió a una recepción en honor de los delegados a la Conferencia Interamericana sobre Conservación de Recursos Naturales.

records.headline: The ten-day Congress of Catholic Culture and Peace in Ciudad Trujillo concluded
records.summary_en: The ten-day Congress of Catholic Culture and Peace in Ciudad Trujillo concluded with an eight-point declaration urging closer international ties and the surmounting of nationalism. The assembly appealed for peace founded on human equality and family rights, while calling on nations to pledge atomic energy exclusively to peaceful purposes under an international control organization following an address by Professor Enrico Medi of the University of Rome. The gathering also heard an opening message sent on behalf of Pope Pius XII by Vatican Substitute Secretary of State Monsignor Angelo Dell'Acqua.

La asamblea abogó por una paz fundada en la igualdad humana y los derechos de la familia, al tiempo que pidió a las naciones comprometer la energía atómica exclusivamente para fines pacíficos bajo una organización internacional de control tras una alocución del profesor Enrico Medi, de la Universidad de Roma. El encuentro escuchó además un mensaje de apertura enviado en nombre del papa Pío XII por el sustituto de la Secretaría de Estado del Vaticano, monseñor Angelo Dell'Acqua.

records.headline: Concern mounted over the disappearance of Jesus de Galindez
records.summary_en: Concern mounted over the disappearance of Jesus de Galindez, a 42-year-old Spanish Republican exile and critic of the Dominican Republic's Trujillo regime who vanished after missing his international law classes at Columbia University on March 12. Although his apartment at 30 Fifth avenue showed no signs of struggle, deposed Dominican newspaper publisher Dr. German Ornes told reporters he believed Galindez had been kidnaped and murdered. On March 20, members of 11 organizations in Latin American affairs and human rights petitioned Attorney General Brownell to assign FBI agents to investigate the case.

Aunque su apartamento en 30 Fifth avenue no mostraba señales de forcejeo, el destituido director de periódicos dominicano doctor Germán Ornes declaró a los periodistas creer que Galíndez había sido secuestrado y asesinado. El 20 de marzo, miembros de 11 organizaciones de asuntos latinoamericanos y derechos humanos solicitaron al fiscal general Brownell la asignación de agentes del FBI para investigar el caso.

Ornes, former publisher of El Caribe. The denial answered charges made in Bermuda by Inter-American Press Association president James G. Stahlman, who stated that the State Department refused a deportation request after IAPA directors intervened on Ornes's behalf. Herrera Baez conferred on the matter with United States Ambassador William Pheiffer, while State Department officials in Washington stated they knew of no deportation request in the case.
records.summary_es: El canciller dominicano Porfirio Herrera Báez negó las acusaciones de que la República Dominicana hubiera pedido a los Estados Unidos deportar al editor autoexiliado Germán E. Ornes, antiguo director de El Caribe. El desmentido respondió a las afirmaciones hechas en Bermudas por el presidente de la Sociedad Interamericana de Prensa, James G. Stahlman, quien indicó que el Departamento de Estado rechazó una solicitud de deportación tras la intervención de directivos de la SIP a favor de Ornes. Herrera Báez trató el asunto con el embajador estadounidense William Pheiffer, mientras funcionarios del Departamento de Estado en Washington manifestaron no tener constancia de ninguna petición de deportación en el caso.

records.headline: The Dominican government announced its decision to establish
records.summary_en: The Dominican government announced its decision to establish a free port at the World's Fair in Ciudad Trujillo to boost regional tourism. Authorities are actively purchasing merchandise in countries worldwide to stock the new facility. The $25 million International Fair along the Caribbean shoreline has become a primary attraction, and officials recently decided to extend the exposition throughout 1956.
records.summary_es: El gobierno dominicano anunció su decisión de establecer un puerto libre en la Feria Mundial de Ciudad Trujillo para impulsar el turismo regional. Las autoridades se encuentran adquiriendo mercancías en diversos países del mundo para abastecer la nueva instalación. La Feria Internacional de $25 millones a lo largo del litoral caribeño se ha convertido en un atractivo primordial, y los funcionarios resolvieron recientemente prolongar la exposición durante todo 1956.

records.headline: A visiting Puerto Rican athletic squad suffered an unexpected
records.summary_en: A visiting Puerto Rican athletic squad suffered an unexpected defeat against a 14-man Dominican team at Ranfis Park in Ciudad Trujillo, losing by a score of 15 points to 9. The match was arranged during an excursion to Santo Domingo where the hosts requested that everyone play instead of a planned 10-man team with two substitutes. Defeats suffered by former champion Francisco Benitez against A. Malagon, Antonio Higuera against A. Pichardo, and Nevaldo Padilla accounted for the visiting team's limited score.
records.summary_es: Una selección atlética puertorriqueña visitante sufrió una sorpresiva derrota ante un equipo dominicano de 14 hombres en el parque Ranfis de Ciudad Trujillo, cayendo por un marcador de 15 puntos a 9. El partido fue organizado durante una excursión a Santo Domingo en la que los anfitriones pidieron que jugaran todos en lugar de un conjunto previsto de 10 hombres con dos sustitutos. Las derrotas sufridas por el excampeón Francisco Benítez frente a A. Malagón, Antonio Higuera frente a A. Pichardo y Nevaldo Padilla explicaron la limitada anotación del equipo visitante.

records.headline: In a copyrighted Chicago Tribune story reported by Jules Dubois
records.summary_en: In a copyrighted Chicago Tribune story reported by Jules Dubois, Mr. Prio denied accusations by the Cuban government, alleging that he and President Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic had cooperated to stir up Cuban unrest. Prio maintained that since returning to Cuba he had not purchased a single revolver and characterized himself as a peaceful man. In Washington, Immigration Commissioner Joseph M. Swing stated that in light of Mr. Prio's admitted violation of the Neutrality Act, it was a question of grave national concern whether the pair should be readmitted to the United States.

Prío sostuvo que desde su regreso a Cuba no había comprado un solo revólver y se describió como un hombre pacífico. En Washington, el comisionado de Inmigración Joseph M. Swing declaró que, ante la admitida infracción de la Ley de Neutralidad por parte del señor Prío, resultaba una cuestión de grave preocupación nacional si la pareja debía ser readmitida en los Estados Unidos.

records.headline: On May 1, Mr. Roosevelt asked Attorney General Brownell to exert
records.summary_en: On May 1, Mr. Roosevelt asked Attorney General Brownell to exert and exhaust every effort to solve the disappearance of Mr. Galindez, a Dominican opponent of Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo who vanished in New York on March 12 where he lectured at Columbia University. Assistant Attorney General Warren Olney III, head of the Justice Department's criminal division, replied asking the former congressman whether he had addressed any such appeal to the Dominican government, for which Roosevelt is a registered agent, and what response was received. Speaking from his farm near Hopewell Junction, New York, Mr. Roosevelt stated he had not received the letter and would not comment until seeing it. The Justice Department indicated there was no evidence of a federal violation warranting a full-scale investigation, though President Eisenhower stated the FBI was prepared to enter the case if warranted.
records.summary_es: El 1 de mayo, el señor Roosevelt solicitó al fiscal general Brownell agotar todos los esfuerzos para esclarecer la desaparición del señor Galíndez, un dominicano opuesto al régimen del generalísimo Rafael L. Trujillo que desapareció en Nueva York el 12 de marzo, donde se desempeñaba como profesor en la Universidad de Columbia. El fiscal general adjunto Warren Olney III, jefe de la división penal del Departamento de Justicia, respondió preguntando al excongresista si había dirigido alguna petición similar al gobierno de la República Dominicana, del cual Roosevelt es agente registrado, y cuál había sido la respuesta obtenida. Desde su finca cercana a Hopewell Junction, Nueva York, el señor Roosevelt manifestó que no había recibido la carta y que no formularía comentarios hasta revisarla. El Departamento de Justicia señaló que no existían pruebas de una infracción federal que justificara una investigación exhaustiva, aunque el presidente Eisenhower declaró que el FBI estaba preparado para intervenir si correspondía.

records.summary_en: Dominican Consul General Arturo R. Espaillat criticized, regarding Dr. Galindez's book, a New York Times story as another step in that newspaper's anti-Trujillo campaign. Espaillat asserted that the report would serve as the signal for fresh public protests against the Dominican Republic by a small band of malcontent expatriates. Meanwhile, Galindez supporter Nicholas Silfa reported receiving a threatening telephone call regarding an anti-Trujillo bulletin he publishes. Silfa announced that a memorial service for Galindez would be held outside the office of Franklin D. Roosevelt Jr., legal representative of the Trujillo government.

records.headline: A foe of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: A foe of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic, Dr. Jesus de Galindez, was thrown alive into the flaming furnace of a freighter, according to reports that the New York district attorney announced an investigation into. Galindez was a lecturer at Columbia University who vanished last March and was an outspoken opponent of the Trujillo regime in the tiny Spanish-speaking Caribbean republic. Representatives of the Dominican Revolutionary Party picketed the law offices of Franklin D. Roosevelt Jr., who is legal counsel here for the Dominican Republic, and Nicholas Silfa, a spokesman for the party, told newsmen Galindez was shanghaied sometime between March 13 and 16, when the Dominican Steamship Line's freighter Fundacion was in port here, later repeating the story to investigators from the office of District Attorney Frank Hogan: “We got it right from the ship herself. Dr. Galindez was kidnapped onto the Fundacion and thrown alive into the boiler. Our contacts in the underground told us the story.” Hogan's office said Silfa had been questioned about the report and the books and records of the New York agent of the steamship line had been subpoenaed, and the crew of the vessel will be questioned when the ship docks here again on June 7. The Dominican Republic information center here described the murder theory as “fantastic” and Silfa's activities as “dramatic publicity-seeking by any and all means.”
records.summary_es: Opositor al generalísimo Rafael Trujillo de la República Dominicana, el doctor Jesús de Galíndez fue arrojado vivo a la caldera en llamas de un carguero, según los informes sobre los que el fiscal de distrito de Nueva York anunció una investigación. Galíndez era profesor en la Universidad de Columbia, desapareció el pasado marzo y era un opositor declarado del régimen de Trujillo en la pequeña república caribeña de habla española. Representantes del Partido Revolucionario Dominicano hicieron un piquete ante las oficinas del bufete de Franklin D. Roosevelt Jr., asesor legal aquí de la República Dominicana, y Nicolás Silfa, portavoz del partido, dijo a los periodistas que Galíndez fue secuestrado en algún momento entre el 13 y el 16 de marzo, cuando el carguero Fundación, de la Dominican Steamship Line, estaba en puerto aquí, repitiendo después la historia a investigadores de la oficina del fiscal de distrito Frank Hogan: «Lo supimos de la propia nave. El doctor Galíndez fue secuestrado a bordo del Fundación y arrojado vivo a la caldera. Nuestros contactos en la clandestinidad nos contaron la historia». La oficina de Hogan dijo que Silfa había sido interrogado sobre el informe y que se habían citado los libros y registros del agente en Nueva York de la línea naviera, y que la tripulación del buque será interrogada cuando el barco atraque aquí de nuevo el 7 de junio. El centro de información de la República Dominicana aquí calificó la teoría del asesinato de «fantástica» y las actividades de Silfa de «dramática búsqueda de publicidad por todos los medios».

records.full_text:
Dominica Offers Crew For Galindez Probe

NEW YORK, May 31 (AP).—The Dominican government has offered to bring here the entire original crew of a Dominican freighter reportedly linked with the mysterious disappearance of Dr. Jesus de Galindez.

Dr. Galindez, Columbia University lecturer and a critic of the Caribbean republic's Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, disappeared March 12.

On Tuesday Nicholas Silfa, spokesman for the anti-Trujillo Dominican Revolutionary Party, alleged that Dr. Galindez was shanghaied aboard the Fundacion here and tossed, alive, into the ship's firebox sometime between March 13 and 17.

Letters Made Public

Arturo R. Espaillat, Dominican consul general here, yesterday made public a letter to District Attorney Frank S. Hogan and Police Commissioner Stephen P. Kennedy.

Mr. Espaillat's letter termed the Silfa story "a terrible hoax," adding:

"My office will have all the original crew members brought to New York, should it be required by you. . . ."

Reportedly some of the Fundacion's crew members jumped ship after it sailed from here.

The consul general's letter said "key members" of the crew will be flown here before Sunday. On Sunday, the letter said, they could attend a meeting of Trujillo's supporters called by the Dominican Republic Cultural Society.

All Leads Studied

Deputy Police Commissioner Walter Arm, on learning the gist of the letter, said the Galindez case "is being investigated with complete impartiality" and "we will follow all leads and look into them."

There was no immediate comment from Mr. Hogan.

The Fundacion, due here next on June 7, is operated by the New York and Cuba Steamship Co. The books of the steamship line have been seized by the district attorney's office as part of the investigation.

The New York Herald Tribune said it talked yesterday by trans-ocean phone with Gen. Trujillo. The newspaper quoted him as saying the allegation that Dr. Galindez was murdered aboard the Fundacion was a "scandalous libel" brought against his country by "Communist mice."

"We are completely innocent," the newspaper quoted Gen. Trujillo. "These are nothing more than lies."

records.headline: Upon its arrival, police searched the Dominican Line freighter
records.summary_en: Upon its arrival, police searched the Dominican Line freighter Fundacion following allegations by Nicholas Silva, spokesman for an anti-Trujillo revolutionary party, that missing scholar Dr. Jesus de Galindez had been kidnaped and tossed into the ship's boiler during its prior visit. Galindez, an outspoken opponent of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo in the Dominican Republic, disappeared on March 12 while returning to his apartment from Columbia University. Dominican authorities denounced the story as a lie, and Chief of Detectives James B. Leggett formally reported to Police Commissioner Stephen P. Kennedy that the search produced no evidence of foul play or information of value.

records.headline: Dominican Ship Boilers Searched, No Galindez Murder Clues Found
records.summary_en: New York detectives searched the Dominican freighter Fundación in Brooklyn for four hours after the Dominican revolutionary leader Nicolás Silfa charged that Jesús de Galíndez, a foe of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, had been thrown alive into a steaming boiler aboard the ship. The detectives questioned the 36 crew members and found not a single solid clue to Galíndez's fate, though the boilers' openings were large enough to squeeze a man through. A representative of the Ward Lines, which controls the Dominican Steamship Line, said opening a boiler door while it was fired would burn a man to a crisp, and Silfa, in a statement afterwards, repeated his charge that Galíndez's body was thrown into the firebox on Trujillo's orders.

Los detectives interrogaron a los 36 tripulantes y no hallaron ni una sola pista sólida sobre el destino de Galíndez, aunque las bocas de las calderas eran lo bastante grandes para que cupiera un hombre. Un representante de la Ward Lines, que controla la Dominican Steamship Line, afirmó que abrir la puerta de una caldera encendida quemaría a un hombre hasta dejarlo en cenizas, y Silfa, en una declaración posterior, repitió su acusación de que el cuerpo de Galíndez fue arrojado a la cámara de combustión por órdenes de Trujillo.

records.summary_en: Caribair received an Aviation Safety Award after accumulating 77,937,000 passenger miles with a perfect safety record by the close of 1955. Headed by president Dionisio Trigo, the airline operates daily scheduled passenger flights serving San Juan, Ponce, and Mayaguez in Puerto Rico; St. Thomas and St. Croix in the Virgin Islands; and Ciudad Trujillo in the Dominican Republic. Safety council awards were calculated from Civil Aeronautics Administration records, with Lieutenant General James H. Doolittle and Harry Guggenheim serving on the advisory committee.

records.summary_en: Jose Antonio Aguirre, president of the exiled Basques, affirmed that Dr. Jesus de Galindez was honest in all his actions and that United States authorities were fully informed regarding funds he collected for Basque organizations. Justice Department records indicated that Galindez, a registered agent for the anti-Franco government who vanished in New York, collected slightly more than $1 million since 1949. Aguirre explained that the difference between the $1 million collected and the $500,000 sent to headquarters in Paris reflected disbursements to non-Communist hospitals, schools, and cultural centers worldwide, especially in America. Galindez was an outspoken opponent of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo's regime in the Dominican Republic, and friends suggested he fell victim to Dominican assassins.

Registros del Departamento de Justicia señalaban que Galíndez, agente registrado del gobierno antifranquista que desapareció en Nueva York, recaudó algo más de $1 millón desde 1949. Aguirre explicó que la diferencia entre el millón recaudado y los $500,000 remitidos a la sede de París correspondía a aportes para hospitales, escuelas y centros culturales no comunistas en el mundo, particularmente en América. Galíndez era un frontal detractor del régimen del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo en la República Dominicana, y sus allegados sugirieron que fue víctima de asesinos dominicanos.

PARRIS ISLAND. S. C., July 23.—A 26-year-old George
town Law School graduate is postponing his departure
from active Marine duty to see through to the end the
“death-march” trial of Sergt. Matthew C. McKeon.

Rochester. He also is a graduate of Georgetown University.

lins was due for release July 3. He obtained an extension
until July 31 and hopes for another since the trial appar
ently will not be over by that time.
Lieut. Collins represented Sergt. McKeon in the court

on a night exercise. His work has drawn high praise from
the experienced civilian barrister Emile Zola Berman who
heads the battery of defense lawyers.

for a round of interviews on possible connections there.

records.headline: At a reception hosted by Dominican Ambassador and Señora de Salazar
records.summary_en: At a reception hosted by Dominican Ambassador and Señora de Salazar celebrating the anniversary of the Restoration of the Dominican Republic on August 16, 1863, details were disclosed regarding the mission's search for a new chancery. Dominican authorities decided to sell a Benton Place residence, originally intended as a guest house for visiting dignitaries like Generalissimo Trujillo and later proposed as a chancery, after neighborhood homeowners voiced strong objections. Having sold their current chancery at 4500 Sixteenth Street N.W. to the Cambodian government with an October 13 departure deadline, embassy staff continue seeking a new location. Guests at the reception included Assistant Secretary of State Henry Holland and Deputy Assistant Secretary Roy R. Rubottom.
records.summary_es: En una velada ofrecida por el embajador dominicano y la señora de Salazar para celebrar el aniversario de la Restauración de la República Dominicana del 16 de agosto de 1863, se conocieron detalles de las gestiones diplomáticas para encontrar una nueva cancillería. Las autoridades dominicanas resolvieron vender un inmueble en Benton Place, previsto inicialmente como alojamiento para dignatarios como el generalísimo Trujillo y luego proyectado para cancillería, ante la firme oposición de los vecinos del sector. Tras haber enajenado su sede en el 4500 de la calle 16 N.W. al gobierno de Camboya con plazo de entrega fijado para el 13 de octubre, la embajada prosigue la búsqueda de nuevo local. Entre los asistentes al agasajo figuraron el subsecretario de Estado adjunto Henry Holland y el vicesubsecretario adjunto Roy R. Rubottom.

records.summary_en: Robert Harrison, fifty-year-old publisher of Confidential magazine, was hospitalized in Ciudad Trujillo with a gunshot wound to his left arm, exhaustion, and exposure following a shooting in the Jarabacoa Mountain woods seventy miles northwest of the Dominican capital. Police detained jungle guide Richard Weldy, thirty-five, on a holding charge while awaiting Harrison's statement before deciding on prosecution. Weldy admitted shooting Harrison during a loud argument over an article recounting how he introduced his former wife, actress Pilar Palette, to actor John Wayne in Peru in 1952, though Weldy insisted his rifle discharged accidentally when it fell.

records.headline: Police in Ciudad Trujillo released big game hunter Richard Weldy
records.summary_en: Police in Ciudad Trujillo released big game hunter Richard Weldy, after questioning him in the shooting of Robert Harrison, publisher of Confidential magazine. Weldy had been held in custody since Harrison was struck in the shoulder by a blast from Weldy's shotgun, which discharged after falling onto a rock in a Dominican jungle during an argument over an article concerning Weldy's former wife, Pilar Palette, and actor John Wayne. Both men described the discharge as purely accidental, and Harrison told United Press reporters that he harbored no grudge against Weldy for the mishap.
records.summary_es: La policía de Ciudad Trujillo concedió la libertad al cazador de piezas mayores Richard Weldy, tras someterlo a interrogatorio por el disparo que hirió a Robert Harrison, editor de la revista Confidential. Weldy permanecía detenido desde que Harrison recibió un impacto de perdigones en el hombro al caer la escopeta sobre una roca en una zona selvática dominicana mientras discutían por un reportaje sobre la exesposa de Weldy, Pilar Palette, y el actor John Wayne. Ambos protagonistas calificaron el hecho como un percance fortuito, manifestando Harrison a los redactores de United Press que no guardaba resentimiento alguno hacia Weldy por lo ocurrido.

Beginning September 24 and lasting 10 weeks through November 27, Super 6 Clippers will fly seven round-trip flights each week between various U.S. cities and Ciudad Trujillo. records.headline: An article exploring the disputed final resting place of Christopher Columbus cites
records.summary_en: An article exploring the disputed final resting place of Christopher Columbus cites a plaque in Havana recording that the Spanish government transferred the admiral's supposed remains from the Republic of Santo Domingo (now the Dominican Republic) on January 19, 1796, before moving them to the Seville Cathedral on September 26, 1898. While a substantial number of Cubans believe the explorer's body remains in Havana, partisans of the Dominican case assert that Columbus's remains were removed to Santo Domingo in 1542 and never left. Dominican advocates contend that a false set of bones was transferred to Cuba, though all disputants agree the remains are no longer in Valladolid, Spain, where funeral ceremonies took place on May 20, 1506.
records.summary_es: Un artículo que explora el disputado lugar de descanso final de Cristóbal Colón cita una placa en La Habana que registra que el gobierno español trasladó los supuestos restos del almirante desde la República de Santo Domingo (ahora la República Dominicana) el 19 de enero de 1796, antes de trasladarlos a la catedral de Sevilla el 26 de septiembre de 1898. Aunque un número considerable de cubanos cree que el cuerpo del explorador permanece en La Habana, los partidarios del caso dominicano sostienen que los restos de Colón fueron trasladados a Santo Domingo en 1542 y nunca salieron de allí. Los defensores dominicanos afirman que un conjunto falso de huesos fue trasladado a Cuba, si bien todos los litigantes concuerdan en que los restos ya no se encuentran en Valladolid, España, donde se celebraron las ceremonias fúnebres el 20 de mayo de 1506.

records.headline: A historical note states that Christopher Columbus was buried
records.summary_en: A historical note states that Christopher Columbus was buried in the Carthusian monastery at Seville before his body and that of his son Diego were removed in 1543 to the cathedral in Ciudad Trujillo, Hispaniola. In 1795, when Hispaniola was ceded to the French, the son's body was moved to the cathedral in Havana, Cuba, but Columbus's remains were left in Hispaniola through error. When Spain lost Cuba in 1898, Diego's remains were sent to the Seville Cathedral, while the body of Columbus now rests in the cathedral at Ciudad Trujillo in the Dominican Republic.

records.headline: Señor Plinio Pins Chevalier, Minister and Commercial Counselor of the Dominican
records.summary_en: Señor Plinio Pins Chevalier, Minister and Commercial Counselor of the Dominican Republic, died Wednesday of a heart attack in Bt. Luke's Hospital in New York City. Chevalier resided at 146 Central Park West and was an uncle of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo and Dominican President Hector Trujillo. A career diplomat who had served several years as consul general in New York City and held his commercial post for the last seven years, he is survived by his widow, Ercllia, with his body flown to the Dominican Republic for burial.
records.summary_es: El señor Plinio Pins Chevalier, ministro y consejero comercial de la República Dominicana, falleció el miércoles a causa de un ataque cardíaco en el Hospital St. Luke's de la ciudad de Nueva York. Chevalier residía en el 146 de Central Park West y era tío del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo y del presidente dominicano Héctor Trujillo. Diplomático de carrera que había ejercido varios años como cónsul general en la ciudad de Nueva York y ocupado su cargo comercial durante los últimos siete años, le sobrevive su viuda, Ercllia, y su cuerpo fue trasladado en avión a la República Dominicana para su entierro.

records.full_text:
Bolivia Tin to be Sold to British if U.S. Closes Smelting Plant in Texas

UNITED NATIONS, Oct. 27 — (UP)— The ex-President of Bolivia, Victor Paz Estenssoro, appointed Ambassador in London, declared that all the tin produced by his country will have to be sold to the British, if the Texas smelting plant is closed.

“At present we sell to Great Britain one half of the production; but if the United States close the Texas plant, all our tin will have to go to the British market,” Paz Estenssoro said, indicating the importance of his mission as Ambassador in London.

He told newspapermen that in the Administrative aspect of the nationalized tin mines, Bolivia is counselled by a North American Mining Company, but stressed that this was only in its technical phase.

In answer to a question the ex-President declared:

“The tin mines, definitely, will continue nationalized.”

He pointed out afterward that, on the other hand, a new mine, — a zinc mine, will be leased on a base of royalties, to a North American company. “We are discussing and negotiating on it now,” he said.

He said that the supply of life staples, particularly of food, is improving in Bolivia.

“We had great difficulties with the supply due to troubles in transportation,” he added. “We had to transport machinery and equipment for production, needed by the country, from the Pacific ports to the interior of the nation.”

The Bolivian ex- President spoke with the newspapermen before the beginning of the luncheon offered in his honor by the Ambassadors of the Latin American Republics and the United States.

Dr. José Vicente Trujillo, Ambassador of Ecuador and President of the Latin American Group, delivered a few words of greeting to the distinguished visitor, from his colleagues.

In his statements to newspapermen, Paz Estenssoro said that his country is engaged in a plan of monetary stabilization and that, in this job, it has the cooperation of North American assessors, who now are officials of the Bolivian Government.

“Bolivia will cut down its fiscal expenses and its foreign exchange expenses. Also it will fix a new exchange rate at the beginning of next month,” he explained. “With this plan we aim to attain monetary stabilization and payments balance.”

“On the fixing of a new exchange rate — he said — Bolivia will act in collaboration with the International Monetary Fund, of which she is a member.”

He ended by saying that once the stabilizing plan is enforced, Bolivia will apply for aid fromthe United States. “Such aid could be part as a loan and the rest as help” he said.

BUY MORE SUGAR FROM US SAYS DOMINICAN DIPLOMAT

WASHINGTON—(UP)—The Dominican Ambassador said that the United States should buy more sugar from his country, as beneficial to the two countries.

Joaquín E. Salazar, the Ambassador, said here at a banquet, that the Dominican Republic sugar brought here "is only a drop in a bucket" and added that his Fatherland buys in the United States 80 per cent of all the articles imported there.

records.summary_en: The Dominican Republic cited its precedent as the first nation to give haven to Jewish refugees from Hitler near Sosúa, noting that the colony has become a thriving community whose members enjoy all freedoms as Dominican citizens. In announcing an offer without strings attached to accept Hungarian refugees, President Trujillo strongly denounced Soviet aggression in Hungary and offered asylum to persons from all countries suffering under Communist barbarism. The offer was originally made to Vilis Masens, president of the Assembly of Captive European Nations, with Trujillo pledging Dominican cooperation with United Nations plans aimed at restoring self-determination to Hungary.

Cuban Senator Gives Strong Warning to the Dominican Gvt.

HAVANA, Nov. 23—(UP)— Senator Andrés Rivero Agüero, leader of the government majority in the Senate, affirmed that, if the Dominican Republic would dare to attack Havana, the Cuban Air Force would destroy Ciudad Trujillo.

Rivero Agüero, who claims to be spokesman for President Batista's party, made declarations to the Press at the Presidential Palace, after talking with the Chief Executive.

The Senator said that his declarations were justified by the fact that, according to what the technicians of the Cuban Army pointed out to him, Havana is four hours flight from the Dominican Republic, while Ciudad Trujillo is situated only 36 minutes from Orient province, where Cuba has important military posts.

Rivero Aguero ridiculized the augurs of invasion by mercenary forces stationed in the Dominican Republic, and assured that, even if there were five or six thousand men engaged in the invasion, the Cuban army "would take good care of them."

Magloire Leaves Haiti's Presidency, Prepares to Abandon Country at Once

WASHINGTON, Dec. 12 —(UP)—General Paul E. Magloire resigned today the Presidency of the Haitian Provisional Military Government and prepared to leave the country by plane, according to a creditable information received in this capital.

Dispatchs from Port-au-Prince reveal that Magloire handed over the Presidency, at 11 a.m., to Joseph Pierre Louis, President of the Supreme Court and constitutional successor to the President.

It is expected that Magloire will announce his resignation publicly, making a plea to the Haitian people for the keeping of peace and order during the transition period until celebration of new presidential elections next April.

Magloire was said to have decided to leave Haiti to avert the possibility of an outbreak of violence over his recent unpopular actions.

The people of Port-au-Prince expressed their displeasure by staging a general strike Monday. All normal activities in the capital have been paralyzed since.

The reports said Magloire received a stern lecture from Apostolic Nuncio Msgr. Luigi Raimondi Monday night. Magloire was understood to have been adamant against abandoning the dictatorial powers he assumed last week.

But it was reported he was impressed by arguments that his suspension of the Constitution was so unpopular that his continued stay could bring violence to Haiti.

American tourists arriving in Puerto Rico from Haiti said Haitians appeared solidly against continued rule by Magloire. They said the strike appeared almost 100 per cent effective in the capital. One tourist said there was "some shooting" during the day and that four or five casualties went to a hospital.

Almost all shops and stores remained closed as workers ignored broadcast appeals to return to work. Only one gasoline station was open. Oil companies operating here are American-owned.

records.full_text:
KNOW THY NEIGHBOR

By ANTONIO RUIZ

HAITI — In all the seaports, the chief cities of the Republic of Haiti, beautiful green mountains form the background of the charming landscape. Of the total area of the country of 10,700 square miles, 8,000 square miles are mountains. There are three principal ranges with several large plains lying between them and along their outer fringes. One range, including large groups known as La Horte and La Selle, extends from east to west along the lower peninsula, while the other two stretch from the southeast to the northeast across the mainland an northern peninsula.

The highest mountain in Haiti is Morne La Selle in the southeast, which reaches an altitude of 8,700 feet above sea level. There are four plains of major importance in the country: the North Plain, lying along the northern east coast between the mountains and the sea; the Central Plain, a large interior flatland, bordering the Dominican Republic, and the Artibonite and Cul-de-Sac Plains, which spread eastward from the Gulf of Gonave.

Haiti has numerous rivers, most of them short, rapid streams coursing down the mountain slopes into the sea. The Artibonite River, however, which drains the Artibonite Plain on its way to the Gulf of Gonave, has a length of 200 miles from its headwaters in the Dominican Republic to its mouth. It furnishes the water for the Republic's principal irrigation system and is the only river of sufficient size to be of importance as a means of transportation.

There is one large lake in Haiti, the Etang Saumatre, and a number of small ones. The Etang Saumatre, with an area of approximately 43 square miles, is located east of Port-au-Prince, on the Dominican border. It has no visible outlet to the sea, but the fact that its waters have been receding for some years seems to indicate the existence of a subterranean chanel between the lake and the Gulf of Gonave.

The temperature in all the main centers of population of the Republic of Haiti, most of which are seaports, is warm and uniform. In the chief cities, the yearly range is from 70 to 85 degrees Fahrenheit, with a slight variation of three or four degrees between summer and winter. The mountain heights are considerably cooler, and sometimes are event subject to frost.

Rainfall is highly variable in the different sections of the country being abundant on the windward slopes, while the slopes and enclosed plains in the shadow of the higher mountain ranges usually receive less rainfall, and at times are deficient in moisture. Normally rain comes in two distinct seasons, the first from April through June, and the second during October and November.

The oppressive humid heat usually felt in most of the tropical lowlands, is dissipated to a great extent on the Haitian coasts by sea breezes which seldom fail.

On the map, Haiti looks almost like a crab whose claws reach toward the west; two peninsulas, a long one in the south, and a shorter one in the north, stretch westward, and embrace between them the Gulf of Gonave. The peninsulas form a considerable portion of the total area of the country, which is about 10,700 square miles, including the territory of its dependent islands. The Republic has an extensive seacoast.

During his visit, Barreto traveled to Baní, birthplace of Cuban independence hero Generalissimo Máximo Gómez, paying tribute to the Dominican Republic and to Rafael L. Trujillo as supreme chief of the Dominican people. records.full_text:
All is Well, at Least Temporarily, Between Caribbean "Strong Men"

By Francis L. Mc Carthy

HAVANA, Jan. 16. (UP)— The two "strong men" of the Caribbean seem to have mended, at least for the time being, their political differences.

President Fulgencio Batista, of Cuba and Generalissimo Rafael Leonidas Trujillo, of the Dominican Republic, seemingly by initiative of the first, are on the verge of starting a political honeymoon, after a year and a half of not speaking diplomatically, and accusing each othee of entertaining extraterritorial ambitions.

Now, not even two weeks after the last public interchange of accusations, in the columns of "Vision" magazine, the Cuban Minister of Agriculture, Fidel Barreto, returned to this city, after four days of visiting Ciudad Trujillo, with a "Special Message" from the generalissimo to Batista, in which the former says that "the Dominican people feel great esteem and deep admiration" for the Cuban President.

Last Saturday, Barreto assured Trujillo, during ceremonies at a Live Stock Exhibition, in Ciudad Trujillo, that "Cuba feel great affection for the Dominican Republic and admiration and esteem for the Generalissimo, great citizen and statesman.

The new era of political understanding between the two leaders, both with military background, started last December while the government daily "Tiempo", maintained that "an expeditionary force of 1.800 men, supported by two "Mosquito" bombers, financed and aided by Trujillo, was ready to attack Cuba before Christmas".

According to unconfirmed reports, Washington decided that it was time for friendly mediation of the problems of both countries and without delay, Barreto received an official invitation to visit the Dominican Republic.

After that, the attacks of the press and radio against the Generalissimo and also the Dominican official insults against the Cuban authorities, stopped.

The event do not have complete approval of all sectors of public opinion here as it is manifest in an editorial note in "Tiempo" written by Senator Rolando Masferrer—President of the Commission of the Armed Forces of the Senate—in which Barreto is accused of "placing Cuba in a ridiculous position", by his attitude during his visit to Ciudad Trujillo and for the "nonsensical remarks" he made.

"To us, six millions Cubans, it seem an indignity of the kind that makes you vomit unexpectedly", said Masferrer's editorial.

"Ataja", another official organ, does not give any immediate hints of having abandoned the anti-Trujillist line and continues reproducing paragraphs of the anti-Trujillist book authored by Jesús de Galíndez, "The Trujillo Era", which "Ataja" calls "The Book that caused a death".

records.headline: Reports from Havana indicate that the Dominican government has given
records.summary_en: Reports from Havana indicate that the Dominican government has given Cuban revolutionaries residing in its territory a prudent length of time, rumored to be forty days, to get out of the country. Well-informed sources stated that these rumors gained credibility following a recent political understanding between the Cuban and Dominican governments. Travelers arriving from Ciudad Trujillo reported that between one hundred and three hundred Cubans remain in the country, while many others have entered and departed in small groups.
records.summary_es: Informes procedentes de La Habana señalan que el gobierno dominicano ha otorgado a los revolucionarios cubanos residentes en su territorio un plazo prudencial, que según rumores sería de cuarenta días, para salir del país. Fuentes bien informadas indicaron que estos rumores cobraron credibilidad tras un reciente entendimiento político entre los gobiernos cubano y dominicano. Viajeros llegados desde Ciudad Trujillo informaron que entre cien y trescientos cubanos permanecen en el país, mientras que muchos otros han entrado y salido en pequeños grupos.

records.summary_en: Dominican authorities in Ciudad Trujillo refused a marriage license to an eloping 17-year-old British heiress and a New York interior decorator, though the decorator later stated they had married. The elopement prompted the bride's mother to send detectives in pursuit of the pair.

records.headline: A sugar transaction reported at $35,830,000 transferred Dominican properties of the West Indies
records.summary_en: A sugar transaction reported at $35,830,000 transferred Dominican properties of the West Indies to the country's principal domestic producer. The purchasing company paid $10,000,000,000 in cash when the contract was signed, with the balance payable in three equal installments on September 30 in 1957, 1958, and 1959. The sale included four sugar mills—Baramona, Consuelo, Boca Chica, and Quisqueya—along with 108,000 hectares (270,000 acres) of agricultural land, railroads, and ships. A statement issued by both companies indicated that the operation supports the sugar expansion policy undertaken by Dominican President Hector B. Trujillo, with the purchasing firm believed to be controlled by interests led by Generalissimo Rafael Leonidas Trujillo.

La venta incluyó cuatro ingenios azucareros—Baramona, Consuelo, Boca Chica y Quisqueya—, junto con 108.000 hectáreas (270.000 acres) de tierras de cultivo, ferrocarriles y barcos.
