records.headline: Amid political unrest in Haiti, Pan-American Airways began flying
records.summary_en: Amid political unrest in Haiti, Pan-American Airways began flying Americans out of the island republic to nearby Caribbean destinations on Wednesday. The airline transported more than 160 Americans from Port-au-Prince to Kingston and Ciudad Trujillo, the respective capitals of Jamaica and the Dominican Republic. Flights had been suspended when a strike in the Haitian capital forced the resignation of provisional president Joseph Nemours Pierre-Louis, whose opponents accused him of being insufficiently opposed to the policies of the former president who went into exile last December. Pan-American resumed its Haiti service on Wednesday with four 54-passenger flights, sending two planes to Kingston and two to Ciudad Trujillo.
records.summary_es: En medio del malestar político en Haití, Pan-American Airways comenzó el miércoles a trasladar en avión a estadounidenses desde la república caribeña hacia destinos vecinos. La aerolínea transportó a más de 160 estadounidenses desde Puerto Príncipe hasta Kingston y Ciudad Trujillo, las capitales respectivas de Jamaica y la República Dominicana. Los vuelos habían sido suspendidos cuando una huelga en la capital haitiana forzó la renuncia del presidente provisional Joseph Nemours Pierre-Louis, a quien sus adversarios acusaban de no oponerse con suficiente firmeza a las políticas del expresidente que marchó al exilio en diciembre pasado. Pan-American reanudó su servicio a Haití el miércoles con cuatro vuelos de 54 pasajeros, enviando dos aviones a Kingston y dos a Ciudad Trujillo.

records.headline: Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo-Molina, described as regarded
records.summary_en: Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo-Molina, described as regarded by his countrymen as the George Washington of the Dominican Republic, cooperated with high-ranking officials to complete the final link in a chain of radar-radio stations stretching from Cape Canaveral, Florida, to Puerto Rico. The new installation enables the U.S. Air Force to launch missiles from either of two Florida bases, track their flight by radar, and receive radio transmissions at four stations in the Bahamas, the Sabana de la Mar station, and a terminal base in Puerto Rico. The report states that flight-testing over this 2,000-mile course will accelerate the development of longer-range missiles, offering reassurance to allies in Central and South America. Trujillo's cooperation is commended as providing a constructive example to the leaders of all Latin America.
records.summary_es: El generalísimo Rafael L. La nueva instalación permite a la Fuerza Aérea de los Estados Unidos lanzar misiles desde cualquiera de dos bases en Florida, rastrear su trayectoria por radar y recibir transmisiones de radio en cuatro estaciones de las Bahamas, la estación de Sabana de la Mar y una base terminal en Puerto Rico. El despacho señala que las pruebas de vuelo a lo largo de este trayecto de 2.000 millas acelerarán el desarrollo de misiles de mayor alcance, brindando tranquilidad a los aliados de Centro y Sudamérica. La cooperación de Trujillo es elogiada como un ejemplo constructivo para los líderes de toda América Latina.

records.summary_en: A historic animal airlift marked the opening in Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic, of the $3,500,000 'Livestock City'. Livestock arrived by plane from the United States, Canada, Cuba, Mexico, Haiti, Central America, and Puerto Rico to compete for $250,000 in prizes at the International Livestock Fair during the winter months. Dedicated to Western Hemisphere solidarity by Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo, Dominican leader and owner of the Fundación ranch, the complex is described as the largest permanent exposition site of its kind in the world. Encompassing four city blocks, the facility includes 73 buildings, paved driveways, a 4,000-seat stadium, and stables built to accommodate 3,000 animals.
records.summary_es: Un histórico puente aéreo de animales marcó la inauguración en Ciudad Trujillo, República Dominicana, de la «Ciudad Ganadera» de $3.500.000. El ganado llegó en avión desde Estados Unidos, Canadá, Cuba, México, Haití, Centroamérica y Puerto Rico para competir por $250.000 en premios en la Feria Ganadera Internacional durante los meses de invierno. Dedicado a la solidaridad del hemisferio occidental por el generalísimo Rafael L. Trujillo, líder dominicano y propietario de la hacienda Fundación, el complejo es calificado como el mayor recinto de exposición permanente de su tipo en el mundo. Con una extensión de cuatro manzanas urbanas, la instalación cuenta con 73 edificios, calzadas pavimentadas, un estadio de 4.000 asientos y establos construidos para albergar a 3.000 animales.

records.headline: Life magazine reported its investigative findings connecting
records.summary_en: Life magazine reported its investigative findings connecting the disappearance of Jesus de Galindez with American pilot Gerald Murphy. Galindez, a 40-year-old Columbia University instructor and outspoken opponent of Dictator Rafael Trujillo for the past 10 years, vanished after leaving his classroom on March 12, prompting allegations of Dominican involvement that the Trujillo regime repeatedly denied. The investigation revealed that Murphy, who befriended the Dominican consul general in New York and was engaged for a flight, rented a twin-engine plane and landed at Amityville, Long Island. An ambulance arrived that evening to load an 'invalid' aboard Murphy's aircraft, after which the 23-year-old pilot took off early on March 13, refueled in Florida, and continued southward before later disappearing in December.

records.full_text:
Members of Congress Decorated By the Dominican Republic

Three members of Congress, an American businessman, and a Catholic priest were awarded the Dominican Republic's highest decoration yesterday.

The ceremony took place at the embassy preceeding a large 5-to-7 reception commemorating the 113th anniversary of the national independence of the Dominican Republic.

Dominican Ambassador Salazar presented the "Order of Merit of Duarte, Sanchez and Mella" to House Majority Leader John W. McCormack and Representatives Katharine St. George and Donald L. Jackson. Mr. Jackson was unable to be present yesterday, as he had just departed for the Middle East.

Also honored were Col. Carroll Cone, vice president of Pan-American World Airways and Father Joseph Thorning of Frederick, Md. An award also was received by the widow of Thurmond Chatham, the representative from North Carolina who had been designated to receive the decoration before his death.

AMBASSADOR SALAZAR stressed that these awards were given for important contributions to mankind in general as well as for outstanding services to the Dominican Republic.

He lauded Mr. McCormack as one of the "staunchest and most outspoken enemies of that atheistic communism which would destroy the cherished institutions of the Dominican Republic as well as of the United States."

Honoring Mrs. St. George, the Ambassador explained, "affords the people of my country an opportunity to render deserving tribute to the women of the United States."

The Ambassador said his country's "relentless" fight against communism is why the Dominican Republic is so often "a target of crafty attacks, even of a military nature, by elements who would further the Kremlin's plans for world conquest."

REPORTERS afterwards asked the Ambassador to comment on the recent story in Life Magazine which claimed it had turned up information that the missing Dr. Jesus Maria De Galindez, bitter foe of the Dominican Republic's strongman Rafael Trujillo, was kidnaped in New York last March and flown to the Dominican Republic.

The magazine also contended that the pilot of the plane was a young American Gerald Murphy, who later disappeared in the republic. The story implies that both Dr. Galindez (a professor at Columbia University) and Murphy met with foul play at the hands of the Dominicans.

"It's a tremendous libel," said Ambassador Salazar of the Life article.

Mrs. St. George was asked how she felt about receiving the award in view of the furor created over the Galindez disappearance.

"I feel this order has been given to me for what I've done to better the welfare of women and children and my contributions in general. The award has nothing to do with this particular episode."

And Father Thorning said, "A man or a nation is innocent until proven guilty by a judge or jury of his peers."

Mr. McCormack, when replying formally to Ambassador Salazar's speech referred to the old adage—"a friend in need is a friend indeed"—saying that the real test of friendship comes when a trying incident arises.

"The friendship between the United States and Dominican Republic has been tested and found true," he added, citing the co-operation of the two countries during World War II and now against communism.

After the ceremony witnessed by close friends and relatives, the Ambassador and Mme. Salazar received several hundred guests to celebrate their independence day.

ANGELITA TRUJILLO, the 17-year-old daughter of the generalissimo, attracted more attention than all the other guests put together.

A striking brunette in ruby red satin, her wavy hair worn youthfully long and loose, Miss Trujillo has recently come to Washington to attend school here. With her was Miss Elsa Alvarez, daughter of the Dominican Minister of Finance, who is a classmate of hers.

Mrs. John Foster Dulles, wife of the Secretary of State, headed the list of United States dignitaries attending. And of course there was the usual large turnout from the South American diplomatic missions.

Chilean OAS Ambassador Sepulveda said the new Chilean Ambassador to the White House, Mariano Puga, will arrive in Washington on Sunday, accompanied by his 22-year-old daughter, Josefina.

Panama's handsome Ambassador Arias and his wife were among the guests, as were the new Ambassador of Paraguay and Senora de Chaves; Senora de Urrutia, wife of the Colombian Ambassador; the Philippines Ambassador and Mrs. Romulo, the Mexican Ambassador and Senora de Tello, former Ambassador and Mr. John F. Simmons, Italy's Ambassador Brosio, Canada's Ambassador and Mrs. Heeney, Argentina's Ambassador to the OAS and Senora de Garcia, the Secretary General of the OAS, Jose Mora.

Others were Representatives Eugene Keogh and Albert Morano, Mr. and Mrs. Leslie Biffle, Brazil's Ambassador Peixoto, Ambassador Berckemeyer of Peru, Miss Marianna Moran and her fiance Michel J. Parsons, Mrs. Ray Henle, Mr. Jack Neal, and Mr. and Mrs. Harold Mott.

records.headline: Shortly after noon, Representative Porter took the floor of the House
records.summary_en: Shortly after noon, Representative Porter took the floor of the House to request an official inquiry into the death of his constituent Gerald Lester Murphy, a young flyer who disappeared in the Dominican Republic. Porter cited a Life magazine report alleging that Murphy had been hired to transport Jesus Maria de Galindez, a Columbia University instructor and outspoken foe of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, to the republic drugged and disguised as an ambulance patient before Galindez was killed. Porter recounted that Dominican authorities maintained Murphy was pushed off a cliff during a quarrel with Dominican aviator Octavio De La Maza, who subsequently committed suicide in a jail cell. Porter informed his colleagues that he had conducted his own personal investigation into the case.
records.summary_es: El representante Porter hizo uso de la palabra en la Cámara, poco después del mediodía, para solicitar una investigación oficial sobre la muerte de su elector Gerald Lester Murphy, un joven piloto que desapareció en la República Dominicana. Porter citó un reportaje de la revista Life en el que se afirmaba que Murphy había sido contratado para trasladar a Jesús María de Galíndez, docente de la Universidad de Columbia y declarado opositor del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo, hacia la república sedado y disfrazado de paciente de ambulancia antes de que Galíndez fuera asesinado. Porter relató que las autoridades dominicanas sostenían que Murphy fue arrojado por un acantilado durante una riña con el aviador dominicano Octavio de la Maza, quien posteriormente se suicidó en una celda carcelaria. Porter informó a sus colegas de que había llevado a cabo su propia investigación personal sobre el caso.

records.summary_en: Representative Charles O. Porter announced that for self-defense he is carrying a pistol after denouncing Dominican Republic strongman Rafael Trujillo on the House floor last week, Democrat of Oregon. Porter explained that he obtained a gun permit from Washington Police Chief Robert V. Murray after veteran metropolitan police officers cautioned him that even a member of Congress might not be immune from Trujillo's vengeance. An Air Force veteran who previously served as a weapons instructor, Porter told The Star that he does not carry the firearm around the Capitol, where weapons are strictly prohibited inside the legislative chamber.

records.headline: Speaking at an anniversary ceremony commemorating the disappearance of Dr. Jesus de Galíndez
records.summary_en: Speaking at an anniversary ceremony commemorating the disappearance of Dr. Jesus de Galindez, Representative Porter proposed establishing a committee composed of two U.S. citizens, two Dominicans, and a neutral person to investigate the fates of Galindez and American pilot Chester Murphy. Galindez, a Columbia University professor and representative of the Basque Government in Exile, had vanished a year earlier, while Murphy disappeared in the Dominican Republic on December 3, 1956. Addressing representatives of roughly 50 organizations, Porter stated that the joint investigation would depend on the approval of both the State Department and the Dominican government. Porter asserted that if Rafael Trujillo had nothing to fear from the facts, he would welcome the chance to clear his name of serious suspicion.
records.summary_es: Al intervenir en un acto de conmemoración del aniversario de la desaparición del Dr. Jesús de Galíndez, el representante Porter propuso la creación de un comité integrado por dos ciudadanos estadounidenses, dos dominicanos y una persona neutral para investigar la suerte de Galíndez y del piloto estadounidense Chester Murphy. Galíndez, profesor de la Universidad de Columbia y representante del Gobierno Vasco en el Exilio, había desaparecido un año antes, mientras que Murphy desapareció en la República Dominicana el 3 de diciembre de 1956. Ante delegados de unas 50 organizaciones, Porter señaló que la investigación conjunta dependería de la aprobación tanto del Departamento de Estado como del gobierno dominicano. Porter sostuvo que si Rafael Trujillo no tenía nada que temer de los hechos, acogería con beneplácito la oportunidad de limpiar su nombre de graves sospechas.

records.headline: Representative Porter, Democrat of Oregon, charged that the Dominican government
records.summary_en: Representative Porter, Democrat of Oregon, charged that the Dominican government was directly responsible for the fate of pilot Gerald Murphy, implying that Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo ordered him eliminated because he knew too much about the disappearance of Columbia University Professor Jesus Maria de Galindez. Breaking its public silence on the affair, the U.S. State Department formally delivered an urgent diplomatic request asking the Dominican Republic to reopen its investigation into Murphy's disappearance. The diplomatic note effectively challenged the official Dominican account of the incident after the department received an initial response to previous inquiries.
records.summary_es: El representante Porter, demócrata de Oregón, acusó al gobierno dominicano de ser directamente responsable del destino del piloto Gerald Murphy, sugiriendo que el generalísimo Rafael Trujillo ordenó su eliminación debido a que sabía demasiado sobre la desaparición del profesor de la Universidad de Columbia Jesús María de Galíndez. Al romper su silencio público en torno al asunto, el Departamento de Estado de los Estados Unidos cursó formalmente una urgente solicitud diplomática en la que pedía a la República Dominicana que reabriera la investigación sobre la desaparición de Murphy. La nota diplomática rebatió de hecho la versión oficial dominicana sobre el suceso tras haber recibido el departamento una respuesta inicial a consultas previas.

records.full_text:
U. S. Government Rejects
Dominican Statements on
Murphy’s Disappearance

WASHINGTON, March 16 (UP) The United States rejected today the Dominican government explanation about the mysterious disappearance of the North American aviator Gerald L. Murphy, in the Dominican Republic.

23 years old Murphy disappeared in the Dominican Republic on December 3rd. last.

In official note, delivered by the United States Embassy in Ciudad Trujillo, the U. S. government rejected the explanation offered by the Dominican government that Murphy was assassinated by the Dominican pilot Octavio de la Maza, who later committed suicide at Ciudad Trujillo, leaving a letter in which he confessed his crime.

A copy of the note delivered in Ciudad Trujillo was handed today to the Dominican Ambassador in Washington, Dr. Joaquín Salazar.

The note urges the Dominican Government to continue “vigorously” the investigation on the disappearance of Murphy, who was said to have been the pilot who took to the Dominican Republic professor Jesús de Galíndez, who disappeared in New York on March 12, 1956. It has also been said Murphy was murdered because he talked too much.

Last January, the Dominican Government delivered to the State Department an alleged letter-confession of pilot de la Maza and other documents, all of which have been carefully examined by the FBI.

The note delivered today by the U. S. Government says:

“Upon examination of these documents and evidence, this Government has reached the conclusion that, if the handwriting samples submitted by Dominican authorities as belonging to Maza are really his, that means the suicide note was not written by de la Maza.”

Other points rejected by the State Department over the explanation are:

1. That Murphy did not know any person with political influence in the Dominican Republic. The U. S. investigation, says the Department of State, shows that Murphy had “good relations” with high Dominican officials, including the then Undersecretary of the Army, now Consul General in New York, Arturo Espaillat.

2. That Murphy’s income while in the Dominican Republic was $350 per month. The investigation shows, the note says, that the missing pilot had a capital substantially bigger than what Dominican authorities say.

“The Government of the United States is gravely concerned by the disappearance of one of its citizens in the Dominican Republic — the note says — and assumes this concern is shared by the Dominican Government.”

Murphy, as de la Maza, worked for the Dominican Air Line, and disappeared when he had announced his intention to return to the United States for good.

As soon as the contents of the note were revealed, Rep. Charles O. Porter, who has realized a personal investigation on Murphy’s disappearance, said the note shows the need of a Congress investigation of the relations of the United States with the Dominican Republic.

Porter urged a congressional investigation into United States relations with the Dominican Republic, challenging official explanations regarding the disappearance of 23-year-old Oregon pilot Gerald Murphy and questioning the fate of Columbia University professor Jesus Maria de Galindez. The report notes that Murphy, like De La Maza, flew for the Dominican airline and vanished after announcing plans to return to the United States for good. Concurrently, a Dominican spokesman confirmed that Clark and the son of the late President Roosevelt were negotiating the termination of their two-year, $60,000 legal advisory contract signed on March 1, 1956. Both attorneys faced an official Justice Department filing deadline regarding their representation of Trujillo over the previous six months, subject to a 30-day grace period.

Ambos letrados afrontaban el plazo oficial de presentación ante el Departamento de Justicia sobre sus gestiones en favor de Trujillo durante los seis meses previos, con un período de gracia de 30 días.

records.headline: The Dominican government announced that it terminated its representation
records.summary_en: The Dominican government announced that it terminated its representation contract with attorney Franklin D. Roosevelt, Jr., and his Washington associate, Charles Patrick Clark, stating that the pair were considered overpaid. The two lawyers had registered with the U.S. Department of Justice a year earlier to serve as legal counsel for the Dominican Republic at a rate of $60,000 annually. Roosevelt's New York office confirmed that neither man was still employed by the Dominican authorities, following criticism from opponents of Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo over Roosevelt's representation of the regime. Dominican official Alvarez Sanchez declared that services rendered by the two American lawyers were 'nil' and failed to justify their compensation.
records.summary_es: El gobierno dominicano anunció la rescisión de su contrato de representación con el abogado Franklin D. Roosevelt, Jr., y su socio en Washington, Charles Patrick Clark, afirmando que consideraba excesiva su retribución. Los dos juristas se habían registrado ante el Departamento de Justicia de los Estados Unidos un año antes para actuar como asesores jurídicos de la República Dominicana con una remuneración de $60.000 anuales. La oficina de Roosevelt en Nueva York confirmó que ninguno de los dos continuaba empleado por las autoridades dominicanas, tras las críticas vertidas por los opositores al generalísimo Rafael L. Trujillo contra la representación del régimen por parte de Roosevelt. El funcionario dominicano Álvarez Sánchez declaró que los servicios prestados por ambos abogados estadounidenses fueron «nulos» y no justificaban su remuneración.

records.headline: Mr. Abrahams, honorary vice consul for the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: Mr. Abrahams, honorary vice consul for the Dominican Republic in Philadelphia, announced that a court-ordered financial payment was delivered by Antonio de la Maza on behalf of his deceased brother and the brother's widow. According to a suicide note released by Dominican authorities, aviator Octavio de la Maza confessed that he struck Oregon pilot Gerald Murphy during a quarrel, causing the flyer to fall into the sea. Both men flew for a Dominican airline, and the Dominican government denied allegations that Murphy was killed for investigating the fate of Columbia University instructor Jesus de Galindez. Life magazine had reported that Murphy flew the plane transporting Galindez to the Dominican Republic after the anti-Trujillo scholar was abducted in New York.

Ambos volaban para una aerolínea dominicana, y el gobierno dominicano negó las acusaciones de que Murphy fuera asesinado por indagar sobre el paradero del profesor de la Universidad de Columbia Jesús de Galíndez. La revista Life había afirmado que Murphy pilotó el avión que transportó a Galíndez a la República Dominicana tras el secuestro en Nueva York del académico opositor a Trujillo.

Murphy in the Dominican Republic.

records.headline: A commentary examining counter-terrorism and escalating political unrest
records.summary_en: A commentary examining counter-terrorism and escalating political unrest in Cuba observes that official repression is inflaming an already embittered atmosphere rather than restoring internal peace. The editorial notes that the Cuban regime cannot expect to persuade its citizens or the international community through staged demonstrations modeled on those demonstrated by General Juan Perón of Argentina and Generalissimo Trujillo of the Dominican Republic. The analysis emphasizes that official denials regarding rebel leader Fidel Castro are counterproductive, asserting that Castro remains active in the Sierra Maestra and stronger than ever.
records.summary_es: Un comentario que analiza el contraterrorismo y la creciente agitación política en Cuba señala que la represión oficial está exacerbando un ambiente ya enconado en lugar de restablecer la paz interna. El editorial advierte que el régimen cubano no puede aspirar a convencer a sus ciudadanos ni a la comunidad internacional mediante manifestaciones manipuladas, semejantes a las que mostraron organizar el general Juan Perón en Argentina y el generalísimo Trujillo en la República Dominicana. El análisis subraya que desmentir la presencia del líder rebelde Fidel Castro resulta contraproducente, asegurando que Castro continúa activo en la Sierra Maestra y más fuerte que nunca.

records.headline: Dominican Deputy Rosenzweig, identified as a Jewish refugee
records.summary_en: Dominican Deputy Rosenzweig, identified as a Jewish refugee serving in the national parliament, hosted four Jewish members of the U.S. House of Representatives visiting the Dominican Republic. Rosenzweig cited his election as proof that discrimination does not exist in the country, pointing out that devout Catholics formed the vast majority of the electorate that chose him, and praised Generalissimo Trujillo's Program of National Reconstruction. The dispatch notes that Trujillo established the Sosúa refugee colony across more than 3,000 hectares, providing haven to thousands of escapees from Nazi Germany during and after World War II. The visiting congressmen issued a statement praising the Dominican government for welcoming Jewish refugees, particularly those expelled from Egypt after the Suez Canal crisis, contrasting that policy with United States restrictions.
records.summary_es: El diputado dominicano Rosenzweig, identificado como un refugiado judío que ocupa un escaño parlamentario, recibió a cuatro miembros judíos de la Cámara de Representantes de los Estados Unidos durante su visita a la República Dominicana. Rosenzweig calificó su elección como prueba de que no existe discriminación en el país, señalando que devotos católicos conformaron la gran mayoría del electorado que lo respaldó, y elogió el Programa de Reconstrucción Nacional del generalísimo Trujillo. El despacho recuerda que Trujillo estableció la colonia de refugiados de Sosúa sobre más de 3.000 hectáreas, brindando asilo a miles de fugitivos de la Alemania nazi durante y después de la Segunda Guerra Mundial. Los congresistas visitantes emitieron una declaración en la que elogiaron al gobierno dominicano por acoger a refugiados judíos, en particular a los expulsados de Egipto tras la crisis del Canal de Suez, contrastando esa política con las restricciones de los Estados Unidos.

records.headline: Dominican official Herrara Baez branded Honduran charges that the Dominican Republic dispatched
records.summary_en: Dominican official Herrara Baez branded Honduran charges that the Dominican Republic dispatched planes, pilots, and war materials to Nicaragua as "a rude lie" and "seriously offensive," announcing that the Dominican ambassador had been ordered to return immediately to Ciudad Trujillo. In response to the closing of the Dominican Embassy in Tegucigalpa, Honduran Minister of Foreign Relations Jorge Fidel Duron stated that personnel of the Honduran Embassy in Ciudad Trujillo were likewise ordered to return. Dominican Ambassador Fernando Brea declared that the Honduran allegations were inaccurate and that he was closing the embassy because he could not remain in a country "where Trujillo is insulted." Duron separately reported to the OAS Committee in Tegucigalpa that Dominican planes and arms had been sent to Nicaragua on the 6th instant, citing an intercepted message from the Nicaraguan National Guard.
records.summary_es: El funcionario dominicano Herrara Baez calificó las acusaciones hondureñas de que la República Dominicana envió aviones, pilotos y pertrechos de guerra a Nicaragua de "una burda mentira" y "gravemente ofensivas", anunciando que se había ordenado al embajador dominicano regresar de inmediato a Ciudad Trujillo. En respuesta al cierre de la embajada dominicana en Tegucigalpa, el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores de Honduras, Jorge Fidel Durón, declaró que igualmente se ordenó el regreso del personal de la embajada hondureña en Ciudad Trujillo. El embajador dominicano Fernando Brea afirmó que los señalamientos hondureños eran inexactos y que clausuraba la legación diplomática porque no podía permanecer en un país "donde se insulta a Trujillo". Durón informó por separado al Comité de la OEA en Tegucigalpa que aviones y armas dominicanos habían sido enviados a Nicaragua el día 6 del corriente, citando un mensaje interceptado de la Guardia Nacional nicaragüense.

records.headline: An Evening star travel article reports on Caribbean airline
records.summary_en: An Evening star travel article reports on Caribbean airline services offered by KLM Royal Dutch Airlines operating out of Miami. A round-trip fare of $311.40 from Washington allows passengers to make a circle trip encompassing Havana, Jamaica, Aruba, and Curacao, with return travel via Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic, and Port-au-Prince, Haiti, at the same price. The itinerary provides first-class accommodations throughout the journey.

El itinerario ofrece acomodación en primera clase durante todo el recorrido.

records.headline: A District Court grand jury returned a four-count indictment
records.summary_en: A District Court grand jury returned a four-count indictment against lawyer Frank, charging him with acting as an unregistered foreign agent for Generalissimo Trujillo and the Dominican Republic in violation of the Foreign Agents Registration Act of 1938. The grand jury is investigating the disappearances of Columbia University professor Jesus de Galindez, who vanished in New York in March 1956, and twenty-three-year-old American pilot Gerald L. Murphy, who was last seen on December 3 in Ciudad Trujillo after reportedly claiming knowledge of Galindez's fate. Frank, identified in the indictment as also known as John Kane, was arrested by three FBI agents at Seventeenth and I streets N.W. while walking with his attorney, Edward L. Carey.
records.summary_es: Un gran jurado de un tribunal de distrito presentó una acusación de cuatro cargos contra el abogado Frank, imputándole actuar como agente extranjero no registrado del generalísimo Trujillo y la República Dominicana, en violación de la Ley de Registro de Agentes Extranjeros de 1938. El gran jurado investiga las desapariciones del profesor de la Universidad de Columbia Jesús de Galíndez, quien se esfumó en Nueva York en marzo de 1956, y del piloto estadounidense de veintitrés años Gerald L. Murphy, visto por última vez el 3 de diciembre en Ciudad Trujillo tras afirmar presuntamente que conocía la suerte de Galíndez. Frank, identificado en la acusación bajo el alias de John Kane, fue arrestado por tres agentes del FBI en las calles Decimoséptima e I del noroeste mientras caminaba con su abogado, Edward L. Carey.

records.headline: CBS commentator Edward R. Murrow reported in an hour-long documentary radio
records.summary_en: CBS commentator Edward R. Murrow reported in an hour-long documentary radio broadcast that the finger man in the disappearance of Professor Jesus de Galindez was a lame man with a glass eye in the pay of Dominican dictator Rafael Trujillo. Operating under the names "Felix Velasquez" and "El Cojo," or "The Lame One," the individual was allegedly paid by Trujillo to arrange the assassination of the former Columbia University professor in 1950. The broadcast noted that Galindez is believed to have been spirited away from a Long Island airport by American pilot Gerald L. Murphy, who was subsequently believed murdered in the Caribbean nation because of what he knew.
records.summary_es: El comentarista de CBS Edward R. El sujeto, que utilizaba los nombres de "Félix Velásquez" y "El Cojo", presuntamente recibió pagos de Trujillo para planear el asesinato del exprofesor de la Universidad de Columbia en 1950. La transmisión señaló que se cree que Galíndez fue trasladado clandestinamente desde un aeropuerto de Long Island por el piloto estadounidense Gerald L. Murphy, quien a su vez se cree que fue asesinado en el país caribeño debido a lo que sabía.

records.headline: The State Department reported that it asked the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: The State Department reported that it asked the Dominican Republic on May 2 to place General Arturo R. Espaillat, a Dominican official and former consul general in New York, at the disposition of a United States court in connection with the Galindez-Murphy investigation. The request, described as unprecedented in United States diplomatic history, has received no reply from Dominican authorities. The diplomatic move arose from investigations into the disappearance of Oregon aviator Gerald Lester Murphy in Ciudad Trujillo last December 3 and the disappearance of Columbia University teacher Dr. Jesus Galindez from New York about two years ago.
records.summary_es: El Departamento de Estado informó que solicitó a la República Dominicana el 2 de mayo poner al general Arturo R. Espaillat, funcionario dominicano y excónsul general en Nueva York, a disposición de un tribunal de los Estados Unidos en relación con la investigación del caso Galíndez-Murphy. La petición, descrita como sin precedentes en la historia diplomática estadounidense, no ha recibido respuesta de las autoridades dominicanas. La gestión diplomática surgió a partir de las pesquisas sobre la desaparición del aviador de Oregón Gerald Lester Murphy en Ciudad Trujillo el pasado 3 de diciembre y la del profesor de la Universidad de Columbia doctor Jesús Galíndez en Nueva York hace aproximadamente dos años.

records.headline: A news report notes that the Dominican government claimed American pilot
records.summary_en: A news report notes that the Dominican government claimed American pilot Murphy was pushed into shark-infested Dominican waters during a fight with a Dominican aviator who subsequently committed suicide, following congressional statements identifying Murphy as having flown Galindez to the Dominican Republic. In response, the AFL-CIO Council expressed deep shock at these "monstrous crimes" and demanded federal action against Trujillo's operatives. The labor organization called on the United States government to adopt strong measures preventing the activities of dictator Trujillo's agents in the country and urged Congress to initiate a full-scale investigation into the Galindez-Murphy case and its ramifications.
records.summary_es: Una crónica periodística señala que el gobierno dominicano afirmó que el piloto estadounidense Murphy fue arrojado a aguas dominicanas infestadas de tiburones durante una pelea con un aviador dominicano que posteriormente se suicidó, tras declaraciones en el Congreso que identificaron a Murphy como quien transportó a Galíndez a la República Dominicana. En respuesta, el Consejo de la AFL-CIO expresó su profunda conmoción por estos "crímenes monstruosos" y exigió acciones federales contra los agentes trujillistas. La organización sindical pidió al gobierno de los Estados Unidos adoptar medidas enérgicas para impedir las actividades de los agentes del dictador Trujillo en el país e instó al Congreso a iniciar una investigación exhaustiva del caso Galíndez-Murphy y todas sus ramificaciones.

records.headline: President Eisenhower accepted the credentials of Dominican Ambassador Manuel de Moya Alonzo
records.summary_en: President Eisenhower accepted the credentials of Dominican Ambassador Manuel de Moya Alonzo in Washington, expressing pleasure at assurances that the Dominican Republic remains firm in its alliance with the United States and the Western world against communism. Eisenhower emphasized the historical bonds uniting the two countries while making no mention of the controversy surrounding the disappearance of American pilot Gerald Lester Murphy. Although the Dominican government maintained Murphy was killed by pilot R. de la Maza, who subsequently committed suicide, the State Department has refused to accept that explanation. A separate note in the passage mentions a Dominican naval delegation led by Rear Admiral Rafael B. Richardson, Chief of Staff of the Navy, consisting of officers, 36 subaltern officers, 20 marines, 30 army cadets, and 400 soldiers and sailors aboard visiting vessels.

Eisenhower destacó los vínculos históricos que unen a ambas naciones sin hacer alusión a la controversia sobre la desaparición del piloto estadounidense Gerald Lester Murphy. Aunque el gobierno dominicano sostuvo que Murphy fue muerto por el piloto R. de la Maza, quien posteriormente se suicidó, el Departamento de Estado se ha negado a aceptar dicha explicación. Richardson, jefe de Estado Mayor de la Marina, integrada por oficiales, 36 oficiales subalternos, 20 infantes de marina, 30 cadetes del ejército y 400 soldados y marineros a bordo de embarcaciones visitantes.

records.headline: A State Department statement disclosed allegations that the death of Dominican citizen
records.summary_en: A State Department statement disclosed allegations that the death of Dominican citizen Octavio de la Maza was not a suicide, but rather a murder resulting from a knife wound in the abdomen. The United States Embassy in Ciudad Trujillo was first notified of the death at 11:45 a.m. on January 7, 1957, after being told he had committed suicide at 4 a.m. Independent information gathered by embassy officials indicated De la Maza's body was transported for burial to a town sixty miles away, where two American officers examined the corpse and observed a wound on the left side three inches above the waistline, alongside neck bruising consistent with strangulation. The department concluded that all it knows with certainty is that De la Maza died within the territory of the Dominican Republic.

Información independiente obtenida por funcionarios de la embajada indicó que el cuerpo de De la Maza fue trasladado para su entierro a una localidad situada a sesenta millas de distancia, donde dos oficiales estadounidenses examinaron el cadáver y observaron una herida en el costado izquierdo a tres pulgadas por encima de la cintura, además de hematomas en el cuello compatibles con estrangulamiento. El departamento concluyó que lo único que sabe con certeza es que De la Maza falleció dentro del territorio de la República Dominicana.

records.full_text:
Hundreds Flee In Fear Of New Haiti Violence

PORT AU PRINCE, Haiti, June 19 (AP).—Hundreds of workers and peasants have fled this seething capital city in fear that fresh violence may erupt.

Loaded with personal belongings, they began streaming out of Port au Prince yesterday as the ruling military junta started jailing political partisans on a wide scale.

Those fleeing to the countryside included supporters of both presidential candidate Louis Dejoie and his arch rival, ousted Provisional President Daniel Fignole.

Seek to Bar Strikes

Mr. Dejoie himself was in hiding. Six of his top advisers and scores of his followers were among those arrested.

The military rulers apparently concentrated on Dejoie's backers to keep them from organizing general strikes again. Most business firms in the capital followed orders from Mr. Dejoie in the recurrent strikes staged during the political turmoil that has unseated six governments since December.

The ruling junta has outlawed strikes. Heavily armed troops and police patrolled the streets, forcing stores and shops to remain open.

The junta also pushed a widespread shakeup of the nation's army commands. The junta president, Brig. Gen. Antonio Kebreau, named new commanders for Northern and Southern Haiti and announced a long list of promotions of junior officers.

The junta also kept a sharp eye on 67 former army officers, most of them Dejoie supporters. The officers were ousted by Mr. Fignole before he was deposed last week, and there have been persistent rumors that they might try to topple the junta.

Port Au Prince newspapers published detailed accounts of Mr. Fignole's activities in New York, where he fled after he was overthrown.

Junta Sends $10,000

They said the junta had sent him $10,000 and that he also will receive $500 a month salary. His seven children left behind when Fignole and his wife were hurried out of the country were reported in good health and safe with friends in Port Au Prince.

The number of persons arrested after Saturday's violent riots appeared to be near 2,000, but scores were released after being questioned.

The Dominican Republic became the first nation to recognize the junta government. Dominican Ambassador Porfirio Baseora laughed off reports that police were finding large numbers of Dominican-made arms in searches of homes and vehicles. He said there also are big supplies of American-made arms in Haiti and declared his government never "interferes in the internal affairs of another nation."

American tourists have cleared out of the island.

records.summary_en: A group of twenty-five students from the Agricultural and Technical College in Greensboro, North Carolina, has begun a two-week study tour of Caribbean educational methods. Negro College Group To Visit Caribbean Area

A two-week study of educational methods in the Caribbean is being made by a group of 25 Negro students from the Agricultural and Technical College, Greensboro, North Carolina.

The students fly to San Juan, Puerto Rico, by Pan American World Airways today from Miami, then continue by Clipper to Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic, June 23; to Port au Prince, Haiti, June 26; to Kingston, Jamaica, June 29, and return to Miami from Montego Bay July 6.

records.headline: A feature article describes the Dominican Republic as an agricultural
records.summary_en: A feature article describes the Dominican Republic as an agricultural country and the "Cradle of the Americas," with sugar serving as the primary driver of its economy by supplying over half of export earnings and more than one-third of government revenues. Major agricultural exports include sugar, coffee, cacao, beef, tobacco, molasses, corn, and yucca starch, with milling centered on the southern coastal plain and smaller plantations near Puerto Plata. The capital, Ciudad Trujillo, with a population of 250,000, was founded on the Ozama River in August 1496 under the name Santo Domingo before being renamed in honor of Generalissimo Rafael Leonidas Trujillo. The city blends modern steel-and-concrete buildings with historic colonial sites, including the University of Santo Domingo, the hospital of San Nicolas de Bari, and the Convent of San Francisco.
records.summary_es: Un artículo descriptivo retrata a la República Dominicana como un país agrícola y "Cuna de las Américas", con el azúcar como motor principal de su economía al aportar más de la mitad de los ingresos de exportación y más de un tercio de las rentas gubernamentales. Las principales exportaciones agrícolas abarcan azúcar, café, cacao, carne vacuna, tabaco, melaza, maíz y almidón de yuca, con la molienda concentrada en la llanura costera del sur y plantaciones más pequeñas cerca de Puerto Plata. La capital, Ciudad Trujillo, con una población de 250,000 habitantes, fue fundada a orillas del río Ozama en agosto de 1496 bajo el nombre de Santo Domingo antes de ser rebautizada en honor al generalísimo Rafael Leónidas Trujillo. La urbe combina modernas edificaciones de acero y concreto con monumentos coloniales históricos, entre ellos la Universidad de Santo Domingo, el hospital de San Nicolás de Bari y el convento de San Francisco.

records.summary_en: An editorial column in The People's voice cites a COPE memo listing political grievances that ought to echo in President Eisenhower's ears regarding various controversial administration dealings. Among the listed controversies are disputes over offshore oil, Hells Canyon, Dixon-Yates, and the green sugar deals conducted by the President's brother-in-law with Dictator Trujillo of the Dominican Republic. The commentary contrasts the modern administration's natural resource policies with the conservationist legacy of Theodore Roosevelt.

El comentario contrapone las políticas sobre recursos naturales de la administración moderna con el legado conservacionista de Theodore Roosevelt.

records.headline: Following the disappearance in the Dominican Republic late last year of Murphy
records.summary_en: Following the disappearance in the Dominican Republic late last year of Murphy, who was reported to have assisted in the New York kidnapping of anti-Trujillo figure Jesus Maria de Galindez, Dominican authorities claimed the American aviator was killed in a fight with a Dominican pilot and produced an alleged suicide note from that pilot. The United States Government branded the note a forgery and previously requested that the Dominican Republic waive diplomatic immunity for former New York Consul General Gen. Arturo R. Espaillat so he could be questioned. After Dominican officials refused the waiver but proposed making Espaillat available on Dominican soil, United States officials are considering accepting the offer.

records.headline: Representative Reece, a former Republican National Committee chairman
records.summary_en: Representative Reece, a former Republican National Committee chairman from Tennessee, strongly criticized Representative Porter in the House of Representatives for his attacks on Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, described as the Dominican Republic strongman. Reece charged that Porter was meddling in the internal affairs of sovereign nations to the detriment of American interests by attempting to cut off United States foreign aid to Latin American dictatorships. Warning that well-meaning persons could become unwitting agents of communism, Reece maintained that his principal aim was upholding the nation's historical policy of non-intervention.

Reece acusó a Porter de inmiscuirse en los asuntos internos de naciones soberanas en perjuicio de los intereses estadounidenses al intentar recortar la ayuda exterior de los Estados Unidos a las dictaduras latinoamericanas. Al advertir que personas bienintencionadas podrían convertirse en agentes involuntarios del comunismo, Reece sostuvo que su objetivo principal era salvaguardar la histórica política nacional de no intervención.

records.headline: Sydney S. Baron announced his resignation from Tammany Hall after
records.summary_en: Sydney S. Baron announced his resignation from Tammany Hall after New York Governor Harriman and Mayor Wagner insisted he could not represent both the political organization and the Dominican Republic. The Dominican government had retained Baron to conduct a public goodwill campaign in the United States and organize an inquiry into the disappearance of Dr. Jesus de Galindez, a Columbia University lecturer and critic of Rafael Trujillo who vanished in New York sixteen months earlier. While Trujillo and his administration denied accusations that Galindez was abducted and murdered, Tammany leader Mr. DeSapio agreed that Baron should resign under the circumstances.

records.headline: In his book "The Era of Trujillo of the Dominican Republic," Dr. de Galindez
records.summary_en: In his book "The Era of Trujillo of the Dominican Republic," Dr. de Galindez outlined extensive charges against the regime of Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo prior to his disappearance. Galindez accused the government of hiring assassins who murdered political opponents abroad, including two killings in New York City, and of encouraging the formation of a Communist Party as late as 1949. records.headline: Dr. de Galindez recounts Rafael Trujillo's progression from a young
records.summary_en: Dr. de Galindez recounts Rafael Trujillo's progression from a young telegrapher during the 1919 United States Marine landing to commanding general of the Dominican army. According to Galindez, President Horacio Vasquez never suspected Trujillo until it was too late, resigning following the coup of March 2, 1930. The account quotes a report by United States Minister Charles B. Curtis asserting that Trujillo transferred arms from the Santo Domingo fort to Santiago while actively conspiring with revolutionary forces.
records.summary_es: El doctor de Galíndez relata la trayectoria de Rafael Trujillo desde que era un joven telegrafista durante el desembarco de la Infantería de Marina de los Estados Unidos en 1919 hasta llegar a comandante general del ejército dominicano. Según Galíndez, el presidente Horacio Vásquez nunca sospechó de Trujillo hasta que fue demasiado tarde, renunciando tras el golpe del 2 de marzo de 1930. El relato cita un informe del ministro estadounidense Charles B. Curtis en el que aseguraba que Trujillo trasladó armas del fuerte de Santo Domingo a Santiago mientras conspiraba activamente con las fuerzas revolucionarias.

records.headline: Dr. de Galindez characterizes the Dominican Republic as a personal
records.summary_en: Dr. de Galindez characterizes the Dominican Republic as a personal dictatorship and tyranny, describing the government as "a great farm that belongs to Trujillo" with a constitution functioning only as a facade. The passage details pervasive nepotism, noting that Trujillo's son Rafael L. Trujillo-Martinez was commissioned an army colonel at age 5, while brother Hector B. holds the presidency. Galindez also asserts that New York City police possess sufficient evidence to convict Trujillo operatives of two political murders: the April 28, 1935 slaying of former secretary of war Sergio Bencosme and the October 2, 1952 killing of exile Andres Requena.
records.summary_es: El doctor de Galíndez califica a la República Dominicana de dictadura personal y tiranía, describiendo al gobierno como "una gran finca que pertenece a Trujillo" con una constitución que funciona meramente como fachada. El pasaje detalla un nepotismo generalizado, señalando que el hijo de Trujillo, Rafael L. Trujillo-Martínez, fue nombrado coronel del ejército a los 5 años, mientras que su hermano Héctor B. ocupa la presidencia. Galíndez afirma además que la policía de la ciudad de Nueva York dispone de pruebas suficientes para condenar a agentes de Trujillo por dos homicidios políticos: el asesinato el 28 de abril de 1935 del exsecretario de guerra Sergio Bencosme y la muerte el 2 de octubre de 1952 del exiliado Andrés Requena.

records.headline: Following public controversy over the reported murder in the Dominican Republic of American pilot
records.summary_en: Following public controversy over the reported murder in the Dominican Republic of American pilot Gerald L. Murphy, who was believed to have flown Dr. de Galindez out of the United States, Rafael Trujillo hired two American lawyers to conduct an inquiry into the affair. Former presidential aide Morris L. Ernst of New York and former New York State Supreme Court justice William H. Munson of Buffalo were retained to perform an all-out investigation. With United States-Dominican diplomatic relations strained by the scandal, the Trujillo regime sought to demonstrate its innocence against the allegations.
records.summary_es: Tras la controversia pública por el reportado asesinato en la República Dominicana del piloto estadounidense Gerald L. Murphy, de quien se creía que había transportado al doctor de Galíndez fuera de los Estados Unidos, Rafael Trujillo contrató a dos abogados estadounidenses para realizar una investigación sobre el asunto. El exasistente presidencial Morris L. Ernst de Nueva York y el exjuez de la Corte Suprema del Estado de Nueva York William H. Munson de Buffalo fueron contratados para llevar a cabo una investigación exhaustiva. Con las relaciones diplomáticas entre Estados Unidos y la República Dominicana deterioradas por el escándalo, el régimen de Trujillo intentó demostrar su inocencia frente a las acusaciones.

records.headline: A Varig airlines Super Constellation ditched in waters 300 yards
records.summary_en: A Varig airlines Super Constellation ditched in waters 300 yards off the northern coast of the Dominican Republic after departing Ciudad Trujillo for New York. The aircraft had arrived from Buenos Aires with its No. 2 engine out and discharged 33 passengers at Ciudad Trujillo before taking off for repairs under Captain Geraldo Kippling. Approximately one hour into the flight, progressive engine failure reduced the airliner to one functioning engine, leaving the crew unable to reach the north coast airport at Puerto Plata before coming down.
records.summary_es: Un Super Constellation de la aerolínea Varig amerizó en aguas a 300 yardas de la costa norte de la República Dominicana tras despegar de Ciudad Trujillo con destino a Nueva York. El avión había llegado de Buenos Aires con su motor No. 2 averiado y desembarcó a 33 pasajeros en Ciudad Trujillo antes de salir para reparaciones bajo el mando del capitán Geraldo Kippling. Alrededor de una hora después del despegue, fallas progresivas en los motores redujeron la aeronave a un solo motor en funcionamiento, impidiendo a la tripulación llegar al aeropuerto de Puerto Plata en la costa norte antes de caer al agua.

records.headline: Major General Arturo Espaillat, Dominican Minister of Security
records.summary_en: Major General Arturo Espaillat, Dominican Minister of Security, sought by the United States government for questioning in the disappearance of Dr. Jesus de Galindez, issued an ultimatum requiring Jehovah's Witnesses missionaries to sever ties with Brooklyn or leave the country. President Hector Trujillo signed a law on July 25 prohibiting the group's religious activities, imposing penalties of one to three months imprisonment and fines from thirty to one hundred dollars, backed by an appropriation of over $1 million. Representative Bennie Crump stated that around 250 Witnesses were interrogated and about 50 imprisoned amid beatings and police violence.
records.summary_es: El mayor general Arturo Espaillat, ministro de Seguridad dominicano, a quien el gobierno de los Estados Unidos busca interrogar por la desaparición del doctor Jesús de Galíndez, emitió un ultimátum exigiendo a los misioneros testigos de Jehová cortar nexos con Brooklyn o salir del país. El presidente Héctor Trujillo promulgó una ley el 25 de julio prohibiendo las actividades religiosas del grupo, con penas de uno a tres meses de prisión y multas de treinta a cien dólares, respaldada por una asignación de más de $1 millón. El representante Bennie Crump informó que unos 250 testigos fueron interrogados y alrededor de 50 encarcelados en medio de golpizas y violencia policial.

records.headline: A Varig Airlines Super Constellation carrying ten crewmen ditched
records.summary_en: A Varig Airlines Super Constellation carrying ten crewmen ditched approximately 300 yards off the Dominican north coast after departing Ciudad Trujillo for New York City. The aircraft had arrived from Buenos Aires with its No. 2 engine out and discharged 32 passengers in Ciudad Trujillo before proceeding toward New York for repairs under Capt. Gerald Rippling. After reporting engine failure that left only one functioning engine, Rippling attempted to return to the Puerto Plata airport but lacked power to reach land, and crewman Oswaldo Scherer vanished after the fuselage broke in two upon impact.
records.summary_es: Un Super Constellation de Varig Airlines con diez tripulantes amerizó a unas 300 yardas de la costa norte dominicana tras despegar de Ciudad Trujillo con rumbo a la ciudad de Nueva York. La aeronave había llegado de Buenos Aires con su motor No. 2 inoperativo y desembarcó a 32 pasajeros en Ciudad Trujillo antes de seguir hacia Nueva York para reparaciones al mando del capitán Gerald Rippling. Tras reportar fallas que lo dejaron con un solo motor en funcionamiento, Rippling intentó regresar al aeropuerto de Puerto Plata pero no tuvo potencia para llegar a tierra, y el tripulante Oswaldo Scherer desapareció al partirse el fuselaje en dos con el impacto.

records.headline: Eugene D. Roehm, presiding minister of the Key West congregation of Jehovah's Witnesses
records.summary_en: Eugene D. Roehm, presiding minister of the Key West congregation of Jehovah's Witnesses, reported that ten American missionaries were deported from the Dominican Republic to Puerto Rico on August 3. Dominican authorities paid their airfare and escorted them to the aircraft under arrest following an ultimatum issued by Minister of Security Major General Arturo Espaillat. Church officials stated that the expulsion followed intense religious persecution that ended Bible education work conducted in the Dominican Republic since 1945, noting that Espaillat is sought by the United States government for questioning regarding a missing critic.
records.summary_es: Eugene D. Roehm, ministro presidente de la congregación de los testigos de Jehová en Cayo Hueso, informó que diez misioneros estadounidenses fueron deportados de la República Dominicana a Puerto Rico el 3 de agosto. Las autoridades dominicanas pagaron sus pasajes de avión y los custodiaron bajo arresto hasta la nave tras un ultimátum emitido por el ministro de Seguridad, mayor general Arturo Espaillat. Representantes de la denominación religiosa manifestaron que la expulsión se produjo tras una intensa persecución que canceló la labor de educación bíblica llevada a cabo en la República Dominicana desde 1945, destacando que los Estados Unidos buscan interrogar a Espaillat acerca de un crítico desaparecido.

Held, presiding minister of the West Columbus congregation of Jehovah's Witnesses, announced the deportation of 10 American missionaries from the Dominican Republic to Puerto Rico on August 8. records.full_text:
Dominican Gov. Bans Missionaries Of Jehovah's Witnesses

Ten American missionaries were deported to Puerto Rico from the Dominican Republic August 3, Edwin Long, presiding minister of the Exmore congregation of Jehovah's Witnesses, announced yesterday. Fare was paid by the Dominican government and the missionaries were escorted under arrest to the plane.

Action came on the heels of "a wave of persecution equaled only in Communist countries" climaxed by a total ban proscribing the work of Bible education conducted by the Witnesses in the Dominican Republic since 1945.

An ultimatum to the Christian missionaries to renounce all association with the organization and cease communication with their Brooklyn, N. Y., office or leave the country was made last month by Major General Arturo Espaillat, Minister of Security, whom the U. S. government has sought to question in the disappearance of Dr. Jesus de Galindez. Some of the missionaries have been in the country for 11 years.

According to official news sources of the Dominican Republic, proscription of the Christian activity of Jehovah's Witnesses was legalized by President Hector Trujillo on July 25 and the law carries penalties of from one to three months imprisonment with fines from thirty to one hundred dollars. It was announced that over $1 million had been appropriated by the Dominican government to enforce the ban.

Mr. Long said a full-scale campaign to restrict the religious freedom of the Witnesses has been underway since July 1st. Kingdom Hall meeting places had been ordered closed and about 250 of Jehovah's Witnesses were brought in for questioning. The Witnesses have been subjected to beatings and violence by police and prison guards in an effort to make them renounce all association with the movement, Mr. Long stated. About 59 are now in prison, with sentences of two years.

records.headline: A total prohibition against Bible education work conducted by Jehovah's Witnesses
records.summary_en: A total prohibition against Bible education work conducted by Jehovah's Witnesses in the Dominican Republic since 1945 led to widespread detentions and deportations. Major General Espaillat, the Dominican minister of security sought by the United States government for questioning in the disappearance of Dr. Jesus de Galindez, issued an ultimatum requiring missionaries to renounce the organization or depart. President Hector Trujillo formalized the ban on July 25 under legislation imposing penalties of one to three months imprisonment and fines of $30 to $100, supported by an appropriation of over one million dollars, while church representative Mr. Vallancourt reported that about 250 members were questioned and about fifty imprisoned.
records.summary_es: Una proscripción absoluta contra la labor de educación bíblica desarrollada por los testigos de Jehová en la República Dominicana desde 1945 desencadenó detenciones y deportaciones generalizadas. El mayor general Espaillat, ministro de Seguridad dominicano solicitado por el gobierno de los Estados Unidos para declarar sobre la desaparición del doctor Jesús de Galíndez, emitió un ultimátum exigiendo a los misioneros renunciar a la organización o marcharse. El presidente Héctor Trujillo formalizó la prohibición el 25 de julio en virtud de una legislación que castiga con penas de uno a tres meses de cárcel y multas de $30 a $100, con el apoyo de una partida presupuestaria de más de un millón de dólares, mientras que el representante eclesial señor Vallancourt comunicó que unos 250 miembros fueron interrogados y cerca de cincuenta encarcelados.

records.headline: Unconfirmed reports in Colombia indicated that former dictator
records.summary_en: Unconfirmed reports in Colombia indicated that former dictator General Rojas had arrived in the Dominican Republic with intentions of returning to his country after fleeing to Spain following his ouster last May. The ruling military junta in Bogota announced it would not permit Rojas to return, instructing the Colombian Ambassador in Ciudad Trujillo to warn the ex-dictator that armed forces would bar his re-entry. In response to the rumors, maritime authorities established a coastal watch at Barranquilla, and hundreds of students marched through Bogota in protest.
records.summary_es: Informes no confirmados en Colombia indicaron que el exdictador general Rojas había llegado a la República Dominicana con la intención de regresar a su país luego de haber huido a España tras ser depuesto el pasado mayo. La junta militar gobernante en Bogotá anunció que no toleraría el retorno de Rojas, instruyendo al embajador colombiano en Ciudad Trujillo para advertir al exdictador que las fuerzas armadas impedirían su reingreso. Como respuesta a los rumores, las autoridades marítimas dispusieron una vigilancia costera en Barranquilla y cientos de estudiantes marcharon por Bogotá en señal de protesta.

records.headline: Six additional members of the Jehovah's Witnesses sect have been placed
records.summary_en: Six additional members of the Jehovah's Witnesses sect have been placed under arrest in the Dominican Republic—identified in the headline as Dominica—since August 3rd. On that date ten were seized and deported, according to an announcement by Emil Van Daalen from his headquarters in Puerto Rico. Van Daalen is director of the Puerto Rico Watch Tower Society, an affiliate of Jehovah's Witnesses with headquarters in Brooklyn, New York.

En esa fecha diez fueron apresados y deportados, según anunció Emil Van Daalen desde su sede en Puerto Rico. Van Daalen es director de la Sociedad Watch Tower de Puerto Rico, una filial de los testigos de Jehová con sede en Brooklyn, Nueva York.

records.summary_en: Jules Dubois, Chairman of the Freedom of the Press Committee of the Inter American Press Association, was called an "undesirable adventurer" and forbidden entry to the Dominican Republic. records.headline: Former Colombian President General Gustavo Rojas Pinilla told
records.summary_en: Former Colombian President General Gustavo Rojas Pinilla told the press in Ciudad Trujillo that he was amazed at the extraordinary progress achieved by General Trujillo in his 27 years of government. Rojas Pinilla declared that under Trujillo's direction and control, the Dominican Republic would in a few years become the example of America. The visiting general also commented on the critical situation in Colombia, noted his earlier reception in Madrid by Generalissimo Franco, and stated that only God knows whether he will return to Colombia.
records.summary_es: El expresidente colombiano, general Gustavo Rojas Pinilla, declaró a la prensa en Ciudad Trujillo que estaba asombrado por el extraordinario progreso alcanzado por el general Trujillo en sus 27 años de gobierno. Rojas Pinilla afirmó que bajo la dirección y el control de Trujillo, la República Dominicana se convertirá en pocos años en el ejemplo de América. El general visitante también comentó sobre la crítica situación en Colombia, destacó su recibimiento previo en Madrid por el generalísimo Franco y expresó que solo Dios sabe si regresará a Colombia.

records.headline: General Gustavo Rojas Pinilla, deposed dictator of Colombia
records.summary_en: General Gustavo Rojas Pinilla, deposed dictator of Colombia, returned by plane to Madrid on September 30 after a 20-day trip to the Dominican Republic. General Rojas stated that his journey had been exclusively on business affairs, dispelling rumors that he was en route back to Colombia to attempt a return to power. During a stopover in San Juan on his return flight, he told newsmen that he had traveled to Ciudad Trujillo to sell a farm he owns in the Dominican Republic.
records.summary_es: El general Gustavo Rojas Pinilla, depuesto dictador de Colombia, regresó en avión a Madrid el 30 de septiembre tras un viaje de 20 días a la República Dominicana. El general Rojas declaró que su viaje había sido exclusivamente por asuntos de negocios, disipando los rumores de que se dirigía de regreso a Colombia para intentar volver al poder. Durante una escala en San Juan en su vuelo de regreso, dijo a los periodistas que había viajado a Ciudad Trujillo para vender una finca de su propiedad en la República Dominicana.

records.headline: Gustavo Rojas Pinilla, former Colombian President, departed
records.summary_en: Gustavo Rojas Pinilla, former Colombian President, departed Madrid for Las Palmas, Canary Islands, aboard an Iberia plane on October 1 to establish his residence in exile. He had arrived the previous day from Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic, where according to reports received in Madrid he had been negotiating the sale of goods he possesses in Colombia. His family had remained in Las Palmas during his absence.
records.summary_es: Gustavo Rojas Pinilla, el expresidente colombiano, partió de Madrid hacia Las Palmas, Islas Canarias, a bordo de un avión de Iberia el 1 de octubre para fijar su residencia en el exilio. Había llegado el día anterior procedente de Ciudad Trujillo, República Dominicana, donde según las informaciones recibidas en Madrid había estado negociando la venta de bienes que posee en Colombia. Su familia había permanecido en Las Palmas durante su ausencia.

records.headline: The Dominican Republic government has restored the 447-year-old
records.summary_en: The Dominican Republic government has restored the 447-year-old Alcazar palace in Ciudad Trujillo to its original splendor, with public opening scheduled for October 12, the anniversary of the discovery of America. Built by Diego Columbus, son of Christopher Columbus, the palace will serve as an international museum and repository for Columbiana relics, furnished with authentic imported Spanish colonial furnishings and tapestries. Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo commissioned four prominent Spanish architects to complete the reconstruction. Hotels Embajador and Jaragua are preparing for the influx of tourists and pilgrims visiting the republic for the Columbus Day festivities.
records.summary_es: El gobierno de la República Dominicana ha restaurado a su esplendor original el palacio del Alcázar, de 447 años de antigüedad, en Ciudad Trujillo, con su apertura al público programada para el 12 de octubre, aniversario del descubrimiento de América. Construido por Diego Colón, hijo de Cristóbal Colón, el palacio servirá como museo internacional y depósito de reliquias colombinas, amueblado con auténticos muebles y tapices coloniales españoles importados. El generalísimo Rafael L. Trujillo encomendó a cuatro destacados arquitectos españoles la conclusión de la reconstrucción. Los hoteles Embajador y Jaragua se preparan para la afluencia de turistas y peregrinos que visitan la república para las festividades del Día de la Raza.

records.headline: In letters instructing his followers on measures to regain power
records.summary_en: In letters instructing his followers on measures to regain power in Argentina, exiled dictator Juan Peron wrote that his main interest was to defend Generalissimo Trujillo, who was assisting his cause and had provided effective help in his personal affairs. Peron urged that a campaign be directed against Chicago Tribune correspondent Jules Dubois, chairman of the Inter American Press Association committee on press freedom. According to the letters, a pamphlet containing three Dominican Republic editorials attacking the association and branding Dubois "the Black Beast" was sent to Rio de Janeiro to coordinate action with the Dominican ambassador. Dubois responded that the attack was an honor coming from the man who seized the newspaper La Prensa and shut down more than 100 newspapers.
records.summary_es: En cartas donde instruía a sus seguidores sobre medidas para recuperar el poder en Argentina, el exiliado dictador Juan Perón escribió que su principal interés era defender al generalísimo Trujillo, quien colaboraba con su causa y le había brindado una ayuda eficaz en sus asuntos personales. Perón instó a que se dirigiera una campaña contra el corresponsal del Chicago Tribune, Jules Dubois, presidente de la comisión de libertad de prensa de la Sociedad Interamericana de Prensa. Según las cartas, un panfleto con tres editoriales de la República Dominicana que atacaban a la asociación y tachaban a Dubois de "la Bestia Negra" fue enviado a Río de Janeiro para coordinar acciones con el embajador dominicano. Dubois respondió que este ataque era un honor viniendo del hombre que confiscó el diario La Prensa y clausuró más de 100 periódicos.

records.headline: The convention of the Inter American Press Association unanimously
records.summary_en: The convention of the Inter American Press Association unanimously adopted resolutions urging continuous campaigns for freedom of expression in Venezuela, Paraguay, and the Dominican Republic. The assembly also called for the removal of all press restrictions in Bolivia, Nicaragua, and Cuba. In addition, the organization unanimously urged the United States government to publish the results of its investigation into the disappearance of Jesus de Galindez, an avowed opponent of Dominican strongman Rafael Trujillo.

La asamblea también exigió la eliminación de todas las restricciones a la prensa en Bolivia, Nicaragua y Cuba. Asimismo, la organización instó por unanimidad al gobierno de los Estados Unidos a publicar los resultados de su investigación sobre la desaparición de Jesús de Galíndez, declarado adversario del hombre fuerte dominicano Rafael Trujillo.

records.headline: Leon Snider, owner of the Electric Appliance Company in Quincy
records.summary_en: Leon Snider, owner of the Electric Appliance Company in Quincy, and his wife were awarded an all-expense-paid birthday vacation to Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic, by General Electric's Small Appliance division. The Sniders traveled alongside 376 other dealers and their wives, a group requiring nine plane flights each way. Arriving after an evening flight from Miami on October 20, the couple spent five days touring the Dominican Republic, visiting the tomb containing the remains of Columbus and observing local products and modern capital architecture before returning to Quincy.
records.summary_es: Leon Snider, propietario de la Electric Appliance Company en Quincy, y su esposa recibieron unas vacaciones de cumpleaños con todos los gastos pagados a Ciudad Trujillo, República Dominicana, otorgadas por la división de pequeños electrodomésticos de General Electric. Los Snider viajaron junto a otros 376 distribuidores y sus esposas, un grupo que requirió nueve vuelos de avión de ida y vuelta. Tras llegar después de un vuelo nocturno desde Miami el 20 de octubre, la pareja pasó cinco días recorriendo la República Dominicana, visitando la tumba que contiene los restos de Colón y observando los productos locales y la arquitectura moderna de la capital antes de regresar a Quincy.

records.headline: An editorial from the Washington Daily News quoted in the paper
records.summary_en: An editorial from the Washington Daily News quoted in the paper criticizes United States Senator Johnston for supporting the regime of the Dominican Republic and condemning federal investigations. The paper asserts that Johnston's report attacks the State Department and Justice Department, including J. Edgar Hoover's FBI agents, for investigating the mysterious disappearance of anti-Trujillo professor Jesus de Galindez and the linked death of American pilot Gerald Murphy. While acknowledging that the Dominican regime opposes communism, the editorial states that it remains an implacable enemy of democracy, representative government, civil liberties, and free speech.
records.summary_es: Un editorial del Washington Daily News citado en el periódico critica al senador estadounidense Johnston por apoyar al régimen de la República Dominicana y condenar las investigaciones federales. El diario afirma que el informe de Johnston ataca al Departamento de Estado y al Departamento de Justicia, incluidos los agentes del FBI de J. Edgar Hoover, por investigar la misteriosa desaparición del profesor antitrujillista Jesús de Galíndez y la vinculada muerte del piloto estadounidense Gerald Murphy. Si bien reconoce que el régimen dominicano es adversario del comunismo, el editorial señala que sigue siendo un enemigo implacable de la democracia, el gobierno representativo, las libertades civiles y la libertad de expresión.

records.headline: International Telephone and Telegraph Corporation has completed
records.summary_en: International Telephone and Telegraph Corporation has completed a 238-mile "electronic bridge" providing six two-way telephone channels between Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic. Connecting San Juan and Ciudad Trujillo, the over-the-horizon microwave radio link represents the world's third commercial system of its kind. An engineer with Federal Telecommunication Laboratories, the research unit that designed the system, highlighted its technical operation. The installation was completed to meet growing telephone demands resulting from the influx of industries and increased tourist trade.
records.summary_es: La International Telephone and Telegraph Corporation completó un "puente electrónico" de 238 millas que proporciona seis canales telefónicos bidireccionales entre Puerto Rico y la República Dominicana. Al conectar San Juan y Ciudad Trujillo, el enlace de radio por microondas más allá del horizonte constituye el tercer sistema comercial de este tipo en el mundo. Un ingeniero de los Federal Telecommunication Laboratories, la unidad de investigación que diseñó el sistema, destacó su funcionamiento técnico. La instalación se llevó a cabo para responder a la creciente demanda telefónica provocada por la llegada de industrias y el incremento del comercio turístico.

records.headline: Nicholas Silfa, secretary general of the New York branch of the Dominican Democratic Workers Committee
records.summary_en: Nicholas Silfa, secretary general of the New York branch of the Dominican Democratic Workers Committee in Exile, protested the sudden cancellation of a Catholic mass scheduled in New York. Silfa stated that the 9 a.m. service was sought solely to invoke divine blessings for the health and welfare of Dominican Catholic workers and their families both in exile and in the Dominican Republic, denying any political involvement. In a letter to Francis Cardinal Spellman, Archbishop of New York, Silfa called the cancellation shocking and disappointing. The report notes that Silfa is among those who have accused the Dominican government of responsibility for the March 1956 disappearance of Dr. Jesus de Galindez, a Columbia University lecturer and critic of Dominican dictator Rafael Trujillo.
records.summary_es: Nicolás Silfa, secretario general de la filial neoyorquina del Comité de Obreros Democráticos Dominicanos en el Exilio, protestó por la repentina cancelación de una misa católica programada en Nueva York. Silfa afirmó que el servicio de las 9 a. m. se había solicitado únicamente para implorar bendiciones divinas por la salud y el bienestar de los trabajadores católicos dominicanos y sus familias tanto en el exilio como en la República Dominicana, desmintiendo cualquier implicación política. En una carta dirigida a Francis Cardenal Spellman, arzobispo de Nueva York, Silfa calificó la cancelación de impactante y decepcionante. El informe señala que Silfa figura entre quienes han responsabilizado al gobierno dominicano por la desaparición en marzo de 1956 del doctor Jesús de Galíndez, profesor de la Universidad de Columbia y crítico del dictador dominicano Rafael Trujillo.

records.headline: A reprinted newspaper editorial severely criticizes a Senate subcommittee
records.summary_en: A reprinted newspaper editorial severely criticizes a Senate subcommittee report submitted by Senator Olin Johnston of South Carolina for defending General Rafael Trujillo, whom it describes as the despot of the Dominican Republic. The editorial states that while communist penetration in the hemisphere causes legitimate concern, excusing Trujillo's abuses is inexcusable, observing that similar arguments of bringing order were made on behalf of Stalin in Russia. The editorial condemns Johnston for praising the Dominican Republic while erroneously designating Costa Rica as a communist headquarters. It concludes that the Senate subcommittee would do better to investigate why so many exiled critics of General Trujillo end up in the morgue.
records.summary_es: Un editorial periodístico reproducido critica severamente un informe de un subcomité del Senado presentado por el senador Olin Johnston de Carolina del Sur por defender al general Rafael Trujillo, a quien califica como el déspota de la República Dominicana. El editorial afirma que, si bien la penetración comunista en el hemisferio causa legítima inquietud, excusar los abusos de Trujillo resulta inexcusable, observando que argumentos similares sobre implantar el orden se formularon a favor de Stalin en Rusia. El editorial condena a Johnston por elogiar a la República Dominicana mientras designaba erróneamente a Costa Rica como sede del comunismo. Concluye que el subcomité del Senado haría mejor en investigar por qué tantos críticos exiliados del general Trujillo terminan en la morgue.
