records.headline: A District Court jury was told that Washington attorney John Joseph
records.summary_en: A District Court jury was told that Washington attorney John Joseph Frank, accused of acting illegally as an agent of the Dominican Republic, volunteered in 1956 to supply information about Dominican activities to the Federal Bureau of Investigation. FBI Agent Fred Woodcocke testified on the second day of Frank's trial that the attorney stated in a 1956 interview that his initial contact with Dominican Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo resulted from a 1954 tip from a State Department official regarding Trujillo's planned trip to Europe. Woodcocke testified that Frank identified Robert Cartwright, then connected with the State Department, as the official who provided the tip.
records.summary_es: Un jurado de un tribunal de distrito fue informado de que el abogado de Washington John Joseph Frank, acusado de actuar ilegalmente como agente de la República Dominicana, se ofreció en 1956 a suministrar información sobre actividades dominicanas a la Oficina Federal de Investigaciones. El agente del FBI Fred Woodcocke declaró en el segundo día del juicio de Frank que el abogado afirmó en una entrevista de 1956 que su contacto inicial con el generalísimo dominicano Rafael Trujillo derivó de un dato facilitado en 1954 por un funcionario del Departamento de Estado sobre el viaje planeado de Trujillo a Europa. Woodcocke testificó que Frank identificó a Robert Cartwright, entonces vinculado al Departamento de Estado, como el funcionario que suministró el aviso.

records.summary_en: In the trial of attorney John Frank, Justice Department attorney Plato Cacherls questioned Dr. Ornes regarding the internal organization of the Dominican Republic, prompting Ornes to state that there was confusion between the national treasury and Generalissimo Trujillo's pockets. Defense counsel Edward L. Carey objected, leading Judge James R. Kirkland to overrule the objection before retracting and apologizing to the jury for commenting that a dictator may in fact be the national government. In earlier testimony, FBI agent Fred Woodcocke stated that Frank said in a 1956 interview he represented two private firms located in Dominica, one of which Ornes classified as a Trujillo corporation linked with the Dominican government. Dr. Ornes also testified concerning his acquaintance with Dr. Jesus de Galindez, a Columbia University professor and critic of Trujillo who disappeared in March, 1956.

records.headline: During the trial of John Frank, testimony addressed allegations
records.summary_en: During the trial of John Frank, testimony addressed allegations that former Dominican official Dr. German Ornes had absconded with $14,000 belonging to his newspaper, El Caribe, a case that Mr. Ambrose stated was dismissed because the United States attorney lacked authority to act. Witness Mr. Fox testified that Frank told him in a summer 1955 letter that he was doing legal work with the Dominican Embassy in Washington, D.C., while handling the rental of Fox's home. Concluding his testimony, Ornes told the jury that there is no freedom of the press in the Dominican Republic and explained that he left the country after losing control over the editorial policy of El Caribe, which he bought in 1954. Ornes denied accusations by defense attorney Edward L. Carey that he stole the $14,000, maintaining that as sole owner he was entitled to the funds, and reiterated that he broke with Trujillo after the Dominican strong man had his brother imprisoned.
records.summary_es: Durante el juicio de John Frank, los testimonios abordaron alegaciones de que el exfuncionario dominicano Dr. Germán Ornes se había fugado con $14,000 pertenecientes a su diario, El Caribe, causa que según declaró el señor Ambrose fue desestimada porque el fiscal de los Estados Unidos carecía de competencia para actuar. El testigo Fox declaró que Frank le indicó en una carta durante el verano de 1955 que realizaba trabajo legal para la embajada dominicana en Washington, D.C., mientras administraba el alquiler de la residencia de Fox. Al concluir su declaración, Ornes manifestó al jurado que no existe libertad de prensa en la República Dominicana y explicó que abandonó el país tras perder el control de la línea editorial de El Caribe, rotativo que adquirió en 1954. Ornes rechazó las acusaciones del abogado defensor Edward L. Carey relativas a que había robado los $14,000, sosteniendo que como único propietario tenía derecho a los fondos, y reiteró que rompió con Trujillo después de que el hombre fuerte dominicano encarcelara a su hermano.

records.headline: At the trial of John Frank, Dr. Ornes, resuming his testimony
records.summary_en: At the trial of John Frank, Dr. Ornes, resuming his testimony, stated that under Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo one must approve of the regime or not live long, recalling that he had to assume editorship of a Trujillo-backed newspaper in 1949 "or else." Describing Trujillo as a dictator, Ornes testified that when he broke with the generalissimo in 1955 and came to the United States, he was forced to leave his three children from his first marriage in the Dominican Republic as hostages. He explained that those departing the country must leave loved ones behind to pay retribution if anyone acts against the Dominican government, adding that he does not know where his children are because the regime prevents any contact. In earlier testimony, Dr. Ornes recounted meeting Frank on multiple occasions, including once in Ciudad Trujillo, once in Kansas City during the generalissimo's visit, and once in New York.
records.summary_es: En el juicio de John Frank, el Dr. Ornes, al reanudar su testimonio, declaró que bajo el régimen del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo es necesario aprobar al régimen para no morir pronto, recordando que debió asumir la dirección de un diario respaldado por Trujillo en 1949 «o de lo contrario». Al calificar a Trujillo de dictador, Ornes testificó que al romper con el generalísimo en 1955 y viajar a los Estados Unidos se vio obligado a dejar a sus tres hijos de su primer matrimonio en la República Dominicana como rehenes. Explicó que quienes abandonan el país deben dejar atrás a seres queridos para que respondan si alguien actúa contra el gobierno dominicano, añadiendo que desconoce el paradero de sus hijos porque el régimen impide toda comunicación. En testimonios anteriores, el Dr. Ornes relató haberse reunido con Frank en varias ocasiones, incluyendo una en Ciudad Trujillo, una en Kansas City durante la visita del generalísimo y otra en Nueva York.

records.headline: During the District Court trial in which John Frank was charged
records.summary_en: During the District Court trial in which John Frank was charged with acting illegally as an agent for the Dominican Republic and Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, defense attorney Edward L. Carey asked Judge James R. Kirkland to poll the jury concerning a television program entitled "Suspicion." The program depicted the abduction of an elderly man from the United States to a South American dictatorship. Although juror Mrs. Lyons told Judge Kirkland that she did not connect the broadcast to the Frank proceedings, the judge excused her on his own motion to maintain caution, reiterating his warning to jurors to avoid media coverage related to the case. Another juror was excused due to illness, leaving twelve members in the jury box.
records.summary_es: Durante el juicio en el Tribunal de Distrito en el que se acusó a John Frank de actuar ilegalmente como agente de la República Dominicana y del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo, el abogado defensor Edward L. Carey solicitó al juez James R. Kirkland interrogar al jurado sobre la emisión del programa de televisión titulado «Suspicion». Dicho espacio narraba el secuestro de un anciano desde los Estados Unidos hacia un país sudamericano gobernado por un dictador. Aunque la integrante del jurado señora Lyons aseguró al juez Kirkland que no vinculaba la transmisión con el proceso judicial contra Frank, el magistrado decidió excusarla por iniciativa propia por precaución, reiterando su advertencia a los jurados de evitar coberturas mediáticas relacionadas con la causa. Otro jurado fue apartado debido a una enfermedad, quedando doce miembros en el estrado.

records.headline: Asked whether he considered John Frank an employee of his government
records.summary_en: Asked whether he considered John Frank an employee of his government in connection with charges of acting illegally as an agent for the Dominican Republic, Dominican Ambassador Senor De Moya replied in the negative. De Moya explained that Trujillo desired someone with FBI background to accompany him to Europe and that the State Department recommended Frank, after which Trujillo engaged Frank to reorganize the Dominican Republic's security system. The ambassador initially stated that Frank was paid for this work but subsequently clarified that the compensation consisted of commissions on materials utilized in revamping the security apparatus. The evening prior, De Moya and his wife hosted a dinner at the 1925 F Street Club honoring Assistant Secretary of State for Inter-American Affairs and Mrs. Dick Rubottom.
records.summary_es: Al ser consultado sobre si consideraba a John Frank un empleado de su gobierno en relación con los cargos de actuar ilegalmente como agente de la República Dominicana, el embajador dominicano señor De Moya respondió negativamente. De Moya explicó que Trujillo deseaba a alguien con formación en el FBI para que lo acompañara a Europa y que el Departamento de Estado recomendó a Frank, tras lo cual Trujillo encargó a Frank la reorganización del sistema de seguridad de la República Dominicana. El embajador afirmó inicialmente que Frank recibía un salario por esta labor, pero luego aclaró que la retribución consistía en comisiones sobre los materiales empleados en la reforma del aparato de seguridad. La noche anterior, De Moya y su esposa ofrecieron una cena en el Club de la Calle F 1925 en homenaje al subsecretario de Estado para Asuntos Interamericanos y su esposa, los señores Dick Rubottom.

records.headline: Lester G. Murphy of Eugene, Oregon, father of missing American flyer
records.summary_en: Lester G. Murphy of Eugene, Oregon, father of missing American flyer Gerald L. Murphy, is scheduled to meet at the Congressional Hotel with a group organized by Representative Porter, Democrat of Oregon, to discuss the aviator's disappearance in the Dominican Republic one year earlier. Gerald Murphy's disappearance has been linked to that of Columbia University professor Jesus de Galindez, an outspoken foe of Dominican dictator Generalissimo Trujillo who vanished in March, 1956. Attendees scheduled for the meeting include author Carlton Beals, Professor Robert Alexander of Rutgers University, AFL-CIO representative Serafino Romualdi, Frances R. Grant, and publisher Louise Crane. Dominican authorities claimed the 23-year-old Murphy was thrown from a cliff into the sea by another flyer who later hanged himself in a jail cell, an account rejected as unsatisfactory by the State Department.
records.summary_es: Lester G. Murphy de Eugene, Oregón, padre del aviador estadounidense desaparecido Gerald L. Murphy, tiene previsto reunirse en el Congressional Hotel con un grupo organizado por el congresista Porter, demócrata de Oregón, para tratar la desaparición del piloto en la República Dominicana ocurrida un año antes. La desaparición de Gerald Murphy ha sido vinculada con la del profesor de Columbia University Jesús de Galíndez, enconado adversario del dictador dominicano generalísimo Trujillo que se desvaneció en marzo de 1956. Entre los asistentes previstos figuran el escritor Carlton Beals, el profesor Robert Alexander de Rutgers University, el representante de la AFL-CIO Serafino Romualdi, Frances R. Grant y la editora Louise Crane. Las autoridades dominicanas sostuvieron que Murphy, de 23 años, fue arrojado desde un acantilado al mar por otro piloto que luego se ahorcó en una celda carcelaria, versión calificada de insatisfactoria por el Departamento de Estado.

records.headline: Justice Department prosecutor Mr. Hundley argued to the jury
records.summary_en: Justice Department prosecutor Mr. Hundley argued to the jury that the government had proved overwhelmingly that attorney John Frank acted illegally as a foreign agent, rejecting defense claims of entrapment by stating that Frank was at complete liberty to accept or decline the bodyguard assignment. Hundley reminded jurors that Frank breached the Foreign Agents Registration Act by failing to register his Dominican agency with the United States Attorney General. The prosecutor contended that Frank intentionally chose not to register because disclosing his activities for the Dominican Republic would have ended his usefulness as an agent for Generalissimo Trujillo.
records.summary_es: El fiscal del Departamento de Justicia, el señor Hundley, argumentó ante el jurado que el gobierno demostró de manera contundente que el abogado John Frank actuó ilegalmente como agente extranjero, desestimando los alegatos de inducción dolosa de la defensa al sostener que Frank estuvo en plena libertad de aceptar o rechazar el encargo de guardaespaldas. Hundley recordó a los miembros del jurado que Frank infringió la Ley de Registro de Agentes Extranjeros al no inscribir su condición de agente dominicano ante el fiscal general de los Estados Unidos. El fiscal sostuvo que Frank decidió deliberadamente no registrarse porque revelar sus actividades para la República Dominicana habría puesto fin a su función como agente del generalísimo Trujillo.

records.headline: A federal jury returned a guilty verdict against former FBI agent
records.summary_en: A federal jury returned a guilty verdict against former FBI agent John Frank on charges of acting illegally as an agent for the Dominican Republic and Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo. The conviction hinged on testimony from Frank's former secretary, Mrs. Sally Newcomer, who testified that Frank investigated an alleged plot against Trujillo's life involving Columbia University professor Dr. Jesus de Galindez. The account notes that Galindez vanished in March, 1956, and that an American pilot linked to Frank in testimony disappeared in December, 1956, after publicly claiming knowledge of Galindez's fate. After the jury reported being deadlocked, Judge James R. Kirkland ordered further deliberations and subsequently granted a renewed juror request to review the transcript of Newcomer's testimony over objections from defense attorney Edward L. Carey.
records.summary_es: Un jurado federal emitió un veredicto de culpabilidad contra el exagente del FBI John Frank por los cargos de actuar ilegalmente como agente de la República Dominicana y del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo. La condena dependió en gran medida del testimonio de la antigua secretaria de Frank, la señora Sally Newcomer, quien declaró que Frank investigó un presunto complot contra la vida de Trujillo en el que participaba el profesor de Columbia University Dr. Jesús de Galíndez. La crónica señala que Galíndez desapareció en marzo de 1956 y que un piloto estadounidense vinculado a Frank en las declaraciones se esfumó en diciembre de 1956 tras jactarse públicamente de saber lo ocurrido con Galíndez. Después de que el jurado se declarara estancado, el juez James R. Kirkland ordenó proseguir las deliberaciones y posteriormente concedió una nueva solicitud de los jurados para revisar la transcripción del testimonio de Newcomer, pese a las objeciones del abogado defensor Edward L. Carey.

records.headline: Following his conviction on four counts of acting as an unregistered
records.summary_en: Following his conviction on four counts of acting as an unregistered agent for the Dominican Republic and Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, attorney John Frank faces up to imprisonment and a $10,000 fine on each charge. Federal Judge Kirkland released Frank under $10,000 bond pending a presentence investigation by the probation office, while defense attorney Edward L. Carey announced plans for an immediate appeal. During the trial, Frank's former secretary, Mrs. Sara T. Newcomer, testified that Frank told her early in 1956 he had been hired to investigate an assassination plot organized by Trujillo opponents in New York. Newcomer stated that Frank subsequently dictated a report referencing Jesus Maria de Galindez, who vanished on March 12, 1956, after teaching a class at Columbia University.
records.summary_es: Tras ser declarado culpable de cuatro cargos por actuar como agente no registrado de la República Dominicana y del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo, el abogado John Frank enfrenta penas de prisión y una multa de $10,000 por cada infracción. El juez federal Kirkland permitió que Frank continuara en libertad bajo fianza de $10,000 a la espera de un informe previo a la sentencia por parte de la oficina de libertad condicional, mientras que el abogado defensor Edward L. Carey anunció que presentará una apelación. Durante el juicio, la antigua secretaria de Frank, la señora Sara T. Newcomer, declaró que Frank le confió a principios de 1956 que había sido contratado para investigar un plan de magnicidio organizado por adversarios de Trujillo en Nueva York. Newcomer afirmó que Frank dictó posteriormente un informe que mencionaba a Jesús María de Galíndez, quien desapareció el 12 de marzo de 1956 después de impartir una clase en Columbia University.

records.headline: United Press reports that John J. Frank, former FBI agent, prepared
records.summary_en: United Press reports that John J. Frank, former FBI agent, prepared to appeal his conviction for operating as an unregistered agent for the Dominican Republic and its leader, Rafael Trujillo, a dispatch. A federal jury comprising nine women and three men found Frank guilty on four counts following nineteen hours of deliberations, leaving the 41-year-old attorney facing a maximum penalty of five years in prison and $10,000 in fines on each count. Frank's defense maintained that he was the victim of government entrapment, asserting that federal authorities possessed full knowledge of his role as a security adviser to Trujillo.

Frank, el exagente del FBI, se dispuso a apelar su condena por actuar como agente no registrado de la República Dominicana y de su mandatario, Rafael Trujillo. Un jurado federal integrado por nueve mujeres y tres hombres declaró culpable a Frank de cuatro cargos tras diecinueve horas de deliberación, lo que expone al letrado de 41 años a una pena máxima de cinco años de prisión y $10,000 de multa por cada cargo. La defensa de Frank sostuvo que este fue víctima de una provocación de las autoridades, afirmando que el gobierno tenía pleno conocimiento de sus actividades como asesor de seguridad de Trujillo.

records.headline: A travel feature in Diario las Americas portrays Ciudad Trujillo
records.summary_en: A travel feature in Diario las Americas portrays Ciudad Trujillo as a city blending historic colonial monuments with modern development, featuring historic fortifications along the Ozama River and the coastal Avenida Washington. The overview highlights landmarks of early Spanish colonization, including the Cathedral of Santa Maria containing the remains of Christopher Columbus, the University of Santo Domingo founded in 1538, the hospital of San Nicolas de Bari, and the convent of San Francisco. Alongside these colonial sites, the article notes modern civic establishments such as the Jaragua and Embajador hotels, the Banco de Reservas, and public hospitals. Recreational offerings detailed in the capital include golf at the Santo Domingo Country Club, horse racing at the Pearl of the Antilles track, baseball, boxing, cock-fighting, swimming, and polo.
records.summary_es: Una crónica de viajes en Diario las Américas describe a Ciudad Trujillo como una urbe que combina monumentos coloniales históricos con obras modernas, destacando las antiguas fortificaciones a orillas del río Ozama y la costera avenida Washington. La reseña resalta los hitos de la temprana colonización española, entre ellos la catedral de Santa María con los restos de Cristóbal Colón, la Universidad de Santo Domingo fundada en 1538, el hospital de San Nicolás de Bari y el convento de San Francisco. Junto a estos sitios coloniales, el artículo menciona edificaciones cívicas contemporáneas como los hoteles Jaragua y Embajador, el Banco de Reservas y diversos centros hospitalarios públicos. Entre los atractivos recreativos de la capital se detallan el golf en el Santo Domingo Country Club, las carreras hípicas en el hipódromo Perla de las Antillas, el béisbol, el boxeo, las peleas de gallos, la natación y el polo.

records.headline: Former FBI agent and Washington lawyer John Joseph Frank was sentenced
records.summary_en: Former FBI agent and Washington lawyer John Joseph Frank was sentenced to eight months to two years in prison for failing to register with the United States government as an agent of the Dominican Republic. Federal Judge James R. Kirkland permitted Frank to remain free under a $10,000 bond pending an appeal of his conviction. The 42-year-old attorney is the sole individual indicted thus far by the special grand jury investigating the 1956 disappearances of Columbia University Professor Jesus de Galindez and pilot Gerald L. Murphy of Eugene, Oregon. Federal prosecutors charged that Frank served as a security adviser to Dominican Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo during trips abroad.
records.summary_es: El exagente del FBI y abogado de Washington John Joseph Frank fue sentenciado a una pena de ocho meses a dos años de prisión por no inscribirse ante el gobierno de los Estados Unidos como agente de la República Dominicana. El juez federal James R. Kirkland autorizó a Frank a continuar en libertad bajo una fianza de $10,000 mientras apela su condena. El letrado de 42 años es la única persona acusada formalmente hasta ahora por el gran jurado especial que investiga las desapariciones en 1956 del profesor de Columbia University Jesús de Galíndez y del piloto Gerald L. Murphy de Eugene, Oregón. La fiscalía federal sostuvo que Frank se desempeñó como asesor de seguridad del generalísimo dominicano Rafael Trujillo durante varios viajes al extranjero.

records.headline: The Court of Appeals refused a request by investigator Mr. Schmahl
records.summary_en: The Court of Appeals refused a request by investigator Mr. Schmahl for a stay of his subpoena before the federal grand jury investigating the March, 1956, disappearance of Dr. Jesus de Galindez, a Columbia University professor and opponent of Dominican strongman Rafael Trujillo. Schmahl, who previously testified in April and was questioned by FBI agents in September concerning his connections with convicted Dominican agent John Joseph Frank, argued that federal prosecutors were seeking to name him as a defendant and that further questioning could compel him to testify against himself. Following Judge Luther W. Youngdahl's refusal on December 18 to quash the subpoena and the appellate court's denial of a stay, Schmahl must appear when the grand jury resumes its sessions on Friday.

Schmahl, quien ya había testificado en abril y fue interrogado por agentes del FBI en septiembre sobre sus vínculos con el condenado agente dominicano John Joseph Frank, alegó que los fiscales federales pretendían encausarlo como acusado y que nuevos interrogatorios podrían forzarlo a declarar contra sí mismo. Tras la negativa del juez federal Luther W. Youngdahl el 18 de diciembre de anular la citación y el posterior rechazo del tribunal de apelaciones, Schmahl deberá comparecer cuando el gran jurado reanude sus sesiones el viernes.

records.headline: Attorney Morris Ernst, long prominent in civil liberties, departed
records.summary_en: Attorney Morris Ernst, long prominent in civil liberties, departed on Tuesday for the Dominican Republic to present a report to Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo concerning the disappearance of an anti-regime critic whose vanishing published reports attributed to the Dominican dictator. Trujillo engaged Ernst to conduct an independent investigation of the case, offering assurances that the investigator would be permitted to visit any location and examine any evidence he requested. While Ernst's formal findings have not yet been made public, a Mr. Ross confirmed the investigator's travel to Ciudad Trujillo to deliver the conclusions directly to the Dominican government.

records.headline: A descriptive geographical survey details the principal valleys
records.summary_en: A descriptive geographical survey details the principal valleys, plains, and river systems of the Dominican Republic. It highlights the fertile Vega Real, often called "The Garden of the Antilles," measuring 140 miles long and nine to twenty-eight miles wide, as the country's chief source of agricultural wealth producing fruit, vegetables, and sugar cane. The southern coastal plain between the Cordillera Central and the coast contains most of the republic's principal cities, along with humid forests, savannas, and sugar fields. The survey also traces major rivers descending from the central divide, including the 250-mile Yaque del Norte traversing the Cibao Valley, the Yuna emptying into Samana Bay, the Yaque del Sur, and the Ozama and Isabela uniting at Ciudad Trujillo.
records.summary_es: Un estudio geográfico descriptivo detalla los principales valles, llanuras y sistemas fluviales de la República Dominicana. Destaca la fértil Vega Real, llamada a menudo "El Jardín de las Antillas", que mide 140 millas de largo y de nueve a veintiocho millas de ancho, como la principal fuente de riqueza agrícola del país que produce frutas, vegetales y caña de azúcar. La llanura costera del sur, ubicada entre la Cordillera Central y la costa, alberga la mayoría de las principales ciudades de la república, junto con bosques húmedos, sabanas y campos de caña. El estudio también describe los principales ríos que bajan de la cordillera divisoria central, incluidos el Yaque del Norte, de 250 millas, que atraviesa el valle del Cibao, el Yuna, que desemboca en la bahía de Samaná, el Yaque del Sur, y el Ozama y el Isabela, que se unen en Ciudad Trujillo.

records.headline: Dominican Interior Minister Virgilio Alvarez Pina warned former Argentine dictator
records.summary_en: Dominican Interior Minister Virgilio Alvarez Pina warned former Argentine dictator Juan Peron that he will be expelled from the Dominican Republic if he interferes in Argentina's political affairs. Alvarez Pina stated that if Peron dispatched instructions to his adherents in Argentina, such conduct constitutes a violation of the conditions of his asylum, following allegations that special messengers were used ahead of upcoming elections. Peron arrived in Ciudad Trujillo from Venezuela following the overthrow of his host, President Marcos Perez Jimenez. Alvarez Pina reiterated that any breach of asylum conditions will result in Peron being ordered to leave the country immediately.
records.summary_es: El ministro de Interior dominicano, Virgilio Álvarez Pina, advirtió al exdictador argentino Juan Perón que será expulsado de la República Dominicana si interfiere en los asuntos políticos de Argentina. Álvarez Pina afirmó que si Perón envió instrucciones a sus partidarios en Argentina, tal conducta constituye una violación de las condiciones de su asilo, tras acusaciones de que se utilizaron mensajeros especiales antes de las próximas elecciones. Perón llegó a Ciudad Trujillo desde Venezuela tras el derrocamiento de su anfitrión, el presidente Marcos Pérez Jiménez. Álvarez Pina reiteró que cualquier infracción de las condiciones de asilo resultará en que se le ordene a Perón abandonar el país de inmediato.

records.summary_en: Under the heading Friend of Trujillo's, a report recounts that Colonel Moore entered into a Dominican Republic business venture with National Airlines directors George W. Gibbs, Jr., and John W. Cross. Moore reportedly maintained close personal relations with Dominican dictator Trujillo, who sought White House intervention to stop an FBI investigation into his agents for allegedly kidnapping and murdering Dominican political refugees in the United States. Moore offered to use his influence with Trujillo to resolve difficulties regarding a shipyard Gibbs was constructing in the Dominican Republic.

Moore se ofreció a utilizar su influencia ante Trujillo para resolver dificultades relacionadas con un astillero que Gibbs construía en la República Dominicana.

Baker regarding reports involving Dominican Republic strongman Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo. The information concerned corporate stock Trujillo reportedly gave to airline director George W. Gibbs in a venture that may have also involved Colonel Moore. Subcommittee Chairman Harris indicated the panel would examine whether these reports bear any relevance to allegations of improper influence in the FCC proceedings. Baker and airline vice president Alexander G. Hardy testified they knew nothing substantial about Moore's business dealings with Gibbs, though Baker acknowledged hearing that the two men were involved in a shipyard project in the Dominican Republic.

records.headline: Sixteen-year-old Rhamades Trujillo, son of the generalissimo of the Dominican
records.summary_en: Sixteen-year-old Rhamades Trujillo, son of the generalissimo of the Dominican Republic, left Kemper Military School for health reasons and departed Kansas City by train to return to his homeland. Staff attaches of his brother, Lieutenant General Rafael Leonidas Trujillo, Jr., who attends the United States Army Command and General Staff College at Fort Leavenworth, explained that the youth had been losing weight and suffered from a nose and throat ailment. A Kansas City physician advised that the boy, who enrolled at the military school the previous autumn, return to a milder climate.
records.summary_es: Rhamades Trujillo, de dieciséis años e hijo del generalísimo de la República Dominicana, abandonó la Escuela Militar Kemper por motivos de salud y partió de Kansas City en tren para regresar a su patria. Agregados del personal de su hermano, el teniente general Rafael Leónidas Trujillo, hijo, quien asiste a la Escuela de Comando y Estado Mayor del Ejército de los Estados Unidos en Fort Leavenworth, explicaron que el joven había estado perdiendo peso y padecía una afección de nariz y garganta. Un médico de Kansas City aconsejó que el joven, matriculado en la academia militar el otoño anterior, regresara a un clima más templado.

records.summary_en: Argentina officially protested to the Dominican Republic because ex-dictator Juan Peron and other Peronist exiles residing in Ciudad Trujillo were engaged in political activities that violated the most elemental rules of asylum. The Foreign Affairs Minister made the protest at noon, and an official note was delivered to the Dominican ambassador at Buenos Aires, following an earlier protest made to him some days before. records.full_text:
Argentina Protests Perón's Activities to Dominican Govt.

BUENOS AIRES, (UP) —Argentina has officially protested to the Dominican Republic because ex-dictator Juan Perón and other Peronist exiles residing in Ciudad Trujillo, are dedicated to political activities "which violate the most elemental rules of asylum."

The Foreign Affairs Minister made the protest at noon.

Some days ago this protest was made to the Dominican Ambassador at Buenos Aires, and now an official note in the same way has been delivered to him.

The communique declares that the protests are aimed to stop activities of intervention in Argentine politics by exiles now in Ciudad Trujillo.

The text of the note was not made public immediately.

records.headline: Dominican Admiral Richardson defended his government's ban on Jehovah's Witnesses missionaries
records.summary_en: Dominican Admiral Richardson defended his government's ban on Jehovah's Witnesses missionaries in an interview concluding his official tour as a guest of United States Chief of Naval Operations Admiral Arleigh Burke, asserting that the prohibition was justified because the sect forbids members from saluting the national flag. Richardson highlighted close cooperation with the United States Naval Mission in Ciudad Trujillo, emphasizing programs teaching English to Dominican naval personnel so they can attend American service schools, including three officers currently training at the Fleet Sonar School in Key West. He observed that the Dominican Republic is experiencing growth and encouraging immigration. The visiting delegation, which included Commander Fermin E. Martinez, Lieutenant Ramon Jimenez, Lieutenant Nestor Gonsalez, Captain Federico Betances, and American Commander G. Rood, departed Key West for a brief stop at Guantanamo Bay, Cuba, en route back to Ciudad Trujillo.
records.summary_es: El almirante dominicano Richardson defendió la prohibición de su gobierno contra los misioneros de los Testigos de Jehová en una entrevista al concluir su gira oficial como invitado del jefe de Operaciones Navales de los Estados Unidos, almirante Arleigh Burke, afirmando que la medida estaba justificada porque la secta prohíbe a sus miembros saludar la bandera nacional. Richardson destacó la estrecha cooperación con la Misión Naval de los Estados Unidos en Ciudad Trujillo, resaltando los programas para enseñar inglés al personal naval dominicano para que asistan a escuelas de servicio estadounidenses, incluidos tres oficiales que actualmente se capacitan en la Escuela de Sonar de la Flota en Cayo Hueso. Observó que la República Dominicana experimenta un período de crecimiento y fomenta la inmigración. La delegación visitante, integrada por el comandante Fermín E. Martínez, el teniente Ramón Jiménez, el teniente Néstor Gonsález, el capitán Federico Betances y el comandante estadounidense G. Rood, partió de Cayo Hueso hacia una breve escala en la Bahía de Guantánamo, Cuba, de regreso a Ciudad Trujillo.

records.headline: Brigadier General Antonio Kebreau, the ousted Haitian army strongman
records.summary_en: Brigadier General Antonio Kebreau, the ousted Haitian army strongman removed as chief of staff by President Francois Duvalier earlier in the week, has taken political asylum in the neighboring Dominican Republic. Although Haiti and the Dominican Republic share the island of Hispaniola and have historically been at odds, Kebreau enjoyed close personal relations with Dominican dictator General Rafael Leonidas Trujillo Molina. The dispatch notes that deposed dictators Juan D. Peron of Argentina and Marcos Perez Jimenez of Venezuela have likewise obtained asylum in the Dominican Republic.
records.summary_es: El general de brigada Antonio Kebreau, el derrocado hombre fuerte del ejército haitiano destituido como jefe de estado mayor por el presidente François Duvalier a principios de semana, obtuvo asilo político en la vecina República Dominicana. Aunque Haití y la República Dominicana comparten la isla de La Española y han estado enfrentados históricamente, Kebreau mantenía estrechas relaciones personales con el dictador dominicano, el general Rafael Leónidas Trujillo Molina. El despacho señala que los derrocados dictadores Juan D. Perón de Argentina y Marcos Pérez Jiménez de Venezuela igualmente han obtenido asilo en la República Dominicana.

Pérez Jiménez' Family in Miami

BY UNITED PRESS

The wife and four small daughters of deposed Venezuelan President Marcos Pérez Jiménez arrived in Miami Friday night.

Pérez Jiménez' family were whisked away in a City of Miami Beach limousines after a lengthy trip through Customs.

They refused to discuss their trip to the United States from the Dominican Republic where Pérez Jiménez has been in exile since he was kicked out as dictator of the Venezuelan Republic in January.

Accompanying the party was a man identified as Teófilo Parra Mendoza (apparently an aide to Pérez Jiménez), a governess and a nurse for the small children.

The group arrived aboard a Dominican Republic airliner from Ciudad Trujillo.

It could not be learned if or when Pérez Jiménez expects to follow his family to the United States or how long the family plans to remain here.

records.headline: During House subcommittee proceedings into federal agencies
records.summary_en: During House subcommittee proceedings into federal agencies, Chairman Harris called attention to earlier testimony indicating that Colonel Moore was associated with George Gibbs and John Cross in a Dominican Republic shipyard project financed by Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo. Colonel Moore testified that Cross is his personal attorney, that he knew Mr. Cross and Mr. Gibbs were directors of National Airlines, and that it was a coincidence that he happened to be in the Dominican Republic at the time National Airlines was applying for the Miami Channel 10 TV license and became associated with Mr. Gibbs and Mr. Cross in the shipyard project at that time. He said the Dominican Republic officials were dissatisfied with the handling of the shipyard by Mr. Gibbs, who subsequently left, and that he was asked by Mr. De Moya to take over the shipyard for a short interval until other management could be obtained, remaining there about two months. Col. Moore said he knew very little about the venture's origin or eventual ownership by the Dominican Republic, believed Mr. Gibbs, Mr. Cross and a Mr. Boyd originally were in the project, and emphasized that he was not associated in business with Mr. Gibbs — rather, he replaced Mr. Gibbs in managing the shipyard. His fee for the Dominican shipyard job was $8,300, he said, adding that he would not handle the job if he had it to do over again, and when he did not recall that he was vice president and a director of the shipyard, Representative Mack, Democrat of Illinois, said his lack of memory was “just about as amazing” as that of former FCC Commissioner Richard A. Mack.

El coronel Moore testificó que Cross es su abogado personal, que sabía que el Sr. Cross y el Sr. Gibbs eran directores de National Airlines, y que fue una coincidencia que se encontrara en la República Dominicana en el momento en que National Airlines solicitaba la licencia del Canal 10 de televisión de Miami y que se asociara con el Sr. Gibbs y el Sr. Cross en el proyecto del astillero en ese momento. Dijo que los funcionarios de la República Dominicana estaban insatisfechos con el manejo del astillero por parte del Sr. Gibbs, quien se marchó posteriormente, y que el Sr. De Moya le pidió que se hiciera cargo del astillero por un breve intervalo hasta que se pudiera obtener otra administración, permaneciendo allí unos dos meses. El coronel Moore dijo que sabía muy poco sobre el origen de la empresa o su eventual propiedad por la República Dominicana, que creía que el Sr. Gibbs, el Sr. Cross y un Sr. Boyd estaban originalmente en el proyecto, y enfatizó que no estaba asociado en negocios con el Sr. Gibbs, sino que lo reemplazó en la dirección del astillero. Su honorario por el trabajo en el astillero dominicano fue de $8,300, dijo, añadiendo que no aceptaría el trabajo si tuviera que hacerlo de nuevo, y cuando no recordó que había sido vicepresidente y director del astillero, el representante Mack, demócrata de Illinois, dijo que su falta de memoria era «casi tan asombrosa» como la del excomisionado de la FCC Richard A. Mack.

records.summary_en: Sources close to Juan D. Peron in Ciudad Trujillo denied reports that the former Argentine dictator has departed the Dominican Republic. records.headline: Commenting on security arrangements, Representative Hays observed
records.summary_en: Commenting on security arrangements, Representative Hays observed that the Latin American nation had established specialized installations for the fight against communism. Referring to Trujillo, he noted that the former Dominican president is entitled to take every measure to protect his son, a high-ranking Dominican army officer studying in the United States. Hays cited an American magazine article detailing the younger Trujillo's living conditions in Kansas City, including renting an entire hotel floor, maintaining an automobile fleet, owning a weekend ranch, using private radios, and modifying elevators to ring bells and light up when stopping on his floor. The magazine estimated that these security precautions, which included hiring four former federal agents for protection, cost one million dollars a year.

records.headline: At a wardroom party held at the Sigsbee Park home of Lieutenant
records.summary_en: At a wardroom party held at the Sigsbee Park home of Lieutenant and Mrs. L. Capone, officers and their ladies of the USS Huse (DE-145) spent the evening dancing the merengue, described as a dance originated by President Trujillo of the Dominican Republic. Guests danced to music by the Silver Star Steel Band from a phonograph record brought back from the Caribbean during the ship's previous cruise. The band was noted for its unconventional instruments, including a dented oil drum, a seven-hole papaya stem flute, a marlin twine sardine pan banjo, and a car muffler bass pipe. Attending officers, including Commander and Mrs. Larry Kempf, enjoyed a buffet featuring ham with hot rolls, cocktail rye, chive dip, a cheese tray, and stuffed celery.

Capone en Sigsbee Park, los oficiales y damas del USS Huse (DE-145) pasaron la velada bailando merengue, calificado como un baile originado por el presidente Trujillo de la República Dominicana. Los invitados bailaron con la música de la Silver Star Steel Band de un disco traído del Caribe durante la última travesía del buque. La banda se destacó por sus instrumentos insólitos, entre ellos un tambor de petróleo abollado, una flauta de tallo de lechosa de siete agujeros, un banjo de lata de sardinas y cuerda de sedal, y un tubo de bajo hecho con un silenciador de automóvil. Los oficiales asistentes, entre ellos el comandante y la señora Larry Kempf, disfrutaron de un bufé con jamón y panecillos calientes, pan de centeno de cóctel, salsa de cebollino, bandeja de quesos y apio relleno.

records.headline: Former Argentine dictator Juan D. Peron has vanished from his hotel
records.summary_en: Former Argentine dictator Juan D. Peron has vanished from his hotel in Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic, prompting diplomatic sources in Buenos Aires to report that he has departed for Europe. Several of Peron's associates were likewise reported missing from their hotel quarters in the Dominican capital. One associate remaining at the hotel, Americo Barrios, insisted that Peron was traveling on a tour of the Dominican interior, though he refused to state where the former leader had gone.
records.summary_es: El exdictador argentino Juan D. Perón desapareció de su hotel en Ciudad Trujillo, República Dominicana, lo que motivó a fuentes diplomáticas en Buenos Aires a informar que había partido hacia Europa. Varios colaboradores de Perón figuraban igualmente ausentes de sus habitaciones en la capital dominicana. Uno de los allegados que permaneció en el hotel, Américo Barrios, sostuvo que Perón se encontraba de recorrido por el interior dominicano, aunque se negó a precisar a dónde se había trasladado el antiguo mandatario.

records.headline: President Hector Trujillo of the Dominican Republic, alongside
records.summary_en: President Hector Trujillo of the Dominican Republic, alongside Presidents Jose Figueres of Costa Rica, Fulgencio Batista of Cuba, Jose Maria Lemus of El Salvador, Ramon Villeda Morales of Honduras, and Gen. Alfredo Stroessner of Paraguay, presented their views on economic assistance. Most of the leaders expressed a prevailing Latin American sentiment that the United States could alleviate their most urgent problems using only a small fraction of the aid granted to other parts of the world. In addition, Brazilian President Juscelino Kubitschek called for vigorous technical aid and sustained financing, describing such measures as invaluable for less developed nations.
records.summary_es: El presidente Héctor Trujillo de la República Dominicana, junto a los presidentes José Figueres de Costa Rica, Fulgencio Batista de Cuba, José María Lemus de El Salvador, Ramón Villeda Morales de Honduras y el general Alfredo Stroessner de Paraguay, expusieron sus puntos de vista sobre asistencia económica. La mayoría de los mandatarios manifestó el sentimiento latinoamericano latente de que los Estados Unidos podrían aliviar sus problemas más apremiantes con solo una pequeña fracción de la ayuda suministrada a otras regiones del mundo. Por su parte, el mandatario brasileño Juscelino Kubitschek reclamó una enérgica ayuda técnica y financiamiento sostenido, calificando dichas medidas como de valor incalculable para las naciones menos desarrolladas.

PERONIST LEADER IN PARAGUAY VISIT

ASUNCION, Paraguay. (UP).—John William Cooke, Argentine Peronista Party leader, arrived here from the Dominican Republic last Saturday, it was learned today.

Cooke and his wife, who is with him here, had been living with ex-Dictator Juan D. Perón in Ciudad Trujillo. Perón left the Dominican capital last week to "vacation" in the central resort town of Jarabacoa. Cooke left the Caribbean Island nation about the same time.

The Peronista chieftain and his wife came here by way of Miami, Fla., and after two days at the city's main hotel moved to a private house.

records.headline: Two dozen Cuban and Dominican political exiles from New York picketed
records.summary_en: Two dozen Cuban and Dominican political exiles from New York picketed the White House in Washington. Demonstrators marched to protest against what they termed an illicit shipment of arms to Cuban dictator Gen. Fulgencio Batista by Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, dictator of the Dominican Republic, transported in five American-made C-47 aircraft. Extra municipal police were deployed to maintain order and keep the marchers moving as the pickets carried banners denouncing both Caribbean leaders and protesting United States aid to both nations.
records.summary_es: Dos docenas de exiliados políticos cubanos y dominicanos procedentes de Nueva York protestaron frente a la Casa Blanca en Washington. Los manifestantes marcharon en rechazo a lo que calificaron como un envío ilícito de armas al dictador cubano, general Fulgencio Batista, por parte del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo, dictador de la República Dominicana, transportadas en cinco aviones C-47 de fabricación estadounidense. Policías municipales adicionales fueron apostados para mantener el orden y conservar la marcha en movimiento mientras los manifestantes portaban pancartas que atacaban a ambos mandatarios caribeños y protestaban contra la ayuda de los Estados Unidos a ambos países.

records.headline: Nicaragua will assume charge of Dominican Republic affairs in Argentina
records.summary_en: Nicaragua will assume charge of Dominican Republic affairs in Argentina, following the diplomatic rupture between the two countries. Simultaneously, Peru was announced to take over the representation of Argentine diplomatic affairs in Ciudad Trujillo. The Argentine Foreign Ministry released further explanations regarding its decision to suspend diplomatic ties with the Dominican Republic, citing grievances that public declarations by Juan Peron had interfered in Argentine matters.
records.summary_es: Nicaragua asumirá la gestión de los asuntos de la República Dominicana en Argentina, tras la ruptura diplomática entre ambas naciones. Al mismo tiempo, se anunció que Perú se hará cargo de la representación de los asuntos diplomáticos argentinos en Ciudad Trujillo. El Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Argentina publicó detalles adicionales sobre su decisión de suspender los vínculos diplomáticos con la República Dominicana, citando quejas de que las declaraciones de Juan Perón constituían una injerencia en los asuntos argentinos.

records.headline: Dominican Republic President Hector B. Trujillo, Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo
records.summary_en: Dominican Republic President Hector B. Trujillo, Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo as sponsor of the Patronato project, and Vice President Dr. Joaquin Balaguer attended the formal signing ceremony alongside church representatives from Spain. Under the terms of the agreement, the Dominican Republic will finance operations of the program through a trust fund and pay all salaries, while the Catholic Church assumes responsibility for organizing and sustaining religious, social, and educational projects to complement national development. The Dominican Republic Information Center reported that no specific appropriations or operational details were released. Generalissimo Trujillo emphasized that social integration of lower economic groups can only be achieved through both moral and material measures.

El Centro de Información de la República Dominicana indicó que no se publicaron partidas específicas ni detalles operativos. records.headline: A concerted church-and-state agreement between the Dominican government
records.summary_en: A concerted church-and-state agreement between the Dominican government and the Catholic Church was signed in Ciudad Trujillo to advance the welfare of the nation's frontier. The pact, designated the 'Patronato de San Rafael,' combines spiritual labors with economic and cultural projects in border areas and establishes a government fund to finance Catholic technical personnel. A photograph of the signing portrays Dominican President Hector B. Trujillo alongside church dignitaries, including pact sponsor Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo and Papal Nuncio Msgr. Salvador Siino, representing Pope Pius XII.
records.summary_es: Un acuerdo concertado entre la Iglesia y el Estado fue suscrito en Ciudad Trujillo entre el gobierno dominicano y la Iglesia católica para promover el bienestar de la frontera del país. La fotografía de la firma muestra al presidente dominicano Héctor B. Trujillo junto a dignatarios eclesiásticos, entre ellos el patrocinador del pacto, generalísimo Rafael L. Trujillo, y el nuncio apostólico monseñor Salvador Siino, en representación del papa Pío XII.

records.headline: Brigadier General Ludovino Fernandez, army commander at San Juan de la Maguana
records.summary_en: Brigadier General Ludovino Fernandez, army commander at San Juan de la Maguana in the southern Dominican Republic, was shot and killed by his military aide. Dominican officials identified the aide as Major Luis Ney Lluberes, who turned the weapon on himself and took his own life immediately following the shooting. Authorities in Ciudad Trujillo confirmed that an official investigation into the incident has been initiated.

Funcionarios dominicanos identificaron al ayudante como el mayor Luis Ney Lluberes, quien se quitó la vida con la misma arma inmediatamente después del tiroteo. Las autoridades en Ciudad Trujillo confirmaron el inicio de una investigación oficial sobre el suceso.

records.headline: An American pilot named Taylor refused to operate a chartered
records.summary_en: An American pilot named Taylor refused to operate a chartered Douglas DC-4 flight from Bermuda to Ciudad Trujillo, fearing he would be coerced into altering his course once airborne. Miguel Medina, identified as an associate of former Colombian president Gustavo Rojas Pinilla's son-in-law Samuel Moreno Diaz, hired the aircraft from General Airways in New York and instructed the pilot to fly an unnamed Colombian passenger to the Dominican capital. Rojas Pinilla had visited the Dominican Republic several months prior and claimed sugar interests there, while the Colombian government issued warnings to commercial carriers against transporting the deposed leader back into Colombia. When approached by a United Press reporter at Rojas Pinilla's residence, 'The Breakers,' an unidentified Spanish-accented man claimed no knowledge of Colombia and slammed the door.
records.summary_es: Un piloto estadounidense llamado Taylor se negó a operar un vuelo chárter en un avión Douglas DC-4 de Bermudas a Ciudad Trujillo, por temor a ser coaccionado para alterar su ruta en pleno vuelo. Miguel Medina, señalado como allegado del yerno del expresidente colombiano Gustavo Rojas Pinilla, Samuel Moreno Díaz, alquiló el avión a General Airways en Nueva York e indicó al piloto que debía transportar a un pasajero colombiano anónimo hacia la capital dominicana. Rojas Pinilla había visitado la República Dominicana meses antes y afirmaba tener intereses azucareros allí, mientras el gobierno colombiano emitía advertencias a las aerolíneas contra el traslado del mandatario depuesto de regreso a Colombia. Al ser abordado por un reportero de United Press en la residencia de Rojas Pinilla, 'The Breakers', un desconocido con acento hispano aseguró desconocer a Colombia y le cerró la puerta.

records.headline: Dominican authorities in Ciudad Trujillo denied foreign press
records.summary_en: Dominican authorities in Ciudad Trujillo denied foreign press reports alleging that a clandestine radio station was operating from the Dominican Republic against the government of neighboring Haiti. Secretary of the Interior Virgilio Alvarez Pina asserted that no Dominican radio stations were conducting propaganda campaigns against the Haitian regime, an assertion supported by the management of 'La Voz Dominicana'. In contrast, the Dominican communications department countered that a clandestine transmitter styled 'Radio Liberte' was operating inside Haiti to broadcast communist propaganda against both the Dominican Republic and the United States.
records.summary_es: Las autoridades dominicanas en Ciudad Trujillo negaron informes de prensa extranjeros que aseguraban la operación de una radioemisora clandestina desde la República Dominicana contra el gobierno del vecino Haití. El secretario de Interior Virgilio Álvarez Pina aseguró que ninguna emisora dominicana realizaba campañas de propaganda contra el régimen haitiano, afirmación respaldada por la dirección de 'La Voz Dominicana'. En contrapartida, el departamento de comunicaciones dominicano denunció que una estación clandestina autodenominada 'Radio Liberte' operaba dentro de Haití para emitir propaganda comunista contra la República Dominicana y los Estados Unidos.

records.headline: Speaking from Ciudad Trujillo, capital of the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: Speaking from Ciudad Trujillo, capital of the Dominican Republic, former Argentine president Juan Peron announced that he will return to Argentina only when he considers the moment opportune. Responding to inquiries concerning an amnesty bill proposed by President Frondizi, Peron stated that his return to his homeland depends entirely upon himself and no one else. The dispatch notes that while some Peronists have returned from exile anticipating the legislation, political observers advised that Peron should remain abroad longer due to firm opposition from the Argentine armed forces and Frondizi's party.
records.summary_es: Desde Ciudad Trujillo, capital de la República Dominicana, el expresidente argentino Juan Perón declaró que regresará a Argentina únicamente cuando considere oportuno el momento. Al ser consultado sobre el proyecto de ley de amnistía presentado por el presidente Frondizi, Perón afirmó que su retorno a la patria depende exclusivamente de sí mismo y de nadie más. El despacho señala que aunque algunos peronistas han vuelto del exilio confiados en la medida legislativa, observadores políticos recomendaron a Perón prolongar su estancia fuera del país ante la firme oposición de las fuerzas armadas argentinas y el partido de Frondizi.

records.headline: Addressing controversy over automobile gifts, Zsa Zsa Gabor defended
records.summary_en: Addressing controversy over automobile gifts, Zsa Zsa Gabor defended Rafael Trujillo Jr. by questioning why news reports failed to mention his $25,000 donation to the Damon Runyon Cancer Fund two weeks earlier. Kim Novak expressed surprise upon learning that a car was registered in her name and that Trujillo had purchased a $12,000 vehicle for himself alongside the other gifts, remarking that such spending was equivalent for him to an ordinary man buying a novelty bracelet. Meanwhile, congressional critics targeted Trujillo and his father, alleging that the Dominican dictator spent one million dollars supporting his son's stay in the United States while the Dominican Republic received $1,300,000 in American foreign aid.
records.summary_es: Al referirse a la polémica por los regalos de automóviles, Zsa Zsa Gabor defendió a Rafael Trujillo hijo preguntando por qué los reportes de prensa no mencionaban su donación de $25,000 al Fondo contra el Cáncer Damon Runyon dos semanas antes. Kim Novak expresó sorpresa al enterarse de que un automóvil figuraba registrado a su nombre y de que Trujillo había comprado un vehículo de $12,000 para sí mismo junto con los otros obsequios, comentando que semejante desembolso equivalía para él a lo que para otro hombre sería comprar un brazalete de fantasía. Entretanto, legisladores en el Congreso criticaron a Trujillo y a su padre, denunciando que el dictador dominicano destinó un millón de dólares al sostenimiento de su hijo en los Estados Unidos mientras la República Dominicana recibía $1,300,000 en ayuda exterior estadounidense.

records.headline: Ousted dictator Juan Peron, in a dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo
records.summary_en: Ousted dictator Juan Peron, in a dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo, declared that he is ready and eager to return to Argentina if that nation's Congress grants permission. Peron stated he will remain in the Dominican Republic until the incoming Argentine administration decides whether he may return to reorganize his followers within the Peronist party. Smiling during the interview, the former leader dismissed rumors of traveling elsewhere, insisting he has no intention of departing for Europe or any other destination.
records.summary_es: El dictador depuesto Juan Perón, en un despacho desde Ciudad Trujillo, manifestó que se encuentra listo y deseoso de regresar a Argentina si el Congreso de esa nación lo autoriza. Perón afirmó que permanecerá en la República Dominicana hasta que el nuevo gobierno argentino resuelva si puede volver a reorganizar a sus partidarios en el seno del partido peronista. Sonriente durante la entrevista, el antiguo mandatario desestimó rumores sobre otros traslados e insistió en que no planea viajar a Europa ni a ningún otro destino.

records.headline: Rafael Trujillo Jr., son of the Dominican Republic strongman
records.summary_en: Rafael Trujillo Jr., son of the Dominican Republic strongman, confirmed giving a fur coat to Zsa Zsa Gabor, who explained that she introduced actress Kim Novak to him and helped arrange social gatherings, describing Trujillo as a grateful friend. While convalescing from surgery at a rented Beverly Hills residence, Trujillo declined phone interviews but instructed his secretary to clarify that the garment was mink rather than chinchilla and did not cost the reported $17,000 price. In parallel developments, Kim Novak stated that Trujillo had delivered an $8,400 sports car to her possession, though she viewed the automobile as a temporary loan that a studio representative confirmed she would not keep.
records.summary_es: Rafael Trujillo hijo, hijo del hombre fuerte de la República Dominicana, confirmó haber regalado un abrigo de piel a Zsa Zsa Gabor, quien explicó que le presentó a la actriz Kim Novak y ayudó a concertar reuniones sociales, calificando a Trujillo de amigo agradecido. Mientras convalecía de una cirugía en una residencia alquilada en Beverly Hills, Trujillo declinó responder al teléfono pero instruyó a su secretario para aclarar que la prenda era de visón y no de chinchilla, desmintiendo el precio informado de $17,000. Paralelamente, Kim Novak indicó que Trujillo le entregó un automóvil deportivo de $8,400, si bien consideró el vehículo como un préstamo provisional que un portavoz del estudio confirmó que ella no conservará.

records.headline: Serving as an officer in the Dominican air force, Rafael Trujillo Jr.
records.summary_en: Serving as an officer in the Dominican air force, Rafael Trujillo Jr. entered the United States to study at the U.S. Army Command and General Staff College at Ft. Leavenworth, Kansas, before taking medical leave for surgery. His extravagant personal expenditures provoked sharp criticism in Congress, where Representative Wayne Hays of Ohio questioned allocating $1,300,000 in foreign aid to Trujillo's country as part of an overall $3,603,000,000 assistance measure. Trujillo's secretary, Victor Sued, defended the spending by maintaining that the funds were entirely private, stating that the young general owns sugar mills and an agricultural dairy enterprise in the Dominican Republic.
records.summary_es: Como oficial de la fuerza aérea dominicana, Rafael Trujillo hijo llegó a los Estados Unidos para cursar estudios en la Escuela de Comando y Estado Mayor del Ejército en Ft. Sus cuantiosos desembolsos personales motivaron duras críticas en el Congreso, donde el representante Wayne Hays de Ohio objetó la asignación de $1,300,000 en ayuda exterior para el país de Trujillo en el marco de una partida global de $3,603,000,000. El secretario de Trujillo, Víctor Sued, defendió los gastos asegurando que procedían exclusivamente de fondos privados, afirmando que el joven militar es propietario de ingenios azucareros y una explotación lechera en la República Dominicana.

records.headline: General Garcia disputed claims from Washington circles alleging
records.summary_en: General Garcia disputed claims from Washington circles alleging that the United States government transferred financial funds to the Dominican Republic, asserting that American assistance has been restricted entirely to military equipment. Garcia pointed out that the Dominican government compensates the American Naval Mission with $45,000 annually and provides tax and tariff exonerations, emphasizing that his government accepts neither gifts nor cash donations from external parties. Furthermore, Garcia affirmed that Generalissimo Trujillo personally finances all expenses incurred in the United States by his son, General Trujillo, and announced that a detailed breakdown of American military aid is being prepared for presentation to Congress by the Dominican ambassador.
records.summary_es: El general García desmintió versiones procedentes de Washington según las cuales el gobierno de los Estados Unidos transfirió dinero a la República Dominicana, asegurando que la ayuda estadounidense se ha limitado por completo a equipo militar. García destacó que el gobierno dominicano retribuye a la Misión Naval estadounidense con $45,000 anuales y otorga exenciones tributarias y arancelarias, recalcando que su gobierno no admite dádivas ni dinero en efectivo de terceros. Asimismo, afirmó que el generalísimo Trujillo sufraga personalmente todos los gastos realizados en los Estados Unidos por su hijo, el general Trujillo, e indicó que se elabora un desglose detallado de la asistencia militar estadounidense para que el embajador dominicano lo presente ante el Congreso.

records.headline: An editorial argues that the United States government has deluded
records.summary_en: An editorial argues that the United States government has deluded itself into believing that securing pledges of support from dictators such as Batista in Cuba or Trujillo in the Dominican Republic wins the affection of the people they govern. The commentary states that Communist inroads across Latin America succeed when populations face economic misery, leaving them receptive to demagogues or disciples of Khruschev. It further links anti-American sentiment, including the stoning experienced by Nixon in Peru, to United States economic difficulties, falling prices, and protective tariff disputes affecting the lead and zinc industries.
records.summary_es: Un editorial sostiene que el gobierno de los Estados Unidos se ha engañado al creer que obtener promesas de apoyo de dictadores como Batista en Cuba o Trujillo en la República Dominicana gana el afecto de los pueblos que gobiernan. El comentario afirma que los avances comunistas en América Latina prosperan cuando las poblaciones padecen miseria económica, lo que las hace receptivas a demagogos o discípulos de Khruschev. Asimismo, vincula el sentimiento antinorteamericano, incluida la lapidación sufrida por Nixon en Perú, a las dificultades económicas de los Estados Unidos, la caída de los precios y las disputas por aranceles protectores que afectan a las industrias del plomo y del zinc.

records.headline: Civil courts in Juarez, Mexico, reported having no divorce suit
records.summary_en: Civil courts in Juarez, Mexico, reported having no divorce suit on file regarding the twenty-nine-year-old chief of the Dominican air force, who has been studying at the U.S. Army General Staff College at Ft. Leavenworth, Kansas. His wife, Octavia Adolfina Ricart de Trujillo, and their six children were reported residing in the Dominican Republic. The elder Generalissimo Trujillo, sixty-seven, insisted the divorce had absolutely no connection with his son's romantic adventures in Hollywood, stating his son had the right to spend his own money. The generalissimo also declared his country never received a penny in direct aid from the United States, responding to charges by Representative Wayne Hays that the son's lavish living cost a million dollars annually while the Dominican Republic was earmarked for $1,300,000 in United States aid.

Leavenworth, Kansas. Su esposa, Octavia Adolfina Ricart de Trujillo, y sus seis hijos residían en la República Dominicana. El mayor de los Trujillo, el generalísimo de sesenta y siete años, insistió en que el divorcio no tenía ninguna relación con las aventuras románticas de su hijo en Hollywood y afirmó que este tenía derecho a gastar su propio dinero. El generalísimo declaró además que su país nunca recibió un centavo en ayuda directa de los Estados Unidos, en respuesta a las acusaciones del representante Wayne Hays de que la vida ostentosa del hijo costaba un millón de dólares al año mientras la República Dominicana tenía asignados $1,300,000 en ayuda estadounidense.

records.headline: The young general from the Dominican Republic declared his love
records.summary_en: The young general from the Dominican Republic declared his love for actress Kim Novak in a television interview with Paul Coates, and stated his intention to pursue the relationship after finishing his military studies at the U.S. Army General Staff School at Ft. Leavenworth, Kansas. Addressing criticism from Washington legislators regarding lavish gifts of automobiles, furs, and jewelry, Trujillo insisted he spent his own personal money rather than United States loan funds earmarked for the Dominican Republic. He explained that his family's wealth derives from ownership of sugar refineries and ranches. Describing their courtship, he recalled taking Miss Novak to hamburger drive-ins and fancy restaurants, and recounted surprising her with an automobile.

Al describir su cortejo, relató que llevaba a la señorita Novak a locales de hamburguesas y restaurantes elegantes, y contó cómo la sorprendió con un automóvil.

records.headline: Dominican Ambassador de Moya denied news reports that the Dominican Republic receives
records.summary_en: Dominican Ambassador de Moya denied news reports that the Dominican Republic receives cash under the mutual aid agreement with the United States, citing statements from General Jose Garcia regarding payments for studies by Lieutenant General Rafael L. Trujillo Jr. at Fort Leavenworth. De Moya explained that United States assistance has been limited to military equipment, whereas the Dominican government contributes $45,000 annually to the United States Naval Mission in the Dominican Republic and grants its personnel tax exemptions and customs privileges. The ambassador asserted that the Dominican government accepts neither gifts nor cash from other nations. He added that Trujillo Jr.'s expenses in the United States are paid entirely from a monthly allowance provided by his father.

Trujillo hijo en Fort Leavenworth. De Moya explicó que la asistencia estadounidense se ha limitado a equipo militar, mientras que el gobierno dominicano aporta $45,000 anuales a la Misión Naval de los Estados Unidos en la República Dominicana y otorga a su personal exenciones tributarias y privilegios aduaneros. El embajador afirmó que el gobierno dominicano no acepta donaciones ni dinero en efectivo de otros países. Añadió que los gastos de Trujillo hijo en los Estados Unidos se costean en su totalidad con una asignación mensual suministrada por su padre.

records.headline: Speaking by telephone from Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: Speaking by telephone from Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic, where ousted Argentine dictator Juan D. Peron lives in exile with a small group of followers, press aide Americo Barrios denounced Argentina's new political amnesty law as a trap. Barrios declared that Peron has no immediate plans to return to Argentina, noting that while the measure offers political amnesty, many Peronist leaders still face civil lawsuits. He asserted that President Arturo Frondizi would have to remove judges appointed following Peron's 1955 overthrow before exiled leaders could safely return.

Perón vive en el exilio con un pequeño grupo de seguidores, su asesor de prensa Américo Barrios denunció como una trampa la nueva ley de amnistía política argentina. Barrios afirmó que Perón no tiene planes inmediatos de regresar a Argentina, señalando que aunque la medida concede amnistía política, muchos líderes peronistas aún enfrentan demandas civiles. Sostuvo que el presidente Arturo Frondizi tendría que destituir a los jueces designados tras el derrocamiento de Perón en 1955 antes de que los dirigentes exiliados puedan regresar con seguridad.

records.headline: Contradictory reports emerged over whether actress Kim Novak returned
records.summary_en: Contradictory reports emerged over whether actress Kim Novak returned an 8,500-dollar sports car given to her by Lieutenant General Rafael Trujillo Jr., the twenty-nine-year-old son of the Dominican Republic leader. Novak had announced plans two weeks earlier to return the gift upon learning Trujillo had a wife and six children back home, though he subsequently stated he was seeking a divorce. While Novak stated at a Hollywood party that she had returned the vehicle, an aide to Trujillo in Kansas City, Missouri, where the general was attending the Army Command and General Staff School, denied that it had been returned. Meanwhile, the Hollywood dealership that sold the automobile stated it was merely in the shop for a 300-mile checkup with instructions from Novak to return it to her.
records.summary_es: Surgieron informes contradictorios sobre si la actriz Kim Novak devolvió un automóvil deportivo de 8,500 dólares obsequiado por el teniente general Rafael Trujillo hijo, de veintinueve años e hijo del gobernante de la República Dominicana. Novak había anunciado dos semanas antes su intención de devolver el regalo tras enterarse de que Trujillo tenía esposa y seis hijos en su país, aunque él afirmó luego que se estaba divorciando. Aunque Novak aseguró en una fiesta en Hollywood que había devuelto el vehículo, un asistente de Trujillo en Kansas City, Missouri, donde el general asistía a la Escuela de Mando y Estado Mayor del Ejército, negó que lo hubiera hecho. Entre tanto, la agencia de Hollywood que vendió el coche indicó que solo estaba en el taller para una revisión de 300 millas con instrucciones de Novak de devolvérselo a ella.

records.headline: An editorial reviews the ninety-five-page report released by investigators
records.summary_en: An editorial reviews the ninety-five-page report released by investigators Mr. Ernst and Mr. Munson into the disappearance of Galindez. The inquiry concluded that no evidence connects the Dominican Republic or any of its officials with the disappearance, characterizing the kidnapping and murder allegations as a canard by political enemies or a cover for Galindez's Basque fund of more than $1 million. The investigators suggested that further investigation could locate Galindez dead or alive, endorsing the New York Police Department's listing of the case as a missing person. Their findings included a legal opinion that Generalissimo Trujillo and the Dominican Republic were grossly libeled, and while critics attacked the Trujillo-financed report as a whitewash, the editorial notes the investigators' established reputation for integrity.
records.summary_es: Un editorial analiza el informe de noventa y cinco páginas presentado por los investigadores Ernst y Munson sobre la desaparición de Galíndez. La indagación concluyó que no existen pruebas que vinculen a la República Dominicana ni a ninguno de sus funcionarios con la desaparición, y calificó las acusaciones de secuestro y asesinato como una patraña de enemigos políticos o una tapadera para el fondo vasco de Galíndez, superior a $1 millón. Los investigadores señalaron que una investigación adicional podría localizar a Galíndez vivo o muerto, respaldando la inclusión del caso como persona desaparecida por el Departamento de Policía de Nueva York. Sus conclusiones incluyeron una opinión legal de que el generalísimo Trujillo y la República Dominicana fueron gravemente difamados, y aunque los críticos atacaron el informe financiado por Trujillo tildándolo de encubrimiento, el editorial resalta la reconocida reputación de integridad de los investigadores.

records.headline: Pan American World Airways travel experts highlight the Caribbean
records.summary_en: Pan American World Airways travel experts highlight the Caribbean as a diverse region where Spanish, French, Dutch, English, and Danish cultural influences mingle. The report notes that French-speaking Haiti sits next door to the Dominican Republic, described as a stronghold of Spanish culture since the days of Columbus. Travelers can fly by Clipper in one hour and forty-five minutes from Ciudad Trujillo, capital of the Dominican Republic, to the Dutch island of Curacao, or journey from Port-au-Prince to Jamaica in an hour and ten minutes. The article details popular summer package tours enabling vacationers to visit multiple destinations across the Caribbean at packaged rates covering airfare, lodging, meals, and sightseeing.
records.summary_es: Expertos en viajes de Pan American World Airways destacan al Caribe como una región diversa donde confluyen influencias culturales españolas, francesas, holandesas, inglesas y danesas. La crónica señala que Haití, de habla francesa, se encuentra junto a la República Dominicana, a la que califica como un bastión de la cultura española desde los tiempos de Colón. Los viajeros pueden volar en Clipper en una hora y cuarenta y cinco minutos desde Ciudad Trujillo, capital de la República Dominicana, a la isla holandesa de Curazao, o viajar desde Puerto Príncipe a Jamaica en una hora y diez minutos. El artículo detalla populares paquetes turísticos de verano que permiten a los vacacionistas visitar múltiples destinos del Caribe con tarifas combinadas que cubren pasajes aéreos, hospedaje, comidas y excursiones.

records.headline: The United States Senate voted forty-six to thirty-three to reject
records.summary_en: The United States Senate voted forty-six to thirty-three to reject an amendment proposed by Republican Senator John J. Williams to exclude only the Dominican Republic from foreign aid. During the debate, Senator Proxmire criticized assistance to Caribbean dictatorships, charging that Rafael Trujillo, the son of the Dominican strongman, threw away thousands of dollars entertaining Hollywood women. Proxmire stated that young Trujillo spent in the United States in one year approximately the same amount the country provides in aid to the Dominican Republic. While conceding that the expenditures were not the same funds, Proxmire called the lavish spending an example of dictatorial power in a nation possessing one of the lowest living standards in the world.
records.summary_es: El Senado de los Estados Unidos votó cuarenta y seis contra treinta y tres para rechazar una enmienda propuesta por el senador republicano John J. Williams que pretendía excluir únicamente a la República Dominicana de la ayuda exterior. Durante el debate, el senador Proxmire criticó la asistencia a las dictaduras caribeñas y denunció que Rafael Trujillo, hijo del hombre fuerte dominicano, derrochó miles de dólares agasajando a mujeres de Hollywood. Proxmire señaló que el joven Trujillo gastó en los Estados Unidos en un solo año una cantidad aproximadamente igual a la que ese país otorga en ayuda a la República Dominicana. Aunque admitió que no se trataba de los mismos fondos, Proxmire calificó el ostentoso gasto como una muestra de poder dictatorial en una nación con uno de los niveles de vida más bajos del mundo.

records.headline: Forty prize Holstein heifers from Wisconsin were transported
records.summary_en: Forty prize Holstein heifers from Wisconsin were transported to the Dominican Republic aboard two Pan American World Airways cargo Clippers. The cattle were purchased for the expanding ranches of Generalissimo Rafael Leonidas Trujillo, having been selected at Wisconsin cattle shows by Edwin Houston, a cattle buyer from Boerne, Texas. In a concurrent shipment, Houston also sent three prize Cheviot sheep from Wisconsin and three prize Nubian goats from Texas to the ranch of Enrique Vigil Colunga near Camaguey, Cuba.

En un envío simultáneo, Houston despachó además tres ovejas Cheviot de Wisconsin y tres cabras nubias de Texas hacia la hacienda de Enrique Vigil Colunga, cerca de Camagüey, Cuba.

records.headline: The Dominican Government cancelled permission to return to Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: The Dominican Government cancelled permission to return to Santo Domingo for former Argentine army major Pablo Vicente, one of ousted President Juan Peron's principal aides. The Security Department in Ciudad Trujillo notified airlines that Vicente's entry permit had been revoked following his departure from the island two months earlier to an unknown destination. Vicente previously served as second-in-command of a Buenos Aires garrison regiment during Peron's September 1955 downfall, having resisted the coup before clandestinely returning to Argentina ahead of the February 23 elections to assess Peronist factions and prepare a political report for Peron.
records.summary_es: El gobierno dominicano canceló el permiso para retornar a Santo Domingo al mayor retirado del ejército argentino Pablo Vicente, uno de los principales colaboradores del expresidente Juan Perón. El Departamento de Seguridad en Ciudad Trujillo notificó a las aerolíneas la revocación del permiso de entrada de Vicente luego de que este abandonara la isla dos meses antes con rumbo desconocido. Vicente había sido segundo al mando de un regimiento de la guarnición de Buenos Aires durante la caída de Perón en septiembre de 1955, habiéndose resistido al golpe antes de ingresar clandestinamente a Argentina en vísperas de las elecciones del 23 de febrero para evaluar las facciones peronistas y redactar un informe político para Perón.
