records.headline: Young Rafael Trujillo Jr. was removed from the graduating class
records.summary_en: Young Rafael Trujillo Jr. was removed from the graduating class at the United States Army Command and General Staff College at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas. Although denied a diploma, the free-spending son of Dominican dictator Rafael Trujillo was simultaneously appointed to a newly created position as chairman of the joint chiefs of staff in the Dominican Republic. The twenty-nine-year-old lieutenant general had previously generated widespread controversy over lavish spending while convalescing.
records.summary_es: El joven Rafael Trujillo hijo fue retirado de la promoción de graduados del Colegio de Mando y Estado Mayor del Ejército de los Estados Unidos en Fort Leavenworth, Kansas. Pese a serle denegado el diploma, el derrochador hijo del dictador dominicano Rafael Trujillo fue nombrado de manera simultánea para un cargo de nueva creación como presidente del estado mayor conjunto en la República Dominicana. El teniente general de veintinueve años había provocado con anterioridad una amplia controversia por sus cuantiosos gastos mientras convalecía.

Davison referred to Trujillo as the big spender who had been purchasing furs and gifts for movie personalities. The suspect recalled considering the plot before questioning whether the spender's name was Trujillo.

records.headline: The twenty-nine-year-old commander of the Dominican Air Force
records.summary_en: The twenty-nine-year-old commander of the Dominican Air Force, Lieutenant General Rafael Trujillo Jr., who cannot fly an airplane, will not graduate with his class from the U.S. Command and General Staff College at Ft. Leavenworth, Kansas. Representative Charles Brownson reported that the United States Army advised him Trujillo did not successfully complete the course and would receive only a certificate of attendance rather than a graduation certificate. In the Dominican Republic, his uncle, President Hector B. Trujillo, announced that the young officer will head a newly established combined chiefs of staff designed to better coordinate the Army, Navy, and Air Force. Trujillo previously stated plans to return to Hollywood to continue courting film star Kim Novak en route home following graduation ceremonies.
records.summary_es: El comandante de veintinueve años de la Fuerza Aérea Dominicana, teniente general Rafael Trujillo hijo, que no sabe pilotar un avión, no se graduará con su promoción en el Colegio de Mando y Estado Mayor de los Estados Unidos en Ft. Leavenworth, Kansas. El representante Charles Brownson informó que el Ejército estadounidense le comunicó que Trujillo no completó con éxito el curso y recibiría únicamente un certificado de asistencia en lugar de un diploma de graduación. En la República Dominicana, su tío, el presidente Héctor B. Trujillo, anunció que el joven militar encabezará un recién creado estado mayor conjunto destinado a coordinar mejor el Ejército, la Marina y la Fuerza Aérea. Trujillo había manifestado con anterioridad sus planes de regresar a Hollywood para seguir cortejando a la estrella de cine Kim Novak en su viaje de vuelta a casa tras los actos de graduación.

records.headline: Following his departure from the Command and General Staff College
records.summary_en: Following his departure from the Command and General Staff College at Fort Leavenworth, Lieutenant General Rafael Trujillo Jr. returned to Southern California and announced plans to host a party aboard his yacht. Movie stars Kim Novak and Zsa Zsa Gabor were invited to the gathering. Arriving on the Santa Fe Railroad at Pasadena in his private railroad car, Trujillo stated he expected to remain in Southern California for about fifteen days and planned to meet with Gabor. He did not specify whether the yacht party would take place in United States waters or in the Dominican Republic.
records.summary_es: Tras su salida del Colegio de Mando y Estado Mayor en Fort Leavenworth, el teniente general Rafael Trujillo hijo regresó al sur de California y anunció planes para ofrecer una fiesta a bordo de su yate. Las estrellas de cine Kim Novak y Zsa Zsa Gabor fueron invitadas a la reunión. Al llegar en su vagón privado a Pasadena por el ferrocarril Santa Fe, Trujillo declaró que esperaba permanecer en el sur de California durante unos quince días y que tenía previsto reunirse con Gabor. No precisó si la fiesta en el yate se celebraría en aguas estadounidenses o en la República Dominicana.

records.headline: The Dominican government defended Rafael Trujillo Jr. against United States critics
records.summary_en: The Dominican government defended Rafael Trujillo Jr. against United States critics who suggested the Dominican Republic did not need American aid if he could spend lavish sums in the United States, countering that he was spending his own money and that the republic paid for everything it received. Tension escalated after Representative Brownson of Indiana revealed that Trujillo Jr. was not graduating from the Command and General Staff School at Leavenworth because he had not finished the course. In retaliation, the generalissimo denounced the United States, ordered 90 Dominican cadets and officers out of United States military schools, and summoned the Dominican Congress to act. Meanwhile, young Trujillo returned to Hollywood, where Zsa Zsa stated she would try to find him a new spouse and host a party aboard his family yacht.
records.summary_es: El gobierno dominicano defendió a Rafael Trujillo hijo frente a las críticas en Estados Unidos que señalaban que la República Dominicana no necesitaba ayuda estadounidense si él podía gastar sumas tan elevadas en ese país, respondiendo que gastaba su propio dinero y que la república pagaba por todo lo que recibía. La tensión aumentó después de que el representante Brownson de Indiana reveló que Trujillo hijo no se graduaría de la Escuela de Estado Mayor y Comando en Leavenworth porque no había completado el curso. En represalia, el generalísimo arremetió contra Estados Unidos, ordenó la salida de 90 cadetes y oficiales dominicanos de las academias militares estadounidenses y convocó al Congreso dominicano para que actuara. Mientras tanto, el joven Trujillo regresó a Hollywood, donde Zsa Zsa declaró que intentaría buscarle una nueva cónyuge y ofrecerle una fiesta a bordo del yate familiar.

records.headline: Rafael Trujillo Jr., visiting playboy and lieutenant general from the Dominican
records.summary_en: Rafael Trujillo Jr., visiting playboy and lieutenant general from the Dominican Republic, hosted a party aboard his luxury yacht Angelita in Los Angeles harbor that lasted well into mid-morning. The host threw up a sugar cane curtain around the event, keeping the gangplank chained and padlocked except for a moment when two women departed in a waiting car. Two crewmen at the gatehouse turned away all inquiries while Latin music played across the harbor until after dawn, leaving the full guest list unconfirmed.
records.summary_es: Rafael Trujillo hijo, playboy visitante y teniente general de la República Dominicana, ofreció una fiesta a bordo de su yate de lujo Angelita en el puerto de Los Ángeles que se prolongó hasta bien entrada la mañana. El anfitrión levantó una cortina de caña de azúcar en torno al festejo, manteniendo la pasarela encadenada y con candado salvo por un breve momento en que dos mujeres se marcharon en un automóvil que las esperaba. Dos tripulantes en la caseta de guardia rechazaron todas las preguntas mientras la música latina resonaba en el puerto hasta después del amanecer, quedando sin confirmar la lista completa de invitados.

records.headline: A reported bomb plot overheard in a waterfront bar failed to disrupt
records.summary_en: A reported bomb plot overheard in a waterfront bar failed to disrupt festivities aboard the luxury yacht Angelita belonging to Dominican Lieutenant General Rafael Trujillo Jr. in Los Angeles harbor. While police bomb squad officers, firemen, and Coast Guardsmen conducted a three-hour search of the 350-foot vessel and dock pilings, guests including actress Zsa Zsa Gabor and George Sanders continued dancing to a twelve-piece Latin band. Trujillo Jr. was aboard the yacht, though reporters on the dock did not observe him on deck during the search. The search was initiated after a hungover longshoreman reported overhearing two men boast of planting an explosive device before departing the police station without leaving his name.
records.summary_es: Un supuesto plan de bomba escuchado en un bar del puerto no logró interrumpir las festividades a bordo del yate de lujo Angelita, perteneciente al teniente general dominicano Rafael Trujillo hijo en el puerto de Los Ángeles. Mientras agentes del escuadrón antibombas, bomberos y guardacostas realizaban una búsqueda de tres horas en la nave de 350 pies y en los pilotes del muelle, los invitados, entre ellos la actriz Zsa Zsa Gabor y George Sanders, continuaron bailando con una orquesta latina de doce músicos. Trujillo hijo se encontraba a bordo de la embarcación, aunque los reporteros en el muelle no lo vieron en cubierta durante la inspección. El registro se inició luego de que un estibador con resaca informó haber oído a dos hombres jactarse de haber colocado un artefacto explosivo, tras lo cual se marchó de la comisaría sin dejar su nombre.

records.headline: The Justice Department released documents consisting of a pilot's
records.summary_en: The Justice Department released documents consisting of a pilot's logbook, a pocket memo book, and a page of notes in the handwriting of missing American flyer Gerald L. Murphy after receiving permission from his parents. Representative Porter of Oregon stated the papers provide solid physical evidence of a link between Murphy and Jesus de Galindez, the Basque scholar who vanished in New York on March 12, 1956, after writing a doctoral dissertation on 'The Era of Trujillo.' Murphy was last seen in Ciudad Trujillo on December 3, 1956. The documents were recovered from a steel filing cabinet in Murphy's Ciudad Trujillo apartment by American consular officials and transferred to the Justice Department for a grand jury investigation.

Murphy fue visto por última vez en Ciudad Trujillo el 3 de diciembre de 1956. Los documentos fueron recuperados de un archivador de acero en el apartamento de Murphy en Ciudad Trujillo por funcionarios consulares estadounidenses y entregados al Departamento de Justicia para una investigación de gran jurado.

records.headline: An analysis in the Evening star connects Vice President Nixon's policy
records.summary_en: An analysis in the Evening star connects Vice President Nixon's policy recommendations after his Caracas tour with visible signs of a firmer United States posture toward the Dominican Republic dictatorship of Generalissimo Rafael Leonidas Trujillo Molina. The release of the Murphy papers is highlighted alongside the United States Army's uncompromising decision to flunk Trujillo's namesake son out of the Command and General Staff College following his high-profile Hollywood escapades. Additionally, American military authorities demonstrated an eager willingness to discount Trujillo's importance to hemispheric defense after the Dominican government threatened to cancel a missile tracking station agreement.
records.summary_es: Un análisis en el Evening star conecta las recomendaciones políticas del vicepresidente Nixon tras su gira por Caracas con indicios visibles de una postura más firme de Estados Unidos hacia la dictadura de la República Dominicana del generalísimo Rafael Leónidas Trujillo Molina. La divulgación de los documentos del caso Murphy se destaca junto con la tajante decisión del Ejército de Estados Unidos de reprobar al hijo homónimo de Trujillo en la Escuela de Comando y Estado Mayor tras sus notorias andanzas por Hollywood. Asimismo, las autoridades militares estadounidenses mostraron plena disposición a restar importancia al papel de Trujillo en la defensa hemisférica luego de que el régimen dominicano amenazara con anular el acuerdo sobre una estación de rastreo de proyectiles.

records.headline: The promotion of 29-year-old Rafael Trujillo Jr. to the rank of full
records.summary_en: The promotion of 29-year-old Rafael Trujillo Jr. to the rank of full general in the Dominican Republic's army and air force was announced by his father, Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo. The promotion followed young Trujillo's appointment to the newly created post of chairman of the Dominican joint chiefs of staff, announced on the exact day the United States Army revealed he had flunked out of its Command and General Staff School at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas. The American military reported that Trujillo Jr. would receive only a certificate of attendance because he failed to successfully complete the course. Young Trujillo previously commanded the Dominican air force as a lieutenant general and was currently in Los Angeles, California.
records.summary_es: El ascenso de Rafael Trujillo hijo, de 29 años, al rango de general en el ejército y la fuerza aérea de la República Dominicana fue anunciado por su padre, el generalísimo Rafael Trujillo. La promoción siguió a la designación del joven Trujillo al recién creado cargo de presidente del estado mayor conjunto dominicano, anunciada el mismo día en que el Ejército de Estados Unidos reveló que había reprobado en su Escuela de Comando y Estado Mayor en Fort Leavenworth, Kansas. Las autoridades militares estadounidenses informaron que Trujillo hijo solo recibiría un certificado de asistencia debido a que no completó satisfactoriamente el curso. El joven Trujillo comandaba anteriormente la fuerza aérea con el rango de teniente general y se encontraba en Los Ángeles, California.

records.headline: The four-masted yacht Angelita belonging to Dominican General Rafael Trujillo Jr.
records.summary_en: The four-masted yacht Angelita belonging to Dominican General Rafael Trujillo Jr. has returned to Los Angeles Harbor. Actress Zsa Zsa Gabor announced that she will serve as hostess for a party aboard the 350-foot vessel on July 8, noting that it is now firmly secured to a dock with cables, a gangplank, and a telephone line. Young Trujillo, son of the Dominican Republic's strongman, had briefly sailed the vessel 35 miles northwest to Santa Monica to be nearer to Hollywood attractions. However, the vessel returned after being unable to fit into the local harbor, forcing it to anchor a quarter-mile offshore where telephone lines could not reach.

records.summary_en: New York attorney Morris Ernst asserted in a telegram to Representative Porter of Oregon that missing American flyer Gerald L. Murphy manufactured evidence as a cloak for other operations, though Ernst did not specify what those operations were. Porter had recently released Murphy's pilot logbook, notebook, and handwritten notes, stating they strongly backed earlier reports linking Murphy to Jesus de Galindez. Galindez, an outspoken critic of Dictator Rafael L. Trujillo's regime in the Dominican Republic, disappeared in New York on March 12, 1956. Opponents of Trujillo contend that Murphy flew Galindez to the Dominican Republic, where he was assassinated by regime agents.

Porter había divulgado recientemente el libro de vuelo, una libreta y notas manuscritas de Murphy, sosteniendo que respaldaban con fuerza los informes previos que vinculaban a Murphy con Jesús de Galíndez. Galíndez, un enérgico crítico del régimen del dictador Rafael L. Trujillo en la República Dominicana, desapareció en Nueva York el 12 de marzo de 1956. Los opositores a Trujillo sostienen que Murphy trasladó en avión a Galíndez a la República Dominicana, donde fue asesinado por agentes del régimen.

Trujillo in his position as Generalissimo of the armed forces, United Press International. At the same time, the legislature promoted his brother Hector to the exact same rank. Following the announcement, the Dominican Republic officially possesses two generalissimos at the head of its military establishment.
records.summary_es: Un despacho desde Ciudad Trujillo informa que el Congreso dominicano ha ratificado al hombre fuerte Rafael L. Trujillo en su cargo de generalísimo de las fuerzas armadas, de United Press International. Al mismo tiempo, el cuerpo legislativo ascendió a su hermano Héctor al mismo rango militar. Tras este anuncio, la República Dominicana cuenta oficialmente con dos generalísimos al frente de su estructura armada.

The bill, inspired by reports that Rafael Trujillo is about to retire from active duty as Commander of the Armed Forces, authorized him to wear the uniform whenever he chooses, on or off duty. DOMINICAN REPUBLIC HAS TWO GENERALISSIMOS

CIUDAD TRUJILLO, D. CR. (UPI) — Congress has confirmed strongman Rafael L. Trujillo in his position as Generalissimo of the armed forces and promoted his brother Héctor to the same rank, it was announced today.

The bill, inspired by reports that Rafael Trujillo is about to retire from active duty as Commander of the Armed Forces, authorized him to wear the uniform whenever he chooses, on or off duty.

Héctor Trujillo, who had held the rank of general is President of the Dominican Republic.

records.headline: New York attorney Morris Ernst, who previously cleared Dominican Republic dictator
records.summary_en: New York attorney Morris Ernst, who previously cleared Dominican Republic dictator Rafael L. Trujillo of involvement in the disappearance of Basque scholar Jesus de Galindez, has called for a congressional investigation into the case. Ernst stated that an official congressional probe is now necessary in order to place the facts and the truth properly before the American people. Galindez, an outspoken opponent of the Trujillo regime, vanished from New York on March 12, 1956, amid persistent speculation that he was kidnapped.
records.summary_es: El abogado neoyorquino Morris Ernst, quien previamente exoneró al dictador de la República Dominicana Rafael L. Trujillo de toda implicación en la desaparición del académico vasco Jesús de Galíndez, ha solicitado una investigación del Congreso sobre el caso. Ernst afirmó que una indagatoria legislativa formal es ahora necesaria para presentar los hechos y la verdad de forma adecuada ante el pueblo estadounidense. Galíndez, un enérgico opositor al régimen trujillista, desapareció en Nueva York el 12 de marzo de 1956 en medio de persistentes sospechas de que fue secuestrado.

records.headline: A 22-year-old actress and model, Lynn Heyburn, filed a lawsuit
records.summary_en: A 22-year-old actress and model, Lynn Heyburn, filed a lawsuit in Los Angeles seeking 10,000 dollars against General Rafael Trujillo Jr. for failing to adequately supervise his house guests. The complaint alleges that guests threw Heyburn into the swimming pool of Trujillo's rented Beverly Hills mansion in an unsupervised manner last April. In addition to Trujillo, who is the son of the Dominican Republic's strongman, the suit names playboy Porfirio Rubirosa and his brother Gilberto as the individuals who dunked her for no apparent reason, though Heyburn noted that Trujillo himself was not present.
records.summary_es: Una actriz y modelo de 22 años, Lynn Heyburn, presentó una demanda en Los Ángeles en la que reclama 10.000 dólares al general Rafael Trujillo hijo por no supervisar adecuadamente a sus invitados. La demanda sostiene que varios asistentes arrojaron a Heyburn a la piscina de la mansión alquilada por Trujillo en Beverly Hills de manera no supervisada el pasado mes de abril. Además de Trujillo, hijo del hombre fuerte de la República Dominicana, el recurso legal señala al playboy Porfirio Rubirosa y a su hermano Gilberto como los responsables de haberla empapado sin motivo evidente, aunque Heyburn aclaró que el propio Trujillo no se encontraba presente.

records.headline: Attorneys representing General Rafael Trujillo Jr. accepted
records.summary_en: Attorneys representing General Rafael Trujillo Jr. accepted a summons in San Pedro, California, in connection with a 10,000-dollar damage suit filed by Hollywood actress Lyn Heburn. The actress sued the Dominican Republic's visiting playboy after two of his friends allegedly dumped her fully clothed into the swimming pool at his rented mansion. A deputy county marshal had previously been turned away by aides when attempting to serve Trujillo, but returned to the general's docked luxury yacht, where two lawyers met him and accepted service of the legal papers.
records.summary_es: Los abogados del general Rafael Trujillo hijo aceptaron una citación judicial en San Pedro, California, en relación con una demanda por daños y perjuicios de 10.000 dólares presentada por la actriz de Hollywood Lyn Heburn. La actriz demandó al playboy de la República Dominicana alegando que dos de sus amigos la arrojaron completamente vestida a la piscina de su mansión alquilada. Un alguacil adjunto del condado había sido rechazado previamente por los asistentes de Trujillo al intentar notificarlo, pero regresó al yate de lujo del general que se encuentra atracado en el puerto, donde dos abogados lo recibieron y aceptaron los documentos judiciales.

records.headline: Onlookers and harbor visitors pointed and laughed at General Rafael Trujillo's
records.summary_en: Onlookers and harbor visitors pointed and laughed at General Rafael Trujillo's yacht, the Angelita, after graffiti was discovered near the waterline. When a boatload of press photographers arrived to photograph the gleaming vessel from the water, a crewman looked over the railing and spotted the words 'Zsa Zsa slept here' painted under the deck overhang. Painters from the yacht's 80-man crew promptly covered the lettering, which harbor officials believed was applied from a small boat with a spray can overnight. Actress Zsa Zsa Gabor had previously introduced the son of the Dominican Republic's strongman to Hollywood society.
records.summary_es: Curiosos y visitantes del puerto señalaban y se reían del yate del general Rafael Trujillo, el Angelita, tras descubrirse un grafiti cerca de la línea de flotación. Pintores de la tripulación de 80 hombres del yate cubrieron con prontitud las letras, que las autoridades del puerto consideraron fueron trazadas durante la noche desde un bote pequeño con una lata de aerosol. La actriz Zsa Zsa Gabor había introducido previamente al hijo del hombre fuerte de la República Dominicana en la sociedad de Hollywood.

records.headline: A society notice in The Key West citizen reports that visitors
records.summary_en: A society notice in The Key West citizen reports that visitors staying with the local Ciesinski family are embarking on a ten-day Caribbean cruise aboard the steamer Evangeline. The voyage includes five ports of call, notably Ciudad Trujillo in the Dominican Republic, San Juan in Puerto Rico, and St. Thomas in the Virgin Islands. Following the cruise, the travelers plan to spend several additional days in Key West before returning home to Chicago.

La travesía incluye cinco puertos de escala, en particular Ciudad Trujillo en la República Dominicana, San Juan en Puerto Rico y Santo Tomás en las Islas Vírgenes. Tras el viaje marítimo, los viajeros planean pasar varios días adicionales en Cayo Hueso antes de regresar a su hogar en Chicago.

records.headline: Cuban commercial pilots, including Jorge Foyo, Miguel Enciso
records.summary_en: Cuban commercial pilots, including Jorge Foyo, Miguel Enciso, Luis Tabio, Fausto Gomez, Humberto Armanda, and Rafael Trujillo, stated they would not return to piloting Cuban commercial airplanes until Batista's government is no longer in power. Captain Enciso, a former pilot for Aeropostal Cubana, declared they left their country after refusing to transport arms destined for killing Cubans. Francisco Alvarez stated that last April the Batista government ordered Cuban commercial pilots to collect arms in Ciudad Trujillo and transport them to Cuba. The pilots accepted two-year contracts paying 700 a month with Pakistan International Airline, arranged by the International Rescue Committee and the International Federation of Commercial Airline Pilots.
records.summary_es: Pilotos comerciales cubanos, entre ellos Jorge Foyo, Miguel Enciso, Luis Tabio, Fausto Gómez, Humberto Armanda y Rafael Trujillo, declararon que no volverán a pilotar aviones comerciales cubanos hasta que el gobierno de Batista ya no esté en el poder. El capitán Enciso, expiloto de Aeropostal Cubana, declaró que abandonaron su país tras negarse a transportar armas destinadas a matar cubanos. Francisco Álvarez afirmó que el pasado abril el gobierno de Batista ordenó a los pilotos comerciales cubanos recoger armas en Ciudad Trujillo y trasladarlas a Cuba. Los pilotos aceptaron contratos de dos años con un sueldo de 700 al mes con Pakistan International Airline, gestionados por el Comité Internacional de Rescate y la Federación Internacional de Pilotos de Líneas Aéreas Comerciales.

records.headline: A United States Navy transport plane was reported forced down
records.summary_en: A United States Navy transport plane was reported forced down by fighter aircraft of the Dominican Republic's air force. The aircraft was released after being searched and detained for an hour in Santiago, on the north coast of the Dominican Republic. Dominican authorities were reportedly searching for smuggled arms, although no immediate explanation was provided as to why they intercepted a clearly marked American military plane. Ray Camay of radio station KIOA in Des Moines, Iowa, telephoned the report from the United States Navy base at Guantanamo, Cuba, following the aircraft's return.

Se informó que las autoridades dominicanas buscaban armas de contrabando, aunque no se ofreció una explicación inmediata de por qué interceptaron un avión militar estadounidense claramente identificado. Ray Camay, de la estación de radio KIOA en Des Moines, Iowa, transmitió la noticia por teléfono desde la base naval estadounidense en Guantánamo, Cuba, tras el regreso del avión.

records.headline: A political commentary contrasts the enthusiastic public reception
records.summary_en: A political commentary contrasts the enthusiastic public reception in Caracas for Congressman Porter, who addressed a crowd of 20,000 people and was hailed as a hero, with that accorded to Nixon. The commentary explains that Porter had campaigned vigorously against Generalissimo Trujillo of the Dominican Republic and other Latin dictators. In contrast, Nixon had previously aligned with State Department policy of doing business with dictators and was photographed in an embrace with dictator Trujillo, though Nixon has recently advocated an American policy of discouraging dictators.
records.summary_es: Un comentario político contrasta el entusiasta recibimiento popular en Caracas brindado al congresista Porter, quien habló ante una multitud de 20,000 personas y fue aclamado como héroe, con el trato recibido por Nixon. El texto explica que Porter había hecho una vigorosa campaña contra el generalísimo Trujillo de la República Dominicana y otros dictadores latinoamericanos. En cambio, Nixon se había apegado previamente a la política del Departamento de Estado de negociar con dictadores y fue fotografiado en un abrazo con el dictador Trujillo, aunque recientemente Nixon se ha pronunciado a favor de una política estadounidense que desaliente a los dictadores.

PRESIDENTIAL WELCOME FOR TRUJILLO JUNIOR DECREED BY EXECUTIVE

CIUDAD TRUJILLO. (UPI).—The government decreed Wednesday that Gen. Rafael Trujillo, Jr. be received with the honors due a president of the country when he returns home.

Young Trujillo, who was denied a diploma by the U. S. Army's Command and General Staff College this year, is on his way home from the United States by yacht.

Trujillo is a son of the man who has been the dominant figure in Dominican politics for a quarter of a century, and a nephew of Héctor B. Trujillo, who is now president.

records.headline: The Washington Ballet company will depart on Monday for an air
records.summary_en: The Washington Ballet company will depart on Monday for an air tour of the Dominican Republic, marking the troupe's first foreign booking. Renowned dancers Alicia Alonso, Igor Youskevitch, and Frederic Franklin will accompany the young dancers, with Alonso and Youskevitch cutting short vacations for the engagement. Following a cocktail party held in their honor at the Dominican Embassy, the company is scheduled to depart Washington at 11 a.m. Their three-day performances will be staged at Ciudad Trujillo's outdoor theater, described as one of the world's largest.
records.summary_es: La compañía del Ballet de Washington partirá el lunes en viaje aéreo hacia una gira por la República Dominicana, lo que constituye la primera contratación en el extranjero para el elenco. Destacados bailarines como Alicia Alonso, Igor Youskevitch y Frederic Franklin acompañarán a los jóvenes integrantes, interrumpiendo Alonso y Youskevitch sus vacaciones para cumplir con el compromiso. Tras un cóctel celebrado en su honor en la embajada dominicana, la compañía tiene programada su salida de Washington a las 11 a.m. Sus presentaciones de tres días tendrán como escenario el teatro al aire libre de Ciudad Trujillo, descrito como uno de los más grandes del mundo.

records.headline: President Trujillo acted on the recommendation of his nephew
records.summary_en: President Trujillo acted on the recommendation of his nephew, the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, regarding bilateral relations with Washington. The recommendation asserted that Washington had not fully complied with a confidential agreement between the Dominican Republic and the United States dated December 7, 1056. It suggested continuing the accord to determine whether the United States is genuinely interested in maintaining it. Earlier in the month, Generalissimo Trujillo stated to reporters that he would reject any further American aid unless he received satisfaction.
records.summary_es: El presidente Trujillo actuó según la recomendación formulada por su sobrino, quien ejerce la presidencia del Estado Mayor Conjunto, respecto a las relaciones bilaterales con Washington. Dicha recomendación señalaba que Washington no había cumplido cabalmente con un acuerdo confidencial entre la República Dominicana y los Estados Unidos suscrito con fecha 7 de diciembre de 1056. El texto sugería la continuación del convenio para determinar si los Estados Unidos están realmente interesados en conservarlo. A principios de mes, el generalísimo Trujillo manifestó a periodistas que rechazaría cualquier ayuda estadounidense adicional a menos que obtuviera satisfacción.

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that two
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that two United States senators addressed the Dominican Legislature and warmly praised Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo. Democrat James O. Eastland of Mississippi and Republican William E. Jenner of Indiana lauded the Dominican government's anti-communist stand along with its social and economic achievements. The senators arrived on Tuesday as part of a Caribbean good will tour with several United States representatives. They conferred on Wednesday with Generalissimo Trujillo and his brother, President Hector Trujillo.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Associated Press desde Ciudad Trujillo informa que dos senadores de los Estados Unidos se dirigieron a la legislatura dominicana y elogiaron calurosamente al generalísimo Rafael Trujillo. El demócrata James O. Eastland de Misisipi y el republicano William E. Jenner de Indiana alabaron la postura anticomunista del gobierno dominicano junto con sus logros sociales y económicos. Los senadores llegaron el martes en el marco de una gira de buena voluntad por el Caribe acompañados de varios representantes estadounidenses. El miércoles se entrevistaron con el generalísimo Trujillo y su hermano, el presidente Héctor Trujillo.

records.headline: Travel expenses for the trip to the Dominican Republic by Republican Senator William E. Jenner of Indiana
records.summary_en: Travel expenses for the trip to the Dominican Republic by Republican Senator William E. Jenner of Indiana and Senator James O. Eastland will be paid by the Senate Internal Security Subcommittee. Accompanied by Jay Sourwine, attorney for the Communist-hunting subgroup, the two senators traveled to the Dominican Republic at the invitation of its government. During their visit, the senators addressed a joint session of the Dominican Legislature and highly praised Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo. Congressional aides stated that the senators and Sourwine undertook the journey as official Senate business.
records.summary_es: Los gastos de viaje a la República Dominicana del senador republicano William E. Jenner de Indiana y del senador James O. Eastland serán cubiertos por el Subcomité de Seguridad Interna del Senado. Acompañados por Jay Sourwine, abogado del subgrupo senatorial dedicado a la persecución de comunistas, ambos senadores viajaron a la República Dominicana por invitación de su gobierno. Durante la visita, los legisladores hablaron ante una sesión conjunta de la legislatura dominicana y elogiaron enérgicamente al generalísimo Rafael Trujillo. Colaboradores parlamentarios afirmaron que los senadores y Sourwine realizaron el periplo en misión oficial del Senado.

records.headline: The United States Court of Appeals ordered a new trial for Washington attorney
records.summary_en: The United States Court of Appeals ordered a new trial for Washington attorney John J. Frank regarding charges that he acted illegally as an unregistered agent for the Dominican Republic. In reversing Frank's conviction from the previous year, the court ruled in a 2-1 decision that the prosecutor improperly attempted to connect him before the jury with the March, 1956, disappearance of Dr. Jesus de Galindez, a Columbia University professor known as a foe of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo. Frank had been convicted under the Foreign Agents Registration Act and sentenced to a prison term of eight months to two years. In the majority opinion, Chief Appellate Judge Edgerton and Judge Charles Danaher found that evidence concerning Galindez and missing American pilot Gerald Murphy was improperly introduced.
records.summary_es: El Tribunal de Apelaciones de los Estados Unidos ordenó la celebración de un nuevo juicio para el abogado de Washington John J. Frank respecto a las acusaciones de haber actuado ilegalmente como agente no registrado de la República Dominicana. Al revocar la condena de Frank del año anterior, el tribunal resolvió por 2 votos contra 1 que el fiscal intentó indebidamente vincularlo ante el jurado con la desaparición en marzo de 1956 del Dr. Jesús de Galíndez, profesor de Columbia University conocido como opositor al generalísimo Rafael Trujillo. Frank había sido condenado bajo la Ley de Registro de Agentes Extranjeros y sentenciado a una pena de prisión de ocho meses a dos años. En el fallo mayoritario, el juez principal de apelaciones Edgerton y el juez Charles Danaher determinaron que las pruebas relativas a Galíndez y al desaparecido piloto estadounidense Gerald Murphy fueron presentadas indebidamente.

records.headline: That more than 300,000 Dominicans paraded on the 25th anniversary of Generalissimo Trujillo receiving
records.summary_en: That more than 300,000 Dominicans paraded on the 25th anniversary of Generalissimo Trujillo receiving the title of Benefactor de la Patria, a news item date-lined Ciudad Trujillo reports. The gathering was described as the largest public demonstration on record. During the observance, the Dominican chief announced the launching of a $650,000,000 five-year plan designed to bring the Caribbean republic to the forefront of Latin American nations in material and cultural progress.
records.summary_es: Que más de 300,000 dominicanos desfilaron con motivo del 25.º aniversario de la entrega al generalísimo Trujillo del título de Benefactor de la Patria, una noticia fechada en Ciudad Trujillo informa. La concentración fue descrita como la mayor manifestación pública de la que se tenga registro. Durante la jornada, el líder dominicano anunció la puesta en marcha de un plan quinquenal de $650,000,000 destinado a colocar a la república caribeña a la vanguardia de las naciones latinoamericanas en adelantos materiales y culturales.

records.headline: United States Justice Department officials decided to retry
records.summary_en: United States Justice Department officials decided to retry John Joseph Frank on charges of failing to register as an agent of President Trujillo of the Dominican Republic. Frank's previous conviction on the charge was set aside by the United States Court of Appeals for the District in a 2-to-1 decision. The appellate court ruled that the prosecutor's effort to link Frank, a former FBI agent, with the 1956 disappearance of Columbia University professor Jesus de Galindez was prejudicial. Dr. de Galindez, whose disappearance remains unsolved, was a foe of Generalissimo Trujillo. Authorities chose retrial over appealing the court's decision, though no trial date has been established.
records.summary_es: Funcionarios del Departamento de Justicia de los Estados Unidos decidieron juzgar nuevamente a John Joseph Frank por los cargos de no haberse registrado como agente del presidente Trujillo de la República Dominicana. La condena anterior de Frank por dicha acusación fue revocada por el Tribunal de Apelaciones de los Estados Unidos para el Distrito en un fallo de 2 contra 1. El tribunal de apelación determinó que el intento del fiscal de vincular a Frank, un exagente del FBI, con la desaparición en 1956 del profesor de Columbia University Jesús de Galíndez resultó perjudicial. El Dr. de Galíndez, cuya desaparición continúa sin resolverse, era un opositor al generalísimo Trujillo. Las autoridades optaron por celebrar un nuevo juicio en lugar de apelar la decisión judicial, aunque no se ha fijado fecha para el proceso.

records.headline: Filmmaker Alexander, who recently completed several documentary films
records.summary_en: Filmmaker Alexander, who recently completed several documentary films for Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo's government, described the Dominican Republic as an outstanding example of color integration upon his return. He stated that across his worldwide travels, it was the only nation where he found people of all colors holding top government and private positions, with ability serving as the sole standard of judgment. Alexander noted that Trujillo had often stated his nation was open to all individuals oppressed or denied privileges through color discrimination elsewhere, adding that his tour revealed nothing to the contrary. Alexander was also honored as the first American Negro invited to Trujillo's birthday ball.
records.summary_es: El cineasta Alexander, quien recientemente completó varios documentales para el gobierno del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo, describió a la República Dominicana a su regreso como un ejemplo sobresaliente de integración racial. Afirmó que en todos sus viajes por el mundo era la única nación donde halló a personas de todos los colores ocupando los más altos cargos gubernamentales y privados, siendo la capacidad el único criterio de evaluación. Alexander señaló que Trujillo había expresado a menudo que su país estaba abierto a todas las personas oprimidas o privadas de privilegios debido a la discriminación racial en otros lugares, y agregó que durante su recorrido por la nación no encontró nada en sentido contrario. Alexander fue además agasajado por ser el primer negro estadounidense invitado al baile de cumpleaños de Trujillo.

records.headline: A travel report recounting a Caribbean and South American tour
records.summary_en: A travel report recounting a Caribbean and South American tour describes Caracas as a high-priced city with fine residences and active slum clearance supported by oil revenues. Departing Caracas at 10 a.m., the tour made short stops at the island of Curacao and at Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic. The travelers then arrived in Miami, completing a six-week tour that covered 11,650 miles by air.

Tras partir de Caracas a las 10 a.m., la gira realizó breves escalas en la isla de Curazao y en Ciudad Trujillo, República Dominicana. Los viajeros llegaron luego a Miami, completando una gira de seis semanas que abarcó 11,650 millas por vía aérea.

records.headline: According to local rebel sympathizer Stincer, information from rebel
records.summary_en: According to local rebel sympathizer Stincer, information from rebel circles indicated that Rafael Trujillo, strongman of Santo Domingo, entered an agreement with Cuban President Fulgencio Batista to provide 30 planes flying the Cuban flag to bomb Cuban cities from Dominican bases. The source further alleged that Dominican troops were slated to be transported by air from Santo Domingo to Cuba to assist Batista in quelling the insurrection, with the aim of provoking intervention by the United Nations or the United States. The plan also reportedly involved transferring 45 tanks sold by the United States to Nicaragua over to Batista's forces, as local sympathizers conducted an orderly one-hour street demonstration in Key West. Participants in the demonstration pointed out that Key West was a major point of resistance when the Cuban nation was engaged in the battle for freedom from Spain, and that it was therefore quite fitting that those who believed that the people of Cuba “should be freed from the tyranny of the Dictator Batista” and who are now living in Key West should express their views on the current struggle. There were no indications of further demonstrations being planned at this time here, but a spokesman said that similar protests would be carried out in other cities of the United States; he did not name the specific cities nor did he indicate what form the protests might take.

records.headline: An ANP dispatch from Port-au-Prince reports that Haitian President Francois Duvalier
records.summary_en: An ANP dispatch from Port-au-Prince reports that Haitian President Francois Duvalier and Dominican Republic strongman Rafael Trujillo met for an unannounced one-hour conference in the border town of Malpasse. Dominican President Hector B. Trujillo and other officials from both neighboring countries attended the gathering, marking the first meeting between leaders of the two nations in six years. Haitian refugees in New York City speculated that Trujillo sought closer relations with Haiti because a rebel victory in Cuba might align that country against his regime.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de la ANP desde Puerto Príncipe informa que el presidente haitiano Francois Duvalier y el hombre fuerte de la República Dominicana, Rafael Trujillo, se reunieron en una conferencia imprevista de una hora en la localidad fronteriza de Malpasse. El presidente dominicano Héctor B. Trujillo y otros funcionarios de ambos países vecinos asistieron al encuentro, el cual constituyó la primera reunión entre los mandatarios de las dos naciones en seis años. Exiliados haitianos en la ciudad de Nueva York especularon que Trujillo buscaba estrechar lazos con Haití ante la posibilidad de que una victoria rebelde en Cuba alineara a ese país en contra de su gobierno.

records.headline: Cuban President Fulgencio Batista surrendered executive authority
records.summary_en: Cuban President Fulgencio Batista surrendered executive authority to a military junta and departed Havana for Ciudad Trujillo, capital of the Dominican Republic, aboard a presidential DC-3 around 3:30 a.m. accompanied by his family and aides. Batista stated he relinquished power to avoid further bloodshed following four days of heavy fighting at Santa Clara, though observers indicated he feared an army rebellion. The military junta appointed senior Supreme Court member Carlos Piedra as provisional president before dissolving itself, while other planes carried military officers and civilians into exile in Jacksonville and New Orleans as Havana braced for searches by Fidel Castro's partisans.
records.summary_es: El presidente cubano Fulgencio Batista entregó el poder a una junta militar y partió de La Habana hacia Ciudad Trujillo, capital de la República Dominicana, a bordo de un avión presidencial DC-3 cerca de las 3:30 a.m. acompañado de su familia y colaboradores. Batista afirmó que renunciaba al cargo para evitar un mayor derramamiento de sangre tras cuatro días de intensos combates en Santa Clara, aunque observadores señalaron que temía una sublevación del ejército. La junta militar designó al magistrado decano del Tribunal Supremo, Carlos Piedra, como presidente provisional antes de disolverse, mientras otros aviones trasladaban a oficiales militares y civiles al exilio en Jacksonville y Nueva Orleans en momentos en que La Habana temía incursiones de los partidarios de Fidel Castro.

records.headline: An AP dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that exiled Cuban ruler
records.summary_en: An AP dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that exiled Cuban ruler Fulgencio Batista attributed his military defeat to an insufficient manpower advantage over Fidel Castro's insurgents. Speaking to newsmen following his arrival in exile, Batista cited historical military calculations requiring 100 soldiers for each guerrilla fighter, comparing his situation to campaigns in Yugoslavia and China. Although his 37,000-strong forces held an estimated six-to-one numerical edge, Batista argued that the rebels benefited from guerrilla tactics, continuous arms deliveries, and rural intimidation. Batista also asserted that prior to the uprising he had held Castro's life in his hands three times and pardoned him each time.

Al hablar con periodistas tras su llegada al exilio, Batista citó cálculos doctrinales que exigen 100 soldados por cada guerrillero, comparando su caso con las campañas en Yugoslavia y China. Aunque sus fuerzas de 37,000 hombres mantenían una ventaja numérica estimada en seis a uno, Batista sostuvo que los rebeldes se beneficiaron de tácticas de guerrilla, continuos envíos de armamento e intimidación rural. Batista aseveró además que antes de la sublevación tuvo la vida de Castro en sus manos tres veces y lo perdonó en cada ocasión.

records.headline: Constantine Kangles, United States legal representative for Fidel
records.summary_en: Constantine Kangles, United States legal representative for Fidel Castro, stated that Fulgencio Batista is Cuba's foremost war criminal and that war criminal trials will be among the new government's first actions. Kangles remarked that Batista appears safe from prosecution as long as he remains in the Dominican Republic under the protection of Dictator Rafael Trujillo. However, he warned that if Batista ever attempts to join his family in the United States, Cuban authorities will make every effort to have him extradited to Cuba to stand trial.
records.summary_es: Constantine Kangles, representante legal de Fidel Castro en los Estados Unidos, declaró que Fulgencio Batista es el principal criminal de guerra de Cuba y que los juicios contra criminales de guerra figurarán entre los primeros actos del nuevo gobierno. Kangles señaló que Batista parece estar a salvo de ser enjuiciado mientras permanezca en la República Dominicana bajo la protección del dictador Rafael Trujillo. No obstante, advirtió que si Batista intenta en algún momento reunirse con su familia en los Estados Unidos, las autoridades cubanas harán todo lo posible para conseguir su extradición a Cuba a fin de someterlo a juicio.

records.headline: Following the collapse of his regime, Cuban Dictator Fulgencio
records.summary_en: Following the collapse of his regime, Cuban Dictator Fulgencio Batista, his family, and top military leaders fled Havana, with Batista traveling to Ciudad Trujillo, capital of the Dominican Republic. The article notes that in the ancient city formerly known as Santo Domingo, Batista can compare notes with exiled Argentine leader Juan Peron and the nation's ruler, Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo Molina, known as 'El Benefactor.' The report recounts that Batista's ouster concluded a two-year revolt led by Fidel Castro Ruz, which culminated when insurgents moved outside Oriente Province to attack Santa Clara and divide the island.

El artículo señala que en la antigua ciudad antes llamada Santo Domingo, Batista puede intercambiar impresiones con el líder argentino exiliado Juan Perón y con el gobernante del país, el generalísimo Rafael Trujillo Molina, conocido como 'El Benefactor'. El despacho reseña que la caída de Batista puso fin a una rebelión de dos años encabezada por Fidel Castro Ruz, la cual culminó cuando los insurgentes avanzaron fuera de la provincia de Oriente para atacar Santa Clara y dividir la isla.

records.headline: Cuban courts reportedly will be established to try former ruler
records.summary_en: Cuban courts reportedly will be established to try former ruler Fulgencio Batista, currently exiled in the Dominican Republic, along with other officials of his deposed government. Cuban leader Urrutia declared that he will formally demand Batista's extradition from the Dominican Republic, though the petition is expected to be rejected by Dominican dictator Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo. In Havana, several hundred Batista loyalists have taken refuge in foreign embassies while the new regime has not clarified whether it will grant safe conduct, and Fidel Castro's arrival in the capital was postponed until Thursday.
records.summary_es: Se informó que se establecerán tribunales cubanos para juzgar al exgobernante Fulgencio Batista, actualmente exiliado en la República Dominicana, así como a otros funcionarios de su régimen derrocado. El dirigente cubano Urrutia declaró que exigirá formalmente la extradición de Batista a la República Dominicana, aunque se prevé que la petición sea rechazada por el dictador dominicano, generalísimo Rafael Trujillo. En La Habana, varios cientos de partidarios de Batista se han refugiado en embajadas extranjeras mientras el nuevo régimen no ha aclarado si otorgará salvoconductos, y la llegada de Fidel Castro a la capital fue aplazada hasta el jueves.

records.headline: An editorial commentary in the Labor Citizen celebrates the overthrow of Fulgencio
records.summary_en: An editorial commentary in the Labor Citizen celebrates the overthrow of Fulgencio Batista, describing him as a cowering refugee hiding ignominiously under the protection of Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic, termed the hemisphere's only remaining dictator. By contrast, the article notes Fidel Castro's triumphant entry into Havana and the installation of his chosen president in the presidential palace as Cuban expatriates in Miami begin their return. The commentary observes that Batista carries a price on his head as Cuba's number-one war criminal and questions whether he would even be safe at his Daytona Beach residence.
records.summary_es: Un comentario editorial en el Labor Citizen celebra el derrocamiento de Fulgencio Batista, describiéndolo como un refugiado acobardado que se oculta ignominiosamente bajo el amparo de Rafael Trujillo en la República Dominicana, calificado como el único dictador que queda en el hemisferio. En contraste, el artículo destaca la entrada triunfal de Fidel Castro en La Habana y la instalación de su presidente escogido en el palacio presidencial mientras los expatriados cubanos en Miami emprenden el regreso. El editorial señala que Batista tiene precio por su cabeza como el criminal de guerra número uno de su país y cuestiona si estaría a salvo incluso en su residencia de Daytona Beach.

records.headline: A dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that the heads of state of Haiti
records.summary_en: A dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that the heads of state of Haiti and the Dominican Republic signed a joint declaration pledging to fight international communism and resist any internal or external interference in their respective nations. Meeting in the border town of Malpasse, Dominican President Hector B. Trujillo Molina, his brother Generalissimo Doctor Rafael Leonidas Trujillo Molina, and Haitian President Doctor Francois Duvalier concluded the agreement alongside cabinet members and organizational leaders. The signatories resolved to promote cultural interchange, technical assistance, and close economic cooperation, while agreeing to harmonize their diplomatic positions within the United Nations and the Organization of American States.
records.summary_es: Un despacho desde Ciudad Trujillo informa que los jefes de Estado de Haití y la República Dominicana firmaron una declaración conjunta en la que se comprometieron a combatir el comunismo internacional y rechazar cualquier injerencia interna o externa en sus respectivos países. Reunidos en la localidad fronteriza de Malpasse, el presidente dominicano Héctor B. Trujillo Molina, su hermano el generalísimo doctor Rafael Leonidas Trujillo Molina y el presidente haitiano doctor Francois Duvalier concertaron el acuerdo junto a miembros del gabinete y dirigentes sociales. Los firmantes acordaron fomentar el intercambio cultural, la asistencia técnica y una estrecha cooperación económica, comprometiéndose además a armonizar sus posturas diplomáticas ante las Naciones Unidas y la Organización de los Estados Americanos.

records.summary_en: Representative Powell stated that information from Haiti indicates Dominican dictator Rafael Trujillo masterminded the agreement to send a United States Marine training mission to Haiti. Powell asserted that Trujillo, facing the threat of invasion and defeat, sought American military training for Haiti's army to secure the border as a defensive buffer, alleging the two nations had not spoken since Trujillo massacred 35,000 Haitian laborers at the border. In contrast, Assistant Secretary of State Roy Rubottom told a Senate Foreign Relations subcommittee that the Marine mission would remain only as long as requested by the Haitian government to assist in training its defense forces.

records.summary_en: Reprinting an editorial snippet from the Pittsburgh Press under the heading 'In Passing,' the publication describes the Dominican Republic as the hemisphere's hospitable zoo for ex-dictators where room is always available for one more. The commentary notes that a place had long been reserved for Cuba's deposed leader Fulgencio Batista, welcoming his arrival in Ciudad Trujillo to occupy it. However, the piece cautions that the Cuban struggle is not finished, warning that bloody days may lie ahead because rebel leader Fidel Castro is not universally accepted by everyone who opposed Batista.

records.headline: Fidel Castro announced, in an account of post-revolutionary proceedings
records.summary_en: Fidel Castro announced, in an account of post-revolutionary proceedings, that Cuba is seeking to extradite General Fulgencio Batista, whom he called 'the Hitler of Cuba,' from his refuge in Dictator Rafael Trujillo's Dominican Republic. Castro declared that Batista and his officials must face trial in Cuba for crimes ranging from torture to murder. The dispatch also reports that the provisional Cuban government will review all business investment agreements entered into by Batista's regime, while visiting United States congressmen opted to monitor the trials through press reports rather than attending in person.

records.headline: An AP dispatch reports that the State Department has permitted
records.summary_en: An AP dispatch reports that the State Department has permitted a Canadian firm to transport 12 jet fighter planes across the United States destined for the Dominican Republic. Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo is reportedly acquiring the aircraft to strengthen the Dominican Air Force in the aftermath of the revolution in Cuba. The 12 planes are described as the first shipment of 31 British-built Vampires being purchased by Trujillo, which reach speeds of about 800 miles an hour though considered obsolete relative to modern supersonic aircraft. The Dominican Air Force is currently estimated to maintain 30 or 40 jet fighters, including planes previously acquired from Sweden.

records.summary_en: Despite circulating rumors that exiled former Argentine president Juan Peron was traveling to Brazil or fleeing aboard a yacht to Spain, informants in Ciudad Trujillo confirmed he was seen in the Dominican capital yesterday. records.full_text:
$1 Million Gift By Batista to Trujillo Reported

PORTLAND, Oreg., Feb. 14 (AP).—Representative Porter, Democrat of Oregon, says Fulgencio Batista, the ousted Cuban dictator, gave $1 million to Rafael Trujillo, the Dominican strongman, after taking refuge in the Dominican Republic.

Mr. Porter told the Oregon United Nations Association yesterday that he learned about the gift in Venezuela, where he spent several days this week as a guest of President Romulo Betancourt.

He said the money has been distributed to six advertising agencies in this country to win friends for Gen. Trujillo in the United States.

"When I get back to Washington I am going to disclose where this money is and what it is to be used for, if the disclosure is not made before then," Mr. Porter said.

He went on to say about Gen. Trujillo:

"I definitely feel he faces revolution, not only from inside the palace, where it is apparent he has lost face, but also from the outside."

records.headline: Major Fidel Castro has branded the governments of Paraguay
records.summary_en: Major Fidel Castro has branded the governments of Paraguay, Nicaragua, and the Dominican Republic as dictatorships in numerous speeches since assuming power in Cuba on January 1. Castro has directed particular criticism against the nearby Dominican Republic, which has remained under the control of Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo for the past quarter century, whether serving as president or in private life. The article recalls that the Cuban rebel leader previously took part in an abortive expedition to invade the Dominican Republic and overthrow Trujillo, an enterprise suppressed by the Batista regime before the ships could sail far from Cuban shores. The report also reviews the dictatorial regimes of the Somoza family in Nicaragua and General Alfredo Stroessner in Paraguay.
records.summary_es: El comandante Fidel Castro ha calificado a los gobiernos de Paraguay, Nicaragua y la República Dominicana de dictaduras en múltiples discursos pronunciados desde que asumió el poder en Cuba el 1 de enero. Castro ha dirigido duras críticas contra la vecina República Dominicana, la cual ha permanecido bajo el control del generalísimo Rafael L. Trujillo durante el último cuarto de siglo, ya sea desde la presidencia o en la vida privada. El artículo recuerda que el líder rebelde cubano participó con anterioridad en una fallida expedición para invadir la República Dominicana y derrocar a Trujillo, intento frustrado por el régimen de Batista antes de que las naves pudieran alejarse de las costas cubanas. El despacho reseña además las dictaduras de la familia Somoza en Nicaragua y del general Alfredo Stroessner en Paraguay.

records.headline: A Venezuelan civic campaign combating foreign dictatorships
records.summary_en: A Venezuelan civic campaign combating foreign dictatorships established an anti-Trujillo fund with the goal of raising 1 million bolivars through the street sale of bonds priced at 1 bolivar (30 cents) each. Although organizers have not stated how the funds will be disbursed, the proceeds are expected to purchase arms for Dominican revolutionaries seeking to overthrow Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, who has ruled the Dominican Republic for more than 25 years. The dispatch notes that Venezuelan and Cuban campaigns are also targeting ruling regimes in Nicaragua and Paraguay, as Venezuelan congressional foreign affairs committee chairman Gonzalo Barrios commented on the initiatives.

records.headline: Reports indicate that Trujillo compelled General Fulgencio Batista
records.summary_en: Reports indicate that Trujillo compelled General Fulgencio Batista, the deposed Cuban dictator, to hand over one million dollars for an expanded public relations campaign in the United States. Trujillo reportedly asserted that this expenditure was necessary because of Batista's presence in the Dominican Republic, and Batista complied with the demand. Cubans allege that the Trujillo lobby and public relations representatives in the United States received the funds from Batista and are now representing Batista as well as Trujillo.

Según los rumores, Trujillo afirmó que este gasto era necesario debido a la presencia de Batista en la República Dominicana, y Batista cumplió con la exigencia. Fuentes cubanas afirman que el cabildeo y los representantes de relaciones públicas de Trujillo en Estados Unidos recibieron los fondos y ahora trabajan tanto para Batista como para Trujillo.

records.headline: Amid fears of an invasion launched by Haitian opponents from Cuba
records.summary_en: Amid fears of an invasion launched by Haitian opponents from Cuba, President François Duvalier clamped down in Haiti, restricting exit visas and threatening total revolution if enemies sought his overthrow. Duvalier now holds the active backing of Dominican dictator Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, another ruler marked for removal by Fidel Castro. The report observes that Haiti and the Dominican Republic divide the island of Hispaniola, and recalls that Duvalier and Trujillo met on their frontier in December to issue a joint declaration against communism.
records.summary_es: Ante el temor a una invasión encabezada por opositores haitianos desde Cuba, el presidente François Duvalier endureció las medidas en Haití, suspendiendo las visas de salida y amenazando con una revolución total si sus enemigos intentaban derrocarlo. Duvalier cuenta ahora con el respaldo activo del dictador dominicano, el generalísimo Rafael Trujillo, otro gobernante marcado por Fidel Castro para ser derrocado. El despacho señala que Haití y la República Dominicana se dividen la isla de La Española y recuerda que Duvalier y Trujillo se reunieron en su frontera en diciembre para emitir una declaración conjunta contra el comunismo.

records.summary_en: Defeated Haitian presidential candidate Louis Dejoie is guarded in Cuba by riflemen from Premier Fidel Castro's revolutionary army. records.headline: Dominican Army veterans, including several general officers
records.summary_en: Dominican Army veterans, including several general officers, announced in Ciudad Trujillo that an armed force is being organized to defend neighboring Haiti against foreign invasion. Describing their self-styled foreign legion, leaders stated that Haiti faces invasion threats from international political gangsters in Cuba and Venezuela, and vowed to combat conspiracies originating in those nations. The leaders reported their force of 25,000 men, with a recruitment goal of 28,000, will undergo training in the mountains along the Haitian border on the island shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic.

Los jefes declararon que su contingente de 25.000 hombres, con una meta de reclutamiento de 28.000, se entrenará en las montañas a lo largo de la frontera haitiana en la isla compartida por Haití y la República Dominicana.

records.full_text:
FBI Agent Says Lawyer Claimed Trujillo Tie

An FBI agent and a Jacksonville (Fla.) shipbuilder testified yesterday in District Court as the Government—for the second time—tried to prove John J. Frank, Washington attorney, was an agent of the Dominican Republic.

Mr. Frank is accused of failing to register as an agent of the Dominican Republic and of that country's dictator, Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo. His conviction on the same charge in December, 1957, was reversed last October by the United States Court of Appeals.

The FBI agent, Fred Woodcock, said that Mr. Frank told him in late 1956 that he had acted as "security adviser" for Trujillo on a European trip in 1954 and when the dictator visited Kansas City, Mo., in late 1955.

Mr. Woodcock also testified that Mr. Frank told him he had served as attorney for a Dominican ship repair firm. The firm was not further identified.

George W. Gibbs, jr., president of a Jacksonville shipbuilding company, testified that from 1954 through 1956 he headed a Dominican ship repair firm apparently controlled by Trujillo.

Mr. Frank had been sentenced to a jail term of eight months to two years after his first conviction.

In reversing the decision, the appellate court said the Government should not have attempted to link Mr. Frank with the disappearance in 1956 of a Trujillo foe, Columbia University professor Dr. Jesus de Galindez, and Gerald Murphy, an American pilot who allegedly claimed to know the professor's fate.

ANTI-TRUJILLO SIGNS DESTROYED IN HAITI
Port-Au-Prince, Haiti (ANP)—Placards attacking Generalissimo
Rafel J. Trujillo Molina of neighboring Dominican Republic, found
scattered throughout the city were destroyed by police last week The
signs read "Haiti for Haitians! Down with Trujillo!" and appeared
after Dominican naval vessels were reported patrolling the Haitian
coast.
QUESTION AFRICANS’ READINESS FOR FREEDOM
Chicago (ANP)—Bishop Charles W. Brashares, prelate of the
Methodist Illinois area, said last week upon his return from a two
month African tour that there is some doubt whether Africans “will be
ready for the freedom they will soon receive. He said “If they are not
prepared soon to live as free men, their nations will become dictator
ships instead of democracies when the last colonial ties are severed.',’
LIBERIA APPROVES NEW UNIVERSITY
Monrovia (ANP) —Enabling legislation creating a new university
of West Africa was passed by the Liberian legislation last week.
Coupled with the law was the granting of 50.000 acres of land upon
which $1 million is to be spent in the next three years. The project
is sponsored by an American group headed by Juan T. Trippe, presi
dent. Pan American airways.

records.headline: Fidel Castro stated, addressing an estimated 200,000 Cubans
records.summary_en: Fidel Castro stated, addressing an estimated 200,000 Cubans, that the Dominican Republic possesses more than enough patriots to emulate Cuba's revolt against Fulgencio Batista without requiring direct Cuban military intervention. Castro asserted that Rafael Trujillo and Haitian President François Duvalier were appealing to the United States to intervene in the Caribbean, adding that no outside power would intervene in Cuba. Earlier, General Trujillo warned from Ciudad Trujillo that 'brins and beards will fly like outterflies' if an invasion is attempted from Cuba or Venezuela, noting that the distance from Cuba to the Dominican Republic equals the distance back to Cuba.
records.summary_es: Fidel Castro declaró, al dirigirse a unas 200.000 personas en Cuba, que la República Dominicana cuenta con más que suficientes patriotas para emular la revuelta cubana contra Fulgencio Batista sin necesidad de una intervención militar directa de Cuba. Castro sostuvo que Rafael Trujillo y el presidente haitiano François Duvalier estaban solicitando la intervención de Estados Unidos en el Caribe, añadiendo que nadie intervendría en Cuba. Previamente, el general Trujillo advirtió desde Ciudad Trujillo que volarían cerebros y barbas como mariposas (citado textualmente en inglés como 'brins and beards will fly like outterflies') si se intentaba una invasión desde Cuba o Venezuela, señalando que la distancia de Cuba a la República Dominicana es igual a la distancia de regreso a Cuba.

records.headline: That a third junket departed for the Dominican Republic, the stronghold of Rafael L. Trujillo
records.summary_en: That a third junket departed for the Dominican Republic, the stronghold of Rafael L. Trujillo, whom he calls the 'Little Caesar of the Caribbean,' Louis Lautier reports in the syndicated column 'Capitol Spotlight.' The party of eight, consisting of a congressman along with his friends and secretaries, had all travel expenses and hotel bills paid by the Trujillo government. The column remarks that the Dominican massacre of Haitians under the Trujillo regime appears to have been forgotten.

records.headline: During sentencing, the presiding judge recalled that attorney
records.summary_en: During sentencing, the presiding judge recalled that attorney John Frank's activities on behalf of the Dominican Republic and Generalissimo Trujillo were well known to the United States State Department and other agencies, noting that Frank made no attempt to conceal his work but had reached a mistaken conclusion regarding his obligation to register. Frank had previously been convicted in December 1957 and sentenced to a prison term of eight months to two years, but the Court of Appeals reversed the conviction because prosecutors improperly linked him to the March 1956 disappearance of Columbia University professor Dr. Jesús de Galíndez. Following that appellate ruling, a retrial was held before Judge Youngdahl and a jury, after which Frank and his counsel thanked the jurist upon the pronouncement of sentence.
records.summary_es: Durante la audiencia de sentencia, el juez presidente recordó que las actividades del abogado John Frank en nombre de la República Dominicana y del generalísimo Trujillo eran bien conocidas por el Departamento de Estado de Estados Unidos y otras agencias, señalando que Frank no intentó ocultar su labor, sino que llegó a una conclusión errónea respecto a su obligación de registrarse. Frank había sido condenado previamente en diciembre de 1957 a una pena de prisión de ocho meses a dos años, pero el Tribunal de Apelaciones revocó la sentencia debido a que la fiscalía lo vinculó indebidamente con la desaparición en marzo de 1956 del profesor de la Universidad de Columbia Dr. Jesús de Galíndez. Tras ese fallo de apelación, se celebró un nuevo juicio ante el juez Youngdahl y un jurado, luego del cual Frank y su defensor agradecieron al magistrado al dictarse la sentencia.

records.headline: Facing invasion threats and rising hemispheric opposition to Latin American
records.summary_en: Facing invasion threats and rising hemispheric opposition to Latin American dictatorships, Haitian President François Duvalier joined forces with Dominican dictator Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo. The Haitian and Dominican governments, sharing the island of Hispaniola, set aside their traditional enmity to coordinate mutual defense preparations. Under the agreement, retired Dominican officers, operating with Trujillo's approval, announced plans to organize a 25,000-man volunteer force prepared to take action if Haiti were invaded.
records.summary_es: Ante las amenazas de invasión y el creciente rechazo hemisférico a las dictaduras latinoamericanas, el presidente haitiano François Duvalier unió fuerzas con el dictador dominicano, el generalísimo Rafael Trujillo. Los gobiernos de Haití y la República Dominicana, que comparten la isla de La Española, dejaron de lado su tradicional enemistad para coordinar preparativos de defensa mutua. Conforme al acuerdo, oficiales dominicanos retirados, con la aprobación de Trujillo, anunciaron planes para organizar un contingente voluntario de 25.000 hombres preparado para actuar en caso de que Haití fuera invadido.

The delegates scheduled stops in Havana, Kingston, and Port-au-Prince, planning to inspect other mission fields before attending the Dominican conference. The report notes that Reverend Short had previously completed a similar survey trip in January 1951 with Ezra Steiner of Woodburn, Indiana, to evaluate the growing project.

records.headline: Captain F. M. Lindgren described notable geographical features
records.summary_en: Captain F. M. Lindgren described notable geographical features in the Dominican Republic surveyed by American engineers of the United States Army Engineer Corps. Among these is Largo Enriquilo, a saltwater lake near the Haitian border situated 240 feet below sea level, functioning as a dead sea harboring primitive fish species. Due north of Ciudad Trujillo, the engineers also explored the region of Haitises, an uninhabited 800-square-mile expanse of coral ridges and cactus jungle that could only be mapped by aerial photography.

Entre ellos destaca Largo Enriquilo, un lago de agua salada cercano a la frontera haitiana situado a 240 pies bajo el nivel del mar, semejante a un mar muerto que alberga especies primitivas de peces. Directamente al norte de Ciudad Trujillo, los ingenieros también exploraron la región de Los Haitises, una extensión deshabitada de 800 millas cuadradas de crestas de coral y selva de cactus que solo pudo cartografiarse mediante fotografía aérea.

records.headline: During a press conference, Cuban Prime Minister Fidel Castro
records.summary_en: During a press conference, Cuban Prime Minister Fidel Castro was questioned regarding reports that exiles sheltering in Cuba were plotting revolutionary movements against the Trujillo regime in the Dominican Republic. Asked whether Cuba intended to provide aid in violation of non-intervention principles, Castro affirmed that his country's guiding policy toward other nations remains non-intervention, though exiles receive hospitality. Castro proposed that joint demands by democratic American states for free elections in dictator-led nations would offer an appropriate solution.
records.summary_es: Durante una conferencia de prensa, el primer ministro cubano Fidel Castro fue interrogado sobre informes de que exiliados refugiados en Cuba preparaban movimientos revolucionarios contra el régimen de Trujillo en la República Dominicana. Al preguntársele si Cuba pensaba brindar ayuda violando el principio de no intervención, Castro afirmó que la política rectora de su país hacia otras naciones sigue siendo la no intervención, aunque los exiliados reciban hospitalidad. Castro propuso que la exigencia conjunta de elecciones libres por parte de los Estados democráticos americanos en los países bajo dictadura ofrecería una solución adecuada.

records.summary_en: United States authorities in San Juan detained a 29-year-old Dominican Air Force officer who escaped to Puerto Rico in one of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo's Vampire jet fighters seeking political asylum. The aviator, Captain Juan de Dios Ventura, explained that he had planned his flight for three months and departed when he discovered he was under surveillance. Ventura declined to discuss his motives further, citing concern for the safety of family members remaining in the Dominican Republic.

El aviador, capitán Juan de Dios Ventura, explicó que había planeado su fuga durante tres meses y despegó al enterarse de que estaba bajo vigilancia. Ventura se negó a dar más detalles sobre sus motivos, señalando el peligro que podrían correr los familiares que quedaron en la República Dominicana.

records.headline: Dominican exiles in Cuba, Venezuela, and New York expressed
records.summary_en: Dominican exiles in Cuba, Venezuela, and New York expressed hopes of unseating Trujillo, the official 'Benefactor of the Fatherland,' though observers note overthrowing the regime presents formidable obstacles. In response to invasion threats from exiles supposedly assisted by Cuban and Venezuelan volunteers, Trujillo strengthened his armed forces, hinted at counterstrikes, and organized an 'anti-Communist foreign legion' composed largely of Dominicans. Trujillo is reported to command an efficient army of approximately 18,000 men and a capable air force by Caribbean standards, while the Communist Party has remained outlawed in the republic since 1936.
records.summary_es: Exiliados dominicanos en Cuba, Venezuela y Nueva York expresaron esperanzas de derrocar a Trujillo, el 'Benefactor de la Patria', aunque los observadores señalan que derribar el régimen supone enormes dificultades. En respuesta a las amenazas de invasión de los exiliados, supuestamente respaldados por voluntarios cubanos y venezolanos, Trujillo reforzó sus fuerzas armadas, insinuó contraataques y organizó una 'legión extranjera anticomunista' integrada en gran parte por dominicanos. Según los informes, Trujillo cuenta con un ejército eficiente de unos 18.000 hombres y una fuerza aérea notable para los estándares caribeños, mientras que el Partido Comunista permanece proscrito en la república desde 1936.

records.headline: Under President Horacio Vasquez, Trujillo rose from chief of guards
records.summary_en: Under President Horacio Vasquez, Trujillo rose from chief of guards at a sugar mill to commander of the national police, remaining on the sidelines during a revolt before being chosen president on August 16, 1930, at age 39. Only 18 days after taking office, a devastating hurricane struck the capital, killing more than 1,000 persons and injuring 4,000, after which Trujillo declared martial law, solicited United States aid, and initiated a swift reconstruction program that consolidated his political authority. In 1936, the Dominican Congress renamed the capital city of Santo Domingo as Ciudad Trujillo in his honor, where portraits of Trujillo and his brother the president were displayed across the city of 300,000 alongside an obelisk inscribed with his maxims erected in 1937.
records.summary_es: Bajo la presidencia de Horacio Vásquez, Trujillo ascendió de jefe de guardias en un ingenio azucarero a comandante de la policía nacional, manteniéndose al margen durante una revuelta antes de ser elegido presidente el 16 de agosto de 1930, a los 39 años. Apenas 18 días después de asumir el cargo, un devastador huracán azotó la capital, causando la muerte de más de 1,000 personas y heridas a 4,000, tras lo cual Trujillo declaró la ley marcial, solicitó auxilio a los Estados Unidos y puso en marcha un rápido programa de reconstrucción que consolidó su autoridad política. En 1936, el Congreso dominicano rebautizó la capital de Santo Domingo con el nombre de Ciudad Trujillo en su honor, donde retratos de Trujillo y de su hermano el presidente se exhibían por toda la ciudad de 300,000 habitantes junto a un obelisco grabado con sus frases erigido en 1937.

records.headline: A spokesman described the departure of Dominican diplomat Mr
records.summary_en: A spokesman described the departure of Dominican diplomat Mr. Rubirosa as a temporary absence that would likely last quite a long time, noting that Rubirosa and his wife, former French actress Odile Rodin, took their belongings with them. Relations between Cuba and the Dominican Republic had become strained after former Cuban President Fulgencio Batista took refuge in Ciudad Trujillo on January 1. The report added that an unidentified assailant had tossed a bomb at Mr. Rubirosa's embassy residence a few weeks earlier.

Las relaciones entre Cuba y la República Dominicana se habían vuelto tensas después de que el ex presidente cubano Fulgencio Batista se refugiara en Ciudad Trujillo el 1 de enero. El informe añadió que un agresor no identificado había lanzado una bomba contra la residencia de la embajada del señor Rubirosa unas semanas antes.
