records.headline: United States federal authorities in Miami seized a four-engine
records.summary_en: United States federal authorities in Miami seized a four-engine C-74 aircraft loaded with 200,000 cartridges, rifles, and automatic weapons reportedly destined for the Dominican Republic to arm opponents of Cuban Premier Fidel Castro. Thirteen individuals were arrested and placed under bond, including Dominican Consul Augusto Ferrando, who surrendered after a six-hour standoff at the consulate, and assistant consul José Paulino, who was bonded as a material witness. Consul Ferrando, Miami police officer Joseph Liquori, and Newark dealer Leonard Trento were additionally charged with conspiring to bribe a federal officer, while the two pilots stated they had been hired by plane owner Dominic Bartone to fly to Puerto Rico without knowledge of the contraband.
records.summary_es: Las autoridades federales de los Estados Unidos en Miami incautaron un avión C-74 de cuatro motores cargado con 200,000 cartuchos, fusiles y armas automáticas presuntamente destinados a la República Dominicana para armar a adversarios del primer ministro cubano Fidel Castro. Trece personas fueron detenidas y puestas bajo fianza, entre ellas el cónsul dominicano Augusto Ferrando, quien se entregó tras permanecer seis horas refugiado en el consulado, y el vicecónsul José Paulino, retenido como testigo material. El cónsul Ferrando, el policía de Miami Joseph Liquori y el comerciante de Newark Leonard Trento fueron acusados además de conspirar para sobornar a un funcionario federal, mientras que los dos pilotos declararon haber sido contratados por el dueño del avión Dominic Bartone para volar a Puerto Rico sin saber del contrabando.

records.headline: Customs officers in Miami seized a large C-74 Globemaster aircraft
records.summary_en: Customs officers in Miami seized a large C-74 Globemaster aircraft loaded with arms and ammunition and arrested 11 persons preparing to transport the contraband to the Dominican Republic. The arms were reportedly scheduled to be flown to Ciudad Trujillo and delivered to former dictator Batista to support opponents of Castro. Two Dominican consular officials were among those charged with complicity in attempting to bribe American customs officials.

Según se informó, las armas debían volar a Ciudad Trujillo para ser entregadas al ex dictador Batista y respaldar a los adversarios de Castro. Dos funcionarios consulares dominicanos figuraron entre los acusados de complicidad en un intento de sobornar a funcionarios de aduanas estadounidenses.

records.headline: Two Cuban diplomats stationed in Ciudad Trujillo were ordered
records.summary_en: Two Cuban diplomats stationed in Ciudad Trujillo were ordered recalled to Havana following armed clashes in the Dominican capital. Dominican authorities reported that envoys Mario Rivas Patterson and Juan Jose Dias fired at Cuban exiles during a fight at a bank, fatally wounding a seven-year-old child. records.headline: A former missionary, Mr. Cunningham, was announced as a speaker
records.summary_en: A former missionary, Mr. Cunningham, was announced as a speaker at the annual Bible and Missionary Conference of the Christian and Missionary Alliance of Eastern Montana. Cunningham spent 5 years as a missionary in the Dominican Republic and directed the activities of the West Indies Mission on the island of Santo Domingo for 2 years, conducting several Spanish-language evangelistic campaigns. Prior to entering the gospel ministry 19 years earlier, Cunningham was an athlete playing on semi-professional hockey teams near Edmonton in Canada, and had two missionary brothers serving in China and Brazil.

records.headline: That Venezuela was organizing support among Organization of American States members
records.summary_en: That Venezuela was organizing support among Organization of American States members to present charges accusing the Dominican Republic of conspiring against newly established democratic regimes in Latin America, reports indicated. Sources noted that Cuba, Honduras, Bolivia, Ecuador, and Argentina were prepared to back a move to blacklist Trujillo in the OAS. Diplomatic relations had deteriorated following the January 1958 overthrow of Venezuelan strongman Marcos Pérez Jiménez and reached a crisis after the Trujillo regime refused safe-conduct passes to 13 Dominicans sheltered in the Venezuelan embassy in Ciudad Trujillo. In a related action, Venezuelan authorities in Maracaibo detained the crew of a Norwegian freighter that had called at Ciudad Trujillo carrying alleged subversive propaganda.

records.headline: The government of Rafael Trujillo announced that it had wiped
records.summary_en: The government of Rafael Trujillo announced that it had wiped out a Cuban-supported invasion force near the northern coast of the Dominican Republic and killed its commander. According to the official statement, the 68-year-old Generalissimo, who had ruled the country for 29 years, personally directed coordinated land, air, and sea operations against the invaders the previous week in the Constanza area northwest of Ciudad Trujillo. The announcement marked the regime's first official confirmation of the invasion.

Según el comunicado oficial, el generalísimo de 68 años, quien gobernaba el país desde hacía 29 años, dirigió personalmente operaciones coordinadas por tierra, aire y mar contra los invasores la semana anterior en la zona de Constanza, al noroeste de Ciudad Trujillo. La declaración constituyó la primera confirmación oficial de la invasión por parte del régimen.

records.headline: An armed expedition aboard two launches flying the United States flag
records.summary_en: An armed expedition aboard two launches flying the United States flag was intercepted off the Dominican coast by navy vessels and air force planes that sank both craft, with survivors reaching shore reportedly killed by local farmers with machetes. The report followed previous unconfirmed dispatches from New York, Miami, Havana, and Caracas that revolutionary uprisings had begun against the government of General Rafael Leonidas Trujillo. Although Cuban Premier Fidel Castro had vowed to topple Trujillo and Cuban frigates allegedly escorted the expedition to within 70 miles of the coast, informants aboard the Cuban vessels reportedly kept Dominican authorities informed. Expedition commander Capt. Enrique Jiménez Moya was killed while attempting to evade Dominican army patrols in the hills surrounding Constanza. His body and the bodies of at least six other members of the expedition were recovered, the sources said, and Trujillo would speak before the national congress giving full details of the abortive revolt.

El informe siguió a despachos previos no confirmados desde Nueva York, Miami, La Habana y Caracas de que habían comenzado levantamientos revolucionarios contra el gobierno del general Rafael Leonidas Trujillo. Aunque el primer ministro cubano Fidel Castro había jurado derrocar a Trujillo y fragatas cubanas supuestamente escoltaron la expedición hasta unas 70 millas de la costa, informantes a bordo de los buques cubanos habrían mantenido informadas a las autoridades dominicanas. El comandante de la expedición, el capitán Enrique Jiménez Moya, murió al intentar evadir patrullas del ejército dominicano en las lomas que rodean Constanza. Su cuerpo y los cuerpos de al menos otros seis miembros de la expedición fueron recuperados, según las fuentes, y Trujillo hablaría ante el congreso nacional para dar todos los detalles de la revuelta abortada.

records.headline: The United States State Department addressed two controversies
records.summary_en: The United States State Department addressed two controversies in the Dominican Republic, including an incident in which a transport aircraft flying from Puerto Rico to Cuba was fired on with machine-gun bullets before being released, prompting instructions to the American ambassador to demand an explanation. In a second affair described as placing the ambassador in a compromised position, United States Ambassador Joseph F. Farland and other diplomats were summoned to the Dominican foreign ministry and introduced to Lieutenant Colonel Juan de Dios Ventura Simó, with whom they shook hands for widely published photographs. The encounter drew sharp protests from anti-dictator groups across the Caribbean, who objected to the ambassador's perceived endorsement of Ventura Simó, an officer who had staged a feigned defection from Trujillo's military to infiltrate the invading rebel expedition.

records.summary_en: *The Key West Citizen* reported that a Dominican fighter plane intercepted and fired upon a U.S. Air Force transport en route from Puerto Rico to Cuba, forcing it to land briefly in Ciudad Trujillo. The State Department also expressed concern that American Ambassador Joseph F. Farland had been compromised after being photographed at the Dominican foreign ministry with military pilot Juan de Dios Ventura Simó. The pilot, Williams, said the Dominican fighter fired a short burst from his 50 caliber machine gun; he fired straight ahead and the shot did not come close to their plane, but he came dangerously close to let them know he meant business. Williams said a second Dominican plane joined the first briefly, then both flew away when they were about 70 miles from Ciudad Trujillo. The C-47 landed there because it was short on fuel. Williams said Dominican air force officers at Ciudad Trujillo were unable to explain the incident.

records.headline: An interpretive news report analyzed recent armed expeditions
records.summary_en: An interpretive news report analyzed recent armed expeditions across Latin America, noting that Cuban fighters had allied with exiled nationals, as occurred in the previous week's invasion of the Dominican Republic led by Dominican Captain Enrique Jiménez Moya. The report noted that while Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo's land, air, and naval forces reportedly wiped out the invading force and killed the captain, spokesmen for Dominican exiles denied the casualty report. Additionally, while the regime of President François Duvalier in Haiti did not appear to be a primary target of overthrow, its shared border placed it directly in the path of any potential overland invasion of the neighboring Dominican Republic.
records.summary_es: Un análisis periodístico interpretativo examinó las recientes expediciones armadas en América Latina, señalando que combatientes cubanos se habían aliado con nacionales exiliados, como ocurrió en la invasión a la República Dominicana la semana anterior liderada por el capitán dominicano Enrique Jiménez Moya. El informe indicó que, si bien las fuerzas terrestres, aéreas y navales del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo presuntamente aniquilaron a las fuerzas invasoras y dieron muerte al capitán, portavoces de los exiliados dominicanos desmintieron la noticia de su fallecimiento. Asimismo, aunque el régimen del presidente François Duvalier en Haití no parecía ser un objetivo primordial de derrocamiento, su frontera común lo situaba directamente en la ruta de cualquier eventual invasión terrestre hacia su vecina República Dominicana.

records.headline: HORNER Btr Staff Writer The crisis confronting the Frondizi government in Buenos Aires
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that former Cuban president Fulgencio Batista expressed a desire to leave his exile in the Dominican Republic to rejoin his family. Batista told an interviewer in Ciudad Trujillo that he had retired completely from politics, though attempts to secure entry into the United States and other countries had been rejected.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el expresidente cubano Fulgencio Batista expresó su deseo de abandonar su exilio en la República Dominicana para reunirse con su familia. Batista declaró a un entrevistador en Ciudad Trujillo que se había retirado por completo de la política, aunque sus gestiones para ingresar a Estados Unidos y a otros países habían sido rechazadas.
records.passage: Seen in Frondizi Crisis By JOHN V. HORNER Star Staff Writer The crisis confronting the Frondizi government in Buenos Aires Is seen here as a test in which the Argentine people must decide whether they want a democracy or a return of tyranny. records.summary_en: From his exile in Ciudad Trujillo, Mr. Batista endorsed charges made by Mr. Trujillo that Cuban warships participated in a recent invasion of the Dominican Republic, citing them as evidence of troubling policies pursued by Mr. Castro. Batista insisted that Castro was directing attacks against the Dominican Republic, Panama, and Nicaragua as part of a communist-influenced conspiracy, and denied with indignation that he was secretly allied with the Cuban leader. While seeking an entry visa to relocate to another country, Batista resided under heavy guard in a third-floor apartment in a Ciudad Trujillo waterfront hotel, where secretaries and aides assisted him in petitioning foreign embassies while only a handful of his original followers remained.

records.summary_en: Cuban representative Mr. Lechuga announced that a formal diplomatic note severing relations with the Dominican Republic would cite persistent violations of human rights against prisoners and rebels as the primary reason for the rupture. records.full_text:
Action by OAS On Dominican Quarrel Slated

By JOHN V. HORNER

Star Staff Writer

The Council of the Organization of American States will decide Monday afternoon what to do about a request from the Dominican Republic on its quarrel with Cuba and Venezuela.

At an emergency session late yesterday the council postponed its decision on a Dominican request to act in the dispute until members could receive instructions from their government.

Hot Debate Flares

The delay followed an angry debate in which the delegate of the Dominican Republic accused Cuba and Venezuela of participating in invasions of his country. The Dominican Ambassador based his plea on two invasion attempts in June and on a charge that 3,000 men are being trained in Cuba to attack his country.

At the emergency session yesterday Foreign Minister Raul Roa of Cuba angrily declared that the Dominican Republic is a "bloody" dictatorship which accuses two American governments of illegal activities.

The other American government is Venezuela. The Dominican Ambassador told the OAS that a plane used to invade his country was furnished by Venezuela authorities.

"Lying" Charged

Mr. Roa, who has served as the OAS ambassador of Cuban Prime Minister Fidel Castro, labeled the Dominican complaint as a "lying note." Mr. Roa declared the purpose of the Dominican note was to create an unfavorable international situation for Cuba when his country is trying to make a comeback after overthrowing the regime of dictator Fulgencio Batista.

Ambassador Falcon Briceno of Venezuela joined Mr. Roa in his criticism of the Dominican Republic's plea and categorically opposed invocation of the Rio Treaty.

United States Ambassador John Dreier told the OAS Council that this government regards the Carribbean situation as urgent but, he added, a majority of delegates do not yet have instructions.

He said a prompt decision is desirable but he advocated a postponement until the OAS delegates could consult their governments.

records.headline: State Department officials in Washington closely monitored Caribbean
records.summary_en: State Department officials in Washington closely monitored Caribbean tensions, ready to invoke Organization of American States security agreements if hostilities erupted. Premier Castro warned that Cuba would tolerate no outside interference and denied in a five-hour television speech that Cuba intended to attack the Dominican Republic, having severed diplomatic relations a week earlier following Dominican charges that Cuba backed an abortive invasion on June 10. In London, the Cuban ambassador to Britain charged that Dictator Trujillo was planning an assault on Cuba alongside former dictators Juan Perón, Marcos Pérez Jiménez, and General Batista, citing Dominican purchases of arms, planes, and military equipment in Europe.

En Londres, el embajador cubano en Gran Bretaña acusó al dictador Trujillo de planear un asalto contra Cuba junto a los exdictadores Juan Perón, Marcos Pérez Jiménez y el general Batista, citando compras de armas, aviones y equipo militar por agentes dominicanos en Europa.

records.headline: Dominican warplanes and navy ships were reportedly guarding
records.summary_en: Dominican warplanes and navy ships were reportedly guarding the coasts of Haiti as part of an unpublicized joint defense effort against invasion attempts from abroad. The dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo noted that explosive tensions in the Caribbean were rapidly mounting as bitter charges and countercharges were traded between the Dominican Republic on one side and Cuba alongside anti-regime Dominican exiles on the other. Diplomatic circles indicated that prompt action by the Organization of American States might be unavoidable to prevent a major crisis. Official informants in Ciudad Trujillo said Dominican aircraft flying patrols to protect this country from incursions by rebels from Cuba or elsewhere in the Caribbean had recently widened their operations to include the Haitian coastline, and that Dominican warships had on several occasions used Haitian port facilities for bunkering as their guard against invaders was extended to Haitian waters. In the event an invasion should be launched against Haiti, the regime of Generalissimo Rafael Leonidas Trujillo was prepared to move ground forces into the neighboring country to help in defending Haiti; several months ago the Haitian government of President Francois Duvalier had asked the Dominican Republic for military aid in case of difficulties, and both regimes have been targets of threats by their exiled opponents. There have been reports for months that Haitian exiles were training in Cuba with Dominican anti-regime elements, Haiti was thought to be the next invasion objective, and officials stressed that the mountainous 217-mile Haitian-Dominican border is more difficult to guard than the Caribbean coast. It was believed here that in helping Haiti the Dominican Government would use its Anti-Communist Foreign Legion, now being trained throughout the country. The Legion was created in January largely to counter anti-Trujillo groups in Cuba and elsewhere; it is made up of volunteers of various nationalities and is directed by a group of Dominican generals not technically on active duty in their own Army, and it was understood that Gen. Arturo Espaillat, who once served as consul general in New York, is one of its chiefs. Official informants acknowledged that the Legion was recently augmented by 300 Spanish volunteers, who arrived last month, most of them said to be veterans of the “Blue Division,” which fought in the Soviet Union in World War II with the Germans. General Trujillo is reported to be under strong pressure by some of his top aides to assume an offensive posture instead of awaiting another rebel attack from Cuba. The United States, which is reported to be preparing to invoke the provisions of inter-American agreements for hemisphere action to avoid an outbreak of open warfare in the Caribbean, has been using most of its influence to persuade the Dominican Republic not to resort to arms; it is making a similar effort in Cuba.
records.summary_es: Se informó que aviones de guerra y buques navales dominicanos vigilaban las costas de Haití como parte de un esfuerzo de defensa conjunto no publicitado contra intentos de invasión desde el exterior. El despacho desde Ciudad Trujillo señaló que las explosivas tensiones en el Caribe aumentaban con rapidez mientras se intercambiaban amargas acusaciones entre la República Dominicana, por un lado, y Cuba junto a exiliados dominicanos opuestos al régimen, por el otro. Círculos diplomáticos indicaron que una pronta acción de la Organización de los Estados Americanos podría ser inevitable para evitar una crisis mayor. Informantes oficiales en Ciudad Trujillo dijeron que aviones dominicanos que volaban patrullas para proteger al país de incursiones de rebeldes desde Cuba o cualquier otro punto del Caribe habían ampliado recientemente sus operaciones para incluir la costa haitiana, y que buques de guerra dominicanos habían usado en varias ocasiones las instalaciones portuarias haitianas para abastecerse de combustible al extenderse su guardia contra invasores a aguas haitianas. En caso de que se lanzara una invasión contra Haití, el régimen del generalísimo Rafael Leonidas Trujillo estaba preparado para mover fuerzas terrestres al país vecino para ayudar en la defensa de Haití; varios meses atrás, el gobierno haitiano del presidente François Duvalier había pedido ayuda militar a la República Dominicana en caso de dificultades, y ambos regímenes han sido objeto de amenazas de sus opositores exiliados. Había informes desde hacía meses de que exiliados haitianos se entrenaban en Cuba con elementos dominicanos opuestos al régimen, se pensaba que Haití sería el próximo objetivo de invasión, y los funcionarios subrayaron que la montañosa frontera haitiano-dominicana, de 217 millas, es más difícil de vigilar que la costa caribeña. Se creía en Ciudad Trujillo que, para ayudar a Haití, el Gobierno dominicano utilizaría su Legión Extranjera Anticomunista, que se entrenaba en todo el país. La Legión fue creada en enero principalmente para contrarrestar a los grupos antitrujillistas en Cuba y otros lugares; está formada por voluntarios de diversas nacionalidades y dirigida por un grupo de generales dominicanos que técnicamente no están en servicio activo en su propio ejército, y se entendía que el general Arturo Espaillat, quien una vez se desempeñó como cónsul general en Nueva York, es uno de sus jefes. Informantes oficiales reconocieron que la Legión fue reforzada recientemente con 300 voluntarios españoles, llegados el mes anterior, la mayoría de ellos, según se decía, veteranos de la «División Azul», que luchó en la Unión Soviética durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial junto a los alemanes. Se informó que el general Trujillo estaba bajo fuerte presión de algunos de sus principales colaboradores para asumir una postura ofensiva en lugar de esperar otro ataque rebelde desde Cuba. Estados Unidos, que según se informaba se preparaba para invocar las disposiciones de los acuerdos interamericanos para una acción hemisférica a fin de evitar el estallido de una guerra abierta en el Caribe, había estado usando la mayor parte de su influencia para persuadir a la República Dominicana de no recurrir a las armas; hacía un esfuerzo similar en Cuba.

records.headline: An editorial observes that the dispute between the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: An editorial observes that the dispute between the Dominican Republic and Cuba, with Haiti serving as an unwilling buffer, has taken a nasty turn following invasions launched by Dominican exiles from Cuba. The commentary calls Generalissimo Trujillo's stated fear of an attack by Cuba or Venezuela puzzling, noting that he possesses the strongest army, navy, and air force in the region and that any direct state assault would be suicidal. It emphasizes that Haiti does not want Trujillo's protection, pointing out that President Duvalier's government refused to permit Dominican border patrols, closed no borders to Dominican exiles, and desires only stability and non-interference from its neighbors.

El comentario califica de desconcertante el temor manifestado por el generalísimo Trujillo a un ataque de Cuba o Venezuela, señalando que este posee el ejército, la armada y la fuerza aérea más poderosos de la región y que cualquier agresión estatal directa sería suicida. Destaca asimismo que Haití no desea la protección de Trujillo, subrayando que el gobierno del presidente Duvalier se negó a permitir patrullas fronterizas dominicanas, no cerró la frontera a los exiliados dominicanos y solo aspira a la estabilidad y a no ser perturbado por sus vecinos.

records.full_text:
For Trujillo: Troubles

Year 29 of the Era of Trujillo is undoubtedly the most disturbing ever experienced by the dictator of the Dominican Republic.

The year 1959, like practically everything else in that tiny Caribbean nation, bears the stamp of the sturdy, 67-year-old chief of state, Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, who came to power in 1930.

But ever since the Castro brothers overthrew the Batista government in neighboring Cuba earlier this year, Gen. Trujillo has faced a mounting pile of troubles. The most serious challenge posed to his rule was a small-scale invasion of the country which was attempted several weeks ago.

Gen. Trujillo's well-trained military forces reportedly wiped out most of the tiny rebel band on the landing beach. But a handful of rebels apparently made it through to the hills, and may still be hiding out.

Gen. Trujillo knows well that Premier Castro led a similar band to power in Cuba following his near-disastrous "invasion" that was scarcely any more distinguished in the beginning.

Though news of the revolutionary attempt is sparse and clouded with propaganda, it now appears that at least a few of the invaders—who reportedly journeyed by boat from Cuba—were sons of prominent Dominicans. If that is true, Gen. Trujillo is confronted with the germ of a domestic problem that may be far more serious than invasion threats from abroad.

But it was just those alleged threats that were under consideration Friday by the Organization of American States. Charging before the OAS Council that certain elements in Cuba and Venezuela were plotting the downfall of their government, Dominican representatives asked for action by the organization.

On Friday, however, Virgilio Diaz Ordonez of the Dominican Republic withdrew the charge. The Council of the OAS then postponed until tomorrow consideration of a request to convene foreign ministers of the 21 member nations to consider the Caribbean turmoil.

Though some of the diplomats believe the charges are well founded, there is an underlying belief in the OAS that most member nations would not take part in any defense of the Dominican Republic.

records.headline: The Prime Minister of Cuba remarked that it was "curious" that subcommittee
records.summary_en: The Prime Minister of Cuba remarked that it was "curious" that subcommittee chairman Senator Eastland had delivered a speech before the Dominican Republic's Legislature eulogizing Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, whom Castro denounced as a "despot" and "assassin." Castro asserted that the congressional hearings confirmed foreign agent involvement in Major Díaz's defection, labeling the former officer "the Benedict Arnold of Cuba" and arguing the United States should be haled before the Organization of American States. Simultaneously, Cuban intelligence investigated reports that four gunmen were traveling from the United States to assassinate Castro, his brother Raúl, and several cabinet ministers.
records.summary_es: El primer ministro de Cuba calificó de «curioso» que el presidente de la subcomisión, el senador Eastland, hubiera pronunciado un discurso ante el Congreso de la República Dominicana encomiando al generalísimo Rafael Trujillo, a quien Castro denunció como «déspota» y «asesino». Castro afirmó que las audiencias del Congreso confirmaban la implicación de agentes extranjeros en la deserción del mayor Díaz, calificándolo de «el Benedict Arnold de Cuba» y sosteniendo que Estados Unidos debía ser llevado ante la Organización de los Estados Americanos. Paralelamente, la inteligencia cubana investigaba informes sobre cuatro pistoleros que viajaban desde Estados Unidos para asesinar a Castro, a su hermano Raúl y a varios ministros de su gabinete.

records.headline: In Ciudad Trujillo, a man claiming to be Cuban Army officer
records.summary_en: In Ciudad Trujillo, a man claiming to be Cuban Army officer Delio Gómez Ochoa stated over Dominican radio that the invasion he led against the Dominican Republic the previous month was supported by Premier Castro and Venezuelan President Rómulo Betancourt. The captured officer reported that he had surrendered after leading the invasion of General Trujillo's country in the Constanza area. The broadcast followed rising Caribbean tensions and mutual accusations between Havana and Ciudad Trujillo regarding regional invasion conspiracies.
records.summary_es: En Ciudad Trujillo, un hombre que afirmó ser el oficial del ejército cubano Delio Gómez Ochoa declaró a través de la radio dominicana que la invasión que encabezó contra la República Dominicana el mes anterior contó con el respaldo del primer ministro Castro y del presidente venezolano Rómulo Betancourt. El oficial capturado afirmó haberse rendido tras encabezar la invasión del país del general Trujillo en la zona de Constanza. La transmisión se produjo en medio de crecientes tensiones en el Caribe y acusaciones mutuas entre La Habana y Ciudad Trujillo sobre conspiraciones de invasión en la región.

records.summary_en: The Cuban newspaper Revolución accused the United States of preparing an attack on Cuba and arming "war criminals" in Miami, New York, Washington, and Ciudad Trujillo, the capital of the Dominican Republic. The paper asserted that these elements were preparing assassination attempts against revolutionary leaders and organizing bombing campaigns against Cuba. In response to congressional testimony regarding Communist influence, the publication maintained that Cuba was democratic rather than Communist and noted that Communists had failed to secure important posts in recent union elections.

En respuesta a testimonios ante el Congreso sobre influencia comunista, la publicación sostuvo que Cuba era democrática y no comunista, destacando que los comunistas no habían obtenido cargos de relevancia en las recientes elecciones sindicales.

records.headline: The dispatch reports on the anti-Castro organization known as the "White
records.summary_en: The dispatch reports on the anti-Castro organization known as the "White Rose," which maintained ties with factions in the Dominican Republic where General Batista lived in exile. Meanwhile, the Dominican Republic accused the Castro regime of aiding enemies of General Trujillo preparing an invasion to overthrow him, a charge repeatedly denied by Castro. Haiti, sharing the island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic, went on full alert following a warning from the Dominican Embassy that an invasion might be imminent, while Trujillo strengthened his forces along the Haitian border out of concern that Cuban-based revolutionaries could use Haiti as a springboard for an attack against him.

Mientras tanto, la República Dominicana acusó al régimen de Castro de ayudar a los enemigos del general Trujillo a preparar una invasión para derrocarlo, acusación reiteradamente desmentida por Castro. Haití, que comparte la isla de La Española con la República Dominicana, se declaró en alerta total tras una advertencia de la embajada dominicana de que una invasión podría ser inminente, al tiempo que Trujillo reforzó sus tropas en la frontera haitiana por temor a que revolucionarios radicados en Cuba usaran a la república vecina como plataforma para atacarlo.

records.headline: Rebel leader Major Delio Gómez Ochoa died of a heart attack
records.summary_en: Rebel leader Major Delio Gómez Ochoa died of a heart attack while confined at Victoria Penitentiary awaiting trial for an invasion attempt to overthrow Dominican Dictator Rafael Trujillo. Prison director Lieutenant Colonel Horacio Frías announced the death of the captive officer in Ciudad Trujillo. The rebel commander had been held following the recent unsuccessful invasion attempt against the Trujillo government.
records.summary_es: El líder rebelde, mayor Delio Gómez Ochoa, falleció de un ataque cardíaco mientras permanecía recluido en la Penitenciaría de La Victoria a la espera de juicio por un intento de invasión para derrocar al dictador dominicano Rafael Trujillo. El director de la prisión, teniente coronel Horacio Frías, anunció la muerte del oficial capturado en Ciudad Trujillo. El comandante rebelde permanecía detenido tras el reciente intento fallido de invasión contra el gobierno de Trujillo.

records.headline: Dominican exiles abroad conducted extensive radio propaganda
records.summary_en: Dominican exiles abroad conducted extensive radio propaganda campaigns aimed at listeners inside and outside the country, broadcasting urgent appeals, sound effects, and reports that new invasion boats were sighted along the Dominican north coast. Stations in Havana, Caracas, and Puerto Rico rebroadcast these transmissions, which were financed by the sale of "bonds" by the Dominican government-in-exile and benefit events in Venezuela and elsewhere. The report notes that while the impact of these theatrical broadcasts on Generalissimo Trujillo was uncertain, he was likely shaken more severely by the recent defection of two trusted diplomats: his ambassador to Ecuador and a representative before the United Nations.
records.summary_es: Los exiliados dominicanos en el extranjero llevaron a cabo intensas campañas de propaganda radial dirigidas a oyentes dentro y fuera del país, transmitiendo llamamientos urgentes, efectos de sonido y reportes de que se avistaron nuevas embarcaciones de invasión en la costa norte dominicana. Emisoras en La Habana, Caracas y Puerto Rico retransmitían estas emisiones, financiadas mediante la venta de «bonos» por el gobierno dominicano en el exilio y actos benéficos en Venezuela y otros lugares. El despacho señala que, aunque el impacto de estas transmisiones teatrales sobre el generalísimo Trujillo era incierto, probablemente le afectó mucho más la reciente deserción de dos diplomáticos de su confianza: su embajador en Ecuador y un representante ante las Naciones Unidas.

records.headline: The Cuban cabinet decided to dispatch a seven-man delegation
records.summary_en: The Cuban cabinet decided to dispatch a seven-man delegation headed by Foreign Minister Raúl Roa to the Organization of American States meeting in Santiago, Chile. The conference arose from charges by the Dominican Republic that Premier Castro was assisting Dominican exiles in Cuba plotting to overthrow Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo. Although Mr. Castro had denied the accusations and initially considered boycotting the conference, the cabinet indicated he might travel to Santiago later rather than leading the delegation immediately from Havana.
records.summary_es: El gabinete cubano decidió enviar una delegación de siete miembros encabezada por el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores, Raúl Roa, a la reunión de la Organización de los Estados Americanos en Santiago de Chile. La conferencia surgió a partir de las acusaciones de la República Dominicana de que el primer ministro Castro ayudaba a exiliados dominicanos en Cuba que conspiraban para derrocar al generalísimo Rafael Trujillo. Aunque el señor Castro había negado las acusaciones e inicialmente consideró boicotear la conferencia, el gabinete indicó que podría viajar a Santiago más adelante en lugar de encabezar la delegación de inmediato desde La Habana.

records.headline: An editorial warns that anticipated attacks at the Santiago gathering
records.summary_en: An editorial warns that anticipated attacks at the Santiago gathering against dictatorships such as that of Generalissimo Trujillo in the Dominican Republic risk provoking sharp counterattacks and turning the conference into an oratorical Donnybrook. The piece notes that bitter Caribbean rivalries have escalated beyond a virulent war of words into armed force, pointing out that since June the Dominican Republic has faced two invasions launched from Cuba with Venezuelan assistance. Furthermore, Generalissimo Trujillo is reported to be conducting active intrigue against Premier Fidel Castro in Havana and the Betancourt regime in Caracas alongside his propaganda offensive.
records.summary_es: Un editorial advierte que los previsibles ataques en la reunión de Santiago contra dictaduras como la del generalísimo Trujillo en la República Dominicana amenazan con provocar enérgicas réplicas y transformar la conferencia en una trifulca oratoria. El artículo señala que las amargas rivalidades en el Caribe han pasado de una virulenta guerra de palabras al uso de la fuerza armada, destacando que desde junio la República Dominicana ha tenido que afrontar dos invasiones lanzadas desde Cuba con ayuda venezolana. Además, se informa que el generalísimo Trujillo, al margen de su ofensiva propagandística, participa en constantes intrigas contra el primer ministro Fidel Castro en La Habana y el régimen de Betancourt en Caracas.

records.headline: An Associated Press report states that the newspaper Revolucion
records.summary_en: An Associated Press report states that the newspaper Revolucion, organ of Fidel Castro's 26th of July Movement, attributed an anti-Castro conspiracy to three elements: members of the former Batista army, large landowners affected by land redistribution, and mercenaries hired by Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo, dictator of the Dominican Republic. Remnants of an armed band that clashed with the Cuban army took to the hills in southern Las Villas province, where numerous conspirators were reportedly arrested and a telephone blackout was ordered. records.headline: A dispatch from Santiago reports that any United States declaration
records.summary_en: A dispatch from Santiago reports that any United States declaration at the foreign ministers conference will likely be phrased in general terms without naming dictators, as both Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic and Luis Somoza of Nicaragua remain in office. Direct attacks on them would provoke accusations of interference in domestic affairs and damage Washington's relations with the Dominican and Nicaraguan governments. The conference was convened following a series of invasions by political exiles attempting to overthrow the Trujillo and Somoza regimes and the government of Panama. Frictions were reduced when Cuba's ambassador announced that Prime Minister Fidel Castro would not attend because his government claimed it had just crushed a major counter-revolutionary plot.

Los ataques directos contra ellos provocarían acusaciones de injerencia en asuntos internos y dañarían las relaciones de Washington con los gobiernos dominicano y nicaragüense. La conferencia se convocó tras una serie de invasiones llevadas a cabo por exiliados políticos que intentaban derrocar a los regímenes de Trujillo y Somoza y al gobierno de Panamá. Las tensiones disminuyeron cuando el embajador de Cuba anunció que el primer ministro Fidel Castro no asistiría porque su gobierno afirmó haber sofocado un importante complot contrarrevolucionario.

Kuchilan urged students and other Cubans to send cables to the Inter-American Foreign Ministers Conference in Santiago, Chile, demanding the expulsion of the Dominican Republic from the Organization of American States. records.headline: An editorial notes that Fidel Castro's rise to power brought
records.summary_en: An editorial notes that Fidel Castro's rise to power brought calls for eliminating American dictatorships, making Generalissimo Trujillo's regime in the Dominican Republic a primary target with backing from Venezuela's Betancourt government. Dictator Trujillo responded by engaging in deep intrigues and unrestrained propaganda against Cuba and Venezuela, leaving the entire Caribbean in an explosive state that threatens regional peace. To address the crisis, United States Secretary of State Christian Herter proposed creating a special hemispheric committee to investigate armed intervention and propaganda warfare and report to the Inter-American Conference scheduled for February.
records.summary_es: Un editorial señala que el ascenso al poder de Fidel Castro trajo consigo llamados a erradicar las dictaduras de América, convirtiendo al régimen del generalísimo Trujillo en la República Dominicana en un blanco prioritario con el respaldo del gobierno de Betancourt en Venezuela. El dictador Trujillo respondió involucrándose en profundas intrigas y propaganda desenfrenada contra Cuba y Venezuela, sumiendo a todo el Caribe en una situación explosiva que amenaza la paz regional. Para abordar la crisis, el secretario de Estado de los Estados Unidos, Christian Herter, propuso la creación de un comité hemisférico especial que investigue las intervenciones armadas y la guerra de propaganda e informe a la Conferencia Interamericana prevista para febrero.

records.headline: The Cuban army made its first official announcement confirming
records.summary_en: The Cuban army made its first official announcement confirming the capture of an invasion aircraft at Trinidad airport following an ambush by government forces. The army reported that the plane was piloted by Lt. Col. Antonio Soto, who had flown Gen. Batista into exile in the Dominican Republic on New Year's Day, and that Soto and former Batista captain Betancourt were wounded alongside six members of the ambush squad. The military announcement directly accused Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo, the Dominican dictator, of participating in the landing attempt, and stated that Premier Fidel Castro would address the nation by radio and television regarding the conspiracy.
records.summary_es: El ejército cubano emitió su primer comunicado oficial confirmando la captura de un avión de invasión en el aeropuerto de Trinidad tras una emboscada de las fuerzas gubernamentales. El ejército informó que el aparato estaba pilotado por el teniente coronel Antonio Soto, quien había trasladado al general Batista al exilio en la República Dominicana el día de Año Nuevo, y que Soto y el excapitán batistiano Betancourt resultaron heridos junto a seis integrantes del pelotón de emboscada. El comunicado castrense acusó directamente al generalísimo Rafael L. Trujillo, dictador dominicano, de haber participado en el intento de desembarco, y señaló que el primer ministro Fidel Castro hablaría a la nación por radio y televisión acerca de la conspiración.

records.headline: An Associated Press report from Santiago indicates that foreign ministers
records.summary_en: An Associated Press report from Santiago indicates that foreign ministers must reconcile sharp differences after Cuban Premier Fidel Castro, engaged in a bitter feud with Dominican Republic strongman Rafael Trujillo, denounced the conference from Havana as a farce. Castro criticized United States Secretary of State Christian Herter's proposal to establish a temporary investigative committee on the Caribbean situation. The Castro-Trujillo dispute and rebel invasion attempts targeting Nicaragua, the Dominican Republic, and Panama prompted the gathering, where Cuban and Dominican delegates clashed during three days of stormy oratory as ministers considered a Santiago declaration on democracy and human rights alongside economic development proposals.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Associated Press desde Santiago indica que los cancilleres deben superar marcadas discrepancias luego de que el primer ministro cubano Fidel Castro, enfrentado enconadamente con el hombre fuerte de la República Dominicana, Rafael Trujillo, calificara desde La Habana a la conferencia como una farsa. Castro censuró la propuesta del secretario de Estado de los Estados Unidos, Christian Herter, relativa a crear un comité temporal de investigación sobre la coyuntura del Caribe. La pugna entre Castro y Trujillo y las tentativas de invasión rebelde contra Nicaragua, la República Dominicana y Panamá motivaron la reunión, en la que delegados cubanos y dominicanos chocaron en tres jornadas de oratoria tormentosa mientras los ministros evaluaban una declaración de Santiago sobre democracia y derechos humanos junto con propuestas de desarrollo económico.

records.summary_en: Cuban Premier Fidel Castro denounced Gen. Trujillo as the mastermind behind Caribbean tensions while noting that Cubans had participated in recent abortive invasions of Panama and the Dominican Republic. Castro recounted how William Morgan of Toledo, Ohio, an American major in the Cuban army, acted as his undercover agent and lured Trujillo into believing he was a mercenary adventurer who would do anything for money. According to Castro, Morgan's covert operation unmasked the anti-Castro conspiracy and secured a boatload of arms sent from the Dominican Republic.

Según Castro, la operación encubierta de Morgan desarticuló la conspiración contra el gobierno y consiguió un cargamento de armas enviado en barco desde la República Dominicana.

records.headline: Cuban Premier Fidel Castro declared that the ministers were focused
records.summary_en: Cuban Premier Fidel Castro declared that the ministers were focused on destroying his government rather than the Trujillo dictatorship, denouncing the foreign ministers meeting as a farce, criticizing Christian Herter for discussing invasions instead of hunger. Castro asserted that four shiploads of arms had been sent to anti-Castro factions, one from the United States and three from the Dominican Republic. He described how his aides, led by American soldier-of-fortune William A. Morgan, tricked Rafael Trujillo into sending an arms-laden transport plane to an airfield that served as an ambush. Meanwhile, United States officials preferred to avoid confronting Castro directly, fearing that ill-advised moves might drive him toward communism amid Cuba's mounting economic problems and 500,000 unemployed workers.

records.headline: A feature on 30-year-old Cuban Army Major William Morgan recounts
records.summary_en: A feature on 30-year-old Cuban Army Major William Morgan recounts how Cuban Premier Fidel Castro revealed his undercover role during a television broadcast attacking Rafael L. Trujillo, boss of the Dominican Republic. Castro explained that Morgan deceived Generalissimo Trujillo into believing he had bought his loyalty, leading Trujillo to name Morgan head of the anti-Castro conspiracy in place of Eleuterio Pedraza, a former general under Fulgencio Batista who had been training anti-Castro forces in the Dominican Republic. A Cuban military spokesman stated that Morgan tricked an arms-laden aircraft from the Dominican Republic into landing at Trinidad Airport, where it was seized following a gunfight. The biographical sketch also notes that Morgan joined Castro in 1957 after a friend was killed smuggling arms and later commanded guerrilla fighters known as the Tigers of the Espesura.
records.summary_es: Una semblanza sobre el mayor del ejército cubano William Morgan, de 30 años de edad, relata cómo el primer ministro cubano Fidel Castro reveló su función encubierta durante una transmisión televisiva en la que arremetió contra Rafael L. Trujillo, jefe de la República Dominicana. Castro explicó que Morgan engañó al generalísimo Trujillo haciéndole creer que había comprado su lealtad, lo que llevó a Trujillo a designar a Morgan jefe de la conspiración anticastrista en sustitución de Eleuterio Pedraza, un antiguo general de Fulgencio Batista que venía entrenando fuerzas contra Castro en la República Dominicana. Un portavoz militar cubano afirmó que Morgan indujo a un avión cargado de armas procedente de la República Dominicana a aterrizar en el aeropuerto de Trinidad, donde fue capturado tras un tiroteo. La nota biográfica señala además que Morgan se unió a Castro en 1957 tras la muerte de un amigo que contrabandeaba armas y que luego comandó a guerrilleros conocidos como los Tigres de la Espesura.

records.headline: Colonel John Abbes Garcia, Dominican army intelligence chief
records.summary_en: Colonel John Abbes Garcia, Dominican army intelligence chief, described Cuban Premier Fidel Castro's story regarding the capture of an arms-laden plane as one of the greatest swindles ever perpetrated on American public opinion. Col. Garcia asserted that numerous contradictions prove the narrative was a farce invented by Castro to sow confusion among participants in the movement against his regime. He maintained it was an irrefutable fact that the uprising had been planned for three months and was headed by Cuban Army Majors Gutierrez Menoya and William Morgan. Garcia rejected Castro's claims that Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo had sent the plane from the Dominican Republic and that both majors had acted as undercover agents to break the conspiracy.
records.summary_es: El coronel John Abbes García, jefe de inteligencia del ejército dominicano, calificó el relato del primer ministro cubano Fidel Castro sobre la captura de un avión cargado de armas como una de las mayores estafas jamás cometidas contra la opinión pública de las Américas. El coronel Abbes afirmó que múltiples contradicciones demuestran que la versión fue una farsa inventada por Castro para sembrar confusión entre los participantes del movimiento contra su régimen. Sostuvo que constituía un hecho irrefutable que la sublevación llevaba tres meses planeándose y estaba encabezada por los mayores del ejército cubano Gutiérrez Menoya y William Morgan. Abbes desestimó las afirmaciones de Castro de que el generalísimo Rafael Trujillo había enviado el avión desde la República Dominicana y de que ambos mayores habían actuado como agentes encubiertos para desbaratar la conspiración.

records.headline: Brother Raul was due in Santiago as the foreign ministers of Latin America and the United States
records.summary_en: *The Key West Citizen* reported that Raúl Castro traveled to the Santiago foreign ministers conference carrying documents allegedly linking Dominican dictator Rafael Trujillo to an anti-Castro conspiracy. Concurrently, delegates drafted compromise resolutions granting the Inter-American Peace Committee investigative powers over regional invasions while addressing demands from Cuba and Venezuela regarding human rights. The United States is chairman of the peace committee, whose other members are Venezuela, Uruguay, El Salvador and Mexico, and the committee's findings will be reported to the regular Inter-American foreign ministers' conference scheduled to be held in Quito, Ecuador, next year. Raul Castro said he was going to Santiago to convey the goodwill of the Cuban people, but during a stopover in Caracas Sunday night he described the conference as farcical and said his brother is not interested in it; he also described the OAS as “useless,” declaring, “Nobody in it realizes or will deal with the real problem in the Caribbean and in all Latin America, which is the economic problem.”

records.headline: Cuban Premier Fidel Castro, in a nationwide television broadcast
records.summary_en: Cuban Premier Fidel Castro, in a nationwide television broadcast recounting how the counter-revolutionary plot was crushed, denounced Dominican Republic strongman Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo as the financial boss of those plotting against Cuba. Castro also sharply criticized the United States, charging that Cuban war criminals sheltered there were allowed to operate freely and fly planes from Miami to drop anti-government leaflets and extract fugitives. Castro called the Inter-American Foreign Ministers Conference in Santiago, Chile, a farce, ridiculing proposals presented by United States Secretary of State Christian A. Herter for easing tensions while ignoring Latin American economic hardship and childhood hunger.
records.summary_es: El primer ministro cubano Fidel Castro, en una alocución televisada a todo el país donde relató cómo fue aplastada la conspiración contrarrevolucionaria, denunció al hombre fuerte de la República Dominicana, el generalísimo Rafael L. Trujillo, como el jefe financiero de quienes conspiraban contra Cuba. Castro criticó asimismo duramente a los Estados Unidos, acusando a sus autoridades de permitir que criminales de guerra cubanos allí refugiados actuaran a su antojo y realizaran vuelos desde Miami para lanzar volantes antigubernamentales y recoger fugitivos. Castro calificó de farsa la conferencia de cancilleres interamericanos que se celebraba en Santiago de Chile, ridiculizando las propuestas del secretario de Estado de los Estados Unidos, Christian A. Herter, para aliviar las tensiones por ignorar las penurias económicas de América Latina y el hambre de los niños.

records.headline: An Associated Press report analyzes the outcome of the Santiago
records.summary_en: An Associated Press report analyzes the outcome of the Santiago conference, observing that foreign ministers did not single out culprits or impose specific sanctions despite sharp exchanges between representatives of Prime Minister Fidel Castro of Cuba and Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo of the Dominican Republic. Having decided in advance not to arbitrate invasion attempts across the Caribbean, the ministers directed the Inter-American Peace Committee of the Organization of American States to keep watch over regional trouble spots and explore methods to prevent foreign efforts to overthrow legal governments before reporting to the Quito conference in February. The committee was empowered to conduct investigations either on request or on its own initiative, though on-the-spot inspections require the consent of the investigated nation.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Associated Press analiza los resultados de la conferencia de Santiago, señalando que los cancilleres no individualizaron culpables ni impusieron sanciones específicas a pesar de los intensos intercambios entre los representantes del primer ministro Fidel Castro de Cuba y del generalísimo Rafael L. Trujillo de la República Dominicana. Habiendo acordado de antemano no arbitrar los intentos de invasión en el Caribe, los ministros encomendaron a la Comisión Interamericana de Paz de la Organización de los Estados Americanos vigilar los focos de tensión regional y estudiar formas de impedir tentativas externas de derrocar gobiernos legales antes de informar a la conferencia de Quito en febrero. Se facultó a la comisión para realizar investigaciones a petición o por iniciativa propia, si bien las inspecciones sobre el terreno exigen el consentimiento del país investigado.

records.headline: Major William Morgan declared that Trujillo's immediate collaborators
records.summary_en: Major William Morgan declared that Trujillo's immediate collaborators were so corrupt that the anti-Castro conspiracy had no chance of success. As an example, Morgan stated that when he asked General Trujillo for funds, he received only part of the money because an unnamed Dominican consul took $5,000 and a Spanish priest acting as a go-between also kept a portion. Morgan stated that the consul arranged for the purchase of arms shipped from the United States aboard a private boat, which Morgan intercepted on the high seas and brought to Havana. This account differed from earlier unofficial reports claiming the boat had sailed from the Dominican Republic before Morgan seized control from the crew.

records.headline: Seventeen members of Fulgencio Batista's entourage departed
records.summary_en: Seventeen members of Fulgencio Batista's entourage departed the Dominican Republic by air for Lisbon en route to Madeira after sources in Ciudad Trujillo reported that Portugal had granted them political asylum. In Havana, Cuban government quarters reported that former General Eleuterio Pedraza, regarded as the mastermind of the abortive plot against Fidel Castro, remained behind amid rumors that Dominican strongman Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo imprisoned him over the conspiracy's failure. Additionally, a Dominican rebel radio broadcast monitored in Cuba claimed Batista's position in the Dominican Republic had become delicate after he refused a demand from Trujillo for $10 million to offset the expenses of the operation.

records.headline: That Cuban Premier Fidel Castro is substituting his own dictatorship
records.summary_en: That Cuban Premier Fidel Castro is substituting his own dictatorship for the one he crushed, having assumed powers equal to those of deposed General Fulgencio Batista, an analytical report assessing Caribbean trouble spots concludes. The analysis describes Castro as just as much a strongman as his arch enemies, Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo of the Dominican Republic and President Luis Somoza of Nicaragua. While acknowledging that Castro commands the backing of up to 90 per cent of his people, the report asserts that he has become a demagogue playing into the hands of international communism.
records.summary_es: Que el primer ministro cubano Fidel Castro está sustituyendo la dictadura que aplastó por la suya propia, tras asumir poderes equivalentes a los del derrocado general Fulgencio Batista, un informe analítico que evalúa los focos conflictivos del Caribe concluye. El análisis describe a Castro como un hombre fuerte en la misma medida que sus archienemigos, el generalísimo Rafael L. Trujillo de la República Dominicana y el presidente Luis Somoza de Nicaragua. Si bien reconoce que Castro cuenta con el respaldo de hasta el 90 por ciento de su pueblo, el informe sostiene que se ha convertido en un demagogo que favorece los intereses del comunismo internacional.

records.headline: An editorial commentary analyzes United States policy in the Western
records.summary_en: An editorial commentary analyzes United States policy in the Western Hemisphere, arguing that efforts to contain the spread of Castroism may inadvertently sustain undemocratic regimes such as that of Rafael Trujillo in the Dominican Republic. The piece contends that such an outcome represents an unavoidable consequence of adhering to the doctrine of non-intervention. It notes that the United States, facing high-stakes cold war negotiations with Nikita Khrushchev of the Soviet Union, cannot risk violent regional upheavals. The analysis adds that unilateral military action or economic sanctions would prompt accusations of "Yankee Imperialism," policies that the nation formally repudiated two decades earlier.
records.summary_es: Un comentario editorial analiza la política de los Estados Unidos en el hemisferio occidental, argumentando que los esfuerzos por contener la propagación del castrismo pueden sostener inadvertidamente a regímenes no democráticos como el de Rafael Trujillo en la República Dominicana. El texto sostiene que dicho desenlace representa una consecuencia inevitable de la adhesión a la doctrina de no intervención. Señala que los Estados Unidos, frente a cruciales negociaciones de la guerra fría con Nikita Khrushchev de la Unión Soviética, no pueden arriesgarse a conmociones regionales violentas. El análisis añade que una acción militar unilateral o sanciones económicas suscitarían acusaciones de "imperialismo yanqui", políticas a las que el país renunció formalmente dos décadas atrás.

records.headline: An analytical report reviews international and domestic pressures
records.summary_en: An analytical report reviews international and domestic pressures confronting the Dominican government, noting that congressional resentment in the United States was provoked by a Dominican playboy who failed out of the Army Command and General Staff School at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas. The article highlights widespread American belief that the Trujillo dictatorship was responsible for the mysterious disappearances of Columbia University Professor Jesus de Galindez and United States aviator Gerald Murphy. It further notes suspicion surrounding the recent fatal highway accident of Dominican Labor Minister Ramon Marrero Aristy, who had disagreed with the generalissimo on policy issues. Citing demands from Cuban Prime Minister Fidel Castro and Venezuelan President Romulo Betancourt for collective action against hemispheric dictatorships, the dispatch concludes that the United States may be forced to moderate its tolerant policy and that the Trujillo era appears numbered.
records.summary_es: Un informe analítico examina las presiones internacionales e internas que enfrenta el gobierno dominicano, señalando que el resentimiento del Congreso en los Estados Unidos fue provocado por un playboy dominicano que reprobó en la Escuela de Comando y Estado Mayor del Ejército en Fort Leavenworth, Kansas. El artículo destaca la creencia generalizada entre los estadounidenses de que la dictadura de Trujillo fue responsable de las misteriosas desapariciones del profesor de la Universidad de Columbia Jesús de Galíndez y del aviador estadounidense Gerald Murphy. Además, señala las sospechas en torno al reciente y fatal accidente de carretera del ministro de Trabajo dominicano, Ramón Marrero Aristy, quien había discrepado con el generalísimo sobre temas de política. Citando las demandas del primer ministro cubano Fidel Castro y del presidente venezolano Rómulo Betancourt de una acción colectiva contra las dictaduras hemisféricas, el despacho concluye que los Estados Unidos podrían verse obligados a moderar su política tolerante y que la era de Trujillo parece contada.

records.headline: A federal indictment charged Garland L. Culpepper, jr., a former director of the Mutual radio
records.summary_en: A federal indictment charged Garland L. Culpepper, jr., a former director of the Mutual radio network, and an associate with failing to register with the Justice Department as foreign agents for distributing Dominican government propaganda disguised as news. The defendants allegedly accepted $750,000 from the regime of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo Molina around February 6 under an agreement to broadcast favorable political propaganda. Named as Dominican representatives in the arrangement were Generalissimo Trujillo, Dominican Ambassador to Belgium Porfirio Rubirosa, and government official Otto Vega. The Dominican government itself was also cited among the foreign principals involved in the case.

records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from San Juan reports that the Dominican Republic summoned all army reservists under thirty-five years of age to assemble at a military training camp in Ciudad Trujillo. Notice of the mobilization was published in the Ciudad Trujillo newspaper El Caribe, which arrived in Puerto Rico the following morning. Dominican exiles in San Juan characterized the mobilization order as unusual and said they did not know its cause, while the report notes that military service in the Dominican Republic is compulsory.

El anuncio de la movilización fue publicado en el diario El Caribe de Ciudad Trujillo, el cual llegó a Puerto Rico a la mañana siguiente. Exiliados dominicanos en San Juan calificaron la orden de movilización como inusual y afirmaron desconocer su motivo, mientras que el informe señala que el servicio militar en la República Dominicana es obligatorio.

records.summary_en: An address delivered on behalf of the Dominican Republic asserted that complaints against the regime were unfounded because the Trujillo government had achieved substantial economic and social progress. The speaker devoted much of the speech to describing educational, medical, agricultural, and economic advances accomplished under Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo's administration. He maintained that the government seeks to safeguard human rights and social justice within an orderly society, while upholding the peaceful settlement of international disputes as a foundational foreign policy.

El orador dedicó gran parte de su intervención a describir los avances educativos, médicos, agrícolas y económicos alcanzados bajo la administración del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo. Asimismo, afirmó que el gobierno persigue salvaguardar los derechos humanos y la justicia social dentro de una sociedad ordenada, manteniendo la solución pacífica de las disputas internacionales como un principio fundamental de su política exterior.

records.summary_en: Suspects arrested in Caracas claimed that Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, dictator of the Dominican Republic, had agreed to support a Venezuelan conspiracy by simulating an invasion of Venezuela, though authorities reported no evidence that such an operation took place. The broader plot reportedly included the Sunday prison break from Maracaibo of former General Nestor Prato, a prominent backer of ousted president Perez Jimenez who was facing trial for abuse of power. The conspiracy was accompanied by a series of low-yield bombings across Caracas, damaging property owned by industrialist Eugenio Mendoza, the residence of newspaper publisher Miguel Angel Caprile's brother-in-law, and the studios of Culture Radio Station.

La trama general presuntamente incluía la fuga carcelaria ocurrida el domingo en Maracaibo del exgeneral Néstor Prato, destacado partidario del derrocado presidente Pérez Jiménez que enfrentaba juicio por abuso de poder. La conspiración estuvo acompañada de una serie de atentados con explosivos de baja intensidad en Caracas, que causaron daños en una propiedad del industrial Eugenio Mendoza, la residencia del cuñado del editor periodístico Miguel Ángel Caprile y los estudios de la estación Radio Cultura.

records.headline: Venezuelan police identified a former government comptroller
records.summary_en: Venezuelan police identified a former government comptroller under Marcos Perez Jimenez, Luis Eduardo Chataing, as the fugitive ringleader of a subversive plot linked to the exiled dictator in Miami, Florida. Authorities disclosed that several arrested conspirators alleged Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, dictator of the Dominican Republic, had pledged to assist the operation by staging a simulated invasion of Venezuela. Investigators also connected the scheme to the Sunday jailbreak in Maracaibo of former General Nestor Prato, who was awaiting trial for abuse of power. The conspiracy coincided with small bomb blasts across Caracas that targeted an establishment of industrialist Eugencio Mendoza, the home of publisher Miguel Angel Caprile's brother-in-law, and the studios of Cultura radio station.
records.summary_es: La policía venezolana identificó a Luis Eduardo Chataing, excontralor gubernamental durante el régimen de Marcos Pérez Jiménez, como el cabecilla prófugo de una trama subversiva vinculada al dictador exiliado en Miami, Florida. Las autoridades revelaron que varios conspiradores arrestados afirmaron que el generalísimo Rafael Trujillo, dictador de la República Dominicana, se había comprometido a apoyar la operación mediante la simulación de una invasión a Venezuela. Los investigadores vincularon asimismo la trama con la fuga carcelaria del domingo en Maracaibo del exgeneral Néstor Prato, quien se encontraba en espera de juicio por abuso de poder. La conspiración coincidió con pequeñas detonaciones de bombas en Caracas dirigidas contra un inmueble del industrial Eugencio Mendoza, la vivienda del cuñado del editor periodístico Miguel Ángel Caprile y los estudios de la emisora Radio Cultura.

records.headline: Cuban Premier Fidel Castro maintained that his efforts to purchase
records.summary_en: Cuban Premier Fidel Castro maintained that his efforts to purchase jet aircraft were intended strictly for national defense rather than offensive operations against his regional adversary, General Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic. With the United States enforcing an embargo on American weapon shipments to the Caribbean, both Cuba and the Dominican Republic turned to Western European suppliers for infantry equipment. Cuba reportedly secured twenty thousand modern Belgian rifles along with millions of rounds of ammunition, while the Dominican government bought smaller consignments of weaponry from Italy and France. United States officials expressed curiosity over how Cuba financed these weapons transactions, particularly given Castro's public speeches condemning military expenditures as wasteful.
records.summary_es: El primer ministro cubano Fidel Castro sostuvo que sus gestiones para adquirir aviones a reacción tenían fines exclusivamente defensivos y no de ataque contra su adversario regional, el general Rafael Trujillo de la República Dominicana. Ante el embargo de los Estados Unidos a los envíos de armas estadounidenses hacia el Caribe, tanto Cuba como la República Dominicana recurrieron a proveedores de Europa occidental para obtener equipamiento de infantería. Según informes, Cuba adquirió veinte mil fusiles belgas modernos y millones de proyectiles, mientras que el gobierno dominicano adquirió partidas menores de armas en Italia y Francia. Funcionarios de los Estados Unidos manifestaron extrañeza sobre cómo Cuba financió estas compras militares, sobre todo a la luz de los discursos públicos de Castro que censuraban el gasto en armamento como un despilfarro.

records.headline: Following the resignation of Cuban provincial commander Major Huber
records.summary_en: Following the resignation of Cuban provincial commander Major Huber Matos, thirty young military officers resigned and openly defied Premier Fidel Castro. Castro confronted the dissenting officers directly, angrily yelling in a tirade that they should go join Dominican Republic Dictator Rafael Trujillo. The officers were placed under arrest and shouted slogans against communism and sang the Cuban national anthem as they were escorted into custody. Matos, described as firmly anti-Communist, had previously cautioned Castro against growing communist influence within the administration and objected to the rapid pace of agrarian land seizures.
records.summary_es: Tras la renuncia del comandante provincial cubano, el mayor Huber Matos, treinta jóvenes oficiales del ejército dimitieron y desafiaron abiertamente al primer ministro Fidel Castro. Castro confrontó a los militares disidentes cara a cara, gritándoles con enojo que fueran a unirse al dictador de la República Dominicana Rafael Trujillo. Los oficiales fueron puestos bajo arresto y profirieron consignas contra el comunismo y cantaron el himno nacional cubano mientras eran trasladados bajo custodia. Matos, señalado como resueltamente anticomunista, había prevenido previamente a Castro acerca de la creciente influencia comunista dentro del gobierno y se oponía a la rapidez de las expropiaciones de tierras agrarias.

records.headline: A gala reception was hosted at the Dominican Republic Embassy
records.summary_en: A gala reception was hosted at the Dominican Republic Embassy in Washington to celebrate the birthday anniversary of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo. The event showcased two massive birthday cakes decorated in the red, white, and blue colors of the Dominican flag, complemented by matching floral displays throughout the embassy. Dominican Ambassador Dr. Luis F. Thomen, accompanied by his wife and daughter Maria Consuelo, led nearly two hundred guests in a champagne toast honoring the dictator. Guests included representatives from the United States Department of State and Congress, members of the Organization of American States, and foreign diplomats headed by Nicaraguan Ambassador Sevilla-Sacasa, the dean of the diplomatic corps.
records.summary_es: Se celebró una recepción de gala en la embajada de la República Dominicana en Washington para conmemorar el aniversario del natalicio del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo. El evento exhibió dos enormes pasteles de cumpleaños adornados con los colores rojo, blanco y azul de la bandera dominicana, complementados con arreglos florales a juego en toda la legación. El embajador dominicano, Dr. Luis F. Thomen, acompañado por su esposa y su hija María Consuelo, encabezó a casi doscientos invitados en un brindis con champán en honor al dictador. Entre los asistentes figuraron representantes del Departamento de Estado y del Congreso de los Estados Unidos, miembros de la Organización de los Estados Americanos y diplomáticos extranjeros encabezados por el embajador nicaragüense Sevilla-Sacasa, decano del cuerpo diplomático.

records.headline: Alvarez Sanchez, Virgilio, Dominican Central Bank Governor
records.summary_en: Alvarez Sanchez, Virgilio, Dominican Central Bank Governor, admitted that the nation was experiencing economic strain from depressed global sugar prices but denied claims that Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo's regime faced a monetary crisis. Alvarez Sanchez addressed an article in The New York Times asserting that substantial weapons purchases made to counter invasion threats from Cuba and Venezuela had compelled the Dominican government to pursue foreign credit. The governor acknowledged that military acquisitions had been extensive but insisted that national finances remained stable, while denouncing the Cuban and Venezuelan administrations for seeking to spread communism in the Caribbean. He added that the Dominican Republic was developing new export lines to balance revenue losses caused by falling international commodity values.
records.summary_es: Álvarez Sánchez, Virgilio, el gobernador del Banco Central dominicano, reconoció que el país experimentaba tensiones económicas debido a los bajos precios internacionales del azúcar, pero desmintió las versiones de que el régimen del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo afrontara una crisis monetaria. Álvarez Sánchez respondió a un artículo publicado en The New York Times en el que se afirmaba que las cuantiosas adquisiciones de armamento realizadas para repeler amenazas de invasión desde Cuba y Venezuela habían obligado al gobierno dominicano a gestionar créditos externos. El gobernador admitió que los gastos militares habían sido considerables pero sostuvo que las finanzas nacionales se mantenían estables, al tiempo que acusó a los gobiernos de Cuba y Venezuela de buscar expandir el comunismo en el Caribe. Agregó que la República Dominicana desarrollaba nuevos rubros de exportación para compensar la merma de ingresos derivada de la caída en las cotizaciones mundiales de productos básicos.

records.headline: Dominican Attorney General Luis E. Suero urged the United States government
records.summary_en: Dominican Attorney General Luis E. Suero urged the United States government to enact broader curbs against Caribbean revolutionary conspiracies operating within its borders. Speaking at a press briefing in Ciudad Trujillo, Suero commented that federal crackdowns on Florida airfields used by anti-Castro Cubans were appropriate but late. He insisted that such prohibitions should encompass political exiles from all Caribbean territories, highlighting that two separate invasion expeditions launched against the Dominican Republic earlier that year incorporated United States nationals recruited in New York and San Juan.
records.summary_es: El procurador general dominicano, Luis E. Suero, instó al gobierno de los Estados Unidos a imponer restricciones más amplias contra las conspiraciones revolucionarias del Caribe que operan dentro de sus fronteras. En una rueda de prensa celebrada en Ciudad Trujillo, Suero comentó que las medidas federales contra aeródromos de Florida empleados por cubanos contrarios a Castro resultaban convenientes pero tardías. Sostuvo que tales prohibiciones debían abarcar a los exiliados políticos de todos los territorios del Caribe, señalando que dos expediciones de invasión distintas lanzadas contra la República Dominicana a principios de ese año integraron a ciudadanos estadounidenses reclutados en Nueva York y San Juan.

records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that the Dominican Ministry of Health issued a public advisory cautioning citizens against eating cranberries until further notice. The warning was published through notices in local newspapers without specifying a formal cause, although the limited cranberry supplies sold in the country are imported from the United States. The measure was understood to reflect contemporaneous anxieties in the United States concerning potentially contaminated cranberry shipments.

Se interpretó que la disposición respondía a la inquietud contemporánea surgida en los Estados Unidos respecto a cargamentos de arándanos posiblemente contaminados.

records.headline: A Dominican exile organization in Havana condemned Dictator Rafael
records.summary_en: A Dominican exile organization in Havana condemned Dictator Rafael Trujillo, stating that he made himself look ridiculous by imposing harsh judicial penalties in absentia upon Cuban Prime Minister Fidel Castro and Venezuelan President Romulo Betancourt. Castro, his brother Raul, and Betancourt were among 113 defendants sentenced by a Dominican tribunal to thirty years at hard labor and levied a collective fine of $100 million on charges connected to the June airborne invasion attempt. With only five defendants physically present in the courtroom, the exile group remarked that the astronomical fine merely mirrored the sums Trujillo expended in repelling the expedition.
records.summary_es: Una organización de exiliados dominicanos en La Habana condenó al dictador Rafael Trujillo, afirmando que se puso en ridículo al imponer severas sanciones judiciales en rebeldía contra el primer ministro cubano Fidel Castro y el presidente venezolano Rómulo Betancourt. Castro, su hermano Raúl y Betancourt figuraron entre 113 acusados sentenciados por un tribunal dominicano a treinta años de trabajos forzados y gravados con una multa colectiva de 100 millones de dólares por cargos relacionados con el intento de invasión aérea de junio. Con apenas cinco de los imputados físicamente presentes en la sala judicial, el grupo de exiliados comentó que la descomunal sanción económica reflejaba únicamente las sumas que Trujillo gastó para repeler la expedición.

records.summary_en: Juan D. Peron, the exiled former president and dictator of Argentina, announced in Ciudad Trujillo that he has no intention of departing the Dominican Republic, where he has maintained residence since early 1958. Peron delivered the clarification during an interview when questioned about persistent rumors suggesting that he planned to relocate to Madrid or elsewhere in Western Europe.
records.summary_es: Juan D. Perón, el exdictador y expresidente exiliado de Argentina, anunció en Ciudad Trujillo que no tiene intenciones de abandonar la República Dominicana, donde ha fijado su residencia desde principios de 1958. Perón ofreció estas declaraciones durante una entrevista al ser interrogado acerca de los insistentes rumores que insinuaban que proyectaba trasladarse a Madrid o a algún otro punto de Europa occidental.
