records.headline: An aviation summary reports that Pan American World Airways plans
records.summary_en: An aviation summary reports that Pan American World Airways plans to introduce scheduled passenger jet operations serving the Dominican Republic and Nassau beginning December 11. The introduction of jet service to Ciudad Trujillo will shorten travel times to three hours and fifteen minutes, down from the five hours and forty-five minutes required by conventional propeller equipment. The notice also highlights expanded flight frequency and heavy advance bookings along the carrier's route between New York and San Juan, Puerto Rico.
records.summary_es: Un resumen de temas aeronáuticos informa que Pan American World Airways prevé inaugurar vuelos regulares de pasajeros en aviones a reacción hacia la República Dominicana y Nasáu a partir del 11 de diciembre. La puesta en marcha de este servicio hacia Ciudad Trujillo reducirá la duración del viaje a tres horas y quince minutos, en contraste con las cinco horas y cuarenta y cinco minutos requeridas por las aeronaves de hélice habituales. La nota destaca asimismo un incremento en la frecuencia de los vuelos y un fuerte volumen de reservas anticipadas en la ruta de la aerolínea entre Nueva York y San Juan de Puerto Rico.

records.headline: Two Miami residents, Earl Lloyd Kammann and George A. Irkl
records.summary_en: Two Miami residents, Earl Lloyd Kammann and George A. Irkl, departed Aruba with a twin-engine transport aircraft after presenting documentation establishing ownership by Coastal Air, Incorporated. Local authorities reported that the plane had been stolen in Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic, by two Cuban exile aviators. The Cuban pilots had intended to drop leaflets over an opposing target but mistook the Dutch territory off the Venezuelan coast for their objective, ultimately carrying out a forced landing on Aruba. Dutch island authorities took the aviators into custody, fined them, and expelled them by deportation.
records.summary_es: Dos residentes de Miami, Earl Lloyd Kammann y George A. Irkl, partieron de Aruba a bordo de un avión bimotor de transporte tras presentar documentación que acreditaba su propiedad por parte de Coastal Air, Incorporated. Las autoridades locales informaron que el aparato había sido sustraído en Ciudad Trujillo, República Dominicana, por dos aviadores exiliados cubanos. Los pilotos cubanos tenían la intención de lanzar octavillas sobre otro objetivo pero confundieron el territorio neerlandés frente a la costa venezolana con su destino, viéndose obligados a efectuar un aterrizaje forzoso en Aruba. Las autoridades neerlandesas de la isla detuvieron a los tripulantes, les impusieron una sanción económica y procedieron a su expulsión mediante deportación.

records.headline: At a news conference covering foreign affairs, Senator Capehart
records.summary_en: At a news conference covering foreign affairs, Senator Capehart, Republican of Indiana, was asked his opinion regarding the Trujillo dictatorship in the Dominican Republic. Capehart stated he is 100 per cent against dictators, but questioned how the United States can protest little dictators when Soviet Premier Khrushchev was invited to the White House. A member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, Capehart also criticized the Eisenhower administration for failing to act promptly during Latin American troubles and questioned whether President Eisenhower or Vice President Nixon should travel abroad to the region.
records.summary_es: En una conferencia de prensa sobre asuntos exteriores, al senador Capehart, republicano de Indiana, se le preguntó su opinión acerca de la dictadura de Trujillo en la República Dominicana. Capehart declaró que está cien por ciento en contra de los dictadores, pero cuestionó cómo Estados Unidos puede protestar contra pequeños dictadores cuando el primer ministro soviético Jrushchov fue invitado a la Casa Blanca. Como miembro del Comité de Relaciones Exteriores del Senado, Capehart también criticó a la administración Eisenhower por no actuar con prontitud ante las dificultades latinoamericanas y cuestionó si el presidente Eisenhower o el vicepresidente Nixon deberían viajar a la región.

records.headline: An unarmed United States aircraft carrying military attache
records.summary_en: An unarmed United States aircraft carrying military attache Lt. Col. Robert P. Foley and Maj. John G. Williams was intercepted by Dominican fighter planes along the Dominican-Haitian frontier approximately 20 air miles from Port-au-Prince. Dominican pilots reportedly fired machinegun bullets across the plane's path during its routine flight from Ciudad Trujillo and forced it to land at a Dominican airfield. After the American officers were identified, they were permitted to resume their journey to Port-au-Prince. Observers interpreted the interception as evidence that the Dominican Republic is experiencing renewed invasion jitters, amid circulating reports that Dominican troops are concentrated in the north near the Haitian border.
records.summary_es: Un avión desarmado de Estados Unidos que transportaba al agregado militar teniente coronel Robert P. Foley y al mayor John G. Williams fue interceptado por aviones de caza dominicanos a lo largo de la frontera domínico-haitiana, a unas 20 millas aéreas de Puerto Príncipe. Según informes, pilotos dominicanos dispararon ráfagas de ametralladora frente a la nave durante su vuelo de rutina desde Ciudad Trujillo y la obligaron a aterrizar en un aeródromo dominicano. Tras ser identificados, a los oficiales estadounidenses se les permitió reanudar su viaje hacia Puerto Príncipe. Observadores interpretaron la interceptación como muestra de que la República Dominicana sufre nuevamente de nerviosismo ante invasiones, en medio de informes que señalan que tropas dominicanas están concentradas en el norte, cerca de la frontera haitiana.

records.headline: President Hector Bienvenido Trujillo y Molina, spending part of his wedding
records.summary_en: President Hector Bienvenido Trujillo y Molina, spending part of his wedding day at the ceremony, joined Generalissimo Rafael Leonidas Trujillo y Molina to dedicate a new jet airport along the south coast of the Dominican Republic. The leaders were on hand to greet a Boeing 707 Intercontinental that arrived 31 minutes ahead of schedule on a 1,600-mile flight. The fifteen-million-dollar airport is situated between the sea and a four-lane highway linking Ciudad Trujillo with the beach resort of Boca Chica. The article observes that the surrounding island, named La Espanola by Columbus and known to the English as Hispaniola, served for more than 50 years as Spain's principal base for New World conquests.
records.summary_es: El presidente Héctor Bienvenido Trujillo y Molina, quien dedicó parte del día de su boda a la ceremonia, se unió al generalísimo Rafael Leónidas Trujillo y Molina para inaugurar un nuevo aeropuerto para jets en la costa sur de la República Dominicana. Los mandatarios estuvieron presentes para recibir a un Boeing 707 Intercontinental que llegó 31 minutos antes de lo previsto en un vuelo de 1.600 millas. El aeropuerto de quince millones de dólares está situado entre el mar y una autopista de cuatro carriles que enlaza a Ciudad Trujillo con el balneario de Boca Chica. La crónica destaca que la isla circundante, bautizada La Española por Colón y conocida en inglés como Hispaniola, sirvió durante más de 50 años como base principal para las conquistas españolas en el Nuevo Mundo.

records.headline: An account of Dominican heritage identifies Ciudad Trujillo
records.summary_en: An account of Dominican heritage identifies Ciudad Trujillo as the oldest European settlement in the New World, founded in 1496 by Bartolome Columbus as La Nueva Isabela. The settlement was later renamed Santo Domingo del Puerto and Santo Domingo de Guzman before adopting its present name for Generalissimo Trujillo in 1937. The narrative records that two universities, Santo Tomas de Aquino and Santiago de la Paz, were established in 1503, while early Spanish colonists faced frequent uprisings by Carib Indians who were eventually forced into slavery. Landmark sites for travelers include the Tower of Homage, built in 1503 for swearing allegiance to the Spanish crown, and the restored Alcazar de Colon, where Christopher Columbus' son Diego resided as viceroy.
records.summary_es: Una reseña sobre el patrimonio dominicano identifica a Ciudad Trujillo como el asentamiento europeo más antiguo del Nuevo Mundo, fundado en 1496 por Bartolomé Colón bajo el nombre de La Nueva Isabela. El poblado pasó a llamarse posteriormente Santo Domingo del Puerto y Santo Domingo de Guzmán antes de adoptar su nombre actual en honor al generalísimo Trujillo en 1937. El relato recuerda que dos universidades, Santo Tomás de Aquino y Santiago de la Paz, se fundaron en 1503, mientras que los primeros colonos españoles enfrentaron continuas revueltas de indígenas caribes que finalmente fueron sometidos a la esclavitud. Entre los sitios emblemáticos para los viajeros figuran la Torre del Homenaje, erigida en 1503 para jurar lealtad a la corona española, y el restaurado Alcázar de Colón, donde Diego Colón, hijo de Cristóbal, vivió como virrey.

records.headline: Inside the Cathedral at Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: Inside the Cathedral at Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic, a travel photograph caption from Pan American World Airways describes an elaborate tomb constructed of Florentine marble. The caption states that the monument houses bones said to be those of Christopher Columbus. The remainder of the printed column consists of unrelated travel announcements regarding winter tour packages in Squaw Valley and weekend events in Williamsburg, Virginia.

El resto de la columna impresa comprende avisos de viaje no vinculados sobre paquetes turísticos de invierno en Squaw Valley y actividades de fin de semana en Williamsburg, Virginia.

records.headline: A guide at the Cathedral in Ciudad Trujillo, formerly Santo
records.summary_en: A guide at the Cathedral in Ciudad Trujillo, formerly Santo Domingo, explains that Christopher Columbus died in Spain on May 20, and that 36 years later Charles V granted permission for his remains to be transferred across the Atlantic. Preserving its original walls, ceilings, and columns, the cathedral serves as a prominent starting point for early New World history. The building houses the baptismal font where four of Columbus' grandchildren were baptized, comprising three girls and one boy. Among its fifteen chapels are twelve paintings of the apostles attributed to Velazquez and an admired painting of the Madonna by Murillo.
records.summary_es: Un guía en la Catedral de Ciudad Trujillo, antes Santo Domingo, explica que Cristóbal Colón murió en España el 20 de mayo, y que 36 años después Carlos V autorizó el traslado de sus restos a través del Atlántico. Al conservar sus muros, techos y columnas originales, la catedral constituye un punto de partida fundamental para la historia temprana del Nuevo Mundo. El templo alberga la pila bautismal donde fueron bautizados cuatro nietos de Colón, integrados por tres niñas y un niño. Entre sus quince capillas se encuentran doce pinturas de los apóstoles atribuidas a Velázquez y una admirada representación de la Virgen obra de Murillo.

records.summary_en: Cuban authorities discovered an entrance to escape tunnels under the bed of Roberto Martin Perez, the son of a former army colonel and a prominent figure among 190 prisoners held in connection with the so-called Trujillo plot. Martin Perez was arrested the preceding August after a firefight at Trinidad between Castro forces and the occupants of an arms-laden aircraft that flew in from the Dominican Republic. Fidel Castro has charged that the purported conspiracy was financed directly by Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, the Dominican Republic's head and arch-enemy of the Cuban revolutionary leader.
records.summary_es: Las autoridades cubanas descubrieron la entrada a túneles de escape bajo la cama de Roberto Martín Pérez, hijo de un excoronel del ejército y figura prominente entre 190 prisioneros detenidos en relación con la denominada conspiración trujillista. Martín Pérez fue arrestado el agosto anterior tras un tiroteo en Trinidad entre fuerzas de Castro y los ocupantes de un avión cargado de armas procedente de la República Dominicana. Fidel Castro ha denunciado que el supuesto complot fue financiado directamente por el generalísimo Rafael Trujillo, mandatario de la República Dominicana y acérrimo enemigo del dirigente revolucionario cubano.

records.headline: Dispatches reaching Washington report that authorities in the Dominican Republic smashed
records.summary_en: Dispatches reaching Washington report that authorities in the Dominican Republic smashed a widespread plot to assassinate Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, with well-qualified sources stating police arrested perhaps a thousand or more Dominicans about a week earlier. The conspiracy was regarded by the Dominican government as one of the most serious in the 30 years of Trujillo's rule. Conversely, Col. John Abbes Garcia of the Dominican Military Intelligence Service denounced accounts of mass arrests as maliciously twisted, claiming only 15 to 30 individuals were being held in connection with an alleged Cuban effort to construct bombs and organize communist-type cells.

records.summary_en: A report on the anti-Trujillo conspiracy identifies prominent detainees including Jose Hassin, Asela Morell, Jose Fernandez Carmiero, and engineer Ramon Caceres Troncoso, noting that the involvement of professional men and doctors confirms participation by leading families rather than mere adventurers. Police reportedly discovered hidden arms and imprisoned many individuals in a special detention camp erected outside Ciudad Trujillo, as well as in other cities. Although Col. Según informes, la policía descubrió depósitos de armas y recluyó a numerosos ciudadanos en un campo de concentración especial construido en las afueras de Ciudad Trujillo, así como en otras localidades. Pese a que el coronel John Abbes García de la inteligencia militar dominicana calificó de maliciosamente tergiversados los datos de capturas masivas y sostuvo que solo había de 15 a 20 detenidos vinculados a planes cubanos de fabricación de bombas, versiones sin censura recibidas en Washington consideraron el complot como uno de los más graves en los 30 años de dictadura del general Trujillo.

records.headline: At its sixth congress in Brussels, the International Confederation of Free Trade Unions directed
records.summary_en: At its sixth congress in Brussels, the International Confederation of Free Trade Unions directed General Secretary J. H. Oldenbroek to explore methods of fighting the Trujillo regime, including a potential international boycott, over its long-standing denial of fundamental worker rights. Following the resolution, Salvador E. Pandas, the Dominican government's permanent diplomatic representative in Geneva, met with union officials and pledged positive action to resolve labor criticisms. Soon after, Washington Guareno Marte of the government-dominated Confederation of Workers proposed dispatching a third fact-finding mission to the Dominican Republic, despite a previous 1957 investigation concluding that collective bargaining did not exist while forced labor was actively practiced.

Tras dicha resolución, Salvador E. Poco después, Washington Guareño Marte, de la oficialista Confederación de Trabajadores, propuso enviar una tercera misión de investigación a la República Dominicana, aun cuando una indagación previa de 1957 concluyó que la contratación colectiva no existía y que el trabajo forzado era una realidad.

records.headline: An editorial commentary asserts that his socio-economic program
records.summary_en: An editorial commentary asserts that his socio-economic program in Cuba and Fidel Castro cannot survive the massive weight of American arms, whether applied directly by the United States or channeled through its ally, Dictator Trujillo of the Dominican Republic. The piece observes that Castro is actively denouncing American corporate pressures designed to force a retreat from his goal of economic independence. The author warns that military force or economic retaliation by the United States would be viewed globally as committing a Hungary in the hemisphere, driving millions of impoverished Latin Americans to seek foreign allies against economic colonialism.

El artículo señala que Castro denuncia abiertamente las presiones corporativas norteamericanas orientadas a forzarlo a retroceder en su meta de independencia económica. El autor advierte que el uso de la fuerza militar o las represalias económicas por parte de Estados Unidos serían percibidos en el mundo como una Hungría en este hemisferio, llevando a millones de latinoamericanos desposeídos a buscar aliados externos contra el colonialismo económico.

records.headline: An editorial published under the heading Rough Sailing in The Dominican Republic examines
records.summary_en: An editorial published under the heading Rough Sailing in The Dominican Republic examines an acute political crisis developing against the regime of Generalissimo Rafael Leonidas Trujillo Molina. The piece notes that after more than 30 years of authoritarian domination, the Dominican government has even proposed organizing a fabricated opposition party to participate in the 1962 elections, likely prompted by diplomatic suggestions from abroad to soften its single-party image. In addition, the commentary highlights rumors circulated by official Washington sources regarding the departure of former Argentine dictator Juan Domingo Peron, who reportedly foresaw imminent turmoil in the Dominican Republic and wished to avoid another hasty escape into exile.
records.summary_es: Un editorial publicado bajo el encabezamiento Marejada en la República Dominicana analiza la aguda crisis política que se desarrolla contra el régimen del generalísimo Rafael Leónidas Trujillo Molina. El artículo señala que, tras más de 30 años de dominación autoritaria, el gobierno dominicano ha llegado a proponer la formación de un partido de oposición prefabricado para concurrir a las elecciones de 1962, probablemente impulsado por sugerencias diplomáticas externas para atenuar su imagen de partido único. Asimismo, el comentario destaca los rumores difundidos por fuentes oficiales de Washington sobre la salida del exdictador argentino Juan Domingo Perón, quien según se afirma presagió trastornos inminentes en la República Dominicana y prefirió evitar otra apresurada salida al exilio.

records.headline: An institutional statement published by the Dominican Republic Sugar Commission
records.summary_en: An institutional statement published by the Dominican Republic Sugar Commission in Ciudad Trujillo appeals to the United States for fair and equitable consideration for the country's leading crop. The commission emphasizes that Dominican sugar expansion is deliberate, mechanized, and science-fostered, guided by experienced businessmen, agronomists, and engineers. The text notes that the nation has never failed to satisfy its export commitments to international markets, and has consistently covered the sugar supply deficits of other producing countries.
records.summary_es: Una declaración institucional publicada por la Comisión de Azúcar de la República Dominicana en Ciudad Trujillo apela a los Estados Unidos solicitando una consideración justa y equitativa para el cultivo principal del país. La comisión destaca que la expansión azucarera dominicana es deliberada, mecanizada y promovida por la ciencia, bajo la dirección de empresarios, agrónomos e ingenieros de gran experiencia. El documento subraya que la nación jamás ha dejado de honrar sus compromisos de exportación en los mercados internacionales y ha cubierto reiteradamente los déficits de abastecimiento de otros países productores.

records.headline: Under the printed headline Dominican Arrests Now Total More Than One
records.summary_en: Under the printed headline Dominican Arrests Now Total More Than One Thousand, a UPI report states that a wave of arrests continues in the Dominican Republic two weeks after an alleged plot to kill dictator Rafael Trujillo. Reliable accounts indicate that perhaps 1,500 persons have been herded into a countryside detention camp outside Ciudad Trujillo, where many have suffered extreme physical abuse. Prominent businessmen, professionals, and members of influential families continue to be taken into custody despite official government denials. The Dominican police have refused to publish the names of those imprisoned or the charges lodged against them.

Versiones fidedignas señalan que quizás 1.500 personas han sido concentradas en un campo de detención en las afueras de Ciudad Trujillo, donde muchas han padecido graves abusos físicos. Destacados empresarios, profesionales y miembros de familias influyentes continúan bajo custodia pese a las negativas oficiales del gobierno. La policía dominicana no ha hecho públicos los nombres de los recluidos ni las acusaciones formuladas en su contra.

records.summary_en: Dominican authorities confirmed the discovery of an internal conspiracy against Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo's regime, with Attorney General Luis E. Suero announcing that 123 persons had been rounded up following an investigation by army intelligence. Suero asserted that those accused are being prosecuted with full constitutional guarantees. The official announcement followed reports from neighboring Haiti alleging an armed rebellion against the military garrison in Santiago de los Caballeros. Concurrently, travelers arriving in San Juan, Puerto Rico estimated that between 1,000 and 1,500 individuals have been jailed on charges of plotting against Trujillo.
records.summary_es: Las autoridades dominicanas confirmaron el descubrimiento de una conspiración interna contra el régimen del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo, y el procurador general Luis E. Suero anunció que 123 personas fueron detenidas tras una investigación de la inteligencia militar. Suero aseguró que los acusados están siendo procesados con plenas garantías constitucionales. El pronunciamiento gubernamental se conoció poco después de versiones provenientes del vecino Haití que daban cuenta de un alzamiento armado contra la guarnición militar en Santiago de los Caballeros. Al mismo tiempo, viajeros llegados a San Juan de Puerto Rico calcularon que entre 1.000 y 1.500 personas han sido encarceladas bajo acusaciones de conspirar contra Trujillo.

records.headline: An editorial titled Rome And Washington in the Face of the Dominican Crisis analyzes
records.summary_en: An editorial titled Rome And Washington in the Face of the Dominican Crisis analyzes two major external developments confronting the Trujillo regime during its acute political emergency. First, the Catholic hierarchy of the Dominican Republic issued a dramatic Pastoral Letter denouncing human rights violations in the regime's repressive actions against political opponents, marking the first time Trujillo has faced open resistance from the Church. Second, the United States State Department conducted an intentional press conference expressing serious concern over events in Santo Domingo that threaten Caribbean peace and hemispheric humanitarian principles. The commentary observes that such critical public statements by Washington have rarely been leveled against dictatorships still holding power.
records.summary_es: Un editorial titulado Roma y Washington frente a la crisis dominicana examina dos trascendentales acontecimientos externos que enfrenta el régimen de Trujillo durante su grave emergencia política. En primer lugar, la jerarquía católica de la República Dominicana emitió una dramática Carta Pastoral que denuncia violaciones a los derechos humanos en las medidas represivas del régimen contra sus adversarios, constituyendo la primera ocasión en que Trujillo encara una abierta oposición de la Iglesia. En segundo lugar, el Departamento de Estado de los Estados Unidos convocó una rueda de prensa deliberada manifestando profunda preocupación por los sucesos de Santo Domingo que ponen en riesgo la paz del Caribe y los principios humanitarios de América. El comentario subraya que declaraciones críticas de esa naturaleza rara vez habían sido dirigidas por Washington contra dictaduras que aún se mantienen en el poder.

records.headline: Following their pastoral letter, the archbishops and bishops of the Dominican
records.summary_en: Following their pastoral letter, the archbishops and bishops of the Dominican Republic, during their first episcopal meeting of 1960, published a note requesting all priests to abstain from political intervention or actions altering public order incompatible with sacred ministry. Reflecting official concern over the letter's impact, the regime dispatched Foreign Minister Porfirio Herrera Báez to Rome to confer with the Vatican Secretariat of State, although the minister denied discussing the bishops' statement. Concurrently, Dominican press and radio launched a campaign urging 68-year-old General Trujillo to return to the presidency in 1962, calling a mass demonstration for February 21.
records.summary_es: Tras su carta pastoral, los arzobispos y obispos de la República Dominicana, durante su primera reunión episcopal de 1960, publicaron una nota solicitando a todos los sacerdotes abstenerse de intervenir en política o alterar el orden público de modo incompatible con el ministerio sacerdotal. Como muestra de la preocupación oficial por el impacto del documento, el régimen envió a Roma al ministro de Relaciones Exteriores Porfirio Herrera Báez para entrevistarse con la Secretaría de Estado del Vaticano, aunque el canciller negó haber tratado sobre la pastoral de los obispos. En paralelo, la prensa y la radio dominicanas iniciaron una campaña para instar al general Trujillo, de 68 años, a retornar a la presidencia en 1962, convocando a un acto masivo para el 21 de febrero.

records.headline: Secretary of State Herter added weight to an inquiry by stating
records.summary_en: Secretary of State Herter added weight to an inquiry by stating that United States officials were 'very much disturbed' by reports of mass arrests of Dominican citizens opposed to the dictatorial regime. Recent dispatches indicated that up to 2,000 persons, including members of the country's most prominent families, had been confined to concentration camps after being accused of plotting to overthrow the Trujillo government. In the Dominican Republic, Gen. Trujillo faced fallout from a pastoral letter read on January 31 in all 624 Catholic churches, which declared that human potentates cannot impede human rights and signaled episcopal sympathy for detainees and their families. Venezuelan Ambassador Marcos Falcon Briceno read the letter in full before the OAS Council while accusing Trujillo of patent, flagrant, and ugly violations of human rights extending over many years, with Cuba supporting the charges.
records.summary_es: El secretario de Estado Herter sumó peso a una investigación al declarar que los funcionarios estadounidenses se encontraban 'muy inquietos' por los informes de arrestos masivos de ciudadanos dominicanos opuestos al régimen dictatorial. Despachos recientes indicaban que hasta 2,000 personas, incluidos miembros de las familias más prominentes del país, habían sido recluidas en campos de concentración tras ser acusadas de conspirar para derrocar al gobierno de Trujillo. En la República Dominicana, el general Trujillo enfrentó las repercusiones de una carta pastoral leída el 31 de enero en las 624 iglesias católicas, la cual declaraba que los potentados humanos no pueden impedir los derechos humanos y expresaba la simpatía del episcopado hacia los detenidos y sus familias. El embajador venezolano Marcos Falcon Briceno leyó la carta en su totalidad ante el Consejo de la OEA al tiempo que acusó a Trujillo de violaciones patentes, flagrantes y bochornosas de los derechos humanos a lo largo de muchos años, con Cuba respaldando los cargos.

records.headline: An editorial note accompanying a dispatch from San Juan indicates
records.summary_en: An editorial note accompanying a dispatch from San Juan indicates that reports from trained foreign observers reaching Puerto Rico from Ciudad Trujillo detail present political conditions within the Dominican Republic, United Press International. Observers anticipate that a new wave of political arrests and trials may be expected across the nation. More than 2,000 Dominicans have been detained by national police following the dramatic exposure of an alleged plot to overthrow the 30-year-old Trujillo regime. It remains unknown how many detainees are still confined in Ciudad Trujillo's La Victoria prison and military installations.
records.summary_es: Una nota editorial que acompaña un despacho desde San Juan indica que informes de observadores extranjeros capacitados que llegaron a Puerto Rico desde Ciudad Trujillo detallan las condiciones políticas actuales dentro de la República Dominicana, de United Press International. Los observadores anticipan que puede esperarse una nueva ola de arrestos políticos y juicios en toda la nación. Más de 2,000 dominicanos han sido detenidos por la policía nacional tras el dramático descubrimiento de un presunto complot para derrocar al régimen trujillista de 30 años. Se desconoce cuántos de estos detenidos continúan recluidos en la prisión de La Victoria en Ciudad Trujillo y en instalaciones militares.

records.headline: An inquiry by the Inter-American Peace Committee into alleged
records.summary_en: An inquiry by the Inter-American Peace Committee into alleged violations of human rights in the Dominican Republic appeared possible following a request by Venezuela to the Organization of American States on Monday to investigate reports of mass arrests. Any formal inquiry must first navigate procedural hurdles within both the OAS Council and the Peace Committee itself. Meanwhile, dispatches from Venezuela reported that an uprising aimed at toppling the regime of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo could occur at any moment, though Trujillo denied that his dictatorship faced trouble.
records.summary_es: Una investigación de la Comisión Interamericana de Paz sobre supuestas violaciones de derechos humanos en la República Dominicana pareció posible tras la solicitud presentada por Venezuela el lunes ante la Organización de los Estados Americanos para investigar informes de arrestos masivos. Cualquier investigación formal debe superar primero obstáculos procesales tanto dentro del Consejo de la OEA como dentro de la propia Comisión de Paz. Mientras tanto, despachos procedentes de Venezuela informaban que un levantamiento destinado a derrocar el régimen del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo podría estallar en cualquier momento, aunque Trujillo negó que su dictadura estuviera en dificultades.

records.headline: An editorial notes that while the Dominican government has denied
records.summary_en: An editorial notes that while the Dominican government has denied accusations of mass imprisonments by claiming only a few detainees were remanded to the courts, a recent pastoral letter read in all Catholic churches across the country provides compelling evidence of a serious situation violating human rights. The text argues that national prelates would not have signed a pastoral letter containing such grave accusations unless an extraordinarily serious political crisis prevailed. While the regime could easily dismiss exile accusations as partisan passion, the collective testimony of the bishops carries profound weight during this international crisis over human rights violations in Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: Un editorial señala que, aunque el gobierno dominicano ha negado las acusaciones de encarcelamientos masivos afirmando que solo unos pocos detenidos fueron puestos a disposición judicial, una reciente carta pastoral leída en todas las iglesias católicas del país constituye prueba contundente de una grave situación violatoria de los derechos humanos. El texto sostiene que los prelados nacionales no habrían firmado una carta pastoral con acusaciones tan graves si no prevaleciera una crisis política extraordinariamente seria. Aunque el régimen pudiera desestimar con facilidad las acusaciones del exilio tildándolas de pasión partidista, el testimonio colectivo de los obispos posee un peso profundo durante esta crisis internacional por violaciones a los derechos humanos en Santo Domingo.

records.headline: A Cuban military tribunal in Havana convicted 104 persons on Wednesday night
records.summary_en: A Cuban military tribunal in Havana convicted 104 persons on Wednesday night for conspiring to overthrow Fidel Castro in an alleged plot backed by Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic. The five-man military court handed down prison terms ranging from three to 30 years in the largest conspiracy proceedings conducted since Castro seized power more than a year earlier. The tribunal acquitted 36 defendants of the conspiracy charges.

El tribunal militar de cinco miembros impuso penas de prisión que oscilan entre tres y 30 años en el mayor proceso por conspiración llevado a cabo desde que Castro tomó el poder hace más de un año. El tribunal absolvió a 36 acusados de los cargos de conspiración.

records.headline: The Dominican government made public copies of a letter written
records.summary_en: The Dominican government made public copies of a letter written by Roman Catholic Bishop Tomás F. Reilly of San Juan de la Maguana to United States Ambassador Joseph E. Farland, dated September 6, 1958, protesting Protestant missionary activity. Manuel de Moya, minister without portfolio and chief aide to Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, suggested that official failure to suppress Protestant proselytizing had partly motivated the 1,650-word Catholic pastoral letter read on January 31, which demanded full liberties and human rights. In his letter, Bishop Reilly asked whether American Embassy personnel were being utilized by Protestant groups conducting campaigns among the Catholic populace, while embassy officials noted that Farland is an Episcopal lay reader who has occasionally addressed local congregations.

Farland, fechada el 6 de septiembre de 1958, en protesta por las actividades misioneras protestantes. Manuel de Moya, ministro sin cartera y principal colaborador del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo, sugirió que la falta de intervención oficial para suprimir el proselitismo protestante motivó en parte la carta pastoral de 1,650 palabras leída el 31 de enero, en la que se exigían plenas libertades y derechos humanos. En su misiva, el obispo Reilly preguntó si el personal de la embajada estadounidense estaba siendo utilizado por grupos protestantes que realizaban campañas entre la población católica, mientras funcionarios de la embajada señalaron que Farland es lector laico de la Iglesia Episcopal y en ocasiones ha pronunciado alocuciones ante congregaciones locales.

records.headline: Dominican tribunals sentenced 41 more men to 30-year prison
records.summary_en: Dominican tribunals sentenced 41 more men to 30-year prison terms and assessed collective fines of $1.2 million for plotting to overthrow Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo. All defendants admitted their guilt during two mass trials conducted simultaneously in the Palace of Justice, bringing to 120 the total number of individuals sentenced to maximum conspiracy penalties since the government declared the disruption of a widespread plot. Officials reported that additional suspects were being interrogated and further trials were anticipated, while unconfirmed reports indicated that up to 2,000 persons had been detained, prompting Venezuela to seek an OAS investigation into flagrant human rights violations.
records.summary_es: Tribunales dominicanos sentenciaron a 41 hombres más a penas de 30 años de prisión e impusieron multas colectivas por 1.2 millones de dólares por conspirar para derrocar al generalísimo Rafael Trujillo. Todos los procesados admitieron su culpabilidad durante dos juicios colectivos celebrados de forma simultánea en el Palacio de Justicia, elevando a 120 el total de condenados a penas máximas por conspiración desde que el gobierno declaró desbaratado un extenso complot. Las autoridades informaron que otros sospechosos estaban siendo interrogados y se esperaban nuevos juicios, mientras informes extraoficiales indicaban la detención de hasta 2,000 personas, lo que llevó a Venezuela a solicitar una investigación de la OEA por flagrantes violaciones a los derechos humanos.

records.headline: A Dominican government radio broadcast claimed that an investigation
records.summary_en: A Dominican government radio broadcast claimed that an investigation involving Cuban Jesuit scholastic Antonio Cesar Fabres de la Guardia had been resolved satisfactorily and manipulated by subversive elements to fabricate a large-scale plot, noting that Fabres had been allowed to return to Cuba. On January 29, the station insisted that the Dominican Republic maintained excellent relations with the Catholic Church, asserting that ecclesiastical superiors had affirmed the local Jesuit community was entirely independent from the Cuban branch. In their pastoral letter, the Dominican bishops affirmed they could not remain indifferent to the affliction visiting the nation, enumerated individual liberties including freedom of conscience, press, and assembly, and declared any violation of these natural rights a grave offense against God and human dignity. The pastoral concluded by citing a 1947 address by Pope Pius XII affirming that liberty must flourish.
records.summary_es: Una transmisión radial oficial dominicana afirmó que la investigación en torno al escolástico jesuita cubano Antonio Cesar Fabres de la Guardia se había resuelto satisfactoriamente y había sido aprovechada por elementos subversivos para aparentar un complot a gran escala, indicando que a Fabres se le permitió regresar a Cuba. El 29 de enero, la emisora aseguró que la República Dominicana mantenía las mejores relaciones con la Iglesia católica y señaló que las autoridades eclesiásticas determinaron que la comunidad jesuita local era totalmente ajena a la establecida en Cuba. En su carta pastoral, los obispos dominicanos manifestaron que no podían permanecer indiferentes ante el penoso golpe que afectaba al país, enumeraron libertades individuales como la libertad de conciencia, de prensa y de reunión, y calificaron cualquier violación de estos derechos naturales como una ofensa grave contra Dios y la dignidad humana. La pastoral concluyó citando un discurso pronunciado en 1947 por el papa Pío XII en el que se reafirmaba que la libertad debe florecer.

records.headline: Dominican government official Porfirio Herrera Báez concealed
records.summary_en: Dominican government official Porfirio Herrera Báez concealed his whereabouts from the Rome press corps following rumors that he had met with the Pope at 10 a.m. unrecorded on the official Vatican schedule. Meanwhile, Vatican authorities announced that Coadjutor Archbishop Octavio Antonio Beras of Ciudad Trujillo was appointed Apostolic Administrator of the capital see, assuming administrative duties from Metropolitan Archbishop Ricardo Pittini. Vatican officials clarified that the decision had been made three weeks prior to its public release solely because of Pittini's age of nearly 84 years and failing health, emphasizing that the transfer had no connection to current Dominican political developments. In an unrelated diplomatic appointment, Msgr. Giovanni Ferrofino, a veteran Holy See delegate to international organizations, was named Apostolic Nuncio to neighboring Haiti.
records.summary_es: El funcionario gubernamental dominicano Porfirio Herrera Báez ocultó su paradero a la prensa de Roma tras rumores de que se había reunido con el papa a las 10 a.m., cita que no constaba en la agenda oficial del Vaticano. Mientras tanto, las autoridades vaticanas anunciaron que el arzobispo coadjutor Octavio Antonio Beras de Ciudad Trujillo fue designado administrador apostólico de la sede capitalina, asumiendo las funciones de gobierno del arzobispo metropolitano Ricardo Pittini. Funcionarios vaticanos precisaron que la decisión se había adoptado tres semanas antes de su divulgación exclusivamente debido a los casi 84 años de edad y la salud declinante de Pittini, recalcando que el relevo no guardaba relación alguna con los acontecimientos políticos dominicanos contemporáneos. En una designación diplomática separada, monseñor Giovanni Ferrofino, veterano delegado de la Santa Sede ante organismos internacionales, fue nombrado nuncio apostólico en el vecino Haití.

records.headline: Vatican City dispatches revealed Holy See concern regarding
records.summary_en: Vatican City dispatches revealed Holy See concern regarding developments in the Dominican Republic and Haiti, noting reports of a papal audience requested by a senior Dominican official, the retirement of the aged Archbishop of Ciudad Trujillo, and the appointment of a new Apostolic Nuncio to Port-au-Prince. In the Dominican Republic, a pastoral letter read by Catholic bishops avoided naming Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo or his brother President Héctor B. Trujillo, nor did it directly mention the arrest of hundreds of citizens accused of a plot against the regime. However, the bishops stated that they pray that no member of the authority's family ever experiences during their lifetime the profound suffering that currently afflicts so many Dominican fathers, mothers, children, and spouses.
records.summary_es: Despachos desde la Ciudad del Vaticano revelaron la preocupación de la Santa Sede por los sucesos en la República Dominicana y en Haití, destacando informes sobre una audiencia papal solicitada por un alto funcionario dominicano, el retiro del anciano arzobispo de Ciudad Trujillo y el nombramiento de un nuevo nuncio apostólico en Puerto Príncipe. En la República Dominicana, una carta pastoral leída por los obispos católicos evitó mencionar por su nombre al generalísimo Rafael Trujillo o a su hermano el presidente Héctor B. Trujillo, así como tampoco aludió expresamente al arresto de centenares de ciudadanos acusados de conspirar contra el régimen. No obstante, los obispos manifestaron rezar para que ningún familiar de la autoridad experimente jamás a lo largo de su vida los hondos sufrimientos que hoy afligen a tantos padres, madres, hijos y cónyuges dominicanos.

records.headline: Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, self-styled 'El Benefactor' and absolute
records.summary_en: Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, self-styled 'El Benefactor' and absolute dictator of the Dominican Republic for 30 years, calmly asserted to an interviewer that citizens arrested for anti-regime plotting were deluded by Communists and chronic enemies, predicting they would eventually be pardoned after undergoing corrective incarceration. The government announced that more than 80 Dominicans drawn largely from prominent families, professional classes, and student groups received sentences of up to 30 years during two mass trials in Ciudad Trujillo. While Trujillo promised that a two-party democracy would be established once conditions grew calmer, open criticism in a pastoral letter by the country's six Roman Catholic bishops was regarded by observers as potent evidence of widespread disaffection, despite official claims that the bishops were merely protesting state tolerance of Protestant organizations.
records.summary_es: El generalísimo Rafael Trujillo, autodenominado 'El Benefactor' y dictador absoluto de la República Dominicana durante 30 años, afirmó serenamente ante un entrevistador que los ciudadanos arrestados por conspirar contra el régimen habían sido engañados por comunistas y enemigos crónicos, pronosticando que serían indultados tras cumplir un periodo de reclusión correctiva. El gobierno informó que más de 80 dominicanos, procedentes en su mayoría de familias prominentes, sectores profesionales y grupos estudiantiles, recibieron penas de hasta 30 años en dos juicios masivos en Ciudad Trujillo. Aunque Trujillo prometió instaurar una democracia bipartidista una vez que la situación se apaciguara, las críticas públicas expuestas en una carta pastoral por los seis obispos católicos del país fueron consideradas por los observadores como prueba contundente de un descontento generalizado, a pesar de los alegatos oficiales de que la jerarquía eclesiástica solo protestaba contra la tolerancia estatal hacia los grupos protestantes.

records.headline: In the Dominican Republic, 120 individuals have been sentenced
records.summary_en: In the Dominican Republic, 120 individuals have been sentenced to 30 years of hard labor alongside fines exceeding one million dollars after admitting their involvement in an anti-regime conspiracy. The convictions accompany acute domestic economic difficulties in the 30th year of Rafael Trujillo's dictatorship, where an acute drought reduced sugar and coffee harvests while world commodity prices fell. The resulting drop in state revenues, coupled with extraordinary military expenditures provoked by invasion threats from exiles in Cuba, forced extensive spending cutbacks in public works. A Dominican Central Bank official calculated that imports surpassed exports by 20 million dollars last year compared to nearly nine millions in 1958, while domestic middle-class elements sought a transitional democratic government to avoid an outcome patterned on Fidel Castro's revolution.
records.summary_es: En la República Dominicana, 120 personas han sido condenadas a 30 años de trabajos forzados junto con multas que superan el millón de dólares tras admitir su participación en una conspiración contra el régimen. Las condenas se suman a graves dificultades económicas internas en el trigésimo año de la dictadura de Rafael Trujillo, en el que una severa sequía redujo las cosechas de azúcar y café mientras descendían las cotizaciones en los mercados mundiales. La merma de ingresos estatales, sumada a los extraordinarios gastos militares obligados por amenazas de invasión de exiliados desde Cuba, forzó fuertes recortes en las obras públicas. Un funcionario del Banco Central dominicano calculó que las importaciones superaron a las exportaciones por 20 millones de dólares el año pasado frente a casi nueve millones en 1958, mientras sectores de la clase media local aspiraban a un gobierno democrático de transición para evitar un desenlace semejante al de la revolución de Fidel Castro.

records.headline: United States Senator Smathers reported during a news conference
records.summary_en: United States Senator Smathers reported during a news conference following an extended tour of Latin America that Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo accepted his proposal to hold free elections in the Dominican Republic. Smathers stated that Trujillo gave assurances that no member of his family would seek political office, promising that local elections would occur within 15 months and national voting within two years. The senator warned that Communists could seize power in the vacuum created when Trujillo leaves office, predicting that Haiti, Venezuela, and neighboring nations would subsequently succumb to Soviet influence.
records.summary_es: El senador estadounidense Smathers informó durante una conferencia de prensa posterior a una extensa gira por América Latina que el generalísimo Rafael Trujillo aceptó su propuesta de celebrar elecciones libres en la República Dominicana. Smathers afirmó que Trujillo aseguró que ningún miembro de su familia postularía a cargos públicos, prometiendo comicios locales en un plazo de 15 meses y votaciones nacionales en dos años. El senador advirtió de que los comunistas podrían tomar el poder en el vacío que se produzca cuando Trujillo abandone el mando, pronosticando que Haití, Venezuela y otras naciones vecinas sucumbirían paulatinamente a la influencia soviética.

records.headline: A passerby was reported killed and two police officers wounded
records.summary_en: A passerby was reported killed and two police officers wounded during a shooting confrontation in Ciudad Trujillo between police and students seeking asylum inside the Brazilian Embassy. Diplomatic sources indicated that gunfire struck embassy grounds after the youths informed an embassy official they were sought by authorities on suspicion of subversive activities against Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo's 30-year regime. In Puerto Rico, Columbia Broadcasting System correspondent Bill Leonard stated that he had witnessed and filmed the exchange, reporting that one of 17 youths involved was shot and that the embassy building itself sustained gun damage.
records.summary_es: Un transeúnte resultó muerto y dos policías quedaron heridos durante un enfrentamiento a tiros en Ciudad Trujillo entre fuerzas policiales y estudiantes que intentaban refugiarse en la embajada de Brasil. Fuentes diplomáticas señalaron que disparos impactaron en terrenos de la sede consular luego de que los jóvenes comunicaran a un funcionario diplomático que eran perseguidos por sospechas de conspirar contra el régimen de 30 años del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo. En Puerto Rico, el corresponsal de Columbia Broadcasting System Bill Leonard afirmó haber presenciado y filmado el tiroteo, informando que uno de los 17 jóvenes involucrados recibió un disparo y que el edificio de la embajada fue alcanzado por impactos de bala.

records.headline: A Spanish-language column by Jules Dubois says Senator George Smathers of Florida ended his Latin American trip with statements
records.summary_en: A Spanish-language column by Jules Dubois says Senator George Smathers of Florida ended his Latin American trip with statements in Ciudad Trujillo and Miami that were interpreted as support for Generalissimo Rafael Leonidas Trujillo, producing violent reactions among Dominican exiles and Americans. Dubois reads the statements as a reproach to the State Department's evident displeasure with Trujillo, shown by recalling Ambassador Joseph Farland to Washington for consultations, and believes Smathers hoped for a peaceful transition and Trujillo's departure through votes rather than revolution.
records.summary_es: Una columna en español de Jules Dubois dice que el senador George Smathers de Florida terminó su viaje por América Latina con declaraciones en Ciudad Trujillo y Miami que fueron interpretadas como un apoyo al Generalísimo Rafael Leónidas Trujillo, produciendo reacciones violentas entre los exiliados dominicanos y los americanos. Dubois lee las declaraciones como un reproche al evidente desagrado del Departamento de Estado con Trujillo, mostrado al llamar al embajador Joseph Farland a Washington para consultas, y cree que Smathers esperaba una transición pacífica y la salida de Trujillo mediante los votos en lugar de la revolución.

records.full_text:
American Current Events
Senator Smathers and Trujillo
By JULES DUBOIS

The distinguished United States Senator from the State of Florida, George Smathers, ended his trip through Latin America with a statement that was interpreted as one of support for Generalissimo Rafael Leónidas Trujillo, the Benefactor and Father of the New Fatherland.

Those observations, made at a press conference held in Ciudad Trujillo, and similar statements made upon his return to Miami, produced violent reactions among Dominican exiles and among Americans. Senator Smathers’ statements appear to be a reproach to the State Department’s policy of evident displeasure with Trujillo, which was expressed in a recent pronouncement and was demonstrated by the action of calling the American Ambassador Joseph Farland to Washington for consultations.

So that there be no misunderstanding, Senator Smathers is a prominent member of the Democratic Party. His party has the majority in both Houses of Congress. President Eisenhower belongs to the opposition, to the Republican Party. So the Republicans cannot be blamed for those observations.

I am one of those who believe that Senator Smathers made his statements with sincere intentions, because he undoubtedly considers that a peaceful transition of government and Trujillo’s departure through the votes would be much more preferable than his violent departure through revolution. Without doubt, like many of us, he has been completely disillusioned by the manner in which Fidel Castro has contributed to destroying the confidence of free men and women in announced ideals of liberty, tolerance, justice, and respect for the constitution, which he said would prevail in Cuba after his victory.

Instead of that, Castro has led the people of Cuba into a state of constant agitation, with a direct hostility toward the United States and an incessant conspiracy by those affected by his reforms and by those who do not want to see their country taking the road of communism.

Senator Smathers set down his position in these two sentences: “We Americans cannot support and do not support the remaining old-style dictatorships. But neither do we wish to see dictators of the Right replaced by equally oppressive dictators of the Left.”

That is understandable, and I am sure that Senator Smathers will have the support of many, many people in this particular. But there are some of us who believe that he was prepared to give the greatest hope to his effort to persuade Trujillo to renounce his control over the destiny of the Dominican people in 1962, tolerating the organization of the opposition parties and candidates.

As soon as Smathers held his press conferen-

The official Dominican radio station, La Voz Dominicana, continued promoting what the announcer described as the “apotheosic demonstration” of February 21, in which the entire country was mobilized to implore Generalissimo Trujillo to accept the presidential nomination for 1962.

That mobilization had been going on for three weeks, and Trujillo had no intention of stopping it.

As a positive fact, the Government of Trujillo extended invitations to newspaper directors throughout the United States, so that they might travel to his land and witness that “spontaneous” demonstration of loyalty.

I am sure that if Senator Smathers had known that every night La Voz Dominicana bombards the airwaves inciting the people of Cuba to rise against Castro, and the people of Venezuela to rebel against Rómulo Betancourt, he might have had a few words of advice for the Benefactor in this matter.

A so-called “Radio Liberación de Venezuela,” which transmits a powerful signal all along the waveband of La Voz Dominicana, but which claims to be operating from Venezuela, is the latest addition to Trujillo’s efforts to overthrow Rómulo Betancourt from the presidency.

These are precisely the kind of maneuvers that increase the opportunities of the communists, instead of doing them harm. It is almost a certainty that when the Senator discovers that Trujillo listened attentively, smiling apparently at every moment, but laughing inwardly and accepting the “spontaneous” desire of his people for the presidential candidacy in 1962, Smathers may make a reappraisal of his observations.

records.headline: A syndicated commentary contends that United States arms transfers
records.summary_en: A syndicated commentary contends that United States arms transfers have consolidated Latin American strongmen like Generalissimo Trujillo, fostering tyrannical rule, political instability, and post-regime turmoil, citing prevailing unrest in the Dominican Republic as an immediate illustration. The dispatch notes that notwithstanding public pledges to halt such shipments, the United States Defense Department delivered $1,089,000 in weaponry to Trujillo during fiscal year 1959 and is transferring an additional $445,000 in 1960. It concludes that this policy explains why leaders such as Chilean President Alessandri remain skeptical when meeting with President Eisenhower.
records.summary_es: Un comentario de prensa sindicado sostiene que las transferencias de armas de Estados Unidos han afianzado a hombres fuertes latinoamericanos como el generalísimo Trujillo, propiciando regímenes tiránicos, inestabilidad política y caos tras la caída de los dictadores, señalando la agitación imperante en la República Dominicana como un ejemplo directo. El texto subraya que, a pesar de las promesas de suspender dichos suministros, el Departamento de Defensa de Estados Unidos entregó 1,089,000 dólares en armamento a Trujillo durante el año fiscal de 1959 y enviará otros 445,000 dólares en 1960. Se concluye que esta política explica los recelos de mandatarios como el presidente chileno Alessandri al dialogar con el presidente Eisenhower.

records.headline: Upon arriving in the United States, New York Times correspondent
records.summary_en: Upon arriving in the United States, New York Times correspondent Mr. Burks stated that the Dominican government presented him with the alternative of leaving the country or facing court summons on defamation charges initiated by legal counsel for Col. Horacio Firas, who had been relieved as commander of Victoria Prison in Ciudad Trujillo 10 days earlier. Burks defended his report that Col. Firas was arrested and led away in handcuffs as an eyewitness account relayed by a prisoner's relative visiting the facility, contradicting official claims that the officer was merely transferred to a new post on the Haitian-Dominican border. The article noted that another Times reporter, Tad Szulc, departed under comparable circumstances the prior July and was subsequently convicted in absentia of slandering former chief of staff Brig. Gen. Maximo R. Bonetti Burgos, receiving a two-month prison sentence, a 25-peso fine, and 50,000 pesos in damages.
records.summary_es: Al llegar a los Estados Unidos, el corresponsal de The New York Times señor Burks declaró que el gobierno dominicano le dio la opción de abandonar el país o afrontar una citación judicial por cargos de difamación interpuestos por el abogado del coronel Horacio Firas, quien había sido relevado como comandante de la prisión de La Victoria en Ciudad Trujillo 10 días antes. Burks defendió que su reporte sobre el arresto y traslado esposado del coronel Firas se basó en el testimonio presencial de un familiar que visitaba a un recluso, lo cual contradice la versión oficial de que el militar solo fue transferido a un nuevo mando en la frontera dominico-haitiana. El despacho recordó que otro periodista del Times, Tad Szulc, salió del país en circunstancias similares en julio anterior y luego fue condenado en rebeldía por calumniar al exjefe de Estado Mayor general de brigada Máximo R. Bonetti Burgos, recibiendo dos meses de prisión, una multa de 25 pesos y 50,000 pesos por daños y perjuicios.

records.headline: An official Dominican statement defends the independence of the nation's
records.summary_en: An official Dominican statement defends the independence of the nation's courts, asserting that magistrates render sovereign decisions without outside reproach or interference. The text cites principles proclaimed by Generalissimo Trujillo during an address to judicial magistrates in Santiago in 1933, warning that yielding to outside interests leads to defection, prevarication, or abuse of power. The passage also highlights Trujillo's address on February 2fl, 1959, at the inauguration of the Palace of Justice, where he and President Hector Bienvenido Trujillo Molina were awarded medals of the Order of Judicial Merit, reiterating his commitment to an independent judicial order in the service of the public.
records.summary_es: Una declaración oficial dominicana defiende la independencia de los tribunales del país, afirmando que los magistrados dictan decisiones soberanas sin reproches ni interferencias externas. El texto cita los principios proclamados por el generalísimo Trujillo durante una reunión con magistrados en Santiago en 1933, advirtiendo que ceder a intereses externos conduce a la prevaricación o al abuso de poder. El pasaje también destaca el discurso de Trujillo del 2fl de febrero de 1959 con motivo de la inauguración del Palacio de Justicia, donde él y el presidente Héctor Bienvenido Trujillo Molina recibieron la Orden del Mérito Judicial, reiterando su compromiso con un orden judicial al servicio del público.

records.headline: An official statement by Mario Abreu Penzo, Secretary of State
records.summary_en: An official statement by Mario Abreu Penzo, Secretary of State for Justice and Attorney General in Ciudad Trujillo, reports that the Court of Appeal modified sentences for accused parties, reducing penalties for a considerable group, sentencing another group to up to 2 years in prison, and clearing an important number of appellants. Abreu Penzo asserts that these rulings demonstrate humanitarian progress and refute protests before the Organization of American States by citizens of the United States alleging imaginary violations of human rights. The statement characterizes the protest signers as victims of external anti-Dominican propaganda and defends government safety measures against conspirators attempting to introduce communism, while praising Generalissimo Trujillo as Benefactor of the Country and Father of the New Motherland.
records.summary_es: Una declaración oficial de Mario Abreu Penzo, secretario de Estado de Justicia y procurador general en Ciudad Trujillo, informa que la Corte de Apelación modificó las sentencias de los acusados, reduciendo las penas de un grupo considerable, condenando a otro grupo a un máximo de 2 años de prisión y absolviendo a un número importante de apelantes. Abreu Penzo sostiene que estos fallos demuestran avances humanitarios y desmienten las protestas ante la Organización de los Estados Americanos por parte de ciudadanos de los Estados Unidos que alegan violaciones imaginarias de derechos humanos. La declaración califica a los firmantes de la protesta como víctimas de una propaganda antidominicana externa y defiende las medidas de seguridad del gobierno frente a conspiradores que intentan introducir el comunismo, elogiando al generalísimo Trujillo como Benefactor de la Patria y Padre de la Patria Nueva.

records.headline: In a letter published under the heading “Protest,” reader Larry V. Luther criticizes
records.summary_en: In a letter published under the heading “Protest,” reader Larry V. Luther criticizes The Star for running a Sunday advertisement titled “Communist Infiltration Has Be«n Stopped In The Dominican Republic.” Luther characterizes the advertisement, framed as a report from the Dominican Attorney General to that nation’s congress, as a crude attempt by dictator Trujillo to appeal directly to the American public over the heads of the United States government. He questions whether the newspaper should serve as a propaganda instrument for a regime he describes as one of the crudest and most inhuman dictatorships known.

Cuestiona si el periódico debe servir como instrumento de propaganda para un régimen al que describe como una de las dictaduras más crueles e inhumanas conocidas.

records.headline: An editorial observes that the United States Secretary of State
records.summary_en: An editorial observes that the United States Secretary of State has categorically identified the governments of Nicaragua, the Dominican Republic, and Paraguay as dictatorial before Congress, marking the first time the State Department has named these regimes with proper names. The piece asserts that this classification obliges the Washington government to exercise extreme caution in its relations with the Somoza, Trujillo, and Stroessner regimes. It urges United States ambassadors accredited to these three nations to maintain tact in their dealings, warning that excessive cordiality creates the false impression of United States support, which dictatorships exploit politically.
records.summary_es: Un editorial observa que el secretario de Estado de los Estados Unidos identificó categóricamente ante el Congreso a los gobiernos de Nicaragua, la República Dominicana y Paraguay como dictatoriales, marcando la primera vez que el Departamento de Estado señala a estos regímenes por sus nombres propios. El artículo afirma que esta clasificación obliga al gobierno de Washington a actuar con extrema cautela en sus relaciones con los regímenes de Somoza, Trujillo y Stroessner. Asimismo, exhorta a los embajadores estadounidenses acreditados ante estas tres naciones a mantener tacto en sus tratos, advirtiendo que la cordialidad excesiva crea la falsa impresión de respaldo estadounidense, lo cual las dictaduras aprovechan políticamente.

records.headline: A news dispatch details United States military missions operating
records.summary_en: A news dispatch details United States military missions operating in 17 Latin American countries, noting that training programs are designed to promote understanding of democratic concepts, notably civilian control over the armed forces. Officials emphasize that current United States policy explicitly rules out military funds for Cuba and the Trujillo dictatorship in the Dominican Republic. The report adds that the White House has appointed leadership to direct intensified efforts toward hemispheric assistance before the text transitions into retail audio advertising.

Las autoridades destacan que la política estadounidense vigente descarta explícitamente fondos militares para Cuba y para la dictadura de Trujillo en la República Dominicana. El informe añade que la Casa Blanca ha designado responsables para orientar los mayores esfuerzos de asistencia hemisférica antes de que el texto pase a publicidad de equipos de sonido.

records.headline: An article recounts the development of the DORSA Jewish refugee
records.summary_en: An article recounts the development of the DORSA Jewish refugee colony established at Sosua in the Dominican Republic. Dr. Rosenberg states that the Dominican Republic authorized all its European consulates to issue immigration visas to Jews fleeing Nazi terror, providing life-saving documents for more than 4,000 souls. Each homesteader received 75 acres of fertile land, a frame two-room dwelling, farm buildings, livestock including 10 cows with additional cows for family members, a horse, a mule, and a loan. The piece describes how the Sosua settlement has flourished into an active community with businesses, food production, a hospital, and colonists contributing to national institutions including the University of Santo Domingo and the Dominican National Symphony Orchestra.
records.summary_es: Un artículo relata el desarrollo de la colonia de refugiados judíos de DORSA establecida en Sosúa, República Dominicana. El doctor Rosenberg afirma que la República Dominicana autorizó a todos sus consulados europeos a emitir visados de inmigración para judíos que huían del terror nazi, otorgando documentos salvadores a más de 4,000 almas. Cada colono recibió 75 acres de tierra fértil, una vivienda de madera de dos habitaciones, edificaciones agrícolas, ganado que incluía 10 vacas más vacas adicionales por familiares, un caballo, una mula y un préstamo. El texto describe cómo el asentamiento de Sosúa ha prosperado hasta convertirse en una comunidad activa con comercios, producción de alimentos, un hospital y miembros que colaboran en instituciones nacionales como la Universidad de Santo Domingo y la Orquesta Sinfónica Nacional Dominicana.

records.headline: A political column argues that growing tension in the Dominican
records.summary_en: A political column argues that growing tension in the Dominican Republic, where the Trujillo dynasty has ruled for some 30 years, intensified after failed invasion and rebellion attempts by Castro were followed by a relentless campaign from influential American newspapers. The writer contends that while the United States government treats Castro with kid gloves, it directs sharp words at friendly dictators such as Trujillo and Somoza in Nicaragua. Utterances by Congressman Charles O. Porter and State Department officials are said to bolster this press effort, even though the author maintains the Dominican dictatorship is far less harsh than those in Cuba or the Soviet Union and provides no military-political base to Communist enemies.
records.summary_es: Una columna política sostiene que la creciente tensión en la República Dominicana, donde la dinastía de Trujillo ha gobernado durante unos 30 años, se intensificó tras los fracasados intentos de invasión y rebelión de Castro, a los que siguió una campaña implacable de influyentes periódicos estadounidenses. records.headline: Dominican security police announced they shot and killed alleged
records.summary_en: Dominican security police announced they shot and killed alleged Colombian terrorist Jairo Alberto Calderon in a gunfight outside the locked door of Archbishop Ricardo Pittini's residence on Thursday night. Police identified Calderon as a former Colombian Army member carrying a package containing bombs and linked him to earlier bombings of a school, the Santa Barbara colonial fort, and the home of Agriculture Secretary Manuel Ramos. After surveillance agents followed Calderon into a crowded church, he fled to the adjacent stairway of the archbishop's residence, fired shots at pursuing agents, and attempted to shoot open the locked door before being killed by return fire.

La policía identificó a Calderón como un exmiembro del ejército colombiano que portaba un paquete con bombas y lo vinculó con atentados previos contra una escuela, el fuerte colonial de Santa Bárbara y la residencia del secretario de Agricultura Manuel Ramos. records.full_text:
Rebels Seize
Army Station
In Venezuela

By ARISTEDES MOLEON

CARACAS, Venezuela (AP) — Rebels seized control of an army regiment’s headquarters at San Cristobal near the Colombian border today in an attempt to set off nationwide revolt against President Romulo Betancourt’s government.

Betancourt ordered soldiers to San Cristobal to quell the uprising, and pledges of support came to him at once from military, political and civilian sources.

The moderate Venezuelan President announced he would use all constitutional powers to crush the rebellion, but would not suspend constitutional guarantees in this oil-rich nation.

The strong military garrison at Caracas announced its support at once for Betancourt’s government.

Leaders of the nation’s three major political parties spoke over a national radio network, appealing to their followers in San Cristobal to vigorously oppose the insurrection.

The rebels seized control of the Simon Bolivar army regiment’s headquarters at San Cristobal.

Gen. Pedro Jose Quevado, commander of the Venezuelan armed forces, urged “my companions in arms to set an example of common sense and maturity” and support the constitutional government.

The head of the Central Workers Organization, Jose Gonzalez Navarro, called for its 1,200,000 members to go on strike. He said this would be a demonstration of opposition to the “criminal” insurrection which, he declared, was counting on the support of the Dominican Republic.

The government had announced last Saturday that it had smashed a plot for an armed invasion of Venezuela from Colombia by officers who were dismissed from the army for their support of former dictator Gen. Marcos Perez Jimenez.

Venezuelan naval craft and air force planes were patrolling the coast today on the lookout for two fishing boats which the minister of defense, General Jose Lopez Henrique, said had sailed from Spain with arms for the plotters.

Betancourt, a moderate with a reputation as a social reformer, has faced a series of minor uprisings, threats and harassments since he took office early in 1959. He was elected a year after the overthrow of Perez Jimenez, now in exile in Florida.

Venezuela, a tropical country, lies on the northern hump of South America facing the Caribbean. It has about six million people, and because of the nation’s rich resources, has the highest per capita income in South America.

records.summary_en: An official rebuttal challenges reports by Mr. Burks regarding the Dominican Republic, rejecting his claim that an early showdown looms between General Trujillo and a “harassed professional class” following a smashed January plot. The writer argues that a class is harassed only if excluded from national life or barred from education and professional practice, which does not reflect Dominican reality. Emphasizing the constitutional separation of Executive, Legislative, and Judicial powers, the text points out that the judiciary is staffed entirely by professionals, noting that the Era of Trujillo enacted laws making a law degree mandatory for examining magistrates, justices of the peace, and district attorneys.

records.headline: An editorial discusses the decision of the Colombian government
records.summary_en: An editorial discusses the decision of the Colombian government to break diplomatic relations with the Dominican Republic and present a formal denunciation to the Organization of American States over alleged violations of international non-intervention agreements. Colombia asserts that the Dominican chancellery issued diplomatic passports under false names and nationalities to conspirators plotting a rebellion against Venezuela, thereby deceiving the Colombian Embassy into granting visas used to transit Colombian territory. The piece notes that the Inter-American Peace Committee and the OAS face an extraordinarily delicate situation, warning that the Dominican dictatorship under the Santo Domingo regime confronts its gravest international crisis given the continental prestige of Colombian President Alberto Lleras Camargo.
records.summary_es: Un editorial analiza la decisión del gobierno de Colombia de romper relaciones diplomáticas con la República Dominicana y presentar una denuncia formal ante la Organización de los Estados Americanos por supuestas violaciones a los acuerdos internacionales de no intervención. Colombia afirma que la cancillería dominicana emitió pasaportes diplomáticos con nombres y nacionalidades falsas a conspiradores que planeaban una rebelión contra Venezuela, abusando de la buena fe de la embajada colombiana que otorgó visados usados para cruzar territorio colombiano. El artículo advierte que la Comisión Interamericana de Paz y la OEA enfrentan una situación extraordinariamente delicada, señalando que la dictadura dominicana bajo el régimen de Santo Domingo afronta su más grave crisis internacional dado el prestigio continental del presidente colombiano Alberto Lleras Camargo.

records.headline: A commentary piece warns of impending trouble in the Caribbean
records.summary_en: A commentary piece warns of impending trouble in the Caribbean, turning from unrest in Cuba to the Dominican Republic under Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, whom it characterizes as an old exploiter of human rights. The writer suggests that the central question is not when Trujillo will be killed or driven from the Dominican Republic, but who his successor will be. The article asks whether Trujillo's eventual successor will be pro-American or pro-Russian before the column shifts to local lodge announcements.

El autor sugiere que la interrogante principal no es cuándo Trujillo será asesinado o expulsado de la República Dominicana, sino quién será su sucesor. La nota cuestiona si el eventual sucesor de Trujillo será proestadounidense o prorruso antes de que la columna dé paso a avisos de una logia local.

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch reports that Jose Almoina Mateos
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch reports that Jose Almoina Mateos, 57, who claimed to have served as a secretary to Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, was shot on Wednesday in Mexico City. Almoina accused gunmen hired by the Dominican Republic's dictator of carrying out the attack, stating that a car struck him on his way to work before a gunman emerged and fired five bullets into him. The gunmen fled the scene in the vehicle, leaving Almoina hospitalized in critical condition.

Los pistoleros huyeron del lugar en el vehículo, dejando a Almoina hospitalizado en estado crítico.

records.headline: The United States Ambassador to the Dominican Republic, Mr. Farland
records.summary_en: The United States Ambassador to the Dominican Republic, Mr. Farland, has been recalled to Washington for consultations over strained relations with the Caribbean nation. State Department discussions will focus on the Dominican Republic's expulsion of American Embassy press officer Carl E. Davis, who was accused of providing information hostile to the dictatorship of Rafael Trujillo to a British newsman. Mr. Farland, who had participated in similar talks in Washington two months earlier, is scheduled to arrive tomorrow, and the State Department indicated it was assumed he would return to his post after the consultations.

records.headline: An editorial commends United States diplomat Carl E. Davis
records.summary_en: An editorial commends United States diplomat Carl E. Davis, Director of the United States Information Agency attached to the Embassy in Ciudad Trujillo, following his expulsion by the Dominican government for reportedly providing information about the regime to a British journalist. The piece argues that the United States has a moral obligation to support democratic institutions and that its diplomats must never conceal dictatorships, asserting that Davis performed his duty by speaking the truth in a manner so discreet that the regime could not substantiate charges of slander. The State Department is praised for describing Davis's expulsion as a restriction of freedom of information, with the editorial urging Washington to stand firmly against all totalitarianism in the Americas.

El texto sostiene que los Estados Unidos tienen la obligación moral de respaldar las instituciones democráticas y que sus diplomáticos no deben encubrir dictaduras, afirmando que Davis cumplió con su deber de decir la verdad de una manera tan discreta que el régimen no pudo sustentar el cargo de calumnia. Asimismo, respalda que el Departamento de Estado haya calificado la expulsión de Davis como una restricción a la libertad de información, exhortando a Washington a mantenerse firme frente a todo totalitarismo en las Américas.

records.summary_en: Senator Wayne Morse of Oregon declared that foreign aid is one of the policy areas where he and Senator Jack Kennedy differ radically. Morse stated that he had sponsored legislation to terminate United States assistance to fascist dictatorships such as Generalissimo Trujillo in the Dominican Republic, but that Kennedy voted against the measure. Morse also criticized summit meetings, asserting that major international problems should instead be resolved through the United Nations.
records.summary_es: El senador Wayne Morse de Oregón declaró que la ayuda exterior es una de las áreas políticas en las que él y el senador Jack Kennedy difieren radicalmente. Morse afirmó que había promovido legislación para suspender la asistencia de los Estados Unidos a dictaduras fascistas como la del generalísimo Trujillo en la República Dominicana, pero que Kennedy votó en contra de la medida. Morse también criticó las reuniones en la cumbre, sosteniendo que los grandes asuntos internacionales deben resolverse a través de las Naciones Unidas.
