records.headline: Witness Mr. Nevins testified that he traveled by plane to Ciudad Trujillo
records.summary_en: Witness Mr. Nevins testified that he traveled by plane to Ciudad Trujillo with Mr. Guterma, Mr. Roach, and others on January 30 and February 1, 1959. On the flight back, Guterma showed him a letter outlining terms of an agreement with Dominican government representative Otto Vega under which $750,000 was to be placed in the Royal Bank of Canada for Mutual in return for news items and features supplied by the Dominican Republic. Nevins stated he refused to participate in the transaction and warned Guterma that he would have to register as a foreign agent, though Guterma denied he was an agent. A jury of six men and six women was selected to hear the trial.
records.summary_es: El testigo señor Nevins declaró que viajó en avión a Ciudad Trujillo con el señor Guterma, el señor Roach y otras personas el 30 de enero y el 1 de febrero de 1959. En el vuelo de regreso, Guterma le mostró una carta que detallaba los términos de un acuerdo con el representante del gobierno dominicano Otto Vega, según el cual debían depositarse $750,000 en el Royal Bank of Canada para Mutual a cambio de noticias y reportajes suministrados por la República Dominicana. Nevins afirmó que se negó a participar en la transacción y advirtió a Guterma que tendría que registrarse como agente extranjero, aunque Guterma negó serlo. Se seleccionó un jurado compuesto por seis hombres y seis mujeres para juzgar el caso.

records.headline: In the Cathedral of Santiago de los Caballeros, an address delivered
records.summary_en: In the Cathedral of Santiago de los Caballeros, an address delivered following a Te Deum, a published discourse, titled “The Question of Church and State in the Dominican Republic,” presents. The speaker recounts being asked by a priest friend to prepare a speech for an invitation extended by the Bishop of Santiago, Monsignor Polanco, to speak in the church away from political platforms. Introducing historical commentary on relations between Church and state, the speaker quotes an 1899 article by Dominican writer Americo Lugo reflecting on the moral and intellectual values of the Dominican people.
records.summary_es: En la Catedral de Santiago de los Caballeros, una alocución pronunciada tras un Te Deum, un discurso publicado, bajo el título “The Question of Church and State in the Dominican Republic”, presenta. El orador relata que un sacerdote amigo le pidió preparar un discurso ante la invitación cursada por el obispo de Santiago, monseñor Polanco, para hablar en el templo al margen de tribunas políticas. Al iniciar sus reflexiones históricas sobre las relaciones entre la Iglesia y el Estado, el orador cita un artículo de 1899 del escritor dominicano Américo Lugo que reflexiona sobre los valores morales e intelectuales del pueblo dominicano.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published an analytical article examining Dominican political history through the writings of Américo Lugo and Francisco J. Peynado during the 1916 crisis. The piece argued that Dominican national instability resulted not only from domestic shortcomings but also from foreign intervention and the restrictive 1907 financial convention imposed by Washington.

El texto sostenía que la inestabilidad nacional dominicana obedecía no solo a deficiencias internas sino también a la intervención extranjera y a la restrictiva convención financiera de 1907 impuesta por Washington.

records.headline: Continuing a historical discourse on the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: Continuing a historical discourse on the Dominican Republic, the speaker asserts that between 1899 and 1916 no government in Santo Domingo achieved power through a peaceful, democratic transfer from its predecessor or fulfilled popular social aspirations. The address claims that the same lack of social accomplishment characterized the eight years of the United States military regime that ruled the country. The speaker further argues that “Hostosian rationalism” and materialism following the fall of Heureaux undermined religious feeling, which he views as the essential unifying influence for moderating Dominican individualism, before introducing visionary paragraphs from a 1900 article by Dr. Henriquez y Carvajal.
records.summary_es: Continuando con un discurso histórico sobre la República Dominicana, el orador afirma que entre 1899 y 1916 ningún gobierno en Santo Domingo alcanzó el poder mediante un traspaso pacífico y democrático ni satisfizo las aspiraciones sociales del pueblo. El discurso sostiene que la misma falta de logros sociales caracterizó a los ocho años de régimen militar de los Estados Unidos que gobernaron el país. El orador argumenta además que el “racionalismo hostosiano” y el materialismo tras la caída de Heureaux socavaron el sentimiento religioso, al que considera la influencia unificadora esencial para moderar el individualismo dominicano, antes de presentar párrafos visionarios de un artículo de 1900 del doctor Henríquez y Carvajal.

records.headline: The speaker reflects on launching a Dominican government program
records.summary_en: The speaker reflects on launching a Dominican government program founded on faith and patience that can be summed up in the word “Construct!” Citing the work “Episcopologio Dominicopolitano” by the late historian Fray Cipriano de Utrera, the address quotes Utrera's assessment of Archbishop Ricardo Pittini of Santo Domingo on the twentieth anniversary of his episcopal consecration. Utrera is quoted asserting that the Dominican Church reached unprecedented splendor due to the Catholic and political genius of Generalissimo Doctor Rafael Leonidas Trujillo Molina, Benefactor of the Nation and Father of the New Nation. The excerpt highlights Trujillo's grant of juridical personality to the Church and his support for religious institutions teaching the poor, staffing hospitals and clinics, and establishing university residences.
records.summary_es: El orador reflexiona sobre el inicio de un programa de gobierno dominicano fundado en la fe y la paciencia que puede resumirse en la palabra “¡Construir!”. Al citar la obra “Episcopologio Dominicopolitano” del ya fallecido historiador fray Cipriano de Utrera, el discurso reproduce la valoración de Utrera sobre el arzobispo Ricardo Pittini de Santo Domingo al cumplirse veinte años de su consagración episcopal. Se cita a Utrera afirmando que la Iglesia dominicana alcanzó un esplendor sin precedentes gracias al genio político y católico del generalísimo doctor Rafael Leónidas Trujillo Molina, Benefactor de la Patria y Padre de la Patria Nueva. El fragmento destaca la concesión de personalidad jurídica a la Iglesia por parte de Trujillo y su apoyo a instituciones religiosas dedicadas a la enseñanza de los pobres, la atención de hospitales y clínicas y la creación de residencias universitarias.

records.headline: Ecuador broke diplomatic relations with the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: Ecuador broke diplomatic relations with the Dominican Republic, according to an announcement made by Foreign Minister Carlos Tobar Zaldumbide to diplomatic representatives of American republics summoned to the ministry. The severance follows a course taken by five other Latin American countries against the Trujillo regime. Previously, Venezuela, Cuba, Colombia, Peru, and Bolivia severed diplomatic relations with the regime.
records.summary_es: Ecuador rompió relaciones diplomáticas con la República Dominicana, según anunció el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores Carlos Tobar Zaldumbide ante representantes diplomáticos de repúblicas americanas convocados al ministerio. La ruptura sigue el curso adoptado por otros cinco países latinoamericanos contra el régimen de Trujillo. Previamente, Venezuela, Cuba, Colombia, Perú y Bolivia rompieron relaciones diplomáticas con el régimen.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that the Pan-American Highway Congress concluded its eighth meeting in Bogotá after selecting Washington as the site for its 1963 conference. Approximately 200 delegates attended the gathering, representing every American republic except Cuba and the Dominican Republic.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el Congreso Panamericano de Carreteras concluyó su octava reunión en Bogotá tras elegir a Washington como sede para su conferencia de 1963. Aproximadamente 200 delegados asistieron al cónclave, en representación de todas las repúblicas americanas con excepción de Cuba y la República Dominicana.

C. The eighth meeting closed yesterday with 200 delegates from all American republics except Cuba and the Dominican Republic present. Bill to Hit Terrorists BUENOS AIRES, Argentina, May 30 (AP).—President Arturo Frondizi and his cabinet are reported considering tough new anti-terrorist legislation that includes the death penalty. Government sources said the legislation, which may be sent to congress today, resulted from pressure by Argentine military leaders charged with stamping out terrorist activities attributed to followers of ex-dictator Juan Peron. The sources said the military chiefs were concerned about the number of terrorist incidents, the latest of which was the bombing last Friday of the home of Gen. Alfredo Lagalaye, chief of the government’s intelligence service. Gen. Lagalaye and his family escaped injury.

records.headline: The United States Information Agency has appointed Malcolm McLean of Duluth
records.summary_en: The United States Information Agency has appointed Malcolm McLean of Duluth, Minnesota, as the new public affairs officer in Ciudad Trujillo to replace Carl E. Davis. Strongman Rafael Trujillo's regime had demanded the ouster of Davis the previous month, alleging that he supplied visiting journalists with derogatory information about the Dominican Republic. The agency defended Davis and transferred him to Panama, while McLean, who served as an information officer in São Paulo, Brazil, for the past two years, is scheduled to depart for the Dominican Republic at the end of the month.
records.summary_es: La Agencia de Información de Estados Unidos ha nombrado a Malcolm McLean de Duluth, Minnesota, como nuevo funcionario de asuntos públicos en Ciudad Trujillo para reemplazar a Carl E. Davis. El régimen del hombre fuerte Rafael Trujillo exigió el mes anterior la expulsión de Davis, alegando que había proporcionado información despectiva sobre la República Dominicana a periodistas visitantes. La agencia defendió a Davis y lo trasladó a Panamá, mientras que McLean, quien se desempeñó como funcionario de información en São Paulo, Brasil, durante los últimos dos años, tiene previsto partir hacia la República Dominicana a finales de mes.

records.headline: Dictator Trujillo of the Dominican Republic has launched a campaign
records.summary_en: Dictator Trujillo of the Dominican Republic has launched a campaign to harass United States Ambassador Joseph Farland. Secret police disguised as Dominican citizens have picketed the embassy in order to embarrass Farland and persuade the State Department to recall him. Farland has consistently opposed Trujillo's policy of terror directed against anyone seeking real democracy in the Dominican Republic.
records.summary_es: El dictador Trujillo de la República Dominicana ha emprendido una campaña para hostigar al embajador de Estados Unidos Joseph Farland. Miembros de la policía secreta disfrazados de ciudadanos dominicanos han realizado piquetes frente a la embajada para poner en aprietos a Farland y persuadir al Departamento de Estado de retirarlo. Farland se ha opuesto sistemáticamente a la política de terror de Trujillo dirigida contra cualquiera que busque una verdadera democracia en la República Dominicana.

records.headline: In a published advertisement responding to statements attributed
records.summary_en: In a published advertisement responding to statements attributed to Mr. Burks, defenders of Generalissimo Trujillo challenge claims concerning opposition to the regime, maintaining that detractors concede there would be no fatherland without him. The text rejects allegations that Dominican clergy made insidious declarations against the government, asserting that during Trujillo's 30 years in power the Catholic Church received 30 million Pesos from the government and Trujillo's own pocket, alongside customs exemptions on imports including automobiles. The advertisement contextualizes this expenditure by noting that the Dominican national budget in 1930 scarcely reached seven million Dollars, while the population totals just under three millions at present.
records.summary_es: En un anuncio publicado en respuesta a afirmaciones atribuidas al señor Burks, defensores del generalísimo Trujillo refutan las declaraciones sobre intentos de deponer el régimen, sosteniendo que sus detractores reconocen que no habría patria sin él. El texto rechaza que el clero dominicano haya emitido declaraciones insidiosas contra el gobierno y afirma que durante los 30 años de Trujillo en el poder, la Iglesia católica recibió 30 millones de pesos del gobierno y del propio bolsillo de Trujillo, además de exenciones aduaneras para importaciones como automóviles. El anuncio contextualiza este desembolso señalando que el presupuesto nacional dominicano en 1930 apenas alcanzaba siete millones de dólares, mientras que la población suma poco menos de tres millones en el momento presente.

records.headline: In the concluding portion of a published declaration, signatories
records.summary_en: In the concluding portion of a published declaration, signatories defend Generalissimo Trujillo's uncompromising anti-Communist stance, asserting that bitter resentment of his personal success has led political enemies to spread the basest of lies. The statement argues that United States citizens who criticize Trujillo and the Dominican Republic fail to recognize that supporting his regime protects the interests of the Free World and advances the democratic cause. Rejecting conspiracy, rebellion, and terrorism in favor of loyal collaboration, the signatories urge the American public to assist Trujillo's democratic nature with dignity and respect for the Dominican people.
records.summary_es: En la sección final de una declaración publicada, los firmantes defienden la intransigente postura anticomunista del generalísimo Trujillo, afirmando que el amargo resentimiento hacia su éxito personal ha llevado a sus enemigos políticos a propagar las más bajas mentiras. El texto sostiene que los ciudadanos de Estados Unidos que critican a Trujillo y a la República Dominicana no comprenden que respaldar su régimen defiende los intereses del Mundo Libre y la causa democrática. Al rechazar las conspiraciones, la rebelión y el terrorismo en favor de una colaboración leal, los firmantes exhortan al público estadounidense a respaldar la naturaleza democrática de Trujillo con dignidad y respeto hacia el pueblo dominicano.

records.headline: United States Senator Smathers, following a two-hour conference
records.summary_en: United States Senator Smathers, following a two-hour conference in the Dominican Republic during a 10-nation Latin American tour, urged General Trujillo to establish democratic procedures so Communist forces would not take power after him. When Trujillo questioned how to structure a transition government, Smathers recommended municipal elections as a practical first step. Trujillo agreed to hold free municipal elections within 18 months and free national elections within two years, requesting election experts to guide the transition. Smathers subsequently arranged for a team from the American Political Science Association to visit the Dominican Republic and prepare recommendations for organizing elections.
records.summary_es: El senador estadounidense Smathers, tras una reunión de dos horas en la República Dominicana durante una gira por 10 países latinoamericanos, instó al general Trujillo a establecer procedimientos democráticos para evitar que fuerzas comunistas tomen el poder después de él. Cuando Trujillo preguntó cómo estructurar un gobierno de transición, Smathers recomendó celebrar elecciones municipales como un primer paso práctico. Trujillo aceptó celebrar elecciones municipales libres en un plazo de 18 meses y elecciones nacionales libres en dos años, solicitando la asistencia de expertos electorales para guiar la transición. Posteriormente, Smathers coordinó con la Asociación Estadounidense de Ciencia Política el envío de un equipo a la República Dominicana para elaborar recomendaciones sobre la organización de las elecciones.

records.headline: A commentary argues that despite its dictatorial nature, the Dominican Republic remains
records.summary_en: A commentary argues that despite its dictatorial nature, the Dominican Republic remains more orderly than many neighboring democracies, with the Trujillo administration firmly committed to barring communism from the Caribbean just as it opposed the Nazis during the last war. The column criticizes United States policy for pairing diplomatic rebukes with propaganda and secret funds channeled to foster Generalissimo Trujillo's overthrow. It warns that eliminating the Trujillo dynasty would create a vacuum likely to be filled by Communist followers modeled after Castro, advancing Soviet and Chinese influence close to American shores.
records.summary_es: Un artículo de opinión sostiene que, a pesar de su carácter dictatorial, la República Dominicana se mantiene más ordenada que muchas democracias vecinas, con la administración de Trujillo firmemente comprometida a frenar el comunismo en el Caribe al igual que se opuso a los nazis durante la última guerra. La columna critica la política estadounidense por acompañar los reproches oficiales con propaganda y fondos secretos canalizados para propiciar el derrocamiento del generalísimo Trujillo. Asimismo, advierte que eliminar la dinastía de Trujillo crearía un vacío que probablemente ocuparían adeptos comunistas del tipo de Castro, favoreciendo la influencia soviética y china cerca de las costas norteamericanas.

records.headline: The Inter-American Peace Committee of the Organization of American States issued
records.summary_en: The Inter-American Peace Committee of the Organization of American States issued a report concluding that violations of human rights exist in the Dominican Republic and predicting that Caribbean tensions will increase while they persist. The committee released its findings on June 8 following a four-month study, with Colombia substituting on the panel for Venezuela, which had filed the original charges against the Trujillo regime. Because the Dominican government refused to allow on-the-spot investigations, the committee based its conclusions on testimonies from Dominican exiles, press accounts, and related documentation.
records.summary_es: La Comisión Interamericana de Paz de la Organización de los Estados Americanos emitió un informe en el que concluye que existen violaciones a los derechos humanos en la República Dominicana y pronostica que las tensiones en el Caribe aumentarán mientras dichas violaciones continúen. La comisión publicó sus conclusiones el 8 de junio tras un estudio de cuatro meses, en el cual Colombia sustituyó en el panel a Venezuela, país que había formulado las denuncias originales contra el régimen de Trujillo. Debido a que el gobierno dominicano se negó a autorizar investigaciones sobre el terreno, la comisión fundamentó sus conclusiones en testimonios de exiliados dominicanos, reseñas de prensa y otros documentos.

records.headline: A crowd estimated by government sources at 200,000 gathered
records.summary_en: A crowd estimated by government sources at 200,000 gathered in Ciudad Trujillo to demonstrate against the Organization of American States for alleged intervention in the internal affairs of the Dominican Republic. Organized by university and secondary students following an OAS subcommittee report alleging human rights violations, the rally was held at the altar of the fatherland and attended by Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo, his brother Hector Trujillo, and the entire cabinet. Student speaker Manuel Antonio Jimenez Rodriguez addressed the gathering, declaring that the OAS accusations completely lacked foundation and stemmed from strong Communist influence in Latin America.
records.summary_es: Una multitud estimada por fuentes gubernamentales en 200.000 personas se congregó en Ciudad Trujillo para manifestarse contra la Organización de los Estados Americanos por una supuesta intervención en los asuntos internos de la República Dominicana. Convocada por estudiantes universitarios y de secundaria tras un informe de una subcomisión de la OEA que denunciaba violaciones de derechos humanos, la manifestación tuvo lugar en el altar de la patria y contó con la presencia del generalísimo Rafael L. Trujillo, su hermano Héctor Trujillo y la totalidad del gabinete. El orador estudiantil Manuel Antonio Jiménez Rodríguez intervino en el acto, asegurando que las acusaciones de la OEA carecían totalmente de fundamento y se derivaban de una marcada influencia comunista en América Latina.

records.summary_en: The San Juan Star reported that, an outspoken critic of Dominican strongman Rafael Trujillo, Bishop Francisco Panal Ramirez is feared to be in danger. El obispo Ramírez se había enfrentado anteriormente al régimen de Trujillo tras denunciar la represión de la libertad en la República Dominicana y equiparar la situación del país con la de la China comunista.

records.headline: Dominican President Hector B. Trujillo ridiculed allegations
records.summary_en: Dominican President Hector B. Trujillo ridiculed allegations from Venezuela claiming that the Dominican Republic engineered the assassination attempt against President Romulo Betancourt. Betancourt had charged in a broadcast that the plot was hatched in the Dominican Republic after surviving an attack in which 110 pounds of dynamite exploded near his vehicle. President Trujillo, brother of Dominican strongman Generalissimo Rafael Leonidas Trujillo, asserted at a news conference that his nation had never interfered in foreign domestic affairs and characterized the assassination attempt as strictly an internal Venezuelan matter.
records.summary_es: El presidente dominicano Héctor B. Trujillo ridiculizó las acusaciones de Venezuela que afirmaban que la República Dominicana planificó el intento de asesinato contra el presidente Rómulo Betancourt. Betancourt había denunciado en una transmisión que el atentado se tramó en la República Dominicana tras sobrevivir a una explosión de 110 libras de dinamita cerca de su vehículo. El presidente Trujillo, hermano del hombre fuerte dominicano el generalísimo Rafael Leónidas Trujillo, aseguró en una conferencia de prensa que su país nunca ha intervenido en asuntos internos extranjeros y describió el atentado como un asunto estrictamente interno de Venezuela.

records.headline: An alert broadcast from Ciudad Trujillo placed Dominican forces
records.summary_en: An alert broadcast from Ciudad Trujillo placed Dominican forces on standby, reporting that authorization to mobilize Dominican militiamen was being sought because a virtual state of war existed. Meanwhile, Venezuelan Foreign Minister Ignacio Luis Arcaya informed American diplomats that Venezuela possessed proof that the explosives used against President Betancourt originated in the Dominican Republic. Venezuelan accounts identified former Venezuelan Navy captain Eduardo Morales Luengo, living in the Dominican Republic after being expelled five months earlier, as the ringleader who acquired the electronic equipment to detonate the dynamite.

Entretanto, el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores venezolano Ignacio Luis Arcaya comunicó a diplomáticos estadounidenses que Venezuela poseía pruebas de que los explosivos utilizados contra el presidente Betancourt procedían de la República Dominicana. records.headline: An account of the Betancourt assassination plot details how
records.summary_en: An account of the Betancourt assassination plot details how a plane was borrowed under the pretext of visiting Eduardo Morales Luengo in the Dominican Republic. Although flights to the Dominican Republic had been prohibited since Venezuela broke relations with the island dictatorship the previous year, the aircraft departed ostensibly for Miami carrying Angel Morales before proceeding to Ciudad Trujillo. The plane remained in the Dominican capital for only a few hours and returned to Venezuela with both Morales brothers and implements to explode the dynamite, landing at a cattle ranch airstrip piloted by Juvenal Zabala.
records.summary_es: Un relato del atentado contra el presidente Betancourt detalla cómo se consiguió un avión prestado con el pretexto de visitar a Eduardo Morales Luengo en la República Dominicana. Pese a que los vuelos hacia la República Dominicana estaban prohibidos desde que Venezuela rompió relaciones con la dictadura insular el año anterior, el avión despegó con destino formal a Miami llevando a Ángel Morales antes de continuar hacia Ciudad Trujillo. La aeronave permaneció en la capital dominicana solo unas pocas horas y regresó a Venezuela con ambos hermanos Morales y los artefactos para detonar la dinamita, aterrizando en la pista de un rancho ganadero al mando del piloto Juvenal Zabala.

records.headline: At an Organization of American States Council session, Venezuela's representative accepted
records.summary_en: At an Organization of American States Council session, Venezuela's representative accepted condolences from nineteen member nations but rejected expressions of sympathy from the Dominican Republic, declaring that the Dominican government only lamented that the assassination attempt against President Betancourt had failed. Dominican Ambassador Virgilio Diaz Ordonez immediately protested the remarks, describing them as part of a cataract of baseless accusations directed from Caracas against the government of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo. Diaz Ordonez quipped that amidst the flood of allegations, he was surprised Caracas had not claimed the pilot in the U-2 incident carried a Dominican diplomatic passport.
records.summary_es: En una sesión del Consejo de la Organización de los Estados Americanos, el representante de Venezuela aceptó las condolencias de diecinueve naciones miembros pero rechazó las expresiones de pesar de la República Dominicana, afirmando que el gobierno dominicano solo lamentaba que el atentado contra el presidente Betancourt no hubiera tenido éxito. El embajador dominicano Virgilio Díaz Ordóñez protestó de inmediato contra tales declaraciones, calificándolas de parte de una catarata de acusaciones infundadas lanzadas desde Caracas contra el régimen del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo. Díaz Ordóñez ironizó diciendo que, ante tantas denuncias, le sorprendía que Caracas no hubiera afirmado que el piloto del incidente del U-2 llevaba un pasaporte diplomático dominicano.

records.headline: A local news note reports on a sailor named Bell serving aboard
records.summary_en: A local news note reports on a sailor named Bell serving aboard a United States Navy dock landing ship tasked with transporting supplies and personnel to military bases. During a recent Caribbean cruise, crew members were granted shore leave in Puerto Rico, Ciudad Trujillo in the Dominican Republic, Charlotte Amalie on Saint Thomas, and Port-au-Prince in neighboring Haiti. Bell contrasts these port visits with restrictive stops in Cuba, where naval personnel were denied shore liberties, alongside earlier deployments to Spain and various ports on the Mediterranean Sea.

records.headline: The 21-nation Council of the Organization of American States debated
records.summary_en: The 21-nation Council of the Organization of American States debated for four hours over a Venezuelan petition to convene a meeting of foreign ministers regarding charges of aggression against the Dominican Republic. Venezuelan Ambassador Marcos Falcon Briceno introduced an intelligence report detailing two flights to Ciudad Trujillo, where conspirators allegedly conferred with General Trujillo and the chief of Dominican intelligence. According to the report, the Dominican intelligence chief offered a device operating by short-wave radio with the explosive power of 60 pounds of TNT, which was detonated in a parked automobile as President Betancourt passed on June 24.
records.summary_es: El Consejo de 21 naciones de la Organización de los Estados Americanos debatió durante cuatro horas una petición venezolana para convocar una reunión de ministros de Relaciones Exteriores sobre los cargos de agresión contra la República Dominicana. El embajador venezolano Marcos Falcón Briceño presentó un informe de inteligencia que detallaba dos vuelos a Ciudad Trujillo, donde los conspiradores presuntamente se entrevistaron con el general Trujillo y el jefe de la inteligencia dominicana. Según el informe, el jefe de inteligencia dominicano facilitó un artefacto accionado por radio de onda corta con la fuerza explosiva de 60 libras de TNT, el cual fue detonado en un automóvil estacionado al paso del presidente Betancourt el 24 de junio.

records.headline: A diplomatic analysis reports that while the United States confronted
records.summary_en: A diplomatic analysis reports that while the United States confronted difficulties with Fidel Castro, Venezuela and the Dominican Republic escalated their longstanding conflict following the failed attempt to assassinate Venezuelan President Romulo Betancourt. Venezuela bitterly accused its arch-adversary of orchestrating the assassination plot. The account notes that the conflict between the Caribbean republics stems from deep-seated hostility between the liberal leadership in Caracas and the tightfisted dictatorship of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo in Ciudad Trujillo.
records.summary_es: Un análisis diplomático señala que, mientras Estados Unidos enfrentaba dificultades con Fidel Castro, Venezuela y la República Dominicana intensificaron su prolongado enfrentamiento tras el fallido atentado contra el presidente venezolano Rómulo Betancourt. Venezuela acusó con amargura a su tradicional adversario de orquestar el complot de magnicidio. La crónica explica que el conflicto entre ambas repúblicas caribeñas tiene su origen en la profunda enemistad entre los dirigentes liberales de Caracas y la férrea dictadura del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo en Ciudad Trujillo.

records.headline: At a special meeting of the 21-nation Organization of American States
records.summary_en: At a special meeting of the 21-nation Organization of American States Council, Venezuelan Ambassador Marcus Falcon Briceno accused the Dominican government of Rafael Trujillo of aggression culminating in the June 24 assassination attempt against President Romulo Betancourt, calling for a foreign ministers meeting under the Rio pact. Dominican Ambassador Virgilio Diaz Ordonez emphatically rejected the charges, countering that Venezuela, Cuba, and Colombia had formed a conspiracy against his country and claiming that Venezuelan pressure caused Colombia to break diplomatic relations with the Trujillo regime. Acting Chairman Celeo Davila of Honduras characterized the charges as having grave hemisphere-wide implications and urged an impartial investigation, after which the council adjourned until Friday to allow delegates to consult their governments.
records.summary_es: En una sesión extraordinaria del Consejo de la Organización de los Estados Americanos, integrado por 21 naciones, el embajador venezolano Marcus Falcón Briceño acusó al gobierno dominicano de Rafael Trujillo de actos de agresión que culminaron en el atentado del 24 de junio contra el presidente Rómulo Betancourt, solicitando una reunión de ministros de Relaciones Exteriores bajo el Tratado de Río. El embajador dominicano Virgilio Díaz Ordóñez rechazó enfáticamente las acusaciones, argumentando que Venezuela, Cuba y Colombia se habían unido en una conspiración contra su país y afirmando que la presión venezolana provocó que Colombia rompiera relaciones diplomáticas con el régimen de Trujillo. El presidente interino Celeo Dávila, de Honduras, advirtió sobre las graves implicaciones continentales de las denuncias e instó a realizar una investigación imparcial, tras lo cual el consejo suspendió la sesión hasta el viernes para permitir que los delegados consulten a sus respectivos gobiernos.

records.headline: A study panel invited by the Dominican Republic's Secretariat of State
records.summary_en: A study panel invited by the Dominican Republic's Secretariat of State for Foreign Relations and the University of Santo Domingo issues a declaration rejecting a report by the Inter-American Peace Committee. The panel charges that the committee condemned the Dominican Republic using secret evidence that was never subjected to debate or examination by Dominican authorities, denying the nation its right of defense. The declaration further contends that the committee exceeded its statutory powers and departed from inter-American instruments, including assignments entrusted to it by the 1959 Meeting of Consultation of Ministers of Foreign Relations held in Santiago, Chili. Signatories identified in the text include Licentiate Arturo Despradel, a deputy in the Dominican National Congress, and Dr. Geoffrey Hornsey of the University of Leeds.
records.summary_es: Un panel de estudio invitado por la Secretaría de Estado de Relaciones Exteriores de la República Dominicana y la Universidad de Santo Domingo emite una declaración que rechaza un informe de la Comisión Interamericana de Paz. El panel denuncia que la comisión condenó a la República Dominicana utilizando pruebas secretas que nunca fueron sometidas a debate ni a examen por parte de las autoridades dominicanas, negándole a la nación su derecho a la defensa. La declaración sostiene además que la comisión excedió sus facultades estatutarias y se apartó de los instrumentos interamericanos, incluidas las tareas que le encomendó la Reunión de Consulta de Ministros de Relaciones Exteriores celebrada en Santiago de Chile en 1959. Entre los firmantes identificados en el texto figuran el licenciado Arturo Despradel, diputado del Congreso Nacional dominicano, y el Dr. Geoffrey Hornsey de la Universidad de Leeds.

records.full_text:
Intervention in Any Form is OUT

An International Committee's Report to the Dominican Republic's Secretary of State for Foreign Relations, and to the University of Santo Domingo, in which the actions of the Organization of American States' Inter-American Peace Committee are analyzed . . . leading to the conclusion that there is a trend to disregard any documented evidence concerning invasion of Dominican sovereign territory and intervention in the Dominican Republic's internal affairs.

The members of the Study Panel who have been invited by the Secretariat of State for Foreign Relations of the Dominican Republic and by the University of Santo Domingo to give an opinion on certain juridical matters of an international nature which are of concern to the Dominican Republic, analyzed, firstly, the following questions:

a) Considered in the light of the Inter-American Treaty of Reciprocal Assistance and of precedents in the application of that Treaty, was the request submitted by the Government of the Dominican Republic to the Council of the Organization of American States on July 2, 1959, made upon sound grounds?

b) If the answer is in the affirmative, was it or was it not warranted that the Council of the Organization appoint an investigating committee to ascertain the facts alleged by the Dominican Government for the Inter-American Treaty of Reciprocal Assistance to be applied?

c) In the light of the facts and the circumstances adduced by the Dominican Government in its request of July 2, 1959, to the Council of the Organization of American States, does there exist any cause of action for international responsibility under the terms of the 1928 Havana Convention on the Duties and Rights of States in the event of Civil Strife, or in keeping with general legal principles or those of international common law?

The Study Panel was able to examine material evidence such as the documents taken from members of the revolutionary expeditions which invaded the Dominican Republic in the month of June, 1959, as well as photographs made during the embarkation of the expeditions' members and the testimony of captives taken prisoners by the Dominican Government in the military operations staged upon Dominican territory and to whom the Dominican Government has subsequently granted pardon. Included in the testimony given before the Study Panel there is that of Delio Gomez Ochoa, a former Major in the Cuban Revolutionary Army, and that of Poncio Rafael Pou Saleta and Francisco Medardo German, both Dominicans. Statements were also made before the Study Panel by the Dominican Republic's Secretary of State for Justice, Licenciate Mario Abreu Penzo, and by the Republic's Attorney General, Licenciate Luis E. Suero. As a result of its examination of that testimony and material evidence as well as of the legal texts and precedents applicable in the matter, the Study Panel expresses the opinion hereinafter set forth.

1. That from the facts upon which the Government of the Dominican Republic based the request it submitted to the Council of the Organization of American States on July 2, 1959, it is clear that the invasions of Dominican territory on June 14 and June 20, 1959, by armed bands from abroad were with the aim of starting and fomenting civil strife in the Dominican Republic, and were sufficiently grave, according to the Inter-American Treaty of Reciprocal Assistance, as to warrant that request upon the basis of Articles 6 and 12 of said instrument as well as upon those cases in which, after due investigation of the alleged facts, the Rio Treaty of 1947 had been applied. Among these precedents, the Study Panel bore in mind not only those set forth in the document of the Pan American Union entitled Applications of the Inter-American Treaty of Reciprocal Assistance (1948-1955) but also the other cases immediately preceding the Dominican request of July 2, 1959, and that are part and parcel of the international situation which caused the Fifth Meeting of Consultation of Foreign Ministers in Santiago, Chile, to be held.

2. It was likewise warranted that, in view of the facts alleged by the Dominican Government and bearing in mind precedents in keeping with the application of the Inter-American Treaty of Reciprocal Assistance, the Council of the Organization of American States appoint an investigating committee to ascertain the facts alleged by the Government of the Dominican Republic in support of its request, in order to determine whether that Treaty should be applied.

3. That from the careful study and confirmation that they have made of the facts denounced by the Government of the Dominican Republic in its request of July 2, 1959 to the Council of the Organization of American States, it develops that there do exist circumstances upon which to establish a cause of action for international responsibility, based upon either violation of the Havana Convention of 1928 on the Duties and Rights of States in the event of Civil Strife or upon universally recognized general principles of international law, such as those established under the Three Rules of Washington adopted in 1871.

The following question was considered by the Study Panel: "To give its opinion as to the Report of June 6, 1960 by the Inter-American Peace Committee, in the light of the observations of the Dominican Government on this document, dated June 20, 1960, and in the light of Resolution IV of the fifth meeting of Consultation of American Foreign Ministers held in Santiago, Chile, as well as of the Statutes of the Inter-American Peace Committee currently in force, and of the Charter of the Organization of American States."

The Study Panel has analyzed carefully the above mentioned Report of the Inter-American Peace Committee as well as all the other inter-American instruments which determine the scope of the powers of that body. It also has examined the complete record of the Committee's action and numerous aids for an appreciation of facts and circumstances which in a general manner contribute to the creation of those international tensions obtaining in the relations of countries in the Caribbean area. As a result of the above mentioned study, the Panel sets forth the following opinion.

Resolution 14 which was voted at the Second Meeting of Foreign Ministers held in Havana in 1940, in its only WHEREAS clearly defined the aim of that Resolution by giving as the reasons for it that the solution of the differences existing between some American States is imperative in order to attain greater unity of the Continent.

Based upon this, the Resolution ordained the following: the establishment in the Americas of a committee that would see to it permanently that those States between whom there exist or arise any conflict, of whatever nature it might be, solve said conflict as quickly as possible, and that the committee suggest for that purpose, without prejudice to the manner that might be chosen by the parties or those methods chosen by them, methods and proposals leading to such a solution.

The Inter-American Peace Committee has been functioning as an investigating committee, as a Commission d'enquete, in its first stage, and has devoted itself to ascertaining the facts; but once those facts have been established, it goes on to report, giving—and this is its principal mission—methods and proposals leading to a solution, or what is the same, to conciliation. Adapting, therefore, the provisions of the Gondra Pact and of the General Inter-American Convention on Conciliation in a sui generis fashion and in a quicker and more expeditious procedure, the Inter-American Peace Committee is capable of rendering invaluable services, if only it does not defeat the ends for which it was created, as it has done in its Report.

In accordance with its own provisions, the field of application of the above mentioned Resolution 14 comprises the following elements:

a) A conflict already existing or arising at a given moment.

b) A conflict of any nature, that is, whether legal or political.

c) Need of an immediate or urgent solution.

d) Steps taken by the Committee to find the solution.

e) The Committee's power to suggest methods and proposals leading to the solution of the conflict or difference.

f) Ability of the parties to choose formulas and methods leading to this same end.

g) Express responsibility of the Committee to permanently endeavor to find a solution to the conflict.

With respect to this it is interesting to note that the Statutes currently in force emphasize the separation of the functions of the Inter-American Peace Committee. In the first place, it will be noted that Article 1 of the Statutes introduces an element in the basic definition of the Committee which does not appear in Resolution 14 of the Second Meeting of Consultation of Foreign Ministers, by virtue of which Resolution this body was created. In fact, while Resolution 14 stipulates that the Committee will permanently endeavor that the States between whom there exists some conflict, etc., the Statutes of the Peace Committee states in Article 1 that the Inter-American Peace Committee will permanently endeavor, "within its powers," that the States between whom there exists some conflict, etc.

Moreover, Article 16 of the Statutes in force of the Committee states that the Committee will offer its services in fulfillment of its mission and in accordance with the nature of its functions.

Within the fundamental aims and the field of application of the powers of the above mentioned Committee, the Fifth Meeting of Consultation of Foreign Ministers, held in Santiago, Chile in 1959, extended the powers of the Committee, without abolishing its basic functions, to the following questions:

a) Consideration of the situation of international tensions in the Caribbean area, in its general and multiple aspects, in the light of the principles and norms which govern the Inter-American system, and of the means to insure observance by the States of the principles of non-intervention and non-aggression.

b) To that end, it empowered the Committee to examine: 1) methods and procedures to prevent any activities coming from abroad and intended to overthrow legally constituted government or to create cases of intervention or aggression contemplated in instruments such as the Convention on the Duties and Rights of States in case of Civil Strife—and its Protocol as well, we add—; 2) the relation between the violations of human rights or lack of exercise of representative democracy, on the one hand, and the political tensions which affect the peace of the Hemisphere, on the other hand.

c) The immediate undertaking of a thorough study of the above mentioned questions.

d) The new powers—paragraph 4—were temporary in nature, extending until the conclusion of the XI Inter-American Conference.

Upon examining the Report of the Inter-American Peace Committee, the members of the Study Panel find that this document does not correspond to the ends and competence of the Committee for the following reasons:

a) It has limited the conflict, that is, the political tensions, to the Dominican Republic, in violation of the broader mission embodied in Resolution IV which ordered the Committee to study the situation of international tensions in the Caribbean area in its general and multiple aspects.

b) In submitting its June 6, 1960 Report, it has acted as a Court of Justice by ascribing responsibilities, leveling charges and pronouncing absolutions. The Committee's purpose, which is to investigate for the purpose of bringing about conciliation and pacification, to contribute with the delicate and complex task which an assignment of this nature regarding sovereign powers entails, has been perverted.

c) In dealing with a case directly connected with the general situation of the political tensions obtaining in the Caribbean area, and in view of the intense subjectivity of that situation, the Committee should have borne in mind that circumstance in giving out its Report, inasmuch as the terms in which it has been conceived lend themselves to producing affects that are contrary to the conciliatory aim that constitutes the Committee's raison d'etre.

d) The Committee has failed to exercise permanent vigilance to bring about the disappearance of the above mentioned tensions, which in this case creates a situation of conflict.

On the other hand, and with reference to the new powers provisionally granted to the Committee, it has exceeded its authority also, inasmuch as: a) it has exercised improperly powers which were expressly denied to the Inter-American Committee on Human Rights when the Council of the Organization of American States discussed the Statutes it had drafted for the latter Committee to function; b) in a marked manner, it has not afforded the methods and procedures recommended in order to forestall subversive activities intended to overthrow the Government of the Dominican Republic, ignoring, inexplicably, the investigations conducted by its own Sub-Committee which visited Ciudad Trujillo for the purpose of investigating the invasions of Constanza, Maimon and Estero Hondo; c) it abstained from pointing to the other countries involved in the causes of the tension in the Caribbean area, to condemn only the Dominican Republic, thereby overreaching its authority, as it made a singular condemnation instead of a generalized pronouncement in pursuit of conciliation.

In addition to the foregoing, the members of the Study Panel regard as a substantive objection to the Report of the Inter-American Peace Committee—and, at that, one having a general character—the unwarranted use that body made of secret evidence that was not subjected either to debate or to examination by the Dominican Republic, dropping the full weight of its accusation upon the latter, with an obvious disregard for the right of defense and the judicial guarantee that should have been the rule in said action wherein the Dominican Republic has been condemned without knowledge and without being afforded an opportunity to challenge evidence with which it still remains unacquainted.

For all these reasons, the members of the Study Panel invited by the Dominican Republic's Secretariat of State for Foreign Relations and by the University of Santo Domingo

DECLARE:

That the Report presented by the Inter-American Peace Committee, which is related to the Dominican Republic's situation which has been studied, deviated from the prior record of application of the America instruments which have been approved in inter-American assemblies, meetings and conferences, inasmuch as in that Report there is implicit an exceeding of the Committee's statutory powers ever since its origin, and it does not follow from those additional assignments intrusted to it by the Meeting of Consultation of Ministers of Foreign Relations held in Santiago, Chili in 1959, and, finally has promoted a fissure in the basic conceptions of the Organization of American States which stands in urgent need of a permanent and integral cohesion among the peoples and governments comprising this regional community.

1. International policy in the Americas is grounded upon two abiding basic concepts: one is political in nature and consolidated by the practice of regionalism, and it is marked by integral solidarity; the other is eminently juridical in nature and hallowed by the American republics—that of non-intervention. Integral solidarity, which covers the entire range of the progress of peoples, has moved forward amid obstacles that were not unforseeable in its development. Non-intervention, which stems from an evolutionary process with which the American continent is well acquainted, defines historically the unchanging policy of the American republics. From these concepts which the peoples of the Americas have defined, subscribed and ratified in meetings and international American conferences and which identify the nations of this hemisphere, there stem consistently renewed affirmations proclaiming the recognition of independence, sovereignty and the juridical equality of states in the establishment of the principle of non-intervention.

2. That independence which entails a full awareness in making free pronouncements and the organic structure of nations allowing its exercise against all arbitrary acts by either their own or alien forces, whether domestic or foreign, inasmuch as that state enjoying it is its own master and the one responsible for its own destiny, is a trend that expresses itself unhesitantly.

3. Sovereignty, which is grounded in complete internal autonomy and becomes manifest in unqualified external independence, is assured in the international relations of the peoples of this Continent not by a policy of force, but instead by that juridical harmony that is generated by the rule of law which makes the strong bend before the weak and exalts those principles that go to make the abiding foundations of that rule of law.

4. The juridical equality hallowed in the fundamental rights and duties of states defined, subscribed and ratified in instruments that are in force; unaltered by the contingencies in the international life of the Americas, and whose foremost synthesis is to be found in the Charter of the Organization of American States — presupposes the same powers and capabilities to develop their existence as subjects of international law. There is no admitting differences that are offensive to the honor of democratically organized peoples, nor those that may diminish the full realization of basic equality in the practice and exercise of their activities, either individually or collectively.

5. The principle of non-intervention which has been attained through painful and unforgotten stages of American history and marked devotion to the rule of law, and to which the American peoples have dedicated no less a thing than a policy informed by the loftiest civilizing and progressive spirit would seem to be in jeopardy owing to a backsliding that no one would have thought possible among the countries of this hemisphere, particularly in the light of the history of sovereignty in the Americas, which arose amid the relentless struggle for the conquest of nationality.

THEREFORE, and having in view the solidarity of the American nations that are joined in the Organization of American States,

We Are of The Opinion That:

a) The independence, sovereignty and juridical equality of the American States which have become a hallowed tradition, should be safeguarded by those regional organizations that already have been created or in future will be created, those that are already operating or have still to become so, and, moreover, should be upheld so as to further the most equitable realization of the fate of the peoples of this Continent.

b) Intervention, whether direct or indirect and whatever its cause, in the domestic or external affairs of States, affected by one or more States or by regional international organizations belonging to either the inter-American system or to the world system, is counter to the immutable principles of NON-INTERVENTION, and any weakening whatsoever of this international rule, be it from excessive individualism on the part of the strong or from pressure exerted by international political organizations, implies a deplorable juridical contradiction that impinges upon the effectiveness of those matters falling exclusively within the realm of sovereignty, and is harmful to any organized cooperation in solidarity.

Licenciate Emilio Portes Gil

Former President of the Republic and former Minister of Foreign Affairs of the United States of Mexico.

Professor Marcel Roussin

Director of the Inter-American Institute of the University of Ottawa, Canada.

Licenciate Enrique V. Corominas

Former Chairman of the Organization of American States and former Chairman of the Inter-American Peace Committee.

Dr. Geoffrey Hornsey

Trujillo Near Flight Recently, U. S. Hears

By EARL H. VOSS

Star Staff Writer

The Dominican Republic's Dictator, Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, has been on the verge of flight several times in the last two months, according to information reaching officials here.

His plan, it is said, was to take off in the manner of Gen. Batista in Cuba on New Year's Day, 1959.

Gen. Trujillo is reported to feel that he is getting nowhere in the Dominican Republic against mounting opposition and is running the risk of being forcibly liquidated. But he is said to figure that he could leave now with enough resources to live comfortably in exile.

Fear Worse Problem

There would be no tears shed in the State Department over Gen. Trujillo's departure. But the vacuum that would be left in the Dominican Republic might present a worse problem than the present one, officials here feel.

The Fidel Castro regime in Cuba might try to move some of its Dominican associates into high Dominican government positions, it is feared.

The United States Government is not pushing Trujillo to leave, officials here say, partly because they do not see any alternative to head a government in the Dominican Republic. Dangers of conflict, civil as well as international, would be great in the resulting vacuum.

Other Latin American nations, however—prominent among them Venezuela, whose President has charged the Trujillo regime paid assassins to try to kill him—are eager to see Gen. Trujillo leave, no matter what the consequences.

First Problem of OAS

The Organization of American States met here Monday to consider Peru's call for a Latin American foreign ministers' meeting. Most of them reportedly see Gen. Trujillo as the first problem to be dealt with in Latin America, not the United States' problems with the Castro regime in Cuba.

The Latin American Foreign Ministers' Conference probably will be held in early August, officials here said. Washington is prominent among the sites under consideration.

Gen. Trujillo was elected President of the Dominican Republic in 1930. Although he permits no freedom of press or speech or political opposition, his government supports the free world.

Under his regime, modern housing has been built for workers, schools have been erected and the economy, which formerly had depended entire-cumulated record of at least diversified.

records.headline: An editorial from El Caribe of Ciudad Trujillo, dated July 7
records.summary_en: An editorial from El Caribe of Ciudad Trujillo, dated July 7, 1960, is published as an advertisement translated for the people of the United States. The text denounces the Council of the Organization of American States for convening to hear Venezuelan accusations concerning alleged Dominican participation in the assassination attempt against President Betancourt. Characterizing Venezuela's charges as hasty slander, senseless verbosity, and an hysterical repetition of publicized claims without a single item of proof, the editorial accuses the OAS Council of bias and arbitrariness for failing to reject what it describes as a pack of lies.
records.summary_es: Un editorial de El Caribe de Ciudad Trujillo, con fecha del 7 de julio de 1960, se publica como un anuncio traducido para el público de los Estados Unidos. El texto denuncia al Consejo de la Organización de los Estados Americanos por reunirse para escuchar las acusaciones venezolanas relativas a la supuesta participación dominicana en el atentado contra el presidente Betancourt. Al calificar los cargos de Venezuela como calumnias precipitadas, palabrería sin sentido y una repetición histérica de afirmaciones divulgadas sin una sola prueba, el editorial acusa al Consejo de la OEA de parcialidad y arbitrariedad por no rechazar lo que describe como un cúmulo de mentiras.

records.headline: A commentary in the Evening star argues that efforts to oust
records.summary_en: A commentary in the Evening star argues that efforts to oust Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo without considering who would replace him risk creating a political vacuum that would play into the hands of international communism. While acknowledging that Trujillo is unquestionably a dictator and that freedoms such as speech are curtailed in the Dominican Republic, the article maintains that the United States cannot afford to give him the cold shoulder in the current global climate because he and his government firmly oppose communism. The author notes that invasions from neighboring countries where communism had infiltrated failed to provoke indignation from the U.S. government, whereas the assassination attempt against Venezuelan President Romulo Betancourt prompted an immediate OAS investigation and the prospect of economic sanctions against the Dominican Republic.
records.summary_es: Un comentario en el Evening star sostiene que los intentos de derrocar al generalísimo Rafael Trujillo sin considerar quién lo reemplazaría corren el riesgo de generar un vacío político que favorecería al comunismo internacional. Aunque reconoce que Trujillo es sin duda un dictador y que libertades como la de expresión se encuentran restringidas en la República Dominicana, el artículo afirma que los Estados Unidos no pueden permitirse desairarlo en el actual clima mundial debido a su firme oposición al comunismo. El autor señala que las invasiones procedentes de países vecinos donde se había infiltrado el comunismo no despertaron la indignación del gobierno estadounidense, mientras que el atentado contra el presidente venezolano Romulo Betancourt provocó una investigación inmediata de la OEA y la probabilidad de sanciones económicas contra la República Dominicana.

records.full_text:
DECLARATIONS MADE BY FORMER PRESIDENT OF MEXICO EMILIO PORTES GIL

I HAVE just returned from Santo Domingo where I had been invited by the University and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to become a member of a study Committee to which would be submitted a questionnaire regarding international politics.

The Committee was composed of Professor Marcel Roussin, Director of the Inter-American Institute of the University of Ottawa, Dr. Enrique Corominas, a well-known jurist and former president of the Peace Committee of the Organization of American States, Dr. Geoffrey Hornsey, Dean of the Faculty of Law of Leeds University, Great Britain and Attorney Genaro V. Vasquez, former Minister of the Supreme Court and former Secretary of Labor for Mexico. The Committee completed its task in ten days, having consulted every Statute, Treaty, Juridical Antecedent and Jurisprudence connected with the question.

After carrying out a careful analysis we came to the conclusions which I now have pleasure in handing to you. Any discussion or study in which five lawyers are taking part, is very difficult, but the matter was so clear and concise that right from the first moment, we were in complete agreement on the respective points, that is, two points, without expressing any sort of opinion whatever as to the internal regime of the Dominican Republic, a matter we ignored completely, respecting the doctrine of that great Mexican jurist, Don Genaro Estrada which states that no country has a right to pass judgment on the government of another country since each and every one is entitled to the government of its choice. The report we produced was limited exclusively to Treaties between Nations and the Statutes of the O. A. S.

Diplomats are sometimes indiscreet and in the Dominican Republic, as in the United States, there is the belief that the United States State Department led the maneuver against the Dominican Government, the belief being based on the following conjecture: "I will use the power of the O. A. S. to overthrow Trujillo and, once that precedent has been established, we will use the same power to overthrow Prime Minister Fidel Castro, of Cuba." That means to say, with such a precedent, the organization of the O. A. S. is converting itself into a super state composed of 21 Republics and, if it is dangerous for one country to subvert the institutional order of another, it will undoubtedly be very much more dangerous to use the power of a super state to violate the sovereignty of weaker nations.

What would the United States say if tomorrow, or the day after, a request was presented to the O. A. S. to investigate racial discrimination and the lynching of negroes and, what is still more unjust, the discrimination shown against Mexicans, Puerto Ricans, Cubans and other immigrants and tourists whose skin is dark? Would the United States allow it? Would the O. A. S. super state have the valor and nerve to make such a decision in this connection? I must state that I understand that the President of the O. A. S. Peace Committee who led the maneuver against the Dominican Republic, is a United States delegate who has now resigned. I would also like to cite the declaration made by Don Manuel Tello, the highly erudite Mexican Minister of Foreign Relations: "The Mexican Government on examing the request presented by you, considers that it has before it two grave responsibilities: the first, not to abandon the principle of non-intervention and, the second, not to establish a precedent which might subsequently be invoked to the detriment of other countries in the American Continent." This declaration was made by Foreign Minister Tello on June 5 last, in reply to a petition presented by the Latin American Student Front asking for the breaking off of our diplomatic relations with the Dominican Republic. It would almost appear as if Don Manuel Tello could foresee what was going to happen in connection with the O. A. S. agreement, an agreement that has established a very regrettable precedent by violating the sovereignty of a weaker nation. Furthermore, I am of the opinion that the United States totally lacks justification for what it is doing. To "overthrow Trujillo so as to later overthrow Fidel Castro" is an illusion. Trujillo may fall or he may not, but it will be extremely difficult for Fidel Castro to fall. This man has brought about a deep social revolution which will be extremely difficult to undo in the future, and he has taught Latin America to lose its fear of United States leaders, and I mean, the fear of United States leaders and not of the North American people who are great, well-intentioned and only wishing for peace and coexistence with our Spanish American countries. A peace without human exploitation and without the exaggerated ideas of the great imperialist companies of suffocating, or trying to suffocate the economic freedom of our countries, countries that are ignominiously called under-developed, by extracting raw materials at ridiculous prices and then dumping in order to suffocate free competition. Such actions are in accordance with what former Secretary of State, John Foster Dulles said, when he declared: "The United States are not interested in the friendship of other countries, but they are interested in their investments," through which doctrine the United States has not only lost the sympathy of our poor countries which they unpityingly call under-developed, but also the sympathies of their European allies and of the millions of Asiatics and Africans the United States press call Communists simply because they want to get away from the slavery and colonialism under which they have lived for so many hundreds of years.

To sum up, the Study Committee of which I formed part went to the Dominican Republic to play the part of a Peace Committee and not to serve a regime which we have no right to classify."

Attorney Portes Gil then handed the newspapermen the report issued by the Committee of Jurists to the Dominican Ministry of Foreign Affairs and to the University of Santo Domingo.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published a statement condemning the OAS Peace Committee for infringing on Dominican national sovereignty and violating non-intervention principles. The commentary cited Mexican Foreign Minister Manuel Tello's defense of non-intervention and criticized American racial discrimination, arguing the hemispheric body had overstepped its legitimate authority.

records.full_text:
DECLARATIONS MADE BY FORMER PRESIDENT OF MEXICO EMILIO PORTES GIL

Mexico City, July 7, 1960

I HAVE just returned from Santo Domingo where I had been invited by the University and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to become a member of a study Committee to which would be submitted a questionnaire regarding international politics.

The Committee was composed of Professor Marcel Roussin, Director of the Inter-American Institute of the University of Ottowa, Dr. Enrique Corominas, a well-known jurist and former president of the Peace Committee of the Organization of American States, Dr. Geofrey Hornsey, Dean of the Faculty of Law of Leeds University, Great Britain and Attorney Genaro V. Vasquez, former Minister of the Supreme Court and former Secretary of Labor for Mexico. The Committee completed its task in ten days, having consulted every Statute, Treaty, Juridical Antecedent and Jurisprudence connected with the question.

After carrying out a careful analysis we came to the conclusions which I now have pleasure in handing to you. Any discussion or study in which five lawyers are taking part, is very difficult, but the matter was so clear and concise that right from the first moment, we were in complete agreement on the respective points, that is, two points, without expressing any sort of opinion whatever as to the internal regime of the Dominican Republic, a matter we ignored completely, respecting the doctrine of that great Mexican jurist, Don Jenaro Estrada which states that no country has a right to pass judgment on the government of another country since each and every one is entitled to the government of its choice. The report we produced was limited exclusively to Treaties between Nations and the Statutes of the O. A. S.

Diplomats are sometimes indiscreet and in the Dominican Republic, as in the United States, there is the belief that the United States State Department led the maneuver against the Dominican Government, the belief being based on the following conjecture: "I will use the power of the O. A. S. to overthrow Trujillo and, once that precedent has been established, we will use the same power to overthrow Prime Minister Fidel Castro, of Cuba." That means to say, with such a precedent, the organization of the O. A. S. is converting itself into a super state composed of 21 Republics and, if it is dangerous for one country to subvert the institutional order of another, it will undoubtedly be very much more dangerous to use the power of a super state to violate the sovereignty of weaker nations.

What would the United States say if tomorrow, or the day after, a request was presented to the O. A. S. to investigate racial discrimination and the lynching of negroes and, what is still more unjust, the discrimination shown against Mexicans, Puerto Ricans, Cubans and other immigrants and tourists whose skin is dark? Would the United States allow it? Would the O. A. S. super state have the valor and nerve to make such a decision in this connection? I must state that I understand that the President of the O. A. S. Peace Committee who led the maneuver against the Dominican Republic, is a United States delegate who has now resigned. I would also like to cite the declaration made by Don Manuel Tello, the highly erudite Mexican Minister of Foreign Relations: "The Mexican Government on examing the request presented by you, considers that it has before it two grave responsibilities: the first, not to abandon the principle of non-intervention and, the second, not to establish a precedent which might subsequently be invoked to the detriment of other countries in the American Continent." This declaration was made by Foreign Minister Tello on June 5 last, in reply to a petition presented by the Latin American Student Front asking for the breaking off of our diplomatic relations with the Dominican Republic. It would almost appear as if Don Manuel Tello could foresee what was going to happen in connection with the O. A. S. agreement, an agreement that has established a very regrettable precedent by violating the sovereignty of a weaker nation. Furthermore, I am of the opinion that the United States totally lacks justification for what it is doing. To "overthrow Trujillo so as to later overthrow Fidel Castro" is an illusion. Trujillo may fall or he may not, but it will be extremely difficult for Fidel Castro to fall. This man has brought about a deep social revolution which will be extremely difficult to undo in the future, and he has taught Latin America to lose its fear of United States leaders, and I mean, the fear of United States leaders and not of the North American people who are great, well-intentioned and only wishing for peace and coexistence with our Spanish American countries. A peace without human exploitation and without the exaggerated ideas of the great imperialist companies of suffocating, or trying to suffocate the economic freedom of our countries, countries that are ignominiously called under-developed, by extracting raw materials at ridiculous prices and then dumping in order to suffocate free competition. Such actions are in accordance with what former Secretary of State, John Foster Dulles said, when he declared: "The United States are not interested in the friendship of other countries, but they are interested in their investments," through which doctrine the United States has not only lost the sympathy of our poor countries which they unpityingly call under-developed, but also the sympathies of their European allies and of the millions of Asiatics and Africans the United States press call Communists simply because they want to get away from the slavery and colonialism under which they have lived for so many hundreds of years.

To sum up, the Study Committee of which I formed part went to the Dominican Republic to play the part of a Peace Committee and not to serve a regime which we have no right to classify."

Attorney Portes Gil then handed the newspapermen the report issued by the Committee of Jurists to the Dominican Ministry of Foreign Affairs and to the University of Santo Domingo.

records.headline: Dominican President Generalissimo Hector B. Trujillo Molina issues
records.summary_en: Dominican President Generalissimo Hector B. Trujillo Molina issues a published message calling upon all countrymen and political parties to nominate candidates and participate in elections scheduled for December 15. Citing suggestions from Generalissimo Dr. Rafael Leonidas Trujillo Molina, the message explains that constitutional amendments passed on June 28 made several local offices elective for two-year terms rather than executive appointments. These elective positions include provincial civil governors, the president and members of the Administrative Council of the National District, and municipal aldermen and councilmen.
records.summary_es: El presidente dominicano, generalísimo Héctor B. Trujillo Molina, emite un mensaje publicado convocando a todos sus compatriotas y partidos políticos a postular candidatos y participar en las elecciones previstas para el 15 de diciembre. Citando sugerencias del generalísimo Dr. Rafael Leónidas Trujillo Molina, el mensaje explica que las reformas constitucionales aprobadas el 28 de junio convirtieron varios cargos locales en puestos electivos con mandatos de dos años en lugar de ser designaciones del poder ejecutivo. Estas posiciones electivas abarcan a los gobernadores civiles provinciales, al presidente y miembros del Consejo Administrativo del Distrito Nacional, y a los regidores y consejeros municipales.

records.headline: Amid plans for a foreign ministers' conference to review Venezuelan charges
records.summary_en: Amid plans for a foreign ministers' conference to review Venezuelan charges that Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo took part in the June 24 assassination attempt against President Romulo Betancourt, the Dominican regime suffered a diplomatic and economic setback. The United States Department of Agriculture excluded the Dominican Republic when announcing the reallocation of 617.385 tons of sugar previously assigned to Cuba. Instead, the windfall was distributed among twelve other nations, with Brazil receiving an allotment of a little more than 100,000 tons and non-quota allocations going to countries including El Salvador, Guatemala, the British West Indies, and British Guiana.
records.summary_es: En vísperas de una conferencia de cancilleres para examinar las acusaciones venezolanas de que el gobierno del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo participó en el atentado del 24 de junio contra el presidente Romulo Betancourt, el régimen dominicano sufrió un revés diplomático y económico. El Departamento de Agricultura de los Estados Unidos excluyó a la República Dominicana al anunciar la reasignación de 617.385 toneladas de azúcar originalmente asignadas a Cuba. En cambio, ese beneficio se distribuyó entre otras doce naciones, de las cuales Brasil recibió una asignación de algo más de 100.000 toneladas y otros cupos no tradicionales se otorgaron a países como El Salvador, Guatemala, las Antillas Británicas y la Guayana Británica.

records.headline: In an editorial from El Caribe dated July 8, 1960, translated
records.summary_en: In an editorial from El Caribe dated July 8, 1960, translated and published as a paid advertisement by the Dominican Republic Press Society, Jesus Maria Troncoso analyzes the conflict between the United States and Cuba. Troncoso asserts that the U.S. State Department displayed ignorance of Latin American politics by endorsing Castro's rise under the mistaken assumption that its primary task was to eliminate Batista's dictatorship, giving no thought to what would follow. He criticizes ill-advised officials, including Vice President Nixon, for believing that destroying that regime would cause American nations to pledge allegiance to the United States and forget past imperialist expansionism.
records.summary_es: En un editorial de El Caribe con fecha del 8 de julio de 1960, traducido y publicado como un anuncio pagado por la Sociedad de Prensa de la República Dominicana, Jesús María Troncoso analiza el conflicto entre los Estados Unidos y Cuba. Troncoso afirma que el Departamento de Estado de los Estados Unidos demostró ignorancia sobre la política latinoamericana al respaldar el ascenso de Castro bajo la premisa errónea de que su función principal era eliminar la dictadura de Batista, sin pensar en lo que vendría después. Asimismo, critica a asesores desorientados, entre los que incluye al vicepresidente Nixon, por creer que destruir dicho régimen provocaría que todas las naciones americanas juraran lealtad a los Estados Unidos y olvidaran el expansionismo imperialista del pasado.

records.headline: Miss Linker recounts a visit to Ciudad Trujillo, the capital of the Dominican
records.summary_en: Miss Linker recounts a visit to Ciudad Trujillo, the capital of the Dominican Republic, taken with her college roommate Margaret before starting classes in September. She notes that they stayed near the palace of Trujillo and describes Ciudad Trujillo as a city that is both modern and old. During the trip, she saw what she identified as the New World's oldest cathedral containing the tomb of Christopher Columbus, visited the home of Diego, a former viceroy, and attended gatherings with the diplomatic corps. Linker also visited a large sugar mill, heard the National Symphony Orchestra, and praised the country's scenery, including its brilliant flowers, green mountains, and rocky Caribbean coast.
records.summary_es: La señorita Linker relata una visita a Ciudad Trujillo, la capital de la República Dominicana, realizada junto a su compañera de habitación universitaria Margaret antes de comenzar las clases en septiembre. Señala que se alojaron cerca del palacio de Trujillo y describe a Ciudad Trujillo como una urbe a la vez moderna y antigua. Durante el viaje, conoció la que identificó como la catedral más antigua del Nuevo Mundo, la cual alberga la tumba de Cristóbal Colón, visitó la casa de Diego, un antiguo virrey, y asistió a reuniones con el cuerpo diplomático. Linker también visitó un gran ingenio azucarero, escuchó a la Orquesta Sinfónica Nacional y elogió los paisajes del país, destacando sus flores resplandecientes, verdes montañas y la rocosa costa caribeña.
