records.full_text:
Cooley Says U.S. Violates Sugar Law

By the Associated Press

Chairman Cooley, Democrat of North Carolina, of the House Agriculture Committee, blames the Eisenhower administration for a rise in United States sugar prices.

He declared also that the withholding of a purchase of 291,893 tons of sugar from the Dominican Republic violates the new sugar law and is "in contempt of Congress."

He said in a statement yesterday there are indications "Peru was cut short" in the recent authorization for special purchases.

The Agriculture Department, working with the State Department's approval and guidance, announced recently that purchase of an added amount of sugar from the Dominican Republic had not been authorized "at this time."

Officials said privately that in the case of the Dominican Republic, the United States would have been criticized for "taking the sugar away from the Fidel Castro dictatorship, and giving it to the Dominican dictatorship."

Mr. Cooley did not mention the Dominican Republic in his statement, but told a reporter later "the State Department has no right under the law to play politics with the Sugar Act, and the Dominican Republic is one of our most important and closest sources of sugar. If the administration had followed the law, instead of evading it, the price rise would not have occurred."

Officials said Peru did not get its full share of the July 21 purchase authorizations because it lacked by about 65,000 tons the sugar to meet its normal part of the allocations.

records.headline: The Council of the Organization of American States formally
records.summary_en: The Council of the Organization of American States formally agrees to convene a meeting of American foreign ministers in San Jose, Costa Rica, on August 16. Among the principal items on the agenda, the ministers will consider charges presented by Venezuela alleging that Dictator Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic was behind the late June plot to assassinate President Romulo Betancourt. The conference will also examine the threat of international communism in the hemisphere, a gathering that Cuba's delegate supported in the vote but criticized as a United States maneuver aimed at isolating Fidel Castro's government.
records.summary_es: El Consejo de la Organización de los Estados Americanos acuerda formalmente convocar una reunión de cancilleres del continente en San José, Costa Rica, el 16 de agosto. Entre los puntos principales de la agenda, los ministros examinarán las acusaciones presentadas por Venezuela que señalan que el dictador Rafael Trujillo de la República Dominicana estuvo detrás del complot de finales de junio para asesinar al presidente Romulo Betancourt. La conferencia también abordará la amenaza del comunismo internacional en el hemisferio, un encuentro que el delegado de Cuba respaldó en la votación pero criticó como una maniobra de los Estados Unidos destinada a aislar al gobierno de Fidel Castro.

records.headline: Police in Ciudad Trujillo assert that foreign agents orchestrated
records.summary_en: Police in Ciudad Trujillo assert that foreign agents orchestrated an attempt by twenty-two Dominicans to storm the Mexican Embassy and demand asylum. Police Chief Col. Braulio Alvarez Sanchez stated that the incident was directed and paid for by foreign elements seeking to create an embarrassing situation for Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo's regime while an OAS commission was in the country investigating Venezuelan charges against the government. One participant reportedly told police that he and two others received fifty dollars from a foreigner staying at the Hotel Paz. The intruders smashed the embassy's glass front door and scuffled with Mexican Charge d'Affaires Jose Rojas, who suffered a finger injury, along with his staff and twenty-eight refugees already sheltered inside.
records.summary_es: La policía en Ciudad Trujillo afirma que agentes extranjeros orquestaron un intento de veintidós dominicanos de asaltar la embajada de México para exigir asilo. El jefe de la policía, coronel Braulio Álvarez Sánchez, declaró que el incidente fue dirigido y financiado por elementos extranjeros con el propósito de crear una situación incómoda para el régimen del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo mientras una comisión de la OEA se encontraba en el país investigando las acusaciones venezolanas contra el gobierno. Según se informó, uno de los participantes declaró a la policía que él y otros dos habían recibido cincuenta dólares de un extranjero alojado en el Hotel Paz. Los intrusos rompieron la puerta de vidrio frontal de la embajada y se enfrentaron con el encargado de negocios mexicano, José Rojas, quien sufrió una herida en un dedo, así como con su personal y veintiocho refugiados previamente asilados.

records.headline: Rafael Trujillo only this week announced, he was leaving his office in the National Palace here
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Rafael Trujillo announced his retirement to his country estate and was named head of the Dominican delegation to the United Nations General Assembly. Observers viewed the reshuffle—which included reports that President Héctor Trujillo would take an ambassadorship in Europe—as a maneuver to ease inter-American pressure regarding the assassination attempt against Venezuelan President Rómulo Betancourt.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que Rafael Trujillo anunció su retiro a su hacienda de campo y fue designado jefe de la delegación dominicana ante la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas. records.headline: Dated July 19, 1960, an editorial from El Caribe of Ciudad Trujillo
records.summary_en: Dated July 19, 1960, an editorial from El Caribe of Ciudad Trujillo is published as an advertisement by Editora del Caribe under Director J. A. Osorio Lizarazo. The editorial recalls that twelve years earlier, the Organization of American States came into being through the Bogota Charter on principles of juridical equality, mutual respect, non-intervention, and solidarity rooted in national autonomy. It contends, however, that the enduring spirit of the charter was undermined by shifting political leadership and the emergence of revolutionary regimes inspired by communist ideas that discarded covenants and dismantled inter-American agreements.

records.headline: An editorial in the Evening star examines political shifts in the Dominican
records.summary_en: An editorial in the Evening star examines political shifts in the Dominican Republic, following disclosures that the nation's longtime ruler vacated his national palace offices and that Rafael Jr. was appointed adviser to the GATT mission in Geneva. Observers speculate whether the apparent departure of the ruling family after thirty years in power is genuine or intended to defuse impending inter-American action at the August 16 OAS foreign ministers' meeting in San Jose, Costa Rica, regarding the assassination attempt against Venezuelan President Betancourt. The article notes that an OAS committee had already cited the regime for flagrant human rights violations in early June, while newly installed President Balaguer, described as the first independent leader since the 1930s, has promised free general elections in mid-1962.
records.summary_es: Un editorial del Evening star examina los cambios políticos en la República Dominicana, tras conocerse que el histórico gobernante del país desocupó sus oficinas en el palacio nacional y que Rafael hijo fue nombrado asesor ante la misión del GATT en Ginebra. Los analistas especulan si la aparente salida de la familia gobernante tras treinta años en el poder es real o busca atenuar la inminente acción interamericana en la reunión de cancilleres de la OEA del 16 de agosto en San José de Costa Rica sobre el atentado contra el presidente venezolano Betancourt. El artículo destaca que un comité de la OEA ya había señalado al régimen por violaciones flagrantes a los derechos humanos a principios de junio, mientras que el nuevo mandatario Balaguer, descrito como el primer líder independiente desde la década de 1930, ha prometido elecciones generales libres para mediados de 1962.

records.summary_en: A published statement paid for by the Dominican Republic Press Society of Ciudad Trujillo asserts that efforts to placate Fidel Castro by sacrificing 'us' have backfired. The message observes that Castro is now defended by Russia, which is offering assistance to small American nations in the event of territorial invasion. Warning that regional tensions are escalating, the society declares that unless root causes are addressed impartially and continual abuses halted, the crisis will destroy Pan-American unity and hemispheric solidarity, ultimately leading to a cruel and devastating war.

records.headline: United States Secretary of State Herter expresses hope for hemispheric
records.summary_en: United States Secretary of State Herter expresses hope for hemispheric solidarity during a news conference discussing the upcoming foreign ministers' meeting in San Jose. While addressing the conference agenda, Herter declines to predict what actions the ministers will take regarding the communist threat or Venezuela's complaint alleging that Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo's Dominican regime was behind the June assassination attempt against President Romulo Betancourt. The secretary also comments on United States protests over property confiscations in Cuba and defends the diplomatic reassignment of Assistant Secretary of State Roy R. Rubottom Jr., who is being succeeded by Thomas C. Mann.
records.summary_es: El secretario de Estado de los Estados Unidos, Herter, expresa su esperanza de lograr la solidaridad hemisférica durante una conferencia de prensa en la que analiza la próxima reunión de cancilleres en San José. Al abordar la agenda de la conferencia, Herter se abstiene de pronosticar qué medidas adoptarán los ministros respecto de la amenaza comunista o de la denuncia venezolana que acusa al régimen dominicano del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo de estar detrás del atentado de junio contra el presidente Romulo Betancourt. El secretario también se refiere a las protestas de Estados Unidos por las confiscaciones de bienes en Cuba y defiende el traslado diplomático del subsecretario de Estado Roy R. Rubottom Jr., quien será sucedido por Thomas C. Mann.

records.headline: An editorial in Diario las Americas views the recent governmental
records.summary_en: An editorial in Diario las Americas views the recent governmental changes announced in Ciudad Trujillo as another maneuver by the Trujillo dictatorship designed to project an altered political image ahead of the August 16 foreign ministers' meeting. The editorial notes that the OAS Investigating Commission is scheduled to present evidence at that meeting linking the Dominican regime to the assassination attempt against the president of Venezuela. According to the text, the anticipation of adverse resolutions and punitive sanctions prompted Trujillo to replace his brother in the presidency and announce foreign diplomatic postings for himself and his son, while skeptical Dominicans privately view the shake-up as the same dog with a different collar.
records.summary_es: Un editorial en Diario las Américas califica los recientes cambios gubernamentales anunciados en Ciudad Trujillo como una maniobra más de la dictadura trujillista destinada a proyectar una imagen política distinta de cara a la reunión de cancilleres del 16 de agosto. El editorial señala que la Comisión Investigadora de la OEA presentará en esa conferencia pruebas que vinculan al régimen dominicano con el atentado contra la vida del presidente de Venezuela. Según el texto, la inminencia de resoluciones desfavorables y medidas de castigo motivó la maniobra de Trujillo de sustituir a su hermano en la presidencia y anunciar cargos diplomáticos en el exterior para él y para su hijo, mientras la población dominicana, escéptica, comenta en voz baja que se trata del mismo perro con distinto collar.

records.headline: United States District Judge Emett Choate orders the extradition
records.summary_en: United States District Judge Emett Choate orders the extradition to Mexico City of two Cubans accused of acting as hired assassins sent by Dominican Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo. The court found probable cause to try the men in Mexico for the murder of Jose Almoina Mateos, a former Dominican secretary in Mexico City who had written critical accounts of the Trujillo regime. The extradition decision followed a hearing held in Miami on Thursday.
records.summary_es: El juez de distrito de los Estados Unidos Emett Choate ordena la extradición a la Ciudad de México de dos cubanos acusados de actuar como sicarios enviados por el generalísimo dominicano Rafael Trujillo. El tribunal determinó causa probable para enjuiciar a los individuos en México por el asesinato de José Almoina Mateos, un exsecretario dominicano en la capital mexicana que había escrito textos críticos contra el régimen de Trujillo. La orden de extradición se produjo tras una audiencia celebrada el jueves en Miami.

records.headline: An investigative committee report, presented ahead of the inter
records.summary_en: An investigative committee report, presented ahead of the inter-American foreign ministers' meeting in Costa Rica, details official Dominican involvement in the plot against the Venezuelan government. The committee found that conspirators were welcomed in the Dominican Republic by high army officials, met with Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, and maintained frequent contact with Col. John Abbes Garcia, chief of the Dominican Secret Service. According to the findings, Trujillo, identified as the chief of the armed forces, offered the plotters all necessary assistance to overthrow the Venezuelan regime and urged them to act with speed and decisiveness. Meanwhile, observers remained divided on whether recent Dominican government reshuffles were a ploy to confuse foreign ministers or reflected an actual departure of Trujillo and his relatives into foreign posts.
records.summary_es: El informe de una comisión investigadora, presentado antes de la reunión de cancilleres en Costa Rica, detalla la participación oficial dominicana en el complot contra el gobierno venezolano. La comisión determinó que los conspiradores fueron recibidos en la República Dominicana por altos oficiales del ejército, se reunieron con el generalísimo Rafael Trujillo y mantuvieron contactos frecuentes con el coronel John Abbes García, jefe del servicio secreto dominicano. Según las conclusiones, Trujillo, señalado como jefe de las fuerzas armadas, ofreció a los conjurados toda la ayuda necesaria para derrocar al régimen venezolano y les sugirió actuar con rapidez y decisión. Entretanto, los observadores se mantenían divididos sobre si los recientes cambios en el gobierno dominicano eran una maniobra para confundir a los cancilleres o representaban una salida real de Trujillo y sus familiares hacia cargos en el exterior.

records.summary_en: Western hemisphere foreign ministers meeting in San José, Costa Rica, begin informal talks sponsored by the Organization of American States to seek common ground for dealing with problems posed by the Dominican Republic and Cuba. Eight ministers have arrived ahead of the formal conference opening tomorrow, with more expected, including United States Secretary of State Christian A. Herter. Remarks attributed to Mr. Dillon warn that prevailing hemispheric conditions pose a serious threat to the continued existence of free democratic institutions.
records.summary_es: Los ministros de Relaciones Exteriores del hemisferio occidental reunidos en San José, Costa Rica, inician conversaciones informales bajo el auspicio de la Organización de los Estados Americanos para buscar un terreno común frente a los problemas que plantean la República Dominicana y Cuba. Ocho cancilleres han llegado antes de la apertura formal de la conferencia prevista para mañana, y se espera a más dignatarios, entre ellos el secretario de Estado de los Estados Unidos, Christian A. Herter. Declaraciones atribuidas al señor Dillon advierten que las condiciones prevalecientes en el hemisferio representan una seria amenaza para la subsistencia de las instituciones democráticas libres.

records.headline: A five-nation inter-American investigating committee has submitted
records.summary_en: A five-nation inter-American investigating committee has submitted a report accusing high officials of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo’s Dominican dictatorship of complicity in the June 24 assassination attempt against Venezuelan President Rómulo Betancourt. In response, Venezuelan Foreign Minister Ignacio Luis Arcaya indicated that his country will press for sanctions to isolate the Trujillo regime from other American republics. The dispute between Venezuela and the Dominican Republic is scheduled as the first major subject before the two-part meeting, with Cuban Foreign Minister Roa pledging assistance to Venezuela.
records.summary_es: Una comisión investigadora interamericana de cinco naciones presentó un informe en el que acusa a altos funcionarios de la dictadura dominicana del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo de complicidad en el atentado de asesinato perpetrado el 24 de junio contra el presidente venezolano Rómulo Betancourt. En respuesta, el canciller venezolano Ignacio Luis Arcaya indicó que su país exigirá sanciones destinadas a aislar al régimen de Trujillo de las demás repúblicas americanas. La disputa entre Venezuela y la República Dominicana figura como el primer asunto importante ante la reunión de dos partes, en la cual el canciller cubano Roa prometió ayuda a Venezuela.

records.headline: A sharp split seemed to be developing among other foreign ministers
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that foreign ministers meeting in San José debated Venezuelan demands for Rio Treaty sanctions against the Dominican Republic over the attempted assassination of President Rómulo Betancourt. Dominican Foreign Minister Porfirio Herrera denied complicity and promised exculpatory evidence, while the United States and several South American nations urged caution regarding economic sanctions.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que los ministros de Relaciones Exteriores reunidos en San José debatieron las exigencias venezolanas de sanciones bajo el Tratado de Río contra la República Dominicana por el intento de magnicidio contra el presidente Rómulo Betancourt. El canciller dominicano Porfirio Herrera negó cualquier complicidad y prometió pruebas exculpatorias, mientras que Estados Unidos y varias naciones sudamericanas instaron a la cautela respecto a las sanciones económicas.
records.passage: A sharp split seemed to be developing among other foreign ministers on what to do about the Venezuelan-Dominican dispute, in which Venezuela has charged the regime of Dominican Dictator Raphael Trujillo with masterminding an assassination attempt on Venezuelan President Romulo Betancourt. '47 Sanctions Involved Diplomatic informants said Venezuela had ready a draft Resolution asking to invoke all sanctions in the 1947 Rio Treaty short of armed intervention. The treaty says the ministers, by a two-thirds vote, can suspend diplomatic relations and impose communications bans, but this has never happened. Dominican Foreign Minister Porfirio Herrera denied the Venezuelan charges and said in a news conference late yesterday he had some surprise testimony and proof of his own to submit. records.headline: President Eisenhower urged American foreign ministers meeting
records.summary_en: President Eisenhower urged American foreign ministers meeting in Costa Rica to treat the Cuban and Dominican Republic problems alongside the improvement of living standards as a joint undertaking rather than matters for unilateral United States action. The foreign ministers are studying a complaint from Venezuela charging that the Dominican Republic dictatorship of General Rafael Trujillo masterminded the assassination plot against Venezuelan President Rómulo Betancourt. The conference will also examine United States charges of Communist infiltration in Cuba and Cuban countercharges of American economic aggression.

Los cancilleres estudian una denuncia de Venezuela que acusa a la dictadura de la República Dominicana del general Rafael Trujillo de haber dirigido intelectualmente el plan de atentado contra el presidente venezolano Rómulo Betancourt. La conferencia examinará asimismo las acusaciones de Estados Unidos sobre infiltración comunista en Cuba y las contraacusaciones cubanas de agresión económica estadounidense.

records.headline: Foreign ministers at San José are weighing three approaches
records.summary_en: Foreign ministers at San José are weighing three approaches to Dominican sanctions: immediate unconditional measures, a United States proposal to dispatch an observation committee to ensure free elections before applying sanctions, and a Colombian plan to enact sanctions first and send observers afterward. A compromise under discussion would approve sanctions but suspend them pending free elections in the Caribbean dictatorship ruled for more than 30 years by Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo. Diplomatic sources indicated the compromise would provide Trujillo a six-month grace period to hold elections, with sanctions taking effect if he refuses. Secretary of State Christian A. Herter urged the conference to vote a clear condemnation of Trujillo's regime, while observers noted that sanctions require a two-thirds majority and could lead to a Dominican appeal to the United Nations Security Council.

Una fórmula de compromiso en debate aprobaría las sanciones pero las suspendería a la espera de comicios libres en la dictadura caribeña gobernada durante más de treinta años por el generalísimo Rafael L. Trujillo. Fuentes diplomáticas señalaron que la avenencia otorgaría a Trujillo un plazo de gracia de seis meses para celebrar elecciones, entrando en vigor las sanciones en caso de negativa. El secretario de Estado Christian A. Herter exhortó a la asamblea a votar una condena explícita al régimen de Trujillo, advirtiendo los observadores que las sanciones exigen dos tercios de los votos y podrían provocar un recurso dominicano ante el Consejo de Seguridad de las Naciones Unidas.

records.headline: Following United States Secretary of State Christian A. Herter's call
records.summary_en: Following United States Secretary of State Christian A. Herter's call to establish conditions allowing the Dominican Republic to return to respected membership in the American community and enjoy representative democracy, Cuban Foreign Minister Raúl Roa launched a broad attack against both the Dominican Republic and the United States. Roa argued that if justice is to be done, Generalissimo Trujillo and the United States Government should be sanctioned jointly, asserting that Trujillo was created and sustained for over 30 years by North American imperialism. Roa maintained that it would not be strict justice to condemn Trujillo without also condemning the father of the creature. Secretary Herter replied that he had not anticipated Roa's attack during the Dominican discussions and noted he would address Cuban matters the following week when ministers examine hemispheric Communist threats.

Roa sostuvo que, si ha de hacerse justicia, el generalísimo Trujillo y el gobierno de Estados Unidos deben ser sancionados conjuntamente, afirmando que Trujillo fue creado y sostenido por más de treinta años por el imperialismo norteamericano. Roa afirmó que no habría estricta justicia si se condena a Trujillo sin condenar igualmente al padre de la criatura. El secretario Herter replicó que no esperaba la arremetida de Roa durante los debates sobre el caso dominicano y precisó que abordaría los temas cubanos la semana siguiente, cuando los cancilleres examinen las amenazas comunistas en el hemisferio.

records.headline: An editorial commentary diagnoses Caribbean tensions, stating
records.summary_en: An editorial commentary diagnoses Caribbean tensions, stating that the entire inter-American system is threatened not only by military dictatorships such as Generalissimo Trujillo's in the Dominican Republic, but even more menacingly by the Communist-backed dictatorship of Fidel Castro in Cuba. The article highlights the danger posed by Havana's ties with Moscow and Beijing and its readiness to spread totalitarianism across the Western Hemisphere. Secretary of State Herter and other foreign ministers gathered in San José face an exceedingly difficult task in resolving these crises, though the editorial notes that the Organization of American States' past effectiveness provides reason for hope.
records.summary_es: Un comentario editorial diagnostica las tensiones en el Caribe y manifiesta que la totalidad del sistema interamericano se ve amenazada no solo por dictaduras militares como la del generalísimo Trujillo en la República Dominicana, sino de forma aún más alarmante por la dictadura de Fidel Castro en Cuba, respaldada por el comunismo. El artículo resalta el peligro derivado de los lazos de La Habana con Moscú y Pekín y su disposición a propagar el totalitarismo por el hemisferio occidental. El secretario de Estado Herter y los demás cancilleres congregados en San José enfrentan una labor sumamente compleja para solucionar estas crisis, si bien el editorial señala que la eficacia histórica de la Organización de los Estados Americanos brinda motivos de esperanza.

records.headline: Foreign ministers attending the Organization of American States conference
records.summary_en: Foreign ministers attending the Organization of American States conference in San José agreed today to energetically condemn the Dominican Republic and break diplomatic relations with the Trujillo regime. In a draft resolution requiring approval at a final plenary session late today, the ministers also voted for a partial interruption of economic relations, including an immediate suspension of arms shipments to the Dominican Republic. In a surprise move, the conference bypassed a watered-down United States proposal calling for a special committee to supervise free Dominican elections, referring the matter to a subsequent meeting.
records.summary_es: Los ministros de Relaciones Exteriores congregados en la reunión de la Organización de los Estados Americanos en San José acordaron hoy condenar enérgicamente a la República Dominicana y romper relaciones diplomáticas con el régimen de Trujillo. Mediante un proyecto de resolución que requiere aprobación en una sesión plenaria final prevista para hoy, los cancilleres también votaron la interrupción parcial de las relaciones económicas, incluyendo la suspensión inmediata del suministro de armas a la República Dominicana. En una decisión imprevista, la asamblea desestimó una propuesta suavizada de los Estados Unidos orientada a establecer una comisión especial para supervisar elecciones libres dominicanas, remitiendo el asunto a una sesión posterior.

records.headline: Convening in Costa Rica to address Caribbean crises, foreign ministers
records.summary_en: Convening in Costa Rica to address Caribbean crises, foreign ministers surprised observers by agreeing on firm action regarding the Dominican regime's plot to assassinate President Betancourt of Venezuela. The ministers tentatively voted to energetically condemn the Dominican government, break diplomatic relations, and impose an immediate embargo on arms shipments to the Dominican Republic. A United States proposal for a special committee to supervise free Dominican elections is scheduled for discussion tomorrow. While the ultimate effect of the OAS measures remains unclear, General Trujillo has hinted at stepping down from his 30-year role as absolute dictator and promised to permit free elections.
records.summary_es: Reunidos en Costa Rica para atender las crisis del Caribe, los cancilleres sorprendieron a los observadores al consensuar medidas categóricas frente al atentado planificado por el régimen dominicano contra el presidente venezolano Betancourt. Los ministros votaron de forma preliminar condenar enérgicamente al gobierno dominicano, romper relaciones diplomáticas y aplicar un embargo inmediato a las ventas de armas destinadas a la República Dominicana. Una propuesta de los Estados Unidos para designar una comisión especial que supervise comicios libres en territorio dominicano será examinada mañana. Si bien el efecto definitivo de las medidas de la OEA resulta incierto, el general Trujillo ha sugerido su disposición a retirarse de su condición de dictador absoluto tras treinta años en el poder y ha prometido autorizar elecciones libres.

records.headline: An editorial analyzes the Organization of American States' condemnation of the 30-year
records.summary_en: An editorial analyzes the Organization of American States' condemnation of the 30-year Trujillo regime for its attempt against Venezuelan President Rómulo Betancourt and its flagrant, extensive violations of human rights. The sanctions agreed upon in San José include the severance of diplomatic relations, economic measures, and the establishment of an Inter-American Vigilance Committee to promote the immediate restoration of democratic life in Santo Domingo. The editorial describes this action as a historic precedent offering hope to the peoples of the Americas by delivering a direct threat to the few remaining continental dictatorships that suppress political freedom, murder prisoners under escape pretexts, employ torture, silence the press, and violate habeas corpus.
records.summary_es: Un editorial analiza la condena dictada por la Organización de los Estados Americanos contra el régimen trujillista de treinta años por el atentado contra el presidente venezolano Rómulo Betancourt y sus flagrantes y extendidas violaciones de los derechos humanos. Las sanciones acordadas en San José comprenden la ruptura de relaciones diplomáticas, medidas económicas y la creación de un Comité Interamericano de Vigilancia para fomentar la inmediata restauración de la vida democrática en Santo Domingo. El texto califica esta acción como un precedente histórico que infunde esperanzas a los pueblos de América al significar una amenaza directa contra las escasas dictaduras continentales remanentes que conculcan la libertad política, asesinan cautivos bajo el pretexto de fugas, aplican torturas, amordazan la prensa y vulneran el hábeas corpus.

records.headline: An editorial published in English reviews the verdict of American
records.summary_en: An editorial published in English reviews the verdict of American foreign ministers finding the Dominican dictatorship guilty of participating in the recent attempt against the life of Venezuelan President Rómulo Betancourt and committing flagrant and extensive violations of human rights. Punitive measures adopted against the thirty-year dictatorship include severance of diplomatic relations, economic sanctions, and the creation of an Inter-American Vigilance Commission to promote the immediate restoration of democratic life in Santo Domingo. The commentary highlights this decision as a historic precedent offering hope to American nations by challenging the continent's remaining tyrannies that suppress political liberty, murder prisoners, employ torture, abolish habeas corpus, and expropriate property.
records.summary_es: Un editorial publicado en inglés examina el veredicto de los cancilleres americanos que declaró culpable a la dictadura dominicana por su intervención en el reciente atentado contra la vida del presidente venezolano Rómulo Betancourt y por incurrir en flagrantes y extensas violaciones a los derechos humanos. Las medidas punitivas adoptadas contra el régimen de treinta años abarcan la ruptura de relaciones diplomáticas, sanciones económicas y la creación de una Comisión Interamericana de Vigilancia para promover la inmediata restauración de la vida democrática en Santo Domingo. El comentario resalta esta determinación como un precedente histórico que alienta a las naciones de América al desafiar a las tiranías continentales remanentes que conculcan las libertades políticas, ultiman reclusos, recurren a torturas, eliminan el hábeas corpus y expropian propiedades.

records.headline: Foreign ministers at San José convicted Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo's Dominican regime of aggression
records.summary_en: Foreign ministers at San José convicted Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo's Dominican regime of aggression against Venezuela for supporting a recent plot to assassinate President Rómulo Betancourt and overthrow his government, charges that the Dominican Republic denied. Dominican Foreign Minister Porfirio Herrera Báez refused to comment on the unprecedented hemispheric condemnation and departed the conference, although his exit does not mean formal Dominican withdrawal from automatic OAS membership. In voting with Venezuela, the ministers postponed action on a United States proposal for a special committee to oversee an orderly transition to a new Dominican regime, after Latin American delegates expressed concern that such authority would constitute foreign intervention.
records.summary_es: Los ministros de Relaciones Exteriores en San José condenaron al régimen dominicano del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo por agresión contra Venezuela al patrocinar un reciente complot para asesinar al presidente Rómulo Betancourt y derrocar a su gobierno, acusaciones que la República Dominicana rechazó. El canciller dominicano Porfirio Herrera Báez rehusó hacer declaraciones sobre la inédita condena hemisférica y se retiró de la asamblea, aunque su marcha no supone la renuncia formal dominicana a la membresía automática en la OEA. Al respaldar a Venezuela, los cancilleres postergaron la consideración de una iniciativa de los Estados Unidos orientada a designar una comisión especial que coordinara una transición ordenada hacia un nuevo régimen dominicano, debido a la inquietud de delegados latinoamericanos de que tales facultades implicaran una intervención foránea.

records.summary_en: Speaking before a nearly empty Senate chamber, Senator Ellender voiced scathing criticism of President Eisenhower's request to curb Dominican sugar purchases and urged Senator Eastland to initiate a Senate investigation. Eastland, chairman of the Senate Judiciary Committee and its Internal Security Subcommittee, interrupted to describe General Trujillo as a good friend of the United States. Ellender asserted that not one country in Central or South America has shown the great progress achieved by the Dominican Republic under Trujillo, prompting Eastland to add that Dominicans accomplished these gains without external handouts.

Eastland, quien preside el Comité Judicial del Senado y su Subcomité de Seguridad Interna, intervino para calificar al general Trujillo como un buen amigo de los Estados Unidos. Ellender sostuvo que ningún país de Centroamérica o Sudamérica ha demostrado el gran progreso alcanzado por la República Dominicana bajo el mandato de Trujillo, a lo que Eastland agregó que los dominicanos lograron estos avances sin recurrir a donaciones externas.

records.headline: Undersecretary of State Douglas Dillon appeared before the House Agriculture Committee
records.summary_en: Undersecretary of State Douglas Dillon appeared before the House Agriculture Committee to defend President Eisenhower's proposal to halt Dominican sugar imports, stating the United States should endure short sugar rations if necessary rather than purchase from Fidel Castro or General Trujillo. Dillon labeled Trujillo a tyrant who has tortured and murdered political opponents, adding that the State Department expects a moderate, free government to succeed the dictatorship but declining to name opposition figures because doing so would trigger their immediate execution. Meanwhile on the Senate floor, Senators Ellender and Eastland sharply criticized Eisenhower's call for cutoff legislation, with Ellender declaring he will fight efforts to choke off Dominican imports and expressing the wish that every Latin American nation possessed a strong leader like Trujillo.
records.summary_es: El subsecretario de Estado Douglas Dillon compareció ante el Comité de Agricultura de la Cámara de Representantes para respaldar la iniciativa del presidente Eisenhower de suspender las compras de azúcar dominicana, señalando que Estados Unidos debería soportar un racionamiento azucarero si fuera preciso antes que comprarle a Fidel Castro o al general Trujillo. Dillon calificó a Trujillo de tirano que ha torturado y asesinado a opositores políticos, manifestando que el Departamento de Estado prevé que un gobierno moderado y libre relevará a la dictadura, si bien declinó revelar los nombres de dirigentes de la oposición porque ello causaría su ejecución inmediata. Entretanto en el pleno del Senado, los senadores Ellender y Eastland censuraron severamente la solicitud de Eisenhower; Ellender prometió combatir los intentos de bloquear las importaciones dominicanas y manifestó su deseo de que todas las naciones latinoamericanas contaran con un líder enérgico como Trujillo.

records.headline: In proceedings before the House Agriculture Committee concerning
records.summary_en: In proceedings before the House Agriculture Committee concerning President Eisenhower's request for authority to cut off Dominican sugar purchases, Representatives Cooley and Poage defended General Trujillo and accused the administration of ignoring congressional intent. Cooley charged that the United States is imposing harsher measures against Trujillo, who is free of Communist influence, than against the Communist-oriented Castro regime in Cuba. Undersecretary of State Douglas Dillon disputed the claim, warning that nothing would promote communism across the hemisphere more effectively than United States support for Trujillo. Representative Poage argued that Trujillo is no worse a dictator than those in other nations maintaining diplomatic and economic relations with Washington, while Representative Hoeven gave strong backing to Dillon.
records.summary_es: Durante las sesiones del Comité de Agricultura de la Cámara de Representantes sobre la petición del presidente Eisenhower de facultades para suspender las compras de azúcar dominicana, los legisladores Cooley y Poage salieron en defensa del general Trujillo y acusaron al gobierno de desconocer la voluntad del Congreso. Cooley denunció que Estados Unidos aplica disposiciones más severas contra Trujillo, quien no se encuentra bajo influjo comunista, que contra el régimen castrista procomunista en Cuba. El subsecretario de Estado Douglas Dillon refutó esa acusación, advirtiendo que nada impulsaría tanto el comunismo en el hemisferio como el respaldo estadounidense a Trujillo. El representante Poage sostuvo que Trujillo no es un dictador peor que los de otros países con los que Washington mantiene nexos diplomáticos y económicos, mientras que el representante Hoeven ofreció un firme respaldo a Dillon.

records.summary_en: That it will begin broadcasting daily news feeds from the Soviet agency Tass starting Monday, Radio Caribe announced, an Associated Press dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports. The station operates as the official radio outlet of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo's regime, which had long presented itself as a hemispheric bulwark against Latin American communism. The decision to incorporate Tass reports follows intensifying criticism of the Trujillo dictatorship throughout the Americas and recent votes by inter-American foreign ministers to adopt sanctions.

La determinación de incorporar los despachos de Tass sobreviene tras las crecientes críticas contra el régimen de Trujillo en todo el continente y las recientes votaciones de los cancilleres americanos para acordar sanciones.

records.headline: As Washington moved to cut the Dominican sugar quota, unofficial
records.summary_en: As Washington moved to cut the Dominican sugar quota, unofficial Soviet agents offered barter arrangements to supply Dominican needs in exchange for sugar, even though the Dominican Republic lacks diplomatic ties with Communist nations. Concurrently, Ciudad Trujillo announced that the regime's radio station was negotiating to receive dispatches from the Soviet agency Tass. The commentary notes that while these moves do not signal reconciliation between Fidel Castro and Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, Moscow and Beijing seek to expand anti-American enclaves throughout the hemisphere. The writer observes that inducing Trujillo to turn to Moscow required extraordinary diplomatic pressure at San José, given his longstanding opposition to foreign dictatorships, his admission of Jewish refugees during World War II, and his sustained hostility to international communism.
records.summary_es: Al momento en que Washington se disponía a recortar la cuota azucarera dominicana, agentes oficiosos soviéticos ofrecieron acuerdos de permuta para abastecer las necesidades dominicanas a cambio de azúcar, a pesar de que la República Dominicana carece de nexos diplomáticos con naciones comunistas. De forma simultánea, desde Ciudad Trujillo se anunció que la emisora radial del régimen negociaba la recepción de despachos de la agencia soviética Tass. El comentario señala que, si bien estos pasos no presagian una reconciliación entre Fidel Castro y el generalísimo Rafael Trujillo, Moscú y Pekín aspiran a ampliar las zonas antiamericanas en el continente. El articulista subraya que empujar a Trujillo a recurrir a Moscú requirió una inusitada presión diplomática en San José, dada su histórica oposición a tiranías extranjeras, su acogida de refugiados judíos durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial y su continuada hostilidad hacia el comunismo internacional.

records.headline: An analysis of anti-Castro resistance organizations identifies
records.summary_en: An analysis of anti-Castro resistance organizations identifies the Montecristi Movement, a group established during the Batista regime that derives its name from the Montecristi Manifesto signed by Cuban patriots in the Dominican Republic. Led by Dr. Justo Carrillo, an economist and former bank president, the organization connects seasoned political leaders who opposed Machado and Batista with younger Catholic student and youth figures. The dispatch reports that the broader Cuban public has grown alienated under totalitarian police methods, widely circulating satirical humor directed at Fidel and Raúl Castro.
records.summary_es: Un análisis sobre organizaciones opositoras a Castro identifica al Movimiento Montecristi, agrupación fundada durante el régimen de Batista que toma su nombre del Manifiesto de Montecristi suscrito por patriotas cubanos en la República Dominicana. Encabezada por el doctor Justo Carrillo, economista y expresidente de un banco de desarrollo, la organización vincula a dirigentes políticos veteranos que enfrentaron a Machado y Batista con jóvenes militantes de movimientos estudiantiles y juveniles católicos. El despacho señala que el pueblo cubano en general se muestra desencantado bajo los métodos de control policial y difunde ampliamente chistes satíricos sobre Fidel y Raúl Castro.

records.headline: The executive council of the AFL-CIO reaffirmed its strong condemnation of the Trujillo dictatorship
records.summary_en: The executive council of the AFL-CIO reaffirmed its strong condemnation of the Trujillo dictatorship in the Dominican Republic and called again for sanctions against the country as an unworthy member of the American family of nations. The council urged the Organization of American States meeting in San José to adopt courageous measures to defeat totalitarian threats, including the suspension of the Dominican Republic from the OAS and the severance of diplomatic relations. In addition, the labor body expressed deep concern over Communist domination of the Cuban revolution and proposed substantial, flexible economic assistance programs for Latin America.
records.summary_es: El consejo ejecutivo de la AFL-CIO reiteró su enérgica condena a la dictadura de Trujillo en la República Dominicana y exigió nuevamente la adopción de sanciones contra el país por considerarlo un miembro indigno de la familia de naciones americanas. El consejo instó a la reunión de la Organización de los Estados Americanos en San José a adoptar medidas valientes para derrotar las amenazas totalitarias, incluyendo la suspensión de la República Dominicana de la OEA y la ruptura de relaciones diplomáticas. Asimismo, la central sindical manifestó su profunda preocupación por el dominio comunista sobre la revolución cubana y propuso programas cuantiosos y flexibles de asistencia económica para América Latina.

records.headline: Following diplomatic developments, officials in Washington weigh
records.summary_en: Following diplomatic developments, officials in Washington weigh the fate of a United States missile tracking station located in the Dominican Republic. Authorities indicate they do not know whether the facility's personnel will be withdrawn along with American diplomats. They further speculate that the Trujillo regime might take action to shut down the tracking station.
records.summary_es: Tras los acontecimientos diplomáticos, funcionarios en Washington evalúan el destino de una estación de rastreo de misiles de Estados Unidos ubicada en la República Dominicana. Las autoridades señalan que no saben si el personal de la instalación será retirado junto con los diplomáticos estadounidenses. Además, especulan que el régimen de Trujillo podría tomar medidas para clausurar la estación de rastreo.

records.headline: C Douglas Debe voise, whose firm has extensive sugar interests in the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: The *Atlanta Daily World* reported that sugar executive C. Douglas Debevoise urged Congress to maintain the Dominican sugar quota, warning that economic disruption could allow Communists to replace Rafael Trujillo. Concurrently, the United States prepared to sever diplomatic ties with Ciudad Trujillo pursuant to OAS sanctions, arranging to entrust diplomatic affairs to the British embassy.
records.summary_es: El *Atlanta Daily World* informó que el ejecutivo azucarero C. Douglas Debevoise instó al Congreso a mantener la cuota azucarera dominicana, advirtiendo que los trastornos económicos podrían permitir que los comunistas sustituyeran a Rafael Trujillo. Al mismo tiempo, Estados Unidos se preparaba para romper relaciones diplomáticas con Ciudad Trujillo de conformidad con las sanciones de la OEA, disponiendo encomendar los asuntos diplomáticos a la embajada británica.
records.passage: C. Douglas Debevoise, whose firm has extensive sugar interests in the Dominican Republic, urged Congress to reject President Eisenhower's request that the Caribbean country's sugar quota be reduced. Debevoise said he feared economic chaos would result if the bonus were withdrawn, thus enabling the Communists to take over from dictator Rafael Trujillo. His testimony before the House Agriculture Committee put him at direct odds with Undersecretary of State Douglas Dillon. He said Wednesday that giving the extra sugar to the “inhuman” Trujillo would further Communism in Latin America. Debevoise said he feared eco- S. consumers would be forced to pay higher sugar prices if the quota were reduced Congress raised the Dominican quota last month to make up for a cut in Cuban imports. The United States, meanwhile, was moving toward a break in diplomatic relations with the Trujillo regime as decreed by the foreign ministers of the Organization of American States (OAS) in Costa Rica this week. Several Latin American countries already have complied and the United States will follow suit very soon. But officials said it will not simply walk out of the Caribbean country cold. Important U. S. affairs will be placed in the hands of another government-apparently Britain. This country also probably will leave a handful of consular officials in the Dominican Republic to handle visas, worry about fugitives from U. S. justice and look after American business interests. 5

records.headline: With the closing of the American Embassy in Ciudad Trujillo
records.summary_en: With the closing of the American Embassy in Ciudad Trujillo, about 40 staff members and their families are to be withdrawn from the Dominican Republic. Since the transfer of Ambassador Joseph Farland to Panama, the embassy had operated under Henry Dearborn as Chargé d'Affaires. A career ambassador serving in Luxembourg had been reassigned to Ciudad Trujillo, but will not proceed there in light of developments. The report also notes criticism of the administration for moving to eliminate Dominican sugar sales in the United States.

Un embajador de carrera destinado en Luxemburgo había sido reasignado a Ciudad Trujillo, pero no viajará allí a la luz de los acontecimientos. El informe también señala críticas a la administración por actuar para eliminar las ventas de azúcar dominicano en Estados Unidos.

records.headline: Following Venezuelan accusations of a plot to overthrow its government
records.summary_en: Following Venezuelan accusations of a plot to overthrow its government, which the Dominican Republic denied, the United States broke diplomatic relations at the Costa Rica conference after earlier proposing an election supervisory committee. House Agriculture Committee Chairman Harold D. Cooley strongly criticized the break, calling it crazy to sever ties with a long-friendly regime and warning that a dictatorship worse than Cuba could take power. Officials privately expressed concern over Latin American ties after regional nations watered down an anti-Communist resolution on Cuba. Meanwhile, United States officials expected the remainder of the 20 hemisphere republics to join the 12 that had already broken relations with the Trujillo regime.
records.summary_es: Tras las acusaciones venezolanas de un complot para derrocar a su gobierno, que la República Dominicana negó, Estados Unidos rompió relaciones diplomáticas en la conferencia de Costa Rica luego de haber propuesto antes un comité de supervisión electoral. El presidente del Comité de Agricultura de la Cámara de Representantes, Harold D. Cooley, criticó duramente la ruptura, calificando de locura romper lazos con un régimen amistoso durante años y advirtiendo que una dictadura peor que la de Cuba podría asumir el poder. Los funcionarios expresaron preocupación en privado por los lazos latinoamericanos después de que las naciones de la región suavizaran una resolución anticomunista sobre Cuba. Mientras tanto, funcionarios estadounidenses esperaban que el resto de las 20 repúblicas del hemisferio se unieran a las 12 que ya habían roto relaciones con el régimen de Trujillo.

records.headline: The Dominican Republic delegation staged the second walkout of the two-week
records.summary_en: The Dominican Republic delegation staged the second walkout of the two-week foreign ministers conference, departing on August 20 after ministers found Rafael Trujillo's regime guilty of plotting to assassinate Venezuelan President Betancourt and approved political and economic sanctions. Following a subsequent Cuban walkout, diplomats observed that two dictators—one from the left and one from the right—had departed. Delegates debated the consequences for the 70-year-old inter-American system, with some expecting renewed public faith and others fearing an unhealthy precedent. While the United States pressed for a firm hemispheric stand against Communism, the ministers compromised by omitting direct mention of Cuba in the Declaration of San José.
records.summary_es: La delegación de la República Dominicana protagonizó el segundo abandono de la conferencia de ministros de Relaciones Exteriores de dos semanas, marchándose el 20 de agosto luego de que los cancilleres hallaran al régimen de Rafael Trujillo culpable de planear el asesinato del presidente venezolano Betancourt y aprobaran sanciones políticas y económicas. Tras un abandono posterior de Cuba, los diplomáticos señalaron que dos dictadores —uno de la izquierda y otro de la derecha— se habían marchado. Los delegados debatieron las consecuencias para el sistema interamericano de 70 años, ya que algunos esperaban una renovada fe pública y otros temían un precedente nocivo. Mientras Estados Unidos insistía en una postura hemisférica firme contra el comunismo, los ministros alcanzaron un compromiso al omitir la mención directa de Cuba en la Declaración de San José.

records.headline: In a letter to the editor headed Our 'Inconsistent' Foreign Policies
records.summary_en: In a letter to the editor headed Our 'Inconsistent' Foreign Policies, a reader responds to the newspaper's editorial Break With Trujillo. The writer asserts that taking drastic measures against a right-wing dictatorship like the Dominican Republic, which has given no offense to the United States, while permitting a hostile left-wing dictatorship in Havana to escape almost unscathed, demonstrates deep inconsistencies. The letter argues that such contradictory policies explain why the United States is losing the cold war and warns that Communist infiltration has advanced across Latin America without the loss of a single soldier.

La carta sostiene que tales políticas contradictorias explican por qué Estados Unidos está perdiendo la guerra fría y advierte que la infiltración comunista ha avanzado por América Latina sin la pérdida de un solo soldado.

records.headline: In a letter to the editor, Lieutenant Colonel Charles P. Beazley questions
records.summary_en: In a letter to the editor, Lieutenant Colonel Charles P. Beazley questions Secretary of State Christian Herter and the State Department regarding the diplomatic rupture with the Dominican Republic. Beazley contends that Fidel Castro, rather than Rafael Trujillo, is the true pro-Communist threat, arguing that Castro uses firing squads and confiscates hundreds of millions in American industrial plants while American investors have not lost a dime in Hispaniola. He describes Trujillo as a friend of the Free West who dealt with Communists in the Kremlin's own fashion. An accompanying letter adds that General Trujillo erred in proclaiming himself a bulwark against communism, given that the United States severed diplomatic ties with the Dominican Republic while continuing to recognize Cuba.

records.headline: An editorial reviews the congressional dispute concerning windfall
records.summary_en: An editorial reviews the congressional dispute concerning windfall sugar quota allocations granted to the Dominican Republic after imports of Cuban sugar were restricted. President Eisenhower sought discretionary authority to use the quota as an economic weapon against the dictatorial Trujillo regime. The House balked, refusing to authorize the action unless the Organization of American States imposed economic sanctions before October 15, with House Democratic Leader McCormack arguing that Congress should not join a White House declaration of war against the Dominican Republic. The editorial concludes that because the administration sought to act without comparable moves by other OAS members, the failure of Congress to pass the measure was probably beneficial.
records.summary_es: Un editorial revisa la disputa en el Congreso sobre las asignaciones de cuota azucarera extraordinaria otorgadas a la República Dominicana tras restringirse las importaciones de azúcar cubano. El presidente Eisenhower buscó facultades discrecionales para usar la cuota como arma económica contra el régimen dictatorial de Trujillo. La Cámara de Representantes se opuso, rehusándose a autorizar la medida a menos que la Organización de los Estados Americanos impusiera sanciones económicas antes del 15 de octubre, y el líder demócrata de la Cámara, McCormack, sostuvo que el Congreso no debía unirse a una declaración de guerra de la Casa Blanca contra la República Dominicana. El editorial concluye que, dado que el gobierno intentaba actuar sin medidas comparables por parte de otros miembros de la OEA, la falta de aprobación de la medida por el Congreso fue probablemente beneficiosa.

records.headline: In a letter published under the headline Foreign Relations
records.summary_en: In a letter published under the headline Foreign Relations, Peter Dundas of Franklin Park, Illinois, notes that Undersecretary of State Douglas Dillon described Dominican dictator Rafael Trujillo as a tyrant, torturer, and murderer before the United States severed diplomatic ties. Dundas questions why the United States broke relations only with the small Dominican Republic rather than also severing relations with the Soviet Union. He argues that Nikita Khrushchev alone has killed twice the population of the entire Dominican Republic and asserts that the United States must sever ties with the Soviets and their satellites to avoid appearing to act solely against anti-Communist nations.
records.summary_es: En una carta publicada bajo el titular Relaciones exteriores, Peter Dundas de Franklin Park, Illinois, señala que el subsecretario de Estado Douglas Dillon describió al dictador dominicano Rafael Trujillo como tirano, torturador y asesino antes de que Estados Unidos rompiera relaciones diplomáticas. records.headline: Following the Costa Rica conference and the break in diplomatic
records.summary_en: Following the Costa Rica conference and the break in diplomatic relations with the Dominican Republic, the administration concluded that buying Dominican sugar beyond its normal sales quota of 130,000 would produce disastrous repercussions, though existing legislation required authorization before December 31, 1960. Under the heading The Sugar Issue, the dispatch describes President Eisenhower's request for authority to eliminate the bonus allocation. Although the Senate passed a bill giving the President discretion to purchase from other nations, the House refused to agree during an all-night session, citing fears that a collapse of the Trujillo government would open the door to Communists. Following remarks by House Democratic Leader McCormack opposing congressional participation in a White House declaration of war against the Dominican Republic, President Eisenhower issued a statement calling Congress's inaction extremely serious.
records.summary_es: Tras la conferencia de Costa Rica y la ruptura de relaciones diplomáticas con la República Dominicana, el gobierno concluyó que comprar azúcar dominicano por encima de su cuota habitual de ventas de 130,000 causaría repercusiones desastrosas, aunque la legislación vigente requería la autorización antes del 31 de diciembre de 1960. Bajo el encabezado El asunto del azúcar, el despacho describe la solicitud del presidente Eisenhower de facultades para eliminar la asignación adicional. Aunque el Senado aprobó un proyecto que otorgaba al presidente discreción para comprar a otras naciones, la Cámara de Representantes se negó a aceptar durante una sesión de toda la noche, citando temores de que el colapso del gobierno de Trujillo abriera la puerta a los comunistas. Tras declaraciones del líder demócrata de la Cámara, McCormack, oponiéndose a que el Congreso participara en una declaración de guerra de la Casa Blanca contra la República Dominicana, el presidente Eisenhower emitió un comunicado calificando la inacción del Congreso como extremadamente grave.

records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch reports that about 60,000 women
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch reports that about 60,000 women paraded through Ciudad Trujillo to protest diplomatic and economic sanctions voted against the Dominican Republic at the San José foreign ministers conference. The marchers demonstrated in support of Dominican Dictator Rafael Trujillo. Maria Martinez de Trujillo, wife of the generalissimo, and his daughter, Angelita Trujillo de Leon, paraded alongside the women. Dominican President Joaquin Balaguer and General Trujillo reviewed the demonstration together from a platform.

Las manifestantes marcharon en respaldo al dictador dominicano Rafael Trujillo. María Martínez de Trujillo, esposa del generalísimo, y su hija, Angelita Trujillo de León, desfilaron junto a las mujeres. El presidente dominicano Joaquín Balaguer y el general Trujillo observaron la manifestación juntos desde una plataforma.

records.headline: An editorial commentary reflects on the regime of Dictator Trujillo
records.summary_en: An editorial commentary reflects on the regime of Dictator Trujillo in the Dominican Republic, observing that he has ruled his homeland with an iron hand and treated subjects ruthlessly in political and other spheres. The piece contends, however, that Trujillo has demonstrated he is not a Communist and remains determined to prevent Communism from gaining a foothold in his nation. Quoting Shakespeare's Julius Caesar regarding evil outliving men, the commentary concludes that while Trujillo cannot be compared to Caesar, the evil he has done will likewise endure.
records.summary_es: Un comentario editorial reflexiona sobre el régimen del dictador Trujillo en la República Dominicana, observando que ha gobernado su patria con mano de hierro y tratado a sus gobernados con crueldad en el ámbito político y en otros órdenes. El texto sostiene, no obstante, que Trujillo ha demostrado que no es comunista y sigue decidido a impedir que el comunismo se afiance en su nación. Citando el Julio César de Shakespeare respecto a que el mal sobrevive a los hombres, el comentario concluye que si bien Trujillo no puede compararse con César, el mal que ha hecho igualmente perdurará.

records.headline: In a letter to the editor, Charles P. Beazley strongly criticizes
records.summary_en: In a letter to the editor, Charles P. Beazley strongly criticizes the United States decision to sever relations with the Dominican Republic in an effort to remove anti-Communist leader Trujillo. Beazley cautions that if efforts to displace Trujillo succeed, he will very likely be replaced by a pro-Soviet regime, questioning how many American soldiers would then be sacrificed to retake the country from an adversary. He also denounces those who enabled Castro's pro-Soviet takeover in Cuba and accuses a State Department faction of pushing for the recognition and United Nations admission of Red China.
records.summary_es: En una carta al director, Charles P. Beazley critica duramente la decisión de Estados Unidos de romper relaciones con la República Dominicana en un intento por desplazar al líder anticomunista Trujillo. Beazley advierte que si los intentos por destituir a Trujillo tienen éxito, muy probablemente será reemplazado por un régimen prosoviético, preguntándose cuántos soldados estadounidenses tendrían que sacrificarse luego para arrebatar el país a un adversario. Denuncia además a quienes permitieron la instauración del régimen prosoviético de Castro en Cuba y acusa a una facción del Departamento de Estado de presionar para el reconocimiento y admisión de la China roja en las Naciones Unidas.

records.headline: Diplomats familiar with confidential proceedings at the Costa Rica conference
records.summary_en: Diplomats familiar with confidential proceedings at the Costa Rica conference report that the United States delegation took the lead behind the scenes in demanding stringent action against the right-of-center Trujillo dictatorship. The same sources indicate that the United States initiated only a gentle reprimand of the Cuban regime, despite Cuba having committed far more misdeeds against American interests than the Dominican Republic. The dispatch notes that Washington held substantial influence through its 500 million dollar Latin American economic rehabilitation fund, asserting that equivalent sanctions against Fidel Castro would have passed had the State Department proposed them.
records.summary_es: Diplomáticos al tanto de las deliberaciones confidenciales en la conferencia de Costa Rica informan que la delegación de Estados Unidos encabezó tras bastidores la exigencia de medidas estrictas contra la dictadura de derecha de Trujillo. Las mismas fuentes señalan que Estados Unidos promovió únicamente una suave amonestación contra el régimen cubano, a pesar de que Cuba había cometido muchas más faltas contra los intereses estadounidenses que la República Dominicana. El despacho destaca que Washington mantuvo una influencia sustancial a través de su fondo de 500 millones de dólares para la rehabilitación económica latinoamericana, afirmando que sanciones equivalentes contra Fidel Castro se habrían aprobado si el Departamento de Estado las hubiera propuesto.

records.headline: An editorial assesses the results of the inter-American economic
records.summary_en: An editorial assesses the results of the inter-American economic conference in Bogotá, Colombia, where 19 members of the 21-nation Organization of American States signed the Act of Bogotá. The editorial notes that while Castro's Cuba dissented as expected, Rafael Trujillo's Dominican Republic did not participate. The adopted program establishes broad socio-economic initiatives to improve living standards through land reform, housing, health, and education, backed by an initial United States congressional authorization of 500 million dollars. Signatories pledged mutual cooperation, with each participating nation committing to contribute its fair share of funding, effort, and domestic policy reform.
records.summary_es: Un editorial evalúa los resultados de la conferencia económica interamericana en Bogotá, Colombia, donde 19 miembros de la Organización de los Estados Americanos, integrada por 21 naciones, firmaron el Acta de Bogotá. El editorial señala que, si bien la Cuba de Castro disintió como se esperaba, la República Dominicana de Rafael Trujillo no participó. El programa adoptado establece amplias iniciativas socioeconómicas para elevar los niveles de vida mediante la reforma agraria, la vivienda, la salud y la educación, respaldadas por una autorización inicial del Congreso de Estados Unidos de 500 millones de dólares. Los firmantes prometieron cooperación mutua, y cada nación participante se comprometió a aportar la parte que le corresponde en financiamiento, esfuerzo y reformas de política interna.

records.headline: An Associated Press report states that the Dominican military intelligence
records.summary_en: An Associated Press report states that the Dominican military intelligence service claimed to have smashed a plot to overthrow the government, implicating former United States Embassy cultural attaché William Pugh. Dominican authorities reported that twelve youths in Ciudad Trujillo participated in the conspiracy, with an arrested suspect naming Pugh as the group's inspirer and intellectual guide before the American diplomat hurriedly departed the country on September 7. The official announcement identified Tirso Mejia Guzman as the leader of the plot and Fabio Herrera as second in command, accusing the group of preparing terrorist acts and inciting an armed revolt through subversive pamphlets. The dispatch notes that the United States severed diplomatic ties after the Organization of American States held the Dominican Republic responsible for the assassination attempt against Venezuelan President Romulo Betancourt.
records.summary_es: Un informe de Associated Press señala que el servicio de inteligencia militar dominicano afirmó haber desarticulado un complot para derrocar al gobierno, implicando al ex agregado cultural de la embajada de Estados Unidos William Pugh. Las autoridades dominicanas informaron que doce jóvenes de Ciudad Trujillo participaron en la conspiración, y que un sospechoso detenido señaló a Pugh como el inspirador y guía intelectual del grupo antes de que el diplomático estadounidense partiera apresuradamente del país el 7 de septiembre. El comunicado oficial identificó a Tirso Mejía Guzmán como el líder del complot y a Fabio Herrera como segundo al mando, acusando al grupo de preparar actos terroristas e incitar a una revuelta armada mediante panfletos subversivos. El despacho destaca que Estados Unidos rompió lazos diplomáticos después de que la Organización de los Estados Americanos responsabilizara a la República Dominicana por el atentado contra el presidente venezolano Rómulo Betancourt.

records.headline: A report outlines the gathering of international leaders in New York
records.summary_en: A report outlines the gathering of international leaders in New York for the opening of the United Nations General Assembly session presided over by Dr. Victor Andres Belaunde. Listed among the heads of state and dignitaries expected in the assembly chamber is Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo Molina of the Dominican Republic, alongside Soviet Premier Nikita Khrushchev, Cuban Premier Fidel Castro, and Yugoslav President Josip Broz Tito. The article notes that prominent absentees from the high-level gathering include President Dwight D. Eisenhower, French President Charles de Gaulle, and British Prime Minister Harold Macmillan.
records.summary_es: Un informe describe la reunión de líderes internacionales en Nueva York para la apertura de la sesión de la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas presidida por el Dr. Víctor Andrés Belaúnde. Entre los jefes de Estado y dignatarios que se prevé asistan en la sala de la asamblea se encuentra el generalísimo Rafael Trujillo Molina de la República Dominicana, junto al primer ministro soviético Nikita Jrushchov, el primer ministro cubano Fidel Castro y el presidente yugoslavo Josip Broz Tito. El artículo señala que entre las ausencias notables del encuentro de alto nivel figuran el presidente Dwight D. Eisenhower, el presidente francés Charles de Gaulle y el primer ministro británico Harold Macmillan.

records.headline: Dominican Republic President Rafael Trujillo was omitted from the guest
records.summary_en: Dominican Republic President Rafael Trujillo was omitted from the guest list for a luncheon hosted by President Eisenhower for visiting heads of state at the Waldorf-Astoria Hotel. Under the heading Explains Snub, White House Press Secretary James C. Hagerty stated to reporters that the United States maintains no diplomatic relations with the Dominican Republic and certainly had no intention of inviting Cuba. The dispatch notes that Washington severed diplomatic relations following the Organization of American States' condemnation of the Trujillo regime for alleged involvement in the assassination plot against Venezuelan President Romulo Betancourt. Hagerty gave no specific explanation regarding the snub to Fidel Castro, which reflected worsening relations and expanding ties between Havana and the Soviet Union.
records.summary_es: El presidente de la República Dominicana, Rafael Trujillo, fue excluido de la lista de invitados a un almuerzo ofrecido por el presidente Eisenhower a los jefes de Estado visitantes en el hotel Waldorf-Astoria. Bajo el encabezado Explica desaire, el secretario de prensa de la Casa Blanca, James C. Hagerty, declaró a los periodistas que Estados Unidos no mantiene relaciones diplomáticas con la República Dominicana y ciertamente no tenía intención de invitar a Cuba. El despacho señala que Washington rompió relaciones diplomáticas tras la condena de la Organización de los Estados Americanos al régimen de Trujillo por su presunta implicación en el atentado contra el presidente venezolano Rómulo Betancourt. Hagerty no ofreció una explicación específica sobre el desaire a Fidel Castro, el cual reflejaba el deterioro de las relaciones y los crecientes vínculos entre La Habana y la Unión Soviética.

records.summary_en: A news report indicates that opposition has emerged against United States sugar purchases from the Dominican Republic, calling the move contrary to pledges made by Western Hemisphere foreign ministers at the OAS conference in San Jose, Costa Rica. At that conference, the OAS approved diplomatic and economic sanctions against the government of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo after Venezuela accused him of plotting to overthrow the Betancourt government and backing an assassination attempt against the Venezuelan president. Informants stated that Colombia and other nations supporting Venezuela would take the lead in opposing the United States sugar-purchase decision.

Fuentes informaron que Colombia y otros países que apoyaron a Venezuela encabezarían nuevamente las acciones contra la decisión de compra de azúcar estadounidense.

Sugar Deal Hit

CARACAS, Sept. 30 (AP).—Venezuela hopes the United States Government will reconsider its plan to buy sugar from the Dominican Republic, a spokesman for President Romulo Betancourt said. Venezuela has orally protested the purchase of 321,857 tons of Dominican sugar, calling it a violation of a boycott agreement by the foreign ministers' conference against the dictatorship of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo.

records.headline: The United States defended its decision to purchase sugar from the Dominican Republic shortly
records.summary_en: The United States defended its decision to purchase sugar from the Dominican Republic shortly after agreeing with Latin American foreign ministers to apply economic sanctions against Dictator Rafael Trujillo. Replying to a protest from Venezuela regarding the authorized purchase of 321.000 tons of Dominican sugar, the State Department asserted that Venezuelan concerns stemmed from a misunderstanding of the action taken. The note stated that the United States had eliminated special price benefits worth an estimated $13 million for the remainder of the year, arguing that this measure went beyond the economic actions taken by any other American state except possibly Venezuela.
records.summary_es: Estados Unidos defendió su decisión de comprar azúcar de la República Dominicana poco después de acordar con los cancilleres latinoamericanos la aplicación de medidas económicas contra el dictador Rafael Trujillo. En respuesta a una protesta de Venezuela sobre la compra autorizada de 321.000 toneladas de azúcar dominicano, el Departamento de Estado afirmó que las preocupaciones venezolanas se debían a un malentendido sobre la naturaleza de la medida adoptada. La nota señaló que Estados Unidos había privado a la República Dominicana de beneficios de precio especiales valorados en un estimado de 13 millones de dólares por lo que restaba del año, sosteniendo que esta acción superaba las medidas económicas aplicadas por cualquier otro Estado americano, con la posible excepción de Venezuela.

records.summary_en: General Fernando A. Sanchez, chief of staff of the Dominican Republic's Army, issued a statement in Ciudad Trujillo objecting to the United States' announced intention to supply weapons to Haiti. Sanchez characterized the arms plan as a manifest contradiction of formal State Department declarations establishing an absolute ban on arms sales to Caribbean nations. Sanchez expressed the presumption that the United States would not arm Haiti to commit aggression against the Dominican Republic, amid longstanding tensions between the two neighboring governments on the island of Hispaniola.
records.summary_es: El general Fernando A. Sanchez, jefe de estado mayor del Ejército de la República Dominicana, emitió una declaración en Ciudad Trujillo objetando la intención anunciada por Estados Unidos de suministrar armas a Haití. Sanchez calificó el plan de armamento como una contradicción manifiesta con las declaraciones formales del Departamento de Estado que establecían una prohibición absoluta de ventas de armas a países del área del Caribe. Sanchez expresó la presunción de que Estados Unidos no armaría a Haití para cometer agresiones contra la República Dominicana, en medio de tensiones prolongadas entre los dos gobiernos vecinos en la isla de La Española.

records.headline: In District Court, Judge Joseph R. Jackson imposed a sentence
records.summary_en: In District Court, Judge Joseph R. Jackson imposed a sentence on Guterma and denied his motion to withdraw a no-contest plea entered the previous May. Guterma and associates were charged with receiving $750,000 from Trujillo and the Dominican Republic in early 1959 to broadcast political propaganda disguised as news over the Mutual Broadcasting System. Judge Jackson ordered the sentence to run consecutively to a four-year and 11-month term Guterma was already serving for a New York conviction, rejecting a plea from defense attorney Richard Wells for concurrent sentencing. The report notes that former Mutual board chairman Hal Roach, Jr., had previously been fined $500 after pleading no contest to failing to register the network as a foreign agent.
records.summary_es: En el Tribunal de Distrito, el juez Joseph R. Jackson dictó sentencia contra Guterma y rechazó su moción para retirar una declaración de no impugnación presentada en mayo anterior. Guterma y sus asociados fueron acusados de recibir 750.000 dólares de Trujillo y la República Dominicana a principios de 1959 para emitir propaganda política encubierta como noticias a través de la cadena Mutual Broadcasting System. El juez Jackson ordenó que la pena se cumpliera de forma consecutiva a la condena de cuatro años y 11 meses que Guterma ya cumplía por un fallo previo en Nueva York, denegando la petición del abogado defensor Richard Wells para que las penas fueran simultáneas. El informe agrega que el expresidente de la junta directiva de Mutual, Hal Roach, Jr., había sido multado previamente con 500 dólares tras declararse no contencioso por no registrar la cadena como agente extranjero.

records.headline: An AP dispatch from New Orleans reports that five Dominican Republic exiles
records.summary_en: An AP dispatch from New Orleans reports that five Dominican Republic exiles who fled Cuba in a 15-foot rowboat have been sent to New York after processing by immigration authorities. The five men—identified as Jose Fernandez, Miguel Pichardo, Aguiles Eschavarria, Alphonso Espinal, and Teofilo Hiraldo—originally fled the Dominican Republic to Cuba in 1955 after participating in revolutions against the dictatorship of General Rafael Trujillo. They stated to government interviewers that they subsequently fled Cuba to escape the dictatorship of Premier Fidel Castro. Rescued off the coast of Florida by the freighter SS Thomas Tracy and landed near Baton Rouge, Louisiana, the men were paroled to the agency's New York office according to acting district director Horace A. Nabors.

Los cinco hombres —identificados como Jose Fernandez, Miguel Pichardo, Aguiles Eschavarria, Alphonso Espinal y Teofilo Hiraldo— huyeron originalmente de la República Dominicana a Cuba en 1955 tras participar en revoluciones contra la dictadura del general Rafael Trujillo. Declararon ante entrevistadores del gobierno que posteriormente huyeron de Cuba para escapar de la dictadura del primer ministro Fidel Castro. Rescatados frente a las costas de Florida por el carguero SS Thomas Tracy y desembarcados cerca de Baton Rouge, Luisiana, los hombres recibieron libertad condicional bajo supervisión de la oficina de la agencia en Nueva York, según el director distrital interino Horace A.
