records.headline: A report in The Catholic Times details an anti-religious campaign
records.summary_en: A report in The Catholic Times details an anti-religious campaign broadcast over Dominican Republic radio advocating for a single educational plan that excludes religious instruction. The station argued that revolutionary systems designed to balance wealth require uniform molding of minds, asserting that religious choices must not be imposed upon children before they possess full reason. Accusing the Roman Church of obstructing revolutionary social progress to monopolize human customs, the broadcast called for establishing lay education first in rural areas to free peasant children from religious superstitions. The article mentions Maj. Juan Abbes Garcia, former head of Generalissimo Trujillo's secret police, in connection with the broadcast campaign.
records.summary_es: Un informe en The Catholic Times describe una campaña antirreligiosa transmitida por la radio de la República Dominicana que promueve un plan educativo único que excluye la enseñanza religiosa. La emisora sostuvo que los sistemas revolucionarios concebidos para equilibrar la riqueza requieren moldear las mentes de manera uniforme, argumentando que las convicciones religiosas no deben imponerse a los niños antes de que alcancen el pleno uso de razón. Tras acusar a la Iglesia romana de obstaculizar el progreso social revolucionario para monopolizar las costumbres humanas, la transmisión exigió implantar primero la educación laica en las zonas rurales para liberar a los hijos de campesinos de supersticiones religiosas. El artículo cita al mayor Juan Abbes Garcia, exjefe de la policía secreta del generalísimo Trujillo, en relación con la campaña radial.

records.headline: The Organization of American States was called into an emergency
records.summary_en: The Organization of American States was called into an emergency session in Washington to consider new charges brought by Venezuela alleging Dominican involvement in violent disturbances in Caracas. Spokesmen at the Pan American Union stated that specific details concerning Venezuela's complaint were not yet available but confirmed the charges would be discussed before the council. The report notes that this marked the second time in recent months that the Venezuelan government formally accused the Trujillo dictatorship of meddling in its internal affairs.
records.summary_es: La Organización de los Estados Americanos fue convocada a una sesión de emergencia en Washington para examinar nuevas acusaciones formuladas por Venezuela sobre la implicación dominicana en violentos disturbios en Caracas. Voceros de la Unión Panamericana indicaron que aún no disponían de detalles específicos acerca de la queja venezolana, pero confirmaron que las denuncias serían analizadas ante el consejo. El despacho señala que esta constituía la segunda ocasión en meses recientes en que el gobierno venezolano acusaba formalmente a la dictadura de Trujillo de inmiscuirse en sus asuntos internos.

records.headline: Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo announced in Ciudad Trujillo
records.summary_en: Generalissimo Rafael L. Trujillo announced in Ciudad Trujillo that the Dominican Republic's budget for 1961 will include appropriations dedicated to improving conditions for workers. Speaking at the inauguration of a workers' club in the eastern part of the country, Trujillo stated that 575 workers' clubs will be established, large amounts of land will be distributed to farmers, and hygienic dwellings will be constructed for their use. Trujillo predicted that an intensive social welfare campaign will be carried out across the Dominican Republic in 1961.
records.summary_es: El generalísimo Rafael L. Trujillo anunció en Ciudad Trujillo que el presupuesto de la República Dominicana para 1961 incluirá asignaciones destinadas a mejorar las condiciones laborales de los trabajadores. Al hablar en la inauguración de un club de obreros en la parte oriental del país, Trujillo afirmó que se establecerán 575 clubes obreros, se distribuirán grandes extensiones de tierra entre los agricultores y se construirán viviendas higiénicas para su uso. Trujillo pronosticó que a lo largo de 1961 se llevará a cabo una intensa campaña de bienestar social en toda la República Dominicana.

records.headline: A commentary column in the Minneapolis Spokesman discusses United States hemispheric
records.summary_en: A commentary column in the Minneapolis Spokesman discusses United States hemispheric policy, pointing to actions taken at a recent OAS meeting in San Jose, Costa Rica. The column notes that Secretary of State Herter promoted an image of partnership, rebuked Rafael Trujillo and his Dominican Republic dictatorship, and called for free elections in the Dominican Republic. Herter also condemned Castro and Cuba as a threat to Latin America while emphasizing Washington's renewed concern for the region.
records.summary_es: Una columna de opinión en el Minneapolis Spokesman analiza la política hemisférica de Estados Unidos, destacando las medidas tomadas en una reunión reciente de la OEA en San José, Costa Rica. El artículo señala que el secretario de Estado Herter promovió una imagen de colaboración mutua, reprendió a Rafael Trujillo y a su dictadura en la República Dominicana, y exigió la celebración de elecciones libres en la República Dominicana. Herter también denunció a Castro y a Cuba como una amenaza para América Latina, subrayando la renovada preocupación de Washington por la región.

records.headline: An aviation announcement in the St. Croix Avis reports that Caribair
records.summary_en: An aviation announcement in the St. Croix Avis reports that Caribair will expand its passenger flight schedule to Ciudad Trujillo effective Wednesday, December 21. Under the new schedule, service will operate three times weekly on Wednesdays, Fridays, and Sundays, with westbound flights departing San Juan at 8:00 A.M. and arriving in the Dominican Republic at 9:37 A.M. Return flights will leave Ciudad Trujillo at 9:50 A.M. and reach San Juan at 11:34. The announcement also detailed the existing schedules for Ponce, with six daily round trips Monday through Friday, three flights on Saturday and two on Sunday, and for Mayaguez, with four daily round trips Monday through Friday, three flights on Saturday and two on Sunday.
records.summary_es: Un comunicado sobre aviación en el St. Croix Avis informa que Caribair incrementará sus vuelos regulares de pasajeros hacia Ciudad Trujillo a partir del miércoles 21 de diciembre. Los vuelos de regreso partirán de Ciudad Trujillo a las 9:50 a. m. y arribarán a San Juan a las 11:34. El comunicado también detalló los horarios existentes de Ponce, con seis viajes diarios de ida y vuelta de lunes a viernes, tres vuelos el sábado y dos el domingo, y de Mayagüez, con cuatro viajes diarios de ida y vuelta de lunes a viernes, tres vuelos el sábado y dos el domingo.

records.headline: A report on resolutions adopted by an international trade union
records.summary_en: A report on resolutions adopted by an international trade union board states that the organization welcomed the decision of the Organization of American States to impose sanctions against the Trujillo dictatorship in the Dominican Republic. The meeting also addressed other global matters, calling for negotiations between Indonesia and the Netherlands over the disputed territory of West New Guinea and supporting self-determination within the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland. Additionally, the executive board accepted into affiliation trade union bodies from French-speaking West Africa, Finland, and South Africa.

La reunión también abordó otros asuntos mundiales, solicitando negociaciones entre Indonesia y los Países Bajos sobre el territorio disputado de Nueva Guinea Occidental y apoyando la autodeterminación dentro de la Federación de Rodesia y Nyasalandia. Asimismo, la junta directiva admitió la afiliación de organizaciones sindicales de África Occidental de habla francesa, Finlandia y Sudáfrica.

records.headline: An AP dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that Generalissimo Rafael
records.summary_en: An AP dispatch from Ciudad Trujillo reports that Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, strongman of the Dominican Republic for 30 years, won election as governor of Santiago Province. Although Trujillo stepped down from the presidency several years earlier while maintaining an iron grip on the nation, he ran for the provincial governorship in Thursday's election to demonstrate his popularity. Official tabulations showed Trujillo winning 121,219 votes compared to 7,198 for his two opponents.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de la AP desde Ciudad Trujillo informa que el generalísimo Rafael Trujillo, hombre fuerte de la República Dominicana durante 30 años, ganó las elecciones para la gobernación de la provincia de Santiago. Aunque Trujillo había dejado la presidencia varios años antes mientras mantenía el control férreo sobre el país, se postuló para la gobernación provincial en los comicios del jueves con el fin de demostrar su popularidad. Los cómputos oficiales mostraron que Trujillo obtuvo 121.219 votos frente a 7.198 conseguidos por sus dos oponentes.

records.headline: President Eisenhower declared that the Dominican Republic government
records.summary_en: President Eisenhower declared that the Dominican Republic government, bossed for 30 years by Dictator Rafael Trujillo, was unanimously condemned by hemisphere nations for violating the peace in Latin America. Eisenhower stated that despite his urgent recommendations, Congress failed to relieve him of the statutory requirement to purchase Dominican sugar reallocated from Cuba's former quota. Consequently, official announcements included an allotment of 27,789 tons to the Dominican Republic for the first quarter of 1961 as part of an inflated national sugar consumption estimate of 10 million tons.
records.summary_es: El presidente Eisenhower declaró que el gobierno de la República Dominicana, dominado durante 30 años por el dictador Rafael Trujillo, fue condenado de forma unánime por las naciones del hemisferio por atentar contra la paz en América Latina. Eisenhower explicó que, a pesar de sus urgentes recomendaciones, el Congreso no lo eximió de la obligación legal de adquirir azúcar dominicano procedente de la cuota retirada a Cuba. En consecuencia, los anuncios oficiales incluyeron una asignación de 27.789 toneladas a la República Dominicana para el primer trimestre de 1961, dentro de una estimación nacional ampliada de consumo azucarero fijada en 10 millones de toneladas.

records.headline: An obituary reports that Mr. Llaverias, an acting member of the Dominican Academy of Language
records.summary_en: An obituary reports that Mr. Llaverias, an acting member of the Dominican Academy of Language and the Royal Academy of the Spanish Language of Spain, as well as an honorary member of the Cuban Academy of History, received a doctor of law degree from the University of Santo Domingo. Decorated by the Dominican, Chilean, Argentine, and Colombian governments, he is survived by two sons, including Federico Llaverias, Jr., consul of the Dominican Republic in Washington, and Jose of San Francisco, alongside two daughters and two grandchildren. Following a requiem mass in San Francisco, services and provisional burial were scheduled at Gate of Heaven Cemetery in New York City.

Condecorado por los gobiernos dominicano, chileno, argentino y colombiano, le sobreviven dos hijos, entre ellos Federico Llaverías, hijo, cónsul de la República Dominicana en Washington, y José de San Francisco, junto con dos hijas y dos nietos. Tras una misa de réquiem en San Francisco, los servicios fúnebres y el entierro provisional se programaron en el cementerio Gate of Heaven en la ciudad de Nueva York.

records.headline: Fifty-seven Dominican Republic nationals and exiles, men, women and children representing six anti-Trujillo
records.summary_en: Fifty-seven Dominican Republic nationals and exiles, men, women and children representing six anti-Trujillo revolutionary groups in New York, arrived by bus in Washington and formed a picket line urging the Organization of American States to apply economic sanctions against Dictator Rafael Trujillo, carrying signs including American Mothers Should Condemn Trujillo's Tyranny and Our Country Asks for Sanctions. The pickets, led by the Free Syndicate of Dominican Workers in Exile under its president Fernando Jose Muni, demonstrated two blocks from the Pan American Union Building while inside the OAS Council met to consider the sanctions recommended by the foreign ministers of the American states at their meeting in Costa Rica last August.
records.summary_es: Cincuenta y siete ciudadanos y exiliados de la República Dominicana, hombres, mujeres y niños que representaban a seis grupos revolucionarios antitrujillistas de Nueva York, llegaron en autobús a Washington y formaron una línea de protesta pidiendo a la Organización de los Estados Americanos que aplicara sanciones económicas contra el dictador Rafael Trujillo, con carteles que incluían Las madres americanas deben condenar la tiranía de Trujillo y Nuestro país pide sanciones. Los manifestantes, encabezados por el Sindicato Libre de Trabajadores Dominicanos en el Exilio bajo su presidente Fernando Jose Muni, se manifestaron a dos cuadras del edificio de la Unión Panamericana mientras dentro el Consejo de la OEA se reunía para considerar las sanciones recomendadas por los ministros de Relaciones Exteriores de los estados americanos en su reunión en Costa Rica el pasado agosto.

Amid these shifts, the dispatch reports that Venezuela maintains the Trujillo dictatorship in the Dominican Republic should be dealt with severely first.

En medio de estos cambios, el despacho informa que Venezuela sostiene que la dictadura de Trujillo en la República Dominicana debe ser tratada con severidad en primer lugar.

records.headline: A dispatch reviewing Venezuelan political affairs reports that the government
records.summary_en: A dispatch reviewing Venezuelan political affairs reports that the government has navigated two years of turbulence in the wake of the fallen Pérez Jiménez dictatorship. During this period, the administration has survived an attempted military coup as well as an attempt on President Rómulo Betancourt's life attributed to plots engineered by dictator Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic. Concurrently, the Betancourt government has struggled with severe economic difficulties inherited from past corruption and exacerbated by capital flight.
records.summary_es: Un despacho que revisa los asuntos políticos venezolanos informa que el gobierno ha atravesado dos años de turbulencia tras la caída de la dictadura de Pérez Jiménez. Durante este período, la administración ha sobrevivido a un intento de golpe militar, así como a un atentado contra la vida del presidente Rómulo Betancourt atribuido a complots tramados por el dictador Rafael Trujillo de la República Dominicana. Al mismo tiempo, el gobierno de Betancourt ha lidiado con graves dificultades económicas heredadas de la corrupción pasada y agravadas por la fuga de capitales.

records.headline: Venezuelan President Rómulo Betancourt restored constitutional
records.summary_en: Venezuelan President Rómulo Betancourt restored constitutional guarantees of free speech, assembly, and immunity from arbitrary arrest, only to suspend them again nine hours later. The Venezuelan government stated that the Trujillo Dominican regime had urged ousted military conspirators to make a renewed attempt on Betancourt's life, following a June bomb explosion blamed on Trujillo plotters that severely burned the president. The report notes that the Organization of American States found the Dominican Republic guilty of aggression against Venezuela, prompting most member republics, including the United States, to sever diplomatic relations and curtail economic ties with General Trujillo.

El gobierno venezolano declaró que el régimen dominicano de Trujillo había instado a militares conspiradores destituidos a perpetrar un nuevo atentado contra la vida de Betancourt, tras una explosión de bomba en junio atribuida a conspiradores respaldados por Trujillo que causó graves quemaduras al mandatario. El informe añade que la Organización de los Estados Americanos determinó que la República Dominicana cometió agresión contra Venezuela, lo que llevó a la mayoría de las repúblicas miembros, incluidos los Estados Unidos, a romper relaciones diplomáticas y reducir los lazos económicos con el general Trujillo.

records.headline: In the Dominican Republic, a report describes a philanthropic
records.summary_en: In the Dominican Republic, a report describes a philanthropic housing initiative where deserted mothers receive keys to newly furnished homes fully stocked with food. At presentation ceremonies, Doña María M. de Trujillo urged friends, citizens, and humanitarians to support the project to assist unfortunate women who have known misery and pain, while Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo personally presented keys to recipients. Financed partly through donations including contributions from Florida residents Harry Lazzo of Miami and Brailey Odham of Sanford, the project requires mothers to maintain clean dwellings, attend weekly home economics classes, and exclude men from residing or dining in the houses.
records.summary_es: En la República Dominicana, un informe describe una iniciativa filantrópica de vivienda en la que madres abandonadas reciben las llaves de casas recién amuebladas y abastecidas de alimentos. En las ceremonias de entrega, doña María M. de Trujillo instó a amigos, ciudadanos y personas de espíritu humanitario a sumarse al proyecto para ayudar a mujeres desafortunadas que han sufrido miseria y dolor, mientras que el generalísimo Rafael Trujillo entregó personalmente las llaves a las beneficiarias. Financiado en parte mediante donaciones que incluyen aportes de los residentes de Florida Harry Lazzo de Miami y Brailey Odham de Sanford, el proyecto exige que las madres mantengan limpias las viviendas, asistan a clases semanales de economía doméstica y prohíban que los hombres vivan o coman en los hogares.

records.headline: The Bureau of Information of the National Catholic Welfare Conference challenged
records.summary_en: The Bureau of Information of the National Catholic Welfare Conference challenged newspaper advertisements claiming close cooperation between the Dominican Republic government and the Roman Catholic Church. The bureau characterized the claims as inaccurate, explaining that the advertisements seized upon a mid-January welcoming address delivered to Generalissimo Trujillo by Bishop Juan Félix Pepén of La Altagracia at Higüey. The bureau stated that the advertisement published by the Secretariat of State of Interior and Worship directly contradicts a January 10 letter sent by the six Dominican bishops to Trujillo, which placed responsibility for the regime's anti-Catholic campaign squarely at his doorstep.

La oficina calificó tales afirmaciones de inexactas, explicando que la propaganda aprovechó un discurso de bienvenida de mediados de enero pronunciado ante el generalísimo Trujillo por el obispo Juan Félix Pepén de La Altagracia en Higüey. La oficina afirmó que el anuncio publicado por la Secretaría de Estado de lo Interior y Cultos contradice directamente una carta del 10 de enero dirigida por los seis obispos dominicanos a Trujillo, en la cual responsabilizaron directamente a su régimen por la campaña anticatólica.

records.headline: An editorial in the Evening Star reflects on hemisphere relations
records.summary_en: An editorial in the Evening Star reflects on hemisphere relations, arguing that had the United States and other nations not persistently refused to intervene against the right-wing excesses of the Batista regime in Cuba and Trujillo in the Dominican Republic, Fidel Castro would find no justification today. Contending that actions menacing liberty within any single American nation threaten all others, the piece asserts that internal tyrannies cannot be treated as the exclusive concern of the country involved. Accordingly, the editorial notes that the Kennedy administration is conducting a careful review of the non-intervention doctrine while disclaiming any intention to revive a big stick policy.
records.summary_es: Un editorial del Evening Star reflexiona sobre las relaciones hemisféricas, argumentando que si los Estados Unidos y otras naciones no se hubiesen negado persistentemente a intervenir contra los excesos de derecha del régimen de Batista en Cuba y de Trujillo en la República Dominicana, Fidel Castro no encontraría justificación alguna hoy en día. Al sostener que las acciones que amenazan la libertad en una sola nación americana ponen en riesgo a todas las demás, el texto afirma que las tiranías internas no pueden considerarse un asunto exclusivo del país involucrado. En consecuencia, el editorial señala que el gobierno de Kennedy está llevando a cabo una cuidadosa revisión de la doctrina de no intervención, desestimando cualquier intención de revivir la política del gran garrote.

records.headline: The State Department announced that the Dominican Republic has expelled
records.summary_en: The State Department announced that the Dominican Republic has expelled United States Vice Consul James A. McNamara on allegations of distributing erroneous information about the country. The department emphasized that it maintains full confidence in McNamara as an able career officer and confirmed his reassignment to the United States Embassy in San Salvador, El Salvador. The dispatch adds that while American republics broke diplomatic ties with the dictatorship of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo following its conviction for an assassination plot against the president of Venezuela, consular relations remain in effect.

records.summary_en: In a public letter, the Catholic hierarchy of the Dominican Republic acknowledged past gifts and works estimated at $30 million provided at the initiative of General Trujillo, but declined a proposed title. The letter was signed by Msgr. Octavio A. Beras, coadjutor archbishop, Bishop Hugo E. Polanco of Santiago de los Caballeros, Bishop Francisco Panal of La Vega, Bishop Juan F. Pepén of La Altagracia, and Bishop Tomás F. Reilly of San Juan de la Maguana. The report notes escalating church-state conflict since a January 1960 pastoral letter urging clemency for arrested dissidents, citing the expulsion of at least 46 priests and clerical denunciations by the pro-regime Radio Caribe.

Pepén de La Altagracia y el obispo Tomás F. Reilly de San Juan de la Maguana. records.headline: Dominican Catholic bishops published a letter in the newspaper
records.summary_en: Dominican Catholic bishops published a letter in the newspaper El Caribe declining a proposal to award Trujillo, the country's real ruler, the title of 'Benefactor of the Catholic Church of the Dominican Republic,' stating that such honors are granted solely by the Vatican. While expressing private and public appreciation for benefits, favors, and gifts ordered for the common welfare—with an estimated $30 million spent on church works at Trujillo's initiative—the prelates stood firm. The communication was signed by Msgr. Octavio A. Beras, alongside Bishops Hugo E. Polanco, Francisco Panal, Juan F. Pepén, and Tomás F. Reilly.

records.headline: An aviation schedule reports that weekly jet Clipper flights
records.summary_en: An aviation schedule reports that weekly jet Clipper flights began February 25, departing New York on Saturdays for Curaçao with an intermediate stop at Ciudad Trujillo, Dominican Republic. Service operates over a 2,035-mile route, with return flights departing on Sundays. Flying time from New York to Ciudad Trujillo is scheduled at three hours and 30 minutes, followed by a flight of one hour and 10 minutes from Ciudad Trujillo to Curaçao.
records.summary_es: Un itinerario de aviación informa que el 25 de febrero comenzaron los vuelos semanales en aviones Clipper a reacción, saliendo de Nueva York los sábados hacia Curazao con una escala intermedia en Ciudad Trujillo, República Dominicana. El servicio cubre una ruta de 2.035 millas, con vuelos de regreso los domingos. El tiempo de vuelo de Nueva York a Ciudad Trujillo está programado en tres horas y 30 minutos, seguido de un trayecto de una hora y 10 minutos desde Ciudad Trujillo hasta Curazao.

records.headline: Under the chairmanship of Jules Dubois, Latin American correspondent
records.summary_en: Under the chairmanship of Jules Dubois, Latin American correspondent for the Chicago Tribune, the Freedom of the Press Commission of the Inter American Press Association will convene in Acapulco, Mexico, on Wednesday, March 8. The commission will evaluate continental press conditions and examine dictatorships where freedom of the press does not exist, specifically highlighting Cuba, Santo Domingo, Nicaragua, and Paraguay. The formal complaint against Cuban totalitarian censorship will be presented by exiled editor Dr. Jorge Zayas of Avance.
records.summary_es: Bajo la presidencia de Jules Dubois, corresponsal para América Latina del Chicago Tribune, la Comisión de Libertad de Prensa de la Sociedad Interamericana de Prensa se reunirá en Acapulco, México, el miércoles 8 de marzo. La comisión evaluará las condiciones de la prensa continental y examinará las dictaduras donde no existe libertad de prensa, señalando concretamente los casos de Cuba, Santo Domingo, Nicaragua y Paraguay. La acusación formal contra la censura totalitaria cubana será presentada por el director en el exilio del periódico Avance, el doctor Jorge Zayas.

records.headline: A dispatch recounts harassment tactics directed by the Trujillo regime
records.summary_en: A dispatch recounts harassment tactics directed by the Trujillo regime against the papal nuncio, Archbishop Zanini, following his return to Ciudad Trujillo from San Juan on May 26. Two days later, guests arrived at the nunciature carrying fraudulent invitations bearing the prelate's forged or pilfered seal for an alleged official reception. Archbishop Zanini refused to act as host and turned the crowd away, maintaining his resolve even when Generalissimo Trujillo arrived with motorcycle sirens to pressure him into proceeding. The nuncio subsequently departed for Rome to confer with Pope John XXIII, while a priest who defended Zanini in a sermon was exiled from the country on 12 hours' notice.
records.summary_es: Un despacho relata las tácticas de hostigamiento dirigidas por el régimen de Trujillo contra el nuncio apostólico, el arzobispo Zanini, tras su regreso a Ciudad Trujillo desde San Juan el 26 de mayo. Dos días después, acudieron invitados a la nunciatura portando invitaciones fraudulentas que exhibían el sello falsificado o sustraído del prelado para una supuesta recepción oficial. El arzobispo Zanini se negó a actuar como anfitrión y despidió a la multitud, manteniéndose firme incluso cuando el generalísimo Trujillo llegó escoltado por sirenas de motocicletas para presionarlo a realizar el evento. Posteriormente, el nuncio partió hacia Roma para consultar con el papa Juan XXIII, mientras que un sacerdote que defendió a Zanini en un sermón fue expulsado del país con un aviso de 12 horas.

records.headline: A report describes a sermon delivered by Bishop Francisco Panal
records.summary_en: A report describes a sermon delivered by Bishop Francisco Panal, a Spanish-born prelate who has served his entire priestly career in the Dominican Republic. Observers considered Panal's words the strongest rebuke General Trujillo has received since seizing absolute control of the nation. Panal denounced the government-controlled press and radio campaign against the Church as sacrilegious and impious to the point of causing nausea. Alluding to the Trujillo family's vast wealth, estimated at half the national assets, the bishop decried that impoverished citizens in rags receive only niggardly charity, urging Trujillo to build industries offering living wages and construct hygienic homes for shantytown families.
records.summary_es: Un informe describe un sermón pronunciado por el obispo Francisco Panal, prelado de origen español que ha dedicado toda su vida sacerdotal a la República Dominicana. Los observadores consideraron las palabras de Panal como la crítica más contundente recibida por el general Trujillo desde que asumió el control absoluto del país. Panal denunció la campaña de prensa y radio controlada por el gobierno contra la Iglesia como sacrílega e impía hasta el punto de provocar náuseas. Al aludir a la inmensa fortuna de la familia Trujillo, estimada en la mitad del patrimonio nacional, el obispo lamentó que los ciudadanos empobrecidos en harapos solo reciban una mezquina caridad, instando a Trujillo a fundar industrias con salarios dignos y construir viviendas higiénicas para las familias de los barrios marginales.

records.headline: The artistic career of Mr. Lothar, who exhibited paintings at institutions
records.summary_en: The artistic career of Mr. Lothar, who exhibited paintings at institutions including the Phillips Gallery, the Corcoran Gallery, and the Pan American Union, an obituary outlines. Born in Vienna, where he studied at the Academy of Fine and Allied Arts prior to attending the School for Arts and Crafts in Zurich, he moved in 1940 to Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. He was subsequently appointed professor of painting in the school of fine arts at the University of Santo Domingo. Lothar later emigrated to the United States in 1947 to teach at the Hampton Institute.

Posteriormente fue nombrado profesor de pintura en la escuela de bellas artes de la Universidad de Santo Domingo. Más tarde, Lothar emigró a los Estados Unidos en 1947 para impartir docencia en el Instituto Hampton.

records.headline: State-controlled media organs in Ciudad Trujillo have incited
records.summary_en: State-controlled media organs in Ciudad Trujillo have incited violence against Bishop Thomas F. Reilly, C.SS.R., Prelate Nullius of San Juan de la Maguana, following his public denunciations of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo's regime for persecuting the Catholic Church and the Dominican populace. Two principal propaganda outlets attacked the bishop, warning that he and his clergy will soon be forced to depart. The broadcasts claimed that nationalist mobs are mobilizing to club the bishop inside his own church, adding an explicit wish that such mob violence occur promptly.
records.summary_es: Órganos de difusión controlados por el Estado en Ciudad Trujillo han incitado a la violencia contra el obispo Thomas F. Reilly, C.SS.R., prelado nullius de San Juan de la Maguana, tras sus denuncias públicas contra el régimen del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo por perseguir a la Iglesia católica y a la población dominicana. Dos de los principales medios propagandísticos atacaron al obispo, advirtiéndole que él y su clero pronto se verán obligados a marcharse. Las transmisiones afirmaron que turbas nacionalistas se están congregando para apalear al obispo dentro de su propia iglesia, expresando el deseo explícito de que dicha agresión ocurra sin demora.

records.headline: A long-standing feud between strongman Rafael Trujillo and the Roman Catholic hierarchy
records.summary_en: A long-standing feud between strongman Rafael Trujillo and the Roman Catholic hierarchy in the Dominican Republic flared anew following arrests made by the military intelligence service. The agency announced the capture of three alleged terrorists who reportedly confessed to working under the direction of Bishop Thomas F. Reilly of San Juan de Maguana. According to military authorities, the detainees alleged that Bishop Reilly ordered them to bomb several buildings in San Juan de Maguana, an accusation the prelate dismissed as absolutely untrue.
records.summary_es: Una prolongada disputa entre el hombre fuerte Rafael Trujillo y la jerarquía de la Iglesia católica en la República Dominicana resurgió tras una serie de detenciones practicadas por el servicio de inteligencia militar. El organismo estatal anunció la captura de tres presuntos terroristas que supuestamente confesaron operar bajo las órdenes del obispo Thomas F. Reilly de San Juan de Maguana. De acuerdo con las autoridades militares, los detenidos declararon que el obispo Reilly les ordenó dinamitar varios edificios en San Juan de Maguana, acusación que el prelado desmintió calificándola de absolutamente falsa.

records.full_text:
Pro-Trujillo Mobs Rout Bishop, Wreck Home

CIUDAD TRUJILLO, Dominican Republic, April 14 (AP).—Pro-Trujillo mobs have driven a Roman Catholic bishop to this capital after wrecking his Diocesan residence 100 miles west of here. Nuns and priests also are fleeing the district.

Bishop Thomas J. Reilly, 52, in trouble before with Dominican Dictator Rafael Trujillo, said police and soldiers put him in protective custody for a while yesterday after terrorists ransacked his home.

"I am going to deal with the government over these acts of terrorism," the prelate from Boston said after arriving in Ciudad Trujillo to take refuge in a Catholic school.

He said he will demand that the government guarantee the safety of priests and nuns in the Western part of the country, where his diocese of San Juan de la Manguana is located. Attacks on parishes there are forcing priests and nuns to come to the capital, the bishop said.

The mobs smashed doors and windows, destroyed furniture and records and battered three automobiles at the bishop's office and residence. Police and soldiers ended the attack.

"About all that was saved at my home were my sacred vestments," Bishop Reilly said. "No one can live there now."

The newspaper El Caribe said the attacks started after a priest got into a heated argument aver a pro-Trujillo business shutdown in San Juan de la Maguana. The shutdown was to protest "the machinations of the bishop against national sovereignty," El Caribe said.

The newspaper said pickets marched with banners proclaiming "We're with Trujillo" and "Down with Yankee terrorism." Two priests reportedly were attacked and their robes ripped off, but the bishop said he understood no one was seriously hurt.

The Trujillo-church dispute started last year with a pastoral letter in which the bishops urged Gen. Trujillo to ease what they called repressive measures. The hostility increased when the bishops rejected a Trujillo demand that the title "benefactor of the church" be added to the long list of titles he holds.

Bishop Reilly, a member of the Redemptorist Fathers, was consecrated a bishop in 1956. His 86-year-old mother and a sister live in Boston. His diocesan area is, like the entire Dominican Republic, about 90 per cent Catholic.

Aides Ousted as Aliens

In Washington, the National Catholic Welfare Conference said two aides of the bishop—Fathers John Schomber of Buffalo, N. Y., and John Kelly of Pittsburgh—have been ordered expelled from the Dominican Republic as undesirable aliens.

Bishop Reilly, whose brother Gerard D. Reilly is a Washington attorney, was assigned as an assistant pastor of the Annapolis church conducted by the Redemptorist Fathers in 1937 and 1938.

He had been a graduate student at Catholic University after his ordination, and was awarded a doctor of sacred theology degree in 1937.

records.headline: Asked whether the United States had helped maintain Latin American dictatorships
records.summary_en: Asked whether the United States had helped maintain Latin American dictatorships in power, Mr. Figueres stated that it had done so 'not deliberately, but certainly in fact.' He cited American support in past years for Batista in Cuba and Generalissimo Trujillo in the Dominican Republic as examples, asserting that without the United States, dictatorships and dynasties would have been eliminated long ago. Figueres said he had come to the White House to offer assistance to President Kennedy's Alliance for Progress program to promote hemispheric development, while noting his sympathies were with anti-Castro invaders in Cuba.

records.headline: An armed hijacker identifying himself as 'El Pirata Cofresi' hijacked
records.summary_en: An armed hijacker identifying himself as 'El Pirata Cofresi' hijacked a National Airlines plane over Florida and forced it to fly to Cuba with seven passengers aboard. The gunman told the pilot that Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic had offered him blood money to assassinate Fidel Castro, but claimed he had no intention of doing so because he considered Castro a 'good guy' and wished to 'spill the beans' to him. After the twin-engine airliner landed near Havana, Castro militiamen took the hijacker away, the aircraft was allowed to return to Florida, and the FBI launched an investigation into the man's identity.
records.summary_es: Un secuestrador armado que se identificó como 'El Pirata Cofresi' secuestró un avión de National Airlines sobre Florida y lo obligó a volar a Cuba con siete pasajeros a bordo. El pistolero le dijo al piloto que Rafael Trujillo, de la República Dominicana, le había ofrecido dinero manchado de sangre para asesinar a Fidel Castro, pero afirmó que no tenía intención de hacerlo porque consideraba a Castro un 'buen tipo' y quería contarle todo. Después de que el avión bimotor aterrizó cerca de La Habana, milicianos castristas se llevaron al secuestrador, se permitió que la aeronave regresara a Florida y el FBI inició una investigación sobre la identidad del individuo.

records.headline: An editorial criticizes the United States government for the emergence of a Communist beachhead
records.summary_en: An editorial criticizes the United States government for the emergence of a Communist beachhead near American shores, arguing that Washington has only itself to blame. The article asserts that failing to confront Castro, pulling the rug from under Trujillo in the Dominican Republic, and yielding to mob intimidation in Panama led the Kremlin to believe the United States had abandoned the Monroe Doctrine. It contends that these actions caused Latin American allies to doubt American resolve, citing President James Monroe's 1823 declaration and President Kennedy's remarks on national security.
records.summary_es: Un editorial critica al gobierno de los Estados Unidos por el surgimiento de una cabeza de playa comunista cerca de las costas estadounidenses, argumentando que Washington solo puede culparse a sí mismo. El artículo sostiene que no enfrentarse a Castro, quitarle el apoyo a Trujillo en la República Dominicana y ceder a la intimidación de las turbas en Panamá hicieron creer al Kremlin que Estados Unidos había abandonado la Doctrina Monroe. Afirma que estas acciones hicieron que los aliados latinoamericanos dudaran de la determinación estadounidense, citando la declaración de 1823 del presidente James Monroe y las declaraciones del presidente Kennedy sobre la seguridad nacional.

records.headline: Secretary of State Rusk departed from National Airport for Paris
records.summary_en: Secretary of State Rusk departed from National Airport for Paris, after being held back to handle the Dominican crisis during President Kennedy's meetings with European leaders. Before takeoff, Rusk stated that there was no way to determine at present what kind of government would ultimately take power in the Dominican Republic. United States authorities reported that information emerging from tightly censored Ciudad Trujillo indicated the Trujillo group, under figurehead President Joaquin Balaguer, remained in control of the country.

Autoridades de Estados Unidos informaron que los datos procedentes de una fuertemente censurada Ciudad Trujillo indicaban que el grupo trujillista, bajo el presidente títere Joaquín Balaguer, todavía mantenía el control del país.

records.full_text:
Change For Better Hoped
U.S. Watches Trend In D.R.

WASHINGTON (AP)—Secretary of State Dean Rusk set out today on his delayed trip to join President Kennedy in Europe, signalling a belief that the assassination of Dominican dictator Rafael L. Trujillo will not result in the immediate turmoil officials had feared.

Rusk had been scheduled to leave Wednesday to back up Kennedy in his talks in Paris with French President Charles de Gaulle and later in Vienna with Soviet Premier Khrushchev. Instead he was held here to take personal charge of dealing with the Dominican situation.

That decision underscored the anxiety with which American officials were watching for clues as to which way the Caribbean country will shift.

Rusk’s plane was due in Paris at 9 a.m. Paris time Friday.

Just before takeoff, Rusk told newsmen at National Airport that there is no way of knowing at this time what kind of government will finally take over in the Dominican Republic.

U.S. authorities said information seeping out from tightly censored Ciudad Trujillo indicated the Trujillo group, under figurehead President Jouquin Balaguer, still was in control.

President Kennedy and Rusk, in telephone contact between Paris and Washington, were said to be agreed that the Dominican situation was of such top priority that Rusk could do more by setting the U.S. course as the situation clears than by speeding off to the summit talks.

Informed sources said both the President and the secretary of state had the recent Cuban invasion fiasco very much in mind and were determined to avoid any mistake on the neighboring Caribbean island. They feel the outcome will affect the whole of U.S.-Latin American affairs.

Balking Washington strategists was a scarcity of solid information. Officials said they did not yet know who engineered the assassination or who might be behind the figurehead president who continued in office, Joaquin Balaguer. They said their evidence did not point to pro-Communist Cuba or other foreign manipulators.

The only post-assassination communication from the U.S. Consulate in Ciudad Trujillo reported by late Wednesday was a brief message from Consul General Henry Dearborn saying the capital was calm and he knew of no injury to the 5,200 citizens in the country.

Some U.S. authorities foresaw a struggle for power, both within the Trujillo group and between it and the large elements of Dominican society persecuted during the dictator’s 31-year rule. A continued harsh rightwing regime without Trujillo’s personal leadership, they reasoned, would set off revolt—perhaps pro-Castro the next time.

The United States had several lures to attract Trujillo’s successors down the democratic path, a main aim of Kennedy’s “alliance for progress” Latin American program.

One is resumption of U.S. aid, cut off when Washington joined the other American Republics last year in breaking diplomatic relations and normal commercial ties with Trujillo. Another is a boost in U.S. sugar purchases. The Dominican economy has been sagging.

The United States could also take a leading role in a move by the hemisphere organization, the Organization of American States, in readmitting a progressive Dominican regime to the American family.

Washington congressional reaction was mixed.

Sen. George Smathers, D-Fla., recommended that U.S. Marines be landed in the Dominican Republic to prevent a Communist takeover.

Sens. Homer E. Capehart, R-Ind., Olin D. Johnston, D-S.C., and Allen J. Ellender, D-La., saw a Red Castroite takeover in prospect as a result of Trujillo’s death.

records.headline: An editorial observes that the assassination of Generalissimo Rafael Leonidas Trujillo ended
records.summary_en: An editorial observes that the assassination of Generalissimo Rafael Leonidas Trujillo ended thirty-one years of dictatorial rule, warning that a dangerous power vacuum could spark conflict among left, right, and center factions across the Caribbean. Secretary of State Rusk delayed his flight to Vienna for summit talks at President Kennedy's request to monitor the explosive situation from Washington. While the late dictator's government, headed by President Joaquin Balaguer, appeared to remain in command, fragmentary reports pointed to army defections and potential rebellion following decades of corruption and terror.

records.full_text:
Trujillo Had Outlived His Brand of Tyranny

By JAMES MARLOW

Associated Press Staff Writer

This country's problem with the Dominican Republic is just beginning. The assassination of Dictator Rafael Leonidas Trujillo solved nothing.

The 69-year-old Gen. Trujillo, after 31 years of tyranny, had outlived his particular time.

The middle class had risen against him. Exiles had invaded him. The Catholic church had denounced him. And all Latin American nations had broken relations with him.

He survived as long as he did on sheer muscle at a time when social revolutions were sweeping not only Latin America but the world. What outdated him was this:

While all around him the masses of Latin America were demanding greater gratification of their desire for a better life and a better part in it, he kept his so-called republic frozen in the old ways.

Castro Is Modern

Fidel Castro in Cuba is no less a dictator, with the same contempt for democratic processes. But, beside Gen. Trujillo, he looks extremely modern with his promises of a richer life and a sense of belonging for the Cuban masses.

The United States misunderstood this and learned to its dismay, through the disaster of the April invasion, that many Cubans, promised better living, support Mr. Castro without apparent concern whether he's left or right.

It's an old lesson being relearned painfully around the world: Democracy to people who never really had it means nothing. What they want is to live longer and better.

Gen. Trujillo had some glimmering of the true nature of this wave of discontent which is sweeping over the dispossessed of Latin America. Like Mr. Castro, he pacified the peasants by parceling out land to them. They were docile.

Yet, the farmers scratched out a bare existence. The slum dwellers were ragged.

Became Wealthy

He parceled out little else. He lived in the past. In the end his berserk tyranny—mass arrests, persecutions, executions, repressions—was too excessive and became his undoing as it may become Mr. Castro's.

But he, his family and his friends got rich and fat off the republic. It's unlikely Gen. Trujillo's fat cats will yield control to some other outside, reform force without a struggle. So there may be bloody days.

If they triumph and set up another tyranny without broad reforms, it will be only a matter of time before they, too, are smashed. The sweep toward a richer life for Latin Americans is too strong for standstill reaction.

The real struggle eventually in the Dominican Republic will be between communism and this country. Meaning: The influence this country can bring to bear through economic aid and support for a reform government.

At this point it's impossible to say on which side the odds lie. It depends on how far the American Government is willing to go to keep communism out of the hemisphere.

Ripe for Invasion

The Kennedy administration insists it will not intervene in another nation's affairs but did just the opposite in backing the Cuban invasion.

The area in and around the Dominican Republic is getting ripe for explosion. Sharing the same island with it is Haiti, where living conditions and ignorance are appalling.

And right across the narrow strip of water, called the Windward Passage, is the Cuba of Mr. Castro, who back in 1949 took part in an invasion against Gen. Trujillo. The Dominican dictator demolsihed it.

But Mr. Castro now is in better position for invasion and subversion than he was in 1949 when he was simply a discontented nobody. If he is truly communism's assigned instrument in the Caribbean, he will move against the Haiti-Dominican island.

records.headline: Secretary of State Rusk departed for Paris at 12:10 p.m. to join
records.summary_en: Secretary of State Rusk departed for Paris at 12:10 p.m. to join President Kennedy's summit talks after officials concluded that Rafael Trujillo's assassination would not trigger immediate upheaval. Rusk had initially postponed his departure to oversee the Dominican crisis directly, noting that the position of Assistant Secretary of State for Latin American Affairs remained vacant. Prior to takeoff at National Airport, Rusk stated that while it remained impossible to predict what government would ultimately emerge, he resumed his trip because conditions in the Dominican capital were relatively quiet with no disturbances reported elsewhere.
records.summary_es: El secretario de Estado Rusk partió hacia París a las 12:10 p.m. para unirse a las conversaciones cumbre del presidente Kennedy, luego de que las autoridades determinaran que el asesinato de Rafael Trujillo no provocaría un desorden inmediato. Rusk había postergado inicialmente su salida para supervisar directamente la crisis dominicana, señalando que el puesto de subsecretario de Estado para Asuntos Latinoamericanos permanecía vacante. Antes de despegar en el Aeropuerto Nacional, Rusk declaró que, aunque resultaba imposible prever qué gobierno surgiría en definitiva, reanudaba su viaje debido a que la situación en la capital dominicana estaba relativamente en calma y sin disturbios reportados en otros lugares.

records.headline: A profile of Lieutenant General Rafael Trujillo Jr. details
records.summary_en: A profile of Lieutenant General Rafael Trujillo Jr. details his lavish expenditures in the United States, where he reportedly spent approximately $1 million annually—an amount rivaling total annual American aid to the Dominican Republic. During his stay, which included renting a $100,000 mansion for $2,500 a month, he purchased luxury Mercedes-Benz automobiles for Kim Novak and Zsa Zsa Gabor in 1958. Although the United States Army refused to graduate him from its command college due to excessive absences, his father appointed him chief of staff of all Dominican armed forces. Meanwhile, at the Dominican consulate, where staff had been reduced to five after Washington broke diplomatic relations, officials including Mr. Llaverias fielded continuous telephone inquiries following news of the elder Trujillo's assassination.
records.summary_es: Un perfil del teniente general Rafael Trujillo hijo detalla sus cuantiosos gastos en los Estados Unidos, donde según informes gastaba aproximadamente un millón de dólares al año, una suma equivalente a la ayuda anual estadounidense a la República Dominicana. Durante su estadía, que incluyó el alquiler de una mansión de 100.000 dólares por 2.500 dólares al mes, compró automóviles Mercedes-Benz de lujo para Kim Novak y Zsa Zsa Gabor en 1958. Aunque el Ejército de los Estados Unidos se negó a graduarlo de su academia de mando por inasistencias, su padre lo nombró jefe del estado mayor de todas las fuerzas armadas dominicanas. Entretanto, en el consulado dominicano, cuyo personal se redujo a cinco miembros tras la ruptura de relaciones diplomáticas, funcionarios como el señor Llaverias respondieron constantes llamadas telefónicas tras conocerse el asesinato del dictador.

records.headline: Legislation to seize Catholic schools; eliminate religious instruction
records.summary_en: Legislation to seize Catholic schools; eliminate religious instruction; renounce the 1954 concordat with the Holy See; and declare all Catholic churches the property of the state was introduced in the Dominican Congress. The anti-clerical bill, submitted to a legislature tightly controlled by Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, followed a May 17 motion seeking the expulsion of Massachusetts-born Bishop Thomas F. Reilly of San Juan de la Maguana and Spanish-born Bishop Francisco Panal of La Vega. Both prelates had publicly denounced the regime's reign of terror and church persecution, placing direct responsibility on Trujillo himself.

records.headline: Following the assassination of Rafael Trujillo, who had ruled
records.summary_en: Following the assassination of Rafael Trujillo, who had ruled for thirty-one years, the United States Immigration Service barred Dominican nationals and select American citizens from departing the United States for the Dominican Republic. In Funchal, Madeira, ousted Cuban dictator Fulgencio Batista declined to comment on the plot after hearing the news by radio. From Ciudad Trujillo, UPI correspondent Leo Peterson reported that the capital appeared calm with stores closed for Corpus Christi and armed troops stationed at the airport, while preparations were underway for Trujillo's funeral at San Cristobal Cathedral.
records.summary_es: Tras el asesinato de Rafael Trujillo, quien había gobernado durante treinta y un años, el Servicio de Inmigración de los Estados Unidos prohibió que ciudadanos dominicanos y determinados estadounidenses salieran del país con destino a la República Dominicana. En Funchal, Madeira, el derrocado dictador cubano Fulgencio Batista declinó hacer comentarios sobre el complot tras escuchar la noticia por radio. Desde Ciudad Trujillo, el corresponsal de UPI Leo Peterson informó que la capital parecía en calma, con comercios cerrados por el Corpus Christi y tropas armadas apostadas en el aeropuerto, mientras se preparaba el funeral de Trujillo en la catedral de San Cristóbal.

records.headline: An analytical commentary reflects on the geopolitical repercussions of Rafael Trujillo's
records.summary_en: An analytical commentary reflects on the geopolitical repercussions of Rafael Trujillo's assassination, noting that under past precedents, United States Marines would have deployed immediately to their former bases in San Domingo to counter Communist advances. The article argues that modern Communist tactics operate subtly through patriotic elements without offering clear pretexts for direct intervention, complicating diplomacy following the long-anticipated collapse of the Trujillo regime. While contrasting Trujillo's personal buccaneer-style rule in Hispaniola with Fidel Castro's alignment with foreign Communist powers, the piece notes that Trujillo will be mourned only by those he enriched.
records.summary_es: Un comentario analítico reflexiona sobre las repercusiones geopolíticas del asesinato de Rafael Trujillo, señalando que, bajo precedentes anteriores, los infantes de marina de los Estados Unidos se habrían desplegado de inmediato en sus antiguas bases de San Domingo para contrarrestar los avances comunistas. El artículo sostiene que las tácticas comunistas modernas operan sutilmente a través de elementos patrióticos sin ofrecer pretextos claros para una intervención directa, lo que complica la diplomacia tras el largamente previsto colapso del régimen de Trujillo. Al contrastar el dominio personal de estilo bucanero de Trujillo en La Española con la alineación de Fidel Castro con potencias comunistas extranjeras, la nota señala que Trujillo solo será llorado por aquellos a quienes enriqueció.

records.headline: A national news summary reports that Rafael L. Trujillo, dictator of the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: A national news summary reports that Rafael L. Trujillo, dictator of the Dominican Republic for thirty-one years, was assassinated on Tuesday. The official announcement of his death was delayed until Wednesday, hours after the fatal ambush took place. The dictator was apparently shot to death while driving from his home toward Ciudad Trujillo, the capital city named in his honor.
records.summary_es: Un resumen de noticias nacionales informa que Rafael L. Trujillo, dictador de la República Dominicana durante treinta y un años, fue asesinado el martes. El anuncio oficial de su muerte se retrasó hasta el miércoles, horas después de que ocurriera la emboscada fatal. Al parecer, el dictador fue muerto a tiros mientras conducía desde su residencia hacia Ciudad Trujillo, la ciudad capital que llevaba su nombre.

records.headline: An editorial in Diario las Américas observes that the assassination of Rafael Leonidas Trujillo y Molina
records.summary_en: An editorial in Diario las Américas observes that the assassination of Rafael Leonidas Trujillo y Molina, the dean of Latin American dictators, carries profound continental ramifications for democracy's future. The commentary characterizes Trujillo's thirty-year regime as the most ruthless right-wing tyranny in the hemisphere, marked by domestic absolutism and extraterritorial persecutions including assassinations and cross-border abductions. Stressing that the Inter-American system must remain vigilant to prevent Communist exploitation, the paper urges moral and material assistance to help the Dominican people reconstitute a democratic republic.
records.summary_es: Un editorial en Diario las Américas señala que el asesinato de Rafael Leonidas Trujillo y Molina, decano de los dictadores latinoamericanos, tiene profundas repercusiones continentales para el porvenir de la democracia. El comentario califica el régimen de treinta años de Trujillo como la tiranía de derecha más despiadada del hemisferio, marcada por el absolutismo interno y persecuciones extraterritoriales que incluyeron asesinatos y secuestros en el extranjero. Al subrayar que el sistema interamericano debe mantenerse en guardia para evitar el aprovechamiento comunista, el periódico insta a brindar ayuda moral y material para ayudar al pueblo dominicano a reorganizarse como república democrática.

records.headline: Following the assassination last week of dictator Rafael L. Trujillo
records.summary_en: Following the assassination last week of dictator Rafael L. Trujillo, United States military forces along the Eastern seaboard have been placed on alert, with additional Marine and naval units deployed to the Caribbean on standby. Government officials emphasized that while no decision has been taken to intervene, intervention is not ruled out if the lives of the 5,200 Americans on the island are endangered. Although reports indicate that no Americans have been harmed during crackdowns against the Dominican opposition by Trujillo's successors, mounting repression has heightened official concern. In addition, official sources announced that the seven-member Sanctions Committee of the Organization of American States will meet to discuss sending a mission.
records.summary_es: Tras el asesinato la semana pasada del dictador Rafael L. Trujillo, las fuerzas militares de Estados Unidos a lo largo de la costa oriental fueron puestas en alerta, con unidades adicionales de la infantería de marina y la armada desplegadas en el Caribe en estado de espera. Funcionarios gubernamentales enfatizaron que, aunque no se ha tomado ninguna decisión de intervenir, no se descarta la intervención si peligran las vidas de los 5,200 estadounidenses en la isla. Si bien los informes indican que ningún estadounidense ha sufrido daños durante las medidas de fuerza contra la oposición dominicana por parte de los sucesores de Trujillo, la creciente represión ha aumentado la preocupación oficial. Además, fuentes oficiales anunciaron que el Comité de Sanciones de siete miembros de la Organización de los Estados Americanos se reunirá para debatir el envío de una misión.

records.headline: A continuing report outlines three basic aims of American policy
records.summary_en: A continuing report outlines three basic aims of American policy for the post-Trujillo Dominican Republic. The specified objectives call for a government moving toward representative democracy, a government that does not threaten the peace and security of its neighbors, and a government that complies with inter-American treaties in defending the hemisphere against extracontinental powers.

Los objetivos especificados exigen un gobierno que avance hacia la democracia representativa, un gobierno que no amenace la paz y seguridad de sus vecinos y un gobierno que cumpla con los tratados interamericanos en la defensa del hemisferio frente a potencias extracontinentales.

records.summary_en: Speaking at a news conference, the Dominican Republic's new 32-year-old armed forces chief, son of the slain generalissimo, described Diaz as an ignorant, heavy-drinking traitor who could never have taken over the nation because he lacked standing in the military. Trujillo stated that Diaz, aged 52, had been retired the previous year due to seniority and poor personal conduct, adding that while Diaz was strictly a traitor, other conspirators participated because of political ideologies. He noted that Diaz and the generalissimo were born in the same city of San Cristobal and that the two families had maintained a close friendship for many years. Trujillo added he learned of Diaz's motive of revenge from three men now under arrest on charges of directly participating in the killing; one other person directly involved has been killed, and three are still at large. The armed forces were not involved in the plot, Trujillo declared, and he emphasized his friendship for the U.S. government. This capital appeared calm; censorship on news dispatches out of the country has ended and telephone communication restored with other nations. Friday night, rampaging mobs stoned a Roman Catholic church and invaded headquarters of an opposition political movement; about 2,000 screaming men and women armed with sticks and stones threatened to burn the church of a priest accused of sheltering one of the captured. The crowd dispersed when police arrived and said the priest had been taken into protective custody; the church was not damaged.
records.summary_es: En una conferencia de prensa, el nuevo jefe de las fuerzas armadas de la República Dominicana, de 32 años e hijo del asesinado generalísimo, calificó a Díaz como un traidor ignorante y bebedor empedernido que jamás habría podido tomar el control del país porque carecía de prestigio militar. Trujillo afirmó que Díaz, de 52 años, había sido retirado el año anterior por antigüedad y mala conducta personal, y agregó que, mientras Díaz era estrictamente un traidor, otros conspiradores participaron debido a ideologías políticas. Señaló que Díaz y el generalísimo habían nacido en la misma ciudad de San Cristóbal y que las dos familias habían mantenido una estrecha amistad durante muchos años. Trujillo añadió que supo del móvil de venganza de Díaz por tres hombres ya detenidos bajo cargos de participación directa en el asesinato; otra persona directamente implicada había muerto, y tres seguían en libertad. Las fuerzas armadas no estuvieron implicadas en la conspiración, declaró Trujillo, y subrayó su amistad con el gobierno de los Estados Unidos. La capital parecía en calma; la censura sobre los despachos noticiosos al exterior había terminado y la comunicación telefónica con otros países se había restablecido. El viernes por la noche, turbas enfurecidas apedrearon una iglesia católica e invadieron la sede de un movimiento político de oposición; cerca de 2,000 hombres y mujeres gritando, armados con palos y piedras, amenazaron con quemar la iglesia de un sacerdote acusado de dar refugio a uno de los capturados. La multitud se dispersó cuando llegó la policía y dijo que el sacerdote había sido puesto bajo custodia protectora; la iglesia no resultó dañada.

records.headline: In preparing for an inter-American meeting in Montevideo, a United States envoy
records.summary_en: In preparing for an inter-American meeting in Montevideo, a United States envoy will limit his tour to the South American continent and will bypass both Cuba and the Dominican Republic as both nations recover from the shock of Dictator Rafael Trujillo's assassination. The report notes that the envoy will nonetheless encounter unrest across South America, including a crushed coup attempt against President Romulo Betancourt in Venezuela, pro-Castro student strikes in Colombia, and expanding trade with the Communist bloc under President Janio Quadros in Brazil.
records.summary_es: Al preparar una reunión interamericana en Montevideo, un enviado de Estados Unidos limitará su gira al continente sudamericano y omitirá tanto a Cuba como a la República Dominicana mientras ambas naciones se recuperan del impacto del asesinato del dictador Rafael Trujillo. El informe señala que el enviado encontrará no obstante agitación en toda Sudamérica, incluido un intento de golpe sofocado contra el presidente Rómulo Betancourt en Venezuela, huelgas estudiantiles castristas en Colombia y la expansión del comercio con el bloque comunista bajo el presidente Jânio Quadros en Brasil.

By WILLIAM R. FRYE
Contributing Writer
UNITED nations, n. Y.—lt
always is difficult to separate fact
from fancy when heads of state
come together. Pomp and cere
monial glitter combine to stimulate
the golden trumpets of the propa
gandists, and presently perspec
tive, logic, and good sense have
vanished.
Some of the fancy surrounding
the Khrushchev-Kennedy meeting
has been very fanciful indeed. The
affair has even been compared to
the meeting in 1807 between Na
poleon and Czar Alexander I on a
raft in the Niemen River at Tilsit,
when France and Russia virtually
established a condominium over
Europe.
Nothing of the sort, of course,
is happening in Vienna. A bright
young man who is not quite sure
where he is going is sitting down
with a tough, histrionic man 20
years his senior who is very sure
indeed where he wants to go.
They are not talking each other
into hocking the family Jewels.
President Kennedy is not likely
suddenly to abandon West Berlin,
nor Premier Khrushchev the veto.
They certainly are not carving up
the world into spheres of influence.

records.summary_en: Continuing a regional review, the passage notes that Hispaniola would be a mere tourist stop between Cuba and Puerto Rico without dictators and revolutions. It recounts that the Republic of Haiti, occupying the western third of the island, experienced 130 revolutions in the last 150 years and has been ruled since 1957 by Dr. Francois Duvalier with shortsightedness and inefficiency. Until 1930, the Dominican Republic shared an equally chaotic history until a young, efficient officer seized power, beginning Rafael Trujillo's 31-year rule, which the article characterizes as the most cold-blooded reign in Latin America.
records.summary_es: Al continuar una crónica regional, el pasaje señala que La Española sería una simple escala turística entre Cuba y Puerto Rico, sin dictadores y revoluciones. Hasta 1930, la República Dominicana compartió una historia igualmente caótica hasta que un oficial joven y eficiente tomó el poder, iniciando el mandato de 31 años de Rafael Trujillo, al que el artículo describe como el régimen más despiadado de América Latina.

records.headline: A continuing analysis reports that Rafael Trujillo retained
records.summary_en: A continuing analysis reports that Rafael Trujillo retained power through methods ranging from underworld slayings to a strictly controlled press, with foes asserting that thousands of opponents were murdered or executed on his word alone. The article recalls that conditions deteriorated to the point where the United States broke off diplomatic relations with the republic last August. Furthermore, the Trujillo family not only dominated Dominican politics but also commanded every sector of the national economy while gaining notoriety as international playboys, culminating in his son, Rafael Jr., taking immediate control following the assassination.

El artículo recuerda que las condiciones se deterioraron a tal punto que Estados Unidos rompió relaciones diplomáticas con la república en agosto pasado. Asimismo, la familia Trujillo no solo dominaba la política dominicana sino que controlaba todos los sectores de la economía nacional mientras ganaba notoriedad como playboys internacionales, culminando con la toma inmediata del control por parte de su hijo, Rafael hijo, tras el asesinato.

records.headline: The concluding column of a news analysis reports that Washington's immediate
records.summary_en: The concluding column of a news analysis reports that Washington's immediate concern centered on a potential Castro-type coup, though the Dominican Republic's strongly anti-Communist army appeared capable of repelling any communist invasion. With no indication of immediate democratic reforms, the United States showed no urgency to restore diplomatic ties with Ciudad Trujillo, aligning instead with progressive Latin American leaders urging the Dominican populace to establish a democratic government. Meanwhile, the Organization of American States prepared to convene to evaluate deploying a watchdog committee, while alerted United States military forces in the Caribbean were kept on standby without plans for armed intervention.

Al no haber indicios de reformas democráticas inmediatas, Estados Unidos no mostró prisa en restablecer lazos diplomáticos con Ciudad Trujillo, alineándose en cambio con líderes progresistas latinoamericanos que instaban al pueblo dominicano a fundar un gobierno democrático. Entretanto, la Organización de los Estados Americanos se dispuso a reunirse para evaluar el envío de un comité de vigilancia, mientras que fuerzas militares estadounidenses alertadas en el Caribe permanecían en espera sin planes de intervención armada.

records.headline: A seven-nation committee of the Organization of American States prepared
records.summary_en: A seven-nation committee of the Organization of American States prepared to vote on a United States proposal to dispatch a mission to determine whether the Dominican Republic remains a threat to hemispheric peace following the Trujillo regime's condemnation last year at San Jose, Costa Rica. Militarily, the United States directed the amphibious assault ship Boxer, carrying an estimated 1,000 combat-ready Marines, to reinforce two naval carriers and a 2,000-man Marine battalion landing team already stationed in the Caribbean. Although no incidents have been reported concerning the 8,200 Americans residing in the Dominican Republic, the Navy appeared prepared for potential evacuations, with both the State and Defense departments declining to comment.

En el plano militar, Estados Unidos envió el buque de asalto anfibio Boxer, que transportaba a unos 1,000 infantes de marina listos para el combate, para reforzar a dos portaaviones navales y a un equipo de desembarco de batallón de 2,000 infantes de marina ya apostados en el Caribe. Aunque no se han registrado incidentes relativos a los 8,200 estadounidenses que residen en la República Dominicana, la armada parecía preparada para posibles evacuaciones, mientras que los departamentos de Estado y Defensa declinaron hacer comentarios.

records.headline: Police launched a downtown search after a tip placed Juan Tomas Diaz
records.summary_en: Police launched a downtown search after a tip placed Juan Tomas Diaz and Antonio de la Maza on a street, with a fatal gun battle erupting thirty minutes after the fugitives were refused entry into a residence. During the operation, police cordoned off neighborhood crowds and briefly detained a Puerto Rican correspondent and a Berlin photographer. Armed forces chief General Rafael L. Trujillo Jr. asserted that Diaz led the assassination plot out of bitterness over his forced army retirement, while authorities accounted for the eight-member band as two killed, three captured, and four at large. Meanwhile, in Hollywood, actress Kim Novak disclosed sending a telegram offering prayers and support to Rafael Trujillo Jr., recalling their association in Southern California three years earlier.
records.summary_es: La policía desplegó una búsqueda en el centro de la ciudad tras recibir un aviso de que Juan Tomás Díaz y Antonio de la Maza estaban en una calle, desatándose un tiroteo mortal treinta minutos después de que a los fugitivos se les negara la entrada a una residencia. Durante el operativo, la policía contuvo a multitudes del vecindario y detuvo brevemente a un corresponsal puertorriqueño y a un fotógrafo berlinés. El jefe de las fuerzas armadas, general Rafael L. Trujillo hijo, afirmó que Díaz encabezó el complot de asesinato por resentimiento tras su retiro forzado del ejército, mientras las autoridades informaban sobre la banda de ocho miembros: dos muertos, tres capturados y cuatro prófugos. Entretanto, en Hollywood, la actriz Kim Novak reveló haber enviado un telegrama con oraciones y apoyo a Rafael Trujillo hijo, recordando sus encuentros en el sur de California tres años antes.

records.headline: Responding to reports of wide-scale repressions by Trujillo's
records.summary_en: Responding to reports of wide-scale repressions by Trujillo's successors, the seven-member Sanctions Committee of the Organization of American States met for one hour and fifteen minutes and designated delegates from Panama, Uruguay, and the United States to confer with the Dominican Foreign Minister on terms for a fact-finding mission. The committee was originally created after the August 1960 foreign ministers meeting in San Jose, Costa Rica, which severed diplomatic relations and applied partial economic sanctions against the regime. During the session, Venezuela circulated a declaration insisting that the Dominican government has not changed and demanding an extraordinary OAS Council meeting to mandate the release of political prisoners, free elections, and the return of political exiles.
records.summary_es: En respuesta a informes sobre represiones a gran escala por parte de los sucesores de Trujillo, el Comité de Sanciones de siete miembros de la Organización de los Estados Americanos se reunió durante una hora y quince minutos y designó a delegados de Panamá, Uruguay y Estados Unidos para deliberar con el canciller dominicano sobre las condiciones de una misión de investigación. El comité fue creado originalmente tras la reunión de ministros de relaciones exteriores de agosto de 1960 en San José, Costa Rica, que rompió relaciones diplomáticas y aplicó sanciones económicas parciales contra el régimen. Durante la sesión, Venezuela distribuyó una declaración en la que sostenía que el gobierno dominicano no ha cambiado y exigía una reunión extraordinaria del Consejo de la OEA para ordenar la liberación de presos políticos, elecciones libres y el regreso de los exiliados políticos.

records.headline: President Joaquin Balaguer announced to reporters that he is prepared
records.summary_en: President Joaquin Balaguer announced to reporters that he is prepared to reopen the investigation into the 1956 disappearance of Dr. Jesus de Galindez and the related case of Gerald Murphy, who reportedly flew a stretcher case from New York to Florida en route to the Dominican Republic. While promising new policies following General Trujillo's death, Balaguer indicated that no major political announcements would occur before the conclusion of the nine-day official mourning period on Thursday. Balaguer emphasized his desire to liberalize Dominican political life and re-establish relations with Western Hemisphere nations, particularly the United States, after OAS sanctions cut off vital oil supplies and damaged the domestic economy.
records.summary_es: El presidente Joaquín Balaguer anunció a los periodistas que está dispuesto a reabrir la investigación sobre la desaparición en 1956 del doctor Jesús de Galíndez y el caso conexo de Gerald Murphy, quien según informes transportó a una persona en camilla en un vuelo desde Nueva York hacia Florida en ruta a la República Dominicana. Si bien prometió nuevas políticas tras la muerte del general Trujillo, Balaguer indicó que no se producirían anuncios políticos de importancia antes de finalizar el período de duelo oficial de nueve días el jueves. Balaguer subrayó su deseo de liberalizar la vida política dominicana y restablecer relaciones con las naciones del hemisferio occidental, en particular con Estados Unidos, después de que las sanciones de la OEA interrumpieran los suministros vitales de petróleo y perjudicaran la economía nacional.

records.headline: A political commentary asserts that the United States must assume
records.summary_en: A political commentary asserts that the United States must assume its hemispheric leadership and act immediately to fill the power vacuum in the Dominican Republic following the fall of Rafael Trujillo. Endorsing proposals put forward by Senator George Smathers of Florida, the column advocates making an appeal to the Organization of American States to deploy a collective security force, or otherwise sending United States troops directly. The author argues that military intervention would be entirely justified to prevent civil war, establish constabulary order, and guarantee genuinely free elections within twelve months to enable the Dominican public to choose a new government.
records.summary_es: Un comentario político afirma que Estados Unidos debe asumir su liderazgo hemisférico y actuar de inmediato para llenar el vacío de poder en la República Dominicana tras la caída de Rafael Trujillo. Al respaldar propuestas presentadas por el senador George Smathers de Florida, la columna aboga por apelar a la Organización de los Estados Americanos para desplegar una fuerza de seguridad colectiva, o bien enviar tropas estadounidenses de manera directa. El autor sostiene que una intervención militar estaría enteramente justificada para impedir una guerra civil, establecer el orden policial y garantizar elecciones genuinamente libres en un plazo de doce meses que permitan a la ciudadanía dominicana elegir un nuevo gobierno.

records.headline: Diplomats in Washington are adopting a wait-and-see attitude
records.summary_en: Diplomats in Washington are adopting a wait-and-see attitude toward overtures by Dominican leaders seeking readmission to the Organization of American States. President Joaquin Balaguer hinted that free elections scheduled for next May might justify lifting sanctions, while armed forces chief Rafael Trujillo Jr. professed friendship for the United States and denied persistent allegations of widespread repression. Diplomats interpret the sudden arrival of Dominican Foreign Minister Herrera Baez as a holding action, though he assured the seven-member sanctions committee that his government will welcome and cooperate with a proposed fact-finding committee designed to protect liberal opponents.
records.summary_es: Diplomáticos en Washington han adoptado una actitud de cautela frente a las propuestas de líderes dominicanos que buscan el reingreso a la Organización de los Estados Americanos. El presidente Joaquín Balaguer insinuó que las elecciones libres programadas para mayo próximo podrían justificar el levantamiento de las sanciones, mientras que el jefe de las fuerzas armadas, Rafael Trujillo hijo, declaró amistad hacia Estados Unidos y negó persistentes denuncias de represión generalizada. Los diplomáticos interpretan la repentina llegada del canciller dominicano Herrera Báez como una maniobra dilatoria, aunque este aseguró al comité de sanciones de siete miembros que su gobierno acogerá y cooperará con una comisión de investigación propuesta para proteger a los opositores liberales.
