records.headline: Opposition leader Fiallo charged that the Balaguer government
records.summary_en: Opposition leader Fiallo charged that the Balaguer government is a continuation of the Trujillo regime supported by the same reactionaries Balaguer had previously repudiated. Fiallo made his statement as a general strike aimed at toppling Balaguer showed signs of weakening after paralyzing the country for four days. While businesses remained entirely shut down in Santiago and central Santo Domingo, vehicular traffic increased and stores reopened in outlying areas and in San Cristobal, the birthplace of the late Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo. Balaguer was installed as president by Trujillo but has avowed a policy of gradual democratization and liberalization since the generalissimo was assassinated on May 30. Fiallo said that if the Organization of American States lifted its present sanctions against the Dominican Republic to ease Balaguer's situation, it would be “the destruction of the nation.” His headquarters announced the opposition was willing to resume negotiations with the government on a formula to solve the grave national crisis over formation of a new government, but on condition that opposition information media be restored. The radio chain of the National Civic Union, which claims to be a nonpartisan organization, was shut down several days ago after it made a blistering attack on Gen. Pedro Rodriguez Echavarria, the new army chief who blocked a coup by Trujillo's brothers two weeks ago.
records.summary_es: El líder opositor Fiallo denunció que el gobierno de Balaguer es una continuación del régimen de Trujillo, respaldado por los mismos reaccionarios que Balaguer había repudiado anteriormente. Fiallo hizo estas declaraciones mientras una huelga general destinada a derrocar a Balaguer mostraba señales de debilitamiento tras paralizar el país durante cuatro días. Si bien los comercios permanecieron completamente cerrados en Santiago y en el centro de Santo Domingo, el tráfico vehicular aumentó y las tiendas reabrieron en zonas periféricas y en San Cristóbal, lugar de nacimiento del fenecido generalísimo Rafael Trujillo. Balaguer fue instalado como presidente por Trujillo, pero ha proclamado una política de democratización y liberalización gradual desde que el generalísimo fue asesinado el 30 de mayo. Fiallo dijo que si la Organización de los Estados Americanos levantaba sus actuales sanciones contra la República Dominicana para aliviar la situación de Balaguer, sería «la destrucción de la nación». Su sede anunció que la oposición estaba dispuesta a reanudar las negociaciones con el gobierno sobre una fórmula para resolver la grave crisis nacional en torno a la formación de un nuevo gobierno, pero con la condición de que se restablecieran los medios de información de la oposición. La cadena de radio de la Unión Cívica Nacional, que dice ser una organización no partidista, fue clausurada varios días atrás después de lanzar un ataque fulminante contra el general Pedro Rodríguez Echavarría, el nuevo jefe del ejército que bloqueó un golpe de los hermanos de Trujillo dos semanas atrás.

records.headline: In the Dominican Republic, a news analysis reviews the political situation
records.summary_en: In the Dominican Republic, a news analysis reviews the political situation following efforts to force President Joaquin Balaguer to resign from office. Balaguer, previously the puppet president under dictator General Rafael Trujillo, sought to organize a middle-of-the-road government combining himself and moderate opposition parties that emerged after Trujillo's assassination in May. However, the opposition parties refused to participate until Balaguer expelled the right-wing Trujillo clan members who controlled the military and the national economy. In Washington, the apparent initial solution was to force out the Trujillos to facilitate a compromise government. Two weeks ago, when Mr. Balaguer was threatened by a Trujillo brothers coup, the United States sent warships to the area in support of Mr. Balaguer; the show of force worked, and the coup was destroyed before it started — the Trujillos left the country. This, according to most observers, should have led the way to a coalition cabinet, but it didn't: the same mass of citizenry that had poured into the streets to cheer the expulsion of the Trujillos returned a few days later to call for Mr. Balaguer's resignation. The opposition still fears that Mr. Balaguer is too closely affiliated with the former Trujillo dictatorship; they want him to resign and appoint a caretaker government representing the opposition, whose strength comes from the republic's middle class. Mr. Balaguer has refused, stating that his resignation would lead to chaos; he wants a coalition government until next spring's general elections. The Dominican people, tasting freedom for the first time in 30 years, have been marching through the streets all week, participating in a general strike aimed at forcing Mr. Balaguer out; the military, however, has supported the President, and wants a seven-man junta set up to end the “chaos.” So far, violence has been kept to a minimum. At the end of the week Washington feared that the moderate Balaguer government might be forced to turn even more to the military for support, creating another dictatorship; this in turn might lead to an invasion by Castro forces in the name of “freedom.” Observers hope that the opposition and Mr. Balaguer can patch up their differences before the situation gets out of hand.
records.summary_es: En la República Dominicana, un análisis periodístico examina la situación política tras las gestiones para obligar al presidente Joaquín Balaguer a renunciar a su cargo. Balaguer, anteriormente presidente títere bajo el dictador general Rafael Trujillo, intentaba organizar un gobierno centrista que lo representara a él y a los partidos de oposición moderada surgidos tras el asesinato de Trujillo en mayo. No obstante, las agrupaciones opositoras se negaron a participar hasta que Balaguer expulsara a los miembros derechistas del clan Trujillo, quienes controlaban las fuerzas armadas y la economía nacional. En Washington, la aparente solución inicial consistía en expulsar a los Trujillo para facilitar un gobierno de compromiso. Hace dos semanas, cuando el señor Balaguer se vio amenazado por un golpe de los hermanos Trujillo, los Estados Unidos enviaron buques de guerra a la zona en apoyo del señor Balaguer; la demostración de fuerza funcionó y el golpe fue destruido antes de comenzar: los Trujillo abandonaron el país. Esto, según la mayoría de los observadores, debería haber abierto el camino a un gabinete de coalición, pero no fue así: la misma masa ciudadana que había salido a las calles a celebrar la expulsión de los Trujillo regresó pocos días después para pedir la renuncia del señor Balaguer. La oposición sigue temiendo que el señor Balaguer esté demasiado vinculado a la antigua dictadura de Trujillo; quiere que renuncie y nombre un gobierno provisional que represente a la oposición, cuya fuerza procede de la clase media de la república. El señor Balaguer se ha negado, afirmando que su renuncia conduciría al caos; quiere un gobierno de coalición hasta las elecciones generales de la próxima primavera. El pueblo dominicano, que saborea la libertad por primera vez en 30 años, ha estado marchando por las calles toda la semana, participando en una huelga general destinada a forzar la salida del señor Balaguer; los militares, sin embargo, han apoyado al presidente y quieren que se establezca una junta de siete hombres para poner fin al «caos». Hasta ahora, la violencia se ha mantenido al mínimo. Al final de la semana, Washington temía que el moderado gobierno de Balaguer pudiera verse obligado a apoyarse aún más en los militares, creando otra dictadura; esto, a su vez, podría conducir a una invasión de fuerzas castristas en nombre de la «libertad». Los observadores esperan que la oposición y el señor Balaguer puedan resolver sus diferencias antes de que la situación se salga de control.

records.headline: The general strike that was even more effective there than in Santo
records.summary_en: The general strike that was even more effective there than in Santo Domingo, travelers returning from Santiago and the Cibao Valley reported, aimed at ousting President Joaquin Balaguer, with Santiago employee groups threatening mass resignations if shopkeepers are penalized. Main opposition groups remained firm in demanding Balaguer's resignation in favor of a provisional regime purged of Trujillo holdovers. Meanwhile, in the capital, anti-government crowds turned back a band of approximately 20 hoodlums led by two policemen and an air force officer with a machine gun who attempted to instigate looting in shuttered shopping districts. Although troops were withdrawn from riot duty, military personnel used loudspeakers to invite slum residents to break into stores, resulting in at least five individuals wounded by noise bomb fragments, one man shot in the thigh, and a shopkeeper beaten.

records.summary_en: Associated Press correspondent Robert Berrellez reported from Santo Domingo that anti-government crowds repelled a band of about 20 hoodlums on Monday, thwarting an army and police effort to incite mob violence against a week-old general strike aimed at toppling President Joaquin Balaguer. The armed forces had withdrawn all riot troops from the capital while soldiers with loudspeakers toured slum sections urging residents to break into shuttered businesses, but only a small gang led by two uniformed policemen and an air force officer with a machine gun responded. A large crowd clashed with the club-wielding band using rocks and slingshots, leaving at least five persons wounded by noise bomb fragments, one man shot in the thigh, and a shopkeeper beaten. Riot troops returned in force as the sundown curfew approached, and scattered explosions were heard across the city later that night.
records.summary_es: El corresponsal de Associated Press Robert Berrellez informó desde Santo Domingo que multitudes antigubernamentales repelieron el lunes a una banda de unos 20 maleantes, frustrando un intento del ejército y la policía de incitar a la violencia callejera contra la huelga general de una semana que buscaba derrocar al presidente Joaquín Balaguer. Las fuerzas armadas habían retirado a todas las tropas antimotines de la capital mientras soldados con altavoces recorrían zonas marginales instando a la población a asaltar comercios cerrados, pero solo respondió una pequeña banda liderada por dos policías uniformados y un oficial de la fuerza aérea con una ametralladora. Una gran multitud se enfrentó a la banda armada con garrotes utilizando piedras y hondas, dejando al menos cinco personas heridas por esquirlas de bombas de ruido, un hombre herido de bala en el muslo y un comerciante golpeado. Las tropas antimotines regresaron en gran número al acercarse el toque de queda al atardecer, y más tarde esa noche se escucharon explosiones aisladas en varias partes de la ciudad.

records.headline: Opposition leaflets distributed in Santo Domingo urged citizens
records.summary_en: Opposition leaflets distributed in Santo Domingo urged citizens to conduct a silent mass march on the National Palace to demand the resignation of President Joaquin Balaguer. The appeal circulated while opposition figures and government officials held lengthy overnight talks seeking to resolve a political crisis marked by a general strike and persistent disorder. Although negotiations recessed without an agreement, opposition leaders expressed optimism regarding a new formula for replacing Balaguer's government, having previously resisted a government proposal for a five- or seven-member junta in which Balaguer would remain chief executive. It was learned privately that Balaguer did not participate directly in the discussions due to an illness described by spokesmen as slight.
records.summary_es: Volantes de la oposición distribuidos en Santo Domingo instaron a los ciudadanos a realizar una marcha masiva y silenciosa hacia el Palacio Nacional para exigir la renuncia del presidente Joaquín Balaguer. El llamado circuló mientras representantes de la oposición y del gobierno sostenían prolongadas conversaciones nocturnas para resolver una crisis política marcada por una huelga general y continuos desórdenes. Aunque las negociaciones entraron en receso sin llegar a un acuerdo, los dirigentes opositores manifestaron optimismo respecto a una nueva fórmula para reemplazar al gobierno de Balaguer, habiéndose resistido previamente a una propuesta gubernamental de una junta de cinco o siete miembros en la que Balaguer permanecería como jefe del ejecutivo. Se supo de manera extraoficial que Balaguer no participó directamente en las deliberaciones debido a una enfermedad que sus portavoces calificaron de leve.

records.headline: In downtown Santo Domingo, crowds gathered to boo President Joaquin
records.summary_en: In downtown Santo Domingo, crowds gathered to boo President Joaquin Balaguer, following his rejection of an opposition proposal to resolve the national crisis. Although political leaders resumed talks, the National Civic Union warned it would withdraw if an agreement was not reached, insisting on a timetable that required Balaguer to resign before December 31. The opposition plan further stipulated elections for a Constituent Assembly on August 16, congressional elections on December 1, 1962, and the installation of a new government on January 26, 1963. Shops remained closed on the eleventh day of the nationwide general strike, which coincided with the Feast of the Immaculate Conception, while opposition sources also demanded the replacement of armed forces chief General Pedro Rodriguez Echavarria.
records.summary_es: En el centro de Santo Domingo, multitudes se congregaron para abuchear al presidente Joaquín Balaguer, tras su rechazo a una propuesta opositora para resolver la crisis nacional. Aunque los dirigentes políticos reanudaron el diálogo, la Unión Cívica Nacional advirtió que se retiraría si no se lograba un acuerdo ese mismo día, insistiendo en un calendario que exigía la renuncia de Balaguer antes del 31 de diciembre. El plan opositor estipulaba además elecciones para una Asamblea Constituyente el 16 de agosto, comicios legislativos el 1 de diciembre de 1962 y la instalación de un nuevo gobierno el 26 de enero de 1963. Los comercios continuaron cerrados en el undécimo día de la huelga general nacional, que coincidió con la fiesta de la Inmaculada Concepción, mientras fuentes opositoras demandaban también la sustitución del jefe de las fuerzas armadas, general Pedro Rodríguez Echavarría.

records.headline: National Civic Union leader Viriato A. Fiallo announced that an agreement
records.summary_en: National Civic Union leader Viriato A. Fiallo announced that an agreement had been reached with the government to resolve the Dominican Republic's political crisis through the creation of a seven-man Council of State presided over by President Joaquin Balaguer for a limited period. The compromise excluded board members of the opposition movement and officials connected to the regime from serving on the council. Accord was achieved at about 2:30 a.m. following an all-night vigil observed by United States Consul General John Calvin Hill and Deputy Assistant Secretary of State Arturo Morales Carrion. Nicholas E. Pichardo, president of the University Professors' Association and a strike leader, served as principal mediator, and the opposition radio network Voz Del Tropico announced that the twelve-day general strike had ended.

Fiallo, anunció que se había alcanzado un acuerdo con el gobierno para solucionar la crisis política de la República Dominicana mediante la creación de un Consejo de Estado de siete miembros presidido por el presidente Joaquín Balaguer durante un período limitado. El compromiso excluía del consejo a los integrantes de la junta directiva del movimiento opositor y a funcionarios vinculados al régimen. El pacto se concretó alrededor de las 2:30 a.m., tras una vigilia nocturna presenciada por el cónsul general de los Estados Unidos John Calvin Hill y el subsecretario adjunto de Estado Arturo Morales Carrión. Nicolás E. Pichardo, presidente de la Asociación de Profesores Universitarios y dirigente de la huelga, actuó como mediador principal, y la red radial opositora Voz Del Trópico anunció el fin de la huelga general de doce días.

records.headline: President Joaquin Balaguer denounced continued international
records.summary_en: President Joaquin Balaguer denounced continued international sanctions against the Dominican Republic as intolerable coercion resembling foreign intervention, arguing that a legitimate government exists with minimum respect for human rights. The sanctions had been imposed the previous year after the Organization of American States implicated dictator Rafael L. Trujillo in the failed assassination attempt on Venezuelan President Romulo Betancourt. As Balaguer spoke, violent street demonstrations erupted demanding his resignation, leaving a student seriously wounded as police and army troops employed tear gas and noise bombs. Dominicans generally returned to work despite the collapse of transitional government negotiations on Sunday, while Balaguer reacted sharply to an opposition statement labeling him the puppet of armed forces chief General Pedro Rodrigues Echavarria.
records.summary_es: El presidente Joaquín Balaguer denunció las continuas sanciones internacionales contra la República Dominicana calificándolas de coerción intolerable similar a una intervención extranjera, argumentando que existe un gobierno legítimo con un respeto mínimo a los derechos humanos. Las sanciones habían sido impuestas el año anterior luego de que la Organización de los Estados Americanos implicara al dictador Rafael L. Trujillo en el fallido intento de asesinato contra el presidente venezolano Rómulo Betancourt. Mientras Balaguer hablaba, estallaron violentas protestas callejeras que exigían su renuncia, dejando a un estudiante gravemente herido mientras la policía y el ejército empleaban gases lacrimógenos y bombas de ruido. La población dominicana se reincorporó mayoritariamente al trabajo a pesar del colapso de las negociaciones para un gobierno de transición el domingo, mientras Balaguer reaccionó con dureza ante un comunicado de la oposición que lo calificaba de títere del jefe de las fuerzas armadas, general Pedro Rodrigues Echavarría.

records.headline: The Dominican government announced that Rafael L. Trujillo
records.summary_en: The Dominican government announced that Rafael L. Trujillo, Jr., departed the country with $30 million. Checks and certificates drawn on Canadian banks, payable to and endorsed by the son of the slain dictator, were discovered aboard the yacht Angelita, which he had used to sail into exile before traveling on to Paris. The financial documents were reportedly issued by private enterprises and the Reserve Bank, prompting official legal proceedings to freeze the accounts and recover the assets. The younger Trujillo, who briefly led the armed forces after his father's assassination on May 30, traveled aboard the vessel only as far as Guadeloupe, after which the yacht returned to the Dominican Republic and was confiscated.
records.summary_es: El gobierno dominicano anunció que Rafael L. Trujillo hijo huyó del país con 30 millones de dólares. Cheques y certificados girados contra bancos canadienses, emitidos a favor y endosados por el hijo del dictador asesinado, fueron descubiertos a bordo del yate Angelita, que utilizó para salir al exilio antes de trasladarse a París. Según se informó, los documentos financieros fueron emitidos por empresas privadas y por el Banco de Reservas, lo que motivó acciones legales oficiales para congelar las cuentas e intentar recuperar los fondos. El joven Trujillo, quien encabezó brevemente las fuerzas armadas tras el asesinato de su padre el 30 de mayo, viajó en la embarcación únicamente hasta Guadalupe, tras lo cual el yate regresó a la República Dominicana y fue confiscado.

records.summary_en: Prior to a dinner at the Governor's residence, President John F. Kennedy conferred privately for an hour with United States officials regarding the crisis in the nearby Dominican Republic. The discussions focused on stalled negotiations between anti-Trujillo groups and the military over the formation of a transitional government. Following the conference, the President ordered Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for Inter-American Affairs Arturo Morales Carrion and Consul General John C. Hill to return immediately to Santo Domingo to monitor developments.

Las deliberaciones se centraron en el estancamiento de las negociaciones entre grupos antitrujillistas y los militares para la formación de un gobierno de transición. Tras la reunión, el presidente ordenó al subsecretario adjunto de Estado para Asuntos Interamericanos Arturo Morales Carrión y al cónsul general John C. records.headline: A news analysis reports that the removal of Organization of American States sanctions—including
records.summary_en: A news analysis reports that the removal of Organization of American States sanctions—including an embargo on exports of petroleum, arms, trucks, and spare parts—remains a central objective in the Dominican Republic's democratization process following the assassination of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo in May. The successor government contends that the continuing measures are causing economic and political bankruptcy and undermining the nation's international standing. However, the OAS committee has hesitated to lift the sanctions due to political instability and rising concerns that elements of the Dominican military and remnants of the old regime intend to establish a new dictatorship.

records.headline: The opposition National Civic Union announced its conditional
records.summary_en: The opposition National Civic Union announced its conditional acceptance of President Joaquin Balaguer's proposal for a provisional government, agreeing to give the plan a trial provided the Dominican armed forces remain entirely out of politics. Under the proposal, a seven-member council would govern until national elections are held in December 1962. However, the Civic Union voiced grave concern over Balaguer's intention to remain in office until the Organization of American States lifts political and economic sanctions, asserting that his continued presidency poses a danger to national security and well-being. Balaguer named Monsignor Eliseo Perez Sanchez, vicar general of the Roman Catholic Church, as one of the members of the proposed ruling council.
records.summary_es: La opositora Unión Cívica Nacional anunció su aceptación condicionada a la propuesta del presidente Joaquín Balaguer para un gobierno provisional, aceptando poner a prueba el plan siempre y cuando las fuerzas armadas dominicanas se mantengan totalmente al margen de la política. Según la propuesta, un consejo de siete miembros gobernaría hasta la celebración de elecciones nacionales en diciembre de 1962. No obstante, la Unión Cívica manifestó una profunda preocupación ante la intención de Balaguer de permanecer en el cargo hasta que la Organización de los Estados Americanos retire las sanciones políticas y económicas, advirtiendo que su continuidad en la presidencia constituye un peligro para la seguridad y el bienestar del Estado. Balaguer designó a monseñor Eliseo Pérez Sánchez, vicario general de la Iglesia católica, como uno de los integrantes del proyectado consejo de gobierno.

records.summary_en: President Kennedy declared that the United States will resume diplomatic relations with the Dominican Republic promptly, in a White House statement, if the Council of the Organization of American States lifts sanctions. In Santo Domingo, Dominican President Joaquin Balaguer welcomed the announcement, stating it would significantly help stabilize the political situation in his country. Viriato A. Fiallo, president of the National Civic Union, also applauded the move, while Dominican Revolutionary Party president Juan Bosch urged caution, noting the remarks should not be viewed as an immediate flood of aid. Kennedy added that once sanctions are removed, the Agriculture Department will authorize non-quota sugar purchases for the first six months of next year.

records.headline: An editorial commentary highlights effective United States foreign actions
records.summary_en: An editorial commentary highlights effective United States foreign actions, pointing to the show of American naval power in the Dominican Republic when the right-wing Trujillo dictatorship threatened chaos that could have installed a Communist regime. The column asserts that this intervention halted the advance of communism in that part of the hemisphere and created a clear prospect for establishing a decent government in the Dominican Republic. It concludes that if such a government ensues, it may be regarded, in the best sense of the phrase, as the creation of the United States Government.

La columna afirma que esta intervención detuvo el avance del comunismo en esa parte del hemisferio y abrió una clara perspectiva para establecer un gobierno decente en la República Dominicana. Concluye que si dicho gobierno llega a concretarse, podrá considerarse, en el mejor sentido de la expresión, una creación del gobierno de los Estados Unidos.

records.headline: An Associated Press report from Santo Domingo states that a new seven-man
records.summary_en: An Associated Press report from Santo Domingo states that a new seven-man government is prepared to take over rule of the Dominican Republic after 31 years of Trujillo dictatorship. The National Assembly of Deputies and Senators gave final approval to constitutional changes establishing a provisional state council to govern until elections are held and a new government installed in February, 1963. President Joaquin Balaguer is expected to formally designate the council's membership today. Under a compromise formula accepted without enthusiasm by major opposition groups, Balaguer will remain head of the council until the Organization of American States lifts sanctions imposed against the Dominican Republic in 1960, after which he has promised to resign.
records.summary_es: Un despacho de Associated Press desde Santo Domingo informa que un nuevo gobierno de siete miembros está listo para asumir el mando de la República Dominicana tras 31 años de dictadura trujillista. La Asamblea Nacional de Diputados y Senadores otorgó su aprobación definitiva a las reformas constitucionales que establecen un consejo de estado provisional para gobernar hasta que se celebren elecciones y se instale un nuevo gobierno en febrero de 1963. Se espera que el presidente Joaquín Balaguer designe formalmente a los miembros del consejo hoy mismo. Según una fórmula de compromiso aceptada sin entusiasmo por los principales grupos de oposición, Balaguer permanecerá al frente del consejo hasta que la Organización de los Estados Americanos levante las sanciones impuestas contra la República Dominicana en 1960, tras lo cual ha prometido renunciar.

records.headline: President Joaquin Balaguer announced the composition of his new Council of State
records.summary_en: President Joaquin Balaguer announced the composition of his new Council of State in Santo Domingo, stating that it will take charge of the Dominican government on Monday. The National Assembly approved the council, which will govern until elections are held following 30 years under the Trujillo dynasty. Balaguer will head the council temporarily alongside members Msgr. Eliseo Perez Sanchez, lawyer and teacher Rafael Bonnelly, retiring Supreme Court president Eduardo Read Barreras, University Professors Association president Dr. Nicolas Pichardo, and businessmen Luis Amiama Tio and Antonio Imbert. As first vice president, Bonnelly will assume executive duties once Balaguer steps down.
records.summary_es: El presidente Joaquín Balaguer anunció en Santo Domingo la composición de su nuevo Consejo de Estado, afirmando que asumirá el mando del gobierno dominicano el lunes. La Asamblea Nacional aprobó el consejo, que gobernará hasta la celebración de elecciones tras 30 años bajo la dinastía de Trujillo. Balaguer presidirá el consejo provisionalmente junto a los miembros monseñor Eliseo Pérez Sánchez, el abogado y educador Rafael Bonnelly, el presidente saliente de la Suprema Corte Eduardo Read Barreras, el presidente de la Asociación de Profesores Universitarios doctor Nicolás Pichardo y los empresarios Luis Amiama Tió y Antonio Imbert. Como primer vicepresidente, Bonnelly asumirá las funciones ejecutivas una vez que Balaguer renuncie.

The seven-member council included Antonio Imbert and Luis Amiama Tió, the sole surviving conspirators of the plot that assassinated Rafael Trujillo.

records.summary_en: Dispatches from Santo Domingo indicate that the Dominican leader is expected to resign from the seven-man State Council later in the week once Organization of American States action is completed, clearing the way for interim President Rafael Bonnelly of the National Civic Union. Washington officials note that beyond ending diplomatic isolation and embargoes on arms, petroleum, trucks, and spare parts, the Dominican Republic's greatest economic boon will be entering the redistributed Cuban sugar quota in the United States market. President Kennedy stated before Christmas that the country would qualify immediately upon resuming diplomatic ties, with State Department officials expecting inclusion in February quotas. Department of Agriculture officials estimate the additional Dominican sugar sales could reach $35 million in the first six months of 1962, generating a $15.5 million profit over depressed world prices.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that OAS Secretary General José A. Mora and Inter-American Development Bank President Felipe Herrera scheduled missions to Santo Domingo to assess reconstruction aid under the Alliance for Progress. Mora planned discussions with President Joaquín Balaguer and incoming interim leader Rafael Bonnelly to prepare substantial technical and financial assistance programs.

Mora, y el presidente del Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo, Felipe Herrera, programaron misiones a Santo Domingo para evaluar la ayuda a la reconstrucción en el marco de la Alianza para el Progreso. Mora tenía previsto mantener conversaciones con el presidente Joaquín Balaguer y con el mandatario interino entrante Rafael Bonnelly a fin de estructurar cuantiosos programas de asistencia técnica y financiera.
records.passage: This group has been described as a “pre-planning” mission to investigate what aid the Dominican Republic needs under the inter-American Alliance for Progress sponsored by the Kennedy administration. Bank Chief to Visit Felipe Herrera, president of the Inter-American Development Bank, also is scheduled to make a personal visit to investigate the possibility of low cost loans for Dominican reconstruction. The Inter-American Development Bank, with assets of over $1 billion, is the hemispheric institution which also administers a $394 million Social Progress Trust fund voted by Congress for the Alliance for Progress. Secretary General Mora’s visit is to last four days. Sources close to him say he will meet with Dominican President Joaquin Balaguer and Rafael Bonnelly, the chief representative of the democratic opposition on the new Council of State. President Balaguer, who is a holdover from the Trujillo regime, has said he will resign once the OAS sanctions are lifted. OAS sources expected, therefore, that most of Secretary General Mora’s dealings would be with Mr. Bonnelly. who will become interim President, and members of his group, the National Civic Union. Experts Gather Data In his statement here, Mr. Mora noted that experts of the OAS are busy collecting data which will be used in planning a technical co-operation program in both economic and social fields. A source close to Mr. Mora said a major aim of his visit is to lend more prestige to these efforts of the experts.

records.summary_en: The United States and the Dominican Republic resumed diplomatic relations following internal political reforms in the Caribbean nation. Diplomatic restoration occurred when an American representative presented credentials to the Dominican foreign office.

records.full_text:
U.S. and Santo Domingo Renew Diplomatic Ties

By the Associated Press

The United States and the Dominican Republic resumed diplomatic relations today.

The step was the latest in a series of international moves to return the island nation to a normal situation within the inter-American system as a result of internal political changes.

The United States and other American countries broke off formal diplomatic relations after a decision by Western Hemisphere foreign ministers in August, 1960, to impose sanctions as a result of an assassination attempt on President Romulo Betancourt of Venezuela.

A year ago the sanctions were stiffened. They continued in force for months after the assassination of the late Dominican dictator, Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo. His death, however, opened a period of political reform in the republic which led to the present improvement in its international relations.

Restoration of relations occurred when a United States representative presented his credentials to the foreign office in Santo Domingo at the same hour a Dominican representative in Washington presented credentials to the State Department.

"These two acts constituted the resumption of diplomatic relations between the two countries," the State Department then announced at noon.

The United States representative is John Calvin Hill, jr., who has been consul general at Santo Domingo. He now holds the position of diplomat temporarily in charge of United States affairs in Santo Domingo pending the appointment of an ambassador.

The Dominican government designated Dr. Marco A. de Pena as its temporary diplomatic representative in Washington.

The resumption of relations, the State Department said, "follows the decision of the Council of the Organization of American States on January 4, 1962, to discontinue the (sanction) measures... which called for, among other things, the breaking of diplomatic relations of all the member states of the Organization of American States with the Dominican Republic."

records.headline: An editorial urges the United States to lose no time re-establishing
records.summary_en: An editorial urges the United States to lose no time re-establishing diplomatic ties with the new regime in Santo Domingo, formerly Ciudad Trujillo, and extending economic aid under the Alliance for Progress. It quotes interim President Balaguer, who stated that economic assistance and the moral effect of lifting sanctions will help establish a climate of tranquility. The commentary argues that tranquility is vital for the Dominican Republic to carry out necessary social, political, and economic reforms, emphasizing that firm support from Washington and the Organization of American States is required to counter the menace posed by Fidel Castro's neighboring Communist regime.

Cita al presidente interino Balaguer, quien afirmó que la asistencia económica y el impacto moral del levantamiento de las sanciones contribuirán a instaurar un clima de tranquilidad. El comentario sostiene que la tranquilidad resulta vital para que la República Dominicana lleve a cabo las reformas sociales, políticas y económicas necesarias, subrayando que se requiere un firme respaldo de Washington y de la Organización de los Estados Americanos para contrarrestar la amenaza que plantea el vecino régimen comunista de Fidel Castro.

records.summary_en: Following the formal resumption of ties with the Dominican Republic, other members of the Organization of American States, with the exception of Cuba, are expected to restore relations shortly. President Balaguer stated that the Dominican Republic does not want diplomatic relations with Fidel Castro's Communist regime. Simultaneously, an aid mission led by Teodoro Moscoso, head of the Latin American division of the Agency for International Development, arrived in Santo Domingo to integrate the republic into the Alliance for Progress. Formal diplomatic relations were completed when John Calvin Hill, Jr., former consul general in Santo Domingo, presented credentials to the Dominican foreign ministry.

records.headline: Teodoro Moscoso, Latin American director for the United States Agency
records.summary_en: Teodoro Moscoso, Latin American director for the United States Agency for International Development, arrived in the Dominican Republic with technical staff only four days after diplomatic relations were resumed following the lifting of Organization of American States sanctions against the defunct Trujillo dictatorship. Moscoso conferred briefly with President Joaquin Balaguer and the ruling State Council, which faces heavy trade deficits and unemployment estimated as high as 600,000. Moscoso stated that the mission aims to assist the nation's democratic destiny and demonstrate that economic growth and social justice can occur without sacrificing human dignity or freedom. Meanwhile, domestic political instability surfaced when three air force officers threatened to resign unless armed forces chief General Pedro Rodriguez Echavarria steps down.
records.summary_es: Teodoro Moscoso, director para América Latina de la Agencia para el Desarrollo Internacional de los Estados Unidos, llegó a la República Dominicana con personal técnico apenas cuatro días después de reanudarse las relaciones diplomáticas tras el levantamiento de las sanciones de la Organización de los Estados Americanos contra la extinta dictadura de Trujillo. Moscoso se reunió brevemente con el presidente Joaquín Balaguer y con el Consejo de Estado gobernante, que hace frente a cuantiosos déficits comerciales y a un desempleo calculado en hasta 600,000 personas. Moscoso afirmó que la misión busca apoyar el destino democrático de la nación y demostrar que el crecimiento económico y la justicia social son posibles sin menoscabar la dignidad humana ni la libertad. records.headline: An editorial praises the Dominican Council of State for appointing
records.summary_en: An editorial praises the Dominican Council of State for appointing Dr. José Antonio Bonilla Atiles as Secretary of Foreign Affairs, describing him as a cultured, honest democrat dedicated to the Panamericanist ideal. The paper welcomes the appointment as timely and essential for the cause of representative democracy in the hemisphere, which entails confronting dictatorships of both the left and right. The editorial recalls that Bonilla Atiles suffered fierce persecution under the Trujillo dictatorship that threatened his life while serving as Vice-Dean of the University of Santo Domingo, forcing him to leave the country under diplomatic protection and spend years of honorable exile in the United States aiding his homeland.

El diario celebra la designación por considerarla oportuna y necesaria para la causa de la democracia representativa en el hemisferio, la cual exige hacer frente a las dictaduras tanto de izquierda como de derecha. El editorial recuerda que Bonilla Atiles sufrió una feroz persecución bajo la dictadura de Trujillo que puso en peligro su vida mientras se desempeñaba como vicedecano de la Universidad de Santo Domingo, obligándolo a abandonar el país bajo protección diplomática y a pasar años de digno exilio en Estados Unidos apoyando la causa de su patria.

records.headline: A report discusses a proposal for United States agricultural
records.summary_en: A report discusses a proposal for United States agricultural cooperatives to assist the Dominican Republic as a Caribbean model of agricultural organization. The initiative was presented by Welch grape juice company head Jack Kaplan, who cited the success of a 3,000-farmer cooperative he established in New York State during discussions with the State Department. Kaplan argued that vast lands seized by the late dictator Trujillo would create an economic void without proper management, creating an opportunity for American cooperatives to demonstrate private enterprise without raising suspicions of imperialism associated with large sugar firms. United States experts in Latin American affairs subsequently traveled to Santo Domingo carrying his proposals.
records.summary_es: Una crónica reseña una propuesta para que cooperativas agrícolas de Estados Unidos ayuden a la República Dominicana a convertirse en un modelo caribeño de organización agrícola. La iniciativa fue presentada por Jack Kaplan, presidente de la empresa de jugo de uva Welch, quien expuso ante el Departamento de Estado el éxito de una cooperativa de 3,000 agricultores que organizó en el estado de Nueva York. Kaplan sostuvo que las extensas tierras incautadas por el difunto dictador Trujillo dejarían un vacío económico de no administrarse debidamente, ofreciendo una oportunidad para que cooperativas estadounidenses demuestren las ventajas de la iniciativa privada sin suscitar sospechas de imperialismo como las grandes empresas azucareras. Expertos estadounidenses en asuntos latinoamericanos viajaron posteriormente a Santo Domingo llevando consigo sus propuestas.

records.headline: A dispatch reveals that armed forces leader General Pedro Rodriguez Echavarría issued
records.summary_en: A dispatch reveals that armed forces leader General Pedro Rodriguez Echavarría issued instructions ordering the director of the nationalized Dominican Cement Company, previously owned by the Trujillo family, to submit all business accounting directly to him without interference, even from the President of the Republic. President Kennedy reacted with indignation upon reading the letter, instructing United States Consul John C. Hill that preventing a military dictatorship in the Dominican Republic holds as high a priority as checking the spread of Castroism. United States delegation head Teodoro Moscoso confronts a delicate challenge as Rodriguez Echavarría, an American-trained jet pilot, dominates the Council of State and infringes on President Joaquín Balaguer's authority without making any pledge to step down when Balaguer leaves office on February 27.

El presidente Kennedy reaccionó indignado al enterarse de la carta e instruyó al cónsul estadounidense John C. Hill que impedir una dictadura militar en la República Dominicana constituye una prioridad tan alta como frenar la expansión del castrismo. El jefe de la delegación de Estados Unidos, Teodoro Moscoso, enfrenta un complejo reto debido a que Rodríguez Echavarría, piloto de reactores entrenado en Estados Unidos, domina el Consejo de Estado y vulnera la autoridad del presidente Joaquín Balaguer sin formular promesa alguna de renunciar cuando Balaguer deje el cargo el 27 de febrero.

records.summary_en: The Haitian government announced from Port-au-Prince that diplomatic relations between Haiti and the Dominican Republic have been reestablished. records.summary_en: Diplomatic relations were re-established and economic sanctions lifted by the United States on January 6 after the Organization of American States determined that the Dominican Republic was no longer a threat to hemispheric peace. Washington had originally broken relations after American nations called for sanctions in August 1960 against the dictatorship of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, who was assassinated the following May as the country began moving toward democracy. Diplomatic circles reported that the appointment of Mr. Martin, who previously visited the country as a writer, may be announced within the week. Career diplomat John C. Hill, Jr., who served as consul general in Santo Domingo during the unrest following Trujillo's assassination, is currently in charge of the United States Embassy.

Círculos diplomáticos indicaron que el nombramiento del señor Martin, quien visitó previamente el país como escritor, podría anunciarse durante la semana. El diplomático de carrera John C. records.headline: Dominican Air Force troops and armored vehicles took positions
records.summary_en: Dominican Air Force troops and armored vehicles took positions inside the National Palace grounds in Santo Domingo, with civilian visitors required to be accompanied by armed guards. A tank and three armored cars were stationed within the grounds with guns pointing outward while about fifty people gathered outside the fence to air grievances. Although palace business appeared to proceed normally and no official explanation was offered, President Joaquin Balaguer and his military chief faced renewed opposition efforts to unseat them. The Air Force had also staged a midnight show of strength with four tanks, a half-track, and about forty troops along the capital's main street.
records.summary_es: Tropas de la Fuerza Aérea Dominicana y vehículos blindados tomaron posiciones en los jardines del Palacio Nacional en Santo Domingo, exigiéndose que los visitantes civiles estuvieran acompañados por guardias armados. Un tanque y tres vehículos blindados fueron apostados en los terrenos con las armas apuntando hacia afuera, mientras unas cincuenta personas se congregaban frente a la verja para exponer reclamos. Aunque las actividades del palacio parecían desarrollarse con normalidad y no se ofreció explicación oficial, el presidente Joaquín Balaguer y su jefe militar enfrentaban renovados intentos de la oposición para destituirlos. La Fuerza Aérea también había realizado una demostración de fuerza a medianoche con cuatro tanques, un semioruga y cerca de cuarenta soldados a lo largo de la calle principal de la capital.

records.headline: UPI reported from Santo Domingo that infantrymen riding the lead
records.summary_en: UPI reported from Santo Domingo that infantrymen riding the lead tank of a five-tank column opened fire with sidearms on an opposition demonstration in Independence Park on Tuesday. At least four people were reported killed and many others wounded among more than one hundred opposition members gathered to hear National Civic Union demands for the immediate ouster of President Joaquin Balaguer. The correspondent, standing less than a block away, observed bullets mowing down fleeing civilians and saw numerous casualties on the ground, with the injured taken to clinics and hospitals. All of the shooting seemed to be directed at the crowd from point blank range at the edge of the park. The new opposition effort to force Balaguer from office started in the park about noon: Civic Union leaders set up loudspeakers in the square and started vigorous attacks on Balaguer, demanding his immediate resignation, and a crowd of about 100 youths stood in the street and on the edge of the park cheering the orators. At about 2 p.m., police officers demanded that the loudspeaker assault be halted, but opposition sponsors of the rally refused. The tanks arrived about 3:45 p.m.; infantrymen on the lead tank opened fire with sidearms, and as the tanks withdrew citizens immediately ran into the park picking up the dead and wounded, some of them crossing in front of the remaining tanks, which pulled away without firing. The violence marked a new and vigorous opposition attempt to oust Balaguer.
records.summary_es: La agencia UPI informó desde Santo Domingo que soldados de infantería que iban sobre el tanque guía de una columna de cinco tanques abrieron fuego con armas cortas el martes contra una manifestación opositora en el Parque Independencia. Se reportó la muerte de al menos cuatro personas y muchos heridos entre más de cien miembros de la oposición congregados para escuchar las demandas de la Unión Cívica Nacional para la destitución inmediata del presidente Joaquín Balaguer. El corresponsal, situado a menos de una cuadra de distancia, observó cómo las balas alcanzaban a civiles que huían y vio numerosas víctimas en el suelo, mientras los heridos eran trasladados a clínicas y hospitales. Todos los disparos parecían dirigidos contra la multitud a quemarropa desde el borde del parque. El nuevo esfuerzo opositor para forzar la salida de Balaguer comenzó en el parque hacia el mediodía: los líderes de la Unión Cívica instalaron altavoces en la plaza y lanzaron vigorosos ataques contra Balaguer, exigiendo su renuncia inmediata, y una multitud de unos 100 jóvenes se situó en la calle y en el borde del parque vitoreando a los oradores. Hacia las 2 p.m., agentes de policía exigieron que cesara el asalto por altavoces, pero los patrocinadores opositores del mitin se negaron. Los tanques llegaron hacia las 3:45 p.m.; los infantes sobre el tanque guía abrieron fuego con armas cortas, y cuando los tanques se retiraron, los ciudadanos corrieron de inmediato al parque a recoger a los muertos y heridos, algunos cruzando por delante de los tanques restantes, que se alejaron sin disparar. La violencia marcó un nuevo y vigoroso intento de la oposición de derrocar a Balaguer.

records.headline: American officials stated they had no plans to dispatch United States fleet
records.summary_en: American officials stated they had no plans to dispatch United States fleet units to the Dominican area, contrasting the situation with the earlier return of the Trujillo regime's heirs. About 2,000 Americans were reported living in the Dominican Republic, with no indication that any were in danger. John Calvin Hill, the regular American Chargé d’Affaires, departed Miami to return to Santo Domingo, though officials questioned whether his plane would be permitted to land due to intermittent airport closures during recent unrest. In the interim, Charles Hodge, economic counselor and first secretary, served as Acting Chargé d’Affaires.

Se informó que unos 2.000 estadounidenses residían en la República Dominicana, sin indicios de que alguno estuviera en peligro. John Calvin Hill, el encargado de negocios titular de Estados Unidos, partió desde Miami para regresar a Santo Domingo, aunque las autoridades dudaban si su avión podría aterrizar debido a los cierres intermitentes del aeropuerto en recientes disturbios. Mientras tanto, Charles Hodge, consejero económico y primer secretario, se desempeñaba como encargado de negocios interino.

Armed forces chief General Pedro Rodríguez Echavarría announced the installation of a civilian-military junta to govern the country, while arresting council members who refused to cooperate.

Pedro Rodriguez Echavarria, the armed forces chief who thwarted an attempted coup d'etat by the brothers of former dictator Rafael Trujillo last November, emerged grimfaced from the Presidential Palace and announced the change of government. City Now Quiet The center of Santo Domingo was quiet this morning. Many stores were closed. Shattered glass littered some streets, Many store fronts were shattered in the night of violence. Conditions through the interior also were reported quiet. The official announcement said four members of the old council, besides Mr. Balaguer, resigned. Informed sources said, however, that they refused to go along with creation of a new civilian-military junta and were placed under arrest. records.headline: Following a sudden military takeover, the Dominican opposition
records.summary_en: Following a sudden military takeover, the Dominican opposition and specifically the National Civic Union were accused of instigating unrest, leading to the arrest of organization president Dr. Viriato Fiallo and his brother Antoine. Ten government officials resigned, issuing a statement that proclaimed no legitimate authority existed and accusing President Joaquin Balaguer and Gen. Rodriguez Echavarria of betraying democratic ideals through a military coup. Tanks and troops called to disperse a student protest against the change reportedly opened fire, killing one youth and wounding two others amid widespread rioting. Roving mobs in Santo Domingo set fire to a school, stoned police cars, and burned several houses, including the home of the parents of tank commander Col. Manuel Antonio Cuervo Gomez.
records.summary_es: Tras un repentino golpe militar, la oposición dominicana y específicamente la Unión Cívica Nacional fueron acusadas de instigar disturbios, lo que llevó al arresto del presidente de la organización, el Dr. Viriato Fiallo, y de su hermano Antoine. Diez funcionarios gubernamentales renunciaron emitiendo una declaración que proclamaba que no existía autoridad legítima y acusando al presidente Joaquín Balaguer y al general Rodríguez Echavarría de traicionar los ideales democráticos mediante un golpe militar. Tanques y tropas movilizados para dispersar una protesta estudiantil contra el cambio presuntamente abrieron fuego, causando la muerte de un joven y heridas a otros dos en medio de disturbios generalizados. Turbas en Santo Domingo incendiaron una escuela, apedrearon vehículos policiales y quemaron varias viviendas, entre ellas la casa paterna del comandante de tanques coronel Manuel Antonio Cuervo Gómez.

records.full_text:
New Strongman Likes To Deny Political Goal

By the Associated Press

Maj. Gen. Pedro Rodriguez Echavarria, new military strongman of the Dominican Republic, is a boyish-looking plane pilot who likes to hunt, fish, follow baseball and disclaim political ambitions.

A recurrent statement voiced by the 37-year-old Armed forces chief goes: "I am not a politician; I am a soldier and I support constitutional order."

Weeks ago, after he had emerged as the top military figure of the post-Trujillo era, he scoffed at talk that he wanted to replace Joaquin Balaguer as chief executive.

Gen. Rodriguez Echavarria represents a long military tradition. A great-grandfather was Gen. Santiago Rodriguez, leader of the fight against Haitian domination in 1844. One of his grandfathers was a minister of war.

Gen. Rodriguez Echavarria was reared in the country's agricultural north, the oldest of 10 children of a functionary who held a succession of political posts under the Trujillo dictatorship.

The youngster, remembered by classmates as a shy, withdrawn boy, joined the air force after graduation from high school. He learned to fly from a United States instructor contracted for by the Dominican air force and acquired a reputation as a hot pilot.

That helped him advance, because the air force was the favorite service of the old dictator, the late Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo. He also became friends with the dictator's son, Rafael Trujillo, jr., who commanded the air force.

Among close associates, the general often speaks of retiring some day to become a farmer. He is married to his home-town sweetheart, Dolorez Martinez. They have four children.

records.headline: A first-person commentary recounts how General Rafael L. Trujillo
records.summary_en: A first-person commentary recounts how General Rafael L. Trujillo Molina, as Dominican Republic army chief, seized power in 1930 following a fraudulent election. The writer recalls soldiers dressed in civilian clothes stationed at polling stations under orders to intimidate voters and expel those voting against him. Although the country experienced material progress, Trujillo maintained control through an extensive surveillance apparatus comprising hundreds of spies in the capital alone. The commentary describes his governance as a regime of terror and extermination directed against any faction or individual perceived as a threat to his authority.

Aunque el país experimentó avances materiales, Trujillo mantuvo el poder mediante un extenso aparato de espionaje que incluía cientos de espías sólo en la capital. El artículo califica su mandato como un régimen de terror y exterminio dirigido contra cualquier facción o individuo considerado una amenaza para su autoridad.

records.headline: Surgeons in Coral Gables reported that General Jose Garcia Trujillo
records.summary_en: Surgeons in Coral Gables reported that General Jose Garcia Trujillo, nephew of the assassinated Dominican dictator and former Dominican military chief of staff, might survive an apparent suicide attempt. Detectives reported that the 51-year-old general shot himself in the head with a 357-magnum pistol at a friend's residence, leaving no note behind. Police stated that he had apparently taken the firearm from the home of 26-year-old Luis Rafael Trujillo and speculated that despondency prompted the shooting. Garcia Trujillo, a resident of Miami's Brickell Avenue, was identified as the son of Jose Garcia and Julietta Trujillo de Garcia.
records.summary_es: Cirujanos en Coral Gables informaron que el general José García Trujillo, sobrino del asesinado dictador dominicano y exjefe del estado mayor militar dominicano, podría sobrevivir a un presunto intento de suicidio. Los detectives señalaron que el general de 51 años se disparó en la cabeza con una pistola magnum 357 en la residencia de un amigo, sin dejar ninguna nota. La policía indicó que aparentemente tomó el arma de fuego de la casa de Luis Rafael Trujillo, de 26 años, y conjeturó que el desaliento motivó el disparo. García Trujillo, residente de Brickell Avenue en Miami, fue identificado como hijo de José García y Julieta Trujillo de García.

records.headline: The United States moved swiftly to extend political and economic
records.summary_en: The United States moved swiftly to extend political and economic support to the constitutional seven-member council restored to power in the Dominican Republic following a bloodless countercoup. Preparations were immediately resumed for American purchases of $45 million worth of Dominican sugar, transactions previously halted by the abortive 24-hour takeover led by Maj. Gen. Pedro Rodriguez Echavarria. A State Department spokesman indicated that prompt action was anticipated on recommendations from a returning economic aid mission. U.S. officials stated that formal diplomatic recognition was unlikely to be an issue because Council President Rafael Bonnelly was the constitutionally designated head of state pending elections.
records.summary_es: Los Estados Unidos actuaron con rapidez para brindar respaldo político y económico al consejo constitucional de siete miembros restablecido en el poder en la República Dominicana tras un contragolpe incruento. Se reanudaron de inmediato los preparativos para la compra estadounidense de 45 millones de dólares en azúcar dominicana, negociaciones previamente suspendidas por el frustrado golpe militar de 24 horas encabezado por el mayor general Pedro Rodríguez Echavarría. Un portavoz del Departamento de Estado indicó que se esperaba una acción pronta sobre las recomendaciones de la misión de ayuda económica que regresaba de Santo Domingo. Funcionarios estadounidenses afirmaron que el reconocimiento diplomático formal difícilmente sería un obstáculo, ya que el presidente del consejo Rafael Bonnelly era el jefe de Estado designado constitucionalmente en espera de elecciones.

records.headline: Following a countercoup that formally removed President Joaquin
records.summary_en: Following a countercoup that formally removed President Joaquin Balaguer, restored civilian government, and imprisoned military strongman Maj. Gen. Pedro Rodriguez Echavarria, Santo Domingo erupted in joyous street celebrations. Crowds chanted slogans mocking Balaguer while clapping and dancing along El Conde, bringing traffic to a halt in a festive carnival atmosphere after days of tense military patrols. The countercoup was carried out by the general's own officers, who jailed him just two days after his military junta took control. Rafael Bonnelly, a 57-year-old lawyer and university professor linked to the National Civic Union, was sworn in as president almost exactly 48 hours after being arrested at the National Palace.
records.summary_es: Tras un contragolpe que destituyó formalmente al presidente Joaquín Balaguer, restauró el gobierno civil y encarceló al líder militar mayor general Pedro Rodríguez Echavarría, Santo Domingo estalló en jubilosas celebraciones callejeras. Multitudes corearon consignas burlándose de Balaguer entre aplausos a lo largo de la calle El Conde, paralizando el tránsito en un ambiente festivo y carnavalesco tras jornadas de tensas patrullas militares. El contragolpe fue ejecutado por los propios oficiales del general, quienes lo encarcelaron apenas dos días después de que su junta militar asumiera el control. Rafael Bonnelly, abogado y profesor universitario de 57 años vinculado a la Unión Cívica Nacional, fue juramentado como presidente casi exactamente 48 horas después de haber sido detenido en el Palacio Nacional.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published a profile of Dr. Rafael Bonnelly as he prepared to lead the Dominican transitional government toward general elections. The profile traced his career as a university rector, diplomat, and cabinet minister during the Trujillo era, noting his efforts to maintain professional independence before joining the democratic opposition.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* publicó una semblanza del Dr. Rafael Bonnelly mientras se preparaba para encabezar el gobierno de transición dominicano hacia las elecciones generales. El perfil repasó su trayectoria como rector universitario, diplomático y ministro de gabinete durante la era de Trujillo, destacando sus esfuerzos por preservar su independencia profesional antes de sumarse a la oposición democrática.

Long in Government The late Dominican dictator, Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo, exerted various forms of economic pressure to bring the country’s influential citizens into his service. For the first 10 years of the Trujillo regime, Dr. Bonnelly stayed clear of any association with the govern ment, but in the 1940s he joined the official family. Among the high posts he held were Secretary of the Interior, Ambassador to Spain and to Venezuela. He was also rector of Santo Domingo University, a job in which he still takes pride since it gave him a chance to teach and direct what Dominicans consider the hemisphere’s oldest institution of learning. During this career, Dr. Bonnelly says he was able to avoid identification with the regime except in a purely professional capacity. Former President Joaquín Balaguer remained under guard at his residence, asserting that he had previously resisted resigning precisely to avoid provoking a military seizure of power.

He disclaimed responsibility for the violence between Tuesday and Thursday, when Gen. Rodriguez Echavarria was in command. records.headline: An editorial in Diario las Américas praises the restoration of the Council of State
records.summary_en: An editorial in Diario las Américas praises the restoration of the Council of State in the Dominican Republic as an event of extraordinary moral significance for the hemisphere following the collapse of a brief military coup. The commentary underscores the moral authority of Dominican Foreign Minister Bonilla Atiles in continental efforts against communism and in defense of representative democracy. It asserts that the unpopular coup, which attempted to impose a new dictatorship after more than thirty years of oppression, failed to reflect the true sentiment of the armed forces or the Dominican people. The paper highlights a declaration of resistance issued by National Civic Union leaders Dr. Viriato A. Fiallo and Dr. Luis Manuel Baquero upholding republican principles.
records.summary_es: Un editorial de Diario las Américas celebra la restitución del Consejo de Estado en la República Dominicana como un hecho de extraordinaria trascendencia moral para el hemisferio tras el fracaso de un breve golpe militar. El comentario resalta la autoridad moral del canciller dominicano Bonilla Atiles en los esfuerzos continentales contra el comunismo y en defensa de la democracia representativa. Afirma que la impopular intentona castrense, que pretendió imponer una nueva dictadura tras más de treinta años de opresión, no reflejaba el sentir mayoritario de las fuerzas armadas ni del pueblo dominicano. Asimismo, destaca el pronunciamiento de resistencia emitido por los líderes de la Unión Cívica Nacional, el Dr. Viriato A. Fiallo y el Dr. Luis Manuel Baquero, en defensa de los principios republicanos.

records.summary_en: Bruce Parker, internationally recognized as the father of water skiing, arrived in the Virgin Islands after fleeing the Dominican Republic amid widespread civil turmoil. Parker described Santo Domingo as extremely tense, citing tank and troop maneuvers along public thoroughfares, machine-gun fire causing mass casualties, and street crowds throwing rocks through storefront windows. He also reported that rioters had burned the Olympia Theater to the ground during the disturbances.

records.headline: Continuing his account, water-ski champion and underwater photographer
records.summary_en: Continuing his account, water-ski champion and underwater photographer Bruce Parker explained that he was in Santo Domingo to arrange promotional films for the Dominican Republic's Department of Tourism. When martial law was declared, negotiations abruptly ended, and he managed to board the last departing flight before authorities imposed a freeze on departures. Parker described the airport as crowded with people seeking to leave and noted that his taxi was delayed by a tank convoy. Because external communications were severed, he carried press dispatches out of the country for the San Juan Star.

Debido a la interrupción de las comunicaciones con el exterior, transportó despachos de prensa fuera del país para el San Juan Star.

records.headline: A first-person commentary observes that the old Dominican Party
records.summary_en: A first-person commentary observes that the old Dominican Party has disappeared for good and that four opposition parties are committed to eradicating the legacy of dictatorship forever. The writer reports widespread optimism in the Dominican Republic and notes the emergence of a distinct middle class, in contrast to the historical divide between the very rich and very poor. While localized poverty persists, the article emphasizes that starvation is absent, supported by an active agricultural program and moderately low food prices. Expressing strong confidence that the new government will resolve the nation's entanglements by 1963, the author affirms plans to return to his Santo Domingo office within days.
records.summary_es: Un comentario en primera persona observa que el antiguo Partido Dominicano ha desaparecido definitivamente y que cuatro partidos de oposición están comprometidos a erradicar el legado de la dictadura para siempre. El autor reporta un optimismo generalizado en la República Dominicana y resalta el surgimiento de una clase media definida, en contraste con la división histórica entre los muy ricos y los muy pobres. Aunque persiste la pobreza en ciertos lugares, el texto subraya que no hay hambruna, gracias a un activo programa agrícola y precios de alimentos moderadamente bajos. Confiando plenamente en que el nuevo gobierno resolverá las complejidades del país para 1963, el autor afirma sus planes de regresar a su oficina en Santo Domingo en pocos días.

records.headline: In the Dominican Republic, an analytical dispatch reviews the turbulent
records.summary_en: In the Dominican Republic, an analytical dispatch reviews the turbulent succession following the overthrow of a military junta that held power for only 48 hours. The opposing factions had agreed in December to establish a transitional seven-member Council of State to govern until general elections in 1963, originally led by holdover Joaquin Balaguer until he was to transfer power to 57-year-old liberal lawyer Rafael F. Bonnelly. While masses distrusted Balaguer over his ties to the late dictator Trujillo, armed forces and business groups backed him out of fear of Castroism. Although the council assumed office on January 1 with diplomatic recognition and sanctions relief from the United States and the Organization of American States, rumors that Balaguer would not step down and street protests resulting in four deaths prompted Air Force Gen. Rafael Rodriguez Echevarria to launch a military coup that ousted Balaguer and imprisoned council liberals.
records.summary_es: En la República Dominicana, un despacho analítico examina la turbulenta sucesión tras el derrocamiento de una junta militar que permaneció en el poder únicamente 48 horas. Las facciones opuestas habían acordado en diciembre constituir un Consejo de Estado transitorio de siete miembros para gobernar hasta las elecciones generales de 1963, encabezado inicialmente por Joaquín Balaguer hasta transferir el mando al abogado liberal de 57 años Rafael F. Bonnelly. Aunque las masas desconfiaban de Balaguer por sus vínculos con el difunto dictador Trujillo, las fuerzas armadas y sectores empresariales lo respaldaban por temor al castrismo. Pese a que el consejo asumió funciones el 1 de enero con reconocimiento diplomático y levantamiento de sanciones por parte de Estados Unidos y la Organización de Estados Americanos, los rumores de que Balaguer no dimitiría y las protestas callejeras con saldo de cuatro muertos llevaron al general de la Fuerza Aérea Rafael Rodríguez Echevarría a perpetrar un golpe militar que expulsó a Balaguer y encarceló a los miembros liberales del consejo.

records.headline: During a Friday evening visit to Diario las Américas, Dominican
records.summary_en: During a Friday evening visit to Diario las Américas, Dominican Foreign Minister Dr. José Antonio Bonilla Atiles declared that the Dominican people saved the upcoming Punta del Este Foreign Ministers' Conference through their heroic restoration of democracy. The newspaper's editorial commentary stresses that had the Dominican public not defeated the fleeting military coup, Santo Domingo would likely have missed the conference or sent representatives lacking the moral authority to speak on democracy. Furthermore, discounting the Dominican vote from the thirteen firmly anti-communist votes in the hemisphere would have severely weakened continental democracy in its confrontation with Soviet imperialism. The editorial concludes that the sacrifices of the Dominican people safeguarded freedom and significantly enhanced the chances of a democratic victory at Punta del Este.
records.summary_es: Durante una visita el viernes por la noche a Diario las Américas, el canciller dominicano Dr. José Antonio Bonilla Atiles declaró que el pueblo dominicano salvó la próxima Conferencia de Cancilleres de Punta del Este mediante su heroica restauración democrática. El comentario editorial del periódico subraya que, de no haber derrotado la ciudadanía dominicana el efímero golpe militar, Santo Domingo probablemente se habría ausentado de la reunión o habría enviado representantes desprovistos de autoridad moral para hablar de democracia. Asimismo, descontar el voto dominicano de los trece votos decididamente anticomunistas del hemisferio habría debilitado con gravedad a la democracia continental en su confrontación frente al imperialismo soviético. El editorial concluye que el sacrificio dominicano salvaguardó la libertad e incrementó considerablemente las posibilidades de un triunfo democrático en Punta del Este.

records.headline: An editorial reports that a group of young Dominican Air Force
records.summary_en: An editorial reports that a group of young Dominican Air Force officers, largely trained in the United States, restored civilian governance after ousting a right-wing military junta that held power for only two days. Santo Domingo greeted the swearing-in of Dr. Rafael Bonnelly with carnival-like street celebrations following the defeat of another prospective dictatorship. Dr. Bonnelly, a National Civic Union founder characterized as a centrist liberal opposed to extremes of right and left, received immediate backing from the U.S. State Department, which praised the countercoup, designated his administration a constitutional government, and promised expedited economic aid. The commentary reflects that while Dominicans have had little experience with political freedom after more than a generation under dictatorship, a more responsible political consciousness is taking root.
records.summary_es: Un editorial señala que un grupo de jóvenes oficiales de la Fuerza Aérea Dominicana, formados en su mayoría en los Estados Unidos, restauró la gobernanza civil tras derrocar a una junta militar derechista que permaneció en el poder sólo dos días. Santo Domingo recibió la juramentación del Dr. Rafael Bonnelly con celebraciones populares de tono carnavalesco luego de disiparse la amenaza de una nueva dictadura. El Dr. Bonnelly, cofundador de la Unión Cívica Nacional definido como un liberal de centro opuesto a los extremismos de derecha e izquierda, contó con el respaldo inmediato del Departamento de Estado estadounidense, que elogió el contragolpe, calificó a su administración de gobierno constitucional y prometió agilizar la ayuda económica. El comentario añade que, si bien los dominicanos tuvieron escasa experiencia de libertad política durante más de una generación bajo la dictadura, una conciencia política más responsable está comenzando a afianzarse.

records.headline: President Kennedy announced an emergency credit offer of up
records.summary_en: President Kennedy announced an emergency credit offer of up to $25 million to the Dominican Republic, expressing encouragement over the country's progress toward restoring orderly democratic processes. The financial support follows the reinstatement of the civilian Council of State headed by President Rafael Bonnelly after the collapse of last week's abortive military coup. In Santo Domingo, Bonnelly confirmed that while figures implicated in the junta would face justice, former president Joaquin Balaguer remained free to travel wherever he chose. Balaguer, a prominent holdover from the dictatorship of Rafael Trujillo, had originally presided over the council formed on January 1 alongside anti-Trujillo opposition leaders.
records.summary_es: El presidente Kennedy anunció una oferta de crédito de emergencia de hasta 25 millones de dólares para la República Dominicana, manifestando su satisfacción ante los avances del país hacia el restablecimiento de procesos democráticos ordenados. El respaldo financiero llega tras la restitución del Consejo de Estado civil encabezado por el presidente Rafael Bonnelly después del fracaso del intento de golpe militar de la semana anterior. En Santo Domingo, Bonnelly confirmó que aquellos implicados en la junta serían sometidos a la justicia, pero que el expresidente Joaquín Balaguer gozaba de libertad para dirigirse adonde deseara. Balaguer, remanente de la dictadura de Rafael Trujillo, había encabezado inicialmente el consejo instaurado el 1 de enero junto a líderes opositores antitrujillistas.

Pedro Rodriguez Echavarria. The former armed forces chief remains under arrest following his unsuccessful attempt to impose a military junta on the Dominican Republic the previous week. records.headline: A news photograph caption describes anti-government strikers
records.summary_en: A news photograph caption describes anti-government strikers rolling barrels across a street in Santo Domingo to obstruct military traffic during intense rioting. The caption notes that a general strike, which virtually halted the Dominican economy, forced the resignation of President Joaquin Balaguer, characterized as one of the final holdovers of the Trujillo dictatorship. The newly established Dominican government, described as slightly left of center, is led by President Rafael F. Bonnelly.

El nuevo gobierno dominicano, descrito como de centroizquierda moderada, se encuentra encabezado por el presidente Rafael F. Bonnelly.

records.headline: The State and Defense Departments announced that a ten-member
records.summary_en: The State and Defense Departments announced that a ten-member military team will arrive in Santo Domingo to evaluate resuming a military assistance program requested by the new Dominican government. The survey team, comprising Army, Navy, and Air Force personnel, is headed by Brig. Gen. William A. Enemark, director of the Western Hemisphere office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense for International Security Affairs. The mission marks an additional step in regularizing relations following an earlier economic aid visit and the ongoing restoration of diplomatic ties. The United States had severed military aid to the Caribbean nation during the final months of the late dictator Rafael Trujillo's regime.
records.summary_es: Los Departamentos de Estado y de Defensa anunciaron que un equipo militar de diez miembros llegará a Santo Domingo para evaluar la reanudación de un programa de asistencia militar solicitado por el nuevo gobierno dominicano. La delegación evaluadora, integrada por personal del Ejército, la Armada y la Fuerza Aérea, está encabezada por el general de brigada William A. Enemark, director de la oficina del hemisferio occidental del subsecretario de defensa para asuntos de seguridad internacional. La misión representa un paso adicional en la normalización de las relaciones bilaterales tras la visita previa de una misión de ayuda económica y el restablecimiento en curso de los lazos diplomáticos. Los Estados Unidos habían suspendido la ayuda militar a la nación caribeña durante los últimos meses del régimen del difunto dictador Rafael Trujillo.

records.headline: United States Secretary of State Dean Rusk stated in Punta del Este that the United States welcomed a free Dominican Republic to the inter-American community
records.summary_en: United States Secretary of State Dean Rusk stated in Punta del Este that the United States welcomed a free Dominican Republic to the inter-American community, expressing hope that a free and progressive government would soon flourish in Havana so the Cuban people could join hemispheric goals. The editorial observes that at the Eighth Meeting of American Foreign Ministers, following more than thirty years of slavery under dictatorship, the Dominican people were honorably represented in a continental assembly. The presence of a Dominican delegation representing a genuine republic lent prestige to the Punta del Este meeting, establishing moral authority to combat communism and advocate democracy.
records.summary_es: El secretario de Estado de los Estados Unidos, Dean Rusk, afirmó en Punta del Este que Estados Unidos dio la bienvenida a una República Dominicana libre en la comunidad interamericana, manifestando su esperanza de que pronto florezca en La Habana un gobierno libre y progresista para que el pueblo cubano pueda unirse a las metas del hemisferio. El editorial señala que en la Octava Reunión de Consulta de Ministros de Relaciones Exteriores, tras más de treinta años de esclavitud bajo la dictadura, el pueblo dominicano estuvo honorablemente representado en una asamblea continental. La presencia de una delegación dominicana que representaba a una verdadera república aportó prestigio a la reunión de Punta del Este, consagrando la autoridad moral para combatir el comunismo y defender la democracia.
