records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* detailed the fortunes of the exiled Trujillo family residing in Florida, reporting the suicide of nephew General José García Trujillo in Miami. The article noted local controversy surrounding former President Héctor Trujillo's stay on Miami Beach's Sunset Island and contrasted the regime's public works achievements with its legacy of political oppression.

El artículo señaló la controversia local en torno a la estancia del expresidente Héctor Trujillo en Sunset Island, en Miami Beach, y contrastó las realizaciones en obras públicas del régimen con su legado de opresión política.

records.summary_en: In a biographical notice of a beverage company executive, a Louisville native and Coast Guard Academy graduate who served in the military from 1942 to 1946 is noted as having served as an officer aboard the Sea Cloud. The 317-foot yacht was once owned by Ambassador Joseph E. Davies and later by General Rafael L. Trujillo, Jr., of the Dominican Republic. The vessel has since been confiscated by the Dominican republic.

El yate de 317 pies perteneció primero al embajador Joseph E. Davies y más tarde al general Rafael L. Trujillo hijo, de la República Dominicana. Desde entonces, la embarcación ha sido confiscada por la república dominicana.

records.headline: That the United States and the Dominican Republic reached agreement
records.summary_en: That the United States and the Dominican Republic reached agreement on twenty-five million dollars in Alliance for Progress credits to help ease the country's economic burden, government sources in Santo Domingo reported. The reported accord concluded after nearly a month of negotiations over credit terms, following initial United States conditions that were branded harsh and unacceptable in some government quarters and openly denounced by extreme left-wing circles. While specific conditions were not made public, officials understood the terms to represent a considerable easing from previous proposals. A left-wing opposition newspaper had claimed earlier terms required four percent interest, credit use restricted to the American market, exclusive use of United States shipping, and partial American supervision of expenditures, though Dominican sources remarked that current terms were nowhere near those earlier demands.

records.headline: A group of about fifty anti-Communist demonstrators cheered
records.summary_en: A group of about fifty anti-Communist demonstrators cheered the United States outside the National Palace in Santo Domingo during the signing of an agreement granting the Dominican Republic a twenty-five million dollar credit. Placards carried by the demonstrators stated that they were hungry but wanted no disorders, extremism, or communism. The accord, concluded after a month of negotiations, made the funds available at a nominal interest rate of one percent with twenty years allowed for repayment. Left-wing opponents had previously asserted that the United States was demanding four percent interest, repayment within eight years, partial American supervision of expenditures, restriction of credit use to American markets, and exclusive use of United States shipping.
records.summary_es: Un grupo de unos cincuenta manifestantes anticomunistas aclamó a Estados Unidos frente al Palacio Nacional en Santo Domingo durante la firma de un acuerdo que concedió a la República Dominicana un crédito de veinticinco millones de dólares. Las pancartas portadas por los manifestantes afirmaban que tenían hambre pero no deseaban desórdenes, extremismo ni comunismo. El pacto, alcanzado tras un mes de negociaciones, puso a disposición los fondos a una tasa de interés nominal del uno por ciento con un plazo de veinte años para su reembolso. Opositores de izquierda habían denunciado previamente que Estados Unidos exigía un interés del cuatro por ciento, amortización en ocho años, supervisión parcial de los desembolsos por funcionarios estadounidenses, limitación de las compras a los mercados de Estados Unidos y transporte exclusivo en buques de bandera norteamericana.

records.headline: The Dominican Republic was placed under a state of emergency
records.summary_en: The Dominican Republic was placed under a state of emergency as authorities cracked down on terrorists accused of attempting to restore a dictatorship. The administration of President Rafael Bonnelly acted after vandals set fire to cane fields and sugar mills in the worst flareup since an abortive military coup was quelled the previous month. Bonnelly ordered the seizure of property belonging to members of the ousted Trujillo dictatorship, charging that his regime was menaced by a conspiracy from both the left and right. In declaring the emergency to defend the nation's incipient democracy, Bonnelly accused terrorists of following a plan to lead the country into chaos or totalitarian dictatorship, as six fresh fires raised the total number of blazes set in sugar mills and fields in recent weeks to 116. Informed sources also reported the arrest of five young leftists on charges of smuggling arms into the country.
records.summary_es: La República Dominicana fue declarada en estado de emergencia mientras las autoridades reprimían a terroristas acusados de intentar restaurar la dictadura. La administración del presidente Rafael Bonnelly intervino luego de que vándalos prendieran fuego a cañaverales e ingenios azucareros en el peor estallido registrado desde que se sofocó un golpe militar fallido el mes anterior. Bonnelly ordenó la incautación de bienes pertenecientes a miembros de la derrocada dictadura de Trujillo, denunciando que su régimen estaba amenazado por una conspiración procedente tanto de la izquierda como de la derecha. Al declarar la emergencia para defender la incipiente democracia del país, Bonnelly acusó a los terroristas de seguir un plan destinado a llevar a la nación hacia el caos o una dictadura totalitaria, al tiempo que seis nuevos incendios elevaron a 116 el total de siniestros provocados en cañaverales e ingenios en semanas recientes. Fuentes informadas reportaron también la detención de cinco jóvenes izquierdistas acusados de contrabandear armas al país.

records.summary_en: An Associated Press wirephoto caption reports that workers rushed into the home of a farmer on a sugarcane plantation near Santo Domingo to salvage possessions as flames consumed a cane field and menaced the dwelling. Authorities blamed the fire on extremists and identified it as one of many such blazes set in the area over the preceding few days. Total damage from the fires was estimated at about $2,700,000.

Las autoridades responsabilizaron del siniestro a extremistas y lo señalaron como uno de los múltiples incendios provocados en la zona en los últimos días. Los daños materiales ocasionados por los incendios se estimaron en unos 2.700.000 dólares.

records.headline: A dusk-to-dawn curfew cleared streets in the Dominican capital
records.summary_en: A dusk-to-dawn curfew cleared streets in the Dominican capital after crowds rioted when the government allowed former president Joaquin Balaguer and armed forces chief General Pedro Rodriguez Echavarria to leave the country. Demonstrators directed anger at the United States, charging the State Department was behind the leniency, while crowds shouted that the two men linked with the old Trujillo dictatorship should have been brought to trial. Street gangs burned two United States consulate cars, damaged two others, and set fire to automobiles and other property. Armed police patrols deployed to contain the demonstrations as businesses closed, schoolchildren were dismissed early, and Dominican officials stated the presence of the two men represented a threat to national tranquility.
records.summary_es: Un toque de queda de anochecer a amanecer despejó las calles de la capital dominicana después de que turbas se amotinaran al permitir el gobierno que el expresidente Joaquín Balaguer y el jefe de las fuerzas armadas, general Pedro Rodríguez Echavarría, abandonaran el país. Los manifestantes dirigieron su cólera contra Estados Unidos, acusando al Departamento de Estado de estar detrás de la benevolencia, mientras la multitud gritaba que ambos hombres vinculados a la antigua dictadura de Trujillo debieron ser llevados a juicio. Pandillas callejeras quemaron dos automóviles del consulado de Estados Unidos, dañaron otros dos e incendiaron vehículos particulares y otras propiedades. Patrullas policiales armadas se desplegaron para frenar las manifestaciones mientras los comercios cerraban, los escolares eran enviados a sus casas temprano y las autoridades dominicanas sostenían que la permanencia de ambos hombres representaba una amenaza para la tranquilidad nacional.

records.headline: Martin McReynolds reports, in a dispatch from Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: Martin McReynolds reports, in a dispatch from Santo Domingo, that street mobs attacked United States embassy offices and burned three official cars, including the ambassador's personal limousine, during widespread rioting and looting. The street disorders were ignited by the Dominican government's decision to permit two alleged enemies of the state to flee the country, and protested the United States granting them refuge on American soil. The two exiled figures were former president Joaquin Balaguer and former armed forces secretary General Pedro Rodriguez Echavarria, who had arrived in San Juan, Puerto Rico, en route to exile in Spain. The unrest was not exclusively anti-American: while a crowd of more than 1,900 youths attempted to storm the embassy's passport offices in the heart of the city, other demonstrators were shouting “down with the government” before the presidential palace and also demonstrating in Independence Square. The police used tear gas grenades to disperse park mobs after they broke into nearby offices of opposition political parties, and the mob which demonstrated before the palace also created a disturbance at the justice department, preventing the holding of a hearing on criminal charges against 18-year-old Rafael Bueno, described by police as a professional agitator. The march on the embassy was the day's most serious disorder, with police standing by idly as the thousand or more youths marched the length of El Conde street brandishing palm branches and carrying large pieces of iron for use as weapons; embassy guards quickly pulled down steel shutters over doors and windows, and the rioters smashed, overturned and set fire to the three vehicles — the personal limousine of Ambassador John B. Martin, a car owned by Passport Division Chief Matt Ortwein, and an embassy station wagon.

records.full_text:
Dominican Republic: Test for Democracy

Continued From Page A-1

tend to carry out what they call a "legal revolution." They plead for time and patience. They refuse to bring political criminals from the old regime to justice without proper legal preparations and fair trials.

"Our people must learn to wait. It is part of growing up," said one harrassed leader of the National Civic Union (UCN), the one-time opposition group of middle-class lawyers and doctors who now staff the new government.

Since the new government was installed during the last week in January, the UCN has changed from a national civic group to a mass political party. The seven members of the new State Council and their subordinates are only lieutenants in this group. But they have committed themselves to holding the fort until they resign next February after a new constitution has been drawn up and genuinely free elections are held in December.

All these democrats inside and outside the government have been tried in combat with the old Trujillo dynasty. Past suffering is their chief source of popular strength. Their claim to leadership rests on it. And they count on the continued "good sense" of the Dominican people who got rid of one of the worst dictatorships in Latin history with a minimum of bloodshed.

"But everyone seems to be in a big rush now," said Dr. Manuel Vaquero, secretary of the UCN. "No one wants to wait. People expect everything to change overnight." He and others told of fantastic claims for 400 per cent wage increases which—though justified in terms of living costs—cannot be met from near-empty coffers.

Statistics Tell Story

"How do we make people realize that the Trujillos left the country flat broke?" moaned another official. Statistics tell a woeful tale. An estimated 50 per cent of the million-man working force is unemployed. Books at the treasury have been rigged for so long no one is sure how much money is in circulation, how many millions the Trujillo family took out of the country with them, or how vast are their property holdings now in hands of a government receivership.

In such straits, the government and its supporters really rely on much more than the good will of the masses. They are counting on three main trump cards to see the new order through this painful "reconstruction" period:

1. Their own resolve to maintain law and order, even if temporary cost to their own popularity.

2. Quick economic recovery through well-prepared reforms.

3. All-out aid from the United States.

"Within legal limits we intend to put down everything which violates the public order," President Rafael Bonnelly said during an interview. "I and others have said this repeatedly on the radio, and we mean it." We spoke in the presidential palace where the State Council now presides.

Several days later the council issued a decree calling for deportation of "agitators and provocateurs" after proper legal investigation. Maximo Lopez Molina, chief Communist leader in the country, is currently being sought under this decree.

It was issued after gangs of terrorists had burned an estimated 245,000 tons of sugar cane (worth some $2.7 million) as it was being harvested in fields all over the island. The Dominican economy is based upon sugar, and this crop is absolutely vital for economic recovery.

Military Backs Leaders

In addition, the police have begun to crack down on gangs of anti-government youths. Recently pitched battles have raged around the Cafe Sublime, favorite hangout in the capital for organizing raids on city shops and the American consulate.

Government resolve seems to be strengthened by the conviction that the military stands firmly behind it. The Secretary for the Armed Forces is directly responsible to the new President. He has now moved his office into the presidential palace.

The feeling in Santo Domingo is that the young officers now taking over control in the military want to support constitutional government and will not meddle in politics, if—and it is a big if—the government keeps their oversized forces and privileges intact. For the moment, at least, the government appears to have little choice.

"Once the economy returns to normal, Communist subversion will not find fertile soil in the Dominican Republic," President Bonnelly said. "We hope to begin distributing the first land under the land reform in April," he added. "Everything is being planned now for the period of renovation."

This careful, step-by-step approach is the creed of the new order. It is the creed of basically conservative men with social consciences, men who believe in evolution, not revolution. Rather than drama, they want stability.

They have already raised the basic wage of sugar workers 100 per cent—to a minimum of $3.25 per day. These and other lesser wage increases—plus confiscation of the huge Trujillo holdings—are estimated to have redistributed 40 per cent of the wealth of the country already. An emergency public works program emphasizing manpower more than scarce materials is also making the first minor dent in widescale unemployment.

"We are open for foreign investment," affirmed Mr. Bonnelly, "and we want it. But that investment must benefit both the Dominican people and the investors. It will be channeled through our new planning commission."

U. S. Aid Important

It was a gentle—but clear—slap at the small trickle of North American "businessmen" who have arrived to speculate on the Dominican future. They check in at the best hotel in town and then pursue new officials with a high-pressure sales pitch.

But the new leaders are far more intent on how the United States Government lives up to its commitments of all-out aid. This potential aid is the third and by far the strongest trump in government hands. By general consensus the aid is essential to swift economic recovery. And that recovery, in turn, is essential for stable democratic government.

The stated North American aim is to build a "showcase of democracy" next to Castro's Cuba in the Caribbean. United States warships hastened the downfall of the Trujillo clan and their hangers-on last November. The United States took the lead in removing hemispheric economic and diplomatic sanctions in January, once the old order was completely removed.

Subsequently the Kennedy administration extended a $25 million long-term loan for emergency relief. The Dominican Republic has been readmitted to its share of the former Cuban sugar quota which at special prices in the United States should net another $25 million during the first half of 1962.

But that is just the beginning of United States involvement. A high-powered mission of the Agency for International Development has set up shop in the capital to help plan financing of long-range development. A new United States military mission has arrived to help train and educate the Dominican military for the new democratic order.

Some 50,000 simple Spanish-language pamphlets—"What is a Communist?"—already have gone through the United States Information Service office. Nine other similar titles in equal numbers are arriving. Ten distribution centers are being opened in the interior. Graphic documentary films on Castro's Cuba—one is entitled "The Eyewitness" — are shown in gatherings as varied as society clubs and workers meetings.

Battle Against Leftists

United States trade union officials — together with their democratic counterparts from Latin America — have helped set up a new trade union organization. This new "front" is fighting against a leftist-orientated group for the allegiance of some 100,000 workers now freed from the Trujillo-dominated Confederation of Dominican Workers.

An equally bitter struggle goes on at the autonomous University of Santo Domingo among some 4,000 unorganized students. Rebellion against the emerging order is greatest among youth. It is led by the "14th of June" group—a radical offshoot of the National Civic Union, and led by a young lawyer, Manuel Tavarez Justo.

Mr. Tavarez Justo and his followers identify themselves with Fidel Castro. They want the same "national solution" for the Dominican Republic as Mr. Castro has found for Cuba against "Yankee imperialism." They claim they are not Communist. Many refuse to believe Mr. Castro is a Communist. And their organization is a perfect cover for Communists who need to camouflage their real aims with nationalist labels.

In recent student elections at the university, the 14th of June group lost ground. Dominican student leaders who returned from exile in Costa Rica, Venezuela and Puerto Rico joined with home-trained Catholic action groups against the extremists.

Furthermore, all three candidates for new rector of the university are reputable democrats, and the government has recently called upon a special commission of the Organization of American States for assistance in reforming teaching methods.

The final battle is far from won—either among the students or elsewhere. The struggle for power can only gain in intensity in the months ahead. For all sides now know that the stakes go far beyond this small half an island perched between Cuba and Puerto Rico.

The United States and other democratic forces in the hemisphere are fully committed. Their prestige rides on the outcome.

Tomorrow: Mexico's Curious "American Complex."

records.headline: In the first article of a reporting series on the Americas in transition
records.summary_en: In the first article of a reporting series on the Americas in transition, George Sherman writes that the genuine struggle for the Dominican Republic is only beginning following the installation of a democratically inclined government after 32 years. Less than a year after the assassination of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo Molina, all trappings of tyranny have vanished, leaving only national chaos, misery, and a few defaced monuments to preserve his reign from oblivion. The central challenge confronting the country is whether democratic methods and leadership can hold together a bankrupt land bursting with newly unleashed freedom. As rival factions of urban workers, rural farmers, and university students contend for authority wrested from the old regime at the end of January, years of enforced silence have given way to demagoguery and bitter public conflict.
records.summary_es: En el primer reportaje de una serie sobre las Américas en transición, George Sherman escribe que la verdadera lucha por la República Dominicana apenas comienza tras la instauración de un gobierno de inclinación democrática después de 32 años. Menos de un año después del asesinato del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo Molina, todos los vestigios de la tiranía han desaparecido, dejando únicamente caos nacional, miseria y unos pocos monumentos desfigurados para salvar su régimen del olvido. El desafío central que enfrenta el país radica en si los métodos democráticos y sus dirigentes podrán mantener unida a una nación en bancarrota y desbordada por una libertad recién estrenada. Mientras facciones rivales de obreros urbanos, campesinos y estudiantes universitarios se disputan el poder arrebatado al antiguo régimen a finales de enero, los años de silencio forzoso han dado paso a la demagogia y a encarnizadas disputas públicas.

records.headline: A policeman was shot dead in Santo Domingo and at least one
records.summary_en: A policeman was shot dead in Santo Domingo and at least one other person was reported killed during a third consecutive day of violence in the Dominican Republic. Unknown gunmen firing from a speeding automobile killed the policeman and wounded two others, while one man was reported killed and several wounded in street clashes at San Cristobal, 18 miles from the capital. Knife-wielding youths also broke into two radio stations in Santo Domingo and broadcast appeals to overthrow the ruling Council of State, which was preparing the country for elections following a generation of Trujillo dictatorship.
records.summary_es: Un policía murió por disparos en Santo Domingo y se informó de al menos otra persona muerta durante una tercera jornada consecutiva de violencia en la República Dominicana. Pistoleros no identificados que abrieron fuego desde un automóvil en marcha mataron al agente e hirieron a otros dos, mientras que se reportó la muerte de un hombre y varios heridos en enfrentamientos callejeros en San Cristóbal, a 18 millas de la capital. Asimismo, jóvenes armados con cuchillos irrumpieron en dos emisoras de radio de Santo Domingo y transmitieron llamamientos para derrocar al gobernante Consejo de Estado, organismo que preparaba al país para elecciones tras una generación de dictadura trujillista.

records.headline: Julio Senior Hansen, Director General of Tourism for the Dominican
records.summary_en: Julio Senior Hansen, Director General of Tourism for the Dominican Republic, along with several travel officials from Santo Domingo, met with Virgin Islands Commissioner of Commerce Henry L. Kimelman to study the territory's expanding tourism industry. The visiting Dominican officials conferred with Commissioner Kimelman and commerce department representatives regarding strategies for boosting visitor travel across the Caribbean. The discussions placed special emphasis on reviving tourism to the Dominican Republic. Kimelman told the visitors, “Our problems are nice problems — only those caused by a skyrocketing economy,” adding that tourist expenditures in the Virgin Islands this year are expected to total $35,000,000, against $25,000,000 last year, and that advertising promotion and public relations were the key factors in building a tourist economy, with climate, cultural atmosphere and scenic beauty as the natural assets to be implemented by good facilities, food and service. Attending the meeting at the Department of Commerce were Alfredo Leschorn, Caribair's manager for Santo Domingo, G. Santoni Calero, Varig's manager for the Dominican Republic, and other travel executives, and the Dominican visitors sampled Charlotte Amalie's shopping bargains, toured St. Thomas, and were guests of the Department of Commerce at a luncheon at the Mountain Top Hotel.

records.headline: In the political maneuvering reaching a climax in the Dominican
records.summary_en: In the political maneuvering reaching a climax in the Dominican Republic, observers report evidence of anti-Catholicism among certain groups, manifested through indirect attacks where assailants attempt to conceal their identities. As an example, a group of young boys, many only 12-year-olds, entered the church of María Auxiliadora in a working-class neighborhood of Santo Domingo on April 21, creating disturbances by insulting churchgoers, making noise, and threatening violence. While the instigators of this disruption and several similar occurrences remain unconfirmed, the Santo Domingo daily El Caribe called on public authorities to prevent future outbreaks.
records.summary_es: En las maniobras políticas que alcanzan un punto culminante en la República Dominicana, los observadores señalan indicios de anticatolicismo entre ciertos grupos, manifestados mediante ataques indirectos en los que los agresores intentan ocultar su identidad. A modo de ejemplo, un grupo de muchachos, muchos de ellos de apenas 12 años de edad, ingresó a la iglesia de María Auxiliadora en un sector obrero de Santo Domingo el 21 de abril, causando desórdenes al insultar a los feligreses, hacer ruidos y amenazar con actos de violencia. Aunque aún no se ha determinado con certeza quién incitó ese incidente ni varios otros similares, el diario El Caribe de Santo Domingo instó a las autoridades a impedir nuevos brotes.

records.headline: A delegation of Virgin Islands officials and San Juan airline
records.summary_en: A delegation of Virgin Islands officials and San Juan airline and travel executives traveled to Santo Domingo aboard Caribair's new Convair as guests of airline president Dionisio Trigo. Senator Percival H. Reese of the Virgin Islands Legislature attended a luncheon at the El Embajador Hotel during the visit. Dominican Republic tourism head Sr. Hansen declared that the country is expanding promotional efforts to attract Caribbean vacationers and intends to emulate the Virgin Islands' successful advertising and public relations program. The visitors also attended a dinner meeting at the Santo Domingo Country Club with members of the Skoal Club, which plans to establish a Dominican chapter.

Los visitantes también asistieron a una cena en el Santo Domingo Country Club con miembros del Skoal Club, entidad que planea establecer una filial dominicana.

records.headline: The Dominican Republic was selected to replace El Salvador on the Inter-American Peace Commission
records.summary_en: The Dominican Republic was selected to replace El Salvador on the Inter-American Peace Commission by a vote of seventeen in favor and three abstentions. The editorial emphasizes that the entire hemisphere has welcomed the Dominican people's democratic reorganization, viewing this appointment as public recognition of the enduring nation and an inter-American vote of confidence in the moral responsibility of its new government. This post-dictatorship standing is contrasted with the previous thirty years under Trujillo, when the Dominican regime was repeatedly denounced before the commission for violating international laws, including complicity in an attempt against the life of a democratic president.

El editorial destaca que el continente entero ha recibido con beneplácito la reorganización democrática del pueblo dominicano, considerando este nombramiento como un reconocimiento público a una nación noble y un voto de confianza interamericano en la responsabilidad moral de su nuevo gobierno. Esta posición posterior a la dictadura contrasta con los más de treinta años bajo el régimen de Trujillo, cuando el gobierno dominicano fue denunciado en reiteradas ocasiones ante dicha comisión por violar las leyes internacionales, incluida su complicidad en un atentado contra la vida de un presidente democrático.

records.headline: Dominican pitcher Juan Marichal reflects on his off-season regimen
records.summary_en: Dominican pitcher Juan Marichal reflects on his off-season regimen after an earlier close play at first base sidelined him for the remainder of the previous season and winter. Discussing his career from the Dominican Republic, the report notes that sportswriters have bestowed numerous nicknames upon him, including 'Don Juan,' the 'Dominican Dandy,' and the 'Count of Montecristi.' Marichal has lived up to these monikers by pitching complete games for all of his victories this year while competing with Bob Purkey of Cincinnati and Don Drysdale of the Dodgers for top National League right-hander honors.

records.headline: United States and Dominican investigators have spent several months
records.summary_en: United States and Dominican investigators have spent several months reviewing long-locked files and questioning imprisoned members of Rafael Trujillo's intelligence police regarding the disappearance of Jesús de Galíndez. Opponents of Trujillo had long maintained that the dictator eliminated the Columbia University international law professor by having him drugged and flown to the Caribbean by an American pilot who subsequently vanished. A State Department source stated that following Trujillo's assassination in May 1961, the new Dominican government is eager to solve the case, which also links the disappearance of American freelance pilot Gerald Murphy. Murphy had arrived in the Dominican Republic on Dec. 3, 1956, after getting a job as a co-pilot on the Dominican airline. The Dominican government said Murphy was knocked into a shark-infested bay during a fight with another airline pilot, Octavio de La Maza, who later hanged himself in his prison cell, but Trujillo's opponents alleged that Murphy had piloted the plane carrying Galíndez and was later killed to silence him.
records.summary_es: Investigadores estadounidenses y dominicanos llevan varios meses revisando expedientes clausurados e interrogando a miembros de la policía secreta de Rafael Trujillo encarcelados, en relación con la desaparición de Jesús de Galíndez. Los adversarios de Trujillo sostuvieron durante mucho tiempo que el dictador eliminó al profesor de derecho internacional de la Universidad de Columbia haciéndolo narcotizar y trasladar en avión al país caribeño por medio de un piloto estadounidense que luego desapareció. Una fuente del Departamento de Estado afirmó que, tras el asesinato de Trujillo en mayo de 1961, el nuevo gobierno dominicano tiene sumo interés en resolver el caso, vinculado también a la desaparición del piloto estadounidense independiente Gerald Murphy. Murphy había llegado a la República Dominicana el 3 de diciembre de 1956, tras conseguir trabajo como copiloto en la aerolínea dominicana. El gobierno dominicano afirmó que Murphy fue arrojado a una bahía infestada de tiburones durante una pelea con otro piloto de la aerolínea, Octavio de La Maza, quien luego se ahorcó en su celda, pero los adversarios de Trujillo alegaron que Murphy había piloteado el avión que llevó a Galíndez y que luego fue asesinado para silenciarlo.

records.headline: The Kennedy administration is preparing to announce a special
records.summary_en: The Kennedy administration is preparing to announce a special assistance package for the Dominican Republic to support the nation's anti-communist administration. Strategic planners view the Dominican Republic's democratic progress as a crucial test case for Latin America to demonstrate how democratic governance compares against Castro communism in neighboring Cuba. Santo Domingo is governed by a seven-man Council of State that assumed control in January, bringing an end to the generation of dictatorship established by the late Rafael L. Trujillo which depleted the public treasury. The United States seeks to sustain the transitional government through scheduled elections expected by the end of the year.
records.summary_es: El gobierno de Kennedy prepara el anuncio de un paquete de asistencia especial para la República Dominicana con el fin de respaldar a la administración anticomunista del país. Los estrategas consideran que la evolución democrática dominicana constituye un ejemplo crucial para toda América Latina sobre cómo el sistema democrático puede superar al comunismo castrista de la vecina Cuba. records.headline: A State Department source disclosed that the Dominican government
records.summary_en: A State Department source disclosed that the Dominican government is eager to resolve the Jesús de Galíndez case to overcome the disrepute incurred during the regime of General Trujillo. Over recent months, United States and Dominican investigators have examined sealed records and interrogated members of Trujillo's intelligence apparatus held in prison. American freelance pilot Gerald Murphy disappeared in the Dominican Republic on December 3, 1956, after becoming an airline co-pilot. Dominican officials originally claimed Murphy was pushed into a shark-infested bay by fellow pilot Octavio de la Maza, who subsequently hanged himself in prison, but Trujillo opponents charged that Murphy flew Dr. Galíndez to the island and was murdered to ensure his silence.
records.summary_es: Una fuente del Departamento de Estado reveló que el gobierno dominicano tiene sumo interés en esclarecer el caso de Jesús de Galíndez para superar el descrédito adquirido bajo el régimen del general Trujillo. Durante los últimos meses, investigadores de Estados Unidos y de la República Dominicana han examinado expedientes sellados e interrogado a miembros de los cuerpos de inteligencia de Trujillo recluidos en prisión. El piloto independiente estadounidense Gerald Murphy desapareció en la República Dominicana el 3 de diciembre de 1956 tras emplearse como copiloto en la aerolínea dominicana. Aunque las autoridades dominicanas alegaron en su momento que Murphy cayó a una bahía infestada de tiburones tras una riña con el piloto Octavio de la Maza, quien luego se ahorcó en su celda, los opositores a Trujillo denunciaron que Murphy transportó en avión al Dr. Galíndez y fue asesinado para silenciarlo.

records.headline: An editorial argues that the House of Representatives should approve
records.summary_en: An editorial argues that the House of Representatives should approve a Senate amending bill to prevent severe economic injury to Peru, Argentina, and the Dominican Republic under recently enacted sugar legislation. The commentary warns that failing to provide legislative relief could destabilize moderate governments, including the administration that replaced the Trujillo dictatorship in Santo Domingo, leaving them vulnerable to overthrow by Castroite Communists. While criticizing sugar lobbyists for influencing initial congressional action, the paper expresses hope that the Senate's revision will establish meaningful reform in national sugar policy.
records.summary_es: Un editorial sostiene que la Cámara de Representantes debe aprobar el proyecto modificatorio del Senado para evitar un grave perjuicio económico a Perú, Argentina y la República Dominicana derivado de la legislación azucarera recién aprobada. El comentario advierte que la falta de una rectificación legislativa podría desestabilizar a los regímenes moderados, entre ellos la administración que sucedió a la dictadura de Trujillo en Santo Domingo, dejándolos expuestos a ser derrocados por comunistas castristas. Aunque critica a los cabilderos del azúcar por condicionar la legislación inicial, el periódico manifiesta su esperanza de que la medida del Senado dé paso a una auténtica reforma en la política azucarera.

records.headline: Representative Cooley, chairman of the House Agriculture Committee
records.summary_en: Representative Cooley, chairman of the House Agriculture Committee, strongly denied granting secret meetings to Dominican representatives or other foreign delegates following disclosures that agents of late dictator Rafael Trujillo attempted to influence him regarding sugar preferences. President Kennedy is working to gradually eliminate the lobbyist-dominated premium quota purchasing system while maintaining friendly diplomatic relations with Latin American nations. In response, the Senate passed an amendment allocating additional sugar quotas to three dissatisfied countries—the Dominican Republic, Argentina, and Peru—requiring final confirmation by the House.
records.summary_es: El representante Cooley, presidente del Comité de Agricultura de la Cámara, desmintió categóricamente haber concedido reuniones secretas a emisarios dominicanos u otras delegaciones tras revelarse que agentes del extinto dictador Rafael Trujillo intentaron influir en él sobre preferencias azucareras. El presidente Kennedy busca suprimir de manera gradual el sistema de cuotas preferenciales que atrae cabilderos, procurando preservar a la vez relaciones cordiales con los países latinoamericanos. Ante esta situación, el Senado aprobó una enmienda que asigna cuotas azucareras adicionales a tres países inconformes —la República Dominicana, Argentina y Perú—, medida que ahora depende de la ratificación de la Cámara de Representantes.

records.headline: Dr. José Fernández Caminero of the Dominican Republic Council of State
records.summary_en: Dr. José Fernández Caminero of the Dominican Republic Council of State and Juan Bonnelly, son of President Rafael Bonnelly, led a Dominican delegation visiting St. Thomas. The group, which included leading travel agents and representatives of Dominican radio and newspaper organizations, arrived at Harry S. Truman Airport aboard a Caribair Convair flight hosted by airline president Dionisio Trigo. Official arrival ceremonies at the airport featured the presentation of a Dominican Republic flag to a representative of the Virgin Islands Department of Commerce. The presentation was a gesture of inter-island good will: a delegation of Virgin Islands officials, on a recent trip to Santo Domingo, had presented their territorial flag to Julio Senior, Director General of Tourism for the Dominican Republic. The Dominican visitors were to be given a police-escorted motorcade through downtown Charlotte Amalie, winding up at Bluebeard's Castle Hotel for an official luncheon, where they would be officially welcomed by Governor Paiewonsky and Caribair President Trigo. After the luncheon, the balance of the afternoon was left free for a sightseeing tour and shopping in the free port shops of St. Thomas, and the Caribair Convair was scheduled to depart St. Thomas shortly after 5 p.m. for a direct return flight to Santo Domingo.
records.summary_es: El Dr. José Fernández Caminero del Consejo de Estado de la República Dominicana y Juan Bonnelly, hijo del presidente Rafael Bonnelly, encabezaron una delegación dominicana en visita oficial a Saint Thomas. El grupo, que incluía a destacados agentes de viajes y representantes de emisoras y periódicos dominicanos, llegó al aeropuerto Harry S. Truman a bordo de un vuelo de Convair de Caribair cortesía del presidente de la aerolínea, Dionisio Trigo. Los actos oficiales de bienvenida en el aeropuerto incluyeron la entrega de una bandera de la República Dominicana a un representante del Departamento de Comercio de las Islas Vírgenes. La entrega fue un gesto de buena voluntad interinsular: una delegación de funcionarios de las Islas Vírgenes, en un viaje reciente a Santo Domingo, había entregado su bandera territorial a Julio Senior, director general de Turismo de la República Dominicana. Los visitantes dominicanos recibirían una caravana con escolta policial por el centro de Charlotte Amalie, que terminaría en el Bluebeard's Castle Hotel para un almuerzo oficial, donde serían recibidos oficialmente por el gobernador Paiewonsky y el presidente de Caribair, Trigo. Después del almuerzo, el resto de la tarde quedaría libre para una visita turística y compras en las tiendas francas de St. Thomas, y el Convair de Caribair tenía previsto partir de St. Thomas poco después de las 5 p.m. en vuelo directo de regreso a Santo Domingo.

records.headline: A published roster identifies Dominican editors, commercial figures
records.summary_en: A published roster identifies Dominican editors, commercial figures, and public officials scheduled to make a goodwill trip from Santo Domingo. The media delegation includes editors and editorial staff from La Nación, El Caribe, and the magazine Ahora, accompanied by hotel executives from El Embajador and the Hotel Jaragua Corporation. Other participants encompass travel agency managers from Vimenca and Patem, the president of the Dominican Republic Chamber of Commerce, the manager of the Bank of Nova Scotia, and airport customs and migration officials. Tentatively scheduled to join the traveling party are central banking administrators and Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs José A. Bonilla.
records.summary_es: Una lista publicada detalla a directores de periódicos, figuras comerciales y funcionarios públicos de Santo Domingo programados para realizar una visita de buena voluntad. La delegación periodística incluye a directores y redactores de La Nación, El Caribe y la revista Ahora, junto con ejecutivos hoteleros de El Embajador y la Corporación Hotel Jaragua. Otros participantes comprenden a directivos de agencias de viajes como Vimenca y Patem, el presidente de la Cámara de Comercio de la República Dominicana, el gerente del Bank of Nova Scotia y autoridades de aduanas y migración del aeropuerto. Asimismo, figuran provisionalmente en la comitiva directivos del Banco Central y el secretario de Estado de Relaciones Exteriores, José A. Bonilla.

records.headline: Twenty-one Peace Corps volunteers completed preliminary training
records.summary_en: Twenty-one Peace Corps volunteers completed preliminary training in Puerto Rico and have advanced to the concluding phase of preparation in the Dominican Republic. Administrator Simms is assigned to collaborate with André Hernandez of New Mexico, who serves as Peace Corps Representative in the country. A second group of volunteers will depart for Santo Domingo soon, with more than 200 personnel expected on duty by the end of the year to serve a population of three million people. The program provides assistance in education, community development, forestry, cooperative organizing, housing, well drilling, and self-help school construction.
records.summary_es: Veintiún voluntarios del Cuerpo de Paz completaron su preparación preliminar en Puerto Rico y avanzaron a la fase final de capacitación en la República Dominicana. El administrador Simms fue asignado para colaborar con André Hernandez, de Nuevo México, quien ejerce como representante del Cuerpo de Paz en el país. Un segundo grupo de voluntarios partirá en breve hacia Santo Domingo, y se espera que más de 200 colaboradores estén prestando servicio para fines de año para atender a una población de tres millones de personas. El programa abarca asistencia en educación, desarrollo comunal, silvicultura, organización de cooperativas, vivienda, perforación de pozos y construcción escolar por esfuerzo propio.

records.headline: An editorial reflects on exchange flights sponsored by Caribair
records.summary_en: An editorial reflects on exchange flights sponsored by Caribair that brought Dominican leaders to Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands while enabling American islanders to tour the Dominican Republic. The commentary expects these reciprocal trips to produce beneficial effects on Santo Domingo's fiscal affairs as the nation emerges from political and economic instability. Recounting personal impressions from a recent visit as an airline guest, the writer found luxury hotels largely shuttered or empty and hospital staff well-meaning but unprepared. While forecasting that the Dominican Republic will become an important Caribbean tourism hub in several years, the paper notes that substantial reconstruction remains necessary among a still-unsettled public.
records.summary_es: Un editorial reflexiona sobre los vuelos de intercambio patrocinados por Caribair que llevaron a dirigentes dominicanos a Puerto Rico y las Islas Vírgenes y permitieron a ciudadanos de las islas estadounidenses visitar la República Dominicana. El comentario confía en que estos viajes recíprocos generen un impacto positivo en las finanzas de Santo Domingo mientras la nación sale de la inestabilidad política y económica. Al compartir sus impresiones sobre una visita reciente como invitado de la aerolínea, el autor observó que los hoteles de lujo se encuentran prácticamente cerrados o vacíos y que el personal de servicio, aunque hospitalario, carece de preparación adecuada. Si bien pronostica que en pocos años la República Dominicana se convertirá en un centro turístico relevante del Caribe, el escrito destaca que aún se requiere un amplio programa de reconstrucción entre una población todavía intranquila.

records.headline: Community organizer Simms, who led efforts during the 1950s
records.summary_en: Community organizer Simms, who led efforts during the 1950s to eliminate race and color designations on New York City birth certificates, has accepted an appointment as deputy Peace Corps representative in the Dominican Republic. Simms and his wife, Patricia, will take up residence in the capital city of Santo Domingo. A graduate of the University of Kansas music program, Simms will serve as chief assistant to André Hernandez of New Mexico, head of the Dominican contingent. In this post, Simms will support the overall administrative direction and supervision of Peace Corps operations across the country.
records.summary_es: El líder comunitario Simms, quien encabezó protestas durante la década de 1950 para suprimir las designaciones de raza y color en las actas de nacimiento de la ciudad de Nueva York, aceptó el nombramiento como representante adjunto del Cuerpo de Paz en la República Dominicana. Simms y su esposa, Patricia, fijarán su residencia en la capital, Santo Domingo. Egresado de la facultad de música de la Universidad de Kansas, Simms se desempeñará como asistente principal de André Hernandez, de Nuevo México, titular de la delegación en el país. En este cargo, Simms colaborará en la coordinación general y supervisión de los proyectos del Cuerpo de Paz en territorio dominicano.

records.headline: A bilingual column reflects on authoritarian regimes in the hemisphere
records.summary_en: A bilingual column reflects on authoritarian regimes in the hemisphere, acknowledging that right-wing dictatorships have severely suppressed political freedom. It characterizes the Dominican Republic's experience under Rafael Trujillo as an omnipotent tyrant as a horrible, cruel, and brutal episode. However, the commentary contends that right-wing rulers never reached the extremes of communist governance, asserting that Soviet-backed rule under Fidel Castro in Cuba systematically attacks private property, religion, family structures, and personal honor. The paper concludes that the daily atrocities in Cuba justify disregarding minor legal technicalities to enable swift liberating action.
records.summary_es: Una columna bilingüe reflexiona sobre los regímenes autoritarios en el hemisferio, reconociendo que las dictaduras de derecha reprimieron de forma implacable la libertad política. Califica la experiencia de la República Dominicana bajo el mando de Rafael Trujillo como tirano omnipotente de episodio horrible, cruel y brutal. No obstante, el comentario sostiene que los gobernantes de derecha jamás llegaron a los extremos de los regímenes comunistas, afirmando que el modelo soviético encabezado por Fidel Castro en Cuba vulnera sistemáticamente la propiedad privada, la fe, la familia y el honor personal. La publicación concluye que las atrocidades cotidianas en Cuba justifican pasar por alto formalismos legales secundarios para facilitar una pronta acción liberadora.

records.headline: An editorial highlights growing diplomatic concerns surrounding
records.summary_en: An editorial highlights growing diplomatic concerns surrounding Hispaniola, noting that two-thirds of the island and nearly half of its 6.2 million people are in the Dominican Republic, with Haiti comprising the remainder. While the Dominican Republic was freed from the Trujillo clan with State Department encouragement, the commentary warns that rival factions are competing for power and could produce a Castro-style communist regime. The paper questions why Washington pays $108 per ton for government-owned Dominican sugar compared to $56 on the world market, arguing that the United States may be bankrolling an administration destined to turn adversarial.

El diario cuestiona además que Washington pague $108 por tonelada por el azúcar estatal dominicano frente a los $56 del mercado mundial, advirtiendo que Estados Unidos podría estar financiando a un gobierno que luego resulte adversario.

records.headline: Canadian immigration authorities have ordered the deportation of Arturo
records.summary_en: Canadian immigration authorities have ordered the deportation of Arturo Espaillat, former head of the secret police under the late Dominican Dictator Rafael Trujillo. Espaillat, who served as state secretary for security when Trujillo was assassinated on May 31, 1961, lived quietly in Ottawa for 10 months with his wife, daughter, and two sons following his arrival on November 4, 1961. Known in the Dominican Republic as the 'Razor Blade,' the 40-year-old former official was served deportation orders after losing an extended behind-the-scenes effort to secure permanent immigrant status in Canada.
records.summary_es: Las autoridades de inmigración canadienses ordenaron la deportación de Arturo Espaillat, exjefe de la policía secreta del extinto dictador dominicano Rafael Trujillo. Espaillat, quien se desempeñaba como secretario de Estado de Seguridad cuando Trujillo fue ultimado por ajusticiadores el 31 de mayo de 1961, residió discretamente en Ottawa durante 10 meses junto a su esposa, su hija y sus dos hijos tras ingresar al país el 4 de noviembre de 1961. Conocido en la República Dominicana con el sobrenombre de 'Navajita' ('Razor Blade'), el exfuncionario de 40 años recibió la orden de expulsión tras fracasar en sus prolongadas gestiones reservadas para obtener el estatuto de inmigrante permanente en Canadá.

records.summary_en: The Canadian Immigration Department stated that Mr. Espaillat, wanted in the United States for questioning by the FBI, has been given 30 days from Tuesday, September 18, to leave Canada voluntarily. The deportation order does not apply to his wife, Ligia Fernandez, his 13-year-old daughter Rita, or his two sons, Arturo Jose, 11, and Rafael Alberto, 8. Espaillat was Dominican consul in New York in 1957 when Jesus de Galindez, an outspoken critic of the Trujillo regime, disappeared. records.headline: An Associated Press dispatch reports that a disciplined and well-organized
records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch reports that a disciplined and well-organized Castro-Communist hard core numbering perhaps 70,000 members intends to plunge the Dominican Republic into violent confusion ahead of national elections scheduled for December. Communists are believed to be smuggling arms and ammunition from Cuba to disrupt the nation's progress, while anti-communist citizens rally around the slogan 'Basta ya!' ('Knock it off and get to work'). That rallying cry was shouted in Santo Domingo's Independencia Square following July riots by Dr. Viriato Fiallo, a 67-year-old physician-philosopher running for president under the National Civic Union banner. Fiallo, who endured prison and persecution under the dictatorship, expressed confidence that a vigorous United States aid program—which he likened in scale to the Marshall Plan for Europe—will help defeat the Communist push.

Se cree que los comunistas están contrabandeando armas y municiones desde Cuba para frenar el avance de la nación, mientras ciudadanos anticomunistas se agrupan bajo el lema '¡Basta ya!'. records.headline: The Petal Paper contrasts a congressional exchange between Senators Ellender
records.summary_en: The Petal Paper contrasts a congressional exchange between Senators Ellender and Eastland—who credited Rafael Trujillo with establishing stability, ruling with a strong arm, and opposing communism—with recent findings by Dominican prosecutor Rafael Valera Benitez. Quoted by Dom Bonafede of the Miami Herald, the 34-year-old prosecutor investigating the trail of murder left by Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo estimated that Trujillo killed at least 100,000 people and probably many thousands more during his 30-year rule. Valera Benitez stated that it was impossible to estimate the number of people beaten and tortured, noting that few families lacked a victim and comparing the country to walking over a field of skeletons.

Citado por Dom Bonafede del Miami Herald, el fiscal de 34 años encargado de investigar el rastro de asesinatos dejado por el generalísimo Rafael Trujillo calculó que Trujillo mató al menos a 100.000 personas y probablemente a muchos miles más durante sus 30 años de mandato. Valera Benítez afirmó que resulta imposible calcular el número de personas golpeadas y torturadas, señalando que casi ninguna familia quedó sin víctimas y comparando el país con caminar sobre un campo de esqueletos.

records.headline: In a letter to the editor of the Evening Star, Frederick I. Ordway
records.summary_en: In a letter to the editor of the Evening Star, Frederick I. Ordway, Jr. criticizes United States foreign policy for undermining friendly regimes while accommodating neutral and hostile governments worldwide. He asserts that the United States helped ease out friendly leaders including Batista in Cuba and Trujillo in the Dominican Republic. Ordway warns that the Dominican Republic may become the next communist victory, arguing that once leftist elements gain control and unleash forces for agrarian reform, the trend becomes difficult to reverse.
records.summary_es: En una carta al editor de Evening Star, Frederick I. Ordway, Jr. critica la política exterior de los Estados Unidos por socavar regímenes amigos mientras contemporiza con gobiernos neutrales y hostiles en todo el mundo. Afirma que los Estados Unidos ayudaron a apartar del poder a gobernantes aliados como Batista en Cuba y Trujillo en la República Dominicana. Ordway advierte que la República Dominicana podría convertirse en la próxima victoria comunista, sosteniendo que una vez que los sectores de izquierda tomen el control y desaten fuerzas hacia la reforma agraria, resultará difícil revertir esa tendencia.

records.summary_en: That all Latin American nations will be invited to send observers for the Dominican Republic's general election on December 20, marking the country's first free vote in 38 years, Foreign Minister Antonio Bonilla Atiles announced. He stated in an interview that an effort would even be made to invite Cuban observers, while official invitations to other nations would be conveyed through the Organization of American States. Seven candidates are seeking the presidency of the Dominican Republic, which had been governed by the Trujillo dictatorship through most of the years since United States Marines ended their occupation in 1924. Dominicans will also elect 74 deputies and 27 senators.

records.headline: Associated Press correspondent Robert Berrellez reports from Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: Associated Press correspondent Robert Berrellez reports from Santo Domingo on the widespread adoption of 'oye burgués' among the Dominican poor as an all-purpose verbal dart popularized by leftist orators. The phrase reflects a national election campaign turning into a struggle between the haves and have-nots ahead of the country's first free vote in 38 years. Berrellez notes that traditional street campaigning is largely absent, with campaign messages confined to radio and newspapers in a country where half the population is illiterate. A year after emerging from dictatorship, a general sense of well-being has fostered political apathy, leaving citizens to view the peaceful atmosphere as a pleasant dream.
records.summary_es: El corresponsal de Associated Press Robert Berrellez informa desde Santo Domingo sobre la adopción generalizada de la expresión 'oye burgués' entre las clases populares dominicanas como un dardo verbal de uso común difundido por oradores de izquierda. La frase refleja una campaña electoral nacional que se va transformando en una disputa entre ricos y desposeídos antes de las primeras votaciones libres del país en 38 años. Berrellez señala que la propaganda tradicional en las calles está ausente y los mensajes se limitan a la radio y la prensa en un país donde la mitad de la población es analfabeta. Un año después de salir de la dictadura, una sensación general de bienestar ha generado cierta apatía política, llevando a los ciudadanos a percibir este clima pacífico como un grato sueño.

records.headline: The party of presidential candidate Juan Bosch demanded a postponement of the Dominican
records.summary_en: The party of presidential candidate Juan Bosch demanded a postponement of the Dominican elections, one month, after a Spanish Jesuit priest publicly charged that Bosch is a Communist. Bosch, who fought the late dictator Rafael L. Trujillo from exile for 25 years, and Dr. Viriato Fiallo, 67, of the rightist National Civic Union, are considered the two leading candidates in a field of seven. The governing Council of State gave no immediate answer to the postponement request but warned that interference by foreign elements, potentially including foreign clergy, would not be tolerated. Archbishop Octavio Beras of Santo Domingo and three Dominican bishops affirmed the Catholic Church's neutral position and denied attempting to persuade peasants against voting for Bosch.
records.summary_es: El partido del candidato presidencial Juan Bosch exigió postergar las elecciones dominicanas, por un mes, después de que un sacerdote jesuita español acusara públicamente a Bosch de ser comunista. Bosch, quien combatió desde el exilio al difunto dictador Rafael L. Trujillo durante 25 años, y el doctor Viriato Fiallo, de 67 años, de la derechista Unión Cívica Nacional, son considerados los dos principales candidatos entre siete contendientes. El Consejo de Estado gobernante no ofreció una respuesta inmediata a la solicitud de aplazamiento, pero advirtió que no tolerará la interferencia de elementos extranjeros, lo que podría incluir al clero foráneo. El arzobispo Octavio Beras de Santo Domingo y tres obispos dominicanos ratificaron la postura neutral de la Iglesia católica y negaron intentar persuadir a los campesinos para que no votaran por Bosch.

records.summary_en: The Associated Press reported from Santo Domingo that the Dominican Republic is prepared to conduct its first dictator-free election in 38 years on Thursday after a major dispute was resolved. The Rev. Laudico Garcia, a Spanish Jesuit, retracted his accusation that the left-of-center Dominican Revolutionary Party was communistic during a five-hour radio and television debate with presidential nominee Juan Bosch. Bosch expressed satisfaction with the priest's explanation and the positive public reaction. Consequently, party leaders met with a majority favoring the withdrawal of their boycott threat and their demand for a one-month postponement of the election.

Bosch expresó su satisfacción con las explicaciones del sacerdote y con la favorable respuesta popular. En consecuencia, la directiva del partido se reunió con una mayoría inclinada a retirar la amenaza de boicot y la solicitud de posponer las elecciones por un mes.

records.headline: The Associated Press reported from Santo Domingo on December 19 that Dominicans are carrying concealed firearms
records.summary_en: The Associated Press reported from Santo Domingo on December 19 that Dominicans are carrying concealed firearms as political tension rises on the eve of the nation's first free election in 38 years. The vote concludes a 19-month transition period from the Trujillo dictatorship to representative government. While relative peace had prevailed in recent months, tension erupted into scuffles and gunfire into the air the previous night before helmeted riot squads dispersed crowds, although a weekend dispute involving a major party appeared settled.
records.summary_es: The Associated Press informó desde Santo Domingo el 19 de diciembre que los dominicanos portan armas de fuego ocultas ante el aumento de la tensión política en vísperas de las primeras elecciones libres del país en 38 años. La votación pone fin a un período de transición de 19 meses desde la dictadura de Trujillo hacia un gobierno representativo. Si bien en los meses recientes había prevalecido una relativa calma, las tensiones desembocaron en forcejeos y disparos al aire la noche anterior antes de que escuadrones antimotines con cascos dispersaran a la multitud, aun cuando una disputa de fin de semana con uno de los partidos principales parecía resuelta.

records.headline: The Associated Press reported from Santo Domingo that thousands of Dominicans voted
records.summary_en: The Associated Press reported from Santo Domingo that thousands of Dominicans voted peacefully on December 20 in their first free election in 38 years, dispelling predictions of low voter turnout. Ruled by a provisional government since the collapse of the Trujillo dictatorship in 1961, the country is selecting leaders for the next four years under nearly ideal weather conditions. Unlike past elections under the dictatorship, when failing to vote for the regime's party could result in hard labor, citizens turned out in large numbers hoping to secure stable representative government. Despite disputes during the final days of the campaign, minimal police presence was needed to keep order as election results are awaited by Christmas.
records.summary_es: The Associated Press informó desde Santo Domingo que miles de dominicanos votaron de manera pacífica el 20 de diciembre en sus primeras elecciones libres en 38 años, disipando los pronósticos de una escasa concurrencia a las urnas. Gobernado por una administración provisional desde el colapso de la dictadura de Trujillo en 1961, el país elige a sus dirigentes para los próximos cuatro años bajo condiciones meteorológicas prácticamente ideales. A diferencia de las elecciones pasadas bajo la dictadura, en las que no votar por el partido del régimen podía acarrear penas de trabajos forzados, los ciudadanos acudieron en gran número con la esperanza de afianzar un gobierno representativo estable. Pese a las discrepancias en los últimos días de la campaña, se requirió una mínima presencia policial para preservar el orden mientras se esperan los resultados electorales para Navidad.

records.headline: United Press International reported from Santo Domingo on December 21
records.summary_en: United Press International reported from Santo Domingo on December 21 that the left-leaning Dominican Revolutionary Party surged into an impressive early lead in unofficial returns from the Dominican Republic's first free election in 38 years. Compilations by independent newspapers and radio stations showed reform-minded Juan Bosch running far ahead of Dr. Viriato Fiallo of the Conservative Civic Union in the presidential race. While unofficial returns favored Bosch's party, observers noted that the absence of recent electoral benchmarks precluded definite predictions of the final outcome.

Los datos reunidos por periódicos y radioemisoras independientes mostraron al reformista Juan Bosch muy por delante del doctor Viriato Fiallo, de la conservadora Unión Cívica, en la contienda presidencial. Aunque los resultados extraoficiales favorecían al partido de Bosch, los analistas señalaron que la falta de referentes electorales recientes impedía emitir predicciones definitivas sobre el resultado final.

records.headline: Nearly complete unofficial election returns in Santo Domingo indicate
records.summary_en: Nearly complete unofficial election returns in Santo Domingo indicate that moderate leftist candidate Juan Bosch of the Dominican Revolutionary Party routed conservative opponent Dr. Viriato A. Fiallo of the National Civic Union by 300.000 votes. Both candidates are regarded as friendly to the United States, and the balloting marked the country's first free vote after long years of the Trujillo dictatorship. Roman Catholic Archbishop Octavio Beras of Santo Domingo called upon the defeated candidates to accept the verdict of the voters and collaborate for the people's welfare. Bosch, who campaigned on a pledge of dignity against money, proved particularly strong in the federal district surrounding the capital.
records.summary_es: Los cómputos extraoficiales casi definitivos en Santo Domingo indican que el candidato de izquierda moderada Juan Bosch, del Partido Revolucionario Dominicano, derrotó ampliamente a su rival conservador, el Dr. Viriato A. Fiallo, de la Unión Cívica Nacional, por 300.000 votos. Ambos candidatos son considerados favorables a los Estados Unidos, y la votación constituyó el primer sufragio libre del país tras largos años de dictadura trujillista. El arzobispo católico Octavio Beras de Santo Domingo exhortó a los candidatos derrotados a aceptar el veredicto popular y colaborar por el bienestar colectivo. Bosch, cuya campaña se basó en el lema de dignidad frente al dinero, mostró especial fuerza en el distrito federal que rodea la capital.

El artículo destaca la estatura continental de Bosch y sus prolongados años de exilio consagrados a promover la democracia frente a las dictaduras, recordando que fue elegido para presidir el mandato que inicia el 27 de febrero.

records.headline: Outfielder Felipe Alou confirmed in Santo Domingo that he and San Francisco Giants teammate
records.summary_en: Outfielder Felipe Alou confirmed in Santo Domingo that he and San Francisco Giants teammate Juan Marichal were each fined 8250 for playing exhibition baseball games in the Dominican Republic last November without league permission. Major League Commissioner Ford Frick announced in New York that several players were fined a total of 82,500 for unauthorized play in the country. Alou called the disciplinary action arbitrary, asserting that as Dominicans they have a right to play in their own country, and stated that none of the players had paid the fines. Other major league players listed as having played in the country that winter include Camilo Pascual, Pedro Ramos, Leo Posada, Jake Azcue, Julian Javier, and Diomedes Olivo.
records.summary_es: El jardinero Felipe Alou confirmó en Santo Domingo que él y su compañero de los Gigantes de San Francisco, el lanzador Juan Marichal, fueron multados con 8250 cada uno por jugar partidos de exhibición en la República Dominicana el pasado noviembre sin la debida autorización de las Grandes Ligas. El comisionado Ford Frick anunció en Nueva York multas por un total de 82,500 a varios peloteros por jugar en el país sin el permiso reglamentario. Alou consideró arbitraria la sanción, manifestando que como dominicanos tienen derecho a jugar en su patria, y señaló que ninguno de los jugadores había abonado la multa. Otros peloteros de Grandes Ligas que jugaron en el país ese invierno fueron Camilo Pascual, Pedro Ramos, Leo Posada, Jake Azcue, Julián Javier y Diómedes Olivo.

records.headline: A federal grand jury in Washington returned a four-count indictment
records.summary_en: A federal grand jury in Washington returned a four-count indictment charging New York newspaper gossip columnist Igor Cassini with failing to register as an American publicity agent for the Trujillo government of the Dominican Republic. The indictment accuses the 47-year-old columnist of sharing in nearly 1200,000 in payments from the Dominican government, naming 76-year-old New York attorney R. Paul Englander as a co-defendant on two counts. Attorney General Robert F. Kennedy stated that both defendants were indicted under the Foreign Agents Registration Act of 1938 following a six-month FBI investigation. Named as co-conspirators were Martin T. Birnbaum, E. Haring Chandor, and former public relations man Pablo Frontaura.
records.summary_es: Un gran jurado federal en Washington presentó una acusación de cuatro cargos contra el columnista de sociedad neoyorquino Igor Cassini por no haberse registrado como agente publicitario estadounidense del gobierno de Trujillo en la República Dominicana. La acusación señala al columnista de 47 años de participar en casi 1200,000 en pagos recibidos del gobierno dominicano, nombrando al abogado de 76 años R. Paul Englander como coacusado en dos cargos. El fiscal general Robert F. Kennedy afirmó que ambos fueron procesados bajo la Ley de Registro de Agentes Extranjeros de 1938 tras una pesquisa del FBI de seis meses. Como co-conspiradores fueron identificados Martin T. Birnbaum, E. Haring Chandor y el ex relacionista público Pablo Frontaura.

records.headline: Republican members of Congress intend to question Mr. Roosevelt

records.headline: In the search for the hijacked Venezuelan freighter Anzoategui
records.summary_en: In the search for the hijacked Venezuelan freighter Anzoategui, shipping circles in Caracas reported that the motorship Sucre sighted the vessel midway between Venezuela and the Dominican Republic. The sighting placed the freighter roughly 450 miles southeast of Santiago, Cuba. Venezuelan President Rómulo Betancourt ordered an all-out effort to intercept the hijackers, identified as nine members of the Communist Armed Forces for National Liberation (FALN) linked to Fidel Castro's regime.

El avistamiento ubicó al carguero a unas 450 millas al sureste de Santiago de Cuba. records.headline: New York gossip columnist Igor Cassini and 76-year-old attorney
records.summary_en: New York gossip columnist Igor Cassini and 76-year-old attorney R. Paul Englander pleaded not guilty in District Court to indictments charging them with failing to register as American publicity agents for the former Trujillo government of the Dominican Republic. Chief District Court Judge Mathew F. McGuire set bail for each defendant at $1,000 and scheduled trial for May 13. Prominent author and attorney Louis Nizer appeared for Cassini, stating that the defense would require trips to various foreign countries to obtain witnesses and documents.

El destacado jurista y escritor Louis Nizer compareció en representación de Cassini y expuso que la defensa requerirá trasladarse a diversos países extranjeros para conseguir testigos y documentos.

records.headline: A restricted cablegram from the U.S. Embassy characterized the Vice President's visit
records.summary_en: A restricted cablegram from the U.S. Embassy characterized the Vice President's visit as an outstanding success, after State Department officials feared demonstrations during LBJ's flight to the Dominican Republic for President Bosch's inauguration. The Embassy reported that crowds of ordinary Dominicans warmly received Johnson and that the local press highlighted his embrace of Bosch in the Latin American manner. President Bosch was described as pleased and impressed by an ambulance presented by the Vice President in the name of the American people, while Mrs. Johnson's visits to a school for the blind and a maternity hospital received widespread media coverage. The dispatch concluded that Johnson's unaffected mixing with crowds produced a strong and favorable impact, noting that driving through the city without hostility would have been unlikely months earlier.
records.summary_es: Un cablegrama confidencial de la embajada estadounidense calificó la visita del vicepresidente como un éxito sobresaliente, después de que funcionarios del Departamento de Estado temieran manifestaciones durante el vuelo de LBJ a la República Dominicana para la toma de posesión del presidente Bosch. La embajada informó que multitudes de dominicanos comunes recibieron calurosamente a Johnson y que la prensa local destacó su abrazo a Bosch al estilo latinoamericano. El presidente Bosch fue descrito como complacido e impresionado por una ambulancia entregada por el vicepresidente en nombre del pueblo estadounidense, mientras que las visitas de la señora Johnson a una escuela para ciegos y a un hospital de maternidad recibieron amplia cobertura mediática. El despacho concluyó que el trato espontáneo de Johnson con las multitudes causó un impacto fuerte y favorable, señalando que circular por la ciudad sin hostilidad habría sido improbable meses antes.

records.headline: Appearing before the Senate Commerce Committee on his nomination
records.summary_en: Appearing before the Senate Commerce Committee on his nomination as Undersecretary of Commerce, Franklin D. Roosevelt, Jr., defended having served as a registered foreign agent and legal counsel for the regime of the late Dominican dictator Rafael Trujillo in the mid-1950s. Roosevelt insisted that he did nothing inimical to the interests of his country during that year of service, though he conceded he would rather not have accepted the retainer at that time. Committee Chairman Magnuson recessed the hearing at noon until the following morning, leaving four Democrats and all Republican committee members waiting to question the nominee.
records.summary_es: Al comparecer ante el Comité de Comercio del Senado sobre su nominación como subsecretario de Comercio, Franklin D. Roosevelt, Jr., defendió haber servido como agente extranjero registrado y asesor legal para el régimen del difunto dictador dominicano Rafael Trujillo a mediados de la década de 1950. Roosevelt insistió en que no hizo nada perjudicial para los intereses de su país durante ese año de servicio, aunque admitió que hubiera preferido no aceptar dicho contrato en aquel momento. El presidente del comité, Magnuson, suspendió la audiencia al mediodía hasta la mañana siguiente, dejando a cuatro demócratas y a todos los miembros republicanos en espera de interrogar al nominado.

The newspaper observes that President Kennedy owed a debt to Roosevelt and doubts the Senate will overturn the appointment, despite criticizing Roosevelt's earlier West Virginia primary attacks on Senator Hubert Humphrey. The editorial concludes that while Republicans raise partisan objections, paying political debts is simply an established reality of American politics.
records.summary_es: En un editorial sobre el patrocinio político, el Evening Star señala que las alarmas partidistas sobre el historial de infracciones de tránsito de Franklin D. Roosevelt Jr., su limitada experiencia empresarial y sus servicios pasados como asesor legal de la República Dominicana de Trujillo no perturban a los editores. El periódico observa que el presidente Kennedy tenía una deuda con Roosevelt y duda que el Senado desestime el nombramiento, a pesar de criticar los ataques previos de Roosevelt contra el senador Hubert Humphrey durante las primarias de Virginia Occidental. El editorial concluye que, aunque los republicanos plantean objeciones partidistas, el pago de deudas políticas es simplemente una realidad establecida de la política estadounidense.

records.headline: In a foreign policy commentary, the writer contends that Washington indirectly
records.summary_en: In a foreign policy commentary, the writer contends that Washington indirectly assisted the overthrow of the Trujillo regime in the Dominican Republic, only to foster a left-of-center government headed by President Juan Bosch. The column cites this outcome alongside developments in Brazil, Indonesia, and Laos as evidence of repeated diplomatic failure following openings to the political left. The author further asserts that Cuba should have demonstrated the hazards of such policies to American officials.
records.summary_es: En un comentario sobre política exterior, el autor sostiene que Washington colaboró indirectamente en el derrocamiento del régimen de Trujillo en la República Dominicana, solo para propiciar un gobierno de centroizquierda encabezado por el presidente Juan Bosch. La columna cita este resultado junto con los acontecimientos en Brasil, Indonesia y Laos como prueba del reiterado fracaso diplomático tras las aperturas hacia la izquierda política. El autor afirma además que Cuba debería haber demostrado a los funcionarios estadounidenses los peligros de tales políticas.

records.headline: The new President of the Dominican Republic, Juan Bosch, has generated
records.summary_en: The new President of the Dominican Republic, Juan Bosch, has generated concern within the military by permitting a political indoctrination school attended by numerous known communists to open in Santo Domingo. Bosch sought to calm army anxieties by making his first public statement against communism on March 13. The recent military coup in Guatemala is reported to have increased the likelihood of similar armed action against Bosch if commanders conclude his administration is moving too far to the left.

Bosch intentó disipar los temores del ejército emitiendo su primera declaración pública contra el comunismo el 13 de marzo. Se señala que el reciente golpe militar en Guatemala ha incrementado las probabilidades de una acción armada similar contra Bosch si los comandantes consideran que su administración se inclina demasiado hacia la izquierda.

records.headline: Society columnist Mr. Cassini, author of the syndicated 'Cholly
records.summary_en: Society columnist Mr. Cassini, author of the syndicated 'Cholly Knickerbocker' column published in more than 50 newspapers, was indicted in Washington on charges of acting as an unregistered foreign agent. The indictment alleges that he failed to register as a publicity agent from 1050 to 1901 for the late Dominican dictator Rafael Trujillo. Mr. Cassini pleaded not guilty and was released on 11,000 bail while taking leave from his column, amid reports from friends that his wife was deeply depressed over the charges.
records.summary_es: El columnista de sociedad señor Cassini, autor de la columna sindicada 'Cholly Knickerbocker' publicada en más de 50 periódicos, fue acusado formalmente en Washington por cargos de actuar como agente extranjero no registrado. La acusación formal sostiene que no se registró como agente publicitario de 1050 a 1901 para el difunto dictador dominicano Rafael Trujillo. El señor Cassini se declaró no culpable y quedó en libertad bajo fianza de 11,000 mientras se apartaba temporalmente de su columna, en medio de informes de allegados según los cuales su esposa estaba profundamente deprimida por las imputaciones.
