records.summary_en: Following their wedding ceremony and reception at the Towers, Mr. and Mrs. Moore flew to San Juan, Puerto Rico, for a week before traveling on to Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. While in Santo Domingo, the newlyweds are scheduled to stay as guests of United States Ambassador John Bartlow Martin. La pareja concluirá su viaje a través de la ciudad de Nueva York para una visita de fin de semana con el señor y la señora Louis Nizer antes de fijar su residencia en Chicago.

records.headline: Senate Democratic leader Senator Mansfield proposed transforming
records.summary_en: Senate Democratic leader Senator Mansfield proposed transforming an international body into a policy-making organization to consider establishing a hemisphere quarantine against Cuba. Mansfield cited as precedent for this action the 1960 economic sanctions imposed against the Dominican Republic when dictator Rafael Trujillo held power. The proposal is intended to tighten economic pressure on Cuba without resorting to armed forces, following President Kennedy's decision ruling out military action under present circumstances.
records.summary_es: El líder demócrata en el Senado, el senador Mansfield, propuso transformar un organismo internacional en una entidad formuladora de políticas para evaluar el establecimiento de una cuarentena hemisférica contra Cuba. Mansfield citó como precedente de esta medida las sanciones económicas impuestas en 1960 contra la República Dominicana cuando el dictador Rafael Trujillo detentaba el poder. La propuesta tiene como fin intensificar la presión económica sobre Cuba sin recurrir a fuerzas armadas, tras la decisión del presidente Kennedy de descartar una acción militar en las circunstancias actuales.

records.summary_en: A news analysis surveying the armed forces across Latin America highlights their diverse roles in regional political developments. In the Dominican Republic across the Caribbean, the military supported the transition toward democracy following the tyrannical Trujillo dictatorship. Conversely, on the western end of the island in Haiti, the armed forces are viewed as the most probable force to overthrow the dictatorship of François Duvalier.

En la República Dominicana, al otro lado del Caribe, los militares respaldaron la transición hacia la democracia tras la tiránica dictadura de Trujillo. Por el contrario, en el extremo occidental de la isla, en Haití, las fuerzas armadas son consideradas la fuerza más probable para derrocar la dictadura de François Duvalier.

records.headline: During a tense confrontation between Haiti and the Dominican
records.summary_en: During a tense confrontation between Haiti and the Dominican Republic, the Dominican Embassy along with Brazilian, Venezuelan, and Ecuadoran missions gave shelter to Haitian political refugees fleeing President Duvalier's crackdowns. A comparative assessment contrasts Haiti's armed strength—including Duvalier's 10,000-man Tonton Macoute militia, a distrusted 5,000-man army, 15 Mustang fighters, and six patrol boats—with the Dominican military, which boasts 12,000 well-equipped soldiers, two 20-plane air squadrons, and a 2,000-man navy with two destroyers, two frigates, five corvettes, six patrol vessels, and three landing craft. Meanwhile, in Santo Domingo, police utilized tear gas to disperse several hundred students who had attacked the Haitian Embassy and broken windows with stones.
records.summary_es: Durante un tenso enfrentamiento entre Haití y la República Dominicana, la embajada dominicana junto con las legaciones de Brasil, Venezuela y Ecuador dieron asilo a refugiados políticos haitianos que huían de las redadas del presidente Duvalier. records.headline: A report describes violent clashes between rival student factions
records.summary_en: A report describes violent clashes between rival student factions in the Dominican Republic, on Christian Democratic movements across Latin America. The autonomous university in the capital of Santo Domingo was forced to close for six weeks following gunfire over student representation on the governing council. Pedro Iturbides, a twenty-year-old law student and secretary general of the Social Christian student organization in the capital, stated that two separate student bodies now exist because communists refused to accept their defeat in university elections.

records.headline: The Dominican Republic suspended its threat to dispatch troops
records.summary_en: The Dominican Republic suspended its threat to dispatch troops and warships to Haiti on condition that no further actions aggravate existing tensions between the two neighboring states. Although the Dominican Republic broke diplomatic relations with Haiti over the weekend, President Juan Bosch announced that embassy personnel would not depart until Haitian authorities grant safe-conduct passes to Duvalier opponents sheltered inside the embassy. Foreign Minister Freites confirmed asking Colombia to represent Dominican affairs in Haiti, while Jean Louis Charles, Haiti's consul general in Santo Domingo, resigned to seek political asylum and issued a statement condemning the Duvalier regime.

El canciller Freites confirmó haber solicitado a Colombia que represente los asuntos dominicanos en Haití, mientras que Jean Louis Charles, cónsul general de Haití en Santo Domingo, renunció para solicitar asilo político y emitió una declaración condenando al régimen de Duvalier.

records.headline: Tensions deepened between the two nations on the island of Hispaniola
records.summary_en: Tensions deepened between the two nations on the island of Hispaniola, after President François Duvalier offered safe conduct out of Haiti for only 15 of 22 political refugees sheltered in the Dominican Republic's Embassy. The Dominican government was expected to insist that all 22 refugees be permitted to leave before ending the diplomatic confrontation. A five-nation mission from the Organization of American States prepared to fly to Santo Domingo to confer on the refugee dispute with President Juan Bosch and continue its investigation into the conflict.
records.summary_es: Las tensiones se agravaron entre las dos naciones de la isla de La Española, después de que el presidente François Duvalier ofreciera salvoconducto fuera de Haití para solo 15 de los 22 refugiados políticos asilados en la embajada de la República Dominicana. Se esperaba que el gobierno dominicano insistiera en que se permitiera la salida de los 22 refugiados antes de dar por terminada la confrontación diplomática. Una comisión de cinco naciones de la Organización de los Estados Americanos se dispuso a volar a Santo Domingo para tratar la disputa de los refugiados con el presidente Juan Bosch y continuar su investigación sobre el conflicto.

records.headline: Reflecting on the 1937 border killings for which Pope Pius XI arbitrated
records.summary_en: Reflecting on the 1937 border killings for which Pope Pius XI arbitrated an indemnization of $750,000 from the Trujillo government to Haiti, Dominican Ambassador to the United Nations Doña Carmen Natalia Martínez stated that Dominicans strongly condemn the Trujillos for the massacre. Martínez noted that as a member of the clandestine anti-Trujillo Democratic University Council, she joined many colleagues in signing a letter to the Haitian people deploring the murders. She acknowledged, however, that the bitter memory of the tragedy will continually affect Haitian-Dominican relations.

Martínez señaló que, como integrante del clandestino Consejo Universitario Democrático antitrujillista, se unió a numerosos compañeros para firmar una carta dirigida al pueblo haitiano deplorando los asesinatos. Reconoció, sin embargo, que el amargo recuerdo de la tragedia afectará continuamente las relaciones domínico-haitianas.

records.headline: As thousands of Haitians entered the Dominican Republic illegally
records.summary_en: As thousands of Haitians entered the Dominican Republic illegally, they came to be viewed as an unmanageable deadweight on the Trujillo regime. Informed Dominicans believed the army command acted on its own after hearing their president, during a drunken revelry, express a desire that Haitians be cleaned out. Trujillo's government desperately sought to deny responsibility, first claiming a few deaths in a border skirmish and subsequently blaming Dominican landowners near the border for killing Haitian thieves and squatters until the truth became known to Haitian President Stenio Vincent.

records.headline: Duvalier declared martial law soon after the inter- American peace
records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* reported that Haitian President François Duvalier declared martial law following the departure of an OAS peace commission led by Alberto Zuleta Ángel. While the mission obtained assurances of safe conduct for political refugees sheltering in foreign legations, Duvalier continued to accuse Dominican President Juan Bosch of aiding Haitian dissidents.
records.summary_es: El *Evening Star* informó que el presidente haitiano François Duvalier declaró la ley marcial tras la partida de una comisión de paz de la OEA encabezada por Alberto Zuleta Ángel. Si bien la misión obtuvo garantías de salvoconducto para los refugiados políticos asilados en legaciones extranjeras, Duvalier continuó acusando al presidente dominicano Juan Bosch de amparar a disidentes haitianos.

The peace mission from the Organization of American States won assurances from the Duvalier government that Haiti would protect foreign embassies and the rights of Haitians who had taken asylum in them. Five who took refuge in the Spanish Embassy were supposed to be flown out of Haiti yesterday but arrived at the airport too late to catch their scheduled flight. Five to Depart Plans now call for the five in asylum at the Spanish Embassy and 15 of the 35 in the Brazilian embassy to leave today. There was no word on when the 15 of 22 in asylum at the Dominican Embassy will receive safe conduct passes. Seven there are to be transferred to the Colombian Embassy. records.headline: Mr. Cassini, author of the Cholly Knickerbocker column for Hearst
records.summary_en: Mr. Cassini, author of the Cholly Knickerbocker column for Hearst newspapers, faced federal charges for failing to register as an agent for the former Trujillo regime of the Dominican Republic following his indictment on February 8. Defense attorney Mr. Nizer moved to dismiss the indictment, alleging that the Justice Department leaked secret grand jury testimony to Peter Maas for a January 18 article in The Saturday Evening Post titled 'Boswell of the Jet Set.' Judge William B. Jones deferred ruling on the dismissal to allow Nizer a week to ten days to produce further evidence, while postponing the trial from May to October following the death of Cassini's wife. Justice Department attorney Kevin Maroney submitted an affidavit from Maas denying that he obtained grand jury materials from the government.

El abogado defensor señor Nizer solicitó desestimar la acusación, alegando que el Departamento de Justicia filtró testimonios secretos del gran jurado a Peter Maas para un artículo del 18 de enero en The Saturday Evening Post titulado 'Boswell of the Jet Set'. El juez William B. El abogado del Departamento de Justicia Kevin Maroney presentó una declaración jurada de Maas negando haber recibido materiales del gran jurado por parte del gobierno.

records.headline: Reviewing Haitian history as a sequence of civil conflict, strife
records.summary_en: Reviewing Haitian history as a sequence of civil conflict, strife with the Dominican Republic, and United States intervention, the report examines mounting unrest in Port-au-Prince ahead of the May 15 expiration of President Francois Duvalier's constitutional term. Following military purges by Duvalier, several disaffected officers and other Haitian citizens sought political asylum in the Dominican Republic's Embassy. Dominican President Juan Bosch reported from Santo Domingo that Haitian police had entered the embassy premises and stationed guards on the diplomatic grounds.
records.summary_es: Al repasar la historia haitiana como una secuencia de conflictos civiles, disputas con la República Dominicana e intervenciones de Estados Unidos, el informe examina la creciente agitación en Puerto Príncipe antes de que venza el 15 de mayo el mandato constitucional del presidente Francois Duvalier. Tras las purgas militares de Duvalier, varios oficiales descontentos y otros ciudadanos haitianos buscaron asilo político en la embajada de la República Dominicana. El presidente dominicano Juan Bosch informó desde Santo Domingo que la policía haitiana había ingresado a las instalaciones de la embajada y apostado guardias en los terrenos diplomáticos.

records.headline: Dominican authorities stated that President Francois Duvalier failed
records.summary_en: Dominican authorities stated that President Francois Duvalier failed to fulfill his commitment to an Inter-American Peace Commission to grant safe-conduct passes for 15 of 22 Haitians sheltered in the Dominican Embassy in Port-au-Prince, with the Colombian Embassy assuming protective custody over the mission and the refugees. The Duvalier regime accused the Dominican Republic of hosting rebel training bases and planes and massacring Haitians, though informed circles in Santo Domingo dismissed the massacre allegation while believing President Juan Bosch was assisting anti-Duvalier rebels. Following earlier border deployments and Bosch's threats of military action over embassy violations, additional Dominican forces were dispatched to the border and Dominican naval vessels, led by two destroyers, stood by off the Haitian coast.

El régimen de Duvalier acusó a la República Dominicana de albergar bases de entrenamiento y aviones rebeldes y de masacrar haitianos, aunque círculos bien informados en Santo Domingo desestimaron la acusación de masacre al tiempo que consideraban que el presidente Juan Bosch ayudaba a los rebeldes contrarios a Duvalier. Tras los despliegues fronterizos previos y las amenazas de acción militar de Bosch por las violaciones a la embajada, fuerzas dominicanas adicionales fueron enviadas a la frontera y buques de la armada dominicana, encabezados por dos destructores, permanecieron a la expectativa frente a la costa haitiana.

records.headline: Confronting poverty and injustice inherited from the 30-year
records.summary_en: Confronting poverty and injustice inherited from the 30-year dictatorship of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo alongside tensions with Francois Duvalier's regime in Haiti, Dominican President Juan Bosch showed signs of physical and political strain after two months in office. During an hour-and-a-half interview in Santo Domingo, Bosch observed that it remained too early to tell which direction their galloping horse was headed, remarking that building democracy is an arduous struggle in which the president becomes a victim by remaining accessible to everyone. Although visitors must pass five separate checkpoints in the presidential palace, Bosch continued to rise at 5 a m. and work nearly a 24-hour day to manage state affairs.
records.summary_es: Al enfrentarse a la pobreza y la injusticia heredadas de la dictadura de 30 años del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo, junto con las tensiones con el régimen de Francois Duvalier en Haití, el presidente dominicano Juan Bosch mostraba signos de agotamiento físico y político tras dos meses en el cargo. Durante una entrevista de hora y media en Santo Domingo, Bosch señaló que aún era demasiado pronto para saber hacia qué dirección galopaba el caballo en que montaban, comentando que construir la democracia es una lucha ardua en la que el presidente se convierte en víctima al tener que estar disponible para todos. Aunque los visitantes deben superar cinco puestos de control independientes en el palacio presidencial, Bosch continuaba levantándose a las 5 a m. y trabajando casi una jornada de 24 horas para atender los asuntos del Estado.

records.headline: Dominican troops advanced to the border town of Jimani amid
records.summary_en: Dominican troops advanced to the border town of Jimani amid unconfirmed reports that President Juan Bosch might order an invasion unless Haitian President Francois Duvalier granted safe conduct to 15 political opponents sheltered in the Dominican Embassy in Port-au-Prince. In Santo Domingo, Bosch conferred privately with Alberto Zuleta Angel, chairman of an Organization of American States peace mission, while Dominican charge d'affaires Frank Bobadilla returned from Port-au-Prince carrying a message from the refugees. With sources suggesting Bosch was prepared to use any pretext to provoke an armed clash, OAS Council President Gonzalo Facio convened an executive session in Washington to review the mission's findings on the highly tense border crisis.

records.headline: President Juan Bosch met in Santo Domingo with his army, navy
records.summary_en: President Juan Bosch met in Santo Domingo with his army, navy, and air force commanders for nearly an hour to assess military readiness before conferring with his cabinet on plans regarding Haiti. Countering diplomatically, Haitian Ambassador Carlet R. Auguste delivered an urgent request to the United Nations Secretariat in New York calling for an immediate Security Council session within 24 hours to address the Dominican threat. Observers speculated that the appeal to the United Nations might prompt Bosch to accelerate his invasion timetable, while OAS Council Chairman Gonzalo Facio highlighted the severity of the crisis. Facio said after a one-hour OAS meeting that war between Haiti and the Dominican Republic was distinctly possible, and that the council would remain in permanent session. Following his meeting with the military, Bosch ordered new tank and infantry units to the frontier and an anti-guerrilla battalion from Constanza to take up positions at Mao, a small village near the north coast a few miles from the Haitian town of Cap Haitien, and Dominican paratroop units were ordered to reinforce infantry troops in the Barahona area facing the road route to Port-au-Prince. Bosch also stated that the Dominican Republic had received a pledge from Costa Rica of full support for any Dominican effort to topple the present Haitian government, and trained Dominican infantry were estimated to outnumber the Haitians by more than 3-to-1. Bosch told UPI, “We are moving additional forces to have complete control of the frontier.” A spokesman said the Dominican armed forces were in attack position the length of the border, a U.S. Navy task force at sea within 30 miles of Port-au-Prince stood ready to move at ten minutes' notice to evacuate some 1,000 American residents in the Haitian capital if fighting broke out, and the British sent a Royal Navy frigate to international waters just off Haiti to evacuate British nationals if that became necessary.
records.summary_es: El presidente Juan Bosch se reunió en Santo Domingo con sus comandantes del ejército, la marina y la fuerza aérea durante casi una hora para evaluar la preparación militar antes de deliberar con su gabinete sobre los planes relativos a Haití. Como contraofensiva diplomática, el embajador haitiano Carlet R. Auguste entregó una solicitud urgente a la Secretaría de las Naciones Unidas en Nueva York pidiendo una sesión inmediata del Consejo de Seguridad en un plazo máximo de 24 horas para tratar la amenaza dominicana. Los observadores especulaban que la apelación ante las Naciones Unidas podría inducir a Bosch a acelerar su cronograma de invasión, mientras el presidente del Consejo de la OEA Gonzalo Facio subrayaba la gravedad de la crisis. Facio dijo, tras una reunión de una hora de la OEA, que una guerra entre Haití y la República Dominicana era claramente posible, y que el consejo permanecería en sesión permanente. Tras su reunión con los militares, Bosch ordenó el envío de nuevas unidades de tanques e infantería a la frontera y de un batallón antiguerrillero de Constanza para tomar posiciones en Mao, una pequeña aldea cercana a la costa norte a pocas millas de la población haitiana de Cabo Haitiano, y unidades dominicanas de paracaidistas recibieron orden de reforzar a las tropas de infantería en la zona de Barahona, frente a la ruta terrestre hacia Puerto Príncipe. Bosch también declaró que la República Dominicana había recibido de Costa Rica la promesa de pleno apoyo a cualquier esfuerzo dominicano por derrocar al actual gobierno haitiano, y se estimaba que la infantería dominicana entrenada superaba en número a los haitianos en más de 3 a 1. Bosch dijo a la UPI: «Estamos moviendo fuerzas adicionales para tener el control completo de la frontera». Un portavoz dijo que las fuerzas armadas dominicanas estaban en posición de ataque a lo largo de toda la frontera, una fuerza naval estadounidense en el mar, a menos de 30 millas de Puerto Príncipe, estaba lista para moverse con diez minutos de aviso para evacuar a unos 1,000 residentes estadounidenses en la capital haitiana si estallaba la lucha, y los británicos enviaron una fragata de la Royal Navy a aguas internacionales frente a Haití para evacuar a los ciudadanos británicos si ello se hacía necesario.

records.headline: Too new to be judged without reservation, though his administration
records.summary_en: Too new to be judged without reservation, though his administration remains, an editorial notes that Dominicans have pinned their hopes on President Bosch to lift the country out of the morass left by a generation of misrule under the late Rafael L. Trujillo. The commentary argues that a Dominican Republic pursuing enlightened administration, industrial expansion, and extensive socioeconomic reforms cannot border Haiti without mounting friction, as opponents of the neighboring dictatorship will continue seeking asylum in Santo Domingo. It urges member nations of the Organization of American States to act boldly within their powers, asserting that a regime maintained through fear and oppression cannot coexist peacefully in the modern Caribbean.
records.summary_es: Demasiado reciente para juzgarla sin reservas, aunque su administración sigue siendo, un editorial señala que los dominicanos han depositado sus esperanzas en el presidente Bosch para sacar al país del marasmo dejado por una generación de desgobierno bajo el difunto Rafael L. Trujillo. El comentario sostiene que una República Dominicana que persigue una administración ilustrada, expansión industrial y profundas reformas socioeconómicas no puede limitar con Haití sin crecientes fricciones, ya que los opositores a la dictadura vecina continuarán buscando asilo en Santo Domingo. Exhorta a los países miembros de la Organización de los Estados Americanos a actuar con firmeza dentro de sus facultades, afirmando que un régimen sostenido mediante el miedo y la opresión no puede coexistir pacíficamente en el Caribe contemporáneo.

records.headline: Haitian Foreign Minister Rene Chalmers announced that opponents of President Francois
records.summary_en: Haitian Foreign Minister Rene Chalmers announced that opponents of President Francois Duvalier, who took asylum in foreign embassies, would be permitted to leave Haiti gradually following routine background checks. In Santo Domingo, Dominican President Juan Bosch charged that Haitian troops had set up machine-gun emplacements outside the Dominican Embassy in Port-au-Prince, leaving 22 sheltered Haitians in a desperate plight. Bosch nonetheless refrained from ordering troops and tanks on the border to invade, advising the Organization of American States that he would withhold an attack unless current aggressions continued.

En Santo Domingo, el presidente dominicano Juan Bosch denunció que tropas haitianas habían instalado posiciones de ametralladoras frente a la embajada dominicana en Puerto Príncipe, dejando a 22 haitianos refugiados en una situación desesperada. No obstante, Bosch se abstuvo de ordenar la invasión a las tropas y tanques desplegados en la frontera, informando a la Organización de los Estados Americanos que suspendería cualquier ataque a menos que continuaran las agresiones presentes.

records.headline: A dispatch from Santo Domingo reports that internal debate over going
records.summary_en: A dispatch from Santo Domingo reports that internal debate over going to war with neighboring Haiti, between hawks and doves, has temporarily resulted in victory for the doves. President Juan Bosch, who previously voiced aggressive rhetoric, shifted toward the side of the doves and accepted Organization of American States mediation to find a peaceful solution with Haitian dictator Francois Duvalier. Dominican troops and armor nonetheless remained positioned at key border locations within a 30-mile striking distance of Port-au-Prince.
records.summary_es: Un despacho desde Santo Domingo informa que el debate interno sobre ir a la guerra con el vecino Haití, entre halcones y palomas, ha resultado temporalmente en una victoria para las palomas. El presidente Juan Bosch, quien previamente había adoptado una retórica agresiva, se inclinó hacia el bando de las palomas y aceptó la mediación de la Organización de los Estados Americanos para encontrar una solución pacífica con el dictador haitiano Francois Duvalier. No obstante, las tropas y los blindados dominicanos permanecieron apostados en puntos estratégicos de la frontera a una distancia de ataque de 30 millas de Puerto Príncipe.

records.summary_en: Reports from Santo Domingo indicated that border tension had eased and that Dominican President Juan Bosch stated his nation would resort to force only if aggression against the Dominican embassy in Haiti continued. Meanwhile, President Francois Duvalier cabled the Organization of American States offering to permit 42 of an estimated 100 political refugees in Latin American embassies in Port-au-Prince to leave the country. However, Duvalier refused to grant safe-conduct passes to seven Haitian army men, prompting initial impressions that the gesture did not go far enough to resolve the dispute.

Mientras tanto, el presidente Francois Duvalier envió un cable a la Organización de los Estados Americanos ofreciendo permitir que 42 de unos 100 refugiados políticos en embajadas latinoamericanas en Puerto Príncipe salieran del país. Sin embargo, Duvalier se negó a otorgar salvoconductos a siete hombres del ejército haitiano, provocando la impresión inicial de que el gesto no era suficiente para resolver el conflicto.

records.full_text:
OAS Again Scrutinizes Haiti-Dominican Crisis

SANTO DOMINGO, Dominican Republic, May 14 (AP).—A peace mission of the Organization of American States arrived last night for another look at the Haitian-Dominican crisis, eased further by the Dominican Republic's announcement that it is withdrawing its troops from the Haitian border.

Part of the OAS fact-finding team was to fly on today to Port au Prince, where opponents of President Francois Duvalier have vowed to assassinate him by tomorrow.

The Dominican government's announcement gave no reason for the troop pullback.

The main consideration apparently was Haiti's gradual release of Duvalier opponents who had taken refuge in Latin American embassies in Port au Prince. Dominican President Juan Bosch rushed troops to the border two weeks ago after Haitian militiamen invaded the Dominican Embassy in search of refugees there.

Army Leaders Reluctant

The Dominican army hierarchy also was known to be reluctant to launch an attack against Haiti. There also has been some criticism here of Mr. Bosch because he did not consult the Dominican Congress before putting the army on a war footing.

Associated Press Correspondent William L. Ryan reported from Port au Prince that the consensus there was that Dr. Duvalier would survive to start a second presidential term despite opposition vows to destroy him by tomorrow.

Dr. Duvalier's first six-year term expires tomorrow. Although the Haitian constitution bars a President's re-election, he is to be inaugurated May 22 for a second six-year term to which he declared himself elected after a rigged election two years ago.

Mr. Ryan said fear of an uprising was evidenced by a steady exodus of Haitians from Port au Prince into the countryside. The movement reversed a normal trend of poverty-stricken country people seeking a better living in the city.

Opposition Leader Clement Barbot, once Dr. Duvalier's trusted deputy president, apparently was still heading an underground band somewhere in the country. Interior Minister Luc Francois said reports that Mr. Barbot had gone into asylum in the Argentine Embassy were not true.

Mr. Barbot, a master of terrorist tactics, has sworn to assassinate Dr. Duvalier by tomorrow. Circulars were distributed to Port au Prince several weeks ago threatening that a revolution would start tomorrow.

Most Latin-American members of the OAS hold the view that, repugnant as the Duvalier dictatorship is to them, they cannot interfere in Haiti's internal affairs.

American warships remained on emergency stations off Port au Prince to evacuate Americans from Haiti should it become necessary. The State Department last week moved out several hundred dependents of United States officials and military officers, but there has been no exodus of the estimated 1,600 other Americans living in Haiti.

records.headline: With United States naval forces deployed near Haiti during the 18-day
records.summary_en: With United States naval forces deployed near Haiti during the 18-day crisis encompassing Hispaniola, speculation mounted that Francois Duvalier might flee to Curacao as his constitutional six-year term expired on Wednesday. In Santo Domingo, Haitian exile leader Louis Dejoie, who had contested the presidency against Duvalier in 1957, organized plans for hemispheric recognition of a newly formed government in exile. Dejoie predicted that Duvalier would fall very soon, joining with former interim president Daniel Fignole in leading exile hopes for political change.

En Santo Domingo, el líder del exilio haitiano Louis Dejoie, quien había disputado la presidencia contra Duvalier en 1957, preparó planes para lograr el reconocimiento hemisférico de un recién constituido gobierno en el exilio. Dejoie pronosticó que Duvalier caería muy pronto, uniéndose al expresidente interino Daniel Fignole al frente de las esperanzas del exilio para un cambio político.

records.summary_en: A 14-member Organization of American States commission led by Colombian diplomat Alberto Zuleta Angel arrived in Port-au-Prince from Santo Domingo to continue investigating the dispute between Haiti and the Dominican Republic, while an Ecuadorian member remained behind in the Dominican Republic. records.headline: A statement issued by the Dominican embassy announced that the country's
records.summary_en: A statement issued by the Dominican embassy announced that the country's improved fiscal situation has allowed it to begin paying off old debts. The embassy stated that the Dominican Republic has informed the International Monetary Fund that the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic is prepared to pay an item of $9 million ahead of schedule. Repayments were originally scheduled to begin in January 1968, but the economy was still recovering from the Trujillo regime, leading President-elect Juan Bosch to visit Washington in early January to obtain an approved postponement. Following Bosch taking office on Feb. 27, the economic situation improved considerably due to sound economic policies and an austerity program.

Originalmente estaba previsto que los reembolsos comenzaran en enero de 1968, pero la economía aún se estaba recuperando del régimen de Trujillo, lo que llevó al presidente electo Juan Bosch a visitar Washington a principios de enero para obtener un aplazamiento aprobado. Luego de que Bosch asumiera el cargo el 27 de febrero, la situación económica mejoró considerablemente gracias a políticas económicas sólidas y a un programa de austeridad.

records.headline: A dispatch reports that Lt. Francois Benoit, accused of leading
records.summary_en: A dispatch reports that Lt. Francois Benoit, accused of leading an abortive April 26 plot to kidnap the children of Dr. Duvalier, is among 10 political refugees sheltering in the Dominican Embassy. The embassy has remained under Colombian protection since Duvalier broke diplomatic relations with the Dominican Republic during a crisis that nearly brought the two nations into armed conflict. Meanwhile, the Santo Domingo newspaper El Caribe reported that Haitian militiamen set fire to hundreds of huts along the border to create a no-escape zone and prevent Duvalier's opponents from fleeing into the Dominican Republic.

La embajada ha permanecido bajo protección colombiana desde que Duvalier rompió relaciones diplomáticas con la República Dominicana durante una crisis que casi condujo a ambas naciones a un conflicto armado. records.headline: An editorial commentary reflects on the psychological devastation
records.summary_en: An editorial commentary reflects on the psychological devastation left by the Trujillo dictatorship, arguing that its worst crime was eroding self-respect, dignity, and trust among Dominicans through spies and informers. It describes President Juan Bosch's primary mission as teaching the Dominican people that democracy could serve them just as Trujillo had mastered them, thereby restoring a sense of nationhood. Chosen as president by an invulnerable majority after 26 years in exile, Bosch estimates that completing the work of reform and redemption will require 25 years. The column observes that Bosch has begun this undertaking by working 16 hours a day starting at five in the morning.
records.summary_es: Un comentario editorial reflexiona sobre la devastación psicológica dejada por la dictadura de Trujillo, argumentando que su peor crimen fue socavar la autoestima, la dignidad y la confianza entre los dominicanos mediante espías e informantes. Describe la misión principal del presidente Juan Bosch como la de enseñar al pueblo dominicano que la democracia podía estar a su servicio, tal como Trujillo había sido su amo, restaurando así un sentido de nación. Elegido presidente por una mayoría invulnerable tras 26 años de exilio, Bosch estima que completar la labor de reforma y redención requerirá 25 años. La columna señala que Bosch ha iniciado esta labor trabajando 16 horas al día a partir de las cinco de la mañana.

records.summary_en: The *Evening Star* published an editorial urging the United States to adopt stronger measures against Haitian dictator François Duvalier, suggesting economic boycotts and clandestine support for anti-Duvalier insurgents. The commentary argued that Washington's official reluctance to intervene disregarded past precedents like Guatemala and the Bay of Pigs, warning that inaction could allow Communist influence to expand next to Cuba.

El artículo sostenía que la renuencia oficial de Washington a intervenir ignoraba precedentes pasados como Guatemala y Bahía de Cochinos, advirtiendo que la inacción podría permitir la expansión de la influencia comunista junto a Cuba.

Obviously we take the position nowadays that armed intervention cannot be undertaken in this hemisphere, barring a spectacular threat to our security like the presence somewhere of Soviet rockets. There are ways, however, of accomplishing these things. For one thing, as we pointed out the other day, there is economic pressure. Our purchases from Haiti are not extensive. But, for instance, could we not get along without Haitian coffee while Duvalier remains in power? Duvalier could be toppled, as he should be, by the Haitians themselves— relatively few of them. The men to topple him are there and, sooner or later, one of them will organize the job. They need guns, grenades and explosives. If the United States remains a spectator, growling only when its na tionals seem to be menaced, the next leader of Haiti will owe us even less than the present one. records.headline: Reporting from Santo Domingo at the conclusion of Juan Bosch's
records.summary_en: Reporting from Santo Domingo at the conclusion of Juan Bosch's first three months in office, Max Freedman draws sharp contrasts between the Dominican president and Fidel Castro's regime in Cuba. While Castro seized power by force and established a dictatorship, Bosch was elected president of the Dominican Republic by a huge majority after the dictator was overthrown. Unlike Castro, who executed critics or jailed them without trial, Bosch has prevented mob rule and police brutality. Furthermore, while Castro confiscated bank deposits, repudiated debts, and seized land, Bosch avoids confiscation, repays national debts, seeks a convertible currency, and has launched an authentic agrarian reform granting ownership titles directly to farmers.
records.summary_es: Reportando desde Santo Domingo al término de los primeros tres meses de Juan Bosch en el cargo, Max Freedman establece marcados contrastes entre el presidente dominicano y el régimen de Fidel Castro en Cuba. Mientras Castro tomó el poder por la fuerza y estableció una dictadura, Bosch fue elegido presidente de la República Dominicana por una inmensa mayoría tras el derrocamiento del dictador. A diferencia de Castro, quien fusiló a sus críticos o los encarceló sin juicio, Bosch ha evitado el desgobierno de las turbas y la brutalidad policial. Además, mientras que Castro confiscó depósitos bancarios, desconoció deudas y se apoderó de tierras, Bosch evita las confiscaciones, paga las deudas nacionales, procura una moneda convertible y ha iniciado una auténtica reforma agraria que otorga títulos de propiedad directamente a los agricultores.

records.headline: For private aviators traveling toward Dorado Beach, an air cruise
records.summary_en: For private aviators traveling toward Dorado Beach, an air cruise itinerary includes a scheduled refueling stop in the Dominican Republic. Following an overnight stop in the Bahamas, the participants are scheduled to fly the final leg of their route on Friday, landing at Puerto Plata. A Dominican government delegation will officially greet the group upon arrival in Puerto Plata before the flight continues to Puerto Rico. Prominent aviation figures participating in the cruise include Max Karant of the Aviation Owners and Pilots Association, William Piper of Piper Aircraft, and trick shot golfer Paul Hahn.

records.headline: A federal grand jury investigating multi-million-dollar commercial espionage
records.summary_en: A federal grand jury investigating multi-million-dollar commercial espionage at the Mayflower Hotel identified individuals with past ties to the Dominican Republic. Probing the electronic bugging of a suite occupied by San Francisco attorney Malcolm T. Dungan during Federal Power Commission hearings in March 1962, the inquiry uncovered two police officers, two private investigators, and a soldier of fortune previously implicated with the Trujillo dictatorship. The investigation began after Dungan discovered a 4-inch transmitter taped beneath a coffee table during a secret business conversation. Dungan subsequently secured an injunction from Federal Judge George H. Hart before marshals and detectives raided the adjoining room.
records.summary_es: Un gran jurado federal que investiga un caso multimillonario de espionaje comercial en el Hotel Mayflower identificó a individuos con vínculos pasados con la República Dominicana. Al indagar sobre la colocación de micrófonos en la suite ocupada por el abogado de San Francisco Malcolm T. Dungan durante audiencias de la Comisión Federal de Energía en marzo de 1962, las pesquisas descubrieron a dos policías, dos investigadores privados y un soldado de fortuna implicado anteriormente con la dictadura de Trujillo. La investigación comenzó después de que Dungan descubriera un transmisor de 4 pulgadas adherido con cinta debajo de una mesa de centro durante una conversación comercial secreta. Posteriormente, Dungan obtuvo una orden judicial del juez federal George H. Hart antes de que los alguaciles y detectives allanaran la suite contigua.

records.headline: Congressional backing to update and strengthen enforcement of the Foreign Agents Registration Act followed
records.summary_en: Congressional backing to update and strengthen enforcement of the Foreign Agents Registration Act followed the disclosure of closed-session testimony from Washington attorneys representing Dominican Republic sugar interests during the Trujillo regime. One closed hearing examined Michael B. Deane, a Washington lawyer and public relations counsel who served as a District delegate to the 1960 Democratic National Committee. Deane admitted that he had no prior experience in sugar, describing himself instead as a knowledgeable figure around Washington. Senator Fulbright stated that Deane's testimony demonstrated the necessity of stricter regulations to curb non-diplomatic representatives acting on behalf of foreign principals.
records.summary_es: El respaldo del Congreso para actualizar y hacer más estricta la aplicación de la Ley de Registro de Agentes Extranjeros surgió tras divulgarse testimonios a puerta cerrada de abogados de Washington que representaban intereses azucareros de la República Dominicana durante el régimen de Trujillo. Una de las audiencias a puerta cerrada examinó a Michael B. Deane, un abogado y asesor de relaciones públicas de Washington que fue delegado del Distrito ante el Comité Nacional Demócrata de 1960. Deane admitió que no tenía experiencia previa en el sector azucarero y se describió a sí mismo como una persona bien informada en los círculos de Washington. El senador Fulbright declaró que el testimonio de Deane demostraba la necesidad de regulaciones más estrictas para frenar las actividades de representantes no diplomáticos que actúan en nombre de mandantes extranjeros.

records.headline: A news note reports that the Dominican Republic retained Dr. Eaves earlier
records.summary_en: A news note reports that the Dominican Republic retained Dr. Eaves earlier this year as a special consultant in education. In this capacity, Dr. Eaves directed the reorganization of Dominican elementary schools amid the chaotic aftermath that followed the deposition of the Trujillo government. The educator is currently executive secretary of the National Education Association Department of Elementary School Principals and will be on a leave of absence during his stay in Chapel Hill. The dispatch adds that he previously helped establish a public elementary school system in Hawaii.
records.summary_es: Una nota informativa señala que la República Dominicana contrató al doctor Eaves a principios de este año como asesor especial en educación. En esa función, el doctor Eaves dirigió la reorganización de las escuelas primarias dominicanas en medio del caos que siguió a la caída del gobierno de Trujillo. El educador es actualmente secretario ejecutivo del Departamento de Directores de Escuelas Primarias de la National Education Association y estará de licencia durante su estancia en Chapel Hill. El despacho agrega que anteriormente ayudó a establecer un sistema de escuelas primarias públicas en Hawái.

records.summary_en: An Associated Press dispatch from Santo Domingo reports statements from a spokesman for Haitian rebels who invaded the northern coast of Haiti. The spokesman stated that two columns of rebel troops had surrounded Cap Haitien, Haiti's second city. He denied morning rumors circulating in Santo Domingo that the port city of 25,000 had fallen, clarifying that rebel forces held the territory in front of the city and much of the surrounding area. The invading units, operating under the command of General Leon Cantave, were reported to consist of exiled Haitian soldiers.

records.headline: Dominican President Juan Bosch conferred with his armed forces
records.summary_en: Dominican President Juan Bosch conferred with his armed forces chiefs at the national palace following rebel military operations across the border in northern Haiti. The newspaper Listin Diario reported that several Haitian officials and soldiers crossed into the Dominican Republic seeking asylum. Haitian exile sources in Santo Domingo stated that at least 500 well-armed guerrilla fighters landed at Fort Liberte, 18 miles east of Cap Haitien, and quickly captured the towns of Fort Liberte, Derac, Trou, and Limonade. Meanwhile, American families were evacuated to Cap Haitien on orders of the Duvalier government from the United States-owned Dauphin sisal plantation, situated about 5 miles west of the Dominican border. Gen. Léon Cantave, chief of the Haitian armed forces for five months in 1957, led the invasion under the banner of the National Democratic Union, telling an interviewer he was not interested in becoming president, only in ousting Duvalier. Paul Verna, a former Haitian diplomat representing the Union, said an unidentified island off the coast was used as a staging area for the invasion and that some of the invaders were former Haitian army officers who had been living in Santo Domingo; the rebels expected to form a military-civilian provisional government in north Haiti. Duvalier, who had given himself an illegal second term extending until 1967 after a rigged election in 1961, had built up a civilian militia of about 5,000 and a force of 5,000 Tonton Macoute while cutting the regular army to about 3,300 men, and the United States — which had cut off economic aid the year before and suspended diplomatic relations when Duvalier remained in office past his constitutional term — had resumed relations on June 3.

Fuentes del exilio haitiano en Santo Domingo afirmaron que al menos 500 guerrilleros bien armados desembarcaron en Fort Liberte, a 18 millas al este de Cap Haitien, y tomaron rápidamente las localidades de Fort Liberte, Derac, Trou y Limonade. Mientras tanto, familias estadounidenses fueron evacuadas hacia Cap Haitien por orden del gobierno de Duvalier desde la plantación de sisal Dauphin, de propiedad estadounidense, situada a unas 5 millas al oeste de la frontera dominicana. El general Léon Cantave, jefe de las fuerzas armadas haitianas durante cinco meses en 1957, encabezó la invasión bajo la bandera de la Unión Democrática Nacional, declarando a un entrevistador que no le interesaba la presidencia, sino solo derrocar a Duvalier. Paul Verna, exdiplomático haitiano representante de la Unión, dijo que una isla no identificada frente a la costa sirvió de zona de concentración para la invasión y que algunos de los invasores eran exoficiales del ejército haitiano que habían estado viviendo en Santo Domingo; los rebeldes esperaban formar un gobierno provisional cívico-militar en el norte de Haití. Duvalier, que se había otorgado un segundo mandato ilegal hasta 1967 tras unas elecciones fraudulentas en 1961, había creado una milicia civil de unos 5,000 hombres y una fuerza de 5,000 tonton macoutes, reduciendo el ejército regular a unos 3,300 hombres, y Estados Unidos —que había cortado la ayuda económica el año anterior y suspendido las relaciones diplomáticas cuando Duvalier permaneció en el cargo tras expirar su mandato constitucional— había reanudado las relaciones el 3 de junio.

records.summary_en: A dispatch reports that medical supplies were sent to villages near the northeastern frontier with the Dominican Republic amid rebel fighting against President François Duvalier. The regime of Dr. Duvalier accused invading forces led by former Haitian army general Leon Cantave of launching their attack from the Dominican Republic, which shares the island of Hispaniola with Haiti. The government of Dominican President Juan Bosch firmly denied the charge. While foreign correspondents conducted an aerial tour of Cap Haitien under military escort, Haitian authorities denied them permission to visit the scene of the fighting on the ground.

records.headline: The paper reports Haiti's government marshaled its regular army and civilian armed forces to combat rebel bands
records.summary_en: The paper reports Haiti's government marshaled its regular army and civilian armed forces to combat rebel bands entrenched in mountains near the Dominican border, after Haitian exile invaders crossed from the Dominican border at Capotille into the Mont Organisé area. Reports also spoke of rumors of reprisals against disloyal civilians by the Tonton Macoutes, President Duvalier's security force, with official sources tight-lipped.

Los informes también hablaban de rumores de represalias contra civiles desleales por los Tonton Macoutes, la fuerza de seguridad del presidente Duvalier, con fuentes oficiales reservadas.

records.headline: Haitian Foreign Minister Chalmers met in closed session in Washington
records.summary_en: Haitian Foreign Minister Chalmers met in closed session in Washington with the four-nation Organization of American States committee investigating the dispute between Haiti and the Dominican Republic on Hispaniola. Chalmers presented documents, captured weapons, and uniforms bearing Dominican military insignia to argue that Dominican President Juan Bosch was behind rebel attacks against the Duvalier government. The Dominicans denied the accusations, explaining that surplus military equipment acquired during the regime of late dictator Rafael Trujillo had been auctioned to private bidders by the current government. The diplomatic meetings took place amid fresh reports of fighting inside Haiti.

Chalmers presentó documentos, armas capturadas y uniformes con insignias militares dominicanas para sostener que el presidente dominicano Juan Bosch respaldaba los ataques rebeldes contra el gobierno de Duvalier. Las autoridades dominicanas rechazaron las acusaciones, explicando que el material militar excedente adquirido durante el régimen del difunto dictador Rafael Trujillo había sido subastado a compradores privados por el actual gobierno. Las gestiones diplomáticas coincidieron con nuevos informes sobre combates dentro de Haití.

records.headline: A proposed TVA-type project in the Dominican Republic is estimated
records.summary_en: A proposed TVA-type project in the Dominican Republic is estimated to raise the annual income of some 25,000 families from $700 to about $1,700 and justify resettling another 25,000 families. The undertaking would improve living conditions for 250,000 Dominicans out of a total population of 3,500,000, addressing an economy where per capita income is $170 and the arid southeast is among the poorest regions. Agrarian reform represents a primary goal for President Bosch, the first freely elected president since the assassination of Dictator Trujillo, who has faced technical and financial constraints amid mounting political pressures. Financing is anticipated from agencies such as the Export-Import Bank, the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development, or the World Bank at a service charge of three-fourths of one per cent.
records.summary_es: Se estima que un proyecto propuesto de tipo TVA en la República Dominicana elevará el ingreso anual de unas 25,000 familias de $700 a cerca de $1,700 y justificará el reasentamiento de otras 25,000 familias. La obra mejoraría las condiciones de vida de 250,000 dominicanos de una población total de 3,500,000, en un contexto donde el ingreso per cápita es de $170 y el sudeste árido se cuenta entre las zonas más pobres. La reforma agraria constituye un objetivo clave del presidente Bosch, el primer mandatario electo libremente tras el asesinato del dictador Trujillo, quien ha enfrentado limitaciones técnicas y financieras ante crecientes presiones políticas. Se prevé que el financiamiento provenga de entidades como el Export-Import Bank, el Banco Internacional de Reconstrucción y Fomento o el Banco Mundial, con una tasa de interés o comisión de servicio de tres cuartos del uno por ciento.

records.headline: A feature recounts that six years ago in the Dominican Republic
records.summary_en: A feature recounts that six years ago in the Dominican Republic, nineteen-year-old Juan Marichal took a bus ride into Ciudad Trujillo before San Francisco Giants scouts sent him to Florida. Although his fastball was not exceptional and his breaking pitches appeared ordinary, his pinpoint control helped him develop into an outstanding pitcher over three and a half seasons in the National League. Marichal recently notched his twentieth victory of the season, becoming the first tan twenty-game winner since Don Newcombe in 1956. Earlier in June, the Giants righthander tossed a no-hitter against the Houston Colts, winning one to zero.

Aunque su bola rápida no era excepcional y sus lanzamientos quebrados parecían comunes, su control milimétrico le permitió consolidarse como un lanzador sobresaliente a lo largo de tres temporadas y media en la Liga Nacional. Marichal sumó recientemente su vigésima victoria de la temporada, convirtiéndose en el primer ganador de veinte juegos de tez morena desde Don Newcombe en 1956. A principios de junio, el lanzador derecho de los Gigantes tiró un juego sin hits contra los Colts de Houston, ganando por uno a cero.

records.summary_en: An official Dominican radio broadcast reported that the civilian population of Dajabon was being evacuated thirty miles north to the coastal town of Montecristi following border shelling, with Haitian forces massing at Ouanaminthe across the frontier. Foreign Minister Hector Garcia Godoy briefed the diplomatic corps on the incident in Santo Domingo, though few details were made public. In Washington, reports of the shelling prompted urgent discussions regarding an emergency meeting of the Council of the Organization of American States. Council President Gonzalo Facio of Costa Rica reported the outbreak based on information from Dominican Ambassador Enrique A. del Rosario.

El ministro de Relaciones Exteriores, Héctor García Godoy, informó al cuerpo diplomático sobre el incidente en Santo Domingo, aunque se divulgaron pocos detalles. En Washington, las noticias del ataque desencadenaron conversaciones urgentes con miras a una reunión de emergencia del Consejo de la Organización de los Estados Americanos. El presidente del Consejo, Gonzalo Facio, de Costa Rica, informó del estallido sobre la base de datos suministrados por el embajador dominicano Enrique A. del Rosario.

records.headline: After rebel forces led by former general Leon Cantave retreated
records.summary_en: After rebel forces led by former general Leon Cantave retreated across the frontier following a clash in Haiti, Dominican authorities interned about 120 Haitian fugitives. Haiti accused the Dominican Republic of aiding Cantave's insurgent effort to overthrow President Francois Duvalier, an allegation that Santo Domingo denied. As the rebels crossed over, witnesses reported rifle and machine gun fire striking the Dominican border town of Dajabon. While Haiti denied shooting across the border and accused Dominican soldiers of firing into Ouanaminthe, Cantave reported losing sixty men against a 500-man government garrison and claimed Haitian forces suffered 100 casualties.

records.summary_en: Following a border engagement between Haitian troops and rebels led by ex-general Leon Cantave, the Dominican Republic denied Haitian charges that it aided the insurgents, who retreated across the border into Dajabon under rifle and machine gun fire. Cantave reported losing sixty men against a 500-man garrison in Ouanaminthe and claimed Haitian forces suffered 100 casualties, while Dominican officials stated the internees would be transferred to Santo Domingo and about twenty wounded were receiving hospital treatment in Dajabon. Organization of American States Council President Gonzalo Facio appealed to both Dominican President Juan Bosch and Haitian President Francois Duvalier to avoid escalating the conflict. Facio stated the Dominican Foreign Ministry assured him no ultimatum had been issued to Haiti, despite official Dominican radio reports threatening an aerial bombing of Duvalier's palace in Port-au-Prince in retaliation for border firing.

records.headline: United States officials stated that the Dominican government
records.summary_en: United States officials stated that the Dominican government recognized by Washington ceased to exist following a military coup that overthrew President Juan Bosch. State Department spokesman Richard I. Phillips confirmed Bosch's arrest through the American embassy in Santo Domingo and noted that Washington lacked information regarding the military junta's intentions. The ouster was viewed as a major setback to American policy, which had sought to foster constitutional democracy through aid programs following the May 1961 assassination of dictator Rafael Leonidas Trujillo. Before communications were severed, Bosch and his wife placed early morning telephone calls to the presidents of Mexico, Costa Rica, and Venezuela, as well as the governor of Puerto Rico.
records.summary_es: Funcionarios de los Estados Unidos declararon que el gobierno dominicano reconocido por Washington dejó de existir tras un golpe militar que derrocó al presidente Juan Bosch. Phillips, confirmó el arresto de Bosch a través de la embajada estadounidense en Santo Domingo y señaló que Washington carecía de información sobre las intenciones de la junta militar. La destitución fue considerada un duro revés para la política norteamericana, que había buscado fomentar la democracia constitucional mediante programas de ayuda tras el asesinato del dictador Rafael Leonidas Trujillo en mayo de 1961. Antes de que se cortaran las comunicaciones, Bosch y su esposa realizaron llamadas telefónicas de madrugada a los presidentes de México, Costa Rica y Venezuela, así como al gobernador de Puerto Rico.

records.headline: Dominican military leaders carried out a pre-dawn coup in Santo
records.summary_en: Dominican military leaders carried out a pre-dawn coup in Santo Domingo, placing fifty-four-year-old President Juan Bosch under arrest in the presidential palace just two days short of seven months in office. Shortly before the uprising, machine gun bursts fired from the Haitian town of Ouanaminthe into the Dominican border town of Dajabon caused damage to a local church and school, continuing intermittent shooting sparked when Haitian forces fired on fleeing rebels led by former general Leon Cantave. Bosch, the first freely elected Dominican president since the assassination of strongman Rafael Trujillo, had repeatedly faced near-war conditions with neighboring Haiti while domestic governmental administration and the economy deteriorated.
records.summary_es: Jefes militares dominicanos ejecutaron un golpe de Estado de madrugada en Santo Domingo y arrestaron en el palacio presidencial al presidente Juan Bosch, de 54 años, a solo dos días de cumplir siete meses de mandato. Poco antes de la sublevación, ráfagas de ametralladora disparadas desde la localidad haitiana de Ouanaminthe contra el poblado fronterizo dominicano de Dajabón causaron daños a una iglesia y una escuela locales, prolongando los tiroteos intermitentes provocados cuando tropas haitianas dispararon contra rebeldes en fuga liderados por el exgeneral León Cantave. Bosch, el primer presidente dominicano libremente electo desde el asesinato del hombre fuerte Rafael Trujillo, había quedado en varias ocasiones al borde de la guerra con el vecino Haití mientras la administración estatal y la economía interna se deterioraban.

records.headline: Following a bloodless pre-dawn military coup in Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: Following a bloodless pre-dawn military coup in Santo Domingo, deposed President Juan Bosch was expected to be sent into exile in Puerto Rico, where Governor Luis Munoz Marin had anticipated his arrival. The Dominican military command announced that the fifty-four-year-old leader was receiving full guarantees, while the United States suspended diplomatic relations and its aid program, declaring the overthrow a blow to hemispheric democratic policy. Dominican Ambassador in Washington Enriquillo del Rosario refused to serve the junta, condemning it as illegal and accusing business interests enriched under the Trujillo dictatorship of undermining the constitutional government. Bosch's seizure in the presidential palace ended seven months of governance by the republic's first freely elected president since the May 30, 1961, assassination of Rafael Trujillo.
records.summary_es: Tras un golpe militar incruento ejecutado antes del amanecer en Santo Domingo, se esperaba que el derrocado presidente Juan Bosch fuera enviado al exilio en Puerto Rico, donde el gobernador Luis Muñoz Marín aguardaba su llegada. El mando militar dominicano anunció que el mandatario de 54 años recibía plenas garantías, mientras que Estados Unidos suspendió las relaciones diplomáticas y su programa de ayuda, calificando el derrocamiento como un duro revés para las políticas democráticas del hemisferio. El embajador dominicano en Washington, Enriquillo del Rosario, se negó a servir a la junta por considerarla ilegal y acusó a empresarios enriquecidos bajo la dictadura trujillista de sabotear al gobierno constitucional. La detención de Bosch en el palacio presidencial puso fin a siete meses de gestión del primer presidente libremente electo en la república desde el asesinato de Rafael Trujillo el 30 de mayo de 1961.

records.headline: Following the Wednesday military overthrow of Dominican President Juan
records.summary_en: Following the Wednesday military overthrow of Dominican President Juan Bosch, the United States delayed formal diplomatic relations until the character of the new regime becomes clear. American Ambassador John B. Martin in Santo Domingo was instructed to determine the military leadership's intentions without establishing formal diplomatic contact before returning to Washington for policy conferences. The State Department ordered the United States aid mission to freeze all disbursements and suspend operations while remaining in the country, whereas a small Peace Corps contingent will continue its work. Meanwhile, United States officials privately voiced concern over a potential return to Trujilloism without the Trujillos following the 1961 assassination of Generalissimo Rafael Trujillo. The military leaders who ousted Bosch have denied any Trujillo connections, but some officials here believe most of the Dominican military was so much a part of Trujillo's regime that it would be hard to separate them. The Dominican defense minister, Maj. Gen. Victor Viñas Román, who apparently commanded the coup against Bosch, is regarded as largely owing his position in life to the Trujillos. U.S. officials were disappointed with Bosch, the country's first freely elected president in 31 years; they regarded him as well-intentioned and liberal, but ineffective and “drifting.” But these officials regarded the military coup as a much worse blow to U.S. policy to foster democracy in Latin America.
records.summary_es: Tras el derrocamiento militar del presidente dominicano Juan Bosch ocurrido el miércoles, Estados Unidos postergó las relaciones diplomáticas formales hasta esclarecer el carácter del nuevo régimen. El embajador estadounidense John B. Martin recibió instrucciones en Santo Domingo de determinar las intenciones del mando militar sin entablar contactos diplomáticos oficiales antes de regresar a Washington para consultas políticas. El Departamento de Estado ordenó a la misión de ayuda estadounidense congelar los desembolsos y suspender operaciones aunque permanezca en el país, mientras que un pequeño contingente del Cuerpo de Paz continuará sus labores. Entre tanto, funcionarios norteamericanos expresaron en privado su inquietud ante un eventual retorno al trujillismo sin los Trujillo tras el asesinato del generalísimo Rafael Trujillo en 1961. Los líderes militares que derrocaron a Bosch han negado toda conexión con los Trujillo, pero algunos funcionarios aquí creen que la mayor parte de los militares dominicanos formaba parte tan intrínseca del régimen de Trujillo que sería difícil separarlos de él. El ministro de Defensa dominicano, el mayor general Víctor Viñas Román, quien al parecer comandó el golpe contra Bosch, es considerado deudor en buena medida de su posición en la vida a los Trujillo. Los funcionarios estadounidenses estaban decepcionados con Bosch, el primer presidente libremente elegido del país en 31 años; lo consideraban bienintencionado y liberal, pero ineficaz y «a la deriva». Pero esos funcionarios consideraban el golpe militar un golpe mucho peor para la política estadounidense de fomentar la democracia en América Latina.

records.headline: Mexico announced, following the military coup in the Dominican
records.summary_en: Mexico announced, following the military coup in the Dominican Republic, plans to maintain diplomatic relations with the new authorities under its doctrine that nations have no right to judge another's government. Costa Rica urged a meeting of foreign ministers to examine Dominican developments and evaluate measures against military coups, noting that Juan Bosch's administration was the third constitutional government overthrown in Latin America within six months. The United States withheld an immediate decision on the proposal, while Senator George Smathers of Florida encouraged President Kennedy to dispatch a mission of Latin American specialists to evaluate Dominican conditions. In Santo Domingo, Bosch remained held prisoner in the presidential palace, where guards allowed his wife to visit.
records.summary_es: México anunció, tras el golpe militar en la República Dominicana, su propósito de mantener relaciones diplomáticas con las nuevas autoridades bajo la doctrina de que los países carecen de derecho para calificar el gobierno de otros. Costa Rica propuso una reunión de cancilleres para examinar la situación dominicana y debatir medidas frente a los golpes militares, destacando que el régimen de Juan Bosch era el tercer gobierno constitucional derrocado en América Latina en seis meses. Estados Unidos aplazó una decisión inmediata sobre dicha propuesta, mientras el senador George Smathers de Florida instó al presidente Kennedy a enviar una comisión de especialistas en América Latina para evaluar las condiciones dominicanas. En Santo Domingo, Bosch continuaba recluido como prisionero en el palacio presidencial, donde los guardias permitieron el ingreso de su esposa.

records.headline: The United States Weather Bureau in San Juan maintained a hurricane
records.summary_en: The United States Weather Bureau in San Juan maintained a hurricane warning for the Dominican Republic east of San Pedro de Macoris, including the Samana Peninsula, as Hurricane Edith moved across the country's eastern tip. Chief forecaster Gordon Dunn in Miami reported that the storm posed no threat to the American mainland and was expected to move into the Atlantic after slight intensification. Meteorologists anticipated some further weakening as Edith traversed the eastern Dominican coastline, while gale warnings and heavy rains persisted across western Puerto Rico.

El meteorólogo jefe Gordon Dunn, desde Miami, informó que la tormenta no representaba una amenaza para el territorio continental estadounidense y que se esperaba su desplazamiento hacia el Atlántico tras una leve intensificación. Los expertos previeron un debilitamiento adicional conforme Edith cruzaba el litoral este dominicano, mientras continuaban las alertas por vendavales y las lluvias torrenciales en el oeste de Puerto Rico.

records.headline: Hurricane Edith, the season's fifth tropical storm, lost strength
records.summary_en: Hurricane Edith, the season's fifth tropical storm, lost strength as it passed over the eastern tip of the Dominican Republic during the night, reducing its winds from 100 miles per hour to seventy-five. Gordon Dunn, chief hurricane forecaster in Miami, stated that Edith remained a dangerous hurricane capable of regaining intensity over the open ocean. Amid the storm conditions and recent political upheaval, Radio Santo Domingo, the official government transmitter, went abruptly off the air at 11:34 a.m. without explanation.

Gordon Dunn, jefe de pronósticos de huracanes en Miami, afirmó que Edith continuaba siendo un huracán peligroso capaz de recobrar intensidad sobre mar abierto. En medio del temporal y las recientes convulsiones políticas, Radio Santo Domingo, la emisora oficial del gobierno, salió abruptamente del aire a las 11:34 a.m. sin que mediara explicación alguna.

records.headline: George Sherman, reporting from Santo Domingo, observes that gale-force
records.summary_en: George Sherman, reporting from Santo Domingo, observes that gale-force winds from Hurricane Edith and the uneasy aftermath of the military coup have left the Dominican capital gripped by tension. White-helmeted riot police carrying tear-gas canisters patrol the streets, while businesses along Calle El Conde remain shuttered behind steel security bars. The newly opened United States Information Service office is closed behind corrugated metal doors under protective Dominican police guard. Meanwhile, a local taxi driver from the airport proclaimed that normalcy had returned and that the country was rid of communism that had grown under deposed President Juan Bosch.

Policías antimotines con cascos blancos y botes de gas lacrimógeno patrullan las calles, mientras los comercios de la calle El Conde permanecen protegidos tras rejas de acero. Las flamantes oficinas del Servicio de Información de los Estados Unidos se encuentran clausuradas tras compuertas metálicas bajo custodia policial dominicana preventiva. Entretanto, un taxista local proveniente del aeropuerto aseguró que la normalidad había retornado y que el país se había librado del comunismo que proliferaba bajo el derrocado presidente Juan Bosch.

records.headline: A three-man civilian junta was established in Santo Domingo
records.summary_en: A three-man civilian junta was established in Santo Domingo as a provisional government pending general elections scheduled for 1965, following the military coup against President Juan Bosch and his cabinet. The armed forces announced that opposition party leaders selected Emilio de los Santos, Ramon Tapia Espinal, and Manuel Enrique Tavares to head the administration. De los Santos and Tapia are lawyers, while Tavares is an engineer, and all three members were prominent opponents of the former Trujillo dictatorship. De los Santos previously served as president of the electoral board that certified Bosch's presidential election victory.
records.summary_es: Una junta civil de tres miembros se constituyó en Santo Domingo como gobierno provisional a la espera de elecciones generales programadas para 1965, tras el golpe militar contra el presidente Juan Bosch y su gabinete. Las fuerzas armadas anunciaron que dirigentes de partidos de oposición seleccionaron a Emilio de los Santos, Ramón Tapia Espinal y Manuel Enrique Tavares para encabezar la administración. De los Santos y Tapia son abogados, mientras que Tavares es ingeniero, y los tres integrantes destacaron en el pasado como opositores a la dictadura trujillista. De los Santos se había desempeñado previamente como presidente de la junta electoral que certificó el triunfo electoral de Bosch a la presidencia.

records.headline: Informed sources in Santo Domingo reported on Saturday that United States Ambassador John Bartlow Martin
records.summary_en: Informed sources in Santo Domingo reported on Saturday that United States Ambassador John Bartlow Martin was being summoned to Washington for consultations and was not expected to return, following the suspension of diplomatic relations and aid programs after military leaders ousted President Juan Bosch on Wednesday. Although the State Department confirmed Martin had been called home for consultations, it stated that no final decision had been made regarding his return. Meanwhile, the military junta kept secret its plans to deport the former president into exile aboard a navy frigate to Europe, possibly Spain, once seas ruffled by Hurricane Edith had calmed, seeking to avoid triggering disorders.
records.summary_es: Fuentes informadas en Santo Domingo informaron el sábado que el embajador de Estados Unidos John Bartlow Martin estaba siendo llamado a Washington para consultas y no se esperaba que regresara, tras la suspensión de relaciones diplomáticas y programas de ayuda luego de que los militares derrocaran al presidente Juan Bosch el miércoles. Si bien el Departamento de Estado confirmó que Martin había sido llamado a consultas, afirmó que no se había tomado una decisión definitiva respecto a su regreso. Entretanto, la junta militar mantuvo en secreto sus planes de deportar al expresidente al exilio a bordo de una fragata naval hacia Europa, posiblemente España, una vez calmadas las aguas agitadas por el huracán Edith, buscando evitar desórdenes.

records.headline: Deposed President Juan Bosch was sped out of the National Palace
records.summary_en: Deposed President Juan Bosch was sped out of the National Palace on Saturday night for deportation aboard the Dominican Navy frigate Melia following his overthrow in a pre-dawn military coup on Wednesday. General Antonio Imbert Barrera, leader of the military junta, declined to disclose the frigate's destination, amid speculation that Bosch faced a two- to three-week voyage to Europe. In the palace, newly appointed Foreign Minister Donald Reid Cabral undertook the difficult task of securing foreign recognition for the hastily established regime, as United States Ambassador John Martin departed for Washington by way of San Juan after receiving instructions earlier that day.
records.summary_es: El depuesto presidente Juan Bosch fue retirado rápidamente del Palacio Nacional el sábado por la noche para su deportación a bordo de la fragata Melia de la Marina dominicana, tras su derrocamiento en un golpe de Estado militar en la madrugada del miércoles. El general Antonio Imbert Barrera, líder de la junta militar, se negó a revelar el destino de la fragata, en medio de especulaciones de que Bosch enfrentaba una travesía de dos a tres semanas hacia Europa. En el palacio, el recién nombrado ministro de Relaciones Exteriores, Donald Reid Cabral, asumió la difícil tarea de obtener el reconocimiento exterior para el régimen establecido apresuradamente, mientras el embajador de Estados Unidos John Martin partía hacia Washington vía San Juan tras recibir instrucciones más temprano ese mismo día.

records.headline: Costa Rica severed diplomatic relations with the Dominican Republic pursuant
records.summary_en: Costa Rica severed diplomatic relations with the Dominican Republic pursuant to its policy against recognizing governments that seize power through coups, while the United States and Venezuela suspended relations. Costa Rica also proposed a foreign ministers' meeting to examine Dominican affairs and consider collective measures against coups in the hemisphere, noting the Bosch administration was the third constitutional government overthrown in Latin America in six months. In Santo Domingo, deposed President Bosch was held prisoner in the presidential palace, where his wife visited him after arriving from Puerto Rico, while the provisional government prepared to determine whether to exile him under military accusations of coddling Communists and causing economic chaos.
records.summary_es: Costa Rica rompió relaciones diplomáticas con la República Dominicana en cumplimiento de su política de no reconocer gobiernos que toman el poder mediante golpes de Estado, mientras que Estados Unidos y Venezuela suspendieron relaciones. Costa Rica también propuso una reunión de ministros de Relaciones Exteriores para examinar los asuntos dominicanos y considerar medidas colectivas contra los golpes en el hemisferio, señalando que el gobierno de Bosch fue el tercer régimen constitucional derrocado en América Latina en seis meses. En Santo Domingo, el depuesto presidente Bosch permaneció detenido en el palacio presidencial, donde su esposa lo visitó tras llegar desde Puerto Rico, mientras el gobierno provisional se preparaba para determinar si lo exiliaba bajo acusaciones militares de tolerar a los comunistas y causar el caos económico.

records.headline: The withdrawal of United States Ambassador John Bartlow Martin
records.summary_en: The withdrawal of United States Ambassador John Bartlow Martin and the chiefs of the military and aid missions over the weekend has dealt a severe blow to the new Dominican regime amid its urgent drive for foreign recognition. Following deposed President Juan Bosch's departure on Saturday night, the civilian triumvirate installed by the military has sought to demonstrate effective governance by lifting the emergency state of siege and the strict 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. curfew. Regime apologists have emphasized the reopening of two closed radio stations, the military's return to barracks, and the release of several hundred of an estimated 700 persons arrested during a recent anti-Communist sweep to show adherence to pledges restoring civil liberties.
records.summary_es: La retirada del embajador de Estados Unidos John Bartlow Martin y de los jefes de las misiones militar y de ayuda durante el fin de semana asestó un duro golpe al nuevo régimen dominicano en medio de su urgente búsqueda de reconocimiento exterior. records.summary_en: The Weather Bureau advised residents along a peninsula of the Dominican Republic to seek safety before it was too late as Hurricane Flora advanced through the Caribbean. Forecasters predicted the center of the dangerous storm would pass approximately 100 miles south of Isla Beata, Dominican Republic, around 8 o'clock tonight and 30 miles south of Les Cayes, Haiti, by noon Thursday. The San Juan Weather Bureau placed the storm center 240 miles south of Santo Domingo at 11 a.m. EST, tracking west-northwest at 14 miles per hour after devastating Tobago on Monday night.

records.headline: Exiled Dominican official Diego Bordas denounced the leaders of the new government
records.summary_en: Exiled Dominican official Diego Bordas denounced the leaders of the new government as pupils of Trujillo who inherited his vices and used anti-communism as a ruse to justify political purges. Bordas charged that police chief General Belisario Peguero had to fabricate communists to rationalize holding 3,500 prisoners in Santo Domingo alone and more than 10,000 across the republic. Describing his own detention with his 14-year-old son Ivan in a cell measuring 20 feet by 10 feet packed with 101 inmates and running water for only one hour daily, Bordas declared he would join ousted President Juan Bosch in exile while Dominicans prepared a general strike to paralyze the nation.

Bordas acusó al jefe de policía, el general Belisario Peguero, de tener que fabricar comunistas para justificar la detención de 3.500 prisioneros sólo en Santo Domingo y más de 10.000 en toda la república. Al describir su propia detención junto a su hijo Iván, de 14 años, en una celda de 20 por 10 pies abarrotada con 101 reclusos y agua corriente durante apenas una hora al día, Bordas declaró que se uniría al derrocado presidente Juan Bosch en el exilio mientras los dominicanos preparaban una huelga general para paralizar la nación.
